title: Egypt approves military support for Saudi Arabia after Houthi attacks escalate
body: Parliament authorized Egypt's military on Monday to provide support to help defend Saudi Arabia, parliamentarians said, and local media reported, a move that could push Cairo directly into the regional conflict that has expanded with intensified attacks by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis on the Gulf kingdom.President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi had asked parliament last week to approve defending its Gulf Arab ally and the world's biggest oil exporter if Riyadh requests help against the Houthis, whose advances also threaten the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait - a gateway to Egypt's Suez Canal.Egypt has frequently condemned Iranian and Iranian-backed attacks on Gulf countries but has not publicly engaged in direct combat or joined the Mecca mutual defense pact between Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey that was signed in August.Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said this month that Egyptian membership in the pact remains "under serious consideration."Egypt joined Saudi-backed anti-Houthi coalition in 2015Egypt, the Arab world's most populous state with one of the region's largest militaries, joined the Saudi-led coalition in an earlier phase of Yemen's war in March 2015 mainly as a naval partner, sending warships to secure Red Sea shipping lanes while pledging air support. It also deployed around 800 ground troops but played only a limited combat role.Egypt was involved in a costly military intervention in Yemen in the 1960s and has not undertaken a large-scale ​foreign ground deployment since the 1991 Gulf War.Saudi Arabia is a major political and financial partner of Cairo, providing billions of dollars in aid, deposits at the central bank, and energy supplies under Sisi.Fighting between the Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's internationally recognized government and the Houthi militia, which controls the capital Sanaa, has escalated in recent weeks, becoming a volatile front in the US-Israeli war on Iran.Houthis attack Saudi airport, energy infrastructureThe Houthis have attacked Riyadh's international airport and the state oil giant Saudi Aramco, disrupting flights and oil exports, while aid agencies have warned of worsening conditions in Yemen, already suffering one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.Abdelatty and Egyptian intelligence chief Hassan Rashad traveled to Riyadh on Wednesday to deliver a letter to Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman from Sisi, who said Egypt's support would be limited to defending Saudi territory and borders rather than attacking Yemen. Abdelatty said after that visit that Cairo advocates exploring "every opportunity" to resolve the Yemen conflict diplomatically.The Saudi crown prince visited Sisi in Cairo on September 15 to discuss security and navigation in the Red Sea after the fighting in Yemen reignited.

title: From reserve duty to Knesset candidate: Meet B'Yachad's Amir Sturgo - interview
body: The current Knesset elections are imminent, but with a new race and new parties come new names and faces.Depending on how this election turns out, these newcomers of today could be the ministers of tomorrow and can help shape the course of Israeli politics going forward. One such newcomer is Amir Strugo, a candidate on Naftali Bennett's B'Yachad list. What is his story? What brought him to politics?Strugois the CEO of Aharai, an organization that promotes leadership skills in Israeli youth. A veteran of the Second Lebanon War, he saw combat during the October 7 massacre. Sturgo spent over 450 days on reserve duty. Today, he lives in the Negev and helps lead B'Yachad party policies on combating crime, particularly in the region he calls home. Shortly before the elections, we spoke briefly with him to hear his story.What got you into politics?After losing 66 Aharai alumni and serving over 450 days in the military reserves, I decided this must be my mission. I view my entry into politics as a continuation of the path I forged in the military, in education, and in civil society.What made you want to run with B'Yachad?I believe Bennett possesses the experience and skills required to lead Israel at this critical juncture. B'Yachad is the only party offering detailed action plans to address the root causes of the challenges we face - from the conscription crisis and the collapse of our education system to rampant crime and the erosion of governance (a reality my neighbors and I witness daily in the Negev), and more.What do you think are the biggest issues in this election?We must invest in Israel's social, security, and economic engines of growth. In practical terms, this means implementing the "Revolution for Those Who Serve" - a policy we propose. When we invest in the segment of the public that serves and works, the nation becomes stronger, more secure, and more prosperous.Conversely, when we invest in draft evasion and educational systems that fail to teach core subjects, the consequences for our national security and economy are predictable.This is the choice before us.Why do you think Bennett is the right person to handle them?Throughout his tenure as minister of education, minister of economy, minister of defense, and prime minister, Bennett has proven his ability to focus on what truly matters and deliver tangible results on the ground - such as the "5-unit" (advanced-level) reform in education, achieving the quietest year in the south in terms of security, and driving down prices in the economy.Judging by his track record, he has succeeded in every role he has held - both before entering politics, as a businessman and a commander, and since.There is no substitute for this kind of experience. As someone who served as a military commander and chose to live in a community that integrates both religious and secular residents, unity is important to me - not merely as a slogan, but as a way of life. I see Bennett as a leader capable of uniting all segments of the nation and forging a shared Israeli narrative.What advice do you have for anyone interested in getting into politics?Follow your heart and your inner convictions all the way, and do not let peripheral noise hold you back.

title: Israel to supply Cyprus with new offshore patrol vessel equipped with Rafael systems
body: Israel and Cyprus signed an agreement on Monday for the acquisition of a new offshore patrol vessel (OPV) equipped with advanced Israeli naval systems, the Defense Ministry announced.It was signed in Cyprus by Defense Ministry Director General Maj.-Gen. (res.) Amir Baram and Stelios Kountouris, acting permanent secretary of the Cyprus Defense Ministry.According to the Defense Ministry, the deal was led by its International Defense Cooperation Directorate (SIBAT) and the Cypriot Defense Ministry's Armaments & Defense Capabilities Development Directorate."Israel will supply Cyprus with a new patrol vessel built by Israel Shipyards and fitted with a range of Rafael naval systems," the ministry said. "In parallel, the systems aboard Cyprus's existing Israel Shipyards-built patrol vessel will be upgraded.”The signing ceremony was attended by Head of SIBAT Brig.-Gen. (res.) Yair Kulas, Ambassador to Cyprus Shuli Davidovich, Israel Shipyards CEO Eitan Zucker, and Rafael's Head of Naval Warfare Systems Directorate Ran Tavor."This agreement marks another important step in strengthening the operational capabilities of the Cyprus Naval Command and enhancing its capacity to respond to maritime security challenges," the ministry said."The new OPV, alongside the upgraded OPV IOANNIDES, will support expanded patrol, surveillance, and search-and-rescue missions."The ministry added that the agreement reflected the two countries' commitment to regional stability.Israel and Cyprus have expanded their defense cooperation in recent years, including naval security, military exercises, and defense procurement. Cyprus previously acquired the OPV Ioannides from Israel Shipyards, providing a foundation for the latest agreement, which includes upgrades to the existing vessel.The two countries also cooperate with Greece on regional security matters, including exercises and military coordination in the eastern Mediterranean.Cyprus received its first Israeli-built offshore patrol vessel, Commodore Andreas Ioannides, in 2018. The vessel was equipped with Rafael Typhoon naval weapon stations. Cyprus has also acquired Israeli defense equipment including the Barak MX air-defense system and Spike LR2 anti-tank missiles, according to a report by Cyprus Mail. The value of the new naval agreement was not disclosed in the ministry's statement, although Calcalist previously reported that the proposed package was worth approximately $100 million.

title: IDF stops short of denying report Zamir, Netanyahu clashed over Iran strike before elections
body: The IDF on Monday issued a statement addressing an avalanche of reports about controversy between IDF Chief of Staff Lt.-Gen. Eyal Zamir and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over the handling of a potential war with Iran.The statement emphasized that Zamir was above political considerations and any specific party, noting that his and the IDF's sole focus is Israel's national security, apart from politics.However, the statement did not deny that Zamir blocked Netanyahu from taking further action against Iran, citing concerns that politics might influence the prime minister's decision-making.According to the IDF, regarding "various reports in the Israeli and international media over the last day or so, including various statements related to the IDF chief of staff or senior officials, we would like to clarify: The army is focused on its missions and is on high alert on every front, according to the warnings and sensitivity of this [election] period.""The operational activities and factors considered by the IDF are based solely on security, professional, substantive, and nonpartisan considerations, and any other discussion is misleading and irrelevant," said the military.IDF chief pushed back on Netanyahu order for 'action' against Iran, fearing political motivesIsrael's Channel 12 reported on Sunday that Netanyahu and Zamir clashed over a military action that could renew the conflict with Iran days before Israel's elections.Recently, Zamir received a directive from the political echelon to carry out an action, which security officials told N12 would "trigger a rapid escalation into a confrontation with Iran."Due to the sensitive nature of the action, N12 reported that Zamir requested an in-depth discussion and formal authorization before moving forward with the action.Sources familiar with the details told N12 that Zamir and additional IDF leadership are concerned that the political echelon may be trying to exploit the front with Iran ahead of elections for political gain. Netanyahu denied the report late on Sunday night, saying on Channel 14's The Patriots that “there is no confrontation” and that “someone is trying to obscure the fact that Zamir himself had said Iran was attempting to interfere in the elections.”The Mossad declined to respond to the Post's report that Mossad Director Roman Gofman sided with Netanyahu over Zamir.Miriam Sela-Eitam contributed to this report.

title: Israeli lawyer indicted over alleged contact with foreign agent, obstruction of justice
body: An Israeli lawyer was arrested nearly two-and-a-half weeks ago by Israel Police and the Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency) on suspicion of security offenses. The State Attorney's Office filed an indictment against her with the Central District Court in Lod on Monday, charging her with contact with a foreign agent and obstruction of justice.The case remains under a gag order; the Central District Court in Lod allowed only a summary to be published at the request of security authorities.The prosecution said that the investigation revealed that she was in contact with a foreign agent and committed acts of obstruction of justice.The prosecution also requested that she be detained until proceedings against her conclude.The announcement concerning the lawyer did not identify the foreign agent's affiliation or disclose the nature of their alleged contact.Authorities announce efforts by Iran to recruit IsraelisAuthorities have announced a series of cases involving alleged Iranian efforts to recruit Israelis through social media and online messaging platforms. In those cases, prosecutors have described offers of payment for assignments ranging from photography and information-gathering to threats and violent acts.In April, prosecutors indicted two young Israelis in a case involving alleged contact with Iranian intelligence. According to the indictment, the main defendant was approached through a Telegram group and offered money for illegal assignments. The second defendant allegedly helped prepare forged documents purporting to contain classified information about Israeli and US plans to attack Iran.In February, the Jerusalem District Court sentenced Elimelech Stern to three years in prison after convicting him of contact with an Iranian intelligence operative and conspiracy to threaten. His case involved assignments carried out in exchange for cryptocurrency payments.

title: Hundreds of Hebron families displaced by IDF operations, uncertain when they can return - interview
body: The IDF did not give families ample time to pack before they were made to evacuate their homes and has not offered any assurances on whether and when they will be allowed to return, Riyad Khamis, the spokesperson for Hebron's official Support and Relief Committee, told The Jerusalem Post on Monday.The IDF has established new checkpoints and evacuated parts of Hebron following a terrorist attack carried out on Friday by Ahmed and Hamouda al-Jabar, two Palestinians from the Ein Deir Bahha neighborhood, which killed two Israeli soldiers and wounded several others.Sharing data collected on Monday from Ein Deir Bahha, Al-Jilda, Khillet Al-Magharbeh, Farsh al-Hawa, and surrounding areas, Khamis said 407 households, comprising 2,649 people, were affected by the military action.The figure included 1,109 people under the age of 18, of whom 180 were under the age of two; 218 elderly people; 115 pregnant or postpartum women; 28 people with disabilities; and 162 living with chronic illnesses.Milena Ansari, the director of the Occupied Palestinian Territory Department at Physicians for Human Rights Israel, told the Post on Sunday that the disruption of routine for the chronically sick and/or disabled might create an emergency.“People with chronic conditions like diabetes, hypertension, kidney disease, or cancer depend on regular treatment and medication. These arbitrary closures interrupt that care. Displacement also separates people from their medications, doctors, and medical records,” Ansari warned.“A condition that could be managed with routine care can quickly become an emergency, which then runs into the same blocked roads, closures, and restrictions on movement. Of course, winter makes every one of these risks even worse,” she added.Majority of displaced Palestinians have found alternative accommodationThough the large majority of the displaced Palestinians have found alternative accommodation, with relatives or by renting other homes, Khamis said that 168 households had no available housing options.“Some families found themselves without safe accommodation or a suitable alternative, and some were forced to spend the night outdoors,” he said.“When we say that 185 families have no safe place to stay, we are describing a difficult humanitarian reality. These families have no alternative accommodation beyond staying with relatives, resulting in overcrowded and unsuitable living conditions. Some are also struggling to obtain the most basic necessities of life.”Asserting the need for humanitarian intervention, he told the Post that, based on data collected from the displaced so far, 231 households needed food supplies, 129 needed medicines, 107 needed baby formula and diapers, and 126 needed shelter.Others have reportedly requested aid with clothing, mattresses, blankets, and psychological support.Displaced families given inadequate time to prepare for their evacuationKhamis said that the displaced families said they were not given enough time by the IDF to prepare to leave their homes and that the evacuations “took place under difficult, high-pressure conditions … without sufficient clarity about how long the evacuation would last or when families would be allowed to return to their homes.”“There was no direct communication with the military, except through notices and demands to leave. These did not provide clear and sufficient information about the duration of the operation, the nature of the measures being taken, or the guarantees concerning residents' return to their homes,” he said.Adding to this, Khamis said that they had received no information to suggest Israeli authorities established any arrangements to help facilitate the evacuation of elderly, disabled, or sick Palestinians, which “presented a significant humanitarian challenge, particularly because some families include people who require medical care and ongoing assistance.”In a statement to The Post, the IDF said that the operation, which came in response to Friday's terror attack, has seen a cordon imposed where the military is operating and that civilians were allowed to voluntarily leave the area as a way to mitigate potential harm.“Their departure was facilitated through designated, safe corridors that had been established in advance and communicated to the civilian population,” the military insisted. “Consequently, residents were unable to return to the area while the operation was underway.“Once military activity in the area concludes, and in accordance with the law, residents will be permitted to return to their homes immediately.”The military also emphasized that the area of operations is affiliated with Hamas and has a “direct link” to the terrorists responsible for the murder of two soldiers on Friday.

title: IDF finds underground shaft near West Bank home of Hamas terrorist who killed two soldiers
body: The IDF announced on Monday that it had discovered a concealed underground shaft near the home of one of the Hamas terrorists who killed two IDF soldiers in an attack on Friday.According to the IDF, the shaft was approximately 15 meters deep and relatively narrow. It was found near the terrorist's home in the Hebron area of the West Bank.While the discovery was not unprecedented, underground shafts are extremely rare in the West Bank. Underground warfare has been more commonly associated with Hamas in Gaza and Hezbollah in Lebanon, where tunnels have played a significant role in military operations, than with Hamas in the West Bank, where the IDF maintains greater control and surveillance.The discovery came after the IDF searched approximately 500 Palestinian homes and other locations throughout the West Bank, particularly in the Hebron area, as part of its efforts following Friday's attack.The IDF also said it had found an unidentified electronic device inside the shaft. The device was transferred to investigators for examination.Two troops killed after terrorists with machine gun open fire in West BankStaff Sergeant Ron Yonatan Roytman, 23, from Ashkelon, and Sergeant Yuval Shai Svilem, 20, from Hod Hasharon, were named on Friday as the two soldiers killed in the attack.Roytman was a squad commander, while Svilem was a combat soldier in the Ari Battalion (775) of the Search and Rescue Brigade, according to the IDF.Both soldiers were killed in combat at the Judea Junction when two terrorists traveling in a car, armed with an M4 machine gun and a pistol, opened fire on soldiers at the scene.

title: Mecca defense pact faces test as Saudi delegation arrives for high-stakes Iran talks - analysis
body: On Monday, Saudi Arabia's Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman arrived in Tehran. He will partake in talks between the countries that signed the Makkah Joint Defense Agreement (Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan) and Iran. These talks are significant and will test the new agreement.The Makkah Joint Defense Agreement is a defense agreement, partially modeled on NATO. Some have questioned how the agreement will function, however. The Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia led to questions about whether Turkey and Pakistan would help Riyadh.Tehran presents a new test for the agreement: can its member countries produce results? Skeptics have argued that the three countries aren't giving the agreement the bite to match its bark. Pakistan's army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, and Turkish Intelligence Chief Ibrahim Kalin will also be in Iran. Notably, these men are some of the region's heavy hitters.Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said on Monday that Iran's hosting of senior military and security officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey is a key development toward establishing regional diplomacy. He added that this could help with lasting stability and security in the Middle East.Baghaei then argued that such stability could be achieved only if the region's countries worked together. This suggests the region needs to handle its own problems without the US.It's unclear if the US and Israel will sign on. The two have openly said that the war with Iran will continue.Most Israelis see the US-Israel relationship as larger than just one personUS President Donald Trump has twice endorsed Israel's prime minister to remain in power. He has, in essence, argued that the US cannot work with anyone else in Israel when it comes to war with Iran. This is surprising to many Israelis because most see the US-Israel relationship as larger than just one person. In fact, most Israelis agree on the need to confront Iran.Iran, for its part, knows that Israel has ordered the toppling of its regime. After all, it can read the news like anyone else. Iran also knows of reports that say the IDF was reluctant to carry out strikes right before Israel's elections. The presence of high-level Turkish, Pakistani, and Saudi delegations in Tehran implies that they think the war can be postponed for a few more days.The upcoming talks may show that the Makkah Defense Agreement is more about shared interests and diplomacy instead of tanks and warplanes.Many commentators asked whether the Makkah Joint Defense Agreement would be like NATO. NATO, however, has shown that it historically isn't about waging war; it's more about bringing together Western democracies, with militaries training together and sharing operations and culture. NATO hasn't engaged in many wars in its 77 years since its founding in 1949. The demand from some that the Mekkah pact will immediately rush into war largely misunderstands the pact and the countries involved.Saudi Arabia is a cautious and conservative state. Monarchies tend to be cautious and conservative; otherwise, they put themselves at risk. Turkey, by contrast, was more militarily active in 2016-2022 and has since become more cautious. Pakistan, despite recent clashes with India and Afghanistan, is also a conservative and cautious state in contrast to how it was decades ago.Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan established a new trilateral security alliance in AugustThe background of the Makkah pact is worth examining. Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan signed the Makkah Joint Defense Agreement on August 7, 2026, establishing a new trilateral security alliance. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif signed the agreement in Makkah.The agreement includes a collective defense clause under which an armed attack against one member is considered an attack against all three. It also calls for expanded military cooperation, joint exercises, intelligence sharing, defense technology development, and cooperation between defense industries.The alliance brings together three significant military powers, including nuclear-armed Pakistan and NATO member Turkey. It could have important implications for the regional balance of power and emerging security arrangements in the Middle East. The agreement also establishes a Strategic Political and Defense Committee to coordinate cooperation. Turkey published the full text in October as it moved toward parliamentary ratification.Meanwhile, in Riyadh, Arab News said that “the Kingdom's Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman is leading a delegation to Tehran for talks between countries party to the Makkah Joint Defense Agreement and Iran, to help ease regional tensions, Saudi Arabia's deputy minister for public diplomacy said on Monday.”The report added that “the meeting will be held with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and the Secretary-General of the Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaei.” This is important because Riyadh views it as part of ongoing efforts by the Makkah pact states to de-escalate the current situation and encourage dialogue and diplomatic solutions, Arab News added, based on a post by Saudi Arabia's Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Dr. Rayed Krimly.

title: As Syrian families struggle with missing loved ones, Assad's government figures reemerge
body: For nearly 15 years, Hussein al-Tawil and his family have waited to learn what happened to Ali Ahmad al-Tawil, a 29-year-old civilian from Jabal al-Zawiya in the Idlib countryside who disappeared in Damascus in late 2011. Year after year, the family received no answers. They did not know whether Ali was alive or dead. According to his brother Hussein, Ali disappeared at the hands of militias loyal to former Syrian President Bashar al-Assad. When Assad's government collapsed, the family hoped Ali might be among the detainees released from prisons or that newly accessible detention facilities and records might finally reveal his fate. But they found no trace of him. They received neither a death certificate nor any official document explaining what had happened. Now, as Hussein continues waiting for news of his brother, he watches figures who once supported Assad reappear in public life, with some seeking proximity to Syria's new authorities. For Hussein, Assad's fall did not end his family's ordeal. Instead, it raised another question: How can Syria pursue national reconciliation while so many families still do not know what happened to their loved ones? "We had hoped for transitional justice that would hold criminals accountable, and for moral justice that would remove from public life those who supported Assad through the media, arts, politics, and sports," al-Tawil told The Media Line. He said the renewed public prominence of former government supporters has deepened the anguish of victims' families, particularly those still waiting for information about missing relatives. His concerns extend beyond the absence of accountability. He fears that networks of influence established under Assad could survive by shifting their allegiance to the new leadership. In his view, some figures who supported the former government may now be prepared to offer their loyalty to the new authorities in exchange for preserving their economic interests and influence. Without meaningful institutional change, he warned, the same practices that enabled authoritarian rule could reemerge under different leadership. Al-Tawil's experience reflects a broader debate in Syria over the return of individuals associated with Assad's government to economic, political, and public life, even as victims' families continue demanding information about the disappeared and accountability for past abuses. Syrian political activist and former opposition figure Jubair al-Sukkari believes Assad's removal has not yet produced the deeper changes many Syrians expected. Speaking to The Media Line, al-Sukkari criticized the appearance of figures associated with the former government in institutions established during Syria's transition, particularly those involved in transitional justice and preserving the memory of victims. He cited what he described as the appointment of Futah Saqr, whom he characterized as having a Baathist background and family ties to figures associated with the former government, to a role at the National Commission for Transitional Justice involving the preservation of historical memory and archives. Al-Sukkari questioned the criteria used to select individuals entrusted with documenting the Syrian uprising and preserving the experiences of its victims, arguing that such responsibilities require the confidence of survivors and their families. The Media Line has not independently verified Saqr's alleged position, the nature of her responsibilities, or the background al-Sukkari described. His statements are allegations, not established findings. Al-Sukkari also raised concerns about Fadi Saqr, a figure formerly associated with the pro-Assad National Defense Forces, questioning the public reemergence of individuals linked to armed formations from the previous era without adequate scrutiny of their past roles. He referred to allegations of abuses involving pro-government armed groups in Damascus and other parts of Syria and called for investigations into those suspected of participating in violations. Such allegations alone do not establish individual criminal responsibility, which must be determined through evidence and appropriate legal proceedings. Fall of regime only first objective of revolution, political activist saysFor al-Sukkari, the renewed visibility of former Assad supporters sends a painful message to those who opposed the previous government and lost relatives during the conflict. "As families of victims and relatives of martyrs, we have so far achieved only the first objective of our revolution, which was the fall of the regime," he said. He also criticized what he described as the marginalization of some military officers who defected from Assad's forces, arguing that individuals who opposed the former government have not always been given the roles they expected in the new state. Nevertheless, al-Sukkari emphasized that backing Assad did not necessarily mean someone had committed crimes."There is a difference between a supporter and a criminal," he said.He argued that Syrians who supported Assad politically or worked in civilian state institutions should not automatically be treated in the same way as individuals found responsible for abuses against civilians. Financial settlements involving businessmen associated with Assad's government have become another major source of controversy. One prominent example is the settlement involving businessman Mohammed Hamsho, who was closely tied to the economic circles around the former president. Syrian President Ahmad al-Sharaa defended such settlements during a September meeting with members of the Syrian diaspora in New York. Al-Sharaa said authorities had confiscated about 80% of Hamsho's assets while allowing him to keep the portion they determined was not acquired unlawfully. He argued that companies associated with Hamsho provided employment for approximately 40,000 people and that confiscating all their assets could jeopardize those jobs and harm Syria's economy. The president also stressed that a financial settlement would not protect Hamsho from criminal prosecution if he were found responsible for other offenses. His remarks outlined the government's argument for separating asset recovery and economic continuity from criminal accountability. Critics, however, question whether such a distinction can be maintained in practice, particularly when individuals with substantial financial resources and established networks may retain influence over public institutions or investigations. Businessmen associated with Assad retained wealth after government changeBishr al-Hawi, a member of Syria's People's Assembly, told The Media Line that it is important to distinguish between the political return of former government figures and the continued economic activity of businessmen previously associated with Assad. According to al-Hawi, former political figures have not returned to their previous positions of influence, while some businessmen have negotiated financial settlements with the new authorities and retained portions of their wealth. He acknowledged that traders and business figures associated with the former government have resumed economic activities but said they are less prominent than under Assad. Al-Hawi argued that these individuals have not necessarily regained their former economic standing or political influence, adding that Syria needs the resources some of them possess. At the same time, he acknowledged delays in implementing transitional justice. "The transitional justice file has not received the momentum we had hoped for," al-Hawi said. He said the People's Assembly seeks to accelerate the process in cooperation with the relevant executive institutions. In a significant acknowledgment, al-Hawi said the assembly had not yet received a draft transitional justice law from the National Commission for Transitional Justice. He explained that the commission was expected to submit a legislative proposal for parliamentary consideration and eventual approval, but it had not yet done so. The People's Assembly is awaiting the proposal before beginning its legislative review, he said. His comments highlight a central tension in Syria's transition: Economic settlements involving figures associated with the former government are moving forward while, according to a member of the legislature, the proposed legal framework for transitional justice has yet to reach parliament. Reintegration of former Syrian government officials must abide by legal standardsAl-Moutassim al-Kilani, a researcher specializing in international criminal law, said the reintegration of individuals associated with the former government must be governed by clear legal standards that protect victims' rights and prevent financial or political influence from replacing accountability. Speaking to The Media Line, al-Kilani stressed that support for Assad alone does not establish criminal responsibility. Criminal accountability, he explained, must be based on specific conduct and evidence rather than former political affiliations. He warned, however, that financial settlements could produce impunity in practice if money, personal connections, or political influence obstruct investigations or shield individuals from prosecution, even without any formal grant of immunity. He argued that recovering public assets does not extinguish criminal liability or eliminate victims' rights to truth, justice, and reparations. "Recovering the money is a duty, but it does not pay the price of torture, killing, or enforced disappearance," al-Kilani said. He maintained that genuine national reconciliation requires establishing the truth, acknowledging abuses, compensating victims, and reforming the institutions that allowed violations to occur. He also rejected collective punishment, emphasizing that former political affiliation or employment in state institutions should not be treated as proof of criminal wrongdoing. For al-Kilani, one of the greatest risks is that old networks of influence could preserve their ability to shape political decisions, security institutions, the judiciary, and the economy simply by transferring their loyalty to the new leadership. "Changing loyalties does not dismantle a corruption network, and changing faces is not enough if the same mechanisms of control remain in place," he said. He argued that preventing a recurrence of past abuses requires an independent judiciary, accountable security institutions, transparent economic agreements, and effective protections for victims seeking justice. Economic settlements are not pardons for violations in SyriaThe National Commission for Transitional Justice has previously stated that economic settlements do not constitute pardons for serious violations and do not grant immunity from criminal prosecution. Questions remain, however, about how that principle will be enforced, whether independent mechanisms exist to examine the records of individuals entering settlements, and what safeguards will protect victims' claims from political or economic interference. The Media Line contacted the head of the National Commission for Transitional Justice for comment on criticism of the transitional justice process and settlements involving figures associated with Assad's government. The commission's chairman referred the request to its media office. After several hours of follow-up, the media office said it would respond later but did not specify when. The Media Line had not received responses to its questions by the time this report was prepared. The debate reaches beyond whether former Assad supporters should be allowed to participate in Syria's public life. While the authorities defend certain settlements as a way to recover assets, preserve jobs, and support a fragile economy, some former opposition activists and victims' families fear that reintegrating influential figures without sufficient scrutiny could undermine confidence in the country's new institutions. Legal experts emphasize that transitional justice should neither criminalize everyone who supported the former government nor let economic arrangements replace investigations and accountability. With a member of the People's Assembly acknowledging delays in the legislative process, the question of how Syria will balance economic stability, reconciliation, and victims' rights remains unresolved. Individuals remain lost after Syria government collapsesFor Hussein al-Tawil, however, the debate is not primarily about financial settlements or political appointments. It is about one missing person. Nearly 15 years after his brother Ali Ahmad al-Tawil disappeared in Damascus, Hussein and his family still do not know what happened to him. The government Hussein holds responsible for his brother's disappearance has fallen, but its collapse has not brought the family the answer it has awaited for so long. And as figures from Syria's past return to public life, Ali remains missing, leaving his family to ask what political change can mean for those who are still waiting for the truth.

title: A short guide to the linguicide of the Ukrainian language | Infographics (updated)
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); From the 17th to the 20th century, Ukrainian lands were split between empires and states. Their rulers tried to assimilate Ukrainians and block their self-determination by going after what set them apart: their language and culture. Nobody has an exact count of the bans. Historian Pavlo Hai-Nyzhnyk says there were more than 100 and that the real number is likely higher, because governors issued local bans too. These measures differed in purpose and reach. Some restricted publishing, schooling, or official use; others suppressed cultural institutions or pushed assimilation. Most served the forced Russification of Ukrainians in the Russian Empire and the USSR. The timeline below is a selection of documented events, not a count of bans. Russia has not stopped. In 2025, it removed Ukrainian from the federal school programs it imposes on the territories it occupies. Here are some of the most important restrictions on the Ukrainian language and cultural life imposed by the regimes ruling over Ukraine. Graphic by Ganna Naronina. Click to enlarge. 17th century 1627 : Muscovy. Moscow church authorities condemn Kyrylo Trankvilion-Stavrovetskyi’s Didactic Gospel, a collection of sermons printed in Ukraine in 1619, and order copies burned in Moscow . 1697 : Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. An act requires tribunal and court decisions in the Grand Duchy of Lithuania to be written in Polish, displacing Ruthenian in those courts. 18th century 1720 : Russian Tsardom. Peter I’s decree restricts the Kyiv and Chernihiv presses to approved reprints of church books and requires them to conform to Russian editions, suppressing local textual and linguistic differences. 1728 : Russian Empire. Under the Decisive Points (Reshytelni punkty), the legal texts used in the Hetmanate’s courts are to be translated into Russian and compiled into a single code. 1730s : Russian Empire. Under Empress Anna, Kyiv’s archbishop is instructed to replace older locally printed church books with Moscow editions . 1769 : Russian Empire. The Holy Synod refuses the Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra permission to print primers in the local language and tells it not to submit such requests again . 1775 : Russian Empire. A Russian army destroys the Zaporozhian Sich , the Cossacks’ last stronghold and one of Ukraine’s own political institutions. 1789 : Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. The Commission of National Education orders the Ukrainian parish schools of Right-Bank Ukraine Polonized . 19th century 1847 : Russian Empire. After suppressing the Cyril and Methodius Brotherhood, a secret society that called for a federation of free Slavic peoples, the authorities ban and withdraw from sale specified works by Taras Shevchenko, Panteleimon Kulish, and Mykola Kostomarov. 1859 : Austrian Empire. Austrian officials back a plan to replace the Cyrillic alphabet used for Ukrainian in Galicia with a Latin one. Ukrainian opposition defeats the plan in what became known as the “alphabet war.” 1862 : Russian Empire. The authorities close the Sunday schools , free schools for working adults and young people, including Ukrainian ones. They begin reopening under tighter control in 1864. 1863 : Russian Empire. Interior Minister Pyotr Valuev’s circular tells censors not to approve Ukrainian religious, school, and popular-reading books, while still allowing fiction under censorship. It claims that most Little Russians themselves argue that “there was not, is not, and cannot be any special Little Russian language.” 1864 : Russian Empire. The 1864 statute requires Russian as the teaching language in the elementary schools it regulates. 1869 : Austria-Hungary. Polish becomes the internal language of administration and the courts in Galicia. The 1867 school arrangements had already strengthened Polish dominance, while leaving limited room for Ukrainian-language schooling. 1876 : Russian Empire. Alexander II’s secret Ems Ukaz severely restricts Ukrainian publishing and bans Ukrainian publications from abroad, Ukrainian stage performances and public readings, and Ukrainian lyrics printed with music. Exceptions allow historical documents in their original spelling and fiction in Russian spelling under censorship. 1883 : Russian Empire. Kyiv Governor-General Aleksandr Drenteln bars Ukrainian theater troupes from performing in the Kyiv, Podillia, Volhynia, Poltava, and Chernihiv governorates. 1895 : Russian Empire. The censorship authorities ban the publication of Ukrainian children’s books . 20th century 1910 : Russian Empire. A circular from Pyotr Stolypin’s interior ministry tells governors to refuse registration to non-Russian national societies, Ukrainian ones included, and to review existing ones for closure. Kyiv’s Prosvita is dissolved the same year. 1914 : Russian Empire. The authorities ban public celebrations of Taras Shevchenko’s centenary . After the empire enters World War I, they close most Ukrainian periodicals , including the Kyiv daily Rada. 1914–15, 1916–17 : Russian Empire. Russian occupation authorities suppress Ukrainian institutions and publications in Galicia and Bukovyna. The first occupation brings mass arrests and deportations, the destruction of Ukrainian books, and the arrest of Metropolitan Andrei Sheptytskyi. 1923 : Soviet Ukraine. Dmytro Lebid, second secretary of the Communist Party of Ukraine, sets out the “theory of the struggle of two cultures ,” which holds that the Russian culture of the city is more advanced than the Ukrainian culture of the village. The party rejects it and adopts Ukrainization the same year. 1924 : Poland. Three laws of 31 July make Polish the state language of administration and the courts, keep limited rights for minority languages, and set school rules that favor Polish-Ukrainian bilingual schools over separate Ukrainian ones. 1924 : Romania. The primary education law requires citizens of Romanian origin who have “lost their mother tongue” to send their children to Romanian schools. Ukrainian historians say it was applied to Ukrainians in Bukovyna. 1925 : Poland. The Lviv Underground Ukrainian University , which had taught clandestinely since 1921, stops teaching after police raids and the Polish state’s refusal to recognize it. 1926 : USSR. In a letter to Kaganovich and the Ukrainian Politburo, Stalin attacks Oleksandr Shumskyi and Mykola Khvylovyi and rejects Ukrainizing Russian workers “from above,” while still backing controlled Ukrainization of official institutions. 1932–33 : USSR. A secret resolution of 14 December 1932 orders the Ukrainian-language paperwork and press of the North Caucasus switched to Russian at once and its schools prepared for teaching in Russian. In Soviet Ukraine, it puts Ukrainization under tighter party control and demands purges of “nationalist” elements. The repression of 1933 dismantles Ukrainization. 1938 : USSR. A decree of 13 March makes Russian a compulsory subject in the non-Russian schools of the national republics and regions. 1947 : Poland. In Operation Vistula , Polish authorities forcibly resettle about 150,000 Ukrainians to northern and western Poland, under an assimilation policy that sought to keep them below 10% of any locality. 1958–59 : USSR. The school reform expands parents’ choice of teaching language and makes the study of Ukrainian optional in Russian-language schools in Soviet Ukraine. 1960s–70s : Romania and Poland. Romania nearly eliminates Ukrainian-language schooling from the mid-1960s. In Poland, Ukrainian schools and Ukrainian classes shrink. 1978 : USSR. The USSR Council of Ministers orders wider study of Russian in the union republics. Ukraine’s implementing resolution of 2 November requires Russian from first grade in Ukrainian-language schools from the 1980/81 school year. 1983 : USSR. A resolution of 26 May gives specified teachers of Russian in non-Russian schools in villages and small towns a 15% pay raise from 1984. 1984 : USSR. The school reform resolution of 12 April adds two to three hours of Russian a week in grades 2 to 11 of non-Russian schools. 1989 : USSR. The Communist Party’s party platform of 20 September calls for making Russian, by law, the language of the whole country alongside the republics’ state languages. 1990 : USSR. The April 1990 law on the languages of the peoples of the USSR makes Russian the official language of the Soviet Union, while letting the republics set their own state languages. 21st century 2025 : Russia. Education Ministry Order No. 729, in force since 15 December , removes Ukrainian language and literature from Russia’s federal primary and lower-secondary programs, the UN human rights office reports . Russia imposes these programs on schools in the occupied territories, where about 582,000 children study, the Almenda center says . What we changed in October 2026 Editor’s note: We revised this 2017 timeline for dates, territorial scope, exceptions, and the quality of its sources, removed entries we could not confirm, and added the 2025 measure in the occupied territories. We removed entries for 1690, 1763, 1817, 1832, 1870, 1881, 1888, 1892, 1908, 1911, 1933 (Romania), 1934, 1970, 1972, 1973, and 1984 (museum records). For most we found no reliable source; a few described events that were not language measures. Some may be restored if documents turn up. We corrected or narrowed: 1728 (the order concerned legal texts used in the Hetmanate’s courts, not books in general), 1859 (the Latin-alphabet plan was defeated), 1876 (the Ems Ukaz’s exceptions), 1883 (Drenteln’s regional ban on Ukrainian troupes, formerly dated 1884), 1910 (registration was refused; closures followed), 1923 (formerly 1922), 1932–33 (the reversal of Ukrainization), 1983 (the 15% raise applied to specified teachers in villages and small towns), and 1990. We dropped the figure of 60 prohibitions, which we could not source, and replaced it with an attributed estimate.

title: World reacts to Lula’s victory in Brazil’s presidential election
body: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has secured a fourth nonconsecutive term, defeating right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in a run-off . Bolsonaro, however, has called for Sunday’s vote to be annulled over an “unacceptable” two-hour voting extension granted by Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin, despite both candidates having requested additional voting time. The election results have drawn reactions across the world, with left-wing global figures celebrating Lula’s victory. Here’s how the world reacted: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum Sheinbaum congratulated Lula in a post on X. “Long live democracy, the people of Brazil won,” she wrote. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney In his congratulatory post, Carney credited Lula with advancing relations between Canada and Brazil. “Let us seize this opportunity to strengthen them further, together – to create new promising commercial prospects, protect the environment, and ensure greater prosperity for both our populations,” he wrote on X. US officials and politicians US President Donald Trump’s son Donald Trump Jr criticised the result, referring to the two-hour voting time extension. “If a conservative government in Brazil did this, everyone in the mainstream press in America would lose their minds, but I guess they’re just choosing to be silent because it’s all for the cause,” he said. Progressive Senator Bernie Sanders, meanwhile, congratulated Lula’s “extraordinary re-election victory”, saying the Brazilian president has “stood up” for workers and democracy and will continue to do so for the next four years. Congressman Ro Khanna said in a post on X: “People all across the world are fighting back against extremism. With Lula in Brazil, they just won. Authoritarian leaders always attack democracy because they stand no chance against the will of their people.” Khanna added that Trump “must respect the results and not undermine Brazil’s elections”. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani wrote on X: “The people united will never be defeated!” California Governor Gavin Newsom’s media office released a statement, saying he is “proud to stand with Brazil and partners around the world who share our commitment to defending democracy, protecting our environment, strengthening workers’ rights, and building an economy that works for working families”. Chinese Foreign Ministry China congratulated Lula through a statement by Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun. “China has noted that Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court has announced President Lula has won the second round of the Brazilian general election, and expresses its congratulations,” Guo Jiakun said at a regular briefing, adding that Beijing was “willing to work with Brazil to continue advancing the building of a China-Brazil community with a shared future.” Russian presidency The Kremlin says it welcomed the re-election of Lula da Silva and praised him for his contribution to bilateral ties and to the intergovernmental BRICS organisation. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Lula had done a lot for bilateral ties and for developing BRICS and hoped for more of the same. Cuban President Miguel Diaz-Canel Diaz-Canel said Lula’s “historic” win “ensures the continuity of the path of peace, sovereignty, and social justice embarked upon by the Brazilian people under your leader”. “Brazil can count on Cuba in the construction of the unity and integration of our Great Homeland, Latin American and Caribbean,” he wrote in a post on X. Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast Kast said he spoke on the phone with Lula to congratulate him on his victory. “Chile and Brazil have a lot of shared future ahead, and we will continue working on an agenda that strengthens relations between our countries in economic integration and the fight against organised crime in the region,” he said on X. Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori In a congratulatory post on X, Fujimori reaffirmed Peru’s “willingness to strengthen our strategic alliance, integration, cooperation and the sustainable development of the Amazon that we share” with Brazil. Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz “Bolivia and Brazil are neighbouring and sister countries, united by a shared history and common challenges,” Rodrigo wrote on X. The two countries will continue to work together to strengthen ties and “generate more opportunities for our nations”, he added. Panamanian President Jose Raul Mulino “I congratulate the ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌Brazilian ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌people for this democratic day and especially President Lula for the victory!” Mulino wrote on X. “We will continue working together for our countries.” European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen Von der Leyen congratulated Lula on X, proclaiming that democracy and multilateralism “have won” in Brazil. “Europe’s partnership with Brazil is thriving. We will remain by your side for the years to come,” she added. “Together we will keep working closely for free and open trade. A rules-based global order. And strong ambitions for our climate.” Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez Sanchez hailed the victory of his leftist Brazilian ally as a “progressive comeback”. “A great victory for Lula! What has happened in Brazil will happen in Spain. The global progressive comeback has just begun,” Sanchez posted on X, after Lula’s recovery from a first round loss halted a string of right-wing gains in Latin America. French President Emmanuel Macron Macron called for efforts to “strengthen our strategic partnership” after Lula’s win. “France and Brazil have much to build together,” Macron said on X, saying their two countries should nurture their friendship “in the service of a fairer world”. Ecuador President Daniel Noboa “Our region has common enemies, shared challenges, and much to gain when we work together,” Noboa wrote on X, congratulating Lula. Paraguayan President Santiago Pena “I salute the Brazilian people for this great democratic journey,” Pena wrote on X. “Paraguay and Brazil share a common agenda of integration and development. We will continue working together for the wellbeing of our people.” Uruguayan President Yamandu Orsi Orsi wrote on X that he had just spoken with his “friend” Lula and congratulated him “on the victory and on the democratic celebration that an electoral process represents”. Argentina’s former President Cristina Kirchner “Congratulations,” Kirchner wrote on X, “first to the Brazilian people”, and also to Lula, for knowing “how to awaken in your compatriots feeling and sense to win this battle”.

title: Poultry sold at GH¢80 by farmers reaches consumers at GH¢200 – Dumelo
body: Deputy Minister of Food and Agriculture John Dumelo says the government is taking the country’s poultry sector seriously and is committed to addressing challenges affecting local production. Speaking on behalf of the government at a poultry round-table discussion with the Netherlands in Accra on Monday, October 26, Mr Dumelo said data on the sector had highlighted the need for urgent attention and stronger collaboration. “We are taking the poultry sector very seriously,” he said. He also raised concerns about the high cost of locally produced poultry, attributing part of the problem to middlemen who increase prices along the supply chain. Mr Dumelo explained that although farmers could sell poultry at about GH¢80, the price could rise to around GH¢200 by the time it reached consumers. “One thing that is of concern to me is the cost of producing poultry. If you look at the cost of production, the number of middlemen that carry it to the consumer, so yes, even though the farmer sells at affordable prices, maybe GHC80 before it gets to the final consumer, it is around GHC 200, and so let’s look at it,” he noted. READ ALSO: 80% poultry import dependence highlights need to grow local production – Netherlands Ambassador He said the price difference made locally produced chicken less affordable and weakened its competitiveness against imported poultry. The Deputy Minister subsequently signed a memorandum of understanding with the Netherlands Ambassador to Ghana, Hans Akerboom, to strengthen cooperation in the poultry sector. The partnership is expected to support efforts to improve local production through technical expertise, knowledge exchange and investment. The government earlier established the Nkoko Nkitinkiti initiative. It is a poultry development programme under the Feed Ghana Programme, launched in November 2025 to boost household poultry farming, improve food security, create jobs and reduce Ghana’s reliance on imported chicken. The government aims to distribute millions of birds and chicks, with support for household producers, small and medium-scale farmers and commercial poultry operators. In July 2026, Feed Ghana Coordinator Bright Demordzi said about 2.5 million birds had been distributed under the initiative. The programme also targets a 50% reduction in poultry imports in the medium term, according to Mr Demordzi. The government has said the initiative is intended to strengthen local production and make Ghana less dependent on imported poultry products.

title: Duchess Hospital marks five years of giant milestones
body:
Just five years after it opened its doors to the first patient, one of the missions of establishing the Duchess International Hospital Ikeja- to reverse medical tourism- is being realized as more Nigerians in the Diaspora are choosing to come back home, trusting Duchess Hospital to perform complex surgeries, thereby saving time of being on the waiting list abroad, reducing cost of such surgeries by over 50 per cent and have the benefit of being surrounded by family and friends in Nigeria during the period of recovery. This is in addition to numerous Nigerians who are having their healthcare needs met at Duchess International Hospital instead of traveling to India, South Africa, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, the United Kingdom or any other country to have world-class healthcare.
Speaking at the event in Ikeja, Lagos, to mark the fifth anniversary of Duchess Hospital, Dr. Olajide Ojo, Chief Operating Officer (COO) of the hospital said the theme of the anniversary: “Five years of delivering world-class healthcare: Transforming medicine through innovation and excellence” encapsulates the giant milestones the hospital has attained in the last five years. Dr. Ojo said that the hospital had provided care to an estimated 40,000 out-patients annually, delivered 500 babies and performed 2,053 paediatric and adult surgical procedures with about 65 per cent being major and complex operations like spinal surgeries.
He said the hospital has performed successful 44 open heart surgeries comprising 20 Paediatric and 24 adult procedures since 2023 when the open heart surgery programme was launched. Dr.Ojo explained that the collaboration with the Lagos State University Teaching Hospital (LASUTH) through the Duchess Waiting List Initiative helped to improve access to cardiovascular surgery for patients facing prolonged waiting periods. “These milestones tell a strategic story of a hospital committed to advancing boundaries of specialist medicine while never losing sight of the individual human being at the centre of every encounter”, Ojo said. He noted that the first five years of Duchess Hospital represents “not just the growth of an institution but the steady building of clinical capability, the strengthening of trust and the transformation of healthcare, one patient at a time”.
Chairman of Duchess International Hospital, Dr. Yemi Onabowale, said the hospital has touched lives over the past five years through its affordable healthcare programmes and corporate social responsibility initiatives. Dr. Onabowale commended the hospital’s management and staff for their dedication to quality patient care which has seen Duchess Hospital win the prestigious Nigerian Healthcare Excellence Award as the best private healthcare facility in Nigeria in 2024 and 2025. “Our future ambition is to continue to expand access to quality healthcare, strengthening specialist services, investing in our people and technology and ensuring that more Nigerians can receive advanced medical treatment at home”, Dr. Onabowale said.
Minister of State for Health, Dr. Adekunle Salako, who was one of the special guests, harped on the need to address the high exodus of medical professionals abroad (also known as japa) by creating the enabling environment for a good practice at home through establishment of modern hospitals and good remuneration package for medical personnel. Dr. Salako commended the Duchess Hospital for their medical cutting-edge facility and excellent patient care that have stood the hospital apart from its peers.
Wife of the governor of Lagos State, Dr.(Mrs) Ibijoke Sanwo-Olu who was the special guest at the event, said a strong partnership between the public and private sectors is important to expand healthcare capacity, encourage innovation and improve service delivery . She was represented at the event by the Medical Director of the General Hospital, Ebute Metta,Dr.(Mrs) Folakemi Irewole-Ojo.
The anniversary lecture was delivered by Prof. Nicholas Ossei-Gerning, a professor of cardiology, Spire Hospital, Cardiff, the United Kingdom. He spoke extensively on how to manage cardiovascular health and the major risk factors such as high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol, stress, depression, anxiety and lack of social support. Prof. Ossei-Gerning explained that erectile dysfunction in a major marker for cardiovascular disease and advised men to go for regular checks to avoid sudden death as a result of heart failure.
The management of Duchess International Hospital expects the next five years to usher in stronger clinical capabilities, greater access to specialist care, more lives transformed, deeper social impact and renewed confidence in Nigerian healthcare.

title: Number of those injured in missile attack on Yelets up to seven
body:
MOSCOW, October 26. /TASS/. The number of those hurt in Ukraine’s missile attack on Yelets in the Lipetsk Region on October 25 has raised to seven after one more man sought medical care on Monday, the region’s health minister, Lilia Samoshina said.
Lipetsk Region governor Igor Artamonov said earlier that a security guard of one of enterprises was wounded in the missile attack on Yelets’ industrial area. Five more people sought medical assistance. Several residential houses and the building of a medical college were damaged.
"Today, a 55-year-olf man was brought to the emergency room at the Semashko City Clinical Hospital with a non-penetrating shrapnel wound to the chest. An examination revealed that a foreign object was stuck in his soft tissues, presumably a piece of metal shrapnel. The man was admitted to the hospital. He is scheduled to undergo surgery tomorrow," Samoshina wrote on messaging app Max.

title: Government announces open competition for ARMA head – Koretsky
body:
Ukrainian Prime Minister Serhiy Koretsky has announced an open and transparent competition for the position of head of the National Agency for Detection, Search and Management of Assets Derived from Corruption and Other Crimes (ARMA).

"The agency needs a leader trusted by both society and partners. I invite everyone with management experience, an impeccable reputation and a desire to serve their country to apply," Koretsky wrote on Telegram.

He stressed that during the war, every seized asset must work in the interests of the state.

title: Cargo traffic over Northern Sea Route reached 33 mln tons as of Q4 start
body:
MOSCOW, October 26. /TASS/. The cargo traffic over the Northern Sea Route amounted to 33 mln metric tons as of the start of the fourth quarter of this year, which is 17% more than in the like period of the last year, according to the presentation of Russian Minister of Far East and Arctic Development Alexey Chekunkov.
"According to data as of the beginning of the fourth quarter, the cargo traffic over the Northern Sea Route stood at 33 mln tons, which is 17% more than the figure in the like period of the last year," the presentation indicates.
The transit traffic increased by 1.5 times from the last-year figure (3.2 mln metric tons) and reached 4.8 mln metric tons in the reporting period, Chekunkov noted. Two nuclear-powered icebreakers, two hydrographic ships, five emergency and rescue ships were already built for the Northern Sea Route development and four satellites were launched, the minister said. "Construction of four more nuclear-powered icebreakers, three emergency and rescue centers, 41 emergency and rescue ships and launch of 11 satellites are stipulated by 2035," he added.

title: Invest In Training, Boost Production To 3m/b Per Day, PETAN Urges Indigenous Oil Firms
body: The Petroleum Technology Association of Nigeria (PETAN) has urged indigenous oil and gas companies to invest in training young Nigerians and strengthening technical capacity to support the country’s ambition of producing three million barrels of crude oil per day. PETAN Chairman, Wole Ogunsanya, made the call at the association’s media roundtable in Lagos on Monday, warning that the transfer of oil and gas assets from international oil companies to indigenous operators had created an urgent need to train the next generation of industry professionals. He said Nigeria faced a widening gap between experienced oil and gas workers and younger professionals entering the industry, stressing that local operators must develop training programmes to sustain production and retain technical expertise. “We have a huge gap between those that are experienced in the industry versus age. Training is a very important aspect of our industry,” Ogunsanya said. PETAN Chairman, Wole Ogunsanya, while addressing journalists at a media roundtable in Lagos on Monday, October 26, 2026. He noted that many experienced Nigerian professionals had received their training through multinational companies, including Shell, ExxonMobil, Chevron and TotalEnergies, often benefiting from international placements and technical development programmes. However, he questioned whether similar opportunities would remain available as international operators divested some of their onshore, swamp and shallow-water assets. “Now we are divesting the assets. We are selling the assets to indigenous companies. Almost 100 per cent of the assets on land, in the swamp and shallow waters are owned by Nigerian indigenous companies. “Who is going to train the Nigerians? The new generation of Nigerians are coming behind to take over and operate those assets and work for these companies successfully,” he said. Training Centre Ogunsanya said Nigeria had sufficient human resources to develop its oil and gas industry, but needed to do more to attract graduates and provide them with practical skills. “The issue is not that we don’t have Nigerian young educated graduates that can come into the industry. The issue is how do we encourage these young educated Nigerian graduates to look into the oil and gas industry?” he asked. He said the industry required professionals with practical experience in drilling, pipeline installation, fabrication, welding and offshore operations, adding that training must prepare young Nigerians for the physical and technical demands of the sector. Ogunsanya disclosed that PETAN recruited nearly 100 engineers every two years through its internship programme, placing them in member companies for practical training. “After two years, PETAN members absorb over 60 per cent of these guys because that’s how good the training that we’re giving them is,” he said. He added that the association was working with the Nigerian Content Development and Monitoring Board (NCDMB) on human capacity development initiatives. The chairman also disclosed plans to establish a training centre in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, with facilities, including drilling rigs, to train more Nigerian professionals locally. “If Shell will send 10 people to train, we can train 100 Nigerians if we bring the trainers into the country and we have the facilities,” he said. The PETAN boss warned that experienced Nigerian professionals were increasingly being recruited by countries in the Middle East, including Qatar, Saudi Arabia and Kuwait, making local training investment more urgent. Drill-Or-Drop Policy Ogunsanya also backed the Federal Government’s drill-or-drop policy, which seeks to compel operators to develop their oil assets or risk losing them, describing it as critical to achieving Nigeria’s three-million-barrel-per-day production target. “The cheapest oil to produce in the world is already discovered, and we need to drill a few more wells to bring the oil,” he said. The PETAN chairman argued that developing existing discoveries could deliver additional production more quickly than relying exclusively on new exploration, which requires significant investment and carries geological risks. “We cannot have those assets sitting there that have potential to produce 10, 20, 50,000 barrels. Every drop of oil adds up to get to that three million barrels,” he said. According to him, enforcing the policy would also benefit indigenous service companies by increasing demand for drilling, equipment deployment and other technical services. He explained that service companies often have equipment and signed contracts but generate little revenue when operators fail to commence work. “If they say, ‘Ah, we don’t have work,’ you can have the contract in your hand, it’s signed. If they don’t call you, you don’t do any work,” he said. Ogunsanya added that increased activity would enable service companies to earn more revenue, purchase additional equipment and contribute to higher production. He also supported a review of aspects of the Nigerian Oil and Gas Industry Content Development Act, saying developments in the industry had created areas requiring attention. Gas Development Gaps The PETAN chairman also called for greater investment in gas production and distribution infrastructure, describing it as essential to expanding electricity generation and supporting industrial growth. He cited Nigeria’s estimated 210 trillion cubic feet of gas reserves and said the country had yet to maximise the resource’s potential across power generation, industry and domestic consumption. “This country needs a minimum of 100,000 megawatts of installed power capacity, and we will not have it unless we produce enough gas, unless we lay the pipelines where those gas turbines are going to be,” he said. Ogunsanya compared Nigeria’s installed electricity generation capacity of about 12,000 megawatts with the much higher capacities of South Africa and Egypt, arguing that increased gas utilisation was necessary to close the gap. He said the oil and gas industry remained central to Nigeria’s economic growth and urged operators, regulators and the government to address the constraints limiting investment and production. The post Invest In Training, Boost Production To 3m/b Per Day, PETAN Urges Indigenous Oil Firms appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Counter-Terrorism: Africa must lead in shaping, implementing solutions to challenges – Ribadu
body: By Kingsley Omonobi National Security Adviser, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu has said that Africa must lead in defining, shaping and implementing solutions to the terrorism challenges facing the continent. Ribadu said this reality has become inevitable because, “Terrorist networks move across borders, communicate across platforms and finance their activities through channels that are often transnational. Delivering the keynote address at the High Level African Lessons Learned Forum on Counter-Terrorism Cooperation, Intelligence Sharing and Emerging Technologies’ on Monday, Ribadu said, “No country can address such threats in isolation. We must strengthen mechanisms that allow for timely, trusted and actionable intelligence exchange, while respecting national sovereignty and legal frameworks. The NSA said, “The theme places intelligence sharing at the centre of effective counter-terrorism cooperation. Our partners remain important, and we value their continued support. However, sustainable solutions must be rooted in African ownership, African priorities, African institutions and the lived experiences of our communities. “The theme recognizes the growing role of emerging technologies. Artificial intelligence, digital communications, encrypted platforms, drones, synthetic media and other technological tools that are reshaping the threat landscape. “These technologies present risks when exploited by terrorist groups, but they also offer opportunities for early warning, threat analysis, digital investigation, strategic communications, border security and the protection of vulnerable communities.Our task is to ensure that technology is used responsibly, lawfully and effectively in support of peace and security. “The theme also emphasizes strategic partnerships. Counter-terrorism today requires partnerships among states, regional bodies, international organizations, security agencies, financial intelligence units, communities, civil society, academia, the private sector and technology actors. It also requires trust, consistency and practical cooperation beyond formal declarations. To participants from across the globe, Ribadu said, “Your presence here reflects a shared recognition that the threat of terrorism and violent extremism remains one of the most serious challenges to peace, stability and development across our continent. “This Forum is convened at a time when Africa continues to confront an increasingly complex and adaptive terrorist threat environment. Terrorist groups are exploiting porous borders, local grievances, illicit financial networks, digital platforms, misinformation, online radicalization and emerging technologies. “They are also adapting their methods in ways that challenge traditional security responses. These developments require sustained cooperation, stronger intelligence sharing, coordinated national and regional action, and a deeper commitment to practical lessons learned among African states. “Nigeria’s experience over the past fifteen years has shown that counter-terrorism cannot be sustained through military and kinetic action alone. While security operations remain necessary, they must be complemented by intelligence coordination, law enforcement, financial intelligence, justice, strategic communications, prevention, rehabilitation, reintegration, reconciliation, community resilience, education, youth engagement, research, training and technology-enabled analysis. “This is why Nigeria has continued to advance a Whole-of-Government and Whole-of-Society approach to counter-terrorism and preventing and countering violent extremism, need for African countries to strengthen real-time intelligence sharing, improve coordination, exchange practical lessons and build trusted professional networks. “It is therefore fitting that we are gathered here under the theme: “Strengthening Africa-Led Counter Terrorism Cooperation through Intelligence Sharing, Technological Innovation and Strategic Partnerships.” The NSA commended the African Union, Regional Economic Communities, the United Nations, the European Union and other partners for advancing practical counter-terrorism cooperation noting, “We are also committed to supporting African-led approaches that place national ownership, regional solidarity and institutional learning at the centre of our collective response. Disclosing that Nigeria is pleased to host the Forum at the National Counter Terrorism Centre because the Centre represents an important part of our national counter-terrorism coordination architecture, Ribadu said, “The NCTC-ONSA has grown as a platform for strategic threat assessment, intelligence fusion, research, training, policy coordination, technology-enabled analysis and non-kinetic programming. It is also increasingly positioned to serve as a continental resource for peer learning and capacity development. “Through this Forum, participants will have the opportunity to engage Nigeria’s experiences, including our efforts in counter-terrorism coordination, preventing and countering violent extremism, strategic communications, countering terrorism financing, rehabilitation and reintegration, and community-based approaches. Initiatives such as Operation SAFE CORRIDOR and the European Union-supported DDRR of Persons “Formerly Associated with Non-State Armed Groups in North-East Nigeria provide lessons on the difficult but necessary connection between security operations, accountability, reintegration, reconciliation and community recovery. “These experiences are not presented as perfect models. Rather, they are offered as practical lessons from which we can all learn. Every country represented here has experience to share. Each of us has confronted challenges, developed institutional responses, recorded successes and encountered setbacks.” The post Counter-Terrorism: Africa must lead in shaping, implementing solutions to challenges – Ribadu appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Call of the Wilde: Montreal Canadiens win first two in four game road trip shading the Winnipeg Jets in the Heritage Classic
body:
The Montreal Canadiens continued their four game road trip in Winnipeg with a Heritage Classic outdoors at the home of the Blue Bombers. Over 30 thousand in attendance as the Canadiens edged the Jets 2-1.
Jacob Fowler shone again in the Montreal net. He is one of the strongest goalies in the NHL right now. What is interesting about Fowler is he made 34 saves, but only one, a glove save off Mark Scheifele, looked spectacular.
Fowler is so positionally sound and technically strong that he’s in front of the shots so well, almost nothing looks amazing. Even on the rebound, he makes it look easy. He’s down in the butterfly, and up so quickly, with such perfect balance, that the second shot doesn’t look all that challenging either.
That is when there is a rebound. Most of the time, it is kicked into the corner perfectly. Fowler is also operating at about 50 beats per minute. He makes everyone feel relaxed around him because he is so calm.
Fowler frustrated the Jets all night. He stopped 34 of 35 shots for a .971 save percentage. His Goals Saved Above Expected was a sparkling 2.93. He moves to 6.3 GSAE for the season. Fowler moves into fifth place in that category in the league.
This was a match-up between the fourth ranked Corsi team in the league and the 22nd. Montreal should have had the advantage in possession, and they did when three of the four Winnipeg lines were on the ice.
It took over 27 minutes for the first goal thanks to the combination of Noah Dobson and Lane Hutson put back together for this contest. It was Dobson with a gorgeous cross-crease pass to Hutson for his third goal of the season.
This was the best pair on the club last season in analytics. The best pair recently is Alexandre Carrier with Kaiden Guhle, but they were broken up with the return of Mike Matheson on Friday.
