title: Russian strikes on Kramatorsk community kill one, injure 10
body:
This was reported by Oleksandr Honcharenko, Head of the Kramatorsk City Military Administration, on Facebook , according to Ukrinform.
According to the report, Russian forces launched four strikes on Yasnohirka in the morning.
“At least one person was killed and 10 injured in the strikes on the Kramatorsk community. A 13-year-old girl is among the injured,” the post said.
Relevant emergency services are working at the scene.
According to the official, the exact number of casualties and the extent of the damage are still being assessed.
As reported, on October 23, Russian forces dropped three FAB-250 aerial bombs on Kramatorsk. One person was killed and six were injured, including three children.

title: TASS provides its news feeds free of charge to over 300 African media outlets
body:
MOSCOW, October 26. /TASS/. The TASS news agency provides its news feeds free of charge to more than 300 media outlets in Africa, TASS Strategy Director Sergey Kuzovnikov said.
"Today, TASS already provides its news feeds in Arabic and French free of charge to more than 300 media outlets in Africa so that they can receive first-hand information about what is happening in Russia and around the world," he said at the Russia-Africa media forum.
He invited the forum’s participants to join the agency’s news feeds. "I would like to invite all those who are taking part in this media forum to join these feeds. TASS is ready to provide them free of charge," he said.
He noted that the forum provides African countries with an opportunity to tell its own story. "We don't let anyone speak for anyone else, or speak for Africa. Instead, we let Africa tell its own story," Kuzovnikov stressed.
Moscow is hosting the Russia-Africa media forum from October 26-29. Delegates from the leading Russian and African media outlets are attending. Participants will, in particular, discuss the role of countries of the global majority in the mass media space, outline prospects for the development of media resources as a tool for combating disinformation, and address the issue of the decolonization of media content.
TASS is the forum’s information partner. It will hold two panel sessions, on new platforms and formats of cooperation (October 26) and on media resources as a tool to fight disinformation and strengthen Russia and Africa’s positive image (October 28).

title: TOR records GH¢1.24bn profit in 2025 after a decade of losses
body: The Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) recorded a profit before tax of GH¢1.24 billion in 2025, marking its first return to profitability in a decade, Managing Director Edmond Kombat has disclosed. He attributed the financial improvement to prudent management, improved commercial operations and measures introduced to strengthen the refinery’s financial position following years of losses and mounting liabilities. Speaking at the Government Accountability Series at Jubilee House on Monday, October 26, 2026, Mr Kombat said the refinery had made significant progress in addressing its financial challenges under the administration of President John Dramani Mahama. He said the company’s trade and other payables declined from GH¢7.1 billion to GH¢5 billion within a year, while its receivables days dropped from 1,099 to 652. “What matters more is that trade and other payables fell from GH¢7.1 billion to GH¢5 billion in a single year, and receivable days fell from 1,099 to 652,” he stated. The Managing Director said the improved financial performance reflected management’s efforts to rebuild the company’s commercial operations, strengthen accountability and restore confidence among business partners. According to him, commercial operations generated more than 36 per cent revenue growth in 2025 compared with 2024, with revenue increasing by almost 60 per cent as of September 2026. He said management had also recovered outstanding receivables, improved financial controls and continued upgrading the refinery’s Quality Control Laboratory. The results represent a significant shift from the financial position inherited in May 2025, when the refinery had accumulated losses of approximately GH¢10 billion and debt estimated at US$517 million. Mr Kombat said management was also pursuing a financial restructuring programme, including independent assessments of liabilities and discussions with the Ghana Revenue Authority, SSNIT and other creditors to establish sustainable repayment arrangements. He added that the Ministry of Finance was working with TOR to consider writing off US$120 million in legacy debt owed to the government or converting the amount into equity. Mr Kombat said management remained focused on sustaining the financial gains and improving performance in 2026. “The team is focused to deliver even better results for 2026,” he said.

title: We are spending where it matters most, five statutory funds paid in full – Ato Forson
body: Finance Minister Dr. Cassiel Ato Forson says the government is directing spending towards essential services Ghanaians rely on, following the timely and full payment of third-quarter allocations to five statutory funds. In a social media post, the Minister linked the payments to the everyday needs of citizens, including education, healthcare, roads and community development. “We are spending where it matters most, on the services Ghanaians depend on every day,” he stated. The five funds are the District Assemblies Common Fund (DACF), the Ghana Education Trust Fund (GETFund), the National Health Insurance Fund (NHIF), the Ghana Medical Trust Fund and the Road Maintenance Trust Fund. An accompanying Ministry of Finance graphic indicated that all five had received their third-quarter payments for 2026 in full. “These five funds have received their third-quarter payments on time and in full, supporting schools, healthcare, roads and development in our communities,” Dr Forson said. The Minister emphasised the human significance of meeting these obligations, pointing to the people who depend on the services the funds support. “Behind every payment are people whose needs cannot wait,” he added.

title: Ukraine raises its stalled Patriot request with Washington again after almost a month without Hegseth’s signature
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Ukraine has waited almost a month for US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to sign off on missiles for its Patriot and NASAMS air defense systems, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on 26 October. He ordered his team to raise it with Washington again. Two other US holds on Ukraine, on Starlink speeds and intelligence sharing, have been lifted, leaving the interceptors as the last one. Russia keeps firing ballistic missiles at Ukrainian cities and the power grid before winter, and Patriots are the only systems in Ukraine that reliably stop Iskander-M, Kinzhal, and Zircon missiles. Zelenskyy has told EU leaders Ukraine needs 300 interceptors to get through winter, diplomatic sources told Radio Svoboda. The holds came as Washington pressed Kyiv to stop striking Russian refineries, which Trump blames for high US fuel prices before the midterms. Zelenskyy: almost a month waiting for Hegseth’s signature Zelenskyy held a meeting on weapons supplies with Ukraine’s defense minister, foreign minister, and commander-in-chief. They reported on interceptors for air defense, above all for Patriot systems. Afterward, Zelenskyy wrote: “ We are working in several directions: with the United States, Europe, and other partners that have stocks of PAC-2 and PAC-3 missiles. In particular, for almost a month we have been waiting for Mr. Hegseth’s signature on missiles for Patriots and NASAMS. I have instructed the team to discuss this with the American side once again .” Talks with other countries continue, he added. The meeting also covered preparations for November’s Ramstein meeting of Ukraine’s allies, where Zelenskyy wants decisions already on the table carried out faster. Aftermath of a Russian ballistic missile attack on Kyiv, 19 October 2026. Photo: State Emergency Service of Ukraine Allies’ missiles need US approval Some of the transfers come from friendly countries and need Hegseth’s approval, because the US must sign off on any re-transfer of its missiles, a US official and three people familiar with the matter said on 19 October. Hegseth has neither refused nor approved them. Explore further The Starlink hot potato: Musk points to Trump, Trump points to nobody, then credits Musk with the fix. The speed limit stays A Ukrainian official said in mid-October that only “a couple” of interceptors were left. Hegseth has said the US wants “ our guys ” to have “ the most possible ” interceptors, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio insisted nothing was “ being deliberately denied to Ukraine .” Two of three US holds lifted In an interview aired on 25 October, Zelenskyy listed three problems from his Oslo talks with the Americans: air defense, Starlink limits, and limits on US intelligence sharing. Full Starlink speeds returned on 24 October, and missile warnings resumed after his 20 October call with Rubio. Progress on Patriot missiles is “ very slow ,” he said, “ slower than the flight of Russian missiles .” Kyiv has also tried to trade for the missiles. Zelenskyy told US senators he had offered US envoys a 30-day pause in strikes on Russian refineries in return for Patriot interceptors. The envoys showed no openness to the idea. Trump has called those refinery strikes a disgrace that only pushes oil prices higher. He said it days after striking a deal with Putin to bring Russian diesel back to the US ahead of the midterm elections on 3 November. Trump treats Ukraine as the weak link to squeeze and wants a visible win partly with US domestic politics in mind, Ukrainian diplomat Oleksandr Khara has argued. title: Iran, Pakistan, Turkey, and Saudi Arabia meeting kicks off
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 26 (MNA) – Iranian officials and respresentatives from Pakistam, Turkey and Saudi Arabia held a meeting in Tehran amid efforts to deescalate tensions in the region.
Saudi Arabia's Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman Al Saud, Pakistani Army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir and the chief of National Intelligence Organization of Turkey Ibrahim Kalin held a meeting with the Supreme National Security Council (SNSC) secretary Major General Mohsen Rezaei and President Masoud Pezeshkian as well as Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. The meeting was held in Saadabad Palace in the north of the Iranian capital.
The four-wat talks focused on regional security, the fallout from military aggression, and support for Palestine and Lebanon, the local Iranian media reported.
Earlier on Monday, Ali Bagheri, Deputy Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, announced that senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey will travel to Tehran as part of efforts to implement the idea of endogenous security in West Asia.
Referring to General Asim Munir’s visit last week, Bagheri noted that the Pakistani army commander, in a meeting with Major General Mohsen Rezaei, the Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, announced that senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan had decided to travel to Tehran, meet with Iran’s Supreme National Security Council Secretary, and hold a joint meeting.
The purpose of these senior officials’ trip is consultation with Major General Mohsen Rezaei regarding regional security, he stressed.
All three countries attending this meeting, along with Iran, can take an effective step toward creating endogenous security within the framework of Iran’s effective idea for regional security-building with the participation of regional actors, drawing on Iran’s successful experience in national security-building, he stated.
US-Zionist aggression strengthened Iran's national unity: Pezeshkian
President Pezeshkian at the meeting said that "The region has witnessed widespread Israeli crimes in recent years. A united front among Muslim countries could prevent Israel from continuing its aggression."
He also said "Israel thought pressure and military aggression would lead to Iran’s collapse, but instead strengthened national unity and solidarity."
"He further said, "Despite the losses and hardships, Iranians stood firm in defending their country. The belief that Iran can be forced to surrender is misguided."
Accoridng to Pezeshkian "Iran supports any understanding that leads to Islamic countries' unity."
He continued to say that, "Relying on shared capacities, Islamic states can present world with a model of justice, development"
Iranian officials reportedly told Reuters prior to the meeting that he Tehran meeting did not include talks on the nuclear issue as Tehran demand Washignton meet its conditions before any talks about the nuclear issue.
The talks centered on the war on Iran, US naval blockade and esclated tensions in the region.
FInal statement: Participants vow to continue dialogue
The delegations from Iran, Pakistan, Turkey, and Saudi Arabia released a press statement after concluding their security meeting in Tehran on Monday.
The participants agreed to continue the dialogue to strengthen cooperation amongst the four regional countries, including for peace and security in the region.

title: Russia scores big diplomatic win by returning DPR POWs — ombudswoman
body:
DONETSK, October 26. /TASS/. Russian diplomacy scored a big win by returning servicemen born in the Donetsk People’s Republic’s (DPR) from Ukrainian captivity last week, DPR human rights commissioner Daria Morozova told TASS.
On October 23, Russian human rights ombudswoman Yana Lantratova announced the release of 31 servicemen from the DPR who had been held captive by Ukraine. According to her, this was the first such release since 2022.
"As part of the prisoner exchange between Russia and Ukraine, soldiers who defended the Donetsk People’s Republic have returned home for the first time in a long while. This is a significant achievement and victory for Russian diplomacy. Until now, the exchange of our defenders had been blocked by the Ukrainian side for political reasons," Morozova said.
The ombudswoman added that this work is ongoing.
Earlier, Morozova told TASS that about 500 natives of the DPR remain in Ukrainian captivity. According to the ombudswoman, Kiev is manipulating the exchange of prisoners from the DPR by dragging out the process.

title: CICMG calls for flexible lending conditions to expand credit access
body: The Chartered Institute of Credit Management, Ghana (CICMG), is calling for more flexible lending conditions, increased credit capital and stronger financial literacy programmes to improve access to finance for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and informal-sector operators. President of the Institute, Evelyn Osei Tutu, says stringent collateral requirements, high interest rates and inadequate borrower education are limiting access to credit, particularly for businesses and individuals in rural communities. Speaking at the 2026 Ghana Credit Excellence Awards in Accra, she urged banks, regulators and policymakers to balance responsible lending with measures that allow more viable businesses to access financing. “It’s making facilities a bit slow when banks are issuing to the SMEs because some of them don’t really have the requirements,” she said. Mrs Osei Tutu acknowledged the importance of credit assessment in preventing defaults but argued that overly rigid lending conditions could discourage potential borrowers. “If we are able to get more capital injected and if the regulators also make things a little flexible. I think we should be able to do more, especially with the rural areas and other markets we manage with the informal sector too,” she added. Mrs Osei Tutu also identified financial literacy as essential to improving repayment rates, saying borrowers must understand their obligations before accessing credit. “You realise that we are very much in a hurry to give out the credits to people, but we don’t tell them the consequences of what you tend to benefit and the things that you have to do right,” she said. She called for stronger education programmes for borrowers and credit officers, alongside improved loan monitoring and recovery systems. “Loans are easy to give but they are difficult in recovery,” she said, warning that inadequate guidance could result in borrowers mismanaging facilities and lenders losing their investments. Meanwhile, General Manager of Emmanuel Cooperative Credit Union, William Atta-Pearce, says credit unions can help address financing gaps among rural borrowers who struggle to meet conventional bank collateral requirements. “Many individuals, particularly those in rural areas, are denied of credit because of issue of collateral, but we as Credit Union, that is where we come in, so that we make credit accessible for such individuals,” he said. He explained that credit unions can extend financing to borrowers who lack property to use as security while relying on their structures to support loan recovery. Mr Atta-Pearce, whose institution was recognised as Cooperative Credit Union Brand of the Year at the awards, called for efforts to expand access to credit regardless of borrowers’ locations. “I think that it’s high time we look at how we can make credit accessible, irrespective of wherever you are, so that people can easily get access to money and that will also help us to grow the economy,” he said. Both credit management professionals stressed the need to improve access to financing while maintaining responsible lending practices, effective borrower education and mechanisms to ensure loan repayment.

Anthropic has filed its S-1 prospectus with the Securities and Exchange Commission, preparing the company behind Claude to beat OpenAI to the punch with an IPO. In a filing with the SEC, Anthropic said it plans to list on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker symbol “ANT.”
The AI company confidentially filed with the SEC earlier this year in June, but the public document reveals more details, as well as the company’s plans for the future in its own words, as well as potential risks for investors and the world. According to the S-1, in the first half of this year Anthropic had an $80.7 billion net loss on $16.3 billion in revenue. As previously reported by the Wall Street Journal based on leaked versions of the document, the majority of that loss is from accounting charges related to notes issued by the company for funding.
It also lays out billions of dollars in deals it’s made for access to compute to power its AI, including about $3.1 billion per month to SpaceX for access to Nvidia GPUs once all of the planned capacity is delivered, totaling as much as $120.5 billion by 2029. Other commitments include spending $44.9 billion with Microsoft through 2033, at least $114.5 billion with Google through 2033, and $110 billion with Amazon over the next ten years.
We believe that AI is one of the most consequential technologies in human history. If managed well, it could rapidly accelerate scientific innovation, greatly increase economic growth rates, bring cures for major diseases within reach, and solve problems that have resisted generations of human effort.
Anthropic aims to realize these benefits while navigating and preventing the risks that come with a technological revolution this fast and this powerful. There are four things that we would like any investor in Anthropic to understand: the incredible potential of AI, the risks we must address, Anthropic’s unique approach to building a company and operating in the world, and the ways in which our behavior may differ from that of a purely profit-maximizing company.
According to the filing, cofounder and chief executive officer Dario Amodei’s compensation totaled nearly $18 million in 2025, most of which came from stock and option awards. His sister, Daniela Amodei, who also cofounded the company and serves as its president and director, was the second highest-paid executive, receiving $16.4 million in 2025.
Anthropic set out a long list of risk factors that could affect its business, including the prospect of its AI models developing “forms of sentience,” “AI-specific taxes,” and unfavorable resolutions to the many ongoing copyright disputes relating to how its models are trained. The company also warned about the risk of “catastrophic” AI-related incidents, and said it was likely no single insurer — “and potentially the insurance industry in the aggregate” — could underwrite such risk.

title: Kiir heads to Moscow for Russia-Africa summit
body: South Sudanese President Salva Kiir Mayardit left Juba on Monday for Moscow to attend the third Russia-Africa Summit on October 28–29, his office said, as his government seeks to strengthen ties with Russia and attract investment. Kiir is expected to hold bilateral talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin on relations between the two countries and opportunities to expand cooperation, Presidential Press Secretary Ambassador Arek Ayou Deng said. Preparations for the summit have entered their final stage, according to the Russian Foreign Ministry. The meeting will bring together African leaders and Russian officials to discuss political, security and economic cooperation. Putin and Burundi’s President Évariste Ndayishimiye, who chairs the African Union, are due to co-chair the summit’s plenary session on October 29. The summit’s agenda includes trade, investment, energy, infrastructure, agriculture, technology and food security. Russia’s Africa strategy Russia has sought to expand its diplomatic and security engagement across Africa, positioning itself as an alternative partner to Western powers. However, its trade and investment presence on the continent remains smaller than that of major economic partners such as China and the United States. Moscow has framed its engagement with African countries around the idea of a multipolar world order and greater independence from Western-led institutions. The push has also taken place as Russia faces economic and diplomatic isolation from Western countries over its war in Ukraine. African governments, for their part, have sought to diversify international partnerships to attract investment, secure military and security cooperation and strengthen food supplies and agricultural production. For South Sudan, the summit offers an opportunity to pursue closer ties with Moscow as the country seeks investment and cooperation in sectors including energy, infrastructure and agriculture. title: Top Russian, Slovak diplomats discuss Russia-EU crisis, Ukrainian issue — Foreign Ministry
body:
MOSCOW, October 26. /TASS/. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and his Slovak counterpart Juraj Blanar discussed Moscow's and Bratislava's positions on the Ukrainian settlement, as well as the crisis in relations between Russia and the EU, the Foreign Ministry reported.
Blanar arrived in Moscow, heading a Slovak delegation, to participate in the 22nd meeting of the bilateral Intergovernmental Commission on Economic, Scientific, and Technical Cooperation.
"A number of practical issues concerning Russian-Slovak relations, the prospects for developing political dialogue, and cooperation in the trade, economic, cultural, humanitarian, and military-memorial spheres were discussed in a constructive manner. [The sides] exchanged views on the situation around Ukraine and the crisis in relations between Russia and the EU," Russian diplomats said in a statement.

title: Damascus struggles to assert control in southern Syria amid ISIS threat, Druze tensions - analysis
body: Southern Syria is facing renewed security challenges. Armed groups have been attacking government security forces, tensions are on the rise in Sweida, and the Syrian government has been confronting threats from ISIS cells in the areas surrounding Damascus.These developments illustrate the difficulties Syria's government faces as it seeks to maintain security across the country.Southern Syria is particularly complex for several reasons. One reason is the continued Israeli raids along the border. Syrians are becoming increasingly angry and frustrated with Israeli patrols into Syrian villages. Last week, a Syrian was killed, and this led to protests.Another issue pertains to the Druze in Sweida. The Druze area is not under government control and has sought varying degrees of independence.At the same time, ISIS cells and other threats appear to continue to pose problems in the areas between Damascus and Daraa and the Golan border. Israel has demanded southern Syria be demilitarized, which means that Syria can only deploy lightly armed Interior Ministry forces.The situation is particularly serious in southern Syria, where instability in Daraa and Sweida has implications for the region near Israel's border. Syria's government is attempting to expand its authority, but local armed groups and other security threats might complicate these efforts.Clashes with authorities, terroristsSyria's state-owned news agency SANA reported on Sunday that a highway security officer had been killed and another wounded when armed men attacked a security checkpoint in the Busra al-Sham area of the eastern Daraa province.According to SANA, the Internal Security Forces said specialized units responded to the attack and arrested the perpetrators following an exchange of fire. Authorities said investigations were continuing to determine the circumstances and motives behind the incident.The attack illustrates the challenges in Daraa, a province that played an important role in the uprising against the Assad regime that started in 2011.This area has experienced years of division during the civil war, and the latest incident depicts how armed attacks remain a threat to government efforts to establish security.In general, Daraa is known for supporting Damascus, but during the era when the former Syrian regime ran Daraa from 2018 to 2024, there were many mysterious killings. Some may have been linked to local feuds.SANA noted that the attack followed another incident on October 13, when three highway security officers were killed in an attack on their patrol along the Salamiya-Sheikh Hilal-Athriya road in the eastern Hama province.Although the incidents took place in different areas, they underscore the dangers facing Syrian security personnel.Meanwhile, the situation in the neighboring Sweida province remains tense. SANA reported that armed groups in Sweida closed the main highway connecting the province to Damascus on Saturday.Drug, weapon smuggling rampantNotably, SANA represents the government's stance. Druze authorities have rejected the claims. They were also angered by recent comments from US Special Envoy Tom Barrack, who slammed Sweida, describing it as an area rife with drug smuggling.According to the recent Syrian state media report, the road was blocked in both directions at the Um al-Zaytoun checkpoint, which is controlled by what was called a “local armed group.”Qutaiba Azzam, the director of media relations at the Sweida Media Department, said the groups had prevented traffic from passing through the area.The report also said about 100 employees were prevented from reaching their workplaces earlier in the week. Similar restrictions had previously affected students seeking to leave the area to take national examinations.On October 18, Sweida Gov. Mustafa al-Bakour warned that residents were suffering from difficult living conditions and deteriorating security. According to SANA, he accused armed groups of kidnappings, threats, and obstructing efforts to resolve the situation.It is important to note, again, that SANA presents these developments from the perspective of the Syrian government, describing the armed factions as outlaw groups. Nevertheless, the continuing dispute exhibits the difficulties Damascus faces in extending its authority over Sweida.Road closures and restrictions on civilian movement matter because they affect daily life and economic activity. Another dimension to this is the way in which local armed groups have clearly been exercising control even when the government seeks to restore normal administration.In another development, Syrian security forces have continued operations against suspected ISIS cells around Damascus. Per Rudaw, two members of Syria's Internal Security Forces were killed, and five were wounded during an operation targeting an ISIS cell in Rankous, approximately 45 kilometers north of Damascus.The Internal Security Forces said the suspects refused to surrender and opened fire. The operation reportedly ended with five suspected ISIS members killed, six arrested, and weapons and explosive belts seized.ISIS plots to attack government forcesSANA also reported the operation, saying it was carried out in cooperation with the General Intelligence Service.The operation followed an October 16 announcement that Syrian intelligence and security forces had disrupted an alleged ISIS plot to attack a police patrol in the Damascus countryside. Two suspects were arrested, and an explosive device was seized.Rudaw noted that ISIS continues to operate in parts of Syria despite a decline in its attacks. It cited an August 27 report by the US Lead Inspector General for Operation Inherent Resolve monitoring office that described a reduction in ISIS attacks following the withdrawal of American forces in April, while noting continued attacks on Syrian government forces.Taken together, the developments point to several overlapping security challenges.In Daraa, armed attacks threaten government personnel. When it comes to Sweida, the situation is unlikely to be resolved any time soon. Druze accuse the government of complicity in a massacre of more than 1,000 people in July of 2025. Around Damascus, ISIS cells remain a security concern.These are not necessarily connected threats. However, they demonstrate the fragmented security environment confronting Syria's new government.For Israel, developments in Daraa and Sweida are particularly relevant because both provinces are part of the wider southern Syrian region bordering or close to the Golan Heights. Instability in these areas could complicate efforts to establish predictable security arrangements along the frontier.The larger question is whether Damascus can consolidate security without creating new confrontations with local communities and armed groups.Based on the incidents reported over the past week alone, restoring government authority seems to remain a difficult process, particularly in southern Syria, where local tensions intersect with broader regional security concerns.

title: Delta: Police arrest school bus driver over alleged kidnap, assault of 14-year-old
body: By Emmauel Okogba The Delta State Police Command has arrested a 28-year-old school bus driver, Onome Lucky Ughagha, over the alleged kidnapping and sexual assault of a 14-year-old female student in Sapele. The suspect was also accused of demanding and collecting ₦503,000 from the victim’s father as ransom before abandoning the girl along Oton Road, Sapele. The police said the incident was reported at the Sapele Area Command on October 20, 2026, by the victim’s father, who alleged that the suspect abducted his daughter while she was preparing to leave for school. According to a statement by the Police Public Relations Officer, Delta State Command, SP Bright Edafe, the suspect allegedly contacted the girl’s father, demanded ₦503,000 and threatened to kill the minor if the money was not paid. The statement said the victim was abandoned along Oton Road after the ransom was paid and subsequently reunited with her family in a traumatised condition, with indications that she had been sexually assaulted. Following the report, operatives of the Sapele Area Command commenced investigations, while the victim was taken to a medical facility for examination and treatment. The police added that the school principal and vice principal were invited for questioning as efforts intensified to apprehend the suspect, who had allegedly abandoned the school bus and fled. Edafe said the suspect was eventually arrested on October 23 at his hideout in the Ajimele area of Sapele following intelligence-led operations. “During preliminary interrogation, he reportedly confessed to his involvement in the crime,” the statement said. The police disclosed that arrangements were underway to transfer the suspect to the State Criminal Investigation Department in Asaba for further investigation. The Commissioner of Police in Delta State, CP Samuel Erale, condemned the incident and reaffirmed the command’s commitment to protecting children from violence and exploitation. He assured that the investigation would be thorough and that anyone found culpable would be brought to justice. The commissioner also urged school authorities, parents and transport operators to strengthen measures to protect children, stressing that the safety of every child entrusted to their care must remain a priority. The post Delta: Police arrest school bus driver over alleged kidnap, assault of 14-year-old appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Russia to be guest of honor at 2026 Hainan Winter Trade Fair — newspaper
body:
HAIKOU /China/, October 26. /TASS/. Russia will be the guest of honor at the 29th Hainan International Tropical Agricultural Products Winter Trade Fair, which will be held this year in the southern Chinese province of Hainan, Sanya Ribao reported.
According to the newspaper, Ethiopia has also been granted guest-of-honor status at the fair. Other countries that will have their own pavilions at the fair include Australia, Argentina, Bulgaria, Brazil, Vietnam, Zambia, Cameroon, Kenya, Colombia, Malaysia, New Zealand, Serbia, Slovakia, Thailand, and Uganda. Russia will showcase not only its agricultural products, which are in high demand in China, but also its national potential in the fields of culture and tourism.
Sanya Ribao noted that fair visitors will be able to explore a variety of Russian goods, including meat and dairy products, ice cream, baked goods, cookies, ready-to-eat breakfasts, chocolate, honey, and much more. According to the newspaper’s authors, this exhibition “will bring the authentic flavors of the North to Hainan and demonstrate the unique competitiveness of high-quality Russian agricultural products.”
The article emphasized that the exhibition will showcase products and cutting-edge agricultural technologies from several countries. The event's program includes numerous presentations. Organizers promise an "impressive international lineup of participants" for the Hainan fair, which is attracting growing public interest.
A special zone dedicated to helping national agricultural brands enter the global market will open on the exhibition grounds. Leveraging the advantages of the Hainan Free Trade Port, the zone is expected to become an effective platform for cooperation between Chinese and foreign agribusiness companies. It will strengthen global supply chains for relevant products, boost the influence of Chinese brands abroad, and help foreign products gain a more secure foothold in China. In addition, a delegation from the city of Sanya on Hainan’s southern coast will attend the event. It will comprise representatives from leading local agricultural enterprises and cooperatives.
The 2026 Hainan International Tropical Agricultural Products Winter Trade Fair will be held on December 3-6 at the International Convention and Exhibition Center in Haikou, the administrative center of Hainan. This year, the exhibition has expanded its international cooperation zone further and attracted a wide variety of agricultural products from around the world.

title: Okyeame Kwame urges President Mahama, Jane Naana to honour Ghana’s founding mothers
body: Ghanaian musician and cultural advocate Okyeame Kwame has appealed to President John Dramani Mahama and Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang to lead a national campaign to recognise women who contributed to Ghana’s independence and nation-building. In an open letter dated Wednesday, 21st October 2026, Okyeame Kwame proposed four interventions to honour Ghana’s founding mothers, including reforms to history education, a national recognition programme, initiatives to empower women and girls, and public art commemorating their contributions. Addressing the President and the Vice President, he said they were well positioned to lead the initiative, citing the historic decision by Mr Mahama to select a woman as his running mate, who subsequently became Vice President. “I write to you (Your Excellency John Dramani Mahama and Your Excellency Mrs. Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang) because I believe that in this material moment, you are the best-positioned duo with the will to lead the charge to empower women in Ghana,” he wrote. Okyeame Kwame argued that women played significant roles in Ghana’s independence struggle but their contributions have received less recognition than those of their male counterparts. “Ghana’s freedom was not won by men alone. Women organised communities, financed political movements, challenged colonial authority, communicated ideas of freedom, and helped shape our institutions and national identity,” he stated. He warned that the underrepresentation of women in the country’s historical narrative has implications beyond recognition, affecting gender equality, national development and the aspirations of future generations. As part of his Ayekoo (Big Up) campaign, the musician highlighted five women whose contributions he believes deserve greater recognition: Susanna Al-Hassan, Rebecca Naa Dedei Aryeetey, popularly known as Dedei Ashikishan, Theodosia Salome Okoh, Mabel Dove Danquah and Ama Nkrumah. He described Susanna Al-Hassan as a pioneering public servant who served in ministerial roles and contributed to education and social welfare; Rebecca Naa Dedei Aryeetey was a businesswoman whose resources and influence supported the independence movement. Theodosia Salome Okoh designed Ghana’s national flag, while Mabel Dove Danquah was a pioneering journalist, writer and political figure elected to the Gold Coast Legislative Assembly in 1954. Ama Nkrumah, he said, was a political activist and organiser whose work demonstrated the importance of grassroots mobilisation. He stressed that the women did not represent an exhaustive list, adding that Hannah Kudjoe, Oforiwaa Tagoe and other women who contributed to independence and early nationhood should also be recognised. Okyeame Kwame acknowledged existing efforts to honour distinguished women, including naming public facilities after them, but called for a broader national programme. He said the proposal was not intended to diminish the contributions of Ghana’s founding fathers, but to provide a fuller account of the country’s history. Among his recommendations is a review of the history curriculum by the Ministry of Education, the National Council for Curriculum and Assessment (NaCCA), the Ghana Education Service and historical experts to ensure women’s contributions are taught accurately and consistently. He also proposed establishing a National Founding Mothers Recognition Programme to coordinate historians, educators, women’s organisations, traditional authorities, museums and local assemblies in documenting women’s contributions, verifying historical records and developing exhibitions and educational resources. The programme, he said, should adopt a transparent, evidence-based approach to selecting women for recognition, ensuring that the process is not determined by political affiliation or popularity. The musician further called for greater access to mentorship, leadership development, science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) education, technical and vocational training, financial literacy and enterprise support for women and girls. He recommended that the initiative have measurable objectives, adequate funding and periodic public reporting. He also suggested commissioning historically informed murals and graffiti on suitable bridges and other public spaces, while naming selected roundabouts and new infrastructure after women whose contributions have helped shape Ghana. Okyeame urged the President’s Office to designate a lead institution to coordinate the proposals and make recognition of the founding mothers a lasting national commitment. “Let us honour the women who helped make Ghana possible by remembering their contributions and creating conditions in which the next generation of Ghanaian women can help shape the country’s future,” he wrote. Okyeame Kwame’s ‘Big Up’ song which features Jah Lead is now available on various streaming platforms.

title: Opinion: Why agreement between Abkhazia’s interior ministry and Russia conflicts with Abkhaz law
body: The opposition in Abkhazia is demanding the immediate resignation of Interior Minister Robert Kiut. The call follows an agreement he signed with Russia’s Interior Ministry . The opposition argues that the deal violates Abkhazia’s constitution and undermines its national interests. One provision has provoked particular outrage. It envisages sharing with the Russian side data on individuals who could “destabilise the situation in the border region”. Many suspect that the agreement would legitimise a growing trend in which Russian authorities punish Abkhaz public figures and politicians who oppose arrangements with Russia that they consider detrimental to Abkhazia. Abkhazia-Russia police cooperation: ‘shameful incompetence’ or boost to effectiveness? The interagency cooperation agreements published by journalist Nizfa Arshba have sparked a heated debate in Abkhazia’s public sphere. Prominent Abkhaz public figure Akhra Bzhania has examined whether the agreement complies with Abkhaz law. He concludes that it does not. Akhra Bzhania: “Most supporters of the agreement between Abkhazia’s Interior Ministry and Russia cite legal continuity with the provisions of the 2014 Treaty of Alliance between Russia and Abkhazia as their main argument. But can these references really be considered made in good faith? Here is what Article 10 of the 2014 treaty says in its main provisions on cooperation between the two sides’ interior ministries: 1. Within one year of the treaty’s entry into force, the parties must establish a Joint Information and Coordination Centre for their interior affairs agencies. 2. The Joint Information and Coordination Centre for Interior Affairs Agencies is responsible for: organising the exchange of operationally significant information between the law enforcement agencies of the Russian Federation and the Republic of Abkhazia, as well as maintaining the necessary operational and forensic records; compiling and maintaining a specialised database on organised criminal groups whose illegal activities affect the interests of the contracting parties; collecting, consolidating and analysing information on efforts to combat organised crime and other serious offences; assisting with the international search for and extradition of people who have evaded criminal prosecution or the enforcement of a sentence; facilitating the implementation of necessary coordinated measures to combat serious crimes that threaten the security of the contracting parties; developing and submitting proposals to the contracting parties on improving the effectiveness of their cooperation. Opinion: ‘Irakli Bzhinava’s arrest in Russia is blow to freedom in Abkhaz society’ Abkhaz lawyer Irakli Bzhinava, who holds dual citizenship, was arrested for criticising an agreement to transfer a famous state-owned holiday residence in Abkhazia to Russia. None of these provisions, nor the treaty as a whole, states or implies that the Joint Information and Coordination Centre (JICC) may be used to “monitor and analyse the crime situation and operational environment in the Republic of Abkhazia, as well as the activities of Abkhazia’s interior affairs agencies”, as stated in Article 1 of the new agreement. That last point is particularly absurd. Why have an entire ministry if it needs to rely on an external organisation to monitor its activities? Not to mention that Abkhazia’s Interior Ministry may have internal matters that the JICC should know nothing about. The 2014 treaty also says nothing about the JICC, let alone specialised units of Russia’s Interior Ministry, tackling “economic crime and corruption” in Abkhazia. Nor does it mention any Russian Interior Ministry units directly engaging in “countering the spread of criminal ideas on social media and messaging platforms”. Yet Article 4 of the new agreement between the two interior ministries explicitly includes this provision. Incidentally, many have interpreted this clause as an attempt to monitor online spaces for dissenting views. There is also the fact that the very definition of what constitutes “criminal” content online may differ significantly between our two countries. In Russia, for example, even this text, published on Facebook, a platform owned by Meta, is illegal. And, of course, the 2014 treaty nowhere states that the Russian and Abkhaz interior ministries will “conduct joint operational and preventive measures in border areas” — activities that infringe on our sovereign jurisdiction. Yet Article 6 of the new agreement explicitly provides for them. And so it goes with many other provisions… International treaties are not folk songs from which you can create a new work by developing the main theme. They are complete legal documents, and their provisions cannot be freely reinterpreted. For this reason, and because the two instruments differ substantially in their content, the new agreement cannot be said to “derive” from the 2014 treaty, as some “experts” are trying to argue. If anyone really wants to establish a new legal framework for the work of Abkhazia’s Interior Ministry, they should try doing so openly and through the lawful procedure. Then we can see how that works out. The terminology, place names and views expressed in this article are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the editorial position of this website.

title: Iran fully united, on highest alert amid US-Israeli threats
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 26 (MNA) – Iran’s Deputy Foreign Minister Saeed Khatibzadeh has said that Iran remains fully united and on the highest level of alert amid continuing threats from the United States and Israel
Speaking to reporters on Sunday on the sidelines of the inauguration of the Martyr Kamal Kharrazi Documentation Center and Museum in Tehran, Khatibzadeh emphasized Iran’s national unity and readiness to respond to threats against its security.
According to Tehran Times, he said Europe had made a series of misguided decisions in recent months and was now facing the consequences of its own policies, adding that European countries had marginalized themselves on major international issues through their approach to regional developments.
Khatibzadeh called on European governments to distance themselves from the Israeli regime’s actions and repeated violations of international and humanitarian law.
He stressed that confidence in European countries would remain difficult to establish unless they explicitly condemned such actions, stopped allowing the United States to use their military bases, and demonstrated a genuine commitment to upholding international law.
The Iranian official also warned Washington against further military action, saying that if the first and second wars against Iran had failed to achieve their objectives, another military campaign would prove equally unsuccessful.
He stressed that efforts should instead focus on building a peaceful Iran and a stable region, free from 'the destabilizing presence of the United States and its allies.'
In separate remarks at the inauguration ceremony, Khatibzadeh condemned the Israeli attack on the Foreign Ministry’s specialized library, saying the strike had disrupted the activities of the century-old institution for the first time in its history.
Comparing the attack to the destruction caused by the Mongol invasions, he described the library as one of Iran’s leading specialized academic resources in foreign policy, international economics, international relations and international law. The collection contains Iranian and foreign publications in multiple languages.
The ceremony marked the inauguration of the Documentation Center and Museum dedicated to Seyyed Kamal Kharrazi, a prominent Iranian diplomat and former foreign minister who died on April 9, 2026, from injuries sustained in a US-Israeli airstrike on his Tehran residence on April 1.

title: Kremlin Urges Serbia’s New Leaders to Maintain Russia Ties After Vucic’s Election Defeat
body:
The Kremlin on said Monday, Oct. 26, that it hoped Serbia’s incoming leaders would maintain cooperation with Russia after a student-backed opposition movement defeated longtime Moscow-friendly leader Aleksandar Vucic in Sunday’s parliamentary election.
“We would like to express hope ... that these new political forces understand that cooperation with Russia is in Serbia’s interests, because it brings benefits to Serbia,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters .
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Vucic conceded defeat on Sunday, Oct. 25 , saying preliminary estimates showed the Student List winning 135-140 seats in the 250-member parliament, compared with about 105 for his United Serbia coalition. A majority requires 126 seats.
The result marks a setback for one of Moscow’s closest political partners in Europe. Under Vucic, Serbia maintained close ties with Russia and refused to join Western sanctions over its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, while continuing to pursue European Union membership.
President Volodymyr Zelensky welcomed the election result, calling it a “new chapter in the history of the country and its people.”
“We are ready to continue expanding our cooperation, and may all the good hopes of the people of Serbia come true!” Zelensky wrote on X .
Despite the Student List’s victory, a change in Serbia’s Russia policy is not guaranteed.
Vucic predicted that the incoming authorities would impose sanctions on Russia by March or April 2027, but the movement had pledged before the election to oppose such measures.
In a foreign-policy platform published in September, the Student List said Serbia would continue to reject sanctions against Russia, citing the country’s own historical experience with restrictive measures.
Vucic also accused unnamed European countries and what he called an “American deep state” opposed to US President Donald Trump of backing his opponents. He provided no evidence for the allegations.
The movement emerged from nationwide student-led protests following the November 2024 collapse of a railway station canopy in Novi Sad that killed 16 people.
Demonstrators demanded accountability over suspected corruption and construction failures, turning the protests into a broader challenge to Vucic’s political dominance.
Serbia has sought to balance its EU membership ambitions with longstanding ties to Moscow. Russia supplies Serbia with energy and backs Belgrade’s position on Kosovo, whose independence Serbia does not recognize.
Belgrade has also supported Ukraine’s territorial integrity and provided humanitarian and financial assistance to Kyiv, while avoiding sanctions against Moscow.
Vucic traveled to Moscow last year to attend commemorations marking the 80th anniversary of the Soviet Union’s victory in World War II, despite criticism from European leaders.

title: Afreximbank records net income growth of 24% to US$813.5m; assets and contingencies exceed US$54.1bn
body: African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) and its subsidiaries (the “Group”) delivered a satisfactory financial performance for the nine months ended 30 September 2026, demonstrating resilient growth, sound asset quality and continued support for trade and economic development across Africa and the Caribbean Community (CARICOM). Net income rose by 24% to US$813.5 million, compared with US$654.3 million in the corresponding period of 2025, driven by growth in lending activities, improved interest income and disciplined cost management, despite a challenging global operating environment. The Group’s total assets and contingencies increased by 12% to US$54.1 billion, from US$48.5 billion in 2025. This growth was underpinned by an expansion of the Bank’s lending portfolio, with net loans and advances increasing by 8% to US$36.2 billion, compared to US$33.5 billion at year-end 2025. Gross income increased to US$2.7 billion in nine months of 2026, up 11% from the prior period, supported by continued balance sheet growth and strong earnings generation. This performance was largely driven by a 9.1% increase in interest income to US$2.4 billion, from US$2.2 billion in nine months of 2025, underpinned by growth in average loan balances, which increased from US$28.9 billion in nine months of 2025 to US$34.8 billion in nine months of 2026, reflecting sustained demand for trade and project financing across the Bank’s member countries. Net interest income also strengthened by 15% to US$1.5 billion. Fees and commission income from unfunded business activities, including guarantees, letters of credit and advisory services, increased to US$136.9 million, from US$117.2 million in the prior-year period. The Group maintained strong operational efficiency, with its cost-to-income ratio improving to 20%, compared with 21% for the nine months ended September 2025, remaining comfortably below the Bank’s strategic ceiling of 30%. Return on average shareholders’ equity (ROAE) remained robust at 12%, while return on average assets (ROAA) improved to 2.48%, from 2.34% compared to the nine months of 2025. Asset quality remained sound, with the non-performing loans (NPL) ratio at 2.48%, compared with 2.43% as at 31 December 2025. Provisions for expected credit losses amounted to US$537.6 million, compared with US$481.3 million in the corresponding period of 2025. The Group’s liquidity position remained strong, with liquid assets totalling US$6.1 billion, representing 13% of total assets, compared with 15% at the end of 2025. The capital adequacy ratio stood at 22%, compared with 23% at the end of 2025, underscoring the resilience of the Bank’s balance sheet and alignment with its long-term capital management objectives. Shareholders’ funds increased to US$9.0 billion, from US$8.4 billion at the end of 2025, supported by internally generated profits and US$195.2 million in new equity contributions under the Bank’s General Capital Increase programme. Commenting on the results, Denys Denya, Afreximbank’s Senior Executive Vice President, said, “This performance underscores Afreximbank’s ability to deliver strong and sustainable performance while continuing to fulfil its development mandate across Africa and the Caribbean. Our expanded lending portfolio, robust profitability and strong capital position demonstrate the effectiveness of our strategy and the growing relevance of our interventions across our target markets. As global economic and geopolitical uncertainties persist, Afreximbank remains committed to providing the financing, trade facilitation and strategic investments needed to strengthen regional value chains, support industrialisation and accelerate the continent’s economic transformation.” During the period, Afreximbank further strengthened its access to international debt capital markets, successfully completing a US$1.5 billion dual-tranche bond issuance in July 2026. The transaction comprised US$750 million in 5.5-year notes and US$750 million in 10-year notes and was approximately two times oversubscribed. As a result, debt securities in issue increased to US$4.4 billion, from US$3.4 billion at the end of 2025, further supporting the diversification of the Group’s funding base. The Bank continued to demonstrate its countercyclical role in response to geopolitical and economic disruptions. Its US$10 billion Gulf Crisis Response Programme was established to provide critical liquidity support, facilitate trade and payment flows, and help member countries maintain access to essential imports, including energy products, fertilisers, food and other strategic commodities. In line with its commitment to transformative development, the Group’s high-impact investments also increased by 23% to US$1.6 billion, from US$1.3 billion at the end of 2025, supporting strategic development projects that advance industrialisation, trade competitiveness and economic resilience.

title: Egypt's parliament authorises El Sisi to send troops to defend Saudi Arabia
body: Egypt 's parliament has authorised President Abdel Fattah El Sisi to send troops to Saudi Arabia , an MP close to the government said on Monday, clearing the last constitutional hurdle to a possible deployment against the Houthis. “Parliament approved authorising President El Sisi to send forces to Saudi Arabia if required, and after co-ordination between the two countries,” Mostafa Bakry wrote on X after a closed session in Cairo, the third over the past nine days to discuss the natter. The parliament, he said, had given the president “freedom of decision according to his assessment”. It has not published the result of the vote, which was held by roll call behind closed doors. However, under Article 152 of the constitution, sending the army on a combat mission abroad requires the backing of two-thirds of the 596-member house, or 398 MPs. The approval does not mean troops will deploy immediately. Mr El Sisi, as supreme commander of the armed forces, now has the legal authority to act, but has said Egypt will do so only if Riyadh asks. No formal Saudi request has been announced. Monday's vote came after more than a week of debate. Mr El Sisi asked parliament for the mandate on October 17, at a graduation ceremony at the Egyptian Military Academy, saying it was inconceivable that Saudi Arabia's security would be harmed. The National Defence Council, which he chairs, met the following day and pledged “all necessary and possible forms of support” to the kingdom, without specifying their form, size or duration. MPs were expected to approve the request quickly. The four main pro-government parties hold 403 of the 568 elected seats. Instead, the House met in two closed sessions on October 18 and 19, then adjourned for a week. Assem El Gazzar, deputy speaker and head of the pro-government National Front Party, said nearly 500 MPs had asked to speak, more than he had seen on any other issue. Most parties backed the request. The Wafd, Egypt's oldest liberal party, said Saudi security was “an inseparable part” of Egypt's national security. The Justice Party told its MPs to vote in favour, and the Salafist Nour Party called for defensive co-ordination with Riyadh. The Egyptian Social Democratic Party, which has about a dozen seats, told its MPs to abstain, citing the economic cost and the risk of regional escalation. Maha Abdel Nasser, one of its MPs, rejected what she called an open-ended and vague mandate and urged a diplomatic solution. Mohamed Abdel Aleem Dawoud, head of the Wafd's parliamentary bloc, and the independent MP Diaa El Din Dawoud also reserved their positions. The crisis became personal for many Egyptians on October 10, when a Houthi strike on Riyadh's airport killed 12 people. Among them was Azza Ramzy, a 28-year-old from Beheira province. The Houthis have warned Cairo against intervening. Yahya Al Raei, speaker of the Houthi-run parliament in Sanaa, wrote to his Egyptian counterpart Hisham Badawi that involvement would pose “a grave danger” to Egypt's national security. Egypt has strong reasons to side with Riyadh. Saudi Arabia is one of its biggest financial backers, and Houthi attacks on Red Sea shipping have already cut revenue from the Suez Canal, one of Egypt's main sources of foreign currency. It is not yet clear what form Egyptian support would take. Officials have described any mission as defensive, and have not said whether it would involve ground troops, air defence or naval forces.

title: Hainan’s Yangpu port expanding its network of trade routes to Southeast Asia — news outlet
body:
HAIKOU /China/, October 26. /TASS/. The deep-water port of Yangpu in the southern Chinese province of Hainan is expanding its transport links with Southeast Asian countries and steadily increasing its cargo turnover with them, the ChinaNews outlet reported.
According to its information, Yangpu, located on the island’s northwestern coast, currently operates a total of 68 regular maritime container routes. These routes primarily connect Hainan with major port cities in China and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), as well as with countries in the Middle East and on the east and west coasts of the US.
At the same time, Du Chengcai, deputy general manager of production operations center at Hainan Harbor and Shipping International Port Co, noted that Yangpu will accommodate even more large vessels, which will help increase exports from southwestern China and other regions. According to him, after Hainan transitioned to a new customs regime in December 2025, the port’s cargo throughput growth rate increased significantly.
“This will allow Yangpu to reach its design capacity of five million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEU) per year more quickly,” Du Chengcai emphasized. “Thanks to expedited customs clearance, transit time has been reduced to five days, and efficiency has increased by nearly 30%,” he noted.
ChinaNews recalled that the Yangpu International Container Terminal has a shoreline totaling 1,970 meters, which allows it to accommodate ultra-large container ships with a capacity of up to 24,000 TEU. At this stage, the port administration is focusing on serving extensive transportation networks, as well as transit and interregional routes. Meanwhile, efforts are underway to increase sailings on existing shipping routes and develop multimodal transportation.
Last week, the nearly 399.67-meter-long CSCL ATLANTIC OCEAN, with a deadweight of 188,638 metric tons, docked at the Yangpu International Terminal. It is reportedly the largest container ship ever served by the Hainan Free Trade Port.
According to the General Administration of Customs of the People’s Republic of China, the country’s trade volume with ASEAN member states grew by 27.9% year-over-year from January to September, totaling $994.34 billion. Notably, China’s exports to ASEAN countries during this period increased by 28.7%, reaching $627.76 billion. Imports from Southeast Asian countries rose by 26.6%, reaching $366.58 billion.

title: Exclusive: Russia significantly expands glide-bomb production, research shows
body:
Russia is significantly expanding its glide-bomb production, indicating that Moscow has no plans to scale back its war against Ukraine, a new report by Kyiv-based think tank Center for Defense Reforms exclusively shared with the Kyiv Independent reveals.
"Given the role of guided aerial bombs in destroying defensive positions, isolating battlefields and facilitating ground advances, this provides a basis for sustaining high-intensity offensive operations over an extended period," the report concludes.
The report reveals that in 2025, the centralized procurement entity TRV-Engineering JSC obtained nearly 278,000 servo drives, used to control the flight surfaces of glide bombs — enough to manufacture 139,000 of the deadly munitions. The report identifies the key Russian supplier of servo drives, CED Sail LLC, which is currently not subject to any Western sanctions, and suggests this entity should be a "priority target" for sanctions designation.
"Russia is building the military-industrial capacity to continue waging wars even after the war in Ukraine ends. These are not the actions of a country preparing for lasting peace," Oleksandr Danylyuk, chairman of the Center for Defense Reforms and former chief adviser to Ukraine’s defense minister, told the Kyiv Independent.
The report also identifies a network of interconnected Russian companies which are responsible for importing key components and raw materials essential for the production of UMPK and UMPB glide bomb kits.
Russia converts older, unguided bombs into precision-guided weapons with these guidance kits, significantly increasing their range and accuracy. The increase in range allows Russian fighter-bomber aircraft to remain within Russian territory, out of range of Ukrainian air defenses, as they deploy their deadly payloads.
As with many other Russian munitions, both UMPK and UMPB glide bomb kits are heavily reliant on foreign components for their manufacture.
Ukrainian military intelligence has repeatedly identified a range of foreign components in Russian glide bombs, including parts from the U.S., Japan, China, Switzerland, and Taiwan, among others.
The report also reveals the majority of entities and individuals involved in the production of Russia's glide bombs are currently unsanctioned, despite the munitions being a key part of the Kremlin's offensive airborne arsenal.
Out of 20 corporate entities involved in the manufacture of Russian glide bombs, only eight are subject to some level of Western sanctions or export restrictions. The "uneven sanctions coverage," the report assesses, allows Russia to continue to "procure necessary components without significant restrictions."
Four Chinese companies are identified as being critical to the supply chain, with some, such as Shenzhen Fire Power Control Technology Limited, not hiding the explicitly military application of their products. Only one of the four Chinese companies is subject to U.S. export restrictions, and none are sanctioned by the U.K. or the EU.
"Despite its repeated declarations of readiness for peace, Russia continues to dramatically expand the production of offensive weapons, particularly guided aerial bombs," Danylyuk said.
Russia has heavily relied on glide bombs to support its slow advance in the east of Ukraine, targeting Ukrainian fighting positions, fortifications, and buildings. Russian forces have also increasingly used the munitions to target Ukrainian cities that have come within range of the bombs.
Earlier this month, five Russian glide bombs struck the city of Zaporizhzhia , killing 20 people, including three children, and injuring 32 others.
Ukraine has attempted to counter Russia's glide bombs using electronic warfare to disrupt their guidance systems, as well as targeting the Su-34 fighter-bomber aircraft used to deploy them. Earlier in October, Ukraine struck six Russian Sukhoi Su-34M fighter-bombers in a "Neptune" cruise missile strike on a Russian airfield in Borisoglebsk, Voronezh Oblast, destroying at least four and likely heavily damaging two more.

title: UK sanctions 15 Sudanese military commanders, officials, for sexual violence, civilian attacks
body: Britain on Monday sanctioned 15 military commanders, militia leaders, and security officials from both sides of Sudan's conflict, accusing them of waging sexual violence, torture, and attacks on civilians linked to the fall of al-Fashir.Those targeted include commanders from the Rapid Support Forces and Sudanese Armed Forces, as well as leaders of armed groups allied to the army, in what London said was its latest effort to hold perpetrators of abuses accountable.The measures come a year after the fall of al-Fashir, the North Darfur capital that became a focal point of Sudan's war, where civilians were subjected to a prolonged siege, reported mass killings and widespread sexual violence.UK sanctions follow documentation of starvation, sexual violenceBritain said the action followed the publication of UK-funded research by the Center for Information Resilience, which documented what it described as systematic starvation and conflict-related sexual violence against civilians by both sides in the war.It pledged an additional £15 million in humanitarian and survivor support for Sudan.

title: Toyota Tsusho Manufacturing Ghana invests in new Hilux assembly
body: Toyota Tsusho Manufacturing Ghana has launched the ninth-generation Hilux and the new Land Cruiser FJ, with fresh investment in local assembly operations expected to support the company’s market expansion and contribute to the development of Ghana’s automotive industry. Speaking at the launch, Head of Sales Operations at Toyota Tsusho Manufacturing Ghana, Andrew Lamptey, says the company has invested in new equipment and workforce training to facilitate the assembly of the latest Hilux model in Ghana. He added that the new model required additional investment because the equipment used for the previous generation could not be used for the latest version. “We’ve been assembling the Hilux in Ghana over the past four or five years. And this is the confidence we have in the Ghanaian economy. Over the years, we’ve contributed so much to the Ghanaian industry. We’ve invested a lot in ensuring that we are able to assemble this particular new brand.” he said. Mr Lamptey says developing local component manufacturing could further expand the industry’s contribution to employment and economic growth. “For the moment, a lot of the assemblers are importing most of the components. But the idea is to be able to develop the industry to a point where we’ll be able to manufacture some of the components locally,” he said. He added that building local capacity could create jobs and support exports, noting that “the main goal is to be able to have a lot of component manufacturers.” National Sales and Marketing Manager at Toyota Tsusho Manufacturing Ghana, Jerry Mensan, says the launch also forms part of the company’s strategy to increase market share while improving mobility and creating employment opportunities. “Our core reason for bringing these products onto the market is to aid mobility in Ghana. Automobile mobility is part of our core. Of course, we are a business entity. And definitely market share is also a priority for us. Once we invest, we would want to get something out.” he said. Mr Mensan said the company’s local assembly operations were contributing to employment, with Ghanaians accounting for nearly all its workforce. He added that local assembly does not compromise the company’s quality standards. “About 99.9% of employees there within Toyota Ghana are all Ghanaians. The standards are not compromised although they are produced here from Ghana. We maintain the same standards that Toyota keeps way back in any of the assembly plants,” he said. Mr Lamptey said the new Hilux also incorporates customer feedback, while Toyota’s vehicles are designed with features suited to Ghana’s road conditions. The company says developing local component suppliers will be critical to expanding the automotive value chain beyond assembly, creating more jobs and positioning Ghana to benefit from future vehicle exports.

title: Australian judge rejects prisoner's human rights challenge to Vegemite ban
body:
FILE - A piece of toast is prepared with Vegemite in Sydney, Australia, Monday, Nov. 17, 2025. Rick Rycroft/AP hide caption
MELBOURNE, Australia — A prisoner on Monday lost his challenge to an Australian state's ban on inmates eating Vegemite after he argued in court that withholding the polarizing yeast-based spread breached his human right to "enjoy his culture as an Australian."
Andre McKechnie, 55, who is serving a life sentence for murder, took his battle for the salty, sticky, black-brown byproduct of brewing beer to the Supreme Court of the state of Victoria last year.
He had argued being refused Vegemite denied him his right under the Charter of Human Rights and Responsibilities Act to "enjoy his culture as an Australian in the community with other persons of Australian background," court documents showed.
Justice Claire Harris accepted prison authorities' refusal to allow McKechnie Vegemite "limited his cultural rights" under the charter.
But she found the ban was justified in meeting authorities' goals of removing illicit drugs and alcohol from the prison system.
"The limitation on Mr. McKechnie's ability to enjoy Vegemite in community with other persons of Australian background is primarily that he is a prisoner," Harris wrote in her 47-page judgment.
Prison officials testified at a trial in July that Vegemite had been banned throughout the state's 12 prisons for the past 20 years because it could potentially impair sniffer dogs' ability to detect narcotics and could be used to brew alcohol because of its yeast content.
McKechnie, who represented himself in court by video link from maximum security Barwon Prison west of Melbourne, argued that the fact that neighboring New South Wales state did not ban Vegemite from its prisons was evidence that there were "less restrictive means reasonably available" to achieve such drug and alcohol outcomes.
Most Australians revere Vegemite as an unfairly maligned culinary icon, and more than 80% of Australian households are estimated to have a jar in their pantries. Vegemite is typically considered an acquired taste at best by those who weren't raised on it.
The last U.S. president to visit Australia, Barack Obama, once said: "It's horrible."
McKechnie had initially testified that the lack of Vegemite had contributed to his thiamine deficiency.
He said both Vegemite and pork were sources of thiamine, also known as vitamin B1. As a Jew who observed kosher law, he told the court he couldn't eat pork either and took daily doses of the vitamin.
Vegemite has long been marketed as a source of B vitamins thiamine (B1), riboflavin (B2), niacin (B3) and folate (B9) which are promoted as healthy additions to the diets of growing children.
But McKechnie dropped the thiamine issue as "not important," after lawyers for the prison authorities objected to his evidence.
McKechnie said not eating Vegemite made him feel "deprived of being able to practice my Australian culture, sad and disconnected from my family and community."
The judge responded that "it is difficult to accept that the inability to consume Vegemite, rather than the fact of his imprisonment, is a material cause of his sadness and disconnection from his family and community."
McKechnie cited an article published in the food studies journal "Gastronomica" in 2003 that said, "Vegemite may be the best predictor of national identity of any food in the world."
The article, based on research by Australia's Queensland University in 1995, found that a "taste for the spread strongly correlates with early exposure and to Australian birth and ancestry."
McKechnie also referred to the Australian Olympic Committee overturning an Chinese import ban on Vegemite ahead of the 2008 Summer Olympics in Beijing.
He cited Australian band Men at Work's 1980s international hit "Down Under" that mentions a "Vegemite sandwich."
On the effectiveness of smearing contraband with Vegemite, McKechnie cited a Melbourne newspaper article from 2017 that reported a man's unsuccessful attempt to use the odor of the spread to conceal illicit drugs that he attempted to smuggle into a music festival in Victoria. The attempt was thwarted by police sniffer dogs.
The judge upheld prison authorities' argument that McKechnie had failed to provide any proper foundations for his opinion that Vegemite does not interfere with drug sniffer dogs.
McKechnie also argued that Vegemite contained "no live yeast" and that any piece of fruit would be more useful in making alcohol than the spread.
A state prison department manager, Kevin White, cited publicly available research that said Vegemite helped home-brewed beer ferment more quickly.
Vegemite's owner, Bega Group, did not respond to a request for comment on Monday.
