title: Digital Consumer Choice in Nigeria: Comparing online platforms, ratings and casino rankings
body:
Nigeria’s digital economy gives consumers an expanding choice of platforms for shopping, entertainment, financial services and online gaming. As competition intensifies, your challenge is to assess credibility, convenience, service quality and value before committing money or personal information. Product descriptions, customer reviews, comparison websites and promotional claims all influence decisions, yet their usefulness depends on the evidence behind them and the transparency of the organizations publishing them.
DataReportal’s Digital 2026 report estimated that Nigeria had 109 million internet users in October 2025, representing 45.5% of its population. This substantial audience highlights the scale of the country’s connected market, although access remains uneven. For you as a consumer, digital choice depends on affordability and connectivity alongside the information available to compare competing services. Overall, understanding these factors helps you make decisions that reflect your priorities and financial circumstances.
Casino comparison websites demonstrate how specialist platforms organize information about competing operators. So, the GambleGuru rankings offer a starting point for examining online casinos and sportsbooks through considerations such as licensing, payment methods, withdrawal conditions, available games, bonuses and customer support. These categories help you move beyond advertising claims and assess the practical features of different services. However, a ranking is most useful when you understand its evaluation criteria and the evidence supporting its recommendations.
For Nigerian consumers, the distinction between popularity and suitability deserves careful attention. A highly ranked operator is not automatically authorized to accept customers in your jurisdiction, nor does a favorable review guarantee a satisfactory experience. Before registering, check the relevant licensing requirements, payment availability, currency arrangements, withdrawal restrictions and promotional terms. You should also establish whether the review reflects current conditions, as operator policies and service features change over time. Independent verification gives comparison results greater practical value.
Ratings condense complicated information into scores that consumers can assess quickly. On a retail website, an average product rating summarizes customer experiences, while written reviews explain particular strengths and weaknesses. Casino comparison websites apply a similar principle, although their assessments require additional scrutiny because payment disputes, identity checks, withdrawal restrictions and account conditions can affect customers financially. A score provides an initial indication of perceived quality, yet its meaning depends on the criteria used to calculate it.
When you examine reviews, consider their number, publication dates, specificity and consistency across independent sources. An unusually enthusiastic testimonial provides limited evidence if it lacks concrete details, while repeated complaints about delayed withdrawals deserve closer investigation. Incentives and commercial relationships also complicate the interpretation of customer feedback. Consequently, you should distinguish verifiable information from promotional language and investigate unexplained differences between ratings . A credible assessment explains its methodology clearly and acknowledges limitations that could affect your decision.
Different digital services require different comparison criteria, so your assessment should reflect the purpose of each platform. Retailers can be judged through product authenticity, delivery charges, return policies and customer support. Payment services require attention to transaction fees, transfer limits, security procedures and dispute resolution. Casino platforms introduce further considerations, including licensing, game rules, wagering requirements and withdrawal conditions. Comparing relevant features gives you a clearer understanding of the actual service behind its marketing.
Mobile accessibility also matters in Nigeria’s digital economy, where connection quality and data costs influence online experiences. A platform that loads slowly, obscures payment instructions or offers limited customer assistance can create unnecessary difficulties. Before opening an account, check whether your preferred payment method is supported and whether fees are clearly disclosed. You should also assess the quality of customer service and the accessibility of essential terms. These practical details provide a stronger basis for comparison than promotional offers alone.
Gambling regulation requires particular attention because Nigerian licensing arrangements involve state-level authorities. Following a November 2024 Supreme Court decision on the constitutional allocation of gaming regulation, the legal framework shifted toward state jurisdiction. The Federal Capital Territory Lottery Regulation Office oversees gaming activities within Abuja and publishes a list of approved operators. Consumers should consult the appropriate regulator for their location and activity, as an overseas license does not automatically establish authorization to operate locally.
Transparency also matters when you assess individual transactions. Read privacy policies, eligibility rules, complaint procedures, payment conditions and restrictions attached to promotional offers before sharing information or depositing funds. For gambling services, set a firm spending limit and treat betting as paid entertainment, never as a dependable source of income. A trustworthy comparison explains its scoring methods and distinguishes verified facts from editorial opinions. These safeguards help you evaluate both an operator’s claims and the reliability of the recommendation.
Digital comparison tools work best when you combine them with independent research. Begin by identifying your priorities, then shortlist services that meet your practical requirements. Check current terms, verify the relevant regulatory position, compare recent customer experiences and investigate significant disagreements between sources. Rankings can narrow your options, yet the final decision should reflect verifiable evidence and the suitability of the service for your circumstances. This approach also helps you recognize gaps in the information presented.
Nigeria’s expanding online audience creates opportunities for businesses that compete through transparent communication and dependable service. However, greater choice also increases the value of digital literacy and informed skepticism. Whether you are selecting a retailer, comparing payment providers or reviewing casino operators, question broad claims and examine the evidence before committing money or personal information. When you balance convenience and popularity against reliability, accountability and consumer protection, you can navigate digital platforms with greater confidence and make decisions that serve your needs.

title: Macron says ‘social media is damaging our democracies’
body: President Emmanuel Macron said on Monday that social media was “damaging our democracies” as France struggled to contain weeks of protests marked by street violence and looting. He said on a visit to Marseille that social media was especially used during unrest on October 17 “to bring young and not-so-young people to places where criminal acts, attacks and looting were taking place”. He described social media as “tools for mobilising the worst impulses”. The post Macron says ‘social media is damaging our democracies’ appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Vodza Iron Breakers: You have given Keta a reason to stand tall
body: There are victories whose meaning travels far beyond the final whistle. They enter our homes, bring old friends together and give an entire community something to celebrate. Vodza Iron Breakers have given us such a victory. Their emphatic 4–1 win in the beach soccer final deserves a special tribute. To the players, technical team, management and supporters: you carried the name of Vodza with distinction and gave Keta a powerful reason to stand tall. A scoreline records the goals. It cannot fully capture the work that made them possible: the training, the corrections, the discipline and the willingness to keep pursuing a shared ambition. On the day that mattered, the Iron Breakers delivered. Four goals in a final. A trophy secured. A community made proud. For those of us who call this coast home, the achievement has a special resonance. Our beaches are part of our identity, our livelihoods and our everyday lives. To see our young people turn that familiar setting into a stage for sporting excellence is deeply moving. They have shown what can emerge when talent meets organisation, commitment and belief. Special recognition must go to Joshua Mawuli Kukuia and the entire management of Vodza Iron Breakers. Thank you for everything you have done to support this team and bring it to this proud moment. Behind a successful team are people who keep showing up long before the applause begins. Their work continues between competitions, away from the cameras and beyond the excitement of match day. It takes patience to build a team, commitment to sustain it and belief to keep others focused on what they can achieve together. Joshua Mawuli Kukuia and the management deserve our gratitude for that dedication. This victory belongs to them too. As we applaud the players who delivered on the sand, let us also honour those whose efforts helped make that performance possible. On Saturday, October 17, 2026, the team presented their trophy to me. It was a privilege to receive them and share in their joy. Looking at that cup, I thought about everyone whose contribution stood behind it: the players, the coaches, Joshua and his fellow management members, and the supporters who stayed with the team. Every one of them deserves a place in this celebration. During the visit, the team’s Chief Executive Officer invited me to serve as patron. I accepted with gratitude and a strong sense of responsibility. The team had already given us a reason to believe. Accepting that invitation means helping to sustain the work that brought them this far. And we must give these champions more than a moment of applause. Too often, a team wins, congratulations pour in and attention quickly moves elsewhere. Yet the next training session still has to happen. Players still need equipment, preparation, care and opportunities to improve. Management still has to plan for the next competition. If we value this achievement, our support must reach those everyday needs. Businesses, institutions, community leaders and individuals can help build a dependable foundation beneath the team. Consistent backing would allow the players, technical team and management to prepare with greater confidence and pursue even higher ambitions. The Iron Breakers have demonstrated the talent. We should help create the conditions in which that talent can keep growing. Their victory also speaks to the young person watching from the touchline and wondering how far their own ability might take them. Here is an achievement close enough to touch. Here are players carrying a familiar community’s name and succeeding together. That example matters. It gives ambition a local address. To the players: enjoy the honour you have earned. Then protect it through your conduct, discipline and preparation. Young people will watch how you train, how you treat one another and how you respond when the next challenge comes. To Joshua Mawuli Kukuia and the entire management: accept our heartfelt appreciation. Your contribution deserves to be remembered whenever the story of this victory is told. May this success strengthen your resolve and attract the support needed to carry the team further. To the coaches and technical team: thank you for preparing these champions. To the supporters: your loyalty is part of the club’s strength. Keep showing up. And to Vodza and Keta: let us celebrate with the fullness of our pride and the seriousness of our support. Vodza Iron Breakers, you carried our name into the final and brought a trophy home. You have added a proud chapter to our community’s story. May the children who watched you lift that cup one day tell their own stories of achievement and remember that you helped them believe it was possible. Congratulations, champions. You have honoured Vodza. You have honoured Keta. Now let us help you go further.

title: Terraform Google Cloud 8.0 发布：告别“永久 Diff”，代价是破坏性升级
body:
HashiCorp 宣布 ，Terraform Google Cloud Provider 8.0 现已正式可用。这个大版本更新了两种 Compute Engine 资源的默认负载均衡行为，移除了与已退役 Google Cloud 服务相关的资源，并将若干不考虑顺序的属性由列表改为集合，以避免持续出现计划差异。由于这是一个包含破坏性变更的版本，HashiCorp 建议用户先升级到最新的 7.x 版本，清除弃用警告后再升级至 8.0。
最明显的行为变化涉及 google_compute_backend_service 和 google_compute_global_forwarding_rule 。它们的默认 load-balancing_scheme 已由 EXTERNAL 改为 EXTERNAL_MANAGED 。这意味着，没有设置该字段的配置将使用新的外部应用负载均衡器，而非经典负载均衡器。依赖经典行为的团队必须显式设置 load_balancing_scheme = "EXTERNAL" ，否则 Terraform 计划可能会提议修改现有负载均衡器。
此次发布还移除了一些资源和数据源，因为它们所依赖的服务已经关闭或被替代。被移除的资源包括 google_iap_brand 和 google_iap_client （IAP OAuth Admin API 关闭后），三个 google_notebooks_* 资源（用户应迁移至 google_workbench_instance ）、 google_ml_engine_model ，以及 BeyondCorp 的应用连接、连接器和网关资源；这些资源由 Security Gateway 资源替代。 google_vertex_ai_schedule 则由 google_colab_schedule 替代。升级前，必须更新所有引用这些资源的配置。
在 Schema 行为方面，不具备顺序语义的属性已由列表改为集合，其中包括 Compute Service Attachments、GKE 日志和监控配置，以及 Cloud Security Compliance Frameworks 中的字段。HashiCorp 表示，这可以避免 API 返回值顺序与配置不同而产生永久性差异。部分 Google Cloud API 的验证规则也变得更加严格。例如， google_workflows_workflow 现在必须提供 source_contents ；创建 Workforce Identity Pool Provider SCIM 租户时，也必须提供 claim_mapping 。某些状态变化，例如部分整数到字符串的转换，会自动迁移，但其他变化则需要修改配置。
公告还总结了 8.0 建立其上的一些 7.x 时代功能。该 Provider 现在支持 Terraform 列表资源，这些资源可以配合 terraform query 工作流使用。用户能够搜索状态之外的现有基础设施，并选择生成资源配置和导入配置。目前覆盖 Compute Engine、IAM、BigQuery、Pub/Sub、Secret Manager、Migration Center 和 Network Services。Resource Identity 支持也有所扩展，为 Provider 提供了一种清晰表示远程对象的方式，可与传统 ID 一样用于导入。只写属性可以将敏感值发送给 API，而不将其保存下来，目前已覆盖证书私钥、AlloyDB 密码和 IAP 凭证。
该 Provider 由 Google Cloud 工程团队、HashiCorp 和 Terraform 社区共同开发，8.0 版本现已在 Terraform Registry 中提供。官方文章没有提供基准测试或采用数据，也没有列出所有被移除的资源，因此升级指南和 GitHub 变更日志才是权威参考。
固定 Provider 版本，先升级到最新的 7.x 版本。解决所有弃用警告后，再在非生产环境中升级至 8.0。
在代码中搜索上述已移除资源，以及未设置 load_balancing_scheme 的负载均衡器资源。显式设置该字段，避免意外迁移至 EXTERNAL_MANAGED 。
仔细检查 terraform plan ，重点关注被标记为销毁或替换的资源。尤其要留意列表到集合的转换，以及类型发生变化或改为必填的只写版本属性。
使用 OpenTofu 的团队可以采用该版本的大部分功能，但并非全部。该 Provider 的破坏性变更包括默认值改为 EXTERNAL_MANAGED 、资源移除以及列表到集合的转换。这些变化都发生在 Provider 中，因此无论使用哪种 CLI 都会生效。只写属性需要 OpenTofu 1.11 或更高版本，因为该版本才引入了这项功能。
使用 Terraform 查询和列出资源的发现工作流在 OpenTofu 中尚无对应功能。关于 tofu query 的功能请求（ issue #3787 ）仍处于待处理状态。因此，这些团队仍需使用 import 块和生成的配置来管理现有基础设施。
截至本文撰写时，OpenTofu 是否支持 Resource Identity 尚未得到确认，因此计划使用基于身份导入的团队应先查看 OpenTofu 变更日志。固定版本前，团队还应确认 OpenTofu Registry 中是否已经提供 8.0 Provider 构建版本。

title: What to know about China's plenum as Xi seeks stronger party discipline
body:
FILE - In this photo released on July 18, 2024, by Xinhua News Agency Chinese President Xi Jinping speaks at the third plenary session of the 20th Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee held from July 15 to 18 in Beijing. Xie Huanchi/Xinhua via AP hide caption
HONG KONG — China's political leaders and elites began a four-day meeting Monday to discuss strengthening the ruling Communist Party's discipline, as Chinese President Xi Jinping pushes for greater loyalty and reliability from officials while deepening his yearslong campaign against corruption.
This week's closed-door gathering, known as the fifth plenum of the Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party, comes roughly a year before Xi is widely expected to secure his fourth five-year term as the party's leader and personnel changes to key leadership bodies.
Xi began the meeting by delivering a work report and speaking about a draft policy decision on advancing "full and rigorous party self-governance," according to China's official Xinhua News Agency. The policy aims to make cadres more disciplined, effective and less corrupt.
While Xi has consolidated his grip on power, analysts say the plenum will offer him an opportunity to further align what Chinese officials do with what Beijing wants.
"The plenum is a chance to ensure the new generations rising the ranks share Xi's assessment of the opportunities and risks China faces," said Ruby Osman, a senior policy adviser at London's Tony Blair Institute for Global Change.
Here's what to know about one of Beijing's most significant political meetings this year.
Xi's anti-graft drive has been a defining feature of his rule since he came to power in 2012. Purges of officials — including some viewed as his political rivals — have been carried out on a scale that led critics to argue the campaign was also used to consolidate his power.
But his focus has expanded to cracking down on underperforming cadres too. In recent years, the number of officials punished for "formalism" and "bureaucratism" — misconduct such as dereliction of duty, inaction and reckless acts that seriously hinder development — has surged.
Xi's policy proposals reflect his emphasis on the party's "self-revolution," a concept centered on the party reforming itself through efforts such as rooting out corruption and building ideological commitment, analysts say.
Osman said the disciplinary crackdowns are now aimed more at institutional longevity.
"It's less about purging elite rivals and more about building a disciplined system that can sustain Xi's political priorities across leadership cycles," she said.
Record-high disciplinary campaigns also do not necessarily mean a rebound in corruption, but rather that Xi has been steadily raising the bar for the party's expectations of officials, she added.
Mingda Qiu, senior analyst of Eurasia Group's China practice, said Beijing has been building its agenda for months.
"The message is clear: the anti-corruption campaign is not winding down. Officials are not only tested for loyalty, but also for compliance and action," he said.
Xi said in a January meeting that while decisions by the party's top leadership were smoothly implemented in general, inspections and audits found problems such as failures to comply and improper execution, according to an October article in the Qiushi Journal, a publication of the central committee.
Xi warned against "two-faced people" who might profess political loyalty while privately defying orders and doing as they please.
"During leadership transitions, we must keep our eyes sharp, elevate good cadres who are truly loyal and reliable, consistent in word and deed, and willing to take responsibility, and never allow 'two-faced people' or those driven by self-interest to slip through," Xi was quoted as saying.
The number of empty seats in the conference hall this week will help observers gauge how widespread Xi's purges have been.
Neil Thomas, senior fellow at the Asia Society Policy Institute, and his colleagues Lobsang Tsering and Shengyu Wang noted that while Xi's civilian purges are record-breaking, 42 out of 44 officials affiliated with the military elected as full central committee members in 2022 have also been purged or disappeared.
The central committee started its term in 2022 with more than 370 full and alternate members. Thomas and his colleagues estimated turnout this week could be less than 80%, potentially setting a record low at any plenum since the end of former leader Mao Zedong's rule in 1976.
Attention will also be on new demands on the officials who remain.
Thomas expects tighter scrutiny of public spending and major projects, more use of technology to uncover corruption, and tougher consequences for officials who fail to deliver on Xi's priorities.
New personnel appointments are possible, though Xi may wait until a once-in-five-years Communist Party Congress next year to anoint his picks, said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London. If he does fill any openings, it will be with loyalists, he added.
The underlying theme of the fifth plenum is that it will be another opportunity for Xi to position himself for an unprecedented fourth term in office.
Xi, who removed presidential term limits in 2018, is viewed by some as the most powerful Chinese leader since Mao. He is widely expected to be confirmed as party leader for the next term in the fall of 2027.
Ahead of that, Thomas said new ideological language reinforcing Xi's authority might emerge at this week's meeting.
He said the plenum should prepare the ground for Xi's fourth term and reinforce expectations of political and policy continuity.
"After Xi has purged so many of the people that he promoted at the last congress, watch for tougher scrutiny of the officials competing to join his next leadership team," he said.

title: CIB Ghana, GhISP build financial institutions capacity to drive gender-smart
body: Chartered Institute of Bankers, Ghana (CIB Ghana), in partnership with the Ghana Investment Support Programme (GhISP), held a two-day workshop for the SME portfolio managers from banks across Ghana. This programme was designed specifically to support financial institutions in capacity-building and inclusive lending towards Small and Medium-sized Enterprise (SME) sector. Held on 15 th and 16 th October 2026 at CIB Ghana in Accra, the workshop brought together professionals from banks and selected Finance Houses to deepen their understanding of contemporary approaches to SME financing. Reflecting on the programme, one participant noted: “One of the challenges we face in financing SMEs is assessing businesses that may be viable but do not always have the financial records or structures we traditionally rely on for credit decisions. The workshop has given us practical approaches to look more closely at cash flows, the business model and other indicators of viability. We will take these insights back to our institution to strengthen how we assess SMEs and structure financing that better responds to their needs.” SMEs constitute an important component of Ghana’s economy, supporting employment, innovation and economic growth. However, challenges including weak financial records, inadequate governance, poor cash-flow management and limited investment readiness continue to constrain access to finance. Against this background, the workshop focused on strengthening financing opportunities and developing lending approaches that are both commercially sound and responsive to emerging sustainability and inclusion considerations. Participants were taken through practical areas including SME business models, inclusive product design, governance and risk assessment, climate risk and green SME financing, credit assessment, cash-flow-based lending, gender-smart finance and inclusive investment. The programme adopted an interactive approach combining expert presentations, practical case studies, experience sharing and group discussions, enabling participants to relate the concepts to real lending and portfolio-management situations within their institutions. The workshop forms part of a broader CIB Ghana – GhISP initiative aimed at improving the quality of SME lending, enhancing financial inclusion and encouraging financial institutions to integrate climate considerations into lending decisions. At the conclusion of the programme, participating institutions were encouraged to translate the lessons from the workshop into practical actions within their organisations, particularly in credit assessment, product development, portfolio management and engagement with SMEs. Commenting on the expected impact of the programme, Mr. Robert Dzato, CEO of CIB Ghana, stated that “Strengthening the capacity of financial institutions to adopt sound, inclusive and sustainable lending practices is essential to improving SMEs’ access to finance and supporting their long-term growth. CIB Ghana remains committed to equipping banking professionals with the knowledge and skills to make informed financing decisions that support SME development and Ghana’s economic growth.” The Accra workshop represents the first of two ecosystem workshops under the initiative, with the second scheduled to take place in Kumasi in November 2026. About CIB Ghana Chartered Institute of Bankers, Ghana (CIB Ghana) is the professional body for the practice of banking in Ghana, established under the Chartered Institute of Bankers, Ghana Act, 2019 (Act 991). The Institute’s mandate is to promote the study of banking and regulate the practice of the banking profession in Ghana. Through professional education, certification, capacity building and industry engagement, CIB Ghana supports the development of competent and ethical banking professionals and contributes to the advancement of the banking and financial services industry. For further information, contact CIB Ghana at info@cibgh.org . About GhISP The Ghana Investment Support Programme (GhISP) is a technical assistance initiative, powered by British International Investment (BII) and supported by SECO and Norfund. The programme aims to increase investment flows to underserved SMEs in Ghana, with a particular focus on gender, inclusion and climate investing. Through tailored pre- and post-investment support, GhISP helps SMEs get investment-ready and connect them to capital, supporting investments for Growth Investment Partners (GIP) Ghana and other relevant funds in Ghana. Learn more at ghisp.org or contact GhISP Communications Lead, Tine Frank at tine_frank@ghisp.org .

title: Oti Akenteng slams GFA for ‘disrespect’ of local coaches in national team appointments
body: Former Technical Director of the Ghana Football Association (GFA), Francis Oti Akenteng, has questioned the role of the institution in ignoring local coaches during national team appointments. Akenteng’s statement follows Kim Lars Björkegren’s appointment as the interim technical team lead for the Black Stars ahead of the doubleheader against Somalia in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifiers. The Black Stars have lost their opening two matches in the qualifiers following a 2-0 defeat to Ivory Coast in Bouaké and a humiliating 4-2 loss to Gambia at the Accra Sports Stadium. The results led to former Portuguese head coach Carlos Queiroz and the GFA mutually parting ways. Bjorkegren will be assisted by Medeama head coach Ibrahim Tanko and Godwin Attram, with Fatawu Dauda still remaining the goalkeeper coach. Akenteng admitted that Ghana has many experienced local coaches, and when given the privilege, could coach the Black Stars on an interim basis. “There are local coaches who are capable of coaching the Black Stars,” he said in an interview with Asempa FM. “If they are always overlooked, that is a sign of disrespect, and if the local coaches are not respected, they will not have an interest in coaching.” Black Stars remain at the bottom of Group C and are set to face Somalia in November, after which Bjorkegren will turn attention to the Black Queens, who fight for a spot in the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup with the play-off preliminary phase scheduled between November 24 and December 5, 2026.

title: Duchess Meghan confronted dad over child abuse claims last year
body: London — Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, confronted her estranged father last year about child sexual abuse allegations leveled against him, about six years after she was first made aware of the claims, according to new information from CBS News' British partner BBC News.Last week, police in the Philippines confirmed they were investigating Thomas Markle Sr. over his alleged possession of a large stash of child sexual abuse photos and videos, which were handed in to authorities by his son, Thomas Markle Jr.Meghan, who is married to Britain's Prince Harry, said in a statement last week that she was "deeply distressed" by word of the investigation into her father, and that she had first learned of allegations against him in 2018, when London's Metropolitan Police shared a letter with her laying out related claims. She said it was based on that information that she and Harry decided to cut her father off from contact with their children.Video that the British tabloid the Daily Mail says it obtained exclusively shows Markle accepting a letter sent by his daughter in his hospital room in the U.S. in December 2025. According to the BBC, in that letter the duchess wrote that she and authorities "knew he had abused young girls," adding that he would never meet Meghan and Harry's children Archie and Lilibet.Thomas Markle Sr., 82, was quoted by the Mail in a Sunday article as saying he didn't remember what was written in the letter from his daughter, but "if Meghan says that's what she wrote, then she's probably right."The Mail quoted her father on Friday as saying he had "never downloaded anything like that in my life," and dismissing the allegations against him as "sick lies." On Sunday, the tabloid ran a new article quoting him as saying he had paid for sex in the Philippines, but reiterating his denial of possessing child sexual abuse materials and insisting he never had sex with anyone under the age of 18.He vowed to cooperate with authorities, according to the Daily Mail.Another British tabloid, The Sun, reported over the weekend that the Metropolitan Police were made aware in 2019 of a number of claims against Markle, including alleged sexual abuse of a child, and that they had passed them on to the Duchess of Sussex's office at that time.In a statement last week, the duchess said it was because of these allegations that she had  kept her family distanced from her father."In 2018, a letter was sent to the Metropolitan Police and Royalty and Specialist Protection. That letter was subsequently shared with me. It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father and I was given assurances that these were being investigated," Meghan said in her Friday statement. "I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications' distortion over the years, any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them," she said."We are aware of media reports that officers from the Met's Royalty and Specialist Protection Command were involved in the passing on of a letter in 2018," a Metropolitan Police spokesperson said last week. "We are undertaking enquiries internally in an effort to confirm this."It is understood that the London police are not currently investigating Thomas Markle.It is unclear what allegations were in the letter about her father that Meghan says police shared with her in 2018, or what allegations she was referring to when she wrote to him last year.CBS News contributor Roya Nikkhah, royal editor for the Sunday Times newspaper, told CBS News on Monday that the revelations of the last week were very likely to garner new public sympathy for the duchess."I don't think the wider public can not have sympathy for Meghan going through this," she said. "It's an ordeal, an extraordinary thing to learn about your own father.""I think a lot of the feeling by the British public around what has happened the last few years has been more about the way Harry and Meghan left the royal family and what we have heard from them since, which is completely separate to this — their grievances against the royal family, their feelings of not feeling comfortable here," said Nikkhah. "But they are now back, and they are back, we understand, for a considerable period of time. I'm sure the British public and wider public will have sympathy for what's happened regarding her father. I don't know whether this will change people's views about what's been said and done the last six or seven years since they've left."

title: Zelensky: Hegseth’s approval for Patriot missiles has been pending for nearly a month
body:
The President said this on Facebook following a meeting on weapons supplies from Ukraine’s partners and efforts to restore the energy system after Russian strikes, Ukrinform reports.
“The Minister of Defense of Ukraine, the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, and the Minister of Foreign Affairs reported on the supply of air defense interceptors to Ukraine, first and foremost Patriot missiles. We are working on several tracks – with the United States, Europe, and other partners that have stocks of PAC-2 and PAC-3 missiles. In particular, we have been waiting for nearly a month for Mr. Hegseth to sign off on missiles for Patriots and NASAMS. I instructed our team to raise this with the American side once again. Conversations with other countries are also ongoing,” Zelensky said following the meeting.
According to Zelensky, Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi reported on the work underway in the regions.
“I thank every repair crew and all energy companies that are fully carrying out their assigned tasks. The work is continuing virtually nonstop, and we are using the equipment reserves we have built up,” the President said.
He added that preparations for the November Ramstein meeting were also discussed. According to Zelensky, it is important to speed up the implementation of decisions that have been on the table for some time.
“Every support package is an opportunity to protect people's lives. Thank you to everyone who is providing real support and, in particular, helping speed up these critically important deliveries,” the President said.
As reported earlier, in an interview with TSN Tyzhden, Volodymyr Zelensky said there had been progress on the issue of providing Ukraine with missiles for Patriot systems, but the process was moving very slowly.

title: Likud braces for turnout battle, divided over Netanyahu's chances on eve of Election Day - analysis
body: Likud insiders are divided over the party's chances on Monday, one day before Israelis go to the polls. Some members are confident of victory, while others worry about efforts to turn out voters in the camp opposed to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, according to a Likud source.Those who are confident rely on the optimistic forecasts of Shlomo Filber, who runs Likud's internal polls.“We have some who are very sure of themselves, and some who are less so,” the Likud source said. Regarding Filber, he added: “Either Momo comes out a king, or Momo goes home. It's one or the other.”'The nonprofits affair on steroids'One of the Likud's concerns is the activity of organizations and nonprofits that, according to party sources, are pouring large sums of money into boosting turnout in the rival camp. Sources said a wide-ranging effort, not directly funded by the parties, ran throughout the campaign. It included social media campaigns, signs, field events, rides for Arab voters, and efforts to get Israelis abroad to fly in and vote.A Likud source called this “the nonprofits affair on steroids,” claiming the organizations give parties opposed to Netanyahu an extensive support network outside party-financing rules.The party also criticized the Central Elections Committee, which, it claimed, focused on enforcing limits on campaign videos and the use of public resources while paying too little attention to the organizations' activity. However, the sources did not provide documentation for the funding amounts they cited or for the claim that the activity broke the law.Likud is preparing for an extensive field operation on Election DayAt the same time, Likud is preparing a large-scale ground operation for Election Day, despite restrictions on getting information from polling stations, and is focused on keeping right-wing votes from going to smaller parties. Efforts to persuade Brig.-Gen. (res.) Ofer Winter, a former Givati Brigade commander and head of the People of Israel party, to drop out of the race failed, even after talks involving Rabbi Eli Sadan, who later issued a statement backing Winter.Likud is also courting supporters of other right-wing slates, including the joint ticket of Yoaz Hendel and Yaron Zelekha. Meanwhile, Rabbi Abergel's Ahi party has already dropped out of the race after talks with Likud, during which they also raised the possibility of legislation allowing the party to name a deputy minister.Israelis head to the polls on Tuesday, after the election date was set for October 27, allowing Netanyahu's government to complete its full term. A survey published days before the vote found that nearly one-third of Israeli voters were still undecided.

title: Drone attack on Pavlohrad: one person killed, three others wounded, incl two 10-year-old girls
body:
One civilian has been killed and three others wounded following a drone attack on Pavlohrad (Dnipropetrovsk region), reported Serhiy Lysak, head of the Regional Military Administration.

"One person has died, and at least three others have been wounded. The enemy struck Pavlohrad with a drone. All the wounded are currently in the hospital. Among them are two 10-year-old girls," he wrote on his Telegram channel.

According to the Regional Military Administration, the strike caused a vehicle to catch fire and damaged several multi-story residential buildings and a shop.

title: Kazakhstan Marks Republic Day as World Leaders Send Congratulations
body: Kazakhstan marked Republic Day on October 25 with a flag-raising ceremony in Astana and congratulations from its international partners. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio used the occasion to describe bilateral relations as the “strongest” in their history. “Our countries are working together to strengthen regional security, expand economic cooperation, and create new commercial opportunities which will pair Kazakh ambition with American innovation to benefit both of our nations,” Rubio said in his October 24 statement . He praised Kazakhstan’s diplomatic role and support for President Donald Trump’s “peace initiatives,” and said the U.S. looks forward to further cooperation in the year ahead, both bilaterally and through the C5+1 framework, which brings together the United States and the five Central Asian countries. Trump sent a separate message to President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. According to Akorda’s account , he welcomed the enhanced strategic partnership and said he wanted to continue developing his relationship with the Kazakh leader. Russian President Vladimir Putin also congratulated Tokayev, describing bilateral relations as developing “in the spirit of strategic partnership and alliance.” He pledged to strengthen cooperation and linked closer ties to security and stability across Eurasia. Chinese President Xi Jinping expressed his readiness to deepen cooperation, while praising Kazakhstan’s development. The presidents of the other four Central Asian countries also sent congratulations. King Charles III of Great Britain conveyed his wishes to Tokayev and the Kazakh people, highlighting the friendship between the two countries. French President Emmanuel Macron pointed to growing cooperation ahead of the 35th anniversary of diplomatic relations. UN Secretary-General António Guterres was also among those who sent messages. Image: Akorda.kz In Kazakhstan, Tokayev attended the national flag-raising ceremony outside the Akorda presidential residence. The honor guard commander reported to the president before the flag was raised and the national anthem played. The presidency announced similar ceremonies across the country’s regions. In Almaty, more than 1,500 people gathered near the Medeu mountain skating rink for a flag-raising ceremony . A military brass band played the national anthem as the flag rose on a 40-meter pole. The city also marked Republic Day with a festive concert at the Republic Palace. Image: Almaty Akimat Republic Day commemorates the Declaration of State Sovereignty , adopted by the Supreme Soviet of the Kazakh SSR on October 25, 1990. The declaration affirmed territorial integrity and established the political and legal foundations for the country’s future independence. Kazakhstan remained within the Soviet Union at that point. It formally declared independence on December 16, 1991, becoming the last Soviet republic to do so. This year’s Republic Day therefore marks 36 years since the sovereignty declaration, ahead of the 35th anniversary of independence in December. The holiday itself has undergone several changes. Republic Day was removed from the public holiday calendar in 2009. Tokayev proposed restoring it at the first National Kurultai in June 2022, and legislation later that year reinstated October 25 as a national holiday. December 16 remains Independence Day, commemorating the separate decision that formally established Kazakhstan as an independent state.

title: Drones keep sinking ships off Romania and Bulgaria—French and US patrol planes are watching
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); French and US maritime patrol planes are watching the western Black Sea, where drones keep hitting merchant ships, Romanian outlet Curs de Guvernare reported on 19 October, citing flight-tracking data. Romania blames Russia for the attacks, while Bulgaria says it cannot prove who launched them. Ukraine’s three small Danube ports have kept its grain exports from collapsing further, and Russia has pounded those ports since the summer. The ships serving them are now being hit in the economic zones of two NATO members. Many were anchored near or heading to the Sulina Canal, which links the Danube to the sea. That puts the allied patrols over these waters in the middle of the fight over Ukraine’s grain trade. Map: Euromaidan Press Two patrol planes over the western Black Sea A French Navy Atlantique 2 maritime patrol plane arrived in Constanța, Romania’s main Black Sea port, on the evening of 18 October, Curs de Guvernare said. On 24 October, French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said in the Bulgarian port of Varna that a French patrol plane had been operating in the area under NATO for two weeks and had contributed to rescue operations. Explore further Two tankers burn off Romania’s Sulina as Bulgaria says it lacks proof Russia is behind the Black Sea ship attacks Meanwhile, a US Navy P-8A Poseidon flew into Varna from Sicily on 18 October, AFP reported , citing flight-tracking data. Two days later, Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said it had begun reconnaissance patrols after Sofia asked allies for help, and that some allies had responded quickly. Bulgarian Defense Minister Dimitar Stoyanov called the deployment a joint decision of Bulgaria and NATO. He said the plane cannot strike targets and passes its data to NATO, Anadolu Agency reported . NATO promises more On 20 October, NATO’s North Atlantic Council met at Romania’s request . Afterward, the alliance said it would send more maritime patrol aircraft, radar systems, and drones to the Black Sea. NATO military spokesman Col. Martin O’Donnell added that allies have sent or will send intelligence personnel and explosives-forensics teams. NATO itself has not attributed the attacks to any country. Romania names Russia, Bulgaria hedges Romania has been blunter. On 15 October, after four merchant ships were hit within a day, acting Foreign Minister Oana Țoiu wrote on X that “ Russia bears full responsibility for these developments .” On 17 October, Romanian F-16s shot down two jet-powered Russian Geran drones near Sulina, Romania’s Defense Ministry said . Unitățile aeriene și navale ale Gărzii de Coastă (GdC/MAI) și ale Inspectoratului General pentru Situații de Urgență (IGSU/MAI) sunt implicate activ în operațiunile de căutare și salvare, în vederea găsirii membrilor dați dispăruți ai echipajului navei care a fost atacată în… — Toiu Oana (@oana_toiu) October 15, 2026 On 23 October, a drone sank the cargo ship Khoryv off Constanța, killing a Ukrainian sailor, and President Nicușor Dan blamed Russia too. “ It is part of Russia’s escalation process in its war in Ukraine ,” Dan said . Bulgaria is more cautious. Radev told parliament on 14 October that the attacks worked in Russia’s favor but that Sofia could not prove it. Since taking office in May, he has sought a thaw in ties with Moscow.
