title: ‘No party will get even 25% of Kaduna votes; everyone wants Tinubu’ – Uba Sani
body:
Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu will secure overwhelming support in the state in the 2027 presidential election, declaring that no opposition candidate will get even 25 per cent of the votes.
Mr Sani attributed his optimism to what he described as the Tinubu administration’s unprecedented interventions in Kaduna, particularly in infrastructure, education, agriculture, security and human capital development.
The governor spoke during an interview with TVC on Sunday, a day after the All Progressives Congress (APC) formally launched Mr Tinubu’s re-election campaign at Ranchers Bees Stadium in Kaduna.
“In Kaduna, we are not talking about 70 per cent. Allowing any candidate to even get 25 per cent in Kaduna is a failure on our side because President Tinubu has done for Kaduna something we never dreamt of having,” Mr Sani said.
He urged voters in the North to support the president based on his performance rather than ethnic or regional considerations, arguing that the federal government’s interventions demonstrated its commitment to the development of Kaduna and other northern states.
“No leader in the history of Nigeria has supported subnational governments as you have done, Mr President,” he told Mr Tinubu at Saturday’s rally.
Mr Sani cited several federal projects and interventions as reasons residents should support the president’s re-election bid.
He commended Mr Tinubu for handing over Ahmadu Bello Stadium to the Kaduna State Government, saying his administration would reconstruct the facility to meet FIFA standards, with a seating capacity of 33,000.
He also highlighted the reconstruction of the 123-kilometre Kaduna–Birnin Gwari Road, which he said had been abandoned for more than four decades. According to the governor, ₦178 billion had been released for the project.
On rail transportation, Mr Sani said the federal government had approved $865 million for the proposed Kaduna metropolitan light rail project. He added that the contractor, China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation, had received $300 million in mobilisation funds.
The governor also mentioned the ongoing reconstruction of the Zaria–Soba-Kambuwa Road and the expansion of federal tertiary education institutions in the state.
He said Kaduna now has four federal universities, including the Federal University of Education, Zaria, and the Federal University of Applied Sciences, Kachia. He also cited the proposed Shehu Musa Yar’Adua University of Petroleum Studies in Kaduna and the conversion of Kaduna Polytechnic into a federal university of technology.
Mr Sani argued that the projects and other federal interventions justified his expectation that Kaduna residents would overwhelmingly support Mr Tinubu in 2027.
Beyond defending the president’s record, Mr Sani challenged opposition parties to intensify their grassroots campaigns rather than concentrate on criticising the APC and its activities on social media.
“If you are campaigning to win elections, you have to go out and meet with the people,” he said.
The governor said he had observed the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) responding to the ruling party’s activities without presenting what he considered convincing campaign strategies or engaging sufficiently with ordinary Nigerians.
He singled out the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), saying he had seen the party organising town hall meetings and reaching out to voters.
“You can’t run a campaign by reacting to what another party is doing. Go and do your own campaign,” he advised opposition parties.
Mr Sani also accused opposition politicians of using artificial intelligence and manipulated images to discredit the APC, rather than taking their messages directly to voters.
He expressed confidence that the ruling party’s grassroots mobilisation would give it an advantage in the 2027 elections, adding that whether opposition parties formed alliances was not the APC’s concern.
Meanwhile, ADC, whose presidential candidate is former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, criticised Saturday’s APC campaign launch, calling it disappointing rather than evidence of widespread public support for Mr Tinubu.
In a statement, Kola Ologbondiyan, director of media and publicity for the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, alleged that the APC mobilised supporters from across the seven North-western states and beyond, with payments reportedly ranging from ₦50,000 to ₦100,000 per person.
Mr Ologbondiyan also claimed that the stadium remained sparsely occupied, with empty seats visible despite the alleged mobilisation.
The ADC’s claims and the governor’s assertions about the APC’s popularity reflect the competing narratives emerging as political parties position themselves ahead of the 2027 general election.
While the APC presented the rally as evidence of its mobilisation strength, the ADC questioned whether the gathering represented genuine voter support.
Mr Sani’s projection that no opposition candidate would secure even 25 per cent of Kaduna’s votes contrasts sharply with the outcome of the 2023 presidential election.
Mr Tinubu, then the APC candidate, finished second in the state with 399,293 votes, representing approximately 29.36 per cent of valid votes.
Mr Atiku, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) candidate at the time, won Kaduna with 554,360 votes, or about 40.76 per cent. Labour Party candidate Peter Obi came third with 294,494 votes, representing approximately 21.65 per cent.
The results showed that the three leading candidates commanded substantial support across the state. Mr Atiku won 14 local government areas, while the Labour Party won seven and the APC won two, according to reported results.
Kaduna’s political landscape is shaped by differences across its northern, central, and southern areas, along with competing party loyalties, local political networks, security concerns, and economic interests.
Although the 2023 results provide a benchmark for assessing the APC’s 2027 ambitions, they do not determine the next election’s outcome.
Voter preferences, political alliances and perceptions of government performance can change between electoral cycles.
The 2027 contest will ultimately depend on how voters assess the federal and state governments’ records, including their responses to insecurity, economic hardship, infrastructure deficits, education, and other public concerns.
Mr Sani has set an ambitious target for the APC in Kaduna. Voters at the ballot box will determine whether the party can achieve the level of support he predicts.

title: ARCON Honours Osaren Emokpae with Award
body: The Advertising Regulatory Council of Nigeria (ARCON) has honoured Chairman of Mindshare Communications Limited, Professor Osaren Philips Emokpae, with the Frontrunner Award for his pioneering contributions to Nigeria’s advertising industry, particularly in media independent practice. The award was presented at the maiden edition of the ceremony in Lagos, which brought together captains of the advertising industry, government representatives and other distinguished guests. Organised by ARCON, the event is expected to become an annual affair, providing a platform to celebrate individuals whose contributions have helped shape the growth and direction of advertising practice in Nigeria. With more than three decades of experience spanning marketing communications, strategic planning, media management, education and entrepreneurship, Professor Emokpae has played a part in shaping the development of Nigeria’s advertising industry. His contribution to media independent practice stands out, particularly his role in establishing the Media Independent Practitioners Association of Nigeria (MIPAN). A scholar, strategist, educator and entrepreneur, Professor Emokpae began his career at Unilever, where he rose to the position of Senior Brand Manager for Household Cleaning Products. He later joined Insight Communications as an Account Director before moving to Troyka Holdings as its pioneer Group Executive Director, Strategic Planning. During his 13 years at Troyka, he also served as Chief Executive Officer of All Seasons Mediacom Limited, which became Nigeria’s first full-service media independent company. The company helped change the way media planning and buying were approached in the country’s advertising market. His involvement in media independent practice grew out of a concern about the need for advertisers to measure and justify their advertising expenditure more scientifically. Working with other leading practitioners, including former classmates and colleagues from Lever Brothers, Professor Emokpae championed the formation of MIPAN and gave the association its name. Senator Akin Odunsi was invited to serve as its pioneer chairman, while Professor Emokpae became its founding president. He later served as a trustee and patron of the association. He and Dr Thorpe started a research programme to provide the necessary data for scientific Media Planning. His work in this area helped advance the case for specialised media planning and buying, as well as media inventory management as a distinct professional practice within Nigeria’s advertising industry. Professor Emokpae is the founder and Chairman of Mindshare Communications Limited, an advertising and communications agency in Nigeria. Beyond his corporate responsibilities, he has contributed to the development of the profession through teaching, research, public lectures and mentorship. His career extends well beyond advertising. Through the Havilah Open Door Group, he has built businesses across education, consulting, advertising, security, logistics, courier services, export, trading and events, creating employment opportunities for thousands of people across Nigeria. He has also chaired the boards of LAPO Microfinance Bank and LAPO NGO for 21 years, alongside other board appointments. Across business and ministry, he has mentored young leaders in Nigeria, the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, Europe and the Caribbean, reflecting a commitment to leadership development that extends beyond the organisations he has led. The Forerunner Award celebrates Professor Emokpae’s record of vision, pioneering effort and service, with particular emphasis on his contribution to the growth of Nigeria’s advertising industry and the advancement of media independent practice. For Mindshare Communications, the award marks a proud moment for the agency and its Chairman, whose career has bridged industry practice, scholarship, entrepreneurship, service and Ministry. The launch of the annual ARCON event also creates an opportunity to celebrate the contributions of other practitioners whose work continues to influence the profession.

title: LemFi launches ‘Ambition has no passport,’ its biggest product expansion yet
body: Editor’s note: This press release is sponsored by LemFi and was handled by BrandRap, the sales and marketing arm of Rappler. No member of the news and editorial team participated in the publishing of this piece. LemFi, the financial platform for people building lives across borders, announced the launch of its new global brand platform, “Ambition has no passport”, alongside a completely rebuilt app, launching the largest product expansion in its history. More than two million customers use LemFi to move money to more than 30 countries, with over $2 billion in monthly transaction volume, and the company plans to add more countries next year. The expanded platform now includes savings and credit in the UK, eSIMs in more than 100 destinations, alongside LemFi’s existing international payments service. People who move countries arrive with a career, a qualification and a savings record, only to find that almost none of it counts. A credit history rarely survives a border crossing. Around 304 million people now live outside the country where they were born, sending some $905 billion home each year. However, many financial services remain designed around individual products or customers living their financial lives in a single country. LemFi is building its platform around that gap, extending from the international transfers on which the company was founded into a wider range of financial services designed for people whose lives span borders. “We started LemFi because sending money home was broken. What we learned is that the harder problem starts after the transfer,” said Ridwan Olalere, co-founder and CEO of LemFi. “Our customers are building careers and businesses in one country while supporting people in another, and the financial system treats them as if they can only exist in one place at a time. That is the wrong answer for people this ambitious, so we have rebuilt LemFi to work the way their lives do. Ambition travels. The infrastructure behind it should travel too.” LemFi co-founder and CEO Ridwan Olalere and co-founder and CFO Rian Cochran Inside LemFi’s expanded platform Transfers, still at the heart of it. Send money to more than 30 countries across Africa, Asia, Europe and beyond, from the same account that now saves, borrows and connects. Savings that stay within reach in the UK. The LemFi Instant Access Savings Account currently pays a boosted 5% AER for the first six months from account opening; it then reverts to 3.04% AER (tracker), tracking the Bank of England base rate. Accounts open from £1, with no penalty for withdrawals. Deposits are held by ClearBank and protected by the Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS) up to £120,000 per eligible depositor. A credit history that travels in the UK . A revolving credit line, available subject to availability, is issued by Lemfi Credit through Pillar, the FCA-regulated credit provider LemFi acquired in 2025. It is available as a virtual card through Apple Pay and Google Pay and can be used for both spending and sending. Eligible customers can also see their Equifax credit score in the app for free. eSIM in more than 100 destinations, in every market . Buy mobile data before arriving, with no SIM swap and no roaming bill. A brand and an app rebuilt together The app has been re-architected from the ground up to hold several products across several countries in a single account, rather than bolting them onto a transfer app. The redesign also brings LemFi’s products to the forefront of the experience, making them easier to discover and creating an architecture that lets the company add new services as it expands. The company has also introduced its new global brand platform, “Ambition has no passport”, reflecting its focus on customers building careers, businesses, families and financial lives across borders. The new identity spans LemFi’s product interface, website, marketing and social channels and will roll out across its global markets. “LemFi started as a way to send money home. Our customers turned it into a way to build a life across borders,” said Isabel Ron-Pedrique, vice president of design and brand at LemFi. “They are not defined by the country they left. They are defined by what they are building. Ambition has no passport is not a line we placed on top of the product. It is the idea the whole system is built from, from the app you open in the morning to the poster you walk past on the way to work. We have built this brand to keep up with them.” Savings and credit are available in the UK at launch, with other markets to follow. – Rappler.com

title: Ukraine Seeks Earlier Russia Talks and EU Role
body:
Ukraine and the United States are seeking to bring planned negotiations with Russia forward by at least a week, while Kyiv is pushing for European involvement, according to a report published Monday, Oct. 26.
Ukrainska Pravda reported the initiative, citing sources close to Ukraine’s negotiating team and President Volodymyr Zelensky’s administration.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The outlet placed the tentative start of the Abu Dhabi talks at around Nov. 10, after the US congressional midterm elections. Moscow had not confirmed an earlier date as of the evening of Oct. 25.
A source in Zelensky’s team linked the urgency to approaching winter and the time needed for successive negotiating rounds.
“When you have no electricity, water or heating, every day matters,” the source said.
Kyiv does not expect an immediate breakthrough. Sources suggested that possible delegation changes could make the first meeting introductory, with substantive negotiations and potential decisions coming in later rounds.
According to the underlying report , Russia opposes European representatives joining the first meeting at the negotiating table.
Ukraine nevertheless plans to bring European officials to Abu Dhabi and brief them as discussions unfold, a source close to the negotiating group said.
The source identified a further obstacle: Europe lacks a single representative authorized to make decisions. Björn Seibert, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen’s chief of cabinet, has represented the EU at recent meetings, the report noted.
Kyiv also wants negotiations to address Ukraine’s long-term protection and Europe’s postwar security arrangements, rather than remain focused on Moscow’s territorial demands. The proposal concerns the direction of future discussions; it does not establish agreement on a settlement or European participation.
The reported push for earlier negotiations follows Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov’s statement that Russia would be ready to resume talks after Nov. 4 , its National Unity Day holiday.
Speaking Sunday, Oct. 25, Ushakov described the prospective meeting as preliminary and exploratory, playing down expectations of an immediate agreement. He did not announce a definitive date.
His remarks followed renewed shuttle diplomacy involving US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. Talks with Ukrainian and European representatives in Oslo on Oct. 20 preceded a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg on Oct. 21.
Earlier reporting identified Abu Dhabi or Switzerland as possible venues for working-level negotiations. The contacts have reopened discussion of a trilateral format, while differences over territory and security guarantees remain unresolved.
Zelensky has separately ruled out neutrality and restrictions on Ukraine’s armed forces as conditions of a peace agreement.
In an interview broadcast Sunday, Oct. 25, he said Ukraine should be able to maintain an army of 800,000 personnel if sufficient funding is available. He described the force’s size as an internal Ukrainian matter and said the central questions were financing and effective security guarantees.
Zelensky said Ukraine expects guarantees from the United States and Europe that would prevent another Russian attack. He also argued that territorial questions require decisions by leaders, while technical groups can work on other elements of a settlement.
An energy ceasefire, he said, could demonstrate that Moscow is genuinely prepared to move toward peace. He cautioned that Russia’s stated willingness to negotiate must be judged by practical results.
Ukraine remains prepared to participate in technical-level talks, Zelensky said, but such a meeting alone would not deliver a complete resolution of the war. Kyiv wants the renewed process to produce concrete outcomes.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Molbog leader raises fears, concerns over Balabac EDCA site
body: MANILA, Philippines – A Molbog indigenous leader raised fears and concerns over disruptions to their ancestral land and daily lives caused by the construction of military facilities on Balabac Island in southern Palawan . Balabac Island faces the West Philippine Sea and sits between the Sulu Sea and the South China Sea (connected by the Balabac Strait). It is designated as one of the four additional sites under the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA). As Balabac is becoming what defense experts say is one of the most consequential military hotspots, indigenous people are protesting the developments on the land they claim as ancestral domain. Among the constructions on the island is a three-kilometer runway. “ ‘Yung libingan ng aming ninuno, tinambakan (The graveyard where we bury our ancestors, they filled with soil),” Emmanuel San Esteban, president of indigenous-led group Bangsa Molbog, said during a briefing in Quezon City on Monday, October 26. “ At ‘yung bundok na pinagri-ritwalan noon ay wala na po. Tinibag na rin. ” (And the mountain where we hold our rituals before is gone. It was cleared.) The Molbog leader also said he experienced physical harm and intimidation from unknown men. Last May, US, Australian, and Philippine Army soldiers conducted a live-fire assault on the island as part of the Balikatan exercises. San Esteban said their people were taken aback by the military drills conducted earlier this year. “ Hindi namin po alam na magpapaputok pala sila doon sa sinasabing EDCA, ” said San Esteban. “[‘Yung] mga tao, nagtakbuhan, lalo na po [ang] mga kabataan.” (We didn’t know they would open fire in the EDCA site. The people fled, especially the young ones.) He was accompanied by Anjilon Flores, also of the Molbog people, who expressed concerns about livelihood and the government’s National Greening Program (NGP). Flores, who spoke in the Molbog language translated by San Esteban, said the state’s program restricted them from farming and their access to food. Some lands where they used to farm are now covered by the reforestation program. The Molbog people have been applying for their certificate of ancestral domain — an area spanning 26,000 hectares in Catagupan village on Balabac Island. Balabac, composed predominantly of Molbog people, has a population of 42,662 . Catagupan, San Esteban’s village and the site of the runway, has a population of a little over 2,000 people. Earlier in October, human rights group Karapatan denounced alleged military and police harassment of journalists and researchers in Balabac. Karapatan said “the incident has brought even more fear to the local Molbog community, which has been suffering intimidation and the destruction of the environment in their ancestral lands due to the construction of the EDCA site.” Rappler has reached out to the Armed Forces of the Philippines Western Command for comment, but it has yet to respond as of posting. – Rappler.com

title: Energy security is Slovakia’s priority at meeting in Moscow — minister
body:
BRATISLAVA, October 26. /TASS/. Energy security is Slovakia's priority at the meeting of the Russian-Slovak intergovernmental commission on economic, scientific, and technical cooperation currently taking place in Moscow, Juraj Blanar, the Minister of Foreign and European Affairs of Slovakia and co-chairman of the intergovernmental commission, wrote on his Facebook (banned in Russia, owned by Meta recognized as extremist in Russia) page.
"The priority with which we arrive in Moscow is, for us, the energy security of Slovakia," he said. It is "vital to maintain a pragmatic and constructive dialogue with Russia," Blanar added.
"Even in the current tense situation, we reject the raising of any new 'Iron Curtain' with Russia and consider it essential to maintain dialogue," the minister stressed.
The intergovernmental commission on economic, scientific, and technical cooperation serves as one of the tools for Slovakia for maintaining dialogue with Russia. At the same time, the republic fulfills its obligations regarding the anti-Russian sanctions adopted by the European Union, the minister said.
"However, as an EU member state, we have not lost our sovereignty, and therefore we will discuss topics with Russia that are important to us," Blanar wrote. Experts from both sides will hold negotiations in the areas of energy, nuclear energy, agriculture, environment, tourism, sports, and culture," he added.

title: New Rural Service Centre to advance climate-resilient cocoa farming in Ahafo Region
body: …Proforest facility in Asumura will extend practical services for farmers and strengthen sustainable land-use governance Proforest has commissioned a new Rural Service Centre in Asumura, Asunafo North Municipality in the Ahafo Region, to expand support for cocoa farmers seeking to improve productivity, strengthen climate resilience and protect forests. Established under the Building Deforestation-free Climate Resilient Cocoa Landscape programme with funding support from the Walmart Foundation, the Centre will provide technical training, farm-management services and a local platform for community leadership and social and environmental governance. The Asumura facility builds on Proforest’s first Rural Service Centre, commissioned at Dadiesoaba in the Asutifi South District in 2024. That Centre now provides technical training and farm-management services for farmers and surrounding communities. Hon. Joseph Akparibo, Municipal Chief Executive of Asunafo North, said: “This project being carried out within the framework of the Ghana Cocoa Forest REDD+ Programme (GCFRP), is closely aligned with the Government’s Agriculture for Economic Transformation Agenda and its flagship Feed Ghana Programme. Feed Ghana seeks to raise productivity, strengthen food security, create jobs, supply raw materials to industry and connect farmers to markets.” Abraham Baffoe, Executive Director, Global and Africa, Proforest, said: “Through our collective efforts, we are demonstrating that sustainable production, environmental stewardship, and community development can go hand in hand. Let us continue to demonstrate that together, we can build a prosperous, climate-resilient, and deforestation-free landscape for current and future generations.” Walmart Foundation, the funder of this project emphasised the importance of collaboration. “We are very proud to support this work and look forward to seeing how farmers use it to help grow more sustainable cocoa and how the community uses it to help advance local governance of the landscape initiative”, said Simon Hall, Director of Strategic Initiatives at Walmart Foundation. The Asumura Rural Service Centre marks an important step in strengthening climate-resilient and deforestation-free cocoa production in the Ahafo Region. By bringing technical training, farm-management support and community-led governance closer to farmers, the facility will help improve livelihoods and productivity while promoting responsible land use and forest protection. title: Defense Ministry, EC discuss mechanisms for monitoring Ukraine Support Loan funds
body:
Organization of control and procurement accountability for funds under the Ukraine Support Loan program, which foresees nearly €60 billion for Ukraine's defense needs (including the procurement of weaponry, drones, missiles, and the development of the defense-industrial complex), was discussed at meetings between representatives of the Ukrainian defense department and a joint mission of the European Commission's Directorate-General for Defence Industry and Space (DG DEFIS) and the European External Action Service (EEAS).
"Nearly €60 billion from the Ukraine Support Loan is designated for Ukraine's defense needs in 2026-2027. To ensure the transparent and controlled use of these funds, the Ministry of Defense conducted a series of meetings with a joint mission of the European Commission's Directorate-General for Defence Industry and Space (DG DEFIS) and the European External Action Service (EEAS)," the Ministry of Defense of Ukraine said in a Telegram message on Monday.
The Ukrainian side presented the defense sector's needs for 2027. Among the priorities are support for the production of FPV drones, middle- and deep-strike capabilities. The parties also discussed joint ventures, the Drone Deal initiative, and the further integration of the Ukrainian defense industry into the EU defense-industrial ecosystem.
"Special attention was paid to the control and accountability of defense procurement: transitioning to competitive procedures, electronic bidding, audits, and risk-oriented verification of counterparties," the Defense Ministry noted in the statement.

title: INS Trishul arrives in Italy, conducts joint exercise with Italian Navy warship
body:
New Delhi, Oct 26. Indian Navy warship INS Trishul arrived at Civitavecchia, Italy, on October 25 as part of its ongoing operational deployment to the Mediterranean Sea, reinforcing maritime cooperation between the Indian and Italian navies.

Before entering the harbour, INS Trishul conducted a Passage Exercise (PASSEX) with Italian Navy ship Carlo Margottini. The exercise involved coordinated manoeuvring drills, communication procedures, replenishment approaches, cross-deck landings, personnel transfers and boarding operations.
The exercise enabled the two navies to exchange operational best practices and improve coordination and interoperability. Such engagements provide opportunities for naval personnel to familiarise themselves with each other’s procedures and strengthen their ability to operate together during maritime deployments.

According to a statement issued by the Ministry of Defence, during its stay in Italy, INS Trishul is scheduled to participate in professional interactions, cultural visits and exchanges with Italian counterparts. The ship will also be opened to visitors, offering them an opportunity to gain insights into the Indian Navy’s maritime traditions and operational capabilities.
The port call reflects the longstanding maritime partnership between India and Italy and the shared commitment of their navies to strengthening professional ties and expanding operational cooperation.

The engagement also highlights the role of naval visits and joint exercises in building mutual trust, enhancing maritime cooperation and fostering closer ties between partner countries across strategically important maritime regions.

title: Astranis Upgrades Falcon 9 Launch Contract to Dedicated Mission for Entire Block 4 Production Run of Satellites
body:
SAN FRANCISCO —October 26, 2026—Today, Astranis announced it has upgraded its 4th launch to a dedicated mission aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket set to launch in 2028, allowing it to carry all of the “Block 4” production run of Astranis MicroGEO satellites.
The mission will carry six MicroGEO satellites, placed directly into GEO via direct-inject using an Impulse Helios upper stage. These new satellites expand Astranis’ capacity to serve commercial and government customers around the world. The launch will bring Astranis’ total fleet size to 16, adding to the 10 satellites built across Blocks 1, 2, and 3. Astranis has already signed a number of initial customers for Block 4, to be announced at a later date. This is an amendment to an initial contract Astranis signed with SpaceX in late 2024 that gives Astranis the full payload capacity on the mission.
Securing launches for multi-satellite blocks is a core benefit of Astranis’ responsive business model and provides the capacity needed to support the increased demand for dedicated space infrastructure.
Governments and enterprises around the world are increasingly seeking dedicated space infrastructure for communications and other missions such as space domain awareness that they can fully control, rather than relying on shared capacity. Higher orbits like GEO are uniquely suited for this requirement.
“We’ve only just begun to ramp up production to meet the demand we are seeing for commercial and national security missions,” said John Gedmark, CEO and co-founder of Astranis. “This launch means we can accelerate the critical infrastructure we’re building for customers in GEO and other higher orbits.”
This contract marks another step in Astranis’ continued expansion of high-orbit infrastructure and follows the recent introduction of Perceptor , which extends the company’s reach beyond communications into space domain awareness and maneuverability for commercial and national security missions. Astranis first proved that high-performance GEO satellites could be built faster and at scale. The company is now developing broader high-orbit platforms to connect, safeguard, and sustain critical infrastructure in GEO.
About Astranis Astranis builds advanced satellites for high orbits, expanding humanity’s reach into the solar system. Today Astranis satellites provide dedicated, secure networks to highly-sophisticated customers across the globe — large enterprises, sovereign governments, and the US military.
With multiple satellites now on orbit serving customers around the world, the company is servicing a backlog of more than $1 billion of commercial contracts. Astranis is the preferred satellite communications partner for buyers with stringent requirements for uptime, data security, network visibility, and customization.
Astranis has raised over $1.2 billion from some of the world’s best investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, BlackRock, Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, and Snowpoint, and employs a team of 500 engineers and entrepreneurs. Astranis designs, builds, and operates its satellites out of its 153,000 sq. ft. headquarters in Northern California, USA.

title: Women Groups Demand End to Child Marriage in Nigeria
body: Segun James Women’s Rights Organisations under Renewed Women’s Voice and Leadership Nigeria (RWVL-N) have demanded an end to child marriage and protection of the girl-child rights. They also want the assurance that every girl has the opportunity to complete her education, make informed decisions about her future and reach her full potential. The organisations, in a statement by Communications Specialist, Emmanuel Olonade, said they demanded an end to child marriage and greater investment in girls’ rights in the country. As part of activities commemorating the International Month of the Girl Child, the organisations called on parents, government institutions, traditional and religious leaders, educators and community stakeholders to take urgent and collective action against child marriage and other harmful practices that threaten the safety, dignity and future of girls. Under the theme: “End Child Marriage; Invest in Girls’ Rights,” the organisations engaged girls and young people across different communities through school-based activities, interactive discussions, debates, drama presentations and online conversations. These activities created platforms for girls to speak about the challenges they face, understand their rights and demand meaningful action to protect their futures. In Abuja, the Association of Women in Social Work and Humanitarian Activities Network (ASWHAN) joined students and teachers of Spiritan International Girls Secondary School, Lugbe, to commemorate the month. Students, teachers and ASWHAN staff emphasised the responsibility of parents and guardians to support girls’ education, nurture their aspirations and provide opportunities for them to contribute meaningfully to society. In Bauchi State, the Fahimta Women and Youth Development Initiative (FAWOYDI) engaged schoolgirls from Alkaleri, Bauchi and Ganjuwa Local Government Areas at Government Girls College, Bauchi. Through drama and a debate on “Early Girl Child Marriage: Should It Be Abolished?” the students highlighted the harmful consequences of early marriage and called on parents, government and community leaders to protect girls’ rights and ensure they remain in school. Speaking during the engagement, FAWOYDI Executive Director, Amina Suleiman, stressed that child marriage deprives girls of their childhood, disrupts their education and exposes them to responsibilities they may not be physically or emotionally prepared to handle. She called for stronger child-protection mechanisms, safe learning environments, mentorship opportunities, vocational training and life-skills development. She also urged parents, teachers, traditional rulers and religious leaders to work together to prevent child marriage and ensure that girls participate in decisions affecting their lives. Similarly, the Gender and Development Action (GADA) engaged students at Government Girls’ Secondary School, Big Qua, Calabar, Cross River State, through an interactive teen-talk session. The discussion provided girls with an opportunity to ask questions and share concerns about abuse, gender inequality, teenage pregnancy and support for survivors. Participants were encouraged to understand their rights, speak out against violations, challenge harmful stereotypes and remain in school. The Young Urban Women Movement Nigeria (YUWMN) also convened an online conversation on child marriage, bringing together 45 participants to examine the social, economic and cultural factors that contribute to the practice. The conversation featured developmental journalist and gender advocate Lois Tofunmi; youth advocate and project manager Khadijat Tijjani; women’s rights advocate and YUWMN Southwest Zonal Coordinator Rehanat Amusu; and gender-based violence expert Niri Goyit. Participants identified poverty, gender inequality, cultural pressure, insecurity and limited access to education as factors that increase girls’ vulnerability to child marriage. They called for stronger enforcement of existing laws, gender desks in police stations, community-based monitoring mechanisms and safe spaces for girls. They also emphasised the need to work with traditional and religious leaders to challenge harmful social norms and strengthen prevention and response mechanisms for girls at risk. Across these engagements, a common message emerged: girls must not be forced into marriage at the expense of their childhood, education, safety and aspirations. Their voices must be heard, their rights respected and their choices protected.Child marriage is a violation of children’s rights with far-reaching consequences for education, health, personal development and social and economic participation. Addressing it requires sustained action from families, communities, institutions and government, alongside stronger systems for preventing abuse and supporting survivors. The women’s rights organisations therefore, call on the federal and state governments to strengthen the implementation of child-protection laws, improve access to quality and inclusive education, provide safe spaces for girls and ensure that protection services are accessible to children at risk. They also urged parents and guardians to prioritise their daughters’ education and wellbeing, while encouraging community and religious leaders to challenge practices that place girls’ futures at risk. The organisations further called on schools, civil society groups, the media and development partners to sustain public awareness, expand mentorship and life-skills opportunities, and create platforms where girls can participate meaningfully in decisions affecting their lives.

title: 'I'll kill you' — Finnish schools increasingly report threatening behaviour to police
body:
Teachers say threats of violence and rude talk have become more common in recent years.
Last year, police received close to 7,000 crime reports from schools, universities and research institutions, according to the National Police Board.
But the numbers do not reveal much about where exactly these incidents are happening, since they lump together daycares, comprehensive schools, upper secondary schools, universities and other research institutions.
Regional differences are also large, which may be partly explained by the varying number of educational institutions in different areas.
The most common suspected offense in these cases was assault.
In Rovaniemi, principal Petri Mäkelä said even younger pupils are threatening each other with serious violence.
"Lines like 'I'll kill you' and 'I'll shoot you' are already familiar among first-graders. The language has become harsher, but kids that age obviously don't understand what they're saying. It's a way of expressing emotional strain," Mäkelä told Yle.
Nationwide, school staff get their share of threats too. According to the teacher union OAJ, teachers are reporting such incidents more than ever before.
A recent education sector survey found that 14 percent of respondents had been the target of violence or threats of violence at work over the past year.
"This year we've had around 200 people contact us about this. Five years ago, we got only a few dozen of these kinds of crime-related contacts a year," explained Ulla Walli , OAJ's director of legal affairs.
Teachers have been threatened with murder or assault, for example. The threat can come from a pupil, a former pupil or a guardian.
Over the past two years, violence or the threat of it has increased most in primary education.
Cases in which a teacher is the victim often involve a pupil hitting, kicking or scratching an adult. According to OAJ, typical situations in which a teacher is suspected of a crime involve maintaining classroom order.

title: Houthi attacks ground nearly 90% of Riyadh flights, forcing cancellations, paralyzing nation
body: Attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis have nearly emptied the skies over Riyadh this month, aviation data showed on Monday, with cancellations grounding almost nine out of every 10 scheduled flights at the Saudi capital's airport.About 86% of scheduled flights at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, or 4,071 out of 4,736, were canceled between October 8 and October 25, according to the latest data from aviation analytics firm Cirium.The Houthis have stepped up attacks on Saudi Arabia this month, targeting airports, ports and oil facilities with ballistic missiles and drones. Riyadh's airport, the kingdom's second-busiest after Jeddah, has been struck repeatedly, including an attack on October 10 that killed 13 people, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade.Saudi authorities partially reopened the airport on Sunday after a halt that had started on October 10. Domestic flights resumed from Terminal 1, while national carriers were allowed to operate international services from Terminal 2.However, the Houthis said they had attacked Riyadh's airport again on Monday, calling it a "military target." The attacks have prompted international airlines to suspend services to the Saudi capital into November, while Delta Air Lines has postponed the launch of its Riyadh route until next year.Riyadh events canceled, other airports face disruptionThe disruption has forced several events in Riyadh to be canceled or postponed, including Saudi Arabia's marquee investment conference, as flight cancellations hamper travel to and across the kingdom.The upheaval also spread beyond the Saudi capital. More than 7,800 flights, or 45% of all scheduled departures from Saudi airports, were canceled between October 8 and October 25, according to Cirium. The peak came on October 12, when cancellations exceeded 60% of scheduled flights nationwide.Several major airports recorded severe disruption, including Riyadh at 86%, Dammam at 42% and Abha at 46.7%, where the Houthis have claimed strikes. A number of smaller regional airports saw the vast majority of flights canceled, including Najran, near the Yemeni border, where all flights were canceled.Cancellations across Saudi airports in October https://reut.rs/3UKliak

title: Ukraine changes tactics for using Patriot systems, Ihnat says
body:
Yurii Ihnat, head of the Communications Department of the Air Force Command, made this statement on the RBC-Ukraine podcast, according to Ukrinform.
Ihnat explained that during the full-scale war , the Ukrainian military has changed its approach to using the American systems. In particular, they have learned to use the Patriot in various tactical situations and to use the expensive interceptor missiles more efficiently.
One example is the ability to deploy the system not only from fixed positions but also for ambushes followed by a change of location.
“For example, you can use the Patriot not as a stationary system—the way the Americans keep it at airfields or bases—but make it, so to speak, ‘mobile’: set up an ambush, shoot down five aircraft, and return unscathed,” explained the Air Force spokesperson.
Another difference concerns ammunition consumption. According to Ihnat, Ukrainian crews have learned to use one missile against a single target, whereas in the Middle East, in some cases, up to eight interceptors could be launched simultaneously.
He explained that the Patriot has three operating modes: automatic, semi-automatic, and manual. In automatic mode, the system can launch a significant number of interceptors, and in the absence of relevant combat experience, the entire salvo of missiles could be fired from the launcher at a single target.
“Due to a lack of such experience, they could have fired the entire salvo of interceptors from a single launcher at a single Shahed or a single ballistic missile,” Ihnat noted.
According to his estimate, the number of missiles used in the Middle East would have been enough for Ukraine to operate these systems for several years.
“That is why we now find ourselves in the crisis we are in—because what was spent in the Middle East would have been enough for us to operate the Patriot systems for several more years,” Ihnat concluded.
As reported by Ukrinform, Volodymyr Zelensky stated that progress is being made on the issue of providing Ukraine with missiles for the Patriot systems, but the process is moving very slowly.

title: Europe must keep open channels of communication with energy producers — senior Slovak MP
body:
MOSCOW, October 26. /TASS/. Europe needs to keep open channels of communication with major energy producers, Slovak Parliament Deputy Speaker Tibor Gaspar said in an interview with TASS.
"Slovakia’s interests lie in ensuring sufficient energy supplies, maintaining the competitiveness of its industry, and protecting households from excessive price increases. Therefore, when making decisions in the energy sector, it is important to consider not only political goals but also real economic consequences for the population, as well as technical capabilities of individual states. In the long term, it is in the interest of both Slovakia and Europe to maintain open channels of communication with major energy producers and to seek solutions that help strengthen energy security, price stability, and the predictability of supplies," he said when asked whether Europe still needs Russian energy resources.
The current situation in energy markets demonstrates that energy security, the availability of raw materials, and price stability remain critical issues for all leading global economies, Gaspar noted. "According to reports from October 2026, US President Donald Trump reached an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin to ease restrictions, allowing for the supply of Russian diesel fuel to the American and global markets. Subsequently, American administration granted the necessary authorization for conducting such operations. The agreement drew criticism from a number of European officials pointing to its potential implications for the effectiveness of the sanctions policy," he stated.
"This situation indicates that certain states may prioritize different instruments and interests when addressing energy and economic issues. For countries with high energy consumption, it is essential to ensure stable supplies at economically acceptable prices, whereas the sanctions policy also pursues broader foreign policy goals and security objectives. For the Slovak Republic, this issue is of particular significance, given its geographical location, energy infrastructure, and long-standing historical relationships with energy suppliers," the politician emphasized.

title: AY Comedian promises ticket refunds after payment dispute disrupts Cardiff concert
body:
Nigerian comedian Ayo “AY Comedian” Makun has apologised to furious fans who turned up for his Cardiff concert in Wales but waited for hours without seeing him perform.
The incident occurred on Sunday at Valegate Retail Park in Cardiff, where AY was scheduled to perform as part of his “AY Live: Single and Not Searching” UK tour.
Angry attendees took to social media to condemn the experience, saying they wasted hours waiting for a performance that never materialised.
Some fans said music played at the venue while they received repeated assurances that AY was around. However, the wait continued, confusion mounted, and heated arguments broke out, leaving some attendees to return home without seeing the comedian they paid to watch.
The incident sparked criticism from fans who sacrificed their time and paid for tickets. AY addressed the backlash on Monday in a video posted on his Instagram page , apologised to disappointed attendees, and explained what happened.
He said: “To everyone who bought tickets, travelled and waited, I am sincerely sorry you did not get the show you paid for. You fulfilled your commitment, and you deserve better. My team and I travelled to Cardiff and arrived before 5pm, ready to perform. Their standing balance for our appearance was due at the end of September. It remained unpaid.
“Before travelling, we raised this, and we were assured that payment would be settled before we left our accommodation for the venue. This mattered because, a few days ago at the store in Leicester, we performed after similar assurances, but our balance remained unpaid. As I speak, they haven’t paid. Afterwards, we also struggled to reach the organisers, even to arrange accommodation for us.”
AY said he and the other comedians made it to Cardiff and entered the venue, but the organisers’ failure to resolve the financial dispute promptly cost them their chance to perform.
He said that after the issues were resolved, most of the audience had left for home.
He acknowledged that the audience had every right to be frustrated, noting that nobody should expect people to wait endlessly without telling them what is going on.
The comedian demanded that the organisers explain themselves and take responsibility, asking them to tell the audience why he and the other performers never made it on stage.
“We were outside for like 3 a.m. before my card was charged for everyone of us to get a room. We made it clear we couldn’t repeat that experience. Even so, we travelled to Cardiff in good faith. Unfortunately, efforts to resolve the payment for this particular show continued into the night. Around 10 p.m., a gentleman introduced himself as a sponsor.
“His name is Enoch Adekoya, Koya Group. Following that intervention and further commitment, the comedians and I proceeded to the venue. We entered the hall and found that people had left. We met a few people who were recording us. I also recorded the empty large venue myself. But by then, most of the people had left”, said the comedian.
AY said he had dedicated over 20 years to building his brand and would not jeopardise that effort by letting his supporters down in Cardiff.
He maintained that he wouldn’t leave his family and responsibilities in Nigeria, travel for hours with his team and then show up without giving his best.
He said he respected the people who supported him too much to disappoint them, insisting that he brought the same energy to Cardiff as he did to Belfast and Sheffield.
“It’s not every time that they’ll say, ‘ It’s the artist. Let’s look at it logically. I understand my name and face were on the flyer, so people would naturally look to me for answers. But an event also depends on promoters and organisers fulfilling their responsibilities to the audience and to the performers. Apororo, Monika, and I, along with the rest of the crew, are working professionals with families and obligations.
“The agreed payments matter. This whole thing might even affect my relationships with people in other cities. If you don’t know the truth, please don’t let this experience define the entire tour or our longstanding partnership. For over 15 years, I’ve been coming to the UK to do shows. My show in Birmingham is October 30th. London is October 31st. And Manchester is November 1st.”
AY apologised to fans who bore the consequences of what he admitted was a failure to organise the event properly and communicate effectively.
He acknowledged that the attendees had every reason to be angry and should never have been subjected to such an experience. He promised that their ticket money would be refunded.
He said, “For Cardiff, please, everybody with your tickets. And we need to call on the organisers and my management team for a practical resolution, including how refunds will be made. So we need to contact wherever these tickets were sold. Anywhere you got your tickets from. I think you people know how to do it now.
“You can request your bank or card provider, whether it’s a payment dispute that you people call it, or a chargeback for any transaction concerning this show. Please get your money back. You shouldn’t have to wait for a possible return show or seek resolution. Before we seek any form of resolution.”
AY said he would gladly return to Cardiff under the right conditions, provided he worked with a reliable local partner who could help deliver the memorable evening fans expected.
He added that he took fans’ trust seriously and would not agree to another performance without proper arrangements and a clear agreement with the right partner.
“My team and I would also review what happened tonight and the appropriate formal steps available to us, even if it means going to report to the police officially, because I didn’t come here illegally. I came here to work with a work permit. I respect your disappointment. I value your support. And I sincerely apologise for how the evening ended.”
He said fans deserved better than the poor organisation and lack of timely information. They paid to enjoy the show, not to get caught up in a payment dispute that had nothing to do with them.
As of press time, the organisers had not yet publicly addressed the incident.

title: Army rescues two kidnap victims
body:
Troops of Operation Whirl Stroke have rescued two kidnap victims after confronting suspected kidnappers along the Naka–Ahume Road in Benue State , the military has said.
The troops encountered the armed suspects during a fighting patrol on Saturday, 24 October, while the assailants were allegedly attempting to abduct motorists and other road users.
In a statement issued on Sunday, Ahmad Zubairu, the acting media information officer of the task force, said the troops engaged the suspects in a gunfight, forcing them to abandon their captives and flee.
He said the troops pursued the fleeing suspects but did not make further contact with them.
One of the rescued victims, Mngunengen Ihom, 36, from Ahume, sustained machete wounds during the incident and was taken to Naka General Hospital for treatment. The military did not disclose the identity of the second victim.
The Force Commander of Operation Whirl Stroke, Moses Gara, urged troops to sustain intelligence-led operations and improve intelligence gathering to prevent attacks.
He also urged residents to provide credible and timely information to security agencies.
The rescue comes amid recurring security concerns in Benue, including attacks and kidnappings along roads and in rural communities.
On 13 October, gunmen abducted Catholic priest John Inalegwu Otache and other people along the Ugbokolo–Ajegbe-Awume Road in Benue. In a statement on 19 October, the police said eight victims had been rescued and two suspects arrested, but did not confirm whether the priest was among those rescued.
The latest incident underscores continuing concerns about the safety of travellers on roads in the state, where armed groups have targeted motorists and other residents.

title: Serbia’s Vucic Loses Vote, Predicts Sanctions on Russia
body:
Serbia’s former president Aleksandar Vucic conceded his coalition’s defeat to a student-backed opposition movement on Sunday, Oct. 25, and predicted that the incoming authorities would impose sanctions on Russia within months.
Speaking at his Serbian Progressive Party’s headquarters in Belgrade, Vucic said preliminary estimates showed the Student List winning 135-140 seats in the 250-member parliament, compared with around 105 for his United Serbia coalition.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“It is clear that we have lost these elections,” he said, acknowledging that final results were not yet available. A parliamentary majority requires 126 seats.
The defeat marks a major setback for one of Moscow’s closest political partners in Europe. Under Vucic, Serbia maintained ties with Russia and refused to join Western sanctions over its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, while continuing to pursue EU membership.
Vucic accused his opponents of implementing an agenda devised abroad and alleged that unnamed European countries and an “American deep state” opposed to President Donald Trump had supported their victory.
“By March or April, you will have sanctions imposed on the Russian Federation,” he said , according to RFE/RL. However, his prediction conflicts with the Student List’s stated pre-election position.
In a foreign-policy platform published in September, the movement said Serbia would continue opposing sanctions against Russia. N1 reported that the statement cited Serbia’s own experience and history with sanctions, indicating that such restrictive measures do not help resolve political and security disputes.
The election outcome therefore does not establish that Belgrade will change its sanctions policy. Vucic’s remarks were a forecast about his opponents’ intentions, rather than an announcement by the projected winners.
The opposition movement emerged from protests following the November 2024 collapse of a railway station canopy in Novi Sad, which killed 16 people.
Demonstrators demanded accountability over suspected corruption and construction failures. The protests developed into a nationwide challenge to Vucic’s political dominance, with students organizing a parliamentary slate drawn from outside the established governing parties.
Supporters celebrated in Belgrade, Novi Sad, and other cities after Vucic conceded. The movement’s leading candidate, cardiologist Ilija Srdanović, said its next task would be building a state governed by the rule of law.
Vucic had resigned as president on Sept. 27 to contest the parliamentary election, hoping to return as prime minister. He previously held that position before becoming president in 2017.
His resignation left parliamentary speaker Ana Brnabić serving as acting president pending a separate presidential election. Sunday’s vote concerned control of parliament and the formation of the next government.
Serbia’s relationship with Russia extends beyond sanctions. Belgrade has relied on Russian energy supplies and Moscow’s diplomatic support over Kosovo, whose independence Serbia does not recognize.
At the same time, Serbia has supported Ukraine’s territorial integrity , received Ukrainian refugees, and provided humanitarian and financial assistance. President Volodymyr Zelensky visited Belgrade in August for talks on bilateral cooperation and European integration.
Serbia had provided roughly €60 million ($69 million) in nonmilitary assistance to Ukraine since Russia launched its full-scale invasion, according to earlier reporting.
The EU remains central to Serbia’s economic interests, accounting for nearly 60% of its foreign trade. But maintaining Russian ties while seeking deeper European integration has complicated Belgrade’s foreign policy. The next government will inherit that balancing act alongside the student movement’s central domestic promises to tackle corruption and restore public institutions.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: ‘Enough for Years’: Ihnat Says Patriot Missiles Used in Middle East Could Have Protected Ukraine
body:
Ukraine could have had enough Patriot air defense missiles to sustain its systems for several years if a significant portion of the interceptors had not been expended in the Middle East , Yuriy Ihnat, head of the Communications Department of the Ukrainian Air Force Command, said.
Speaking on the RBC-Ukraine podcast Tse Baza (“This Is the Basics”), Ihnat said Ukrainian forces had adapted their tactics for using the US-made Patriot systems throughout Russia’s full-scale war, learning to employ them in different combat scenarios while conserving expensive interceptor missiles.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Ukraine’s approach differs significantly from that of other countries, Ihnat said. Ukrainian crews can deploy Patriot systems for ambushes rather than keeping them at fixed positions, such as airfields or military bases, and then relocate after engaging targets.
“For instance, rather than using the Patriot as a stationary asset – the way the Americans typically deploy it at airfields or bases – it can be used, in a sense, as a ‘roving’ system: set up an ambush, shoot down five aircraft, and then withdraw safely,” he said.
Ihnat also pointed to an incident in Russia’s Bryansk region as an example of the capabilities Ukrainian forces have demonstrated with the system.
Another key difference, he said, is ammunition use. Ukrainian crews have learned to use a single interceptor against a single target, while air defense forces in the Middle East have reportedly fired as many as eight missiles at one target.
The Patriot system has three operating modes: automatic, semi-automatic and manual. Ihnat said that in automatic mode, the system can launch multiple interceptors at once.
Without sufficient combat experience, crews could end up firing an entire salvo from one launcher at a single target, including a relatively inexpensive Shahed drone.
“Because of this lack of experience, they might have fired an entire salvo of interceptors from a launcher at a single Shahed drone or a single ballistic missile,” Ihnat said.
He estimated that the number of interceptors expended in the Middle East could have kept Ukraine’s Patriot systems operational in combat for several more years.
“That is why we now find ourselves in the current crisis; the ammunition expended in the Middle East would have been enough to keep our Patriot systems operational in combat for several more years,” Ihnat said.
Notably, in March, a senior Ukrainian Air Force officer speaking to The Times criticized Gulf forces for using excessive numbers of expensive interceptor missiles against relatively cheap Iranian Shahed drones, saying Ukrainian crews typically use one or two missiles even against more complex targets.
Ukrainian officers said their battlefield experience has not been fully incorporated despite sharing operational data with allies.
They also described the March 1 incident in which Kuwaiti air defenses shot down three US F-15E fighter jets as “clear negligence,” arguing that better coordination could have prevented the friendly-fire incident.
During the first four days of the Iran war, the US and its allies reportedly fired more than 800 Patriot missiles – more than Ukraine received over three years of Russia’s full-scale invasion.
Ukraine has received just 24 Patriot air defense missiles from the US over the past 90 days, despite needing around 350 interceptors per month to defend against Russian ballistic missile attacks, President Volodymyr Zelensky said in an interview with ABC News.
Zelensky contrasted the limited deliveries to Ukraine with the roughly 2,000 partner-supplied interceptors fired during the first 84 hours of fighting in the Middle East.
Ukrainian officials have warned that the allocation of US-made Patriot PAC-2 and PAC-3 missiles to the region is affecting supplies available to defend Ukrainian cities and energy infrastructure.
On Oct. 16, Zelensky asked European leaders to provide 300 Patriot interceptors for the winter, warning that deliveries of just two to four missiles every few months were insufficient to counter Russian attacks.
He proposed that European countries with existing Patriot stocks help bridge the gap until new procurement arrangements and defense projects become operational.
However, efforts to secure missiles from European stockpiles have faced resistance. Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis said Athens would not transfer PAC-2 missiles if doing so compromised Greece’s own defense capabilities in the Eastern Mediterranean.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Netanyahu’s legacy on the line as Israelis head to elections this week
body:
When Hamas-led militants attacked Israel on Oct. 7, 2023, it looked like Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ’s days in office were numbered.
With the country overwhelmed by grief and anger after the deadliest security breakdown in its history, his resignation seemed like a matter of time.
But the divisive veteran Israeli leader has scratched, scraped and literally battled his way back during a stormy three-year period of nonstop domestic crises and wars across the region. Confounding his critics, he now finds himself in a tight race for reelection on Tuesday.
Netanyahu has been the country’s most dominant politician for nearly two decades, and his legacy is on the line. A poor showing could end the 77-year-old’s lengthy career on a bitter note and open the door to a new era in Israeli politics. A victory would cement his image as the ultimate political survivor.
Former Prime Minister Ehud Olmert, a onetime ally turned rival of Netanyahu, said there has never been so much at stake — from national security to the future of Israel’s democratic institutions and its standing in the world. After a series of wars that have destabilized the region and jolted the global economy, the world is watching closely.
Politicians often say the current election is the most fateful in their country’s history, Olmert said, but “this time it really is.”
Netanyahu’s opponents, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, see Tuesday as a day of reckoning. They say Netanyahu should be held accountable for Oct. 7 and the failure to turn battlefield victories into diplomatic achievements.
“What he is offering is an eternal war,” Eisenkot, whose son and two nephews were killed in combat, said in a radio interview. “Choosing a leader whose only goal is not to surrender means choosing a leader who will not deliver victories.”
Netanyahu’s supporters say he was betrayed by Israel’s defense establishment and that he has led the country through a remarkable turnaround with devastating strikes against Hamas, Lebanon’s Hezbollah and Iran.
The Israeli leader has also turned to his traditional use of scare tactics. His campaign slogan, “Right or Palestine,” which rhymes in Hebrew, suggests his opponents would establish a Palestinian state alongside Israel, something his main rivals vehemently reject.
A two-state solution, still seen internationally as the only realistic way to solve the conflict, is politically toxic in Israel — another legacy of Netanyahu’s long rule.
Nearly every poster, stump speech or televised debate seems to reference the Oct. 7 attack, which has scarred the country and remains fresh in the minds of voters.
Some 1,200 people were killed that day and 251 others taken hostage, the last of whom were returned in a ceasefire deal last year.
Israel responded with a military offensive that has killed over 74,000 Palestinians in Gaza, according to local health authorities, left the territory in ruins and triggered open-ended wars in Lebanon and Iran. Netanyahu faces an international arrest warrant, experts have accused Israel of genocide, and Israel’s image has further deteriorated with a spike in settler violence in the occupied West Bank.
Most Israelis across the political spectrum reject the war crimes and genocide allegations. But Netanyahu’s opponents, including many former hostages, refer to his outgoing coalition as the “failure government” and have pledged to launch an official investigation into how Oct. 7 was allowed to happen.
Netanyahu has refused such an inquiry and calls his ongoing — and inconclusive — military campaigns a “war of redemption.”
Boosted by an endorsement from President Donald Trump, Netanyahu has also tried to turn attention to Iran, threatening to resume the war, and vowing to destroy its nuclear program and topple its government.
“Donald, we have a job to finish. You said it and we’ll finish it together,” he said in a conversation with Trump released by his campaign.
Netanyahu’s rule has left Israelis bitterly divided over other issues, especially a longstanding system granting ultra-Orthodox men exemptions from military service.
In a country where enlistment is mandatory for most Jewish men and women, these exemptions have always angered the broader public. But resentment has grown as hundreds of young soldiers have been killed in battle and tens of thousands have been pulled away from families and careers for reserve duty.
Netanyahu, who has close ties with politically powerful ultra-Orthodox parties, has resisted attempts to end the exemptions.
He has also outraged many Israelis with his attempts to overhaul the legal system.
Before the war, Netanyahu, who is on trial for corruption charges, launched a controversial plan to weaken the courts. That prompted mass anti-government demonstrations by crowds who accused him of undermining the country’s system of checks and balances to escape prosecution.
Each side has accused the other of weakening Israel on the eve of the Oct. 7 attacks. The plan has been mostly frozen since then, but Netanyahu’s allies want to revive it.
Israelis vote for political parties, not individual candidates. Since no political party has ever captured a 61-seat majority on its own, political leaders must form coalitions.
Netanyahu has been a master at forming coalitions with religious and nationalist partners, but opinion polls suggest a tight race between his bloc and the one led by Eisenkot.
With non-aligned Arab parties campaigning hard, there is a strong possibility that neither of the main Jewish blocs will capture a majority. That could set the stage for weeks or even months of negotiations among around a dozen parties expected to win seats.
Netanyahu’s allies and members of Eisenkot’s bloc both say they will not govern with Arab partners.
Amid so much uncertainty, a number of scenarios are possible — including a unity government between Eisenkot and Netanyahu, or an Eisenkot-led government backed by Arab partners from outside the coalition.
Eisenkot says he will not serve in a Netanyahu government. But politicians have broken promises before. The alternative would be to hold new elections early next year — leaving Netanyahu in office until then.
Largely missing from the Israeli public discourse is any discussion of the dire situation in Gaza or Israel’s open-ended military rule over millions of Palestinians.
The Oct. 7 attack, which came after decades of conflict and four previous wars with Hamas, convinced many Israelis there was no partner for peace, while Netanyahu and his allies have largely succeeded in branding the Israeli left as weak or even traitorous.
Palestinians have little hope their lives will improve regardless of whether Netanyahu wins or loses.
Olmert, who led the last serious negotiations with the Palestinians before a corruption scandal forced him from office and Netanyahu replaced him in 2009, said the candidates aren’t discussing the two-state solution because it is not popular with voters.
But given the international outrage over the situation in Gaza and settler attacks, he said it will be impossible for the next government to ignore the issue for long.
“Sooner or later, a new government will have to deal with it,” he said.

title: Man Utd crisis deepens as Carrick faces axe
body: Winless in eight games and hovering just above the Premier League relegation zone, struggling Manchester United are facing the prospect of yet another managerial change, with Michael Carrick likely to pay the price. The former United midfielder was warmly applauded by fans as he made his way down the tunnel after his team’s chastening 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday. Moments later a chorus of boos erupted as the players left the pitch — with fans clear in their minds where the blame lies for United’s current malaise. Carrick was handed a two-year deal in May after inspiring an impressive revival following the team’s struggles under Ruben Amorim — United secured third place in the Premier League and a return to the Champions League. But a drastic decline this season is an all-too-familiar story for United supporters, who last witnessed a Premier League title triumph 13 years ago under Alex Ferguson. An emotional Carrick denied his lap of the pitch at full-time on Sunday was a goodbye as he struggles to come to terms with his team’s precipitous decline. “I definitely knew that we hadn’t cracked it and there was a lot of work to be done, but that doesn’t mean to say that it should have gone this way,” he said. Carrick, 45, is clinging on but his position appears increasingly precarious, with former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann apparently in the frame for the job. The United boss, who won multiple titles in the club’s golden era under Ferguson, was the seventh permanent appointment since the Scot retired. David Moyes was proven in the Premier League, Louis van Gaal and Jose Mourinho had stellar records and Erik ten Hag and Amorim were seen as rising stars of coaching. – Sentimental choice – Carrick is in the same category as Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, who was in charge for three years from 2018 — a sentimental choice as a former player who played a major role in the club’s glory years under Ferguson. “The Manchester United fans are singing the Michael Carrick song because I think they know what’s going to happen here. They’ve seen this before. He’s one of their own and he’s popular,” former United captain Gary Neville told Sky Sports. “But the owners, the sporting department and the players are not popular and they’ve badly let this football club down.” The problems at the club, as Neville points out, go far beyond the dugout. Despite fierce, ongoing protests from fans, the US-based Glazer family still hold a majority stake in the club Malcolm Glazer bought via a leveraged takeover in 2005, saddling United with huge debts. Any hopes that the arrival of British billionaire Jim Ratcliffe as a minority owner in 2024 would signal a new dawn have been dashed. Ratcliffe has overseen cost-cutting measures including widespread redundancies and ticket hikes but the club’s debt has still soared above £1.1 billion ($1.47 billion). United, who for years bullied their rivals in the transfer market, lost out on the biggest names as they targeted a summer midfield rebuild, with Elliot Anderson, Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes all choosing other clubs. United instead recruited Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos — none of whom have made a strong impression — for combined fees of about £150 million. Significant rifts have emerged in recent weeks. Lisandro Martinez criticised director of football Jason Wilcox for not doing more to strengthen Carrick’s squad. Last week captain Bruno Fernandes publicly questioned Carrick’s tactics in a 4-1 humbling by Champions League debutants Como. Carrick is expected to take the blame, but the route back to the top for one of the world’s biggest clubs appears tougher than ever. “It can’t just be the manager again. There has got to be consequences above that. You can’t keep letting the people pick the manager who keep getting it wrong,” said Neville. “It’s years now without a Premier League title. That will be another five or 10 before you know it because there are other clubs set up for success and Manchester United aren’t.” The post Man Utd crisis deepens as Carrick faces axe appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Sweden selects four Saildrone USVs to monitor Baltic Sea
body:
Sweden has selected Saildrone to operate four unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) for a 360-day mission to monitor its territorial waters and exclusive economic zone in the Baltic Sea.
This deployment marks the first national deployment of Saildrone USVs under the Nordic Defence Cooperation (NORDEFCO) framework that enables participating Nordic nations to rapidly procure Saildrone maritime domain awareness services. Additional national deployments under the framework will follow, according to Saildrone.
NORDEFCO is a cooperative organization that unites Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden, and other Northern European countries to streamline defense cooperation and field proven regional security solutions.
The Saildrone Voyager fleet will continuously patrol Sweden’s territorial waters in the Baltic Sea to deliver real-time maritime intelligence directly to the Swedish Armed Forces. Operating as a managed service, Saildrone maintains, deploys, and tasks the USVs to enable Sweden to maintain persistent maritime domain awareness without deploying additional crewed ships.
"This is fundamentally not about four unmanned vessels, but about access to sustained intelligence collection at sea. In other words, we are purchasing a persistent maritime surveillance service, and Saildrone provides the vessels that supply the Navy with data,” said Johan Wahren , project manager at Sweden's Defence Materiel Administration (FMV).
“This mission reflects Sweden’s commitment to securing the Baltic Sea and highlights Saildrone’s growing operational presence across Northern Europe,” said Robert Kleist , Saildrone’s European managing director.
“Sweden is investing in year-round maritime awareness as an operational capability. The NORDEFCO framework gives Nordic nations a common mechanism for accessing that capability while allowing each country to define and operate its own mission.”
Saildrone delivers persistent maritime domain awareness for navies and law enforcement. The company has supported defense and security missions in places ranging from the Baltic Sea and the High North to the Southern Ocean and the Middle East.
The company recently registered four Saildrone Voyager USVs in Denmark to operate under the Danish national flag. The registration establishes a clear flag-state framework for Saildrone USVs operating internationally and supports the company operating alongside various European nations. Saildrone Europe will flag additional Saildrone USVs in the coming weeks.
