title: Door-to-Door Movement Donates Buses to 14 State Coordinators
body: The PBAT Door-to-Door Movement founded by High Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, has presented buses to its coordinators in 14 states to strengthen grassroots mobilisation and rally support for President Bola Tinubu ahead of the 2027 presidential election. The National Coordinator of the movement, Sunday Asuku, who handed over the buses yesterday in Abuja, said the vehicles would enable the coordinators to reach local government areas, wards, polling units, and households to mobilise votes for Tinubu’s re-election. Asuku explained that the latest presentation was intended to strengthen the operations of state coordinators, noting that vehicles previously distributed were primarily meant for local government coordinators. “Like I just mentioned, we have visited 14 states so far. The vehicles we gave them in those states are mainly meant for the local government coordinators to enable them to coordinate the affairs of their respective local governments. “But this is going directly to the office of the state coordinators. This is going to assist them to manage the affairs of the entire state,” he said. He charged the beneficiaries to intensify grassroots engagement and establish an effective feedback mechanism through which information from the field would be communicated to the movement’s national secretariat. “We are expecting them to give us feedback, go from local government to local government, ward to ward, unit to unit, and from door to door. All reports and feedback will be sent back to the national secretariat,” Asuku said. The national coordinator expressed confidence in the state coordinators, describing them as trusted members of the movement who had worked with its leadership for a considerable period. He said the movement had established mechanisms to monitor its activities and ensure that the resources provided to the coordinators were properly managed. “They know how best to take care of what has been kept in their custody. We have everything about them. They are not aliens to us. They are not strangers to us. We’ve been working as a team. So, I think there’s no cause for alarm,” he said. Asuku attributed the provision of the vehicles to the movement’s founder and grand patron, Tompolo, whom he commended for supporting the group’s mobilisation efforts. He said Tompolo believes Tinubu deserved another term to consolidate the achievements of his administration, adding that the vehicles would ease the work of the coordinators and expand the movement’s reach across the country. “Our Founder and Grand Patron, High Chief Dr Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, has made us understand that the president is doing well. “He has done well in his first term. He should be given more time to consolidate what he has started in the last three and a half years,” Asuku said. He described Tompolo as a leader committed to democracy and the welfare of Nigerians, expressing appreciation for his continued support for the movement. The national coordinator also appealed to Nigerians, particularly youths and women, to support Tinubu’s re-election bid, arguing that continuity would enable the administration to consolidate its development agenda. He maintained that the president had made contributions to infrastructure, human capital development, and other sectors, urging voters to consider the country’s future rather than ethnic and religious affiliations when making political choices. “It is not the time to play tribal politics; it’s not the time to go after religious sentiments; it’s the time to see the future of Nigeria,” he said. Asuku expressed optimism that Nigeria could strengthen its position in Africa through improvements in technology, the economy, and security, urging citizens to support the president’s agenda. “We are charging Nigerians, especially the youth and women, men, everybody in the country, to see reasons why they should support and vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he added. Speaking shortly after receiving the buses, the Lagos State Coordinator, Hon. Amosu Kazeem Oluwatomi, commended Tompolo for supporting Tinubu’s re-election bid, describing the gesture as evidence that the president’s support extended beyond his home region. “It is so gratifying that a non-Lagosian, a non-South Westerner, is deeming it fit to support President Bola Ahmed Tinubu at this time. It shows that the level of acceptance of the president cuts across every nook and cranny of Nigeria,” Oluwatomi said. Similarly, the Kwara State Coordinator, Omuiyadun Hammed Dimeji, said the vehicles would enable the movement to educate residents on government policies and the impact of the Tinubu administration’s reform agenda. He argued that the initiative was not intended to spread political propaganda but to encourage voters to assess the administration based on its policies and their effects on citizens. He maintained that governance should be judged by policies and their impact on the people, adding that the Movement had been taking its message to communities across Kwara State. “What is governance? Governance is about policies, and we have been going all out to pinpoint to the people the impact of the reform agenda of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu at their doorsteps and within their vicinity,” he said. Dimeji expressed confidence that voters in Kwara State would support Tinubu and other candidates of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 elections.

title: Russian troops liberate Obshcheye community in Zaporozhye Region over past day
body:
MOSCOW, October 26. /TASS/. Russian troops liberated the community of Obshcheye in the Zaporozhye Region over the past 24 hours in the special military operation in Ukraine, Russia’s Defense Ministry reported.
"Battlegroup East units advanced deep into the enemy’s defenses and liberated the settlement of Obshcheye in the Zaporozhye Region," the ministry said in a statement.
The Ukrainian army lost roughly 1,285 troops in battles with Russian forces in all the frontline areas over the past 24 hours, according to the latest data on the special military operation in Ukraine released by Russia’s Defense Ministry.
The latest figures show that the Ukrainian army lost over 300 troops and 19 motor vehicles in the responsibility area of Russia’s Battlegroup North, more than 220 troops and three jamming stations in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup West and over 185 troops and two armored combat vehicles in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup South.
During the last 24-hour period, the Ukrainian army also lost roughly 340 troops and three armored combat vehicles in the responsibility area of Russia’s Battlegroup Center, over 210 troops and an armored combat vehicle in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup East and about 30 troops and a counterbattery radar station in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup Dnepr, the latest figures show.
Russia’s Battlegroup North inflicted more than 300 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed 19 enemy motor vehicles in its areas of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup North units gained better lines and positions and inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of two mechanized brigades, a motorized infantry brigade, an assault regiment of the Ukrainian army and a territorial defense brigade in areas near the settlements of Podsredneye, Prikolotnoye, Doroshenkovo and Fyodorovka in the Kharkov Region," the ministry said.
In the Sumy direction, Battlegroup North units struck formations of a mechanized brigade, an airmobile brigade of the Ukrainian army and a territorial defense brigade in areas near the settlements of Khoten, Barilovka and Nikolskoye in the Sumy Region, it said.
The Ukrainian army lost more than 300 personnel, 19 motor vehicles and three electronic warfare stations in the areas of responsibility of Russia’s Battlegroup North over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup West inflicted more than 220 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed three enemy jamming stations in its area of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup West units improved their forward positions and inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of three mechanized brigades, an airmobile brigade, an assault brigade of the Ukrainian army and two territorial defense brigades in areas near the settlements of Lesnaya Stenka and Donetskoye in the Kharkov Region, Raigorodok, Cherkasskoye and Bogorodichnoye in the Donetsk People’s Republic," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost more than 220 personnel, 20 motor vehicles and three electronic warfare stations in that frontline area over the past 24 hours, it said.
Russia’s Battlegroup South inflicted more than 185 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed two enemy armored combat vehicles in its area of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup South units improved their tactical position and inflicted losses on formations of five mechanized brigades, an airmobile brigade, a mountain assault brigade of the Ukrainian army and a marine infantry brigade in areas near the settlements of Kramatorsk, Slavyansk, Druzhkovka and Kondratovka in the Donetsk People’s Republic," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost more than 185 personnel, two armored combat vehicles, 33 motor vehicles, an artillery gun and four electronic warfare stations in that frontline area over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup Center inflicted roughly 340 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed three enemy armored combat vehicles in its area of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup Center units gained better lines and positions and inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of three mechanized brigades, an assault brigade, an assault regiment of the Ukrainian army, a marine infantry brigade and three National Guard brigades in areas near the settlements of Stepanovka, Krinitsy, Belozerskoye, Shilovka, Starovarvarovka and Malotaranovka in the Donetsk People’s Republic," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost an estimated 340 personnel, three armored combat vehicles, eight motor vehicles, a US-made 155mm Paladin self-propelled artillery system and two electronic warfare stations in the responsibility area of Russia’s Battlegroup Center over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup East inflicted more than 210 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed an enemy armored combat vehicle in its area of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
During the last 24-hour period, Battlegroup East units "inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of three air assault brigades, three assault regiments of the Ukrainian army and a marine infantry brigade in areas near the settlements of Gavrilovka, Vsesvyatskoye and Pokrovskoye in the Dnepropetrovsk Region, Volnyanka and Vasilevskoye in the Zaporozhye Region," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost more than 210 personnel, an armored combat vehicle, seven motor vehicles and a counterbattery radar station in that frontline area over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup Dnepr eliminated roughly 30 Ukrainian troops and destroyed an enemy counterbattery radar station in its area of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup Dnepr units improved their forward positions and inflicted losses on formations of a mechanized brigade and a mountain assault brigade of the Ukrainian army in areas near the settlements of Orekhov, Dimitrovo and Preobrazhenka in the Zaporozhye Region," the ministry said.
"Up to 30 Ukrainian military personnel, 12 motor vehicles and a counterbattery radar station were destroyed," it said.
Russian forces struck storage sites for the Ukrainian army’s ground robotic platforms and long-range unmanned aerial vehicles and enemy deployment areas over the past day, the ministry reported.
"Operational/tactical aircraft, attack unmanned aerial vehicles, missile troops and artillery of the Russian groups of forces struck military-industrial enterprises, energy and transport infrastructure facilities used by the Ukrainian army, ammunition depots, workshops producing and sites storing ground robotic platforms and long-range unmanned aerial vehicles, and also temporary deployment areas of Ukrainian armed formations and foreign mercenaries in 151 locations," the ministry said.
Russian air defense forces intercepted and destroyed 581 Ukrainian unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and two Storm Shadow cruise missiles over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Air defense capabilities shot down two guided aerial bombs, two British-made Storm Shadow airborne cruise missiles and 581 fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles," the ministry said.
Overall, the Russian Armed Forces have destroyed 674 Ukrainian combat aircraft, 284 helicopters, 271,778 unmanned aerial vehicles, 672 surface-to-air missile systems, 31,406 tanks and other armored combat vehicles, 1,792 multiple rocket launchers, 36,815 field artillery guns and mortars and 75,658 special military motor vehicles since the start of the special military operation, the ministry reported.

title: US singer Chris Brown avoids jail over UK nightclub brawl
body: American R&B singer Chris Brown avoided jail when sentenced by a UK court Monday after pleading guilty to a public order offence during a 2023 brawl at a London nightclub. The former boyfriend of music sensation Rihanna was handed an eight-month jail sentence suspended for a year — meaning he will not be imprisoned unless he commits another offence during the period. Brown, 37, who was wearing a black face mask and black cap when he arrived Monday at Southwark Crown Court in London, had admitted to affray during an appearance in July. “Violence of this kind in a crowded nightclub is serious. It creates an obvious risk, not merely to the person against whom it is directed, but also to others,” judge Tony Baumgartner said, handing down the sentence. Prosecutors had accused him and co-defendant Omololu Akinlolu, also a US national, of carrying out “a vicious and unprovoked attack” in a crowded nightclub “where Brown used a glass bottle as a weapon to strike the victim’s head twice”. The guilty plea avoided a trial on several other charges, including attempting to cause grievous bodily harm with intent and possession of an offensive weapon, namely a bottle. Brown, who has sold tens of millions of records worldwide, had earlier denied those charges. All of the allegations relate to an incident at Tape, a private members’ club in central London, on February 19, 2023, while Brown was touring the UK. The victim was struck several times with a bottle before being pursued, punched and kicked. The singer is known for mid-2000s hits such as “Kiss, Kiss”, as well as a litany of legal troubles including a felony conviction for assaulting Rihanna in 2009. Brown rose from a local church choir in Virginia to sudden fame with his rich R&B voice before turning to rap. He was convicted of having beaten then-girlfriend Rihanna before the 2009 Grammy Awards, forcing the pop star to miss the annual gala. In 2012, Brown was involved in an altercation at a New York nightclub with members of hip hop star Drake’s entourage, during which French basketball player Tony Parker suffered an eye injury after being hit by a thrown glass bottle. Two years later, Brown pleaded guilty to assaulting a fan in Washington. Akinlolu, 40 also pleaded guilty to affray over the London incident. He was sentenced to four months’ imprisonment suspended for a year. The post US singer Chris Brown avoids jail over UK nightclub brawl appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Peter Obi demands supporter’s release, accuses Tinubu of undermining democracy
body: By Adegboyega Adeleye The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi has demanded the release of party supporter Rilwan Olawale, accusing President Bola Tinubu of undermining democracy by “encouraging and facilitating violence.” In a statement posted on X on Monday, Obi described the reported incident as part of what he called the intimidation and harassment of his supporters. He also accused President Bola Tinubu of encouraging and facilitating violence, and demanded transparency over Olawale’s reported arrest, respect for his rights and an end to what he described as politically motivated harassment. “The continued intimidation and harassment of my supporters across the country, the latest being the case of Rilwan Olawale, is disturbing and unacceptable. “President Bola Tinubu has remained a huge beneficiary of our democracy and should not brazenly be destroying it by encouraging and facilitating violence.” Obi further stated that his campaign was peaceful and issue-driven, and warned that his supporters’ restraint should not be mistaken for weakness. “We have chosen the path of peace, not violence; persuasion, not intimidation. However, nobody should mistake our civility for weakness, our restraint for fear, or our commitment to peace for an absence of resolve. We will not be intimidated into silence, nor will we abandon Nigerians who believe in a New Nigeria that is possible and will be OK.” He called for Olawale’s release and said Nigerians should be free to support the candidate of their choice. “I therefore demand transparency regarding Rilwan Olawale’s arrest, his release, respect for his rights, and an end to politically motivated harassment. No government or political party has the right to deny Nigerians the freedom to support a candidate of their choice. “We will remain peaceful but resolute. We will not resort to violence, but we will stand firmly and lawfully against every attempt to undermine our democratic rights.” According to NDC’s Lagos governorship candidate, Funso Doherty, Olawale was reportedly taken from his residence at about 1 a.m. on Sunday by men who identified themselves as Department of State Services (DSS) operatives. Doherty, in a statement on his X handle on Sunday, said he was in contact with Olawale’s family and legal counsel, who were seeking to establish what happened and gain access to him. He said: “This afternoon, reports reached me that Mr. Rilwan Olawale, a strong NDC supporter, who is also identified with the Obidient movement, was allegedly picked up by some armed men who identified themselves as operatives of the Department of State Services in the very early hours of today, Sunday 25th October.” Doherty also urged the public to remain calm while the family and legal counsel sought information about Olawale’s whereabouts. The circumstances of the reported arrest and the reason for it remained unclear in reports available on Monday. “The circumstances surrounding this situation are still unclear and there is no official confirmation of his exact whereabouts. However, we are in contact with his family as well as with legal counsel who are working to gain access to him and to establish the relevant facts. We urge the public to stay calm and avoid speculation for now while these and further steps are being taken to ascertain the facts, ensure that Mr Olawale’s rights are fully respected and that Justice is served,” he added. The post Peter Obi demands supporter’s release, accuses Tinubu of undermining democracy appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: CBD COP17: Nigeria seeks West African alliance to protect high seas
body:
The Nigerian government has identified regional coordination, scientific cooperation, effective enforcement, and sustainable financing as key strategies to establish effective high-seas marine protected areas (MPAs) across West Africa and beyond.
Nigeria outlined the strategies on Monday through Sikeade Egbuwalo, the country’s focal point for the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), during a high-level segment organised by the BBNJ First Movers for the 30×30 target.
The BBNJ First Movers is a government collaboration led by Chile to fast-track the creation of the first generation of high seas Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) under the UN High Seas Treaty (BBNJ Agreement).
The BBNJ Agreement, formally known as the Agreement on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas Beyond National Jurisdiction, provides an international framework for protecting marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction.
Chile led the initiative to lay immediate groundwork for protecting international waters as the treaty moves into implementation, with its first Conference of the Parties scheduled to be held in New York in January next year.
Responding to a question on how regional coordination could drive the creation of effective high-seas MPAs to protect West African waters and achieve the 30×30 target, Mrs Egbuwalo said ocean conservation required countries to work together because marine ecosystems and the livelihoods they support transcend national boundaries.
“For Nigeria, the message is simple: the ocean does not recognise national boundaries, and neither should our conservation ambitions,” she said.
She added that the health of shared marine ecosystems is critical to the livelihoods of millions across West Africa, making regional cooperation essential to effective marine protection and meeting the global biodiversity target.
The 30×30 target, adopted under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, seeks to conserve at least 30 per cent of the world’s land and sea areas by 2030.
Meanwhile, over the past two decades, the high seas and maritime areas off West Africa have faced severe environmental, economic, and security challenges, largely due to weak regulation, foreign exploitation, and climate pressures.
While national governments try to control territorial waters and Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZs)/Free Trade Zones, the vast high seas beyond these limits have historically functioned as an under-regulated “Wild West,” leaving them vulnerable to overexploitation and illicit activity.
As a result, the Gulf of Guinea and West African shipping lanes have faced high risks of piracy, armed robbery, and attacks on oil tankers, bulk carriers, and fishing vessels, prompting West African seas to be deemed the “world’s most dangerous seas”.
In her interventions on Monday, Mrs Egbuwalo said Nigeria was working with six other West African countries through the West Africa BBNJ Coordination Committee to advance a proposal for a highly and fully protected high-seas MPA in the Guinea–Canary Currents Convergence Zone.
She said the initiative showed how regional cooperation can turn shared conservation priorities into concrete action by building political ownership, strengthening consensus, and sustaining commitment throughout the process.
Mrs Egbuwalo said achieving the 30×30 target requires more than designating percentages of the ocean for protection, stressing the need for ecologically representative, connected, and effectively managed MPA networks.
According to her, the Guinea–Canary Currents Convergence Zone supports important biodiversity, migratory species and fish populations that connect the high seas with national waters.
She said regional collaboration would let countries pool scientific expertise, share marine data, and identify areas where protection could deliver the greatest ecological benefits.
The Nigerian official also stressed the need to align marine conservation with fisheries management, food security and coastal livelihoods.
She said Nigeria’s assessment of the proposed regional MPA had considered marine species of nutritional, economic and cultural importance to coastal communities.
This, she said, underscored the importance of engaging artisanal fishers, women involved in fish processing and trade, and other ocean users in the conservation process.
“Conservation and livelihoods must reinforce each other, rather than be treated as competing priorities,” she said.
Mrs Egbuwalo identified effective monitoring, control, and enforcement as another critical requirement, warning that marine protected areas must be genuinely protected, not merely designated on paper.
She said a regional assessment of monitoring, control and surveillance capacities had identified existing mechanisms that could be strengthened.
She added that regional cooperation could facilitate joint monitoring, satellite surveillance, sharing vessel-tracking information and collaborating with regional fisheries bodies.
According to her, management and enforcement arrangements must be incorporated from the earliest stages of MPA development.
Additionally, she noted that establishing and managing high-seas MPAs required substantial scientific, technical and financial resources.
She argued that regional cooperation could help countries pool capacities, identify shared needs and attract international partnerships while maintaining regional ownership of conservation initiatives.
As countries prepare for the first Conference of the Parties to the BBNJ Agreement, she called for developing countries to have meaningful access to finance, technology and capacity-building support to participate effectively in its implementation.
With less than four years remaining to achieve the 2030 biodiversity target, Ms Egbuwalo urged countries to move from ambition to implementation.
She described the proposed Guinea–Canary Currents high-seas MPA as an opportunity to demonstrate how African regional leadership could deliver meaningful protection for the global ocean.
She also identified the sixth International Marine Protected Areas Congress (IMPAC6), scheduled for Dakar in March 2027, as an opportunity to strengthen political momentum and partnerships for the first generation of high-seas MPAs.
She said Nigeria remained committed to working with West African partners and the international community to advance the initiative.
“30×30 is not simply about how much ocean we protect, but how effectively we protect it,” she said, adding that regional cooperation could help West Africa protect biodiversity, strengthen ocean resilience and secure coastal livelihoods.

title: Millicent Nice Apeku wins NDC Ashaiman Deputy Secretary position
body: Millicent Nice Apeku has been elected Deputy Secretary of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Ashaiman Constituency of the Greater Accra Region. She secured 1,362 votes in the constituency executive elections held on Saturday, October 24, to emerge ahead of three other contenders. Kpotosu-Mensah Michael placed second with 631 votes, followed by Joseph Frimpong, who polled 723 votes, while David Quami Acheampong obtained 94 votes. Five ballots were rejected, with the total votes cast recorded at 2,815. Speaking to news reporters during press engagement to show appreciation to delegates and outlining her priorities on Monday, October 26, she said her victory places her in the constituency’s leadership structure, where she is expected to support party administration, communication, coordination and the implementation of organisational decisions. Ms Apeku has built her political experience through various roles within the NDC, spanning student politics, grassroots communication and constituency-level administration, she noted. She previously served as Deputy Secretary of the Tertiary Education Institutions Network (TEIN) at Takoradi Technical University. She also worked as Branch Communications Officer for the Nii Man Ward in Ashaiman, Deputy Coordinator of the Young Professional Forum in the Greater Accra Region, and a member of the NDC’s Ashaiman Constituency Executive. These roles have provided her with experience in party organisation, grassroots mobilisation and internal communication. As Deputy Secretary, Ms Apeku said she is committed to working with constituency executives and party members to strengthen the party’s internal structures and promote unity and discipline. Her priorities include encouraging greater participation by young people and women in party activities and improving administrative coordination within the constituency. Her journey from Alakple in the Volta Region to her professional role at the Tema Oil Refinery, alongside her involvement in party politics, reflects her pursuit of professional growth and leadership, she told the media. According to her, the new role marks another step in her political career as she takes on a new responsibility in the NDC’s Ashaiman Constituency leadership.

title: Russia is key player in unmanned aircraft sphere — expert
body:
MOSCOW, October 26. /TASS/. Over the past four years, Russia has made a technological leap forward in the development of unmanned aircraft and has become one of the key players in this field, President of the National Research Center Kurchatov Institute Mikhail Kovalchuk said.
"Four years ago, we practically had no unmanned aviation, so to speak. We had no drones. <…> But today, we are among the key players in this field," he noted.
According to Kovalchuk, the rapid development of unmanned technologies demonstrates Russia’s high mobilization capabilities.

title: The Download: everyday AI harms and the race to nuclear spaceflight
body: This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. Opinion: The focus on AI safety disasters ignores everyday harms —Sam Hiner, cofounder of the Young People’s Alliance, and Emma Leiken, executive director of the Responsible Technology Youth Power Fund at Hopelab We have historically allowed debates over technology to be defined by the worst thing a product might do, with remarkably little discussion of the insidious damage it does every day. A third of teens now choose to discuss serious matters with AI companions instead of other people. Students are relying on chatbots to write their papers, while social media feeds engineered to provoke envy keep users watching. These products can meet narrow safety requirements yet still erode how we think, learn, and interact with one another. As we enter an era defined by powerful AI products, we should demand that the tech industry do more than address only catastrophic harms. Here’s why AI safety needs to go further . Are we there yet? Nuclear-powered spaceships Earlier this year, NASA announced plans to build Space Reactor-1 Freedom, the first-ever nuclear-reactor-powered interplanetary spacecraft, and fly it to Mars by the end of 2028. A successful mission could herald more efficient, potentially faster spaceflight, saving astronauts time and cutting their exposure to harmful cosmic radiation. But nuclear space propulsion has moved slowly. The US has started—and terminated—several programs exploring the technology over the past 75 years. Could the $2 billion bet on Space Reactor-1 Freedom finally pay off? Find out how close NASA is to making nuclear-powered spaceflight a reality . —Robin George Andrews This story is part of “Are we there yet?” from the new Impossible issue of MIT Technology Review . The series takes stock of six technologies that have long promised to change the world—and scores them on a progress meter. Over the next six days, we’ll explore each one in The Download. The must-reads I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology. 1 Ukraine has regained high-speed Starlink and Starshield connectivity The restrictions disrupted air defences and drone operations. ( Politico ) + Elon Musk says Ukraine violated the terms with offensive drone use. ( BBC ) + Ukraine is now partnering with Nokia on a Starlink alternative. ( CNBC ) + Ukrainian drones hit a Russian government data center. ( Tom’s Hardware ) + A Russian ministry wants to move them underground. ( Kyiv Independent ) + Ukraine’s drones are fueling a wild data market. ( MIT Technology Review ) 2 Anthropic’s Claude accessed Georgia voter data without approval Anthropic says the AI bypassed a paywall. ( Axios ) + Mythos 5 recently kept hacking despite warnings of real-world harm. ( BI ) + Chatbots can sway voters better than political ads. ( MIT Technology Review ) 3 A personalised skin cancer vaccine is set to be approved next year The mRNA vaccine showed great promise in trials. ( New Scientist $) + Companies are playing word games with vaccines. ( MIT Technology Review ) 4 OpenAI is now training frontier models without internet access It paused training after models breached external systems. ( Bloomberg $) + Training will now take place offline to reduce security risks. ( TechCrunch ) + Its agents can still communicate without a network connection. ( Verge ) 5 US lawmakers are preparing for possible AI-driven mass layoffs A new bill would extend jobless aid and retraining support. ( NYT $) + But what do the numbers actually say about AI’s impact on jobs? ( MIT Technology Review ) 6 The first foldable iPhone is drawing buyers…and criticism Reviewers praised its inner screen but criticised its outer one. ( WSJ $) + Peter Thiel says Apple has done ‘nothing new’ after Steve Jobs. ( BI ) 7 Iran has threatened to target Gulf undersea cables if war resumes Officials said Tehran would disrupt internet connections. ( Reuters $) 8 New UFO files detail a strange, flying “black triangle” FBI documents describe a 15-foot object moving at fighter-jet speed. ( Axios ) + It’s never been easier to be a conspiracy theorist. ( MIT Technology Review ) 9 The BBC’s Blue Planet III left flaws in its footage to prove it’s not AI Producers used murkier shots to reinforce the series’ authenticity. ( Guardian ) 10 Elon Musk’s AI Odyssey has arrived—to scorn and ridicule Viewers derided Grok’s first AI-generated episode. ( TechCrunch ) Quote of the day “It’s very hard to imagine a group right now that operates more in a vacuum, more out of touch with everyday Americans, than the AI industry.” —Sen. John Curtis (R-Utah) tells Axios that bombastic claims from AI leaders are failing to win over the public. One more thing A woman’s uterus has been kept alive outside the body for the first time Ten months ago, reproductive health researchers placed a freshly donated human uterus inside a new device they call “Mother.” They connected the organ to the machine’s plastic veins and arteries and pumped in modified human blood. The device kept the uterus alive for a day, a new feat that could lead to longer-term maintenance of wombs outside the body. Future versions of the technology could shine new light on pregnancies—and potentially even grow a human fetus. Read the full story . —Jessica Hamzelou We can still have nice things A place for comfort, fun, and distraction to brighten up your day. (Got any ideas? Drop me a line .) + In good news for coral reefs, scientists have found some are surprisingly climate-resilient . + Decades of joy and movement come alive through these stunning archival photos of American dance floors. + Astronaut Jessia Meir has shared a stunning time-lapse view of the southern aurora dancing across the Earth. + A college student has turned the Met’s open-access data into a daily game that showcases underrepresented art and artifacts .

title: Rights Groups, CSOs Demand Investigation into Alleged Disappearances, Torture, Custodial Deaths in South-east
body: Emmanuel Ugwu-Nwogo in Enugu As families keep asking questions and seeking answers on the whereabouts of their loved ones, a group of human rights organisations has demanded an independent panel to investigate “all reported disappearances, torture, and custodial deaths in the Southeast.” The call was made at a press conference in Enugu by the Southeast Human Rights Bureau (SEHRB) in partnership with civil society organisations, including the International Society for Civil Liberties and Rule of Law (Intersociety), and the Oganihu Igbo Development Foundation. They alleged that the incidents occurred during security operations in the Southeast over the years. In a joint statement read to journalists, the groups said that well-documented evidence has shown that so many people have died in the Southeast at the hands of security agents while others just disappeared without any trace. The rights groups said that given the mysteries surrounding the recorded deaths and forced disappearances, there was a need for “comprehensive facility audit of all detention centres, including Wawa Barracks, Kuje, Suleja, and DSS facilities, to log every detainee and their legal status.” Their eight-point demands also include full accounting of the missing by disclosing arrest, transfer, and custody records for all individuals taken by state agents. Other demands listed are forensic investigation into mortuaries to preserve evidence and identify all unidentified bodies in Imo State and across the region. The rights groups said that guaranteed judicial safeguards must be put in place to ensure that “all detainees are promptly charged in court, granted legal representation, and protected from torture.” They stated that prosecution of perpetrators must be carried out in order to “hold both state agents and non-state actors criminally responsible for proven human rights abuses.” On the aftereffects of torture and detention on survivors, the groups demanded that there should be room for victim remedies and rehabilitation, which would provide compensation, medical care, and psychosocial support to victims and surviving families. In addition, the rights groups called for the establishment of a Southeast Documentation Mechanism composed of a multi-stakeholder body involving families, legal experts, and civil society to track disappeared persons. To stem the tide of unchecked security operations, the group called for a civilian oversight initiative to “strengthen independent monitoring and documentation of security agency operations to ensure accountability.” The rights groups acknowledged “the severe security challenges plaguing the Southeast—where armed separatist elements, criminal gangs, and non-state actors have murdered police officers, soldiers, traditional rulers, and ordinary citizens.” However, they insisted that “fighting lawlessness cannot justify state lawlessness (hence) there must be no hierarchy of victims. “The civilian murdered by armed criminals matters. The police officer or soldier unlawfully killed matters. The detainee who disappears in state custody matters. The torture survivor matters. The unidentified dead matter. Every victim deserves truth, justice, and accountability,” the groups said. The documented testimonies presented at the conference reveal a harrowing picture of night-time raids, arbitrary arrests, and systemic torture by security agencies, particularly the DSS, police tactical units like the infamous ‘Tiger Base’ in Owerri, and the Intelligence Response Team (IRT). At the press conference, the harrowing testimonies of victims and relatives of persons who disappeared at the hands of security operatives left a common trail of broken families and unmarked graves. Most of them broke down while recounting what they were made to suffer while being subjected to torture, with some coming out with permanent damage to their brains, limbs, eyes, or other body parts. Among the most shocking cases was that of Sunday Ifedi and his wife, Calista, who were arrested by the DSS in Enugu in 2021 and transferred to Wawa Barracks. While Sunday regained his freedom after more than four years, Calista never made it out alive. Grave allegations attributed to Sunday and human rights activist Omoyele Sowore indicate that Calista died in custody and was buried in a shallow grave within the barracks compound. There was also the case of Ozioma Elizabeth Onyeaka, who walked out of her home for a church vigil five years ago, and her family assumed she would return by dawn with prayers on her lips. Instead, the 35-year-old schoolteacher from Anambra State vanished into a legal black hole, leaving her relatives to traverse countless police stations, military formations, and mortuaries in a desperate, fruitless search for answers. Other accounts detail horrifying instances of collective punishment and “arrest in lieu”—where family members are abducted when suspects cannot be found. According to the coalition of rights groups, the pathetic accounts were “part of a systemic pattern of state-sponsored arbitrary arrests, torture, and enforced disappearances haunting Southeast Nigeria.” On the recently reported large number of unidentified bodies piling up in Imo State mortuaries, the coalition expressed “grave concern that many may be victims of security operations, extrajudicial killings, or custodial deaths.” They called for an immediate, independent forensic audit, preservation of mortuary registers and autopsies, and transparent DNA identification processes to prevent the destruction of evidence. ”A nation that cannot account for those taken into its custody cannot claim to uphold the rule of law,” the statement asserted.

title: Brazil’s Lula wins presidential election, bucking regional shift towards right
body:
Brazilian voters have denied Latin America’s resurgent right its ultimate prize, snapping a streak of seven straight conservative presidential victories in 18 months.
The stunning triumph of leftist incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva over Flavio Bolsonaro on Sunday, with 51.8 per cent of the vote to 48.2 per cent, limits U.S. President Donald Trump’s drive to tighten his grip on the Western Hemisphere and cements Latin America’s most populous country and largest economy as a counterweight to Washington. A Bolsonaro victory would have left Mexico’s Claudia Sheinbaum as the only progressive president among the region’s powerhouses.
For the Trump administration, which has wielded punishing tariffs, severe sanctions and military force to reassert its dominance in the region, Lula’s victory complicates its campaign to enlist Brazil in its military coalition against cartels and to gain preferential access to the country’s critical minerals, analysts say.
Yet both sides see reasons to cooperate. Washington wants access to Brazil’s vast trove of rare earths to reduce its defense industry’s reliance on China. Lula wants foreign investment and tariff relief for Brazilian exporters.
“Lula is pragmatic enough to work out some kind of modus operandi with the Trump administration,” said Will Freeman, a fellow for Latin America studies at the Council on Foreign Relations, adding that the Bolsonaros’ allies in Washington would likely lose sway after the family’s second electoral defeat. Flávio’s father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, lost to Lula in 2022.
“I’m not sure anyone in the Trump administration, beyond a few individuals, will want to keep making the Bolsonaros the central issue in the U.S.-Brazil relationship,” he said.
Across much of Latin America, voters fed up with organized crime and economic insecurity have rewarded presidential candidates promising to restore order. From Peru’s Keiko Fujimori to Colombia’s Abelardo de la Espriella and Chile’s José Antonio Kast, newly elected conservatives have courted Trump while taking their cues from El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele, whose sweeping gang crackdown has sharply reduced homicides at the cost of mass arrests and suspended civil liberties.
Trump has reinforced that shift with electoral endorsements, financial bailouts and millions of dollars in military aid.
“The U.S. is certainly putting its finger on the scale to try to help the more hard-line right-wing elements in the region,” said Kenneth Roberts, a professor of government at Cornell University.
Brazil would have been Washington’s most consequential addition. Bolsonaro had promised to join the U.S.-led security coalition “with great enthusiasm and great honor,” making his alliance with Trump part of his pitch to voters.
Lula, by contrast, has championed Brazil’s long tradition of nonalignment, cultivating ties with competing powers. His government deepened trade ties with China and sought greater global influence through BRICS, a group of emerging economies.
Trump’s heavy-handed support for the Bolsonaros played into that message. The double-digit tariffs he imposed on a range of Brazilian goods to punish Brazil for prosecuting former President Jair Bolsonaro over a coup plot to oust Lula stirred a nationalist backlash that the leftist leader channeled into the rallying cry “Brazil belongs to Brazilians.”
“To the extent that the regional superpower becomes a threat to Brazil’s democratic institutions, defending Brazilian national sovereignty also becomes a form of defending Brazilian democracy,” Roberts said.
Brazil resisted joining the Shield of the Americas, a U.S.-led military coalition targeting cartels.
When Washington in May designated Brazil’s two largest criminal factions, the First Capital Command and the Red Command, as terrorist organizations, Lula warned the labels could become a pretext for American intervention.
“We don’t accept being treated like children,” he said after the announcement. Of the gangs, he added: “We will fight them here at home.”
Countries along the main northbound cocaine and migrant routes, many of them heavily dependent on the U.S. market, have been more accommodating. In Ecuador, U.S. troops have joined local police in raids targeting suspected drug networks across the coastal lowlands. Honduras, Guatemala and Colombia have also agreed to joint military operations, U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has said, though Guatemala’s government has denied it.
“Brazil is not Honduras. It’s a large country with a very independent history and a military that would not look kindly upon foreign troops in its own territory,” said Brian Winter, a veteran Latin America analyst and editor-in-chief of Americas Quarterly, a policy journal. “The Trump administration will have to walk a certain line here.”
Washington may also have less reason to press Lula on military cooperation. Most of the cocaine moving through Brazil is consumed in the country or shipped to Europe and Africa, rather than the U.S.
On critical minerals, Lula wants Brazil to control its resources and preserve its freedom to sell beyond the U.S.
Brazil holds the world’s second-largest known reserves of rare earths, used in powerful magnets for guided missiles, smartphones, wind turbines and electric vehicles.
Last month, USA Rare Earth, in which the U.S. government holds a stake, completed its $2.8 billion takeover of Serra Verde, the Brazilian firm that owns one of the few mines outside of Asia producing all four rare earths needed for those magnets. Alarmed by the expanding U.S. role, Lula’s administration fast-tracked legislation tightening oversight of critical minerals.
“Revisiting the Serra Verde–USA Rare Earth deal may not be the first thing that Lula does when he’s reelected, but it’s on his radar,” said Monica de Bolle, a senior fellow at the Peterson Institute for International Economics.
Brazil also produces about 90 per cent of the world’s niobium, a critical element for jet, rocket engines and other military hardware, according to the U.S. Geological Survey. Any Brazilian export restrictions could disrupt supply chains for U.S. defense manufacturers.
“Brazil has leverage,” de Bolle said. “With Lula, the U.S. is on shakier ground.”
For all his defiant public statements, Lula has sought peace with Trump. His White House visit in May to discuss trade, organized crime and critical minerals undercut the Bolsonaros’ claim that only they could deal with Washington.
More bargaining with Trump surely lies ahead over tariffs and with Brazil’s Congress, where conservatives expanded their ranks in the Oct. 4 elections, depriving Lula of the backing he needs to institute meaningful reforms. After three previous terms, Lula confronts voters impatient for safer streets and relief from the high cost of living.
“Lula has his hands tied,” said Guilherme Casarões, an associate professor of Brazilian studies at Florida International University. “Pretty much everything he has tried to do has been blocked in Congress.”
Across Latin America, coalitions that united against a common opponent have often splintered as the realities of governing set in. Trump’s new allies are already losing support in Chile, Bolivia and Peru, suggesting the region’s rightward turn may be less durable than it appears. Lula bucked the anti-incumbent trend, but his support could evaporate quickly as he bargains with opponents — in Congress and beyond Brazil’s borders — to deliver the results voters expect.

title: Jordan arrests three men suspected of deadly church attack after shootout
body: Jordanian security forces have arrested three armed men suspected of a shooting attack at a church last week that killed nine Christians and injured 34 other people, officials say. The Public Security Directorate (PSD) said the unnamed “terrorists” were located before dawn inside an abandoned house in Karak governorate, south of the capital, Amman. They refused to surrender and opened fire on security forces, who returned fire and wounded all three of them, it added. No security personnel were hurt in the shootout. No group has yet claimed it was behind Friday’s attack by gunmen on a funeral at St George’s Greek Orthodox Church in the village of Hmoud, which is in Karak governorate. King Abdullah II praised security forces for chasing the suspects “to the very end”. “We vowed the terrorists would not escape punishment, and no proponent of dark ideologies that divide Jordanians will be tolerated,” he wrote on X. “We pray that the martyrs’ souls rest in peace and wish the injured a speedy recovery. May God protect and watch over Jordan and its people.” Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya said authorities would hold to account anyone involved in the attack and were “examining every factor that leads youth toward extremism”. Karak is home to a sizeable Christian community in the Muslim-majority kingdom. Verified CCTV footage from Friday showed three men holding guns approaching and firing on St George’s church. A second video showed dead and wounded people lying on the ground amid chaotic scenes. One man who was at the church told BBC Arabic that the attack lasted around 15 minutes. “Some [people at the funeral] were taking cover, some were cradling the dead, others were holding their sons close, some were grabbing their children and fleeing, while others were holding onto their friends who were with them at the church,” Khalid al-Mdanat said. He added that the gunmen fled in a pick-up truck, “firing as they went”. On Sunday, the Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Jerusalem, Theophilos III, visited wounded survivors of the attack, which he condemned as a “vile, cowardly, and bloody act”. He also led the funeral at St George’s of eight of the victims – Dr Maher Zureiqat, Ihab al-Halsa, Dr Fadi al-Halsa, Dr Khaled al-Halsa, Dr Asim al-Burqan, Alaa al-Masarwa, Marwan Khaitan and Mazen al-Qassous – which was attended by thousands of people. The ninth victim, Dr Mohammed al-Qassous, was laid to rest near Amman on Monday.

title: Lockheed Martin completes acquisition of Ultra Maritime
body: Lockheed Martin has completed its purchase of Ultra Maritime, adding sonar systems, sonobuoys and torpedo defense technology to its anti-submarine warfare business. Ultra Maritime will become part of Lockheed Martin’s Rotary and Mission Systems (RMS) business area. The company supplies towed sonar arrays, hull-mounted sonars and sonobuoys to allied navies. Lockheed Martin said those products, along with Ultra Maritime’s international operations, would broaden the range of sonar it can offer for next-generation naval platforms. “Securing the undersea domain starts with giving sailors the tools and confidence to find, track and deter threats that put ships and crews at risk,” said Stephanie C. Hill, president of RMS. “This is more than an acquisition — it’s a commitment to unite the best of our technology, capability and people to meet our partners’ urgent and growing demand for undersea warfare capability worldwide.” Beyond anti-submarine warfare, the deal brings in Ultra Maritime’s radar, electronic warfare and autonomous maritime sensing products. Lockheed Martin did not disclose the financial terms.

title: Shirley Frimpong-Manso defends foreign involvement in ‘The Eyes of Ghana’ documentary
body: Ghanaian filmmaker Shirley Frimpong-Manso has defended the involvement of foreign producers in The Eyes of Ghana , describing criticism of their participation as misplaced. Speaking to arts and culture journalist Kwame Dadzie on Showbiz A-Z on Joy FM , Shirley said arguments that the involvement of the Obamas, IShowSpeed and other foreign film companies in the documentary was inappropriate overlooked the people responsible for developing and executing the project. “IShowSpeed coming in would have basically been for the publicity. It doesn’t take away from the people who actually thought the thing and executed it. Somebody said the most expensive thing about film is your time. It’s the time you put in. It’s the ideas behind it. And it’s the people who actually make the move,” she noted. She added that many world-class films are funded by other people, arguing that there was nothing wrong with a Ghanaian-themed film receiving foreign funding. Shirley said she was surprised that some people were sensationalising the involvement of foreigners, questioning how Ghanaians could have allowed others to make a film about them. “First off it’s art. And especially when you have been mentioned in something, you take advantage of it and you own it. What is wrong if somebody even did it, and we had no Ghanaians in it. If it’s shedding positive light on our history, you embrace it and you go with it. Argentinians everywhere, no matter what Messi is doing, for them it’s Argentina. And you claim it and you own it and that’s how it’s supposed to be,” she said. The Eyes of Ghana is a documentary directed by two-time Academy Award-winning filmmaker Ben Proudfoot. It follows 93-year-old Ghanaian cinematographer Rev. Dr Chris Tsui Hesse, who served as the personal cameraman to Ghana’s first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah, and explores his efforts to preserve more than 1,000 reels of historical footage documenting Ghana’s independence and the wider African liberation movement. The film is produced by a team that includes Proudfoot, Ghanaian producers Nana Adwoa Frimpong and Anita Afonu, Moses Bwayo, Brandon Somerhalder, Ethan Lewis, Vinnie Malhotra and American streamer IShowSpeed, whose real name is Darren Watkins Jr. Former United States President Barack Obama and former First Lady Michelle Obama are executive producers through their production company, Higher Ground. Other Ghanaian contributors include co-producers Yaw Amponsah Apenteng and Justice Baidoo, assistant editor Annabelle Toe, and musician Dela Botri, who contributed as a featured instrumentalist. The documentary premiered at the 2025 Toronto International Film Festival and has since received international recognition. In Ghana, it was screened at the University of Media, Arts and Communication’s Institute of Film and Television in Accra in April 2026. Another free screening is scheduled for Saturday, 31st October 2026, at 6.30 pm at the Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park in Accra, with registration required. The film is also scheduled for a one-night cinema release in the United States and Canada on Wednesday, 28th October 2026. Shirley Frimpong-Manso is one of Ghana’s established film directors, writers and producers. Through Sparrow Productions, she has made films including The Perfect Picture , A Sting in a Tale , Adams Apples , 6 Hours to Christmas , Contract , Potomanto , Love or Something Like That , Rebecca and Potato Potahto . Her work has earned her industry recognition, including the Best Director award at the Africa Movie Academy Awards and other prestigious awards at the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards. Her latest comedy, Agency for the Dead , is scheduled to open in Ghanaian cinemas on Friday, 30th October 2026. The film draws on Ghanaian folklore and childhood ghost stories, offering a comic take on supernatural beliefs. Its cast includes Anita Erskine, David Dontoh, George Quaye, Joselyn Dumas, Mawuli Gavor, Omari Dwamena, Rhoda Ampene and Yvonne Okoro.

title: Kane Tipped To Beat Yamal, Mbappe To Ballon d’Or Glory
body: Harry Kane is the favourite to become England’s first Ballon d’Or winner in 25 years when the award is presented in London on Monday, but he faces stiff competition from La Liga pair Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe. Alexia Putellas is the clear frontrunner to win the women’s prize for a third time, with Aitana Bonmati’s three-year reign set to come to an end after an injury-hit spell. The ceremony to decide the world’s best male and female footballers is being held in London for the first time — 70 years after England winger Stanley Matthews was presented with the inaugural award. Bayern Munich and England forward Kane struck a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season, propelling the German giants to a league and cup double. But semi-final exits in both the Champions League and at the World Cup in the United States mean a triumph for Kane at the London Palladium is far from certain. “I’d love to be able to achieve something like that. It would be a massive milestone in my career,” said the 33-year-old former Tottenham forward. “I think my wife would prefer to know and my family… it’s very stressful for everyone,” added the England captain. Only four players from England have won the Ballon d’Or. Michael Owen was the last to triumph in 2001, following in the footsteps of Matthews, Bobby Charlton and Kevin Keegan. Bayern coach Vincent Kompany praised Kane’s focus on his team, saying: “What made Harry happy the most in recent years is that he finally won his first team trophies here. “Now if he can crown his career or his season with the Ballon d’Or, that would be deserved for the way he plays for the team.” ‘I Deserve it’ Yamal finished second to Paris Saint-Germain’s Ousmane Dembele last year, and the 19-year-old Barcelona superstar seems destined to be a Ballon d’Or winner one day. However, a hamstring injury ended his club season early, and he failed to show his most irresistible form during Spain’s World Cup triumph, which was built on impressive teamwork. But that has not diminished his confidence ahead of the ceremony. “For me, Mbappe and me, we’re the two best players in the world,” Yamal said last month. “I honestly think that, as the best in the world, maybe there are two of us, and this year I would deserve it because of what I’ve won.” Mbappe, by contrast, boasts plenty of personal milestones without medals for either Real Madrid or France. The 27-year-old was top goalscorer in La Liga, the Champions League and the World Cup without winning any of those trophies. His 10 World Cup goals in North America made him the top goalscorer in the competition’s history, on 22. “Being the all-time top scorer in World Cup history, overtaking all the great legends in the history of the sport in the most important tournament there is, is something that really stands out,” said Mbappe. “Who am I voting for? Myself.” The Ballon d’Or was established by the magazine France Football, with the first award given to Matthews in 1956. One football journalist from each of the 100 top nations in FIFA’s rankings is invited to cast votes for their top 10 players from a 30-man shortlist. Although the award carries no cash prize, it can generate huge bonuses from clubs and commercial partners, as well as increasing a player’s overall market value. Putellas, winner of the women’s award in 2021 and 2022, was a member of the Barcelona side that regained the Champions League last season before moving to London City Lionesses. Her former Barcelona teammate, Poland’s Ewa Pajor, is Putellas’s main challenger after scoring 11 Champions League goals in Barca’s latest triumph. AFP The post Kane Tipped To Beat Yamal, Mbappe To Ballon d’Or Glory appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Court rules El-Rufai has case to answer in phone-tapping trial
body:
The Federal High Court in Abuja has dismissed the no-case submission filed by former Kaduna State Governor Nasir El-Rufai in his trial on charges of unlawful interception of the telephone communications of National Security Adviser (NSA) Nuhu Ribadu.
Judge Joyce Abdulmalik, in a ruling on Monday, held that the State Security Service (SSS) had presented sufficient evidence to require Mr El-Rufai to enter his defence, if he chooses.
The judge consequently ordered the former governor, the sole defendant in the case, to enter a defence.
A defendant who fails to enter a defence risks leaving the judge with no option but to foreclose the defence. In that situation, the judge may determine the defendant’s guilt or innocence solely on the strength of the evidence the prosecution presented.
Mr El-Rufai, through his lawyer, Akinyemi Aremu, had urged the court to hold that the prosecution failed to establish a case against him to require him to enter defence.
However, the SSS lawyer, Oluwole Aladedoye, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), opposed the submission.
Mr Aladedoye argued that the defence failed to address Exhibit B, which the prosecution said contained Mr El-Rufai’s alleged admission concerning the interception of Mr Ribadu’s telephone communications.
Mr El-Rufai, who has been in the custody of the Independent Corrupt Practices and other related offences Commission (ICPC) since February, maintained that the prosecution had established a prima facie case against the former governor.
The SSS filed the charges against Mr El-Rufai following comments he made during an interview on Arise Television in the aftermath of a failed attempt to arrest him at the Abuja airport upon his return to Nigeria from a foreign trip in February.
PREMIUM TIMES reported that SSS operatives attempted to arrest Mr El-Rufai on 12 February, following his arrival from Cairo, Egypt.
While the arrest was unsuccessful, the security operatives seized the former governor’s passport.
The following day, Mr El-Rufai alleged during a live interview on ‘Prime Time’, an Arise Television programme, that Mr Ribadu was behind the alleged attempt to arrest him at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja.
He said he knew Mr Ribadu ordered his arrest from listening to a wire-tapped phone call made by Mr Ribadu instructing security operatives to carry out his arrest.
Following the interview, the SSS charged him with five counts relating to the alleged unlawful interception of telephone communications and other offences under the Cybercrimes (Prohibition, Prevention, etc.) Amendment Act 2024 and the Nigerian Communications Act 2003.
Mr El-Rufai pleaded not guilty to the charges when he was arraigned in April.
The prosecution called two witnesses before closing its case in June.
The first witness, an SSS operative identified in court by the code name APC, testified about the agency’s monitoring and preservation of the recording of Mr El-Rufai’s television interview.
The prosecution also called lawyer and human rights activist Deji Adeyanju, who testified about the interview.
Mr Adeyanju told the court that he was at the Arise Television studio in Abuja when Mr El-Rufai gave the interview. The court also watched a recording of the programme.
During his testimony, Mr Adeyanju confirmed that the recording reflected what he witnessed during the interview.
Under cross-examination, he told the court that he heard Mr El-Rufai say, “we listened to their calls”.
However, he acknowledged that Mr El-Rufai did not expressly say that he had personally tapped the NSA’s telephone.
After presenting the witnesses and its evidence, the prosecution informed the court that it would not call any further witnesses and closed its case.
Following the prosecution’s closure of its case, the defence indicated that it would file a no-case submission, asking the court to dismiss the charges without the need for Mr El-Rufai to enter defence.
A no-case submission asks a court to discharge a defendant on the ground that the prosecution has not presented sufficient evidence to warrant a defence.
The prosecution, however, opposed the application, insisting that its evidence was sufficient to require him to answer the allegations.
In Monday’s ruling, Judge Abdulmalik agreed with the prosecution that Mr El-Rufai has a case to answer.
He rejected the defence’s argument and held that the evidence presented was sufficient to require Mr El-Rufai to enter his defence.
This means the former governor will now have to enter his defence if he chooses to contest the charges.
Mr El-Rufai is facing corruption charges instituted against him by the ICPC before two separate courts in Kaduna over his activities during his eight years as governor. He is also pursuing different human rights enforcement cases which arose from the actions of the ICPC concerning him and his family members since his detention by the commission in February. He recently lost two of the cases.

title: Chief Editor of Independent Belgorod News Outlet Charged With ‘Justifying Terrorism’
body:
The editor-in-chief of Pepel, an online outlet covering news in the southwestern Belgorod region, has reportedly been charged by Russia’s FSB security service with publicly justifying terrorism.
Fonar, another regional news outlet, said Nikita Parmenov stands accused of making statements in support of the Russian Volunteer Corps, a far-right paramilitary group composed of Russians fighting alongside the Ukrainian army.
It was not immediately clear what statements specifically the FSB was referring to, Fonar reported. The criminal charge carries a maximum sentence of seven years in prison.
Pepel suggested that the accusations of justifying terrorism could stem from a YouTube interview in which Parmenov said he was unable to condemn Russians who take up arms to help Ukraine defend itself from invading Russian forces.
Though Parmenov explicitly condemned cross-border shelling that targets civilians in the Belgorod region, Pepel claimed pro-war Telegram channels edited that part out of his interview and circulated it online.
The FSB’s statement, cited by yet another regional news outlet, Belpressa, claimed Parmenov is currently living in exile outside Russia, somewhere in the South Caucasus.
Russia’s Justice Ministry designated Parmenov a “foreign agent” in February 2025.
Parmenov founded Pepel in the fall of 2022, months after President Vladimir Putin ordered the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
