title: Yiaga Africa Raises Poser on Voters Register, Asks if Young People were Removed
body: Chuks Okocha in Abuja The Executive Director of Yiaga Africa, Samson Itodo, has raised a serious poser over the voters’ list released by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), asking whether the commission deliberately reduced the number of young persons’ capacity to vote. In a statement made available to THISDAY yesterday, Itodo raised a question on the declining number of young voters. According to Itodo, who compared the percentage of young persons in the 2023 voters register, said: ‘’The recent voter registration figures released by INEC have raised important questions about the declining number of young people on Nigeria’s voter register. Let’s look at what the data tells us. According to INEC, Nigeria had 93,469,008 registered voters in 2023, distributed across four age categories: Youth: 18–34 years: 37,060,399 (39.6%); Middle age: 35–49 years: 33,413,591 (35.8%), and Elderly: 50–69 years: 17,700,270 (18.9%), while 70 years and above: 5,294,748 (5.7%).’’ Continuing, Itodo said: ‘’The 2026 figures show that the voter register has increased to 103,428,715 registered voters, representing an increase of 9,959,707 voters, or 10.66 percent compared with the 11.27 percent increase recorded in 2023. The 2026 age distribution is as follows: Youth: 18–34 years: 29,777,578 (28.79%); Middle age: 35–49 years: 43,265,946 (41.83%); Elderly: 50–69 years: 22,982,900 (22.22%), while 70 years and above got 7,402,291 (7.16%).’’ Accordingly, the Executive Director of Yiaga Africa said: ‘’What do these figures tell us? While the overall voter register figure for 2026 increased by 10.66 percent, the number of registered voters aged 18–34 declined by 7,282,821, representing a 19.65 percent reduction in this age category. Their share of the register also declined from 39.6 percent in 2023 to 28.79 percent in 2026, a decrease of approximately 10.9 percentage points. “The number of registered voters aged 35 to 49 increased by 9,852,355, representing an increase of approximately 29.5%.’’ Then, Itodo asked: ‘’Does this mean young people were removed from the register? Not necessarily. Between 2023 and 2026, three years elapsed. Voters who were aged 32, 33, and 34 in 2023 would have transitioned into the 35–49 age category by 2026. This demographic shift could partially explain the decline in the youth category and the increase in the older age category. However, ageing alone does not fully account for these changes. It is also necessary to examine new additions to the register, particularly the rate of youth registration, and any administrative adjustments.’’ Accordingly, he said: ‘’This raises a critical question: Are young Nigerians registering to vote at a rate sufficient to replace those who are ageing out of the youth category? ‘’For historical perspective, Nigeria’s voter register increased from 68,833,476 in 2015 to 84,004,084 in 2019, representing a 22.04 percent increase. Between 2019 and 2023, the register grew to 93,469,008, an increase of 9,464,924 voters (11.27%). By 2026, it had risen further to 103,428,715, representing an additional 9,959,707 voters (10.66%). Although the absolute increase between 2023 and 2026 was slightly higher than that recorded between 2019 and 2023, the percentage growth was marginally lower. These figures demonstrate a declining rate of growth in Nigeria’s voter register: 22.04 percent in 2015–2019, 11.27 percent in 2019–2023, and 10.66 percent in 2023–2026. The most recent period, however, covers three years rather than four. ‘’The critical issue, therefore, is not simply whether the voter register is growing, but who is entering the register, how voters are transitioning between age categories, and what these demographic changes mean.’’ Itodo then challenged INEC, saying: ‘’My proposal to INEC is to publish a detailed age-cohort analysis explaining changes between the 2015, 2019, 2023 and 2026 registers, including new registrations, age transitions, removal of dead and unqualified persons on the register and other adjustments. ‘’If the decline shows inadequate registration among newly eligible young voters, it must prompt increased investment in youth mobilization for voter registration. If it reflects administrative adjustments, those changes must be clearly documented and explained,’’ he stated.

title: ‘You need people, not money’ – Expert urges young people to explore agribusiness
body: Young people and aspiring entrepreneurs should not wait until they have substantial start-up capital before exploring opportunities in agribusiness, an agricultural development expert has said, urging them to identify market needs and build relationships that can help turn ideas into viable businesses. Executive Director of the Centre for Climate Change & Food Security (CCCFS) and Director of WAJESHA, Engr Mahmud Mohammed-Nurudeen, says he has trained, advised and guided nearly 300 people in 2026 alone to consider opportunities in the agricultural sector. The group includes students, graduates, businesspeople, politicians and teachers, whom he has reached through workshops, seminars, webinars, farm field visits, meetings and informal conversations, including on buses. “Sometimes, you don’t need money at the first point; you need people,” he told participants at an Agribusiness Incubation Workshop organised by residents of Jacob Jonas Nortey Hall at Valley View University’s Oyibi campus on Friday, 23 October 2026. Held under the theme “Developing the Anti-Fragile Mindset: Agribusiness as a Catalyst,” the workshop explored how young people could approach agriculture as a business and identify opportunities across its value chain. Identify a problem before investing Mohammed-Nurudeen said aspiring entrepreneurs should begin by identifying a problem they can solve rather than pursuing immediate profits without a clear understanding of the market. “If you really want to go into agribusiness, first problem identification. What problem do you want to address?” he asked. He illustrated the point with the story of a woman whose business collapsed during the COVID-19 pandemic but who found another source of income through the sale of locally produced rice. According to him, she identified people who needed rice, sourced the product from producers and supplied it to customers at a price that allowed her to make a profit. “Her business actually collapsed during the COVID-19, and she decided to solve that problem for people,” he said. The example, he explained, demonstrates how recognising an unmet need can help people identify business opportunities even when their original plans have failed. He also recounted how he advised a vegetable farmer who was struggling to find customers to prepare flyers and distribute them at ministries, where workers might have limited time to visit markets. Mohammed-Nurudeen said he encouraged the farmer to offer potential customers samples of the vegetables. “When he did that, the first week, second week, they started calling him for orders,” he said, describing the approach as an opportunity that opened the door to new customers. The experience highlights the importance of understanding customers and actively promoting products instead of relying on production alone to generate sales. ‘Networking first before money’ For Mohammed-Nurudeen, relationships can help aspiring entrepreneurs find customers, obtain advice and identify potential partners before they have the resources to establish a business. He drew on his experience travelling to nearly 2,500 communities across Ghana’s 16 regions, saying the relationships he had built over the years continued to provide access to people who could help him solve problems. “I’ve travelled to many communities and at least I have friends in each of the districts that I went to,” he said. He explained that he could contact people in those communities when he needed assistance, while relationships beyond Ghana had also helped him access professional opportunities. He cited invitations to contribute to international work involving climate change and health as examples of how professional networks and recommendations could open doors. “You might even have the money and you might even establish your business, but the business will collapse because you don’t have that strong network system,” he cautioned. He urged young people, particularly those below 25, to start building relationships early and not to measure every interaction by immediate financial returns. “There are things you need to do for free and these things can bring a lot of benefits to you,” he said. He also advised aspiring entrepreneurs to think carefully about what would distinguish their products from those of competitors. “If you want to go into maize cultivation, there are a lot of maize farmers. What unique thing are you bringing on board that you would want people to buy your maize?” he asked. Agribusiness goes beyond farming Mohammed-Nurudeen said entering agribusiness does not necessarily mean cultivating crops or rearing animals. Opportunities also exist in processing, marketing, distribution and other activities that connect agricultural products to consumers. “Setting up a business does not necessarily mean that you have to go and grow a crop,” he said. “You don’t necessarily have to go into farming physically.” He added: “The value chain is very long; you can choose any of them.” The advice encourages aspiring entrepreneurs to consider how their existing skills, resources and interests could fit into different parts of the agricultural sector rather than assuming that land ownership or direct involvement in production is essential. He also urged businesses to diversify so they could better withstand market disruptions and competition. Using the example of a business facing new competitors offering better products or services, he asked what an entrepreneur should do when customers begin moving elsewhere. “That is why we have always told farmers that they need to diversify,” he said. Diversification, he explained, can create additional income streams and reduce the risks associated with depending on a single product or business activity. Persistence is not enough Mohammed-Nurudeen challenged the idea that patience and persistence alone will guarantee business success, arguing that entrepreneurs must be willing to reassess their decisions when results do not improve. “Many instances you can be patient for 20 years, 30 years, it won’t work,” he said. “How do you persist when you are doing the wrong thing?” He urged aspiring entrepreneurs to use their time productively, evaluate what is happening in their businesses and adjust their approaches instead of continuing with strategies that are not working. Integrity, he added, is equally important to building a sustainable livelihood. Recounting a conversation with a retired public servant he met during a journey from Kumasi to Kintampo, Mohammed-Nurudeen said the man reflected on how he had previously withheld part of money intended for colleagues while working in public service. The man later decided to stop the practice and share a contract payment among his team members, according to Mohammed-Nurudeen’s account. The story reinforced the advice the retired public servant had given during their roadside conversation: “Money is good, but don’t be eager to make money by any means.” For Mohammed-Nurudeen, trust and sound judgement are as important as identifying a market opportunity. A business idea may create an opening, but sustaining it requires the ability to adapt, maintain relationships and act with integrity. A university initiative to expand agribusiness The workshop forms part of efforts by residents of Jacob Jonas Nortey Hall to develop and expand their agribusiness activities. The hall has previously undertaken a yam farming project and more recently ventured into mushroom production, with plans to diversify and scale up its initiatives. For students, graduates and others considering the sector, Mohammed-Nurudeen’s message was that a lack of substantial capital need not prevent them from exploring possibilities. Identifying a genuine need, finding ways to reach customers and building relationships can provide a starting point. The challenge, he suggested, is not simply to enter agriculture, but to identify where value can be created and remain ready to change course when circumstances demand it.

title: Open letter to President Mahama, Vice President Opoku-Agyemang and NDC leadership: Justice for Obuasi SHTS girls
body: Dear Mr President, Madam Vice President and leaders of the NDC, I write to you not as an adversary, but as a citizen who once believed that the phrase “social democratic” meant something more than a campaign slogan. I write because the events of the past week have made it impossible to remain silent. The sexual misconduct allegations against the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School involving 19 female students are not merely a criminal matter. They are a moral test of your government. And thus far, the response has been lackadaisical, reactive and, in the case of the Vice President, disturbingly belated. When investigative journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni’s documentary, Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow, exposed the allegations, the party’s Functional Executive Committee first directed the accused, Zakaria Abdulai, to step aside from the Juaben constituency chairmanship race. Then, within days, the party reversed itself and cleared him to contest, citing the “presumption of innocence” and “the timelines of the ongoing electoral process”. It was only after public outrage that the party suspended its Amasaman Communications Officer, Daniel Nortey, for trivialising rape on live television. This is not principled leadership. It is crisis management. The signal sent to every girl in Obuasi and to every survivor of sexual violence in Ghana is unmistakable: when political convenience collides with your dignity, convenience wins. The signal being sent is that victims who are suffering may be discouraged from speaking up by what is happening today. Madam Vice President, you are the first woman to hold your office. That is a historic achievement, and it is not lost on the women of this country. But history is not a shield from accountability. Some organisations argue that you are “the Vice President of Ghana and not just the Vice President for women and girls”. They insist that your gender should not confine your leadership to women’s issues and that criticism of you is disproportionate. They are right about one thing: no woman should be reduced to her gender. But they are dangerously wrong about the political reality that put you in office. Madam Vice President, you did not win the sympathy of women voters by accident. You won it because your presence on the ticket promised representation; a promise that the highest office in the land would finally feel the weight of women’s lived realities. Women voted for you not because they expected you to be a “women’s officer”, but because they believed your gender would inform your judgement on issues that disproportionately affect them, such as rape, domestic violence, child defilement and the everyday indignities that too often go unspoken. To now position yourself as a neutral national leader, above the fray of gender, is to betray that promise. You cannot collect the political capital of women’s sympathy and then claim neutrality when women’s bodies are the battlefield. The argument by some organisations that you are “Vice President of Ghana, not for women” is technically true and politically dishonest. It is a sophisticated way of saying that the first woman in your position will be judged by the same standards as the men who preceded her, which is precisely the problem because those standards have failed women for generations. Mr President, your party’s response to Obuasi reveals a deeper disorder: the belief that the only real accountability is electoral. Polls and public commentary are treated as noise to be managed until the next vote. But elections are not a licence to govern without scrutiny. They are a mechanism for accountability, and that is only one of many. Public outrage, the media’s questions and the protests of civil society are not obstacles to your mandate. They are the tools by which a democracy checks power between elections. Until Ghanaians go to the polls again, public commentary is one of the checks on your government’s conscience. And that conscience, on Obuasi, has been found wanting. It is my humble appeal, Mr President, that you direct the Criminal Investigations Department to expedite its probe and ensure that no political consideration interferes with justice for the 19 girls of Obuasi SHTS in the alleged rape cases. I humbly appeal again to Madam Vice President, Her Excellency Professor Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang, to break your silence, not with another call for “due process”, but with a clear, unequivocal condemnation of sexual violence and a concrete commitment to survivor support. Use your office to convene, to demand and to protect. That is not the work of a “Vice President for Women”. It is the work of a Vice President for Ghana. And I call on the NDC to remember that, with so much happening in the last month, I believe it is too early to be comfortable. You made a promise to the vulnerable. Please, do not trade their pain for political advantage. The girls of Obuasi are watching. So are the women who voted for you. So is history. Long live the President and the Vice President, and long live Ghana. Yours in citizenship, Rebecca Abafum Former Organising Secretary, Ghana Association of Writers

title: Lana Nusseibeh issues call for 'security and freedom' as Palestine backs UN bid
body: UAE Minister of State Lana Nusseibeh has spoken of her commitment to ensuring Palestinians and Israelis can live in 'security, freedom and dignity' after entering the running to be the next UN Secretary General. Ms Nusseibeh, who previously served as the country's representative to the organisation, welcomed Palestine's support for her candidacy, which was announced on Wednesday. Secretary General Antonio Guterres's second and final term will finish at the end of the year, and Ms Nusseibeh is attracting widespread support in the region for her bid to take on the position. The senior Emirati diplomat has played an instrumental role in UAE foreign policy in recent years and has been a prominent voice in calling for peace in Gaza, stressing the need to deliver crucial aid to the enclave. “Throughout my career, including at the United Nations, I have worked to advance a political pathway that enables Palestinians and Israelis to live in security, freedom and dignity,” Ms Nusseibeh said on social media platform X, in response to Palestine backing her campaign. “I deeply appreciate Palestine’s confidence in my candidacy.” In November 2025, she set out the importance of providing continuing assistance to needy civilians affected by the Gaza war during a visit to Cyprus aimed at bolstering aid efforts. Ms Nusseibeh said during the trip that a maritime corridor from Cyprus would be essential to efforts to step up the relief response. Ms Nusseibeh was appointed as Minister of State in September 2025 and has previously served as Assistant Minister for Political Affairs and Envoy of the Minister of Foreign Affairs. Before that, she was the UAE's ambassador to the UN for more than a decade until April 2024. UAE aid drive The Emirates remains at the forefront of efforts to provide financial assistance to Gaza and ensure a steady of flow of aid reaches needy civilians. In August, the UAE passed 1,000 days of continuous support, with more than Dh14.2 billion ($3.89 billion) of aid sent. That funding has helped set up a floating hospital in Egypt and two medical centres in Gaza and has brought thousands of medical patients, including many suffering from cancer and war-related injuries, to the Emirates to receive care. A US-backed ceasefire in October 2025 halted large-scale fighting in Gaza, but it has not ended Israeli strikes, and little progress has been made towards a permanent peace. Much of Gaza's population of more than two million has been displaced by the war, with chronic food shortages and limited access to health services and aid leading to a worsening humanitarian crisis.

title: ‘Some cannot afford to come home’ – Evacuees’ leader urges continued repatriation
body: The leader of the Aggrieved South Africa Evacuees, Michael Addo, has called for continued government support in repatriating Ghanaians stranded abroad, stressing that many citizens in South Africa and other countries are desperate to return home. According to him, several Ghanaians remain stranded overseas, with some unable to finance their return journeys despite their willingness to come back to Ghana. “We should rather encourage the government to continue with the repatriation because we still have individuals who are stranded not only in South Africa but in other countries who are willing to come home,” he stated. His appeal comes amid public scrutiny of the government’s reported GH¢49.72 million expenditure on the evacuation of 1,964 Ghanaians from South Africa. Mr Addo explained that the desire of stranded Ghanaians to return home is not motivated by the financial reintegration packages offered to returnees, but by the hardships they continue to endure abroad. “Not because of the reintegration package, but because they are tired. Some do not even have the funds to come home,” he emphasised. He maintained that the ongoing controversy surrounding the evacuation exercise should not discourage the government from extending assistance to other vulnerable Ghanaians seeking to return. Mr Addo consequently urged the public to support further repatriation efforts, stressing the importance of prioritising the welfare of stranded citizens while discussions over the cost of the exercise continue.

title: Ken Rosely wins Kwabre East NDC Organiser position
body: In the National Democratic Congress (NDC) constituency executives elections held on Saturday, 24 October 2026, Ken Rosely was elected the Organiser of the Kwabre East Constituency. Ken Rosely won resoundingly, securing 1,220 of the total votes cast. His competitors, Shaibu Abu and Mustapha Amidu, polled 450 and 384 votes respectively. Speaking to the media after his victory, Ken Rosely expressed gratitude to God and the delegates for the confidence reposed in him. He noted that party members had demonstrated great faith in his leadership and pledged to continue serving the NDC diligently while working to ensure the party retains power in 2028. Rosely called for unity, urging the defeated candidates to rally behind him and the other newly elected executives as they commit to winning Kwabre East for the NDC and improving on the votes secured by the party’s presidential candidate in the 2024 elections. “I am extremely happy and grateful to God and the delegates for the confidence reposed in me. Today, they have demonstrated that the NDC rewards commitment and hard work. They recognised the work I have done for the party and given me the mandate for another four years. “My message to the other candidates is that we must come together and work for the party. Elections can produce only one winner, so we have to put this behind us and commit fully to sustaining the party in power. Once again, thank you to the good people of Kwabre East, thank you to the NDC, and God bless Ghana,” he said. title: Trump blasts Norway over Nobel Peace Prize snub
body: US President Donald Trump attacked Norway during a campaign rally, calling it a “shit house country,” and said that Norwegian immigrants were not welcome in the United States because its Nobel Committee had not awarded him the Peace Prize. “Frankly, Norway sucks. Norway has become a shit house country, actually,” he said during Sunday’s speech. Since returning to the White House in January 2025, Trump has made no secret of his desire to win the prestigious Nobel Peace prize. Judge and former UN rights chief Navi Pillay of South Africa was this year’s recipient of the prize. Trump has called the committee’s choice “a disgraceful and embarrassing decision” and argued that the award should have gone to him. Trump said Sunday he would welcome immigrants from certain countries but not Norway “because I didn’t get the Nobel Prize.” “So I don’t want anybody from Norway,” he said during the rally in the Michigan town of Port Huron ahead of crucial US midterm elections on November 3. There was no official indication of a new US policy on Norwegian immigrants. Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide responded to Trump’s comments about the Nobel prize on Monday, maintaining that the committee is independent. “He knows very well that the Nobel Committee is independent. We have reminded him of that, in case anyone is wondering – and that is still the case,” he told national broadcaster NRK. Trump came under fire in 2018, during his first term, after using similar vulgar expressions to refer to Haiti and certain African countries. The post Trump blasts Norway over Nobel Peace Prize snub appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: GPHA celebrates industry excellence at 40th Anniversary Awards Night
body: The Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority (GPHA) has honoured outstanding customers, stakeholders and individuals for their contributions to the growth of Ghana’s maritime industry at a special Industry Awards Dinner held on Friday 23rd October, 2026 as part of activities marking the Authority’s 40th Anniversary celebration. Delivering the keynote address, the Minister for Transport Hon. Joseph Bukari Nikpe commended GPHA, its past and present leadership, staff and industry stakeholders for their collective role in transforming Ghana’s ports over the past four decades. He described the anniversary as a celebration of institutional growth, visionary leadership and enduring partnerships that have strengthened Ghana’s position in regional and international trade. Hon. Nikpe noted that Ghana’s ports remain strategic national assets that facilitate trade, create employment and support economic growth. He stressed the need for continuous improvements in port efficiency, digitalisation, multimodal connectivity, sustainability, workforce development and regional integration to position Ghana as the preferred logistics gateway for West Africa. According to him, achieving these objectives will require stronger collaboration among government, GPHA, private sector operators, customers and all stakeholders within the transport and logistics value chain. He urged industry players to sustain the spirit of partnership that has underpinned the Authority’s success over the years. The Chairman of the GPHA Board of Directors of GPHA, Johnson Asiedu Nketiah in his remarks, said the awards ceremony provided an opportunity to celebrate the individuals and institutions whose commitment, professionalism and partnership have contributed significantly to the Authority’s development and the growth of Ghana’s maritime sector. He acknowledged the critical role played by shipping lines, terminal operators, freight forwarders, transport operators, regulatory agencies and other stakeholders in supporting the Authority’s mission over the past 40 years. He reaffirmed the Board’s commitment to providing strategic direction and oversight to ensure that GPHA remains competitive and responsive to the evolving demands of global trade. Earlier, welcoming guests to the dinner, Director-General of GPHA, Major-General Paul Seidu Tanye-Kulono, described the Authority’s 40-year journey as a testament to the vision of its leaders, the dedication of employees and the confidence of stakeholders whose support has shaped the institution’s success. He noted that the growth of the ports has been driven by collaboration across the maritime and logistics value chain and expressed appreciation to stakeholders for their continued partnership and confidence in the Authority. Major-General Tanye-Kulono urged all stakeholders to build on the legacy of the past four decades by embracing innovation, strengthening partnerships and pursuing greater efficiency to ensure a stronger and more competitive port sector in the years ahead. The event brought together government officials, former Directors-General, members of the GPHA Board, management and staff, industry partners and customers to celebrate four decades of service, partnership and progress while recognising excellence across the maritime and logistics industry.

title: Defense startup wants to make genetically enhanced military dogs
body: A new defense tech startup aiming to produce genetically enhanced dogs for military and law enforcement use launched Friday with $200 million in seed funding. Texas-based Warhound was conceived by Anduril Industries founder Palmer Luckey and entrepreneur Ben Lamm, who started Colossal Biosciences , a company best known for its efforts to revive extinct species. In a press release , Warhound chief executive David Spirk said the company aims to reduce the United States’ dependence on a “shrinking” European supply chain for working dogs . “Our long-term goal is simple: healthier dogs, better-prepared teams, and more service members and first responders coming home safely,” Spirk said, adding that he cares deeply about “protecting people and helping the animals who support them.” Before joining Warhound, Spirk held several defense-related positions, including senior counsel at Palantir Technologies and chief data officer at both the Defense Department and U.S. Special Operations Command, or SOCOM. According to the announcement, Luckey and Lamm conceived the idea for Warhound years ago at the annual Moonshots Summit, a gathering where entrepreneurs discuss ambitious ideas. They recognized two challenges with military working-dog programs: Most of the canines never complete training, and the U.S. relies heavily on a foreign supply chain. According to Warhound, overseas suppliers provide 80% of military working dogs. The company also says the United States must train roughly 200 dogs to field 100, in part because so many fail to complete training. Warhound plans to combine the founders’ respective areas of expertise to address those problems. “Colossal’s science will help produce healthier dogs with characteristics suited to demanding missions, while Anduril’s technology will give dogs and their handlers greater awareness and protection in the field,” the company said. Warhound also said it will work with the American Humane Society to safeguard the animals’ health and welfare. The company said its goal is to reduce training washouts, limit the number of dogs entering intensive training unnecessarily and enable safer, more effective missions.

Texas-based Warhound was conceived by Anduril Industries founder Palmer Luckey and entrepreneur Ben Lamm, who started Colossal Biosciences , a company best known for its efforts to revive extinct species. In a press release , Warhound chief executive David Spirk said the company aims to reduce the United States’ dependence on a “shrinking” European supply chain for working dogs . “Our long-term goal is simple: healthier dogs, better-prepared teams, and more service members and first responders coming home safely,” Spirk said, adding that he cares deeply about “protecting people and helping the animals who support them.” Before joining Warhound, Spirk held several defense-related positions, including senior counsel at Palantir Technologies and chief data officer at both the Defense Department and U.S. Special Operations Command, or SOCOM. According to the announcement, Luckey and Lamm conceived the idea for Warhound years ago at the annual Moonshots Summit, a gathering where entrepreneurs discuss ambitious ideas. They recognized two challenges with military working-dog programs: Most of the canines never complete training, and the U.S. relies heavily on a foreign supply chain. According to Warhound, overseas suppliers provide 80% of military working dogs. The company also says the United States must train roughly 200 dogs to field 100, in part because so many fail to complete training. Warhound plans to combine the founders’ respective areas of expertise to address those problems. “Colossal’s science will help produce healthier dogs with characteristics suited to demanding missions, while Anduril’s technology will give dogs and their handlers greater awareness and protection in the field,” the company said. Warhound also said it will work with the American Humane Society to safeguard the animals’ health and welfare. The company said its goal is to reduce training washouts, limit the number of dogs entering intensive training unnecessarily and enable safer, more effective missions.

title: General Staff confirms strike on Yelets plant producing batteries for aerial bombs and Iskander-M missiles
body:
According to Ukrinform, the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reported this on Facebook .
Specifically, the strike targeted a production facility for power sources used in enemy weapons at the “Energia” plant in Yelets, Lipetsk Oblast, Russian Federation.
“A fire broke out on the plant’s premises. The strike complicates the Russian Armed Forces’ production of power sources for missiles, guided aerial bombs, and other weapons,” the statement reads.
As noted by the General Staff, “Energia” is the sole manufacturer of batteries for air bomb guidance and correction modules, and also produces batteries for the “Iskander-M” operational-tactical missile systems and sea-based cruise missiles.
Additionally, based on the results of previous strikes, the destruction of the main microchip production workshop has been confirmed, and the building and servers of the “Proton-Elektrotex” enterprise in the city of Orel, Oryol Region, Russia, have been damaged. The strike took place on October 23.
“This complicates the enemy’s production of components for cruise and ballistic missiles, which it uses to strike Ukrainian cities,” the General Staff commented.
On October 23, a storage, preparation, and launch site for attack UAVs in the Donetsk area was struck. Three buildings used for preparing and equipping attack UAVs and one launch rail were damaged.
The General Staff noted that this reduces the Russians’ ability to attack Ukraine and civilian infrastructure with various types of drones.
On October 24, the “Tolyattikauchuk” plant in the city of Tolyatti, Samara Oblast, Russian Federation, was struck. A process pipeline, two butyl rubber production units, and one rectification unit were damaged.
“This disrupts the production chain for solid rocket fuel used in tactical and ballistic missiles,” the General Staff emphasized.
The General Staff stressed that the Ukrainian Defense Forces are striking enemy military targets within the framework of the right to self-defense guaranteed by Article 51 of the UN Charter.
“Operations against key enemy military targets will continue until Russia’s armed aggression against Ukraine ceases completely,” the General Staff added.
As reported by Ukrinform, Russian authorities confirmed fires at several industrial facilities in the Voronezh region following a nighttime drone attack.

title: “I’ll always defend my colleagues” – Ablakwa says over S.A. evacuation allegation
body: Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa has defended the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and its finance officers against allegations of financial irregularities in the evacuation of Ghanaians from South Africa. Speaking at a press conference on Monday, October 26, organised by some of the evacuees, Mr Ablakwa said he would continue to defend his reputation, the ministry and the officials responsible for managing the funds. He insisted that no money had been misappropriated, despite media reports and allegations by the Minority in parliament regarding the disbursement of funds for the exercise. Although he acknowledged that he did not personally distribute the reported GH¢5,500 to every evacuee, the minister expressed confidence in the work of the ministry’s finance officers, maintaining that they had performed their duties diligently. “Now, I will always defend my colleagues at the foreign ministry, even though I did not personally hand over these funds, but I know that the team at the finance directorate of my ministry, the NADMO team, the National Security team, these are all public servants of impeccable integrity and nobody will seek to take advantage of traumatised evacuees from another country,” he said. The press conference comes amid growing scrutiny of the government’s expenditure on the evacuation exercise, following media fact-checks and claims by the Minority that not every evacuee received the reported GH¢5,500. Questions have also been raised about discrepancies in the dates of birth recorded in some of the documents provided by the ministry, further intensifying calls for clarification on the payments and the documentation process. The controversy centres on the transparency and accountability of the funds used to evacuate Ghanaians from South Africa, as well as the support reportedly provided to those who returned home. Mr Ablakwa’s defence is the latest development in the ongoing debate over the management of the exercise, with questions about the payments and supporting records remaining central to the public discussion.

title: Kremlin briefs media on Alyoshki agreements, decision on trilateral talks
body:
MOSCOW, October 26. /TASS/. Agreements on a humanitarian operation in Alyoshki in the Kherson Region, a decision on the resumption of trilateral talks on Ukraine, and the outcome of the parliamentary elections in Serbia were among the key topics of Russian presidential press secretary Dmitry Peskov’s Monday briefing.
TASS has summarized the Kremlin spokesman’s key statements.
Russian President Vladimir Putin will hold a meeting with Gazprombank Board Chairman Andrey Akimov on Monday.
The president continues his preparations for the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) summit and the third Russia-Africa summit, both of which will take place this week.
The Russian leader is scheduled to hold a series of bilateral meetings on the sidelines of these forums.
The decision on resuming trilateral talks "does not imply any restrictions on combat operations."
Russian forces continue delivering massive strikes on Ukraine’s defense sector: "Our armed forces are continuing the special military operation, delivering massive and sustained strikes against Ukraine’s military-industrial complex, as well as military and military-related targets."
The territorial issue may, in one way or another, become a subject of discussion during efforts to reach a peace settlement on Ukraine: "All these issues may, in one way or another, become a subject of discussion during efforts to reach a peace settlement."
A serious discussion covering every little detail is needed to settle the conflict in Ukraine: "A very serious discussion lies ahead, one that involves a vast number of details."
Russia will not publicly discuss details of Ukraine settlement talks as it may get in the way of the potential peace process: "We would prefer not to discuss these details in public, as we believe it would undermine a potential future peace process."
Agreements on a humanitarian operation in Alyoshki could serve as a precedent for missions in other areas: "For humanitarian purposes, absolutely. Especially when it comes to a direct, very positive, and coordinated involvement of the American side, American negotiators, and US First Lady Melania Trump in the process. We highly appreciate these efforts, and, of course, this could set a precedent."
Russia hopes that Kiev will fulfill all agreements regarding the humanitarian mission in Alyoshki: "We would like to hope that the Ukrainian side will fulfill all the agreements that were reached with the direct participation of American negotiators representing Melania Trump."
Moscow welcomes Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva’s victory in Brazil’s presidential election: "We welcome Mr. Lula’s victory."
Lula da Silva is doing a great deal to develop cooperation with Russia, both bilaterally and on the international stage more broadly: "He is doing a great deal not only to develop bilateral relations, but also to advance processes within BRICS and other organizations, as well as cooperation with Russia on the international stage."
Moscow hopes these processes will continue: "We hope all these processes will continue in the future."
Moscow highly values the contribution that former Serbian President and Serbian Progressive Party leader Aleksandar Vucic has made to the development of bilateral relations between Russia and Serbia: "We acknowledge the results of the elections held in Serbia. We highly value the contribution that Vucic has made to the development of our bilateral relations."
Moscow hopes that Vucic will continue playing a role in the development of bilateral relations with Russia, even in opposition: "We know that Mr. Vucic will remain active in politics and we hope that, even in opposition, he will continue to contribute to the development of bilateral relations [between Serbia and Russia]."
Russia will continue doing everything it can to foster the development of relations with Serbia: "For our part, we intend to continue to do everything possible to promote the development of our relations with Belgrade, but, as you know, it takes two to tango."
Russia hopes that the new political force coming to power in Serbia will understand that cooperation with Moscow is beneficial for Belgrade: "When it comes to the new political force that will come to power as a result of the elections [in Serbia], we would like to express the hope that its actions will also be constructively aimed at further developing relations [with Russia]. And that these new political forces will understand that cooperation with Russia is in Serbia's interest because it brings benefits to Serbia. It is, first and foremost, advantageous for Serbia."
Russia welcomes the International Weightlifting Federation’s (IWF) decision to hold the 2030 World Weightlifting Championships in Moscow, viewing it as an important step toward depoliticizing sports: "Of course, we welcome such decisions. This is a very important step toward depoliticizing sports."
"Russia must return to the global sporting community as a full-fledged member, because this community cannot function fully without Russia’s participation."
The question of bidding to host the Olympics in Russia again is not currently on the agenda: "One must weigh all the pros and cons when making such decisions, of course. For now, this issue is not on the agenda."

title: Machar: ‘I am not leader of White Army’
body: Former First Vice President Riek Machar on Monday denied leading the White Army, telling the special court in Juba that he does not command the armed youth group accused of taking part in the March 2025 attack on a military garrison in Nasir, Upper Nile State. Presenting his defence statement during the 124th session of the trial on Monday, Machar, the fifth accused in the case, described the White Army as a loosely organised, community-based armed youth group associated particularly with Nuer communities in parts of Upper Nile and Jonglei states. “The charge that I lead armed civilians is false. The charge that armed civilians are only in Nuer areas is also false,” Machar told the court. The 74-year-old leader of the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-in-Opposition (SPLM-IO) said the movement had no political or military control over the White Army, describing its members as ordinary civilians, most of them young people. White Army structure “I first want to explain what is referred to as the White Army. The White Army are ordinary civilians, the majority of whom are youths. I refer to these civilians as youth. They sometimes include women who accompany them and act as ICRC if one of them is wounded,” Machar said. He said the White Army was neither commanded nor supported by the SPLM/A-IO, describing its members as civilians who take up weapons to defend their land rather than as a militarily trained force. “They are armed with firearms and spears,” he said. “They are not militarily trained. Once they feel the need to take up arms, spears or any other object for fighting when fighting arises, they come from their homes or towns. They have no barracks and are not registered in any SPLA-IO document.” Machar denied that the White Army received military support or food supplies from the SPLM/A-IO. “They don’t get any military support from the SPLM-IO, nor do they get food supplies from the SPLA-IO. They organise themselves on their own, from their clans or at lower levels under headmen, sub-chiefs and paramount chiefs,” he said. “They loosely associate on some matters with their tribesmen at each level. They are volunteer warriors at each of those levels mentioned. They elect and remove their leaders, mostly yearly or at any time they wish.” Machar said the White Army should not be classified as a militia because its organizational structure doesn’t fit that definition. He described its members instead as traditional African village warriors whose weapons had become more advanced because of the proliferation of modern small arms. “They are not sponsored by the SPLA-IO. They are therefore unlike Dutkubeny and Mathiang Anyoor. They may have similarities with Gelweng, Titweng or Monyemiji and Lokoya youth, or various age sets of the Murle,” he said. “Any male youth from 18 years of age could be elected as their leader by the Nuer youths. They are the largest part of the Nuer community. Fighting them means fighting the community of that area; they are the community.” Machar said this was why the British had taken more than 30 years to establish an administration in Nuer territory, adding that they eventually abandoned the use of force and resorted to peaceful means. The court adjourned the hearing until Wednesday, October 28, 2026, when Machar is expected to continue his defence testimony. Charges and allegations Machar and his seven co-defendants face charges of murder, conspiracy, terrorism, treason, destruction of public property and crimes against humanity. Machar is under house arrest, while the other defendants are being held at National Security Service facilities in Juba. The co-defendants are Puot Kang Chol, Mam Pal Dhuor, Gatwech Lam Puoch, Lt. Gen. Gabriel Duop Lam, Camilo Gatmai Kel, Mading Yak Riek and Dominic Gatgok Riek. Prosecutors allege that SPLA-IO forces allied with the White Army killed 257 South Sudan People’s Defence Forces soldiers, including commander Gen. David Majur Dak, and destroyed or captured military equipment worth about $58 million during the March 2025 attack on the Nasir military garrison. The post Machar: ‘I am not leader of White Army’ appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: KPMG-GIPS 2026 Procurement Enhancement Survey: 86% of respondents say procurement fraud occurs in their organisations
body: A KPMG-Ghana Institute of Procurement and Supply (GIPS) 2026 Procurement Enhancement Survey Report has revealed that 12% of respondents have experienced retaliation after reporting suspected fraud, compared with 26% in 2023. Also, 86% of respondents indicated that procurement fraud occurs in their organisations, but to varying degrees, compared with 89% in 2023. Again, 62% of respondents reported the desire for personal financial gain as the primary motivation for engaging in procurement fraud. The 2026 survey indicated improvements in procurement governance, including stronger awareness of anti-fraud policies, procurement monitoring, investigation processes and performance measurement. However, fraud remains a persistent risk, highlighting the need for organisations to embed fraud risk assessments into enterprise risk management frameworks, regularly assess the effectiveness of procurement controls and strengthen oversight through periodic reporting to executive management and the board. Most respondents who suspected procurement fraud reported it through established channels, demonstrating a willingness to report potential misconduct. However, limited access to anonymous reporting channels remains a concern. The report said organisations should strengthen reporting mechanisms by implementing anonymous reporting channels and provide regular fraud awareness training to improve understanding of fraud risks, reporting obligations and escalation procedures. The 2026 Procurement Enhancement Survey is the second edition of the KPMG-GIPS Procurement Survey and builds on the baseline established in 2023. Respondents were asked about their awareness, experiences and perceptions of procurement processes controls, fraud risks and related practices within their organisations. They were, however, not required to identify their organisations. The survey received 505 responses, and they were mainly procurement practitioners.

title: Kano students win national entrepreneurship contest with AI farming platform
body:
Students from Sunflower School, Kano State , have won Junior Achievement Nigeria’s (JAN) 2026 National Company of the Year Competition with an artificial intelligence-powered platform designed to help farmers make better agricultural decisions.
The team, Agrolens Technologies, comprising Fadillah Abdulsalam, Ruqayya Jallo, Hayfa Mukhtar and Maryam Butu, won a US$250 cash prize and an all-expenses-paid trip to Cape Town, South Africa, where it will represent Nigeria at the African Company of the Year Competition.
Their innovation, AgroLens AI, is a free mobile platform that combines crop disease and pest detection, treatment recommendations, real-time market prices, connections to buyers and information on agricultural financing.
AgroLens AI supports English, Hausa, Yoruba, Igbo and Nigerian Pidgin. Its voice-enabled features are designed to make agricultural information more accessible to farmers with limited literacy or those who find speaking easier than typing.
The team’s victory was announced at the national competition and a youth entrepreneurship convening held in Lagos on Wednesday, 21 October, under the theme, “Augmenting Innovation: Equipping Nigeria’s Youth for Entrepreneurship and Livelihoods in a Changing Economy.”
New Era Company of Community Secondary School, Asokoro, Abuja, placed second, winning US$150, while Nexora International School Lagos came third with US$100. New Era also received an additional US$100 after winning the Best Corporate Social Responsibility Award.
The competition is part of JAN’s School-to-Work Educational Transition for Long-Term Youth Fulfilment (SET4LYF) programme, which equips girls with practical skills to pursue further education, entrepreneurship and employment.
Through activities including Ideathons, JA DEEP, and the JA Company Programme, participants gain experience developing business ideas, solving practical problems, and presenting products and services.
A report published by THISDAY highlighted the programme’s broader reach, saying SET4LYF reached more than 98,000 girls in its first two years. The initiative seeks to bridge the gap between classroom learning and opportunities beyond school.
Speaking at the event, Olaolu Akogun, acting executive director of Junior Achievement Nigeria, said young people needed practical skills to adapt to an economy increasingly shaped by technology.
“The young people we are equipping today cannot afford to be prepared only for the opportunities that existed yesterday. Technology is changing how we work, trade and create value. Our responsibility is to ensure that young Nigerians, especially girls, have the skills, confidence and practical experience to participate in and shape that changing economy,” Mr Akogun said.
He highlighted JAN’s partnerships with the National Youth Service Corps, the Joint National Association of Persons with Disabilities and state governments. He called for sustained collaboration to expand access to entrepreneurship education.
Aliyu Abdullahi, assistant director of education and youth development at the Ministry of Youth and Social Development, delivered the keynote address on behalf of the minister.
He called for an education system that prioritises practical competence and problem-solving alongside academic qualifications.
“Degrees alone are not enough. We must move young people from being consumers of digital technology to becoming creators, problem-solvers and innovators. Training must lead to opportunity, and opportunity must lead to livelihoods,” Mr Abdullahi said.
He advocated stronger collaboration among government, educators, and businesses to integrate entrepreneurship, apprenticeships, internships, and practical skills into learning.
He also stressed the importance of connecting youth development programmes to market access and emerging opportunities in the digital economy.
Beyond the main competition, Agrolens Technologies received the Product Innovation and Operational Excellence Award, presented by Food Concepts.
UOFAM Group of Companies from Unique Secondary School, Akure, won the Public Choice Award and US$50. Meanwhile, EcoFlame Innovation received the Excellence in Project Management and Execution Award from the Project Management Institute Nigeria.
Ezekiel Sekegh was named Outstanding Volunteer of the Year, while Isaac Egbe of Sunflower School received the Best Facilitator Award.
In a separate opportunity, 15 girls from participating schools were selected for a fully sponsored leadership training camp in Ghana scheduled for March 2027. Delta Air Lines is sponsoring the programme, which recognises leadership, teamwork, commitment and excellence.
Edwin Idoko, JAN’s Kano State programme officer, credited the state’s education authorities, volunteers and field officers with supporting the students’ achievement. He said the victory marked Kano State’s third consecutive year of success at the national competition.
The event also featured a panel discussion on bridging foundational learning with entrepreneurship and market access. Participants examined how mentoring, project management, disability inclusion and private-sector partnerships could help young people turn classroom learning into viable businesses.
The 2026 competition was supported by FirstBank Nigeria, the Project Management Institute Nigeria, Food Concepts and Nigerian Bottling Company.
Agrolens Technologies will now take its agricultural innovation to the continental competition in Cape Town, where it will represent Nigeria against student-led enterprises from other African countries.

title: Ebola Index Case in Stable Condition Before Evacuation Abroad, Says Pate
body: Onyebuchi Ezigbo in Abuja The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, has said that index case for Nigeria’s first imported Ebola virus disease was clinically in stable condition before being moved to Switzerland Monday morning. Pate who confirmed the evacuation of the Ebola patient via his X- handle said he granted the approval for referral treatment abroad on behalf of the federal government “I Confirm that, with my approval, earlier this morning, the index case for Nigeria’s first imported Ebola virus disease departed Abuja for Switzerland. “The index patient was clinically much improved, stable, conscious, communicating, and her clinical laboratory test results closing towards baseline. “This does not mean she is not still infectious, hence the strict protocols in place” he said. According to the Minister, the patient was evacuated along with her spouse whom he said has remained asymptomatic. “I thank all the various clinical staff for the high quality care they provided the patient as well as the public health personnel who ensured the evacuation was carried out in line with best public health measures for such evacuations. “We will provide further updates later this afternoon after the patient and her spouse lands successfully in their destination. “All public health measures are continuing to ensure successful containment of the imported virus. I urge Nigerians to remain vigilant and rely on information from credible sources”, Pate added.

title: Claims some South Africa evacuees received only GH¢500 or GH¢5,000 are false – Aggrieved evacuee group
body: The leader of the Aggrieved South Africa Evacuees, Micheal Addo, has dismissed claims that some Ghanaians repatriated from South Africa received only GH¢500 in transport allowances while others were given GH¢5,000 as reintegration support. According to him, all members of the group received their respective support packages upon arrival in Ghana, contrary to allegations circulating in the public domain. “The claims that some people received only the 500 transportation allowance while others received only the 5,000 reintegration allowance are all false. We want to place on record that we all received the package on our respective dates of arrival,” he stated. His comments come amid public scrutiny of the government’s reported GH¢49.72 million expenditure on evacuating 1,964 Ghanaians from South Africa. Mr Addo explained that the returnees were provided with reintegration packages to support their resettlement and adjustment to life in Ghana. He further alleged that some members of the group had received telephone calls and coaching intended to persuade them to make statements against the government. “We are aware that some members of our groups have received calls and coaching to speak against the government, but our conscience will not allow us to do so,” he alleged. He stressed that political affiliation should not influence the accounts given by beneficiaries of the evacuation exercise, insisting that honesty must take precedence over partisan considerations. “Even if we support the opposition party rather than the government of the day, it is only fair that we state the facts and refuse to allow petty politics to make us liars,” he said. Mr Addo maintained that the group was not seeking to defend the government against legitimate scrutiny but rather to clarify what its members had received. “We are not here to speak for the government, but we are certain in our hearts that we received the best treatment and support as Ghanaians when we needed it most,” he added. He reiterated the group’s appreciation for the assistance provided during the evacuation and urged the public to distinguish between legitimate demands for accountability and what he described as inaccurate claims about the support received by returnees.

title: Dubai to redistribute surplus food from weddings and events to reduce waste
body: Dubai has unveiled plans to reduce food waste by collecting and distributing excess food from wedding celebrations to beneficiaries. The UAE Food Bank and Dubai’s Community Development Authority (CDA) have signed an agreement and laid the groundwork to safely collect, transport and distribute surplus food. The partnership expands the initiative's community impact while promoting food sustainability and social responsibility. It supports the objectives of the Dubai Social Agenda 33 by encouraging responsible consumption, strengthening community participation and advancing food security. Under the agreement, the two entities will co-ordinate the collection and redistribution of surplus food from weddings and events identified by the CDA. All donations will follow approved regulations and food safety requirements to ensure food suitable for consumption reaches those in need. The MoU also provides for joint awareness campaigns and community programmes to promote food preservation, sustainable consumption and responsible food management. The co-operation will further support volunteer participation in relevant activities, strengthening community engagement and encouraging people to contribute to humanitarian and charitable initiatives. Dr Ahmed Al Hashemi, chief executive of the Social Regulation and Services Sector at the CDA, said the Dubai Weddings initiative will play an important role in supporting family formation and stability, and that the partnership would extend its benefits to the wider community. “By ensuring that surplus food from weddings and events is safely recovered and redistributed to those in need, we are creating additional opportunities for giving while encouraging responsible consumption and the efficient use of resources,” he said. He added that the partnership reflects Dubai’s values of solidarity and generosity and demonstrates the importance of co-operation between government entities and humanitarian organisations. Wider mission Manal Obaid bin Yaroof, head of the UAE Food Bank’s executive team, said the partnership would strengthen the bank’s ability to recover surplus food and ensure it reaches beneficiaries through safe and organised collection and distribution processes. Extending the programme to the Dubai Weddings initiative would help preserve valuable food resources, reduce waste and turn sustainable practices into tangible community benefits, she said. Ms bin Yaroof added that the agreement supports the food bank’s wider humanitarian and charitable mission by raising awareness of food preservation, encouraging volunteering and strengthening co-operation with government entities. The partnership aims to expand the reach of food recovery initiatives, improve surplus food management and promote a culture of giving and social responsibility across Dubai. The agreement forms part of the CDA’s continuing efforts to enhance the Dubai Weddings initiative and broaden its contribution to community well-being. It also supports the UAE Food Bank’s commitment to developing a sustainable approach to surplus food management, ensuring that food fit for consumption is recovered and redistributed while reducing waste and conserving resources.

title: Man dies in Kherson hospital from injuries sustained in Russian drone attack, another in grave condition
body:
A man wounded in a Russian drone attack the previous day has died in a Kherson hospital, reported Head of the Regional Military Administration Oleksandr Prokudin.

"Yesterday, a Russian drone attacked a minibus in the Central district of Kherson. Seven people were injured. Unfortunately, one of the victims, a 67-year-old man, died in the hospital's reception department," Prokudin wrote on Telegram on Monday.

According to the Regional Military Administration, another man remains in critical condition. Medics continue to fight for his life.

title: Karate-do: Ashesi University’s Kevin Bigirimana wins silver at Japanese Ambassador Championships
body: Ashesi University karate athlete Kevin Bigirimana won silver in the Lightweight Division at the 2026 Japanese Ambassador Karate-do Championships on October 24. Bigirimana secured victories in his first three bouts before losing the final by a single point to an opponent from Kokusai Karate Club. His performance earned him a silver medal at the competition, highlighting his ability to combine academic pursuits with sporting excellence. Ashesi Karate Dojo coach Dickson Acolatse praised Bigirimana’s achievement, describing it as evidence of what students can accomplish through consistency and determination. “As a coach at Ashesi Karate Dojo, Kevin’s silver-medal achievement is proof that with consistency and determination, students can pursue excellence both academically and in sports,” Acolatse said. “It shows you do not have to choose between academic excellence and sporting achievement. You can develop both.” The Japanese Ambassador’s Cup Karate-do Championships brings karate athletes together to compete across different divisions, providing a platform for them to demonstrate their skills and discipline.

title: Oman Investment Authority Plans $500 Million Fund for Central Asia and Caucasus
body: The Oman Investment Authority (OIA) and five other investment institutions have agreed to establish a private equity fund for Central Asia and the Caucasus that aims to raise $500 million . A letter of intent was signed in Beijing on October 20, with a formal agreement expected in early November 2026. The other participating institutions are China Investment Corporation and Shenwan Hongyuan Securities, both based in China; Uzbekistan’s Fund for Reconstruction and Development; Turkey’s Armed Forces Pension Fund, known as OYAK; and the Eurasian Development Bank (EDB). The initiative is led by OIA. The fund will be known as the Central Asia and Caucasus Private Equity Fund. An Omani company is expected to manage it. OIA has identified Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan as prospective investment markets. Priority sectors will include logistics, renewable energy, mining, agriculture, food production, and healthcare. The fund plans to acquire ownership stakes in regional companies, providing them with capital to expand their operations. The organizers will seek investment from sovereign wealth funds and other institutional investors, although they have not disclosed how much of the $500 million target has been committed. Daniyar Imangaliyev, deputy chairman of the EDB’s Management Board, said the fund would help regional companies expand into new markets while attracting additional international capital to the bank’s member states. The initiative builds on the EDB’s cooperation with Oman. On October 6, the bank and the sultanate’s Ministry of Finance signed an agreement governing the EDB’s operations in the country. This marked a step toward Oman’s potential accession as a shareholder of the bank, which would make it the first Gulf state to join.

title: Ensign Global, University of Utah graduate 20 entrepreneurs under business creation programme
body: Ensign Global University and the University of Utah have graduated 20 entrepreneurs from the second cohort of the Master of Business Creation (MBC) programme, an initiative designed to help business owners strengthen their enterprises and create employment opportunities. The programme takes a practical approach to entrepreneurship education, allowing participants to apply lessons in areas such as marketing, financial projections and human resource management directly to their businesses. President of Ensign Global University, Professor Stephen Alder, said the initiative could help address Africa’s employment challenges by equipping graduates to create jobs rather than rely solely on existing vacancies. Speaking at the graduation ceremony, Professor Alder said the continent produces millions of higher education graduates each year, while the number of available jobs remains limited. “If you look at the African continent, for example, there are about 12 million graduates from higher education every year. Yet it’s estimated that there are reasonably three million jobs for those 12 million graduates, meaning that three quarters of the graduates are not going to find successful employment,” he said. He said the business creation approach was intended to help participants build their own economic opportunities instead of depending entirely on the labour market. “This business creation approach is now designed to say, we’re not sort of creating graduates and then send them out to hope they find a job. But instead, they are creating their own future,” Professor Alder added. Programme focuses on existing businesses The MBC programme is delivered through a partnership between Ensign Global University and the University of Utah, based in Salt Lake City in the United States. Global Director of the programme, Jeff Davis, said it differs from conventional graduate programmes because admission places greater emphasis on business ownership than on academic qualifications alone. “We call it an MBA for entrepreneurs. So the most important criteria is not so much that you have an undergraduate degree but that you actually have a company. So you come in with a company to have a highly applied curriculum,” he said. Mr Davis explained that participants complete assignments based on their own businesses rather than relying on conventional examinations and theoretical case studies. “Every assignment, there are no quizzes, no tests, no textbooks, no Harvard case studies. Everything is an assignment on your company. Marketing plans, financial projections, HR organization,” he said. The approach is intended to help entrepreneurs apply what they learn to practical business challenges while developing strategies for growth. Building an entrepreneurial community Mr Davis said the programme also seeks to establish a community of entrepreneurs who can support one another beyond the classroom. “I think one of the most important things we’re building is not so much a program in Africa but we’re building a movement, a community of builders and dreamers and doers,” he said. On post-graduation support, he pointed to opportunities available through the University of Utah’s Lassonde Entrepreneur Institute, which supports entrepreneurs and business development. He said the institutions were also exploring possible funding opportunities for businesses in Africa. “At the University of Utah we have a very nationally ranked Institute called the Lassonde Entrepreneur Institute and we have programs for graduates from the MBC and people beyond the curriculum there in the United States. And so we’re also exploring funding for the companies here in Africa as we continue to build our entrepreneurs here in Africa,” he said. Applying classroom lessons to business Facilitating Lecturer Nana Dr Oboafo Kwamena Asumang Appiah I said the programme enables entrepreneurs to translate classroom learning into practical improvements within their businesses. “It’s Masters of Business Creation. It’s experiential, meaning that whatever you learn in school, you apply it directly to your business,” he said. He explained that participants are expected to implement lessons immediately, particularly in areas such as financial management and business development. “So if you talk about finances, you go and apply the financial models that we taught you in the classroom to your business, and then you take action,” he added. The graduation of the second cohort marks another stage in the partnership’s efforts to support entrepreneurs as they develop their businesses and pursue growth. The programme is expected to help participating founders strengthen their operations, expand their enterprises and create employment opportunities, while building connections with other entrepreneurs.

title: Elbit Systems Awarded Approximately $200 Million in Contracts for Airborne ISTAR and Training Solutions in Asia-Pacific
body:
Haifa, Israel. Elbit Systems Ltd. announced on Oct 26, 2026 that, it was awarded contracts in an aggregate value of approximately $200 million from a country in Asia-Pacific for the supply of airborne Intelligence, Surveillance, Target Acquisition and Reconnaissance (“ISTAR”) and Training solutions. The contracts will be performed over a period of up to 5 years.



Under the contracts, Elbit Systems will supply the SPECTRO™ 12 multispectral Intelligence, Surveillance, Reconnaissance (“ISR”) and targeting payload for integration on helicopters. The SPECTRO 12 is the latest addition to Elbit Systems’ SPECTRO family of airborne ISR and targeting payloads, introducing a compact multispectral payload designed for platforms with strict size, weight and power constraints. The SPECTRO 12 combines high-resolution multispectral sensing, precision targeting technologies, including a Laser designator, and AI-powered image processing, enabling long-range target detection, identification, tracking and engagement performance in complex operational environments and adverse weather conditions.

The contracts further include follow-on support and upgrade services for airborne live training systems installed on aircraft and used in live virtual constructive and virtual combat training scenarios. The systems support realistic air-to-air and air-to-ground training, including real-time combat simulation, weapon scoring and mission debriefing capabilities, contributing to enhanced pilot readiness and training effectiveness.

In addition, under the contracts Elbit Systems will supply advanced Head-Up Display (HUD) systems. The HUD systems feature high-resolution display technologies, enhanced video capabilities and low power consumption, supporting day and night operations across a range of airborne platforms.

Bezhalel (Butzi) Machlis, President and CEO of Elbit Systems: "Elbit Systems’ airborne solutions combine advanced technologies with extensive operational experience across a wide range of mission environments. We are proud to provide our customers with innovative capabilities that enhance mission effectiveness, situational awareness and operational readiness across a broad spectrum of airborne missions."

title: PRODUCT OF THE WEEK: VITA 62 Power Supply from Vicor
body:
This week’s product, the VITA 62 Power Supply from Vicor, is a commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) power supply engineered for 3U and 6U OpenVPX systems and aimed at avionics, autonomous systems, aircraft radar, shipboard platforms, and other defense applications.
The Vicor VITA 62-compliant 3U power supply is based on Vicor DCM™ DC-DC converter technology, which provides superior density in a low-profile package. This solution can provide up to 600W within the 3U package. Employing high efficiency, two-sided conduction-cooled modules, the Vicor VITA 62 converter meets the 85°C operational temperature (at the card edge) while powering the downstream loads.
Aircraft radar systems have unique power and current requirements driven by the need for high-peak power, rapid scanning, and strict environmental constraints (weight, space, and altitude). These radars require sophisticated power management of Vicor’s VITA 62 power supply to handle rapid, high-current pulses for transmitter modules while operating within the stringent limits of aircraft electrical systems. The VITA 62 solution is used in harsh environments, that meets the power and current requirements, and can be deployed quickly.
