title: U.S. Army leaders focus on drones, electronic warfare and data to strengthen readiness
body: U.S. Army Europe and Africa leaders discussed unmanned aircraft, electronic warfare and battlefield data at AUSA 2026 in Washington on October 12–14. The discussions drew on operational challenges in Europe to identify capability requirements and strengthen readiness. Commanders also examined requirements for large-scale combat and multi-domain operations. They exchanged lessons learned and stressed the need to integrate U.S. forces with allies and partners. “AUSA gave us the opportunity to bring Europe’s operational challenges directly to Army leaders and industry partners, helping shape solutions that strengthen deterrence and give our Soldiers and Allies the capabilities they need to win,” said Brig. Gen. Steven Carpenter, commanding general of Multi-Domain Command Europe. His command joined three other formations in presenting operational perspectives at the Association of the United States Army’s annual meeting. V Corps, Multi-Domain Command Europe, 7th Army Training Command and 10th Army Air and Missile Defense Command delivered six presentations during the October 12–14 event in Washington. The Army said the exchanges helped identify capability requirements and reinforced the importance of integrated operations with allied and partner forces. The discussions will continue at LANDEURO 2026 in Wiesbaden, Germany, on December 3–4. Hosted by AUSA in partnership with U.S. Army Europe and Africa, the event will bring military, industry and government representatives together to turn shared priorities into fielded solutions.

title: Despite thousands of sanctions, Russia stands firm — Medvedev
body:
MOSCOW, October 26. /TASS/. More than 30,000 sanctions have been imposed against Russia, yet the country has held firm and continues to develop, Dmitry Medvedev, the chairman of the United Russia party, said at the third meeting of the standing committee of the For the Freedom of Nations! movement.
"As is well known, more than 30,000 illegal, unilateral restrictive measures have been imposed against Russia. You might think - 30,000! - but Russia stands firm; it continues to hold its ground and even develop, despite the pressure of these 30,000 measures," he said.

title: EchoHouse founders Beryl and Bright Agyekum-Ayaaba graduate as joint valedictorians
body: Nearly two decades after turning a university magazine into EchoHouse, a marketing agency operating in eight countries, married founders Beryl Agyekum-Ayaaba and Bright Mamud-Ayaaba have reached another milestone in their journey together, graduating as joint valedictorians from a Master of Business Creation programme. Together since 2006 and married for 10 years, the couple has built their business and personal lives in tandem, learning to balance marriage, parenthood, entrepreneurship and academic demands while growing EchoHouse from a campus idea into an international company. For Bright, sharing the honour with his wife was both surreal and deeply personal. “The experience of being called on stage as a valedictorian together with my wife was quite surreal,” he said. “It’s not been an easy experience through the academics and working together as well, but we’ve kept pushing on. It’s been a whole year of rigorous assignments and meetings and all that, but we managed to combine that with work. It hasn’t been easy, but we are very proud of ourselves today.” The achievement followed a demanding year in which the couple combined academic work with the responsibilities of running a growing business. It also reflected a partnership built around shared ambition, resilience and an understanding of each other’s strengths. Even as they shared the spotlight, Bright was quick to credit his wife. “For me, I’ve always said it should be Beryl. She pushes me more, so she basically deserves it. I’m the guy in the back, you know, so I was very happy when we both got it, but I’ll give it to her. It’s hers,” he said. His remarks offered a glimpse into a relationship in which success is celebrated collectively rather than claimed individually. The couple’s entrepreneurial journey began while they were university students. In 2008, they started what would become EchoHouse as a magazine intended to tell the university’s story. The initiative eventually evolved into a full-service marketing agency, taking the founders into an industry far removed from their academic training. Both studied civil engineering for their first degrees but went on to build a business in marketing and related services. “We have a background of civil engineering, and that’s what we did for our first degree, and our business is in a totally different world, marketing services and all that,” Bright said. Their transition into the industry required them to develop new skills, learn through experience and navigate the uncertainties of entrepreneurship. They also had to build a viable business model and confront the challenge of securing the resources needed to support growth. Today, EchoHouse operates in eight countries, marking a significant evolution from its beginnings as a university publication. The company’s growth has demanded more than an initial idea. It has required the founders to develop their leadership, understand the practical demands of expansion and establish a working relationship that allows both to contribute without competing for the same responsibilities. For Beryl, the strength of their partnership lies partly in recognising that they bring different qualities to the business. “Bright doesn’t need any motivation. He’s motivated by himself,” she said. “But I think our dynamic, we’ve come to understand each other in terms of what I do versus what he does. Even in the business, we don’t do the same thing. If it’s a Bright thing, it’s Bright. If it’s my thing, it’s me. So we sort of have a dynamic that makes it work that way.” That division of responsibilities has helped them work together while maintaining distinct roles. Rather than trying to lead in the same areas, they have learnt to recognise where each person can contribute most effectively. Beryl serves as Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Echo House Ghana Limited. Her career has earned her recognition in Ghana’s business community, including a place among the country’s Top 50 Young CEOs in 2019 and the Female Young Achiever’s Award at the 2020 EMY Africa Awards. She has also been associated with the creation of Tidal Rave, a major youth-oriented beach festival that has become a prominent fixture on Ghana’s entertainment calendar. Her experience reflects a wider theme in EchoHouse’s development: starting with an idea, learning through experience and continuing to build. The Master of Business Creation programme gave the couple an opportunity to deepen their entrepreneurial knowledge and strengthen their approach to the business they have spent years developing. Their experience illustrates the demands of building a company without a formal academic background in its industry. It also highlights the need for entrepreneurs to keep acquiring skills as their businesses grow and their responsibilities change. For Beryl and Bright, the academic experience came with the added challenge of studying alongside a spouse who is also a business partner. Their success required them to manage assignments and meetings while keeping the company running. The graduation, therefore, was not simply the end of a year of study. It marked another stage in a longer process of learning and adaptation that began when they were students building a university magazine. Their journey has not been one of having every answer from the beginning. Instead, it has involved making decisions, learning new skills and pushing through difficult periods while keeping a shared ambition in view. The joint valedictorian honour brings that journey into focus. The couple who began building EchoHouse as university students have continued to invest in their own development while managing the demands of marriage, parenthood and entrepreneurship. They now hope to apply the lessons from the classroom to take the business to its next level. For Beryl and Bright, the achievement is more than an academic distinction. It reflects a partnership in which both have had to grow, adapt and make room for each other’s strengths. From a university magazine to a company operating across eight countries, their story traces the evolution of an idea into an international business—and of two young entrepreneurs who have continued learning together along the way. At graduation, they stood side by side not only as business partners, but as husband and wife, sharing the recognition that followed years of building together.

title: General Staff reports strike on Energia plant in Russia's Yelets
body:
The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine has reported a strike on Energia plant in Yelets, the sole Russian manufacturer of batteries for glide bomb planning and correction modules, and provided updates on the aftermath of strikes against Proton-Electrotex and Tolyattikauchuk.
"On October 25 and into the night of October 26, units of the Ukrainian Defense Forces struck: The battery production workshop for enemy strike weapons at the 'Energia' enterprise in the city of Yelets, Lipetsk region of Russia. A fire broke out on the enterprise's territory. The strike complicates the Russian army's production of power sources for missiles, guided aerial bombs, and other weaponry," the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine said in a Telegram message on Monday.
The General Staff notes that Energia is the sole manufacturer of batteries for glide bomb planning and correction modules, and also produces batteries for Iskander-M operational-tactical missile systems and sea-launched cruise missiles.
The General Staff also reported that following combat operations on October 23, the destruction of the main microchip production workshop, along with damage to the building and servers of the Proton-Electrotex enterprise in Orel, Orel region, Russia, has been confirmed. This is noted to complicate the enemy's production of components for cruise and ballistic missiles used to strike Ukrainian cities.
According to the General Staff, it is also confirmed that on October 23, at a strike UAV storage, preparation, and launch site in the Donetsk area, three buildings used for preparing and equipping strike UAVs and one launch rail were damaged.
As the General Staff noted, at Tolyattikauchuk combine in Samara region, Russia, which was struck on October 24, damage was recorded to a process pipeline, two butyl rubber production units, and one rectification unit. This severely impacts the production chain of solid rocket fuel for tactical and ballistic missiles.

title: Ukraine awaits Hegseth's signature for nearly a month on Patriot and NASAMS missiles – Zelenskyy
body:
Ukraine has been waiting for nearly a month for U.S Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth's signature regarding the supply of missiles for Patriot and NASAMS air defense systems, reported President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy following a conference call, adding that he has instructed relevant officials to hold talks with the American side.
"The Minister of Defense of Ukraine, the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, and the Minister of Foreign Affairs reported on the situation regarding the supply of air defense interceptors to Ukraine, primarily 'Patriots'. We are working in several directions: with the United States, Europe, and other partners who have a reserve of PAC-2 and PAC-3 missiles. In particular, for nearly a month we have been awaiting Mr. Hegseth's signature regarding missiles for 'Patriots' and 'NASAMS'. I instructed to discuss this once again with the American side. Talks are also ongoing with other countries," Zelenskyy wrote in a Telegram channel on Monday.
Also during the conference call, participants discussed preparations for the meeting of the Ukraine Defense Contact Group in the Ramstein format in November.
"It is important to accelerate the implementation of decisions that have been on the table for some time. Every support package is an opportunity to protect people's lives," Zelenskyy emphasized.
On October 20, it was reported that the administration of U.S President Donald Trump is holding up the transfer of anti-aircraft interceptor missiles for Patriot systems to Ukraine from partner countries, which coincides with a sharp deterioration in diplomatic relations between Washington and Kyiv over disagreements regarding strikes on Russian oil refineries.
According to U.S officials, the transfer of weaponry from states friendly to Ukraine requires official approval from U.S Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, as the systems are manufactured in the U.S and are subject to export control rules. Officials note that Hegseth has not yet formally rejected these applications, but has also not taken the necessary steps to approve them. Against this backdrop, Ukrainian representatives previously stated a critical deficit and a remaining stock of "only a few" interceptor missiles in their arsenal.

title: Ebola: Nigeria has no active case after patient’s evacuation — WHO
body:
Nigeria currently has no active Ebola case after the country evacuated its index patient to Switzerland, the World Health Organisation ( WHO ) said.
The WHO Regional Director for Africa, Mohamed Janabi, said this in a post on X on Monday, shortly after Nigeria’s Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, confirmed the patient’s evacuation from Abuja.
According to Mr Janabi, the patients were evacuated because they are both Swiss citizens. He said the patient was clinically stable after Nigerian health workers managed the acute phase of the illness. The Ebola patient in Nigeria and her contact, who is also her husband, were medically evacuated to Switzerland,” Mr Janabi said.
He said Switzerland would now take responsibility for the patient’s continued management. At the same time, the follow-up f her husband would be handled six days after Nigeria confirmed its first Ebola case in more than a decade.
Mr Pate said the patient was “clinically much improved, stable, conscious, communicating,” with her laboratory test results moving towards baseline. Still, he added that she was no longer infectious, while her husband, who accompanied her, remained asymptomatic.
The patient is the wife of a Swiss diplomat based in Abuja. She arrived in Nigeria on 3 October after travelling from Uganda and developed symptoms a few days later.
Nigeria confirmed her infection on 20 October after laboratory testing detected the Bundibugyo virus.
Although the evacuation means Nigeria currently has no active Ebola cases, Mr Janabi said public health authorities would continue monitoring 52 contacts linked to the patient.
Her husband, who is listed as contact number 53, will be followed up by Swiss authorities.
“However, vigilance remains critical,” Mr Janabi said. “Nigeria will continue the close follow-up of 52 contacts, while Switzerland will assume responsibility for the continued management of the patient and the follow-up of contact number 53, her husband.”
The NCDC had identified 53 contacts as of 24 October, including healthcare workers, domestic staff and the patient’s spouse.
Mr Janabi commended the Nigerian government, health workers, clinicians, emergency responders and other partners involved in the response, describing the successful management and evacuation as a demonstration of African public health capacity.
Nigeria confirmed the imported case amid an ongoing regional outbreak of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease, with cases also reported in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Kenya.
WHO reported 9,704 confirmed cases and 4,687 deaths in the DRC as of 20 October, while Kenya had recorded nine cases, including two deaths.

title: Iran To Hold Security Talks With Saudi, Pakistan, Turkey
body: Senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan will hold talks on regional security with Iranian officials on Monday in Tehran, Iranian and Saudi authorities said. The meeting follows eight months of war in the Middle East and recent US and Israeli threats of renewed attacks against Iran. “As agreed, Saudi Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman, Pakistani army chief General Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin will participate in this meeting,” said Ali Bagheri Kani, deputy secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council. In an interview with state television, Kani said the meeting will also include Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei. Saudi Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Dr Rayed Krimly confirmed that the kingdom’s defence minister was heading a delegation to Tehran on Monday. “The visit comes as part of the continued efforts by the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement countries for de-escalation between parties involved in the ongoing crisis,” Krimly said in a post on X. It is aimed at “promoting dialogue and diplomatic solutions, in support of the mediation efforts carried out by the State of Qatar and the Islamic Republic of Pakistan”, he added. War has engulfed the Middle East since late February when the United States and Israel launched a wave of surprise attacks on Iran, just as Washington and Tehran were in the middle of negotiations on Iran’s nuclear programme. An April ceasefire brought an end to the initial phase of intense bombardment but the two sides have continued to vie for control of the Strait of Hormuz, through which around a fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas used to travel. Iran claims control over the strait and regularly targets vessels that attempt to cross without its authorisation, while the United States has imposed a naval counter-blockade on Iranian ports. Diplomatic efforts to resolve the crisis remain stalled, especially since the collapse of a June deal which laid out a pathway to a permanent settlement. The war has since spread across the region to include fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen. AFP The post Iran To Hold Security Talks With Saudi, Pakistan, Turkey appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Manchester United: Five managers who could replace Michael Carrick
body: The writing is on the wall for beleaguered Michael Carrick after what has been a disastrous week for the Manchester United manager. On Wednesday, Carrick watched his side suffer a 4-1 Uefa Champions League thumping at Italian side Como , after which club captain Bruno Fernandes publicly blamed the humiliation on the coach's tactics . The Portuguese was dropped and left as an unused substitute four days later as United slumped to a 3-0 home loss against Bournemouth which leaves the Red Devils in 16th place, one point outside the relegation zone. Their seven points from eight Premier League games is their lowest at this stage of a campaign since Ron Atkinson's side in 1986/87 (four points) while their eight game winless streak is the club's worst since 2015 under Louis van Gaal. While Carrick retains the backing of United fans, who sang his name on Sunday and who feel he is just the symptom of wider club failures rather than a cause. But his position appears unattainable and it would be a huge surprise if he is still in the dugout for next Saturday's match against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge. Below, we take a look at who could be there in his place. 7 - Manchester United have won just seven points from eight Premier League games this season (W1 D4 L3), their lowest at this stage of a league season since 1986-87 (4). Nightmare. pic.twitter.com/9IpGCx77xo — OptaJoe (@OptaJoe) October 25, 2026 Eddie Howe (unattached) Howe is currently a free agent having left his job as Newcastle United manager this summer after nearly five years in charge. He enjoyed a hugely successful spell on Tyneside when – with the financial backing of Newcastle's Saudi Arabian owners – he transformed the club from relegation candidates to top-four contenders playing a high intensity, physical brand of football. Under Howe's stewardship, the Magpies twice qualified for the Champions League while also winning their first domestic trophy in 70 years when they beat Liverpool in the League Cup final. His final campaign was a struggle, though, as Newcastle finished down in 12th place having lost the services of top-scorer Alexander Isak to Liverpool. The 48-year-old had previously led Bournemouth from the fourth tier to the Premier League – during two spells in charge – keeping them in the top-flight for five consecutive seasons. Antonio Conte (unattached) The Italian is a serial trophy-winning coach with the likes of Juventus, Chelsea, Inter Milan and Napoli. He left Napoli in May one year after securing the Serie A title. After spells as manager at the likes of Arezzo, Bari and Atalanta, Conte then took over at Juventus, the club where he made more than 400 appearances as a player and won just about every major honour. He led Juve to three successive Serie A titles from 2011 to 2014 before becoming Italy's national team manager for two years and then moving to England in 2016, winning the Premier League crown for Chelsea in his first season and FA Cup in his second. Another scudetto would follow at Inter Milan while a return to England with Tottenham Hotspur saw him lead the club back into the Champions League. The 57-year-old would undoubtedly arrive with the winning mentality required to be Man United coach but also brings a combustible character who has no problem going public with his grievances with club bosses if he sees fit. Julian Nagelsmann (unattached) Another out of work coach who stepped down as Germany manager following a shock World Cup exit in the last-32 at the hands of Paraguay. Nagelsmann became the youngest manager in Bundesliga history when he took charge of Hoffenheim at the age of 28 years and 203 days in 2016. Took the club from relegation candidates to Champions League qualification during his three and half years in charge. Nagelsmann then led RB Leipzig to third- and second-place finishes in the Bundesliga as well as reaching the Champions League semi-finals and last-16. Bayern Munich then came calling as the Bavarian giants reportedly forked out €25 million to release him from his Leipzig contract in 2021. His two season at Bayern saw them win the Bundesliga and two Germany Super Cups but also saw him fall out with players, including influential goalkeeper Manuel Neuer. Nagelsmann, now 39, worked with Man United's current head of recruitment, Christopher Vivell, at RB Leipzig so will certainly be in the mix should Carrick go. Unai Emery (Aston Villa) Spaniard is firmly established as one of Europe's top coaches having now lifted the Europa League five times with Sevilla, Villarreal and Aston Villa, as well as winning the domestic double at Paris Saint-Germain. Emery is the only manager to have won the Europa League three seasons in a row, a feat he achieved between 2013 and 2016 when Sevilla defeated Benfica, Dnipro and Jurgen Klopp's Liverpool in the final. His PSG reign would see them dominate domestically over two seasons but fail to secure the Champions League crown their Qatari owners craved. An unsuccessful spell at Arsenal was followed by another Europa League crown at Villareal before moving back to England in October 2022 where he led Aston Villa from a relegation fight to seventh place and the Europa Conference League in seven months. Since then, he led Villa back into the Champions League as well as winning the Europa League last season – the club's first trophy in 30 years. Clearly has to stature required for United job but would cost huge compensation fee. And it is far from certain that the 54-year-old would be willing to swap the relative calm of Villa for the chaos of Old Trafford. Unai Emery has won the Europa League five times already 😮‍💨 Football heritage 🏆 pic.twitter.com/HIXRgEfbih — Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) May 21, 2026 Cesc Fabregas (Como) The Spaniard just hammered one of the final nails in Carrick's coffin with the drubbing in Lombardy last week. His first senior manager's role saw him secure Como a spot in the Champions League for the first time in their history when they finished fourth place last season. The current campaign has seen Como win two out of three games in European football's premier competition and are fifth in Serie A after losing just once eight matches. Is building an exciting side at Como, where he is a minority shareholder, and the 39-year-old probably lacks the managerial experience needed to sort out the mess at Old Trafford right now.

title: EU debt to reach one trillion euro in 2027 — chief auditor
body:
BRUSSELS, October 26. /TASS/. The EU budget debt will reach one trillion euro next year and will be over 500% of the bloc’s budget, President of the European Court of Auditors Tony Murphy told Rapporteur news portal.
The figure refers to the debt of the European Union as an organization and not to total debts of EU member-states.
"We’re looking at 1 trillion euro by the end of 2027. It’s a substantial amount," he said, cited by the news portal. Financial pressure on the EU budget is growing like in a "pressure cooker," Murphy said.

title: Rivers ADC inaugurates 600-man campaign council
body: …alleges abandonment of governance in Rivers By Davies Iheamnachor Rivers State chapter of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, has inaugurated its Governorship Campaign Council. The council composed of 600 persons is chaired by the Sen. (Ohna) Andrew Uchendu was inaugurated with Hon. Chimbiko Akarolo as the Director General. Addressing members of the council during the inauguration in Port Harcourt, Monday, the State Chairman of the Party, Chief (Dr) Chukwudi Dimkpa, charged members of the council to discharge their duties with utmost sense of responsibility. He said: “Having duly presented the leadership, directorates, departments, and membership of the River States 2027 Governorship Campaign Council, and acting in my capacity as the state chairman of the ADC River States, I hereby formally inaugurate the campaign council. “I charge every member to discharge his or her responsibilities faithfully, diligently, and in accordance with the constitution of our party, the approved terms of reference, and the laws of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.” Dimkpa, who officially handed the responsibility of the governorship campaign of the party in the state to the team, enjoined the council to work in unity and be result driven. He said: “I now formally hand over the responsibility for the coordination and execution of our governorship campaign to the campaign council under the leadership of distinguished Senator Andrew Uchendu as chairman and Honorable Chimbiko Akarolo as Director-General, subject to the overall authority and policy direction of the state party leadership.” “I expect this council to operate as one united, disciplined, and result-oriented team. By this declaration, the River States ADC 2027 Campaign Council is hereby formally inaugurated.” In his acceptance speech, the Chairman of the Campaign Council, Sen. Andrew Uchendu, regretted that some political elites in the state had converted the state to a battle field, noting that the party would rescue the state from such grip. Uchendu alleged that governance in the state has been abandoned, stressing that the administration of Sir Siminalayi Fubara has failed the state. He said ADC was interested in stabilising leadership in the state, adding that the party wants a situation where the Executive, Legislature and the Judiciary would carry out their responsibilities independently. Uchendu noted that the state was not created for one man to own or control, regretting that recent political crisis had wrecked damage on the state. He said: “While Godfathers wage private wars of ego in Abuja and Port Harcourt, governance in Rivers State has been completely abandoned. An elected government has been decapitated by legislative rascality. Healthcare has collapsed. “Hospital bills by previous administrations have been left to rot, leaving ordinary mothers and infants without access to basic medicine. Schools are abandoned. Our children sit on the floor. “While neighbouring states build for the future, our state is paralyzed by executive/legislative drama and Godfatherism. Our state is rich, but our people are poor. We produce oil that feeds the nation, but we have no light, no good roads, no clean water. “This administration has failed, and will continue to fail. For four years going, we lost the state, the sovereignty of the state. And we have been told that we will lose another four years. God forbid.” Uchendu said the task ahead is that the party must rescue the state from the grip of Godfatherism, urging members of the council to take the rescue message of ADC to the units and ward and local government areas of the state. He also declared that the party would be focused on non-violent and issue based campaign, adding that every vote in the forthcoming election must count. He said: “That is why ADC is here. We want a state where the legislature will do their work, the executive will do their work, the judiciary will do their work. On behalf of the people, not on behalf of themselves. “Our task is clear. We must rescue what we have before, that has been lost. We must recover and rebuild our state for ourselves and our children yet more. And take it to where we believe it should be. Our task is very clear. Take our rescue message to all the 23 local government areas of River State. “Run an issue-based campaign. Non-violent campaign. Unite all tribes. We are one people. We will need to unite our people and fight as a common front. And therefore, run a government that is fair, inclusive.” The post Rivers ADC inaugurates 600-man campaign council appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Accusations against Raul Castro legally null and void — Russian Foreign Ministry
body:
MOSCOW, October 26. /TASS/. The charges brought against Cuba’s former leader Raul Castro are not legally credible, as has already been clearly stated by Russia and confirmed by a UN Security Council resolution adopted 30 years ago saying that the incident currently being blamed on Castro was resolved, Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said.
Responding to a request to clarify how the 1996 UN Security Council resolution was adopted, which the Russian foreign ministry had previously referred to in a statement in connection with the United States’ issuance of an arrest warrant for Castro, the diplomat said that Russia’s and the United States’ permanent representatives to the United Nations played the most active role in intensive consultations, thanks to whom a statement satisfying all parties, which "did not contain any personal accusations, much less calls for measures to bring anyone to justice" was produced.
"Subsequently, the approach proposed in the statement formed the basis for the aforementioned UN Security Council resolution S/RES/1067 (1996) dated July 26, 1996. This effectively meant that all members of the Council agreed that the incident was resolved. We recall this episode of Russian-American cooperation at the UN precisely to emphasize the legal insignificance of the charges currently being leveled against Cuba’s historical leader Raul Castro," Zakharova said. "We clearly stated this in the statement issued by the Russian Foreign Ministry on October 20."

title: Abu Dhabi announces new youth orchestra with free music education
body: A new music institution in Abu Dhabi will offer free tuition and instruments to children aged six to nine when it opens in January. Youth Orchestra Abu Dhabi will be based in a building designed by the late Frank Gehry in the Mina Zayed district, with a 600-seat concert hall and 18 rehearsal and practice rooms. Established by the Department of Culture and Tourism Abu Dhabi, the institution is accepting applications for its first cohort of 100 pupils before its January 2027 opening. “Youth Orchestra Abu Dhabi is about creating opportunities for young people to discover and develop their potential through music,” says Mohamed Khalifa Al Mubarak, chairman of DCT Abu Dhabi. “Beyond musical skills, it helps build confidence, creativity, discipline and collaboration. It reflects our belief that investing in young people today is essential to building a vibrant and sustainable cultural future for Abu Dhabi.” Pupils will attend group lessons four times a week after school and on two Saturdays each month, led by teaching artists. Each child will be provided with a musical instrument at no cost, with training covering both western classical and Arabic musical traditions. The programme is intended to support pupils over the longer term, allowing them to develop their skills and progress through ensemble playing. Additional ensembles for advanced pupils are planned during its first year. Its approach draws on Youth Orchestra Los Angeles, founded by Venezuelan conductor Gustavo Dudamel and inspired by El Sistema, the music education movement that began in Venezuela. Through the Los Angeles programme, the LA Philharmonic and its community partners provide free instruments and intensive music training to young people from underserved communities. There is an architectural connection, too: Gehry designed its Beckmen Yola Centre in Inglewoeod, which opened in 2021. The Abu Dhabi institution will be among the architect’s final completed works, according to the department. Alongside its teaching programme, the venue will host public performances, master classes and community events. It joins several Gehry projects in Abu Dhabi, including Guggenheim Abu Dhabi , which opens on December 11, and the forthcoming Dar Al Funoon performing arts centre. Announced in June and scheduled to open near Saadiyat Cultural District in 2030, Dar Al Funoon will accommodate opera, ballet, theatre and orchestral concerts, with plans for international touring partnerships, co-productions and artistic residencies. Youth Orchestra Abu Dhabi adds a programme of regular music education for children to that expansion, with its first pupils set to begin learning in January.

title: ‘Historic Victory’: World Leaders Celebrate Lula’s Re-Election
body:
World leaders congratulated Brazil’s left-wing President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on Monday, after he pulled off a dramatic comeback to claim a re-election victory.
Lula’s win was acknowledged by left and right-wing leaders alike, despite his challenger Flavio Bolsonaro refusing to accept the loss.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Lula received 51.8 percent of the vote compared to 48.2 percent for Bolsonaro.
EU chief Ursula von der Leyen hailed Lula’s victory as a win for “democracy and multilateralism.”
“Europe’s partnership with Brazil is thriving,” she said in a post on X.
Mexico’s leftist President Claudia Sheinbaum celebrated Lula’s win on Sunday, saying on X: “Long live democracy, the people of Brazil won.”
Cuban President Miguel Diaz-Canel congratulated Lula on his “historic victory that guarantees the continuity of the path of peace, sovereignty, and social justice.”
Argentina’s former president Cristina Kirchner, who is currently under house arrest for corruption, said on X that Lula “knew how to awaken in his compatriots the feeling and sense needed to win.”
Uruguay’s President Yamandu Orsi said on X that he had spoken with Lula and “congratulated him on his victory and on the democratic celebration that an electoral process represents.”
With Lula’s victory, Brazil staved off a conservative wave that has seen numerous countries -- such as Argentina, Chile, Colombia and Peru -- all shift right, backed by US President Donald Trump.
Peru’s right-wing President Keiko Fujimori praised Brazil’s “democratic day” of elections and congratulated Lula on his win.
“I reaffirm our willingness to strengthen our strategic alliance, integration, cooperation, and the sustainable development of the Amazon that we share, for the benefit of both our peoples,” she said on X.
Chile’s President Jose Antonio Kast, a staunch ally of Bolsonaro, said on X that “Chile and Brazil have a great future in common.”
Ecuador’s conservative President Daniel Noboa called for cooperation with the leftist leader through his fourth term.
“Our region has common enemies, shared challenges, and much to gain when we work together,” Noboa said on X.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez celebrated Lula’s win as the beginning of a “progressive comeback.”
“What has happened in Brazil will happen in Spain,” said the Spanish leader, who is trailing in the polls ahead of his country’s November vote.
French President Emmanuel Macron called for efforts to “strengthen our strategic partnership” with Brazil.
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who is the current chair of the BRICS geopolitical and economic bloc, which includes Brazil, offered Lula his “heartiest congratulations.”
“I look forward to working closely with him to further deepen and expand the multifaceted India-Brazil Strategic Partnership,” he said.
Russia, which is also a BRICS member, welcomed Lula’s victory, with a Kremlin spokesperson saying he had done “a lot, not only for the development of bilateral relations but also for advancing processes within the framework of BRICS.”
China also congratulated Lula. A foreign ministry spokesperson said the country was “willing to work with Brazil to continue advancing the building of a China-Brazil community with a shared future.”
US Senator Bernie Sanders, a firebrand leftist, said: “Lula has stood up for Brazilian workers & democracy -- and will continue to do so in the next four years.”

title: Bishops lament White House meeting that produced photo with Trump
body: Two Catholic bishops have expressed regret about agreeing to a White House meeting that produced a publicly distributed photo of them praying with President Trump.  Milwaukee Archbishop Jeffrey Grob, in a statement titled "A Public Apology," said Sunday that he had received many questions and comments — some of them distraught — about the meeting on Thursday that he and 11 other bishops attended.  He said the meeting was speedily publicized by the White House with photos and a video without consent of the participants, less than two weeks away from the midterm elections.  "I feel a heavy sadness, not only over the pain I caused, but also for the fact that something so sacred to a group of religious leaders, prayer to our Heavenly Father, would be manipulated in that way," Grob said.The bishop of Des Moines, Iowa, William Joensen, also issued a statement making clear he felt the White House had taken advantage of the bishops.  "I wish I had been more shrewd and less simple, like those who exploited our meeting for partisan political purpose," he wrote. "I pray I am more prudent and wise going forward, even as I remain resolute in my openness to engaging and praying for political leaders at all levels."  Asked whether the White House had received the bishops' consent for releasing the photos and video, the press office declined to answer. Instead, White House spokesperson Taylor Rogers replied, "There has never been a greater president for Catholic Americans than President Trump, and his strong record proves it."  The White House invitation to the bishops, extended in September, offered discussion about such issues as immigration enforcement, religious worker visas, abortion and the use of federal tax credits to support private education, according to Joensen and Grob.  "The meeting was in no way an endorsement of the president, his policies, or his party," wrote Grob. "We were told the meeting was to be a private discussion, that several Catholic members of the Cabinet might make an appearance, and that there could be an opportunity to pray privately with the president."  "It did not take long thereafter for the White House to post a video and photos of the prayer," Grob said.   "I soon began receiving messages of serious concern over the possibility that I had inadvertently participated in a political event less than two weeks before a national election," he added. "I also heard from some who felt wounded because of the ways they or their family had been harmed by the president's policies." ... We came in good faith to try to work for the betterment of our fellow human beings, to ease their suffering, to build up the common good, and to pray with a president, not to pose for a political photo opportunity to benefit the few. We should never have been put in that position by the White House.   "I did not go without reservations. I wish I had heeded them," Grob concluded. "Please know that I have heard these concerns, understand how I caused them, and I apologize for any damage my actions have done." Collectively, members of the U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops have diverse views on Mr. Trump and his administration's policies. Minnesota-based Bishop Robert Barron, for example, agreed to serve on his Religious Liberty Commission, which was filled almost entirely with conservative Christians. Some other bishops vehemently denounced aspects of Mr. Trump's tough stance on immigration enforcement, saying it runs counter to Catholic teaching.

title: Ukrainian PM urges business to plan for worst case, warns of $1.5 bln budget gap
body:
Prime Minister of Ukraine Serhiy Koretsky has called on the business community to prepare in advance for the most critical scenarios regarding enemy attacks and economic challenges.
"When we talk to founders and top management, I've sensed a certain attitude that 'it will somehow blow over.' Perhaps I won't be targeted by missiles or drones, perhaps my sector won't be touched. Therefore, first: I would strongly ask and recommend thinking according to the most critical scenario of events. Thinking ahead about alternative production sites: who you can cooperate with, where you can make a private label if we are talking about consumer goods, if your enterprise is hit. How to talk in advance with suppliers, perhaps even for imported goods, how to conclude framework contracts and be ready rather than doing it all later. Looking at alternative premises for relocation, for restoration. In other words, think in the most critical scenario. It is better to be ready for this and have it not happen than to find oneself in an unexpected situation," Koretsky said at the 12th Kyiv International Economic Forum (KIEF) themed "People. Business. Economy. What's Next?" in Kyiv on Monday, as reported by an Interfax-Ukraine correspondent.
According to the Prime Minister, enemy strikes have already caused over $7.7 billion in losses, with more than 1 million square meters of various types of real estate, both state and private, destroyed or damaged. Significant destruction has hit energy, metallurgy, logistics, processing enterprises, retail, and other sectors.
"Considering these losses, considering the strikes, we already see that by the end of the year the state budget will underfulfill its plans and forecasts by about $1.5 billion. That is the baseline forecast we have today," he stated.
At the same time, he emphasized that despite all this, the country's economy continues to function.
"If we think in terms of PnL (Profit and Loss statement), allocating a lot of funds to support business is impossible. There is no such PnL, because we can only cover one-third of the budget. Even realizing, clearly realizing this, we live even on a cash flow principle and in a certain way go all-in, allocating certain funds to support programs, to various subsidies, to grant programs. Because we realize that without this support, business – small, medium, and large in particular – cannot be sufficiently resilient to counter enemy attacks. And this is the conscious logic and tactics of the government," Koretsky said.
The Prime Minister stressed that the government will continue programs that have proven their effectiveness, notably the "Affordable Loans 5-7-9%" program. He noted that since the program's inception, UAH 580 billion has been issued, with the current loan portfolio principal standing at around UAH 200 billion. He recalled the recent decision allowing large businesses to receive about UAH 1 billion "in one hand per group of companies" at a preferential interest rate of around 10%.
"The 2026 budget allocated UAH 18 billion. We are expanding this program and see that by the end of the year it will be UAH 22 billion. We currently have a certain deficit on four billion, but one way or another we will cover it, because we consider this to be one of the fundamentally important, correct programs that genuinely supports business," the Prime Minister said.
He also pointed out the necessity of establishing a war risk insurance and damage compensation system. Koretsky recalled the proposal to create a special fund in the budget with an initial state contribution of $1 billion, which partners would double or triple.
"How will this work further? A simplified procedure. Compensation within 30 days after processing. And the tariff for this insurance risk must be very basic, symbolic, we are aiming at approximately 2%. And the maximum damage compensation will be about $5 million in one hand," the Prime Minister detailed.
Koretsky also stated that there is currently no consensus or support for increasing the Value Added Tax (VAT) from 20% to 21% to fund this special fund.
"There is no consensus among big and medium business, there is no support in parliament yet. We are looking for other mechanisms. We will see how the budgetary process proceeds in parliament and build from that. But we have no other path, we must find the instrument. Together we will see what we can contribute," Koretsky said.

title: ‘Still Just a Child’: The Russian Teenagers Fighting and Dying in Ukraine
body:
“Why?! A young soldier who’d never seen combat … Still just a child,” Svetlana Serezhkina, a resident of the Moscow region, wrote on social media after news emerged of the death of Alisher Svirin, the first publicly identified Russian soldier born in 2008 to be killed in the war in Ukraine.
“It’s such a shame they let him sign a [military] contract,” wrote another commenter, Andrei. Dozens of similar comments written by residents of Svirin’s hometown of Pavlovsky Posad appeared under the same post.
According to his obituary, Svirin had served as a machine gunner in a motorized rifle brigade. He was just 14 when President Vladimir Putin launched the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
More than 200 Russian soldiers aged 18 have been killed in the war, according to a count by the BBC’s Russian service and the exiled news outlet Mediazona.
The real number may be higher, as the tally excludes soldiers listed as missing and fighters from the Russian-backed separatist territories in Ukraine’s Donetsk and Luhansk regions.
The pro-war Orthodox Christian VKontakte group Synodik, which has about 50,000 followers, carries dozens of obituaries for soldiers who were teenagers when the invasion began.
In Orthodox Christianity, a synodik is a list of names of the living or the dead who are remembered in prayers and church services. Likewise, Synodik’s members pray for Russian soldiers like they would in a real church. The comments, mostly posted by women, are filled with Orthodox prayers, animated images of icons and cross emojis.
One recent post commemorates Kirill Tretyakov, who was born Feb. 7, 2007, near the end of Putin’s second presidential term. He had just turned 15 when the full-scale war began.
Tretyakov grew up in Kamensk, a settlement of about 6,300 people roughly 100 kilometers (62 miles) from Ulan-Ude, the capital of Russia’s republic of Buryatia. After completing ninth grade at a local school, he enrolled in a vocational college to study construction. He enjoyed kettlebell lifting and football in his free time.
Tretyakov signed a contract with the Defense Ministry six days after his 18th birthday, according to his obituary.
“From an early age, Kirill strove to be a worthy citizen of his country. On Feb. 13, 2025, Kirill made the courageous decision to defend the Fatherland and signed a contract with the Defense Ministry,” the group’s administrators wrote.
The Moscow Times found identical obituaries in a VKontakte group about Ulan-Ude and on the website of Buryatia’s Kabansky district. Tretyakov served as a combat engineer in an obstacle-laying company of the 656th Separate Guards Engineer-Sapper Battalion. He was killed on Sept. 22 of this year.
“Kirill strove to learn everything a real man should know. He was a brave, determined and fearless warrior who always put the common cause above his own,” his obituary reads.
A psychologist in Russia who works with adolescents said that many young people struggle to grasp the reality of going to war.
“The risk of being killed is very high, but young people don’t think about that,” the psychologist told The Moscow Times, speaking on condition of anonymity for safety reasons.
“When you’re young, you feel like life will last forever, like you’re invincible. Teenagers lack the social circle, the word-of-mouth networks, that could help them think critically about the war.”
That illusion of invulnerability is compounded by a broader devaluation of life in Russia, the psychologist said, referencing television propagandist Vladimir Solovyov’s comment on air that “life is greatly overrated.”
The number of “newly departed warriors,” as the Synodik group calls them, rises almost every day. The group also publishes obituaries for soldiers from Russian-occupied Ukrainian territories.
“Nikolai was a simple guy. He finished school in our village and was open, cheerful and kind,” the head of the Voikovsky rural settlement in annexed Crimea, said of Nikolai Ruzov, 19. Ruzov was six when Russia annexed the peninsula in 2014 and 14 when the full-scale war began.
Like all draft-age men without a deferment, Ruzov completed a year of compulsory military service before signing a contract with the Defense Ministry and going to fight in Ukraine’s Donetsk region. He was killed on Aug. 18, 2026, less than three months after his 19th birthday.
A Crimean news outlet illustrated his obituary with an apparently AI-generated image presented as a portrait of Ruzov that was later reposted by other outlets. The soldier in the image wears a U.S. flag patch on his shoulder. The Moscow Times analyzed the image using Hive’s AI-detection software , which returned a 100% confidence score that it was AI-generated.
Ruzov had been the commander of an assault squad, state media reported .
“Can someone explain how a 19-year-old boy ended up commanding an assault squad?!” one commenter, Maxim Borisov, asked .
Among those offering condolences online were mothers whose own sons had been killed in the war.
“May Nikolai enter the Kingdom of Heaven, and may you find the strength to learn to live with this irreplaceable loss. Our children don’t die … they are joining the Lord’s army. My boy has been there for four years,” Tamara Romanova wrote on the social network Odnoklassniki.
Ruzov was posthumously awarded Russia’s Order of Courage.
Another 19-year-old soldier, David Fedorov, died on Oct. 20 after being sent on an assault mission, according to his mother.
Police stopped Fedorov on the street in Cheboksary, the capital of the Volga republic of Chuvashia, in May and forced him to sign a contract with the Defense Ministry, his mother told the independent news outlet Astra. He was officially assigned to serve as a driver despite having no driver’s license, she added.
The deaths of young soldiers also feature in state efforts to promote the war in schools.
On Sept. 21, materials for “Important Conversations,” a series of state-mandated patriotic lessons, highlighted two soldiers killed in the invasion at ages 20 to 25. One was Nurmagomed Gadzhimagomedov, a soldier from Dagestan who died in the first month of the full-scale war.
“When I see examples of heroism like this young man ... I want to say: ‘I am a Lak, I am a Dagestani, I am a Chechen, Ingush, Russian, Tatar, Jew, Mordvin, Ossetian’,” Putin said after Gadzhimagomedov’s death in March 2022.
Footage of Putin’s remarks was included in a seven-minute video shown to schoolchildren, while pupils were also offered an interactive lesson about Gadzhimagomedov’s life.
Military personnel in their early 20s also visit schools to deliver patriotic lessons. The children’s psychologist said in-person meetings with returning soldiers could have an even stronger influence on teenagers.
“Soldiers are surrounded by an aura of heroism,” the psychologist said. “The person who comes to speak to you is alive. He fought for three years and came back. Now he’s addressing an audience and has a stable position in society.”
“Young people have little to lose,” the psychologist continued. “They don’t yet have families of their own or things they would find painful to give up, so war can seem appealing.”
We are facing unprecedented challenges. Russia's Prosecutor General's Office has designated The Moscow Times as an "undesirable" organization, criminalizing our work and putting our staff at risk of prosecution. This follows our earlier unjust labeling as a "foreign agent."
These actions are direct attempts to silence independent journalism in Russia. The authorities claim our work "discredits the decisions of the Russian leadership." We see things differently: we strive to provide accurate, unbiased reporting on Russia.
We, the journalists of The Moscow Times, refuse to be silenced. But to continue our work, we need your help .
Your support, no matter how small, makes a world of difference. If you can, please support us monthly starting from just $ 2. It's quick to set up, and every contribution makes a significant impact.
By supporting The Moscow Times, you're defending open, independent journalism in the face of repression. Thank you for standing with us.

title: Trump failed to stop inflation. Now Republicans may pay the price in the midterms
body:
One week before midterm elections, President Donald Trump is struggling to deliver on his promise to bring down costs
WASHINGTON -- President Donald Trump would prefer that voters not worry about inflation . But it's hard for them to ignore.
Filling up a basic Ford F-150 truck now costs about $100, up $30 from a year ago. Mortgage rates have jumped to levels that have depressed home sales. And for the past 12 months, consumer prices have risen faster than paychecks, making the average family poorer.
One week before midterm elections that will serve as a referendum on his second term, Trump is struggling to deliver on his campaign promise to bring down costs, even as he insists the country has entered an economic “golden age." The same frustration that powered his comeback two years ago could now cost Republicans control of Congress.
“Our nation is doing better now than ever before,” Trump insists while campaigning, vowing that interest rates and oil prices will plunge once the war with Iran — which he started — comes to an end.
The word “affordability,” he says, is nothing but “a con job by the Democrats," adding that “it doesn’t mean anything to anybody.”
That rhetoric comes as voters say they're struggling to afford basics like fuel and groceries and as they blame Trump for higher costs , pointing to the Republican president's aggressive tariff policies and the ongoing, unpopular war with Iran.
Record-high diesel prices, in particular, have driven up shipping and farming costs , creating trouble for Republicans in typically conservative states such as Iowa, Kansas, Ohio and Texas, where Democrats appear uniquely competitive in races that will shape Trump's final two years in office.
“The costs of things are absolutely the first thing people talk about, but also it’s their pay not keeping up with the cost,” said AFL-CIO President Liz Shuler. “It’s a double whammy.”
Prices at the pump have become a preeminent issue for voters.
"People hate paying more money for gas, and the prices have gone up a lot,” said Stephen Moore, who has previously advised the president on the economy. “It’s frustrating because Trump’s done so many good things for the economy. But with the Iran situation, that’s really had a big effect on the economy, and Republicans may pay a high price for that.”
Misty Reeder, 48, said she considers herself “in the middle” politically but picked all Democrats on her ballot in Easley, South Carolina.
“I’ve noticed that things have been getting a lot harder,” said Reeder, who receives disability payments. “You hear about it everywhere you go."
In the six years that she and her husband have been renting their home, Reeder said their rent had increased by hundreds of dollars.
“Something’s gotta give,” she said. “It’s like a dam — the pressure’s too much, and it’s going to break.”
Sandra Capell, 69, said she wants “to see some change" when it comes to the economy even though she voted Republican in Easley, which is part of South Carolina's conservative Upstate region.
“I think everybody is kind of suffering when it comes to groceries, gas, everything really,” she said. “I’m looking at the Republican Party to jump on the wagon, get in the saddle and let’s bring it back.”
Beti Rosales, 47, said higher prices have taken a toll on her family's Mexican restaurant in Allentown, Pennsylvania , part of the Lehigh Valley that has seesawed between the parties in recent years. Limes and avocados cost more than before. So does the plumber who's occasionally needed.
Two years ago, Rosales decided to give Trump and Republicans a chance, hoping for relief from inflation.
“The reality now is that it actually didn’t get better," she said. "It actually got worse. The prices of everything have increased."
Rosales is now considering voting Democratic in the midterms.
"Maybe fresh new faces might make a difference?” she said.
While running in 2024, Trump hammered President Joe Biden and Vice President Kamala Harris, his Democratic opponent in the election, for high inflation, which climbed as high as 9.1% in June 2022. He promised voters he would lower gasoline prices and unlock roaring growth.
“With your vote in this election, I will end inflation,” he vowed.
In less than two years, Trump has aggressively remodeled the U.S. economy. He's slapped double-digit tariffs on many trading partners — including the European Union, India, Japan, Canada and Mexico — and sparked trade wars with allies. The U.S. government now holds stakes in several dozen private companies. He's signed broad income tax cuts into law.
But the persistent challenge of inflation has continued, overshadowing the positives of continued economic growth and a low unemployment rate. Inflation was 3% when Trump took office and reached 3.7% last month .
The president has played down the intensity of inflation, claiming that it is under 2% and “under control.”
Democrats have seized on the discontent, using the same high cost of living that sank them before to pressure vulnerable Republicans and put congressional districts Trump won by even double digits in play.
“Now remember, they promised to lower prices on Day One. Instead, under the failed President Donald J. Trump, it costs more than ever in American history to fill up your truck, stock your fridge, visit the doctor or power your home,” said Georgia Sen. Jon Ossoff, a Democrat running for reelection, at a recent rally in Atlanta.
“You work harder and harder, but the treadmill gets faster and steeper and the bills get higher and higher," he told the crowd.
Cait Conley, a Democrat running in New York against Republican Rep. Mike Lawler, one of his party’s most vulnerable incumbents, harkened back to his tweet from the last midterm elections, when Biden was president. Lawler had advised voters to "fill up your tank and go grocery shopping — it will inform your decision.”
In a new ad, Conley said voters should follow that advice this year "and then tell me if the system’s working for you.”
“You deserve better. It shouldn’t be this hard," she says.
Conley and other candidates have pounded on a theme that Democrats believe will be especially effective this cycle: accusing Trump and other Republicans of compounding voters' economic pain by corruptly pursuing policies that help their billionaire donors at the expense of everyday Americans.
“I know you’re frustrated. Washington politicians get rich while you get hurt. Corporations make huge profits while your costs go up," North Carolina Senate candidate Roy Cooper says in an ad airing in the competitive state.
That has included a particular focus on the war with Iran.
“Trump’s war abroad costs taxpayers a billion dollars a day on a war we have no business fighting. Our schools crumble, our factories shutter, our gas prices skyrocket. But when they want war, billion-dollar blank checks," says Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed in another spot.
The president "thinks that the economy is doing well because he and his family have enriched themselves to the tune of several billion dollars,” said Amy Richards, 56, a onetime Republican who has voted Democratic since Trump became his party's 2016 nominee.
“He has zero idea what it is like to receive a paycheck and have to feed yourself and your family,” said Richards, standing outside a polling place in her town of Round Rock, Texas, on Friday, "and he doesn’t care.”
Republicans, meanwhile, have tried to cast Democrats as extreme, pointing to an ascendant populist wing that includes a number of Democratic socialists .
Moore, who advised Trump's campaigns, said he wished Republicans would spend more time talking about the economy’s strengths, including rising median incomes and a record-setting stock market , even as he acknowledged those numbers might not resonate with voters.
“What matters is how people feel, and clearly people are feeling stressed out financially,” he said.
Some Trump supporters remain satisfied. Renee Blood, 57, an executive assistant in Round Rock, feels the economy has “improved quite well."
“Of course we see gas prices up and down, but things are much more affordable,” she said.
She plans to vote Republican because she worries things will get worse if Democrats return to power.
Trump’s golden age might not have arrived, she said, but “we are still working on it.”
Colvin reported from New York. Associated Press writer Meg Kinnard in Easley, S.C.; Mike Catalini in Allentown, Pa.; and Jesse Bedayn in Round Rock, Texas, contributed to this report.
