TOR had faced significant operational challenges before the current management assumed office in May 2025. Its Crude Distillation Unit had been shut down since April 2021, while the RFCC unit had been inactive since 2019. The shutdown of the major processing units had limited the refinery’s activities largely to storage services, reducing its ability to undertake its core function of processing crude oil. Management subsequently introduced Project Restore TOR, which prioritised the rehabilitation and restart of the CDU, improvements to financial controls and measures to rebuild confidence among workers and business partners. Mr Kombat said management had also addressed more than 300 outstanding staff petitions and promotion-related cases, some of which had remained unresolved for more than a decade. He said efforts to improve staff welfare included reviewing conditions of service, job descriptions and performance-management systems. The refinery’s recovery programme also includes further work on the RFCC unit, boiler systems, crude-heating equipment and other infrastructure intended to improve operational capacity. Mr Kombat said the planned expansion of TOR would support additional economic opportunities as Ghana sought to increase domestic refining capacity. He added that management intended to pursue further development projects, including a new refinery, petrochemical facilities and additional storage capacity. The Managing Director said the objective was to build a more sustainable refinery that could contribute to employment, industrial development and national energy security.

title: TOR records 216% increase in product storage volumes between 2024 and 2026
body: The Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) has recorded a 216.19 per cent increase in product storage volumes between 2024 and 2026, as management intensifies efforts to restore the refinery’s commercial operations and strengthen its role in Ghana’s petroleum supply chain. Managing Director Edmond Kombat said storage volumes increased from 426,954 metric tonnes in 2024 to 1,107,389 metric tonnes in 2025, representing year-on-year growth of 159.37 per cent. The volume increased further to 1,350,000 metric tonnes in 2026, an additional 21.91 per cent rise over the 2025 figure. Speaking at the Government Accountability Series at Jubilee House on Monday, October 26, 2026, Mr Kombat said the figures demonstrated significant growth in TOR’s storage activities and its contribution to the petroleum industry. “Overall, this represents a 216.19% increase between 2024 and 2026, demonstrating significant growth in TOR’s product storage activity and its contribution to Ghana’s petroleum supply chain,” he said. The Managing Director said the improvement formed part of a broader recovery effort aimed at restoring confidence among petroleum service providers, increasing commercial activity and preparing the refinery for long-term sustainability. When the current management assumed office in May 2025, TOR’s major processing units were inactive, leaving the company largely dependent on renting out storage space to petroleum service providers. The CDU had been out of operation since April 2021, while the RFCC unit had been shut down since 2019. Management subsequently introduced measures to improve cash controls, extend operating hours at the loading gantry and strengthen accountability in product handling. Mr Kombat said these interventions helped restore confidence among private petroleum companies and regional partners, encouraging them to store and lift products through the refinery. The company also resumed crude processing on December 19, 2025, following the completion of turnaround maintenance on the CDU. He said the refinery’s recovery had been supported by collaboration with institutions including the National Petroleum Authority, the Ghana National Petroleum Corporation, GOIL and the Bulk Oil Storage and Transportation Company. Mr Kombat said the improved storage activity, together with the resumption of refining operations and renewed crude supplies, had positioned TOR to make a stronger contribution to Ghana’s petroleum supply chain.

title: Why do planes keep circling before landing? The UN has a plan to fix it
body:
By R Anil Kumar

UN, Oct 25, 2026. Air traffic delays cost billions and turn journeys into ordeals. Some countries are already proving that better coordination saves thousands of flying hours: and cuts emissions – and the UN’s aviation agency wants the rest of the world to follow.



Most frequent flyers know the feeling: the plane begins its descent but, instead of heading for the runway, starts circling overhead.

It isn’t necessarily a fault or bad weather. Often, it is a holding pattern – a manoeuvre that keeps aircraft airborne until there is room for them to land.

It is one symptom of increasingly crowded skies, where a storm, an emergency or a closed route in one place can cause delays thousands of kilometres away.

The bill is enormous. In Europe alone, air traffic management delays cost an estimated $2.3 billion or more in 2025, according to EUROCONTROL, the continent’s air navigation body.

Green light

What if countries coordinated their flights the way a city synchronises its traffic lights?

That is the idea behind a push by the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), the UN agency that sets global aviation standards.

“If the traffic lights work independently, traffic becomes chaos and there are jams on every corner,” ICAO Secretary General Juan Carlos Salazar told UN News.

“If you get a green light on one street and are stopped at the next, the backlog builds immediately. The same happens with air traffic across the world’s airspace.”

The fix starts long before landing. If an airport knows it cannot take more aircraft for a while, it can coordinate with other airports to hold back departures, rather than leave planes circling overhead.

This approach, known as air traffic flow management, lets airlines, airports, controllers and weather services share information and make decisions together.

Need to know:

Several countries already use it, but the benefits are limited when national systems don’t talk to each other. After five days of talks in Montreal convened by ICAO, governments and industry backed a faster global rollout.

For passengers, that should mean earlier warning of cancellations and delays as well as quicker recovery when things go wrong.

“When people get to the airport, wait all day and nobody tells them anything, that creates huge problems,” Mr. Salazar said.

Disruption snowballs, he explained. A problem lasting an hour or a day knocks on to every flight scheduled after it and today’s system is slow to bounce back.

Minutes, money and fuel:

The gains are already measurable. In the Americas, collaborative trials supported by ICAO saved more than 265,000 minutes of flying time in 2026, about 4,400 hours, and over $38.9 million.

They also saved some 13,330 tonnes of fuel and avoided 42,160 tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions, a contribution to the goal of net zero carbon emissions from international aviation by 2050.

In Europe, a EUROCONTROL programme anticipating weather and congestion avoided around 3.1 million minutes of delay between May and August 2026, saving an estimated $448 million and making the network 14 per cent more stable on the worst days.

Airlines carried nearly five billion passengers on 38 million flights in 2025, according to ICAO.

Sharing is the hard part

Brazil and Colombia have run such systems for years, Mr. Salazar said, but largely at national level while international flights cross many countries’ airspace.

“Technology alone is not the answer,” he said. Information has to be shared and often it isn’t, sometimes for lack of will, sometimes for lack of the means to transmit it in real time.

“A flight from Europe to Australia or New Zealand passes through four or five regions, different continents and that requires excellent coordination which doesn’t exist today,” he said. “No country or region acting alone can manage that.”

ICAO, with 193 member States, sets common standards and provides technical help so countries can coordinate regardless of resources. New international rules on flow management are due in November 2030, with regional workshops planned for 2027.

The pressure is mounting. ICAO projects air travel could reach 12.4 billion passengers by 2050.

A busier sky:

Other challenges are piling up. Conflicts force airlines to reroute around danger zones, creating new bottlenecks. Drones, air taxis, rocket launches and unplanned re-entries of objects from orbit all demand closer coordination.

For Mr. Salazar, the goal is simple: “an air transport system that reaches every person in the world, so that everyone sees the benefits of being connected.”

title: Iran nation is father, mother of bombs: Army cmdr. warns US
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 26 (MNA) – Lashing out at the US threat of Iran with bombs, Iranian Army Deputy Chief for Executive Affairs Brigadier General Alireza Sheikh has said that the Iranian nation is the father and mother of the bombs.
Referring to the US threat of renewing was against Iran, he stressed that people of the country will respond firmly to the enemy’s excessive demands and there is, therefore, no cause for concern in this regard.
The enemy cannot achieve its goals against such a nation, because a civilization cannot be destroyed by bombs, the Army commander highlighted.
“What matters is the readiness of the Army and other Armed Forces to respond to threats,” he said, adding that necessary preparations are in place, and today the Army Force stands ready, with its finger on the trigger, to respond to any threat.
Earlier, Deputy Coordinator of the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps, Brigadier General Mohammad Reza Naqdi, had warned the United States against any military miscalculation against Iran, saying Tehran would respond to Washington's "mother of all bombs" with the "father of bombs."

title: 2027: Atiku to campaign in all states — ADC campaign council
body: By Adegboyega Adeleye The African Democratic Congress (ADC) says its presidential candidate, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, will campaign in all 36 states ahead of the 2027 presidential election, according to the party’s Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu. Shaibu made the announcement during an interview on ARISE News on Sunday, saying no state would be left out of Atiku’s campaign. “We are going to release our schedule in a few days. Or in a few hours. And you will see for yourself. You will be able to interrogate for yourself. That look, Atiku Abubakar – no state will be left out,” Shaibu said. He said Atiku’s campaign would include town hall meetings and community visits, as well as rallies, and would reach local government areas and villages. “We are not going to limit our campaign to just state capital or to just rallies. Atiku is already connected with the people. The people are hungry. People are dying. Do you understand? He needs to connect with them. He needs to listen to them,” he said. Shaibu argued that economic hardship was affecting Nigerians across the country and said Atiku’s appeal was not confined to the North. “As for the pathway, I’ll tell you. Our pathway is clear and simple. The man who is hungry in Zamfara is the same as the man who is hungry in Lagos. Forget the noise,” he said. “Hungry Nigerians will vote for Atiku Abubakar. Atiku’s pathway is not limited to Northern Nigeria. Atiku’s pathway is across the length and breadth of Nigeria,” Shaibu added. Asked which southern states Atiku expected to win, he said, “I will not just be bold; I will be audacious about it. Atiku will win the entire country.” The pledge contrasts with Tinubu’s remarks at the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council in Abuja on October 14. The president said he would not travel with the campaign team to every rally, citing his duties in office and the country’s financial obligations. Vanguard previously reported Tinubu’s statement that “the responsibility of this office does not pause” and that the campaign team should “excuse me from going everywhere with you.” The ADC campaign council has also criticised Tinubu’s reported plan to make personal appearances in 12 states, arguing that a presidential candidate seeking re-election should meet voters across the country. The post 2027: Atiku to campaign in all states — ADC campaign council appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: TOR says refinery revival helped shield Ghana from Iran conflict fuel shocks
body: The Managing Director of the Tema Oil Refinery (TOR), Edmond Kombat, says the restoration of refining operations has helped strengthen Ghana’s resilience against international disruptions to petroleum supplies, including those associated with the Iran conflict. He said the refinery’s revival underscored the importance of maintaining domestic processing capacity at a time when geopolitical tensions could affect the availability and cost of imported petroleum products. Speaking at the Government Accountability Series at Jubilee House on Monday, October 26, 2026, Mr Kombat recalled President John Dramani Mahama’s remarks during the commissioning of TOR’s refurbished Crude Distillation Unit on August 1, 2026. “On August 1, 2026, H.E. the President noted that, because of the role played by TOR, Ghanaians were largely spared the effects of the Iran conflict on fuel supply,” he said. “This is why local refining capacity matters when international supplies are disrupted,” he added. Mr Kombat explained that TOR’s recovery was intended not only to restore an important state-owned enterprise but also to improve Ghana’s ability to process crude oil locally and support the domestic supply of petroleum products. The refinery’s Crude Distillation Unit had been out of operation since April 2021, while the Residue Fluid Catalytic Cracking unit had been shut down since 2019. The shutdowns significantly limited TOR’s capacity to process crude oil, leaving it largely dependent on storage-related activities rather than its core refining function. Following the current management’s appointment in May 2025, a turnaround maintenance programme was undertaken to rehabilitate the CDU and prepare it for a safe restart. Crude processing resumed on December 19, 2025, after the National Petroleum Authority inspected the plant and cleared it to restart operations. Mr Kombat said TOR had since received several crude cargoes, including Ghanaian indigenous crude from the Jubilee and Sankofa fields. He said the refinery’s nameplate capacity of 45,000 barrels per stream day would be equivalent to approximately 35 per cent of the 128,000 barrels of clean petroleum products Ghana imported daily in 2025. He noted that domestic refining could reduce the volume of finished petroleum products the country needs to import, while careful scheduling of crude deliveries could help maintain adequate stocks. Mr Kombat also highlighted the role of partnerships with the Ghana Oil Company Limited (GOIL), the National Petroleum Authority and the Bulk Oil Storage and Transportation Company Limited in strengthening petroleum supply arrangements. He said TOR’s recovery would continue to focus on restoring operational capacity, improving the reliability of crude supplies and supporting greater resilience in Ghana’s petroleum market.

title: Hearts of Oak’s Osei Asibey ‘ready’ for Black Stars call
body: Hearts of Oak defender Kelvin Osei Asibey believes he is ready for an invitation into the Black Stars team following his strong start to the season. The defender has been a strong force for the Phobians, who are joint-top of the Ghana Premier League after eight games played. Following his impressive performances, including his outing against Basake Holy Stars over the weekend, Asibey has expressed readiness to wear the national team colours for the upcoming 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifiers against Somalia. “As long as I am a citizen of the Republic of Ghana, I am ready; whenever the nation needs my services, I’ll come and serve the nation very well,” Asibey said following the Phobians’ victory over Holy Stars. As recognition for his sterling performances, Asibey has been named Player of the Match for Heart’s last three games, indicating his importance for Nebojsa Kapor’s side in the Ghanaian top flight. The Black Stars are chasing a first win in the qualifiers after losing to Cote d’Ivoire and Gambia but are up for a doubleheader against Somalia next month.

title: Octopus Kokkinisto: A Simple Greek Octopus Stew in Tomato Sauce
body: Octopus kokkinisto, a slow-simmered Greek favourite, needs just seven ingredients and no added water. Octopus in tomato sauce with red onions. Photo: Allrecipes What is octopus kokkinisto? Kokkinisto comes from the Greek word for red, and it describes meat or seafood braised in a tomato sauce. The same method gives us the Sunday beef stew found in many Greek homes. With seafood, the result is octopus kokkinisto, also called octapodi kokkinisto. Octopus has a long history at the Greek table. According to Wikipedia , it counts as a superb meze, especially alongside ouzo. On the islands, fishermen hang octopus in the sun before grilling, as we explained in why Greeks sun-dry their catch . This braise takes a gentler route, so it suits a home kitchen. It is also a popular choice during Lent. Orthodox Christians may eat shellfish and molluscs while they fast from meat. Seafood dishes are also a tradition on Kathara Deftera , or Clean Monday. Read more about the custom on Wikipedia . Ingredients for six serves This octopus kokkinisto comes from Diana Moutsopoulos, a contributor on Allrecipes. It holds 4.6 out of 5 from 15 ratings, and 27 home cooks say they have made it. Each serve has about 412 calories and 24 g of protein, according to Allrecipes. You need: 2 pounds (about 900 g) octopus, cut into 7.5 cm pieces 3/4 US cup (about 180 ml) olive oil 8 small red onions, cut into thin wedges 3 bay leaves 2 US cups (about 500 ml) crushed tomatoes 1/2 teaspoon sea salt Freshly ground black pepper, to taste Australian cooks can use one 400 g tin of crushed tomatoes plus a little extra. Frozen octopus from the fish market works well too, but thaw it in the fridge overnight first. Diana gives one firm rule for octapodi kokkinisto. Never add water, because the octopus should cook in its own juices for the best flavour. How to make octopus kokkinisto Allrecipes lists 20 minutes of preparation and 70 minutes of cooking. So, octopus kokkinisto takes about 1 hour and 30 minutes in total. First, place the octopus pieces in a large saucepan without any liquid. Cover and cook over medium-high heat for 10 to 15 minutes, until the octopus gives off its juices. Next, remove the lid and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, until only 45 to 60 ml of liquid remains. Drizzle in the olive oil, then add the onions and bay leaves. Stir often for about 10 minutes, until the onions soften. Add the tomatoes, salt and pepper, then lower the heat to medium-low. Cover and simmer for about 25 minutes, until the octopus is tender and the sauce is thick. Finally, if the sauce looks thin, cook it uncovered for the last 10 minutes. Octopus kokkinisto rewards patience. Test a piece with a knife before you serve it, and give it more time if it still feels firm. A heavy pot with a tight lid helps, since it holds in the juices during the first stage. Remove the bay leaves before serving. Tips from home cooks Allrecipes shows seven reviews for this octopus kokkinisto. In the most helpful review, Victoria used frozen octopus, two large onions and some chopped Greek olives. She called the result “‘out of the park’ delicious” and said the leftovers were just as good. Kristi Howell, however, gave four stars because of the eight onions. She used two large red onions instead and found the dish improved after a night in the fridge. Ken Roberts was full of praise: “Best octopus recipe I’ve tried.” Nisan Vue said it beat expectations for something so simple, and added, “I think patience was the key ingredient.” Other cooks made small changes to the octopus in tomato sauce. Anastasia Daleiden deglazed the pan with brandy, while Richard used squid instead of octopus. Olga found it a bit salty, so taste the sauce before you add all the salt. Hester G. used whole baby octopus with some cuttlefish, and had to look up how to clean them. If you are unsure, ask your fishmonger to clean it for you. A first-timer, zackmania, also added garlic and halved Greek olives before the tomatoes. Serving octopus kokkinisto Diana suggests serving the dish with hand-cut chips or rice. Some reviewers served it with pasta or crusty bread to soak up the sauce. If you love seafood, try our white wine version or this version with short pasta . Both make a good match for a Greek salad and a glass of ouzo. The full method is in the original recipe on Allrecipes . Octopus kokkinisto also makes great leftovers, and one reviewer found it even better the next day. title: Russia, Ethiopia discuss increasing flights to Addis Ababa — Russian ambassador
body:
MOSCOW, October 26. /TASS/. Russian and Ethiopian officials are in talks on increasing flight frequencies, Russian Ambassador to Ethiopia Evgeny Terekhin told TASS in an interview ahead of the Russia-Africa Summit.
"Expanding flight frequencies and launching services by Russian airlines remain on the agenda of discussions between the two countries’ aviation authorities and depend on commercial passenger demand," the diplomat said.
He pointed out that "Bole International Airport in Addis Ababa serves as a key aviation hub for travel to Africa." "Ethiopian Airlines operates six direct flights a week between Addis Ababa and Moscow," Terekhin noted.
In his view, "the construction of a new transcontinental airport in Bishoftu, 40 km from the capital, designed to handle 100 mln passengers annually, will be a significant factor in improving the region’s transport accessibility."

title: TOR says GH¢10bn accumulated losses, US$517m debt confronted under new management
body: The Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) had accumulated losses of approximately GH¢10 billion and debt of about US$517 million when the current management assumed office in May 2025, Managing Director Edmond Kombat has disclosed. He said the refinery’s financial position had deteriorated significantly over the years, alongside prolonged operational shutdowns, outstanding statutory obligations and growing liabilities to creditors. Speaking at the Government Accountability Series at Jubilee House on Monday, October 26, 2026, Mr Kombat said the company had also recorded negative equity of GH¢7.6 billion by the end of 2024. He contrasted the position with January 2017, when the previous NDC administration handed over a refinery whose debt had been reduced from approximately US$650 million to US$300 million. According to him, the earlier restructuring was supported by the Energy Sector Levies Act, while exposures to four banks had been settled. By the time the current management took over, however, the CDU had been inactive since April 2021 and the RFCC unit since 2019. The refinery had also failed to file audited financial statements for six consecutive years, from 2019 to 2024. Mr Kombat said TOR owed approximately GH¢200 million to the Ghana Revenue Authority and GH¢20 million to SSNIT, alongside outstanding amounts due to the Electricity Company of Ghana, Ghana Water Company and other creditors. The company also had about GH¢190 million in outstanding obligations to its staff provident fund, retirees and former employees. “By the end of 2024, TOR had negative equity of GH¢7.6 billion,” he said. He added that the company had been reduced largely to renting storage space instead of carrying out its core mandate of refining crude oil. Mr Kombat said management had responded by introducing a financial restructuring programme, commissioning an independent assessment of liabilities and engaging creditors on sustainable repayment arrangements. It also pursued outstanding receivables, reviewed unaudited accounts and improved financial controls. The refinery has since completed the outstanding audited accounts for 2019 to 2024 and the 2025 accounts, while recording a profit before tax of GH¢1.24 billion in 2025, according to SIGA. Mr Kombat said the company’s trade and other payables had fallen from GH¢7.1 billion to GH¢5 billion within a year. He disclosed that the Ministry of Finance was working with TOR to consider writing off US$120 million in legacy debt owed to the government or converting it into equity. The Managing Director said management recognised that the refinery still had significant obligations to address but remained committed to improving its financial position and restoring its commercial viability.

title: Ukraine ready to expand cooperation with Serbia – Zelenskyy
body:
President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy has congratulated the Student List on its victory in the parliamentary elections in Serbia, calling it a new page in the country's history, and stated Ukraine's readiness to expand cooperation with Serbia.
"Changes have taken place in Serbia – the victory of the 'Student List', and this is obviously a new page in the history of the country and the people," Zelenskyy wrote on the social network X on Monday.
He wished Serbia success, real development, and warm relations with the European community.
"We in Ukraine thank Serbia for its respect for our people and state, our independence. And we are always glad of our common results – everything that strengthens our societies and gives people more opportunities. We are ready to continue increasing our cooperation, and may all the good hopes of the people in Serbia be realized," the president noted.
On October 25, the leader of the ruling Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) and candidate for prime minister, Aleksandar Vucic, conceded defeat of his political force in Sunday's snap parliamentary elections, losing to the opposition student protest movement, Reuters reported.
"We do not have final results yet, but based on the sample... it is clear that we lost these elections. The Student List won: they will have between 135 and 140 seats, and we have 105, no one else entered parliament," Vucic told reporters.
The snap elections were called by Vucic in September following nearly two years of continuous student protests against corruption and the tightening of government authoritarianism. The demonstrations erupted after the tragedy in the city of Novi Sad in 2024, where 16 people died due to the collapse of a canopy at the railway station.
The student movement gained broad public support and became the biggest political challenge to Vucic since he came to power as prime minister in 2014 and was subsequently elected president in 2017.

title: Trump praises Libyans after campaign insult sparks diplomatic protest
body: US President Donald Trump praised Libyans as “proud, resilient, hospitable” after his disparaging remarks at a campaign rally prompted a diplomatic protest from Tripoli and condemnation across the country’s political divide. The conciliatory statement, posted on Sunday evening, stopped short of an apology and included a demand that Libya stop serving as a corridor for irregular migration. “The Libyan people are proud, resilient, hospitable, and deserving of peace and prosperity,” Mr Trump wrote on Truth Social, reaffirming Washington’s commitment to stronger relations with the North African country. “We respect the Libyan people and the sacrifices that brave Libyans made fighting ISIS, the common enemy of both our peoples, but Libya cannot remain a corridor for illegal migration, and this must end now,” he said. The remarks followed Libya’s decision to summon the US chargé d’affaires on Sunday over comments Mr Trump made a day earlier at a rally in Perry, Georgia. Attacking Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff over immigration, Mr Trump accused him of sponsoring legislation to bring migrants from countries he described as “terror-infested”, including Libya, Yemen, Haiti and Somalia. “Remember what I called them?,” he said, using a highly disparaging expletive. Libya’s Foreign Ministry delivered a formal protest to the American diplomat over what it said were statements undermining the dignity of Libyans. The Presidential Council said it had instructed the ministry to summon the head of the US diplomatic mission and demanded an explicit apology and correction. It said relations between countries should be based on mutual respect. Prime Minister Abdul Hamid Dbeibah, who heads the Tripoli-based Government of National Unity, also rejected the remarks in a social media post, saying Libya’s sovereignty and its people’s dignity should not become material for American electoral disputes. “We value our relationship with the United States on the basis of mutual respect, and we will not accept Libya’s dignity and that of its people becoming material for electoral disputes,” he said. Mr Dbeibah invoked Libyans’ sacrifices in fighting terrorism, a contribution Mr Trump subsequently acknowledged in his statement describing ISIS as a common enemy of both countries. The criticism extended beyond the Tripoli administration. Libya’s rival eastern government called for a retraction and formal apology, while a committee of the House of Representatives sought an official clarification from Washington. The committee said the remarks diminished Libya’s standing. The competing administrations’ responses placed them on common ground in rejecting the insult, despite their wider political differences. In his subsequent statement, Mr Trump backed efforts to unify Libya and its institutions and move towards national elections. He said Washington supports Libyans in restoring their sovereignty after years of terrorism and foreign interference. He offered no timetable or new initiative to advance those goals, and did not specify what measures he expected Libya to take on migration.

title: What happens on Israeli election day?
body: Read the latest on Israel's election here Israel heads to the polls on Tuesday in what is seen as one of the most pivotal and consequential elections in its recent history. The election is Israeli voters' first opportunity to hold leaders accountable for security failures surrounding the October 7, 2023, attacks, decide who should lead Israel in the regional conflict and weigh in on the contentious issue of military service. So what happens on election day and when can we expect the results? The timeline All times are Israel local time. The UAE is two hours ahead. 7am: Polling stations open Voting begins at most polling stations nationwide, with Israelis electing representatives to the 120-seat Knesset. About 7.3 million Israelis are eligible to vote. Thirty six parties are running, although most will not pass the 3.25 per cent threshold needed to enter parliament. 8am: Special polling stations open Voting begins in smaller communities, hospitals, prisons and care homes, where polling stations generally operate for shorter hours. Throughout the day: Voting continues Turnout figures are expected at regular intervals, offering an early indication of voter enthusiasm. Political leaders will cast their ballots. 8pm: Special polling stations close Voting ends at most smaller-community and institutional polling stations. Voters who arrived before closing can still cast their ballots. 10pm: Main polling stations close Voting officially ends at most polling stations nationwide, although those already in line can still vote. After 10pm: Exit polls and vote counting Israeli television networks are expected to release their exit polls, providing the first indication of how parties may perform. Preliminary results will emerge as votes are counted overnight. Final results will take another week or so. The election process Israel's parliament, known as the Knesset, has 120 seats, with 61 needed for an outright majority. Israel uses a proportional representation system, meaning voters choose political parties rather than directly electing a prime minister. No single party has ever won an outright majority, so governments have always been formed through coalitions. Once the results are confirmed, Israeli President Isaac Herzog will task a member of parliament with forming a government, usually the leader considered most capable of securing parliamentary support. If no coalition can secure a majority, a minority government could still be formed with sufficient parliamentary backing. If attempts to form a government fail, Israel could face another election, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu leading a caretaker government in the meantime. The results At 10pm on election day, Israeli broadcasters will release exit polls. But these are only projections and can differ significantly from the actual results. Preliminary results are expected the following day, with official results scheduled to be published by November 4. The deadline for appeals is November 18. Election results will not necessarily determine who Israel's next prime minister will be. Coalition negotiations can take weeks or even months as parties attempt to reach agreements on who will govern and under what terms. Israel has a history of political deadlock. Between 2019 and 2022, the country held five elections as parties repeatedly struggled to form stable governments. So while voters may have an indicator of the results on election night, it could take much longer to know who will actually lead the country.

title: WHO: Nigeria Has No Ebola Cases After Patient’s Evacuation to Switzerland
body: The World Health Organisation (WHO) Regional Director for Africa, Dr Mohamed Janabi, says Nigeria currently has no Ebola cases following the medical evacuation of the patient and her husband to Switzerland. Janabi disclosed this in a statement on his official X handle on Monday, adding that Nigeria would continue monitoring 52 contacts, while Switzerland would manage the patient and follow up her husband. He said the evacuation took place earlier in the morning, noting that both the patient and her husband were Swiss citizens. According to him, the patient was clinically stable after Nigerian medical teams successfully managed her through the acute phase of the illness and stabilised her condition. Janabi congratulated the Federal Government, health workers, clinicians, emergency responders and other partners involved in the Ebola response, describing the development as a remarkable achievement. He said the successful management of the patient demonstrated Africa’s expertise, resilience and leadership in public health, particularly when countries worked together to respond to health emergencies. However, the WHO regional director stressed that vigilance remained critical despite the evacuation, urging continued attention to contact monitoring and other response measures. He said Nigeria would maintain close follow-up of 52 contacts, while Switzerland would assume responsibility for the continued management of the patient and monitoring of contact number 53, her husband.(NAN)

title: Adamawa govt distributes relief materials to flood victims
body: The Adamawa State Emergency Management Agency (ADSEMA) has distributed food and non-food relief materials to victims of recent flooding in Madagali and Guyuk Local Government Areas of the state. The distribution exercise, conducted on Saturday , was coordinated by the agency’s Permanent Secretary, Dr. Celine Kwamoti La’ori, through representatives of ADSEMA. The intervention, approved by Governor Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri, was aimed at alleviating the hardship faced by flood-affected households and providing immediate assistance to vulnerable families in the affected communities. In Madagali Local Government Area, the relief materials were received on behalf of the Executive Chairman by his Protocol Officer, Mr. Buba Mohammed, alongside his Media Aide, Yusuf Abba. Similarly, in Guyuk Local Government Area, the items were received by the Commissioner for Transportation, Hon. Wunfe Anthony, and the Vice Chairman of Guyuk Local Government Council, Hon. Zamani Saidu. Representatives of both local government areas expressed appreciation to Governor Fintiri for approving the intervention and responding to the needs of flood-affected communities. ADSEMA reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to disaster response, humanitarian assistance and the welfare of vulnerable residents, assuring affected communities of continued support. Beneficiaries in both local government areas also commended the state government for the timely intervention, describing the relief assistance as crucial to easing their hardship.

title: Sweden Selects Saildrone for Year-long MDA Mission in the Baltic Sea
body: Saildrone announced a year-long mission with the Swedish Armed Forces to deliver persistent Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA) across Sweden’s territorial waters and exclusive economic zone in the Baltic Sea. Saildrone press release Under the agreement, Saildrone will deploy and operate four Voyager unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) for 360 days each, representing 1,440 contracted vehicle-days of continuous maritime security operations. This deployment marks the first national deployment of Saildrone USVs under the Nordic Defence Cooperation (NORDEFCO) framework that enables participating Nordic nations to rapidly procure Saildrone maritime domain awareness services. Additional national deployments under the framework will follow. The 12-month commitment highlights a decisive shift toward long-term operational capabilities, with the Swedish Armed Forces securing a full year of persistent maritime domain awareness to safeguard critical waters from the outset. “This is fundamentally not about four unmanned vessels, but about access to sustained intelligence collection at sea. In other words, we are purchasing a persistent maritime surveillance service, and Saildrone provides the vessels that supply the Navy with data,” said Johan Wahren, project manager at Sweden’s Defence Materiel Administration (FMV) in a FMV press release . Saildrone picture NORDEFCO is a cooperative organization that unites Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden, and other Northern European countries to streamline defense cooperation and field proven regional security solutions. The Saildrone Voyager fleet will continuously patrol Sweden’s territorial waters in the Baltic Sea, delivering real-time maritime intelligence directly to the Swedish Armed Forces. Operating as a managed service, Saildrone maintains, deploys, and tasks the USVs, enabling Sweden to maintain persistent maritime domain awareness without deploying additional crewed ships. “This mission reflects Sweden’s commitment to securing the Baltic Sea and highlights Saildrone’s growing operational presence across Northern Europe,” said Robert Kleist, Saildrone’s European managing director. “Sweden is investing in year-round maritime awareness as an operational capability. The NORDEFCO framework gives Nordic nations a common mechanism for accessing that capability while allowing each country to define and operate its own mission.” Saildrone delivers persistent maritime domain awareness for navies and law enforcement operating in the world’s harshest maritime environments. The company has supported defense and security missions in places ranging from the Baltic Sea and the High North to the Southern Ocean and the Middle East. Saildrone recently registered four Saildrone Voyager USVs in Denmark to operate under the Danish national flag. The registration establishes a clear flag-state framework for Saildrone USVs operating internationally and supports the company operating alongside various European nations. Saildrone Europe will flag additional Saildrone USVs in the coming weeks. – End – The post Sweden Selects Saildrone for Year-long MDA Mission in the Baltic Sea appeared first on Naval News .

title: Netherlands pledges technical support and investment to boost Ghana’s poultry industry
body: The Netherlands has pledged to support Ghana’s efforts to develop a stronger and more competitive poultry industry through technical expertise, knowledge exchange and investment. The Netherlands Ambassador to Ghana, H.E. Hans Akerboom, said his country was ready to work with Ghanaian stakeholders to identify practical solutions to challenges facing the sector and expand opportunities for local poultry farmers and businesses. Speaking at a poultry round-table discussion in Accra on Monday, October 26, 2026, he said stronger collaboration between the two countries could help Ghana harness its growing poultry market to increase domestic production and create jobs. H.E. Akerboom said the Netherlands welcomed the country’s ambition to strengthen its poultry sector and was committed to exploring ways to translate the partnership into tangible results. “We warmly welcome this ambition and we are committed to exploring how we can translate it into a clear result,” he said. He noted that the Netherlands had developed its poultry industry through sustained investment in knowledge, innovation and collaboration, adding that these experiences could help inform Ghana’s efforts, taking into account the country’s specific needs. The Ambassador said the partnership was particularly important given Ghana’s reliance on imported poultry to meet domestic demand. He disclosed that Ghana imported poultry worth approximately €18 million from the Netherlands alone in 2024, while other supplies came from countries including Belgium, the United States and Brazil. The two countries have also signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on how to strengthen the sector According to him, the figures highlighted the potential for Ghanaian farmers and businesses to increase their share of the domestic market. Mr Akerboom stressed that the objective should go beyond reducing imports to creating conditions that would enable local farmers to expand production, supply the market consistently and benefit from existing demand.

title: Gov Fintiri urges FG to upgrade FCE Yola to university
body: Adamawa State Governor, Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri, has appealed to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to consider upgrading the Federal College of Education (FCE), Yola, to a Federal University of Education to strengthen teacher training and produce more qualified teachers for the country. Governor Fintiri made the appeal on Saturday during the institution’s 16th Combined Convocation Ceremony in Yola, where he was represented by his Deputy, Professor Kaletapwa Farauta. The Governor reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to educational development, stressing that the state remains focused on implementing policies aimed at improving access to quality education and working towards the 26 per cent budgetary allocation benchmark for education commonly associated with UNESCO. He noted that the administration has introduced several people-oriented policies to revitalise the education sector through increased funding, institutional strengthening and improved learning opportunities. According to him, the government has also made significant investments in Information and Communication Technology (ICT), introducing student-friendly programmes designed to equip young people with essential skills for a technology-driven economy. The Governor further highlighted initiatives targeting youth empowerment, including business grants, startup incubation programmes and mentorship opportunities. He disclosed that the state government had introduced the Adamawa State Teacher Recruitment, Deployment and Retention Policy to strengthen teacher education and align the state’s educational system with 21st-century demands. He consequently urged the institution to align its programmes with relevant education policies to enhance teacher training and professional development. Earlier, the Provost of FCE Yola, Mohammed Usman Degereji, disclosed that the institution graduated 3,555 students, comprising 1,818 from the 2024 academic session and 1,737 from 2025. He explained that the graduands had satisfied the academic and character requirements for the award of the Nigeria Certificate in Education (NCE). Degereji encouraged educational institutions and other stakeholders to make effective use of the graduates’ skills and knowledge, noting that several had distinguished themselves through outstanding academic performance. He added that more than 200 academic staff members had participated in national and international conferences under his leadership as part of efforts to improve teaching standards and academic excellence. Also speaking, the Minister of Education, represented by Dr. Uchenna Uba, Director of Colleges of Education at the Federal Ministry of Education, reiterated the Federal Government’s commitment to improving the welfare of education sector personnel. She highlighted the Tertiary Institutions Staff Support Fund (TISSF), a Federal Government initiative designed to provide financial assistance and improve the welfare of staff in tertiary institutions.

title: Outrage as viral video shows youth preaching religious intolerance, violence
body:
Nigerians on social media have demanded an investigation of a viral video showing a young man leading a group of boys in chanting violent threats against Christians.
The footage, which has circulated widely on Facebook and X, captures the unidentified man leading the boys, all dressed in JIBWIS volunteer uniforms, through an unpaved street as they march and chant in Hausa.
In the video, the leader is heard soliciting assault rifles to carry out mass killings in churches in Enugu and Plateau states.
“Give me an AK-47 so that I will go to Enugu and kill non-Muslims on Sunday while they are praying. Give me guns so I will go to Jos and kill more infidels,” the man chants, with the children chorusing after him.
The uniforms worn by the children match the attire of the First Aid Group of Jama’atu Izalatil Bid’ah Wa Iqamatis Sunnah (JIBWIS)—the prominent Islamic organisation’s humanitarian wing, locally known as ’Yan Agaji.
However, it remains unconfirmed whether the participants are officially registered members of the group or if the display was sanctioned by JIBWIS leadership.
The clip has sparked widespread condemnation across religious and ethnic divides, amplifying fears over child indoctrination, rising religious intolerance, and threats to national unity.
Reacting on Facebook, Najib Sani called for urgent reform in local religious schools.
“Some Islamiyya teachers need reorientation; they must stop poisoning the minds of children with hatred. In Nigeria, Muslims and Christians, northerners and southerners, are brothers sharing the same nation. This brand of bigotry has no place in our society.”
Another user, Abban Malami, warned of the long-term national security implications:
“We are not serious as a country. These small children are openly being groomed in religious extremism and Boko Haram ideology. We watch this happen without taking decisive action, and when they pick up arms tomorrow, we will pretend to be surprised and tell people to pray.”
Joining her voice to the outrage, Maryam Abdullahi noted:
“Children are blank slates; what you pour into them is what comes out. Whoever weaponised these innocent kids with such toxic hatred should be arrested immediately.
True Islam preaches peace and the preservation of human life, not slaughtering neighbours.”
Ali Chukwudi, another Facebook user, said:
“These are the monsters some political vampires, hiding under the title of scholars, are grooming and training in Northern Nigeria. It is frightening how hatred is being packaged as religious knowledge and fed to young minds.
“Let me make this clear to those tagging me in this post: This is not Islam. Our religion teaches love, justice, compassion and peaceful coexistence, not hatred, intimidation or violence against people of different faiths.
“However, religious extremism and hate speech should never be treated as harmless statements. The government and relevant security agencies must wake up and address this growing danger before it becomes another national tragedy.
“I vividly remember that last year, a group of people allegedly created a platform where they discussed plans to capture and bury Igbo Muslims alive. The disturbing plot eventually leaked to the public, yet, to the best of my knowledge, nobody has been arrested or held accountable.
“How many more threats must be made before the authorities take action?
“I am calling on the relevant security agencies to investigate this matter, identify and apprehend not just the individuals directly involved but also the leadership of the organisation responsible for creating an environment where such dangerous ideologies are promoted. You cannot preach peace with one hand and groom hatred with the other”, Mr Chukwudi stated on Facebook.
As of filing this report, neither security agencies nor the national leadership of JIBWIS have issued an official statement regarding the incident.
The location of the recording and the precise identities of those involved have yet to be independently verified.

title: TOR targets 55,000 barrels per stream day as F-61 crude heater work continues
body: The Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) is working to increase its crude-processing rate from approximately 28,000 barrels per stream day to between 45,000 and 55,000 barrels per stream day, Managing Director Edmond Kombat has announced. He said engineers from Verga Engineering were working alongside TOR’s technical team to complete the tie-in and commission the F-61 crude heater, a critical component in the refinery’s ongoing operational recovery. Speaking at the Government Accountability Series at Jubilee House on Monday, October 26, 2026, Mr Kombat said the work was expected to improve the performance of the Crude Distillation Unit (CDU) and move the plant towards its nameplate capacity. “Engineers from Verga Engineering are currently on site, working on with TOR’s technical team to increase the throughput to between 45,000bpsd to 55,000bpsd,” he said. The CDU was refurbished under a turnaround maintenance programme conducted between August 1 and October 30, 2025. Crude processing resumed on December 19, 2025, after the National Petroleum Authority inspected the plant and cleared it for operations. President John Dramani Mahama subsequently commissioned the refurbished unit on August 1, 2026. Mr Kombat said management had prioritised the CDU’s rehabilitation after inheriting a refinery whose major processing units had remained inactive for several years. The CDU had been out of operation since April 2021, while the Residue Fluid Catalytic Cracking (RFCC) unit had been shut down since 2019. He said the turnaround maintenance was funded entirely from TOR’s internally generated funds and carried out by the refinery’s engineers and technicians. “Work also resumed on critical stalled projects, including Boiler No. 8, the F-61 Crude Heater, the Residue Air Cooler and the Steam Turbine Generator,” he said. Management is also planning to install a new air cooler to increase processing capacity to 60,000 barrels per stream day and replace the existing 6,500-barrel-a-day catalytic reformers with a 10,000-barrel-per-day continuous catalytic reformer. Mr Kombat said a new 120-tonne boiler had been installed, while work continued on the RFCC turnaround and the SCADA system. Beyond the immediate engineering interventions, the government has directed TOR’s board and management to develop a roadmap for increasing processing capacity to 100,000 barrels per day, with a longer-term ambition of reaching 200,000 barrels per day. Mr Kombat said the proposed improvements were intended to strengthen refining capacity, improve operational reliability and increase the refinery’s contribution to domestic petroleum supply. He acknowledged that the recovery process was ongoing, adding that management remained focused on completing outstanding engineering works and sustaining the gains made since operations resumed.

title: Gram 3.4.0 released
body:
This release was triggered by the eMudhra CA debacle and getting informed that Gram is vulnerable due to shipping the rustls-webpki and webpki-roots packages. Thus, I recommend everyone to upgrade to 3.4.0 as soon as possible. If you want to stay on an older version you should rebuild from source with updated webpki packages.
Although the release was ultimately due to that, it was getting time to tag a new release anyway. There have been a lot of fixes and some really great new features implemented, and I want to give a huge thank you to everyone who have been contributing and helping with the editor. One of the reasons why I have been holding off on the release is just that I have been so busy this week and haven't had time to highlight all the improvements as much as I would like to.
Here is a very incomplete list of highlights with this release. More complete changelog below..
...OK, it's already too many things, I'm getting lost. Check out the changelog for more!
One thing that has changed that isn't entirely positive is that I have found and patched a lot more cases where the editor would download stuff behind our backs without consent. I am determined to close all of these gaps over time, but a consequence of this is that the editor is a bit more annoying to use now. The UI for allowing downloads or discovering why a language server isn't running is not good. I know. I am working on something better. A couple of us have also been experimenting with replacing or supplanting the Zed extension system with something more light-weight which would make installing and managing extensions better. I guess another reason why I didn't tag a release sooner is because I was hoping to fix some of these usability issues. It'll just have to wait until the next release. My apologies for any inconvenience caused by these changes.
Again a massive thank you to everyone who are contributing, hanging out in the XMPP chat channel or just using the editor.
Downloads will as usual be available on Codeberg .

title: Greece Announces Air Force Celebrations With F-16 and F-35 Displays
body: Greece will mark the Hellenic Air Force’s annual celebration honouring its patron saint, Archangel Michael, from November 4 to 8, with aircraft displays, public events, flight simulators and demonstrations across the country. The five-day programme will give the public opportunities to experience military aviation, explore air bases and watch aerial demonstrations by the Hellenic Air Force’s renowned F-16 “Zeus” and T-6A “Daedalus” display teams. Ahead of the main celebrations, an aviation exhibition will operate at Syntagma Metro Station in central Athens from October 30 to November 1, between 9am and 9pm. Admission will be free, with F-16 and F-35 flight simulators, virtual reality experiences, aviation exhibits, information stands and a concert by the Air Force music ensemble. Aircraft Displays Across Greece On Thursday, November 5, Hellenic Air Force aircraft are scheduled to fly over cities, towns and islands across northeastern, northern and southeastern Greece, beginning at approximately 9am. The planned routes include Larissa, Ioannina, Alexandroupoli, Kavala, Volos, Rhodes, Karpathos, Heraklion, Rethymno and Chania, alongside numerous Aegean islands. Further flyovers are scheduled for Friday, November 6, covering eastern Greece, the Peloponnese, central Greece and the northwest. Planned locations include Chios, Samos, Mykonos, Chalkida, Patras, Corfu, Kefalonia and Zakynthos. The Air Force said flight routes and timings may change, or displays may be cancelled, depending on weather conditions. Air Shows in Crete, Alexandroupoli and Beyond The public programme will feature several headline aerial displays. On Saturday, November 7, the F-16 “Zeus” display team and the T-6A “Daedalus” team are scheduled to perform at Karavola Park in Heraklion, Crete, from 11am. An F-16 “Zeus” display is also planned for Alexandroupoli beach at noon. On Sunday, November 8, the F-16 “Zeus” team is scheduled to perform at Larissa Air Base at noon, followed by a T-6A “Daedalus” display at Kalamata beach at 2pm. These demonstrations are also subject to weather conditions. Air Bases Open to the Public Hellenic Air Force bases will welcome visitors from November 4 to 7, between 9am and 5pm, and on November 8 from 1pm to 5pm. The main celebration on Sunday will take place at the Icarus School at Dekelia Air Base, beginning with a memorial service and wreath-laying ceremony at 9am at the Monument to Fallen Airmen. An official doxology will follow at 11am. An open day will run from 1pm to 8pm, featuring F-16 and F-35 flight simulators, virtual reality activities, aviation exhibitions, an aviation-themed escape room, quizzes, a historic aircraft diorama and children’s sporting activities led by distinguished Olympians. The programme will also include a screening of the film Stealth: The Invisible Menace , martial arts demonstrations, food and drink areas, a concert featuring DJ Pablo Nuevo and radio producer Fanis Lambropoulos, and a drone demonstration scheduled for 6.30pm. Additional activities include a flight experience for selected students at the Icarus School on November 6. Celebrating Greece’s Air Force Archangel Michael is the patron saint of the Hellenic Air Force, and the annual celebrations honour the service and sacrifice of Greek military aviators. The events combine official commemorations with public engagement, offering families, aviation enthusiasts and students opportunities to learn more about Greece’s air power and the personnel who protect its skies. The Hellenic Air Force has advised that all flight displays and outdoor activities remain subject to operational requirements and weather conditions.
