title: [Ask the Tax Whiz] BIR backs down on QR badges. Will it dare audit the powerful?
body: An open letter to Commissioner Charlito Mendoza : Suspending the QR badge mandate is a welcome development. But the real test of tax reform is whether the BIR can investigate unexplained wealth without fear or favor. Dear Commissioner Mendoza, Your decision to suspend the mandatory display of BIR Registration Seal Badges under Revenue Memorandum Circular (RMC) No. 113-2026 deserves recognition. The October 31 deadline has been suspended . Display is now voluntary, with no penalties solely for non-display during the suspension. Listening to taxpayers is good governance. But reversing a requirement five days before its deadline raises a bigger question: Why weren’t privacy concerns, technical readiness, and stakeholder consultations addressed before compliance was required? The Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) reported that more than 52,700 registration documents with badges had been secured by October 14. This warrants an assessment of taxpayers’ time and compliance costs. The suspension should not mark the end of reform. It should establish a new standard for taxpayer-centered regulation. Consider electronic invoicing or e-invoicing. The TRAIN Law established a system-dependent framework beginning in 2018. Eight years later, RMC No. 98-2026 requires specified taxpayers to comply by December 31, with micro e-commerce taxpayers exempted. RMC No. 110-2026 introduces accreditation requirements for third-party service providers. (READ: [Ask the Tax Whiz] Guidelines on VAT for Nonresident Digital Service Providers ) I support digitalization. But if government needed eight years to implement reform, why should taxpayers shoulder disproportionate software costs, technical difficulties, and potential penalties? Accreditation must safeguard data and promote competition—not create unnecessary barriers for Filipino technology providers. GOVERNMENT DELAYS MUST NOT BECOME TAXPAYER PENALTIES. Businesses struggling to comply are not automatically tax evaders. Modernization must make compliance easier for taxpayers—not merely administration easier for the BIR. According to 2024 government statistics, MSMEs account for 99.63% of Philippine establishments and 66.58% of employment. These enterprises deserve proportionate regulations, not unnecessary bureaucracy. Meanwhile, the Philippines scored just 32 out of 100, ranking 120th among 182 countries, in Transparency International’s 2025 Corruption Perceptions Index . The index does not establish wrongdoing by any individual. But it underscores a serious public-trust challenge. One disturbing sentiment circulating online captures the frustration: “PAYING TAXES AT THIS POINT FEELS LIKE SPONSORING CRIMINALS.” This is no justification for tax evasion. It is a warning about eroding confidence in government accountability. Commissioner, I challenge the BIR to launch a NATIONWIDE, RISK-BASED TAX AUDIT INITIATIVE targeting credible evidence of undeclared taxable income and unexplained wealth involving politicians, political dynasties, and public officials—from barangay halls to Malacañang. NO SACRED COWS. NO POLITICAL EXEMPTIONS. NO SELECTIVE ENFORCEMENT. Wealth or political connections alone do not establish wrongdoing. But credible discrepancies between lawful income and accumulated assets deserve investigation. Use legally authorized cross-checks of tax returns, Statements of Assets Liabilities and Net Worth (SALNs), property records, and beneficial ownership information. Coordinate with the Ombudsman and the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) when warranted. Build on RMO No. 22-2026 through three measurable reforms: First, protect low-risk taxpayers. Generally exclude startups during their first three years and MSMEs with annual sales not exceeding ₱100 million from routine audit, except where credible tax risks exist. Second, reduce compliance costs. Provide affordable electronic invoicing, just transition, and competitive provider accreditation. Third, demonstrate accountability. Publish anonymized results on high-risk investigations, final assessments, actual collections, and taxpayer compliance costs. Commissioner, suspending the badge requirement shows that the BIR can respond when taxpayers raise legitimate concerns. But the bigger test is whether it can investigate the politically powerful with the same determination it regulates ordinary Filipinos. CAN THE BIR AUDIT THE POWERFUL WITH THE SAME ZEAL IT AUDITS ORDINARY TAXPAYERS? Because honest taxpayers are not the enemy. Corruption and tax evasion are. AUDIT THE POWERFUL. PROTECT THE SMALL. RESTORE PUBLIC TRUST. – Rappler.com Mon Abrea , CPA, MBA, MPA (Harvard) is a global tax policy expert and Chief Tax Advisor of Asian Consulting Group (ACGlobal). He advises governments, multinational enterprises, and international organizations on tax policy, investment competitiveness, and fiscal reform. He is the author of Reimagining the World Without Corruption and Why Invest in the Philippines? CREATE MORE Edition, and has represented the Philippines in policy dialogues at the OECD, World Bank, and other international forums. Must Read [Ask the Tax Whiz] When power is inherited, who holds it accountable?

title: Iran says Policies will remain unchanged amid renewed War Threats
body:
By R Anil Kumar

Tehran/ Bengaluru, Oct 25, 2026. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has said Tehran will maintain its existing policies regardless of whether another conflict breaks out, warning that any renewed military action against Iran would be irrational, according to Iranian news agency ISNA.



Araghchi made the remarks at the inauguration of the Martyr Seyyed Kamal Kharrazi Documentation Centre and Museum, along with a specialised meeting on the role of Kharrazi in shaping foreign policy consensus and the opening of a specialised library at Iran’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The Iranian Foreign Minister said discussions about the possibility of another war had resurfaced, but stressed that Iran’s policies would remain unchanged. He also asserted that the regional security situation had fundamentally changed following what he described as the 40-day war.

Araghchi said the Strait of Hormuz would not return to its previous state after the conflict, adding that the war had altered regional security arrangements. He described the conflict, which he referred to as the “Ramadan War”, as a turning point in the region’s history and called for any eventual end to the war to cover all fronts.

The Iranian Foreign Minister also claimed that Iranian forces had destroyed more than 80 American aircraft and fighter jets during the conflict, alleging that nearly all had been struck by missiles while on the ground. He further claimed that almost all US military bases in the region had been severely damaged, with hundreds of buildings destroyed. These claims were reported by ISNA and have not been independently verified in the material provided.

His remarks come amid renewed speculation over possible US military action. US President Donald Trump, while speaking to reporters after casting his ballot in Florida, said an attack on Iran was possible but also left open the prospect of reaching an agreement with Tehran. Trump questioned whether Iran would adhere to any potential deal.

Trump also praised the performance of the US military and made claims about the damage inflicted on Iran’s military capabilities and naval assets.

Meanwhile, Iran has denied reports that it had offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for the lifting of a US naval blockade. The IRGC-affiliated Tasnim news agency, citing sources, reported that Tehran had made no new proposal to Pakistani mediators and described reports of such an offer as fabricated. The reports had earlier appeared in a Saudi Arabian outlet, according to Press TV.

title: ‘I’m not discouraged’ – Ablakwa responds to criticism over South Africa evacuation
body: Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa says he remains committed to protecting the welfare and dignity of Ghanaians despite what he describes as “all the vilification” directed at him amid controversy over the cost of the evacuation exercise from South Africa. He said criticism from the Minority and other commentators would not discourage him from carrying out his responsibilities. Speaking at a press conference on Monday, October 26, organised by some of the evacuees to tell their part of the story, Mr Ablakwa reaffirmed his commitment to serving Ghanaians, insisting that the criticism would not distract him from his duties. “I give you one assurance: despite all the vilification, I remain fully committed to the welfare, the protection, the dignity, and the rights of all Ghanaians. I am not discouraged at all,” the minister said. He also defended the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and its finance officers against allegations of financial impropriety in the management of funds for the evacuation exercise. The minister maintained that he had confidence in the work of the officials involved, insisting that no money had been stolen. His comments follow media fact-checks and allegations by the Minority that not every evacuee received the reported GH¢5,500 in support payments. Questions have also been raised about discrepancies in some dates of birth contained in documents provided by the ministry. The controversy has triggered public scrutiny of the expenditure on the evacuation exercise and the accuracy of the records used to account for payments to returnees. Mr Ablakwa’s latest comments signal his determination to continue his work despite the mounting criticism, as calls for clarity over the payments and documentation remain part of the debate surrounding the exercise.

title: Prince William Praises Kazakhstan’s Saiga Recovery
body: Britain’s Prince William has highlighted Kazakhstan’s success in restoring its saiga antelope population, crediting government support for the animal’s recovery during an appearance on The Graham Norton Show . Asked about the distinctive antelope and the Altyn Dala conservation initiative, William said the species had recovered from critically endangered status to large numbers. Kazakhstan’s government had recognized the animal’s importance to the country and to conservation, he said: “They threw their full weight behind it.” Video: The Graham Norton Show / So Television / BBC The exchange came during an Earthshot Prize edition of the BBC chat show broadcast on October 23, with a photograph of a saiga displayed in the studio. William appeared alongside actors Cate Blanchett and Hannah Waddingham and conservationist Robert Irwin. Altyn Dala won the 2024 Earthshot Prize in the Protect and Restore Nature category, receiving £1 million to support its work. The initiative helps restore Kazakhstan’s vast steppe ecosystems, with the saiga’s recovery among its most prominent achievements. In an October 2025 update , Earthshot said Altyn Dala had helped the saiga population grow from around 40,000 to more than four million over two decades. The recovery followed a steep decline caused by poaching and disease. The initiative brings together Kazakhstan’s government and the Association for the Conservation of Biodiversity of Kazakhstan, with international conservation partners. Its work includes tracking saiga movements to help protect breeding and feeding grounds. Altyn Dala has also helped return endangered Przewalski’s horses to Kazakhstan, extending its restoration work beyond the antelope that drew attention on Norton’s sofa. Separately, King Charles III sent President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev a congratulatory telegram for Kazakhstan’s Republic Day, according to an October 25 statement from Akorda. The king praised the friendship between the two countries and reaffirmed his commitment to expanding bilateral cooperation.

title: Campaign flag off: Tinubu shuts down Kaduna
body: Kaduna metropolis was filled to the brim as from Friday when party supporters and government officials converged on the former capital of Northern Nigeria, for the flag-off of the 2027 APC presidential campaign on Saturday. The Township stadium burst at the seams as people spilled out of the campaign venue onto Independence way and adjourning boulevards around the arena. As early as 6am on Saturday, party members massed at the event’s venue, wearing T-shirts with party colors and logos, as well as apparels of various designs, bearing President Bola Tinubu’s picture or broken shackles symbol. APC-led State Governors, Ministers of the Federal Government of Nigeria, members of the National Assembly, APC National Working Committee members, federal and state appointees were at the stadium. Musicians kept the party faithful entertained as they waited for the event to kick off while supporters chanted the praises of their various Governors and President Tinubu. Arriving in a coaster bus with Vice President Kashim Shettima, Governor Uba Sani and other dignitaries, the crowd greeted President Tinubu with a chorus of “Baba Oyoyo.” Speaking during the flag off, President Bola Tinubu urged Nigerians to support his re-election, promising to sustain efforts towards economic recovery, prosperity and a better future for the youth. Tinubu, who thanked Kaduna residents for their support during the 2023 presidential election, said he had returned to seek another mandate to continue his administration’s policies and programmes. The president dismissed criticisms of hunger and poverty bedevilling the nation, accusing previous administrations of creating the problems he is working to address. Commending his administration for paying salaries regularly, President Tinubu praised APC governors for their efforts to develop their respective states. He urged supporters to mobilise voters ahead of the January 16, 2027 election, calling on them to vote for APC candidates at the presidential, governorship, National Assembly and state assembly levels. “Your prosperity is here. Your future is in your hands. Your fingerprints on the ballot will determine it,” he said, warning supporters against misinformation and attempts to mislead voters. Earlier, Governor Uba Sani thanked the president for significant federal government interventions in transportation, education, healthcare, agriculture, security and human capital development. The interventions has brought renewed hope to Kaduna State and other parts of Northern Nigeria, he said, adding that residents should support continuity in the 2027 election. Governor Uba Sani highlighted the reconstruction of the Kaduna-Birnin Gwari 123 km road, saying N178bn has been released for the project, which had been abandoned for more than 40 years. He recalled that Tinubu visited Birnin Gwari during the 2023 presidential campaign despite security concerns, where promised to improve security along the corridor. The Governor told the gathering that ‘’today, you can travel to Birnin Gwari without a police escort. That is progress, Mr President, and we thank you for it.’’ He added that more than 300 schools and over 150 primary healthcare centres that had been closed because of insecurity in Kaduna State have been reopened. He also thanked the president for the ongoing reconstruction of the Zaria-Soba-Kambuwa road and the proposed Kaduna metropolitan light rail project. According to him, $865m had been approved for the rail project, while the contractor, China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation have been mobilised with $300m. On education, Sani said the North-West had received N84bn through the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), supporting about 414,000 students across the region. Also speaking, Senator AbdulAzeez Yari, Director-General of the Tinubu presidential campaign, said Kaduna was deliberately selected to host the campaign flag-off because of its political importance in Northern Nigeria. Yari commended Governor Uba Sani and other APC leaders for their preparations, saying the turnout reflects the collective efforts of party members across the country. He dismissed claims that the federal government is working against farmers, as about two million have indicated their commitment to support Tinubu in the 2027 election because the administration has taken steps to improve their livelihoods. The campaign director-general also defended the administration’s economic policies, arguing that the country’s foreign reserves have increased from about $33.9bn when Tinubu assumed office to approximately $54.7bn. Yari called on traditional rulers, Islamic scholars, imams and other community leaders to mobilise support for the president, saying continuity is necessary for national development and peace. “By God’s grace, Northern Nigeria is 101 per cent behind you, Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu, and we are determined to deliver our promise in the 2027 general election,” he said. Speaking at the event, Vice President Kashim Shettima said the APC had demonstrated its commitment to national unity and development through cooperation with state governments. Shettima said the party won the 2023 election because Nigerians believed the alternative would have been disastrous for the country. He also praised Kaduna residents for electing Governor Sani, saying his administration had helped promote unity across the state. According to him, Kaduna has become a state where residents from different communities could regard one another as brothers and sisters, with the benefits of democracy extending beyond the metropolitan area. Shettima said the federal government had supported educational development in Kaduna through the establishment of the Federal University of Applied Sciences in Kachia and the transition of the Federal College of Education, Zaria, into the University of Education. The vice president said the administration had continued projects initiated by previous governments, including the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano gas pipeline, the Kano-Maradi railway, the Lagos-Kano rail corridor and the Abuja-Kaduna-Kano Expressway. Shettima also defended Tinubu’s political relationship with Northern Nigeria, citing his past support for northern political leaders seeking the presidency, recalling his support for former Vice President Atiku Abubakar after he left the PDP. According to him, the president had consistently demonstrated political goodwill towards the North and urged the region to reciprocate by supporting his re-election bid.

title: Change of power in Serbia. Vučić announced the defeat of his party
body:
In Sunday’s snap parliamentary elections in Serbia, the opposition „Student List” won the most seats – admitted the leader of „Ujedinjena Srbija” (United Serbia) and former president Aleksandar Vučić. The election turnout was the highest since the breakup of Yugoslavia.
Vučić, who served as Prime Minister from 2014–2017 and held the office of President from 2017 until his resignation on 27 September 2026, announced at the election headquarters in Belgrade that he does not yet have full results, but based on a stratified sample, it is clear that his list has lost.
„We do not have the full results yet; many will be surprised, and you will understand how much some people lied. Based on the sample, it is clear that we have lost these elections,” he said. He added that the „Student List” would secure between 135 and 140 seats in the 250-member parliament, while his formation could expect around 105.
According to preliminary projections from independent election monitoring organisations, the „Student List” won approximately 51–53 per cent of the vote (estimated at over 2.1–2.2 million), which would grant it around 138–140 seats, while the „Aleksandar Vučić – Ujedinjena Srbija” (United Serbia) list secured about 39–40 per cent (approx. 1.7 million votes) and 103–105 seats. Turnout was record-breaking – nearly 65–70 per cent, the highest since the breakup of Yugoslavia in 1992. Smaller national minority lists are also likely to enter parliament.
The snap parliamentary elections, held on 25 October, were brought about by nearly two years of mass protests. Their spark was the tragedy at the railway station in Novi Sad on 1 November 2024 – the collapse of part of a concrete canopy killed 16 people. Protesters, primarily students, accused the authorities of corruption, negligence, and a failure to hold those responsible to account. The student movement organised university blockades, marches, and demonstrations across the country, demanding accountability and early elections. In the elections, they fielded a list of 250 candidates – mainly representatives of various professions, selected by the student plenum, with no students themselves on the list.

title: Nigerians Abroad: Iheanacho extends scoring streak as Ajayi, Awaziem shine
body:
Nigerian footballers enjoyed a productive weekend across Europe, with Kelechi Iheanacho extending his scoring streak in Turkey, Semi Ajayi delivering an outstanding defensive performance for Hull City and Chidozie Awaziem scoring twice for Konyaspor.
Gift Orban and Olakunle Olusegun also found the net for their respective clubs, while David Okereke contributed a goal and two assists in Italy. In England, Alex Iwobi reached another Premier League milestone, while Friday Etim continued his impressive form in Denmark.
Iheanacho led the weekend’s headlines after scoring in Bursaspor’s 4-2 victory over Keçiörengücü in Turkey.
The forward took his tally to 16 goals and three assists in 12 appearances, extending his scoring streak to 12 consecutive league matches. The victory also sent Bursaspor to the top of the Turkish 1. Lig table.
His continued goalscoring form has made him one of the standout Nigerian performers abroad this season.
Semi Ajayi was another Nigerian who attracted attention after helping Hull City secure a 1-1 draw against Brentford at the MKM Stadium.
Semi Ajayi [Credit: Hull City on X] The Nigerian international was instrumental in the Tigers’ defensive effort as they responded to their previous defeat to Fulham, earning two Man of the Match awards for his performance.
“It’s important that we had a good bounce back from last week; we did that,” Ajayi told Sky Sports after the match.
The defender won five of the six tackles he attempted, made four clearances, recorded five recoveries and produced two interceptions.
His display earned him the Premier League Player of the Match award, while he also won Hull City’s official Man of the Match poll with 43.6 per cent of the votes, finishing ahead of Oli McBurnie, Tim Iroegbunam and Lewis Coyle.
Despite the individual recognition, Ajayi admitted that Hull City were disappointed not to claim all three points.
“We are definitely disappointed not to come away with the three points, but a point at home is always positive,” he added.
In Turkey’s top flight, Awaziem produced one of the weekend’s most notable performances, scoring twice to help Konyaspor beat Gençlerbirliği 2-0.
The Nigerian centre-back opened the scoring shortly before half-time before adding a second early in the second half to secure the victory.
The brace was a significant attacking contribution from a defender and helped Konyaspor claim all three points.
Orban also made a decisive contribution, converting a penalty as Amedspor came from behind to defeat Samsunspor 2-1.
Gift Orban [Credit: Amedspor on X] The Super Eagles forward scored in the 73rd minute to draw his side level before Dia Saba struck the winner in the 84th minute. Orban’s goal took his league tally to eight for the season.
In Russia, Olusegun ended his wait for a league goal by scoring in Rostov’s 2-0 victory over Lokomotiv Moscow.
The forward doubled Rostov’s advantage in the 24th minute, finishing an assist from Oumar Sako after Andrei Langovich had opened the scoring.
Denmark also provided a memorable moment for Nigerian football, with Etim scoring in Midtjylland’s 3-2 victory over Lyngby.
The forward found the net three minutes after the restart, extending his team’s lead. He has now recorded six league goals and three assists this season.
The match also marked a milestone for 18-year-old midfielder Joseph Okuaghare, who came off the bench to make his senior debut for Midtjylland.
His appearance represents an important step in the young Nigerian’s development at the Danish club.
In Italy’s Serie B, Okereke produced an impressive attacking performance, scoring once and providing two assists as Benevento defeated Arezzo 3-0.
His contribution underlined the growing list of Nigerian players making decisive impacts for their clubs across Europe.
Iwobi also reached a significant career milestone over the weekend, becoming the joint-second most-capped African player in Premier League history.
Alex Iwobi [Credit: Fulham FC Facebook Page] The Fulham midfielder matched Egypt international Mohamed Salah’s tally of 328 appearances in the English top flight.
At 30, Iwobi is 25 appearances short of the record held by former Ivory Coast international Kolo Touré, who made 353 Premier League appearances.
The milestone further highlights the Nigerian midfielder’s longevity in English football, having played for Arsenal, Everton and Fulham.

title: Agreements reached to resume Russian gas supplies to Moldova — politician
body:
CHISINAU, October 26. /TASS/. Agreements were reached to resume Russian gas supplies to Moldova, head of the Socialist Party of Moldova Igor Dodon said.
"We have reached an agreement with Russia <…>, and now we are working to find an economic agent whom we will help complete all the necessary procedures and secure the delivery of cheaper Russian gas to the border of the Republic of Moldova," the ex-president said on his Telegram channel.
In September of this year, a 60-day state of emergency in the energy sector was introduced in Moldova due to forecasts of further gas price hikes, as well as a potential shortage in electricity and fuel supplies.
"I want to see how the authorities will reject an offer that could provide Moldova with more favorable gas supply terms," Dodon said, noting that he would come forward with specific proposals in the near future.

title: Victims of shooting outside Gen. Akol Koor’s house seek $341,150 compensation
body: Two people injured during an exchange of fire by security forces outside the residence of former National Security Service (NSS) Internal Security Bureau Chief Gen. Akol Koor Kuc in Juba in November 2024 are seeking a combined USD 341,150 in compensation from South Sudan’s Ministry of Defense and Veteran Affairs. The two plaintiffs, advocate Manawa Gabriel Makwach and Gum Anderia, are also seeking compensation for moral damages, medical expenses and legal costs, according to their lawyer, Angelo Thon Pal. A court in Juba is expected to deliver its judgment in the civil case on Tuesday, October 27. Thon told reporters on Monday that the case stems from the November 21, 2024, shooting incident, during which the two plaintiffs sustained injuries and required medical treatment. “Today’s [Monday] session was fixed for the pronouncement of judgment against the Ministry of Defense and Veteran Affairs. The case goes back to 21 st November 2024. An incident that took place at around 7 p.m. at the residence of Gen. Akol Koor, the former Director General of the National Security Service’s Internal Security Bureau, who is still under house arrest to this day,” he said. “The two plaintiffs got involved in that incident and sustained several injuries in different parts of their bodies, and they were taken to a hospital for medical treatment. They have been under treatment for almost two years.” According to the lawyer, Manawa is seeking USD 260,150 in material compensation, while Gum is claiming USD 81,000. He said the National Medical Commission assessed Manawa’s disability at 60 percent following the injuries he sustained. Pal said the plaintiffs initially submitted documents to a military investigation committee established following presidential directives in December 2024. The committee, led by Lt. Gen. James Koang Chuol, reportedly completed its work and submitted a report to the presidency, but the victims had not received its findings. The lawyer said the plaintiffs later pursued legal action after receiving no outcome from the investigation. He added that the Ministry of Defense was notified through the Ministry of Justice before the civil suit was filed. According to Pal, the ministry was served with court documents and attended several hearings. He said the court allowed the parties to settle the matter amicably, but no settlement was reached. The plaintiffs subsequently asked the court to proceed with their statements in the absence of the ministry’s representative, the lawyer said. In addition to the material compensation claims, Pal said the plaintiffs were seeking compensation for moral damages, as well as court fees and legal expenses. He said the amount for moral damages would be assessed by the court. The shooting occurred on the evening of November 21, 2024, near the residence of the former security chief in Juba. The incident involved an exchange of gunfire between security personnel and resulted in deaths and injuries, according to earlier reports. The civil case, identified by the lawyer as case number 276 of 2026, seeks compensation from the Ministry of Defense and Veteran Affairs. The court’s ruling is expected to determine the outcome of the plaintiffs’ claims. The post Victims of shooting outside Gen. Akol Koor’s house seek $341,150 compensation appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Iranian Embassy Posts on Samarkand’s Persian Heritage Spark Uzbek Protest
body: Uzbekistan has lodged a diplomatic protest with Iran over social media posts describing Samarkand’s architecture as part of Persian civilization. The posts targeted United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio. On October 23, Uzbekistan’s First Deputy Foreign Minister Bakhromjon Aloyev met with Iranian Ambassador Mohammad Ali Eskandari, who was handed a diplomatic note of protest . Uzbekistan’s Foreign Ministry described posts published by Iranian diplomatic missions on X as a one-sided and politicized interpretation of Samarkand’s history. Tashkent demanded that the posts be removed and that similar incidents be avoided in the future. The dispute followed Rubio’s visit to Samarkand on October 19, when he recorded a video in Registan Square highlighting the city’s historical role in international trade. Iran’s embassy in Armenia described the site where Rubio stood as part of Persian civilization . The embassy in Zimbabwe called Registan’s arches a “hallmark of Iranian-Islamic civilization,” accusing Rubio of seeking to destroy that heritage. Iran’s embassy in Bulgaria also criticized Rubio for disparaging Persian civilization while standing in front of monuments bearing its influence. Earlier, during an October 7 speech in Athens, Rubio recalled the destruction of the Acropolis by the forces of Persian King Xerxes in 480 BCE. He also attacked Iran’s current clerical rulers, accusing them of promoting a “cult of death.” Uzbekistan’s Foreign Ministry said that the heritage of Samarkand, Bukhara, Khiva, and other historic cities reflects centuries of statehood and cultural development among the Uzbek people. Tashkent objected to the use of the country’s history in political disputes between other states. Samarkand has deep ties to the Persian-speaking world. Before the Arab conquest, it was one of the centers of Sogdiana, whose inhabitants spoke a language belonging to the Iranian language family. Persian later became widely used in Central Asian cities, including in literature and scholarship. In the late 14th and early 15th centuries, Samarkand was the capital of Timur’s empire. Craftsmen from various regions, including Iran and the historic region of Khorasan, participated in the construction of its monumental buildings. The Registan architectural ensemble was built between the 15th and 17th centuries, combining local artistic traditions with those of the wider Islamic world. The concept of Persian civilization encompasses a cultural area much larger than modern Iran. UNESCO describes Samarkand as a crossroads of cultures , reflecting influences from successive civilizations. The Iranian embassies did not make territorial claims against Uzbekistan; their posts concerned cultural and architectural history. Samarkand’s heritage has also been a subject of debate within Central Asia. During the Soviet redrawing of Central Asia’s internal borders in 1924, Samarkand and Bukhara became part of the Uzbek Soviet Socialist Republic. Both cities historically had substantial Persian-speaking populations, and Tajik continues to be spoken there today. Historians have also documented Soviet-era pressure on Tajik residents to register as Uzbeks , contributing to longstanding disputes over the cities’ ethnic composition. The dispute occurred amid increased U.S. diplomatic engagement in Central Asia. During his visit, Rubio attended a C5+1 meeting with the foreign ministers of the five Central Asian countries. The talks focused on expanding economic cooperation , including investment and critical minerals. Uzbekistan is developing economic relations with Washington while maintaining an interest in cooperation with Tehran. Transportation routes through Iran provide access to Persian Gulf ports, an important consideration for landlocked Central Asian countries. In its statement on the protest, Uzbekistan’s Foreign Ministry also stressed the importance of bilateral relations with Iran.

title: TOR targets 100,000 barrels-a-day capacity as Ghana eyes 70% local fuel supply by 2028
body: The Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) is working towards a major expansion of its crude-processing capacity to 100,000 barrels per day, as the government targets meeting about 70 per cent of Ghana’s national fuel demand through local refining by 2028. Managing Director Edmond Kombat said the expansion formed part of a broader strategy to strengthen domestic refining, reduce dependence on imported finished petroleum products and improve the country’s energy security. Speaking at the Government Accountability Series at Jubilee House on Monday, October 26, 2026, Mr Kombat said President John Dramani Mahama had directed the Energy and Green Transition Minister to work with TOR’s board and management on a strategic roadmap for the refinery’s expansion. He said the President issued the directive when he commissioned the refurbished Crude Distillation Unit on August 1, 2026. According to Mr Kombat, the roadmap includes an initial increase in capacity to 100,000 barrels per day, with a longer-term ambition of reaching 200,000 barrels per day. “TOR is part of a national plan. With the refinery’s expansion from 45,000 to 100,000 barrels a day, the Government is targeting about 70 percent of national fuel demand from local refining by 2028,” he said. In the immediate term, engineers from Verga Engineering are working with TOR’s technical team to complete the tie-in and commission the F-61 crude heater. Mr Kombat said the work was expected to increase the CDU’s throughput from its current level of about 28,000 barrels per stream day to between 45,000 and 55,000 barrels per stream day. Management also plans to install a new air cooler to increase processing capacity to 60,000 barrels per stream day and replace the existing 6,500-barrel-a-day catalytic reformers with a 10,000-barrel-per-day continuous catalytic reformer. He said a new 120-tonne boiler had been installed, while work continued on the RFCC turnaround and the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system. Beyond the immediate improvements, TOR is advancing plans for a new greenfield refinery and petrochemical facilities, alongside additional storage capacity. The refinery’s longer-term Restoration and Legacy Projects programme for 2026 to 2029 proposes expanding the existing plant to 85,000 barrels per stream day and constructing a new refinery with a capacity of 115,000 barrels per stream day. Together, the proposed developments would provide a combined capacity of 200,000 barrels per stream day. Mr Kombat said the projects would be pursued with strategic partners and in line with the government’s climate-compliance principles. He said increasing local refining capacity would strengthen Ghana’s ability to meet domestic demand while supporting industrial growth and reducing exposure to disruptions in international petroleum supply chains.

title: Ukrainian regulator stalling EBRD-backed capital market plan – National Bank governor
body:
Implementation of an integrated capital markets infrastructure model, developed jointly by the National Bank of Ukraine (NBU), the Ministry of Economy and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), is currently being held up by the position of the head of the National Securities and Stock Market Commission (NSSMC), NBU Governor Andriy Pyshnyy said.
"We are being asked what is happening with the capital markets. We explain the capital markets infrastructure model that has been developed jointly by the NBU, the Ministry of Economy and the EBRD. Unfortunately, its implementation is currently being held up by the position of the head of the NSSMC," Pyshnyy said in an interview with Interfax-Ukraine at the Annual Meetings of the IMF and the World Bank Group in Bangkok.
In the NBU governor's view, the proposed model takes the state's interests into account in building a vertically integrated system, and therefore confidence in it should not be undermined.
"The key idea is to bring the entire capital markets infrastructure chain together under a single holding company. The strategic investor in this infrastructure holding company should be an entity trusted by global private capital: Deutsche Börse, Euroclear, Clearstream… Naturally, it should be selected through a competitive process. But in the current circumstances, national security requirements must also be taken into account. Our model provides for all of this. So why is the process being held up?" Pyshnyy concluded.
As reported, EBRD President Odile Renaud-Basso expressed hope at the Annual Meetings of the IMF and the World Bank Group that Ukraine would pay greater attention to the capital market development project.
"Despite all the short-term challenges, we have indeed managed to move this process forward, and I hope this issue will soon become a priority," she said.
In July last year, a memorandum of understanding was signed at the Ukraine Recovery Conference in Rome by the Ministry of Economy, the Ministry of Finance, the NBU, the NSSMC and the EBRD on supporting integrated capital markets infrastructure in Ukraine. Its signing was preceded by the Financial Stability Council's approval of a plan for the practical implementation of the target capital markets infrastructure model.
In early September 2025, the National Bank announced the launch of the memorandum's implementation. The first stage involved optimizing the ownership structure and corporate governance of the National Depository of Ukraine (NDU) by transferring management of the state-owned stake, previously managed by the NSSMC, to the NBU.
The next stage envisages the creation of a holding company involving a reputable international strategic investor selected through an open tender, an operator of trading and post-trading infrastructure, international financial institutions, local market participants, and the state and state-owned banks. The holding company, in turn, will establish a new stock exchange in Ukraine, which will become the majority owner of the Central Counterparty Clearing Institution, the Settlement Center (SC), replacing the National Bank in that role. In addition, the exchange will own a minority stake in the NDU, while the National Bank will hold a majority stake.
The final stage is to consolidate depository services under the NDU, which is to operate as a single central securities depository, by transferring to it the functions of recording and servicing the circulation of government bonds from the National Bank.
In early June this year, the Cabinet of Ministers approved a bill on establishing a capital markets infrastructure holding company with the participation of a foreign strategic investor. However, due to a change of government, the document was submitted to the Verkhovna Rada only on September 4. The NSSMC subsequently proposed substantial amendments to the government's bill, including tightening the conditions for attracting a foreign strategic investor.
In addition, an alternative bill (No. 16038-1) was registered on September 21. Its authors include 12 members of parliament, among them Serhiy Taruta, first deputy head of the Verkhovna Rada's economic committee; Andriy Nikolaienko, head of the capital markets subcommittee of the parliament's finance committee; Oleksandr Fediyenko, head of a subcommittee of the parliament's security committee; and Anton Yatsenko.

title: JAL expands driverless towing tractors to Fukuoka after Haneda and Narita
body: Japan Airlines (JAL) announced it has started Level 4 autonomous towing tractor operations at Fukuoka Airport (FUK), making it the third airport in its domestic network to use driverless vehicles for airside logistics. The operations began on October 26, 2026, and were introduced together with airport operator Fukuoka International Airport Co, (FIAC). Level 4 autonomy means the vehicles run fully driverless within specified operating conditions. The move follows JAL’s launch of Level 4 towing tractor operations at Tokyo Haneda Airport (HND) and Narita International Airport (NRT) in December 2025. It is the airline’s first such deployment outside the Tokyo metropolitan area. Driverless cargo runs at Fukuoka At Fukuoka, the autonomous tractors transport cargo containers along a route of about 1.7 kilometers between the domestic cargo terminal and the ground support equipment (GSE) holding area. JAL and FIAC have set joint operating rules and upgraded airside infrastructure to allow the vehicles to run without a driver. The airline said demand for both domestic and international travel at Fukuoka continues to grow rapidly. The tractors are EZTow electric vehicles made by TLD Robotics, formerly known as TractEasy. Each measures 3.2 meters long, 1.84 meters wide and 2.05 meters high, weighs 4.07 tons and can tow up to 14 tons. Responding to labor shortages JAL has been introducing advanced airside technologies since 2018 as part of the Autonomous Driving Committee initiative led by the Civil Aviation Bureau of Japan’s Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT). The airline said automating routine ramp logistics helps offset labor shortages caused by Japan’s shrinking working-age population. It added that the electric vehicles produce zero emissions and reduce the risk of human error on busy ramps, where aircraft, specialized vehicles and ground staff operate side by side. Plans for wider rollout JAL plans to gradually expand its autonomous vehicle fleet, operating routes and coverage to more airports across Japan. Alongside the towing tractors, the airline is using other automated equipment, including remote-controlled aircraft tugs, automated aircraft washing equipment and snowplows that can be run by a single operator. With MLIT’s support, JAL also plans to deepen cooperation across the industry, including with All Nippon Airways (ANA), which is considering adopting similar systems. title: FG Disburses N38.93bn to 166 Public Tertiary Institutions
body: Ndubuisi Francis in Abuja The Federal Government has disbursed N38.93 billion to 166 public tertiary institutions nationwide under the Needs Assessment Revitalisation Fund. The disbursement covers 79 universities, 46 polytechnics and 41 colleges of education to support approved projects aimed at addressing infrastructure gaps and improving teaching and learning facilities across the institutions. The university component accounts for N28.5 billion for 79 institutions, while 46 polytechnics have allocations totalling N5.8 billion. The 41 colleges of education are allocated N4.7 billion, a statement by the Federal Ministry of Finance explained Sunday. According to the statenent signed by the Head of Media, Efe Ovuakporie, the intervention forms part of the Federal Government’s efforts to address the needs of public universities and support the implementation of agreed measures under the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Federal Government and the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU). The funds are expected to enable beneficiary institutions to commence or advance approved projects addressing critical infrastructure and other identified institutional needs, with the overall objective of strengthening the quality of tertiary education in Nigeria. “The disbursement underscores the importance of effective coordination between the Federal Ministry of Finance, the Federal Ministry of Education and beneficiary institutions in ensuring that approved public funding translates into tangible improvements in educational infrastructure and institutional capacity. For further information on the beneficiary institutions and their respective allocations, members of the public are advised to visit the official website of the Federal Ministry of Finance, the statement said.

title: Moscow highly values Vucic’s contribution to Russia-Serbia relations — Kremlin
body:
MOSCOW, October 26. /TASS/. Moscow highly values the contribution that former Serbian President and Serbian Progressive Party leader Aleksandar Vucic has made to the development of bilateral relations between Russia and Serbia, Russian Presidential Spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters.
"We acknowledge the results of the elections held in Serbia. We highly value the contribution that Vucic has made to the development of our bilateral relations," Peskov said.
Serbia held snap elections to the National Assembly, its unicameral parliament, on October 25. With 96.47% of the vote tally reports processed, the Republic Electoral Commission announced that United Serbia, led by former President Aleksandar Vucic, had lost to the opposition Student List, receiving 39.27% of the vote against 52.57%, respectively.

title: AI Scope Creep and Productivity
body:
I was recently asked to look at a change one of our developers made to RavenDB. He was chasing a particularly slow query with spatial sorting (a “find me all the nearest Thai restaurants” style of query). He found the root cause and had a fix ready. The fix gave us a 25% improvement in query processing time, and the change was about 15 lines of code.
A few years ago, I would have said: great job, merge it, ship it, let customers enjoy the faster queries. But I got a hunch that we could do something different. We asked the AI model to try it out. It took a non-trivial amount of work to even test that, while in the past, it would have taken a few days just to try it out.
The model was able to complete the spike while we were talking about why this should be a good approach and the architectural-level aspects that were driving it.
The result of that spike was an improvement of 12x. Not 12%. Twelve times faster. A 25% improvement is a wow; a 1,100% improvement is damn . In essence, we took a shortcut a couple of decades ago and had to pay a lot more than we could have.
Note that a 15-line fix is local, easy to understand and verify. A structural change like this is… not. We also have to deal with backward compatibility concerns (we had to change the index format), verify that we get the same output in both cases, etc.
Along the way, we found three separate bugs that had been in the product for 10 to 15 years. They're all in very weird edge cases. What happens when you sort on a spatial field that doesn't exist?
If a document has no spatial value, we would treat the missing value as zero distance, which means it is the closest result. I can argue that this is the correct behavior, but not convincingly.
The PR went from 15 lines of code to about a thousand. Review time for that went from under 10 minutes to over an hour.
Compare this to the same task four years ago: a few hours to isolate and understand the problem, a couple of hours to figure out how we could optimize this, write the code, etc. The overhead of actually reviewing the code and merging it would be pretty minimal.
Today, it took an hour to reproduce the problem, another with the model to find & propose the original 15-line fix. Then we dove deeper into this and did the rest in another couple of hours. The 1K LoC PR would take two hours to review.
Interestingly enough, I don’t think we would have hit on the 15-line fix if we had been working manually. That took advantage of a library function I didn’t even know existed. We would have headed directly to the proper fix we ended up with.
That leads to a few observations about the process. The quick fix with the AI would have delivered an inferior end result. It is funny when I say that a 25% improvement is inferior, but it would have been in this case.
The other aspect is that each decision we made along the way made sense , but we ended up with something that was big . To the point that you need to meditate over the code to understand it.
This is a very small and focused change, mind. And it grew from 15 lines to 1K. We are seeing the size of PRs grow from a few hundred to many thousands of lines of code.
All of that pushes the complexity into the review process. And for long-lived software, review is not something you can skimp on. RavenDB has been around since 2009. Code we merge today is code we will be supporting and reasoning about for the next decade.
There is a wide spectrum of opinions on this right now. Some people say they never read the code; some have an agent review it. Others insist on going through every line, and that is where I stand.
The code that goes into RavenDB gets a manual review by a person who understands everything about the system. Not just whether the code is correct, but how it interacts with all the other stuff we have, the history behind it, and the things that are not in the diff.
As an industry, we expected AI to make us dramatically faster. If AI writes 90% of the code, sometimes 100%, shouldn’t we be shipping more often? And better software as well, no?
Every developer I've talked to says the same thing: I cannot not use AI. The benefits are too high to give up. I have seen people who left the IDE entirely and some who just use AI to explain and reason about the code, but everyone is using AI in some capacity. But we aren't seeing the change in productivity that everyone predicted.
I think a big part of the answer is in the story above. We aren't doing the same work faster. We're doing more work, arguably better work. We find opportunities we would never have considered, because the cost of checking a hunch dropped significantly. The cost of accepting the answer didn't decrease; in fact, I would argue that it became much higher.
To be clear about the scale of this: RavenDB did not suddenly get 12 times faster across the board. As much as I wish a 1K PR could do that. A single scenario got dramatically better. That is great, but it is also more code, more behavior to understand, and more surface area to maintain.
When we keep going like that, we end up with better software overall, but also a much larger mass of code to work with. It also means much more effort from the people who actually have to deliver it.
I think that we’ll see major shifts in how we build and maintain software, but at the same time, I think that the key fundamentals haven’t really changed. In the past quarter, RavenDB (the company, not the software) hired more R&D staff than we did in the past two years , to give you some context.
There is going to be a greater need for developers than ever, and even more digitalization of the world.

title: Luxury SUVs for APC youths insult to struggling Nigerians – Atiku slams Tinubu
body: By Ayobami Okerinde Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has described the reported distribution of luxury sport utility vehicles to All Progressives Congress (APC) youth leaders as an insult to Nigerians grappling with hunger and rising living costs. Atiku, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, called on President Bola Tinubu and the Presidency to explain the source of funding for the vehicles, reportedly 2026 models valued at more than N150m each. In a statement on Monday issued by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku questioned the reported donation of the vehicles by First Lady Oluremi Tinubu, saying Nigerians deserved to know who paid for them. “The APC National Youth Leader says these vehicles were donated by First Lady Oluremi Tinubu. Nigerians deserve to know where the money came from to buy and distribute so many 2026 model SUVs, each worth more than N150 million, for political mobilisation,” he said. Atiku asked whether the vehicles were purchased with the First Lady’s personal funds, donations or public resources, demanding that the Presidency disclose the total cost and source of the money. “The First Lady holds no elected or executive office. She is only a domestic appendage of the office of President. Were these vehicles bought with her personal funds, donations or public resources? Who paid for them? What was the total cost? The Presidency must provide a clear account,” the former vice-president said. He argued that the reported gifts were inappropriate at a time when many Nigerians were struggling to afford food, transportation and other basic necessities. “At a time families cannot afford food, transport and other basic necessities, these gifts are a brazen insult to the people. The government has found a way to provide luxury SUVs for APC youth leaders, yet millions of Nigerians are still waiting for meaningful relief from the cost of living crisis,” he said. Atiku also questioned the timing of the reported vehicle distribution, alleging that APC women leaders had previously received luxury vehicles and that the earlier gifts came shortly before the abduction of schoolchildren in Oyo State. He said the latest reported distribution raised concerns about the government’s spending priorities amid economic hardship and insecurity. “While Nigerians continue to ask where the savings from subsidy removal have gone, the Presidency must explain how such costly gifts are being funded. If the vehicles were paid for privately, the source of the funds should be disclosed. If public resources were used, the government must identify who authorised the spending and under what legal authority,” he said. The ADC presidential candidate further alleged that the scale of the reported gifts raised questions about whether wealth and public resources were being used to secure political loyalty. He also criticised what he described as displays of privilege among individuals associated with the President, citing reports that the APC National Youth Leader travelled by private jet. Atiku extended his criticism to the President’s son, Seyi Tinubu, referring to widely circulated photographs said to show him wearing a Richard Mille RM 67-02 Sébastien Ogier wristwatch reportedly valued at about $500,000. “A worker on the national minimum wage would need several lifetimes to earn what the President’s son wears on one wrist. When the household of the President and the youth leader of his party flaunt such wealth in a season of hunger, insecurity and joblessness, they are not merely displaying poor taste; they are telling Nigerians, in the plainest possible terms, how little their suffering registers in the corridors of power,” Atiku said. He asked why Nigerians were being made to endure economic hardship while people close to the administration allegedly enjoyed lavish privileges. “Nigerians need answers, not another display of wealth for political mobilisation,” he said. Atiku pledged to investigate any public funds found to have been spent illegally if elected president. “When I am sworn in as president, every naira found to have been spent illegally will be thoroughly investigated, and everyone found culpable will be brought to justice,” he said. He added, “Tinubu made life difficult. I will make life affordable again.” The post Luxury SUVs for APC youths insult to struggling Nigerians – Atiku slams Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: UN report warns Security Council veto power is hindering efforts to prevent global conflicts
body:
By R Anil Kumar 

 	
The United Nations has warned that the veto power held by the five permanent members of the Security Council is hampering international efforts to resolve conflicts

 	
The report warns that conflicts and security rivalries disrupt trade and supply chains while diverting money and political attention from poverty reduction, healthcare, education and other development priorities




New York/ Bengaluru, Oct 25, 2026. The United Nations has warned that the veto power held by the five permanent members of the Security Council is hampering international efforts to resolve conflicts, as rising geopolitical rivalries make global cooperation increasingly difficult.

The UN's World Social Report 2026 says competition among major powers is weakening multilateral institutions and diverting resources away from development.

It calls for reforms to make global decision-making more representative, alongside stronger cooperation on debt, technology, climate change and social investment.

The report highlights a growing gap between the need for countries to work together on shared challenges and their ability to take collective action.

Although the emergence of multiple centres of power could, in principle, create opportunities for broader cooperation, competition for strategic influence is instead putting international coordination under strain, the report observes.

Veto power and global rivalries weaken UN action

The report identifies the Security Council's decision-making structure as a major obstacle to effective international responses to conflicts.

The veto allows any of its five permanent members- China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States, to block substantive resolutions, even when other members support them.

The resulting deadlock has renewed calls for changes to the Council, including expanding its membership.

The UN secretary-general has backed reforms to improve representation for regions such as Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean, and the Asia-Pacific, whose influence in global decision-making remains limited.

The report also points to the spread of geopolitical influence across the world. The number of countries exercising substantial influence over another country has increased from six in the 1970s to 34 today.

Relations between neighbouring countries have also deteriorated. According to the report, in 2024-25, 59 countries recorded worsening relations with their neighbours, while only 19 reported improvements.

The growing number of competing powers has encouraged countries to form smaller groups or coalitions to pursue shared interests.

However, the report warns that such arrangements risk weakening broader multilateral institutions and making collective responses to international challenges more difficult.

Rising military spending adds to development pressures

Geopolitical tensions are also increasing the pressure on national budgets.

More than half of all countries raised defence spending as a share of their gross domestic product between 2020 and 2024. All nine nuclear-armed states have expanded their arsenals since 2022, the report said.

The report warns that conflicts and security rivalries disrupt trade and supply chains while diverting money and political attention from poverty reduction, healthcare, education and other development priorities.

The consequences are particularly severe for low-income countries and economies affected by conflict.

Violence destroys infrastructure, discourages investment and weakens public institutions. Displacement also interrupts access to schools, healthcare and employment, making it harder for vulnerable communities to recover.

Meanwhile, rapid technological change and climate pressures are creating new demands on governments, even as many developing countries struggle to secure affordable financing and access to digital infrastructure.

UN calls for stronger cooperation on debt and technology

The report outlines three priorities for reviving international cooperation.

These include improving access to funding for social programmes through tax cooperation and debt relief measures, widening access to technology and digital infrastructure, and reforming global institutions to make them more inclusive and accountable.

It argues that developing countries need greater support to manage debt costs, attract investment and benefit from technological and economic changes.

The report stresses that economic, digital and energy transitions are advancing rapidly, but billions of people remain unable to access the jobs, skills, services and social protections needed to benefit from them.

It calls for renewed multilateral efforts to ensure that global progress does not deepen existing inequalities or leave vulnerable countries further behind.

title: Award-Winning Production Designer Dies at Moscow Hospital After Arrest for Treason
body:
Alexander Kondratov, an award-winning production designer for the popular Russian TV series “Liquidation,” has died at a Moscow hospital after being transferred from a detention center where he was awaiting trial on treason charges, the rights NGO Perviy Otdel said Monday.
Kondratov, 52, was reportedly hospitalized at the Botkin hospital last Friday for an undisclosed ailment. The cause of his death has not been made public.
Russian law enforcement authorities charged Kondratov with treason on Aug. 5, though he had been held for more than 70 days under so-called “carousel arrests,” a practice of consecutive detentions on charges of disorderly conduct.
Born and raised in Moscow, Kondratov moved to Kyiv, Ukraine, in 2012, where his family currently resides.
Russian border guards at Vnukovo International Airport detained him on May 5, when he arrived to renew his international passport.
His defense attorney Natalia Tikhonova said the treason charges, which carry a maximum sentence of life in prison for men, stemmed from “at least six” online posts Kondratov had made. The nature of those posts has not been disclosed.
Kondratov was best known for his work as an art and production designer for the 2007 post-World War II detective drama “Liquidation.” His work on the series earned him two of Russia’s highest honors in television production — the TEFI and Golden Eagle awards.
Perviy Otdel reported that Kondratov’s death marks at least the 11th known case of someone dying in Russian custody this year while standing trial on charges widely viewed as being politically motivated.

title: Russia May Seek NATO Rollback to 1997 in Ukraine Talks
body:
Russia may use renewed peace talks on Ukraine to seek concessions that weaken NATO’s defenses in Europe, The Telegraph reported on Sunday, Oct. 25, citing diplomatic sources.
The sources said Moscow’s push to include European countries in the negotiations could be aimed at securing concessions on NATO expansion and the alliance’s military presence near Russia’s borders. Russian President Vladimir Putin has repeatedly described NATO’s enlargement as a “root cause” of the war.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
One possible demand, according to the report, would be for NATO to return to its 1997 configuration, before former Soviet bloc countries began joining the alliance. Such a move could mean withdrawing NATO forces from Poland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, and Finland – all of which border Russia.
The report did not cite an official Russian proposal or say that a demand for a NATO rollback had been formally added to the agenda. It remains a scenario attributed to diplomatic sources, rather than an agreed negotiating position.
Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov has argued that European countries should be included in discussions on ending the war, saying an agreement would be difficult to reach without them. Russian officials have also said future talks should address a broader European security framework.
Putin said last week that negotiations should focus on “ensur[ing] the security of Ukraine and Russia” after a final peace agreement. He added that discussions should also cover “the architecture of European security as a whole,” according to Reuters .
Moscow has previously sought changes to NATO’s posture in Europe. In December 2021, Russia presented the US and NATO with draft security agreements that included demands to halt further NATO enlargement and limit military activity in countries that joined the alliance after May 1997. NATO rejected the demand that it closed its doors to new members, while saying it was open to talks on arms control and other security issues.
The Telegraph’s report suggests the Kremlin could again link its demands on NATO to negotiations over Ukraine. The outlet cited sources who said Putin may argue that concessions on the alliance’s military presence are necessary to resolve the conflict.
The report comes as Ukraine, Russia, and the US discuss restarting negotiations at the technical level. Kremlin aide Ushakov said Russia was prepared to resume trilateral talks after its Nov. 4 National Unity Day holiday, describing the next meeting as preliminary and exploratory.
Kyiv has said it is ready to take part in talks but wants concrete steps, including a ceasefire and humanitarian measures. President Volodymyr Zelensky has also said Ukraine supports proposals for an energy ceasefire and an end to the war.
As the EU is seeking a role in the next round of discussions, EU officials have proposed a broader format that would include European representatives, while the Kremlin has said the talks currently being prepared are trilateral. The exact format and participants have not been confirmed.
Earlier, Kyiv Post reported that Russian officials and analysts have used the prospect of renewed talks to raise wider demands on European security, sanctions, and territory. Moscow’s stated focus on postwar security could therefore extend beyond Ukraine’s borders, though the reported NATO rollback demand has not been confirmed as an official condition.
That said, NATO membership remains a key point of disagreement. Ukraine has said it needs strong security guarantees to prevent future Russian attacks, while Putin has rejected Ukrainian membership in the alliance. Kyiv has also rejected Russia’s demands that it surrender territory as a condition for ending the war.
The talks’ agenda, any Russian proposal on NATO, and the degree of European participation remain unsettled.
