title: Uba Sani To Opposition: ‘Don’t Rely On Social Media, Go Out And Campaign’
body: Governor Uba Sani of Kaduna State has advised the opposition to reach out to the people directly through campaign rallies, instead of reacting to what the All Progressives Party(APC) is doing on social media. The Governor who pointed this out during an interview with TVC on Sunday night, further said that “if you are campaigning to win elections, you have to go out and meet with the people.” According to him, “the only party that I see reaching out through town hall meetings, other than our party, is probably APM. I’m surprised. I have seen them going round. But you can not say the same with ADC and NDC.” “Are they reaching out to the public, particularly the downtrodden? The answer is no. Have they come out with any strategy on their campaign? The answer is no. You can’t run a campaign by reacting to what another party is is doing. Go and do your own campaign,” he advised. The Governor noted that instead of canvassing for the people’s support, the opposition is using digital technology like Artificial Intelligence and doctoring pictures and posting on social media to disparage APC. He expressed optimism that the ruling APC is doing very well because “we are the only party that is reaching out, talking to the people. So, whether the opposition decides to come together or not, it’s not our business.’’ Governor Uba Sani recalled that the National Chairman of APC, Professor Nentawe Yilwatada, had promised that the north will give President Bola Tinubu 70% of its votes, promising that Kaduna State will give a higher percentage. “In Kaduna State, allowing any candidate to even get 25% of the votes is a failure on our side,” he pledged. The Governor cited various projects that the president has sited in Kaduna State in the last three and half years, which the people never dreamt of, adding that “now we can see development, we can see intervention, we can see support.” He commended the president for handing over the Ahmadu Bello Stadium to Kaduna State Government, promising to re-construct it to a FIFA-standard 33,000 seating-capacity stadium. Governor Uba Sani also highlighted the reconstruction of the Kaduna-Birnin Gwari 123 km road, saying N178bn has been released for the project, which had been abandoned for more than 40 years. The Kaduna State Governor also thanked President Tinubu for the ongoing reconstruction of the Zaria-Soba-Kambuwa road and the proposed Kaduna metropolitan light rail project, the second in the country. According to him, $865m has been approved for the rail project, while the contractor, China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation have been mobilised with $300m. Governor Uba Sani also disclosed that Kaduna State now has four federal universities, including the upgraded Federal University of Education, Zaria, the Federal University of Applied Sciences, Kachia and the proposed Shehu Musa Yar’adua University of Petroleum Studies, Kaduna, as well as Kaduna Polytechnic which has been converted to Federal University of Technology. According to him, the only way that the good people of Kaduna State can reciprocate this kind gesture is to vote for President Tinubu massively.

title: TOR receives over 5 million barrels of crude after zero receipts in 2024
body: The Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) has received more than five million barrels of crude oil following a period in which it recorded no crude receipts in 2024, Managing Director Edmond Kombat has disclosed. He said the renewed supply of crude reflected growing confidence among suppliers and business partners following efforts to restore the refinery’s operations. Speaking at the Government Accountability Series at Jubilee House on Monday, October 26, 2026, Mr Kombat said TOR had received several crude cargoes since the recovery programme began, including shipments of Ghanaian indigenous crude. “TOR has maintained a steady supply of crude oil for refinery operations, reflecting the renewed confidence among suppliers and business partners, who are once again willing to do business with the refinery,” he said. The Managing Director listed Bonga, Baleine and Bonnie Light among the crude grades received since May 2026, followed by Ghana’s Jubilee Medium Sweet crude delivered aboard the MT Apache on July 15, 2026. He said TOR paid for the Jubilee cargo in full, describing it as the refinery’s first Jubilee crude shipment in a decade. On September 25, 2026, the refinery received a further 950,000-barrel shipment of Sankofa crude from the Ghana National Petroleum Corporation (GNPC). The crude deliveries followed the restart of refining operations on December 19, 2025, after the completion of turnaround maintenance on the Crude Distillation Unit (CDU). Mr Kombat said the restoration of crude supplies had been central to management’s efforts to return TOR to its core mandate of processing crude oil into petroleum products for the domestic market. He explained that the refinery had been largely inactive when the current management took office in May 2025, with the CDU out of operation since April 2021 and the Residue Fluid Catalytic Cracking (RFCC) Unit shut down since 2019. Management subsequently prioritised the rehabilitation of the CDU, with turnaround maintenance conducted between August 1 and October 30, 2025. Following inspections by the National Petroleum Authority, the refinery received clearance to resume refining operations. The refurbished CDU was commissioned by President John Dramani Mahama on August 1, 2026. Mr Kombat said the crude deliveries and renewed commercial relationships demonstrated the importance of collaboration among state institutions and private-sector partners in restoring TOR. He said management would continue working to ensure a steady supply of crude, improve operational efficiency and increase processing capacity.

title: HYT Consulting, TTS Nigeria Programme Advance Women’s Employability Through Practical Workforce Devt
body: Leading human capital development and outsourcing firm, HYT Consulting, has successfully concluded a five-day Employability Bootcamp, equipping 30 young women with practical, job ready competencies for sales roles in Nigeria’s financial services industry (FSI) and fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) sectors. Held from October 5 to 9, 2026 at HYT Consulting’s training facility in Lagos, the bootcamp formed part of the pilot cohort of the Talent Technology Service (TTS) Nigeria Programme. The consortium initiative is led by Tech4Dev, in partnership with Univelcity, Semicolon and the Policy Innovation Centre (PIC), with support from the Mastercard Foundation. The TTS Nigeria Programme aims to train 30,000 Nigerian women aged 18–35 and connect at least 25,000 to dignified employment opportunities in technology, technology-enabled and technology-adjacent roles, including business process outsourcing (BPO) and related sectors. To support this objective, HYT Consulting, in collaboration with Semicolon, co-designed and delivered a practical, competency-based training programme. Drawing on its industry insights and recruitment expertise, HYT structured the five-day experience around the practical skills and professional competencies required in the workplace. The training moved beyond theory to prepare participants for the demands of employment and help them contribute meaningfully to employers from day one. Speaking on the firm’s approach and its contribution to the programme, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of HYT Consulting, Folusho Odegbaike, said: “At HYTConsulting, our work is centred on closing the gap between the talent young people possess and the competencies required to succeed in the workplace. We were pleased to bring our training and recruitment expertise to the TTS Nigeria Programme. “Employability goes beyond securing a job; it is about preparing people to perform, contribute to business objectives and build sustainable careers. Ultimately, we want employers to have access to capable, work-ready talent, while helping young people build the skills and confidence to succeed professionally.” She added that investing in women’s employability is also an investment in the strength and productivity of the wider workforce. “When young women have access to the skills and opportunities they need to participate meaningfully in the economy, the benefits extend beyond individual careers. Businesses gain access to a broader pool of capable talent, families and communities benefit from greater economic participation, and the country strengthens its human capital base. For us, preparing these women for employment is part of the wider work of building a more inclusive, capable and productive workforce.” For the TTS Nigeria Programme, the focus on young women reflects the importance of expanding access to formal employment and supporting more inclusive economic participation. By building relevant skills and strengthening pathways into work, the programme is helping develop a talent pipeline that responds to employers’ needs while creating opportunities for women to participate more fully in Nigeria’s economy. Head of Communications, TTS Nigeria Programme, Oluwatoyin Ashipa, said: “The TTS Nigeria Programme is focused on building the skills and pathways that enable young Nigerian women to access dignified employment and participate meaningfully in the economy. This bootcamp demonstrates the value of working with industry partners to translate training into practical, workplace-relevant competencies. By connecting skills development with real employment pathways, we are helping young women prepare for opportunities while supporting businesses with a stronger pipeline of talent.” Senior Learning Manager at TTS Nigeria Programme, Simisola Aluko, said: “Building an inclusive workforce means ensuring young women have the skills, preparation and employment pathways to participate meaningfully in the economy. Through the TTS Nigeria Programme, we are working to connect skills development with dignified, formal employment opportunities in the BPO and allied sectors. Partnerships with specialist training providers such as HYT Consulting are vital to translating our competency-based approach into practical opportunities for young women and helping make the pathways into formal employment more accessible.” At the heart of HYT Consulting’s work is the recognition that closing the employability gap requires more than academic qualifications alone. Through its Employability Bootcamps, recruitment and placement services, the firm equips young talent with the practical competencies employers need, strengthening the connection between workforce readiness, business performance and Nigeria’s broader human capital development goals. The completion of this pilot cohort marks a step towards translating workforce development objectives into practical outcomes: a group of young women better prepared to meet employers’ needs and pursue meaningful careers.

title: Former Russian President Calls on Trump to ‘Remove’ Zelensky
body:
Dmitry Medvedev, Deputy Chairman of Russia’s Security Council, has called for the US to remove Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky from power by means of assassination.
Medvedev, often seen as a megaphone for the more extreme views among Kremlin hawks, made a string of allegations on the messaging platform MaxMessenger before calling on US President Donald Trump to remove Ukraine’s president.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
MaxMessenger – often referred to simply as Max – is the Russian state-sponsored social media platform, intended to supplant Western channels, that requires the user to hold a Russian or Belarusian phone number to register.
According to an Oct. 25 report by The Moscow Times , the comments made on the Russian messaging platform included the statement: “American history itself offers a solution. All he [Trump] has to do is summon the secretary of war and the CIA director and tell them to take care of this ‘unfortunate little problem.’”
He then added: “The how, where, and by what means are irrelevant.”
Medvedev has frequently called for the “physical elimination” of Zelensky or, alternatively, a repeat of the “Venezuelan scenario” – the forcible removal of the Ukrainian head of state – on a number of social media channels, including Telegram.
On Oct. 16 he wrote in a post on Telegram:
“They [the Ukrainians] won’t make peace with Zelensky. He doesn’t want to make peace. He says he wants to make peace, but he doesn’t really want to.”
He suggested a solution to the impasse that Zelensky “should be given rat poison or consume a horse-sized dose of its favorite cocaine,” before adding he “is so cowardly that he won’t even consider such a thing.”
Medvedev, who is considered to be on of President Vladimir Putin’s closest confidantes, suggests the elimination of the Ukrainian president is the answer solving the war in Ukraine, which Russia launched, rather than a diplomatic solution.
According to the Moscow Times there have at least 10 attempts to assassinate Zelensky by Russian sabotage and reconnaissance groups.
His comments, while more extreme, echo the Oct. 10 sentiments expressed by Trump that Ukraine needs to elect a new president who can “make a deal” to end the war with Russia.
