title: Raytheon international orders surge, with overseas business at 37% of $130 billion backlog
body: Raytheon’s international orders reached 2.5 times their year-earlier level in the first nine months of 2026, RTX Chairman and CEO Chris Calio said, citing strong demand across its main overseas markets. The business booked $9 billion in international orders during the third quarter, with more expected before year-end. Calio told investors on RTX’s October 20 earnings call that demand remained strong across Europe, the Middle East and North Africa, and Asia-Pacific. Chief Financial Officer Neil Mitchill said international customers accounted for 37% of Raytheon’s $130 billion backlog. “Our international bookings at Raytheon are up 2.5x year-to-date on a year-over-year basis,” Calio said. “So the demand internationally continues to be exceptionally robust.” The overseas share of Raytheon’s backlog rises to 52% when the Tomahawk and AMRAAM contracts added during the quarter are excluded, Mitchill said. RTX booked approximately $23 billion for Tomahawk and more than $14 billion for AMRAAM after converting framework agreements into multiyear production contracts. “We booked $9 billion worth of international orders at Raytheon during the third quarter,” Mitchill said. “A little overshadowed by the size of Tomahawk and AMRAAM, but still really, really strong bookings, and we expect some more here in the fourth quarter.” Calio said defense budgets were expected to grow across Europe, Asia-Pacific, and the Middle East and North Africa in 2027. He singled out Germany, Poland and Japan among countries planning significant spending. RTX works with local companies and suppliers across those regions to support production of systems including Patriot, GEM-T, Standard Missile and Coyote, alongside military engines. Calio said more than 130 suppliers supported the company’s production work in Europe. Raytheon’s major third-quarter awards included $3.1 billion to provide training systems for the British Army, Vice President of Investor Relations Nathan Ware said. Total bookings reached $52.3 billion, equivalent to 6.54 times quarterly sales. Sales rose 14% to $8 billion, driven by higher volumes across naval programs and land and air defense systems, including Patriot, Standard Missile and Tomahawk. Adjusted operating profit increased by $275 million to $1.1 billion, reflecting improved productivity, higher volumes and a favorable program mix. RTX raised Raytheon’s full-year sales growth forecast to the low teens from its previous range of high single digits to low double digits. It also raised the expected annual increase in operating profit to $800 million–$850 million from $575 million–$650 million.

title: Ebola: Yobe Govt Activates Emergency Response Centres, Border Surveillance
body: The Yobe State government said it has not yet recorded any Ebola virus but has activated its Public Health Emergency Incident Management System and developed a comprehensive Emergency Preparedness and Response plan to monitor the possible outbreak of the disease. The Commissioner for Health, Dr. Mohammed Lawan Gana, represented by the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry, Hadiza Sabo, disclosed this while briefing journalists in Damaturu on Monday. According to her, the state government is building 6 technical pillars recommended by the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control for the Ebola Virus Disease response, which are coordinated through the Emergency Operations Centre (EOC). “Yobe State shares an international border; consequently, the state is strengthening cross-border surveillance and coordination with transport and relevant border authorities at key entry points to enhance vigilance, facilitate the timely detection and reporting of public health threats, and support prompt response to potential disease outbreaks” “We have outlined six pillars of coordination and management: epidemiology and surveillance, case management, infection prevention and control, laboratory services, communication and community engagement, as well as point of entry,” she said. Sabo further added that the government is intensifying public awareness campaigns using radio, television, community town carriers and engagement with traditional leaders. “Our message is simple; Ebola is real, but it is preventable and controllable. We are advising citizens to maintain good hand hygiene, avoid direct contact with the bodily fluids of anyone showing symptoms, and report any unusual illness or death to the nearest health facility immediately”. The government advises the general public to shun any rumours or misinformation and rely on verified information from the State Ministry of Health, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) and other official sources, and not to spread unverified reports on social media, as doing that can cause unnecessary panic and harm. The post Ebola: Yobe Govt Activates Emergency Response Centres, Border Surveillance appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Ebola: Plateau reactivates isolation centres, strengthens surveillance
body: By Golok Nanmwa JOS – The Plateau State Government has reactivated isolation centres, intensified public awareness campaigns and strengthened disease surveillance as part of measures to prevent the spread of Ebola into the state. The state Commissioner for Health, Dr Nicholas Ba’amlong, disclosed this during a press briefing, saying the government had also directed its emergency preparedness team to assess safety measures at the airport and alert local government areas bordering neighbouring states. “Residents should maintain proper hygiene and avoid contact with potentially infected persons,” Ba’amlong said. “Maintain good hygiene, wash your hands regularly and avoid direct contact with the blood and body fluids of suspected infected persons,” he urged. “Remain vigilant and report suspected cases to health authorities,” the commissioner said, stressing that public cooperation was critical to preventing the spread of the disease.” ” The measures were announced alongside 10 resolutions approved at the 12th Plateau State Council on Health meeting held last week “ “The resolutions include establishing a state health trust fund, strengthening disease surveillance, addressing shortages of health workers and establishing an emergency fund for public health threats,” Ba’amlong said. He added, “These measures are aimed at strengthening the state’s preparedness to respond to disease outbreaks and improving the delivery of healthcare services to residents.” The commissioner urged residents to “follow public health guidance and report suspected cases promptly to health authorities.” The post Ebola: Plateau reactivates isolation centres, strengthens surveillance appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Can John Healey conjure a budget to keep investors’ money in Britain?
body: By one measure, John Healey’s budget has already been a success. He has avoided the paralysis that hit the UK before his predecessor Rachel Reeves delivered her tax and spending plans in November 2025. That budget had such an agonisingly long build-up that a combination of speculation and leaks caused jitters in financial markets, property transactions ground to a halt, and the wealthy packed their bags for sunnier climes. It forced Ms Reeves into policy pivots that dented her reputation and confidence in the government’s messaging. Mr Healey has led a more orchestrated run-up, allowing messaging to get out that he will not match Capital Gains Tax to income tax, that banks can expect a fresh levy, and that business red tape is set to be torn apart. His goal when he rises to the dispatch box is to unveil short-term help with the cost-of-living, stem the tide of super-rich moving abroad, while also seeking to stabilise public finances hit by spending pressures and the fallout from the US-Iran war. So what do those who invest in Britain want to see come out of his red box, or perhaps more importantly, discarded as a bad idea? Property stakes In terms of property, London’s golden postcodes have seen sluggish sales in recent years as the prime market fails to ignite, with prices still behind their 2014 peak. Tom Bill, head of UK residential research at Knight Frank, hopes the greatest threats to the market – such as an even broader mansion tax than first announced – have already been abandoned. “Sentiment in the prime London property market would improve because of what is not in the budget rather than anything the Chancellor includes,” he told The National . “He has reportedly dropped plans to lower the bottom threshold for the high-value council tax, and there would be a collective sigh of relief if property is not targeted in the way it has been in previous budgets.” The mansion tax would add an annual fee for properties above £2 million on top of council tax. Buyers in high-value residential markets such as London require “a sense of stability that has been missing for several years”, he said. London has had a comparatively positive summer, largely thanks to the absence of tax speculation ahead of the budget, he said. September recorded the first period of quarterly price growth (+0.3 per cent) in prime central London (PCL) for four years. Sales of properties above £5 million dropped by 14 per cent in the 18 months after Ms Reeves’ first budget in October 2024, when she raised second-home stamp duty to 5 per cent from 3 per cent. That created an estimated stamp duty loss of £541 million based on a comparison of sales in the preceding 18 months, according to Knight Frank. “The stamp duty loss is one of many indicators that show what happens when Britain is not competitive on a global stage in attracting overseas investors,” said Leslie Macleod-Miller, chief executive of Foreign Investors for Britain (FIFB). “Of course, it also grossly understates the wider loss to the country’s economy.” Unworkable For Matthew Robertson, co-founder and chief financial officer of luxury developer Valouran, there are three focal points for the budget: capital gains tax, wealth tax and the mansion tax. “As we saw play out ahead of the autumn budget last year, when people don’t know what’s coming, they wait,” he told The National . “Buyers pause, deals are deferred, and the Treasury loses out too because there is no tax intake when no one is buying or selling. Since real estate investment is inherently long term, my hope is that this budget will, at a minimum, provide businesses and investors with confidence that they can plan without constantly worrying that a new tax or policy change is just around the corner.” He believes the mansion tax is unworkable due to the requirement to have hundreds of thousands of homes revalued. He said the £2 million threshold already drags a great many people into the levy, “many of whom would not consider themselves rich”. Proposals to reduce this to £1.5 million must be resisted, he cautioned. “If mansion tax is here to stay, it would be good to have it accompanied by a reduction in stamp duty. The objective should be to encourage a more efficient and dynamic housing market, rather than simply increasing the tax burden.” Budget flops Research by Beauchamp estates found that the autumn budgets of the Boris Johnson and Rishi Sunak governments had the most positive impact on London’s prime property market, while Liz Truss’s mini-budget spooked the market and led to the exodus of wealthy owners. Under Keir Starmer and Rachel Reeves, the market struggled. It found that after the 2024 budget there were significant drops in sales. The number of £5 million+ properties sold dropped by 16 per cent, from 148 deals pre-budget to 124 deals post-budget, with the overall value of deals slipping from £1.42 billion to £1.4 billion. The £10 million+ homes market declined the most, with the number of sales falling by 25 per cent, from 51 pre-budget to 38 post-budget. Beauchamp Estates says that the 2024 decline in sales was due to Conservative rather than Labour policies, namely the scrapping of non-doms, which was initially planned by Mr Sunak. Jeremy Gee, managing director of Beauchamp Estates, said: "Our detailed analysis of the autumn budgets over the last 11 years clearly shows that domestic UK and international buyers of property in London like political, economic and taxation certainty. Cameron/Osborne raising Stamp Duty was negative for the market. However, the upbeat and business-friendly stance of Boris/Sunak was good for property sales, the uncertainty caused by May/Hammond was unhelpful, and Truss/Kwarteng temporarily tanked the market and were made to look foolish." He said that over the last few years the top end of the market has proved more resilient since sales are heavily influenced by wider global economic and political shifts, rather than UK domestic policies. Mr Gee said: "It is our firm belief that it is not tax that stops a buyer moving. It is a buyer not knowing what the tax will be that kills a sale. Over the past few years, the leaks and mixed messages that circulate for months before each budget have left buyers and sellers paralysed by fear of the unknown, and the market simply pauses until after the budget and sales decline.” He added: "Our greatest concern around the 2026 autumn budget is further taxation of wealth, whether CGT is aligned with income tax, or the introduction of a new wealth tax. The international buyers who underpin the prime central London market have already had to absorb a lot, and we must not forget that they have no shortage of alternative locations to invest in real estate." Who gains? He said Mr Healey’s dismissal of calls from Labour MPs to align capital gains tax with income tax rates is very welcome. “We need people to be motivated and confident enough to invest capital and build businesses in the UK, and the current CGT regime is one of the very few remaining incentives for those prepared to back businesses for the long term. Raising rates would make the UK a far less attractive place to invest and build. “Not a day goes by without more news that another ultra-high net worth individual has left the UK. These individuals take with them significant personal taxable incomes that have contributed so much to our public finances. Even more concerningly, they are relocating their successful businesses elsewhere, businesses that paid corporation tax and employed many other high earners in the UK. Tax policy must evolve to stem this exodus.” People representing about $160 billion on the Bloomberg Billionaires Index have already left the UK in the past two years. It coincided with the scrapping of non-dom status, which allowed international income to be kept out of the reach of UK tax authorities. Most of that group originally came from overseas, but the recent relocation of British hedge fund founder Chris Rokos to Greece has underscored a growing unrest among local entrepreneurs. A poll of 500 UK business owners during August for the London professional services group S&W found about half of them would consider relocating if capital gains taxes are increased in the autumn budget. There are suggestions of how to encourage wealthy investors to reconsider Britain. There is some speculation around an investor visa. “The details are unclear, and it may not be attractive enough to reverse the flow of wealthy individuals leaving the UK, but it would show the government acknowledges that it needs to address the issue,” said Mr Bill. The proposal by FIFB is based on a minimum investment of £2.5 million and an annual flat-rate tax of £200,000 for up to 15 years, with a route to indefinite leave to remain. FIFB estimates the plan could attract more than £225 billion of inward investment over a decade. The current non-dom replacement exempts newcomers’ foreign income and gains from UK tax for their first four years of residence. “Four years is simply not long enough, which is a message we have been giving to the government,” Mr Macleod-Miller said. “The problem so far is the gap between what the government has said in relation to creating economic growth and what they have done.” Deals done In recent days, Mr Healey has said he wants a business-friendly budget, and has hinted that CGT, which is levied on a person's profits from an asset sale, may not rise at all. That may be bittersweet for those wealthy Britons who rushed to ensure they weren’t hit by any increase ahead of the budget. Investors have been seeking to take advantage of the current 24 per cent higher rate, according to many wealth advisers. A lot of people rushed to get deals done earlier in October to secure the current rate, said Chris Etherington, a private client tax partner at RSM UK who advises business owners and entrepreneurs. He saw people “trying to accelerate deals ahead of the budget”. Capital gains tax fears had been “the number one issue”, said Iain Tait, head of the private investment office at wealth management firm W1M. “We’ve had a lot of clients asking about what they could do to crystallise gains at 24 per cent.” One investor nervous about further tax hikes is Konstantin Sidorov, whose London investment fund is sitting on a gain of more than 500 per cent through its bet on Revolut, the UK fintech giant founded by billionaire Nik Storonsky. Mr Sidorov called a dedicated wealth tax a “red line” that would make him consider relocating after more than a decade. “My feeling is quite bad – the question is: How bad?” he said in an interview. If capital gains taxes rise, “we’ll see far fewer investors who would like to take more risks”. Do no harm After his predecessor hiked taxes by more than £60 billion ($80 billion) in her two budgets, Mr Healey has no appetite for another big set-piece. “They’ve calculated that this budget should just be ‘do no harm’, given everything else that’s going on in the world,” said James Nation, managing director at Forefront Advisers and a former special adviser to Rishi Sunak when he was chancellor and prime minister. “They don’t want to do anything that derails them.” Mr Healey’s approach means crunch issues such as overhauling the welfare system and long-term investment in defence will be deferred. It also shies away from demands from the Labour left that he should ramp up taxes on wealth and raise spending on public services. On Friday, he announced his budget would include measures to reduce the regulatory burden on businesses such as simplifying corporate reporting requirements, while also extending import tariff suspensions on products across sectors including chemicals, plastics and hydrogen. “British firms are fed up with form-filling and pointless paperwork that eats into valuable time and money,” he said in a statement. “That is why we are cutting unnecessary bureaucracy and giving businesses the breathing space they need to invest, innovate and create good jobs.” Iron triangle Treasury officials describe Healey’s budget as a stepping stone moment, saying a major “10-year plan” speech planned by Mr Burnham later this year is the real main fixture for addressing Britain’s big structural problems. A Labour official acknowledged to The National the limited scope for action. “Everything’s a bit in the long grass,” he said, including decisions on defence, welfare and taxation. “The PM is actually stuck with the commitments that Starmer had, which is no increases in most of the taxes, so we are scratching around for income, most likely from a bank tax hike that might only raise a couple of billion.” Andrew Murray, a former adviser to Labour’s leadership, said the budget would establish the direction of Mr Burnham’s government after he raised expectations of a different economic approach. “Obviously, everyone will give him a bit of latitude, but the budget will really set the direction,” he told The National. “If it is, as expected, a bit flat, a bit of a non-event, the only thing will be his 10-year plan for Britain that he promised before Christmas. He would need to really paint that in vivid colours and get it done soon if people aren’t going to start feeling a bit disappointed.” But the government remained constrained by the competing demands of welfare, taxation and defence. “It’s like an iron triangle, that really boxes you in,” he said, adding that the budget would test Mr Burnham’s promise of a more social-democratic future. “All the briefing is that apart from bank tax, Healey isn’t going to do anything very decisive.” Further taxes on the well-off were unlikely, said the Labour official, because the government had already gone as far as it could, particularly following changes to the non-dom tax regime. “It would be a surprise if there’s anything more on the wealthy because the non-dom tax has clearly had some impact,” the official said. The Institute for Fiscal Studies has warned that the government faces spending pressures, particularly with its plans to increase defence spending to 3 per cent of GDP by 2030, which would require tax increases or benefit cuts of around £35 billion. The budget will be a test of whether Mr Burnham can deliver on his Labour conference speech, which promised higher living standards and economic renewal while keeping spending within limits. If he succeeds, it could sow the seeds for a Labour election victory. If he doesn't, Britain could revert once again to political and financial uncertainty, and a further exodus of the money-makers.

title: Russia doing its best to ensure safe choice for Alyoshki residents during evacuation
body:
MOSCOW, October 26. /TASS/. Russia is doing everything it can to see to it that people can safely choose where to evacuate from the city of Alyoshki in the Kherson Region and hopes Kiev will not hinder this, Russian Human Rights Commissioner Yana Lantratova said.
"And the Russian side is doing and will continue to do everything possible to ensure that people are granted the freedom of choice that best takes their safety into account. We hope that the Ukrainian side will not take any steps that would hinder this, as has happened on more than one occasion," she wrote on messaging app Max.
She stressed that the key task of the upcoming humanitarian operation in Alyoshki is to learn about the needs of the city’s residents, form a humanitarian convoy and deliver relief aid, including medicine, food products, hygiene and sanitation products, and daily necessities.
Another task is to ensure the evacuation of those willing to leave the city, she said, adding that, according to the local authorities, there are not so many people ready to take that step. "Since most of those who wanted to leave have already left, and they left entirely of their own free will. The remaining people will certainly be given the same opportunity," she noted.
She also said that Russian soldiers are providing people with humanitarian aid and all necessary supplies, as well as clearing roads of mines after Ukrainian drone attacks, all at peril to their own lives. Russian doctors are also being killed and injured when Ukrainian drones strike ambulances, Lantratova added.

title: Police arrest suspected motorcycle thief, recover 2 bikes in Jigawa
body: The Jigawa State Police Command has arrested a 24-year-old man suspected of motorcycle theft and recovered two stolen motorcycles in Malam Madori and Shuwarin communities of the state. The command disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, October 25, 2026, by its Police Public Relations Officer, SP Lawan Shisu Adam. According to the statement, the arrest followed a report of the theft of a red Boxer motorcycle in Malam Madori town at about 5:00 a.m., on October 19, 2026. The police said a team of operatives launched an investigation into the incident, leading to the arrest of the suspect, identified as Saleh Muhd, at Kashin Dila Junction, where the stolen motorcycle was recovered in his possession. Nigeria’s lone Ebola patient evacuated to Switzerland FCT: Rising transport fares threaten children, teachers’ school attendance The statement added that the suspect had been arraigned in court for prosecution. In a separate incident, police operatives attached to the Shuwarin Division recovered an abandoned, unregistered red Hunter motorcycle in Gwazaye village, Kiyawa Local Government Area, on October 19. The motorcycle was taken to the police station for investigation. The police said a 32-year-old man from Tunubu village in Jahun Local Government Area later reported at the division on October 21, presenting documents to establish ownership of the motorcycle. He reportedly told the police that unknown persons entered his residence while he was sleeping on October 18 and stole the motorcycle. According to the statement, police investigations confirmed that the documents matched the motorcycle’s chassis and engine numbers, leading to its release to the claimant on bond. The command said efforts were ongoing to identify and arrest those responsible for the theft. The Commissioner of Police in Jigawa State, CP Tijjani Murtala, reiterated the command’s commitment to tackling motorcycle theft and other criminal activities across the state. He urged residents to report suspicious movements promptly and provide credible information to assist the police in preventing and detecting crime.

title: TenTrade in Lagos: A conversation about education and the future of trading
body: Ahead of TenTrade’s “One Community, One Future” seminar on November 7th, we spoke with Andreas Andreou, Partner & Chief Revenue Officer; Obasi Wilfred, Regional Director, Africa; and Ademola Adeagbo, Head of Education, Africa. Together, they discuss what traders need to learn, how mentors can help and what building a trading community means in practice. Q: What does “One Community, One Future” mean to you? Andreas Andreou: It expresses the kind of company we want TenTrade to become. A global business needs more than a presence in different markets, it needs meaningful relationships within them. For us, bringing educators, mentors and traders together is part of building those relationships. Obasi Wilfred: For me, the important word is “community.” Our work in Africa has to reflect the people here, their questions, circumstances and ambitions. Community means having a two-way conversation and allowing what we hear locally to influence how we support traders. Ademola Adeagbo: I see it as creating an environment where learning is an ongoing conversation. You can attend a presentation and understand a concept, then struggle when you try to apply it. Having access to educators and mentors gives you somewhere to bring those questions. That is the value I want people to see. Q: Why Lagos, and why now? Andreas Andreou: If we want a lasting presence in Africa, we need to invest time in meeting people and understanding their expectations. Lagos gives us an opportunity to do that in person. The decision to hold this event reflects the direction we want to take, which is building our presence through education and relationships. Obasi Wilfred: Lagos is a starting point. Nigeria matters in our regional thinking in its own right, and we want to understand what traders here need rather than approach Africa as one single market. Meeting people allows us to hear the details behind a request for “more education”, which topics need explaining and what makes learning difficult. Ademola Adeagbo: From my side, the reason to bring people together is the quality of the learning we can do face to face. A participant can ask a question and work through an example with an educator. We can move beyond defining risk management to discussing how someone would actually apply it. That is what makes an in-person seminar worth it. Q: How would you describe the Nigerian trader today, and what do they need most? Andreas Andreou: From a company perspective, I would be cautious about putting every Nigerian trader into one category. We need to serve people at different stages of experience without assuming they all want the same thing. That requires clear information. Our global experience gives us a foundation, but our regional team helps us understand how to make that useful locally. Obasi Wilfred: I would describe a range of people rather than a single profile. Someone learning alongside a full-time job has different needs from an experienced trader refining a process. In Nigeria, we need to understand the practical circumstances around those ambitions: the time someone can dedicate and the resources available to them. It also needs to be honest about the difference between wanting an additional income and being ready to take financial risk. Ademola Adeagbo: What a trader needs most depends on where the gaps are. A beginner may know the language of trading without fully understanding leverage or position sizing. Someone with more experience may understand those concepts but struggle to apply them consistently. My priority is to help people identify what they actually need to learn next. Q: What do new traders most often get wrong, and how will the seminar address it? Andreas Andreou: One misconception we want our education to address is that access to a trading platform is not enough. As a broker, we have a role in making learning part of the relationship from the beginning. The seminar reflects that approach by giving education and direct conversations with mentors a dedicated space. We want people to leave better equipped to assess decisions for themselves. Obasi Wilfred: I would highlight the danger of allowing other people’s apparent success to set your expectations. If you are introduced to trading through a persuasive story or a result shared online, you may see very little of the risk behind it. For our audience in Nigeria, I want the event to make room for questions about those expectations. People should feel comfortable discussing uncertainty and losses as well as opportunities. Ademola Adeagbo: A common mistake is leaving risk until later. Before entering, you need to consider how much you could lose and how the position size fits that limit. Our educational aim is to make that sequence practical through clear frameworks and discussion. No seminar can remove uncertainty, but it can help someone approach a trade with a more structured decision process. Q: How can this become a lasting community rather than a one-day event? Andreas Andreou: That comes down to consistency. The longer-term vision is for education and engagement to be part of how people experience TenTrade, rather than something associated only with an event. We should judge the value of the day by what it teaches us about the support people want next. Building a community takes consistent work. Obasi Wilfred: Regional relevance will determine whether people want to remain involved. If participants raise questions about their learning needs, those questions should inform our thinking after the seminar. We also need to recognise differences within Nigeria and across Africa as we develop that approach. A community becomes meaningful when people can see that their contribution matters. Ademola Adeagbo: Educationally, there needs to be a next step. Someone might leave realising that they need to understand something better or start reviewing their decisions more carefully. A useful learning community helps them pursue that next step and return with better questions. Q: What is the one thing you would like someone to take away from 7 November? Andreas Andreou: A clear understanding of where we want to take TenTrade: a global business that builds lasting local relationships, with educators and mentors playing a meaningful role in that development. Obasi Wilfred: The feeling that their perspective belongs in the conversation. We want our work in Nigeria and across Africa to be informed by the people we serve, and that starts with listening to them. Ademola Adeagbo: One practical habit: consider the potential loss before the potential return. If someone leaves with a better way to assess risk and a clear idea of what they need to learn next, that is a good outcome. Event information TenTrade’s “One Community, One Future” seminar takes place on November 7th at Watercress Hotels & Events, Ikeja, Lagos. This in-person event has 250 seats and focuses on practical learning, risk management and direct access to mentors. Click here to register, with no entrance fee. The post TenTrade in Lagos: A conversation about education and the future of trading appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Baltic Fleet divers conduct underwater combat drills at depths of up to 30 meters
body:
KALININGRAD, October 26. /TASS/. Service members of the Russian Navy’s Baltic Fleet Base’s counter-sabotage unit conducted diving operations at depths ranging from 20 to 30 meters, according to the Baltic Fleet’s press service.
"During the exercise, the navy men practiced diving to depths of 20 to 30 meters and elements of underwater navigation using propulsion devices, and also conducted a search for possible sabotage devices, underwater caches, and hiding places in the naval forces’ basing area," the Baltic Fleet said in a statement.
It noted that the exercise took place under challenging hydro-meteorological conditions. In addition, the troops conducted battle firing using the SPP-1 special underwater pistol and the APS special underwater assault rifle. They also practiced elements of underwater combat.

title: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan Hold Regional Security Talks in Tehran Amid US-Israel-Iran Conflict
body:
Top leaders from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan are meeting Iranian leaders in Tehran today to discuss regional security and cooperation, as the ongoing conflict involving Iran, the United States and Israel continues to destabilise West Asia.



Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, Pakistan's Army Chief General Asim Munir and Turkey's Intelligence Chief Ibrahim Kalin are holding discussions with Major General Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council (SNSC).

The leaders were to meet the Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian. The Iranian President left for Moscow on Monday afternoon to attend a summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum and meet Russian President Vladimir Putin, his office’s public relations director said.

The high-level engagement assumes significance as the four countries explore ways to strengthen regional security through cooperation among neighbouring states, amid growing geopolitical uncertainty and concerns over energy security.

Ali Bagheri Kani, Deputy Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said the visiting officials would congratulate Rezaei on his appointment and discuss regional security.

He said the initiative originated during General Munir's visit to Tehran last week, when the Pakistani army chief proposed a meeting involving senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan.

Bagheri Kani described the discussions as an effort to establish a regional security framework without external involvement, adding that Tehran regarded the role of the United States and Israel as a source of instability.

The talks come as the conflict has placed the Strait of Hormuz at the centre of international concern. Disruptions to shipping through the strategic waterway have heightened uncertainty over oil and gas supplies and their potential impact on the global economy.

Despite the military confrontation, diplomatic channels between Tehran and Washington remain open. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said on Sunday that messages were continuing to be exchanged through intermediaries, although he accused Washington of maintaining unilateral demands.

Earlier on Sunday, Qatari mediators, at the behest of the United States, were in Tehran as part of an effort to ease regional tensions.

However, the prospects for a broader settlement remain uncertain. US President Donald Trump said the conflict would not end until Washington was confident that Iran no longer possessed nuclear capabilities. He also indicated that the United States was weighing a diplomatic agreement against further military action.

The military situation remains tense, with US Central Command chief Admiral Brad Cooper visiting the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday. CENTCOM said US forces had assisted more than 3,000 commercial vessels in transiting the waterway and helped Persian Gulf partners export over 1.5 billion barrels of crude oil.

Against this backdrop, the Tehran meeting represents a significant attempt by regional powers to address security challenges through direct engagement. Whether the discussions translate into a concrete framework for cooperation remains to be seen, but the participation of senior Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials signals a growing emphasis on regional coordination.

title: Rada extends martial law for another 90 days
body:
According to a Ukrinform correspondent, 293 members of parliament supported draft law No. 16182 , “On the Approval of the Decree of the President of Ukraine ‘On the Extension of Martial Law in Ukraine.’”
The law will take effect on October 31. Under its provisions, martial law is extended until January 29, 2027.
“The implementation of the Presidential Decree ‘On the Extension of Martial Law in Ukraine’ will facilitate the adoption of adequate measures to counter armed aggression, ensure Ukraine’s independence, its sovereignty, and territorial integrity, and provides for the extension of the powers granted to the relevant state authorities, military command, military administrations, and local self-government bodies necessary to repel armed aggression,” said National Security and Defense Council Secretary Ihor Klymenko in the Verkhovna Rada before the law was adopted.
The next bill under consideration by members of parliament is “On the Approval of the Decree of the President of Ukraine ‘On the Extension of the Term of General Mobilization’” No. 16183.
As reported, President Volodymyr Zelensky today submitted to the Verkhovna Rada bills to approve his decrees on extending martial law and conducting general mobilization in Ukraine.

title: Ukraine unable to restore industry on its own, says political analyst
body:
MOSCOW, October 26. /TASS/. Ukraine will be unable to restore its industrial sector after the conflict with Russia using its own national budget alone, given the course pursued by the Kiev authorities, Ukrainian political analyst Taras Sidorets told TASS.
According to the analyst, following the 2014 government coup, the Ukrainian leadership adopted a strategy centered on securing financial assistance from Western countries rather than promoting domestic development.
"There is one very significant caveat: these funds will only be provided if Ukraine maintains its ‘anti-Russia’ stance and continues to fight against Russia. A peaceful Ukraine would, of course, receive no Western funding for the restoration of its industry," Sidorets said.
He argued that this policy had left Ukraine’s industrial sector largely devastated. "In August-September 2026, following high-profile statements by Vladimir Zelensky, who announced a 40-day campaign to ‘force Russia into peace,’ and the subsequent launch of strikes against non-military targets inside Russia, Moscow delivered a sufficiently strong and decisive response," he said.
The Russian Defense Ministry has reported an increase in strikes on industrial facilities in Ukraine. According to the ministry, Russian combat drones and missile systems target infrastructure facilities used by the Kiev authorities to support the needs of the Ukrainian armed forces.

title: Kremlin welcomes Lula da Silva’s victory in Brazilian presidential election
body:
MOSCOW, October 26. /TASS/. Moscow welcomes Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva’s victory in Brazil’s presidential election, Russian presidential press secretary Dmitry Peskov told reporters.
"We welcome Mr. Lula’s victory," he said.
Peskov noted that Lula da Silva was doing a great deal not only to develop bilateral relations but also to promote cooperation with Russia on the international stage as a whole. The Kremlin hopes that all these processes will continue.
The second round of Brazil’s presidential election took place on October 25. According to the electoral commission, after 100% of ballots had been counted, Lula da Silva was reelected president with 51.79% of the vote. His fourth term as head of state will begin on January 5, 2027.

title: Koretsky urges business to plan for worst case, warns of $1.5 bln budget gap
body:
Prime Minister of Ukraine Serhiy Koretsky has called on the business community to prepare in advance for the most critical scenarios regarding enemy attacks and economic challenges.
"When we talk to founders and top management, I’ve sensed a certain attitude that 'it will somehow blow over.' Perhaps I won't be targeted by missiles or drones, perhaps my sector won't be touched. Therefore, first: I would strongly ask and recommend thinking according to the most critical scenario of events. Thinking ahead about alternative production sites: who you can cooperate with, where you can make a private label if we are talking about consumer goods, if your enterprise is hit. How to talk in advance with suppliers, perhaps even for imported goods, how to conclude framework contracts and be ready rather than doing it all later. Looking at alternative premises for relocation, for restoration. In other words, think in the most critical scenario. It is better to be ready for this and have it not happen than to find oneself in an unexpected situation," Koretsky said at the 12th Kyiv International Economic Forum (KIEF) themed "People. Business. Economy. What's Next?" in Kyiv on Monday, as reported by an Interfax-Ukraine correspondent.
According to the Prime Minister, enemy strikes have already caused over $7.7 billion in losses, with more than 1 million square meters of various types of real estate, both state and private, destroyed or damaged. Significant destruction has hit energy, metallurgy, logistics, processing enterprises, retail, and other sectors.
"Considering these losses, considering the strikes, we already see that by the end of the year the state budget will underfulfill its plans and forecasts by about $1.5 billion. That is the baseline forecast we have today," he stated.
At the same time, he emphasized that despite all this, the country's economy continues to function.
"If we think in terms of PnL (Profit and Loss statement), allocating a lot of funds to support business is impossible. There is no such PnL, because we can only cover one-third of the budget. Even realizing, clearly realizing this, we live even on a cash flow principle and in a certain way go all-in, allocating certain funds to support programs, to various subsidies, to grant programs. Because we realize that without this support, business – small, medium, and large in particular – cannot be sufficiently resilient to counter enemy attacks. And this is the conscious logic and tactics of the government," Koretsky noted.
The Prime Minister stressed that the government will continue programs that have proven their effectiveness, notably the "Affordable Loans 5-7-9%" program. He noted that since the program's inception, UAH 580 billion has been issued, with the current loan portfolio principal standing at around UAH 200 billion. He recalled the recent decision allowing large businesses to receive about UAH 2 billion "in one hand per group of companies" at a preferential interest rate of around 10%.
"The 2026 budget allocated Hr 18 billion. We are expanding this program and see that by the end of the year it will be Hr 22 billion. We currently have a certain deficit on four billion, but one way or another we will cover it, because we consider this to be one of the fundamentally important, correct programs that genuinely supports business," the Prime Minister said.
He also pointed out the necessity of establishing a war risk insurance and damage compensation system. Koretsky recalled the proposal to create a special fund in the budget with an initial state contribution of $1 billion, which partners would double or triple.
"How will this work further? A simplified procedure. Compensation within 30 days after processing. And the tariff for this insurance risk must be very basic, symbolic, we are aiming at approximately 2%. And the maximum damage compensation will be about $5 million in one hand," the Prime Minister detailed.
Koretsky also stated that there is currently no consensus or support for increasing the Value Added Tax (VAT) from 20% to 21% to fund this special fund.
"There is no consensus among big and medium business, there is no support in parliament yet. We are looking for other mechanisms, we will see how the budgetary process proceeds in parliament and build from that. But we have no other path, we must find the instrument. Together we will see what we can contribute," Koretsky emphasized.

title: Agricultural Year Recap and Spring Planting Scenarios: UCAB to Host #DoAgro26 Conference
body:
On December 4, the 18th International Conference “Agribusiness in Ukraine” (#DoAgro26) will take place in Truskavets (Lviv Oblast). The event will be attended by government officials, market leaders, and leading agricultural producers.
This was reported by the press service of the organizers—the “Ukrainian Agribusiness Club” and the UCABevent agency.
This year, the event is completely revamping its format and usual location to take stock of the past year and develop a roadmap for the upcoming season.
This isn’t about monologues or dry reports—those are a thing of the past. What lies ahead is the search for new operating models: open dialogue with government officials, collective brainstorming, and making strategic decisions right here and now. The main goal is to find effective operating models under the new rules of the game.
The “Agribusiness in Ukraine” conference will be held in cooperation with the International Finance Corporation (IFC), a member of the World Bank Group, and in partnership with the Ministry of Finance of the Czech Republic. Valtra, part of AGCO Corporation, is the exclusive technical partner, and Credit Agricole is the gold financial partner.
Agricultural producers and participants in previous UCAAB events are eligible for a 20% discount off the base price, while association members receive special terms.
For more information about the event, follow the links: https://cutt.ly/9yQmTlnY
Interfax-Ukraine is the conference’s media partner.

title: Anambra Student Wins 2026 National Head Girl Competition
body: Jane-Frances Chiamaka Gabriel of Queen of the Rosary College Onitsha has emerged champion of the 2026 National Head Girl Competition, organised by the Women in Leadership Advancement Network (WILAN Global). She won a cash prize of ₦1 million and a brand-new laptop at the grand finale held on Tuesday, October 13, at Alliance Française in Ikoyi, Lagos. Jane-Frances, who represented her school in the competition, clinched the top prize with an innovation that uses plantable pencils made from recycled paper to teach children about climate change. Her victory followed a multi-stage selection process that saw her advance from an initial pool of applicants to the top 16 contestants, then the top eight, before securing a place among the final three. Her progression earned her an all-expenses-paid trip to Lagos, which she undertook alongside the school’s principal, Reverend Sister Maria Chijioke Nwankwo, for the grand finale. At the final, Jane-Frances competed against some of Nigeria’s most promising young female student leaders while presenting her innovation as a practical way to introduce environmental awareness to children while encouraging sustainable habits from an early age. The competition concluded with Fetuga Ameerah of the International School, University of Lagos, taking second place, while Oritsematosan Jackson of Royal Family Academy, Abuja, finished third. Organised by WILAN Global, the National Head Girl Competition is an innovation and leadership platform for head girls across Nigeria. It provides participants with an opportunity to demonstrate their leadership abilities, develop innovative solutions to real-world challenges and showcase their capacity to contribute meaningfully to their communities. Speaking on the school’s achievement, the school’s principal, Rev. Sr. Maria Chijioke Nwankwo, said the victory reflected the school’s sustained commitment to preparing young girls for leadership, entrepreneurship and the future of work. “Wins like this are not entirely new to QRC. At QRC, we take entrepreneurship education and digital skills training seriously because we believe that girls must be equipped not just to participate in the future economy but to shape it,” she said. The principal also acknowledged the contributions of teachers and the school’s proprietor, Archbishop Valerian Maduka Okeke, whose support continues to strengthen the school’s commitment to nurturing confident and socially responsible young leaders. For Gabriel, the victory provided an opportunity to put her creativity to practical use and demonstrate how young people can contribute to addressing challenges in their communities. “I am incredibly excited and grateful for this opportunity from WILAN Global. I am also deeply grateful to my entrepreneurship education coach and mentor, Mr John Onuigbo, who has helped me understand what is possible and encouraged me to turn my ideas into solutions that can make an impact,” she said.

title: Nigeria’s Ebola Patient Evacuated to Switzerland
body: The Federal Government has confirmed the evacuation of Nigeria’s first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) to Switzerland following significant clinical improvement. The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Pate, said this on Monday in a post on his official X handle. Pate said the evacuation was approved by him and carried out early on Monday, with the patient accompanied by her spouse, who remained asymptomatic. He said the patient was stable, conscious and communicating, while her laboratory test results were approaching baseline levels. “The index patient was clinically much improved, stable, conscious, communicating, and her clinical laboratory test results closing towards baseline. “This does not mean she is not still infectious, hence the strict protocols in place,” he said. Pate commended the clinical staff for providing quality care and public health personnel for ensuring that the evacuation complied with appropriate public health measures. He said the government would provide further updates after the patient and her spouse arrived safely at their destination. The minister said public health measures remained in place to ensure that the imported virus was contained, urging Nigerians to remain vigilant and rely on credible information sources. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Nigeria confirmed its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola Virus Disease on Oct. 20, following laboratory confirmation of infection in a woman with recent travel history to Uganda. The patient developed symptoms on Oct. 7, four days after arriving in Nigeria, and sought medical care in Abuja on Oct. 11, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) activated its incident management system, while health authorities commenced contact tracing, laboratory investigations and infection prevention measures. The NCDC’s Oct. 24 situation report identified 53 contacts linked to the case, including healthcare workers, domestic staff and the patient’s spouse. None had tested positive at the time of the report. On Oct. 23, Pate said genomic analysis showed that the virus isolated from the Nigerian patient appeared closely related to that identified in the index case in Kenya. He, however, cautioned that the genetic relationship did not establish a direct transmission link between the two cases. The Federal Government has also intensified surveillance at points of entry, strengthened infection prevention and control in health facilities, and urged healthcare workers to promptly report suspected cases. Bundibugyo virus disease is caused by a species of Ebola virus. Transmission occurs through direct contact with the blood or body fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials. The government has urged Nigerians to observe basic preventive measures, cooperate with public health officials and avoid spreading unverified information about the disease.(NAN)

title: Koretsky: government must deliver new mobilization social contract by Dec 1
body:
Prime Minister of Ukraine Serhiy Koretsky predicts that following changes to the reservation system, over 90-95% of employees in the fuel-energy and defense-industrial complexes will be re-reserved.
"We are separating the concept of criticality from economic reservation criteria. This is very important. Why? Because salary and the absence of tax debt are not the same as an enterprise's criticality. This is important, it indeed brings transparency, cleanup, and additional revenues, but it does not equal criticality. Critical means energy, the defense-industrial complex, communications, housing and communal services, pharmacies, groceries, logistics, and so on. But there are enterprises, a large number already, that got there largely due to salaries and a lack of tax debts. Therefore, we are separating criticality from the economy," Koretsky said at the 12th Kyiv International Economic Forum (KIEF) themed "People. Business. Economy. What's Next?" in Kyiv on Monday, as reported by an Interfax-Ukraine correspondent.
He emphasized that workers currently in the energy sector or the defense-industrial complex have nothing to worry about, as over 90-95% will be re-reserved.
"However, creating a large number of enterprises, whether IT or conditionally defense industry, where three drones are made and hundreds of people are reserved – I am conditionally simplifying, hyperbolizing in a certain sense, but that is how it is. And there are very many such cases. Contracting organizations. And it grows, grows, grows," he added.
According to the Prime Minister, changing the rules is designed, on the one hand, to cut down on unfair reservations without letting the economy collapse, and on the other hand, to give active military personnel a clear understanding regarding rotations.
"To say that these mobilization and reservation rules will produce a super-effect – no, there is no such thing, but we are at least stopping the endless growth of sometimes unfairly reserved individuals. And now, most importantly, what I am appealing to enterprises, business, and the economic sector about: we need to jointly come up with a new social model where, even if everyone is reserved, enterprises provide predictable mobilization of people into the army. This is an idealistic model. If such a solution could be found, the need to search for people on the streets would disappear. And if a business, entrepreneur, manager, or head takes on such a commitment – then nothing else is needed at all, this is a new social contract. But not thinking about it, not preparing for it, is a super-strategic mistake," Koretsky stated.
He stressed that failing to prepare in advance for a potential tightening of mobilization in Russia, which could reach 300,000–500,000 troops, would mean being forced to make unpopular decisions in manual mode once again.
"Then it won't be about reservations, or percentages. The issue is the survival of the state, and therefore this must be taken into account. Seeking to increase accountability for those who hide is also on the agenda – this is all a comprehensive story. By December 1, we must deliver a new social contract," he added, announcing a meeting with businesses on this issue.
As reported, on October 23, Prime Minister Serhiy Koretsky stated that the Cabinet of Ministers had finalized changes to the reservation system – an enterprise's criticality is being separated from its economic indicators, sectoral and regional criticality criteria will be updated, and enterprises will be checked for abuses.
The second change is that the maximum reservation level, particularly for the energy sector and defense industry, will no longer be 100% (dropping to 95%). The government will not weaken the work of those manufacturing weapons or maintaining critical infrastructure, and if uninterrupted operation requires reserving more, the enterprise can submit a justified appeal to a special Coordination Center.
The third change involves the Ministry of Defense strengthening liability for draft evasion. The fourth is the preparation of a mechanism for 100% reservation provided mobilization obligations are fulfilled: an enterprise will be able to fully reserve employees if it regularly and voluntarily recruits a portion of them for military service.
The Cabinet has also initiated a review of sectoral and regional criticality criteria, taking into account new requirements within 10 days.

title: Otti rewards Abia world debate champions with N1m each
body:
Governor Alex Otti of Abia State has rewarded five students who represented Nigeria at the 2026 International Schools Debate Championship in Doha, Qatar, with N1 million each.
Mr Otti announced the rewards on Saturday at a welcome ceremony in the Michael Okpara Auditorium, Umuahia, for the contingent made up of students from Abia Model Junior Secondary School.
The team won four major awards: Best International School Debate Team, Overall Best Team in the junior category, Best Debater Award, and Best Leadership Award, alongside 12 medals for outstanding individual performances.
The governor approved the team’s request to participate in the 2027 competition, announcing financial rewards for the school and the officials who facilitated the team’s participation.
Mr Otti announced N750,000 each for three education officials involved in the students’ participation and N1 million for the Executive Chairman of the Abia State Universal Basic Education Board (ASUBEB), Lydia Onuoha.
He also approved N1.75 million for Abia Model Junior Secondary School, which produced the debating team.
Mr Otti announced another N1 million reward for Okonkwo Onyinyechi, winner of the 2026 National Essay Championship.
Mr Otti also directed the Alex Otti Foundation to sponsor 15-year-old Esther Christian, captain of the debate team, making an exception to its usual undergraduate scholarship programme.
“Because you lost your dad when you were four, today you have another dad. So, the Alex Otti Foundation takes over your sponsorship,” Mr Otti said.
The governor said that the decision was an exception to the foundation’s usual practice of supporting undergraduates.
He said the girl would be admitted into its scholarship programme before university.
Mr Otti congratulated the students and commended their coaches, school authorities and other stakeholders, urging the team to sustain its commitment to excellence.
He said that his administration was renovating public schools and improving teaching and learning facilities across the state.
The governor disclosed that the government had approved 21 smart schools, with two completed and handed over, while a third was expected before the end of the year.
He urged individuals, community leaders and other stakeholders to adopt schools in their communities to complement government efforts.
Mr Otti said the government was working to deploy armed personnel of the Homeland Security outfit to schools to protect pupils and school property.
Earlier, the Executive Secretary of the Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC), Aisha Garba, commended the state government’s investment in education.
Ms Garba, represented by the commission’s Abia Coordinator, Unyime Umoetti, urged political office holders and other stakeholders to support grassroots development by visiting their communities and adopting local schools.
She encouraged the students to remain focused and pursue greater achievements.
In her remarks, the ASUBEB chairman, Ms Onuoha, said the team won four trophies and 12 medals at the international championship, competing against teams from Jordan, Pakistan, India, Kenya and Ghana.
She said that Chukwuemeka Akamnonu won the Best Speaker Award in the final, adding that the team’s success reflected ongoing investments in school renovations, teacher training and free, compulsory basic education.
Speaking on behalf of the parents of the debate team members, Christopher Akamnonu, thanked the government for its efforts in enhancing the standard of education in the state.
Mr Akamnonu said Abia’s investment in education was transforming the school system in the state and creating opportunities for students to excel.
Speaking on behalf of the team, Miss Christian said the team competed against 84 teams and 168 debaters, with all five members ranking among the world’s top 10 speakers.
She thanked the governor, the team’s coach, Emmanuel Chigozie, and other stakeholders for supporting the team, pledging that the students would continue to strive for excellence.
The ceremony featured the presentation of certificates and trophies to the champions and education officials, as well as a demonstration of the British Parliamentary debating format by the students.
The names of the debaters are Simon Nduoma, aged 18; Chikodi Nmesooma, aged 15; Akamnonu, aged 16; and Ifeanyichukwu Cherechukwu, aged 16.

title: Sheffi Paz, prominent Tel Aviv anti-illegal immigration activist, dies at 74
body: Prominent anti-illegal immigration activist Sheffi Paz, who led protests against illegal immigration in south Tel Aviv, died at the age of 74, the Save Tel Aviv organization announced on Monday.Paz, one of the leading figures in the protest movement among residents of south Tel Aviv's older neighborhoods, devoted many years to public activism aimed at improving residents' personal safety and changing government immigration policy.Paz died following a battle with cancer. The disease was diagnosed for the fourth time over the past month, after she had previously battled cancer on three occasions.The daughter of Holocaust survivors who immigrated to Israel from Poland during her childhood, Paz began leading the public campaign against the presence of illegal migrants in south Tel Aviv in 2013. Over the years, she organized demonstrations and protests, confronted government officials and local authorities, and became one of the most recognizable figures associated with the movement.Her activism also led to confrontations with law enforcement authorities and legal proceedings. In September 2024, she was sentenced to 45 days in prison after being convicted of offenses related to her protest activities, including spraying graffiti and disturbing public order. Paz served her prison sentence and continued her public activism following her release.Held to her demands despite personal price paidIn a statement, the Save Tel Aviv organization said Paz had dedicated the final years of her life to fighting for south Tel Aviv residents and refused to abandon her demands despite the personal costs she had paid.The organization's deputy director-general, Amalia Ozer, and spokesperson, Yaakov Sela, paid tribute to her."Today we lost a courageous leader, a dear friend, and a woman who became a symbol of determination, dedication, and love for the country," they said."Sheffi dedicated her life to the residents of south Tel Aviv," the organization continued. "She was the voice of the invisible people, those who had been left behind, and proved time and again that even one person, armed with truth and faith in the justice of their cause, can shake an entire country."The organization also addressed the legal proceedings brought against Paz over the years."Sheffi sought justice for neighborhood residents and was unwilling to remain silent in the face of injustice. Even when she was persecuted, arrested, and sent to prison, she continued to stand tall."Concluding their statement, members of the organization pledged to continue the public campaign Paz had led.'Struggle is not over'"Sheffi is gone, but her struggle is not over. We pledge to follow in her footsteps, fight for south Tel Aviv, combat illegal immigration, and work until we achieve the goals to which she dedicated her life. May her memory be a blessing."Paz's close friend and the organization's deputy director-general, Amalia Ozer, spoke to Walla on Monday morning about the loss and the period she spent accompanying Paz in the hospital."It was a very rapid and unexpected downward spiral," Ozer said. "The State of Israel has lost a precious asset, someone who cared for the invisible people. I'm not sure she can be replaced."Ozer said they intended to continue Paz's work and the campaign she had led.She recounted spending nights at Paz's bedside in the hospital for a month. Although they were aware that her condition was deteriorating, they had not expected the end to come so quickly."We didn't think it would end so quickly. Who could have imagined it would be cut short so suddenly?" she said.Ozer added that the question of who would carry on the campaign had occupied them even before Paz became ill."We always talked about who would inherit the struggle. I'm the one who does all the parliamentary work, but I'm not her. Sheffi is the recognizable face of our movement.""I have never known anyone so inspiring, especially at her age," Ozer added. "A 74-year-old woman who, until her very last moment, functioned like a lioness."

title: NASS Roundup: Ebola, fuel import, unity college funding, other top Senate stories
body:
The Senate on Tuesday debated and passed for second reading a bill seeking to amend the National Senior Secondary Education Commission Act to strengthen the administration and funding of federal unity colleges and Armed Forces senior secondary schools.
The Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, announced the passage after the bill received majority support in a voice vote.
The bill was subsequently referred to the Senate Committee on Primary and Secondary Education for further legislative scrutiny and a public hearing.
Sponsored by the Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele, the bill seeks to strengthen the administration, coordination and funding of public senior secondary schools across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).
It also proposes a legal framework for direct government intervention to address infrastructure deficits and shortages of learning resources in public senior secondary schools.
The Senate on Wednesday rejected a proposal for lawmakers to visit the entry points through which a woman infected with Ebola reportedly entered Nigeria before she was isolated at a private hospital in Abuja.
Instead, the upper chamber urged the federal government to immediately release emergency funds from the Service Wide Vote to prevent the spread of the virus.
The lawmakers adopted the resolution while debating a motion on the need to enforce mandatory health screening at all international airports and other entry points to prevent the spread of Ebola and other epidemic-prone diseases.
The motion was sponsored by Francis Faduyile, the senator representing Ondo South Senatorial District.
On Wednesday, the upper chamber of the National Assembly resolved to engage the presidency on reviewing Nigeria’s Quarantine Act to bring it in line with modern public health legislation and the International Health Regulations.
Mr Akpabio directed the Senate Committee on Judiciary to liaise with the executive arm of government and relevant health agencies to develop proposals for amending the law.
He gave the directive during plenary while lawmakers debated a motion on the need to enforce mandatory health screening at all international airports and other entry points to prevent the spread of Ebola and other epidemic-prone diseases.
The Senate president said the proposed amendment should be treated as urgent to strengthen Nigeria’s public health response to the Ebola outbreak and prevent further spread of the disease.
A bill seeking to repeal and re-enact the National Universities Commission (NUC) Act to strengthen the commission’s regulatory powers and modernise university accreditation processes passed second reading in the Senate on Thursday.
The bill was subsequently referred to the Senate Committee on Tertiary Education and TETFund for further legislative scrutiny and a public hearing.
The executive-sponsored bill seeks to strengthen the NUC’s regulatory framework, promote global best practices in university education, and encourage innovation and research.
It also proposes stronger enforcement measures against universities that violate the commission’s guidelines and procedures. In addition, it seeks to reinforce the NUC’s role as the apex regulatory body responsible for accrediting academic programmes in Nigerian universities.
The Senate Committee on Public Accounts on Tuesday resolved to summon the heads of the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA), the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) and the Nigeria Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (NEITI) over discrepancies in records of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS) imports into Nigeria between 2021 and 2023.
The committee’s chairperson, Ibrahim Dankwambo, announced the resolution on Tuesday after the NMDPRA appeared before the panel to respond to queries raised in NEITI’s Oil and Gas Industry Audit Report covering the period.
Mr Dankwambo, who represents Gombe North Senatorial District, said the heads of the three agencies would be required to explain the discrepancies and work towards reconciling the conflicting figures.
On Thursday, the Senate on urged the federal government to explore appropriate budgetary provisions and international climate adaptation financing to protect coastal communities threatened by ocean surges and sea incursion.
The upper chamber also directed the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) and relevant state authorities to provide immediate humanitarian assistance, including safe water, healthcare services and temporary shelter, to residents whose homes and livelihoods have been destroyed by ocean surges.
The lawmakers adopted the resolutions during plenary while debating a motion on the urgent need to construct shoreline protection infrastructure to save Ayetoro community in Ondo State from sea incursion.
The motion was sponsored by Francis Faduyile (APC, Ondo South).

title: Australian billionaire James Packer paid firm defending Netanyahu in trial over $1.25m. - report
body: While defending Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in his criminal trial, the law firm representing him received at least US$1.25 million from James Packer, the Australian billionaire whose alleged gifts to Netanyahu form part of Case 1000, The Sydney Morning Herald reported on Monday.This has not been independently confirmed; a source familiar with Packer's financial dealings told the newspaper that the payments were for work carried out for Packer himself and were unrelated to Netanyahu's trial.The Herald report alleges that the money was paid through monthly wire transfers of USD 50,000 over the past two years, starting on September 23, 2024. It identifies the payments as transfers from the Citibank account of Packer's company, Consolidated Press International, to the account of Tel Aviv law firm Hadad Roth Shenhar at Bank Mizrahi Tefahot.The newspaper said it had not confirmed that Netanyahu benefited from the payments. A source familiar with Packer's financial dealings told the Herald that the transfers were for work Packer did, including finding investment deals in Israel, and were unrelated to Netanyahu's trial.The Herald said it later requested evidence of deals or work the firm undertook, but neither Packer nor his company had responded by publication.At the Jerusalem District Court, where hearings in the evidentiary stage are ongoing, Netanyahu's defense attorney Amit Hadad refused to address queries on the matter.פרקליטו של נתניהו, עו"ד עמית חדד, מסרב לענות אם התחקיר האוסטרלי שפורסם לפיו המיליארדר ג'יימס פאקר העביר למשרדו של חדד 50 אלף דולר כל חודש. חדד בתגובה:" נו באמת". נזכיר שנתניהו מואשם שקיבל שמפניות וסיגרים במאות אלפי שקלים מפאקר. תחקיר מטורף ושווה בדיקה של הרשויות בישראל https://t.co/DuuNv9hvW3— aviad glickman (@aviadglickman) October 26, 2026Packer declined to comment when approached by the Herald, which reported that he did not deny the payments. Hadad did not respond to the newspaper's questions.Netanyahu spokesman refuses to respond amid electionsA spokesman for Netanyahu told the newspaper: “I couldn't give a monkey's about your questions. We are very busy. We have an election on right now.”The report comes on the eve of Israeli elections, as Netanyahu's criminal trial continues.In Case 1000, Netanyahu is alleged to have received gifts from Packer and billionaire businessman Arnon Milchan. He faces a charge of fraud and breach of trust in the case. Packer is not a defendant.The critical allegation in Case 1000 is not just that Netanyahu received gifts. Prosecutors allege the gifts were provided regularly, including in response to requests and demands, until they became a “supply line.” They also allege that Netanyahu acted in Milchan's interests through his public positions while in a serious and continuing conflict of interest.Those alleged interventions concerned Milchan's US visa, a proposed extension of tax benefits for returning residents, and regulatory matters connected to a potential investment in Israeli television.Netanyahu allegedly received approximately NIS 690,000 in giftsAccording to the indictment, the gifts to Netanyahu and his wife, primarily cigars and champagne, amounted to approximately NIS 690,000. The allegations concerning Milchan cover October 2011 through December 2016, while those concerning Packer cover 2014-2016.Specifically, the indictment alleges gifts from Packer totaling NIS 229,174 - NIS 145,577 in cigars and NIS 83,597 in champagne.Hadas Klein, who worked for Milchan and Packer, was a central prosecution witness concerning the gifts and their delivery.Netanyahu's trial, which began in May 2020, concerns three cases involving alleged gifts and dealings with media owners. He faces fraud and breach-of-trust charges in all three and a bribery charge in Case 4000, concerning alleged regulatory benefits for Bezeq in exchange for intervention in Walla's news coverage. He denies wrongdoing.

title: NPP can welcome Alan Kyerematen back as a member, but not as flagbearer now – Joe Wise
body: Former First Deputy Speaker of Parliament and Chairman of the New Patriotic Party’s Disciplinary Committee, Joseph Osei-Owusu, popularly known as Joe Wise, says the party is willing to welcome former Trade Minister Alan Kyerematen back as a member but will not consider him for the flagbearer position at this stage. According to him, the NPP has already elected its flagbearer for the next general election, making it impossible for Mr Kyerematen to assume the position without going through the party’s established electoral process. He says Mr Kyerematen would, however, be welcomed if he follows the party’s procedures for members who have left and wish to return. Mr Osei-Owusu’s comments follow Mr Kyerematen’s public declaration that the only condition under which he would consider returning to the NPP is if he is offered the opportunity to lead the party as its flagbearer. Speaking to the media at the Ashanti Region NPP sensitisation programme for the constituency secretaries in Kumasi, Joe Wise described the demand as unacceptable, adding that he initially considered the former minister’s comment a joke. “The party has a channel of electing a flagbearer, and that procedure has been completed. So, if Bawumia finishes his term and Alan comes back, we will see whether he can go unopposed. But for now, I don’t think the party can accept him as flagbearer,” he said. He explained that the NPP has established procedures governing the return of former members and urged Mr Kyerematen to follow the appropriate process if he is serious about rejoining the party. Mr Osei-Owusu stressed that the NPP needs more members to strengthen its ranks, noting that Mr Kyerematen had served the party in various capacities during his time as a member. “Alan Kyerematen has duly served the party in so many ways, so if he comes, we will accept him,” he stated.
