title: SCO Economic Ambitions Outpace Agreement
body: The Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) renewed calls for a development bank at its October 20 heads of government meeting in Dushanbe, but the institution remains under negotiation more than a year after members reached political agreement on its creation. Participants adopted a joint communiqué and decisions on economic cooperation, including joint manufacturing and transportation. Financing those ambitions remains a central challenge. Members backed the bank at their September 2025 summit in Tianjin. A year later, the Bishkek summit ended without a founding agreement or capital commitments, and no launch date was set. The SCO brings together ten countries whose economic priorities differ sharply. China and India are among the world’s largest economies, while Russia and Iran face Western sanctions. For Central Asian members, the organization offers another route to investment, but agreement on shared goals has yet to produce a common financing institution. Different Priorities Tajik Prime Minister Kohir Rasulzoda reported that SCO countries accounted for 70% of Tajikistan’s foreign trade turnover in January–August 2026. Meanwhile, foreign direct investment from member states amounted to just $350 million for the whole of 2025. “These figures demonstrate the enormous untapped potential of our investment cooperation, which significantly lags behind the dynamics of trade relations,” Rasulzoda said. Iran has different concerns. First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref called for wider use of national currencies in trade, alongside export insurance and investment protection. Tehran has long sought to reduce its foreign trade dependence on Western financial infrastructure. Sanctions make this an urgent priority, but Iran’s interests in international settlements differ considerably from those of India or China, for example. Beijing and New Delhi conduct extensive trade with Western countries, so a single financial model for all SCO members is unlikely to satisfy everyone. Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin encouraged joint manufacturing projects using Russia’s special economic zones and investment protection agreements. Kyrgyzstan, meanwhile, is seeking investors for the Tamchy special investment and financial territory, established in July 2025 in the Issyk-Kul region. First Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers Daniyar Amangeldiev invited SCO partners to develop joint projects there. Financing the Bank A development bank could provide a common source of funding for such projects. In Dushanbe, Belarusian Prime Minister Alexander Turchin renewed calls to accelerate its establishment. “We consider it fundamentally important that this institution become a multilateral development bank with a unique mandate, providing access to long-term investment financing without political conditions,” he said. Kyrgyzstan also supported establishing the bank. Amangeldiev urged members to draw on existing financing channels, including the SCO Interbank Consortium, while negotiations continue. Kazakh Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov confirmed Astana’s willingness to host the bank’s headquarters. Bishkek had already put forward its candidacy at the September summit. Choosing a headquarters is only part of the task. Members must agree on their financial contributions and how the bank will operate, including who decides which projects receive loans. China has far greater financial resources than most of its SCO partners, giving it the potential to become the bank’s principal source of capital. Its role in funding the institution would make the distribution of voting power particularly important. For smaller members, the terms would determine how far the bank broadens their financing options. Central Asian governments have reasons to seek a wider choice of lenders. China is already a major source of investment and credit, while Russia remains important for trade and labor migration. The region is also developing economic ties with partners outside the SCO. Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan are cultivating relations with the European Union and the U.S., as well as Turkey, the Gulf states, and international financial institutions. An SCO bank would enter a region where governments already have competing offers and their own investment priorities. Why the SCO Is Not Becoming an Economic Union The difficulty of establishing the bank reflects the limits of the SCO as an economic institution. Over a quarter of a century, it has built an extensive system of meetings and agreements, but it has no single market or common customs territory. The organization emerged out of security cooperation. Unlike the European Union, its members have not transferred authority over economic policy to supranational institutions. All major decisions are made by consensus. This principle allows every member’s position to be taken into account, including those of smaller states. But serious disagreements can also stall decisions. Political tensions also persist among SCO members. India and Pakistan have a long history of conflict, while India and China have unresolved border disputes. Sanctions on Russia and Iran affect their foreign trade and banking operations, while Central Asian countries are pursuing their own multi-vector foreign policies. Joint projects can still proceed without agreement across the entire organization. A railway or industrial facility needs an arrangement among the participating countries and their financiers, rather than approval from every SCO member. Such arrangements can deliver investment, but they leave the SCO primarily as a forum for negotiations. A development bank would give it a more direct role in financing projects across its membership. For now, political support for the bank has yet to translate into an agreed institution. How much members will contribute, and what influence those contributions will confer, remain central questions.

title: Middlemen making local chicken more expensive than imported ones – Deputy Agric Minister, Dumelo
body: Deputy Minister of Agriculture John Dumelo has blamed middlemen for the high cost of locally produced poultry, warning that their pricing practices make imported chicken cheaper than Ghanaian poultry products. He said intermediaries often buy poultry from farmers at relatively low prices but sell it to consumers at significantly higher prices, making it difficult for Ghanaians to afford locally produced chicken. Speaking on behalf of the government at a poultry round-table discussion in Accra on Monday, October 26, 2026, with the Netherlands, Mr Dumelo said the situation was undermining efforts to strengthen Ghana’s poultry industry. He explained that consumers’ inability to buy directly from farmers was driving up prices for locally produced poultry, putting domestic producers at a disadvantage against imported products. “One thing that is of concern to me is the cost of producing poultry. If you look at the cost of production, the number of middlemen that carry it to the consumer, so yes, even though the farmer sells at affordable prices, maybe GHC80 before it gets to the final consumer, it is around GHC 200, and so let’s look at it,” he noted. According to him, the price disparity risks discouraging consumers from buying Ghanaian poultry, even as the government seeks to increase local production and reduce dependence on imports. Mr Dumelo said the Ministry of Agriculture was taking the poultry sector seriously, particularly in view of the data highlighting Ghana’s reliance on imported chicken. “We are taking the poultry sector very seriously,” he said. His comments follow concerns raised by the Netherlands Ambassador to Ghana, H.E. Hans Akerboom, who disclosed that about 80 per cent of Ghana’s poultry supply was imported. The Ambassador also revealed that Ghana imported poultry worth approximately €18 million from the Netherlands alone in 2024, in addition to supplies from countries such as Belgium, the United States and Brazil. The figures have highlighted the need for stronger local production, improved market access and collaboration between government and private-sector stakeholders. Deputy Agric Minister John Dumelo and Hans Akerboom, Ambassador-designate of the Netherlands to Ghana, signed an MoU on partnership in the sector As part of efforts to address the challenges facing the industry, Mr Dumelo and Mr Akerboom signed a memorandum of understanding to strengthen cooperation in the poultry sector. The agreement is expected to provide a framework for closer collaboration between Ghana and the Netherlands to support the development of the industry. The Netherlands has pledged to support Ghana through technical expertise, knowledge exchange, innovation and investment. H.E. Akerboom said the partnership would seek to create conditions for Ghanaian poultry farmers to expand their businesses, supply the domestic market consistently and benefit from existing demand. He said the Netherlands’ experience in developing its poultry industry through sustained investment in knowledge and innovation could provide useful lessons for Ghana. The partnership also aligns with the government’s Feed Ghana programme and its 24-hour economy initiative, which are intended to create opportunities for agricultural production and business growth.

title: NovaPay Invest to acquire 100% of BTA Bank
body:
NovaPay Invest LLC, established by Nova Group and Nova Poshta owners Vyacheslav Klimov and Volodymyr Popereshniuk together with Supervisory Board Chairman Taras Kyrychenko, has notified the National Securities and Stock Market Commission (NSSMC) and BTA Bank of its intention to acquire 100% of the bank's shares.
According to a notice from NovaPay Invest published in the National Securities and Stock Market Commission's disclosure system on Friday, the company intends to acquire 20 million registered ordinary shares of BTA Bank, representing 100% of the total number of its ordinary shares.
As of the date of the notice, NovaPay and its affiliates do not own any shares in BTA Bank.
As reported, NovaPay filed an application with the Antimonopoly Committee of Ukraine (AMCU) on June 24 seeking preliminary conclusions on whether it needed to obtain permission to acquire control of BTA Bank.
The company's press service declined to comment to Interfax-Ukraine on the preliminary conclusions issued by the AMCU.
As of early 2026, BTA Bank was 100% owned by Kenes Rakishev, a citizen of Kazakhstan. According to the National Bank of Ukraine, as of September 1, 2026, the financial institution ranked last, 59th, among Ukrainian banks by total assets, at UAH 338.49 million. The bank posted a profit of UAH 1 million in the first eight months of the year.
Klimov, Popereshniuk and Kyrychenko, who headed Pravex Bank for a long time, each hold a 33.33% stake in NovaPay Invest.
The founders of Nova Group, which is represented in the financial sector by NovaPay, announced plans to enter the banking market in March this year.
In June, Ekonomichna Pravda reported that Nova had signed a memorandum with BTA Bank on the future acquisition of the institution and the establishment of a financial inclusion bank on its basis.

title: APC defends Tinubu’s poverty claim, blames PDP’s 16 years in power
body:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) has defended President Bola Tinubu’s claim that opposition politicians caused the hunger and poverty confronting Nigerians, blaming previous administrations, particularly the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), for failing to address the country’s longstanding economic problems.
The party’s National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka, said the foundations of Nigeria’s current poverty crisis were laid before Mr Tinubu assumed office in May 2023, arguing that former leaders should not portray the hardship as a problem that emerged under the current administration.
Mr Morka spoke on Monday during an appearance on News Central Television’s Breakfast Central programme, where he responded to questions about Mr Tinubu’s remarks at the APC’s 2027 presidential campaign flag-off in Kaduna on Saturday.
At the rally, Mr Tinubu accused opposition politicians of creating hunger and poverty, insisting that his administration was working to eradicate both problems.
“I have heard the opposition talking about hunger and poverty. Who created them? They did. They created the hunger; they created the poverty. We are trying to eradicate it,” the president said.
Defending the statement, Mr Morka said former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, now an opposition figure, had been part of a political establishment that governed Nigeria for 16 years under the PDP between 1999 and 2015 but failed to eliminate poverty.
“Poverty has been with us. As a matter of fact, the foundations for the endemic poverty we’re dealing with today were laid in that era,” he said.
He argued that Atiku, who served as vice president from 1999 to 2007, should explain why successive administrations failed to address poverty before criticising the current government over the economic hardship Nigerians are experiencing.
Mr Morka maintained that Mr Tinubu was referring to the historical roots of poverty rather than suggesting that the current administration had no responsibility for the conditions Nigerians face today.
However, the defence comes amid persistent concerns about the cost of living, declining purchasing power and the impact of the Tinubu administration’s economic reforms on households.
The World Bank estimated that 69.6 per cent of Nigerians lived below the lower-middle-income poverty line of $4.20 a day in 2025, while 50.8 per cent, or about 123 million people, were living in extreme poverty. The figures underscore the scale of the challenge facing the government, even as it argues that its reforms are necessary to stabilise the economy.
Mr Morka disputed the way poverty figures are sometimes presented in public discussions, arguing that currency depreciation and changes in the exchange-rate system must be considered when assessing incomes and living standards.
He said the government’s decision to harmonise the exchange rate was intended to correct distortions in the economy and that assessing the policy only through its immediate effects on purchasing power would give an incomplete picture.
The APC spokesperson acknowledged that the reforms had reduced Nigerians’ purchasing power and contributed to the high cost of living but argued that the government had little alternative to addressing what he described as deep-rooted economic distortions.
He also defended the removal of petrol subsidy, saying the policy was necessary to reduce the burden on public finances and end a system that successive governments had struggled to reform.
Mr Morka argued that the government should be assessed not only by whether Nigerians have immediately felt improvements in their living conditions but also by whether its policies are producing measurable progress towards economic recovery.
He said economic transformation could not be achieved overnight, citing countries such as China, Malaysia and Singapore as examples of economies whose development took time.
“We didn’t tell you we had a magic wand to correct Nigeria’s generational problems in one day or in two weeks or in one year,” he said.
According to him, the Tinubu administration has introduced several measures to cushion the effects of its reforms, including cash transfers to vulnerable households and initiatives aimed at reducing transportation costs and improving access to financing.
He said the government was not denying the hardship caused by the reforms but argued that the effects of removing long-standing economic support systems would inevitably be felt by households.
Mr Morka also defended the administration’s electricity-sector reforms, saying the changes had empowered states and other actors to develop power-generation capacity, although the results would take time to materialise.
He maintained that the reforms would eventually improve electricity supply and support economic growth.
The APC’s defence comes as Mr Tinubu begins his campaign for a second term amid public concerns over the cost of living and the effects of his administration’s economic policies.
While the government argues that the reforms are necessary to restore economic stability, the immediate impact on household incomes and the persistence of widespread poverty remain central issues in the debate over its economic record.
Mr Morka also defended the provision of vehicles for political campaigns by First Lady Remi Tinubu, amid the controversy surrounding the presentation of seven new Toyota Land Cruiser Prado sport utility vehicles (SUVs) to selected APC youth leaders.
The party’s National Youth Leader, Dayo Israel, had said the vehicles were intended to support election mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections, prompting criticism over the reported cost of the fleet amid the economic hardship facing Nigerians.
Responding to questions about campaign vehicles, Mr Morka argued that such provisions were part of the logistics required for electioneering and should not be interpreted as rewards for party loyalists.
“During the campaign, every campaign season, people brand vehicles to move because it’s an activity. It’s not as if they were given as a reward,” he said.
He added that vehicles provided for campaign purposes should be understood within the context of preparations for the 2027 elections.

title: Celebrations in Serbia after veteran ruler Vučić loses election to student-led protest movement
body: Serbia’s long-standing leader Aleksandar Vučić has admitted defeat to a student-led protest movement in snap parliamentary elections. Celebrations erupted as crowds descended on the centre of Belgrade, Novi Sad and other cities. The student movement was formed less than two years ago in response to a railway station disaster blamed on corruption and negligence, but fought the election with candidates from a cross-section of Serbian society. “It is clear we have lost these elections,” right-wing populist leader Vučić said as he conceded late on Sunday, citing preliminary figures that gave the students 2.2 million votes and his party 1.72 million. The students were on course to win 52.9% of the vote, according to a later projection by independent pollsters CeSID, with the highest turnout for years of 69.34%. Vučić had spent two terms as president and could not seek a third term, so was leading his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) with the aim of returning to the post of prime minister, which he left in 2017. He called the snap elections after two years of protests triggered by the collapse of a canopy in front of Novi Sad station which killed 16 people. The Student List’s lead candidate Ilija Srdanović told BBC Serbian: “This will be a free state.” He said the anti-corruption movement, which had attracted anti-government voters across Serbia, hoped to “free the country from tyranny”. There were celebrations on the streets of the city, with people dancing and chanting “victory”, cars honking, and fireworks set off. “Serbia is free,” one student told the BBC. “It’s a miracle.” During a celebration speech, Student List candidate Radomir Saicic said Serbians had shown “no obstacle was greater than their will”, Reuters reported. “No force can forever overpower a people who have decided to take their destiny into their own hands,” he added. Amid scenes of people dancing in the streets Belgrade, Selena Lebovic said the result was “really fabulous”. “We are all crying, and what to say. We couldn’t believe that it would be so easy,” she told Reuters. Vučić made his announcement at the headquarters of his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) in the capital Belgrade. The centre of Novi Sad – the northern city that triggered the student-led protests – was crowded. “Everything is going to get better now,” David Vasić, one of those celebrating, told BBC Serbian. The Student List – which has no obvious leaders and whose members are not used to politics – had attracted anti-government voters across Serbia. It decided to field candidates to the 250-member parliament from across Serbian society including doctors, actors, academics and sports personalities. The anti-corruption movement campaigned on a manifesto that included purging officials who broke rules cracking down on protesters, stopping party loyalists from leading public enterprises, and freeing the public broadcaster of political control. Vučić and the SNS party have repeatedly denied corruption. Vučić, who backed Serbia’s candidacy for the European Union while refusing to impose sanctions on Russia over its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, had pledged to increase pensions and public sector salaries, and investment in state healthcare. His defeat was welcomed by Hungary’s prime minister, Péter Magyar, who said he was delighted to hear from the Student List’s leaders “how much strength our victory in April had given them”. Magyar’s party ended 16 years of Viktor Orbán rule, while Vučić’s SNS party had been in power since 2012. European Commissioner for Enlargement Marta Kos said “a new chapter can begin for Serbia. The door to the EU is open, and we are ready to move forward together”. Earlier in the day, long queues were seen outside polling stations in cities and towns across Serbia. This was also the case outside booths in a number of countries with sizeable Serbian communities – including Slovenia’s capital Ljubljana, Germany’s Munich, and Los Angeles and Chicago in the US. In France, Serbian voters waited in line in heavy rain in Paris. The election was held amid high tensions across Serbia, with police sealing off streets around the Republic Electoral Commission (RIK) in Belgrade. Attention will now turn to who will lead the Student List as prime minister. Presidential elections are due to take place in December, with parliament speaker Ana Brnabić currently filling the role in a caretaker capacity.

title: Slovakia opposes funding Ukrainian army with frozen Russian assets — senior Slovak MP
body:
MOSCOW, October 26. /TASS/. Slovakia considers it unacceptable to use frozen Russian assets to finance the Ukrainian army, Slovak Parliament Deputy Speaker Tibor Gaspar said in an interview with TASS.
"Regarding the issue of frozen Russian assets, Slovakia stressed the need for a thorough legal assessment, prudence, and consideration of the long-term consequences of decisions made. In November 2025, Prime Minister of the Slovak Republic Robert Fico rejected the proposal to confiscate frozen Russian assets and use them to fund Ukraine’s military needs. Such an approach [of confrontation and confiscation] is unacceptable," he said.
Fico highlighted potential legal proceedings, the risk of retaliatory measures, and the implications of such a move for future peace negotiations, Gaspar noted. "At the same time, he emphasized that using these assets for Ukraine’s post-war reconstruction could be more appropriate than directing them toward the continued financing of military operations. The Slovak Republic is interested in ensuring that any decision in this area has a clear legal basis, complies with international obligations, and reduces the risk of a further deterioration in international relations. At the same time, it is necessary to seek sustainable solutions for financing the reconstruction of Ukraine that will promote regional stability and create the conditions for achieving lasting peace," he explained.

title: Army Explains Troops Encounter With Police In Plateau
body: The Joint Task Force, Operation Enduring Peace, has explained the circumstances surrounding a viral video showing an encounter between its troops and personnel of the Nigeria Police Force in Bassa Local Government Area of Plateau State. In a statement issued on Monday, the task force said its troops responded to a distress call on October 20 over reports of sporadic gunfire in Mai Farin Moto, Maraban Dere and neighbouring communities, as well as the reported killing of a resident, Adamu Suleiman. According to the statement signed by the Media Information Officer, Chinonso Polycarp Oteh, troops of Sector 3 were deployed to assess the security situation, establish the circumstances of the incident, prevent further escalation and protect lives and property. The statement said the troops sought to engage police personnel operating in the area to clarify the situation and facilitate a coordinated security response. However, the task force regretted that the interaction was characterised by a lack of cooperation from some police personnel, despite efforts to de-escalate tensions and maintain operational discipline. It maintained that the troops’ intervention was prompted by an operational distress call and undertaken in the interest of public safety, urging the public to consider the circumstances surrounding the deployment when assessing accounts of the encounter. Operation Enduring Peace reaffirmed its commitment to professionalism, impartiality and the protection of lives and property, stressing that effective security operations depend on inter-agency cooperation, mutual respect and adherence to established procedures. It added that issues arising from the incident were being addressed through appropriate command and inter-agency channels to establish the facts, strengthen operational cohesion and prevent a recurrence. The task force also urged the public and media practitioners to verify information before publication and avoid spreading unsubstantiated accounts capable of undermining public confidence or straining relations among security agencies. It assured Plateau residents of its continued commitment to maintaining law and order, protecting innocent citizens and consolidating peace and security across its joint operations area. The post Army Explains Troops Encounter With Police In Plateau appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Health Ministry opens recruitment portal for 36th batch of medical officers and dentists
body: The Ministry of Health has announced that it will open its recruitment portal on Tuesday, October 27, for the 36th batch of medical officers and dentists who have completed their house jobs and been verified by the Medical and Dental Council. According to a notice issued by the ministry on October 25, the recruitment exercise is intended to fill staffing gaps in health facilities across the country. The portal will open at 10 am on Tuesday, with qualified applicants required to submit their applications by Thursday, October 29. In the notice, the ministry said the exercise was open to members of the 36th batch who had completed their house jobs and received verification from the Medical and Dental Council. “Qualified applicants are requested to formally apply on the Ministry of Health online application portal by logging on to https://mohrecruitment.com and following the instructions to select their preferred districts and agencies,” the statement said. Applicants are expected to use the online platform to submit their details and indicate their preferred districts and agencies as part of the recruitment process. The ministry has urged applicants to remain alert to individuals who may attempt to exploit the recruitment exercise by promising to secure placements in exchange for money. It said that the process would be transparent and warned prospective applicants against paying anyone for assistance. “Kindly be informed that the recruitment process remains transparent.” “The Ministry of Health advises all applicants NOT to make any payment for this process,” the statement stated.

title: Algerian upper house of parliament approves troop deployment to Niger
body:
Algeria’s upper house of parliament has approved deploying troops to Niger to protect its energy facilities.
The country’s Council of Nations approved the deployment during an emergency session on Sunday, while the lower house is expected to hold a session on Monday.
If the deployment is approved in the lower parliament, it means the country is highly likely to deploy troops to protect its facilities located along the border area in the north of Niger, particularly the Kafra oil region and other energy facilities linked to Algeria’s state-owned energy company Sonatrach.
If approved, it would also be the first mission outside Algeria’s borders since the 1973 War between Israel and several Arab countries.
The vote came after Niger’s Defence Minister, Salifou Modi, visited Algeria. Mr Modi met with Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune and the Chief of Staff of the People’s National Army, Said Chanegriha, last week. Both countries signed a military cooperation protocol during the meeting. But the details of the cooperation were not made public.
Mr Tebboune had also earlier disclosed that Algeria sent fighter jets to Niger in late August to help thwart a “coup attempt” that shook the capital, Niamey.
The Algerian Ministry of Defence previously said it had sent four jets to Niger following the unrest. It said two patrols of four Sukhoi Su-30 aircraft had landed at Niamey airport, accompanied by an air-to-air refuelling plane.
The ministry said the warplanes were deployed at the request of Nigerien authorities on “a mission to support the Nigerien army in confronting an attempt to destabilise the brotherly state of Niger.”
Niger’s defence minister, Salifou Mody, said a group of soldiers, in August, detained some of their comrades and opened fire at “certain sensitive sites” in the capital.
Fighting between the group and Niger forces lasted for several hours, during which the state broadcaster was temporarily taken off air, while gunfire and explosions were reported around the airport and presidential palace.
Niger faces persistent attacks by armed groups, including in areas near the border with Algeria.
The country has also grown increasingly isolated since the democratic government was overthrown in 2023. The military junta cut off relations with France, leading to the complete withdrawal of French and US troops.
It withdrew from the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) in 2025, alongside Burkina Faso and Mali.
This vacuum has forced Niger to seek alternative regional and Western allies.

title: Plateau motorcycle rider killed, mutilated body found
body: By Golok Nanmwa A motorcycle rider has been killed by unknown assailants, with his mutilated body reportedly discovered along Longvel Road in Shendam Local Government Area of Plateau State. The victim’s motorcycle was also reportedly stolen, while the circumstances surrounding the killing remained unclear as of the time of filing this report. A resident of the community, Henry Homsuk, told newsmen that “Residents woke up on Monday to the disturbing news of the incident.” “It is sad that someone would be killed and his motorcycle carted away. We woke up to the news this morning, and it was disturbing,” Homsuk said. “It is painful that somebody would lose his life in such circumstances. We are worried about what happened and hope the authorities will take the matter seriously,” he added. ” The issue has been reported to security operatives,” he added “We appeal to the security agencies to investigate this matter thoroughly and ensure that those responsible are arrested.” ” People should be able to go about their lawful activities without fear,” Homsuk said. “Security should be strengthened along Longvel Road and in other vulnerable communities to protect lives and property and prevent a recurrence,” he added. Efforts to reach security operatives for confirmation of the incident were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. The post Plateau motorcycle rider killed, mutilated body found appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: National Bank of Kazakhstan Cuts Base Rate to 15.75%
body: The National Bank of Kazakhstan cut its base interest rate from 16.25% to 15.75% on October 23, marking its fourth consecutive reduction since June 2026. The central bank has indicated that it may keep the rate unchanged through the end of the year, despite a continued slowdown in inflation.Annual inflation declined to 9.3% in September from 9.8% in August, while households’ inflation expectations fell from 12.1% to 11.8%. According to the National Bank, a stronger tenge and relatively tight monetary policy helped slow price increases. Food inflation declined to 8.5%, while non-food inflation fell to 11%. The base rate had remained at 18% since October 2025. It was lowered to 17% in June 2026, 16.75% in July, and 16.25% in September. The cuts have lowered the base rate by 2.25 percentage points. The base rate influences bank lending costs and deposit yields. Lowering it creates conditions for a gradual reduction in borrowing costs for businesses and households, although commercial banks set their own interest rates based on borrowers’ credit risks and funding costs. Nevertheless, borrowing costs remain high, reflecting the challenges facing Kazakhstan’s economy. Inflation is still almost twice the central bank’s 5% target, meaning prices continue to rise rapidly, even as the pace of increase slows. Meanwhile, strong economic growth has brought limited relief to households: official figures show that real per capita incomes increased by just 0.7% year-on-year in the second quarter. National Bank Governor Timur Suleimenov said that further rate cuts will require a more sustained slowdown in inflation. The central bank identifies rising global energy and food prices, high government spending, and potential increases in regulated utility tariffs among the main risks. Annual inflation could rise slightly toward the end of the year because current prices will be compared with those recorded when Kazakhstan restricted utility tariff increases, from October 2025 to March 2026. However, the National Bank intends to focus primarily on how tariff changes affect other prices rather than responding to the tariff increases themselves. Kazakhstan’s gross domestic product grew by 4.2% in January–September 2026, driven mainly by construction, manufacturing, and transportation. Fixed capital investment increased by 7%, while investment in the non-resource sector, excluding budget funds, rose by 25%. Strong investment activity supports domestic demand while also complicating efforts to bring inflation under control. The National Bank aims to reduce inflation to 6.5–8.5% in 2027 and reach its 5% target in 2028. The next base rate decision is scheduled for December 4.

title: Two Black Bombers reach semifinals at IBA Africa Boxing Championships
body: Ghana’s Amadu Mohammed and Joseph “Jaguar” Commey have secured semifinal places at the 2026 IBA Africa Elite Men’s and Women’s Boxing Championships in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo, guaranteeing themselves medals. Mohammed advanced in the featherweight division (57kg) after his quarterfinal opponent suffered an injury in the opening round, forcing the referee to stop the contest. Commey, competing in the light welterweight category (63.5kg), also progressed after securing a narrow 3-2 victory in his quarterfinal bout. Their victories mean both boxers are assured of at least bronze medals, with the pair now targeting places in the final as Ghana seeks further success at the continental competition. The progress of the two Black Bombers provides a positive start for Ghana at the championships, which have attracted a record 171 boxers, comprising 132 men and 39 women. The competition is taking place in Kinshasa, which also hosted the 2024 edition, when 148 boxers participated. The latest turnout represents the highest participation in the history of the Africa Elite Championships.

title: US forces ready to launch new strikes on Iran within 96 hours of Trump’s order — CNN
body:
NEW YORK, October 26. /TASS/. US forces in the Middle East could launch new, potentially large-scale operations against Iran within 96 hours of an order from US President Donald Trump, CNN reported, citing two US officials.
According to the broadcaster, sufficient forces have already been deployed in the region to conduct such attacks. The officials said the operations could go beyond the limited strikes on radars, launchers and other Iranian facilities that can be quickly restored, which the United States has conducted since suspending full-scale hostilities earlier this year. They stressed that the question was not whether an order would be issued, but when. The officials believe this could happen before the end of the year, but more likely after the US midterm elections, although Trump has not made a final decision.
CNN noted that the US Central Command and the Pentagon have already drawn up an extensive list of targets, including Iranian energy infrastructure, military facilities and nuclear sites. According to US intelligence assessments, Iran and Houthi rebels from Yemen’s Ansar Allah movement would likely respond immediately to any strike by attacking US troops and facilities both in the region and beyond.
The US and Israel launched a war against Iran on February 28. In June, Washington and Tehran signed a memorandum of understanding providing for an immediate cessation of hostilities on all fronts, including in Lebanon. However, in the early morning hours of July 8, the US resumed large-scale strikes against Iran, accusing it of violating the terms of the agreements reached on the Strait of Hormuz.
Nearly 25% of global oil trade and about 20% of global liquefied natural gas trade pass through the strait. The US administration then effectively indicated that it would stop using large-scale military force against Iran and instead seek to economically strangle the country through sanctions.

title: Ukraine proposes new pathway to attract foreign workers to address labor shortages
body:
Ukraine’s government has proposed a new mechanism to attract foreign professionals and skilled workers in sectors facing labor shortages — in a bid to help employers fill vacancies and support the economy amid Russia's ongoing invasion.
The draft resolution, published by the Economy Ministry, would establish an annual list of in-demand professions and standardize the assessment of foreign applicants’ qualifications. The proposal is not yet in effect, and its provisions could change.
The plan could help Ukrainian businesses fill critical jobs needed to keep the economy running during war by making it easier to recruit qualified workers from abroad. While still in its early stages, its effectiveness will depend on which jobs are available, how easy the application process is, and whether Ukraine can realistically attract foreign professionals despite the security risks.
The State Employment Service would compile the list each year, drawing on information from employers, government agencies, and regional employment centers. Employers would be able to report their staffing needs by Oct. 1, with the proposed list published by Dec. 31.
Foreign applicants would need to demonstrate their education and work experience and provide an employment contract, job offer, or other evidence of an employment arrangement in Ukraine.
Volodymyr Landa, who has led investment screening at the Economic Security Council of Ukraine since September 2025, welcomed the government’s recognition that foreign recruitment may be necessary to address labor shortages.
"Ukraine is not the number one destination for international labor migration, so we need to make this journey as simple and clear as possible," he said.
But Landa said the draft leaves practical barriers unresolved. He sees it as excessive bureaucracy, including document translation requirements, and the potential need to use the government online platform Diia.
He also questioned how foreign professionals would find vacancies and navigate the recruitment process, noting that the proposal focuses on submitting documents rather than attracting candidates in the first place.
Further changes would be needed to connect international professionals with Ukrainian employers and reduce administrative barriers, he said.
The government's plan includes running a pilot project during martial law while the war continues, for three months after it ends or is lifted, and a maximum of two years from the resolution’s entry into effect.

title: Daily Insight for CEOs: The CEO’s role in Reviewing Organisational Performance
body: By Ernest De-Graft Egyir Insight. Performance reviews are most valuable when they help leaders understand why results occurred and what must change to improve future performance. As the year approaches its final weeks, CEOs must examine financial outcomes, operational effectiveness, customer satisfaction, employee performance, and progress against strategic objectives. The purpose is not simply to identify what went wrong. It is to recognize what worked, understand performance gaps, and take corrective action while there is still time to influence year-end results. Key Strategies: Compare actual results with strategic objectives and approved targets. Identify the main drivers of strong and weak performance. Examine operational bottlenecks and unresolved execution gaps. Assign clear ownership for corrective actions. Apply lessons from current performance to 2027 planning. CEO Leadership Actions. Review the organization’s performance against its most important year-end targets. Require executives to explain significant variances and propose practical corrective actions. Track agreed actions through to completion. Actionable Tip. Ask each executive to identify one result that exceeded expectations, one significant performance gap, and one action that could improve results before December 31. Why This Matters? A disciplined performance review converts information into action. It helps the CEO address problems before they become more costly, reinforce practices that deliver value, and make better-informed decisions about the year ahead. About the Author. Ernest De-Graft Egyir, CEO advisor, Thought Leader and Founding CEO of Chief Executives Network Ghana, convenes the Ghana CEO Summit and served on Ghana’s Economic Dialogue Planning Committee.

title: Access Holdings Has Built Scale: Now Comes The Test Of Creating Value
body: After two decades of acquisition-led growth, one of Africa’s most widely spread banking groups has made returns, not reach, its measure of success. The early numbers are encouraging. The real test is whether the discipline lasts. For most of its history, Access Bank measured progress by size. Acquisitions, entry into new markets, repeated capital raises and steady diversification turned a mid-sized Nigerian lender into one of Africa’s most extensive financial services groups, with total assets of ₦51.56 trillion at the end of 2025. That strategy worked. But it has limits. Beyond a certain point, getting bigger stops being the best measure of a business, and does not necessarily translate into stronger returns Access Holdings appears to have reached that point. More notably, it has said so itself. The Group now describes its strategy as a move “from scale to value,” and management has told shareholders that its central aim is to deliver stronger earnings per share and generate returns on equity that consistently exceed the cost of capital. After a period of heavy acquisition activity, the stated priority is to get more from the businesses it already owns. That is the right ambition. Whether the Group can deliver it consistently is what will determine how investors value it over the next few years. Why size alone is no longer enough Scale matters in banking. A larger bank attracts more deposits, can serve bigger corporate clients, can spread the cost of technology and compliance across more customers, and is less exposed to any single economy. But scale has costs, and they tend to arrive later than the benefits. Every acquisition brings new systems, staff, regulators, and risks. Every new country demands management time and capital. A bigger balance sheet produces more income, but also more credit exposure, larger funding needs, and heavier capital requirements. During rapid expansion, these costs are easy to miss. Assets, deposits, and customer numbers keep rising, and the headline story is one of success, even where parts of the business earn less than the capital they consume. Access Holdings’ 2025 results show both sides of this picture. Group profit before tax passed ₦1 trillion, and the cost-to-income ratio improved from 56.7% to 51.7%, a sign that the enlarged group is starting to run more efficiently. Yet return on average equity fell from 21.6% to 18.4%, reflecting higher impairment charges during the year, as the Group accelerated provisions on legacy loans and on exposures previously covered by regulatory forbearance. Addressing these credit exposures, through appropriate provisioning, rather than carrying them forward, is the kind of decision that tends to pay off later. A cleaner balance sheet is a stronger base for the next phase than a flattering short-term profit figure. It also makes clear that future growth must come from better returns, not wider reach. Every subsidiary needs a clear job Access Holdings operates in markets with very different economies, competitors, and regulators. Some of its subsidiaries are mature and highly profitable. Others are newly acquired, being restructured, or still building a customer base. Holding them all to the same short-term targets would be a mistake. An established bank, a recently acquired franchise, and a young payments business are at different stages and should be judged accordingly. But those differences must have limits. Each significant subsidiary should have a clear economic purpose, a target return, and a timetable for reaching it. Where a business falls short, investors should be able to tell whether the cause is temporary, such as currency weakness or a one-off clean-up, or structural. There is early evidence that the approach can work. Pre-tax profit from the Group’s subsidiaries elsewhere in Africa grew double-digit to about N284 billion in 2025 from ₦201 billion in the previous year, with Access Bank DR Congo alone doubling its net profit. Operations outside Nigeria now account for close to half of the Group’s pre-tax profit by segment. The same discipline has to apply in the other direction. Where a business cannot reach acceptable returns within a reasonable period, the options should include restructuring it, bringing in partners, or reducing exposure. The goal is not to abandon every subsidiary that is struggling. It is to ensure that every naira of capital has a clear commercial reason to be where it is. Nigeria: the biggest opportunity is at home Nigeria remains the core of the Group, and it is where the most work remains. Pre-tax profit from the Nigerian business increased year on year by 8% in 2025, despite higher provisions and pressure on interest margins, which weighed on earnings. The answer is unlikely to be another large acquisition or a wave of new branches. It is more likely to come from deepening existing customer relationships. For individuals, that means bringing salary payments, savings, transfers, cards, and credit into one relationship. For businesses, it means handling collections, payroll, supplier payments, trade finance, and cash management. The more of a customer’s financial life a bank handles, the more stable and recurring its income becomes. The Group’s non-banking businesses strengthen this case. Access Pensions, Access Insurance Brokers, and Hydrogen Payments provide the opportunities to grow fee-based income, while Oxygen X Finance focuses on digital consumer lending. Together, these businesses can broaden the Group’s earnings base, deepen customer relationships, and support stronger returns. The economics still have to add up. Adding customers creates little value if serving them costs more than they bring in. Growing the loan book does little for profitability if credit losses and funding costs absorb the margin. The Nigerian business is where investors will see most clearly whether the strategy is working. Making the international network pay The Group’s international footprint is a genuine strategic asset. A Nigerian company that imports equipment, exports goods, or expands into other African countries needs banking services in several markets at once. A group present in those markets, and in financial centres such as London, can build deeper relationships and earn income from trade finance, payments, and foreign exchange. Presence alone, however, does not guarantee returns. Some international subsidiaries add to the Group’s reach and reputation, while earning modest profits. That can be justified for a period where the long-term opportunity is clear, but investors should be able to see the reasoning and the timetable. Currency movements add a further layer of risk: gains earned in local currencies can shrink when translated into naira, as the Group’s 2025 accounts showed. A diversified group creates value when its businesses, taken together, produce stronger and steadier earnings than they would on their own. Owning banks in many countries does not prove that. Consistent results do. How investors can assess progress For shareholders, the move from scale to value means using a different scorecard. Assets, customer numbers, and country count matter less. Profitability, efficiency, asset quality, and return on capital matter more. Over the next two to three years, a credible delivery of this strategy will show: return on equity held consistently above the cost of equity; further improvement in the cost-to-income ratio; loan-loss charges returning to normal levels once the legacy clean-up is complete; a rising share of earnings from fee-based and non-bank businesses; clear disclosure of returns by subsidiary and by region; and improved capacity for sustainable shareholder distributions from subsidiaries to the holding company, and from the holding company to shareholders. That last point deserves attention. Consolidated profit and cash available to shareholders are not the same thing. Subsidiaries often have to retain capital for regulatory or commercial reasons, which limits what they can pass up to the parent. Access Holdings did not declare dividends for FY2025 amid outstanding regulatory requirements, and its Board has said the decision does not reflect weaker performance and that payments could resume once those conditions are met. How quickly that happens will be an important indicator of progress in restoring dividend capacity. More broadly, the holding company must show that capital retained in a subsidiary earns more there than it would elsewhere in the Group. The clearer the link between each business and the Group’s overall returns, the stronger the investment case becomes. The harder phase Access has shown that it can build. Running a large multinational portfolio well is a different skill. Acquisitions and market entries come with visible milestones. Strong returns, efficient use of capital and dependable shareholder payouts require consistent delivery, year after year. The early signs are encouraging: better efficiency, stronger profits from the African subsidiaries, a willingness to take provisions early, and a clearly stated focus on returns. They suggest that management understands the nature of the task. What remains is to sustain that discipline long enough for the results to speak for themselves. Scale has given Access Holdings a platform few African financial groups can match. The task now is to show that this platform can earn returns that justify the capital, complexity, and management attention it demands.

title: Zelensky submits bills to Rada on extending martial law, mobilization for three months
body:
MOSCOW, October 26. /TASS/. Vladimir Zelensky has submitted bills to Ukraine’s Verkhovna Rada (parliament) to extend martial law and mobilization in the country for another 90 days, according to the Ukrainian parliament’s website, which published the relevant documents.
The documents will now be considered by the relevant committee before being put to a general vote by the deputies.
Martial law and general mobilization were introduced in Ukraine on February 24, 2022. This will mark the 21st extension of these measures. Due to the ongoing extensions of martial law and mobilization, Ukraine holds no parliamentary, presidential, or local elections. Meanwhile, Zelensky’s term in office officially expired on May 20, 2024.

title: Indian wins Dh5million in UAE Lottery days before his 60th birthday
body: A Sharjah resident who won Dh5 million on the UAE Lottery plans to apply for a Golden Visa after travelling the world with his wife. Kishore Pandurang Rao, an Indian who has lived in the UAE for three decades, found out he had won the prize in the October 3 draw, only days before his 60th birthday. Mr Rao said he was shocked when he realised that he had won. "I was sitting quietly and scrolling online when I received an email from The UAE Lottery. Initially I thought it was a routine verification email," he said. "I was stunned. For some time, I just sat there without knowing what to say or do." Mr Rao said his plan was to focus first on his family. "I would like to support my elder son as he explores starting his own business and support my younger son with his higher education," he said. "I also want to bring my family together in the UAE after we have spent periods living apart. My wife and I are thinking about buying a home and cars, both here and in India. "I also want to keep our family home in India, which is very important to me because it is where I grew up. These are all plans, though, and I want to do them one at a time." Dh5 million prize When most people think of the lottery they have a dream purchase lined up to treat themselves to something that would otherwise have been out of reach. Mr Rao is lining up something a little different. "I didn’t think of a watch or a luxury item. One of my long-term wishes has been to explore the possibility of getting a UAE Golden Visa," he said. "After spending around 30 years in the country, the UAE means a great deal to me, so that is something I would really like to look into. I am also considering buying a new car and eventually a home, but I haven't made those decisions yet." Mr Rao said he was determined not to make rash choices about how to spend his winnings. "It will change some of the choices available to me, but I don't want to make every decision immediately just because I have won," he said. "I have just turned 60 after spending around three decades working in the UAE, so I see this as a new stage of my life. I want to spend more time with my wife and children, support their plans, travel with my wife and enjoy experiences together that we haven't had much time for before. "For me, the biggest change is really about what comes next and how we choose to spend that time together."

title: Naval Group pitches FDI frigates to Denmark with local construction and maintenance
body: Naval Group is offering to build and maintain FDI frigates in Denmark as it seeks a role in the Royal Danish Navy’s modernisation. The French shipbuilder signed three memoranda of understanding with Danish companies on 21 October to support its proposal. The agreements cover cooperation with Copenhagen Global, Saab Danmark and SH Defence. They were signed at an industry event hosted by Naval Group in Copenhagen. Copenhagen Global will cooperate on drones, autonomous systems and military payloads, while Saab Danmark’s agreement covers communications equipment. SH Defence will work on research and development involving containerised mission modules, drone launch and recovery systems, and diving equipment. “We’ve been working with these partners for quite some time now, and globally with the Danish industry, and we are honored to involve them even more in our proposal for Denmark’s future frigates,” said Guillaume Weisrock, Naval Group’s senior vice president of sales for Europe and North America. Construction and maintenance in Denmark would depend on selection of the FDI. “We have an extensive experience of working with local industry all over the world and we will build on that experience in Denmark, should the FDI frigate be selected. With our Danish partners, Naval Group is able to build and maintain the FDI frigate in Denmark.” Naval Group said it has worked with more than 20 Danish companies over the past 15 years and maintains contacts with almost 50. It is inviting more suppliers to join the Danish proposal and participate in its wider supply chain, including maintenance and in-service support. The company cited its work with more than 75 Greek partners supplying FDI production and other programmes. That experience forms part of its case for involving Danish industry in construction and long-term support. France, Greece and Sweden have ordered a combined 13 FDI frigates. At the time of the announcement, two had been delivered, another was due within days and five were at various stages of production.

title: Drone attack damages civilian infrastructure facility in Vinnytsia
body:
Natalia Zabolotna, head of the Vinnytsia Regional Military Administration, reported this on Telegram , according to Ukrinform.
“A civilian infrastructure facility was damaged in Vinnytsia as a result of an enemy attack,” Zabolotna wrote.
According to her, all relevant services are already on the scene and are dealing with the aftermath of the attack.
According to preliminary information, there were no casualties.

title: Police detain 28-year-old for robbing POS operator at gunpoint
body:
The Police Command in Enugu State has detained a 28-year-old suspect for allegedly robbing a female Point-of-Sale (POS) operator of N200,000 at gunpoint in Obollo-Afor within Udenu Local Government Area of the state.
This is contained in a statement issued by the command’s spokesperson, SP Daniel Ndukwe, on Sunday in Enugu.
Mr Ndukwe, a superintendent of police, said that on 18 October at about 12:26 p.m., police operatives attached to Udenu Division, supported by members of the Neighbourhood Watch Group, arrested and detained the suspect.
He said the detention of the suspect followed a report that he had robbed the victim at her shop along Old Orba Road, Uhulor, Obollo-Afor, on 17 October at about 9 a.m.
“Preliminary investigations indicate that the victim raised the alarm as the suspect fled and was allegedly threatening to shoot anyone pursuing him.
“A Beretta-like pistol and an expended 9mm ammunition shell were recovered from him, while the suspect has confessed to the crime during interrogation.
“The suspect will be arraigned in court upon conclusion of investigations,” Mr Ndukwe said.
Mr Ndukwe quoted the Commissioner of Police in Enugu State, Mamman Giwa, as commending the operatives for the successful operation and acknowledged the complementary support provided by the neighbourhood watch group.
The commissioner reiterated the command’s commitment to combating crime and urged residents to promptly report suspicious activities to the police and other recognised security agencies.

title: Websites Should Be Printable
body:
If you have questions or thoughts on the post I'd love to hear about it! I'm currently looking for work in the northeastern US. I'll be graduating with a BS in both Computer Science and Cyber Operations at the end of the school year. I have worked in web application development especially, but I'm interested in any job where I get to work with well-built software. If you're curious about what I've done in the past, I keep up a short list of public projects here or contact me to give me a place to send my resume. I figure anyone who reads my posts will have an interesting offer, so all leads are appreciated!
I read a lot of printed papers these days. While I enjoy reading on a laptop as much as the next guy, marking up a printed document engages me better. Also, there's something about sitting with a whiteboard and a printed document that makes me rightly feel like I'm doing something important. So I've been thinking about how to best allow others to enjoy this medium for content that I write.
Luckily for me, printed documents were a major focus of web design a while ago. You can print any webpage you like, by hitting CTRL-P and hoping your printer driver decides to cooperate today. I tested this on my own webpage, foolishly thinking I would have a decent print job without any effort.
It wasn't great, although you can at least see all the content. The text was too big by about 2 levels, the header looks awful when printed, and my links look awfully gray in black-and-white. Totally unacceptable.
Edit 2026-10-26: I feel it's relevant to say, this has almost entirely changed already because of feedback I received from people both on lobste.rs and HN about obvious things I'd missed. I'm currently simplifying my stylesheet as much as I can. Thanks!
Luckily, the web community has had this aforementioned focus on printing documents from HTML pages. CSS has selectors to allow styling specifically printed content, and they can be useful. Here's my print-related snippet for this page now:
You can see the effects of this snippet by hitting CTRL-P or the print button on this page. Here's the functions this does for me, in order:
After attempting to optimize my website in this way, I am sympathetic for those who wouldn't prioritize printing. Hiding and showing all the right things in print took me a decent chunk of my morning. My site isn't very complex. I also doubt how many people regularly print webpages out. I might be the only one.
Still, if all your website consists of is text, allowing people to experience the text in their favorite medium is never a bad thing. The digital medium allows a lot of flexibility. The road to good software is paved with kindnesses from software engineers to their users. One day, perhaps someone shall find this kindness and smile, even if just for a fleeting moment. And that will be worth it.
Edit 2026-10-26: I was informed by a friend that this post ended up on the front page of HN and lobste.rs after I submitted it. Fun! Despite the several flaws I am now informed of in my CSS, I hope this article at least pushes a few to consider this medium more carefully. Thanks all for reading!
If you liked the above, subscribe via RSS .
If you didn't like the above, I don't know why you bothered scrolling to the footer, but I guess you can email me about it .

title: Alex Eala back on track after defeating Mika Stojsavljevic in Toray Pan Pacific Open
body: MANILA, Philippines – Alex Eala defeated Great Britain’s Mika Stojsavljevic, 6-1, 6-2, in a round-of-32 match of the Toray Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo, Japan, on Monday, October 26. The game marked Eala’s debut in the WTA 500 tournament, and also doubled as the first time the eighth seed and 17-year-old British player went head-to-head with each other. Stojsavljevic, who entered the Toray Pan Pacific Open as a wild card, stands at 6-foot-1. She towers over the 5-foot-9 Eala — with the latter commending her for her strong serves. “I think it’s a part of my style,” Eala said about her aggressive plays. “She’s a great server. I definitely think that’s one of the key points from the match today. That’s one of the things that made it a bit more difficult for me, so I’m really happy that I was able to do that.” World No. 19 Eala’s win against Stojsavljevic comes just after her round-of-16 exit at the Ningbo Open in China on October 22 at the hands of Russian player Diana Shnaider, 5-7, 4-6. Must Read Alex Eala bows out of Ningbo Open after loss vs Diana Shnaider The 21-year-old Filipina tennis ace will play against World No. 38 Talia Gibson of Australia on Wednesday, October 28, in the round of 16. – Rappler.com

title: US Consulate, Mandela Washington Fellowship alumni mentor Akwa Ibom students
body:
Secondary school students in Akwa Ibom State have received mentorship on leadership, career development and digital literacy through an initiative by the Mandela Washington Fellowship Alumni Association of Nigeria (MWFAAN), as stakeholders seek to prepare young people for responsible leadership.
The third phase of the association’s Future Forward Mentorship Programme was held on 21 October at Uyo High School, bringing together students, mentors, education stakeholders and representatives of partner organisations.
The programme, themed “Building Purpose-Driven Student Leaders,” focused on equipping students with practical skills and guidance to navigate their academic, personal and future professional lives.
Nicole Compton of the United States Consulate General in Lagos , in her opening address, commended the Akwa Ibom State Ministry of Education for supporting youth education and development.
She also praised the school’s management and MWFAAN for sustaining the mentorship initiative, calling on the students to take advantage of the opportunity by asking questions, exchanging ideas and learning actively from their mentors.
Ms Compton’s remarks highlighted the importance of engaging young people early in their development, particularly in building the confidence, knowledge and values needed to assume leadership responsibilities.
The vice-principal of Uyo High School, Emem Udofia, welcomed the organisers and commended MWFAAN for bringing what she described as an internationally benchmarked mentorship initiative directly to the students.
Susanne Ogunleye, the project’s overall coordinator, also delivered a goodwill message, encouraging the students to use the mentorship network to develop their abilities and achieve their potential.
The sessions covered inclusive leadership and civic integrity, self-confidence and effective communication, career discovery and digital literacy, as well as personal well-being and essential life skills.
The interactive format enabled students to engage directly with facilitators, reflect on their aspirations and consider practical ways to apply the lessons in school and their everyday lives.
Participants also received educational materials, including branded school bags, reusable water bottles and writing materials, to support their learning.
James Akan, MWFAAN’s publicity secretary, coordinated the event, with support from Uyi Effiom, the association’s South-east zonal coordinator.
The Future Forward Mentorship Programme is part of MWFAAN’s efforts to empower young Nigerians and nurture a generation of confident, responsible and purpose-driven leaders.
The association said the initiative seeks to provide secondary school students with the guidance and practical knowledge needed to make informed decisions about their education, personal development and future careers.

title: Serbia Releases First Footage of 203mm TSMB M-25 Heavy Mortar Firing
body:
Serbia’s Ministry of Defense has released the first publicly available footage of the 203mm TSMB M-25 heavy self-propelled mortar firing.
The video was published on October 21. Developed by Serbia’s Military Technical Institute, the TSMB M-25 draws on design solutions from the 155mm M-65 howitzer, the Yugoslav version of the American M114. It features a 203mm barrel measuring 24 calibers in length and an automated loading mechanism.
According to the ministry, the system has a stated firing range of 6–12 kilometers and can fire up to three rounds per minute. Its ammunition includes high-explosive and concrete-piercing projectiles. A standard 203mm round weighs approximately 100 kg, including 27 kg of explosives. The design also accommodates rocket-assisted ammunition and Precision Guidance Kit (PGK) systems. However, the ministry has not confirmed the firing rate achieved during testing or disclosed which ammunition was used in the footage.
Mounted on a FAP 2026 6×6 wheeled chassis, the approximately 19-tonne system features an armored cabin for a four-person crew. Its fire-control suite includes inertial navigation, a ballistic computer, communications equipment and a gunner’s computer.
The TSMB M-25 was previously presented at the Partner 2025 defense exhibition in Belgrade. The system, or a suspected 203mm self-propelled artillery platform, had reportedly been spotted locally on September 17, before its presentation.
Although the footage confirms a public firing demonstration, Serbia has released no details on the test conditions, results or operational readiness of the system.

title: Mandelblit resumes testimony as Netanyahu defense presses on investigation approvals
body: Former attorney-general Avichai Mandelblit testified Monday that police questioning of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Case 1000 went beyond the warning given at the outset, and that the warning in Case 2000 did not match the suspicions being investigated.His testimony at the Jerusalem District Court came as Netanyahu's defense continued to challenge the scope and timing of his investigation approvals. The judges also pressed Mandelblit on when he authorized questioning Netanyahu as a suspect in Case 2000, and whether an earlier decision he recalled had been documented.Mandelblit, who authorized the investigations and later approved the indictment, was called as a defense witness. His questioning by Netanyahu's lawyer, Amit Hadad, has focused on what investigators were permitted to examine and what Netanyahu was told about the suspicions against him before being questioned.Case 1000 concerns expensive gifts Netanyahu allegedly received from businessmen Arnon Milchan and James Packer, and actions he allegedly took to benefit Milchan. Hadad argued that the warning given to Netanyahu described suspicions concerning the rules on accepting gifts, rather than bribery or fraud and breach of trust.Mandelblit said that, to the best of his recollection, he had not been involved in drafting the warnings. He agreed that questioning about Netanyahu's relationship with Milchan went beyond the wording presented to him.Hadad compares language used in Case 1000, 4000Hadad also compared the language used in Cases 1000 and 4000. Mandelblit said the wording in Case 4000 was intended to preserve room to determine whether the suspicions amounted to bribery or fraud and breach of trust. Hadad challenged the consistency of that explanation with his earlier answers about Case 1000.Much of Monday's hearing concerned the decision to question Netanyahu as a suspect in Case 2000, which centers on discussions with Yediot Aharonot publisher Arnon Mozes about favorable coverage in exchange for steps against rival newspaper Israel Hayom.Mandelblit said recordings of the conversations established reasonable suspicion against Mozes, while he deliberated over Netanyahu's position. He recalled testimony from former Netanyahu chief of staff Ari Harow as a development that led him toward approving questioning of the prime minister as a suspect.The judges pressed him to distinguish that developing assessment from a formal authorization.Asked about a decision preceding January 5, 2017, Mandelblit said he could not identify documentation of it. He described discussions with other officials rather than a formally recorded decision, and agreed that the actual approval was given on January 5, the day Netanyahu was first questioned in Case 2000.Mandelblit maintains he intended to have Netanyahu questioned as suspectMandelblit nevertheless maintained that he intended to have Netanyahu questioned as a suspect, possibly as early as December 25, 2016, when arrangements for questioning in both cases were discussed. He said final approval may have awaited Mozes's questioning on January 4.Hadad argued that Netanyahu had initially been summoned without approval to question him as a suspect in Case 2000. Mandelblit rejected the suggestion that he intended Netanyahu to be questioned merely as a witness.Mandelblit also agreed that the Case 2000 warning, which referred to requesting and receiving improper benefits from businessmen in connection with his position, did not fit the suspicions in that case.Monday's exchanges followed testimony on Sunday in which Mandelblit said he had ordered police to stop wiretapping Netanyahu confidant Natan Eshel. Although investigators had obtained a court warrant, Mandelblit said the operation should have been brought to him for approval beforehand.Netanyahu's trial began in May 2020. He faces fraud and breach-of-trust charges in all three cases and a bribery charge in Case 4000, concerning alleged regulatory benefits for Bezeq in exchange for intervention in Walla's news coverage. He denies wrongdoing.

title: Military clears air on troops’ clash with police personnel in Plateau
body: The Special Task Force Operation Enduring Peace (JTF-OPEP) has cleared the air on the recent encounter between its troops and personnel of the Nigeria Police Force (NPF) in Bassa Local Government Area (LGA) of Plateau. The media officer of the operation, Capt. Polycarp Oteh, in a statement on Monday in Jos, said that the encounter between the two security agencies was misconstrued to be a clash. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that videos and photographs of an alleged clash between the military and police personnel went viral on social media a few days ago. It was alleged that troops had prevented the police personnel from going after some criminals in the area. But Oteh said that troops only responded to a distress call, following a sporadic shooting at Mai Farin Moto, Maraban Dere and adjoining communities of the area. “On Oct. 20, troops of our Sector 3 responded to a distress call reporting sporadic gunfire in Mai Farin Moto, Maraban Dere and adjoining communities. This is alongside reports of the suspected killing of a resident, Mr Adamu Suleiman. “The troops were deployed to the affected area to assess the security situation, establish the circumstances of the incident, prevent escalation and protect lives and property. “On arrival, the troops sought to engage the police personnel operating in the area to clarify the situation and facilitate a coordinated security response. “Regrettably, the interaction was characterised by a lack of cooperation from some personnel in spite of efforts to de-escalate tensions and maintain operational discipline,” he said. Oteh emphasised that troops’ intervention was prompted by an operational distress call, adding that it was undertaken in the interest of public safety. “JTF-OPEP remains committed to impartiality, professionalism and the protection of lives and property. “As a joint security arrangement, our operational effectiveness depends on inter-agency coordination, mutual respect, adherence to established procedures and unity of effort. “Issues arising from the incident are being addressed through appropriate command and inter-agency channels to establish the facts, sustain operational cohesion and prevent recurrence,” he explained. The media officer advised members of the public and reporters to verify information before going to the press, adding that such move would ensure credibility and professionalism. He assured residents of Plateau of its resolve to maintain law and order, protect innocent residents and consolidate peace and security across its joint operations area. (NAN) The post Military clears air on troops’ clash with police personnel in Plateau appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: WPL 2026/27: Police Ladies beat Jonina Ladies in Antie Aku; Samartex hold Epiphany Warriors
body: Southern Zone provided all the drama on the opening weekend of the 2026/27 GoldFields Ghana Women’s Premier League (WPL) season with three wins across five game centres. Police Ladies claimed a famous victory over Jonina Ladies in the opening weekend, recording a 2-0 away victory at the Antie Aku AstroTurf. Jane Ayieyam and Gifty Boakye were both on the scoresheet for Abu Kassim Tabasu’s side. Drama unfolded in La, where Lady Strikers came from a goal down to defeat newcomers Immigration Ladies away from home. Pearl Antwi opened the scoring for Immigration Ladies, but Bathseba Nyarko, Eunice Darkoa and Hawa Usmanu turned the fixture around for the Cape Coast-based side. At the Teshie Mats Park, Hasaacas Ladies continued their dominance over Army Ladies as they picked up a third win in their last three league meetings. Milot Pokuaa and Belinda Kpoglo scored for the Hasmal Ladies, while Zinatu Alhassan scored the consolation for the security side. Fati Ibrahim gave Oak Ladies the lead against newly promoted Rootz Sistaz but they were held to a draw as Janet Eyram Zikpui drew the home side level. In the Northern Zone, Ampem Darkoa Ladies had their game against Northern Ladies postponed as the defending league champions prepare for their WAFU B Women’s Champions League qualifier final replay against Edo Queens. Safiatu Mahamud scored a 90th-minute winner for Fosu Royal Ladies in the opening game of the season against league newcomers Ashanti Ladies. Dormaa Candy Soccer Ladies played out a goalless draw against Dreamz Ladies. Supreme Ladies and FC Savannah also ended in a goalless stalemate. Abigail Tutuwa scored a late equaliser for Prisons Ladies to earn them a point on the road against Tamale Super Ladies after Rahama Azimpaga Mohammed had given the home side the lead.

title: 2027: Minister’s son dares father over ‘federal might’ comment
body:
Marshall Ekperikpe Ekpo, who has publicly identified the Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Gas), Ekperikpe Ekpo, as his biological father, has vowed to lead what he called the “people’s might” against the combined political influence of the federal, state and local governments in the 2027 general elections.
Marshall made the declaration in a Facebook post on Saturday, directly addressing the minister amid a public dispute over their alleged biological relationship.
“The people might will be fully waiting for you,” he wrote, warning that the electorate would resist intimidation and insist on its right to determine who represents it.
“We are no longer afraid of the federal might. The days of intimidation are over,” Marshall said.
His remarks followed a political rally in Etim Ekpo, Akwa Ibom State, where PREMIUM TIMES reported that the minister declared that the federal, state and local government structures would combine their “might” ahead of the forthcoming elections.
In his Saturday post, Marshall, who, a months ago, indicated interest to represent Abak/Etim Ekpo/ Ika Federal Constituency at the House of Representatives said he would personally lead a campaign to challenge what he portrayed as the combined political power of the three tiers of government.
“It is not going to be a game as usual. This time, the people will speak, and their voice will be heard,” he wrote.
“Come 2027 general election, I will personally lead the people might. We will stand for what is right, without fear.”
He also appealed to the minister to avoid actions that could deepen political divisions within the family, calling on him not to create more enemies for his children through politics.
“Let the will of the people prevail; stop creating more enemies to your children in the name of politics,” he wrote.
The post ended with the line, “One Love is the Way Forward.”
The latest declaration comes on the heels of a controversy over Marshall’s paternity, which attracted public attention after he challenged the minister to undergo a DNA test to establish their alleged biological relationship.
