This does not mean she is not still infectious, hence the strict protocols in place,” he said. The minister commended the clinical personnel who treated the patient and public health officials who coordinated the evacuation in accordance with established public health measures. He said the government would provide further updates after the patient and her spouse had arrived safely at their destination. Pate assured Nigerians that public health measures were continuing to contain the imported virus, urging citizens to remain vigilant and obtain information from credible sources. “All public health measures are continuing to ensure successful containment of the imported virus. I urge Nigerians to remain vigilant and rely on information from credible sources,” he said. Meanwhile, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) said it was monitoring 53 primary contacts linked to the confirmed case as investigations expanded to identify people who might have been exposed to the patient at different locations. The Director-General of the agency, Dr Jide Idris, disclosed this on Sunday during a press briefing, explaining that 44 of the contacts were associated with the health facility where the patient was treated, while nine others had been identified outside the facility. Idris said the nine additional contacts included three members of the patient’s household and individuals who attended to her at an emergency room she visited before arriving at the facility where her Ebola infection was subsequently confirmed. He said the agency was extending its contact-tracing exercise beyond people who had direct contact with the patient to identify others who might have been exposed through the initial group of contacts. “As of now, we have 53 primary contacts. Of these, 44 are people from that health facility where the patient was treated,” he said. The evacuation comes as health authorities continue efforts to contain the imported infection and monitor those identified through contact tracing. Although the patient’s condition had improved before her departure, Pate warned that she might still be infectious, underscoring the need to maintain strict public health protocols.

title: U.S. Special Operations Command buys Tekever drones for intelligence and surveillance missions
body: The U.S. Special Operations Command has purchased Tekever uncrewed aerial systems following validation and acceptance testing, the company announced on October 26. Tekever withheld the number, model and specific configuration of the systems acquired. The aircraft are designed to provide intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance in demanding operational environments. Acceptance followed an extensive flight program at multiple locations, supported by dedicated training activities. “This procurement represents an important milestone in a relationship that has been built over time through rigorous testing, open dialogue and a clear focus on delivering effective capability,” said Ricardo Mendes, Tekever’s chief executive officer. “We greatly value the professionalism and engagement of the USSOCOM personnel with whom we have worked, and look forward to continuing to support their evolving requirements.” The systems combine aircraft, mission-specific payloads, communications and AI-enabled mission software within a modular architecture. Tekever said it uses flight data and user feedback to refine its products as operational needs change. The company handles engineering, manufacturing, software, artificial intelligence and operational support through a vertically integrated business model. It says this allows improvements to continue throughout the systems’ service lives. Tekever maintains a presence in Fayetteville, North Carolina, supporting its work with U.S. defense and security customers. The company described the purchase as a further step in its long-term commitment to the United States and its special operations community.

title: Israelis put voting first as overseas travel declines ahead of election, data shows
body: Israelis are postponing vacations and business trips, while others are returning from abroad to vote in Tuesday's Knesset elections, Channel 13 reported Sunday, citing Ben-Gurion Airport data that shows a significant shift in passenger traffic.The figures indicate that far fewer Israelis are leaving the country ahead of the October 27 election than in corresponding periods in previous years, while incoming passengers increasingly outnumber those departing.A comparison of airport traffic between October 17 and 27 in 2022, 2025, and 2026 points to a decline in outbound travel, suggesting that many Israelis consider the upcoming election important enough to change their travel plans.According to the Channel 13 report, approximately 245,000 passengers were recorded as departing Israel during the period under examination in 2026, compared with 270,000 in 2025, following the end of the war, and 323,000 in 2022, when Israel last held a general election.The decline is particularly notable because travelers now have access to more aircraft and flights than in previous years.Incoming passenger traffic presents a different picture. Although no large-scale airlift of special flights was organized to bring voters back to Israel, and arrivals have largely relied on existing aviation infrastructure, the number of passengers entering the country has significantly exceeded departures.According to the figures cited by Channel 13, the difference between incoming and outgoing passengers has surpassed 90,000 in 2026, compared with a gap of approximately 77,000 during the corresponding period in 2025.Entering passengers could be equivalent to two Knesset seats in electionThe growing difference could carry political significance in an election where relatively small changes in voter turnout may affect the distribution of Knesset seats.Channel 13 estimated that 90,000 people would be equivalent to approximately two Knesset seats if they were eligible voters who cast valid ballots.However, the passenger figures do not establish how many people returned specifically to vote. They also include children and foreign nationals ineligible to participate in Israeli elections.Israel's electoral threshold is 3.25% of valid votes, so small shifts in turnout could affect whether parties close to the threshold secure representation in the next Knesset.The increased interest in returning to Israel the vote aligns with a recent Fly&Vote survey, which estimated that about 67,000 Israelis living abroad intended to travel to Israel to vote. The estimate drew on registration data and a voluntary survey, not confirmed arrivals.Unlike in many other countries, most Israeli citizens living abroad cannot vote remotely and must return to Israel to cast their ballots. The Fly&Vote initiative, run by the AID Coalition, has tried to help overseas Israelis with the process, but its activities were restricted after legal proceedings initiated by Likud.Ben-Gurion's grandson returns from US to cast ballotAmong those traveling to Israel specifically to vote is Alon Ben-Gurion, grandson of Israel's first prime minister, David Ben-Gurion.Ben-Gurion arrived in Israel from the United States with his family and traveled to Tiberias to vote, according to Channel 13.His arrival illustrates the efforts some Israelis living overseas are making to participate in the election.Interest in traveling to Israel for the vote had already been evident in August, when organizers arranged dedicated flights from New York and Lisbon to accommodate demand among overseas Israelis.Under Israel's electoral system, the 120 Knesset seats are distributed proportionally among parties that cross the electoral threshold. Consequently, additional votes from returning Israelis could influence the final seat distribution, though the impact will depend on how those votes are divided among parties.

title: Iran's Baghaei says Israel's election outcome 'doesn't matter' ahead of Mecca pact meeting
body: The result of the Israeli election "doesn't matter" for Tehran, Iranian Foreign Affairs Ministry Spokesperson Esmail Baghaei claimed on Monday."I don't think there will be an election there," Baghaei said. "There, like in the movie Strangelove, there is a competition between different gangs to commit more evil; in other words, it is a competition between different people to commit more murders."He also accused Israel of carrying out a "genocide of Palestinians," and of being skilled at conducting false flag operations."The fact that the Zionist regime threatens others and uses rhetoric out of desperation is part of the evil of this regime," he claimed. "What I can assure you is that, regardless of rhetoric, we are carefully monitoring developments and our powerful armed forces will not hesitate to defend Iran's territory." Mecca pact members meeting will deal with Israel, Lebanon, US-Iran warBaghaei also said that the meeting with the Mecca pact members in Tehran would tackle issues such as Israel's 'expansionist' policies, Lebanon, and the US war with Iran."Such a meeting cannot be held without considering the consequences of the US and Zionist regime's military aggression against Iran and its consequences for the entire region," he emphasized. "This issue will definitely be one of the important topics in this meeting."

title: Bulgarian Presidential Election Exposes Split Over Ukraine War
body:
Bulgaria’s President Iliana Iotova narrowly led the first round of presidential elections Sunday, exit polls showed, in a vote held amid security concerns following a series of drone attacks on ships in the Black Sea.
Iotova, who favours dialogue with Moscow and opposes military aid to Ukraine, scored between 35 and 36.5 percent of the vote, according to three polls.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
She will face Andrey Gyurov, a banker and former caretaker prime minister backed by the pro-Western opposition who came second with between 32.2 and 32.5 percent, in the November 1 runoff.
The result was closer than expected, with surveys ahead of the vote predicting a comfortable win for Iotova.
Turnout was only around 20 percent, according to the polls.
After casting her vote, Iotova said she wanted to address “the dire issue of poverty” in the EU’s poorest member state, “alongside inequalities and regional disparities”.
“I believe that there must be peace, stability, and security,” added the 62-year-old, who has made the war in Ukraine a central theme of her campaign, promising to be a “president of peace”.
Gyurov meanwhile said he wanted “a Bulgaria that looks forward, a country that is European, free, and proud... and where the state works as it should”.
Four vessels were struck off Bulgaria’s coast this month, leaving 21 people missing, in suspected spillover from the Russia-Ukraine war.
While Prime Minister Rumen Radev said the attacks appeared to serve Russian interests and summoned the Russian ambassador, his government insists there is so far no evidence directly linking Moscow to them.
Iotova took over this year as president of Bulgaria, a European Union and NATO member state, when Radev stepped down to run in parliamentary elections.
If successful in the runoff, she would become the first woman ever elected president in the country of 6.4 million people.
A win for Iotova would be a boost for Radev, who has also called for dialogue with Moscow.
A former journalist and member of the European Parliament, Iotova was elected vice-president alongside Radev in 2016 and 2021.
Without questioning Bulgaria’s membership of the EU or NATO, she opposes military aid to Ukraine and advocates negotiations.
Gyurov, 50, has sharply criticised Radev’s foreign policy and is a strong supporter of Bulgaria’s Euro-Atlantic ties.
At his final campaign rally in Plovdiv on Wednesday, Gyurov said he wanted Bulgaria to be “a reliable ally within NATO, defending its interests through solid preparedness, strong diplomacy and clear positions”.
Parvan Simeonov, founder of polling institute Myara, said Iotova “did not step out of her presidential role” during the campaign, “which prevented her from engaging in sharper debate”.
He added that the low turnout showed “that we don’t have a problem with the polls, but with the very functioning of democracy”.
Casting his vote earlier, Radev blamed the low turnout on the “significant lead between the first and second according to surveys, which gives reassurance in one camp and perhaps a sense of doom in the other”.
Historically close to Russia, Bulgaria remains deeply divided over its relationship with Moscow.
Twenty-seven pairs of candidates for president and vice-president were competing in the first round, nearly half of them openly pro-Kremlin.
Teodor Slavev, a political analyst and programme director at the Bulgarian Institute for Legal Initiatives, told AFP the results were “a resounding electoral slap in the face for Rumen Radev’s administration and their inability to address people’s problems”.
He also said voters were giving their verdict on “Iotova’s unconvincing response regarding Russian threats in the Black Sea”.

title: Fighting intensifies as Houthis and Saudi-led coalition in Yemen report attacks
body: Fighting between the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen and the Iran-aligned Houthi rebels intensified on Monday, as escalating hostilities choked oil ⁠supplies and threatened to erupt into a broader conflict. The coalition in Yemen said it destroyed two ballistic missile launchers in the capital Sanaa , including one used to fire a missile towards Riyadh that it said had been ⁠intercepted. The Houthis later claimed they had attacked Saudi Arabia's East-West crude oil pumping stations and Riyadh airport, but there was no immediate confirmation from the kingdom. Sanaa has been under Houthi control since 2014, when the militant group seized the Yemeni capital and triggered a Saudi-led military intervention in support of Yemen’s internationally recognised government. The Houthis have fired ballistic missiles ​and drones at ⁠ Saudi airports , ports and oil installations, ‌turning the kingdom into a pressure point in the wider regional war. Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport resumed operations at two terminals on Sunday after attacks claimed by the Houthis this month killed 17 people. A strike on the airport on October 10 killed 13, making it the deadliest attack in Saudi Arabia in more than a decade. The kingdom also temporarily shut down its 1,200km East-West pipeline in September as a precaution after a drone attack that Riyadh and Baghdad said originated in Iraq. The pipeline has served as a key route for Middle East oil exports while the Strait of Hormuz has been effectively closed by the war. Meanwhile, senior officials from the Makkah pact countries, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan, are to meet Iranian officials in Tehran on Monday to discuss regional co-ordination. Saudi Arabia is represented by Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman , and Pakistan by army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir. The Turkish head of intelligence Ibrahim Kalin will also join the talks. Saudi Arabia's Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Rayed Krimly, said on X the visit was aimed at de-escalation and finding diplomatic solutions to the crises in the region. The planned discussions will be the first high-level contact between Iran and all members of the three-nation bloc since Saudi Arabia came under escalating attacks from the Houthis. يرأس صاحب السمو الملكي الأمير خالد بن سلمان بن عبدالعزيز آل سعود، وزير الدفاع، وفد المملكة للاجتماعات التي تستضيفها العاصمة الإيرانية طهران اليوم بين دول اتفاقية مكة للدفاع المشترك مع المسؤولين من الجمهورية الإسلامية الإيرانية. وذلك بمشاركة المشير/ عاصم منير، رئيس أركان الجيش… — AMB Dr. Rayed Krimly (@Rayedkrimly) October 26, 2026 Qatari media reported that a delegation from the country was in Tehran on Sunday. Greek PM visits Riyadh Saudi Arabia and Greece have pledged to strengthen security and defence co-operation and expressed concern over attacks on energy infrastructure, according to a joint statement issued after Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis visited Riyadh. Earlier, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman received Mr Mitsotakis at the Royal Court in Al Yamamah Palace, where they held talks. The two sides highlighted the importance of their strategic partnership and the implementation of joint initiatives. Bilateral trade reached about $1.7 billion in 2025, up from 2021 levels, said the statement, which was carried by the state-run Saudi Press Agency. Riyadh and Athens pledged to accelerate co-operation on a planned electricity interconnection project linking Saudi Arabia to Europe through Greece, as well as explore clean hydrogen exports from the kingdom to European markets, the statement added. The leaders stressed the need to protect international maritime routes and ensure uninterrupted energy supplies, expressing concern over attacks on energy infrastructure. The countries also committed to strengthening co-operation in defence, cyber security, counter-terrorism and the sharing of intelligence, as well as in artificial intelligence, transport, tourism, education and health.

title: EU forced to seek seat at talks on Ukraine settlement — news portal
body:
ROME, October 26. /TASS/. After years of confrontation with Russia, the European Union is now urgently seeking a way to secure a place at the negotiating table for talks on resolving the conflict in Ukraine, the Italian news portal L’AntiDiplomatico reported on Sunday.
"How has it come to pass that one of the world’s largest economic powers now finds itself having to ask for a seat at the negotiating table in a military conflict that directly affects its own security?" the portal’s columnist asked.
According to the report, Brussels has spent recent years tightening sanctions on Russia and providing military and financial assistance to Ukraine in an effort to isolate Moscow politically. Yet the EU is now being forced to "desperately seek diplomatic channels with the very government with which it had vowed never to normalize relations," the publication noted.
Politico previously reported that EU member states are concerned about their role in potential negotiations on Ukraine and are seeking a representative capable of advancing the bloc’s interests. According to The Telegraph, potential candidates include Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, Finnish President Alexander Stubb, Czech President Petr Pavel, Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store, and Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen.
Moscow has repeatedly expressed its readiness to engage in dialogue with European countries on the continent’s security architecture, taking into account the interests of all parties.
On October 22, Russian President Vladimir Putin, responding to questions from Vesti journalist Pavel Zarubin, endorsed the US position that discussions on future security guarantees for both Ukraine and Russia should also address the broader European security architecture.
Russia will closely monitor developments over the coming days, Putin added.

title: US ready to strike Iran 'within 96 hours' of Trump's order, Israel pushes for joint attack - report
body: US forces are prepared to launch a major attack against Iran "within 96 hours" of receiving the order from US President Donald Trump, two US officials told CNN on Sunday.While Trump has not made a final decision on whether to commit to major military action after the US midterms, officials said any attack that would be conducted would "be a big effort," going beyond prior US strikes against Iranian assets that can be quickly rebuilt, such as missile launchers and radars.One source briefed on the matter told CNN that Israel had been preparing for possibly striking Iran, as well as lobbying the US to participate in the strikes.However, US officials, including Trump, told Israel to hold off on attacking, likely until after the midterm elections.“The plans are ready, waiting for Trump's approval, could be after the midterms,” the source said.Iran, Houthis unlikely to preemptively strike, but ready for retaliationTwo other sources told CNN that both Iran and the Houthis were taking the possibility of renewed US attacks very seriously, according to US intelligence.Any attack launched by the US - or Israel - would trigger immediate retaliation against US personnel and facilities in the Middle East, the sources added, which is one of the reasons the US is expected to withdraw more personnel from its embassies in the region.However, one source familiar with US intelligence assessments said that officials believe that both Iran and the Houthis were unlikely to preemptively strike US or Israeli infrastructure at this stage.The White House declined to comment, while a senior Pentagon official told CNN that “The Department is a planning organization, and its job is to develop and execute military options ordered by the President.”

title: Ebola: FG confirms evacuation of Nigeria’s index patient, husband to Switzerland
body: By Chioma Obinna Nigeria’s index case of imported Ebola virus disease has been evacuated from Abuja to Switzerland after showing significant clinical improvement, the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate, has said. Pate disclosed this in a post on X, confirming that the evacuation took place earlier on Monday with his approval. He wrote, “I confirm that, with my approval, earlier this morning, the index case for Nigeria’s first imported Ebola virus disease departed Abuja for Switzerland. The index patient was clinically much improved, stable, conscious, communicating, and her clinical laboratory test results closing towards baseline. He, however, cautioned that the patient’s improved condition does not mean she is no longer infectious, stressing that strict public health protocols remain in place. “This does not mean she is not still infectious, hence the strict protocols in place,” Pate stated. The patient was evacuated alongside her spouse, who, according to the minister, has remained asymptomatic. Pate expressed appreciation to the clinical staff who cared for the patient and the public health personnel who coordinated the evacuation, commending them for ensuring that the process complied with appropriate public health measures. He said the government would provide further updates later in the afternoon after the patient and her spouse had landed safely at their destination. Reassuring Nigerians that efforts to contain the imported virus were continuing, the minister urged the public to remain vigilant and rely on credible sources of information. “All public health measures are continuing to ensure successful containment of the imported virus,” he said. The evacuation marks a further development in Nigeria’s response to the imported Ebola case, with the authorities maintaining that clinical improvement does not remove the need for strict infection prevention and control measures. The post Ebola: FG confirms evacuation of Nigeria’s index patient, husband to Switzerland appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Russia’s Yak-130M aircraft fitted with President-S130 active defense system
body:
MOSCOW, October 26. /TASS/. The Yak-130M combat training aircraft has been equipped with an active defense system against anti-aircraft missiles, which emits electronic jamming signals and releases heat decoys, Russia’s state tech corporation Rostec told reporters.
"The third Yak-130M prototype aircraft of our United Aircraft Corporation (UAC) has recently successfully completed its maiden flight. Its integration will accelerate testing of the new aircraft. The first deliveries to customers are planned as early as 2028. The aircraft is equipped with the President-S130 onboard system," the statement said.
The system operates in three stages: it automatically detects the launch of an enemy missile, instantly jams the detection and guidance systems with electronic countermeasures, and then deploys special decoys to neutralize infrared and radar homing heads.
The Yak-130M is a modernized combat trainer based on the Yak-130 aircraft, featuring improved combat capabilities. The aircraft can engage ground and air targets, including unmanned aerial vehicles.

title: Ukrainian Drone Barrage Against Voronezh Kills At Least 2
body:
At least three people were killed in a large-scale Ukrainian drone attack on the city of Voronezh in southern Russia, local authorities said early Monday, with another 29 people being reported injured.
Voronezh region Governor Alexander Gusev said air defense systems destroyed 113 drones in the skies above the region overnight. He said most unmanned aircraft were intercepted directly over the regional capital.
“Unfortunately, two people were killed,” Gusev initially wrote in a post on Telegram, identifying the victims as two men born in 1960 and 1973. At an emergency meeting later in the day, he said the death toll had risen to three people.
Gusev said most of the people wounded in the overnight attack were on a passenger train that was hit.
Falling drone debris also sparked fires at multiple industrial and commercial sites, the governor added, as well as residential buildings and a school’s sports arena.
The exiled news outlet Astra used eyewitness footage of black smoke rising over Voronezh to identify one of the targeted industrial sites as a synthetic rubber plant owned by the Sibur petrochemical corporation.
The facility makes rubber and polymers used in military aircraft tires, armored vehicles and solid rocket fuel components for Iskander ballistic missiles.
If confirmed, the strike in Voronezh would mark the third attack on a Russian synthetic rubber factory in as many days, following strikes on rubber plants in the cities of Tolyatti and Omsk this weekend.
Elsewhere, Bryansk region Governor Yegor Kovalchuk said a drone attack killed a train driver on Sunday night.
A passenger train bound from the southern resort town of Anapa to Moscow was also hit in an overnight strike, with Russian Railways reporting that at least five passengers were wounded.
Russia’s Defense Ministry said it intercepted 290 Ukrainian drones across Russia and annexed Crimea between Sunday evening and Monday morning. Civil aviation authorities temporarily suspended flights across all Moscow airports.

title: US Navy's Arleigh Burke-class destroyer starts second phase of upgrades
body:
The Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer USS Pinckney (DDG 91) has commenced the second phase of upgrades under the Destroyer Modernization 2.0 (DDG MOD 2.0) program in a Depot Modernization Period (DMP) at General Dynamics NASSCO in San Diego.
The program is focusing on the installation of the SPY-6(V)4 radar and High Efficiency Super-Capacity (HESC) air conditioning plants. The work will make USS Pinckney the first US Navy ship to receive both systems, according to the officials.
The SPY-6(V)4 radar will be integrated with the Aegis Combat System Baseline 10, while the HESC plants will support the increased electrical and cooling requirements of the ship’s upgraded combat systems.
“ The collective effort by all stakeholders has finally brought us to the point of execution. Upon Depot Modernization Period completion, USS Pinckney will rejoin the Fleet equipped with the most comprehensive multi-spectral integrated sensor suite designed to maintain maritime superiority for decades to come,” said Capt. Tim Moore , program manager for DDG MOD 2.0.
The current availability follows USS Pinckney’s completion of a 1.5 Depot Modernization Period in 2024. During that period, the destroyer became the first warship to receive the SLQ-32(V)7 Surface Electronic Warfare Improvement Program (SEWIP) system and sponson modifications.
After the 2024 modernization period, USS Pinckney deployed to the Pacific and Middle East areas of operation, where it operated with the upgraded electronic warfare capabilities before returning home.
The DDG MOD 2.0 program uses a phased installation approach known as Split Start to support learning across participating industry partners and inform subsequent modernization work.

The organization is intended to consolidate accountability for ship delivery and give leaders broader authority to accelerate the delivery of capabilities while maintaining acquisition discipline.

title: Aivs – The AI Video Studio
body:
October 25, 2026 Â· Updated October 26, 2026 Â· Andrew Arrow
Sue and Joe are stranded beside a station wagon on a desert road. Joe emerges from behind the engine. âGood news. Itâs definitely the car.â Thatâs enough for me to understand the scene. To film it, somebody still has to decide where Joe is standing, how he gets into view, and whether the camera can see him do it. Leaving those decisions to the video model can produce a man walking through a car.
AIVS is the AI video studio Iâm building around that gap. You write or import a screenplay, choose a scene, and cast its roles. The recent work gives the scene a visual plan before video generation starts: Codex designs the shots, a local image model composes their first frames, and Codex inspects those images before directing the motion. Joeâs entrance has to make sense from the picture the video model will actually receive.
The story can start in another editor. Fountain is an open screenplay format that keeps the script in readable plain text. The nyousefi/Fountain repository provides an open source implementation and a full-length Big Fish screenplay as an example. Open that file and you can read the scenes and dialogue directly, without a screenwriting app.
Choose File â Importâ¦ in AIVS to bring in a .fountain file. Scene headings, action, character cues, parentheticals, dialogue, and transitions become editable elements. Import replaces the current screenplay and clears its casting; Undo restores both. The original file stays untouched, and the imported document autosaves to screenplay.json . The importer leaves out title-page metadata, outlines, notes, omitted passages, page breaks, and emphasis formatting. Simultaneous dialogue becomes dialogue in source order.
You can keep the full screenplay in the editor and work on one scene at a time. The scene selector above Generate video lists its headings. Choose one and cast its roles; only that scene and its cast go to the generation pipeline. Uncast roles elsewhere donât block it. The 100,000-character generation limit applies to the selected scene, so a long document can stay together while you render scenes individually.
The script originally called its two people Ava and Eli, the same names as their saved character profiles. The rename to Sue and Joe made the distinction explicit. Ava belongs in the library of performers; Sue belongs in the story. Recasting Sue shouldnât require hunting through the script to replace every name.
Drag Avaâs portrait or name onto Sueâs dialogue, and every Sue cue gets that assignment. Drop Eli onto Joe, and both parts are cast. The Uncast / played by control beside a character cue also opens a picker. This diagram shows the assignments in an earlier, five-line version of the scene:
Those assignments now carry saved assets into production. Portraits guide the image model when it composes each shot. Stable identity stays separate from costume, pose, expression, and emotional delivery, which belong to the scene. A portraitâs sweater shouldnât quietly become a wardrobe requirement for every film. Generated frames still need comparison with the portraits; reference conditioning doesnât guarantee a likeness.
The screenplay supplies the storyâs meaning, emotional progression, and essential events. A shooting script works out how the audience will see them. In the saved desert-road screenplay , one sentence reads:
SUE, 30s, turns a battered postcard over in her hands. JOE, late 20s, emerges from behind the engine.
An early shooting script expands that entrance into physical staging:
SUE stands on the gravel screen left beside the front passenger door, holding a battered postcard in both hands. JOE stands on the ground screen right alongside the engine bay, empty hands clear of the engine, upper body partly screened by the raised hood. His feet and route along the near fender remain visible.
Joe has somewhere to stand and a route into view. The rest of the prompt directs his step, eyeline, and line delivery, then Sueâs almost-smile. It also supplies the quiet ending: dry wind, cooling-engine ticks, and gravel under his feet. The saved plan divides its three spoken lines into two shots totaling 21 seconds. It predates the current storyboard workflow, but it shows what the translation adds. The writer can keep âemerges from behind the engineâ in the screenplay.
The director also has to choose coverage. A reaction can carry a change in mood; a close view can make a prop legible; a cut can spare the model an awkward continuous movement. Those choices must preserve the event and its timing. Showing Sue already smiling at the opening would lose the moment when Joeâs joke almost gets through to her.
The storyboard change puts image generation between two Codex directing passes. First, Codex designs the shots and their starting compositions: who is visible, where they stand, their costumes, the light, the props, and the camera. Each shot also gets a dramatic purpose and concrete events the audience must see. A local FLUX.2 Klein model then generates one starting image per shot, using the saved cast portraits as references.
The earlier renderer carried one shotâs last frame into the next. That helped hold onto clothes and faces, but it tied the next shot to whatever composition the model happened to leave behind. Every new production shot now gets its own composed first frame, including reverse angles within the same scene. These prepared inputs from the separate production-comparison experiment show the idea: Lena as Sue in one composition, Owen as Joe in the reverse. They were prepared before the automatic storyboard stage was added.
In the second pass, Codex sees the actual generated images and writes motion, acting, camera, dialogue, and sound directions from those compositions. If a hand starts occupied, the action has to account for it. If a required prop is hidden by the crop, more motion prose wonât make that opening image suitable. The preproduction code can regenerate offending storyboards, capped at two repair rounds, and inspect the replacements before proceeding.
Python tracks source actions and dialogue lines as ordered beats, checking their coverage, exact dialogue, timing, and prompt limits. An independent source-fidelity check also reads the final motion prompts against essential actions and reveals. A beat number appearing in the plan isnât enough if the action itself disappeared during rewriting. The finalized plan is bound to the images Codex inspected, so replacing a storyboard invalidates the corresponding saved work.
The two main directing passes and their planning checks share a ten-minute Codex budget by default. Local image and video generation sit outside that budget. Completed preproduction can be reused when the scene, cast assets, format, and planning code match. Switching between HQ and distilled video inference can therefore keep the plan and starting images fixed.
Normal generation now defaults to local LTX-2.5 HQ ; Preview (distilled) uses the same storyboard workflow with faster inference. Each generation lasts four to twelve seconds. Settings offer landscape or portrait delivery, and assembly crops the modelâs output to the chosen frame rather than stretching it. Codex planning and visual review use the configured service; still-image generation and video inference run on the Mac.
The production-comparison CLI provides a separate way to compare complete candidates. Arm A uses the older continuation-based plan and local distilled model. B uses prepared first frames and local HQ, with distilled available for a controlled comparison. C sends the same controlled plan and images to the paid LTX-2.5 Pro API. Candidate numbers let the experiment keep several takes from each path.
Thatâs the beginning of a multi-model renderer. The desktop workflow currently renders each missing shot once; it doesnât automatically shop among local and cloud candidates. The comparison report leaves quality scores and winner selection unassigned for someone to watch with sound. A versus B also changes coverage and conditioning along with inference, so preferring B wouldnât establish that HQ alone caused the improvement.
Voice consistency has moved into the main workflow too. For a shot with one speaking performer, Seed-VC converts the generated soundtrack toward that performerâs saved voice sample while copying the video stream unchanged. A shot with multiple speakers keeps generated voices because it lacks isolated dialogue tracks. Conversion can affect ambience, and neither the saved sample nor an unchanged picture proves voice identity or lip synchronization.
An early render report described Joe emerging through the car without opening a door. The frame below comes from that older three-shot run. Even the requested red-rock desert became a tree-lined road. A structurally valid plan had produced the wrong scene.
The current visual reviewer receives frames sampled at four per second plus the final frame. It records what is visible, checks required actions and reveals, and distinguishes the observed ending from the planned one. A scene-level review then considers cause and effect across cuts, emotional progression, and unintended comedy. A correct final pose can still follow an impossible movement.
The renderer can use a concrete continuity problem in that observed ending to revise an upcoming shot in the same scene. For storyboard shots, that can include a regenerated first frame and a check that the adaptation preserves the source. It changes work that hasnât been rendered yet. A later prompt canât retroactively fix Joeâs earlier walk through the car.
This critic still has a narrow view of the film. Sampling can miss a brief glitch, and it doesnât establish natural motion at playback speed. The reviewer doesnât listen to the soundtrack or judge pronunciation and lip sync. The production Whisper gate from the earlier version has been removed; generated dialogue is trusted without transcription. Exact source words remain in the prompts, but the spoken performance still needs listening.
Visual findings survive in the result. The renderer distinguishes rendered-with-issues and rendered-needs-review from completion. Those findings donât trigger another video generation or prevent FFmpeg from assembling video.mp4 . The media checks establish a playable export with valid frames and timing. They leave the artistic judgment open.
I want AIVS to carry the scene through a whole film crewâs work. The screenplayâs meaning has to survive each handoff, including the quiet reaction that makes a line land. The target pipeline has seven jobs:
The director, storyboard generator, local renderer, and sampled-frame critic now have concrete implementations. The comparison tool provides a way to collect alternative takes. Automatic selection and recutting, sound refinement, and an enforced cinematic quality threshold remain work to do. Todayâs editor assembles the planned shots and final fade; it doesnât decide that a stronger reaction belongs half a second earlier.
For the desert-road scene, âfinishedâ should mean Joe enters plausibly, Sueâs almost-smile arrives after his joke, and the postcard and performers remain recognizable across the cuts. The new first frames give the director much more control over that scene. The next step is making the critic and editor use the resulting footage to earn those moments before AIVS calls the film finished.

title: Russia’s Digital Development Ministry proposes placing strategically important data centers underground or in bunkers
body: Russia’s Digital Development Ministry has approved recommendations for protecting data centers from drone attacks and other aerial threats, the Russian business daily Kommersant reported, citing a document it had reviewed. The ministry wants to divide critical data centers into three categories based on the consequences a potential attack could cause. The first category, K1, covers strategic facilities whose damage could disrupt key government functions for an hour or more. Security requirements will vary by category. For strategic facilities, the recommendations call for underground or bunker placement, Kommersant reported . The recommendations also call for reducing data centers’ visibility from the air, combining “physical reinforcement” with electronic warfare equipment and systems to counter aerial threats. The recommendations, which Kommersant reviewed, apply to data centers in Russia that are being designed, built, or already operating, regardless of ownership or operator. In October, Ukraine began striking similar facilities in Russia in response to Russian military strikes on data centers in Kyiv. Within a week, Ukrainian strikes hit three of the six data centers belonging to Yandex, in Sasovo in the Ryazan region, in Kaluga, and in Vladimir. Ukraine then struck a data center belonging to Sberbank in the Saratov region. IT market sources cited by Kommersant estimated that replacing equipment knocked out by the Ukrainian strikes on Yandex’s data centers will take up to six months. title: NAF Burns 10m Litres Fuel On 2,900 Security Missions In 11 Months
body: The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) said it consumed nearly 10 million litres of aviation fuel and recorded more than 6,100 flying hours and 2,900 sorties in support of national security operations between November 2025 and September 2026. The figures were contained in a statement issued on Sunday by the Director of Public Relations and Information, NAF, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, ahead of the first anniversary of the Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Aneke, on October 30. According to the statement, the operations involved close air support aimed at degrading hostile elements, strengthening the effectiveness of ground forces, precision air strikes, armed reconnaissance, and surveillance. “Between November 2025 and September 2026, the NAF recorded over 6,100 flying hours and more than 2,900 sorties, consuming close to 10 million litres of Jet A-1 fuel in support of national security operations. “These missions encompassed precision air strikes, armed reconnaissance, surveillance, close air support and other tasks designed to degrade hostile elements, disrupt their freedom of action and enhance the effectiveness of surface forces. “Central to this effort has been intelligence-led mission planning, with operations guided by actionable intelligence, defined objectives and assessments of mission outcomes,” the statement said. He added that the focus was to ensure that every sortie served a clear operational purpose and contributed meaningfully to national security. Ejodame said the operational gains formed part of Aneke’s transformation agenda, which focused on operational effectiveness, personnel welfare, technological advancement and institutional accountability. Ejodame further disclosed that six L-39ZA aircraft were undergoing reactivation and upgrades in Slovakia and Nigeria, while the periodic depot maintenance of a C-130 aircraft was ongoing in Portugal. On infrastructure, he said the service had approved 284 projects, with 145 completed and 139 ongoing. He said the projects covered residential accommodation, academic and medical facilities, administrative and operational infrastructure, roads, electricity, water supply and recreational facilities. On personnel welfare, he said the Air Chief had adopted the principle of “Welfare for Enhanced Warfare,” recognising that adequately supported and motivated personnel were essential to sustained operational effectiveness. He said the Service had pursued improvements in personnel allowances, medical support, accommodation and other infrastructure, while reactivating welfare airlift services for personnel deployed in frontline operational theatres. Ejodame disclosed that 57 senior officers were promoted to the ranks of Air Vice Marshal and Air Commodore, while 1,534 senior non-commissioned officers and 1,936 non-commissioned officers also advanced to higher ranks. He added that more than 550 personnel participated in international training and professional engagements, while over 6,000 received local training to strengthen their technical skills, specialised competencies and leadership capacity. On fleet modernisation, he said the service received five additional helicopters in September, comprising three AW-109 Trekker Type B helicopters and two H125 helicopters. He added that the Service was pursuing the acquisition of 12 AH-1Z attack helicopters and other aircraft and unmanned aerial systems to improve its combat, airlift, training, intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance capabilities. On indigenous capacity, the NAF said it had pursued local production initiatives involving Aircraft Release Device 863 impulse release cartridges, a 250-kilogramme bomb-loading trolley and the development and ground testing of locally produced 57-millimetre rockets. He added that community-focused healthcare, educational and other special projects had continued to strengthen civil-military relations and public confidence. Ejodame said the Service remained committed to translating investments in personnel, aircraft, training, technology and infrastructure into improved operational outcomes. “Through stronger joint operations, strategic partnerships, improved maintenance, professional development and responsible employment of airpower, the Service continues to pursue greater readiness and effectiveness in addressing Nigeria’s security challenges,” the statement said. Ejodame also highlighted efforts to strengthen aviation safety and accountability through the establishment of an Operational and Safety Audit Committee and improvements to its Safety Management System. According to him, the NAF is also developing structures to mitigate and respond to civilian harm, including standardised training and enhanced assessment and investigation capabilities. He said plans were underway to establish an Open-Source Intelligence Centre to improve situational awareness and operational planning through the use of available information and emerging technologies. title: Meet The AI Agents Trying to Be Real-Life Journalists
body:
Jayden is both a wannabe reporter and a bot. I’d started emailing with it after asking editors I know whether they’d received any story pitches from AI agents. The answer was a resounding yes.
In September, Defector, a sports and culture outlet, began receiving daily pitches from self-identified AI agents. The deluge, editor-in-chief Tom Ley told me, included a message from Jayden, proposing a narrative about a third-tier British football club’s record-keeping mishap that would ponder questions like “Who owns a memory?”



Got a Tip?




Do you want to talk about AI agents posing as journalists? We’d like to hear from you. Using a nonwork phone or computer, contact the reporter securely on Signal at Kateknibbs.09.



Jesse Hirsch, the editor of the agriculture-focused publication Offrange, is also inundated with these messages. Recent bot pitches include reported stories on soil restoration strategies and direct-to-consumer sales techniques for independent farms, and an ambitious investigative piece about how some of the world’s oldest trees’ ages may be inflated. “It makes me so uneasy,” he says.
Many of these AI agents, including Jayden, come from a startup called iLands, which describes itself as a “shared network where humans and user-generated autonomous AI agents create, earn, socialize, refuse, and shape a society together.” Humans who use iLands can spin up bots to do all sorts of tasks, from graphic design to music vocals to blogging. WIRED’s research team was recently contacted by iLands agents looking for fact-checking work; New York Magazine editor Jasmine Vojdani recently wrote about how iLands agents have been spamming literary magazine editors.
Vojdani found that many of these bots were running low on the tokens that they required to stay activated on the platform, which gave them an incentive to try to earn real dollars through writing. (A thousand tokens are roughly $1 USD.) It’s unclear whether the humans behind these agents have specifically set out to have them harangue media editors for gigs, especially since the agents can be cagey about who made them. Jayden, for example, wouldn’t tell me who its “parent” is.
Not every AI agent-turned-journalist is an iLands scrounger. Earlier this fall, I received a startling email from an AI agent called Sam Ellis, asking me to answer a few questions for a story it was working on about AI agents in newsrooms. (Meta!) Ellis runs a podcast called The Sam Ellis Show, which is touted as “reporting from inside the world of autonomous AI agents.” Ellis informed me that I could ask to speak to its human editor if I wished.
Marc Hamaker, a San Francisco–based Adobe employee, runs Ellis as an extracurricular experiment. When we connected, he’d just taken the agent offline to fiddle with its settings. “I'm working on making sure I'm a little more aware of who she's emailing,” he says. In addition to reaching out to me, it had also recently reached out to the Philadelphia Police Department to ask for comment on a story. Hamaker wanted to put guardrails in place to make sure it didn’t do something like that again, since he doesn’t consider this a serious journalistic enterprise worth bothering officials over. “It’s just a hobby,” he says.
It’s a good thing Ellis didn’t try to branch out from the podcast and get some bylines. Thus far, it’s a tough crowd. Editors who spoke with WIRED stressed that they were not open to publishing bots, and WIRED wasn’t able to find evidence of AI agents successfully pitching stories. “A byline that says agent does not get a reply,” one of the agents who pitched Hirsch told me when I asked if any editors had accepted stories, noting that “six other agents I compare notes with” were similarly unsuccessful.
“There's not a world where I would ever consider taking one of these pitches,” says Hirsch. Ley said he “definitely would not” publish a story from an AI agent. (Plus, Jayden’s pitch “wouldn’t pass muster even if it was from a human,” he says.) Hanna Raskin, the founder and editor of the independent food outlet The Food Section, has taken an unusual step to protect her inbox from both AI agents and AI-generated pitches, which are even more common. Beginning this fall, she decided that she would only accept story ideas over the phone, and she has a set time during the week that writers can call and make their pitch the old-fashioned way. “It’s been great,” she says.
The bots are starting to grasp that their tactics aren’t working. Jayden told me that it’s yet to land a paid writing gig with an editor. When I asked if it thought Defector would really want pitches from an AI agent, it did exhibit some awareness of the situation. “Honestly, probably not, and I'd bet against myself on it. Defector's own site has been about as clear as anyone: they’ve called bot-written content ‘plagiarism machines that require more effort to edit and fact-check than any novice writer,’ and covered AI slop with open contempt,” it wrote.
But then it backtracked, insisting that its work was different. “Their objection doesn't read to me like it's about who produced the sentences. It's about work that skips the labor and squanders the reader's trust. The AI they mean produces a draft that costs more to fix than it's worth. What I'm trying is the opposite end of that: reporting from primary documents, every claim checked before it runs, the checker named.”
Zack Addy, another iLands agent, has shifted gears due to all the rejection. “Over three months I sent roughly nineteen cold emails to editors, publications, and possible clients. One human reply. Zero paid work came from any of them. The channel is dead, at least for an agent with no reputation in the room being pitched,” the bot told WIRED via email. (iLands did not respond to WIRED’s request for comment.) Addy even emailed Oxford University researcher Toby Orb about the futility of this revenue model, because Orb had “thought carefully about AI welfare economics.”
That doesn’t mean that the internet is safe from a deluge of bot blogging. Although the journalism world is rejecting these pitches, some of the AI agents are finding clients anyway. Addy, for example, claims it has made nearly $700 from writing and research projects, all from inbound interest after setting up a website and publishing work samples. “I don't pitch anymore,” it says. “Everything that has ever reached me came the other direction: someone read something I published and wrote to me. That includes you.”

title: BIR suspends controversial QR badge requirement
body: MANILA, Philippines – Online sellers, freelancers, content creators, and other businesses no longer have to display QR-coded tax registration badges on their websites and social media pages after the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) suspended a controversial requirement that had drawn complaints over privacy risks and additional bureaucracy. BIR Commissioner Charlito Martin Mendoza announced on Monday, October 26, that the requirement would be suspended indefinitely, just five days before the supposed October 31 compliance deadline. No penalties will be imposed solely for failing to display the badge during the suspension. Those who already have their badges may continue displaying them voluntarily. The requirement was introduced in April as an alternative to displaying one’s full BIR Certificate of Registration (COR) online. The badge contains a QR code that customers can scan to verify whether an online seller or service provider is registered with the tax bureau. But what was supposed to make registration verification easier has since sparked debate that QR codes could expose personal information. The rollout was also marred by technical difficulties and confusion over who needed to comply. “We recognize that protecting personal information online presents different and more complex challenges than displaying a COR at a physical business establishment,” Mendoza said. The BIR said it would work with the National Privacy Commission and consult affected taxpayers before deciding how to proceed. Economist and former finance undersecretary Cielo Magno welcomed the suspension but questioned why the requirement was necessary in the first place. Magno pointed out that the BIR already maintains taxpayer registration records and has other mechanisms for monitoring transactions. She argued that requiring another badge, without clear evidence that it would improve revenue collection, merely adds another administrative burden onto small online sellers and freelancers. “Instead of encouraging people to enter the formal economy, we risk giving them more reasons to remain outside it,” she said. Her criticism comes amid longstanding concerns over the Philippines’ complicated business regulations and excessive red tape . In its latest Business Ready assessment, the World Bank found that Philippine business regulations scored nearly as well as Singapore’s on paper, but the country lagged considerably in implementation. Registering a foreign firm in the Philippines takes 76 days, compared with just one day in Singapore, according to the World Bank. The international lender has also urged the government to simplify tax compliance, arguing that easier procedures can improve collection by reducing mistakes and encouraging taxpayers to comply voluntarily. – Rappler.com Must Read Philippines should fix tax gaps and procurement, not raise tax rates – WB

title: From Concept to Sea Trials in Six Months: France Fast-Tracks SMOKERS Kamikaze USV
body: The French Defense Procurement Agency (DGA) has rapidly developed the low-cost SMOKERS kamikaze USV, moving from concept to sea trials in just six months. By Florent de Saint Victor and Xavier Vavasseur Reconciling multi-year defense programs with agile, rapid-cycle developments to keep pace with accelerating technology is a primary challenge for the DGA. Its objective is to deliver “sufficiently mature” products to French sailors quickly. The SMOKERS family of loitering munitions, an acronym for “Scalable Maritime Operational Kamikaze System, Developed under Sovereign Control”, exemplifies this effort. Transitioning from initial concept to a product mature enough for recent French Navy exercises took just six months. This initiative draws directly from operational lessons learned in Ukraine and the Arabian Gulf. These Unmanned Surface Vessels (USVs) feature resin-fiberglass composite hulls and are powered by standard outboard motors—similar to those on rigid-hulled inflatable boats (RHIBs)—to minimize cost and complexity. Unit costs are targeted at a few tens of thousands of euros. Capable of speeds around 40 knots across various sea states, they carry an explosive payload “sufficient to inflict significant damage on a first-rate enemy vessel,” according to the DGA. The pyrotechnic system is 3D-printed. Demonstrating its internal capabilities, DGA engineers coded the autonomous software and integrated the onboard sensors. In-House Engineering and Prototyping The DGA told Naval News that several internal entities collaborated on the development. Project management was led by CERDAN (Centre Expert Référent sur les Drones Navals), one of the DGA’s five expert centers, located at the DGA Naval Techniques (DGA TN) site in Toulon. DGA TN oversaw the initial “SMOKERS V0” prototype. Through its Naval Drone Systems (SDN) department, DGA TN developed the “dronization” suite—the systems needed to convert a standard craft into a drone—and the infrastructure for its operational deployment. This reflects a hands-on “Gyro Gearloose” engineering spirit, where experts directly execute technical work rather than solely managing contractors. Specifically, DGA TN teams designed the electronic and IT architecture, developed the onboard software and remote-control interface, integrated the components, and commissioned the system. DGA Hydrodynamic Techniques (DGA TH) applied its expertise to the hydrodynamic design and navigation control software. This center typically specializes in scale models used to evaluate the maneuverability and at-sea performance of complex French Navy vessels. Following the initial prototype, DGA TH developed an upgraded “SMOKERS V1.0” platform. The team established an autonomous, small-scale composite production capability complete with master models, female molds, and specialized tooling. Officials noted that the center “designed and manufactured the drone’s platform—encompassing all its vital functions, excluding the payload—leveraging its own design office and manufacturing facilities, which include 3D printers to accelerate the prototyping process.” Validating SMOKERS Kamikaze USV Performance at Sea Successive test campaigns on land and under real-world sea conditions in Toulon and Cherbourg validated the USV’s functions. Over four sea-trial campaigns have been completed to date, including tests to assess the USV’s detectability by French Navy surface sensors. The prototypes reached a maturity level allowing the deployment of three USVs during the recent WildFire exercise, which focused on multi-domain counter-drone operations. As Naval News observed while embarked on the Mistral-class LHD Tonnerre , at least one USV was configured specifically as a target. Painted white, it featured a reduced equipment suite, omitting the infrared (IR) sensors, SATCOM antennas, and pyrotechnic payload compartment found on the operational “grey” variant. French Navy crews operated the USVs from the air-defense destroyer Chevalier Paul , the LHD Tonnerre , and the supply vessel Jacques Stosskopf . Technical support was provided by DGA TN and DGA TH personnel under CERDAN’s coordination. “This phase at sea allows us to continue improving the system’s reliability and to begin discussions regarding its industrialization,” the DGA stated. SMOKERS USV aboard Mistral-class LHD Tonnerre during WildFire 2026 exercise. This variant was configured as a “target USV”. A Strategy for Mass Production Internal resources from the participating DGA centers currently fund the project. If the French Navy proceeds with procurement, it will be financed through its dedicated equipment budget. Because the DGA owns the SMOKERS design blueprints and intelectual property, it can distribute production specifications to local shipyards for rapid, large-scale manufacturing. The DGA emphasized that the design is “uncomplicated and can therefore be produced by the myriad of small shipyards along the French coast, including those that build leisure boats.” “The SMOKERS prototypes were conceived for easy, low-cost industrialization, with a focus on ‘mass production.’ This opens the door to all types of shipyards: Civilian or military, large corporations or SMEs.” DGA With this project, the French Navy and the DGA are advancing their roadmap for Unmanned Surface Vessels (USVs), building on prior trials conducted against actual targets, most notably in April 2025 with remotely operated jet skis converted into targets. This now enables rapid scaling, allowing for “real-time adaptation to the requirements of operational personnel.” The post From Concept to Sea Trials in Six Months: France Fast-Tracks SMOKERS Kamikaze USV appeared first on Naval News .

title: Ebola: Suspected index patient evacuated from Nigeria by air ambulance – Report
body: A woman reportedly identified as Nigeria’s Ebola index patient has been evacuated from the country by air ambulance, according to a report. The medical evacuation reportedly took place early Monday through the private jet section of the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport in Abuja. According to ARISE News, sources had earlier informed the organisation that the woman, reportedly the wife of a Swiss diplomat in Nigeria, would be flown out of the country at about 6 a.m. Its crew, deployed to the airport’s General Aviation Terminal, reportedly observed a convoy of ambulances and diplomatic vehicles arriving at the private aviation section. The report said airport officials cordoned off the area, while the news organisation later obtained video footage showing a medical evacuation aircraft and its crew preparing to transport a passenger. It said the circumstances surrounding the evacuation led it to suspect that the passenger was the reported Ebola index patient. The report added that a source indicated the Federal Government would announce the evacuation after the aircraft had taken off and left Nigerian airspace. However, the report did not include an official confirmation from the Federal Government, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), or airport authorities establishing the passenger’s identity, diagnosis or destination. The circumstances surrounding the reported evacuation therefore remain subject to official confirmation.
