title: A Brave New World (Of AI)
body:
today we launched ChatGPT. try talking with it here: https://t.co/uWra8LKFMN
For modern AI there was Sam Altman. Todays LLMs have gotten good. We still donât really quite grasp how their emergent capabilities work. Large parts of daily developer life have been erased in the last year and will most likely never come back.
There was a time where you could burn the midnight oil tracing a bug or reading to understand a system and this form of deep thinking was valuable. Today companies expect engineers to ship more code faster and leave the coding to the LLMs. Some are even asking engineers to leave the review to the bots as well.
There is a certain liberation to knowing that weâll most likely never need to use the human brain to reverse a binary tree ever again. But where does this leave software engineers and the field as a whole? There is a tremendous amount of uncertainty at the moment for many good reasons.
Computer science and programming up until this point has been functionally deterministic. The user experiences and operating systems weâve built up over the decades are based on that expectation. LLMs change that deterministic behavior and open new ways to interact with technology. I donât think we can take for granted that layering this new technology on the old is the right sequence and thereâs a lot of development happening to explore an Agent OS.
Software is dramatically changing and with that our role as engineers. Thereâs a lot of ways to think about it but for me the exciting part about programming was never about typing, it was watching ideas come to life and feeling like the computer was a magical canvas. LLMs make that imagination to canvas pipeline dramatically faster.
Engineering was always about finding a problem and inventing a solution using a tool (e.g. a computer). That part hasnât changed, people still have problems that need solutions and a computer is still a multipurpose tool. But without a doubt, what has changed is the SDLC of an engineer.
Unfortunately many treat AI as a magic black box function where input goes in and the answer comes out. We learned with the rise of social media that software can have ripple effects across society. We will certainly be learning new lessons with the increased offloading of cognitive labor to machines.
Weâre also learning that much of our technology up until today was a house of cards. 70% of the internet was exposed overnight due to a vulnerability in PHP . Weâre certainly living in interesting times.

title: We do not think, yet here we are, By Uddin Ifeanyi
body:
Thinking, it would seem, is not one of the talents God gifted the Nigerian politician; you apparently do not need much grey matter if your core deliverable is to line your pockets with ill-gotten lucre. Put this way, one runs the risk of being charged with including in the statement of proof that which still has to be proved. A plenitude of anecdotes is at hand, thank God. The strongest of which, so far, is the fact that the Nigerian politician (we have vanishingly few females of this subspecies) is some of the world’s most conservative types.
Take your pick of subject. Subsidies? As part of a government’s policy responses, the tension in their implementation is often between succouring consumers (potential voters, also) under pressure from rising prices (irrespective of the causes) and bleeding government coffers dry. That, at least, is the first level of disorder. Invariably, government interventions in an economy, by creating winners and losers, generate perverse responses. In the conversation around subsidies, the unavoidable adverse consequence is in distortions to an economy’s allocative efficiency.
What about taxes? Governments slobber at the prospects of the extra revenue that higher tax rates imply. But this increase in the public spending remit is always at a cost. Consumer spending tails of, business investment drops. Except in times of crisis, when increased government spending could jump-start stalling economies, any increase in government spending at the expense of businesses and consumers is nearly always suboptimal (as in, there are more efficient market-based ways to spend the money) and it is nearly always supportive of a rise in domestic prices.
And minimum wages? At this point, the pretence is not necessary anymore. From the incumbent government to the opposition, Nigeria’s policymaking elite struggle to understand basic economics. And “no be today!” “…the inflation was not a direct fallout of the ‘Udoji Award’ payments but of foreign companies jerking (sic) up the prices of their goods.” This is how General Yakubu Gowon (rtd.) explained the price hikes that accompanied Nigeria’s first such major intervention in this space.
If it is no news that the Nigerian politician is not an economic being, it should not surprise us that our outcomes defy economic logic. Nonetheless, the more useful line of enquiry is, “Why is the former the case?” Much of the thinking about economics and the ideological platforms that have arisen on this basis are but derivatives of social and cultural constructs.
Did consumers’ deeper wallet after the Gowon windfall (and subsequent such wage increases) mean too much money pursued the same amount of goods? Yes. Since the Gowon administration, and unlike the possibilities available to that government, successive Nigerian governments have had a money problem. And remarkably, if unfortunately, they have spent it the same way his did. Pinched coffers notwithstanding, our governments have binged on Monopoly® money straight off the central bank’s printing presses.
If it is no news that the Nigerian politician is not an economic being, it should not surprise us that our outcomes defy economic logic. Nonetheless, the more useful line of enquiry is, “Why is the former the case?” Much of the thinking about economics and the ideological platforms that have arisen on this basis are but derivatives of social and cultural constructs. Before the elaboration of fancy economic theories, there were attitudes to wealth and its distribution. Indeed, much of Marxism is one outcome of the person of faith’s outrage at extremes of poverty and affluence nestled cheek-to-jowl in the same suburbs. While the Right’s insistence that the Left’s nannying of the people saps economies of the animal spirits that society needs to thrive is an argument that the history of the United States of America makes impossible to look askance at, we cannot also forget that the Iron Chancellor purloined social welfare from the left in a bit to take the sting out of it.
Is there a middle road to all of these? John Maynard Keynes offered strong arguments for when governments may interfere in an economy, sometimes running against the markets’ grain in the collective interest. This journey down economics’ history underscores how the road we have not taken in these parts matter a lot. Straight of the back of the proverbial envelope, the dearth of much thinking around such matters in these parts is the most obvious shortcoming of our approach to the development challenge.
As a reminder of who we are, and where we have been, much of the beautiful parts of our culture and tradition ought to adorn museums and tourist trails. What about the useful parts? Ideally, these should provide the “lever long enough and a fulcrum on which to place it” that Archimedes argued was sufficient to move the world.
Thinking, it would seem, is not one of the talents God gifted the Nigerian politician; you apparently do not need much grey matter if your core deliverable is to line your pockets with ill-gotten lucre. Put this way, one runs the risk of being charged with including in the statement of proof that which still has to be proved. A plenitude of anecdotes is at hand, thank God. The strongest of which, so far, is the fact that the Nigerian politician (we have vanishingly few females of this subspecies) is some of the world’s most conservative types. What does he conserve? Cultural and traditional practices that are in our current context the moral equivalent of surrendering to long-dead black men a veto over the choices we make today. That would, still, be too smug a response. For as it has been demonstrated elsewhere, culture and traditions break up into a beautiful and useful part.
As a reminder of who we are, and where we have been, much of the beautiful parts of our culture and tradition ought to adorn museums and tourist trails. What about the useful parts? Ideally, these should provide the “lever long enough and a fulcrum on which to place it” that Archimedes argued was sufficient to move the world.
At which point one wonders how our leaders became such frightening caricatures of the American slaveholders’ refusal to concede to black people the one thing that distinguishes our species from the rest of the animal kingdom — self-awareness. You can argue in rebuttal, as Frederick Douglass did so many years ago, that the black man “learns from the past, improves upon the past, looks back upon the past, and hands down his knowledge of the past to after-coming generations”, but no people can tell the difference between the beautiful and useful lines of their heritage, whose leaders cannot think.
Except of course, it is not our intention to “move the world.”
Uddin Ifeanyi , a journalist manqué and retired civil servant, can be reached @IfeanyiUddin .
Mr. Udin is Business Intelligence expert. He is a Member of Premium Times Editorial Board and a Columnist par excellence.

title: Trump escalates anti-Muslim attacks against El-Sayed in Michigan
body:
President Donald Trump departs after speaking during a campaign rally at McMorran Place Sports and Entertainment Center, Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026, in Port Huron, Mich. Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP hide caption
PORT HURON, Mich. — President Donald Trump intensified his anti-Muslim rhetoric against Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed on Sunday, portraying him as a threat to national security and questioning his loyalty to the United States in remarks that drew a sharp rebuke from a former top Arab American ally.
Trump called El-Sayed, a former Detroit health official, a "jihadist" who was "on the side of the terrorists" and would "have to go through a metal detector before he's allowed to go into the Senate." He also repeatedly invoked the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, drawing a comparison between stopping El-Sayed from entering the Senate chamber and the passengers who fought back against the hijackers aboard United Flight 93.
El-Sayed, who would become the nation's first Muslim senator if elected, has called attacks on his loyalty to the country "shameful" and repeatedly denied any ties to extremist groups. The Republican president's remarks were condemned by Bishara Bahbah, a founder of Arab Americans for Trump, the group that helped lead the president's outreach to Arab American voters in 2024.
"The president's statements are out of line," he said in a phone interview. "They are crossing a red line. They are racist."
With Republicans on the defensive over inflation, soaring fuel prices and the Iran war, the president has been trying to generate turnout by claiming that El-Sayed and other Democrats are existential threats to America, instead of electoral rivals. Michigan's Senate race between El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers is among a handful of contests that could determine control of the chamber.
Trump made his remarks in Port Huron, a Canadian border city about an hour north of Detroit and near communities where he made significant gains among Arab American voters in 2024. He became the first Republican presidential candidate since 2000 to win Dearborn, a city with one of the nation's largest concentrations of Arab Americans.
Trump, who imposed a travel ban targeting several predominantly Muslim countries during his first term, has increasingly leaned into anti-Muslim rhetoric as Election Day approaches. He also attacked Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar of Minnesota at Sunday's rally, where he declared that he had come to Michigan "to keep a jihadist Muslim Brotherhood member from becoming a United States senator."
Responding to Trump, who also regularly mocks his name, El-Sayed told supporters at a rally in Grand Rapids later Sunday that he doesn't care how Trump pronounces or misrepresents it.
"I don't even care that he remembers my whole name because he can just go on and call me 'senator' after November," El-Sayed said, drawing cheers. "I will be Senator Muhammad to you, bro."
Central to Republicans' strategy against El-Sayed in the final weeks of the campaign has been an effort to link him to the Muslim Brotherhood, an Islamic movement with branches that the U.S. government has designated as terrorist organizations.
There is no evidence that El-Sayed has any affiliation with the Muslim Brotherhood. His half-sister, Eman Abdelhadi, wrote on social media in 2012 that "my family has long been MB" and described a conversation with her mother about her involvement in the Muslim Brotherhood in the early 1970s.
El-Sayed was born in the United States to Egyptian immigrant parents who divorced when he was young. He was raised by his father, not his biological mother.
Trump on Sunday also targeted El-Sayed's ties to popular streamer Hasan Piker, who appeared alongside the Democrat multiple times during the primary campaign, including at his election night event.
Piker in the past has said that "Hamas is a thousand times better" than Israel, describing some Orthodox Jews as "inbred" and that "America deserved 9/11."
El-Sayed has faced criticism for his own rhetoric. He has repeatedly refused to answer questions about whether Iran or Israel poses a bigger threat to the country. Earlier this year, he said "hurt people hurt people" after an attack on a synagogue in the Detroit area. The attacker had lost four relatives in an Israeli airstrike on Lebanon the week earlier. El-Sayed later apologized, saying he was not trying to justify what happened.
"To anyone who feels like my comments might have been hurtful, I'm really sorry," he said. "That was not my intention."
Bahbah, whose organization has since changed its name to Arab Americans for Peace, said Trump's remarks were unacceptable to Arab and Muslim communities, including Christian Arabs.
"The remarks are out of line and crazy. I mean, no sane individual would say these things," Bahbah said.
Dearborn helped Trump win Michigan in 2024 after many voters in the city were outraged by the Biden administration's handling of the war in Gaza.
"The president of the United States saying that about a person because of his religion, that is just not acceptable," said Bahbah. "And people are going to remember that on Nov. 3."
Sen. Bernie Sanders, speaking at the Grand Rapids rally, said Trump and his allies were using Islamophobia because they have "nothing to say" about the issues most important to working people, such as health care, housing and income inequality.
"All they can do is foment hatred and divisiveness," Sanders said.
Rogers and El-Sayed have been locked in a bitter race to fill the seat of retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters.
During their second and final general election campaign debate, Rogers questioned El-Sayed's loyalty to the United States.
"Are you for America, or are you for these terrorist groups overseas?" Rogers asked.
El-Sayed said that questioning was "shameful."
"I'm proud of our Constitution that guarantees all of us the right to pray as we choose to pray," he said.
Speaking before Trump's appearance Sunday, Rogers repeated his allegations linking El-Sayed to the Muslim Brotherhood.
"The Muslim Brotherhood celebrated exactly one victory in the United States in the primary this year," Rogers said on stage. "Abdul El-Sayed's."
President Donald Trump listens as Nicki Minaj speaks during a campaign rally at McMorran Place Sports and Entertainment Center, Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026, in Port Huron, Mich. Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP hide caption
Trump has routinely announced new investments in factories at his campaign rallies, but he did not do so as part of his speech in Michigan, a state defined by the auto industry.
The president instead repeated investments already being made by domestic automakers. Those automakers could see their finances slump if the president expands his trade war with Canada, which has been an essential partner for the U.S. automotive sector.
While it lacked a fresh promise for Michigan's economy, Trump's rally did deliver a bit of star power.
Rapper Nicki Minaj appeared on stage and urged people to get out and vote for the state's Republican ticket. Her appearance followed an awkward moment from Trump, who has increasingly been fixated on commenting about other people's body parts.
After praising the body of Ohio Sen. Jon Husted, a Republican in a close election contest, Trump turned his eye toward Minaj and commented on her posterior.
The president then signaled for Minaj to stand for the crowd and she did, after which Trump said, "I hope Nicki wasn't insulted, but we love Nicki. She's been with us for a long time."

title: Nigeria’s lone Ebola patient evacuated to Switzerland
body: Nigeria’s index case of the imported Ebola virus disease has been evacuated to Switzerland for further care, Minister of Health, Ali Pate, has said. Pate disclosed that the patient departed Abuja earlier Monday with his approval, adding that her spouse, who has remained asymptomatic, accompanied her. In a statement, the minister said the patient’s clinical condition had improved significantly before the evacuation. He said she was stable, conscious and able to communicate, while her laboratory test results were approaching baseline levels. Uba Sani To Opposition: ‘Don’t Rely On Social Media, Go Out And Campaign’ INEC to decide on Pantami, Gwarzo, Adebutu, others October 29 However, Pate cautioned that the improvement did not necessarily mean the patient was no longer infectious, stressing that strict public health protocols remained in place. “The index patient was clinically much improved, stable, conscious, communicating, and her clinical laboratory test results closing towards baseline. This does not mean she is not still infectious, hence the strict protocols in place,” he said. The minister commended the clinical personnel who treated the patient, as well as public health officials who coordinated the evacuation in accordance with established public health measures. He said the government would provide further updates later Monday after the patient and her spouse had arrived safely at their destination. Pate assured Nigerians that public health measures were ongoing to contain the imported virus, urging citizens to remain vigilant and obtain information from credible sources. “All public health measures are continuing to ensure successful containment of the imported virus. I urge Nigerians to remain vigilant and rely on information from credible sources,” he said. The minister did not provide further details about the circumstances of the evacuation or the treatment arrangements in Switzerland.

title: Customs urges importers, exporters to minimise documentation errors to enhance efficiency
body: The Customs Division of the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) has urged importers, exporters and other actors in Ghana’s international trade ecosystem to minimise documentation errors, cautioning that inaccurate or incomplete declarations contribute significantly to delays in Customs processing and ultimately increase the cost of doing business. Rubben Kwaku Satu, Esq., Supervisor at the Customs Technical Services Bureau (CTSB) and officer in charge of Strategy, Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation, identified the lack of supporting documentation for declarations and appeals; data-entry errors involving vehicle chassis numbers, models, and engine cubic capacities; incomplete certificates of origin; and the attachment of incorrect invoices and bills of lading as some of the recurring problems confronting Customs. Speaking during a UK-Ghana Chamber of Commerce (UKGCC) and PwC Ghana webinar on “Customs, Import Documentation, and Trade Facilitation: Improving Efficiency for Businesses,”Mr. Satu continued that without supporting documentation, an officer may be unable to justify accepting the importer’s position, which can prolong processing. Data-entry errors, on the other hand, can lead to incorrect assessments and require subsequent corrections, modifications, or cancellations. Furthermore, incomplete certificates can result in claims for preferential tariff treatment being rejected until the documentation is corrected, while the cancellation or modification of declarations containing incorrect invoices or bills adds both cost and time to the clearance process. “These documentation errors or compliance errors, when minimised, ensure that Customs is efficient for businesses,” Mr. Satu remarked, and urged business owners to get involved in the process to reduce the errors. “As a business owner, get involved in the clearance process. That is the only way errors will be minimised and you’ll get value for money to protect your business,” he said. Get it right before the goods arrive To reduce these errors, Mr. Satu advised businesses to engage qualified and licensed Customs house agents, use pre-arrival processing and, where applicable, seek advance rulings on classification and origin. He said regular importers could use advance rulings to establish the applicable classification and origin treatment of goods before arrival, improving predictability and allowing them to plan appropriately. Businesses importing large volumes could also consider becoming self-declarants, enabling their staff to specialise in their own import transactions. Businesses using Customs house agents, however, should not leave the entire process to the agent. “What businesses that use Customs house agents should do is they should study the declarations received from their agent and ensure all anomalies are corrected before the goods arrive,” Mr. Satu advised. He strongly recommended pre-arrival processing so that declarations could be submitted and discrepancies dealt with before consignments reach the ports. “Pass the declaration before the goods arrive. It will ensure that every contestation, anomaly or mistake will be corrected before the goods arrive,” he said. Businesses should also have their Import Declaration Form (IDF), bill of lading, commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, permits, licences, exemptions and authorisations, relevant bonds and guarantees, sales contracts, letters of credit and evidence of payment readily available where applicable. A panelist, Ebenezer Agawu, Operations Manager at Consolidated Shipping Agencies LTD., concurred with Mr. Satu’s position, emphasising the importance of getting the documentation right before making a submission. “If you are able to present an accurate document, that should actually enhance the facilitation of Customs procedures and other agencies without any difficulty,” he remarked. Customs as a shared responsibility Mr. Satu encouraged businesses to approach Customs offices with their concerns, follow Customs’ media engagements, prepare adequately before importing, and take advantage of suspense regimes and preferential arrangements including AfCFTA, the ECOWAS Trade Liberalisation Scheme and the UK-Ghana Trade Partnership Agreement. “For us to be efficient as Customs, it’s a shared responsibility between us and you. Help us to be efficient, so you also benefit as businesses,” Mr. Satu concluded. Beyond documentation and clearance efficiency, the webinar, moderated by Maxwell Ntiri, an Associate Director with PwC Ghana’s Tax Services, examined Publican- one of Customs risk management tools, Customs classification and valuation, advance rulings and appeals, post-clearance audits, the new Customs Act, non-tariff barriers and trade arrangements including AfCFTA, the ECOWAS Trade Liberalisation Scheme, and the UK-Ghana Trade Partnership Agreement.

title: Global snag delays Finnish flu vaccinations
body:
Finland's public health authority, THL, says the problem affects all of Europe as well as other parts of the world.
Several regional healthcare authorities in Finland are delaying the roll out of flu vaccinations because of delivery problems, after the World Health Organization (WHO) settled on this year's vaccine composition later than usual.
Finland has received about one million doses so far, with another 800,000 still expected.
The issue has led several regional authorities to announce delays to their flu vaccination programmes. Kymenlaakso, Satakunta and Ostrobothnia are among those that have changed their vaccination schedules because of supply problems.
According to Mia Kontio of Finland's public health authority THL, the problem affects all of Europe and parts of the rest of the world.
This year's situation is unusual because all three components of the flu vaccine were changed, delaying production. The WHO also settled on the vaccine's composition later than usual.
Vaccine makeup is updated so that they protect as well as possible against the viruses currently circulating. The THL says influenza viruses have changed substantially since the previous flu season.
Kontio says Finland is doing well by European standards, since more than half of its doses have already been delivered. In some European countries, the first jabs won't begin until late November.
Finland normally starts vaccinating early, but Kontio says there is still plenty of time to get the shot in November or before Christmas. The flu typically peaks after the new year. Although some cases have already been detected, she says the actual flu season starts later.
Once more vaccines arrive in Finland, they will be offered to people over 65, children under 7, pregnant women, and those whose health puts them in a flu risk group.

title: The price of fuel woke the Europeans up
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 26 (MNA) – After months of accompanying America's policies against Iran, European countries are now worried about the expansion of conflicts and the rise in oil and fuel prices.
After months of accompanying America's policies against Iran, European countries are now worried about the expansion of conflicts and the rise in oil and fuel prices; a concern that shows the consequences of a military adventure do not remain confined to the battlefield and can affect the daily lives of citizens and the economic stability of countries that played a role in shaping the crisis. Now, the increase in energy costs and the possibility of expanding instability in global markets have led European governments to conclude that continuing the confrontation with Iran can have consequences beyond their initial calculations.
The Guardian newspaper, in a report by Patrick Wintour, wrote that the foreign ministers of eight European and Middle Eastern countries at a meeting in Istanbul have called on America and the Zionist regime not to resume their attacks on Iran. They have warned that the resumption of conflicts could expand the crisis across the region and push oil prices even higher. According to this newspaper, the formation of a kind of multinational "anti-war bloc" has gained importance under conditions in which Tehran's nuclear negotiations are at a deadlock and signs of Washington's and Tel Aviv's willingness to resume military actions are visible.
But the fundamental question is: to what extent did European countries, when accompanying America's and the Zionist regime's actions against Iran, take into account the consequences of such a policy for their own security and economy? Some European governments, by providing facilities and military or logistical support to America, participated in a process that increased pressure on Iran. Now those same countries are warning about the expansion of the crisis and its economic consequences; as if the increase in energy costs has made them more aware than before of the real dimensions of this confrontation.
Europe now faces the contradictory result of a policy in which accompanying military pressure against Iran has been combined with concern about the consequences of that same pressure for the European economy. European governments cannot, on the one hand, play a role in providing the ground for military actions or supporting Washington's policies, and on the other hand, expect the potential consequences of these actions to remain directed only at Iran and the countries of the region. In today's interconnected world, security crises are quickly transferred to energy markets, supply chains, and the living costs of citizens.
In this context, the Strait of Hormuz is one of the most important determining variables in security and economic equations. This strategic waterway is considered the passage route for an important part of the global trade in oil and gas, and any serious disruption in the transit of energy-carrying ships through it can confront global markets with a shock. The rise in oil prices, the growth of transportation costs, and the increase in the price of petroleum products are among the consequences that can quickly be transferred to the economies of energy-importing countries.
Iran, too, due to its geographical position and strategic capacities in the region, is an important part of the global energy security equations. For this reason, the possibility of disruption in the transit of energy through the Strait of Hormuz, even without the realization of the scenario of this waterway being closed, can affect market expectations and governments' calculations. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz is not a certain and inevitable consequence, but ignoring the risks arising from the intensification of the confrontation around it would also not be realistic. Governments that support increased military pressure on Iran must also take into account in their calculations the possibility of reciprocal reactions and their effects on the global energy market.
For European countries, this issue is doubly important. The rise in oil and fuel prices does not only raise the cost of energy supply; it can also increase production costs in factories, the transportation of goods, services, and the provision of households' daily needs. Under such circumstances, inflationary pressure intensifies, and European industries may face greater difficulty in competing with producers in other regions of the world. In this way, the consequences of the crisis go beyond the level of foreign relations and become a direct issue in the lives of citizens and the performance of European economies.
For this reason, today's concern of European countries cannot be considered merely a diplomatic position; this concern reflects the collision of political calculations with economic and geopolitical realities. Accompanying Washington may have political or security considerations for some European governments, but this accompaniment does not mean immunity from the consequences of America's decisions. When the crisis expands, Washington's allies may also face costs in which they had no determining role in the initial decision-making and whose effects they cannot easily prevent.
The position taken by the foreign ministers of eight countries in Istanbul shows that concern about the expansion of the crisis has now become one of the serious considerations in relations among the countries of the region and Europe. However, opposition to the resumption of military actions does not necessarily mean a fundamental change in the policy of these countries toward Iran; perhaps concern about economic and security costs has driven them to adopt such a position more than any other factor. Nevertheless, this same concern also shows that the continuation of the confrontation can create divisions even among America's allies and increase the political costs of Washington's decisions.
Ultimately, the increase in Europe's concern about oil and fuel prices is a reminder of a clear reality: one cannot play a role in intensifying a crisis and expect its costs to remain solely on the shoulders of the opposing side. European governments must learn from the current experience that their energy security and economic stability are not separate from developments in the Middle East, and that military policies can create unforeseen consequences for their own supporters. Now that the increase in energy costs has become a serious concern, the fundamental question remains: why were the economic and security consequences of this path not given the place they have today in the calculations of European countries before accompanying military actions against Iran?

title: What we know about derailment of cargo train in Sverdlovsk Region
body:
MOSCOW, October 26. /TASS/. A cargo train derailed on a section of the railway in Russia’s Sverdlovsk Region, followed by a fire, according to a post on the Max channel of the Sverdlovsk Railway.
TASS has compiled the main facts about the incident.
On October 26 at 1:30 a.m. local time (11:30 p.m. Moscow time or 8:30 p.m. GMT on October 25), several cars of the cargo train derailed and subsequently caught fire along the section between the Makartsevo and Sedelnikovo stations of the double-track electrified Reshety-Aramil line on the Sverdlovsk Railway, according to a post on the Sverdlovsk Railway’s channel on Max.
The clearance gauge of the adjacent track was damaged; traffic was suspended.
Fire and recovery trains were sent to the site.
Passenger train traffic on this section is not provided for and does not take place, the Sverdlovsk Railway noted.
Twenty cars derailed on the Reshety-Sedelnikovo section in Yekaterinburg, the press service of the Sverdlovsk Region’s Main Directorate of the Emergencies Ministry said later.
Seven rail tankers are on fire; they have been uncoupled.
The remaining cars are being towed away to a safe distance.
Some 316 people and 35 pieces of equipment were deployed to respond to the incident, including 58 people and 20 pieces of equipment from the Russian Emergencies Ministry.
The fire was contained, with flames covering an area of 1,500 square meters.
The regional office of the Emergencies Ministry reported later that the open flames had been extinguished.
It also specified that 39 cars had derailed.
The Sverdlovsk Railway is carrying out recovery operations and monitoring the environmental situation at the site of train cars’ derailment in the Sverdlovsk Region, the press service reported.
Recovery and fire trains, along with other specialized equipment, are operating at the scene, with 250 personnel of the Sverdlovsk Railway involved.
Law enforcement officials have launched an investigation into the derailment of freight cars followed by a fire in the Sverdlovsk Region, according to information on the Max channel of the Central Interregional Investigative Department for Transport of Russia’s Investigative Committee.
Investigators and forensic experts have been dispatched to the site; the full circumstances of the incident are being established.
The Sverdlovsk Region’s transport prosecutor has traveled to the site of the train derailment, the press service of the Ural-based office told TASS.
No excessive levels of harmful substances in the air or threats to the environment have been recorded, the press service of the Sverdlovsk Railway reported.
Monitoring of air and soil conditions will continue until the aftermath of the incident is completely cleared, the report said.
No excessive levels of harmful substances have been detected in the air in populated areas near the site where the tanker cars caught fire, the press service of the regional office of the Federal Service for Surveillance on Consumer Rights Protection and Human Wellbeing (Rospotrebnadzor) said.
The Service continues to monitor air quality.

title: Toyota is betting $6.4 billion a year on humanoid robots and factory automation
body:
Toyota wants to turn itself into a global robotics company, and it's betting on humanoid robots and factory automation to get there. The world's largest automaker plans to deploy 400,000 robots as part of a $6.4 billion annual investment plan, the Financial Times reports.
In July, Toyota's AI robotics spinout Walden Robotics went public with a $1.1 billion valuation and $300 million in funding. Goldman Sachs analysts think Toyota could grab three to eight percent of the humanoid robot market by 2035. Its rivals include Tesla, Xpeng, and Hyundai, which plans to start building its Atlas robot in the US in 2028.
A Toyota executive says the company's own factories come first for robot deployment because the environment there is easier to control. Investors are more cautious. They point out that Toyota has fallen short of expectations before with hydrogen cars and solid-state batteries. Ad Ad

title: Asian Cup 2027 to go ahead as planned in Saudi Arabia
body: The 2027 Asian Cup will go ahead as planned in Saudi Arabia, with the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) confirming the tournament ⁠schedule and venues on Monday. The tournament will kick-off on January 7 with Saudi Arabia taking on Palestine at Riyadh's ‌King Fahd Sports City Stadium. The 24-team continental championship will run until February 5, ⁠with the opening match and final both ​scheduled ⁠to take place at the King Fahd Sports City Stadium. The tournament will take place across eight venues in three cities – Riyadh (five), Jeddah (two) and Al Khobar (one). The UAE are in Group E and begin their Asian Cup campaign against Vietnam on January 11 at the Imam Mohammed Bin Saud University Stadium in Riyadh. Their next group game is against Yemen on January 15 at Riyadh's ‌King Fahd Sports City Stadium. The UAE conclude their group phase against South Korea on January 20 at the Imam Mohammed Bin Saud University Stadium. Defending champions Qatar will begin their title defence against Thailand on ​January 11, while Japan ‌open their campaign ⁠against Indonesia the ​same day. title: ‘That’s hard to miss’ – Donald Trump compliments Nicki Minaj’s backside at Michigan rally
body:
US President Donald Trump has once again made Nicki Minaj’s appearance a talking point, resorting to a lewd joke about the American rapper’s backside during a campaign rally in Michigan.
Mr Trump made the crude remark after travelling with the 43-year-old aboard Air Force One on Sunday to attend a rally in Port Huron, Michigan, as Republicans confront predictions of a possible Democratic wave in the midterm elections.
His latest comment follows two earlier occasions this year when he praised Minaj’s appearance. PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that Mr Trump had complimented her skin and long nails and described her as respected, sexy and “so hot”.
“I looked at one hell of a beautiful arse before, Nicki Minaj. That’s hard to miss,” Mr Trump said, asking the rapper to stand up in a video posted on Fox News’ Instagram page .
He later apologised for the inappropriate remark, saying he hoped he had not offended Minaj, whom he praised for supporting him for a long time.
Later that evening, Mr Trump praised Ms Minaj after she delivered a two-minute speech backing the Republicans.
He described the ‘Starships’ singer as a special human being and an intelligent woman.
“She never looked more beautiful, and she is a very special person. She gets it, smart,” Mr Trump added.
Speaking to the crowd, Minaj stood by her decision to support Mr Trump, crediting him with changing the country’s direction.
She argued that the president embodied resilience and had transformed the national mood, giving citizens fresh reasons to believe in the future.
“He represents resilience. So many people were maybe giving up a little bit, a little bit hopeless. And since he’s come back, he’s changed the energy of our country and he’s given us a future to look forward to, a brighter future for us and our children. So, let’s make some noise for this great man. I love him so much.
“We need this place to lead in the movement, right? And we’re not going to give up because we want our children to grow up in a place where we can be proud of… So, President Trump, it is an honour to stand with you every single time, and I will continue to support you forever.”
Minaj added that mothers in the country want their children to grow up in a place they can be proud of, rather than one where they are constantly bombarded with messages about sex changes.
“We want people to leave the children alone, leave them out of it.”
Minaj declared her unwavering support for Mr Trump, saying she considered it an honour to stand with him and would back him if he sought another term.
“I will continue to support you forever and ever. If you run again, I will support you again.”

title: Borno NDC sanctions assembly candidate over alleged pro-Atiku campaign
body: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Borno State has announced the dismissal of its state House of Assembly candidate, Mohammed Bunu, following allegations of anti-party activities. According to a letter dated October 25, 2026, and signed by the NDC State Deputy Chairman, Umar Fema, Bunu was penalized for allegedly campaigning for the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar. The party stated that Bunu’s conduct is a direct violation of its constitution, rules, regulations, and established principles of discipline. The controversy centers around campaign materials discovered bearing the logo of the ADC, the slogan “SABON TAFIYA, SABON SALO,” alongside the photographs and names of both Atiku Abubakar and Hon. Mohammed Bunu. INEC to decide on Pantami, Gwarzo, Adebutu, others October 29 Police arrest 8 suspected members of ‘one-chance’ gang in Abuja The party leadership noted that the appearance of Bunu alongside an opposing presidential candidate raised serious concerns regarding his political allegiance, loyalty, and ongoing commitment to the NDC. Tracing the disciplinary process, Fema explained that the matter originated at the Hausari Ward level. The Ward Executive reportedly invited Bunu to appear before them on October 23, 2026, to address the allegations, but he failed to attend. Following his non-appearance, the ward secretary, Rabiu Umar, recommended disciplinary measures and escalated the case to the Maiduguri Metropolitan Council (MMC) Working Committee. Bunu was reportedly summoned a second time on October 24 to face an investigation committee, but again failed to show up for the proceedings. Upon reviewing the committee’s findings, MMC Party Chairman Adamu Ibrahim endorsed the recommendation for dismissal and forwarded the dossier to the state leadership for final action. With the state chapter’s endorsement, the NDC officially recorded Bunu’s dismissal from the ticket, subject to the party’s constitutional guidelines and relevant organs. Bunu has been directed to cease representing himself as an authorized candidate or agent of the NDC. However, the letter noted a distinction in the disciplinary scope, clarifying that any action regarding Bunu’s status as an NDC candidate should be evaluated separately from the formal termination or expulsion of his general party membership.

title: Thales opens Sydney sonar facility for Hunter-class frigates, submarines and uncrewed systems
body: Jointly funded by Thales Australia and the Commonwealth, the multimillion-Australian-dollar facility includes a 100-metre-long production hall at Rydalmere. Defence Industry Minister Pat Conroy opened the site within Thales’ existing Acoustics Centre of Excellence. The hall is designed for the end-to-end manufacture of towed array sonar systems for Australian and export customers. These sensors help submarines, surface ships and autonomous platforms detect, track and identify underwater objects, including submarines and torpedoes. “Through this new co-invested manufacturing facility, Australia is strengthening national security, creating high-value jobs and establishing a sovereign centre of excellence for advanced acoustic systems that will support both Australian Defence and export opportunities for decades to come,” Conroy said. The facility is expected to create dozens of engineering and advanced manufacturing jobs over the coming years, alongside work for supply-chain partners. The facility will supply towed array sonars for the Hunter-class frigate programme, supporting long-range submarine detection and tracking. It will also support Collins-class submarine sonar systems, extending more than 35 years of collaboration between Thales Australia, the Royal Australian Navy and Australian defence science organisations. The production capability includes thin-line towed arrays for uncrewed maritime platforms. Thales’ BlueSentry surveillance system combines this fibre-optic sonar technology with uncrewed vessels. “The capabilities developed and manufactured at Rydalmere demonstrate Australia’s ability to deliver sovereign undersea warfare technology, from the Collins Class submarine fleet of today to the Hunter Class frigates and autonomous BlueSentry surveillance systems of the future,” said Jeff Connolly, chief executive of Thales Australia and New Zealand. “Thales Australia is proud to design and deliver high-quality sensors that return best-quality data, allowing for quicker and better decision that relate to national security.” Rydalmere has supplied sonar technology to the Royal Australian Navy for more than three decades. Thales said the new maintenance capacity would help Australian assets spend more time at sea conducting intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance missions.

title: Tongues wagging as Dankwambo’s name appears on Gombe APC campaign list
body: There is confusion in Gombe State following the appearance of the name of former Governor of Gombe State, Senator Ibrahim Hassan Dankwambo, on the list of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Campaign Council . Dankwambo, who is the leader of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in the state, is contesting for the Gombe North Senatorial seat in the 2027 general elections under the platform of the party. The list, which was published on national dailies on Monday showed Dankwambo as a member of the APC campaign structure, a development that created confusion among the PDP supporters in the state. The 666-member campaign council list to be chaired by Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, contains the name of prominent members of the APC including Senator Muhammad Danjuma Goje, Senator Usman Bayero Nafada, Senator Saidu Ahmed Alkali and Senator Dankwmabo among other top party chieftains appointed to drive the APC campaign ahead of the 2027 elections. 2027: Kebbi pilgrims welfare chair’s donations and electoral act Ebola: NCDC places 53 contacts under watch, approves N100,000 weekly support Senator Dankwambo is number seven on the 666-member campaign council list and 6 on the 66-member advisory council, above the names of even some key figures of the APC in the state. The development is already generating reactions. As a former governor and serving political leader, Dankwambo is widely regarded as the face of the PDP in Gombe State, making his appearance on the ruling APC’s campaign list a major talking point. Daily Trust reports that Governor Yahaya is seeking to displace Dankwambo via the platform of the APC. The inclusion has sparked questions on whether the senator has defected to the APC or relinquished his contest and entered into an alliance with the ruling party in the state. As at the time of filing this report, Senator Dankwambo is yet to clarify his position on the appointment. Similarly, the APC in Gombe is yet to explain the rationale behind including an opposition leader in its campaign council. The development is coming at the time former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Prof. Isa Ali Pantami, is fighting to secure a place on the ballot under the PDP, after he was removed in the final list released by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). Our correspondent reports that Dankwambo belongs to the faction of the PDP, led by the Minister of FCT, Barr. Nyesom Wike.

title: Russian ministry recommends underground data centers following Ukrainian drone strikes
body:
Russia's Digital Development Ministry has proposed building data centers underground, camouflaged from the air, and fitted with drone defenses, Russian state-controlled media Kommersant said on Oct. 25, following several Ukrainian drone attacks on data centers.
Guidelines for existing, planned, and under-construction facilities outline the protection standards for three tiers of data centers, including whether sites are placed above ground or underground, according to Kommersant.
The top tier includes strategic sites whose loss could disrupt key state functions for an hour or more; the second tier includes sites supporting regionally or economically important systems, where outages could last four hours or more; and the final tier covers corporate data centers whose damage would not have wider consequences for the state, Kommersant said.
Existing data centers should be protected by reducing their visibility from the air and by deploying layered defenses, including reinforced structures, electronic warfare measures, and drone defense systems.
The announcement came after Ukrainian drones struck three Yandex data centers, a Sberbank facility under construction, and a data center belonging to social media giant VK between Oct. 8 and Oct. 18.
Russia's centralized digital infrastructure leaves Moscow facing two challenges: inflicting comparable damage on Ukraine and protecting its own data centers from further strikes. Serhiy Petrenko, former head of Yandex Ukraine, estimated that around 80% of Russia's data centers are concentrated in Moscow and the surrounding region — within reach of Ukrainian long-range drones.
The consequences of Ukraine's strikes on Russian data centers could extend far beyond disrupted banking and online services, potentially setting back the country's AI development and affecting military technology.
On Oct. 16, Kemerovo Oblast governor Ilya Seredyuk proposed housing data centers inside depleted open-pit mines and quarries, given their natural protection from aerial bombardment.

title: GUR discloses data on foreign tech equipment used by Russian ballistic missile makers
body:
The Main Directorate of Intelligence of the Ministry of Defense of Ukraine (GUR) published data on the War&Sanctions portal regarding three dozen units of foreign-made technological equipment used by cooperation enterprises producing Russian ballistic armaments, the GUR press service reported.
"The Russian military-industrial complex retains a significant dependence on foreign technologies. In particular, despite all efforts, Russia is still unable to replace industrial equipment from global manufacturers with localized analogs. Today we are publishing 30 units of technological equipment of Chinese, German, Taiwanese, American, Turkish, Swiss, and Italian manufacture used by Russian factories producing ballistic missiles and their components – altimeters, aerodynamic rudders, gyroscopes, etc. Characteristic is the growing number of Chinese machine tools and machining centers, including five-axis ones," the message on Telegram reads.
It is noted that Chinese machine tools utilize European, Japanese, and Taiwanese components – CNC systems, servo drives, high-precision spindles and bearings, measuring and rotary systems, linear guides, thermal stabilization tools, and machining process control systems, among others.
The publication notably includes a 5-axis universal machining center GX-650 manufactured by Hyper Machine Tool (PRC), used by Votkinsk Plant – a manufacturer of 9M723 Iskander-M ballistic missiles and the missile section of the Kh-47M2 Kinzhal aeroballistic missile; Shtral (PRC) turning and milling machining centers involved in the production processes of JSC PEMZ Molot, which produces electronic equipment units for Iskander-M missiles; and measuring equipment from German manufacturer Rohde & Schwarz installed at UPKB Detal, which produces altimeters for Zircon missiles.
GUR reminded that in order to deprive the aggressor of the capability to continue the war, it is necessary, in particular: to strengthen end-user control and the actual location of product use, including introducing on-site inspections by authorized representatives at the declared equipment installation address; and to extend enhanced control procedures to spare parts, components, technical fluids, consumables, software, updates, and maintenance required for equipment operation.
GUR also noted that it is necessary to regularly conduct audits of distributors, dealers, and other intermediaries, especially those supplying to high-risk jurisdictions, as well as to identify signs of re-export or end-user changes, investigate cases where a manufacturer's products are detected in the Russian military-industrial complex, establish their supply chains, and take measures to halt further deliveries through relevant intermediaries.
In addition, it is necessary to restrict deliveries of CNCs, tools, and other components to Chinese manufacturers that supply their equipment to Russian military-industrial complex enterprises, the message states.

title: 2027: Oluremi Tinubu confirms vehicle donation to APC youth leaders
body:
Oluremi Tinubu, wife of Nigeria’s president, Bola Tinubu, has confirmed donating Sports Utility Vehicles (SUVs) to the National Youth Wing of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to support its grassroots mobilisation ahead of the 2027 elections.
Mrs Tinubu made the disclosure on Sunday during a campaign strategy meeting with regional APC youth leaders led by the party’s National Youth Leader, Dayo Israel, at the State House, Abuja.
The disclosure comes hours after Mr Israel posted a video showing seven brand-new Toyota Land Cruiser Prado SUVs, saying he had presented them to selected youth leaders to support their election mobilisation activities.
Mr Israel subsequently deleted the post after it triggered widespread reactions on social media, with Nigerians questioning the reported cost of the vehicles and the use of expensive SUVs for political mobilisation amid economic hardship.
In her remarks at the meeting, Mrs Tinubu said her office would provide campaign materials, footwear and other items to support the APC youth leaders during the campaign.
She also said she had donated additional utility vehicles to facilitate their movement and strengthen their grassroots outreach.
Mrs Tinubu urged the APC youth leaders to intensify their grassroots mobilisation and focus on delivering tangible results rather than social media activities.
She also encouraged them to demonstrate independence, competence and versatility, while developing original ideas and taking initiative in their political activities.
Mrs Tinubu urged the youth leaders to focus on tangible political results rather than social media activity, while encouraging them to develop original ideas, demonstrate competence and take initiative.
She also stressed the need for young leaders to be independent and versatile rather than rely on their parents or others to provide direction.
Recall that this is not the first time Mrs Tinubu has donated vehicles for public or institutional use.
Earlier, she donated 50 buses and 30 tricycles to her alma mater, Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU), Ile-Ife, Osun State, following complaints about transportation difficulties on the campus.
In a statement announcing receipt of the vehicles, the university said the donation was intended to ease students’ transportation challenges and improve mobility within the institution.
“The management of Obafemi Awolowo University, Ile-Ife, wishes to inform the University Community, particularly our dear students, of the successful receipt of 50 buses and 30 tricycles graciously donated by the First Lady of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, CON,” the statement said.
The university described the donation as a demonstration of Mrs Tinubu’s commitment to students’ welfare, adding that the vehicles were expected to significantly ease transportation difficulties on campus.
PREMIUM TIMES contacted Mrs Tinubu’s spokesperson, Busayo Kukoyi, and Mr Isreal to seek the Presidency’s response to the public reactions, including concerns about the cost of the vehicles and the circumstances surrounding the donation, but there was no response as of the time of filing this report.
Meanwhile, speaking after the meeting, Mr Israel later confirmed the donation, expressing gratitude to Mrs Tinubu for providing the vehicles to the APC National Youth Wing.
He said the vehicles would enable the youth leaders to reach rural communities, particularly areas with difficult terrain in the South-east and South-west, as the party intensifies its grassroots mobilisation.
“The primary objective is to communicate the administration’s achievements in healthcare, education and welfare, particularly interventions such as the student loan programme and the establishment of primary healthcare centres,” he said.
Mr Israel said he would embark on a nationwide mobilisation tour to promote the administration’s programmes and seek support for President Bola Tinubu’s second-term bid.
He said the tour would take the administration’s message to rural communities and highlight government interventions in healthcare, education and welfare.
The APC youth leader also called for greater coordination among groups supporting Mr Tinubu’s re-election, saying all such groups should operate under the official party structure.
“All APC groups must align with the official party structure.
“All support groups, including PBAT, Door to Door, City Boy and Tinubu Again, are expected to work directly with the APC,” he said.
The meeting was part of preparations by the APC youth wing for its grassroots mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections.

title: Abu Dhabi esports team Red Dunes takes top prize in prestigious Street Fighter tournament
body: Abu Dhabi esports team Red Dunes has won the Street Fighter League championship for the Europe, Middle East, Africa and Asia region, defeating some of the world's leading players to secure a place at next year's international finals in Japan. The team claimed the title on Saturday at the MCM Comic Con London, held at the Excel centre in the British capital. Red Dunes beat GTW 70-30 in the grand final of the Street Fighter 6 competition. The victory earned the Abu Dhabi team $60,000 from the tournament's $100,000 prize pool and a place in the Street Fighter League World Championship in Tokyo next March. For Abu Dhabi-raised player Adel Anouche , better known as Big Bird, the result was particularly significant as it was the team's first championship under the Red Dunes name. "This win means a lot to me because it's our first win with our organisation, Red Dunes esports, and SFL is known to be a tournament to crown the best team!" he tells The National . "It's definitely ranked high for me. Truly best way to showcase our Abu Dhabi, UAE home team." Street Fighter League differs from traditional fighting game tournaments by placing competitors in four-player teams, with victories contributing towards an overall score. This year's EMEAA competition brought together 24 players across six teams representing Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia. Red Dunes entered the playoffs as the second seed after finishing the regular season behind GTW. Its roster comprised Anouche; Jordanian Amjad Al Shalabi , known as AngryBird; Norwegian veteran Arman Hanjani, known as Phenom; and Swede Joel Sundell, who competes as Juicy Joe. Hanjani has been competing internationally for more than a decade, finishing third at Capcom Cup in 2019. Sundell reached the semi-finals of Capcom Cup 11 last year, defeating Al Shalabi along the way. Red Dunes defeated YESports 60-20 in the semi-finals before overcoming GTW in the championship match. Anouche led the comeback after an early deficit, securing two important victories using the character C Viper. Sundell contributed a win against Bravery, while Al Shalabi sealed the championship by defeating Zhen with Akuma. Anouche admits the competition initially left him uncertain about his team's chances. "I even thought we had a low chance of winning after seeing all the teams, but I guess I was wrong and underestimated our team," he says. The championship adds to the achievements of Anouche and Al Shalabi, childhood friends who grew up in Abu Dhabi and are known collectively as The Birds. Al Shalabi won the Street Fighter 6 championship at Evo in Las Vegas in 2023, while Algerian-born Anouche has finished as runner-up twice at the prestigious fighting game tournament. The pair's international reputation was apparent at Tokyo Game Show last month, where they drew crowds of Japanese fans during a meet-and-greet. Anouche believes their success reflects the strength of the Middle East's fighting game community, which developed partly through the region's arcade culture. "Even though the quantity is not there, the quality is definitely present in our players," he says. "With enough dedication and discipline, I'm sure we'll see a lot more champions coming out of Middle East." Saturday's result marks the roster's third consecutive regional Street Fighter League title. At the world championship, taking place at Tokyo's Ryogoku Kokugikan from March 10 to 14, they hope to improve on two previous unsuccessful attempts. "Our next goal is to win SFL world finals. We were able to get a shot at it twice but never made it happen, hopefully 3rd time is the charm now," Al Shalabi says. The team has adopted the slogan "Third Impact" for its latest attempt at the world title.

title: ‘Student List’ wins 52% of vote, Vucic’s supporters get 39% — Serbian electoral commission
body:
BELGRADE, October 26. /TASS/. The opposition Student List is leading in Serbia’s snap parliamentary elections with 52.57% of the vote, while the United Serbia list backed by former President Aleksandar Vucic has received 39.27%, the Republic Electoral Commission reported after counting 96.47% of the voting records.
The remaining parties failed to clear the 3% electoral threshold. The Alliance of Vojvodina Hungarians will also be represented in the 250-seat National Assembly, Serbia’s unicameral parliament, as it is exempt from the requirement to reach that threshold.
On October 25, Vucic conceded defeat for his supporters in the election. He said the Student List would be able to form a parliamentary majority on its own.

title: Lula da Silva reelected Brazilian president: voting results
body:
MOSCOW, October 26. /TASS/. Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court, which carries out the functions of the Central Election Commission, has completed the vote count for the second round of the presidential election. According to the final results, with 100% of ballots counted, incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has officially been reelected.
TASS has compiled the key information about the voting results.
According to the election authority’s final statistics, Lula da Silva, the candidate of the left-wing Workers’ Party, won with 51.79% of the vote, receiving 64,256,232 votes.
His rival, right-wing opposition Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, received 48.21%, with 59,826,041 people voting for him.
The total number of valid votes was 124,082,273.
Voter turnout in the second round stood at 80.78%, with 128,236,074 citizens taking part in the vote.
A total of 19.22% of the electorate, or 30,509,005 people, did not vote.
Invalid ballots accounted for 2.12%, or 2,723,305 ballots.
Another 1.12%, or 1,430,496 ballots, were blank.
A total of 158,745,502 people were eligible to vote in the election.
Lula da Silva set a new record by receiving the largest number of votes in the country’s history.
He also became the first politician in Brazilian history to hold the country’s highest office for a fourth time and set a record for the number of reelections since the rule allowing them was introduced in 1997. He has now been reelected twice.
In addition, Lula da Silva became the first candidate in the country’s history to win the election after finishing behind in the first round, when he received 45.16% of the vote against Flavio Bolsonaro’s 47.03%.
He will also become the oldest president in Brazil’s history.
According to CNN Brasil, the politician will be 81 years old when he takes office.
His fourth term as president will officially begin on January 5, 2027.
Flavio Bolsonaro, the right-wing opposition candidate and senator who lost the second round of Brazil’s presidential election, refused to recognize the voting results and said they should be annulled.
He cited the judicial authorities’ decision to extend voting hours by two hours as the reason.
However, Bolsonaro’s campaign team, which refused to recognize the election results over the authorities’ decision to extend polling hours, had itself submitted a similar request, CNN Brasil reported.
According to the broadcaster, the campaign teams of both candidates had formally asked the courts to adjust voting hours.
Bolsonaro’s team requested an extension of voting in Sao Paulo state and several cities in the south of the country because of heavy rains that hit the region on the eve of and during the second round.
Meanwhile, the campaign team of incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva’s ruling left-wing Workers’ Party justified its request by citing a reduced bus fleet and transport problems in several states, including Sao Paulo and Bahia.
According to CNN Brasil, the Supreme Federal Court selectively considered the request submitted by the Workers’ Party’s campaign team.
The request was referred to Justice Cristiano Zanin, who ordered voting hours to be extended nationwide.

title: Iranian president to travel to Russia on Monday for gas exporters' summit — Tasnim
body:
TEHRAN, October 26. /TASS/. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian will travel to Russia this evening to participate in a summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF), the Iranian news agency Tasnim reported.
The summit will take place in Moscow on Tuesday, and Pezeshkian is scheduled to deliver a speech. According to the agency, the visit will last one day; meetings between the Iranian leader and the heads of several other participating nations have not been ruled out.

title: Time to Reform the Ghana Reference Rate: From treasury bill yields to banks’ deposit costs
body: For businesses borrowing to buy equipment, restock a shop or meet payroll, the price of credit affects everyday decisions. The Ghana Reference Rate (GRR) provides a common starting point for that price. Its usefulness depends on whether the formula reflects financing conditions and whether borrowers can understand how it becomes the interest rate they pay. The central weakness is specific. The GRR blends a policy signal, interbank borrowing and government investment returns without directly measuring banks’ deposit costs. Its reserve adjustment also gives Treasury bill movements more influence than the stated 40% weight initially suggests. The evidence supports a review of the benchmark’s weights and a test of a simple formula that directly includes banks’ deposit interest costs. The main questions for this article are: Whose Cost Is Ghana’s Reference Rate Measuring? Why Should Bank Deposit Costs Replace Government Borrowing Rates in the GRR Formula? How the formula works Existing component Weight What it represents Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) 40% The central bank’s policy signal Interbank rate (IBR) 20% The rate banks pay to borrow from one another Reserve-adjusted 91-day Treasury bill rate (T₉₁) 40% Government’s short-term borrowing rate, increased for reserves and vault cash Here, T₉₁ is the annualised 91-day Treasury bill rate. CRR is the cash reserve ratio, the share of eligible deposits banks must hold as reserves. CIV is the cash-in-vault ratio used in the adjustment. The denominator represents the share remaining after these amounts are deducted. The three stated weights sum to 100%. [3, 4] At a 20% CRR and an illustrative 2% CIV, the denominator is 0.78. A 5.38% Treasury bill rate therefore enters the formula as 6.90%, before the 40% weight is applied. The adjustment recognises a cost from funds held in cash and reserves, but its design and size deserve scrutiny. [2, 5] The Treasury bill component has more leverage than it appears With CRR at 20% and CIV at 2%, a one percentage-point rise in the raw Treasury bill rate increases the formula-based GRR by 0.513 percentage points. The same rise in the policy rate increases it by 0.400 points, and an interbank increase adds 0.200 points. These comparisons hold the other inputs constant. Figure 1 A Treasury bill movement has the largest direct effect Sources: Bank of Ghana interest-rate series and reserve information [2, 5]; 40/20/40 formula [3]. Sensitivities use CRR 20% and CIV 2%. One basis point is 0.01 percentage points. The bars show separate responses, not shares that must total 100%. For example, a Treasury bill increase from 5% to 10%, with the other inputs unchanged, would add approximately 2.56 percentage points to the GRR under these assumptions. A business with a floating-rate loan linked to the benchmark could face that increase even without a change in the policy rate or its own creditworthiness, depending on its contract. The formula’s 40% Treasury bill weight is applied to an adjusted rate. Relative to the unadjusted rate that most readers see in the news, the sensitivity is about 51.3%, compared with 40% for the policy rate. This is not an arithmetic error. It is a feature that should be disclosed prominently whenever the benchmark’s weights are explained. The reserve setting changes that sensitivity. At a 10% CRR and 2% CIV, the Treasury bill coefficient is approximately 0.455. At 20% CRR and 2% CIV, it becomes 0.513. Thus, raising reserve requirements changes the GRR’s response to future Treasury bill movements as well as increasing its current level. The required improvement is straightforward: every monthly GRR release should show both the stated weights and the effective sensitivities to the three headline rates. Borrowers should not have to infer this distinction from the formula. Treasury bills dominate the historical movement An analysis of 102 monthly observations from April 2018 to September 2026 shows how significant this design becomes over time. The Treasury bill component, including its reserve adjustment, accounts for 78.8% of the variance in monthly changes in the formula-based GRR. The policy component accounts for 12.6%, and the interbank component for 8.6%. [1, 2] Figure 2 Treasury bills and reserves dominate the model’s variation Data sources: Ghana Association of Banks and Bank of Ghana [1, 2]. Decomposition covers 101 monthly changes in the formula-based GRR. Shares allocate covariance with the total change; they include shared movements and do not establish independent causal effects on published rates. The 78.8% figure concerns variation in the formula-based benchmark, not the percentage of every loan rate attributable to Treasury bills. Nevertheless, it shows that a component with a stated 40% weight has dominated the benchmark’s historical movement. A Treasury bill is an investment available to banks. Its yield is therefore relevant when a bank compares lending with holding government paper. However, an investment return is different from the cost of obtaining deposits. Treasury bill yields can change because of government financing needs, auction supply and investor demand. The formula can transmit those conditions into the starting price of private credit. Using Treasury bill yields in the GRR passes the government’s borrowing pressures on to businesses and households through bank lending rates, rather than directly reflecting banks’ own funding costs (Deposit cost). The policy rate and interbank rate also reflect related monetary conditions. Treating their 40% and 20% weights as independent economic information overstates the diversity of the formula’s inputs. Their relationship does not make the blend invalid, but the allocation needs evidence. BoG and the Ghana Association of Banks should specify whether the GRR measures funding costs, the opportunity cost of lending or monetary policy conditions. If it is primarily a funding benchmark, the present 40% Treasury bill allocation needs to be tested against a measure that includes actual deposit funding costs. A common benchmark does not tell the borrower’s whole story Published rates show that the GRR has a substantial relationship with bank lending. Across 92 matched monthly observations, the statistical fit between the GRR and average lending-rate levels is approximately R² = 0.95. The difficulty is therefore not an absence of connection. It is that the benchmark cannot explain the entire price of a loan or establish whether that price is fair. [1, 2] Figure 3 Lending rates follow the broad cycle but the gap changes Sources: Ghana Association of Banks GRR historical data and Bank of Ghana Summary of Economic and Financial Data [1, 2]. April 2018–September 2026. The MPR line shows prior-month inputs; lending data end in August 2026. Missing lending observations are left blank. The average lending-rate gap above the GRR was 7.34 percentage points in 2019, compared with 1.37 points across the available observations in 2024. By August 2026, the GRR was 10.61% and the average lending rate was 15.94%, leaving a gap of 5.33 points. A changing gap matters to borrowers because a lower benchmark does not guarantee an equally large reduction in the final loan rate. [1, 2] These aggregate gaps are not measures of bank profit or default risk alone. They can reflect funding differences, operating costs, capital charges, risk, loan composition and margins. Fees can raise the annual percentage rate further. BoG’s APR framework distinguishes these additional charges from the reference rate itself. [4] The underlying design problem remains; the GRR contains no direct deposit-cost input, although banks can fund loans with current accounts, savings, term deposits and wholesale borrowing. It also combines overnight and 91-day rates while many business loans run for years. A funding benchmark should acknowledge these differences, with product-specific credit and maturity costs disclosed separately. How the MPR and GRR can move apart The MPR signals monetary policy; the GRR blends that signal with market rates. The MPR is neither a required floor nor a ceiling for the GRR. Comparing 102 published GRRs with their prior-month MPR inputs gives 44 months below, 58 above and none exactly equal. Using prior-month inputs aligns the comparison with the formula’s timing. [1, 2] For the formula-based GRR, let A represent the reserve-adjusted Treasury bill rate. Subtracting the MPR from both sides gives: The gap depends on how the interbank and adjusted Treasury bill rates compare with the MPR. Published gaps can additionally reflect observation dates and calculation conventions. Relationship Period MPR GRR GRR − MPR MPR above GRR Sep 2026 14.00% 10.18% −3.82 pp GRR above MPR Feb 2023 28.00% 33.25% +5.25 pp Nearly equal Aug 2021 13.50% 13.51% +0.01 pp Sources: GAB published GRRs and BoG policy-rate data [1, 2]. The MPR column uses the prior-month input; pp means percentage points. Near equality is not exact equality. When the MPR is greater than the GRR In September 2026, MPR was 14.00% and GRR was 10.18%, a 3.82-point gap. Lower interbank and adjusted Treasury bill inputs pulled the formula below the policy signal. This can weaken the MPR’s influence on the benchmark when other rates remain low. It does not guarantee cheap loans: banks still add contractual margins and charges. When the GRR is greater than the MPR In February 2023, GRR was 33.25% against MPR of 28.00%, a 5.25-point gap. The adjusted Treasury bill input was approximately 41.42%, while interbank was 25.24%. The higher Treasury bill component outweighed the lower interbank component. Government financing conditions can therefore lift the lending benchmark above the policy rate, adding pressure to GRR-linked borrowing costs. When the two rates are equal Exact equality would mean the weighted differences cancel, not that the model is accurate. Hypothetical inputs of MPR 14%, IBR 10% and adjusted Treasury bills 16% produce GRR of 14%. August 2021 was close: GRR was 13.51% and MPR 13.50%. Equality should not be forced through a floor, cap or target. The mismatch also affects changes in the rates. Holding interbank and reserves constant, a one-point MPR cut lowers GRR by 0.40 points, but a simultaneous one-point Treasury bill rise adds 0.513 points at CRR 20% and CIV 2%. The net result is a 0.113-point GRR increase despite the policy cut. The critique is the formula’s mixed signals and indirect funding proxy. The deposit-cost proposal below addresses that proxy; it would not guarantee equality with the MPR. The monthly calculation should be reproducible Using August 2026 month-end inputs of a 14.00% policy rate, 10.20% interbank rate and 5.38% Treasury bill rate, together with CRR of 20% and CIV of 2%, the formula produces 10.40% for September. The published September GRR was 10.18%. The difference is approximately 0.22 percentage points. [1, 2, 5] Under this calculation, the reserve adjustment alone adds about 0.61 percentage points, lifting the unadjusted blend from 9.79% to 10.40%. The question is whether increasing the return on government paper is the best way to represent the cost of deposits held in reserves. An alternative is to calculate that allowance directly from the cost of the funding subject to the reserve requirement. Across the 102-month period, formula-based estimates fall within 0.15 percentage points of published GRRs in 68 months. In 11 months, the difference exceeds 0.50 points. Different observation dates, reserve ratios or conventions may explain these gaps. The comparison cannot identify the cause without the precise inputs used for each announcement. Figure 4 September 2026 shows why input dates matter Sources: GAB historical GRRs; BoG month-end interest-rate series and reserve information [1, 2, 5]. The formula-based estimate uses CIV 2%. Values are rounded. The 0.22 percentage-point difference is a replication gap; it does not establish an error in the published GRR. Under this calculation, the reserve adjustment alone adds about 0.61 percentage points, lifting the unadjusted blend from 9.79% to 10.40%. The question is whether increasing the return on government paper is the best way to represent the cost of deposits held in reserves. An alternative is to calculate that allowance directly from the cost of the funding subject to the reserve requirement. Across the 102-month period, formula-based estimates fall within 0.15 percentage points of published GRRs in 68 months. In 11 months, the difference exceeds 0.50 points. Different observation dates, reserve ratios or conventions may explain these gaps. The comparison cannot identify the cause without the precise inputs used for each announcement. Historical reserve treatment also matters. During the earlier tiered regime, banks faced reserve ratios of 15%, 20% or 25%. A common benchmark should state which ratio was applied and why. BoG subsequently moved to a uniform 20% CRR on 4 June 2026. Any industry averaging and the vault-cash allowance should be explicit.
