title: Ukraine’s strike capability weakens as Russia hits its military facilities — expert
body:
LUGANSK, October 26. /TASS/. The strike capability of the Ukrainian armed forces declined last week amid attacks by Russian forces on Ukrainian military facilities, including those located in the rear, military expert Andrey Marochko reported.
"Last week, the situation on the line of contact worsened for Ukrainian forces, largely as a result of rear logistics disruption and Russian strikes targeting the military-industrial complex facilities, logistics centers, energy and transport infrastructure, weapons and military equipment production sites, military-technical equipment warehouses, as well as temporary deployment sites for Ukrainian armed formations and foreign mercenaries. "The strike capability of Ukraine’s armed formations has fallen to minimal levels," he wrote on his VKontakte page, after analyzing data released by Russia’s Defense Ministry.
Marochko noted that amid this decline in strike capability, effective counterattacks by Ukrainian troops in the special operation zone "have become practically impossible."
The military expert added that due to logistical disruptions in several areas in the special military operation zone, Ukrainian troops are not evacuating the wounded and the dead, and are instead "simply finishing off their seriously wounded comrades."
On Friday, the Russian Defense Ministry reported that over the past week, the Russian military had launched three massive and 11 combined strikes on the enemy’s logistics centers, energy and transport sites. Ukrainian port infrastructure facilities were incapacitated.

title: Sulina Canal capacity must be expanded to develop Ukraine’s Danube ports – expert
body:
Vitalii Nikula, Director of Izmail Sea Commercial Port, made the comment to Ukrinform during the Rebuilding Ukraine Forum in Bucharest.
“We need certain agreements to increase the capacity of the channels connecting the Danube and the Black Sea. First of all, this is the Sulina Canal, which now plays one of the key roles and is the central entry route for vessels from the Black Sea to the Danube cluster,” Nikula said.
He noted the canal allows passage for vessels with a draft of up to seven meters, carrying both export and import cargoes such as fertilizers, construction materials and other goods needed in Ukraine. The main problem remains limited capacity, with work under way at the level of the relevant ministries in Ukraine and Romania.
“Work is being carried out by ministries of both countries and by our Ukrainian Sea Ports Authority, which is in constant contact with colleagues from the Sulina Canal,” Nikula said.
One expected step is the introduction of night navigation, which he believes would increase cargo handling volumes for both exports and imports.
“We hope night navigation will start soon. This will allow us to boost cargo turnover and process more shipments,” he added.
Another challenge for Danube ports is low water levels, which reduce transport efficiency.
“Ports are facing seasonal drops in the Danube’s water level. It is now catastrophically low. Barges that can normally carry 2,000–2,500 tonnes of grain are currently loaded with a maximum of 750–800 tonnes,” Nikula said.
He also stressed the need for investment in port equipment modernization. “As a state stevedore we maintain our handling equipment in proper condition, but investment in upgrading our fleet of machinery would improve efficiency,” Nikula concluded.
As reported, Ukraine exported 2.4 million tonnes of agricultural products in September, equal to 46% of the required potential volume.

title: Former Japan PM Yasuo Fukuda Dies At 90
body: Former Japanese Prime Minister Yasuo Fukuda, known for trying to build stable ties with China, has died at the age of 90, a ruling party official said Monday. Fukuda passed away on October 22, the official from the Liberal Democratic Party told AFP. He led Japan for a year from September 2007 after replacing the late premier Shinzo Abe, whose first term ended after just 12 months. During his stint in power, he sought to improve relations with China and invited then Chinese president Hu Jintao to visit Japan. Hu’s trip in May 2008 made him the first Chinese head of state to visit the country in a decade. The two leaders issued a joint statement committing to a “mutually beneficial relationship based on common strategic interests”. Fukuda resigned in September 2008 as his approval ratings dropped. He retired as a politician in 2012. But as Tokyo’s ties with Beijing worsened over a disputed island chain and other historical issues, Fukuda visited China in 2014 to hold talks with President Xi Jinping, paving the way for a summit between Xi and Abe during his second term in power. title: Birthright Israel to hold first Taglit Global Business Summit in Tel Aviv
body: Birthright Israel will host the inaugural Taglit Global Business Summit, “Shaping Our Future Together,” November 1-3 at the Hilton Tel Aviv.The landmark event will bring together more than 350 prominent business leaders, investors, entrepreneurs, and philanthropists from Israel and around the world at a critical time for the country.More than 100 participants will travel to Israel from over 15 countries, including Argentina, Australia, Switzerland, and the United Arab Emirates, joining leading Israeli executives and entrepreneurs in a major international gathering focused on business, innovation, philanthropy, and Israel's futureThe first-of-its-kind summit marks a milestone in Birthright Israel's 26-year history, bringing its international network of supporters together in Israel to explore opportunities for business collaboration, strengthen global partnerships, and deepen their shared commitment to the country and the next generation.Prominent participants include Dr. Miriam Adelson, a leading supporter of Birthright Israel; Meir Shamir, chairman of Birthright Israel's Israeli Board of Donors; and Josh Nash, international chairman of Birthright Israel and managing member of Ulysses Management. The summit will also bring together business leaders and entrepreneurs associated with companies shaping Israel's economy, including NVIDIA, Wiz, Elbit Systems, El Al, and monday.com.President Herzog expected to attend event, address participantsThe three-day gathering will open on November 1 with a Gala Evening of Recognition honoring the leadership and philanthropy that have sustained Birthright Israel's impact, including Dr. Miriam Adelson's longstanding commitment to the organization. President Isaac Herzog is expected to address the gathering alongside leading supporters from Israel and around the world.On November 2, the summit will feature prominent figures from technology, investment, finance, entrepreneurship, and public life. Speakers include Sir Ronald Cohen, a pioneer of impact investing and co-founder of Apax Partners; Dr. Miriam Adelson, a physician, media publisher, and prominent businesswoman known for her global philanthropy and investments; Eyal Waldman, founder of Mellanox; Yinon Costica, co-founder of Wiz; Sean Rad, founder of Tinder and a Birthright alumnus; Amit Krig, NVIDIA's Israel site leader; former Mossad director Yossi Cohen; investor and ICON founder Yasmin Lukatz; former Microsoft Israel CEO Shelly Landsmann; author and public intellectual Dr. Micah Goodman; real-estate developer and philanthropist Danna Azrieli Hakim; and Angela Homsi, co-founder and president of Ignite Power.The program will also feature Birthright Israel alumni who have become entrepreneurs, business leaders, and investors, showing how a ten-day educational experience can create connections and opportunities that extend far beyond the trip itself.Among the participants will be Avinatan Or, an NVIDIA engineer who was abducted by Hamas from the Nova music festival on October 7, 2023, and released after 738 days in captivity.Also among the participants will be Moran Samuel, an Israeli Paralympic basketball player and world champion rower who gives lectures to Jewish communities worldwide.“For 26 years, Birthright Israel has connected the next generation of Jews to Israel while building an extraordinary global network of leaders who share a commitment to its future. The Taglit Global Business Summit is a natural extension of that mission. We are bringing this network together in Israel to turn shared values into action, foster new business partnerships, strengthen Israel's economy, and invest in the next generation. At this moment, bringing global leaders to Israel is itself a powerful statement of confidence in its future,” said Gidi Mark, Global CEO of Birthright Israel.The initiative builds on Birthright Israel's established Business Forum, which brings together nearly 60 Israeli companies, creating an additional platform for meaningful engagement between Israeli business leaders and their international counterparts.“Trust is one of the most valuable assets in business, and Birthright has spent 26 years building it across borders,” said Ethy Levy, Vice President of Global Resource Development and Partnerships at Birthright Israel. “We are bringing that network into one room, giving people who share a commitment to Israel the chance to discover what they can build together. A conversation here could become a business partnership, a philanthropic initiative, or an investment in Israel's next generation.”Program offers volunteer opportunities alongside current Birthright participantsOn November 3, participants will move beyond the conference setting for curated visits to Israeli companies, innovation centers, and communities engaged in recovery and rebuilding. The program will also offer opportunities to volunteer alongside current Birthright Israel participants and to connect global business leaders directly with communities and initiatives the organization has supported since October 7.The gathering reflects Birthright Israel's impact both on Jewish communities worldwide and on Israel's economy. Since 1999, nearly one million young Jewish adults from 70 countries have participated in Birthright Israel programs. The organization estimates that its activities have contributed approximately $2.6 billion to the Israeli economy over 26 years through travel, accommodation, and spending at local businesses.A March 2026 study by Brandeis University's Cohen Center for Modern Jewish Studies further demonstrated the organization's long-term relevance. Among politically liberal young Jews surveyed, connection to Israel increased by 60% among Birthright Israel participants, compared with a 26% decline among applicants who did not participate. The findings highlight the lasting impact of firsthand experiences in Israel on Jewish identity and connection to the global Jewish community.

title: Navantia splashes seventh Avante 2200 corvette for Saudi Arabia
body:
Spanish state-owned shipbuilding company Navantia has launched the seventh corvette built for the Royal Saudi Naval Forces at its shipyards in the Bay of Cádiz.
The naming ceremony took place on October 25, with the ship named Neom. It is the second vessel in a batch contracted in 2025, following five units built between 2019 and 2024.
The Chief of Staff of the Royal Saudi Naval Forces, Vice Admiral Mohammed Bin Abdulrahman Al-Ghuraybi , highlighted that the ship will carry a name that is one of the flagship projects of Saudi Vision 2030 and reflects the ambition of an entire Kingdom. “NEOM combines “NEO,” meaning “new,” with the letter “M,” representing His Royal Highness Prince Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud , Crown Prince and Prime Minister.
“Launching one ship every four months is in line with the industrial schedule established for the programme and reflects the commitment of Navantia’s workforce to the customer. Your dedication, experience and professional excellence allow us to say with confidence that Navantia is rigorously fulfilling the commitments it has undertaken. This ship, which will soon enter service with our customer, is yet another demonstration of this shipyard’s capabilities," Navantia’s Chairman, Ricardo Domínguez , stated.
The second batch of three corvettes is being built at the San Fernando and Puerto Real facilities, with delivery of the final ship scheduled for 2029.
Navantia will deliver the first ship in Spain and will send the second and third ships to Saudi Arabia for the installation, integration and testing of the combat system, as was the case with the fourth and fifth ships under the previous contract.
The Implementing Agreement between Royal Saudi Naval Forces and the Spanish Navy includes the provision of an integrated logistics support package and crew training, together with a period of operational evaluation of the ships by the Navy at Rota Naval Base, where Navantia will provide support services.
This second batch of three corvettes for Saudi Arabia will be identical to the first batch, according to Navantia. Their design is based on the AVANTE 2200 model, a versatile ship specifically designed for maritime traffic surveillance and control, search and rescue operations, and assistance to other ships, among other missions.
The ships will also offer capabilities for the protection of strategic assets, as well as intelligence, anti-submarine, anti-air, anti-surface and electronic warfare capabilities.

title: Where is the structure? — OK Movement questions NDC campaign council list
body: The Obi-Kwankwaso (OK) Movement has questioned the grassroots structure and preparedness of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) for the 2027 general elections following the party’s unveiling of its National Campaign Council. The Director-General of the OK Movement, John Ughulu, criticised the timing of the announcement, arguing that the party had delayed putting its campaign machinery in place and lacked the grassroots network required to prosecute a nationwide election. Ughulu stated this on Monday in a statement made available to journalists in Abuja, a day after the NDC announced the composition of its campaign council ahead of its inauguration in the Federal Capital Territory. He also boasted that the movement had established a stronger grassroots structure, predicting that some members of the newly announced council would eventually seek its support and mobilisation network. “The funny part of this list is that 90 per cent of the people on it will still come knocking on the doors of the OK Movement to beg for the very structure they have failed to build themselves!” he said. Ughulu further questioned the party’s readiness for the election, challenging its leadership to explain the delay in organising its campaign team. “With less than three months to the general elections, they are only just announcing their Presidential Campaign Council. What exactly have they been doing all this time? Where is the structure? Where is the strategy? Where is the machinery required to prosecute a serious national election?” he asked. The criticism comes amid an escalating disagreement between the NDC and the OK Movement over the movement’s organisational independence and its role in the campaign for the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso. The NDC on Sunday announced its National Campaign Council, naming its National Leader, Senator Seriake Dickson, as chairman and Obi as co-chairman. The party’s National Chairman, Senator Cleopas Moses Zuwoghe, was appointed vice-chairman, while Kwankwaso was named co-vice-chairman. Other appointees include former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Babachir Lawal, as chairman of the National Advisory Council; former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege; former presidential candidate, Pat Utomi; and former National Secretary of the Congress for Progressive Change, Buba Galadima. The NDC National Secretary, Ikenna Enekweizu, was named council secretary, while Ibrahim Abdulkarim was appointed Director-General. Ughulu and the OK Movement’s state, local government and ward coordinators were not listed among the appointees. title: Lagos targets 40% food sufficiency
body: …as BATN Foundation backs farmers By Henry Ojelu The Lagos State Government has unveiled plans to increase food sufficiency from about 20 per cent to 40 per cent of the state’s food demand through a five-year agricultural and food systems roadmap. Deputy Governor, Dr Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, disclosed this at the 2026 Eko World Food Day celebration, held at the Nigeria Police College, Ikeja, Lagos. Hamzat, who represented Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, said the roadmap would focus on agricultural infrastructure, production and processing, human capital development, innovation and farmer support. He identified the planned development of a central food security and logistics hub, middle-level agricultural produce hubs and last-mile distribution networks as key interventions to improve food availability and distribution. The deputy governor commended BATN Foundation and other development partners for supporting the state’s agricultural development agenda, stressing that sustained collaboration was essential to building a resilient, inclusive and sustainable food system. The event, organised in partnership with the Lagos State Ministry of Agriculture and Food Systems, brought together farmers, agripreneurs, financial institutions, corporate organisations, development partners and other stakeholders to discuss practical solutions to food security challenges. Held under the theme, “Innovate Today, Nourish Tomorrow,” the celebration featured exhibitions, market linkages, knowledge-sharing sessions and stakeholder engagements aimed at expanding economic opportunities across the agricultural value chain. Earlier, the Commissioner for Agriculture and Food Systems, Ms Abisola Olusanya, said the state government was strengthening the agricultural value chain through investments in training, mechanisation, processing, livestock development, aquaculture and food distribution infrastructure. Olusanya said the approach recognised agriculture as an interconnected ecosystem in which farmers, processors, traders, logistics providers, financial institutions and consumers all had critical roles to play in achieving food security. Speaking on the foundation’s partnership with the state government, Ruth Owojaiye, Board Director, BATN Foundation, said the initiative had improved the livelihoods of more than 4,000 smallholder farmers since 2019, engaged over 10,000 shoppers and generated millions of naira in income for participating farmers. She said the Eko World Food Day celebration demonstrated how partnerships could expand market access, create economic opportunities for farmers and agripreneurs, and strengthen connections across the agricultural value chain. Owojaiye disclosed that the foundation had invested more than ₦5 billion in empowerment initiatives and reached over 1.9 million beneficiaries through interventions including agricultural training, farm input support and improved access to water. She reaffirmed the foundation’s commitment to sustainable agriculture and rural development, stressing the need for sustained investment in women, young people, rural communities and smallholder farmers. According to her, providing farmers with the knowledge, resources, technology and partnerships required to participate effectively in the agricultural economy would be critical to achieving long-term food security. The 2026 Eko World Food Day celebration highlighted the role of collaboration among government, development partners, farmers and private-sector stakeholders in strengthening food systems and improving livelihoods. title: Moscow mother of eight charged with financing terrorism over payment to ISIS
body: Maria Davydova, a 31-year-old Moscow mother of eight, has been arrested on charges of financing terrorism. The case was opened in July under Russia’s criminal statute against financing terrorism, and a court authorized her arrest. Davydova was added to Russia’s list of terrorists and extremists. Citing a source in law enforcement, the Russian state news agency RIA Novosti reported in July that investigators believe Davydova transferred about 15,000 rubles to the Islamic State. Case materials cited by the Russian state news agency TASS on October 26 state that Davydova “is self-employed, has eight dependent children, including young children and minors, is not married, and has a specialized secondary education.” Russia’s criminal statute under which Davydova is charged allows for a sentence of up to life in prison. A military court will hear Davydova’s case. The trial’s start date has not been announced. At Meduza, we are committed to transparency about our use of artificial intelligence in the newsroom. title: Malaria cases surge amid acute drug shortages in West Darfur
body: The medical director of El Geneina Hospital in Sudan’s West Darfur State, Dr. Al-Shafie Salih Younis, has warned of acute shortages of malaria medication, including intravenous treatments and tablets, amid a growing influx of patients and increased demand for healthcare services. He called on international organizations operating in the health sector to urgently intervene and provide the necessary medicines. “Demand for malaria medication is high as increasing numbers of patients seek treatment at the hospital.” He said. “The shortage is exacerbating the suffering of patients and putting them at risk of deteriorating health. Mortality rates could rise if the drug shortages persist and adequate medical supplies are not secured.” Separately, Dr. Bakhit Hassan, director-general of the medical complex, warned of the serious complications malaria can cause, explaining that the disease can affect the brain, kidneys, liver and joints. “Residents should undergo medical testing and receive a proper diagnosis before taking medication because malaria symptoms can resemble those of other illnesses.” He said. Dr. Hassan also criticized what he described as disruptions in the pharmaceutical supply chain, saying some hospitals were obtaining medicines from unknown sources. He further warned that improper storage practices could cause medicines to deteriorate and lose their efficacy. He also pointed to the presence of inadequately trained healthcare personnel, stressing the need for stronger oversight of drug quality and improvements in healthcare services. The warnings come amid growing concerns over the deterioration of health conditions in West Darfur, where medicine shortages and mounting pressure on healthcare facilities underscore the urgent need for intervention to ensure access to treatment and the safety and reliability of pharmaceutical supplies. title: Ambitious plans and the need for follow-up. Aftermath of Donald Tusk’s visit to India
body:
The October visit of Donald Tusk to India appears promising, particularly in the areas of technological cooperation and the defence sector.
It was the first visit by a Polish Prime Minister to India in 16 years. Tusk had also visited the country in 2010, but at that time both Poland and India were in entirely different places. Today, Poland aspires to join the G20, while India is increasingly spoken of as soon becoming the world’s third major power. “The world looks upon us with envy, at how India is developing and at Poland’s development,” Donald Tusk said during his meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
The main topics of discussion were economic cooperation, with particular emphasis on the latest technologies and the defence sector. Both prime ministers announced that bilateral trade is to double by 2030, reaching USD 12 billion. Later, in remarks to the media, the Polish Prime Minister stated that even a tripling of trade – to USD 18 billion annually – is possible. Two Polish-Indian business forums, held in Delhi and Bengaluru, were also impressive: several hundred businesspeople from both sides met and signed more than a dozen MoUs. Poland and India are counting on the EU–India Free Trade Agreement, which is expected to be signed by the end of this year, to serve as a major instrument for developing economic relations. It will create entirely new conditions for trade.
Political issues were not the most important, although they were also raised. Poland supported UN reform in line with India’s plans, while India backed Poland’s membership in the G20. The Russian aggression against Ukraine was also mentioned – both sides expressed deepest concern over the war raging in Ukraine – as was the situation in Jammu and Kashmir, with both sides condemning in the strongest terms the terrorist attack in Pahalgam. Poland also joined the India-led Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure.
The visit represented a further step in the development of defence cooperation. Tusk emphasised that the Polish company WB Group is already present on the Indian market and operates there with considerable success, one example being the use of Polish weaponry in Operation Sindoor. The two sides agreed on more frequent contacts between working groups on armaments. Cooperation in cybersecurity, defence innovation and critical/emerging technologies was also underlined, and both sides expressed hope for the swift signing of an Agreement on Mutual Protection and Exchange of Classified Information.
The space sector was recognised by both sides as an area with strong development potential. Tusk visited Bengaluru together with representatives of the Polish Space Agency and companies from the sector (including ICEYE).
Much else also took place on the margins of the visit. The Łukasiewicz Research Network signed a letter of intent with the leading Indian institute IIT Madras and held talks with other research and development centres. A Polish-Indian Hub was established at the prestigious Jawaharlal Nehru University in Delhi, thanks to cooperation with the Faculty of Political Science and International Studies of the University of Warsaw and ITECH.
The visit was a success because it gave a clear impetus to the development of cooperation in sectors that had not previously been at the centre of Polish-Indian relations. The most important question now is whether the arrangements made during the visit will be followed up. On this depends whether the visit proves to be a real success. Doubling or even tripling bilateral trade is possible, but only with active state support – the same applies to cooperation in the field of technology. If there is no follow-up, the visit will be just one of many of its kind. If there is follow-up, the visit will prove to be a milestone.

title: Thousands of students celebrate in Belgrade after Vucic concedes in Serbia election
body: Trams and traffic halted by crowds. Tens of thousands of people choking the city's main boulevards; the air thick with smoke; a man on a car waving a flare.Familiar-sounding scenes after a month of sometimes violent protests across European cities as students take to the streets calling for better education standards and better prospects.Except on Sunday night in Serbia's capital, Belgrade, students weren't protesting but celebrating an election victory after long-time ruler Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat to a student-backed list of candidates in parliamentary elections.It was the culmination of a two-year, peaceful protest movement that called for Vucic to step down and an end to what they said is rampant corruption in the Balkan country - a charge Vucic denies.The students' win marks a profound political shift in the country of some 6 million people and shows what power the younger generation has when they are able to harness widespread discontent."That is the best thing that happened in my life. We will now breathe freely," said Milica, a law student.Vucic faces opposition after railway station awning collapseVucic had ruled as prime minister or president since 2014, and oversaw a period of strong economic growth, but he faced growing opposition from student-led protests after the collapse of a railway station awning killed 16 people in November 2024.Tomorrow, the disparate group of 250 student-backed candidates will have to turn towards ruling, but Sunday evening was a time to party.At their headquarters, the unknown candidates, many of them lawyers, professors, actors, or farmers, hugged and cheered in near disbelief at what they had achieved."The people have won! The people defeated a dictator! The people will lead Serbia!" said Nebojsa Cosic while waving a flag on the street.

title: Gov Radda Pledges Sustained Investment As Katsina Records Decline In Malnutrition Cases
body: Katsina State Governor, Malam Dikko Umaru Radda, has reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to sustained investment in nutrition and healthcare, pledging to consolidate the significant progress recorded in reducing malnutrition across the state. Governor Radda gave the assurance on Sunday while receiving nutrition partners operating in Katsina State, led by the Executive Director of the Katsina State Development Management Board (KATDMB), Hajiya Ruqqaya Hamza, at the Government House, Katsina. The Governor said his administration would continue to prioritise nutrition as a critical component of human capital development, while calling on development partners to sustain technical assistance and institutional support to further strengthen the state’s healthcare and nutrition systems. He stressed the need for development organisations to align with the state’s recruitment policy by giving priority to qualified Katsina indigenes in the implementation of their programmes. According to him, building local capacity and integrating skilled professionals into government institutions remain essential for ensuring the long-term sustainability of development interventions. Governor Radda pointed to the Katsina State Development Management Board as an example of the success of such collaborations, noting that several of its personnel were beneficiaries of capacity-building initiatives supported by development partners. He encouraged the organisations to expand investments in human capital development to strengthen local institutions. Earlier, representatives of the nutrition partners presented updates on their interventions across the state during an interactive session. Governor Radda, on Sunday, October 25, 2026, while receiving nutrition partners operating in Katsina State, led by the Executive Director of the Katsina State Development Management Board (KATDMB), Hajiya Ruqqaya Hamza, at the Government House, Katsina. They reported a significant decline in malnutrition cases compared to the previous year, attributing the improvement to the Katsina State Government’s increased investment, strong leadership and unwavering political commitment to nutrition. The partners commended Governor Radda for placing nutrition high on the state’s development agenda and for committing substantial resources to the sector. They also called for deeper collaboration to sustain the gains already achieved and further improve nutrition outcomes across Katsina State. The meeting was attended by representatives of UNICEF, Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF), ALIMA, International Rescue Committee (IRC), JHPIEGO, Première Urgence Internationale (PUI), International Medical Corps (IMC), Médecins du Monde (MDM), Helen Keller International (HKI), Nutrition International, Save the Children/CGPP and Action Against Hunger. The post Gov Radda Pledges Sustained Investment As Katsina Records Decline In Malnutrition Cases appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Russian forces strike firefighters twice as they battle blaze in Odesa region
body:
According to Ukrinform, Ukraine’s State Emergency Service reported this on Facebook .
“An overnight enemy attack destroyed an industrial facility, where a fire broke out. While firefighters were battling the blaze, Russian forces carried out two follow-up strikes directly on the site where they were working,” the statement said.
The rescuers took shelter and were unharmed. However, firefighting and rescue equipment was damaged.
At another location, four garages were damaged, a fire broke out and a passenger car was destroyed.
According to preliminary information, there were no deaths or injuries. More than 50 emergency responders worked at the sites.
As Ukrinform reported, Russian forces attacked an industrial facility and a garage cooperative in the Odesa region overnight, sparking fires.

title: How to track insertions in House-approved 2027 budget
body: MANILA, Philippines – The People’s Budget Coalition (PBC) and BetterGovPH on Monday, October 26, launched a website that allows the public to track budget increases for congressional districts in the proposed 2027 national budget, including allocations for infrastructure projects. “We’re launching budget insertions tracker in better.gov.ph so that every taxpayer, every voter, every Filipino can be empowered to demand that their legislators explain insertions in their district,” PBC co-convenor Ken Abante said during the Senate finance committee hearing on Monday. With this tracker, Abante said the public can determine which districts got the biggest budget insertions and the biggest budget cuts. You can check their dashboard here . Based on their analysis, the district of Ilocos Norte 1st District Representative Sandro Marcos, son of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., received the largest budget increase for infrastructure projects among congressional districts in the House of Representatives. Must Read House increases DPWH budget for Sandro Marcos’ district by P4.3B – watchdog During the hearing, Abante also flagged nearly 7,000 projects worth P190 billion without published project attachments in the House-approved 2027 budget. PBC also found the following insertions made by the House of Representatives: 6,200 Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) projects worth 170 million, many of which are for multi-purpose buildings More than 200 irrigation projects worth P7 billion More than 180 new health facilities worth more than P2 billion 315 new farm-to-market roads worth P6 billion. Abante noted that their analysis has yet to include proposed classrooms in 2027. PBC also earlier flagged several farm-to-market roads in the proposed budget, with coordinates pointing to the sea. – Rappler.com

title: Army drone deal widened to cover heavier aircraft
body: The Ministry of Defence intends to raise the maximum take-off weight allowed under the British Army’s mini drone contract from twenty kilograms to fifty, and to confirm that the contract covers flights beyond visual line of sight, without running a new competition, according to a transparency notice published by the department. The TIQUILA contract was awarded to Lockheed Martin UK on 7 December 2022 and is worth £129,350,000 excluding VAT. It runs for one hundred and twenty months, with options to extend by up to a further twenty four months and to vary the volume of goods and services delivered. The notice says the department proposes “to broaden the contractual technical envelope so that TIQUILA can continue to procure and integrate relevant UAS capability as technology and operational demands evolve” , and that the change will “confirm the inclusion of VLOS and BVLOS Packable MUAS capability” and “increase the platform take-off weight from a maximum of 20kg to 50kg” . Arguing that it can make the change without a fresh procurement, the department says: “The modification does not change the contract into a requirement for a different category of capability. The requirement remains focused on UAS capability supporting field operations through the existing SI-led model, while accommodating unanticipated technological advancement beyond the parameters originally defined.” It goes on: “It preserves the commercial model, of engagement with the wider UAS market and new entrants through flexible supply-chain arrangements; supports the same field-operational purposes and retains the same SI-led integration, modular architecture and through-life delivery model, while responding to technological advancement and developing operational demands in the manner contemplated by the original procurement, and is therefore considered a vertical evolution of the existing UAS capability, rather than horizontal expansion.” The department says all pricing mechanisms stay the same, that it considers the change a permissible non-material modification under the principles established in the Pressetext case and the Defence and Security Public Contracts Regulations 2011, and that it published the notice voluntarily to provide transparency. TIQUILA delivers mini uncrewed air systems for intelligence, surveillance, target acquisition and reconnaissance in packable and portable loads, with Lockheed Martin UK acting as systems integrator and bringing in other suppliers through enabling arrangements intended to reach new entrants, industry and academia. The original scope required a modular technical and digital architecture built on open-standard interfaces so that new capabilities could be integrated as they emerged. The aircraft bought under the programme so far are the Stalker VXE 30, a near-silent long-endurance machine weighing under twenty kilograms, and the Indago, a backpack-sized aircraft under eight kilograms that can be put in the air in around two minutes. Ninety nine Stalkers and fifteen Indagos were ordered, deliveries began in March 2023, and full operational capability for four Future Soldier batteries was expected this year, as this publication reported when the contract was signed . Brigadier Pete Drew, the Army’s senior responsible owner for the programme, said at the time that “TIQUILA will bring the next generation of remotely piloted air systems into service in the Army” , and that it would speed up decision making and make the force more lethal, responsive and resilient. Raising the ceiling to fifty kilograms takes the contract past the weight of anything currently flying under it and into a class of aircraft carrying heavier sensors and flying longer. Louise Sandher-Jones, the Minister for the Armed Forces, told Parliament this week that military flights beyond visual line of sight use temporary segregated airspace notified through the warning system pilots check before flying, or permanent segregated airspace such as danger areas, with the Civil Aviation Authority responsible for United Kingdom airspace throughout. The post Army drone deal widened to cover heavier aircraft first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Plane parts for Russia’s air force, rubber for its industry—Voronezh’s factories came under drone attack
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Drones attacked the VASO aircraft plant in Russia's Voronezh overnight on 26 October, Ukrainian Telegram channel Supernova+ reported . The plant builds Il-96 airliners and parts for Russia's military transport planes. A synthetic-rubber plant was also reportedly hit and fires broke out across Voronezh, while another rubber plant in Tolyatti, farther east, reportedly came under attack again. Ukraine keeps hitting the plants behind Russia's weapons, from Voronezh's missile chips to Urals titanium for warplanes. Each supplier knocked out of rhythm slows how fast Russia replaces the hardware it loses and keeps using against Ukraine. What the Voronezh plant builds Supernova+ described VASO as part of Ilyushin, which belongs to Russia's state-owned United Aircraft Corporation (UAC). The channel published a photo of fire and smoke at the site. The plant lies about 190 km from the Ukrainian border. VASO makes pylons, engine nacelles, and flap rails for the Il-76MD-90A, a modernized military transport plane, and sends them to Ulyanovsk, UAC's press service said in 2024. " We have reached the production pace of Il-76MD-90A aircraft kits that our Ulyanovsk colleagues need ," Igor Butyrin, who runs the plant's Il-76 program, stated at the time. In 2016, the plant built an Il-96-300 that UAC handed over to the Rossiya special flight detachment of Russia's presidential property office. Map of Ukrainian drone strikes on Voronezh and Tolyatti with distances from Ukraine, Russia, 26 October 2026. Map: EP/Datawrapper A rubber plant and a bridge on the list too Supernova+ also named Voronezhsintezkauchuk, a plant of Russian petrochemical group Sibur that makes synthetic rubbers. The channel later reported a hit on the plant's industrial zone and claimed an attack on the city's Northern Bridge. Ukrainian Telegram channel Exilenova+ published footage of a drone arriving, reportedly at the rubber plant. The moment the UAV arrived this morning, reportedly at the Voronezhsintezkauchuk factory. pic.twitter.com/2PXyQ5P7sb — Exilenova+ (@Exilenova_plus) October 26, 2026 Voronezh Oblast Governor Aleksandr Gusev declared a missile alert at 04:47 Kyiv time, but no source has named a missile type. Kyiv has not commented. Ukraine's Air Force, which launches Storm Shadow cruise missiles, and its Navy, which fires Neptunes, have posted nothing on Voronezh. Earlier this month, Ukraine's Navy said it hit six Su-34 bombers in Voronezh Oblast with Neptunes. Storm Shadows reportedly struck an electronics plant in Oryol on 23 October and a battery plant in Yelets two days later. Fires across the city Gusev claimed air defenses downed 113 drones over the region, more than 70 of them over the city. He listed fires at several industrial enterprises, which he said caused no serious consequences, plus a business center, an apartment block, and a school stadium. Russian Telegram channel Astra published video of a drone hitting the Galereya Chizhova business center. Exilenova+ footage showed cars burning below apartment blocks. Voronezh pic.twitter.com/I3WbnGLZhO — Exilenova+ (@Exilenova_plus) October 26, 2026 Damage in residential districts may have come from downed drones or from Russian air-defense missiles falling back on the city. During a 23 October attack on Gorodets, in Nizhny Novgorod Oblast, Exilenova+ claimed a Pantsir air-defense missile hit a house. Explore further Russia still parks its best bombers in the open. Ukraine has spent a year knocking out the air defenses that were supposed to protect them Gusev also claimed two men were killed and 17 people injured, many of them on a train struck by drone debris. Russian Railways said five passengers were hurt at Somovo station and traffic on the line stopped. Russia's Defense Ministry claimed its air defenses downed 290 drones over 15 regions and the Moscow area. Tolyatti's rubber plant reportedly attacked again Locals reported an attack on the Tolyattikauchuk chemical plant in Tolyatti, Samara Oblast, Exilenova+ said . The city lies about 890 km from the front line. Ukraine's General Staff confirmed a strike on the same plant on 24 October. Its synthetic rubbers go into solid fuel for Russia's tactical and ballistic missiles, among other uses. Until Kyiv comments or satellite imagery shows the site, the damage at VASO stays unconfirmed, and so does any delay to Russia's Il-76 parts line. title: Zelensky Says Ukraine Wants to Keep 800,000-Troop Army, Rules Out Neutrality
body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine should maintain an army of 800,000 personnel to ensure its security, adding that the size of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) is an internal matter that will not be negotiated with Russia or the US.
In an interview with Alla Mazur, host of TSN.Tyzhden (TSN.The Week), Zelensky said the key question was how Ukraine’s military would be funded and what security guarantees the country would receive as part of any peace settlement.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“If I have sufficient funding, I want to maintain an army of 800,000 people. If we are in NATO, the number could be 800,000 or less,” he said.
According to Zelensky, the central issue is who is prepared to finance Ukraine’s armed forces.
“And that is my question for NATO,” he added.
Zelensky also said Starlink had resumed operating in Ukraine and that the country was once again receiving uninterrupted intelligence on ballistic missiles following what he described as productive talks in Oslo.
He said Ukrainian intelligence on ballistic missile strikes was now functioning at 100% capacity.
“The dialogue between Ukraine and the US – which had become quite emotional – has returned to a functional state. Starlink is back up and running (as of Saturday, Oct. 24, at 5:20 a.m.). We achieved the right outcome; we secured what we needed. This was one component of our discussions in Oslo,” Zelensky said.
He revealed that tensions in the dialogue with Washington had centered on three main issues: shortages of air defense systems, operational restrictions on Starlink, and limitations on the intelligence provided by the US.
Two of those issues have now been resolved, Zelensky said, although the provision of additional air defense systems remains unresolved.
Zelensky also discussed a document containing US proposals for ending Russia’s war against Ukraine that US special envoy Steve Witkoff delivered to Russian President Vladimir Putin.
According to Zelensky, the document contains various proposals from Washington, but Ukraine has made clear that two issues are non-negotiable: the country’s neutrality and restrictions on its armed forces.
“The document contains various proposals from the American side. We maintain that key aspects of this are that there can be no discussion of our state adopting neutrality, nor can there be any talk of placing restrictions on the Ukrainian army,” Zelensky said.
He did not disclose whether Ukraine’s red lines were explicitly spelled out in the document, saying that agreements with the US prevented him from sharing all the details.
However, Zelensky reiterated that Russia cannot dictate the terms of Ukraine’s security guarantees.
“Therefore, restrictions on our army and the neutrality of Ukraine are not up for discussion. The issue of territory is a ‘red line’ that can only be addressed at the level of the leaders themselves. For us, this has always been a non-negotiable constant,” he said.
“Yet, the Americans frequently raise the question of territory – asking what we might be willing to trade in exchange for certain fundamental principles,” Zelensky added.
Zelensky stressed that Ukraine does not intend to give up territory but remains open to discussions.
He said territorial questions must be addressed directly by the leaders, while other issues could be handled by technical groups.
“If the discussion concerns the territorial issue, it must take place at the level of leaders. Other matters should be handled by technical groups. What constitutes ‘other matters’? Security guarantees. For instance, the issue of NATO – which, naturally, appears in relevant documents and new proposals – is one such matter,” Zelensky said.
“We are discussing security guarantees; someone must provide assurances that Russia will not launch a new act of aggression,” he added.
According to Zelensky, Ukraine expects such guarantees from the US and Europe.
He also stressed that the document delivered by Witkoff was not a plan simply presented to Putin for approval.
“It is not Russia that makes the decision; all parties involved do. There are proposals for discussion – including those from the American side – which are being discussed with us,” Zelensky said.
Asked by Mazur what Putin would need to do to demonstrate that he genuinely intended to end the war, Zelensky pointed to an energy truce as a possible first step.
“This would be a signal. If that doesn’t happen, then we look to a trilateral meeting at the level of leaders,” he said.
Zelensky believes such a meeting involving Ukraine, the US, and Russia is possible. However, he cautioned that Putin’s apparent willingness to resume negotiations does not guarantee that the Kremlin will follow through.
However, he suggested that Moscow could be feigning readiness for dialogue to avoid further confrontation with US President Donald Trump.
Zelensky said it was too early to judge the outcome of a potential leaders’ meeting before it took place.
“One should discuss the outcome ‘after’ the meeting in question, not ‘before’ it. What will unfold there? What escalatory developments might arise in the Middle East? Will this meeting take place in Abu Dhabi, or perhaps in Europe? We shall see,” he said.
Zelensky added that he did not know what had prompted Putin’s sudden shift in position on peace negotiations.
“What influenced this? I cannot say. Perhaps there are some agreements between America and Russia of which I am unaware,” he said.
Ukraine is prepared to participate in trilateral negotiations involving technical groups, Zelensky added, but he stressed that the talks must produce concrete results.
He recalled that the American side had asked what specific outcomes Ukraine wanted to see.
“The Americans asked me, ‘What kind of specifics are you looking for?’ I replied, ‘Look, could the war end in November during a meeting of the technical group?’ Without the leaders present, it won’t be a complete resolution,” Zelensky said.
He then outlined several alternatives that could produce tangible progress even without a comprehensive peace agreement.
“Fine – if that’s not on the table, then let’s have an ‘energy truce,’ address the maritime situation and grain exports, carry out an ‘all-for-all’ prisoner exchange, or hold a meeting of the leaders. That, undoubtedly, constitutes a result. A result creates opportunity,” he added.
Zelensky added that these were proposals put forward to the American side, not demands.
He said it should become clear in November whether Putin was genuinely prepared to negotiate or was merely making political gestures to avoid escalating tensions with Washington ahead of the elections.
“And if this is merely a political stunt – if Putin is simply saying ‘Yes, I’m ready’ because he wants to avoid escalation with America ahead of the elections – we will find out very quickly in November whether it was a ruse or not,” Zelensky said.
Zelensky also said the US had proposed a ceasefire in the Oleshky area starting Tuesday, Oct. 27 and lasting several days to facilitate a humanitarian mission.
Under the proposal, representatives of Ukraine, the US, and Russia would travel to the area. Russian forces would be expected to clear roads of mines, while Ukraine would verify the work and carry out the necessary measures.
Zelensky said he had issued specific instructions to Ukraine’s ombudsman and that the government had also consulted the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) and the military.
He cautioned, however, that Russia could clear the roads in a way that directs people toward Russian-controlled territory, rather than allowing them to leave freely.
Zelensky said some people would nevertheless be evacuated to Ukrainian-controlled territory.
“The main thing is to unblock these people so that they can live. Ideally, they will be able to reach their goal and be evacuated here – to us, to Ukraine,” he said.
Julia is a Deputy Head of News and correspondent for Kyiv Post who has previously worked as a parliamentary editor, journalist, and news editor. She has specialized in covering the work of the Ukrainian parliament, government, and law enforcement agencies.

title: Russia Won’t Negotiate Seriously While It Thinks It Can Force Ukraine to Surrender, Sybiha Says
body:
Russia will not engage in serious peace talks as long as it believes it can force Ukraine to surrender through pressure what it has failed to achieve on the battlefield, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said on Monday, Oct. 26.
“As long as Russia believes it can achieve the goals of its invasion – goals it cannot achieve on the battlefield – by having anyone pressure Ukraine into capitulation, it will not engage in serious negotiations,” Sybiha said in a statement published by Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry .
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“Peace through strength is the only strategy that works. But that strength must be directed against the aggressor, not the country defending itself,” he added.
“This war cannot be ended by stopping Ukraine’s resistance. It can only be ended by stopping the aggressor’s attacks.”
Sybiha was responding to remarks by Yuri Ushakov, an aide to Russian President Vladimir Putin, who complained that Washington had failed to pressure Kyiv into accepting a peace deal.
Ushakov said Moscow had initially expected the US to be able to impose its terms on Ukraine following the Trump-Putin summit in Alaska . He argued that negotiations should also involve European countries.
Ushakov said Sunday, Oct. 25, that Russia was prepared to resume trilateral negotiations with Ukraine and the US after Nov. 4, but described the next meeting as preliminary, playing down expectations of a breakthrough.
The proposed talks could take place in Abu Dhabi or Switzerland in the first half of November, according to media reports. Zelensky has also named Abu Dhabi as a possible venue.
On Oct. 21, Zelensky said Kyiv had received a signal from Washington that Moscow was ready to resume trilateral talks. However, the proposed meeting’s timing and agenda remained under discussion.
The diplomatic push comes amid deep disagreements over the terms of a settlement. Moscow continues to demand territorial concessions, while Kyiv rejects any agreement that would undermine Ukraine’s sovereignty or leave it vulnerable to another Russian invasion.
Zelensky has said Ukraine is ready to stop the fighting along the current front line but insists that a lasting settlement must include credible security guarantees against renewed Russian aggression.
In an Sunday, Oct. 24 address outlining Ukraine’s conditions for peace , he called for firm US and European security commitments, a strong Ukrainian military backed by at least 10 years of international funding, and a ceasefire before broader negotiations.
Kyiv has also warned against easing sanctions on Russia or offering concessions without safeguards against another invasion.
Sybiha’s remarks come as Kyiv faces renewed uncertainty over US military support.
On Oct. 17, Zelensky said Starlink speeds in Ukraine had been capped at 161 kph (100 mph), making the system unusable for some interceptor drones designed to destroy Russian jet-powered Shahed attack drones, and endangering Ukraine’s ability to intercept Russian attacks.
“When an Iranian drone goes with a speed of 450 or 500 kph [280 to 311 mph], and you limit [the speed] one night to 70 or even 100, you cannot intercept anything,” Zelensky told CNN. “And this is terrible.”
Zelensky said Ukraine does not use Starlink to attack Russian military or energy targets inside Russia.
“We don’t attack Russian military targets or energy targets using Starlink. Never,” he said. “That’s why it was strange they limited us in Ukraine. It means limiting our ability to defend ourselves.”
The inability to intercept Russian drones effectively has become a major threat to Ukrainian cities and infrastructure.
On Saturday, Oct. 23, Zelensky added that restrictions on Starlink and Starshield satellite communications remained in place and that agreed deliveries of Patriot interceptor missiles were delayed.
He has described the restrictions and delays as attempts to pressure Ukraine into capitulation. Washington has not publicly confirmed that the measures were intended to force Kyiv to surrender.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Netanyahu must face treason probe over reported Iran plot to delay election, Liberman says
body: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu must be investigated on suspicion of treason, Yisrael Beytenu chairman Avigdor Liberman told 103FM on Monday morning.Calling on Attorney-General Gali Baharv-Miara to open a criminal probe, Liberman accused Netanyahu of attempting to draw Israel into a military confrontation to delay the elections, or prevent them from taking place.The demand follows a report by N12 on Sunday that Netanyahu and IDF Chief of Staff Lt.-Gen. Eyal Zamir had clashed over a proposed military operation that could trigger a confrontation with Iran, just two days before Israel's October 27 election.Liberman accuses Netanyahu of attempting to delay electionsIn a statement published on X/Twitter on Sunday, Liberman said he believed Netanyahu was attempting to force Israel into military action to prevent the vote, describing the alleged conduct as a betrayal of the state and its security.He further argued that the chief of staff had a responsibility to prevent the military from being used for political purposes and to protect soldiers from unnecessary risks.Speaking to 103FM, Liberman said he would approach the attorney-general to request a criminal investigation into Netanyahu on treason allegations."The man has gone off the rails. One day he's preparing a crypto bomb for us, and the next day an atomic bomb. He just said he had destroyed all of Iran's bombs, and now he's dropping bombs on Tel Aviv?" Liberman said, adding that the relationship between the military and political leadership has "never been as strained" as it is now."This is the result of Netanyahu's efforts to provoke a miscalculation with Iran. The chief of staff is strong enough to insist on upholding the law, and under the law, any action whose consequences could lead the State of Israel into war or a large-scale confrontation must be subject to a government discussion and decision," he said.Katz: No strain between IDF and political leadershipDefense Minister Israel Katz decried Liberman's accusation, stating there was no strain between the IDF and political leadership."Since taking office as Defense Minister, the coordination between the prime minister and me and the IDF on the Iran issue has been complete - with unprecedented historic achievements for the security of the State of Israel. This is the sole consideration - and so it will be in the future as well," he said.הפרסומים על פערים בין הדרג המדיני לצה"ל בנושא איראן הם מופרכים ושקריים לחלוטין. מאז כניסתי לתפקיד שר הביטחון התיאום בין רה"מ וביני לבין צה"ל בנושא איראן הוא מלא - עם הישגים היסטוריים חסרי תקדים לטובת ביטחון מדינת ישראל. זהו השיקול היחיד - וכך יהיה גם בעתיד. אני קובע באופן חד משמעי שלא הייתה שום כוונה של ישראל ליזום התקפה על איראן לפני הבחירות בישראל - כאשר הבהרנו שבמידה ואיראן תתקוף את ישראל נגיב בעוצמה רבה, וכל הפרסומים בעניין שקריים לחלוטין. הניסיון של אנשי האופוזיציה לנצל את הפרסומים האלה כדי לתקוף את רה"מ ואותי ולהטיל דופי בשיקולינו - בשעה שאנחנו מנועים מסיבות מובנות מלהתייחס לפרטי הסוגיה האיראנית - הוא מביש וחסר אחריות. נתגבר גם על זה.— ישראל כ”ץ Israel Katz (@Israel_katz) October 26, 2026"I state unequivocally that there was no intention on Israel's part to initiate an attack on Iran before the elections in Israel - when we made clear that if Iran attacks Israel, we will respond with great force, and all reports on the matter are entirely false. The attempt by opposition figures to exploit these reports to attack the prime minister and me and to cast doubt on our judgment - at a time when we are prevented for understandable reasons from addressing the details of the Iranian issue - is shameful and irresponsible. We will overcome this too."

title: Will 70,000 Israelis returning from abroad for Election Day tip the political balance? - analysis
body: An estimated 70,000 Israelis living abroad have returned or are expected to return to Israel ahead of Tuesday's Knesset elections, potentially influencing the results if the race between the political blocs is close.This begs the question: Could the Israelis arriving from abroad influence the election results?In the 2022 elections, approximately 36,000 votes were needed to secure one Knesset seat. Given population growth and an expected increase in voter turnout, estimates suggest that the threshold for a seat could rise to approximately 38,000 to 39,000 votes.It is difficult to determine which parties most of the Israelis arriving from abroad will support. Some estimates suggest that many will vote for the change bloc, but there is no reliable measure of their political preferences.Even if, for example, 60% support the change bloc, this would add at most one to one-and-a-half Knesset seats.These figures, however, remain estimates. The election results will reveal whether Israelis living abroad have tipped the balance in the event of a close race between the political blocs.Election Day boosts hotel occupancy by 23%The vast majority of Israelis arriving from overseas are combining family visits and vacations with Election Day. Most are staying with relatives or friends, or in apartments they own in Israel that are currently vacant.However, some have chosen to stay in hotels.Africa Israel Hotels reported an approximately 23% increase in hotel occupancy during election week. Although the comparison is with October of last year, when the security situation was more complicated, the increase appears significant."We are seeing an increase in occupancy at Africa Israel Hotels properties across the country ahead of Election Day. We are seeing more Israelis choosing to combine exercising their democratic right with a short vacation, taking advantage of the opportunity to break from their routine and enjoy a hotel stay," said Alex Eliyahu, marketing director of Africa Israel Hotels."Alongside the increase in demand, the chain is offering particularly attractive promotions and accommodation packages for Election Day, allowing guests to enjoy vacations at a variety of destinations across the country at affordable prices."Fattal Hotels also reported an increase in room occupancy at its properties, particularly in central Israel."We are seeing an increase in bookings compared with October of last year, apparently due to the elections," said Maya Shalev, vice president of marketing and sales at Fattal Hotels."Many Israelis are taking advantage of the day off to combine voting with a vacation. Accordingly, we have offered promotions of up to 30% off, along with an additional 10% discount for members of the 'Fattal and Friends' club between October 25 and 29. At the same time, we are seeing bookings made from abroad for these dates, which may indicate that Israelis are coming to Israel to vote."'I came from Miami to vote': Israelis returning to the ballot boxAmong the tens of thousands who attended the October Council rally at Hostages Square in Tel Aviv on Saturday night were Israelis living abroad."I came from Miami to vote. I coordinated my vacation in Israel with Election Day, and I'm returning to the US at the beginning of November," said Judy, who has lived in the US for more than 50 years."Many Israelis living in Miami and Los Angeles tend to vote for the Right. I'm different, and I'm not alone."Nurit, from the South Sharon area, attended the rally with her son-in-law and grandson, who had arrived from Canada."My grandson is voting for the first time. He's 18 years old. They're combining a family visit with voting in the elections. My daughter stayed in Canada to be with my younger grandson."Ofer, who arrived from New York, also shared his experience."We came to Israel specifically to vote. We're returning to the US the day after the elections. We have family here, and it's an opportunity to see everyone."Gidi, who arrived from Australia with his wife, is scheduled to fly out of Ben-Gurion Airport on Wednesday."We've already been here for three weeks. We've met with many family members and friends. And I'm going back on Wednesday because I have work commitments. My wife will stay here for another two weeks."In contrast, Zehava, who arrived on a flight from New York, said: "I'm voting for Likud, and I came to visit family ahead of the elections. I planned it in advance."Canceled flights leave some Israelis unable to voteSome Israelis had hoped to travel to Israel but were left stranded abroad after flydubai canceled flights following an attempted terrorist attack."Flydubai's cancellation caused flight prices to the Far East to rise," explained a young man who had planned to travel to Israel ahead of the elections.There are also Israelis who live in Israel but will be abroad on Election Day. However, their number appears to be lower than the number of Israelis arriving from overseas."I booked the flight tickets for a vacation with my husband in Vietnam almost a year ago, and we didn't know the elections would be held in October. This will be the first time I don't vote. It breaks my heart, but we're going ahead with the vacation we started planning a year ago," said Racheli from Ramat Gan."It's a shame that Israelis traveling abroad can't vote on Election Day."

title: RFE/RL: 16 more air defense towers spotted near Putin’s Valdai residence, bringing total to about 50 — nearly half the number in Moscow and its outskirts
body: At least 15 new towers appeared in October within a 50-kilometer radius (31 miles) of Vladimir Putin’s residence in Valdai, likely intended to carry Pantsir or Tor surface-to-air missile systems, RFE/RL’s Russian service reported, citing satellite images it examined. 1/19v It is autumn in Valdai, and time for the latest manifestation of Putin’s paranoia. A new air defense ring of ~16 SHORAD towers so far, was constructed in September. The total number of towers for the protection of Valdai is now 49 or 50. ⚠️the towers are not yet confirmed! pic.twitter.com/hRlnohwthP — jembob 🇺🇦 (@jembobineuse) October 25, 2026 A ring of towers appeared south of the residence, facing Ukraine, according to the journalists. One tower in the “outer ring” was built as early as March 2026 on the grounds of the Khotilovo military base, which is connected to the residence by a dedicated railway line that allows travel by train. According to an OSINT analyst who posts on X under the handle @jembobineuse , Russia now has about 177 towers equipped with short-range air defense systems. About 98 are in and around Moscow, and about 50 are near the residence in Valdai. Russian authorities claimed that more than 90 Ukrainian drones attempted to attack Putin’s residence in Valdai in late December 2025. Ukraine denies attempting such an attack. The CIA concluded that the target of the Ukrainian drone attack in the Novgorod region was an unspecified “military facility” not located near Putin’s residence. The first air defense system near Putin’s residence in Valdai appeared in January 2023, and a second arrived in July 2024. By April 2026, satellite images examined by RFE/RL’s Russian service showed that at least 27 air defense units already ringed the residence.
