title: Two Minors Detained, Charged Over Alleged Plot to Attack Tbilisi School
body: Two minors were detained and charged with preparing to organize and participate in group violence over an alleged plot to attack a school in Tbilisi, facing six to nine years in prison if convicted. “An investigation conducted by the Ministry of Internal Affairs established that the defendants met through social media in April and May 2026 and planned to organize and participate in an attack on a school involving vandalism and violence,” Georgia’s Prosecutor’s Office said in an October 25 statement. “Specifically, they selected a particular school in Tbilisi, studied its internal layout and decided to place a fake explosive device in front of the school,” the statement said, adding that the plan would have allowed them to “enter the school unnoticed, vandalize its premises, and use weapons to inflict injuries on people inside.” According to prosecutors, the minors purchased various items and made preparations to carry out the attack, but “were unable to carry out their plan because their activities were uncovered by law enforcement officers.” According to Sandro Tskharo [“Reliable Source”], a recently established local independent media outlet, the two 14-year-olds communicated through video calls, Telegram and TikTok. The outlet cited the father of one of the detainees as saying that the teenagers had discussed the 2011 terrorist attack in Norway and feature films based on real events depicting acts of violence. The father also told Sando Tskaro that law enforcement officers seized a starter pistol, ammunition, pepper spray, gloves, a helmet and a knife during a search. The minors were charged under Articles 18 and 225 of Georgia’s Criminal Code, covering preparation to commit a crime and organizing or participating in group violence. One of the minors has been remanded in custody as a pretrial measure, while prosecutors said they would ask a court to impose a pretrial measure on the second defendant “within the timeframe prescribed by law.” Also Read: 25/09/2026 – Suspect With ‘Nazi-Fascist’ Group Links Detained Over Abuse of Minors 07/07/2026 – Minor With ‘Fascist-Nazi’ Ideology Sentenced to 14.5 Years for Organized Group Torture, Violence, Prosecutors Say 02/06/2026 – Three More Prison Sentences Handed Down in Murder Case of Teacher Giga Avaliani 26/11/2025 – GD’s Controversial Juvenile Justice Bill Could Place Minors in Closed Facilities

title: Thailand receives IWI's ARBEL anti-drone solution
body: As Thailand approved a $104.4 million emergency defense fund to buy military equipment and reinforce defenses along the Cambodian border, IWI (Israel Weapon Industries) announced it delivered its ARBEL Anti-Drone System (ADS) to Thailand's Defense Ministry.Thai forces have integrated the platform into their existing rifles after troops received on-site training from company officials.Developed by IWI after close to a decade of design work, the fire control technology transforms standard infantry rifles into precision-guided interceptors.“Small tactical drones have become a direct and growing threat to soldiers on the battlefield. We developed the ARBEL ADS to give soldiers an effective means of defending themselves against this evolving threat, while providing armed forces with a critical tactical advantage in an increasingly complex battlespace,” said SK Group's vice chairman Ronen Hamudot.Integrated directly into the AR-15 platform and IWI's own ARAD assault rifles and Negev machine guns, ARBEL allows soldiers to engage threats, including aerial ones, using their existing weapons, optics, and ammunition with no additional gear required. Depending on the selected firing mode, it can hit targets up to 450 meters away using standard 5.56 mm ammunition.With electronic sensors and gyros, it simplifies the shooting cycle after the initial shot and enables effective target engagement within a window of opportunity of several seconds, typical of real combat situations. According to IWI, it significantly improves efficiency and lethality by increasing hit probability for static and moving threats by two to three times.Depending on the platform, the ARBEL system can be integrated into the lower receiver of the A-15 or mounted as an external unit on the grip of the Negev machine gun. The system adds only 900 grams to the weapon and meets MIL-STD-810 military standards, ensuring reliability under extreme environmental conditions. The Thai forces chose to integrate the system onto their existing rifles, which, according to the company, “enables militaries to upgrade their existing platforms locally without replacing their rifle inventories or procuring entirely new weapons.”Battery-operated, ARBEL's power supply allows for 50 hours of continuous operation. It's optic-agnostic, mission-configurable, and its built-in fire control system releases rounds when the shooter is stable on the target, depending on the operational scenario. IWI told Defense & Tech by The Jerusalem Post that the system compensates for and mitigates shooting errors typical of combative scenarios such as heavy breathing, fatigue, and stress. “As Southeast Asian militaries place greater emphasis on counter-drone capabilities, Thailand's adoption of ARBEL ADS reflects this growing operational priority. We see rising demand across the region for solutions that can help soldiers meet this challenge,” said SK Group vice president Doron Korol, who oversees the Asia-Pacific region.According to the company, Thai military officials are in discussions with IWI about an additional order for the ARBEL ADS, and several other countries are at various stages of the procurement process. The company expects to announce additional deployments of the solution in the coming months.Modernization plansEarlier in October, local media reported that Bangkok approved emergency defense funding to repair combat-damaged gear and purchase new weapons, including long-range Rampage standoff missiles manufactured by Elbit Systems and Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI), along with bunker-buster bombs and High Mobility Artillery Rocket System (HIMARS) artillery upgrades.According to a report in The Nation, the Royal Thai Air Force's procurement plan includes 20 Israeli Rampage missiles, with an estimated value of approximately $30 million (1.04 billion baht), for use with the country's F-16 fighter aircraft along with Elbit's MPR-500 penetrating bombs and Lizard III laser guidance kits. Under the modernization plan, the Royal Thai Army will procure HIMARS and M777 howitzers to replace older artillery, along with Stryker armored vehicles.Thailand has been acquiring Israeli defense technology since the 1970s, and the relationship has only grown stronger with the transfer of knowledge to locally manufacture and produce certain weapons systems.

title: Russian forces pound Ukrainian logistics hubs, energy, port sites in overnight strike
body:
MOSCOW, October 26. /TASS/. Russian forces delivered an overnight strike on Ukraine’s logistics hubs, energy facilities and port infrastructure used to support the Ukrainian army’s operations, Russia’s Defense Ministry reported.
TASS has put together key facts about the targets of the strikes.
- During the past night, the Russian Armed Forces continued delivering strikes by unmanned aerial vehicles against logistics centers, energy facilities powering their operation and also ports in Ukraine and sea vessels used to support the Ukrainian army’s operations, Russia’s Defense Ministry reported.
- According to the ministry’s report, the strikes hit a storage facility for long-and medium-range unmanned aerial vehicles and their components in the settlement of Olshany in the Kharkov Region.
- Russian forces also struck the PS-330 Zalyutino electrical substation in Kharkov, which supported the operation of Ukraine’s military-industrial sector.
- In addition, the strikes hit the PS-330 electrical substation in Kamenets-Podolsky in the Khmelnitsky Region, which supported the operation of logistics infrastructure facilities.
- In the Odessa Region, the strikes hit cargo handling infrastructure at three berths of the port of Chernomorsk, as well as four warehouses containing military and dual-use cargo intended for the Ukrainian military.
- In addition, a cargo vessel carrying military equipment for the Ukrainian army to the Odessa port was struck at sea, the statement said.

title: Malaysia’s ageing C-130Hs: upgrade or replace?
body:
Malaysia has indicated it is considering replacements for its aging Lockheed Martin C-130H Hercules transport aircraft, despite longstanding plans to upgrade at least part of the fleet.
General Tan Sri Muhamad Norazlan Aris, the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) chief, said in June that the service was assessing future transport aircraft requirements as part of its long-term capability recapitalisation plans.
“Yes, it’s a good aircraft, but when the time comes that we need to change, sometimes it’s better to replace rather than continue maintaining old aircraft,” Norazlan told media.
Local newspaper New Straits Times then reported in September that the C-130J and Embraer C-390 are among the aircraft being discussed as potential replacements.
“The eventual successor to the C-130 should have a similar carrying capacity. We know that’s the capacity we need most of the time. Not too big and not too small. Just the right size,” Norazlan said.
He added, “Extending the lifespan of an aircraft is possible through intensive maintenance, but the question is, how far do you want to extend it?”
This statement is noteworthy, as efforts to upgrade the RMAF’s fleet of 14 C-130Hs have been pursued over the past two decades.
In 2014, local maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) company Airod was reportedly awarded a letter of intent to upgrade the fleet’s avionics and communication, navigation, surveillance and air traffic management systems.
However, the programme did not proceed for several reasons, reportedly including disagreements over the choice of international partner.
More recently, in August 2024, an international tender was issued to upgrade six C-130Hs, with an estimated project cost of RM278 million (US$68 million).
According to Malaysian defence analyst Marhalim Abas, writing on his Malaysian Defence website, two foreign bidders were subsequently shortlisted. He noted in June 2026 that Canadian MRO company Cascade Aerospace was among the two shortlisted bidders. However, a requirement for the work to be performed in Malaysia could see the successful bidder partnering with Airod to carry out the upgrade.
As such, it remains unclear whether the RMAF will acquire new transport aircraft, proceed with the C-130H upgrade programme, or pursue both options, as the current upgrade project only covers six aircraft.
The RMAF received 15 C-130Hs in four batches, of which 14 remain in the fleet. The oldest five aircraft were delivered from 1976 onwards, making them up to 50 years old. The six youngest aircraft comprise one delivered around 1990 and five around 1995. These aircraft could be prioritised for the upgrade programme.
It is also worth noting that the RMAF’s Capability Development Plan 2055, unveiled in 2018 and setting out its long-term modernisation plans through to 2055, calls for the C-130H fleet to remain in service until 2040.
If this plan is followed through, it would reinforce the case for upgrading the C-130H to keep the aircraft in service for at least another decade and a half.
Should Malaysia also choose to acquire a new transport aircraft, the C-130J would offer some commonality with the existing fleet in terms of infrastructure and support. However, the C-130H and C-130J variants are separated by a generation of technological advancements.
Cost could also be a significant obstacle, as new C-130Js do not come cheap. For reference, the latest major international order for the type is Australia’s 2023 procurement of 20 stretched C-130J-30s for A$9.8 billion (US$6.6 billion).
This figure, though, is understood to include specialised communications equipment, sensors and self-defence systems beyond the standard aircraft configuration.
Apart from the C-130H, the RMAF also operates four Airbus A400M airlifters and seven PTDI CN-235 light transport aircraft, of which three have been converted for maritime surveillance.

title: FACT CHECK: Chinese embassy did not confirm Duterte’s ‘orchestrated’ ICC arrest
body: Claim: The Chinese embassy confirmed that President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. sent former president Rodrigo Duterte to The Hague at Senator Kiko Pangilinan’s request. Rating: FALSE Why we fact-checked this: Posts made by Facebook users Mike Romero and Gerald Mfgbf Sards Sarmiento claimed that the Chinese embassy confirmed that two government officials were behind Duterte’s arrest. They share an identical statement: “The Chinese Embassy has now confirmed that it was BBM who sent PRRD to The Hague at the request of Senator Pangilinan.” The posts were made on October 21, 2026, several hours after the Chinese embassy in Manila responded to Senator Kiko Pangilinan’s remarks on Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan. As of writing, the posts drew a total of 7,400 reactions, more than 1,000 comments, and 1,254 shares. The facts: While the Chinese embassy did undermine Pangilinan, it did not say that the senator requested Marcos to send Duterte to The Hague. Instead, the embassy replied to an earlier post made by Pangilinan asking the President to send Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan back to China. In his post , Pangilinan wrote: “Mr. President, if you can send Duterte, Quiboloy and Remualdez to jail… then you can most certainly send this arrogant, insulting, crude and insolent alien back to his country of origin,” referring to the Chinese Ambassador. The Chinese embassy’s official Facebook page only responded with rhetorical questions regarding the senator’s language. It did not officially affirm his statements on Duterte, Quiboloy, and Romualdez. The embassy’s post read: “Using thuggish, hooligan-style language to launch personal attacks on others—is this the calibre and standards of a Philippine senator? Is this the diplomacy and prudence that the DFA claims to uphold?” Duterte’s arrest: In March 2025, Duterte’s arrest was facilitated by Philippine authorities, in accordance with an arrest warrant issued by the International Criminal Court (ICC) on charges of crimes against humanity . President Marcos affirmed that this facilitation complied with the Philippines’ commitment to the International Criminal Police Organization (Interpol). The ICC has also repeatedly refuted allegations of dependence on the Philippine administration. In a statement sent to the Inquirer , ICC spokesperson Oriane Maillet said the court is mandated to operate independently and impartially under the Rome Statute. A separate interview with ICC spokesperson Fadi El Abdallah presents a denial of collusion with the Marcos administration, as court judges make decisions independently. Chinese embassy and the West Philippine Sea: In an interview with the media on October 15 , the ambassador said the Philippines “should feel fortunate” that China does not use force in its maritime dispute. His statement was a response to Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr.’s statement saying Beijing was a troublemaker in the region, and not Manila. Public officials, including Pangilinan, then reacted to the ambassador’s statement. Before this incident, it was reported that since Jing took over in December 2025, the Chinese embassy in Manila has amplified its rhetoric and engaged in online word wars with Philippine government spokespersons and officials. Previous fact-checks: As the maritime dispute continues, Duterte remains at the ICC . The actual trial will begin on November 30. Rappler has previously fact-checked claims regarding Duterte at the ICC: FACT CHECK: No ICC admission of being ‘paid’ by Marcos gov’t in Duterte case FACT CHECK: No Trump plan to secure Duterte’s release from ICC FACT CHECK: ICC’s rejection of Duterte’s appeal for interim release misrepresented as reclusion perpetua sentence FACT CHECK: ICC did not junk Duterte’s case – Jade Florido/Rappler.com Jade Florido is a volunteer for Rappler’s Research and Data unit. She is a third-year Development Studies student at the University of the Philippines – Manila. Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

title: Moldovan PM arrives in Ukraine on working visit
body:
Prime Minister of Moldova Vasile Tofan is on a working visit to Kyiv. He is accompanied to Ukraine by three ministers, reports NewsMaker, citing the Moldovan government.
The visit program includes meetings with Prime Minister of Ukraine Serhiy Koretsky, President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy, and Chairman of the Verkhovna Rada Ruslan Stefanchuk.
"The Prime Ministers will discuss strengthening bilateral relations, developing economic and trade cooperation, regional security, and the European path of both countries. Following the meeting, they will deliver joint statements to the press. Together, the heads of government will lay flowers at the Wall of Remembrance of the Fallen Defenders of Ukraine, honoring the memory of those who lost their lives in the war," the Moldovan government reported.
In addition, Tofan, together with the Ukrainian Prime Minister, will participate in the Kyiv International Economic Forum, focused on investment opportunities and the development of economic cooperation.
The Moldovan Prime Minister will also meet with business representatives to discuss the development of economic partnership and the expansion of trade ties between the two countries.
Tofan is accompanied by Minister of Infrastructure and Regional Development Vladimir Bolea, Minister of Defense Anatolie Nosatîi, and Minister of Energy Dorin Junghietu.

title: Moldovan Prime Minister arrives in Kyiv
body:
According to Ukrinform, this was reported by NewsMaker .
Tofan is accompanied by Minister of Infrastructure and Regional Development Vladimir Bolea, Minister of Defense Anatolie Nosatîi and Minister of Energy Dorin Junghietu.
In Kyiv, the Moldovan prime minister will meet with his Ukrainian counterpart, Sergii Koretskyi.
“The prime ministers will discuss strengthening bilateral relations, developing economic and trade cooperation, regional security, and the European path of the two countries. Following the meeting, they will make joint statements to the press. The heads of government will also lay flowers at the Wall of Remembrance of the Fallen for Ukraine, honoring those who lost their lives in the war,” the Moldovan government said.
The program of the visit also includes a meeting between Tofan and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, as well as talks with Verkhovna Rada Speaker Ruslan Stefanchuk.
In addition, Tofan will join his Ukrainian counterpart at the Kyiv International Economic Forum, which will focus on investment opportunities and the development of economic cooperation.
The Moldovan prime minister will also meet with business representatives to discuss strengthening the economic partnership and expanding trade ties between the two countries.
As Ukrinform reported, several weeks ago, First Deputy Prime Minister and Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal met with Moldovan Prime Minister Vasile Tofan during a working visit to Moldova as part of discussions on winter preparations and challenges in the energy sector.

body:

title: IN BRIEF: What is known about Vucic party’s defeat in Serbia’s parliamentary elections
body:
MOSCOW, October 26. /TASS/. The Student List opposition coalition has won the snap parliamentary elections in Serbia, former President Aleksandar Vucic said.
TASS has compiled the key information known at this time.
- The Student List opposition coalition has won the snap parliamentary elections in Serbia, former President Aleksandar Vucic stated.
- According to him, the party will be able to form a majority in parliament on its own.
- The politician noted that his Serbian Progressive Party can expect to win 105-106 seats.
- The other parties failed to clear the three percent threshold.
- The exception will be the Alliance of Vojvodina Hungarians, as it is not subject to this threshold.
- Supporters of the Student List coalition held celebrations in the streets of Belgrade.
- According to a TASS correspondent, people took to the streets of the Serbian capital with flags and fireworks.
- Passing cars honked their horns, and groups of motorcyclists rode toward the city center.
- The crowd tore down the barriers in a park across from the Serbian parliament building.
- Previously, a tent camp for Vucic’s supporters had been located there; after his announcement of defeat in the election, the camp was emptied.
- Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar congratulated the leaders of the Student List opposition coalition on their victory before the official results of the snap parliamentary elections in Serbia were announced.
- The head of government stated that Hungary is ready to provide them with support.
- Milorad Dodik, chairman of the ruling Alliance of Independent Social Democrats party in the Republic of Srpska (an entity of Bosnia and Herzegovina), also congratulated the Student List coalition on its victory.

title: Agudat Yisrael support, Arab parties, or new elections: Post-vote scenarios facing Israel
body: Agudat Yisrael, the three-MK haredi faction led by Yitzhak Goldknopf, could provide some form of support for a government led by a member of the opposition, according to assessments within the political establishment ahead of the elections.With less than a day remaining before the vote begins, political figures are considering several possible scenarios, including forming a government with the support of Arab parties or holding another election. Another possibility being discussed is support from Agudat Yisrael in exchange for budgetary agreements, although even such an arrangement would not necessarily eliminate the need for votes from the Arab parties.The possibility of cooperation between Agudat Yisrael and the change bloc is not new. Maariv reported in August that Agudat Yisrael was examining new political options, including potential cooperation with Gadi Eisenkot.The discussions took place against the backdrop of tensions within United Torah Judaism, particularly disagreements between Agudat Yisrael and Degel Hatorah over the haredi military draft and relations with Netanyahu.According to that report, while Agudat Yisrael expressed disappointment with the coalition's conduct, Degel Hatorah conveyed messages of despair and a lack of confidence in Netanyahu and his government.A letter from Rabbi Dov Lando, expressing reservations about maintaining the commitment to the political bloc led by Netanyahu, further deepened uncertainty surrounding relations between the haredi parties and Likud.Goldknopf, however, faces a significant political obstacle. His voter base is largely identified with the Right, and according to assessments cited in the report, any indication that he would be willing to support a government led by parties from the change bloc could prompt some of his supporters to defect to Likud or Otzma Yehudit.Is Bennett the only politician who could reshape the political blocs?Beyond the possibility of haredi support, political figures are also examining a scenario in which former prime minister Naftali Bennett could determine the composition of the next government if neither bloc secures a majority sufficient to form a coalition.One possibility being raised within the political establishment is that Bennett could join a government led by Netanyahu if neither bloc reaches the 61-seat threshold required for a Knesset majority.Although this is considered a remote scenario, some believe Bennett is the only leader within the change bloc capable of making such a move, given his political background on the Right.Such a decision, however, would require Bennett to change his political support base and would also be complicated by the composition of his current party.Liberman disagreements with Netanyahu make relationship unlikelyThe possibility of Avigdor Liberman taking a similar step has also been raised, particularly in light of his previous decision to join a Netanyahu-led government and serve as defense minister.However, according to the assessment presented, Liberman is currently far from making such a move because of the personal and political disagreements between him and the prime minister.Thus, alongside the possibility of securing outside support from haredi parties, the question of which politician might be willing to shift their political support base could become one of the central issues in coalition negotiations.For now, these remain scenarios and political assessments rather than agreements reached between the parties.

title: Freight train derails near Russia’s Yekaterinburg, tanker cars catch fire
body: Twenty cars of a freight train derailed on the Reshety–Sedelnikovo stretch of track in Russia’s Sverdlovsk region, and seven tank cars caught fire, the Russian state news agency TASS reported, citing the Sverdlovsk region branch of Russia’s Emergency Situations Ministry. The fire has been contained to an area of 1,500 square meters (about 16,000 square feet), the regional branch of the Emergency Situations Ministry said, without specifying what was inside the tank cars. Residents of nearby homes were advised to stay indoors and, if that was not possible, to wear masks and respirators. The Yekaterinburg-based news outlet E1 reports that residents were also asked not to open their windows, to do wet cleaning more often, drink more fluids, and rinse their eyes, nose, and throat. The regional office of Rospotrebnadzor said it would conduct an air quality inspection for “pollutants characteristic of this type of fire.” The cause of the derailment remains under investigation. No official explanation for what happened had been offered as of publication. At Meduza, we are committed to transparency about our use of artificial intelligence in the newsroom. title: HM issues two Royal Decrees
body:
Muscat: His Majesty Sultan Haitham bin Tarik on Monday issued two Royal decrees, reading as follows: Royal decree No (97/2026) on amending some provisions of the Council of Oman’s Law. Article (1) stipulates that the amendments attached to the Council of Oman’s Law promulgated by Royal decree No 7/2021 shall be enforced. Article (2) cancels all that contradicts the amendments attached to this decree or contravenes their provisions. Article (3) says that this decree shall be published in the Official Gazette and enforced from the day following its date of publishing. Royal Decree No (98/2026) on amending some provisions of the Shura Council’s Members Election Law. Article (1) stipulates that a new article, numbered (4-bis), shall be added to the Shura Council’s Members Election Law promulgated by Royal decree No 54/2023. The new article reads as follows: “The Minister shall issue a decision specifying the regulations and procedures for the candidacy of a woman from each governorate for the membership designated to women”. Article (2) cancels all that contradicts this decree or contravenes its provisions. Article (3) says that this decree shall be published in the Official Gazette and enforced from the day following its date of publishing.

title: Greece Keeps Patriot Battery Guarding Yanbu as Houthis Target Saudi Oil Sites
body: Greece will keep its Patriot missile battery in Saudi Arabia, where it guards energy infrastructure at the Red Sea port of Yanbu. The decision comes as Yemen’s Houthis step up drone and missile attacks on Saudi oil facilities, pipelines and airports. Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis told Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Riyadh on Sunday 25 October that Greece “responds positively” to the Kingdom’s request for the Patriots to stay “during these difficult times”, the Greek Prime Minister’s Office said . Mitsotakis condemned the attacks on Saudi Arabia. He said the Greek presence contributes “not only to the security of the Kingdom but also to regional security, as it protects critical energy infrastructure in Yanbu”, GCT reported , citing the state news agency AMNA. A week of Houthi attacks on Saudi energy sites Mitsotakis’s visit came amid a wave of Houthi attacks on the Kingdom’s oil industry. Early on Monday 26 October, the Houthis said they had launched drone attacks on crude oil pumping stations along the East-West Pipeline, as well as firing a ballistic missile at Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport, Anadolu Agency reported . The Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted a missile aimed at Riyadh. The coalition also said it had destroyed two ballistic missile launchers in Sanaa, while there was no immediate Saudi confirmation of the Houthi claims, Reuters reported via Al-Monitor . On Saturday 24 October, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group had targeted an Aramco facility in Yanbu, the Rabigh oil refinery and several airports, Middle East Eye reported . The group also said it had targeted the East-West Pipeline. Again, Saudi authorities did not confirm those claims. Earlier in the week, the Houthis claimed missile and drone strikes on Yanbu and on the Shaybah oil field, saying both sites caught fire. A source told Argus the claim was untrue and that the facilities were intact. However, the attacks have had deadly consequences. On Wednesday 21 October, Saudi Arabia’s Energy Ministry said debris from an intercepted drone that targeted a processing facility at Shaybah killed a Filipino and a Nepali worker and injured two others, Arab News reported . The ministry said oilfield operations were not affected. The next day, the Houthis said they had again attacked Aramco facilities in Yanbu, as well as the Saudi Defence Ministry in Riyadh, The Hindu reported , citing Reuters. The same day, Aramco told staff to evacuate its Dhahran headquarters, according to six people with knowledge of the matter, and oil prices rose to their highest level since May, Reuters reported . That headquarters had already been struck once this month. A Houthi missile hit an Aramco office tower in Dhahran overnight on 13–14 October, causing what the energy ministry called a “limited fire”, the BBC reported . Why Yanbu matters Yanbu has become central to the world’s oil supply. The port is home to three Aramco-linked refineries. Its export terminal became Saudi Arabia’s main crude outlet after the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz in early March, according to Argus . Crude reaches Yanbu through the East-West Pipeline, which runs about 1,200 kilometres from the Abqaiq area in the east to the Red Sea coast, Anadolu reported . Saudi Arabia temporarily shut the pipeline in September after a drone attack that Riyadh and Baghdad said came from Iraq. The Greek mission The Greek Patriot battery, operated by the Hellenic Force in Saudi Arabia (ELDYSA), has been in the Kingdom since 2021. It has helped intercept Houthi drones and missiles aimed at Yanbu and other targets, Kathimerini reported . On 24 September, it fired two interceptors , one at a ballistic missile and one at a drone. In early October, Greece’s Government Council for Foreign Affairs and Defence (KYSEA) granted a one-month extension of the deployment. Sunday’s announcement keeps the battery in Saudi Arabia, although no new end date has been given, Military Press noted . Greece is not alone. The UK said on 20 October that RAF Typhoons would fly defensive missions to protect Saudi cities and critical infrastructure, the Ministry of Defence announced . Mitsotakis also used the talks to stress freedom of navigation. He said Greece, as a major maritime power, attaches “paramount importance” to the security of international shipping lanes, Kathimerini reported . The fighting has effectively ended a UN-brokered truce that had largely held since 2022. Earlier this month, a Houthi attack on Riyadh’s main airport killed 13 people , the deadliest in the Kingdom in more than a decade. GCT has previously covered the attacks on the airport. title: Could Trump's allies push Netanyahu into unity gov't without his far-right partners? - analysis
body: Voices within US President Donald Trump's inner circle are advocating for the establishment of a broad and moderate Israeli unity government without National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, with some even floating the idea of a rotation agreement in which Benjamin Netanyahu would serve as prime minister first.However, Yashar party chairman Gadi Eisenkot and former prime minister Naftali Bennett remain opposed to serving under him, and American officials have yet to discuss the framework with them.American billionaire Bill Ackman, a prominent supporter of Trump with close ties to his circle, publicly called on Sunday for the formation of a broad, moderate Israeli government that excludes Ben-Gvir and Smotrich.In a social media post, Ackman argued that such a government would allow Israel to restore its international standing, expand the Abraham Accords, and improve relations with both major political parties in the United States.I said I wasn't going to weigh in on who should be prime minister of Israel as that is a decision for Israeli citizens. I did, however, want to share one point of view from the perspective of someone who has an understanding of how Israel is perceived in America. Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich have caused Israel enormous reputational damage with their statements and actions which are presented in the global media as representing the voice and will of all Israelis. As such, a government formed without Ben-Gvir and Smotrich will send a message to the rest of the world that Israel is turning a new page. This will allow Israel to rebuild lost credibility, increase the opportunity for an expansion of the Abraham Accords, and enjoy a better relationship with Democrats and Republicans and Americans at large.— Bill Ackman (@BillAckman) October 25, 2026Ackman, who heads the hedge fund Pershing Square, supported Trump in the presidential election and is considered an influential figure in US political and business circles. He criticized Ben-Gvir and Smotrich, stating that their presence harms Israel's global image and its ability to advance key diplomatic objectives. At the same time, he praised Netanyahu and his relationship with Trump. Ackman favors Netanyahu remaining in office, but with a different set of coalition partners.Realizing Trump's Middle East ambitions requires a change in Israel's KnessetAckman is not the only figure in Trump's orbit holding this view. According to several sources, additional figures in Washington believe that over the remaining two years of the president's term, realizing his ambitious Middle East plans requires a change in the composition of Israel's government.Foremost among these plans is the possibility of a historic normalization agreement with Saudi Arabia, a prospect difficult to envision advancing while Ben-Gvir and Smotrich sit at the cabinet table.Several senior advisors to Trump believe an Israeli government without Netanyahu's far-right partners would make it significantly easier to advance the president's regional policy.This comes amid existing friction between Washington and Jerusalem: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are reportedly frustrated by the pace at which Netanyahu is advancing Trump's plan for Gaza; Special Envoy Tom Barrick disagrees with Israel's strategy regarding Syria; and officials around Secretary of State Marco Rubio seek to strengthen the Lebanese government while expressing frustration over insufficient action regarding Jewish violence in Judea and Samaria.These officials place high importance on the composition of Israel's next government, which could impact Trump's chances of achieving major diplomatic breakthroughs before his term ends. A deal with Saudi Arabia, for instance, requires difficult Israeli decisions on the Palestinian issue and other regional matters.A government reliant on Ben-Gvir and Smotrich could struggle to make such choices, even if Netanyahu himself were willing to do so. However, replacing coalition partners alone does not guarantee a deal: Riyadh maintains its own political demands, including tangible progress on the Palestinian issue.Trump's inner circles question viability of diplomacy with Netanyahu aroundSome within Trump's circle even question whether a diplomatic breakthrough is achievable as long as Netanyahu serves as prime minister. Consequently, an idea has emerged within the president's team for a rotation-based unity government: Netanyahu would serve during the first year, after which another prime minister would replace him to lead negotiations with the Saudis before the conclusion of Trump's term.Proponents of the idea believe this arrangement would maintain governance continuity in the first year while entrusting regional diplomatic efforts to a prime minister who is not dependent on Netanyahu's current partners. According to several Israeli and American sources, Netanyahu told Trump he wants to form a unity government and will work toward that goal after the election.Israel's Ambassador to the US, Yechiel Leiter, also publicly said Netanyahu wants a broad government. Leiter said Netanyahu prefers a national unity government over continuing with the current coalition makeup.He also addressed Ben-Gvir's future, saying Netanyahu made it clear he would not serve as national security minister again. The comments drew a sharp reaction from Otzma Yehudit, whose officials fear Netanyahu is paving the way for a coalition with Eisenkot at the expense of his current partners. For his part, Ben-Gvir called on Netanyahu to form a right-wing government rather than one with Eisenkot.Although the idea originated in his inner circle, Trump has not formally endorsed the initiative. The president publicly backed Netanyahu on October 18, even as several advisors expressed reservations. Vice President JD Vance did not join the public endorsement.Furthermore, US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee explicitly denied allegations of an American effort to push a unity government, clarifying that the administration does not intervene in Israeli elections or dictate actions to the prime minister.Meanwhile, the proposals discussed in Washington remain far removed from Israel's political reality. American officials have not conducted a deep feasibility check with leaders of the change bloc, and no substantive talks have taken place with Eisenkot or other senior figures in the opposition regarding the proposed framework. Electoral scenarios also present obstacles for the initiative.If Netanyahu's bloc secures 61 mandates, he is expected to receive the mandate to form a government, but it remains doubtful whether Eisenkot or Bennett would agree to join. Additionally, ultra-Orthodox parties demand the passage of the conscription bill as a precondition for coalition talks. Conversely, if the right-wing bloc fails to secure a majority, Netanyahu may not get the first chance to form a government.Even in the event of a victory for the right-wing bloc, Netanyahu could find himself in a trap: his natural partners will demand the fulfillment of previous commitments, primarily the ultra-Orthodox demands regarding military draft legislation.Reaching out to Eisenkot and Bennett would require offering them a partnership in a government they have pledged not to join. Even within the right-wing bloc, few believe Eisenkot or Bennett would consent to such a move.

title: Canada receives first F-35 fighters while full 88-aircraft order remains under review
body:
The Royal Canadian Air Force (RCAF) has received its first two Lockheed Martin CF-35A Lightning II fighters, formally introducing the type into the Canadian fleet while the government continues to review whether it will proceed with the full 88-aircraft acquisition.
The two fighters were accepted on October 22 at Luke Air Force Base in Arizona, the RCAF said. They will remain in the United States to support the initial training of Canadian pilots and maintainers rather than immediately moving to Canada.
Follow Air Data News: WhatsApp | Instagram | LinkedIn | Twitter | Facebook
Canada plans to base its first eight CF-35As at Luke during the initial training phase. The first aircraft are expected to arrive in Canada in 2028, with initial operational capability planned for 2029-2030.
The milestone comes just over a month after the first Canadian F-35A completed its maiden flight at Lockheed Martin's Fort Worth facility in Texas on September 23.
Luke AFB already hosts international F-35 training and will provide Canada with an established environment to prepare personnel before the aircraft begins operating from Canadian bases.
The RCAF is preparing its infrastructure around two main operating locations, 3 Wing Bagotville in Quebec and 4 Wing Cold Lake in Alberta. Construction and other preparations have been underway ahead of the arrival of the first aircraft in the country.
Canada selected the F-35A in 2022 and signed the acquisition agreement in January 2023 for 88 fighters to replace its CF-18 Hornets. The program was valued at C$19 billion at the time, including aircraft, associated equipment and initial sustainment.
The CF-35A designation is used by Canada for its version of the conventional takeoff and landing F-35A.
The arrival of the first aircraft does not end uncertainty over the eventual size of Canada's F-35 fleet.
Prime Minister Mark Carney's government launched a review of the acquisition in 2025 amid a deterioration in relations with the United States. Canada remains committed to purchasing at least the first 16 aircraft, but Ottawa has not yet confirmed that it will proceed with all 88 originally planned fighters.
The government has also examined alternatives for the remaining requirement, including the possibility of a mixed fighter fleet. Saab has promoted the Gripen E as a potential complement to the F-35 and has offered Canadian production and industrial participation if Ottawa decides to acquire the Swedish fighter.

title: African players in Europe: Jackson brace ends City’s perfect record
body: Senegal star Nicolas Jackson took his goal tally since joining Aston Villa from Chelsea to seven in 11 matches by bagging a brace in a 2-1 Premier League win over Manchester City at the weekend. Victory for Villa ended a seven-match winning streak by City since the league season began. City still top the table, but only on goal difference from defending champions Arsenal. AFP Sport highlights African headline-makers in the major European leagues: ENGLAND NICOLAS JACKSON (Aston Villa) Jackson put Villa ahead in the sixth minute with a fine finish into the roof of the net from John McGinn’s pass. After Erling Haaland equalised for the leaders in the 52nd minute, Jackson clinched a memorable win for Villa eight minutes later. Teenage Senegal international Ibrahim Mbaye teed up Jackson to squeeze his shot past City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma. DANGO OUATTARA (Brentford) The Burkina Faso winger scored for the first time this season to rescue a 1-1 draw at Hull City. Ouattara slotted home in the 63rd minute from Igor Thiago’s pass. The 24-year-old cancelled out Oli McBurnie’s first half penalty, but Brentford were left without a win in their last three games. SPAIN INAKI WILLIAMS (Athletic Bilbao) After Spain 2026 World Cup winner Nico Williams came close to scoring, older brother and Ghana international Inaki struck the second goal in a 4-0 La Liga romp against Getafe. A counterattack ended with Inaki Williams one-on-one against the Getafe goalkeeper and he netted with a low shot. ITALY ANDRE-FRANK ANGUISSA (Napoli) Cameroon midfielder Anguissa sent a brilliant bicycle kick into the corner of the net on 28 minutes after Roma failed to clear a free-kick. It was the opening goal of a 3-3 Serie A thriller. GERMANY SERHOU GUIRASSY (Borussia Dortmund) Guirassy was kept off the scoresheet, but posed a constant threat as Borussia beat Eintracht Frankfurt 1-0 at home. Early in the opening half, the Guinea international was through on goal, but had his chip saved by goalkeeper Noah Atubolu. Just after the break, Guirassy headed a corner against the bar and went close again when he hit a cross inches wide of the left post. FRANCE ELYE WAHI, SOFIANE DIOP (Nice) Internationals Wahi of the Ivory Coast and Diop of Morocco scored as mid-table Nice came from behind to win 2-1 at Brest in Ligue 1. Wahi equalised just past the hour mark after a corner and Diop punished a defensive blunder to grab the 83rd-minute winner. title: Commuters welcome McCarthy-Mallam road repairs after Joy SMS appeals
body: Road users on the McCarthy-Mallam stretch of the Accra-Cape Coast Highway are seeing some relief as rehabilitation works begin after weeks of complaints aired on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show. The Joy SMS team repeatedly highlighted the road’s deteriorating condition after commuters called and messaged the programme to complain about hours spent in traffic. Motorists said potholes and damaged sections of the road had worsened congestion, disrupted their journeys and left many exhausted before arriving at work. One listener, who lives at Kasoa Millennium City Estate, described the daily struggle to reach Mallam Junction despite leaving home early. “Nothing has changed ooo. Good morning, Joy FM Super Morning Show team. “I live at Kasoa Millennium City Estate and left home at 5:30 a.m. today, yet I was nowhere near Mallam Junction. Traffic is terrible between Ayigbe Town Junction, West Hills Mall, the old barrier, Mallam and Kaneshie. “The ongoing construction at Hansonic Junction, the Kaneshie footbridge works, and a major pothole near the traffic lights are making things worse. The stretch between West Hills Mall and the old barrier alone can take 30–48 minutes, especially on Mondays! “Even the new Weija Dam road, which offers an alternative route, is becoming congested as more motorists discover it. Joy FM, please help us amplify our concerns. How much longer must commuters endure this daily struggle? We need urgent action from the authorities!” Another listener, who lives at SCC, recounted how traffic disrupted an early-morning journey to McCarthy Hill. “Good morning, Joy FM. I left my house at SCC at exactly 6:00 a.m. today to meet someone at McCarthy Hill at 7:00 a.m., as agreed. The person left East Legon at 6:00 a.m. and arrived at McCarthy Hill at 6:39 a.m. Meanwhile, I am only just getting to Weija Junction! “How can someone travel from East Legon to McCarthy Hill in 39 minutes while I have spent over an hour travelling from SCC and have not even reached my destination? Hmm.” Sakyibea, another listener, said the poor road conditions and construction works had made commuting from Kasoa increasingly exhausting. “Good morning, Winston. The problem with the Kasoa-Accra road is the deplorable state from the West Hills Mall to Mallam Junction. I live in Kasoa, and I have to leave home by 4:30 a.m. to get to my office at Ridge. I get to work exhausted, and I get little sleep. “The situation has worsened as I have to deal with Darkuman to Kaneshie traffic due to the construction works going on. #joysms,” Sakyibea texted. Listeners report improvement as work begins On Monday, October 26, some listeners reported an improvement in traffic following the commencement of rehabilitation works around Mallam Junction, although concerns remain about other sections of the route. “Good morning, Winston and team. True, the Mallam Junction portion of the road has been worked on, and the traffic situation has improved. However, the Kokrobite-Old Barrier stretch remains unattended to. The Honourable Roads Minister should pay attention to that as well,” Dr Bruce, a listener from Oshiyie near Kokrobite, texted. Another listener welcomed the ongoing work, saying: “Joy FM, they are working on the road from McCarthy to Mallam Junction. God bless you all abundantly!” The reports of improvement follow sustained calls on the programme for authorities to address the road’s deteriorating condition and the resulting congestion. Weija-Gbawe MP petitions Roads Minister On October 19, the Member of Parliament for Weija-Gbawe, Jerry Ahmed Shaib, also petitioned the Minister for Roads and Highways, Kwame Governs Agbodza, to order urgent repairs to the Weija Junction-to-Mallam section. The stretch is notorious for heavy traffic, with congestion often worsening during the rainy season when flooding affects parts of the route. The rehabilitation works have offered some relief to commuters, but residents and road users are calling for the remaining affected sections to be addressed. They hope the ongoing intervention will lead to a lasting solution that reduces travel times, improves road safety and eases the daily burden on commuters travelling between Kasoa and Accra.

title: Tsinghua AI Open-Sources AKV, a Cache Engineering Server for LLM Agents on SGLang
body:
Tsinghua University and CUHK researchers open-sourced AKV , a serving system for KV cache engineering in LLM agents. Instead of summarizing old history, agents drop selected KV cache entries and keep reusing the rest. Across 3 models and 4 agent benchmarks, average cost falls 27.7% . Average task score rises 1.7 points. The code is Apache-2.0 licensed and builds on SGLang . TL;DR What it is: Serving system plus policy library, no weights. Tested on GPT-OSS-120B (5.1B active), MiniMax-M2.7 (230B total, 10B active) and MiroThinker-1.7-Mini (30B total, 3B active). Runs on: NVIDIA GPUs via SGLang. Paper used 8 A800-80GB GPUs in BF16. Quick start serves GPT-OSS-120B on 2 GPUs (tensor parallel 2). Performance: 27.7% lower average cost and +1.7 points average score versus threshold summarization. Best: GPT-OSS-120B on SWE-bench Verified: cost per task 20.0 to 9.7 cents, score 40.0 to 43.2. Worst: MiniMax-M2.7 on BrowseComp-Plus scores 58.9, 3.4 points below Text Engineering’s 62.3. What is cache engineering, and how is it different from context engineering? AKV is a Tsinghua serving system that lets LLM agents drop and reposition their own KV cache. Context engineering trims or summarizes the text history. Editing that prefix invalidates every later KV state. The retained suffix must then be re-prefilled. Harnesses therefore summarize late and aggressively, which can lose details from middle rounds. Cache engineering leaves the text trajectory untouched. It only changes which KV entries stay visible to attention. Retained entries are reused without recomputation. They can still carry information from dropped messages. In the research paper’s cost analysis, KV cache reads made up 82.4% of total API cost. How does AKV work? AKV defines 3 cache operations. Append is the standard update for new tokens. Drop removes selected entries from future attention without changing positions. Repos rewrites retained keys to positions 0 through r-1 using a RoPE rotation . Values stay unchanged, so no hidden states are recomputed. In ablations, adding Repos raised GPT-OSS-120B’s BrowseComp-Plus pass rate from 55% to 62%. The hard part is serving. Identical tokens can produce different cache states under different operation histories. Plain prefix matching could reuse the wrong states. AKV extends SGLang’s radix tree with drop and reposition nodes. It frees dropped KV only when no active request still needs it. Segment-batch attention restores evicted states in 1 prefill pass. What does the AKV API look like? The interface is stateless and OpenAI-compatible . Clients send the full message history and two optional fields. drop_message maps a trigger message index to the messages to drop. reposition lists the indices after which positions get compacted. A CachePolicy builds those fields from a trigger, a selector and a reposition rule. Built-in policies are turn-based, token-based or model-based. A CacheTool lets the model call drop_context itself. How does AKV perform on agent benchmarks? The main policy is a tool-response rolling drop that keeps the latest 12 tool responses. The Standard baseline summarizes at 96K tokens (192K for MiroThinker). Text Engineering summarizes at 48K. Benchmarks are BrowseComp-Plus , GAIA-Text , SWE-bench Verified and xbench-DeepSearch-2510 . Model Standard score / cost Text Eng. score / cost AKV score / cost MiniMax-M2.7 52.4 / 5.0 52.8 / 5.7 53.7 / 4.4 GPT-OSS-120B 51.0 / 11.2 48.3 / 10.2 53.1 / 7.3 MiroThinker-1.7-Mini 44.1 / 20.4 37.1 / 18.1 45.8 / 14.8 Average pass rate (%) and cost (US cents per task) across 4 benchmarks. Source: Table 1 of the paper . AKV also cuts cost 21.9% versus Text Engineering. The accuracy gap opens on long runs. On BrowseComp-Plus at 96K tokens and above, GPT-OSS-120B scores 37% with AKV. Standard scores 24% and Text Engineering 32%, per the project page . Costs are API-equivalent estimates from published rates. Drop and Repos are enabled for Qwen, GPT-OSS and MiniMax-M2 text architectures. Linear attention models are future work.
Self-hosted only
You run the AKV server yourself. It extends SGLang with cache-operation support.
Self-reported, single hardware setup
All results come from the authors, on 8 A800-80GB GPUs in BF16.
Different measurement windows
High-concurrency AKV runs were measured through the first 30 task completions. Standard used a 1-hour window.
Not every benchmark improves
MiniMax-M2.7 on BrowseComp-Plus scores 58.9 with AKV, below Text Engineering at 62.3.
Dropping reasoning cache hurts
On SWE-bench Verified, dropping reasoning cache fell to 36.5, and dropping both to 34.5, versus 41.0 for tool drop.

title: Nollywood Legend Emeka Ike To Host The National Automation Prize Nap 2026
body: -With Over ₦50m All For Grabs In One Of Nigeria’ Biggest Engineering & Technological Competition Celebrated screen personality brings star power to a national showcase of engineering, automation, artificial intelligence and robotics. Advanxis Technologies & Process Automation Ltd announces renowned Nollywood actor and engineering enthusiast Emeka Ike as the host of the third edition of the National Automation Prize (NAP 2026), a national engineering and technology competition that brings innovation, practical problem-solving and reality television together on one stage. Under the theme “Build for Nigeria. Automate for Scale. Compete with the World,” NAP 2026 will celebrate Nigerians building solutions for industrial productivity and everyday challenges in manufacturing, energy, agriculture, water, security and public infrastructure. A new spotlight on Nigerian engineering talent From hands-on demonstrations and mentoring to high-energy competitive challenges, the programme aims to make engineering innovation accessible and compelling to viewers beyond the technical community. Emeka Ike’s familiar screen presence is expected to help bridge entertainment and engineering, inspiring students, inventors, institutions and the wider public. “I am an engineer by training, a Nollywood actor by profession and a passionate believer in Nigerian ingenuity. I know what entertainment has done for Nigeria’s global reputation, and I believe engineering and technology can do even more for our economic future. The National Automation Prize 2026 is about discovering the minds that will build tomorrow’s Nigeria. It is time to put our engineers and Technologists on the biggest stage, celebrate their brilliance and show the world what Nigerian innovation can achieve.” “We have spent decades celebrating talent in music, film and sports. It is time to give our engineers, inventors and technology creators the same national applause. Innovation deserves the spotlight,” Emeka Ike Said. The First Edition NAP 2024 demonstration shows how practical engineering can be made visible and engaging “The National Automation Prize 2026 is more than a competition; it is a movement to discover, celebrate and empower Nigeria’s brightest engineering and technology talents. Having Emeka Ike as our host brings a powerful blend of engineering, entertainment and inspiration to our mission of making innovation a national priority.” -Engr. Anthony James, Managing Director, Advanxis Technologies & Process Automation Ltd. Not just a prize. A new definition of celebrity. The next breakthrough could come from a student developing a low-cost water-treatment controller, a team automating a factory process, or an independent inventor applying robotics to agriculture. Their work may not begin on a red carpet — but its impact could reach far beyond one. NAP 2026 plans to bring those stories to a wider audience while connecting innovators to educators, manufacturers, industry leaders and potential partners. Planned television outreach includes Major National Television as well as Cable TV; specific broadcast arrangements remain subject to confirmation. 2 and Edition NAP 2025 award presentation From early awards to a national ambition Previous editions in 2024 and 2025 established the initiative’s foundation where Participants are awarded millions of Naira in cash Price for their engineering and Technological ingenuity. The 2026 is promising to be a blockbuster with mouth watering price reward of over ₦50m with individual and Higher Institution categories A prize presentation from a first edition of the National Automation Prize in 2024. The Higher Institution category also include the building of state-of-the-art digitalized equipment as well as training/mentorship for the first three top institutions. These equipment prizes matter because their value can continue long after the cameras leave — supporting student projects, laboratory teaching and practical exposure to industrial systems. second runner-up Michael Nwuzu featured in broadcast coverage Why the story matters beyond the stage For Advanxis, the ambition is not simply to discover one brilliant winner. It is to challenge a broader assumption: that Nigeria must remain primarily a buyer of technology designed elsewhere. The organisers want more young people to see engineering as a route to invention, enterprise and industrial development. From automation and robotics to artificial intelligence, energy, agriculture, manufacturing and water infrastructure, the country’s most urgent needs can become starting points for practical innovation. Advanxis representative speaking to the media at a NAP event The prize also creates a compelling proposition for universities, polytechnics, research organisations, sponsors and industry partners: help turn promising prototypes into useful systems, and help the people behind them build careers and companies. NAP 2025 winner Samuel Udofia speaking during the televised event A new kind of national hero A movie star can move an audience. An engineer can move an industry. NAP 2026 is built around the possibility that, together, those two kinds of influence can change what a generation aspires to become. When Emeka Ike steps onto the NAP stage, the spotlight will not be on celebrity alone. It will be on young Nigerians who can transform an idea into a working system — and perhaps a working system into a solution the nation needs. The next Nigerian superstar may not be holding a script or a microphone. They may be holding the blueprint to Nigeria’s future. About the National Automation Prize The National Automation Prize is an engineering and technology innovation competition organised by Advanxis Technologies & Process Automation Ltd. Its third edition seeks to bridge education, innovation and industry for a smarter Nigeria through technical challenges, recognition and practical industrial support. For more Information, participation and Partnership visit www.advanxis.com/prize3 MEDIA & PARTNERSHIP ENQUIRIES Lagos: 16 Karimu Katun Street, Victoria Island, Lagos Port Harcourt: 22 Trans Amadi Road, Trans Amadi Industrial Layout, Port Harcourt, Rivers State info@advanxis.com • +234 816 005 2942 • www.advanxis.com/prize3 The post Nollywood Legend Emeka Ike To Host The National Automation Prize Nap 2026 appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Babcock pitches Type 31 for US Navy frigate programme
body:
Babcock is preparing to offer its Arrowhead 140 frigate, the design behind the Royal Navy’s Type 31, to the US Navy as Washington looks abroad for a proven escort it can build quickly. Any deal would probably see the majority of ships built in American yards, with the UK supplying design and engineering expertise.
A report in the Telegraph has confirmed our prevous speculation that Babcock might offer Arrowhead 140/Type 31 to the US. Initial meetings have been held with Pentagon officials, pending the formal submission of an expression of interest this month. Sir Nick Hine, head of Babcock’s marine business and a former Second Sea Lord, said it would be “insane” not to respond.
The bid is expected to be joint with Huntington Ingalls Industries (HII), America’s largest military shipbuilder, and could involve transferring the intellectual property so American workers can build the Arrowhead 140 in the US. The US wants a small-to-medium general-purpose frigate that can escort convoys or operate independently, with ASW and anti-ship capability. Priority will go to a mature design that can be produced rapidly and in numbers.
Despite the absence of Type 31 from early reports of the designs under study, limited UK construction capacity would shape any offer. The opportunity stems from a presidential memorandum issued on 13 August that uses a national security waiver to open US Navy procurement to allied designs and, in limited cases, overseas construction. The Navy’s assessment is due by 12 November. Japan’s upgraded Mogami, South Korea’s Chungnam and Turkey’s Istanbul class have all been reported as candidates, with Hanwha’s ownership of the Philadelphia Shipyard widely seen as giving the Korean option an early edge.
The idea of a British firm building warships for the US Navy needs qualification. The memorandum follows the ‘Finland model’ in which no more than two ships may be built abroad, and only by suppliers investing in American shipbuilding, with the rest coming from US yards. Babcock has no shipyard in the US and Rosyth is fully committed to the RN’s ships for now, although is looking for export orders to provide sustained work in the long run. The most likely offer would be a design licence and technology transfer to a US yard, with Babcock acting as design authority and providing engineering support.
The Arrowhead 140 design has already been exported to Indonesia and Poland, with Babcock as design provider and technology partner. The same model is being pitched to Chile, where Hine visited in early October to propose local construction with the state yard ASMAR. Rosyth remains the only place Babcock itself is building the ships.
Babcock is already a trusted partner with the US submarine industrial base. Since 2014, its Rosyth and Bristol sites have been manufacturing tactical missile tube assemblies for General Dynamics Electric Boat as part of the Common Missile Compartment shared by the Royal Navy’s Dreadnought class and the US Navy’s Columbia class ballistic missile submarines. The work required major investment in advanced welding, quality assurance and digital manufacturing and supports around 200 specialist jobs.
The relationship with HII has deepened in parallel. The two companies signed a strategic agreement in 2023 covering nuclear decommissioning and construction 5 to combine HII’s REMUS uncrewed underwater vehicles with Babcock’s submarine weapon handling and launch systems. In December 2025, HII awarded Babcock its first outsourced contract for Newport News Virginia class work, authorising Rosyth to build complex assemblies for Block VI attack submarines . It is a small initial engineering contract for now, but it is a rare example of a foreign yard being trusted with structural work on American nuclear submarines, and it means Babcock now supplies both US submarine builders.
Together, Babcock and HII have also developed ARMOR Force (Autonomous and Remote, Maritime Operational Response). In this hybrid fleet concept, a Type 31 acts as the Common Command Vessel (CCV) directing a network of large uncrewed surface vessels from HII’s ROMULUS family.
Adding further complexity to the industrial relationships, HII’s Ingalls Shipbuilding is already the lead yard for FF(X), the US Navy’s patrol frigate derived from the Legend-class cutter, and HII also partners with HD Hyundai, one of the principal designers of the rival Chungnam class.
With the Mogami and Chungnam-class ships already at sea and the RN’s slow delivery schedule, Type 31 faces tough competition. A big attraction of Type 31 is its size, which would allow a broader choice of weapons and sensors, as well as better seakeeping than the Japanese or South Korean options.
Despite the USN’s increasingly desperate need for more surface combatants after the failure of the Constellation class , the whole effort also faces good old-fashioned ‘pork barrel’ Congressional opposition, with moves in the House to block funding for foreign-built combatants. Success, even purely as design licensor, would still be a major endorsement for an export campaign that already includes a head-to-head contest with the upgraded Mogami in New Zealand, the Chilean pitch and cooperation with Danish industry on a future air defence frigate. It would also support British design and engineering jobs, even if construction is all-American.
