title: Which airlines are flying to Riyadh? Latest schedules and cancellations
body: Travel to Riyadh remains disrupted after Yemen’s Houthis claimed they launched another strike on King Khalid International Airport on October 25, hours after Saudi authorities announced flights had resumed. Flightradar24 showed a small number of flights departing the airport on Monday, although most scheduled departures were cancelled. The kingdom's national carrier Saudia is operating some of its Riyadh-linked services through Dammam and Al Qassim, about 400km north-west of the capital. Riyadh Air has shifted several international routes to Al Qassim. UAE airlines Etihad Airways, Emirates, flydubai and Air Arabia have maintained flight suspensions or cancellations on routes to the Saudi capital. For passengers planning to travel to the Saudi capital, here’s what to know. Which UAE airlines have suspended flights to Riyadh? Etihad has cancelled all flights between Abu Dhabi and Riyadh until November 5. Emirates airline services from Dubai to Riyadh are currently scheduled to resume on November 8. But the planned return dates are subject to change. Meanwhile, flydubai has cancelled services to Riyadh through October 29. Air Arabia’s services from Sharjah to Riyadh also remain suspended, with no date announced to resume those flights in the airline's latest update. Where are Saudia flights operating? Saudia says some of its Riyadh flights are operating through Al Qassim and Dammam airports. Tickets include a bus transfer arranged by the airline between the airport and the Saudi capital. Passengers should check their booking and the airline’s instructions to confirm which airport they will use and the arrangements for their bus transfer. Which routes is Riyadh Air operating? Riyadh Air says that until further notice it is operating only to and from Cairo, Dhaka, Jeddah, London Heathrow, Lahore and Islamabad, all through Al Qassim airport. Passengers departing from Riyadh can check in at the InterContinental Durrat Al Riyadh hotel and take a complimentary bus to Al Qassim airport. The airline says the journey takes about four and a half hours. Hotel check-in opens eight hours and 15 minutes before the flight is set to depart and closes six hours and 30 minutes before it takes off. Passengers can also make their own way to Al Qassim airport, where the airline advises arriving at least three hours before departure. Does Riyadh airport reopening mean normal flights have resumed? No. King Khalid International Airport announced the reopening of two terminals from October 25, with Terminal 1 designated for domestic flights and Terminal 2 for international services operated by Saudi airlines. Passengers with confirmed bookings have been asked to contact their airline before heading to the airport. Some flights have taken off, but cancellations continue and airline arrangements vary. Passengers should confirm whether their flight will operate and which airport will be used, rather than relying solely on a published schedule. What should passengers do before travelling? People should check their flight directly with their airline, confirm their departure and arrival airports, and monitor messages about changes to their booking. Anyone using an airline-arranged bus transfer should confirm the meeting point and departure time, allowing time for the journey. Those with onward connections should ask their airline about arrangements if travel disruption affects their itinerary. Passengers whose services have been cancelled should contact their airline or booking agent to discuss rebooking or refund options.

title: Pomors boat museum opens on island in Northern Dvina River delta
body:
ARKHANGELSK, October 26. /TASS/. The museum of the karbas, a traditional vessel of the Pomors (or coast-dwellers), was opened on an island in the delta of the Northern Dvina River in the village of Kalkino near Arkhangelsk, a TASS correspondent reported. The Karbas is a sailing and rowing fishing and transport wooden vessel, common at least from the 15th century in the White and Barents Seas. Karbases are so common in the Arkhangelsk Region, that the world is practically a synonym of "boat".
The first syllable is stressed in the word "karbas." Karbases were mentioned in the Solovki Monastery notes in 1531. Apparently, by then, the White Sea coast inhabitants - the Pomors - had been actively using them.
"We have been building it for two years, quite a long time. The winters were so severe that it was impossible to work, and no roads to use. Now, we have here a museum that tells about the ancient history of karbases, and a club where everyone can learn how to sail karbases," Evgeny Shkaruba, leader of the Pomors' Shipbuilding Association, the project's author, told TASS.
The Karbas Museum's architecture is based on the Pomor wooden port structures of the 19th century: boat sheds, warehouses and fish warehouses that used to be built along coasts in berthing areas of the northern rivers and seas. The museum's building is divided into three zones. The first part is a museum, where a karbas is presented - it was built under the old technology without using nails. This part also hosts an exhibition about traditional Pomor boats.
The second part is a workshop where karbases are stored and repaired. Since 2017, the project participants have built 15 karbases using old technologies. The first one was built in the Arkhangelsk Region's Leshukonsky District back in 2017.
"We built the first karbas in 2017 together with Viktor Kuznetsov in Leshukonye," the project's author said. "It was a revelation. The main revelation was that the tradition, which is more than 500 years old, is still alive. This preserved karbas-building language is unique precisely due to its very long background. Over the time of the kind any structure develops to perfection."
The building's third part is the Karbas Club: a hall and a classroom for the theory of maritime affairs, a meeting place for members of the community that has formed around the Pomors' Shipbuilding Association's initiatives. The museum is located by the water, and four karbases are berthed by the pier there.
The island, where the museum was opened, is called the Krivaya Koshka (Crooked Cat). This is the territory of pilots, who used to settle there for several centuries. The Northern Dvina delta is very complicated for navigation, and thus the pilotage service was established in the area back in the 17th century.
Karbases were used for a variety of purposes. Some karbases were for hay delivery. Arkhangelsk is located in swamps, and hay used to be a problem there. Hay was delivered from the islands and from the Dvina's other side. People needed to have a lot of hay, as hay was practically gasoline of that time, said Evgeny Tenetov, the Northern Maritime Museum's director said. Other variations of karbases were built for herring, for sea hunting, and special pilotage karbases, which pilots used to approach vessels and board them.
"A karbas was in every yard, in every family. Sometimes even more than one - for different purposes," the Northern Maritime Museum's director said.
Interestingly, even houses in Calchino were built of ships. In the late 19th and early 20th centuries, Russian grain supplies to Norway ran through Arkhangelsk. From Vologda, grain was transported along the river on rough-hewn barges. Further on, the grain was re-loaded onto sea schooners, and the barges were dismantled. The locals used their parts to build pavements, warehouses, and parts of houses.
"If you walk along the streets of Calchino and take a closer look at the houses, you will see holes of the same diameter on the log cabins, and those holes are located more or less synchronously. These are the holes for the nails used to hold the logs together when they were not houses, but ships," the historian explained.
Elena Kudryashova, Vice President of the Lomonosov Foundation, Chair of the Arkhangelsk Regional Branch and Vice President of the Association of Polar Explorers, told TASS that Calchino had been one of the biggest pilot villages in the Arkhangelsk Region. Nowadays, it is a very picturesque village, where has been erected a memorial cross in honor of the 400th anniversary of the pilotage service, and a museum of Pomors.
"Nikolay Portyanko, a well-known lawyer, lived here for many years and created a completely unique museum of everyday Pomor culture. He has completely renovated a traditional pilot house, and all rooms there have been turned into museum spaces. He was collecting furniture, utensils, paintings, carpets, and statuettes," she said. "The villagers are very sensitive to shipbuilding and to the development of marine spaces. Even on the playground there are two boats that were once used, but now the kids are playing on them."
The Karbas Museum project won the Museum 4.0 competition of the Vladimir Potanin Charitable Foundation's Museum Without Borders charity program. The Karbas Club project's implementation was supported by the Arkhangelsk Region Governor's Center.

title: Iran in state of war, not hesitate to defend itself: Baghaei
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 26 (MNA) – Highlighting the ongoing war between Iran and US-Israel, Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei says that the country is in a state of war and will not hesitate to defend itself against any renewed aggression.
Speaking in his weekly press briefing on Monday, he emphasized that the powerful Armed Forces of the country do not have the slightest hesitation in defending the Islamic Iran with all its might.
“We are in a state of war and we will certainly not hesitate in exercising our inherent and inalienable rights to defense,” the spokesman underlined.
Referring to recent diplomatic developments, Baghaei stated, "Regarding the region and in particular, the Islamic Republic of Iran itself, we are monitoring the situation very closely with extreme power and and intelligence, and have prepared ourselves for any scenarios."
Turning to the Knesset elections in Israel and the narrative being pushed by Israeli officials concerning the possibility of a preemptive move by Iran to disrupt the electoral process, he stressed, “I do not believe there is an 'election' taking place there. What exists is a rivalry between various factions vying to commit even greater acts of malice. It is a contest among individuals whose primary platform is, 'I can commit more crimes and killings than you can.' It makes no difference to us who takes the helm of a regime whose track record shows it has brought nothing to our region but violence and slaughter. This regime is highly skilled at conducting 'false flag' operations."
Iran does not hesitate to exercise its inherent right to defense.
Iran’s powerful Armed Forces harbor not the slightest hesitation in defending Iran. The country is in a state of war, and it will certainly not delay in exercising its inherent and inalienable right to defense.
Details on Iran hosting officials from three regional countries
Regarding Iran hosting officials from three regional countries, the foreign ministry spokesperson stated, "As announced by the Deputy Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council (SNSC), Tehran is hosting officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey; the initiative for this meeting was proposed during Pakistani Army Chief General Asim Munir’s visit to Tehran."
This meeting could serve as a foundation for further initiatives. For years, “we have maintained that regional security cannot be realized without the involvement of the regional countries itself. Discussions are expected to take place during the meetings these three officials will hold with the President and the Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council. This is the initial session, and its agenda remains to be studied. In general, such a meeting cannot be considered without taking into account the consequences stemming from the acts of aggression by the United States and the Zionist regime.”
Regarding the claims made by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio who, alongside his hostile remarks against Iran and Iranian civilization, has also called on the other side of the world for Cuban cooperation toward "positive change" and the overthrow of the Cuban government, while urging the Cuban people to contact the CIA.
"We are witnessing a reactionary trend and a return to classical colonialism. Whereas the Americans, during the peak of their influence in Latin America, at least attempted to maintain a degree of secrecy, they now openly incite other nations to change their own governments."
Need to declare solidarity with the Cuban people
The foreign ministry spokesperson stated it is necessary to express solidarity with the people of Cuba. The people of this country are facing difficult conditions due to the blockade and illegitimate sanctions imposed by the United States. Cuba possesses neither nuclear weapons nor anything else that would justify such pressures; yet, for seven decades, it has faced severe US sanctions.
Talks underway to resolve border issues with Pakistan and Iraq.
Regarding the closure of the borders and their current status, Baghaei noted that Pakistani side, from the beginning, indicated that the issue is technical in nature and that certain updates are required. Iran has also received reports that several terrorist acts had been planned. Consultations with Pakistan are ongoing, and the process is moving in a positive direction. It is hoped that the technical issues will be resolved as soon as possible.
With regards to Iraq, officials there are also actively following up the issue precisely. For that, Iraqi authorities have stated that sanctions against Iran will inevitably affect the people of Iraq as well. Therefore, the interests of both nations must be taken into account. This is not merely a matter of sentiment—though feelings and emotions certainly hold importance. Officials from neighboring countries, as well as Iranian officials, are pursuing this issue with great seriousness, and the problems will be resolved in the shortest time possible.
Confirmation of Qatari delegation's visit to Tehran
Confirming a visit to Tehran by a Qatari delegation, Baghaei stated this is not unusual. Given the current tensions in the region, it is natural for regional states to make efforts to convey messages and put forward potential proposals. This visit was one of several that have taken place over the past three to four weeks, during which Qatar sought to present its own positions and points of view. The visit was both bilateral in nature and conducted within the framework of mediation.
Referring to the threats surrounding Iran, the foreign ministry spokesperson noted, "Those responsible for closely monitoring these threats are indeed doing so and have the necessary measures on their agenda. We have heard the reports; throughout the 40-day period of defense, whenever any act of malice has been directed at Iran, Iranian forces have defended the country decisively—and this will continue to be the case in the future."
Insecurity of Strait of Hormuz “one of the factors driving up oil prices”
Regarding Trump’s claims about Iran, he added, "As I have stated before, what matters to us is safeguarding Iran’s national interests. The rise in oil prices is due to the Americans themselves, who have rendered the Strait of Hormuz insecure. A few months ago, Trump declared that he acts like a pirate."
A for their other claims, they are hardly surprising. Regarding Minab, they even allege that the crime was the work of artificial intelligence. In reality, however, the actual state of affairs—both in the region and globally—asserts itself over such delusions and baseless claims, he continued.
Iran's armed forces to respond to any military aggression with full readiness
In response to a question regarding Iran’s potential actions against data centers in regional countries, Esmaeil Baghaei stated, "How we would respond to any form of military aggression falls outside my area of ​​expertise, and I cannot offer a comment on it. Our powerful Armed Forces are in a state of full readiness and will demonstrate how they can catch the enemy by surprise. The experience gained over the past eight months will be put to use in the future."
"In our defensive responses, unlike the opposing side, which has made no distinction between military and civilian targets, we have maintained this distinction. As for the selection of targets, the competent authorities will make those decisions."
Regarding Barack Obama’s remarks that Iran did not possess nuclear weapons, the fact is that Iran did not have nuclear weapons is a reality. Iran has never sought nuclear weapons, and this is part of the reality of the last two decades, he maintained.
Iran participated in the negotiations and signed an agreement, but the United States withdrew from it without any reason. American public opinion needs to be informed of these facts.
Baghaei addressed the rising threat levels between Iran and the United States as well as the holding of meetings, stating, "The American side is not serious about negotiations. Over the past two years, the US has demonstrated that it confuses negotiation with dictation, and it keeps repeating the same lie."
Iran never closed the window of diplomacy. It [Iran] demonstrated this in practice and in 2015 we entered into a treaty that it adhered to for three to four years after that and this was the US that violated it. Didn't Obama and Biden sign the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding?
Iran is both resolute in its self-defense and serious about diplomacy.
Find a country more responsible than Iran. Despite all these circumstances, it still keeps the door to diplomacy open. Just as it acted with determination and seriousness in its own defense, it is equally serious when it comes to diplomacy.
The Iranian people possess a capacity for logic and experience in diplomacy, as well as negotiating acumen. However, the other side has yet to reach the conclusion that when it [US] speaks of diplomacy, it must also adhere to its requirements.
In conclusion, regarding the impact of oil prices on the negotiations, he stated, "That is not the case; such a multifaceted equation should not be viewed through the lens of a single cause. What matters to us is securing Iran’s interests. It is absolutely not the case that we would look at oil prices before engaging in negotiations. We are not going to halt diplomacy because of a single factor; we take action whenever the country’s interests dictate it. Bear in mind that any decision in this regard is reached by consensus and is not one-dimensional."

title: Investors see economic upside for Israel if opposition beats Netanyahu in upcoming elections
body: Israel's markets have soared despite three years of war and political turmoil, but some investors see further upside if the opposition defeats Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Tuesday's election, potentially easing regional tensions and political risk.Opinion polls point to a tight contest, with neither Netanyahu's ruling Likud bloc nor an opposition alliance centered on former military chief Gadi Eisenkot expected to secure the 61 seats in the 120-seat Knesset needed to govern.That raises the prospect of lengthy coalition negotiations or even another election, all at time when one of the key drivers of the Israeli market rally - the global frenzy around AI - has also started to splutter.Since the October 7 Hamas attacks in 2023, the Tel Aviv stock market has soared 130%, far outpacing Wall Street's 80% gain, while the shekel has climbed 25%, one of the world's strongest currency performances.Analysts attribute some of that strength to Israel's tech sector and the global AI boom, while defense spending, which has nearly doubled to around 8% of GDP, has also provided a boost.With both Netanyahu and Eisenkot vowing to maintain pressure on Hamas and Iran, markets are focused on their broader policy differences. JPMorgan estimates the shekel could swing as much as 3% depending on the result.Opposition victory could improve Israeli economic positionAn opposition victory that improves relations with Western allies and halts a judicial overhaul that sparked mass protests in 2023 could strengthen the currency, JPMorgan said, while another Netanyahu-led government could weaken it.Billionaire investor Bill Ackman, while stopping short of backing a candidate, said a government without far-right ministers Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich would signal that Israel was "turning a new page," potentially helping rebuild its international credibility and expand the Abraham Accords with its neighbors.IBI Investment House also expects an opposition victory to lift the markets. "From a capital markets perspective, this would likely be reflected in a decline in Israel's risk premium, appreciation pressure on the shekel, and a positive reaction in the local market," IBI's Chief Economist Rafi Gozlan said.According to prediction market Polymarket, close to 60% are betting on Eisenkot becoming the next Israeli prime minister, compared with 27% for Netanyahu."The most significant issue is what the result will mean for the region," said Equity Bank's chief economic adviser Charlie Robertson. "If Netanyahu is reelected, it might increase the chances of further escalation with Iran, whereas a defeat might be seen as lessening the tensions."But the prospect of gains under an opposition government does not mean investors expect Israeli assets to suffer if Netanyahu remains in power. Stocks and bonds have proved remarkably resilient through years of war and political upheaval, and some investors remain confident in the economy regardless of the election outcome.Union Investment's Sergey Dergachev has been buying Israeli bonds ahead of the election, betting the economy and companies he favors will remain fundamentally strong. "We are very constructive on Israeli credits going into the election," Dergachev said, adding that bonds were less prone to major swings and the region's intertwined conflicts should eventually ease.Tel Aviv shares were up around 1% in the final session ahead of Tuesday's vote, taking their year-to-date gain to about 12%.However, both they and the shekel have pulled back some 10% since May. Analysts again point to the strong link to tech, given global AI indexes have also been dropping, although there has been one nagging issue throughout the last three years.Despite the rally, foreign investors remain cautious. Copley Fund Research data show the share of global funds holding Israeli equities is at a record low, having fallen sharply since 2023.TS Lombard's Christopher Granville cited central bank estimates that the war had cost the economy more than $55 billion by last year, equivalent to 8.6% in cumulative lost GDP growth.Public debt, budget deficit high amid Iran warIsrael's fiscal position is another focus. Public debt has risen to nearly 70% of GDP, about 10 percentage points higher than in 2022, while the budget deficit is expected to remain around 4.5% of GDP, up from less than 2% before the conflict.Central bank head Amir Yaron stressed last week the need to "preserve adequate fiscal policy space" given the Iran war.Like stocks, Israeli government bonds have rallied, returning about 30% over the last two years, more than double the main emerging market indexes.The main risk for investors is an inconclusive result that prolongs political uncertainty, delaying budgets, reforms and investment, some investors believe.That uncertainty can produce sharp short-term swings. Tel Aviv Stock Exchange research covering the last 10 elections found volatility in leading share indexes rose by as much as 45% in the weeks after voting compared with a typical week. But initial losses were typically recovered within a month, with the indexes posting an average gain of about 1.7%.Over a longer horizon, the TA-125 returned an average 16.4% in the year following elections, compared with a long-term annual average of 11.5%, the research found. Political deadlock often weighed on stocks before voting, but the effects typically faded within months, said Nissan Avraham, an analyst at the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange's research unit.Israeli businesses continue thriving despite political, regional upheavalThat record supports the view that elections matter less for Israeli companies than many investors assume.Lior Yochpaz, chief investment officer at insurance company Menora Mivtachim, said businesses have continued to thrive despite years of political upheaval, judicial overhaul proposals, and regional conflict, helped by a relatively business-friendly environment.For some investors, however, the more attractive election trade lies outside Israel. TT International's Jean-Charles Sambor said an opposition victory or weakened Netanyahu government could ease regional tensions and benefit Lebanese bonds."The best way to play it for us is through other Middle East countries, and for us Lebanon is a good proxy," Sambor said.

title: Dubai announces lane closures on Emirates Road from Monday to clear the way for self-driving taxi tests
body: Dubai will partially close a stretch on one of the emirate's main motorways during peak hours this week, to enable tests of self-driving taxis to be carried out. Vehicles will be barred from using three lanes on Emirates Road, also known as E611, opposite Al Maktoum International Airport, the Roads and Transport Authority said. The rules will apply between 9am and 4pm daily from Monday, October 26, until Saturday, October 31. Al Maktoum International Airport Tunnel will be fully closed during this period to allow the autonomous vehicle trials to take place. Authorities called on motorists to plan their journeys in advance and follow road signs to ensure smooth travel. Autonomous strategy takes shape The road closures further highlight Dubai's commitment to integrating rapidly evolving autonomous technology into its road infrastructure. In September, the emirate's government launched a cutting-edge testing centre where future fleets of autonomous vehicles will be geared up for the demands of the emirate's busy road network. The Dubai Mobility Labs – based at Dubai Silicon Oasis – features a vast multipurpose area including testing tracks where self-driving technology can be safely put through the paces before being approved for public use. The high-tech centre has been established by the RTA in partnership with the Dubai Integrated Economic Zones Authority and is a key step in the emirate's drive to make 25 per cent of all journeys autonomous by 2030. Dubai Mobility Labs provides a controlled environment to simulate a wide variety of traffic scenarios, alongside real-world testing on public roads extending from Dubai Silicon Oasis to Al Qudra. Self-driving vehicles will be assessed under diverse operating conditions to examine their ability to respond to challenging traffic and weather across 248 test scenarios. The testing ground is critical to check sensing and decision-making systems, to assess the capacity to adapt to evolving road situations, and to ensure vehicle readiness before modes of transport progress to trials on public roads and move to full operations. The Dubai Mobility Labs has already held successful trials of autonomous driving technology and vehicles developed by global companies, including WeRide, Pony.ai and Tesla. Driving progress Meanwhile, new research has shown that the vast majority of UAE motorists are ready to embrace autonomous transport - even as other parts of the world remain more reluctant. The study by Bain & Company, a global consultant company, found 90 percent of people in the UAE would consider purchasing a self-driving vehicle. The survey of more than 12,000 people placed the UAE just behind Indonesia (93 per cent) and India (91 per cent) but ahead of China (84 per cent), Europe (47 per cent) and the US (40 per cent). Hitting the road Uber Technologies started operating Baidu's Apollo Go driverless service in its Dubai network in August, with plans to introduce thousands of the autonomous vehicles in the emirate. The service, which will use Baidu's sixth-generation RT6 robotaxi , will initially be available in Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim, with plans to expand. Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed , Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence, launched a self-driving taxi network in the city in February. Sheikh Hamdan inaugurated the commercial operations of the Chinese-made Baidu Apollo Go self-driving cars and took a trip in one of the vehicles to attend the World Governments Summit. In September last year, Dubai announced that a 15 square kilometre testing zone for self-driving taxis, delivery and other service vehicles would be established in Festival City and Dubai Creek Harbour to evaluate how autonomous transport can work on a larger scale.

title: SPLM-IO rejects claims of mass defection in E. Equatoria
body: The leadership of the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-in-Opposition (SPLM-IO) in Eastern Equatoria State has rejected claims that about 100 members defected alongside former state party leader and former deputy governor Karlo Andrew Akwo to the SPLM Party. During a press conference in Torit on Friday, 23 October, the SPLM-IO acting chairperson, Jildo Abala Remy, described the reported defection as an individual decision rather than a collective move by the party’s membership across the state. The press statement followed reports of Akwo’s defection to the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement (SPLM) in government. According to Abala, the SPLM-IO continues to operate across Eastern Equatoria’s eight counties. He reaffirmed the party’s commitment to peace, political dialogue and national development. He also appealed to President Salva Kiir Mayardit to pardon all political detainees, regardless of their political affiliation, and to call an inclusive dialogue of all political stakeholders. Asked whether they are ready for the elections slated for December, Abala said the SPLM-IO was fully prepared and was organizing its members ahead of the polls. For her part, Imoya Christine Lopwodo of the SPLM-IO and member of the Eastern Equatoria Human Rights Commission, also disputed the reported number of defectors, claiming that Akwo left with only three members rather than the approximately 100 cited in reports. Lopwodo, who announced her intention to contest for a seat in the Eastern Equatoria State Parliament to represent Ikotos County on the SPLM-IO ticket, said the party remained committed to participating in the elections. She described the reported figure of 100 defectors as inaccurate and urged the former party leader not to misrepresent the status of the opposition movement in the state. Meanwhile, Ochola Bosco Oringa, a former SPLM-IO minister of agriculture in Eastern Equatoria, said the defection was a personal decision and did not represent the position of the entire party. He acknowledged that Akwo’s departure could raise questions about the party’s future but maintained that its structures remained operational. He said the SPLM-IO continued to mobilize supporters across the state’s eight counties and was updating its membership records in preparation for forthcoming party activities and elections. The acting chairperson also urged political leaders, party members and the public to avoid inflammatory statements and respect the right of every South Sudanese citizen to choose a political affiliation freely. The statement further called on the caretaker government of Eastern Equatoria, under General Louis Lobong Lojore, to continue working with the SPLM-IO leadership to promote peace and stability in the state. South Sudan is expected to hold national elections in December 2026, although preparations and political activities continue amid ongoing debates over the readiness of political parties and the implementation of the peace agreement. The post SPLM-IO rejects claims of mass defection in E. Equatoria appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Zelensky: Ukraine Offered US 3 Ways to Stop Strikes on Russian Oil Refineries
body:
Ukraine was prepared to halt strikes on Russian oil refineries at the request of US President Donald Trump’s team, but only if one of three conditions was met, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said in an interview with journalist Alla Mazur.
Speaking on the TSN.Tyzhden (TSN.The Week) program, Zelensky said that Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries could not have a significant impact on global prices, noting that Russia accounts for only 2% of global diesel exports, while the remaining 98% comes from other exporters.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“How can one reach an ‘energy truce’ with the Russians? You might be hated, but you should at least be respected as an adversary. They must respect Ukraine – and our strength. He [Putin] inflicts great pain upon us, and we respond. It is a matter of justice,” Zelensky said.
According to him, Ukraine had proposed three possible ways to resolve the dispute to the American side. However, none of the proposals had been implemented, which is why Ukraine continues to strike Russian oil refineries, he said.
“I said: if you want us to stop hitting diesel facilities and refineries, then they [the Russians] must stop striking our power infrastructure. That is fair – an ‘energy truce.’ A second option: you enable Starlink coverage over Russia, and we show you the locations of their ballistic missile launchers. We want to destroy them.
“The third option is this: if you won’t enable Starlink for us – which is entirely up to you – and you’ve said that Musk doesn’t want to, then give us something that doesn’t depend on Musk or Putin: missiles for the Patriot systems,” Zelensky said.
He added that Ukraine had received none of the three proposed forms of support.
“That is why the reaction is what it is – we are fighting for our lives,” Zelensky said.
Zelensky also said that lifting sanctions against Russia should be considered only as part of the process of ending the war, rather than as a precondition for negotiations.
“I would not want us to approach the meeting of the three leaders – Ukraine, the United States, and Russia – having already lifted all sanctions against the Russian Federation. This is a crucial point. Sanctions were imposed in response to aggression, not as a price for the mere opportunity to talk.”
He said he had conveyed this position to the American delegation, cautioning that Russia could benefit from sanctions relief before any agreement on ending the war had been reached.
He warned that once sanctions were lifted, restoring them could prove difficult, requiring Ukraine and its partners to rebuild international support for a new round of restrictions.
“Without sanctions, we could reach a point in the trilateral dialogue where the future remains uncertain, yet the sanctions have already been removed,” Zelensky added.
He said that the international community had adopted more than 20 separate sanctions packages against Russia and questioned whether the same political resolve could be mobilized again if Moscow failed to follow through on its commitments.
“I do not want us to find ourselves without any leverage – lacking sanctions, funds, or frozen assets – when we sit down with Putin. Because then, as Mr. Trump put it, we would truly have very few cards left in our deck,” Zelensky added.
Zelensky also said Ukraine, the United States, the European Union and NATO planned to hold a broad meeting in Brussels this week to discuss security issues, guarantees and European integration.
According to the president, the format of the discussions had expanded following a visit by the American delegation to St. Petersburg and a preliminary briefing to Ukraine.
The talks had initially been limited in scope, but the Americans were now seeking a broader discussion, Zelensky said.
“The Americans [after Oslo] went to St. Petersburg; we received a ‘brief’ from them, but now they want more than just a ‘brief’ – they want a broad discussion regarding security, guarantees, the EU, and involvement,” he added.
The meeting was expected to take place this week, tentatively on Tuesday or Wednesday. Zelensky said the participants would include representatives of Ukraine, the US and the EU at the presidential level, as well as NATO, represented by the alliance’s secretary-general.

title: Russian troops liberate about 50 square km in Sumy, Kharkov Regions over week — expert
body:
LUGANSK, October 26. /TASS/. Fighters of Russia’s Battlegroup North took control of about 50 square kilometers in the Sumy and Kharkov Regions over the past week, achieving the best results in liberating settlements in the special military operations zone, military expert Andrey Marochko reported.
He noted that last week, Russian forces freed 13 settlements: two in the Kharkov Region, four in the Donetsk People’s Republic (DPR), one in the Dnepropetrovsk Region, and six in the Zaporozhye Region.
"The best results in liberating occupied territories over the past week were achieved by servicemen of the Battlegroup North, who gained control of about 50 square km of territory in the Sumy and Kharkov Regions," he wrote on his VKontakte social media page after analyzing data released by the Russian Defense Ministry.

title: Bank of Russia buys $148.81 mln worth of yuan in October 23 settlement
body:
MOSCOW, October 26. /TASS/. The Bank of Russia purchased 12 bln rubles ($148.81 mln) worth of yuan on the domestic market with settlement on October 23, 2026, according to data published on the regulator’s website.
The volume of foreign currency purchases on the domestic market with settlement on October 22 also totaled 12 bln rubles.
The Bank of Russia conducts foreign currency purchase and sale operations on the domestic market through the yuan-ruble instrument in the currency section of the Moscow Exchange.

title: ‘Georgia without Ivanishvili’: Opposition launches new wave of protests – photos and video
body: New wave of protests in Georgia On 25 October, thousands of people gathered in Tbilisi for a major opposition-organised protest under the slogan ‘Georgia without Ivanishvili’. Waving flags and blowing horns, protesters gathered outside Tbilisi State University before setting off on a mass march towards Rustaveli metro station. German foundations leave Georgia: what the crisis in Berlin-Tbilisi relations means EU to consider reviewing its policy towards Georgia: what will change in January? Scenes from the protests in Georgia: video and photos With this rally, the opposition announced the start of a new wave of protests in Georgia . The next rally is scheduled for 28 November. The date is symbolic: exactly two years earlier, the ruling Georgian Dream party publicly announced that it was suspending EU accession talks. The announcement sparked ongoing pro-European protests , with demonstrators demanding fresh, free and fair parliamentary elections. Key messages from opposition leaders The rally’s organisers, leaders of the pro-Western opposition, addressed the demonstrators. “ This day, 28 November, represents a defeat for all of us as long as Bidzina Ivanishvili remains in power. The postponement of our integration into the European Union is a defeat for all of us. The indefinite delay of a brighter future for our children is a defeat for all of us ,” said Nika Gvaramia, one of the leaders of the Coalition for Change. “Ivanishvili’s group is trying to formally strip us of one of the most important achievements secured by the United National Movement – multiparty elections in Georgia. They now seek to legally establish a one-party dictatorship,” said Levan Tsutskiridze, leader of the Freedom Square party. “Don’t like it? Too bad”: third day of Constitutional Court hearings on opposition ban in Georgia The day focused on motions filed by Gakharia for Georgia, all of which were rejected by the court. Hearings will resume on 26 October and continue throughout the week “ It may seem that Bidzina Ivanishvili is making such a brazen decision that we should all despair. In fact, the opposite is true. By banning any alternative, Ivanishvili is acknowledging a crisis of his own legitimacy. He is admitting that he no longer trusts the Georgian people – that he fears the free choice of Georgian citizens, and quite rightly so ,” said Tamar Chergoleishvili , leader of the Federalists movement. Young people and other protesters were also among the speakers. “ Look at one another – you are surrounded by people who refuse to give up, who continue to fight for a better future for our country, ” student Luka Mishveladze told the crowd. Background The 25 October rally was part of Georgia’s pro-European protest movement, which has been ongoing for nearly two years. The demonstration was announced and organised by the opposition. The date was no coincidence: on 24 October 2024, Georgia held crucial parliamentary elections , with the country’s European future at stake. The election results remain disputed both domestically and internationally. The vote marked the beginning of a major political crisis in Georgia, leading to strained relations with Western partners, sanctions and the suspension of multimillion-dollar aid packages. Should state have right to ban political parties? Tbilisi street poll – Video Most respondents said that banning political parties was unacceptable in a country that claims to be a democracy. The protests were met with violent police crackdowns, including beatings, torture and arrests of activists. Several packages of repressive laws were adopted, while pressure on the media and civil society intensified, including measures that effectively blocked access to funding. Western institutions adopted numerous resolutions criticising these developments. The political crisis entered a new phase when the ruling Georgian Dream party moved to ban pro-Western opposition groups it deemed unacceptable. Almost all the parties that organised the 25 October rally and announced a new wave of protests were among those facing a proposed ban. Новая волна протестов в Грузии Новости, события в Грузии

title: Black Stars need time to recover from poor run – GFA
body: Ghana Football Association (GFA) Communications Director Henry Asante Twum has cautioned that restoring the Black Stars to their former level will require time following the team’s disappointing run of results. The men’s senior national team has endured a difficult spell, recording just one victory in their last eight matches across all competitions. Their struggles have also affected their Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualification campaign, with Ghana losing their opening two Group C matches against Ivory Coast and The Gambia. The results have left Ghana at the bottom of Group C, while Ivory Coast and The Gambia occupy the top positions with six points each. “It wouldn’t take a day, wouldn’t take a week; it’ll take a lot more effort and a lot of time to get the team back on track,” Twum told JoySports. “Where we are at this moment, leadership is aware of the challenges that confront us, and efforts are being made to get the team back on track,” he added. “When you win, you’re hailed, but you don’t expect the people to hail you when the results are poor. That’s what leadership must know and accept.” Meanwhile, A five-member committee recommended Black Queens coach Kim Lars Björkegren for the Black Stars coaching job temporarily, with Ibrahim Tanko and Godwin Attram proposed as his assistants, following the departure of Carlos Queiroz. The Black Stars will turn their attention to a double-header against Somalia in November as they look to improve their performances and revive their qualification hopes.

title: Brazil’s Lula clinches poll victory, Bolsonaro seeks to annul election
body: Brazil’s leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva pulled off a dramatic comeback on Sunday as he clinched a re-election victory, but his rival Flavio Bolsonaro refused to accept the loss and said he would seek to annul the vote. With Lula’s victory, Brazil staved off a conservative wave that has seen numerous countries — such as Argentina, Chile, Colombia, and Peru — all shift right, backed by US President Donald Trump. The leftist icon, who turns 81 on Tuesday, defied projections to win an unprecedented fourth term. According to official results, he won 51.8 percent of the votes to 48.2 percent for Flavio Bolsonaro, with Lula pulling around 4.4 million more votes. The senator is the son of former far-right president Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year jail term for attempting a coup after his loss to Lula in the country’s last election in 2022. Sunday’s vote was marked by confusion after a Supreme Court ruling extended voting by two hours as some polling stations had already closed. The move came at the request of Lula who complained that buses had been pulled from circulation in various cities, barring citizens from voting. Flavio Bolsonaro also requested an extension in some regions due to heavy rains, but he described the decision as “unacceptable” and a “dirty trick” “It is impossible to recognize the results. I am going to request the annulment of these elections,” he said, stone-faced, in a brief speech in Brasilia. No candidate who lost the first round has gone on to win the second in Brazil since 1989, the first direct election after the end of the country’s military dictatorship. “People went to vote because we managed to convince them that voting was very important for ensuring democracy in the country,” Lula said in his first comments after the win. Fireworks and vuvuzelas rang out in Rio de Janeiro, while thousands of people dressed in red, the color of Lula’s Workers’ Party, streamed into the streets of Sao Paulo to celebrate. – Lula’s fight back – After the first-round defeat, the left swung into action with massive rallies, declaring “Never Again Bolsonaro” and revamped their social media strategy. The abstention rate decreased from the first round, falling from 21 percent to 19 percent. Julio Canelo, 42, a lawyer celebrating in Rio de Janeiro hailed a victory for “the entire democratic spectrum.” “It was the result of the people mobilizing, in the streets and online,” he told AFP. A fierce social media battle drew in Meta, parent company of WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram, which Lula’s campaign accused of favoring his opponent with “algorithmic manipulation.” Meta denied this but acknowledged that some of Lula’s campaign ads had been mistakenly deactivated due to technical errors. “We are going to have to regulate them,” Lula said of social media companies after his win. A bitter campaign marred by scandals and mudslinging laid bare the deep divisions that have plagued Brazil over the past decade. – A country split in two – Lula heads into a fourth term with almost half of the nation having rejected him, desperate for change. He rose from poverty to become president in 2003 and was re-elected in 2006. Lula made a dramatic return to office in 2022 elections after a corruption scandal saw him jailed for over 18 months. The charges were annulled on procedural grounds. In his third term, Lula oversaw a drop in inflation and unemployment, and lifted millions out of hunger, but many voters felt gloomy about the high cost of living and crime. Flavio Bolsonaro, 45, pitched himself as more moderate and jovial than his father and managed to galvanize conservatives as well as less ideological voters wanting something new. “We’re in a deep hole, things are dire. People can barely afford to eat — buying meat is out of the question,” said Tereza Cristina Ramos, a 68-year-old retiree, who voted in Rio de Janeiro. Already one of the world’s oldest leaders, Lula will be 85 by the end of his new term in 2030. He is also facing a hostile Congress dominated by the right. Lula’s campaign leaned heavily on the theme of sovereignty in the face of commercial and diplomatic pressure from Trump’s United States. “This country will not accept being anyone’s backyard,” he said Sunday. Lula received congratulations from Chile’s far-right president, Jose Antonio Kast, and Ecuador’s right-wing Daniel Noboa — both close Trump allies. Mexico’s left-wing President Claudia Sheinbaum wrote on X, saying “Long live democracy, the people of Brazil won.” The post Brazil’s Lula clinches poll victory, Bolsonaro seeks to annul election appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Ukrainian drone attack on Voronezh causes fires at facilities — governor
body:
VORONEZH, October 26. /TASS/. Fires broke out at several industrial facilities, an office building in central Voronezh, a school stadium, and other locations as a result of a Ukrainian drone attack, regional governor Alexander Gusev reported.

title: Vote For ‘Outstanding Warrior’ Netanyahu, Trump Tells Israelis
body: US President Donald Trump on Sunday called on Israelis to cast their ballots for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in upcoming elections, citing the US-Israel war against Iran as an example of “winning together.” “When you go to the Polls please remember that Bibi has been an outstanding Warrior Prime Minister,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform, referring to Netanyahu by his nickname. Israeli election contender Gadi Eisenkot vowed to unite the country as he held his final major rally before the vote, while Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu received fresh backing from US President Donald Trump. Netanyahu has campaigned heavily on his security credentials, but Eisenkot has cast him as unfit to lead and pledged a state commission of inquiry into the failings that led to Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attack under the incumbent’s watch. Polls had shown Netanyahu and Eisenkot running neck and neck before a ban on new polling took effect in the three days before Tuesday’s vote. On Sunday, Trump urged Israelis to vote for Netanyahu, citing the US-Israel war against Iran as an example of “winning together”. “When you go to the Polls please remember that Bibi has been an outstanding Warrior Prime Minister,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform, using Netanyahu’s nickname. At his event, Eisenkot pledged to heal divisions inside Israeli society after Netanyahu’s divisive tenure, and voiced “a commitment to security and the economy”. “Our goal is not for one side to defeat the other. That is not our way,” he said on Sunday to an audience of hundreds. “We will work to bring all Israelis together again — those who voted for us and those who did not.” Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu (C) waves to his supporters during a Likud Party meet-and-greet held as part of the campaign ahead of Israel’s legislative election, at King Solomon Hotel in Netanya on October 22, 2026….AFP A relative newcomer to politics — in contrast with Netanyahu and his 30 years on the scene — Eisenkot’s pledge to unite Israelis has resonated with some voters, and for many the ex-army chief’s plain-spokenness is part of his appeal. “I feel that he’s a rock for us… he’s someone I can trust,” Yael Shkedi, a 66-year-old jewellery maker, said at Eisenkot’s rally. “Amid all this chaos, what really matters to me is this feeling of someone who can somehow bring everyone together, almost like a father figure.” In his speech, Eisenkot said he would “always look you in the eye and tell the truth”, and pledged to “take responsibility for both successes and failures”. He also appealed directly to wavering supporters of Netanyahu’s Likud party, urging them to change course. “Deep down, you too know that Israel cannot go on like this,” he said. “Israel needs change.” Netanyahu’s critics accuse him of putting his political survival above the greater good, and he is currently facing trial on corruption charges, which he denies. Rally attendee Chen Sharon, an army reservist, said she wanted “people that I can count on” in office. “We need someone that we can actually believe his values and what he represents to us,” she said. Gadi Eisenkot, Israel’s former military chief of staff and leader of the Yashar party, addresses supporters at the party’s final campaign rally before the legislative election, in Tel Aviv on October 25, 2026. ‘A Catastrophe For Israel’ Over the course of the campaign, Netanyahu has played to Israeli voters’ opposition to the creation of a Palestinian state, and posters have been splashed across the country with the slogan “Either the Right or Palestine”. Netanyahu also touted the still-unresolved war that he launched against Iran alongside Trump, seeking to tar his main rival as being soft on the Islamic republic. Appearing after Eisenkot’s rally on Channel 14, Netanyahu again suggested the ex-general and his allies “want to create a Palestinian state, a catastrophe for Israel”. “They will not destroy Iran’s nuclear programme,” he told a boisterous studio audience. “We’ve done 90 percent of the work, 10 percent remains. Who is going to do it? Eisenkot and the Muslim Brotherhood? No. Only I can do it.” Eisenkot has said he is opposed to a Palestinian state, but has vowed to crack down on extremist West Bank settlers who have attacked Palestinians with impunity. Netanyahu on Sunday posted an AI-generated image of a mushroom cloud engulfing Tel Aviv, alongside text attributed to a right-wing political commentator calling Iran an existential threat and arguing that all the other issues discussed this election season were trivial in comparison. In a post on X addressing Netanyahu on Saturday, Eisenkot accused the premier of playing up the Iran threat when it suited him politically. “You have once again failed spectacularly and blatantly to achieve the war objectives you yourself set,” he added. Longtime opposition leader Yair Lapid, who has promised to join a coalition with Eisenkot, said Netanyahu had “lost his grip”. “Yesterday, Netanyahu announced that U.S. security aid was over and that sanctions would crush our economy. This morning, he posted a video in which an atomic bomb lands on Tel Aviv,” he said on X. “This man has lost his grip. We absolutely must send him home.” AFP The post Vote For ‘Outstanding Warrior’ Netanyahu, Trump Tells Israelis appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Ghana U-15s thrash Guam 7-0 to maintain perfect FIFA World Cup Festival run
body: Ghana U-15 Boys team continued their perfect run at the FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival with a dominant 7-0 victory over Guam in their third Group W match in Azerbaijan on Sunday. Ghana made it three wins from three and have now scored 18 goals in the group stage to remain top of Group W. Emmanuel Afful was the star of the show with a brace, while Abdul Aziz Issah continued his fine scoring form to add to his growing tally at the tournament. Abdul Latif Sa-ad opened the scoring with a composed finish to set Ghana on their way, before Afful doubled the lead. Raymond Agyapong added a third with a well-taken strike, while Nathaniel Owusu also got on the scoresheet with a clinical effort. Afful completed his brace after the break and Aziz Issah rounded off the scoring to seal an emphatic 7-0 victory and ensure Ghana kept a clean sheet. After thumping Uzbekistan 4-1 and Myanmar 7-1, Ghana have shown no signs of slowing down and will now turn their attention to their final two Group W fixtures against Bahamas and Kazakhstan on Monday, October 26.

title: Zelenskyy proposes Rada extend martial law, general mobilization
body:
President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy has proposed that the Verkhovna Rada approve his decrees on extending the terms of martial law and general mobilization in Ukraine.

Corresponding draft laws No. 16182 and No. 16183 were registered in the Verkhovna Rada on Monday, according to the parliament's website.

It is proposed to extend the terms of martial law and general mobilization for 90 days starting from October 31.

title: General Staff: Russia has lost 1,580,440 troops in Ukraine since Feb. 24, 2022
body:
Russia has lost 1,580,440 troops in Ukraine since the beginning of its full-scale invasion on Feb. 24, 2022, the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reported on Oct. 26.
The number includes 1,990 casualties that Russian forces suffered over the past day.
According to the report , Russia has also lost 12,448 tanks, 25,609 armored combat vehicles, 167,240 vehicles and fuel tanks, 51,632 artillery systems, 2,239 multiple-launch rocket systems, 1,726 air defense systems, 449 aircraft, 356 helicopters, 3,018 unmanned ground vehicles, 35 ships and boats, and two submarines.
Ukraine's General Staff has not revealed its own losses during the full-scale invasion, citing operational secrecy. Independent Western think-tank reports agree that the Russian casualties significantly surpass Ukraine's losses, with the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) estimating the ratio to be "roughly 2.5:1 or 2:1."
A January 2026 CSIS report said Ukraine has likely suffered between 500,000 and 600,000 casualties from February 2022 to December 2025, of which between 100,000 and 140,000 are thought to be killed in action.
While Ukrainian officials rarely disclose the figure, President Volodymyr Zelensky told France TV on Feb. 4 that at least 55,000 Ukrainian soldiers have been killed in action since the beginning of the full-scale war, in addition to significant numbers who are missing in action.
The intensity of Russian drone attacks and the fighting has made it extremely difficult for Ukraine to retrieve the bodies of fallen soldiers, which are needed for DNA confirmation.

title: Russian stocks up as main trading session opens
body:
MOSCOW, October 26. /TASS/. Russia’s MOEX and RTS indices added 0.15% to 2,468.41 and 965.52 points, respectively, as the main trading session started on Monday, according to trading data as of 9:00 a.m. Moscow time (6:00 a.m. GMT). The yuan exchange rate against the ruble lost 2.65 kopecks compared to previous closing to 12.037 rubles.
As of 9:15 a.m. Moscow time (6:15 a.m. GMT), the indices were up by 0.27% at 2,471.21 and 966.6 points, respectively. Meanwhile the yuan exchange rate was up by 5.3 kopecks at 12.117 rubles.
The MOEX Index added 0.25% as morning trading session started on the Moscow Exchange as of 7:00 a.m. Moscow time (4:00 a.m. GMT) to 2,470.82 points.

title: Unbeaten Spintex Knights stuck in Libya as US$30,036 travel bill remains unpaid
body: Ghana’s Spintex Knights have been left stranded in Libya over an outstanding bill of around US$29,200, raising concerns about the team’s return home and preparations for the next stage of the Basketball Africa League (BAL) qualifiers. The Accra Basketball League champions are unable to return to Ghana because of unpaid travel and visa expenses, despite securing an unbeaten record in the preliminary stage of the Road to BAL competition. The club has appealed for financial support to settle the outstanding costs and enable the players and officials to return home. Spintex Knights recently booked their place in the Elite 16 after winning all three of their Group B matches in the Division West preliminary stage, maintaining their hopes of becoming the first Ghanaian club to qualify for the BAL. Spintex Knights The team opened its campaign with a 96–90 victory over Guinea’s Nabaya Sofas before defeating Liberia’s NPA Pythons 88–66. They completed their unbeaten group-stage run with a 92–71 win over Benin’s Energie BBC. James Amotoe starred against Nabaya Sofas with 29 points and 12 assists, while Khyree Temple contributed 27 points and 15 rebounds. Justin Uwitonze was instrumental in the victory over NPA Pythons, coming off the bench to score a game-high 24 points. Their performances secured another opportunity to compete at the Elite 16 stage, but the financial difficulties now threaten to disrupt preparations for the next phase of the competition. Spintex Knights are scheduled to play in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire, from November 10 to 15, 2026, where they will continue their pursuit of a historic BAL qualification. The club will also be seeking to progress beyond the West Division semifinals after falling short against Ivory Coast’s Jeunesse Club d’Abidjan (JCA) last year, losing 93–82.

title: Iran live updates: Houthis claim new missile attack on Riyadh airport
body:
The president has said the U.S. will not resume strikes before the midterms.
Talks between the U.S. and Iran remain stalled despite the two countries signing a memorandum of understanding in June, aimed at ending the war that began with joint American-Israeli strikes on the country in February. The opening strikes killed a host of top Iranian officials and commanders, among them Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
The two sides have continued to exchange strikes, though have not returned to the intense fighting seen in the early stages of the conflict. The U.S. says it is enforcing a naval blockade of the country's Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman ports, while Iran claims control over the strategic Strait of Hormuz and continues to claim attacks on shipping transiting the waterway.
Meanwhile, intensified fighting between Saudi-backed Yemeni forces and Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen has seen the latter repeatedly attack Saudi military, oil infrastructure and transport facilities.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday that Tehran is prepared for "both defense and diplomacy," amid ongoing talks between Iranian and Qatari representatives over a possible peace deal to end the U.S.-Israeli war against the country that began in February.
“Our armed forces have a very specific mission, and by leveraging the lessons learned from the two previous wars, they are now significantly stronger than before,” Araghchi said, as quoted by the semi-official Mehr News Agency.
Mohsen Rezaei, the secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said in comments broadcast by state television on Sunday that Tehran had received a letter from Vice President JD Vance sent in a bid to revive stalled peace talks.
"The tone has completely changed. The tone of this letter is different from the one [President Donald] Trump wrote to the martyred Supreme Leader [Ali Khamenei]," Rezaei said, adding that he had not yet responded to the message.
Rezaei said Tehran is still waiting "for the Americans' final response" to Tehran's latest proposed deal. But Rezaei, who serves as a key military adviser to Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, said Iran will not capitulate.
"If Trump and America are not punished here, tomorrow other countries will think that they can attack Iran without paying a price," he said. "Our most important deterrent is to end this war in a way that ensures no one ever dares to attack Iran again."
Iranian Defense Minister Mehrdad Akhlaghi warned in a statement on Sunday that Tehran is "committed to strengthening combat readiness and ensuring an immediate, effective and proportionate response to any threat, anywhere, without geographical limits."
Akhlaghi's statement -- which was published by the semi-official Mehr News Agency -- came amid concerns that the U.S. and Israel may soon resume strikes on the country amid stalled peace negotiations. President Donald Trump has said that the U.S. will not launch any new attacks until after the midterm elections on Nov. 3.
Several other top Iranian officials and commanders have issued similar warnings. In comments published by Mehr on Sunday, Mohsen Rezaei -- the secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council and a key military adviser to Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei -- said any new strikes would be met with "devastating" retaliation."
President Donald Trump said on Saturday during a Halloween event at Mar-a-Lago that the U.S. has no hard timetable regarding negotiations with Iran over a possible deal to end the ongoing war with Iran.
"We're not in that much of a hurry from the standpoint that we've knocked out their navy," Trump said. "We've knocked out their air force, we've knocked out their anti-aircraft, we've knocked out almost every piece of military equipment they have."
Trump also said the U.S. had "knocked out" much of Iran's manufacturing capability and nuclear sites. "We still have to take care of, I would say, one or two sites, but we can do that in ten minutes."

title: Former Rubkona commissioner arrested for discharging firearm at airstrip
body: The authorities in Unity State have confirmed that a former Rubkona County commissioner, Stephen Salam Maluit, is in detention after allegedly opening fire at Rubkona County airstrip during the arrival of gubernatorial candidate Michael Chanjiek Geay last Thursday morning. Major General Samuel Tet, the police commissioner in Unity State, said Salam arrived at the airstrip with more than 20 armed individuals but was denied entry by security forces. He added that Salam opened fire after refusing to follow instructions from security personnel, leading to a confrontation and exchange of fire between the armed group and security forces. “When he was advised by the security forces and police officers at the airport to go back with his soldiers and wait for Honorable Chiengjiek at his residence, he opened fire,” he explained. “He could not accept the advice, and then that is what happened.’ Michael Chanjiek Geay, a former national Minister of Land, Housing and Urban Development, was travelling to Unity State as part of his campaign to become governor of the oil-rich state. Gen. Tet said no injuries or property damage had been reported and that the situation had returned to normal, with residents resuming their daily activities. The police commissioner urged aspirants and their supporters to reject violence as the country prepares for elections, stressing the importance of peaceful political participation and stability in Unity State. “Nobody should resort to violence. Definitely, all that we want is a government of Unity State,” he stated. “We want peace; We want our people to live in peace and harmony.” The post Former Rubkona commissioner arrested for discharging firearm at airstrip appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Kane primed to pip Yamal, Mbappe to Ballon d’Or glory
body: England captain Harry Kane is the favourite to win a wide open race to be crowned Ballon d’Or winner at a glitzy London ceremony on Monday, with Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe also in the running to be named the world’s best footballer. The 70th edition of the award, established by the magazine France Football, will be hosted in England for the first time in recognition of the first winner Stanley Matthews and fittingly could have a first English winner for 25 years. Bayern Munich striker Kane struck a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season, leading the German giants to a league and cup double and England to the semi-finals of the World Cup. “I’d love to be able to achieve something like that. I would be a massive milestone in my career,” said the 33-year-old. But semi-final exits in both the Champions League and World Cup for Kane means the outcome is far from certain. “I think my wife would prefer to know and my family … it’s very stressful for everyone,” he added. “I can see why they don’t tell people. They want everyone to go, all the big names, and there will be more people watching it if they don’t know.” – ‘I deserve it’ – Yamal finished second to Paris Saint-Germain’s Ousmane Dembele last year and the 19-year-old Barcelona superstar seems destined to be a Ballon d’Or winner one day. However, after a hamstring injury ended his club season early, he was far from the shining light of Spain’s World Cup triumph that was built on being the best collective unit. Yamal was pipped to both the player and young player of the tournament by his Barcelona team-mates Rodri and Pau Cubarsi. That has not diminished his bullish confidence ahead of the ceremony. “For me, Mbappe and me, we’re the two best players in the world,” Yamal said last month. “I honestly think that, as the best in the world, maybe there are two of us, and this year I would deserve it because of what I’ve won.” Mbappe, by contrast, boasts plenty of personal milestones without medals for either Real Madrid or France. The 27-year-old was top goalscorer in La Liga, the Champions League and the World Cup without winning any of those trophies. His 10 World Cup goals made him the top goalscorer in the competition’s history on 22. “Being the all-time top scorer in World Cup history, overtaking all the great legends in the history of the sport in the most important tournament there is, is something that really stands out,” said Mbappe. “Who am I voting for? Myself.” One football journalist from each of the 100 top nations in FIFA’s rankings is invited to cast votes for their top 10 players from a 30-man shortlist, allocating a maximum of 15 points down to one based on their ranking. The Ballon d’Or goes to the player who accrued the most points. Although the award carries no cash prize, it can generate huge bonuses from clubs and commercial partners as well as increasing a player’s overall marketing value. Alexia Putellas is the frontrunner to win the women’s award for the third time with Aitana Bonmati’s three-year reign to come to an end after an injury-hit year. Putellas, winner in 2021 and 2022, was part of the Barcelona side that regained the Champions League last season before moving to London City Lionesses. Her former club team-mate, Poland’s Ewa Pajor is the main challenger to Putellas after she netted 11 Champions League goals in Barca’s latest triumph. The post Kane primed to pip Yamal, Mbappe to Ballon d’Or glory appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Pezeshkian calls for expanding Iran-Brazil relations
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 26 (MNA) – Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian congratulated Lula da Silva on his victory in Brazil's presidential election, expressing hope for expanded friendly ties and cooperation in the new term.
In a message, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian congratulated Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on his victory in Brazil's presidential election.
Pezeshkian expressed hope that in the new presidential term, friendly relations between the Islamic Republic of Iran and the Federative Republic of Brazil will expand further, and that cooperation between the two countries in areas of mutual interest will be enhanced in line with the interests of both peoples and the strengthening of multilateralism, development and international peace.
The Iranian president also wished Da Silva success in his responsibility and wished the great people of Brazil pride and prosperity.
