title: Air defense downs 112 of 140 Russian UAVs, 3 Kh-59/69 missiles; strikes recorded at 15 locations – Air Force
body:
On the night of Monday, October 26, air defense forces shot down and suppressed three Kh-59/69 guided air missiles and 112 out of 140 drones of various types used by Russian troops to attack Ukraine, the Air Force of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reported on Telegram.
"On the night of October 26 (from 18:00 on October 25), Russia attacked with one Kh-31P anti-radiation missile, three Kh-59/69 guided air missiles from the temporarily occupied territories of Zaporizhia and Kherson regions, and 140 Shahed-type strike UAVs (70 of them jet-powered), Gerberas, and 'Parodiya'-type decoy drones from the directions of Orel, Kursk, Shatalovo, Millerovo – Russia, and the TOT of the Autonomous Republic of Crimea – Hvardiyske," the message reads.
According to preliminary data from the military, as of 08:00, air defenses shot down and suppressed three Kh-59/69 guided air missiles and 112 Russian UAVs, including Shahed-type (56 of them jet-powered), "Gerbera," and other drone types.
At the same time, hits by Russian air attack assets were recorded at 15 locations, while the falling of downed targets (debris) was recorded at four locations.
The air attack was repelled by aviation, anti-aircraft missile troops, electronic warfare and unmanned systems units, as well as mobile fire groups of the Defense Forces of Ukraine. As of the morning, the attack is ongoing, with several Russian UAVs remaining in Ukrainian airspace.

title: Kiev loses 8,300 troops, mercenaries over week of fighting — expert
body:
LUGANSK, October 26. /TASS/. The Ukrainian armed forces’ casualties, including foreign mercenaries, reached 8,300 personnel killed and wounded over the past week, military expert Andrey Marochko reported.
According to him, the enemy suffered the heaviest losses as a result of operations conducted by Russia’s Battlegroup Center.
"The enemy’s medical and irreplaceable losses for the week totaled about 8,340 militants and mercenaries. The greatest losses in manpower were inflicted on Ukrainian armed formations in the area of responsibility of the Battlegroup Center, which operates in the Donetsk People’s Republic (DPR) and in the Dnepropetrovsk Region," the expert wrote on his VKontakte page after analyzing data released by the Russian Defense Ministry.
Marochko added that during the week, the Russian military also destroyed nearly 5,600 Ukrainian unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), 15 marine vessels, 43 field artillery guns, 43 electronic warfare and counter-battery stations, as well as 805 different combat vehicles.

title: Spintex Knights reach Road to BAL Elite 16 unbeaten, set up JCA rematch
body: Ghanaian basketball club Spintex Knights have qualified for the Elite 16 stage of the Road to the Basketball Africa League (BAL) after winning all three of their group-stage matches in Praia, Cape Verde. The Knights secured victories over Guinea’s Nabaya Sofas, Liberia’s NPA Pythons and Benin’s Energie BBC to maintain an unbeaten record and reach the Elite 16 for the third consecutive year. Their latest achievement keeps alive their ambition of becoming the first Ghanaian club to qualify for the BAL, a continental competition established through a partnership between the National Basketball Association (NBA) and the International Basketball Federation (FIBA). Spintex Knights began their campaign with a hard-fought 96–90 victory over Nabaya Sofas, recovering from a challenging contest before producing a decisive finish. James Amotoe led the team with 29 points and 12 assists, while Khyree Temple contributed 27 points and 15 rebounds. Benjamin Ashitei also delivered 16 points and 11 rebounds. The Knights took control during the closing stages, outscoring their opponents 10–2 in the final five minutes. They also made three three-pointers without committing a turnover during that period to secure the victory. Their second match against Liberia’s NPA Pythons proved more comfortable, with the Ghanaian side recording an 88–66 win. Justin Uwitonze was instrumental in the victory, coming off the bench to score a game-high 24 points. He connected on eight of his 13 attempts from beyond the arc, while Benjamin Omari added 10 points. The performance also marked a milestone for Spintex Knights, who recorded consecutive victories in the Road to BAL competition for the first time in their history. They maintained their momentum in the final group-stage fixture, defeating Benin’s Energie BBC 92–71 to complete a clean sweep of their three matches. However, the Knights’ qualification for the Elite 16 is only another step towards their ultimate objective of reaching the BAL. The Ghanaian club will face Ivory Coast’s Jeunesse Club d’Abidjan (JCA) in the West Division semifinals, setting up a rematch of last year’s encounter. In 2025, Spintex Knights lost 93–82 to JCA in the semifinals, bringing their campaign to an end and forcing them to postpone their hopes of reaching Africa’s premier club basketball competition. Their return to the same stage presents another opportunity to advance and move closer to a historic qualification for Ghanaian basketball.

title: Israel's opposition in final show of force before elections as tens of thousands rally in Tel Aviv
body: Supporters of Israel's opposition took to the streets of Tel Aviv at the weekend in a final show of force before polls open on Tuesday, in what many observers are calling the most important elections in the country's history. Tens of thousands of demonstrators flocked to the upmarket neighbourhoods of the city as opposition figures made the case that the country’s future was at risk if Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu won yet another term in office. Four years of his ultranationalist government has plunged the country into wars across the Middle East, deepened internal divisions and fractured Israel's reputation abroad. Mainstream polls have predicted for months that the opposition will gain more seats than Mr Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc, which relies heavily on the most extreme wings of Israel’s settler movement and the ultra-Orthodox community. But neither side is predicted to have a majority, raising the prospect of weeks of complicated negotiations to form a coalition. Mr Netanyahu would remain as a caretaker prime minister during that time. There are fears that the Israeli leader might use such a deadlock to his advantage. There is also the prospect of renewed fighting with Iran before the elections take place, as Mr Netanyahu escalates his rhetoric on social media. On Sunday, there were reports in Israeli media of a stand-off between Mr Netanyahu and the military's leader described as an "unprecedented confrontation" at the top of the Israeli state. Chief of Staff Lt Gen Eyal Zamir resisted carrying out Mr Netanyahu's instructions for unspecified military action in recent days, fearing it would provoke Iran to launch an attack on Israel before polls open, broadcaster Channel 12 reported. “If Benjamin Netanyahu wins again, I’m genuinely scared for this country. I don’t think I have a future here,” Romy Schlegel-Cohen, 17, told The National in Hostage Square on Saturday evening, as she handed out campaign flags to passers-by. Organisers of the rally, who are calling for a state commission of inquiry into the Hamas-led attacks on October 7, 2023, said 100,000 people attended. Some had dressed up, one as Mr Netanyahu with a Pinocchio nose, others as repairmen with tools, symbolising the need to fix Israel. “I can’t vote yet, but I want to be able to show people who can vote that what they’re doing is important – they’re voting for me,” Ms Schlegel-Cohen said. “Change is needed right now. It was needed long ago. If I can convince even one person, it’s enough.” Hostage Square, next to the Tel Aviv Museum of Art and the headquarters of the Israeli military, is a fortress for the anti-Netanyahu protest movement. Soon after Hamas attacked southern Israel in 2023, the area hosted regular protests calling on the government to secure the release of those taken hostage. Since the last Gaza ceasefire was announced last year, that movement has grown to call for a state commission of inquiry, the highest level of investigation in Israel, into how the catastrophic security failure came about. Mr Netanyahu’s far-right government has consistently opposed such an investigation. Ofri Bibas, the sister-in-law of Shiri Bibas, who was killed along with her two young children in Gaza after being taken hostage during the October 7 attacks, told The National that she wanted the elections to be about the day her family members were abducted. “No one who was in a position of power on October 7 should still be in their job. The Prime Minister and the government should have resigned on the day,” she said. “The thing that’s most difficult for me to understand is the hypocrisy. If any other prime minister had been in position on October 7, they would never have considered staying in their job. Just because it’s Netanyahu doesn’t mean he can’t be replaced, or that Israel can’t continue without him. After 20 years, we have to look for something new, for a change and for a better life.” On Sunday evening, the man most likely to realise such hopes for new leadership, Gadi Eisenkot , drew hundreds of people to a large hall in the north of the city. Supporters of his Yashar party say that only an opposition victory can rehabilitate Israel’s position in the world. Support has plummeted since the outbreak of the Gaza war and escalating settler and military violence in the occupied West Bank. Mr Eisenkot, a former military chief of staff, is not opposed to Israeli settlements and has condemned what he described as a “handful of thugs” when talking about the violence in recent months. He lost close relatives in the Gaza war and has vowed to end it if he wins, without setting out a detailed plan. “These are the most dramatic, important and historic elections of all time in Israel,” Lianne Pollak-David, a candidate on Yashar’s electoral list, told The National. “Gadi Eisenkot is not only a top-notch strategist, not only a very brave leader, but simply the kind of person who can unify the country, who can bring us back to where we should be: a model nation among the family of nations. “My message to the Arab world is clear: we’re here for regional integration and we’re here to expand the Abraham Accords. We’re here to drive Israel and the region to be a much more secure, stable and prosperous place. We need to be working together − all the moderate forces. Israel should be at the forefront of that effort. “If we continue with Benjamin Netanyahu’s leadership, it will lead us to being a pariah state.”

title: Voronezh Business Center Hit in Drone Attack as 20 Rail Cars Derail Elsewhere in Russia
body:
A drone attack reportedly hit a 25-story business center and residential buildings in Russia ’s Voronezh, while a separate train derailment in Sverdlovsk Region left seven fuel tankers burning.
The independent Russian outlet Astra reported that a drone struck the Chizhova Gallery business center at 35A Koltsovskaya Street. The complex includes a 25-story high-rise that is one of the city center’s prominent architectural landmarks, according to the facility’s website.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The attack prompted reports of numerous explosions and fires across Voronezh. Astra said a drone threat was declared in the region at around 3 a.m., followed by a missile threat approximately two hours later. Residents told the outlet that they had heard explosions but that no air-raid sirens had sounded.
An Astra OSINT analysis of photographs and videos identified several locations where damage or fires were reported.
According to the outlet, a residential complex at 4K Arkhitektora Troitskogo Street was struck, while the newly built Uritsky residential complex at 135 Uritskogo Street also sustained damage. The latter building was completed last year, Astra reported.
At least 10 cars were reportedly on fire in a parking area at 275/1 45-y Strelkovoy Divizii Street. The outlet also reported fires in residential areas and smoke spreading across the city.
Ukrainian monitoring channel Exilenova+ claimed that some of the impacts resulted from Russian electronic warfare systems operating inside the city, alleging that Russian air defenses caused damage while attempting to counter the drones. The claim has not been independently verified.
Another monitoring channel, Supernova+, reported that the Severny Bridge in Voronezh may also have been targeted, citing reports that the bridge was closed and smoke was visible nearby.
Supernova+, citing their own open-source intelligence analysis, suggested that the Voronezhsintezkauchuk synthetic rubber plant and the Voronezh Aircraft Joint-Stock Company (VASO) may also have been targeted.
Voronezhsintezkauchuk, part of Russian petrochemical group SIBUR, produces synthetic rubber and thermoplastic elastomers. VASO is part of Russia’s United Aircraft Corporation and participates in the production of Il-96 long-haul aircraft and components for other aircraft.
A drone attack reportedly killed two people and injured 17 others in Voronezh.
Voronezh Region Governor Alexander Gusev said the two people killed were men born in 1960 and 1973. One child was among the injured, and two of the wounded were in serious condition.
A significant number of those injured were traveling on a train passing through Voronezh’s left-bank suburbs when drone debris fell onto it, Gusev said. Emergency services were working at the scene.
The attack also sparked fires at several industrial facilities, a business center, an apartment building, two dacha settlements, a school stadium, and a garage cooperative, according to the governor. He said the industrial fires had no major consequences.
Building facades and windows were damaged in nearly every district of the city, Gusev added.
According to the governor, air defense forces shot down more than 70 drones over Voronezh, while 113 were intercepted across the metropolitan area and several districts of the region. These figures have not been independently verified.
Neither the Russian defense ministry nor Ukrainian officials have commented on the reported attack.
Separately, 20 freight train cars derailed in Russia’s Sverdlovsk Region, with seven fuel tankers catching fire, according to reports cited by Astra . The cause of the incident has not been disclosed, and no casualties have been reported.
The Sverdlovsk Railway said traffic on the Reshety-Aramil section had been suspended after the derailment compromised clearance of an adjacent track. Firefighting and recovery trains were dispatched to the scene.
Local residents reported seeing flames and thick black smoke, with one witness telling media that an explosion had illuminated the area near the Chusovsky Tract.
Russia’s consumer rights watchdog, Rospotrebnadzor, said it would test air quality in nearby residential areas.
The derailment comes amid a series of reported disruptions to Russian railway infrastructure in recent months.
The Moscow Times reported that Ukrainian drone attacks on railway infrastructure in the Bryansk Region on Sept. 28 caused 10 railcars to derail after a railway bridge section collapsed, while a separate incident derailed 18 empty freight cars.
Other reported railway incidents in September and July caused train delays and damage, although the causes differed.
Neither Russian nor Ukrainian officials have publicly attributed the Sverdlovsk derailment to an attack.
Julia is a Deputy Head of News and correspondent for Kyiv Post who has previously worked as a parliamentary editor, journalist, and news editor. She has specialized in covering the work of the Ukrainian parliament, government, and law enforcement agencies.

title: Ukrainian forces repel 36 Russian attacks in Pokrovsk sector as 177 clashes reported on front line over past day
body:
According to Ukrinform, this was reported by the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine in a Facebook post on the battlefield situation as of 08:00 on Monday, October 26.
Yesterday, Russian aircraft carried out 64 airstrikes, dropping 224 guided aerial bombs. In addition, Russian forces deployed 9,296 kamikaze drones and shelled settlements and Ukrainian military positions 2,451 times.
Artillery strikes in the Sumy region hit the settlements of Mala Korchakivka, Tovstodubove, Sopych, Korenok, Luzhky, Studenok, Pysarivka, Potapivka, and Nova Sich. In the Chernihiv region, Kliusy, Kamin, and Mykolaivka came under fire. Airstrikes also targeted areas near Ivolzhanske, Hnylytsia, Pustohorod, and Luzhky in the Sumy region.
Over the past 24 hours, Ukraine’s aviation, missile forces and artillery struck one cluster of Russian personnel, an artillery system and an unmanned aerial vehicle command post.
In the Northern Slobozhanshchyna sector, Russian forces attacked three times near Bachivsk, Boiaro-Lezhachi, and Oleksiivka.
In the Southern Slobozhanshchyna sector, Ukrainian units repelled eight Russian attacks. Russian troops attempted to advance near Radkivka, Bochkovе, Okhrimivka, and Zakharivka.
In the Kupiansk sector, Russian forces conducted no assault operations over the past day.
Russian attempts to advance were thwarted in the Lyman sector, where Ukrainian defenders repelled eight attacks near Stepove, Zelena Dolyna, Kolodiazi, Stavky, Lyman, and Zarichne.
In the Sloviansk sector, Russian forces conducted no active offensive operations.
In the Kramatorsk sector, Ukrainian troops repelled one Russian attack near Malynivka.
In the Kostiantynivka sector, 12 Russian attacks were recorded. Russian forces conducted assault operations near Raiske, Mykolaipillia, Dovha Balka, Kostiantynivka, Oleksiievo-Druzhkivka, and Novoselivka.
In the Pokrovsk sector, Ukrainian defenders repelled 36 attacks. Russian troops attacked near Serhiivka and Molodetske and launched assaults toward Nadiia, Novopavlivka, Sofiivka, Vilne, Kucheriv Yar, Hannivka, Novyi Donbas, Chernihivka, Krasnopodillia, and Hulivе.
In the Oleksandrivka sector, Russian forces conducted no active offensive operations.
In the Huliaipole sector, Ukrainian forces repelled 13 Russian attacks near Uspenske, Rizdvianka, Dolynka, Hirke, and Yehorivka.
In the Orikhiv and Dnipro River sectors, Russian forces conducted no active operations over the past day.
In the Volyn and Polissia sectors, the situation remained largely unchanged. No signs of Russian forces forming offensive groupings were detected.
As Ukrinform reported, Russia’s total combat personnel losses since the start of its full-scale invasion of Ukraine on February 24, 2022, through October 26, 2026, are estimated at approximately 1,580,440, including 1,990 over the past day.

body: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) on Sunday released the list of its newly constituted national campaign council for the 2027 general elections. title: Why are Abkhazia residents with dual citizenship asked to show Russian passports at Moscow airports?
body: Abkhazia ‘s Foreign Ministry has said that some residents of the breakaway republic who hold dual Abkhaz-Russian citizenship are experiencing difficulties crossing the Russian border at Moscow airports. Russian border guards have reportedly been refusing to allow dual nationals to enter or leave the country using their Abkhaz passports, instead demanding Russian documents. As Abkhazia is a largely unrecognised republic, its passports are also not widely recognised internationally. Travelling on an Abkhaz passport is virtually impossible, except to a handful of countries, including Russia. For Abkhazians, obtaining a Russian passport is therefore practically the only way to travel internationally. However, this generally means a Russian international passport rather than a domestic identity document. Most do not hold Russian internal passports because they permanently reside in Abkhazia, where Russian passport holders account for around 70% of the population. Russian passport in Abkhazia: ticket to better life or risky luxury? For some Abkhaz, dual citizenship offers a chance to see the world; for others, a way to build a career; and for others still, a source of fear. The ministry added that people holding only Abkhaz citizenship do not encounter such problems at airports. Similar incidents have not been reported at other border crossing points either. Russia explains its position by saying that, for dual nationals, a Russian passport is not merely the primary document required to cross the border, but the only acceptable one. However, the explanation has been met with scepticism in Abkhazia, where some suspect the border guards may have other motives. The issue was discussed by Abkhaz and Russian foreign ministers Oleg Bartsits and Sergei Lavrov during a recent meeting in Moscow. However, no solution has yet been found. According to Abkhazia’s Foreign Ministry, the matter remains subject to “consultations with the competent authorities of the Russian Federation, taking into account the provisions of existing bilateral agreements”. In the meantime, the ministry has advised Abkhaz citizens experiencing difficulties at border crossings to formally report the incidents to the ministry, providing detailed accounts of what happened. Opinion: ‘Irakli Bzhinava’s arrest in Russia is blow to freedom in Abkhaz society’ Abkhaz lawyer Irakli Bzhinava, who holds dual citizenship, was arrested for criticising an agreement to transfer a famous state-owned holiday residence in Abkhazia to Russia. From the perspective of international practice, border guards at Moscow airports are not doing anything unlawful. As a general rule, people holding two or more citizenships are required to present the passport of the country whose border they are crossing , if they are citizens of that country. This requirement is enshrined in national legislation and strictly enforced in countries including Georgia, the United States and many others. This raises the question: what exactly is the problem, why are Abkhaz citizens unhappy, and why are they reluctant to present their Russian passports at the border if they have them? For some Abkhazians with dual citizenship, the right to use an Abkhaz passport is a matter of principle and national pride. While this argument carries little legal weight, it is highly significant in Abkhazia. Others simply want the option of crossing the border using their Abkhaz documents in certain circumstances, such as when their Russian passport has expired and they have not yet received a replacement. The terminology, place names and views expressed in this article are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the editorial position of this website.

title: Iran, Mecca Defence Alliance states to hold talks today

title: Ukrainian attack on Russia’s Voronezh Region kills two — governor
body:
VORONEZH, October 26. /TASS/. Two men were killed, and 17 others, including a child, were injured as a result of a Ukrainian attack on the Voronezh Region in central Russia, Governor Alexander Gusev reported.
"According to updated information, which may be extended, as a result of the terrorist attack in Voronezh, unfortunately, two people were killed (men born in 1960 and 1973) and 17 were injured, including a child," the regional head wrote on his Max channel.
The governor offered his condolences to the families and loved ones of those who lost their lives, both personally and on behalf of the regional government. Gusev also wished those who were injured a speedy recovery and noted that medical professionals will do everything possible to ensure it. In addition, he urged residents not to post photos or videos of the aftermath of air defense work online, especially those with geotags.

title: [New Rx] The Philippines is getting older. What if we treated experience as an asset?
body: The Philippines still thinks of itself as a young country. For decades, our demographic advantage has meant millions of young workers entering the labor force, staffing BPO offices, hospitals, factories and businesses here and abroad. That advantage will not last forever. According to the 2024 Census of Population from the Philippine Statistics Authority , 11.42 million Filipinos were already aged 60 or older in 2024, representing 10.2% of the household population. In 2020, the share was only 8.5%. PSA population projections suggest that by 2055, people aged 60 and above could account for about 19.6% of the population. PSA population projections Almost every discussion of this transition begins with the costs. More pensions. More chronic diseases. More hospital care. Greater demand for long-term care. Fewer working-age people supporting more retirees. Those concerns are real. But they also encourage us to think about older people mainly as liabilities on the national balance sheet. What if we looked at the other side? A Filipino does not wake up on his 60th birthday having suddenly lost 35 years of accumulated knowledge, professional relationships and judgment. Consider a 63-year-old physician. She may no longer want hospital nights, a full clinic or a 60-hour workweek. But she could spend 10 hours a week reviewing clinical cases for an international research organization. She could evaluate medical charts, mentor younger physicians, advise a biotechnology company, review drug-safety reports or teach clinical reasoning. A retired nurse could train virtual-care teams. A former pharmaceutical executive could advise several startups. A retired banker could sit on investment committees. A former regulator could guide companies through systems that took him decades to understand. What these people possess is difficult to manufacture quickly: judgment, networks, institutional memory, pattern recognition and credibility. These are not simply social assets. They have economic value. Some countries have already recognized pieces of this problem. In Singapore, the government raised the statutory retirement age to 64 and the re-employment age to 69 from July 2026. Eligible employees must be offered re-employment, while programs such as the Senior Employment Credit subsidize employers who retain older workers. Singapore has explicitly described the objective as allowing seniors to remain productive while helping employers retain experienced workers. Singapore Ministry of Manpower on senior re-employment Japan has gone further in encouraging continued employment. Its latest policy framework sets targets to raise employment among people aged 60 to 69 and expand measures allowing people to work until 70. It also supports job matching through public employment services and the country’s long-established Silver Human Resources Centers. Japan Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare policy on older workers These are important models. But they still largely approach aging through the lens of employment longevity: how to keep older people in work, improve retirement adequacy and reduce the economic pressures of an aging society. There is a further step the Philippines could explore. Instead of simply asking how older workers can stay employed longer, ask how their accumulated expertise can be organized, matched with demand, digitized and sold as an economic service. In other words, treat experience itself as a productive national asset. Technology now makes that increasingly possible. A person does not have to choose between a 50-hour workweek and complete retirement. Someone could work five hours a week. Ten hours. One project every quarter. One board meeting a month. A retired specialist in Manila could review clinical data from the United States. A former executive in Cebu could advise a Singapore company remotely. A Filipino professional who spent 30 years overseas could mentor local entrepreneurs without permanently relocating home. The objective should not be to force older Filipinos to work longer. People who have worked for decades deserve pensions, healthcare and the freedom to stop working. Some will have health conditions that make continued employment difficult. Others will simply want retirement. The goal is productive choice. Those who remain healthy, capable and interested should not discover that the economy has no use for them unless they return to a conventional full-time job. The World Health Organization itself cautions against equating aging with loss of productivity or contribution. WHO notes that older people contribute through paid and unpaid work, caregiving, communities and the transfer of knowledge, and argues that spending that enables their participation should be considered an investment rather than simply a cost. WHO on ageing, productivity and contribution Artificial intelligence may make this opportunity even more important. AI can summarize a medical chart. But an experienced physician may recognize that it missed the one detail that changes the diagnosis. AI can generate a regulatory document. Someone who has dealt with regulators for 30 years may know which apparently minor sentence will create problems later. AI can produce a financial model. An executive who has lived through several crises may recognize assumptions that look mathematically correct but make no commercial sense. As machines become better at routine work, human judgment may become more valuable, not less. Healthcare offers an obvious opportunity for the Philippines to test this idea. The Philippines already had an estimated $4.2-billion healthcare-services outsourcing industry employing around 190,000 people in 2024, according to government industry-promotion materials. Its activities already include clinical support, medical coding, chart abstraction, data management and clinical-trial monitoring. CITEM’s Healthcare Philippines industry report At the same time, the broader Philippine IT-BPM industry now employs about 1.9 million workers and generates more than $40 billion in annual revenue. IT and Business Process Association of the Philippines The next evolution of healthcare outsourcing could require less repetitive processing and more clinical judgment, pharmacovigilance, research support, medical review, regulatory affairs, real-world evidence and AI supervision. That creates an unusual opportunity for older professionals. A global pharmaceutical company may value a Filipino physician with 30 years of oncology experience for five hours a week more than another full-time junior processor. A startup may not be able to hire a former hospital CEO, but it could afford her expertise several hours a month. A young physician entering clinical research may gain enormously from someone who has spent decades navigating hospitals, ethics boards, regulators and professional societies. Imagine a national marketplace through which Philippine and foreign companies could find retired or semi-retired Filipino doctors, scientists, engineers, accountants, bankers, teachers and executives for fractional assignments. Professional societies could maintain expert networks. Universities could create senior-fellow pools. BPO companies could develop global expertise-as-a-service businesses. Retired Filipinos abroad could participate remotely. Instead of exporting only Filipino labor, the Philippines could increasingly export Filipino judgment. The benefits would extend beyond another paycheck. Older people could maintain income and engagement if they want it. Younger workers gain mentors. SMEs gain access to expertise they could never afford full time. Professional networks are transferred rather than disappearing. Decades of accumulated human capital remain inside the productive economy. The traditional demographic equation is simple: More older Filipinos = more healthcare + more pensions + greater dependency. That equation is incomplete. There is another side: More experienced Filipinos = more knowledge + networks + mentorship + productive capacity. Both are true. Countries such as Singapore and Japan have institutionalized important parts of senior employment. The Philippines can learn from them, but it can also go further: not simply extending working lives, but deliberately creating markets for what older people know. That distinction matters because the Philippines is likely to age while it is still trying to become a much wealthier country. We cannot afford an economy in which millions of people spend four decades accumulating expertise and then, because they cross an arbitrary age threshold, most of that economic capital becomes invisible. The challenge is not to make Filipinos work forever. It is to stop treating experience as something that expires at retirement. An aging population will cost the Philippines money. The more interesting question is how much value the country is allowing to retire with it. – Rappler.com Dr. Jaemin Park is an adjunct professor at the University of the Philippines College of Public Health and works across Southeast Asia on healthcare financing, medical innovation, and public sector reform.

title: EXCLUSIVE: CCB investigates Peter Obi, Saraki, David Mark, four others over offshore assets
body:
Nigeria’s Code of Conduct Bureau (CCB) has opened investigations into seven individuals exposed by PREMIUM TIMES’ Panama Papers and Pandora Papers investigations over their alleged ownership of undeclared offshore assets and business interests.
Sources at the anti-corruption agency confirmed the investigation to PREMIUM TIMES after the newspaper sought an update on the bureau’s handling of reports involving public officials named in the international investigations.
The seven individuals being investigated by the CCB are former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi; former Senate Presidents Bukola Saraki and David Mark; former Aviation Minister Stella Oduah; late former Bayelsa State Governor Diepreye Alamieyeseigha; former Delta State Governor James Ibori; and Stella Ogene, a retired Delta State judicial officer.
“All the Nigerian officials named in the Panama and Pandora papers will be investigated. But seven of them have been assigned to case officers who have already commenced investigations,” one CCB source said.
PREMIUM TIMES had reported how the individuals used offshore companies and other corporate structures to hold assets and business interests while in public office, raising questions about compliance with Nigeria’s asset declaration laws and restrictions on public officers’ private business interests and foreign bank accounts.
Multiple sources said the bureau is expected to extend the investigations to other individuals named in the Panama Papers and Pandora Papers investigations.
The CCB does not have an official spokesperson, but an aide to its chairman confirmed that the agency was investigating the Nigerian officials named in the global journalistic investigations.
In September, the CCB said it was reviewing information and materials relating to allegations of undeclared offshore assets and business interests involving public officials exposed by PREMIUM TIMES’ Pandora Papers investigation.
The bureau had written to PREMIUM TIMES in October 2021, acknowledging the significance of the Pandora Papers investigation led by the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists (ICIJ).
CCB described the investigation as one that had “created ripples across the globe” and sought this newspaper’s cooperation to facilitate investigations and, where possible, the prosecution of Nigerians implicated in the findings.
In a response dated 18 October 2021, PREMIUM TIMES Editor-in-Chief Musikilu Mojeed welcomed the request and pledged the newspaper’s cooperation.
“The primary motivation for our work is to help the public obtain the information they need to ask questions and make informed decisions and for law enforcement agencies to have the leads they require for necessary actions,” Mr Mojeed said.
After several years without a public update on the investigations, PREMIUM TIMES wrote to the bureau again in July 2026 to ask about the status of its inquiries into public officials named in the reports.
This newspaper recalled that the bureau had expressed interest in investigating allegations involving undeclared assets and business interests, foreign bank accounts and other possible breaches of the Code of Conduct for Public Officers.
“Several years after that engagement, however, there has been little or no public indication that investigations have been initiated or concluded regarding a number of public officials named in the Pandora Papers. We are therefore constrained to inquire about the status of any investigations undertaken by the Bureau in respect of these matters,” Mr Mojeed said in the letter dated 29 July.
In September, the CCB responded that the relevant information and materials were under review in line with its constitutional and statutory mandate. It said any necessary action would be taken in accordance with due process.
The bureau also said it might invite a PREMIUM TIMES representative with knowledge of the issues to provide further information or clarification as the investigations progress.
It declined to disclose details that could prejudice ongoing or contemplated action, citing the confidential nature of investigative and verification processes.
In 2021, PREMIUM TIMES reported that Mr Obi, a former governor of Anambra State and the Presidential Candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), maintained undisclosed offshore business interests while in public office.
The investigation was part of the global Pandora Papers, coordinated by the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists (ICIJ). The Pandora Papers were produced from a massive leak of financial documents from 14 offshore tax havens like the British Virgin Islands and Panama.
The investigation found that Mr Obi remained a director of NEXT International (UK) Limited, a British company, for 14 months after becoming governor of Anambra State, contrary to Section 6 of the Code of Conduct Bureau and Tribunal Act.
It also found that he failed to declare certain offshore holdings and operated a foreign bank account while serving as governor, both of which raised questions about compliance with Nigeria’s public service rules.
Mr Obi did not deny the allegations of non-compliance with asset declaration requirements, operating a foreign account and retaining a directorship while in office. He said he was unaware that assets jointly owned with others had to be declared.
Mr Obi has also repeatedly said he did not divert public funds, even though PREMIUM TIMES did not accuse him of diverting public money in its report.
This newspaper also reported that Stella Oduah, a former aviation minister who later became a senator, acquired four London properties worth a combined £6.7 million between October 2012 and August 2013 through an offshore company incorporated in Seychelles.
The investigation identified her as the ultimate beneficial owner of International Trading and Logistics Company Limited (ITCL), through which the properties were acquired. It also found that she retained a directorship in the company while serving as a public officer.
The four properties were purchased without mortgage financing, according to the report. The investigation also linked Ms Oduah to three other London properties, bringing the total number associated with her to seven.
A leaked suspicious activity report submitted by Deutsche Bank to the United States financial intelligence agency FinCEN showed that Sea Petroleum and Gas Company Limited, a Nigerian business associated with Ms Oduah, transferred $71,973 to a London property agency in September 2012, about a month before one of the purchases.
Ms Oduah served as aviation minister from 2011 to 2014 and was elected senator for Anambra North in 2019.
The Pandora Papers also exposed the offshore interests of Stella Ogene, a retired senior judicial officer who headed the Delta State Customary Court of Appeal for 21 years.
Documents obtained by PREMIUM TIMES showed that Mrs Ogene established Assete Media Limited, an offshore company incorporated in Seychelles on 7 September 2009, to acquire a London property.
The documents identified her as the company’s beneficial owner, director and secretary. Cook Worldwide, a financial services firm based in Panama, helped arrange the incorporation through Mayfair Trust Group Limited, an offshore service provider in Seychelles.
The investigation also found that publicly available records of Nigeria’s Corporate Affairs Commission listed Ms Ogene as a director of a private Nigerian company for 10 years while she headed the state’s Customary Court of Appeal.
PREMIUM TIMES also reported that Nicholas Mutu, a member of the House of Representatives, maintained business interests while in public office and used an offshore company to acquire a London property.
Documents from offshore law firm Alemán, Cordero, Galindo & Lee showed that Mr Mutu incorporated Forest Group of Company in Seychelles in 2010, while he was a lawmaker.
The company bought a property in north London in 2012 for £620,000 and sold it in 2014 for £730,000, according to UK Land Registry records.
Mr Mutu denied being a director of the offshore company, saying it belonged to and was controlled by his wife. He also denied that the company had owned a UK property.
However, documents from the UK Land Registry and the Pandora Papers identified him as a director, shareholder and beneficial owner of Forest Group of Company.
We also found that Mr Mutu was listed as a director of several Nigerian companies while serving as a public officer.
The CCB’s investigations also concern individuals exposed in the Panama Papers, a global investigation published in 2016 that revealed how wealthy individuals and public officials used offshore companies to hold assets and conduct business.
The investigation, also coordinated by the ICIJ , drew on leaked documents from Panamanian law firm Mossack Fonseca. It identified more than 140 Nigerian individuals and companies linked to offshore entities.
As the only Nigerian news organisation granted direct access to the leaked files, PREMIUM TIMES published more than 30 stories drawn from the internal records of Mossack Fonseca, the Panamanian law firm at the heart of the scandal.
Among those exposed were former Senate President Bukola Saraki and his wife, Toyin Saraki, as well as his predecessor, David Mark.
The investigations also revealed a network of shell companies in offshore tax havens linked to Africa’s richest man, Aliko Dangote, and his brother, Sayyu Dantata , as well as the offshore companies of Wale Tinubu, the chief executive of Nigeria’s biggest indigenous oil company, Oando Plc, among others.
Similarly, the reports also exposed the secret offshore company of one of Africa’s most influential televangelists, the late Temitope Joshua, popularly called T.B. Joshua.
Other prominent Nigerians named in the investigation are former Minister of Defence and billionaire businessperson, Theophilus Danjuma; Etisalat boss, Hakeem Bello Osaigie; Globacom CEO, Mike Adenuga; former Governor Abubakar Bello of Niger State; the late Ooni of Ife, Okunade Sijuwade; Arik Chairperson Joseph Arumemi-Johnson and his wife, Mary, as well as two former senators – Andy Uba (Anambra) and Ibrahim Gobir (Sokoto).
Top-tier politicians, businesspeople, and members of their families were found across the database, including individuals who continued to hold public office at the time of publication.
It is important to note that the use of shell companies is not inherently illegal.
Many individuals and firms incorporate them for entirely legitimate purposes. However, some of the Nigerian public officeholders identified in the investigation had failed to declare their offshore assets to the CCB, placing them in potential violation of Nigerian law. The CCB can, after its investigations, prosecute the officials found culpable at the Code of Conduct Tribunal.
PREMIUM TIMES reported that the Saraki family had at least four assets held through offshore structures that were not disclosed to the CCB as required by Nigerian law.
The newspaper’s investigation found that four assets linked to Mr Saraki’s wife were held offshore. Nigerian public officers are required to declare their assets, those of their spouses and those of their children under the age of 18.
Documents showed that Mrs Saraki held interests in offshore companies, including Sandon Development Limited, registered in Seychelles. The company was used to acquire a property on Whittaker Street in Belgravia, London, in 2012.
Babatunde Morakinyo, a longtime aide and associate of Mr Saraki, was listed as another shareholder in Sandon Development Limited.
The investigation also examined Girol Properties Limited, registered in the British Virgin Islands in 2004, and Landfield International Developments Limited, incorporated in the same territory in 2014.
Documents showed that Mrs Saraki was initially listed as a shareholder in these companies. The investigation found that Mr Saraki later assumed control of Landfield through Longmeadow Holdings Limited, an offshore company registered in Jersey.
A purported board meeting held in January 2015 approved the sale of Landfield to Mr Saraki for more than £3 million, according to the documents.
The Panama Papers linked Mr Mark, a former Senate president, to at least eight active companies registered in the British Virgin Islands while he held public office.
The companies were Sikera Overseas S.A., Colsan Enterprises Limited, Goldwin Transworld Limited, Hartland Estates Limited, Marlin Holdings Limited, Medley Holdings Limited, Quetta Properties Limited and Centenary Holdings Limited.
Documents from Mossack Fonseca repeatedly classified Mr Mark as a politically exposed person. The records also showed that he provided documents to the law firm to establish his identity and address concerns about his status.
The investigation could not establish the nature of the businesses conducted through the companies.
Although offshore company ownership is not in itself illegal, Nigeria’s Code of Conduct rules restrict public officers from participating in the management or running of private businesses while in office, subject to specified exceptions.
The law also prohibits public officers covered by its provisions from maintaining or operating bank accounts outside Nigeria.
The Panama Papers investigation also exposed how the late Diepreye Alamieyeseigha, who governed Bayelsa State from 1999 until his impeachment in 2005, used offshore companies to hold assets and move funds abroad.
One of the companies identified in the investigation was Solomon & Peters Limited, incorporated in the British Virgin Islands in 1999, months after he became governor.
Documents showed that Mr Alamieyeseigha was appointed the company’s first director and secretary. The investigation linked the company to offshore financial arrangements and property acquisitions in several countries.
British authorities returned more than £5 million recovered from funds stolen by the former governor to the Bayelsa State Government in 2012.
The investigation also traced properties associated with Mr Alamieyeseigha to the United Kingdom, the United States and South Africa, alongside foreign bank accounts that held millions of pounds and dollars.
His asset declarations to the CCB in 1999 and 2003 listed buildings, land, vehicles, a boat, a company and bank balances in Nigeria. The declarations did not reflect the scale of the overseas assets identified in the Panama Papers investigation.

title: France moves ahead of Poland in NATO AI race. Germany and the UK back Rennes
body:
France has secured the support of Germany and the United Kingdom for the establishment of a NATO Centre of Excellence dedicated to artificial intelligence in Rennes. According to the French publication La Lettre , Paris expects the project to receive NATO approval before Christmas, with the centre scheduled to open in 2027. This is an important development for Poland, which presented its own proposal for a NATO AI Centre of Excellence earlier this year. Warsaw now risks losing the opportunity to host one of the institutions that could shape the future of military artificial intelligence within the Alliance.
The French initiative is being promoted by General Cyril Carcy, France’s Military Representative to NATO, and Bertrand Rondepierre, Director of the French Defence Artificial Intelligence Agency (AMIAD). Both have been working to secure support from European capitals, with Germany and the UK now backing the project. Although NATO has not yet formally approved the centre, France has already built a significant political coalition. Paris wants to open the institution in 2027.
As we argued in June on Defence24.com, Poland also has strong arguments for hosting such a centre. The initiative was launched by the SET Foundation and later supported by the Defence Institute and other Polish experts. Poland already hosts two NATO Centres of Excellence, dedicated to counter-intelligence in Kraków and military police in Bydgoszcz. However, the competition for an AI centre concerns more than prestige. It means influence over NATO doctrines, technological standards, military training and the development of future operational capabilities.
Rennes is already an important centre for French military cyber-security and artificial intelligence. The city hosts AMIAD and institutions connected to France’s defence technological development. Paris is investing heavily in military AI, autonomous systems and advanced computing. The French proposal therefore combines existing military infrastructure, industrial capabilities and political support from major European allies.
The backing of Germany and the United Kingdom is particularly important. These are two of NATO’s most influential European military powers, with substantial technological and industrial capabilities. France understands that establishing a Centre of Excellence requires more than presenting a strong proposal. It requires financing, international cooperation and political support within NATO. Paris has been building that support for months.
For Poland, the situation is becoming increasingly difficult. Warsaw has considerable experience in cyber-security, countering Russian hybrid threats and developing defence technologies. Polish institutions also have access to experience from the war in Ukraine, including the military use of drones, artificial intelligence and electronic warfare. However, while Poland has the expertise, France has already secured support from key NATO members. No comparable international coalition backing a Polish location has been publicly announced.
One possibility is direct cooperation with France. As we indicated in June, Poland could seek to co-create the centre in Rennes and secure an important role for Polish military and technological experts. The Polish-French Treaty of Nancy provides an additional political framework for such cooperation. Prime Minister Donald Tusk and President Emmanuel Macron could use this opportunity to strengthen cooperation in military AI, cyber defence and counter-drone technologies. It would also require coordination between the Polish government and the Presidential Chancellery.
There is also another option. Poland could propose a NATO Centre of Excellence dedicated to quantum technologies. The Alliance has identified quantum computing, secure communications and sensing as important areas for future military development. Poland has scientific institutions, technological companies and developing infrastructure that could support such an initiative. However, this would again require a clear political decision, financing and a coalition of interested NATO members.
France has moved from presenting its AI initiative to securing the support of Germany and the United Kingdom, while NATO’s decision is expected before the end of 2026. Poland must now decide whether to continue competing for the location, seek a significant role in the French project or develop another technological specialisation within the Alliance. Estonia demonstrated how a Centre of Excellence can strengthen a country’s position by establishing the NATO Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence in Tallinn.
Poland spends billions on defence and purchases advanced military equipment, but it must also be present where NATO’s future doctrines, technologies and operational standards are developed. Now Polish politicians must take the initiative.

title: Energy markets unlikely to return to pre-war levels in 2027
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 26 (MNA) – The head of the International Energy Agency (IEA) says he does not expect energy markets to return in 2027 to where they were before the US-Israel war on Iran began in late February.
“I am afraid I don’t see any credible pathway that the markets will go next year where we were before this war has started,” IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol told the Singapore International Energy Week conference. “So therefore, we all need to get prepared, taking the energy security as a number one priority in our government, business world, but without forgetting what is the next chapter for the countries and for companies that are all here today,” he said. The war sharply tightened a market that had been projected to be in surplus this year, significantly disrupted global energy flows and pushed up the prices of oil and refined petroleum products. MNA

title: Aksungur UCAV drops aselBUOY sonobuoys for the first time
body: Turkish Aerospace’s Aksungur unmanned aerial vehicle released three ASELSAN aselBUOY 100P passive sonobuoys into the Mediterranean during the Turkish Navy’s TURNAs-26 unmanned systems exercise. The UCAV took off from Ankara and transited to the exercise area off Antalya (around 400 km) under satellite control, powered by the indigenous TEI-PD170 engine. In the mission area, it carried three aselBUOY 100P units and one additional sonobuoy in a pod, descended to 1,000 feet to release them, then climbed to 6,000 feet to begin listening. Aksungur remained on station for roughly four hours, relaying acoustic data to a transfer centre integrated into the ground control station in Ankara, where underwater targets were detected from the processed signals. Carriage, release, listening and evaluation at a remote site were thus exercised in a single sortie. Aksungur dropping aselBUOY 100P (Screenshot from Turkish Aerospace video) aselBUOY 100P passive sonobuoy in the water (Screenshot from Turkish Aerospace video) The milestone follows a similar step by Baykar’s Bayraktar TB3, which released two sonobuoys from a wing-mounted dispenser pod while operating from the deck of TCG Anadolu during the Denizkurdu-I/2026 exercise in September , coordinating directly with a Turkish Navy maritime patrol aircraft. That flight made the TB3 the first Turkish unmanned aircraft to deploy sonobuoys in an operational maritime environment, and only the second platform of its class worldwide after General Atomics’ MQ-9B SeaGuardian. At TURNAs-26 the TB3 repeated the feat from Anadolu , using Baykar’s indigenous dispenser system, while Aksungur flew its own sonobuoy pattern from land. About aselBUOY 100P AselBuoy passive sonobuoy is on the left side on Aselsan’s booth in the naval zone of WDS 2026 The aselBUOY 100P is a NATO A-size passive directional sonobuoy weighing 10 kg and measuring 120 mm in diameter. It listens at depths of 30 or 150 metres, transmits over a range of up to 20 km, and scuttles itself at the end of a programmed operating time of up to eight hours. ASELSAN launched the effort as a self-financed project in late 2015 and ran its first air-launch trials from a Cessna turboprop in 2018. Serial production followed the first contract with the Turkish Naval Forces Command, and the company has since worked on launching pods tailored to Turkish drones — the ASELBUOY POD carried by Aksungur — while standing up an artificial intelligence centre with the Navy to train detection models on underwater acoustic data. TURNAs-26 Unmanned Systems Exercise DEARSAN’s SALVO USV passing TCG Anadolu at high speed during TURNAs 2026 exercise (Credit: Turkish MoD) Held between 19 and 27 October in the Gulf of Antalya and the Eastern Mediterranean, TURNAs-26 was the Turkish Navy’s first exercise built entirely around unmanned systems. It gathered 18 ships, 11 aircraft, 41 systems from 17 defence companies and some 1,300 personnel, among them nine UAVs, seven unmanned underwater vehicles and nine unmanned surface vessels. Scenarios ranged from covert ISR with the LÜFER UUV and mine detection with NETA, GAVIA, OSKA and DERİNGÖZ, to swarm attacks by KARGU loitering munitions, an explosive-free kinetic intercept of a TALON target drone by the radar-equipped TUNGA-X, and the destruction of a kamikaze USV by the TOLGA close-in weapon system aboard TCG Beykoz . “Future naval warfare will be fought with unmanned vehicles,” Admiral Ercüment Tatlıoğlu, Commander of the Turkish Naval Forces, said after the distinguished observer day. Naval News comments Aksungur is the longest-legged aircraft in the Navy’s unmanned fleet. The twin-engine MALE design spans a 24-metre wing, lifts more than 750 kg of payload to a 40,000-foot ceiling and, according to TUSAŞ, stays airborne beyond 50 hours, with work under way toward roughly 60 hours and 1,250 kg. The Turkish Navy took its first example in October 2021. That endurance is what allows the type to absorb a share of the maritime patrol mission, relieving manned aircraft of a portion of their tasking. Removing the crew from the equation changes the arithmetic of persistence. Sortie length becomes a question of fuel and maintenance rather than human fatigue, so the aircraft can hold a patrol box or a chokepoint under watch for far longer than a manned MPA or a shipborne helicopter. The result is persistent surveillance, and through it the detection and classification work that feeds the recognised maritime picture. Aksungur was already useful in anti-submarine operations before this week. A drone that lingers over a suspected transit route for the better part of a day narrows the windows in which a diesel-electric boat can snort or surface to charge batteries, forcing it to stay deep, slow and quiet, and disrupting the rhythm of its patrol. Adding the ability to seed sonobuoys and listen to them raises that contribution: the aircraft now carries its own subsurface sensor layer into the fight, and can push its acoustic efforts to a higher level whenever a commander asks for them. Aksungur and the TB3 are only part of the picture. Surface vessels such as MARLIN and SANCAR, equipped with subsurface sensors and weapons, and unmanned underwater vehicles from ASELSAN and STM point to a layered ASW architecture in which air, surface, and subsurface unmanned systems share the same acoustic picture. For the Turkish Navy, that combination promises to bring a different breath to anti-submarine operations. The post Aksungur UCAV drops aselBUOY sonobuoys for the first time appeared first on Naval News .

title: Ghana celebrate multiple gains at African Scrabble Championship
body: Ghana recorded multiple gains at the 16th African Scrabble Championship (ASC) in Monrovia, Liberia, with Betty Kyeremateng winning the Best Female Player award and Haruna Adamu emerging as the new president of the Pan African Scrabble Association (PANASA). Kyeremateng made history by becoming the first Ghanaian woman to win the Best Female title in the 32-year history of the continental competition, capping an impressive outing for Ghanaian scrabble at the championship, which concluded on Sunday. The Ghanaian finished 13th overall after winning 20 of her 32 games, with a cumulative score of -184 points. However, her performance could have earned her a much higher position in the overall standings, as a better cumulative score would have placed her seventh among the 110 players in attendance. Nigeria’s Sophia Ekeruche, the 2025 and 2026 world-best female junior player, finished second in the women’s category with 18 victories and a cumulative score of +859 points, while compatriot Temituoye Mayuku secured third place. Beyond Kyeremateng’s individual achievement, Ghana’s success at the championship extended to the leadership of the continental body, as Adamu was elected unopposed as PANASA president on Saturday. Adamu’s emergence marks another significant milestone for Ghanaian scrabble, with the passionate administrator and security expert becoming the first Ghanaian to be elected to lead the continental association. He succeeds Nigeria’s Adekoyejo Adegbesan, who previously headed the organisation. The combination of Kyeremateng’s historic triumph and Adamu’s election underlined Ghana’s growing influence in African scrabble, making the 16th edition of the ASC a memorable outing for the West African nation. Meanwhile, Nigeria also enjoyed a strong showing at the championship, with Abdulmumin Jimoh emerging as the individual champion and the country claiming the Best Country title ahead of Kenya and hosts Liberia.

title: We need to be deliberate – Didi Dramani on developing youth football in Ghana
body: Former Black Stars assistant coach Mas-Ud Didi Dramani says Ghana must be deliberate and consistent in its approach to youth football development if the country is to restore its fortunes at the junior level. Ghana have suffered a series of disappointments in youth football, with the national Under-17 and Under-20 teams struggling to make an impact at continental and global tournaments. The latest setback came when the Black Starlets failed to qualify for the U-17 Africa Cup of Nations after losing to Côte d’Ivoire in the semi-finals of the WAFU Zone B U-17 tournament. Speaking to JoySports, Dramani, who led Ghana’s U-20 women’s team to bronze at the 2012 FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup in Japan, said a deliberate and sustainable approach was needed to rebuild the country’s youth football system. “When you want to bring a concept, it is a matter of being very deliberate and remaining very consistent, and you have to be sustainable. Development is all about talent identification, recruitment and also the ability to nurture,” he said. Dramani stressed that success would require more than words, insisting that the right structures and measures must be put in place to produce results. “Creating success is not just talking. You don’t start winning games without putting in the right measures. When you’re deliberate, you’ll train coaches so they manage clubs and schools. Football shouldn’t be a maybe sport; it should be a structured sport,” he added. His comments come amid growing concerns about the state of Ghana’s youth football.

title: Brazil’s Lula Clinches Poll Victory, Bolsonaro Seeks To Annul Election
body: Brazil’s leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva pulled off a dramatic comeback on Sunday as he clinched a re-election victory, but his rival Flavio Bolsonaro refused to accept the loss and said he would seek to annul the vote. With Lula’s victory, Brazil staved off a conservative wave that has seen numerous countries — such as Argentina, Chile, Colombia, and Peru — all shift right, backed by US President Donald Trump. The leftist icon, who turns 81 on Tuesday, defied projections to win an unprecedented fourth term. According to official results, he won 51.8 percent of the votes to 48.2 percent for Flavio Bolsonaro, with Lula pulling around 4.4 million more votes. The senator is the son of former far-right president Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year jail term for attempting a coup after his loss to Lula in the country’s last election in 2022. Sunday’s vote was marked by confusion after a Supreme Court ruling extended voting by two hours as some polling stations had already closed. The move came at the request of Lula, who complained that buses had been pulled from circulation in various cities, barring citizens from voting. Flavio Bolsonaro also requested an extension in some regions due to heavy rains, but he described the decision as “unacceptable” and a “dirty trick” “It is impossible to recognize the results. I am going to request the annulment of these elections,” he said, stone-faced, in a brief speech in Brasilia. Supporters of Brazil’s President and presidential candidate Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva celebrate after learning the results of the presidential runoff election in Sao Paulo, Brazil, on October 25, 2026. No candidate who lost the first round has gone on to win the second in Brazil since 1989, the first direct election after the end of the country’s military dictatorship. “People went to vote because we managed to convince them that voting was very important for ensuring democracy in the country,” Lula said in his first comments after the win. Fireworks and vuvuzelas rang out in Rio de Janeiro, while thousands of people dressed in red, the color of Lula’s Workers’ Party, streamed into the streets of Sao Paulo to celebrate. Lula’s Fight Back After the first-round defeat, the left swung into action with massive rallies, declaring “Never Again Bolsonaro” and revamped their social media strategy. The abstention rate decreased from the first round, falling from 21 percent to 19 percent. Julio Canelo, 42, a lawyer celebrating in Rio de Janeiro, hailed a victory for “the entire democratic spectrum.” “It was the result of the people mobilizing, in the streets and online,” he told AFP. A fierce social media battle drew in Meta, parent company of WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram, which Lula’s campaign accused of favoring his opponent with “algorithmic manipulation.” Meta denied this but acknowledged that some of Lula’s campaign ads had been mistakenly deactivated due to technical errors. “We are going to have to regulate them,” Lula said of social media companies after his win. A bitter campaign marred by scandals and mudslinging laid bare the deep divisions that have plagued Brazil over the past decade. Brazil’s right-wing senator and presidential candidate for the Liberal Party (PL) Flavio Bolsonaro reacts after knowing the first results in the presidential runoff election, in Brasilia, on October 25, 2026. A Country Split In Two Lula heads into a fourth term with almost half of the nation having rejected him, desperate for change. He rose from poverty to become president in 2003 and was re-elected in 2006. Lula made a dramatic return to office in the 2022 elections after a corruption scandal saw him jailed for over 18 months. The charges were annulled on procedural grounds. In his third term, Lula oversaw a drop in inflation and unemployment, and lifted millions out of hunger, but many voters felt gloomy about the high cost of living and crime. Flavio Bolsonaro, 45, pitched himself as more moderate and jovial than his father and managed to galvanize conservatives as well as less ideological voters wanting something new. “We’re in a deep hole, things are dire. People can barely afford to eat — buying meat is out of the question,” said Tereza Cristina Ramos, a 68-year-old retiree, who voted in Rio de Janeiro. Already one of the world’s oldest leaders, Lula will be 85 by the end of his new term in 2030. He is also facing a hostile Congress dominated by the right. Lula’s campaign leaned heavily on the theme of sovereignty in the face of commercial and diplomatic pressure from Trump’s United States. “This country will not accept being anyone’s backyard,” he said Sunday. Lula received congratulations from Chile’s far-right president, Jose Antonio Kast, and Ecuador’s right-wing Daniel Noboa — both close Trump allies. Mexico’s left-wing President Claudia Sheinbaum wrote on X, saying “Long live democracy, the people of Brazil won.” AFP The post Brazil’s Lula Clinches Poll Victory, Bolsonaro Seeks To Annul Election appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Ukraine’s air defenses down 112 Russian drones, three missiles overnight
body:
According to Ukrinform, the Air Force of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reported this on Telegram .
According to the military, overnight on October 26, beginning at 18:00 on October 25, Russian forces attacked Ukraine with one Kh-31P missile, three Kh-59/69 guided air-launched missiles launched from temporarily occupied parts of the Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions, and 140 Shahed-type attack drones, including 70 jet-powered ones, as well as Gerbera drones and Parodiya decoy drones. The attacks came from the directions of Oryol, Kursk, Shatalovo and Millerovo in Russia, as well as Hvardiiske in temporarily occupied Crimea.
The air attack was repelled by aircraft, anti-aircraft missile units, electronic warfare and unmanned systems units, and mobile fire groups of Ukraine’s Defense Forces.
According to preliminary data, as of 08:00 on October 26, air defenses had shot down or suppressed three Kh-59/69 guided air-launched missiles and 112 enemy drones, including Shahed-type drones (56 of them jet-powered), Gerbera drones and other types of unmanned aerial vehicles.
Russian aerial weapons were recorded hitting 15 locations, while debris from downed targets fell at four locations.
The attack is ongoing, with several Russian drones still in Ukrainian airspace.
As Ukrinform reported, over the past week Russia launched about 1,600 guided aerial bombs, 48 missiles and nearly 2,300 attack drones at Ukraine.

title: Week starts with blustery weather across Finland
body:
Gusts may reach 20 metres per second over sea areas.
Strong winds and rain will sweep across much of Finland on Monday, though forecasters say the gusts are unlikely to cause major damage.
Winds will gust up to 15 metres per second in parts of southern and western Finland, according to Yle meteorologist Laura Tuomola .
"Wind speeds like these at this time of year don't necessarily cause much damage," she added.
Authorities will raise the threshold for wind warnings from November, when it moves up to 20 metres per second for the winter months.
Rain is expected in the east, Lapland, and the west. A narrower, drier strip will run between them, stretching from Helsinki through Central Finland to Oulu. Temperatures will range between 6 and 11 degrees across almost the whole country. It will be cooler in northern Lapland, but temperatures there will also remain above freezing.
On Tuesday, skies will be mostly overcast but dry across much of Finland. Lapland will see drizzle, while isolated, scattered showers are possible near the eastern border and in Ostrobothnia.
Temperatures will stay at Monday’s level, between 6 and 11 degrees, except in northern Lapland, where it will be cooler but still above freezing.

title: GPL 2026/27: Berekum Chelsea held to goalless draw by FC Samartex
body: Berekum Chelsea and FC Samartex 1996 played out a goalless draw in their Ghana Premier League Round 8 fixture at the Golden City Park. Both sides started brightly, with an end-to-end opening period producing few clear-cut chances. Berekum Chelsea gradually settled into the game and enjoyed spells of possession as they looked to break the deadlock. However, FC Samartex goalkeeper Musah Zakaria proved crucial, producing an important save in the 40th minute to deny Chelsea during a dangerous counterattack. Chelsea continued to threaten after the break, with Attuquaye testing the Samartex goalkeeper again in the 54th minute with a well-struck free-kick. Zakaria remained resolute between the sticks as the hosts, Berekum Chelsea pushed for a breakthrough. Berekum Chelsea came agonisingly close to snatching a late winner in the 90th minute when a header from a cross narrowly missed the target. Despite their efforts, neither side could find the decisive goal as the contest ended goalless, with both teams settling for a point. The result leaves FC Samartex 1996 third on the Ghana Premier League table with 15 points, while Berekum Chelsea sit 10th with 11 points.

title: Uzodimma, Dokpesi Jnr, NIPR rally for media pact, national centre
body: By John Alechenu, Abuja Imo State Governor, Senator Hope Uzodimma, Chairman, Board of Directors of DAAR Communications Plc, Raymond Dokpesi Jnr and President of the Nigeria Institute of Public Relations, NIPR, Dr. Ike Neliaku, have called for a new partnership between government, media and citizens to deepen democracy and honour late media icon, High Chief Raymond Dokpesi. They spoke on Sunday in Abuja at the 3rd Raymond Dokpesi Annual Diamond Lecture themed “Media, Democratic Consolidation and Development.” Uzodimma set the tone, urging government at all levels to stop treating the media as detractors or enemies. “Going forward, I propose a three-way pact between government, the media, and the citizens that will enable the media to drive national development,” he said. Under the pact, government must jettison its paranoid view of the media, media owners must put professionalism and ethics above commercial and partisan interests, commit to investigative rigour and responsible journalism, while citizens must become discerning consumers of news, verify sources, reject ethnic baiting and support independent journalism. “Those of us in government have a responsibility to protect the freedom within which journalism operates, even when its scrutiny is uncomfortable. The media profession must also defend that freedom through the quality of its work,” Uzodimma said. He said journalism helps the public examine whether resources voted for roads, schools and hospitals were properly used. “The media cannot build the road or staff the hospital, but public scrutiny can help ensure that the money voted produces what citizens were promised,” he said. The governor credited Dokpesi’s AIT as a cornerstone for independent discourse after 1999, through programmes like “Democracy Today,” and recalled its 2019 court victory against the NBC over licence suspension as a defence of press freedom. He linked independent media growth to Nigeria’s longest unbroken civilian rule, stronger institutions, GDP rebasing as Africa’s largest economy, and growth in Nollywood and fintech, while admitting challenges remain in power, unity, insecurity and human development. As tribute, Uzodimma proposed a National Media Centre in honour of Dokpesi as a hub for research on development journalism, pledging to lead the campaign. “The best tribute we can pay to his memory is to protect that freedom and ensure journalism remains worthy of public trust,” he said. In his remarks, Dokpesi Jnr said his father did not enter broadcasting for business but for revolution. “The theme could not be more fitting. It summarizes the purpose of my father’s life’s work. He did not enter broadcasting simply to run a business. He entered it to spark a revolution,” he said. “He understood that democracy cannot take root, and development cannot occur, without a free, vibrant and courageous media. He democratized the airwaves so that the promise of Nigeria could be debated openly.” He noted that digital platforms, AI and fake news have transformed the landscape and made the duty of legacy institutions heavier. Speaking directly to youth, he said: “Democracy is not a static destination. It is a continuous, unfolding journey. For a first-time voter, your PVC is not just a piece of plastic. It is your share certificate in the corporate entity called Nigeria.” He announced that on December 1, 2026, DAAR will unveil a new media incubation and civic-tech initiative to empower young creators and first-time voters with tools to track governance and report elections in real time. “We are moving you from passive consumers of media to active digital architects of our democracy,” he said. Also speaking, NIPR President, Dr. Ike Neliaku, appealed to Nigerians in public and private sectors to use the forthcoming World Public Relations Forum which Nigeria is hosting to market the country positively. Neliaku described the forum as a two-edged sword that could work in the nation’s favour or backfire if not properly handled. According to him, 120 nations will converge on Nigeria and the image they take away will impact global perception of the country. He urged stakeholders to treat the event as a national image project. The post Uzodimma, Dokpesi Jnr, NIPR rally for media pact, national centre appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Nnadozie, Omewa, lead Nigerian women’s stars abroad as Okpe, Nkor shine
body:
Nigerian women footballers enjoyed an impressive weekend across Europe and the Middle East, with Joy Omewa scoring a dramatic late winner for BK Häcken, Chiamaka Nnadozie keeping her first clean sheet of the season for Brighton & Hove Albion , and Blessing Okpe and Blessing Nkor continuing their prolific goalscoring campaigns in Belarus.
Taiwo Lawal also found the net in Saudi Arabia, rounding off a productive weekend for Nigerian players making their mark in different leagues.
Omewa was among the standout performers after converting an 89th-minute penalty to hand BK Häcken a hard-fought 2-1 away victory over Växjö DFF in the Swedish OBOS Damallsvenskan on Friday.
The Super Falcons forward’s late intervention proved decisive, keeping Häcken on course for the league title. The Swedish side now need just two points from their remaining three matches to secure the championship.
The goal also took Omewa’s tally to four since joining Häcken during the summer, underlining her growing contribution to the club’s title push.
In England, Super Falcons goalkeeper Chiamaka Nnadozie recorded her first clean sheet of the 2026/27 Barclays Women’s Super League campaign as Brighton & Hove Albion defeated West Ham United 3-0 on Saturday.
Nnadozie made two saves to help Brighton protect their advantage and secure a convincing home win. Maisie Symonds, Fran Kirby and Kiko Seike were on target for the hosts, whose three-goal performance was backed by a solid defensive display.
The shutout represented an encouraging milestone for the Nigerian international as she continues her campaign in English women’s football.
In Belarus, Blessing Okpe continued her outstanding season in front of goal, scoring in Dnepr Mogilev’s 2-0 away victory over ABFF WU-19 in the Belarusian Women’s Premier League on Saturday.
Okpe struck in the 59th minute to double her team’s advantage and help secure all three points. The effort took her season tally to 22 goals, further highlighting her importance to Dnepr Mogilev’s attacking output.
Blessing Nkor also enjoyed another productive outing, scoring in Dynamo Brest’s emphatic 7-0 victory over Dyussh-Polesgu.
After Nadezhda Ilinykh opened the scoring, Nkor doubled Brest’s lead in the 21st minute, setting the tone for a dominant performance by the hosts.
The Nigerian forward has now scored 13 league goals in 11 appearances this season, while her overall contribution has reached 14 goal involvements. Her consistency in front of goal continues to make her one of the Nigerian players to watch in Belarus.
In the Saudi Women’s Premier League, Taiwo Lawal was also on the scoresheet, although her goal could not prevent Al-Taraji Ladies from suffering a 4-2 defeat to Neom SC on Friday.
Lawal found the net in the 56th minute, registering her first league goal of the season. The strike took her total to five goals in six appearances across all competitions.
The Nigerian had entered the fixture on the back of an impressive cup performance, having scored four times against Eastern Flames in her previous outing.
Despite Al-Taraji’s defeat, Lawal’s continued involvement in the goals offers an encouraging sign as she looks to build on her cup form and make a greater impact in the league.
