title: 2027: Tinubu appoints Keyamo director of APC air mobilisation – Official
body:
President Bola Tinubu has appointed Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo as Director of Air Mobilisation for the All Progressives Congress (APC) 2027 re-election campaign.
The appointment places Mr Keyamo at the head of a campaign directorate responsible for coordinating air travel and aviation logistics for nationwide campaign activities.
Tunde Moshood, the minister’s special adviser on Media and Communications, announced the appointment in a statement issued on Sunday in Abuja.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the APC Presidential Campaign Council is coordinating preparations for Mr Tinubu’s re-election bid ahead of the 2027 general election.
Under the arrangement, the Managing Director of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN), Olubunmi Kuku, will serve as Deputy Director I.
The Managing Director of the Nigerian Airspace Management Agency (NAMA), Farouk Umar, serves as Deputy Director II.
Mr Moshood said the appointments reflected the strategic importance of air transportation, operational coordination and aviation logistics to a nationwide presidential campaign.
He said the directorate would coordinate air travel, facilitate arrangements for designated campaign officials and personnel, and support activities across Nigeria’s six geopolitical zones.
According to him, the directorate would collaborate with other campaign structures to ensure effective planning, operational efficiency and appropriate deployment of logistical resources.
Mr Moshood said Mr Keyamo’s appointment brought the experience of a serving aviation minister to the campaign’s organisational structure.
He added that Mr Keyamo had pursued policy initiatives aimed at strengthening Nigeria’s aviation sector, improving its international standing and positioning the country as a major African aviation hub.
Mr Moshood said Mr Keyamo’s familiarity with the industry’s operational demands was expected to support air-mobilisation planning and establish an effective framework for coordinating the directorate’s activities.
He added that Ms Kuku and Mr Umar would contribute aviation-sector leadership and technical experience to the directorate.
Mr Moshood said air transportation was important to campaign logistics, particularly when political leaders and officials needed to visit multiple locations within tight schedules.
He said the directorate would support campaign operations through structured planning, stakeholder coordination, efficient scheduling and appropriate logistical arrangements.
However, he stressed that its effectiveness would depend on collaboration with other directorates, clear operational procedures and compliance with aviation safety requirements and applicable electoral laws.
Mr Moshood said campaign-related arrangements must remain separate from official government functions and be undertaken through properly authorised channels.

title: Embraer exudes positivity as it eyes Asian defence market
body:
“It’s a good moment for Embraer, not only in defence, but across all the business units. We’re growing on all fronts – very good receptivity about the solutions that we’re putting out in the market.”
These were the opening words of Frederico Lemos, Chief Commercial Officer at Embraer Defense, when he talked to Asian Military Review recently. He noted both the KC-390 Millennium transport aircraft and Super Tucano are proving popular right now.
“Particularly on defence, it’s a growth moment. The KC-390 and the A-29 have been performing very well in terms of sales, but also in terms of receptivity from customers and operational availability.”
A total of 16 KC-390s have been delivered to date – eight to the Brazilian Air Force, four to Portugal, two to Hungary, one to the Czech Republic and, in September 2026, the first to Uzbekistan.
Furthermore, there are about 60 orders and 29 options from 13 countries: Austria, Brazil, Colombia, the Czech Republic, Hungary, the Netherlands, Portugal, South Korea, Sweden, the UAE and Uzbekistan, plus it has been selected by Slovakia and Lithuania. Amongst these, this year Embraer has significantly signed up the UAE, the first customer in the Middle East, as well as Colombia, the first Latin American export customer.
Add to this list Greece, after the Portuguese government authorised the €590 million (US$660 million) onward sale of three KC-390s on 22 October 2026. This is the first concrete application of Portugal’s arrangement with Embraer to promote sales in Europe and to NATO members.
Lemos enthused, “The feedback that we’re getting from customers that are already flying the KC-390 is extremely positive. We’re seeing a 93% mission-capable rate for this type of capability, which is unheard of.” He noted that Embraer is ramping up production capacity to keep up with demand.
Asked to explain the growing popularity of the KC-390, as well as high availability rates, Lemos mentioned flexibility. “Being able to do different types of missions is important. The base mission, of course, is airlift, but then a tanking or aerial refuelling capability is becoming more and more relevant for many of the nations acquiring it.” He also mentioned special operations, firefighting, search and rescue and medical evacuation. The Netherlands, for example has contracted a very high-capability intensive care unit for its aircraft.
Embraer is also working to integrate air-launched kinetic effects into the Millennium. At Farnborough Airshow in July, it announced collaboration with Anduril to deploy stand-off deep-strike missiles from the jet-powered aircraft. No weapons have yet been launched from the aircraft, however.
Lemos also noted the KC-390’s connectivity, which allows it to integrate with command-and-control networks so that it can contribute, receive and relay data. Finally, he also discussed the aircraft’s competitive pricing and affordability, which includes lifecycle costs.
Embraer has calculated that there is an addressable market of 184 transport aircraft in Asia-Pacific, where many decades-old aircraft are coming up for renewal. In fact, Asia-Pacific represents 40% of the global addressable market for cargo aircraft, which underscores the importance of the region to the Brazilian company.
Embraer delivered three Millennium aircraft last year, but it is planning to hand over six in 2026. This should include the first KC-390 for the Republic of Korea Air Force, with the initial aircraft reaching the final stage of its assembly last December. By 2030, Embraer hopes to be producing ten C-390s per annum.
One place where Embraer has high hopes is India, where the KC-390 is competing in Delhi’s Medium Transport Aircraft (MTA) competition seeking 60 aircraft for the Indian Air Force (IAF), along with future options. A request for proposals was issued on 12 August 2026, with responses due before the end of this year. A selection is expected in 2028.
Lemos pointed to Embraer’s cooperation with India on its Netra airborne early warning aircraft based on the ERJ 145 platform. “We’re very committed for India’s next MTA aeroplane, working alongside Mahindra.” Indeed, Embraer and Mahindra have announced a partnership and revealed plans to set up a final assembly line in Nagpur if the KC-390 is selected.
India plans to buy twelve aircraft in flyaway condition, and build the remaining 48 locally. Lemos said: “We’re very committed to all the requirements to be able to bring value to their industry, transfer of technology and, of course, bring the capability to the air force.” He said Embraer “is confident” its platform meets the requirements listed in the tender.
Embraer is also engaging with several companies that could become part of the supply chain. “We see a lot of capability in India, also raw materials, and we’ve been announcing already some collaborations. So we’re confident that we’ll be able to set up the right set of capabilities to meet the requirements for the indigenous content in India.”
Asked about the rest of Asia, Lemos shared: “We actually see a lot of interest from different countries in the region. We have active discussions with several countries.” The executive said the KC-390’s capabilities are being recognised.
“Air forces are looking what to do in the future. They need to plan, they need to start replacing those assets, and the 390 is very well suited for the characteristics of the region, bringing productivity, being able to take off and land from shorter runaways, from all the islands that we have in the region, and again, extracting different capabilities from the asset. There’s the need to often disperse capabilities, to have aircraft spread out in countries in different locations, and having that flexibility for missions in every location is very important for several nations, and that’s what we’re hearing from prospective customers.”
The Philippine Air Force ordered a second batch of six A-29 Super Tucano turboprops, and these are “on the verge of delivery,” Lemos noted. Worldwide, more than 300 Super Tucanos have been ordered to date, and Embraer sees an addressable market for 90 such aircraft in the Asia-Pacific region.
Lemos said there is still “huge demand” for the Super Tucano. Deliveries are occurring to Panama, Paraguay, Portugal and Uruguay, for example. In fact, Portugal was the first NATO country to adopt the A-29.
The Brazilian company is expanding the Super Tucano’s mission set too. “We’re adding a new mission, and that is the counter-drone mission. That’s very valuable for many nations, in the sense that that brings another layer of defence to counter-UAS with a very low cost per kill by using either the machine guns or laser-guided rockets, as an example.”
He said the Super Tucano “is fast enough to be able to intercept even the most recent generation of jet-powered drones, and it’s slow enough to be very effective and efficient in taking them down. That’s what we’re hearing coming from the initial tests that we’ve been doing.
“And coming again to the cost of the engagements, that’s very important. It’s very tough for nations to be spending thousands of dollars per interception when the cost of a drone is very low. The A-29 definitely will be part of a broader system with different layers to intercept different types of threats.”
He said the C-UAS package, which is essentially software-based, could also be offered to existing Super Tucano users. Lemos said customers started asking about a counter-drone capability last year, and that the company “immediately started working on it. We have active developments along that ability, and we hope to bring some more news very soon.”
At Farnborough 2026, Embraer also announced the next iteration of the A-29, which is called the A-29NX “that will bring a different human-machine interface with a large-area display, and also different capabilities in terms of connectivity and kinetic effects”.
Asked what might come off Embraer’s drawing board next, Lemos shared, “We have an amazing team of engineers, very creative. So I’ll say we have a tonne of ideas. What’s coming next? I couldn’t share with you, but the crystal ball is very active!”

title: France works with 10 European nations to increase strength as nuclear deterrent - report
body: France is working with 10 other European nations to expand its capacity as a nuclear weapons power on the continent and a deterrent to Russian aggression as Europe's faith in the US's commitment to its security wanes, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday morning. The 'forward deterrence' plan involves the creation of new infrastructure, communications, early-warning and intelligence-sharing links with France's allies as well as deployments of French nuclear-enabled Rafale jet fighters across Europe. The UK, Germany, Poland, the Netherlands, Belgium, Finland, Norway, Sweden, and Denmark have all joined the project with varying degrees of involvement since French President Emmanuel Macron announced it in March. “We don't have any plans to put nuclear weapons on Finnish soil in peacetime. But we do have plans for creating a strategic dilemma for Russia,” said Finnish President Alexander Stubb. “We felt it would be useful for our security to get information, to be involved in it. We don't know where this is going to end, it's probably a 10- to 15-years process.”Instead of the countries all gathering together to work on the plan, France has been holding individual talks, leading European partner nations to constantly communicate with each other to compare what the French have told them, WSJ cited senior defense officials as saying. European countries doubt US reliabilityThe plan comes as faith in the US's willingness to defend Europe wanes. Doubts over if the US would risk nuclear war over the defense of a European ally have increased as US President Donald Trump strikes energy deals with Russian President Vladimir Putin and puts increasing pressure on Ukraine, WSJ wrote. France claims that the French program is more credible as the safety of European countries is of far more direct importance. “There is one difference between France and the US–we share the same geography, we are part and parcel of the same continent, we have economic and sociological continuity with our neighbors writ large,” Chatel, Macron's adviser, said at the Warsaw Security Conference.In his speech announcing the initiative in March, Macron emphasized that France's vital interests were directly affected by its allies. “Could we consider that the survival of our closest partners may be put at risk without it affecting our vital interests?” Macron said.Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide said that the plan was not intended to "replace anything. It supplements the nuclear guarantees that were already there" from the US. Program under French controlMacron also announced that France would resume making nuclear devices for the first time in decades and that the size of its stockpile would become confidential. Despite the involvement of other countries, the nuclear force will be entirely under French control, WSJ wrote. “The French will let us participate in their nuclear deterrence as much as the Americans,” one government minister of another European nation said. According to the WSJ report, the decision was made to make the forward deterrence strategy acceptable across the political spectrum, including to the far-right party of Marine LePen who is polling ahead in the race for the presidency in next spring's elections.

title: Stock market extend losses, 55 stocks depreciate
body: …As 20 record capital gains By Peter Egwuatu Share prices of 55 companies listed on the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX) depreciated last week following profit taking by the investors. However, 20 stocks appreciated in price during the week under review. The week’s performance highlights the market correction facing the stock market as investors reassess their portfolios following the substantial gains recorded earlier in the year. Although selected stocks attracted buying interest, the recovery was not broad enough to offset losses in influential stocks, leaving the overall market sentiment negative. Analysts emphasised that the decline also came against the backdrop of rising international oil prices, which climbed sharply amid escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. While higher crude prices could support Nigeria’s export earnings and government revenue, their broader implications for domestic fuel costs, inflation and business expenses remain important considerations for investors. A review of the market performance last week showed that the NGX market capitalisation, which represents the total value of stocks, shed over N206 billion to close at N160.519 trillion from N160.725 trillion the previous week. In similar manner, the NGX All Share Index, ASI, close lower to 247,222.27 points from 247539.73 points. Meanwhile, a total turnover of 2.024 billion shares worth N110.773 billion in 173,113 deals was traded last week by investors on the floor of the Exchange, in contrast to a total of 1.659 billion shares valued at N98.088 billion that exchanged hands the previous week in 184,632 deals. The Financial Services Industry (measured by volume) led the activity chart with 1.111 billion shares valued at N53.908 billion traded in 81,787 deals: thus contributing 54.89% and 48.66% to the total equity turnover volume and value respectively. The Consumer Goods Industry followed with 394.039 million shares worth N9.811 billion in 17,912 deals. Third place was the Agriculture Industry, with a turnover of 147.170 million shares worth N2.821 billion in 7,462 deals. Analysing market performance and outlook, analysts at InvestData Consulting Limited, stated: “The near-term outlook for the Nigerian equities market remains cautious as investors balance the need to preserve gains against opportunities in selected stocks. The market’s substantial year-to-date appreciation provides important context for the recent weakness, as some participants may be reducing exposure after the strong returns accumulated earlier in the year. Continued selling pressure in banking, energy and other influential stocks could prolong the market’s consolidation. Further weakness in large capitalised stocks may continue to weigh on the benchmark even if selected equities record positive returns.” The post Stock market extend losses, 55 stocks depreciate appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Newsletters & Email Marketing Manager
body:
The Kyiv Independent is looking to fill a Newsletters & Email Marketing Manager position within the Marketing team.
The Kyiv Independent is Ukraine's largest English-language news outlet. It was founded in November 2021 by a team of reporters and editors who were fired from the Kyiv Post for defending editorial independence. Today, the team consists of over 90 people, mostly based in Kyiv. Publishing in English, we serve as Ukraine's voice in the world and the world's window into Ukraine.
We are seeking an experienced and strategic Newsletters & Email Marketing Manager to join our growing Marketing team. In this role, you will own the growth and performance of our editorial newsletters and email marketing, from growing our contactable base to designing new formats, automated journeys, and experiments that turn readers into engaged subscribers and members. You will work closely with the editorial, reader revenue, audience, and product teams, and report to the Head of Marketing.
The ideal candidate combines a product mindset with hands-on email marketing expertise, is comfortable with data and A/B testing, and understands how newsletters can serve both great journalism and sustainable reader revenue. Within your first months, you will audit our newsletters and emails, establish baseline KPIs, and present a six-month growth roadmap to leadership.
Thanks for taking the time to apply to work with the Kyiv Independent. If you are among the qualified candidates, you will receive an email from a member of our hiring team to schedule an interview. Please note that while we would like to meet with all applicants, we may not be able to do so due to the volume of applications we receive.

title: Kwadaso NCCE educates SHS students on constitutional values
body: The Kwadaso Municipal Directorate of the National Commission for Civic Education (NCCE) has engaged students of two senior high schools in the municipality to promote constitutional awareness and responsible citizenship among the youth. The schools were Prempeh College and Methodist Technical School. The engagement brought together students, teachers, and NCCE officials to discuss the relevance of the 1992 Constitution and citizens’ role in safeguarding Ghana’s democracy. Ms Mavis Achiaa, the Kwadaso Municipal Director of NCCE, addressed the students and described the Constitution as the supreme law of the land and the foundation of the country’s democratic governance. Speaking on the theme, “Upholding Our Constitution in the Digital Age: Our Collective Responsibility,” she urged the students to demonstrate responsible behaviour both online and offline. She said the 1992 Constitution guarantees citizens’ fundamental human rights and freedoms while outlining their civic duties and responsibilities. Ms Opoku noted that the Constitution remained relevant in guiding national conduct and governance, particularly in an era of rapid technological advancement that had transformed communication, access to information, and civic engagement. She said that although digital platforms had expanded access to information and improved communication, they had also created challenges, including misinformation, cybercrime, online abuse, identity theft, and digital fraud. She warned that the irresponsible use of digital platforms, particularly social media, could threaten national cohesion and democratic stability. Students actively participated in the interactive session, raising questions about online safety, cyberbullying, and responsible use of digital platforms. Facilitators provided practical guidance on how young people could protect themselves online while contributing to good governance and national development. Some teachers who attended the programme commended the NCCE for the initiative and urged the Commission to sustain such educational engagements in schools. At the end of the programme, The schools established Civic Education Clubs to promote continuous civic learning and encourage students to become responsible citizens. The students thanked the NCCE for the engagement and pledged to apply what they learned in their academic and personal lives.

title: Do not issue marriage contract without Premarital Screening Certificate, MOH warns registrars
body:
Muscat: The Ministry of Health (MOH) has notified marriage registrars to refrain from concluding a marriage contract unless both parties present a valid Premarital Screening Certificate. Failure to comply with this requirement may result in legal accountability as per the Royal Decree 111/2025 concerning the regulation of premarital screening. For those wishing to undergo premarital medical examinations outside the Sultanate of Oman, the tests must conform to those approved by the Ministry of Health in the Sultanate of Oman, and the original laboratory results report must be certified. A certificate stating the absence of diseases is not sufficient. These tests include the Complete Blood Count (CBC) test, Hemoglobinopathy Panel (HPLC) - Test for hemoglobinopathies or their equivalent, Sickle Cell Solubility Test, Serum Ferritin Test, Human Immunodeficiency Virus Test (HIV), Hepatitis B virus surface antigen test, (Hepatitis B Surface Antigen Test - HBsAg), Hepatitis C virus antibody test, (Hepatitis C Virus Antibodies Test - HCV Ab) and Rapid Plasma Reagin Test for Syphilis (RPR/VDRL). Both parties are obligated, in accordance with Royal Decree No. 111/2025, to undergo a premarital medical examination, according to the procedures stipulated by the Omani Ministry of Health, whether the examination is conducted within or outside the Sultanate of Oman, before concluding the marriage contract. All laboratory tests for hereditary blood disorders and infectious diseases, as stipulated by the Ministry of Health, must be conducted at an accredited health institution in the country where the examination is being performed for the party undergoing the examination outside the Sultanate of Oman. The results of the medical examination must be certified by the health institution where the examination was performed, the competent health authority in that country, and the Omani Ministry of Foreign Affairs To obtain a premarital medical examination certificate, parties must visit one of the government health institutions accredited by the Omani Ministry of Health to verify and document the test results and receive premarital medical counseling, until the premarital medical examination service is activated on the electronic health platform. Marriage contract Issuing a marriage contract document through the Notary Public Platform requires a digital copy of the premarital medical examination certificate. Therefore, individuals whose premarital medical examination certificates were issued with manually entered information must visit the health care institution that issued the certificate to replace it with a digital copy in order to complete the procedures for issuing the marriage contract document. The issuance of a Marriage Contract Document through the Notary Public Platform requires the availability of a digital copy of the Premarital Screening Certificate. Accordingly, individuals whose Premarital Screening Certificates were issued with information entered manually are required to visit the health-care institution that issued the certificate to have it replaced with a digital version, in order to complete the procedures for issuing the Marriage Contract Document. In light of the digital integration between the Ministry of Health's Premarital Screening platform (Tawafuq) and the Notary Public platform (Tawtheeq), any error in entering personal data may prevent the screening certificate from appearing on the Notary Public platform. Accordingly, where one of the parties is a non-Omani, the identification document for the non-Omani partner used to issue the premarital screening certificate must be a valid passport or a valid permanent residence document only; no other document is accepted. Please verify that the identification number is correct and exactly matches across the identification document used, the Premarital Screening Certificate, and the personal data entered on the Notary Public platform.

Therefore, individuals whose premarital medical examination certificates were issued with manually entered information must visit the health care institution that issued the certificate to replace it with a digital copy in order to complete the procedures for issuing the marriage contract document.
The issuance of a Marriage Contract Document through the Notary Public Platform requires the availability of a digital copy of the Premarital Screening Certificate.
Accordingly, individuals whose Premarital Screening Certificates were issued with information entered manually are required to visit the health-care institution that issued the certificate to have it replaced with a digital version, in order to complete the procedures for issuing the Marriage Contract Document.
In light of the digital integration between the Ministry of Health's Premarital Screening platform (Tawafuq) and the Notary Public platform (Tawtheeq), any error in entering personal data may prevent the screening certificate from appearing on the Notary Public platform.
Accordingly, where one of the parties is a non-Omani, the identification document for the non-Omani partner used to issue the premarital screening certificate must be a valid passport or a valid permanent residence document only; no other document is accepted. Please verify that the identification number is correct and exactly matches across the identification document used, the Premarital Screening Certificate, and the personal data entered on the Notary Public platform.

title: FBI probes possible Saudi espionage plot involving former OpenAI engineer - report
body: The FBI is investigating whether to pursue economic espionage charges against former OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan, who was arrested earlier this month for allegedly planting a recording device in a restricted conference room at the artificial intelligence company, the Wall Street Journal reported Saturday.Investigators are examining whether Alfozan obtained confidential information to offer to the Saudi government, even without being recruited to do so, according to a law enforcement official cited by the WSJ. Authorities are also considering potential trade secret theft charges, although the investigation may not result in additional prosecution.Alfozan, 35, a Saudi national and US permanent resident, allegedly concealed a small circuit board and microphone behind a television in a conference room primarily used by OpenAI executives.He currently faces a federal charge of unlawfully intercepting communications, punishable by up to five years in prison. His next court appearance is scheduled for November 6.His attorney, William Pernik, said he had received no indication that additional charges were being considered.“We made it very clear that Mr. Alfozan will fight these charges and allegations in court, not in the press,” Pernik said.Prosecutors examine ties to Saudi royal familyProsecutors say Alfozan exchanged frequent WhatsApp messages with an unidentified member of the Saudi royal family in 2025 and 2026.The royal family member allegedly sought to recruit him for a Saudi artificial intelligence initiative, writing, “Saudi needs you more then [sic] the US!”Alfozan reportedly responded, “100,” but indicated he intended to remain at OpenAI until his company shares had vested.Prosecutors said their last known exchange occurred on October 5, the same day Alfozan allegedly returned to the conference room to retrieve the recording device. OpenAI security personnel had already discovered and removed it, subsequently notifying the FBI.Planned departure, Saudi consulate involvement raise concernsProsecutors also disclosed that Alfozan purchased one-way tickets to Saudi Arabia via Istanbul for himself, his wife, and their three-month-old son. He was arrested three days before their planned departure.His wife and son subsequently traveled to Qatar on business-class tickets purchased by a Saudi military official, according to prosecutors.Defense attorneys said the official was the wife's brother-in-law, that no military funds were used, and that Alfozan frequently booked one-way flights.During an October 19 detention hearing, US Magistrate Judge Alex G. Tse questioned a letter from the Saudi Consulate in Los Angeles offering to cover Alfozan's entire bail bond.“Even if I set it at $10 million?” the judge asked. “I find that problematic. Seems like a blank check. 'We're gonna pay whatever the court wants to make sure he gets out.' ”Alfozan was denied bail after the judge determined he posed a significant flight risk.OpenAI is examining what information the recording device may have captured and whether the incident involved corporate espionage or potential state-sponsored intelligence gathering, according to a person familiar with the investigation.

title: Russia is escalating its confrontation with the West in orbit. Its satellites are pursuing spacecraft from companies helping Ukraine — and Starlink has been put on notice.
body: An ICEYE satellite. Illustration There has long been talk of “hunter” satellites and an intensifying confrontation in space between Russia and the United States. But this week brought an unprecedented escalation in the new “star wars.” On October 18, a Russian inspector satellite came closer than ever to a spacecraft operated by the Finnish-American company ICEYE. The company openly helps Ukraine, giving its armed forces access to satellite images of Russian military facilities, including airfields, naval ports, and oil refineries. Here’s what we know about the exceptionally close encounter, how Moscow is describing it, and why independent experts are alarmed. Russian Kosmos satellites have pursued this spacecraft before, but never like this Overnight into October 18, the Russian satellite Kosmos-2612 approached the radar imaging satellite ICEYE-X36 after a series of maneuvers that began four days earlier. The Ukrainian military uses data from the ICEYE satellite. This was not their first close encounter. In the spring, four Russian spacecraft were “ hunting ” this same satellite: Kosmos-2612, 2610, 2611, and 2613 all approached it. Earlier, in February, news outlets reported on maneuvers by Luch spacecraft pursuing telecommunications satellites operated by Intelsat and Eutelsat. This time, Kosmos-2612 came exceptionally close to its target: hundreds or even tens of meters away, rather than tens of kilometers as before. Observational astronomer Marco Langbroek estimates that at their closest approach, at 1:35 a.m. GMT on October 18, the spacecraft were between 26 and 470 meters apart. Measurement errors make a more precise estimate impossible. Bart Hendrickx, an independent researcher of Russia’s space program, told Meduza that he knew of no previous encounter at such close range in low Earth orbit. In earlier encounters, he said, satellites had remained at least several dozen kilometers apart. He said the complexity and methodical persistence of the maneuvers by Kosmos-2612 and its fellow satellites, numbered 2610, 2611, 2613, and 2614, were also surprising. All these spacecraft, along with satellite 2609, were launched aboard a single rocket from the Plesetsk Cosmodrome on April 16. Maneuvers by Kosmos-2612 (red line) and ICEYE-X36 (blue). The horizontal axis shows time; the vertical axis shows orbital altitude “The satellites used a considerable amount of fuel on these maneuvers. By May, it was already clear that these weren’t ordinary Earth-observation and communications satellites, which generally conserve their fuel. Perhaps [through this latest escalation] Russia is demonstrating its ability to change orbits quickly and unpredictably to threaten enemy satellites,” Hendrickx said. Moscow calls these maneuvers “a tool of strategic deterrence” and a warning to commercial companies The Russian military previously acknowledged launching inspector satellites but said their sole purpose was “monitoring the condition of Russian satellites” — and said they had carried out such monitoring. Now, following Kosmos-2612’s dangerous maneuvers, the government newspaper Rossiyskaya Gazeta has published an article by Yuri Knutov, a military expert, retired colonel, and director of the Air Defense Forces Museum in Balashikha, outside Moscow. The article says Russia’s actions “do not violate international law” and that the inspector satellites themselves are “a tool of strategic deterrence.” “Russia is demonstrating its ability to ‘blind’ or at least identify sources of threats. The approach to ICEYE-X36 sends a clear signal: Any commercial company making its capabilities available for intelligence gathering against Russia must recognize that its spacecraft may be subjected to forced inspection in orbit,” Knutov wrote. He said both ICEYE satellites and the Starlink constellation, which is critical to Ukrainian military command and communications, had effectively become part of NATO’s intelligence apparatus. Like analyst Georgy Trishkin, whose views we quoted here , Knutov believes the Kosmos maneuvers were intended to force the ICEYE satellite to take evasive action to avoid a collision and quickly use up its fuel, turning it into “a useless piece of metal that will eventually burn up in the upper atmosphere.” Knutov said the Russian satellites were less vulnerable to such a tactic because modern inspector spacecraft have much larger fuel reserves than their predecessors. Earlier models could perform only two or three orbital maneuvers before running out of fuel, he said, whereas newer satellites can remain in orbit for extended periods, carry out complex close approaches, and track other spacecraft over long stretches. This latest episode in the space cold war was clearly visible from Earth. On Monday, Spaceweather.com asked whether the close encounter between Kosmos and ICEYE would be visible through binoculars or a backyard telescope. By Tuesday, it had its answer: yes. This image, taken by the Swiss company s2a systems, shows the encounter. The bright object in front is the ICEYE-X36 radar satellite. Its apparent magnitude is about 7, making it invisible to the naked eye but easy to see through binoculars or an amateur telescope. The fainter object behind it is Kosmos-2612. Russia isn’t the only country with space programs like these Other countries, particularly the United States and China, have their own programs to develop inspector satellites. These spacecraft are designed to approach other objects in space that aren’t built for such encounters — those without docking ports, for example. These approaches can have various purposes: intercepting radio transmissions, inspecting another spacecraft, diagnosing problems, or even destroying it. Militaries initiated and funded nearly all of these programs, so the public first learned they existed from amateur astronomers tracking the strange behavior of uncataloged satellites. Since 2011, when these observers identified an American satellite nicknamed Prowler this way, dozens more inspector satellites and many cases of pursuit have been detected, most involving Russian spacecraft. “Prowler” Russian satellite maneuvers are easier to track because of censorship in the Pentagon’s main space catalog Unequal access to information partly explains this pattern of observations. The U.S. military maintains Space-Track , the main publicly accessible catalog of artificial objects in space. It withholds the full orbital parameters of some U.S. military and intelligence satellites or publishes them with a delay. Until 2018, the Pentagon even classified data on civilian spacecraft launched as secondary payloads alongside military ones. The U.S. military does not conceal Russian satellites’ orbital data, so anyone with the relevant skills can use the available data to plot their movements rather than track them through a telescope. In 2018, the State Department protested the “ very abnormal behavior ” of Russian satellites. The U.S. military has protested their “ threatening ” maneuvers and anti-satellite weapons tests (we wrote about these nesting-doll satellites ). Then, in 2024, Washington accused Moscow of preparing to deploy nuclear weapons in space. Yet the United States has operated GSSAP satellites since 2014. These are essentially the same kind of inspector satellites, used to monitor satellites in geostationary orbit. And in June 2026, the U.S. military launched Jackal, built by True Anomaly, and Puma, made by Rocket Lab, as part of the Victus Haze exercise to practice space “hunting” scenarios . In September of this year, the Pentagon acknowledged for the first time that it had deployed weapons in space — both kinetic and nonkinetic . The next few years in Earth orbit will clearly be tense. Inspector satellites are also being developed for entirely civilian purposes. One example is LINK , a spacecraft meant to attempt a rescue of the Swift space telescope, but its mission ended in failure . It’s hard to predict what the Kosmos satellites will do next What happens next depends largely on how much fuel the Russian satellites have left. They may continue maneuvering around ICEYE spacecraft. According to Langbroek , as of midday on October 21, Kosmos-2612 had stopped moving away from its target and was holding at a distance of 480 kilometers. Hendrickx cautioned that the pursuit might not be over: Kosmos-2612 could return if it had enough fuel. He also pointed to four other Russian satellites launched alongside it — Kosmos-2610, 2611, 2613, and 2614 — that operate in similar orbits and probably have the same mission. Both ICEYE-X36 and ICEYE-X37 could be targets, he said. More on military satellites How Ukraine’s military uses Starlink — and what would happen if the Trump administration cut off its satellite communications entirely From Cold War interceptors to Ukraine: how Russia came to park spy satellites next to the West’s most sensitive tech in orbit Space wars don’t work like Star Wars Inside Russia’s ‘nesting doll’ anti-satellite tech and the real threats in orbit At Meduza, we are committed to transparency about our use of artificial intelligence in the newsroom. The story you’re reading was written by one of our living, breathing journalists and translated from Russian using an AI model configured to follow our strict editorial standards. This translation process is the result of extensive testing and refinements to ensure our English-language coverage is timely and accurate. A Meduza editor reviews every draft before publication. If you find any errors in this translation, please contact us at reports@meduza.io . To read Meduza’s exclusive content in English, please subscribe to our newsletter . Meduza

title: Equipment from the US, Korea, and Türkiye in the European SAFE? That's what Poland wants
body:
Poland wants to be able to finance equipment needed for the Polish Armed Forces using money from European Union funds, including the SAFE programme, in specific cases. Warsaw is also seeking the possibility of extending, in exceptional circumstances, the delivery deadlines under the programme. Furthermore, in the coming weeks, likely in November, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defence Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz is expected to travel to Washington.
Magdalena Sobkowiak-Czarnecka, Secretary of State at the Ministry of National Defence (MON), spoke about the postulates related to the SAFE programme on Radio Zet. She was asked about the possibility of using additional funds amounting to approximately €20 billion , the equivalent of nearly 88 billion zloty at the current exchange rate. These are funds from the original allocation among SAFE participant states, which the participating countries ultimately decided not to apply for and which will „return” to Brussels. She replied that talks within the government are currently ongoing regarding this matter. At the same time, she ensured that the pool planned for Poland, amounting to €43.7 billion, will be spent in its entirety.
In the context of the possibility of receiving additional funds, the Deputy Head of the Ministry of National Defence signalled that Poland is in talks with the European Commission regarding potential changes to the rules for using SAFE programme funds. Firstly, Warsaw’s postulate is to extend the time for potential equipment deliveries. She explained that even if a decision were made to pursue further purchases using additional SAFE funds, the deadline for equipment deliveries financed by them remains unchanged at 2030.
At the same time, in practice, taking into account the funding application process, signing delivery contracts financed by these „additional” funds would only be possible in the second half of 2027. By comparison, Poland concluded most contracts and annexes under the SAFE programme, totalling over 120 billion zloty, as early as May 2026. Meanwhile, the latest executive agreement signed in September concerns Piorun anti-aircraft sets—equipment that is, on the one hand, in continuous mass production and, on the other, has seen its delivery volume systematically increased for a long time. It would be different in the case of subsequent contracts from the new package, as these could only cover joint equipment purchases that have yet to be planned. „These are very short deadlines when it comes to the defence industry,” she said.
In the context of deadlines, she also spoke about talks with Spain regarding the acquisition of A330 MRTT multi-role tanker transport aircraft. The purchase of these machines is included in the original pool of funds that Poland has already received. Madrid has ceded production slots to Poland, and according to declarations, there is a possibility of delivery by 2030, but there is the issue of settling these funds and the specifics of the defence industry. „I see what is happening in the arms market—the number of customers is growing, there is plenty of money, but production capacities are limited,” emphasised Magdalena Sobkowiak-Czarnecka.
So far, Spain has not signed the contract for MRTT deliveries as part of joint procurement with Poland; however, it is being prepared. In other programmes, such as drone procurement, deliveries have already begun, and everything points to their efficient implementation. Furthermore, of the 19 countries that joined the SAFE mechanism, only 13 have finalised the procedures enabling the launch of the procurement process and the utilisation of funds. In some countries, approval processes are being delayed.
According to the Deputy Minister of National Defence, the 2030 delivery deadline remains in force for now, but there is „growing understanding” regarding the Polish postulate, especially from the EU Commissioner for Defence and Space, Andris Kubilius. The second Polish postulate is reportedly also meeting with understanding, namely enabling purchases made outside the EU, „particularly” for countries on the Eastern Flank. „Today we are in a situation where the most important thing is that we acquire the best equipment as quickly as possible. This primarily concerns the United States, Türkiye, and Korea—directions we are cooperating with,” she said. The proposal submitted by the Polish side is based on the assumption that financing purchases outside the EU would be possible after specific capabilities are identified as critical for the Eastern Flank by the NATO Supreme Allied Commander Europe or the Secretary General of the Alliance.
Sobkowiak-Czarnecka also stated that the European Commission lacks the tools or legal mandate to force EU states to transfer additional SAFE funds to joint projects with Ukraine. Therefore, the assumption recently presented by EC President Ursula von der Leyen regarding the transfer of unused funds to Ukraine is not current. Furthermore, Poland has no SAFE projects together with Ukraine.
Additionally, „within a few weeks, most likely in November,” a visit to Washington by Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defence Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz is planned. Meanwhile, in less than two weeks , the US Deputy Secretary of Defence for Acquisition and Sustainment, Michael Duffey, is expected to appear in Poland, with whom she held a „very good” conversation yesterday.
As a reminder, the loan pool under SAFE amounts to €150 billion. The European SAFE regulation, adopted in May 2025, provides that loans under it can be taken out for equipment produced within the EU and participating states to an extent of at least 65% (with additional restrictions regarding industrial property for selected groups), and the equipment is to be delivered by 2030. Until May 2026, it was possible for a single state to acquire capabilities; after that time, only joint purchases by at least two participating states are permissible.
The regulation establishing the SAFE (Security Action for Europe) loan instrument was adopted under Article 122 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. This is, in principle, an extraordinary instrument with a limited scope of application, which is partly why the delivery deadline is set for 2030. On the other hand, it was thanks to these solutions that it became possible to enable purchases directly for a single state (which is how Poland is implementing about two-thirds of its projects), the vast majority of which are within the national industry.
Whether Poland succeeds in gaining support for its postulates regarding the possibility of financing non-EU purchases from SAFE and extending the deadline may be of significant importance for the future use of European funds by the Ministry of National Defence. This applies especially to those funds that may become available within the pool of €20 billion in „unused” SAFE funds. However, the decisions are still ahead of us.

title: Tehran hosts Saudi defense pact states as Iran-backed Houthis launch more attacks
body: Top officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan were due in Iran on Monday in a push to de-escalate the regional conflict now afflicting the Gulf kingdom, as Yemen's Houthis launched further attacks on Riyadh's airport and Saudi oil facilities.The talks were the first high-level contact between Iran and the three nations - which signed the Mecca mutual defense pact in August - since a war that began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran also spread to Saudi Arabia and Yemen.The Saudi Foreign Ministry said the visit was part of efforts to "de-escalate" and "promote dialogue and diplomatic solutions." It stressed the need to open negotiating channels to "prevent the return of military escalation."Saudi Arabia was being represented by Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, younger brother of Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman; Pakistan by army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir; and Turkey by intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin, Saudi and Iranian officials said.They were due to consultations with Iran's Supreme National Security Council, its deputy secretary, Ali Baqeri-Kani, told state TV.Pakistan and Qatar have led mediation efforts in the war. On Sunday, Qatari mediators were in Tehran, an official told Reuters.Earlier efforts helped produce an interim peace agreement in June but fighting between Iran and the United States soon resumed. Conflict then flared between the Iran-backed Houthis and US ally Saudi Arabia, opening a new front.US, Iran threaten renewed attacksThe wider fighting has restricted shipping through the energy chokepoint of the Strait of Hormuz, pushed up global oil and gas prices, left Gulf states facing missile and drone attacks, and caused a new humanitarian crisis in Yemen.Tensions between Washington and Tehran have sharpened in recent days. US President Donald Trump said on Friday the US may carry out another military operation against Iran. Iranian security officials have told Reuters that Tehran has drawn up detailed plans to attack Gulf undersea cables if the United States and Israel attack again.The war, which earlier in the year also reignited fighting between Israel and the Iran-backed Lebanese armed group Hezbollah, has weighed on Trump's approval ratings ahead of the midterm elections that decide control of Congress.Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said Monday's discussions would include "Israel's expansionist policies, developments in the Palestinian territories and Lebanon, and the repercussions of US and Israeli military action against Iran".Baghaei said the meeting, proposed when Munir visited Tehran last week, could be a first step towards establishing regional security mechanisms. A senior Pakistani security official said the focus of Monday's meeting was to build a regional non-aggression network. The agenda also included US-Iran talks, Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, the Strait of Hormuz and a US blockade of Iranian ports, the official said.Iranian officials told Munir during that visit that there would be no talks with Washington until Tehran's demands - which include ending the US blockade and lifting sanctions on Iranian its oil exports - were met, according to Iranian media.Pakistan's military media wing and Turkey's Foreign Ministry did not immediately respond to requests for comment.Houthis strike Saudi airport, energy infrastructureSaudi Arabia has ⁠intensified strikes against the Houthis since they captured strategic areas along Yemen's Red Sea coast last month, advancing against Saudi-backed government forces. Houthi attacks have targeted Saudi airports, ports and oil installations.On Monday, the Houthis said they had ‌attacked East-West crude oil pumping stations in Saudi Arabia as well as Riyadh airport, which said it had resumed operations at two terminals a day earlier. There was no immediate Saudi confirmation of the Houthi attacks.The Mecca Joint Defence Agreementsays signatories shall use "all necessary means" to eliminate threats to one another's territorial integrity, sovereignty or internationally recognized borders, according to a text seen by Reuters.The pact's members held an emergency meeting in Riyadh this month and agreed to ensure the "rapid deployment" of military forces and capabilities in Saudi Arabia.Efforts by Turkey's parliament to ratify the agreement began last week and are still underway, while Pakistan approved the pact last week.

title: NCCE engages women’s groups on rule of law and anti-corruption
body: The National Commission for Civic Education (NCCE) in the Krachi East Municipality has organised a follow-up civic engagement with women’s groups to strengthen public understanding of the rule of law, accountability and the fight against corruption. The engagement forms part of the Commission’s Civic Engagements on the Rule of Law and the Fight Against Corruption project, which seeks to promote civic awareness and encourage citizens to uphold the principles of good governance. The initiative builds on earlier awareness campaigns conducted in the 60 project districts, which equipped women’s groups with knowledge of the rule of law, corruption, accountability, civic responsibilities, legal protections and available reporting mechanisms. According to the NCCE, initial engagements have shown the importance of sustained civic education in translating knowledge into practical action. It said continuous engagement, reinforcement of key messages and opportunities for participants to share their experiences and challenges were essential to promoting lasting behavioural change. The Commission observed that women continued to encounter corruption in their daily interactions with public institutions, markets and service providers. It noted that barriers such as fear of victimisation, limited knowledge of reporting procedures and cultural norms that discouraged speaking out against wrongdoing could prevent some women from reporting corrupt practices. The follow-up engagement is therefore intended to assess how participants have applied the knowledge gained during the initial sessions, reinforce positive attitudes and behaviours, address misconceptions and strengthen their capacity to promote integrity and accountability within their families, workplaces and communities. The initiative also seeks to empower women to become active advocates for transparency, accountability and the rule of law. The NCCE Krachi East Municipal Office has invited participants from the initial engagement to attend the follow-up session at the Church of Pentecost, Dambai Central Assembly. The engagement forms part of broader efforts to deepen civic participation and promote responsible citizenship in the fight against corruption. The engagement featured over 60 women who reflected on their first engagement, success, challenges and lessons learned from the Krachi East Municipal Director, NCCE, under the auspices of Mr Clement Kwesi Mamadu, Participants came from across the municipality, where facilitators reminded them of previous engagements and asked whether they were applying them in their daily activities. Chief Inspector Mr Charles Adams of Dambai Division Command led the participants through a reflection on their previous encounters, successes, challenges, and lessons learned. He then guided them in applying the Rule of Law in everyday life and reminded them of practical experiences in identifying and responding to corruption. Mr Samuel Annan (ADO1), of the Krachi East Municipal Fire Command, also engaged participants on overcoming barriers to reporting corruption and building community integrity through women’s association. He again said that personal and collective commitment to promote transparency must be treated fairly.

title: Trump Administration backs Orbán for UN Secretary-General – media
body:
Ukrinform reports this, citing The Wall Street Journal and The Jerusalem Post .
According to the reports, U.S. officials have already approached Orbán with the proposal. He has expressed interest but has not yet made a final decision on whether to enter the race for UN Secretary-General.
Washington believes Orbán’s previous contacts with Moscow and Beijing could help secure their support for the Hungarian politician, who is seen as pro-Russian. This could make Orbán a joint candidate backed by three permanent members of the UN Security Council.
A State Department official estimated that Orbán could secure the support of at least eight of the Security Council’s 15 members, and potentially as many as 10 if circumstances are favorable.
It remains unclear, however, whether the United Kingdom and France, which hold veto power on the Security Council, would be prepared to block his candidacy.
A State Department official described Orbán as a “MAGA conservatives' dream candidate,” citing his positions on mass immigration, liberal nongovernmental organizations, and established centers of influence in Hungary’s judiciary and media.
Orbán has repeatedly clashed with EU leaders while strengthening ties with China. His relations with Moscow and Beijing, as well as his domestic policies, could come under particular scrutiny if he is nominated.
U.S. President Donald Trump supported Orbán in Hungary’s parliamentary election in April, while Vice President JD Vance personally took part in his election campaign.
Another informal vote is scheduled for Wednesday at the UN Security Council to gauge support for the candidates. It remains unclear whether Orbán’s name will be included in the ballot.
António Guterres’s term as UN Secretary-General ends on December 31. The next Secretary-General will be elected by the General Assembly following a recommendation from the Security Council.

title: Dele Cole (1940-2026) and his public service, By Eric Teniola
body:
On 29 July, 1975, General Murtala Mohammed GCFR (8 November, 1938 – 13 February, 1976) became head of state by overthrowing General Yakubu Gowon GCFR (92). On 7 August, 1975, General Mohammed set up a committee on the creation of more states in the country. At that time, Nigeria had 12 states. The committee was headed by Justice Gabriel Ayo Irikefe of the Supreme Court. Other members of the committee were Dr AD Yahaya, Mr SD Lar, Brigadier Godwin G Ally and Mr. C Audifferen. The Secretary of the committee was Dr Patrick Dele Cole of The Cabinet Office.
At that time, Dr Dele Cole was an administrative officer in the Political division of The Cabinet Office. He has returned from his studies at the University of Otago, New Zealand, 1962-1965, Free University of Amsterdam, Netherland, 1966, University of Cambridge, England, 1966-1969, and visiting Professor, University of Pennsylvania, Philadelphia, USA, 1969-1973.
Dr Patrick Dele Cole was a fellow, Kings College, Cambridge, England, 1970-1973.
The political division in The Cabinet Office was headed by Alhaji Umaru Sanda Ndayako (1937 – 8 September, 2003), who later became the Etsu Nupe in 1975. Alhaji Ndayako had his education at the East School, Bida, 1945-1948, Ilorin Middle School, 1949-1950, Government College, Zaria, 1951-1956, Nigerian College of Arts, Science and Technology, Zaria, 1957-59, University College, Ibadan, 1959-1962; Senior Civil Servant, Ministry of Local Government, Kaduna, 1962-1965, Principal Administrative Office, 1965-1967 and deputy Permanent Secretary, later head, Political Division, Cabinet Office.
Top officers in the Political division, Cabinet Office, who were also colleagues of Dr. Dele Cole at that time also included Mr Eniolorunda Ojumu from Kwara state, Alhaji Yahaya Abubakar from Kaduna State, Dr Niyi Adedeji from Ilesa, Osun State, Ambassador Timothy Ayodele Olu Otunla also from Ilesa, Mr Bisi Ogunniyi from Iree in Osun State and Brigadier Ibrahim Ahmed Bako (N/548) (5 March 1943 – 31 December,1983).
On 3 February, 1976, General Murtala Mohammed (GCFR) made the following announcements. “The Supreme Military Council has decided that seven of the present States remain unchanged except for minor boundary adjustments. These are: Lagos, North-Central, Kano, Rivers, Mid-Western, South-eastern and Kwara States. In the case of Kwara, Igala area is excised and merged with Benue. The capitals will remain unchanged except for Lagos State whose capital is now Ikeja. The minor boundary adjustments are for parts of Opobo division in the South-Eastern State and Ndoni area in the Mid-West now merged with Rivers State.
States will no longer be described reference to geographical points such as North and South, West or East. This should help to erase memories of past political ties and emotional attachments. The Mid-Western States is now to be known as Bendel; North-Central becomes Kaduna State and the present South-Eastern is to be known henceforth as Cross River State.
As for the other five States, these have been divided in such a way that the total number of States in the Federation is now nineteen.
The present Western State is divided into three States as follows:
The present East-Central State is divided into two States as follows:
The present North-Western State is divided into two States as follows:
The present Benue-Plateau State is divided into two States as follows:
The present North-Eastern State is divided into three States as follows:
Boundary adjustment Commissions will be set up immediately to look into the various inter-state boundary disputes identified by the panel on creation of States. The peculiar problem of the Riverine areas is to be dealt with through the establishment of a Delta Basin Authority.
The following officers have been posted as Governors of the seven new States. They are Lt Commander Kanu — Imo, Major ID Ikpeme — Ondo, Lt. Colonel A Shelleng — Benue, Lt Colonel SA Balogun — Ogun, Lt Colonel MD Jega — Gongola, Commander Nyako — Niger and Lt Colonel B. Kaliel—Bauchi State”.
After the report, Justice Ayo Irikefe GCON later became the Chief Justice of the Federation from 1985 to 1987. Dr Ali Danlami Yahaya of Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria became a member of The Constitution Drafting Committee and Mr SD Lar, was chairman of African Continental Bank, elected governor of Plateau state in 1979 and became the founding chairman of the People’s Democratic Party (PDP) in 1999 and Mr C Audifferen was a Map Reproduction Officer for the Federal Ministry of Works.
The decision by the Supreme Military Council was as a result of the reports of the Secretariat of the Committee on the creation of states, then headed by Mr Dele Cole. From then on, the Chief of Staff, General Headquarters, General Olusegun Obasanjo (GCFR) bonded with Dr Dele Cole.
Following an internal crisis, the Federal Government on September 19, 1975 acquired 60 per cent equity shares in The Daily Times Group of Companies. They therefore appointed a new Board of Directors for the group. They are Alhaji Aliko Mohammed (Chairman), Alhaji Babatunde Jose, Mr Douglas Briggs, Mr Paul Belabo, Dr Ali Alhakim, Dr Patrick Dele Cole, Lady Alakija and Alhaji J Gana. Dr Dele Cole then became the managing director of The Daily Times. He was deployed from The Cabinet Office.
While serving as Managing Director of Daily Times, Dr Dele Cole was very involved in acquisition of “WEST AFRICA” Magazine – owned by South Africa through her intelligence agencies. This helped weaken apartheid support in the Western Press- during Nigeria’s Seizure of Barclays Bank and British Petroleum (BP) in 1979.
A few years later General Ibrahim Babangida appointed Dr Dele Cole as Nigeria’s ambassador to Argentina and Brazil according to Mr Peter Aribe, a public affairs analyst with deep military background. Ambassador Cole “helped grow tremendously Petrobras involvement in the Nigerian Oil Exploration especially in deep off shore investigations. The partnership between the Nigerian Navy and the Brazilian Navy was also greatly enhanced in this period; with the Brazilian Navy supplying most of the equipment required for the refit and repairs of Navy Boats at Navy Dockyard – Victoria Island, which General Babangida commissioned in 1990.”
When his friend, President Olusegun Obasanjo (GCFR) in 1999 became president, he tapped Dr Dele Cole to be his special adviser, along with Dr Stanley Macebuh (28 December 1942–7 March 2010). During the Obasanjo years, Dr Tunji Olagunju (82) from Offa, Kwara State, Prince Bola Ajibola (March 1934 – 8 April 2023), Dr Christopher Kolade (28 December 1932 – 8 October 2025), Otunba Oyewole Fasawe, the Asiwaju of Owo in Ondo state and Dr Dele Cole, were very close to the president.
In the case of Dr Patrick Dele Cole, he participated in numerous talks with Nigeria’s creditors, especially with the Paris Club on the debt relief. With his death, Nigeria has lost an astounding Public Servant.
Eric Teniola, a former director at the Presidency wrote from Lagos.

title: Cooperation with Russia helps to bolster energy security — Iran’s top diplomat
body:
MOSCOW, October 26. /TASS/. The development of the Iranian energy cooperation with Russia and other members of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum provides for stronger energy security, expansion of investment possibilities and diversification of supply routes, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi was quoted as saying in an article published by Russia’s Vedomosti daily.
"Enhanced cooperation among members of the Forum of Gas Exporting Countries and the further development of strategic relations between Iran and Russia paves ways for important opportunities to up joint investments, transfer technologies, develop infrastructure and increase natural gas supply capacity, which, in turn, will enhance energy security in the region and across the world," he noted.
Among the most important areas of cooperation between Moscow and Tehran, Araghchi named possible investments by Russian companies in the development of Iran’s oil and gas fields, the transfer of technology, the supply of equipment and the use of joint technical and engineering capabilities.
According to him, such cooperation might help to increase the production output volumes and reduce the consequences caused by unilateral coercive measures.

title: Sandra Amarquaye wins PR Professional Practitioner of the Year at IPR Excellence Awards 2025
body: Sandra Amarquaye, Corporate Communications Manager at Karpowership Ghana Company Limited (KGCL), was named PR Professional Practitioner of the Year at the 2025 Institute of Public Relations (IPR) Ghana Excellence Awards. This recognises her contributions to strategic communications, stakeholder engagement, corporate social responsibility (CSR), and reputation management. The award adds to her impressive record of professional achievements, including being named Internal Communicator of the Year at the 2024 IPR Ghana Excellence Awards, recognised among the Top 10 Women in PR in Ghana in 2024, and receiving the Community Development and Relations Leadership Impact Award at the Sustainability and Social Investment Awards. In 2021, she was named Sustainability and External Relations Champion at the Women in Mining and Energy Awards. She also received Karpowership’s Ace of Initiative award in 2018 for her innovative contributions to the organisation. At Karpowership Ghana, Sandra contributes to corporate communications, media relations, stakeholder engagement and CSR initiatives, helping strengthen the company’s reputation and relationships with employees, institutional stakeholders and communities. Her work reflects communication’s strategic role in building trust, supporting partnerships, and communicating corporate responsibility and sustainability initiatives. At the award ceremony, Karpowership was also recognised for Best in Crisis Communications, highlighting the company’s work in crisis communication and reputation management. Sandra credits her achievement to teamwork and the support of colleagues in Ghana and at Karpowership’s headquarters. “This award is not just a personal achievement; it is a recognition I share with the entire Karpowership team. I am grateful to my supportive colleagues in Ghana and at our headquarters, whose collaboration and commitment make my work easier and contribute to our collective success. “I remain committed to using strategic communication to build trust, strengthen partnerships and create meaningful value for our stakeholders and communities,” she said. Before moving into corporate communications, Sandra worked as an energy reporter and producer at TV3 Network Limited. She is an accredited member of the Institute of Public Relations Ghana and holds two Master of Arts degrees in Public Relations and Media Management. Her latest recognition marks another milestone in a career defined by professional growth, purposeful communication, stakeholder relationships and a commitment to excellence

title: NDC cancels constituency election in Amenfi East
body: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has cancelled its constituency-level election in Amenfi East in the Western Region following challenges during the party’s nationwide internal polls. The cancellation was one of the difficulties encountered during the exercise, which also saw delays in some constituencies, partly due to problems distributing ballot papers. Despite the setbacks, the party has expressed satisfaction with the overall conduct of the elections, describing the process as an improvement on the previous exercise. The NDC says it will assess the challenges encountered and draw lessons from the exercise to strengthen preparations for the upcoming regional elections. The party’s Acting Director of Elections and IT, Mahdi Jibril, disclosed the cancellation in an interview with Channel One TV on Sunday, October 25, while reviewing the conduct of the polls. “I would say so far, it is an improvement from the last election. I think the party is happy with the process,” he said, adding that, apart from the cancellation in Amenfi East and other logistical challenges, the exercise had been satisfactory.

title: Villar’s Vista Land 2025 net income falls 59% as delayed figures surface
body: MANILA, Philippines – Billionaire Manny Villar’s Vista Land and Lifescapes (VLL) finally released its long-delayed 2025 earnings figures on Monday, October 26, revealing a steep drop in net income despite higher operating earnings. Its net income plunged 59% to P3.8 billion from P9.37 billion in 2024. The company, however, led its announcement with earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA), which rose 6% to P24.2 billion from P22.82 billion, meeting what it described as “the company’s target for the year.” Unlike net income, EBITDA excludes interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization. This means it can rise even as the bottom line falls if these expenses increase, such as when a company faces substantial borrowing costs. Vista Land also reported P35.8 billion in consolidated revenue, although gross profit from its residential business, after deducting direct costs, fell 18% to P9.7 billion. More puzzling is its September 2025 quarterly report , which showed P9.46 billion in net income for the first nine months alone, more than double the P3.8 billion now reported for the full year. This leaves a more than P5-billion difference, which suggests a substantial fourth-quarter loss, revisions to earlier figures, or some combination of both. Must Read Mark Villar switches camps. Minutes later, family’s troubled firms make their move. What drove the divergence remains unclear, as VLL issued only a press release with selected figures, rather than its set of full audited financial statements. The company did offer one possible explanation, saying its results “reflect, in part, the recognition of interest expenses that were not capitalized into qualifying assets.” Instead, Vista Land emphasized that it launched 46 horizontal housing developments worth an estimated P49.6 billion, mainly under its Camella flagship brand. Its reported assets stood at P376.8 billion at year-end. The earnings release arrives after months of delays in reporting the company’s financials. Vista Land is among six listed companies linked to the Villar family suspended from trading for missed reporting deadlines. On October 8, Vista Land, Vistamalls, and VistaREIT announced a board approval to release their 2025 audited statements. The disclosures came on the same afternoon Senator Mark Villar moved to the Senate majority, while his sister Camille remained in the minority. But so far, Monday’s filing is still limited to a press release attached to an SEC Form 17-C, not the complete audited statements or annual report. It does not clear Vista Land to resume trading. – Rappler.com
