title: Jerry Ahmed Shaib urges safe contraflow, seeks Metro Mass buses for Weija-Gbawe
body: The Member of Parliament for Weija-Gbawe, Jerry Ahmed Shaib, has urged the Ministry of Transport to extend Metro Mass Transit buses to his constituency to help address persistent transport challenges. He welcomed the introduction of contraflow on the Kasoa-Accra road as a potential measure to ease congestion but cautioned that road safety must be the priority. “My expectation is that we should do it in a manner that would not end up actually causing accidents,” he said in an interview on Channel One Newsroom on Sunday, October 26. Mr Shaib said commuters in Weija-Gbawe and surrounding communities, including Tetegu, face high transport costs and often have to board multiple vehicles to reach their destinations. He appealed to the Transport Minister to provide at least four to six Metro Mass Transit buses to serve the area. “I’m praying that the Minister of Transport would also hear our cry and also furnish us with at least four or six Metro buses so that they can ply both Weija and Gbawe, Tetegu, all of these places,” he said. According to the MP, some commuters who normally spend between GH¢15 and GH¢20 on a journey now pay as much as GH¢60 to GH¢70 because of the transport difficulties. He said additional buses would help reduce fares and ease the daily burden on residents.

title: Gender advocate urges sustained breast cancer education in rural Ghana
body: Ghanaian media personality and US-based healthcare professional, Josephine Oppong-Yeboah has urged the Ghana Health Service (GHS) to intensify breast cancer education and outreach programmes, particularly among women in rural communities. She said myths and misconceptions about the disease had contributed to delays in seeking medical care, resulting in preventable deaths. Ms Oppong-Yeboah, who is a gender and disability advocate, said sustained public education, led by the GHS, could help dispel these misconceptions and encourage more women to seek medical attention early. She also commended non-governmental organisations supporting the health service to promote breast cancer awareness across the country. In an interview, she said breast cancer awareness should not be limited to October, when the disease is highlighted globally, but should be maintained throughout the year to reach more women and girls. “Many women are still under the impression that once breast cancer is detected, they are going to die. Such myths can only be corrected through sustained educational outreach,” she said. She noted that some women were afraid they would die if their affected breast had to be removed, prompting them to delay seeking treatment until the disease had progressed and become more difficult to manage. “We need to educate our women and girls about breast cancer. There is life after breast cancer detection. It only becomes a problem when the condition is detected late,” she said. While acknowledging the global campaign to raise breast cancer awareness in October, Ms Oppong-Yeboah said Ghana needed to sustain its education efforts beyond the month. “As a nation, we need not to wait for October to do this education. We have to adopt any means to reach our women, especially those in the remotest parts of the country,” she said. She added that misconceptions about breast cancer were particularly prevalent in remote communities, where access to healthcare remained a major challenge. “We should not be losing our women to breast cancer. We need to do whatever we need to do to get the awareness message to our women,” she said. Ms Oppong-Yeboah also encouraged women and girls to visit health facilities for breast health checks and seek medical advice when they noticed any unusual changes, emphasising the importance of early detection.

title: Multiple explosions reported in Yemen’s Sana’a
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 26 (MNA) – Several explosions heard in Sana'a, capital of Yemen, early on Monday as Saudi Arabia announced operations against Yemen.
Earlier, Yemen's Armed Forces Spokesman Brigadier General Yahya Saree had announced two successful ballistic missile operations carried out against gatherings of Saudi-backed mercenaries in Aden and Lahj provinces, inflicting dozens of casualties.

title: Roads Ministry wins PR Organisation of the Year for the second time
body: The Ministry of Roads and Highways has won the Public Sector PR Organisation of the Year award for the second consecutive time at the Institute of Public Relations (IPR) Ghana Excellence Awards. The award recognises the Ministry’s efforts to improve public communication, stakeholder engagement and access to information on road infrastructure development. The IPR Ghana citation said the Ministry had distinguished itself through timely dissemination of information on road projects and the use of innovative communication tools to engage the public. This year’s awards ceremony, held in Koforidua in the Eastern Region, recognised public institutions that demonstrated leadership in communication and applied public relations best practices to promote public trust. The Institute commended the Ministry’s Public Relations Unit, led by Alhaji Nasir Ahmad Yartey, a public relations practitioner and development communication professional with more than 17 years of experience in Ghana’s public sector, for its strategic and professional work. It said the Unit had strengthened proactive media engagement, community outreach programmes and relationships with key stakeholders to keep the public informed about road infrastructure projects across the country. The Ministry had also introduced digital communication tools to improve access to road development updates, enhanced social media reporting, used visual storytelling to showcase infrastructure progress and strengthened crisis communication systems, it said. In 2022, the Ministry received the Best Social Media PR Unit award at the Government PROs Excellence Awards, while Mr Yartey was named second runner-up in the PRO of the Year category. The Ministry reaffirmed its commitment to sustaining communication reforms, deepening citizen engagement, and supporting the delivery of safe, resilient, and modern road infrastructure. The IPR Ghana Excellence Awards are a major event that recognises individuals and institutions for outstanding performance, accountability, and innovation in public relations practice and professional communication.

title: Six Productions Explore Nazi Occupation, Civil War and Historical Trauma
body: Six theatre productions in Athens and Piraeus explore some of the darkest chapters of modern Greek history, from the German Occupation and the 1944 bombing of Piraeus to political persecution, the Greek Civil War and the lasting wounds these events inflicted on society. Through historical testimony, literature and personal stories, the productions examine resistance, collaboration with occupying forces, memory, guilt and ideological conflict. Together, they highlight how history extends beyond dates and events to encompass the people, experiences and traumas that continue to shape Greece today. 1. The Collaborators Venue: Chora Theatre, Athens (20 Amorgou Street, Kypseli) Theatre of the New World and the Elephas Tiliensis company, led by Dimitris Agartzidis and Despoina Anastasoglou, bring Menelaos Charalambidis’ The Collaborators to the stage for the first time, adapting his book of the same name for theatre. Charalambidis’ historical research examines Greek collaboration with the occupying forces during the German Occupation, betrayal, resistance and the pursuit of justice after the war. Direction: Dimitris Agartzidis and Despoina Anastasoglou. Cast: Dimitris Agartzidis, Despoina Anastasoglou, Markella Giannatou, Tolis Briasoulis, Vicky Katsika, Emmanouil Kontos and Aris Laskos. Performances began: October 26, 2026. 2. Soil Venue: bijoux de kant HOOD, Athens (35 Aktaίου Street, Thiseio) Based on Pavlos Matesis’ novel The Dog Mother , Soil explores the wounds of the German Occupation through the story of a woman and her mother’s relationship with an Italian occupier. The production examines social taboos, guilt and the enduring power of memory. The play premiered in August 2026 at the birthplace of Matesis in the village of Lampeia, in the Elis region of western Greece. It now inaugurates bijoux de kant’s new venue in Thiseio, where the company will present eight performances. Direction: Giannis Skourletis. Dramaturgy: Asimenia Efthymiou. Performers: Sotiria Chrysikopoulou and Charoula Tsalpara. Runs until: December 28, 2026. 3. “…Well, You Died Early” Venue: Sychrono Theatre, Athens (45 Evmolpidon Street, Kerameikos) Chronis Missios’ autobiographical work returns for a fifth consecutive season, demonstrating the continued relevance of the political experiences of one of Greece’s most prominent left-wing figures. Written in an associative, colloquial style, the work transforms painful political experiences into a vivid literary narrative. It condemns the torture Missios endured and the people who carried it out, while also criticising left-wing party bureaucrats and ideological dogmatism. The story begins in the shadow of the Greek Civil War and examines the persecution that followed. The GAFF theatre company brings Missios’ text to the stage under the direction of Sofia Karagianni. Dramaturgy: Sofia Karagianni and Myrto Athanasopoulou. Cast: Iosif Iosifidis, Konstantinos Passas, Dimitris Mamios and Giannis Manthos. Runs until: December 26, 2026. 4. The Purple Umbrella Venue: Poreia Theatre, Athens (3 Trikorfon Street) Based on the novel of the same name by Alki Zei, The Purple Umbrella follows a family shortly before the outbreak of the Second World War in 1940, as seen through the eyes of children. The production explores everyday family life, relationships and the changes approaching as Greece and Europe stand on the brink of a historic upheaval. Direction and dramaturgy: Dimitra Larentzakis. Stage adaptation: Dimitra Larentzakis and Sofia Eftychiadou. Cast: Agapi Moustri, Alexandros Koch, Vangelis Chalkiadakis, Giannis Eskintzoglou, Giorgos Makris, Eirini Ioannou-Papaneofytou, Nikolas Dringas, Triantafyllos Delis and Christina Vraka. Runs until: January 6, 2027. 5. The Monastery of Orthokosta Venue: NØ52 – STAGE, Athens (52–54 Tinou Street, Kypseli) In 1943–1944, while German forces still occupied Greece, civil conflict had already begun tearing apart communities in the mountainous region of Arcadia. Arrests, executions, reprisals and personal vendettas fuelled divisions. The Monastery of Orthokosta in Kynouria became a detention site for people considered enemies of the Greek People’s Liberation Army (ELAS). Writer Thanasis Valtinos explored this turbulent period in his 1994 novel Orthokosta , constructing a narrative through the testimonies of people who experienced the events. Inspired by the novel, the new stage production presents an original theatrical text that revisits the period’s conflicts and competing memories. Concept and direction: Konstantinos Plemm enos. Cast: Paraskevi Dourouklaki and Elli Stergiou. Premiere: November 18, 2026. 6. Listen, Little One – Piraeus Was Bombed Venues: Central Market of Piraeus and Municipal Theatre of Piraeus (32 Iroon Polytechniou Avenue, Piraeus) This documentary theatre production revisits the Allied bombing of Piraeus on January 11, 1944, during the Second World War. It recounts the experiences of people who sheltered in air-raid bunkers, witnessed the destruction and struggled to escape the city. After eight years of research, Hermes Peristeris and Spyros Asimenios of the Mementaλ theatre group developed the production using stories from people who experienced the bombing. The work first appeared at the Municipal Theatre of Piraeus, on its Stage Ω, and continues with special performances and activities at the Central Market of Piraeus on October 26, 27 and 28, 2026. These performances begin at 7.30pm, and admission is free. The production is scheduled to return for a new run at the Municipal Theatre of Piraeus from January 11, 2027. Dramaturgy: Hermes Peristeris and Spyros Asimenios. Cast: Spyros Asimenios, Lydia Giannousaki, Thanasis Kafen tarakis and Katerina Mephsout. title: Government grateful to Benin, Togo, international partners for swift rescue of fishers
body: Government has expressed sincere appreciation to the governments of Togo and Benin, and key international maritime partners, for coordinating the rescue of the seven Fishers. Madam Emelia Arthur, the Minister for Fisheries and Aquaculture, said the coordinated efforts reflected an excellent relationship and strategic regional cooperation on the maritime front. The Minister spoke at a welcome ceremony for the seven fishers who departed the shores of Ngyeresia but went missing for two weeks after an outboard motor failed. She said three million Ghanaians were in the fishing value chain, making meaningful contributions to the national economy; hence, sector players must treat safety as a critical, personal duty. The Sector Minister said, “We are grateful to God for averting such a calamity, but let all remember that safety at sea is a shared responsibility; please let us employ both traditional and modern ways in our expedition to save us in times of trouble”. Madam Arthur said the Ministry was also in talks with industry giants to procure trackers and other gadgets that could make tracing at sea easier. Meanwhile, she urged fishers to obey local regulations set by the Fisheries Commission and chief fishermen, adding that they are planning to implement byelaws, and any offender would be duly punished. Nana Kwesi Ackon, Chief Fisherman for Ngyeresia, urged the government to check the technical standards of outboard motors entering the country. He recounted how brand new outboard motors had failed at sea, leaving fishers helpless. In the last few months, 13 canoes have gotten stuck at sea because of similar engine failures, prompting local rescue efforts. The Chief Fisherman advised families to be cautious in what they say during such adversities. A detailed report from the Ghana Navy revealed that the found fishers travelled 220 kilometres off Ghana’s waters, which was not their original intent. The canoe owner’s distress call to the Police prompted the Police, Navy, Maritime, and local fishermen to conduct a thorough search, including using special boats and aircraft.

title: Physics Fest Brings Leading Scientists to University of Patras
body: Patras will host its first Patras Physics Fest on Friday, October 30, 2026, bringing leading scientists and well-known science communicators to the University of Patras for an afternoon of discovery, interactive activities and entertainment. The event will begin at 2pm at the university’s Conference and Cultural Centre and aims to make physics accessible to audiences of all ages. The student group Young Minds Patras is organising the festival under the auspices of the University of Patras Department of Physics. The event aims to connect the academic community with the wider public, welcoming experienced researchers as well as people curious about the mysteries of the universe. Leading Scientists and Science Communicators The programme will feature talks by distinguished scientists, including Stefanos Aretakis, Charis Anastopoulos and James Weatherall, who will offer audiences different scientific perspectives and insights. Three prominent Greek science communicators will also take part: Pavlos Kastanas, known as Astronio; Stefanos Vamvakos, of Kathimerini Physics; and Christos Kyriakidis, of It’s Just Physics. Through their work, they have helped bring physics to wider audiences across Greece. Experiments, Interactive Games and Stargazing Alongside the talks, visitors will be able to watch live scientific experiments, take part in interactive games with prizes and enjoy stargazing activities organised in collaboration with the Orion Astronomy Society. The combination of scientific presentations and hands-on activities aims to introduce visitors to physics in an engaging and accessible way. body:

title: EC yet to announce Dormaa Central NDC constituency election results
body: The Dormaa Central Electoral Commission (EC) in the Bono Region is yet to declare the winners of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) election in the constituency. This is because instead of 1400 hours, voting ended around 1915hours, with sorting and counting of ballots eaten into the night. The agents of the candidates contesting for the various constituency executive positions had earlier left the Nana Agyemang Badu I Sports Stadium, the venue of the event, as the EC continued with sorting and counting. About 1,290 delegates of the party participated in the constituency election, deciding on 55 candidates, the Ghana News Agency (GNA) learnt. Most of the delegates who had also travelled distances from their respective communities to Dormaa-Ahenkro for the election could also not wait for the outcome of the election. However, supporters of some of the incumbents turned to the streets of the Dormaa Township jubilating, though the EC had not announced the election results. They carried Mr George Adu, the incumbent constituency chairman, Mr David Atta Twum, incumbent constituency secretary, Eric Kyeremeh, incumbent Communication officer and Daniel Hinne, the incumbent deputy constituency secretary, shoulder-high and showered powder on them. Although the election ended peacefully, a misunderstanding which erupted between some supporters of the party and some supporters of Mr John Jack, the Member of Parliament (MP) for the Dormaa Central Constituency, nearly marred the beauty of the polls. The incident happened outside the venue of the polls; however, the timely intervention of the security personnel, who whisked the MP off the scene, saved the situation.

title: UNEP Warns 1.5-Degree Warming Overshoot Is Unavoidable as Kazakhstan Grapples With Coal Dependence
body: The Astana Times provides news and information from Kazakhstan and around the world. ASTANA – The world can no longer prevent warming from exceeding 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels, but deep emissions cuts could still limit the overshoot and bring temperatures back by 2100, according to the United Nations Environment Programme’s (UNEP) Emissions Gap Report 2026 released Oct. 21. Photo credit: Shutterstock The global benchmark UNEP says the chance of limiting warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius with “no or limited” overshoot, meaning less than 0.1 degrees Celsius, has been lost. It now measures progress against a “lowest possible” overshoot scenario that assumes stringent action from 2025. Under it, peak warming stays at 1.7-1.8 degrees Celsius with a 66% chance, and temperatures return to or below 1.5 degrees Celsius by 2100 with around a 50% chance. That path requires global emissions to fall 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035 and 69% by 2040 from 2025 levels, an average of 5.7% a year. It also depends on removing roughly 320 gigatons of CO2 from the atmosphere this century, which UNEP says is uncertain to achieve. New national pledges would cut emissions only 5-8% by 2030 and 11-15% by 2035. “Overshoot is not surrender. We can still keep it as small and as short as possible and bring temperatures back below 1.5 degrees by the end of the century,” UN Secretary-General António Guterres said in a message on the report. “The new Emissions Gap Report from the United Nations Environment Programme shows us what it will take: cutting global greenhouse gas emissions by 18% by 2030 and 45% by 2035, compared with 2025 levels,” he said. If current policies remain unchanged, global temperatures could rise by 2.8 degrees Celsius this century and continue climbing, the report warned. Even if countries fully implement their national climate commitments, known as nationally determined contributions (NDCs), under the Paris Agreement and sustain similar efforts, warming is projected to reach 2.6 degrees Celsius. Both estimates are higher than last year’s projections, largely because of the U.S. withdrawal from the Paris Agreement and updated calculations of historical emissions. The report found that new climate commitments submitted since its previous assessment have done little to improve the outlook. “Every additional fraction of a degree and additional year of warming above 1.5 degrees Celsius increases climate impacts and risks, such as the deadly floods, heatwaves and wildfires that have plagued many nations this year,” said UNEP Executive Director Inger Andersen. “So, we must pull out all the stops to minimize peak warming and return to 1.5 degrees Celsius by the end of the century. This is possible,” she added. Where Kazakhstan stands The report does not assess Kazakhstan or Central Asia individually, and Kazakhstan is not a G20 member, so it does not appear in the report’s country comparisons. But the benchmarks give a yardstick for the country’s own commitments. Kazakhstan’s updated climate pledge, NDC 3.0, targets a 17% cut in greenhouse gas emissions by 2035 compared with 1990 levels. A conditional target of up to 25% depends on international support. In 2023, Kazakhstan became the first Central Asian country to adopt a strategy for carbon neutrality by 2060. A power system built on coal The energy sector is where the challenge lies. Coal accounts for 62% of Kazakhstan’s electricity generation and 40% of its total greenhouse gas emissions, while renewable energy facilities account for 7% of the country’s total electricity production. Official targets point to gradual change. The government aims for renewables to supply 15% of electricity by 2030 and 50% by 2050. UNEP’s findings bear directly on these choices. It says renewable electricity capacity has grown three times faster than anticipated in 2015 and solar seven times faster, but total supply from coal, oil and gas keeps rising. It stresses that scaling up clean technology alone is not enough without moving away from fossil fuels. Finance and methane Guterres urged governments to invest in grids and storage, improve efficiency, cut methane and adopt credible roadmaps away from fossil fuels. He also called on developed countries to lower the cost of capital, expand concessional lending and ease debt burdens for developing economies. These efforts are underway in Kazakhstan. The country is developing QaJET , a platform to coordinate climate finance and identify priority projects, with the energy sector as its main focus, and is working with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development on methane reduction and its emissions trading system. NDC 3.0 also includes a target to cut fugitive methane emissions in the oil and gas sector by 42% by 2035. UNEP adds that developing and emerging economies are underrepresented in studies of what climate policies achieve. It recommends building evaluation into new policies from the outset. The report found that electricity-sector policies cut emissions by an average of 9% relative to a no-policy baseline. Looking ahead Andersen urged countries to raise ambition at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in November in Antalya. “Nations must understand that the point of return begins now. Not later – now,” she said. The report also urged countries to accelerate progress on commitments made during the first Global Stocktake, a review of collective efforts to meet the Paris Agreement goals conducted from 2021 to 2023. These commitments include tripling renewable energy capacity, doubling the annual rate of energy efficiency improvements by 2030, transitioning away from fossil fuels, cutting emissions other than carbon dioxide and reversing deforestation. Progress on most of these targets remains insufficient, according to the report. The second Global Stocktake, set to begin at the COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Türkiye, next month, offers an opportunity to strengthen these commitments by setting clearer, measurable targets for 2035 and 2040. The post UNEP Warns 1.5-Degree Warming Overshoot Is Unavoidable as Kazakhstan Grapples With Coal Dependence appeared first on The Astana Times .

title: Kaduna rally as the North’s referendum on Tinubu, By Abdulaziz Abdulaziz
body:
The gathering was beyond a rented crowd; it was organic, massive, and emotional. A few photos from the event displayed that spectacularly: the excited trio waving so happily at their president who wound down the window to greet them; the many people who kept vigil at the venue so they could get a good spot to witness history; and the excited young men and women who spent the whole day under the sun waving flags and chanting praises. It was Arewa saying, without apology: we still stand with our friend .
Through Kaduna, its old political capital, the North spoke two days ago. And the echo will haunt those who have spent months marketing the lie that the North has abandoned President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.
The Kaduna Township Stadium was full beyond capacity, and the mammoth crowd overflowed into the well-adorned streets. It was a confetti of colours, flags raised high and proudly: a sea of red caps, white babanriga, green wrappers, placards proclaiming “Sai Asiwaju.” It was a cacophony of languages — Hausa, Fulfulde, Tiv, Idoma, Gbagyi, Yoruba, Nupe, Kanuri, and English. Entire APC governors from the North, supported by their southern counterparts, sat shoulder-to-shoulder with former governors, legislators, imams, pastors, women leaders, and artisans who trekked kilometres to see the man they still call Jagaban, the leader.
The gathering was beyond a rented crowd; it was organic, massive, and emotional. A few photos from the event displayed that spectacularly: the excited trio waving so happily at their president who wound down the window to greet them; the many people who kept vigil at the venue so they could get a good spot to witness history; and the excited young men and women who spent the whole day under the sun waving flags and chanting praises. It was Arewa saying, without apology: we still stand with our friend .
As I wrote in February 2023, in the heat of the last campaign, when the same suspects tried to whip up ethnic sentiments against him, Asiwaju Tinubu and the North have always been friends. This friendship is not transactional. It is historic. Tinubu’s consequential political journey did not begin in Lagos. It began with the North.
In 1991, at the beginning of the aborted Third Republic, when General Ibrahim Babangida midwifed two parties, a young Tinubu had a choice. His kinsman, the great Chief Lateef Jakande, was in the field. Yet he chose to pitch his tent with General Shehu Musa Yar’Adua’s Peoples Front (PF) — the most organised, most progressive political machine of that era.
On the SDP platform under that PF, Tinubu became senator for Lagos West in 1992. When MKO Abiola emerged as SDP candidate, Tinubu was instrumental in pushing Ambassador Babagana Kingibe, a son of Borno, as the running mate. He chose North, again. That choice in 1992 has defined his politics ever since.
When President Obasanjo wanted to skin Atiku Abubakar alive in 2007, Bola Tinubu was his saviour. In 2011, he propped up Nuhu Ribadu, and Muhammadu Buhari in 2015 and 2019. In 2011, he supported Aminu Tambuwal for speaker at a time Tambuwal’s own party, the PDP, was against him. No other Southern politician has invested that much political capital in the North.
This is why Arewa for Asiwaju, a political movement of the crème de la crème of the Northern political establishment, is a commendable and timely intervention. At a time when the opposition offers only recycled fuel subsidy — illegal under the PIA — and AI-generated falsehoods which Governor Uba Sani rightly warned about in Kaduna, A4A provides what Arewa needs most: honest conversation, the voice of truth, in Hausa, Fulfulde, Tiv, Nupe, Gbagyi, Kanuri, in every market, motor park, mosque and church.
A4A is not just a campaign apparatus. It is a reminder that friendship is a two-way street and that the North is faithful to its values of fairness, justice, peaceful coexistence and national unity. As a political movement, its raison d’être is consensus-building and evidence-based campaigning. The purpose is to counter with evidence the lies that as president, Asiwaju Tinubu has abandoned his old friend, the North. How? With the Ministry of Livestock Development that the North craved for 60 years? With the North Central Development Commission and North West Development Commission? With the new federal universities in Mubi, Kachia and Kabo? Would the person who abandoned the North rush the completion of the Kano-Maradi rail or the Akwanga-Lafia-Makurdi road? Would he have established cancer centres and upgraded dozens of hospitals and schools? Well, Arewa for Asiwaju is throwing those questions with hard facts.
Kaduna provided a ground to further deflate the vacuous noise of the opposition. The North came together with one powerful voice. Eighteen out of 19 governors, an array of former governors from the class of 1999 to date, a horde of Young Turks, an armada of party faithful. It was a spectacle.
For months, a small but loud echo chamber in Abuja and on social media had been working hard to sell a fiction that the North regrets 2023, that the president and his campaigners can no longer enter Arewa, that 2027 is already decided. Kaduna buried that fiction with one picture.
As the Campaign Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign, Senator Abdulaziz Yari said from the podium, everyone that mattered in the North was at the stadium yesterday. Most of them were there in person, a lot more in spirit. The few and scattered dissenters are too insignificant to cause any political upheaval.
Vice President Kashim Shettima and Yari did not come to Kaduna to speak grammar. They came with history and with receipts.
VP Shettima was as sharp and straight as always. He used a clincher to remind voters from the North of the options before them. “We won in 2023 not because we were the wisest or richest, but because you saw the options before you and knew the alternative was a calamity. We have come to ask you to renew a second term for the APC from top to bottom.”
Senator Yari, who was evidently pleased by the turnout across all walks of life, assured: “By God’s grace, Northern Nigeria is 101 per cent behind you, Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu, and we are determined to deliver our promise on 16 January 2027.” Speaking further in Hausa, Senator Yari said the president should as well go to sleep and wait for victory.
Yet, President Tinubu did not just go to Kaduna to excite the crowd or display supporters. He went with deliveries. In a first for campaign rallies, President Tinubu used the occasion to inaugurate the 81-kilometre section of the Kaduna-Abuja highway with a symbolic ribbon-cutting. It is just one of many dividends Kaduna got from the Tinubu administration, as Governor Uba Sani reeled out so many benefits Kaduna reaped from the Tinubu administration in his welcome address. They range from roads to rail to universities and health institutions. The North, as Governor Sani testified, has never had it this good.
President Tinubu is repaying loyalty in concrete, steel, and care.
From Peoples Front in 1991 to Arewa for Asiwaju in 2026, President Tinubu has always operated as a friend. Kaduna proved it. On 16 January 2027, the ballot will confirm it louder.
Abdulaziz Abdulaziz is senior special assistant to the president on print media and director of media and communication, Arewa for Asiwaju.

title: Benjamin Djakumah retains NDC Tema Central chairmanship
body: Benjamin Djakumah has retained the Tema Central Constituency chairmanship of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), polling 685 votes in the party’s constituency executive elections. He defeated four other contenders: Mr Alex Arkorful (161 votes), Mr Etse Togbenyo (96 votes), Mr Ebenezer Ken Nana Eshun (70 votes), and Mr Nana Boakye Adarkwah Yiadom (56 votes). Mr Emmanuel Swanzy Martin won the vice-chairmanship with 561 votes, beating Mr Courage Apertoli (390 votes), Mr Larry Mensah (72 votes), and Mr George Kofi Imbeah (42 votes). In the secretary contest, Mr Seidu Mohammed won with 580 votes, followed by Mr Oyril Tsatsu Kumedzro with 326 votes, Mr Elinam Attuah Ayensu with 92 votes, Mr Jones Asafo Adjei with 55 votes, and Mr Samuel Yaw Owusu-Akyem with 15 votes. Mr Kenneth Aponsah Decardi-Nelson was elected Deputy Secretary with 517 votes. Mr Abdul-Razak Mohammed Muta-Wakil was elected organiser with 487 votes, defeating Mr Daniel Tsevi Adablah (391 votes) and Mr Anthony Kow Sam-Anoom (183 votes). Mr Fatawu Bansi Dauda was elected Youth Organiser with 95 votes, defeating Mr Christian Adjavon, who polled 47 votes. Mr Richard Amegbedzi won the Deputy Youth Organiser position with 83 votes, beating Mr Emmanuel Nongor, who obtained 57 votes, while Mr Geoffrey Owiredo Oppong was elected Other Youth Representative with 80 votes. For the women’s wing, Ms Gloria Mensah won the Women Organiser position with 68 votes, defeating Ms Francisca Mama Akoshia Bleboo (42 votes) and Ms Ami Sefakor Angela Dablah (30 votes). Ms Evelyn Akos Bediako was elected Deputy Women Organiser with 57 votes. Eight other members were also elected to the constituency executive. They are Mr Ahmed Lare Alhassan; Mr Bernard Nwea-Ackah Mocjah; Mr Fancy Senyo Yaw Akabuo; Mr Joe Neizer Cornilius; Mr Sampson Kofi Acquah; Mr Winfred Washie Amexorga Ameevor; Mr Sylvanus Kofi Geli; and Mr Caleb Doerfnyoh.

title: Drone reportedly strikes business center in Russia's Voronezh as fires break out across city
body:
Editor's note: This is a developing story.
A drone reportedly struck a business center in the Russian city of Voronezh early on Oct. 26, as explosions and fires were reported across the city amid an ongoing drone attack, independent Russian media outlet ASTRA reported.
Footage published by ASTRA appears to show a drone exploding at the Chizhov Gallery business center, a 25-story building in central Voronezh.
Ukrainian monitoring channel Exilenova+ also published imagery of the reported attack.
ASTRA further reported fires in residential areas, having received eyewitness photographs and videos that identified locations near apartment buildings where explosions occurred.
Voronezh Oblast Governor Aleksandr Gusev confirmed that Russian air defenses responded to a drone attack over Voronezh and its surrounding areas on the morning of Oct. 26.
According to ASTRA, a drone threat was announced at approximately 3 a.m. local time, followed by a missile warning about two hours later.
Reports mentioned numerous explosions across the city and thick smoke rising from several locations. Some residents told ASTRA that they had not heard air raid sirens despite the ongoing attack.
The Kyiv Independent could not verify the extent of the damage or whether the explosions near residential buildings were caused by direct drone impacts or falling debris. There were no immediately confirmed reports of casualties.
Voronezh Oblast directly borders eastern Ukraine, with the regional capital located about 200 kilometers (nearly 120 miles) from the nearest Ukrainian-held territory in Kharkiv Oblast. The areas has repeatedly been targeted by Ukrainian long-range strikes against Russian military and industrial infrastructure.
On June 22, Ukrainian forces struck the Voronezh Semiconductor Plant, a facility producing electronic components used in Russian missile and air defense systems, according to Ukraine's General Staff.

title: Wema Bank sets November 6 for Hackaholics 7.0 finale
body: Wema Bank has fixed November 6, 2026, for the grand finale of its flagship innovation platform, Hackaholics 7.0, with 5,329 participants and 1,632 ideas recorded during its nationwide search for young innovators. The grand finale, themed “Festival of the Future,” will bring together technology leaders, startup founders, investors and other stakeholders in Nigeria’s innovation ecosystem to showcase emerging technologies, explore new ideas and recognise innovations with the potential to address real-world challenges. The event will also feature interactive experiences and discussions on how emerging technologies are transforming how people live, work, build and create. Speaking on the initiative, Wema Bank’s Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Moruf Oseni, said the concept reflected the bank’s commitment to encouraging Nigerians to take an active role in shaping the future. “The world is changing at an unprecedented pace. Artificial intelligence and emerging technologies are transforming industries, businesses and everyday life, creating opportunities that would have been difficult to imagine just a few years ago. The question is no longer simply what the future holds, but how prepared we are to shape it,” he said. Oseni said the Festival of the Future was designed to bring innovation closer to people, stimulate meaningful conversations and encourage fresh thinking about future possibilities. He added that Hackaholics had evolved beyond a competition into a platform for identifying talent, nurturing ideas and connecting innovators with opportunities. “Since we launched Hackaholics, our goal has remained consistent; to provide young Nigerians with the platform, resources, opportunities and support they need to transform their ideas into practical solutions. We believe that the future of innovation in Nigeria must be driven by the talent, creativity and potential of our people,” he said. According to him, the seventh edition would deepen the bank’s commitment by bringing together people, conversations and experiences capable of inspiring the next generation of solutions. Hackaholics 7.0 was launched on July 1, 2026, under the theme “Powering Possibilities” and commenced with a nationwide pitch centre tour aimed at discovering innovative ideas from young Nigerians. The four-month tour covered seven locations: Uyo, Kano, Yaba College of Technology, Benin, Ibadan, Enugu and Lagos. The initiative featured three tracks: Ideathon, Hackathon and Social Impact. While the Ideathon focused on promising ideas, the Hackathon provided a platform for technology developers and builders, and the Social Impact track recognised solutions designed to deliver measurable benefits to society. At the end of the nationwide tour, 59 participants emerged from the various pitch centres and will undergo further shortlisting to 20 finalists. The 20 shortlisted participants are expected to present refined versions of their solutions at the pre-pitch event scheduled for November 4. On November 5, participants will embark on an ecosystem tour organised by Wema Bank to visit leading institutions in the technology and innovation sector, interact with industry professionals and gain practical insights ahead of the finale. The programme will culminate in the Festival of the Future on November 6, when outstanding innovators will be recognised for their ideas and solutions. Through Hackaholics, Wema Bank seeks to strengthen Nigeria’s innovation ecosystem, support entrepreneurship and provide young people with opportunities to develop solutions that contribute to economic development.

title: Queen Rania attends funeral for victims of Jordan church attack
body: Jordan's Queen Rania offered condolences to the families of the nine people killed in an attack on a Greek Orthodox church in the Karak governorate. Members of the royal family on Sunday visited the village of Hamoud, where the victims were buried. The funeral was held at the same church where the attack took place on Friday. Queen Rania and Crown Prince Hussein bin Abdullah were accompanied by Princess Rajwa and Princess Salma, Jordan's state-run Petra agency reported. During the visit to the church, Crown Prince Hussein expressed the sympathies and condolences of King Abdullah II to the families. King Abdullah described the attack as "terrorism" and Jordan's Ministry of Interior said three suspects were detained on Monday morning. The king visited the injured in hospital on Friday and spoke with them to check on their condition, according to footage shown by the state-owned broadcaster. Queen Rania prayed for the victims and was seen comforting their family members. It was the biggest attack against Jordan's Christian minority since the 1950s. The dead were all men. One was a doctor and another was a dentist. Most belonged to the Halasah clan, one of the most prominent Christian families in Jordan. It was not immediately known why only eight of the nine were buried in Hamoud. The attack in Karak, about 100km south of Amman, took place during a funeral.

title: Julius Nainoo unseats incumbent NDC constituency chairman in Berekum West
body: Delegates of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Berekum West Constituency of the Bono Region have elected Mr Julius Nainoo as party chairman. He polled 334 valid votes to unseat the incumbent chairman, James Ntim, who had 302 valid votes in an election conducted and supervised by the Electoral Commission (EC) at Koraso in the constituency. The delegates also elected Mr Simeon Sakyi as the Vice Chairman with 336 votes, beating Mr Emmanuel Amankona who had 298 votes. Mr Effah Jame, Mr Victor Abeam Takyi, Mr Ernest Korang and Mr Francis Gyamfi were elected as the party’s constituency Communications Officer, Youth Organiser, and Deputy Organiser by popular acclamation. Madam Regina Ferka won the Women Organiser position with 43 votes, beating her only contender, Madam Diana Koranteng, with 27 votes, while Mr Forster Kyere also secured 59 votes for Deputy Youth Organiser, beating Mr Emmanuel Acheampong, who had 11 votes. Mad Esther Mmra secured 39 votes to beat Madam Gladys Kyeremaa, who had 31 votes, for the Deputy Women Organiser position, while Sampson Adjei polled 445 votes for the Zongo Caucus position, beating Ibrahim Sheikh Idrisu, who had 186 votes. Madam Linda Akrasi won the Deputy Treasurer position with 364 votes, defeating Mr Isaac Yeboah with 269 votes, while Mr Abraham Lincoln won the Deputy Communications Officer position with 348 votes, beating Mr Kofi Mclean with 293 votes. Mr Augustine Nketia was also elected as the Constituency Organiser with 421 votes, beating Mr Anthony Amoah, with 215 votes, while the Treasurer position went to Mr Eric Amponsa Benneh, with 291 votes, beating his two contenders, Mr Francis Kwadwo Atta, with 242 votes and Mr Daniel Osei, with 99 votes. For the secretary position, Mr Kwasi Asoma was elected with 341 votes, beating his sole contender, Mr Eric Kyere, with 294 votes, while Mr Prince Dwabeng polled 354 votes to secure the Deputy Secretary position, beating Mr Peter Adjei, with 276 votes. Other executive members comprised Mr Stephen Kofi Kyere, 60 votes; Mr Eric Aseidu, 100 votes; Mr Samuel Acheaw, 148 votes; Mr Solomon Dadzie, 77 votes; Mr Frank Owusu, 66 votes; Mad Joyce Yeboah, 43 votes; Mr Ransford Korang, 52 votes; Mr Solomon Owusu, 38 votes; and Mr Kofi Baa, 40 votes. In an interview with the Ghana News Agency (GNA), Mr Nainoo, the newly elected constituency chairman, pledged his commitment to work hard to make the NDC more appealing in the constituency. He expressed appreciation to the delegates for the confidence reposed in the newly elected executives and assured their dedication to work hard for the NDC to retain the Berekum West constituency parliamentary seat and political power in the Election 2028.

title: EDITORIAL: Why the US midterm elections matter
body:
On Tuesday, 3 November, Americans will vote in what is known as the midterm elections. In addition to a slew of elections at the municipal levels and a broad range of citizen and legislatively referred initiatives, voters will have their say on all 435 seats in the United States House of Representatives, 35 of the 100 seats in the United States Senate (including two special elections) and for 36 state governors, amongst others.
Yet, the one name that is not on the ballot, that of the US president, looms large over this cycle. Historically, midterm elections have been difficult for the president’s party. Indeed, over the last 22 US midterm elections, from 1934 to 2022, the president’s party gained seats in the House of Representatives in only three elections. It lost House seats in the other nineteen.
The polls, as of 16 October, give Democrats a 90 per cent chance of winning the House and a 63 per cent chance of controlling the Senate. These predictions are par for the course. The problem is that up until these elections, the Donald Trump presidency has opted to alter courses in unpredictable, if not outrightly illegal ways.
Ignore his failed insurrection on 6 January, 2021, and from inciting gerrymanders in Republican-controlled states, to trying to insert the US Postal Services into election processes that are constitutionally state bailiwicks, the Trump administration has been a force for chaos. Its economics, especially the president’s obsession with tariffs, have hurt Americans while strengthening China.
His love of tyrant-leaders has seen him cozy up to dictators in North Korea and Russia. In taking up the dictatorship in Iran, in a war whose goals remain as clear as the president’s thinking, he unintentionally handed leverage on the global economy to one of its pariah states, and helped include Israel in a listing of infamous regimes worldwide.
To think that all of these were aimed at Making America Great Again (MAGA). While accounting for about 26 per cent of the global economy just before the beginning of the second Trump presidency, America was never a tiddler. Yet, the MAGA quest for further US greatness has seen the US gut much of the infrastructure that has held the global system together during the interwar years. PREMIUM TIMES recognises that from the United Nations through to the many agencies that have been critical to maintaining world peace over the years, the world needs to think differently about how it will be organised over the next one hundred years.
The challenges are as onerous as they have always been. The AI revolution and the growing belief in the might-is-right view of international relations only complicate this task further. This newspaper is also aware that much of the thinking for the redesign of the global architecture has already been done by the agencies entrusted with this responsibility. The missing ingredient is the whimsical bent of the leaders of the world’s leading countries. These whimsies, alas, have been lent wings by the capricious Trump administration over the last two years.
Will the next Congress keep or lose its ability to check Trump’s policies? In Africa, as the concerns over the administration’s evisceration of the World Health Organisation (WHO) indicates, this is already a major policy conundrum. As if muzzling the WHO were not enough, the Trump administration’s use of aid as a political lever, continues to put Africa in deficit. One can admit that aid is a sovereign US choice, while objecting to its being used to humiliate and punish. The incumbent US federal government tied its decision to end the President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) support for South Africa to an executive order accusing the country of discriminating against white Afrikaners. Congress has been the backstop before. A similar effort by the administration to claw back unspent PEPFAR funds as part of a wider cut to foreign aid, was stymied by Republican defections in Congress. A renewal of the Trump majority would weaken this backstop.
Opposition from the White House and conservative Republicans created an additional vulnerability for the continent when Speaker Mike Johnson was forced to cut the House’s initial renewal of the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) from three to one year. The US trade preference programme enacted in 2000, which provides duty‑free access to the US market for over 1,800 products from eligible sub‑Saharan African countries, has been kept alive until 31 December, after Trump signed a law extending AGOA by one year. This means the next Congress would decide the programme’s future almost immediately. A Republican Congress aligned with the White House is more likely to turn AGOA, whose effectiveness is already weakened by the administration’s rash of tariffs, into a “reciprocity” bargaining chip. South Africa, for example, may have kept its AGOA eligibility, but the 30 per cent “reciprocal” tariffs imposed in 2025 largely cancel its benefits.
There are, no doubt, few benefits to the continent from America’s collective ban on mobility. Thirty-six of Africa’s 54 countries now face either US travel bans or visa bonds. This disproportionately hurts students, professionals, diaspora ties, and remittances. While these measures are outcomes of executive orders issued by the White House, congressional oversight and appropriations shape how far they can go.
The outcome of the midterm elections will also bear on where deportees go. An AFP investigation found that Washington used the threats of tariffs, visa suspensions, or aid cuts to compel African countries into accepting deportees. Burundi recently became the 15th African nation to agree to this arrangement. The harm here is not only to migrants. As one analysis puts it, these secret deals set precedents that erode the rule of law and transparency that African democracies so sorely need. Congressional scrutiny is one of the few ways these terms become public.
A Congress that holds hearings and demands evidence is a check on policy driven by information disorder. A compliant one is not. This matters most when much of the measures taken by the US administration against South Africa draw on “genocide” framings that the two governments reject and that many analysts consider distorted. Because war powers are essentially congressional powers, the US Congress’ willingness to question an expansive reading of a 2001 counterterrorism law will offer African states far more protection from the Trump administration’s penchant for unilateral action. For Nigeria, this is the sharpest issue. Strikes in northwest Nigeria in December were the first US military strikes ever in the country, authorised under the 2001 Authorisation for Use of Military Force Act.
Built, as it is, on bogus and false narratives, the Trump administration has been an ill-wind that has served the world poorly over the last 24 months. This is why, PREMIUM TIMES looks forward to a return of a Democratic majority in the US House of Representatives, and hopefully, in the Senate, too.

title: Tehran to host Saudi, Turkish, Pakistani officials
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 26 (MNA) – Saudi Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman, Pakistani army chief General Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin will take part in a joint meeting in Tehran, a senior SNSC official said.
Ali Bagheri Kani, deputy secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said Saudi Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman, Pakistani army chief General Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin will take part in a joint meeting during a visit to Tehran. Bagheri said General Asim Munir, in a meeting with Major General Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, announced the decision by senior Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials to travel to Tehran, meet the secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council and hold a joint meeting. Bagheri said all three countries attending the meeting, together with Iran, can take an effective step toward establishing endogenous regional security by drawing on the Islamic Republic's successful experience in building national security during the third imposed war. MNA

title: Nvidia Eyes AI Companies Founded By Greek Scientists
body: A US artificial intelligence company co-founded by Greek scientist Ioannis Antonoglou has attracted interest from Nvidia, highlighting the growing influence of Greek entrepreneurs in the global AI industry. Reflection AI has reached a reported valuation of $25 billion, while Nvidia is discussing a possible acquisition or further investment in the company, according to the Financial Times . The talks remain at an early stage, with no final agreement in place. Nvidia has already invested approximately $800 million in Reflection AI. The options under consideration reportedly include an acquisition, additional funding or the purchase of technology and talent. Reflection AI is among several companies founded by Greek entrepreneurs that participate in the Endeavor network and operate at the forefront of artificial intelligence. Other notable founders include Anastasios Germanidis of Runway, Anastasios Angelopoulos of Arena, Spyros Xanthos of Resolve AI and Niki Goulimis of Tunic Pay. Their companies develop technologies spanning advanced AI models, video generation, software infrastructure automation and banking fraud prevention, with applications across business and everyday life. Reflection AI: The $25 Billion AI Company Attracting Nvidia Ioannis Antonoglou, co-founder and chief technology officer of Reflection AI, has an extensive background in artificial intelligence. He previously worked at Google DeepMind, where he contributed to the development of advanced AI systems. Founded in 2024 by Antonoglou and Misha Laskin, Reflection AI develops large AI models designed to help businesses and organisations deploy and customise the technology for their own needs. In practical terms, the company develops technology that can power intelligent digital assistants and other AI applications. Businesses can use these models to analyse information, answer complex questions and help software developers write and debug code. Reflection AI designs its models to allow companies to install and customise them within their own systems, giving organisations greater control over their technology and data. In October 2026, Reflection AI introduced Beam, its first open-parameter model, as it seeks to compete with leading AI systems, particularly in software development and complex problem-solving. Endeavor’s figures put the company’s valuation at $25 billion. Runway: The Greek Entrepreneur Behind AI-Generated Video Anastasios Germanidis co-founded Runway and serves as its co-chief executive officer. The company operates in one of the fastest-growing areas of artificial intelligence: image and video generation and editing. Runway has developed tools used by content creators, advertising agencies and audiovisual production professionals. For example, an advertiser can create a short video showing a car driving along a fictional road without organising a physical shoot. The user can describe the scene in words or provide a photograph, and the system generates a corresponding video. The technology can also change a scene’s background, lighting or appearance. AI is therefore becoming an additional tool for filmmaking, advertising and digital content production. Runway is also developing systems designed to understand and simulate the physical world, with potential applications beyond video production, including robotics and digital simulations. According to Endeavor, Runway’s valuation exceeds $5 billion. Germanidis also featured on the Forbes AI 50 list for 2026. Arena: Putting Artificial Intelligence Models to the Test Anastasios Angelopoulos co-founded Arena and serves as its chief executive officer. The platform has gained international recognition for evaluating and comparing AI systems. As companies continually introduce new models, Arena seeks to answer a central question: which systems perform best in practice? Users can submit the same question to two different AI systems without necessarily knowing their identities. They then compare the responses and select the one they consider better. Arena aggregates these assessments to help rank different models. The platform allows users seeking AI tools for writing, image generation or software development to compare the capabilities of available systems. Arena has become an important reference point for AI model comparisons and continues to expand into different application categories. In October 2026, the company secured $200 million in funding, bringing its valuation to $3.1 billion. Endeavor Catalyst also participated in the funding round. Resolve AI: An AI Engineer That Identifies and Fixes Technical Problems Spyros Xanthos co-founded Resolve AI and serves as its chief executive officer. The company specialises in automating the operation of complex software systems. Resolve AI develops tools that help software engineers identify the causes of technical problems and restore applications and digital services more quickly. For example, an online shopping platform or payment application might suddenly experience technical failures. Engineers would normally need to examine multiple systems to identify the cause. Resolve AI’s technology can automatically analyse technical data, identify potential causes and recommend corrective measures. Where authorised, it can also carry out recovery actions. The company aims to reduce service disruptions and save valuable engineering time. Resolve AI has attracted international investors, and its valuation exceeded $1 billion during a funding round in February 2026, according to Endeavor. Xanthos also brings previous entrepreneurial experience to the company. Splunk acquired Omnition, which he co-founded. Tunic Pay: Using AI to Help Banks Prevent Fraud Niki Goulimis co-founded Tunic Pay and serves as its chief executive officer. She previously helped establish Nova Credit before moving into the financial technology sector. Founded in London in 2023, Tunic Pay uses artificial intelligence to combat a growing form of financial crime: scams that trick people into transferring money to fraudsters. For example, a customer might receive a message that appears to come from their bank and urges them to transfer money urgently to a specified account. Tunic Pay develops tools that banks can integrate into their services to assess suspicious transactions and examine information supplied by customers. These checks can identify potential warning signs before a payment goes through. The technology helps banks assess risk and warn customers, while leaving the final decision to the customer and the bank’s established procedures. Tunic Pay has developed solutions in partnership with banks, including Britain’s TSB, which offers a suspicious-transaction checking tool powered by the company’s technology. Endeavor and the Growing Global Footprint of Greek Entrepreneurship These five companies illustrate how Greek entrepreneurs are increasingly contributing to the global economy. Rather than building businesses exclusively in Greece before expanding abroad, Greek founders are establishing companies directly in major international technology hubs, attracting substantial investment and developing products for global markets. Endeavor Greece supports a network of entrepreneurs and seeks to strengthen their ties with Greece through investment, partnerships and the transfer of expertise. Panos Karambinis, managing director of Endeavor Greece, highlighted the growing influence of the Greek diaspora in artificial intelligence and the importance of maintaining its connections with the country. Speaking to the Athens-Macedonian News Agency (AMNA) and journalist Alekos Lidorikis, Karambinis said: “The Greek diaspora is building artificial intelligence today at a pace that has astonished even us, who see what is happening up close across dozens of markets around the world.” He described the development as recognition of generations of Greeks who devoted themselves to science, noting that technological progress increasingly depends on advanced research, an area in which Greek scientists have distinguished themselves. “Most importantly, wherever they are, they connect their future with Greece. They want to make an impact here, and they are already giving back. At Endeavor, we will continue to act as a bridge between the two ecosystems so that this impact can grow even further,” Karambinis said. Through Endeavor Catalyst, the international organisation’s investment arm, Endeavor also invests in selected high-growth businesses. Its new Endeavor Catalyst Fund V has raised more than $320 million, with Greek investors contributing over $70 million. Investors include Greece’s four systemic banks and business families from Greece and the Greek diaspora. For Greece, the challenge now extends beyond gaining international recognition for its scientists and entrepreneurs. The country must also find ways to translate their success into benefits for the domestic economy. Attracting investment, creating jobs, transferring expertise and developing partnerships with Greek businesses and research institutions are among the key priorities. As artificial intelligence reshapes the global economy, Greece has an opportunity to turn its growing presence in international technology hubs into a stronger economic and technological footprint at home. title: Vice President commends Black Maidens for reaching FIFA U-17 World Cup Last 16
body: Vice President Prof. Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang has congratulated Ghana’s Black Maidens on reaching the Round of 16 of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco after their impressive 2-0 victory over Canada. In a social media post, the Vice President said she had been following the team’s progress and was encouraged by the confidence and determination the players displayed throughout the competition. She noted that the team’s performances continued to highlight the immense potential of women’s football in Ghana and described the victory over Canada as another important milestone in their campaign. Prof. Opoku-Agyemang urged the players to stay focused, united, and confident as they prepare for the tournament’s knockout stage. “Every stage offers a new opportunity to show the world what they can achieve,” she stated. The Vice President also congratulated the players, technical team, and everyone who has contributed to the team’s success so far. The Black Maidens booked their place in the knockout phase after finishing Group B with four points. After suffering a 3-0 defeat to Norway in their opening match, Ghana bounced back with a thrilling 3-3 draw against Brazil before defeating Canada 2-0 in their final group game. Substitutes Linda Achiaa and Christiana Ashiaku scored to secure the crucial victory for Coach Joe Nana Adarkwa’s side and send them through to the Round of 16. Ghana will now face Argentina on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, for a place in the competition’s quarterfinals.

title: Russian forces attack energy facility in Khmelnytskyi region
body:
Ukrinform reports this citing Serhii Tiurin, Head of the Khmelnytskyi Regional Military Administration.
“An energy facility was damaged in the Kamianets-Podilskyi district as a result of the Russian attack. There are emergency power outages,” he wrote.
According to the official, energy workers are working to restore power supplies.
In addition, windows were damaged in two residential buildings. According to preliminary information, Tiurin added, there were no casualties.
As reported by Ukrinform, on October 22, a business in Khmelnytskyi district was damaged as a result of a Russian attack.

title: Rapper Nicki Minaj joins Trump onstage at Michigan rally
body: Rapper Nicki Minaj said US President Donald Trump has “changed the energy of the country” as she joined him at a Michigan rally to stump for Republicans ahead of the nationwide midterm elections. “He’s given us a future to look forward to,” she said, after Trump praised her figure and called her on stage to speak. Minaj has called herself Trump’s “number one fan” despite criticising some of his first-term policies. In Michigan, Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed is locked in a tight race with Republican Mike Rogers with just over a week to go before the midterms. Former President Barack Obama held a rally – one of the first in this cycle – with the Democrat on Saturday. Democrats are also aggressively hitting the campaign trail, with close elections on 3 November that will decide which party controls Congress for the rest of Trump’s presidency. In his remarks on Sunday, Trump focused on El-Sayed’s Muslim faith and background, alleging that he will “invite jihadists” into America if he wins. El-Sayed has criticised similar remarks by Trump as Islamophobic, saying in an ad to voters last week that the US president “thinks he can use my name and my faith to distract us from the suffering his policies are inflicting on us at the pump, at the grocery store, and at the doctor’s office”. In Port Huron on Sunday, Minaj, wearing a gold-coloured Gucci-branded suit, led the crowd in chanting Trump’s name and the names of Republican candidates in Michigan. “We really need all these great people to be elected, because this is a major turning point for our country,” she said. “She never looked more beautiful,” Trump said as she left the stage. “She gets it. She’s smart,” he added. Earlier in his speech, Trump praised one male Republican candidate’s rear end before turning the crowd’s attention to Minaj. “By the way, I looked at a beautiful ass before,” he segued. “Nicki Minaj. That’s hard to miss.” He then asked her to “stand up” as the crowd cheered and added that he hoped she wasn’t “insulted” by his remark. The Super Bass singer had accompanied Trump to the state aboard Air Force One. She filmed a video with an aide – which was posted to X -on the president’s plane, pretending to be interviewing for the White House press secretary role. The position is currently open after Katie Zacharia left five days after a shaky public debut. The Trinidad and Tobago-born rapper has thrown her star power behind Trump a few times before, including on his allegations that Christians face persecution in Nigeria and his “gold card” visa, which offers applicants residency and a path to US citizenship.

title: For Russia’s sanctions-busting A7 payment service, international transfers start with bags of cash at Moscow markets. At its peak, it processed at least 58 metric tons in a single month.
body: Payment service A7’s booth at the ExpoForum center. On the left is PSB management board chairman Pyotr Fradkov; on the right is A7’s majority shareholder Ilan Shor, who was convicted of fraud in Moldova. June 3, 2026 What A7 is and how it became the largest player in the shadow payments market Sanctions against Russian banks and payment systems, along with their disconnection from SWIFT after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, gave rise to shadow intermediaries offering Russians cross-border money transfers. Many have offices in the capital’s Moscow City business district, the investigative outlet Proekt reported in spring 2026. The largest is A7, a company owned by Moldovan businessman Ilan Shor , who was convicted of fraud and embezzlement in Moldova. Shor owns a controlling stake; the remaining 49% belongs to Russia’s state-owned Promsvyazbank (PSB). In late 2019, PSB officially became the designated bank for Russia’s Defense Ministry and defense industry. Ilan Shor at the Eastern Economic Forum. September 5, 2025 The state development corporation VEB.RF, headed by Igor Shuvalov, “provides support” to A7. Proekt’s journalists suggest that Roman Abramovich may play “an important but secret role in the company.” A source in the cross-border payments business described Abramovich to Proekt as A7’s “protector and sponsor.” In the source’s view, Abramovich began working with Shor because he valued Shor’s ability to “devise financial schemes.” Abramovich’s representatives deny that he is involved in A7. According to Proekt, Shor’s first flight to Russia after a Moldovan court ordered his arrest in absentia was aboard Abramovich’s plane, suggesting that the two knew each other well. Igor Shuvalov, the head of VEB.RF, the state corporation that “provides support” to A7, is a longtime acquaintance of Abramovich’s. In 2024, A7 rented offices in Abramovich’s Belye Sady and Skolkovo Park business centers. Two A7 subsidiaries still occupy offices owned by Abramovich. “Another indication of the oligarch’s involvement is the enormous financial support A7 receives from businessman Viktor Kharitonin, whom the press has long called ‘Abramovich’s protégé,’” Proekt reported. A business partner of Abramovich’s, who spoke to Proekt on condition of anonymity, estimated that A7 handles about 15% of all cross-border transfers in Russia. The company puts its share even higher, at 19%. “No one else even comes close to A7,” a source working in the market told Proekt. The outlet’s other sources agreed that A7 is the largest player in the industry. Proekt obtained a list of all of A7’s clients. They included at least 25 Russian companies already under U.S. and EU sanctions. Five manufacture or supply combat drones used by the Russian army in its war against Ukraine. Other A7 clients include Arkady Rotenberg’s tour operator Biblioglobus, the online marketplace Wildberries, cigarette manufacturer International Tobacco Group, the Sunlight jewelry chain, and industrial companies including Leonid Mikhelson’s natural gas producer Arctic LNG 2, AAEM Turbine Technologies, and S7 Engineering. In late October, journalists from the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists (ICIJ) expanded on Proekt’s investigation. After reviewing internal company documents and speaking with sources, they found that most payments entering A7’s network are funded by hundreds of metric tons of rubles in cash collected from individuals and companies at several Moscow wholesale and retail markets, including the largest, Sadovod. Sadovod is known as a market where most transactions are conducted in cash, and many of its shop employees and owners are migrant workers from countries in the Commonwealth of Independent States. “Sadovod is simply a big client base,” a source familiar with the situation told ICIJ, explaining A7’s choice of location. Sadovod market in summer 2025 How the scheme works Before 2022, intermediaries at Sadovod were already converting cash into ordinary bank transfers or into cryptocurrency, which most often went to China. Western sanctions later disrupted this system by cutting Russian companies off from SWIFT. A7’s improved system allowed a group of brokers at Sadovod to keep operating. They now accept bags of cash brought in by vendors and count the money, according to the documents. A7’s records refer to these initial cash collection points as “departments”; there are at least eight. The brokers then pack the rubles into numbered bags. The bags are loaded into vans along with customers’ payment orders and sent to an A7 payment processing center elsewhere in Moscow. About 50 cashiers work there, recording the cash in A7’s counting system. The cash is then delivered to Promsvyazbank, which places it in a vault and credits A7’s accounts. A7 then uses its shell companies registered abroad. Intermediary companies in Kyrgyzstan buy cryptocurrency through Grinex, a crypto exchange linked to A7. By this point, the money is no longer identified as originating in Russia, thanks to Kyrgyzstan’s permissive policies on cryptocurrency transactions. PSB provides the banking infrastructure for transferring money to Kyrgyzstan, along with loans and guarantees when needed. From Kyrgyzstan, the money goes to intermediary companies linked to A7 in third countries, most often in the Middle East and Southeast Asia. They convert the cryptocurrency into local currencies and send the money to the end recipient. “By the time [an A7 payment] is received, nobody in the chain, from the U.S. clearing bank to the Chinese supplier, knows where it came from,” said illicit finance expert Zachary Tvarozna, who co-authored an investigation into A7 conducted with the British nonprofit Open Source Centre. “Washington essentially created a market for A7 [by restricting legitimate transactions] and then did nothing about it,” he concluded. The risks this scheme poses to the global financial system From November 2024 to July 2025, A7 processed at least 283 metric tons of rubles in cash worth more than $14 billion, ICIJ and Proekt reported. The journalists were unable to trace the cash’s origins, but it is clear that most of it went to China, as before. A registry of A7 promissory notes that leaked online and was reviewed by ICIJ shows that A7’s cash deposits at PSB rose in 2025, reaching 195 billion rubles ($2.3 billion) a month by April and 250 billion rubles ($3.1 billion) in June. At its peak, A7 processed at least 58 metric tons of cash a month. On October 1, 2026, the U.S. Treasury Department designated A7 a “significant transnational criminal organization.” This means U.S. financial institutions will no longer be able to process transfers involving A7’s “Sub-Agents” — foreign shell companies through which the network routes payments for clients in Russia. A7 “uses a modern, multilayered system of controls” and “was established to ensure uninterrupted payments in the Russian market, which has been subjected to unlawful restrictive measures,” the company said in a press release issued after the Treasury Department’s announcement. “All clients are screened to identify risks and prevent us from serving individuals or organizations whose activities violate regulatory requirements,” the company insisted. Just two years earlier, when it launched, A7 presented itself as a “sanctions-proof payment system.” George Voloshin, a financial crime expert at the Association of Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialists, told ICIJ that A7 “not only helps Russia circumvent Western sanctions and export controls” but “is also likely to facilitate cash-based money laundering by effectively legitimizing potential proceeds of crime.” International intermediary banks and beneficiaries effectively become complicit in these activities even though they do not know where the money comes from. The reason lies in the cash itself, Voloshin added: Cash is considered one of the highest-risk payment methods because it is anonymous, can move across borders, and is not tied to a specific person or company. The entire scheme “depends on trusted intermediaries, established relationships and confidence that money will arrive,” said Ilya Shumanov, managing partner of TriTrace Investigations, a Russian company specializing in financial market due diligence. “Its international reach can be extensive, while outsiders have limited visibility into the underlying transactions.” According to documents reviewed by ICIJ, A7 received 314 payment requests totaling $76 million from brokers working at Sadovod in late 2024. All of the money was intended for the Hong Kong export company Yiton Trading Ltd. A7 representatives did not respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. This translation process is the result of extensive testing and refinements to ensure our English-language coverage is timely and accurate. A Meduza editor reviews every draft before publication. title: Armenia, Azerbaijan, and Georgia, top stories this morning
body:
News in Georgia , Armenia , and Azerbaijan . Key headlines and top stories covered by local media, from 26-30 October, 2026
● President Ilham Aliyev will not attend the Organisation of Turkic States summit in Ankara today, despite a personal invitation from Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan. Azerbaijan will be represented by Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov. The official explanation is that Aliyev has a busy schedule, but his absence has attracted attention amid growing tensions between the two countries. The latest dispute was triggered by criticism in Türkiye of Azerbaijan’s effective restrictions on wearing hijabs in schools. Experts, however, also point to Azerbaijan’s close cooperation with Israel as a factor. Baku has accused Turkish politicians and public figures of interfering in its internal affairs, banned 31 Turkish citizens from entering the country and launched criminal proceedings against several others.
● Azerbaijani Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov and his Turkish counterpart Hakan Fidan held a one-to-one meeting on the sidelines of the summit in Ankara. They discussed bilateral relations and regional and international issues. On the same day, Bayramov attended a meeting of the Organisation of Turkic States’ Council of Foreign Ministers, where he spoke about expanding political dialogue, security cooperation, economic and transport links, and joint production of defence equipment.
● Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said he saw no alternative to peace with Azerbaijan and would like to secure it for 400 years. He stressed the need to establish lasting, institutional ties between the two countries.
● Farhad Mammadov of Azerbaijan’s Centre for Analysis of International Relations has criticised Armenian Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan over his remarks that “some statements made by Azerbaijani officials, to put it mildly, do not contribute to peace”. Mammadov said Armenia had no right to tell Azerbaijan what to say or how to speak about the conflict. He also accused Armenia of trying to present the conflict as if it had begun with the 2020 Second Karabakh War, while ignoring the preceding 30 years of Armenian occupation of Azerbaijani territories.
● Azerbaijan has again raised at the UN the issue of more than 4,000 of its citizens who went missing during the First Karabakh War in the early 1990s. Its representative called on the international community to help establish their whereabouts and once again urged Armenia to provide information about possible burial sites, open its archives and hand over any records that could assist the search.
● Azerbaijani Prime Minister Ali Asadov has arrived in Georgia to attend a meeting of the intergovernmental commission on economic cooperation. The agenda includes the economy, trade, transport and energy.
● Azerbaijan has sent Ukraine another shipment of humanitarian aid worth more than $1.47 million to help restore its energy infrastructure. The shipment includes nine power transformers, 186 kilometres of electrical cable and distribution equipment. This is the 159th humanitarian aid shipment from Azerbaijan. Previous deliveries have also included equipment needed to restore electricity supplies disrupted by ongoing Russian attacks on Ukrainian energy facilities.
● Amnesty International has called for the immediate release of researcher and activist Bahruz Samadov. He is serving a 15-year prison sentence on treason charges, with prosecutors alleging that he collaborated with Armenian intelligence services. Samadov denies the charges. According to Amnesty International, he was held in solitary confinement for two months, was denied medication prescribed by a doctor for more than a month, and repeatedly had his requests for medical examinations ignored despite deteriorating eyesight.
● A meeting of the CIS Interstate Council on Antimonopoly Policy was held in Khankendi, Karabakh. Discussions focused on competition issues and cooperation between the anti-monopoly authorities of member states.
● Participants in the Baku World Forum on Intercultural Dialogue visited the Karabakh cities of Shusha and Aghdam. The visit was organised to show them the results of large-scale reconstruction programmes in towns and villages in territories that had been under Armenian occupation for more than 30 years.
