title: 2027: Kebbi pilgrims welfare chair’s donations and electoral act
body: The Chairman of the Kebbi State Pilgrims Welfare Agency, Faruk Enabo, last week donated vehicles, 225 motorcycles and other empowerment items to All Progressives Congress (APC) leaders, political coordinators and support groups across the state. The donations have raised questions about the propriety of a public office holder making substantial contributions to political activities and compliance with the Electoral Act 2026, which sets limits on donations to political candidates. The donation package includes vehicles for coordinators across the state’s 21 local government areas, the three serving senators, eight members of the House of Representatives, the APC state chairman and the party’s Kebbi Central Zonal Vice Chairman. He said the 225 motorcycles were given to APC ward chairmen to improve communication and grassroots political mobilisation. INEC to decide on Pantami, Gwarzo, Adebutu, others October 29 Petrol consumption hits record low amid rising prices Reports on the donations listed 60 saloon cars and two jeeps among the vehicles provided. Based on the supplied market estimates, with each saloon car costing at least N6 million, the 60 cars would be worth no less than N360 million, excluding the jeeps and other items. The 225 motorcycles were estimated to cost at least N337.5 million based on an estimated cost of N1.5 million per motorcycle. The estimated value of the donations by the Kebbi State Pilgrims Welfare Agency chairman has exceeded the N500 million limit set by the Electoral Act for individual contributions to election campaigns. Section 88(8) of the Electoral Act 2026 says an individual or other entity shall not donate to a candidate more than N500,000,000. Section 88(10) provides a penalty for individuals who knowingly exceed the donation limit. It says: “An individual who knowingly acts in contravention of subsection (8) is liable on conviction to a fine of five times the amount donated in excess of the limit placed by the Commission.” Enabo, while presenting the items, dismissed claims that funds belonging to the pilgrims agency or the state government were used to finance the donations. He said the donations were funded through legitimate business activities and personal resources, with support from the governor and other individuals. “I was able to purchase all these vehicles and motorcycles through the support of the governor and other individuals. “Some people have alleged that pilgrims’ funds were used, but I wish to state categorically that the funds belonging to pilgrims remain intact and are properly accounted for,” he said. “I want people to know that no kobo was taken from the pilgrim welfare agency. The proceeds are from my personal income, either through contract or investment. I’m not a poor man,” he added. Giving an account of the agency’s financial operations for the 2027 Hajj, Enabo disclosed that it collected N27.9 billion from intending pilgrims and remitted N25.7 billion to the National Hajj Commission of Nigeria (NAHCON). He said the balance was used to cover pilgrims’ Basic Travelling Allowance and other local Hajj operational expenses. Lawyers, CSO call for probe Lawyers have called for public officials to be held accountable for their actions and urged anti-graft agencies to investigate Enabo’s donations. Kabiru Bala, a lawyer, said the circumstances surrounding money or items given to a political party or candidate should be examined to determine whether they amounted to donations under the law. Bala said the donor’s position as a public office holder also raised questions about the source of the resources used and whether the expenditure was consistent with the person’s declared assets. He called on anti-corruption agencies, including the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) and the Code of Conduct Bureau, to investigate the circumstances surrounding the donations. Another lawyer, Tobechukwu Okoroma, expressed concern about what he described as the ineffective enforcement of laws when politicians are involved, saying public officials do not always appear to be held accountable. According to him, public pressure could help compel public officials to comply with the law. He called for stronger public accountability and a system that ensures the law applies equally, regardless of a person’s social or political status. Victoria Adaji, a lawyer, said the Electoral Act 2026 does not explicitly define in-kind donations or provide a legally binding framework for valuing non-monetary contributions, such as campaign vehicles, billboards, printing equipment and broadcast airtime. According to her, the absence of clear definitions and valuation rules could allow donors to describe high-value campaign support as logistical assistance or temporary equipment loans rather than donations subject to statutory limits. Okechukwu Nwanguma, Executive Director of the Rule of Law and Accountability Advocacy Centre (RULAAC), said the donations raised questions about transparency, campaign financing and the boundary between public office and partisan political interests. “A public officeholder’s political affiliation does not authorise the use of public funds, assets or influence to finance a party,” he said. Nwanguma added that Sections 91, 93 and 94 of the Act also address contributions of assets, their commercial value and financial reporting. “Giving vehicles instead of cash does not remove the need for scrutiny,” he said. He said the authorities needed to establish the independently assessed value of the donated vehicles and motorcycles and which campaigns they were intended to support before determining whether the statutory donation ceiling had been breached. Nwanguma noted that Enabo had reportedly attributed the donations to legitimate business activities and personal resources rather than government or pilgrims’ funds, but said the explanation should be independently verified. He urged the INEC to examine compliance with political financing rules and called on relevant anti-corruption agencies to investigate if evidence raised concerns about the diversion of public resources. He also said the Code of Conduct Bureau should examine any relevant asset-declaration or conflict-of-interest issues. “A large donation alone does not prove corruption. Equally, calling it ‘personal generosity’ does not settle legitimate questions. “Public office demands openness, and the same standards must apply regardless of the party involved,” Nwanguma said.

title: Venezuelan opposition leader María Machado returns after months in exile
body: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado has returned home to a fraught political landscape after more than 10 months in exile. “I am here. With you,” Machado wrote on X on Sunday. Her return comes after repeated attempts to re-enter the country failed. In January, a month after Machado left Venezuela on a speedboat under cover of darkness to accept the Nobel Peace Prize in Norway, the US seized her opponent, President Nicolás Maduro. The Trump administration then backed his deputy, Delcy Rodríguez, as leader, and she was sworn in as interim president, later signing an oil deal that granted the US very favourable terms. Machado was photographed on Sunday attending Mass at a church in the Venezuelan state of Lara, surrounded by supporters hugging her and clasping her hands. She then began travelling to the capital, Caracas, in a caravan of cheering supporters. More supporters lined the route to the capital. She was photographed smiling as she leaned out of a car’s sunroof as she entered Caracas late Sunday night. Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado greets supporters as she arrives in Caracas Her ally, former presidential candidate Edmundo González, confirmed her arrival, writing in a statement: “I am thrilled to announce to you that our leader, my dear María Corina, is on Venezuelan soil.” “Today is a very important day for Venezuelans. Our sovereign voice returns with her to lead and guide this process!” González said. He added that he will soon join Machado in Venezuela to advance the country “toward freedom”. An advisor to Machado said in September that over the previous few weeks Machado had attempted to return to Venezuela seven times, but was denied each time. Reports say the US was involved in delaying her return, but it has denied it. It’s unclear what Machado plans to do next now that she’s back, but she has previously said she would run for president again if an election were held . Her ability to return to her country has always depended on approval from the Trump administration, which it appears has now granted it. A staunch supporter of democracy, Machado won an independent presidential primary election – held outside the Maduro government’s official election authority – in 2023, earning more than 90% of the vote. Despite winning the primary, Maduro’s government barred Machado from running for office, accusing her of fraud and tax violations. Machado denied the allegations, calling them politically motivated. She spent her final days in the country hiding in safe houses before fleeing to Norway to accept the Nobel Prize. In the 2024 election, Machado’s ally González ran in her place against Maduro. The electoral authority, which is closely aligned with the government, declared Maduro the winner without making detailed voting tallies public. The opposition argued that González, not Maduro, won the election, uploading copies of the voting tallies as evidence. Maduro was removed from the country by US forces in January, and is currently jailed in New York where he faces drugs, weapons and torture charges. He has pleaded not guilty. A spokesman for Machado called her return “a major step toward a democratic transition and free, fair, and verifiable presidential elections in the near future”. “We thank President Donald Trump, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, the US Government, Congress, and allied governments for their continued leadership and support,” her spokesperson, David Smolansky, added. Speaking to reporters on Sunday, Trump said, “I don’t know anything about” her return, and added that he hoped she was “safe”. “I think she’s a very nice woman. She gave me her Nobel Prize, so how can I say anything else? And I hope she’s safe,” he said. In January, Machado visited the White House and gifted her Nobel Prize award to Trump . The committee that issues the prize had said: “It cannot be revoked, shared, or transferred to others”. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio praised his country’s role in securing her return through political reconciliation talks. “The conditions allowing for the safe return of Ms Machado to Venezuela are the direct result of the US-supported reconciliation talks, which have already seen hundreds of political prisoners freed, and hundreds of political opposition figures return from exile,” he posted on X. He added: “We expect all political actors to support these talks which represent the best chance Venezuela has had in thirty years to peacefully achieve not just a free and fair election but an enduring democracy.”

title: INEC to decide on Pantami, Gwarzo, Adebutu, others October 29
body: Scores of petitions have flooded the headquarters of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) challenging the omission of names of candidates submitted by some political parties to the commission ahead the 2027 general elections. Sources at the commission which confirmed this to Daily Trust said the issues raised by all the aggrieved candidates would be addressed at its next meeting, scheduled for Thursday, October 29. “There was a kind of a preliminary report, but the final report can only come out after the deadline for receiving petition. “So, our next meeting I know it’s on Thursday because even the chairman is on Zonal tour. Today (Sunday) or tomorrow (Monday) he should be in Gombe and come back on Wednesday. And when they come back on Wednesday, we will have a meeting on Thursday,” he said 2027: Kebbi pilgrims welfare chair’s donations and electoral act Taraba’s bloody market day The sources, who spoke to Daily Trust on condition of anonymity, said the commission had received many petitions before the expiration of the 14-day window allowed for aggrieved political parties and other concerned parties to challenge candidates’ nominations. The window, which elapsed on Saturday, was provided following the publication of the candidates’ particulars by INEC. “Yesterday (Saturday) was the final day for receiving petitions. Up until that time, we were still receiving petitions,” one of the sources said. The petitions include those relating to the omission of the names of the former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Professor Isa Ali Pantami; Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate, Abdulsalam Gwarzo; his counterpart in Kaduna State, Senator Danjuma Laah; Social Democratic Party (SDP) governorship candidate nominee for Benue State, Sebastine Hon; the governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Ogun State, Ladi Adebutu, and others. Another source explained that the commission had received a preliminary report on the petitions but would consider the final report after the deadline for submissions. “It was a kind of preliminary report. But the final report will come after the deadline for receiving petitions,” the source added. Asked how many political parties had filed petitions, the source said he could not provide a definite figure. He said all submissions were directed to the INEC chairman for consideration with advice from the relevant departments. “Of course, all petitions are addressed to the chairman. You need to sit down with them for the advice of the department. As a department, we have been going through all that, and they had a preliminary report,” the source said. On whether the controversy surrounding Pantami’s candidacy would be considered at the next meeting, the source said the commission would examine the petitions in line with the law. “All the cases. It is what the law says. After publication, they have two weeks to petition, whether they think it will be fair or unfair to them,” the source said. The expected meeting comes amid growing attention to the commission’s handling of disputes arising from the publication of candidates’ particulars for the 2027 elections. The source attributed the possible delay in considering the petitions to the ongoing zonal tour by INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, ahead of the 2027 general elections saying the chairman is expected to be in Gombe State this week as part of the tour, a development that could affect the timing of the commission’s next meeting. Efforts to obtain official confirmation from the commission were unsuccessful as of press time as the Deputy Director of Publicity, Wilfred Osilama Ifogah, could not be reached through his direct telephone line and did not respond to a WhatsApp message sent to him. Similarly, the Director of Voter Education and Publicity, Victoria Eta-Messi, said she had only just resumed official duties and did not yet have information on the petitions and could not confirm the number of petitions received or when the commission would consider them. Candidates confirm petitions The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Gombe State confirmed it has submitted a petition over the omission of its governorship candidate, Prof Pantami, from the INEC list for the 2027 elections. The party said it is awaiting INEC’s response to its earlier complaint over Pantami’s exclusion, despite the expiration of the deadline given to the commission to address the matter. The PDP’s Public Relations Officer in Gombe State, Abdulkadir Ahmed Dukku, told Daily Trust that the party had yet to file a fresh petition, insisting that it would first wait for the commission to respond to the complaint already submitted. He said the party remains hopeful that INEC would upload Pantami’s name to the list of governorship candidates, adding that the PDP would determine its next move based on the commission’s decision. According to Dukku, the expiration of the deadline would not immediately prompt the party to take further action, as it was still expecting INEC to address its complaint. The State Chairman of Social Democratic Party (SDP) in Benue State, Idoko Itodo, said that party has done the needful as he expressed optimism that the omission of the party’s candidate, Sabestine Hon on INEC final list might be ‘an error’ which would be corrected. Itodo who spoke to our correspondent in Makurdi on Sunday, explained that the name was in the first list released by INEC as he dismissed the insinuations that the party’s guber candidate may not be part of the forthcoming election. “We have written to INEC. We have done the needful,” he said. Nasarawa State Chairman of the PDP, Joel Daniel Gimba, confirmed that the party has petitioned INEC over the omission of the name of the member representing Lafia North in the Nasarawa State House of Assembly, Esson Mairiga, from its final list of candidates. Gimba described the omission as an error on the part of INEC, noting that the Certified True Copy, CTC, obtained from the commission on September 20th contained Mairiga’s name. By Musa Luka Musa, Abuja; Rabilu Abubakar, Gombe; Abubakar Abdullahi, Lafia; Promise Adagba, Akure; Hope Abah, Makurdi

title: Petrol consumption hits record low amid rising prices
body: Nigerians consumed the lowest amount of petrol in August amidst skyrocketing prices of the product, Daily Trust can report. Analysis of the factsheets released by the Nigerian Midstream showed that the average consumption of 41.6 million litres of petrol consumed in August was 31 percent reduction from the 60.2 million litres consumed in January. While analysis showed consumption wavered from month to month as there is no consistency in the drop, Daily Trust reports that the rising price of petrol has made many Nigerians to jettison their vehicles or stop the use of petrol-fueled generators. Even though the price increase was triggered by the US-Iran war which disrupted fuel supply, most Nigerians have accused the federal government of exposing Nigerians to bear the brunt of the war while other countries have introduced some sort of subsidy to protect their citizens. FCT: Rising transport fares threaten children, teachers’ school attendance INEC to decide on Pantami, Gwarzo, Adebutu, others October 29 A breakdown of the eight months average consumption showed that consumption was highest in January with a daily average of 60.2 million litres consumed. This could be due to the yuletide festivities. Consumption dropped to a daily average of 56.9 million in February and it went down to 47.3 million in March. It however, increased to 51.1 million in April and further dropped to 46.3 million in May. Consumption went back up to 47.4 million in June and it maintained the increase to 48.3 million in July before dropping to 41.6 million in August. PMS supply Ironically, the month of August saw one of the highest daily average PMS supplies into the local market with 50.5 million litres supplied daily. A breakdown showed that 64.9 million litres was supplied daily in January before crashing to 32.5 million in February. It increased to 40.1 million in March and 44.4 million in April and 47.4 in May. It increased significantly to 50.6 million in June but dropped to 45.5 million in July before rising to 50.5 million in August. The report also showed that Dangote supplied 40.1 million litres per day of PMS in January while NNPC and other independent marketers imported 24.8 million. In January, Dangote supply increased to 29.4 million while import dropped to 3m. In March, Dangote’s supply increased to 34.2 million but import increased to 5.9 million. For April, Dangote’s supply was 40.7 million litres while importers supplied 3.7 million. May also saw Dangote’s increase to 41.5 million, importers also increased their supply to 5.9 million. But Dangote reduced its supply to 32.5 in June while importers increased theirs to 18.1 million and the same pattern was followed in July with Dangote reducing supply to 25.8 million while importers increased supply to 19.7 million. August saw Dangote’s supply increased to 35 million while importers reduced supply to 14.6 million. NNPCL’s discount While the government had introduced a N66 per litre discount for Nigerians in October to ease the rising price of the product, most Nigerians have said the discount is inaccessible to everyone and the amount is too little to have an impact on the prices of goods and services. Daily Trust had reported that commercial transport operators across the country have expressed disappointment over the petrol discount at the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) retail outlets, saying the intervention has yet to provide meaningful relief from high operating costs. The transporters said the discount was too small to significantly reduce their operating costs and difficult to access because of the procedures involved. Some also complained that spending time queuing for discounted petrol could reduce their working hours and the number of trips they make daily. Daily Trust reports that on October 8, 2026, the federal government announced a 31-day discount on petrol sold at NNPCL retail outlets, with priority given to public transport operators nationwide. The announcement generated debate over whether the intervention amounted to a return of petrol subsidy, which President Bola Ahmed Tinubu ended on May 29, 2023. The federal government, however, maintained that the discount is not a subsidy. “We are offering a discount on petrol dispensed by NNPC Limited for the next 30 days in the first instance, with priority for public transporters nationwide. It’s not a subsidy; the government is saying we sell to you at a cost,” the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, said while announcing the initiative. However, nearly two weeks after the announcement, commercial transport operators who spoke to Daily Trust said they had yet to feel any significant impact from the initiative.

title: Greek Australian Pilot Makes History on First Western Sydney Airport Flight
body: Aglaya Papadokokolakis was First Officer on Jetstar flight JQ362 to the Gold Coast, which departed shortly before 11.30am on Sunday as the first commercial passenger flight from Western Sydney International Airport (Nancy-Bird Walton). Aglaya Papadokokolakis was First Officer on the first commercial passenger flight from the new Western Sydney International Airport, which departed late for the Gold Coast. The Blacktown-raised Greek Australian described the moment as “such an honour.” The sold-out flight marked the airport’s opening—the first major new passenger airport in Australia in more than 50 years. Aglaya Papadokokolakis / LinkedIn. Located at Badgerys Creek, the 24-hour airport is designed for around 10 million passengers initially, with capacity potentially rising to 82 million by the 2060s. The inaugural flight departed late. title: Stock market extend losses, 55 stocks depreciate; 20 record capital gains
body: By Peter Egwuatu Share prices of 55 companies listed on the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX) depreciated last week following profit taking by the investors. However, 20 stocks appreciated in price during the week under review. The week’s performance highlights the market correction facing the stock market as investors reassess their portfolios following the substantial gains recorded earlier in the year. Although selected stocks attracted buying interest, the recovery was not broad enough to offset losses in influential stocks, leaving the overall market sentiment negative. Analysts emphasised that the decline also came against the backdrop of rising international oil prices, which climbed sharply amid escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. While higher crude prices could support Nigeria’s export earnings and government revenue, their broader implications for domestic fuel costs, inflation and business expenses remain important considerations for investors. A review of the market performance last week showed that the NGX market capitalisation, which represents the total value of stocks, shed over N206 billion to close at N160.519 trillion from N160.725 trillion the previous week. In similar manner, the NGX All Share Index, ASI, close lower to 247,222.27 points from 247539.73 points. Meanwhile, a total turnover of 2.024 billion shares worth N110.773 billion in 173,113 deals was traded last week by investors on the floor of the Exchange, in contrast to a total of 1.659 billion shares valued at N98.088 billion that exchanged hands the previous week in 184,632 deals. The Financial Services Industry (measured by volume) led the activity chart with 1.111 billion shares valued at N53.908 billion traded in 81,787 deals: thus contributing 54.89% and 48.66% to the total equity turnover volume and value respectively. The Consumer Goods Industry followed with 394.039 million shares worth N9.811 billion in 17,912 deals. Third place was the Agriculture Industry, with a turnover of 147.170 million shares worth N2.821 billion in 7,462 deals. Analysing market performance and outlook, analysts at InvestData Consulting Limited, stated: “The near-term outlook for the Nigerian equities market remains cautious as investors balance the need to preserve gains against opportunities in selected stocks. The market’s substantial year-to-date appreciation provides important context for the recent weakness, as some participants may be reducing exposure after the strong returns accumulated earlier in the year. Continued selling pressure in banking, energy and other influential stocks could prolong the market’s consolidation. Further weakness in large capitalised stocks may continue to weigh on the benchmark even if selected equities record positive returns.” Vanguard News The post Stock market extend losses, 55 stocks depreciate; 20 record capital gains appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Lula da Silva wins historic fourth term in Brazil election
body: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio ​Lula da Silva won a historic fourth term on Sunday, the country's electoral court said, in ⁠a shock result that defied polls and global anti-incumbent sentiment to put the brakes on a wave of right-wing ⁠election victories in Latin America. Mr da Silva, a symbol of the global left and the most dominant force in ​Brazilian politics this century, defeated Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the eldest son of former president Jair Bolsonaro. The senator, who led the election's first round but lost in the run-off by more than four million votes, said ⁠he would ask for the result to be annulled owing to a Supreme Court ruling on Sunday that extended voting for two hours. Mr Bolsonaro's refusal to concede has echoes of his father's reaction after losing to Mr da Silva in 2022. Jair Bolsonaro never accepted his loss at the polls and was given a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup to remain in power. The scale of Flavio Bolsonaro's defeat by Mr da Silva – by more than twice his father's ⁠losing margin – and the fact his campaign also asked for an extension because of rain in the south, make any annulment unlikely, analysts said. For Mr da Silva, 80, the victory marks another comeback in a career full of them. He was jailed from 2018 to 2019 after a corruption conviction that was later overturned, paving the way for him to beat Jair Bolsonaro in the 2022 election. He becomes the first candidate since Brazil's return to democracy in the 1980s to ​be elected after finishing second in the first round of a run-off vote. Previously president from 2003 to 2011, he campaigned this year on a potent mix of pragmatism and ‌populism that has shaped his career in national politics for half a century, ⁠introducing reforms aimed at improving the lives of workers and poor Brazilians. They ​gained steam with late-campaign pledges including free nationwide weekend public transport, which has to be formally submitted to Congress, and a 15 per cent increase in his trademark welfare ​programme that is already being put into effect. Mr da Silva ‌also championed a constitutional amendment that became Brazil's biggest labour reform in decades, which passed with wide support in Congress.

title: Gov’t bills face bipartisan scrutiny, not Parliament’s Finance Committee chairman’s orders – Adongo
body: Parliament’s Finance Committee Chairman, Isaac Adongo, says government bills undergo bipartisan scrutiny, with committee members shaping decisions rather than his personal instructions. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express Business Edition, he said the chairman facilitates the committee’s work but cannot dictate its conclusions. “You don’t dictate to the committee what you want,” Mr Adongo said. His comments addressed concerns about whether he could challenge proposals from his own government, including those brought by his friend, Dr Ato Forson. Mr Adongo said the committee’s experience so far gave him no reason to be concerned. “Almost every bill that has come to us has been scrutinised on a bipartisan basis.” He pointed to the opposition members on the committee as evidence of the expertise involved in examining government proposals. They include the ranking member and former Finance Minister, Dr Amin Adam, whom he described as a “very critical and sharp mind”. He also named deputy ranking member Dr Stephen Amoah and Dr Gideon Boako. Mr Adongo said the committee’s responsibility extended beyond its chairman. He explained that its work must take account of the national interest. “Largely we agree on most of the things.” When disagreements arise, he said, they give members on both sides a chance to express their views on what should be done. He cited the bill establishing the Gold Board as an example. According to him, opposition members did not disagree with its principle but were uncomfortable with some provisions. Mr Adongo defended the decision to proceed with the legislation, pointing to what he called the “monumental impact of the gold board”. He nevertheless acknowledged that shortcomings could emerge and that the law could be revisited. “Of course, over time, there will be some lapses that can be identified, and a review is possible at any point in time.” Isaac Adongo expressed confidence that opposition members would support a future review if the executive returned to Parliament with proposals to amend clauses.

title: Gasoline prices get a rollback, diesel prices rise again on October 27
body: MANILA, Philippines – Gasoline prices are set to ease while diesel prices rise for a second straight week starting Tuesday, October 27. The Department of Energy (DOE) announced the following permitted price adjustments for October 27 to November 2: Gasoline – rollback of P0.30 per liter Diesel – increase of to P1.20 per liter Kerosene – rollback of P0.50 per liter Photo from Department of Energy briefing. The adjustments follow last week’s movements , when gasoline prices dropped by P4.30 per liter and kerosene by P1, while diesel increased by P2.60 per liter. The continued diesel price increases come amid tight international supplies, made worse by renewed attacks on Saudi Arabian energy infrastructure and commercial vessels in the Middle East. Escalating hostilities involving Yemen’s Houthis have threatened alternative oil export routes, while tensions around the Strait of Hormuz continue to put pressure on global supplies. Oil prices went up on Friday, October 23, with Brent crude rising 3.14% to $116.72 per barrel, its highest settlement in nearly six months. Local pump prices remain substantially higher than before fighting involving Iran and US-Israeli forces broke out on February 28. In the last full week before the conflict, common Metro Manila prices stood at P56 per liter for RON95 gasoline, P54.70 for RON91, P55 for diesel, and P83.47 for kerosene. The Philippines imports much of its petroleum requirements as finished products, making domestic prices vulnerable to changes in regional fuel markets, freight costs, and foreign exchange rates. Meanwhile, excise taxes on liquefied petroleum gas and kerosene remain suspended under Executive Order No. 125, issued by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. in September. The relief does not cover gasoline or diesel. – Rappler.com

title: Ebola: FG identifies 53 contacts, offers N100,000 weekly support
body: *Says emergency support to cover feeding, accommodation, family upkeep *Patient improves as DG warns against delayed precautions *Rivers suspected case tests negative *Lagos steps up airport surveillance, says no suspected case *Zamfara activates Ebola surveillance after passenger arrives airport with 38°C fever By Chioma Obinna & Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja The federal government has identified 53 contacts linked to Nigeria’s confirmed Ebola case in the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, up from the initial 44, as health authorities intensify efforts to prevent further transmission of the virus. Read Also: Lagos govt on alert, says no Ebola case in state It also announced the approval of an emergency payment of N100,000 per person weekly for individuals placed in isolation or quarantine as part of efforts to contain the Ebola outbreak in the Federal Capital Territory, FCT. This came as Lagos State government weekend intensified Ebola surveillance at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport and strengthened public health preparedness, following the confirmation of an imported case of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease in Abuja,. The Director-General of the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention, NCDC, Dr. Jide Idris, disclosed this at a briefing in Abuja yesterday. The government had initially announced 44 contacts, following the confirmation of the Ebola case in the FCT on October 20, 2026. Idris said the contacts, including healthcare workers, the patient’s spouse, domestic staff and other individuals who might have been exposed to the virus, had been identified, categorised and placed under monitoring. He explained that contact tracing was ongoing and that the number of contacts could change as investigations progressed and more information became available. The NCDC chief maintained that Nigeria had recorded only one confirmed Ebola case, while two additional suspected cases had been investigated. According to him, a suspected case in Rivers State tested negative, while investigations into another suspected case in the FCT were ongoing. He added that no contact had tested positive for the virus and that the FCT remained the only state with a confirmed case. “As of today, we have two suspected cases again. One in FCT, one in Rivers State. But we’ve tested the Rivers case; it’s negative. “So there’s no red line. We have that confirmed case, that’s the patient in the hospital. Contacts with symptoms, none. Contacts positive, none. States affected, only FCT now. Now, that’s the summary,” he said. The NCDC chief said the national incident management system had been activated at the highest level to coordinate the response, involving the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, FCT health authorities, other government agencies and technical partners. He stressed that being identified as a contact did not mean that an individual had contracted the virus, explaining that public health officials needed to monitor such individuals to detect any possible infection early. “Being identified as a contact does not mean that you have Ebola. It means that public health teams need to assess and monitor your health so that any possible infection can be identified early,” he said. He urged Nigerians contacted by public health officials to cooperate fully and provide accurate information about their movements, contacts and any symptoms they might have experienced. Samples collected On laboratory investigations, Idris said samples collected from the confirmed patient on three occasions had remained positive, while a sample taken from her husband tested negative. He added that genetic sequencing had been completed by two laboratory facilities to establish the genetic characteristics of the virus, with the findings being used to facilitate information-sharing with Ugandan health authorities. The NCDC chief said the agency had also strengthened the country’s laboratory capacity, with between nine and 12 public and private laboratories equipped to test for Ebola. He explained that testing for the confirmed case was being conducted at the National Reference Laboratory (NRL), adding that additional reagents and supplies had been positioned across the national laboratory network to improve preparedness. On clinical management, Idris said the confirmed patient was receiving treatment at an isolation facility, while arrangements had been made to accommodate additional cases if necessary. He disclosed that isolation and quarantine arrangements had also been established for contacts requiring closer monitoring. According to him, the agency was providing accommodation and feeding for contacts placed in isolation or quarantine, alongside temporary financial assistance to help them cater for their families during the monitoring period. He said the government had approved emergency payments of N100,000 per person weekly for contacts in isolation or quarantine. “Just to douse the tension, we decided we would do this. We provide N100,000 per person per week just to maintain their comfort and feeding because they were complaining,” he said. The NCDC chief further disclosed that the government had strengthened screening at the country’s international airports, with aviation authorities, immigration, customs and other relevant agencies working together to improve preparedness. He said passenger screening measures had also been expanded following the confirmation of the case, with health declaration forms required for passengers travelling into Nigeria from all countries. Idris called on public and private healthcare facilities to strengthen infection prevention and control measures, including patient screening, triage, hand hygiene, environmental cleaning, safe injection practices and proper medical waste management. He urged healthcare workers to maintain a high index of suspicion when attending to patients with symptoms consistent with Ebola, particularly those with relevant exposure histories. “Healthcare workers should not wait for laboratory confirmation before taking appropriate precautions. Protecting healthcare workers is essential to protecting the communities we serve,” he said.He also advised Nigerians to practise regular hand hygiene, avoid direct contact with the bodily fluids of suspected cases and promptly report possible exposure to public health authorities. If you have symptoms… According to him, anyone who develops symptoms following possible exposure should immediately contact public health officials and follow their instructions before visiting a healthcare facility. Idris assured Nigerians that the response would continue to be guided by evidence, with surveillance, contact tracing, laboratory testing and preparedness activities reviewed as new information became available. He urged the public to remain calm, cooperate with health officials and avoid spreading unverified information as the government intensifies efforts to prevent further transmission of the virus. Lagos steps up airport surveillance, says no suspected case Meanwhile, Lagos State government has intensified Ebola surveillance at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport and strengthened public health preparedness, following the confirmation of an imported case of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease in Abuja. The government, which also assured residents that no suspected case had been reported in the state, urged them not to panic but remain vigilant, promptly report possible exposure and seek medical assessment if they developed symptoms, particularly after travelling from areas reporting Ebola transmission. The Commissioner for Health, Prof. Akin Abayomi, disclosed this in a statement issued by the Lagos State Ministry of Health, saying the state was strengthening surveillance, risk communication and coordination with relevant agencies to ensure early detection and a rapid response to potential cases. According to the statement, the ministry, through its Directorate of Epidemiology, Biosecurity and Global Health, has conducted a strategic engagement and assessment at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport with airport management, Port Health Services and other aviation and public health stakeholders. The engagement focused on passenger screening, information sharing, infection prevention and control, and coordination of emergency response measures. The statement read: “Lagos State is ready to prevent, detect and respond to potential public health threats.” It added that the government was intensifying public enlightenment on Ebola symptoms, transmission and prevention, while urging residents to rely on verified information rather than rumours. “Ebola Virus Disease is a severe illness that can be fatal. It spreads primarily through direct contact with the blood and other body fluids of an infected person showing symptoms, contaminated materials, or the bodies of people who have died from the disease. Infection may also occur through contact with infected animals.” The ministry listed symptoms to watch for as fever, severe weakness, headache, muscle pain, sore throat, vomiting, diarrhoea and abdominal pain. Unexplained bleeding or bruising may occur in some cases. “Symptoms may develop between two and 21 days after exposure, the statement said, warning that early signs could resemble malaria and other common illnesses.” Abayomi advised residents who develop fever to undergo a malaria rapid diagnostic test before taking antimalarial medicines, in line with the state’s fever-management policy. Where the test is negative, a healthcare professional should assess other possible causes and determine appropriate treatment. The government also urged travellers arriving from areas reporting Ebola transmission to cooperate with Port Health Services, provide accurate travel and health information when requested, and comply with applicable public health guidance. “Anyone who develops symptoms during travel or after arrival should notify appropriate health personnel and seek guidance before visiting a healthcare facility. The statement advised anyone who suspects exposure, particularly following contact with a suspected or confirmed case, to contact public health authorities promptly before visiting a healthcare facility. Residents were urged to report suspected cases or relevant exposure concerns through the state’s emergency numbers, 112 or 767, or contact the Directorate of Epidemiology, Biosecurity and Global Health on 0802 316 9485. The government said it would continue to monitor developments, strengthen surveillance and response readiness, and provide verified updates as necessary. It stressed that early detection and prompt reporting were critical to preventing the spread of the disease. Zamfara passenger Zamfara activates Ebola surveillance after passenger arrives airport with 38°C fever Similarly, Zamfara State government has activated Ebola surveillance at Gusau airport and major motor parks after a passenger arriving from Saudi Arabia was found with a body temperature of 38 degrees celsius. The Commissioner for Health, Nafisa Maradun, disclosed this weekend while leading a medical team to flag off passenger screening at the airport. Maradun said the passenger, an indigene of Zamfara, was identified during screening and referred for further medical assessment. The state government has deployed medical personnel at the airport, motor parks and other entry points to screen travellers and support the early detection of suspected cases. Maradun said the surveillance measures were intended to prevent the virus from spreading to Zamfara, and urged residents to remain calm and cooperate with health officials. The state’s ministry of health also directed public and private health facilities, disease surveillance officers and local government health authorities to strengthen preparedness, improve screening and promptly report suspected cases. The government said it was working with relevant agencies, including the Nigeria Customs Service, NCS, and Nigeria Immigration Service, NIS, to strengthen surveillance at entry points. Transport workers are also expected to help identify and report passengers who may require medical assessment. title: Serbia's leader concedes defeat after 12 years in power
body: Serbia's long-time leader Aleksandar Vucic has conceded defeat in a snap election, handing victory to a student-led movement that built mass support by pledging to fight against graft and reverse democratic backsliding. The Student List won more than two million votes in the Balkan country of 6.5 million people, Mr Vucic told his supporters in Belgrade, about 90 minutes after the polls closed on Sunday. That result would give the movement a simple majority in the 250-seat parliament. The outcome marks an astonishing fall from grace for Mr Vucic, who dominated politics in the country for more than a decade, Bloomberg reported. During that time, he skilfully balanced competing interests of remaining friendly with Russia, China and the US administration of President Donald Trump, while pushing join the EU. But it was a grassroots protest movement sparked by outrage over a deadly construction disaster that became his undoing. By resigning as president and calling the election, Mr Vucic hoped to return as prime minister. But that plan, which borrowed a page from Russian President Vladimir Putin’s playbook, backfired amid voter turnout of 69 per cent – the highest in 33 years. The nation's political spectrum is now to be redrawn. Reviews are to be held into deals and policies. The Student List reacted with chants of “Vucic is gone” after the announcement, but what comes next is less clear. The movement does not have a single leader and does not have supporters with extensive experience in government. “This is the victory of the conviction that Serbia can and will do better,” said Radomir Saicic, one of the movement’s leaders. “We call on all citizens to act peacefully and in dignified manner. We didn’t fight for months to lose it today.” Political overhaul Mr Vucic, 56, is the second long-time leader to lose power in eastern Europe this year. His ally, Viktor Orban of Hungary, was toppled six months ago. Mr Vucic told his supporters that the Student List won the ballot with the “direct support from some European countries and the American deep state, the one that is also against President Trump.” He called the movement “just contractors doing some very dirty work”, without providing evidence for his claims. While he conceded defeat, Mr Vucic pledged to make a comeback, saying: “I’ll defeat them much sooner than they think.” But his departure from power marks a tectonic shift for Serbia. The parliament will now effectively have only two sizeable political blocs, removing an array of once mainstream groups from liberals to conservatives and nationalists. The Socialists, once led by late strongman Slobodan Milosevic, are also out for the first time in 18 years. Mr Vucic called the election more than a year ahead of schedule, after unrelenting anti-government rallies sparked by the collapse of a train station canopy that killed 16 people in 2024. Students led the protests, blaming the corruption and incompetence of ruling officials for the deaths. While Mr Vucic is now gone, his geopolitical balancing act may continue. Before the vote, the movement’s representatives were cautious on sensitive issues such as Serbia’s rejection of Kosovo’s unilateral secession, or on adopting sanctions against Russia. The opposition, which gained traction for the first time in more than a decade, pledged to focus on fighting against corruption, overhauling the judiciary, improving election conditions and boosting media diversity. Meeting EU membership conditions is not an immediate priority either. Student List representatives have said the country can decide on that in a referendum. No clear leader European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen welcomed the change of power in a post on X on Sunday. The EU is “ready to support reforms", she added. The movement's representatives pledged to break up monopolies and review large infrastructure contracts signed under Mr Vucic. Those include the $2.4 billion Expo 2027 that Vucic has touted as his legacy project. In Transparency International’s Corruption Perceptions Index 2025 , Serbia’s score ⁠was the lowest in two decades. The Student List has operated through a patchwork of “plenums”, or cells, without a distinct leader and has not yet announced its candidate for prime minister. On election night, the movement was late with a victory speech as its representatives could not decide who would speak on their behalf. “The Student List will have a very hard job organising the transfer of power, which Vucic will probably try to boycott,” said Zarko Puhovski, an independent political analyst from Croatia. “Their list is dominated by people with little political or government experience.”

title: Bolsonaro refuses to concede as would-be Ukraine peace mediator Lula wins Brazil election
body:
Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won reelection on Oct. 25, securing a fourth, nonconsecutive term in office, as his opponent, right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, refused to concede defeat and vowed to challenge the election results.
The election ended with Lula receiving 51.79% of votes compared with Bolsonaro's 48.21%, according to Brazil's electoral authorities.
Bolsonaro said he would seek to annul the election, calling a decision by Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin to extend voting by two hours "unacceptable." The extension was introduced following transportation disruptions and severe weather that affected voting in parts of the country, according to the Associated Press. The electoral court has recognized Lula's victory, and Bolsonaro's refusal to concede does not invalidate the result. Lula had expressed the view in 2024 that Brazil should remain neutral and not interfere in Russia's war against Ukraine, but in the years that followed had been engaging in diplomacy, including efforts to position Brazil as a potential mediator between Kyiv and Moscow.
In June of this year, President Volodymyr Zelensky accepted Lula's offer to assist efforts to negotiate an end to the war, Ukrainian presidential communications adviser Dmytro Lytvyn said , according to Reuters.
The leaders held a bilateral meeting on during the G7 summit in France on June 17, discussing ways to revive stalled diplomatic negotiations, including potential outreach to permanent members of the United Nations Security Council.
While Ukraine maintains close diplomatic ties with three of the five permanent members — France, the United Kingdom and the United States — Brazil has maintained diplomatic relations with Russia and China.
Lula spoke with Russian President Vladimir Putin by telephone in August, discussing the war in Ukraine and bilateral relations, CNN Brasil reported.
Brazil has maintained diplomatic and economic ties with Russia since the beginning of the full-scale invasion in February 2022, opting out of Western sanctions and expressing a wish to have a role in a negotiated settlement to the war.
Lula has also rejected suggestions that Brazil supports Russia's invasion, saying in an April interview that his government has never recognized Moscow's right to occupy Ukrainian territory.
The Brazilian president's victory comes after a closely fought campaign against Bolsonaro, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a prison sentence for his role in an attempted coup following his 2022 election defeat. The elder Bolsonaro also refused to concede defeat after losing to Lula in 2022. He was subsequently convicted for his role in a plot to overturn that election.
The victory makes Lula, 80, the first Brazilian president to win four terms and the first candidate since the country's return to democracy to win a presidential runoff after finishing second in the opening round.
While Bolsonaro refused to concede and asked for the vote to be annulled, election officials have expressed "absolute" confidence in the proceedings and the result, as reported by Reuters.

title: Death toll in Taraba bandits’ attack now 50
body: The death toll from an attack by gunmen in Taraba State has risen to at least 50, survivors and Amnesty International told AFP Sunday, after more bodies were discovered. Read Also: ‘We counted over 20 bodies after attackers left’ – Taraba massacre survivors Both police and Amnesty said some of the victims had drowned while trying to flee the attackers. Gunmen on motorcycles from a suspected “bandit” gang swarmed Binnari, in eastern Taraba, killing dozens of people shortly after Friday prayers. They also looted and burned stores. Taraba is sandwiched between northeastern Nigeria, which has a long-running jihadist insurgency, and the volatile central region, which faces criminal gangs known as bandits. Driven by money rather than ideology, the bandits in Nigeria target poorly policed rural areas, kidnapping for ransom and killing. “On Friday, we found seven bodies after the bandits attacked our community,” said Bashir Mamuda Musa, a resident of Binnari, in Taraba state. “The following day, Saturday, we discovered another 43 bodies in the river, bringing the total to 50,” he added. The new toll was confirmed by resident Abdullahi Zakari. “Many residents, including women and children, fled towards the river in an attempt to escape the gunmen,” Zakari told AFP. “Unfortunately, several people drowned while trying to flee the attack.” ‘Chased into river’ Bodies can often be difficult to recover when communities scatter. Some were discovered in a nearby river, according to both police and Amnesty. Police spokesman for the state Victor Msheliza told AFP on Sunday that they were still searching the area. Officers “found some (bodies) in the river” of people who were trying to escape, he said. Police were immediately deployed to the area after the attack, more deployments being sent, he said. Amnesty International gave a toll of 52 on Sunday, saying the attackers had come “in large numbers and set ablaze shops and market stalls”. “The bandits invaded in large numbers,… chased people and they headed toward the river to escape,” and drowned, Amnesty International Nigeria director Isa Sanusi told AFP. “Some were chased into the river by the gunmen”. Banditry has become a growing problem in northwest and central Nigeria, with powerful gangs battling overstretched police and military across hard-to-reach, rural locations. They raid villages and impose “taxes” on farmers and mining operations in areas with little state presence. Amnesty, in a post on X, blamed the Nigerian authorities for leaving some rural communities “at the mercy of gunmen that repeatedly commit atrocities with impunity. “Consistent failure of the authorities to bring the suspected perpetrators to justice is clearly emboldening impunity,” the rights group said on social media.
