title: Despite Cut in MPR, Average Maximum Lending Rate Rises to 32.62%
body: Kayode Tokede Despite the reduction of the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) to 23 per cent by the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) in its last meeting, the banking sector’s average maximum lending rate increased to 32.62 per cent in September 2026 from 29.20 per cent in August 2026. Maximum lending rate refers to the highest permissible interest rate that lenders can charge borrowers. The rate is crucial for ensuring fair lending practices and protecting borrowers from excessive interest rates. According to the CBN Money Market Indicators, the average maximum lending had opened January 2026 at 32.68 per cent when MPR was at 27 per cent, and reached a peak of 35.17 per cent in March 2026 as MPR stood at 26.50 per cent. An investigation by THISDAY revealed that most Nigerian banks’ maximum lending rate remained flat between September and October 9, 2026 amid the 350 basis points MPR cut by MPC. Specifically, between September 4, 2026 and October 9, 2026, “Manufacturing sector” maximum lending rates of Access Bank, Alpha Morgan Merchant Bank, Coronation Merchant Bank and Ecobank remained flat at 32.28 per cent, 35.00 per cent, and 35 per cent respectively. FCMB Bank, Fidelity Bank Plc, First Bank of Nigeria also posted 41.40 per cent, 36 per cent and 36 per cent, respectively between September 4, 2026 and October 9, 2026… In the period under review, Citi Bank saw its Manufacturing sector maximum lending rate drop to 19 per cent from 20 per cent, while Quest Merchant Bank Manufacturing sector maximum lending rate moved to 30 per cent from 35 per cent. In June 2026, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) had expressed that Nigerian banks are quick to raise lending rates when the CBN tightens monetary policy, but slow to reduce borrowing costs when rates are eased. The Washington-based institution said the country’s monetary policy transmission mechanism has strengthened since the unification of the foreign exchange (FX) market in June 2023, although distortions within the banking system still persist. According to the IMF, interest rate transmission in Nigeria follows what economists describe as a ‘rockets-and-feathers’ pattern, where banks rapidly increase lending rates during tightening cycles but are reluctant to reduce them when policy conditions soften. The report stated that a 100 basis-point increase in the MPR typically pushes treasury bill and lending rates up by about 175 to 180 basis points almost immediately. However, a similar rate cut results in only a 25 to 30 basis-point decline in borrowing costs. “This asymmetry — statistically significant — implies that banks transmit tightening rapidly and even amplify it but adjust much more slowly during easing cycles,” the IMF said. The institution noted that interbank rates respond more evenly to both tightening and easing, while deposit rates remain largely unresponsive in either direction. The IMF attributed the weak response in deposit rates to limited competition among banks for customer deposits and the existence of what it described as ‘captive depositors’ with limited investment alternatives. CBN data revealed that the average prime lending rate also rose to .19.04 per cent in September 2026 from 17.86per cent in August 2026. In January 2026, the average prime lending rate was at 19.54 per cent, making it the highest so far since 2006. The prime lending rate indicates the possible rate offered to the most creditworthy customers by Nigerian banks. Nigeria’s average prime lending rate reached an all-time high of 19.66 per cent in November 2009 and a record low of 11.13per cent in March 2021. The steady increase in interest rate reflected in the average prime lending rate last year as the CBN intensified its effort to tackle inflation rate and stabilize the local currency at the foreign exchange market. Reacting, Investment Banker & Stockbroker, Tajudeen Olayinka stated that Nigerian banks are not compelling to adjusted lending rate to MPR, but to use it as a guide to pricing and repricing loans and advances, plus other financial instruments, in a manner that gives credence to risk/return framework associated with different loan applicants. “You’ll recall MPR was adjusted to 23per cent, to make it aligned with what the market is asking for. Only prime borrowers will receive an interest rate that is close to MPR or risk-free rate. It is also a function of demand and supply,” he said. Also, the Vice President, Highcap Securities, David Adonri stated that the increase in lending rate in the Nigerian banking sector means there was tight money supply in the credit market in September 2026 despite massive cuts in MPR. Cordros Research in a report stated that it expected the market performance to be shaped by the extent to which the policy adjustment translates into lower market yields, improved liquidity and reduced corporate financing costs. “Continued macroeconomic stability, particularly in inflation and the exchange rate, will also remain important to investor sentiment. Against this backdrop, 2026FY earnings and dividend announcements, foreign and domestic portfolio flows, corporate actions and company-specific developments are likely to be the key drivers of the market performance in Q4-2026,” the firm had explained. However, analysts have predicted a further increase in the average maximum lending and primer lending rate amid steady ease in inflation figures.

title: Parliament’s Finance Committee has had no reason to worry over government bills – Adongo
body: Parliament’s Finance Committee Chairman, Isaac Adongo, says the committee has had no reason to worry about government bills brought before it, citing bipartisan scrutiny and broad agreement among members. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express Business Edition, he said the chairman does not dictate the committee’s decisions. “The good thing is that we have not had any reason to be worried. The reason is that almost every bill that has come to us has been scrutinised on a bipartisan basis.” His comments followed a question about whether he could confront his good friend, Finance Minister Dr Ato Forson and reject proposals that went beyond what Parliament had approved. Mr Adongo said scrutiny depended on the whole committee. He pointed to the experience of opposition members, including Ranking Member and former Finance Minister Dr Amin Adam, Deputy Ranking Member Dr Stephen Amoah, and Dr Gideon Boako. “So it is not about the chairman of the Finance Committee. It is the work of that committee taking into account the interests of the nation, and very often all those that have come to us, we have not had reason to disagree as a committee.” He said disagreements gave members on both sides an opportunity to express their views, although the committee largely agreed on proposals. Mr Adongo cited the bill that established the Gold Board as an example. He said opposition members had concerns about some provisions but did not oppose its underlying principle. “The passage of the bill that led to the establishment of the Gold Board, for instance, from a political perspective, our colleagues do not disagree in principle, but their side of the divide was not comfortable with certain provisions.” He defended the decision to pass the legislation and credited the Gold Board with what he described as a monumental impact. But he acknowledged that shortcomings could emerge and require changes. “Of course, over time, there will be some lapses that can be identified, and a review is possible at any point in time.” Isaac Adongo said he believed opposition members would support a review if the executive returned to Parliament seeking changes to particular clauses.

title: Biff 2.0.4: LLM Skills
body:
I've just released Biff v2.0.4 . This release has a hodge-podge of tweaks and fixes based on my own usage . There is also one big addition: a set of LLM skills. From the starter project's README:
After upgrading your biff.tasks dependency to 2.0.4 , these skills will be synced to your local project whenever you run clj -M:run dev .
The most important skill here is biff-code-review . It contains a list of rules for writing code that conforms to Biff conventions. The rules are the result of my own painstaking review of reams of crappy LLM-generated Biff code. From testing them out on a fresh project, I'm fairly pleased with the result. The code I've gotten is definitely still a little weird in places, but it's crossed the "good enough" threshold.
My general flow for making Biff apps is now:
Sometimes I'll use a fancy model to review specs/code and a dumber model to do the implementation.
I had some trouble figuring out a structure for getting LLMs to actually follow my rules. I've had success with this flow:
I try to phrase each rule so it's very explicit/unambiguous/black and white. Either the rule is violated or it's not.
biff-code-review instructs the LLM to copy a checklist for all the rules into your project. The LLM goes through your code and adds a bullet point (with filename and line numbers) to the checklist file whenever it finds a violation. After the code review, any checklist items without violations are checked off.
The LLM then goes through the checklist and applies fixes.
I structured this in a way so that if needed you can do a human-in-the-loop thing: you can edit the checklist before step 3 starts to add any violations the LLM may have missed. During step 3, the LLM doesn't edit the checklist file, so you can manually mark off/not mark off items and then redo step 3.

title: KPMG: Economic Uncertainty, AI Readiness Will Shape Next Phase of African Investment
body: Emma Okonji African business leaders remain confident about growth, but converting that confidence into sustained performance will depend on how effectively organisations navigate economic uncertainty, geopolitical disruption, technological change and structural constraints, according to the 2026 KPMG Africa CEO Outlook. The Outlook examined the priorities shaping business leadership across the continent, from investment and growth expectations to emerging risks, Artificial Intelligence (AI), talent and sustainability. According to the report, while 66 per cent of African CEOs are confident in the global economy, broadly in line with the global benchmark of 65 per cent, confidence in their domestic economies stood at 72 per cent. A further 79 per cent are confident in the growth prospects of their own organisations. The confidence is supported by recent performance, with 86 per cent of African CEOs reporting revenue growth in their latest financial year. However, only 58 per cent expect annual earnings growth of at least 2.5 per cent over the next three years, compared with 68 per cent globally, suggesting that translating revenue gains into sustained profitability remains a priority. According to the findings, cybersecurity and data security, alongside supply-chain resilience, are the leading threats to growth among African CEOs, each cited by 31 per cent of respondents. According to the KPMG Outlook, about 45 per cent of African CEOs are increasing investment in cybersecurity and digital-risk resilience, 36 per cent in regulatory compliance and reporting, and 31 per cent in AI integration. The findings suggested that resilience was no longer simply about protecting organisations against disruption. It is increasingly a condition for growth, enabling businesses to adapt to changing market conditions, protect critical operations and make investment decisions with greater confidence. For businesses operating across diverse African markets, this requires balancing immediate operational pressures with longer-term investment in infrastructure, technology, governance and capabilities, the outlook said. Giving details about the outlook, Senior Partner & CEO at KPMG One Africa, Tola Adeyemi, said: “African businesses are demonstrating confidence in their ability to grow, but the next phase of growth will require more than ambition. Leaders must make deliberate choices about where to invest, how to strengthen resilience and how to build organisations that can adapt to disruption. The opportunity is to translate the continent’s resources, markets and entrepreneurial capacity into more productive, competitive and sustainable businesses.” On sustainability shifts towards measurable business value, the report explained that African CEOs were increasingly approaching sustainability through the lens of commercial performance, operational resilience and reporting readiness. According to the outlook, almost half, or 48 per cent, report embedding sustainability more deeply into core business strategy, compared with 63 per cent globally, adding that 40 per cent are narrowing their focus to sustainability issues most critical to business performance, against 21 per cent globally. Taken together, the findings presented a picture of African business leaders who remain optimistic but face increasingly complex decisions about where and how to invest. “Economic and geopolitical uncertainty is reinforcing the importance of resilience, while AI adoption, skills development and sustainability are placing new demands on organisational capabilities. For Africa, the challenge extends beyond individual business performance. Converting the continent’s resources, demographic potential and expanding markets into sustained growth will require investment in infrastructure, local value chains, skills and competitive business environments,” the report further said.

title: Taraba’s bloody market day
body: An attack launched by gunmen suspected to be bandits on Binnari town in Karim-Lamdo Local Government Area of Taraba State has reportedly claimed the lives of over 50 persons, including women and children. Daily Trust gathered that 51 people were buried on Saturday and the body of one person was recovered on Sunday, bringing the number of those who died in the attacks to 52. Several other persons, including a six-month-old baby, Adamu Rayyanu, sustained gunshot wounds. Amnesty International Nigeria also noted that 40 people were killed in the attack, which occurred on Friday and that additional bodies were being discovered. But the Police Public Relations Officer, Taraba State Command, ASP Victor Mshelizah, said only 10 people were killed. INEC to decide on Pantami, Gwarzo, Adebutu, others October 29 Abuja hotel manager dies during fight with tiler It was learnt that several others are still missing as the search for more bodies inside the bush and Binnari River continues. Jibri Dabo, a boat operator in Binnari, told Daily Trust that he led the team of local divers inside the river, where they recovered 41 bodies inside the water. He said when the bandits invaded the town shortly after Jumm’at prayers, people started running in different directions. According to him, most people drowned inside the river while escaping from the attack. He explained that most of those who drowned were people who attended the market from Gombe, Bauchi and Plateau states and could not swim. Dabo said other victims were from Jigawa and Yobe states who came to work in rice farms, adding that a team comprising mostly young divers from the community recovered the bodies. He said some of the bandits observed the Friday prayer with the residents of the town and started firing shots afterwards. “Shortly after the Friday prayers at about 3pm, bandits entered the town and opened fire in different directions and everybody started running. There was total confusion in the town. Everybody was running and unfortunately many of the residents who were taken unaware by attackers ran into the bandits while others ran into the river where they drowned,” Dabo said. He also revealed that the bandits operated for close to three hours, killing and looting shops unhindered. According to him, the police came to the town around 9am on Saturday, while soldiers arrived in the evening. Amnesty International, in a statement, described the attack as “utter disdain for the sanctity of life,” calling for an impartial investigation and justice for the victims. “The community is now littered with dead bodies, some burnt beyond recognition, as families declare many still missing. The Nigerian authorities continue to leave rural communities in some parts of the north at the mercy of gunmen who repeatedly commit atrocities with impunity. “On the side of the authorities, issuing bland statements condemning these horrific attacks is not enough. Genuine commitment to protecting the people must be demonstrated by ensuring adequate security of lives and property, as well as ensuring justice for the victims. Consistent failure of the authorities to bring the suspected perpetrators to justice is clearly emboldening impunity,” the organisation said. Some of the displaced residents waiting to relocate to neighbouring villages Victims, locals recount ordeal Adama Rayyanu, mother of a six-month-old baby boy who was shot in the foot, told Daily Trust that she was running to enter a boat with the baby cradled in her arms, but the bandits pursued her and other people to the river. She said as she entered the boat, her baby was shot in the foot but did not die, while many others fell into the river and died. Adama explained that her husband escaped, and she left three of her children behind and took them to a nearby village. Alhaji Saidu Ali, who narrowly escaped, said he ran for almost one hour in the forest. “I was running away from the market where I displayed my wares; unknown to me, it was the other traders who were running behind me. I thought it was the bandits that were pursuing me. I kept running until I got tired,” Ali said. He explained that he passed the night inside the forest and when he came back to the market, his wares and money had gone. Owner of a private clinic in Nahuta village, Adams James, told Daily Trust that 15 victims were brought to his clinic with gunshots for treatment, adding that those with serious wounds were referred to hospitals in Mutumbiyu and Jalingo. Bello Lawal, another resident, said the Friday attack was the third in two years, but the latest one was deadlier because of the casualty figure. “Fifty-two people were buried on Saturday and there are still many people who are missing, while many others could be either inside the river or in the forest. The search for the missing persons is ongoing,” he said. He said it is very difficult to give the exact number of people who died because most of the deceased were strangers who came for the market, while others were labourers from different states working on farms in Binnari. Alhaji Tanko Andami, a community leader, told one of our correspondents that the gunmen looted shops and carted away motorcycles as well as provisions including cash and foodstuffs. Another resident, Yahuza Binnari, who escaped into the nearby village, said the attackers in their numbers blocked the entrance to the town while some went straight into the market, shooting sporadically. A trader, Alhaji Abubakar Binnari, lamented that traders lost almost all their goods because the bandits looted the shops in the town. Gov demands action from security agencies Meanwhile, Taraba State Governor, Agbu Kefas, has ordered all relevant security agencies to take urgent steps to restore calm, protect lives and property, and bring the perpetrators to justice. Kefas, in a statement by his Senior Special Assistant on Media and Digital Communication, Mr Emmanuel Bello, stressed that no effort must be spared in apprehending the perpetrators. He maintained that everyone involved must be held accountable in accordance with the law. He pledged his administration’s commitment to addressing insecurity and restoring lasting peace in Karim Lamido, adding that efforts were being made to facilitate the safe return of displaced persons to their communities. “As part of the broader peacebuilding efforts, the governor recently approved N1 billion for the Taraba State Bureau for Peace and Conflict Management to address the aftermath of previous crises and support initiatives aimed at restoring tranquillity in Karim Lamido,” the governor said. He condoled with the families of those killed and urged residents to remain calm and cooperate with security agencies as they work to restore normalcy. Also, Senator representing Taraba North, Shuaibu Isa Lau, condemned the attack and called on security agents to protect the lives and property of the citizens. He also called for the immediate resettlement of the displaced victims and provision of relief materials to them. Meanwhile, the Taraba State Emergency Management Agency (TSEMA) says it is conducting an on-the-spot assessment in the affected community and providing emergency humanitarian assistance to displaced and affected families. The assessment and distribution team was led by the Executive Secretary of TSEMA, Dr. Audu Echuseh, alongside critical stakeholders from Karim Lamido, including members representing Karim Lamido Constituencies at the Taraba State House of Assembly, Hon. Anas Shuaibu Didango and Hon. Abner Shittu, the Vice Chairman of Karim Lamido Local Government Council, Alhaji Uba Munyarda, traditional leaders and other community stakeholders, who jointly participated in the exercise. The relief items delivered include foodstuffs, mattresses, blankets, and other essential non-food items to cushion the hardship of victims who lost their homes and means of livelihood. Poor surveillance, difficult terrain blamed for attack A security analyst, Dr Kabiru Adamu, has blamed poor intelligence sharing, inadequate forest surveillance and weak coordination among neighbouring states for the recent deadly attacks in Taraba State. Adamu, the chairman of Abuja-based Beacon Security Consulting Firm, in a chat with Daily Trust last night, said although Taraba had experienced banditry and communal clashes in the past, gaps in security coordination had allowed armed groups to move across state boundaries and attack communities. He also identified longstanding inter-community conflicts and incursions by Ambazonian fighters from Cameroon as part of the state’s security challenges. Speaking specifically about Karim Lamido, a border local government area, Adamu said its location made it vulnerable to attacks by armed groups moving from neighbouring states. “From time to time, we see incursions from these states. In this current one, the theory is that the incursion is from Plateau State,” he said. He said the attackers might have travelled through the Kambari Forest, possibly towards the Ankari Forest, noting that the forest corridors could provide access to Sambisa Forest and other parts of northern Nigeria. Adamu said the existence of poorly governed spaces and the inability of neighbouring states to coordinate surveillance had made it difficult to track the movement of armed groups. He also faulted the absence of effective community-based early warning systems, saying the attack occurred on a market day and there might have been warning signs before the violence. “If the communities had had early warning systems where they can report, and then there were early response systems too from the government and security agencies, maybe we would not be talking of these unfortunate numbers,” he added. The analyst attributed the escalation partly to the movement of criminal groups fleeing sustained security operations in other states. “Anytime there is sustained security operation in another state, what these criminal, violent actors do is they run away from that state,” he said, explaining that the groups could later emerge from forest hideouts to replenish supplies in areas with limited security presence. To prevent further attacks, Adamu called for a coordinated security framework involving Taraba, Bauchi and Gombe states, alongside the other states in the North-East. He proposed a coordination centre to direct joint security operations and a regional intelligence fusion centre to collate information and transmit actionable intelligence to the military and police. He also urged states without forest guards to adopt the federal government’s initiative, alongside deploying surveillance technology to monitor forest corridors. “It is a marriage of technology, humans, and systems that would help ensure an effective and efficient system that detects, delays, and responds to security incidents,” he said. Also speaking, Iliyasu Gadu, a renowned columnist and analyst from Taraba State, said the recent killings in Karim Lamido were baffling, given the state’s history of containing banditry and kidnapping. Gadu said Taraba had experienced sporadic communal clashes, often arising from disputes over land, grazing rights and territorial claims, but had not witnessed banditry and kidnapping on the scale recorded in other parts of northern Nigeria. “Taraba has not been a hotbed like other states in the North and other parts of the country of banditry, kidnapping and related issues,” he said. He said there had been attempts by criminal elements from states such as Zamfara and Borno to infiltrate Taraba, but the government vigilance had helped check their activities. According to him, successive state governments have also worked with traditional rulers, community leaders and other stakeholders to prevent banditry and kidnapping from taking root. However, Gadu identified Karim Lamido’s difficult terrain, poor road access and extensive forests as factors that could make the area attractive to criminal groups seeking hideouts. “Karim is one of the very inaccessible parts of the state. It’s very remote, and there are no access roads to those areas,” he said. He added that the area’s proximity to Gombe, Bauchi and Adamawa states, as well as the presence of forests and poorly governed spaces, could make it difficult for security agencies to detect movements of armed groups. “That perhaps is a factor. It’s a very strong factor for people who want to perpetrate their activities and make Karim a base,” he said. Gadu urged the Taraba State Government to strengthen security measures and ensure that traditional rulers, religious leaders, community representatives and security agencies work together to identify threats and develop practical responses. He said existing military formations in the state, including a division, a brigade in the southern part and a battalion in Takum, could support efforts to contain the violence. Gadu also urged Governor Kefas, a former military officer, to deploy the necessary personnel and resources to prevent further attacks. “As somebody from Taraba, I would call on the government to ensure that we don’t allow those people to have a toehold in our state. They have no place in our state,” he said. He called for the identification and prosecution of those responsible, in accordance with the law, warning that the state must not allow banditry and kidnapping to undermine the peaceful coexistence of its people.

title: Abuja hotel manager dies during fight with tiler
body: A hotel manager, Joseph Terdoo, has reportedly died after a confrontation with a worker at a hotel in the Utako area of Abuja. The Commissioner of Police in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), CP Ahmed Mohammed Sanusi, who disclosed the incident, said it occurred around 5am on Tuesday after the Utako Police Division received a distress report. He said police operatives mobilised to the hotel following reports of suspicious noise and activity on the third floor of the building. According to the commissioner, the officers found Terdoo unconscious and rushed him to Wuse District Hospital, where he was confirmed dead on arrival. Sanusi said preliminary investigations revealed that Terdoo had been involved in a disagreement with a worker, Samuel Nel, a tiler, which allegedly degenerated into a physical confrontation. “Samuel was alleged to have pushed Joseph, who fell and hit his head on a wooden object and collapsed,” the CP said. Sanusi said the police were treating the incident as a case of alleged culpable homicide and had commenced an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the death. He advised FCT residents to shun violence and self-help during disagreements and embrace peaceful means of resolving disputes. However, in a separate development, the commissioner said operatives of the command intercepted a Lexus LX570 SUV with a concealed number plate in the Maitama District of Abuja. He said the vehicle and its occupant were taken into custody for investigation and possible prosecution. According to him, preliminary investigations revealed that the concealed number plate bore the inscription “PRESIDENCY” and registration number “10B218 FG”. “Following the suspect’s claim of being the legitimate holder of the number plate, further investigations revealed that the plate’s registration documents were forged, as the suspect was impersonating a Permanent Secretary attached to the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation,” Sanusi said. The commissioner said investigations were ongoing and that the suspect would be charged to court upon their conclusion. He urged residents to remain law-abiding, cooperate with police operations and promptly report suspicious persons or activities to the nearest police station.

title: FCT: Rising transport fares threaten children, teachers’ school attendance
body: Some school children from low-income families in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) are missing classes, as rising transport fares make daily movement to school increasingly difficult for such families to afford. Some parents and school children who spoke with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) in an interview on Friday in Abuja, said the development had made regular school attendance increasingly difficult to sustain. According to them, transportation expenses have increased significantly in recent times, forcing them to adopt various means to cope with the situation. Solomon Enemona, a parent and also a tailor who lives in Dutse Alhaji, said previously, he spent N800 daily on transportation for his two children to get to their school in Kubwa, as against the N2,000 he currently spent to the same location, Enemona noted that consequently, he had reduced the number of days his children attended school from five to three weekly, to enable him to meet other essential household demands. “I have no choice but to take this measure because, if I don’t, I may not be able to feed the family, pay our rent and other utility bills. “Desperate times, they say, call for desperate measures,” he added. Danjuma Musa, another parent, on his part, said he was considering transferring his children from a private school in Wuse, to a government school closer to his residence in Mpape, following the rising cost in transporting them to school daily. “Sometimes, they miss school because I am unable to pay for their transportation. “I don’t like them missing school, so I might just move them to a government school close to us. “I now spend three times what I used to pay for their transportation. I cannot cope anymore because, how much is my salary?” he queried. Musa explained that he enrolled his children in a private school far from home because, he wanted them to receive quality education, but that prevailing economic realities might force him to reconsider the decision. Andrew Innocent, another parent, said he sometimes had to decided which of his children’s transportation costs he would need to pay, whenever he had limited amount to accommodate all their fares. He said he sometimes resorted to borrowing money, to ensure his children attended school regularly, as prolonged absenteeism could affect their academic performance. In her contribution, Mrs Rachel Musa, Vice-Principal, Goke Akinwale International Academy, Dawaki, said rising transportation costs had increased absenteeism among pupils and negatively affected their academic performance. She noted that transporting four children to school could cost as much as N4000 daily, making it difficult for some parents to sustain regular attendance. The vice principal added that transportation costs also affected the teachers, some of whom spent about N2,000 daily, commuting to school. “Even the teachers themselves too miss classes because of transportation. “Imagine coming from Gwarimpa, all the way to Dawaki to teach. “You know how much you pay to and fro. At least you pay nothing less than N2, 000 every day,” she added. She said pupils who frequently missed classes, struggled to keep up academically with their peers. According to her, the school sometimes organises make-up tests for absentee pupils and allow them to copy notes from classmates, to help them catch up with missed lessons. She said the school had withdrawn some of its buses because of rising operational costs and parents’ complaints about transportation charges. She added that poor road conditions had also made vehicle maintenance difficult, urging the government to rehabilitate roads and address rising fuel prices to ease the transportation burden. Similarly, Mr Oneyi Edwin, Principal, Smartmind Success Academy, Jikwoyi, said the school had discontinued its bus services for pupils living far away, as a result of the operational cost. He explained that the service had become unsustainable. Edwin said some pupils living as far away as Kurudu had previously relied on the school bus to get to school. According to him, the school eventually lost some of the affected pupils after discontinuing the service, as their parents can no longer sustain the cost of getting them to school. Similarly, Samson Daruwana, a Senior Secondary School (SSS) student, explained that he had missed school twice in the past two weeks, as a result of transportation issues. Daruwana noted that he missed a test on one of the occasions after arriving late, following a long walk to school, as he was unable to afford the fare. Another student, Jonah Jock, said he felt bad about missing classes, while his classmates attended school. Jock said the situation was also affecting his academic performance. Tony Nwachukwu, a Junior Secondary School (JSS) student who lives in Giri, but attends school in Gwagwalada, said he now attended classes four times a week because of the high cost of transportation. According to Nwachukwu, he trekked to school even on the days he attended classes because he could no longer afford the fare. “It used to be N200 from Giri to Gwagwalada, but now, they collect N500, so I just trek Mondays to Thursdays and start my weekends on Fridays, so I can rest properly,” he stated. Other parents, students and school administrators, called on the government to address rising transportation costs and improve road infrastructure. They warned that the situation could further undermine regular school attendance and pupils’ academic performance. NAN reports that there has been a sharp rise in transportation costs in recent months, with transport operators attributing the development to persistent fuel price increases.

title: FCTA urged to establish funding mechanism for primary education
body: The Chairman of the Confederation of the Parents Teachers Association (CPTA), Abuja Municipal Area Council (AMAC) chapter, Mallam Tanko S. Bello, has advised the FCT Minister Nyesom Wike to establish a sustainable funding mechanism for primary education in the territory in order to permanently end the reoccurring teachers strike. Bello, in a statement made available to newsmen on Sunday in Abuja, also suggested the need for the FCT administration to convey an urgent stakeholders meeting with the labour unions, comprised of the Nigeria Union of Teachers (NUT) Nigeria Union of Local Government Employees (NULGE) and the Nigerian Labour Congress (NLC), PTA and the six area council chairmen to find a lasting solution to the teachers welfare. He said the reoccurring primary and secondary school teachers strike has become an annual embarrassment adding that Abuja, which hosts the nation’s capital should always lead by example by prioritizing teachers welfare. “Like last year, our children stayed at home for several months due to a similar strike. This year, history repeated itself again as our children were forced to roam about the streets, hawking, and being exposed to vices while their counterparts in private schools are in class learning,”the statement said. He noted that the academic calendar has completely remained disrupted, while the quality of education has continued to fall, which he said has psychologically traumatised parents and their children. “We believe that the education of FCT children should not be toyed with because an idle mind is a devil workshop. And that is why the association is also advising the FCT administration to ensure teachers welfare is prioritized,” he added.

title: We recorded zero articulated-vehicle crashes on Nyanya Corridor – FRSC
body: The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) says its time-window strategy for managing articulated vehicles along the Nyanya corridor of Abuja has helped prevent crashes involving the vehicles since its introduction in March. The Corps Public Education Officer (CPEO), FRSC, Mr Osondu Ohaeri, disclosed this in an interview on Sunday in Abuja. Ohaeri explained that the strategy was introduced in response to recurring crashes involving articulated vehicles along the busy Abuja corridor. He said the corps adopted the measure under the guidance of the Corps Marshal, Malam Shehu Mohammed, to reduce risks associated with the movement of heavy-duty vehicles during peak traffic periods. “The arrangement operates between 4pm and 9pm, when traffic congestion is usually high. “The Corps has not recorded any crash involving articulated vehicles, including petroleum tankers, along the corridor between the introduction of the strategy in March till date,” he said. Ohaeri described the outcome as an indication that targeted traffic management, combined with enforcement and public enlightenment, could help reduce road traffic crashes. He said the strategy was particularly important along corridors where heavy-duty vehicles operate alongside large numbers of commuters. He explained that during the designated period, articulated vehicles were guided to remain on the hard shoulder while FRSC personnel engage their drivers in road safety education. He said that the initiative was intended to reduce interaction between slow-moving heavy-duty vehicles and other road users during rush hour, while giving drivers an opportunity to receive safety guidance “The vehicles are allowed to rejoin the main carriageway after the peak period, when traffic has eased,” he said. He, however, stressed that the intervention did not remove the need for drivers to maintain their vehicles properly and comply with speed limits and other traffic regulations. He identified speeding, driver fatigue and driving against traffic as persistent violations that could undermine road safety if not effectively addressed.

title: His Majesty congratulates Brazil president
body:
Muscat: His Majesty Sultan Haitham bin Tarik has sent a cable of congratulations to President Lula da Silva on the occasion of his re-election as President of the Federative Republic of Brazil. In the cable, His Majesty the Sultan expressed his best wishes to the President for success in continuing to lead the friendly Brazilian people, and in achieving further accomplishments and aspirations.

title: Man arrested over alleged killing of girlfriend met online
body: Operatives of the Edo State Police Command have arrested a 21-year-old man, Miracle Samuel, over the alleged killing of his girlfriend, whom he met on social media. The state Commissioner of Police, Patrick Daaor, said the suspect and the victim met on social media and became friends after chatting for several months. He said Samuel subsequently invited the woman to his residence in the Ahor area of Benin City, where he allegedly killed her with a knife. Daaor said the suspect was in police custody and would be charged to court upon completion of the investigation. Samuel, however, denied deliberately killing the victim, claiming that she sustained a fatal injury while they struggled over a knife during an altercation. “I didn’t mean to kill her, but she got injured in the process of struggling with her for the knife during an argument,” he said. Samuel said he met the victim online and that they became friends after chatting for several months before she decided to visit him. “On the day she came to my house, we were discussing, but the discussion snowballed into an argument. In the process, she picked up a knife and intended to stab me,” he said. He claimed that the victim sustained an injury to her neck while they struggled over the knife. “I didn’t mean to kill her. I tried to save her after she was injured, but she died,” he said.

title: Nigerien, 3 others nabbed over guard’s killing, theft
body: Operatives of the Edo State Police Command have arrested a Niger Republic national and three others over the alleged killing of a security guard and theft of goods worth over N400 million in the state. The suspects, identified as Hamisu Nuhu, Suleiman Rabiu, Hussaini Gago, a Nigerien, and Ibrahim Haruna, were arrested in connection with a robbery at Paparazzi Communication Complex in Auchi, Etsako West Local Government Area, on July 12, 2026. The state Commissioner of Police, Patrick Daaor, said the suspects allegedly stormed the communication complex, killed the security guard on duty and stole goods worth over N400 million. He alleged that Nuhu, who resides in the area, masterminded the robbery, while Gago received the stolen items from the syndicate for sale in Niger Republic. Nuhu, however, denied involvement in the robbery, insisting that he was not a member of the gang. “Suleiman and I grew up together in Zaria, and he does business in Imo State. He called me in May 2026 and told me that he would be travelling to Kaduna State and would spend a night in my house in Auchi before proceeding on his journey. “He slept in my house, and before he left, he said he wanted to swap his iPhone. I took him to a shop called Paparazzi, where they swap phones, not knowing that he had another agenda. “He left the following day, and in July, he called me to say he was on his way to Kaduna and would spend a night in my house before leaving the next day. “When he arrived, he told me that his friend, with whom he was travelling, had lodged in a hotel and that they would continue their journey the following day,” Nuhu said. He said the robbery occurred four days after Suleiman left his house, adding that he was surprised when police arrested him in connection with the incident. “I don’t know anything about the robbery, and I am not part of them,” he said.

title: NDLEA arrests South African woman, US-based grandma with drugs
body: The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has arrested a 34-year-old South African woman with 36.65 kilogrammes of cocaine at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos, and a 62-year-old Nigerian-American grandmother with 9.45kg of cannabis imported from the United States. The agency also arrested several suspects, including a physically challenged woman, and recovered large consignments of illicit drugs in separate operations across nine states. The NDLEA disclosed this in a statement by its Director, Media and Advocacy, Femi Babafemi, on Sunday in Abuja. According to the statement, the South African woman, identified as Qhina Beauty, was arrested on October 7 at the airport’s departure hall while attempting to board a Qatar Airways flight to South Africa via Doha. A search of her two travelling bags led to the discovery of 30 blocks of cocaine weighing 36.65kg. The drugs, concealed with dried pepper, were wrapped in cellophane tape and packed into seven parcels. The suspect reportedly told investigators that she arrived in Nigeria on September 30 specifically to collect the consignment. She said another South African woman recruited her and promised to pay her 20,000 rand upon successful delivery. She also allegedly identified two other members of the drug trafficking syndicate, one based in the United States and the other a Lagos-based car dealer. The NDLEA said its investigation led to the arrest of the car dealer, 46-year-old Uchenna Victor Umunnakwe, on October 14 at Apple Junction, Ago Palace Way, Lagos, following surveillance at his residence in Shasha. Umunnakwe allegedly admitted receiving Qhina at the airport, lodging her at Santiago Hotel in Amuwo-Odofin and later moving her to Cynarisso Hotel near the airport ahead of her departure. In a separate operation, operatives arrested Anetor Gloria Ubong, a 62-year-old Nigerian-American grandmother and realtor based in Richmond, Texas, upon her arrival from Houston aboard a United Airlines flight on October 21. The statement said a search of her two checked-in boxes uncovered 18 parcels of loud, a high-grade cannabis strain, weighing 9.45kg. The substance was concealed with gift-wrapping paper inside a box. Ubong, who holds Nigerian and United States passports, reportedly told investigators that her daughter and the daughter’s prospective brother-in-law delivered the box to her home in the US for onward delivery in Nigeria to her daughter’s fiancé, identified as Jibola. The agency also reported the arrest of a 41-year-old woman, Eletu Rasheedat, in the Eti Osa area of Lagos on October 23. Operatives recovered 5,820 pills of diazepam, 780 tablets of tramadol, 3.7kg of skunk and 230.25 litres of skuchies from her.

title: Customs foils wildlife smuggling, rescues 5 pangolins
body: The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Federal Operations Unit (FOU) Zone A, has rescued five live pangolins abandoned by suspected traffickers along the Igbo-Ora–Imeko-Afon axis of Ogun State. The rescue of the five animals is coming barely seven days after a similar rescue operation was made. The operation, conducted at about 1am on Friday, October 23, followed intelligence on the suspected movement of endangered wildlife. The suspected traffickers reportedly fled on sighting Customs officers, abandoning the animals concealed in wire-mesh cages. The rescued pangolins were handed over to the Greenfingers Wildlife Initiative Centre for safekeeping, rehabilitation and eventual release into a protected habitat. The Deputy Comptroller in charge of Enforcement, Oluwaseun Oguntuase, who conducted the handover on behalf of the Acting Controller of FOU Zone A, Deputy Comptroller Oladapo Afeni, said the interception of wildlife consignments within about seven days underscored the need for investigations to identify and dismantle the smuggling syndicates. Oguntuase reaffirmed the Service’s commitment to combating wildlife trafficking through intelligence-led operations and collaboration with conservation agencies. “Pangolins are among the world’s most trafficked mammals. This seizure is another clear warning to those involved in the illegal wildlife trade that Nigeria’s borders and transport corridors remain under active surveillance,” he said. He warned that those involved in wildlife trafficking would face the full weight of the law. Receiving the animals, Dr Austin Tochukwu of the Greenfingers Wildlife Initiative Centre, commended Customs for its intervention and assured that the centre would provide the necessary care and facilitate the pangolins’ rehabilitation and eventual release into a protected environment. The Customs Service reiterated its commitment to protecting Nigeria’s biodiversity and enforcing relevant national and international wildlife protection laws.

title: Police arrest 8 suspected members of ‘one-chance’ gang in Abuja
body: Operatives of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Police Command have arrested eight suspected members of a “one-chance” robbery and kidnapping gang in Abuja. The FCT Commissioner of Police, Ahmed Mohammed Sanusi, disclosed the arrests to journalists at the command headquarters in Abuja at the weekend. Sanusi said the arrests followed a distress report involving a woman who boarded a taxi from AYA Roundabout. According to him, the woman, who is the wife of a police officer, allegedly boarded a vehicle operated by members of a “one-chance” syndicate, who dispossessed her of her mobile phone and other valuables. He said the suspects also allegedly transferred money from the victim’s account before dropping her off. Sanusi said the command subsequently directed its tracking unit to investigate the incident using digital technology. “As we deconstructed the entire criminal operation, we traced all electronic transactions and the mobile phone of the victim until we apprehended the eight suspects,” he said. The commissioner identified the suspects as Yunusa Sani, Ismail Mohammed, Abubakar Usman, Haruna Musa, Abdulrazaq Mohammed, Isah Abdulrahman, Isa Abdullahi and Aliyu Shuaibu. He said further investigation led to the recovery of 21 mobile phones and three laptops, including the victim’s phone. Sanusi alleged that one of the suspects, Haruna Musa, specialised in electronically altering the International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) numbers of stolen devices before resale to evade detection. The commissioner said receivers of the stolen items had also been traced and identified, adding that the suspects and recovered exhibits remained in police custody. He said the suspects would be charged to court upon completion of the investigation. “I want to encourage FCT residents to remain security-conscious, cooperate with the police and other law enforcement agencies and promptly report suspicious persons, movements and activities to the nearest police station or through the command’s emergency contact lines,” Sanusi said. He stressed that security was a collective responsibility, assuring residents that the command would continue to carry out its responsibilities while seeking the cooperation of the public.

title: Police arrest 3 for allegedly defiling minors
body: Operatives of the Edo State Police Command have arrested three suspects over the alleged defilement of minors in the state. The state’s Commissioner of Police, Patrick Daaor, said the suspects were arrested in connection with the alleged sexual assault and defilement of two minors aged two years and nine months and four years, respectively. He said the cases were being handled by the command’s Gender and Family Unit, adding that the suspects would soon be charged to court. One of the suspects, identified as Destiny Samson, who was accused of defiling a four-year-old girl, said in an interview that he did not have sexual intercourse with the minor but admitted to digitally penetrating her. The suspect, a bricklayer, said, “I didn’t know what came over me. I didn’t sleep with her; I only fingered her.” He said the incident came to light when the girl’s mother returned home and raised an alarm, attracting the attention of people around. “I begged her mother to forgive me, but she refused, and I was arrested by the police,” he said. He pleaded for forgiveness, saying he had learnt his lesson.

title: Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew Celebrates 35 Years of Priesthood in Constantinople
body: The Ecumenical Patriarchate in Constantinople has marked 35 years of the priesthood of His All-Holiness Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew , with celebrations bringing together clergy, pilgrims and members of the Greek Orthodox community from around the world. The anniversary at the Phanar was marked by solemn religious services and expressions of devotion to the spiritual leader of the Orthodox Christian world, whose patriarchal ministry has spanned more than three decades. Greek Minister of Culture Lina Mendoni paid tribute to Patriarch Bartholomew’s international influence, his commitment to Orthodox Christian tradition and his efforts to strengthen the global role of the Ecumenical Patriarchate. Mendoni highlighted the Patriarch’s longstanding commitment to environmental protection, noting that he had championed the protection of the natural world long before climate change became one of the defining challenges of the modern era. She said his work connected environmental responsibility with social justice, moral duty and the obligation to protect the planet for future generations. Imvros Holds Special Place in Patriarch’s Journey Mendoni also highlighted the special significance of Imvros, the island where Patriarch Bartholomew was born, describing its revival as an important example of the enduring power of historical memory, education and culture. Through the Patriarch’s personal interest and continued support, Imvros has experienced renewed hope, with efforts to preserve its Greek heritage and strengthen its cultural and educational life. Greek Australian Children Travel to Constantinople Among the most moving moments of the celebrations was the participation of approximately 100 children who travelled from Sydney and Melbourne to Constantinople. Organised by the Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of Australia, the young participants presented a cultural and religious programme featuring songs, dances and other performances celebrating their Greek Orthodox faith and heritage. Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew celebrates 35 years of priesthood in Constantinople, with Greek Australian children travelling from Sydney and Melbourne. Their presence highlighted the enduring connection between the Greek diaspora in Australia and the Ecumenical Patriarchate in Constantinople. Thousands of kilometres from their homeland, the children demonstrated how Greek language, Orthodox Christianity and Hellenic cultural traditions continue to be passed on to younger generations. The anniversary served not only as a tribute to Patriarch Bartholomew’s 35 years of priesthood, but also as a powerful expression of the worldwide Orthodox community’s devotion to its spiritual heritage. title: Oil slips from near six-month highs despite supply concerns
body: Oil prices fell on Monday after surging to near six-month highs late last week, though ongoing attacks on Saudi Arabia kept supply concerns in focus. US crude futures fell $1.60, or 1.55%, to $101.67 per barrel by 0018 GMT. Brent crude futures ​were down $1.56, or 1.34%, at $115.16. Prices had settled nearly $3 ​higher on Friday after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked energy supply concerns. Brent finished the week up 6%, and WTI ended 2.3% higher. Attacks continued over the ‌weekend ⁠with Houthis saying they had attacked the Saudi airport and oil facilities on Saturday. Saudi Arabia said on ​Sunday ​it had ⁠intercepted more missiles and drones. The top oil exporter restarted partial ​operations at its main airport ​on ⁠Sunday after damage in a previous round of Houthi attacks, even as ⁠the ​militant group vowed to ​keep targeting the facility.

title: Canberra Launches Hellenic Week With Evzones and Greek Film
body: A major highlight of Hellenic Week is the historic visit of Greece’s Presidential Guard, the Evzones , to Canberra on Wednesday, October 28, marking Ohi Day. Hellenic Week 2026 in Canberra celebrates Greek culture, Ohi Day and the visit of the Greek Presidential Guard, the Evzones. The Evzones will participate in commemorative and community events across the capital, including a Divine Liturgy at St Nicholas Greek Orthodox Church in Kingston, a visit to Australian Parliament House, and a wreath laying ceremony at the Australian War Memorial. Evzones and Sydney’s Greek Community at Anzac Memorial 2026 The day will culminate with the Evzones marching into the Hellenic Club of Canberra, followed by a special Guard of Honour. The program offers the Greek Australian community and the wider public a rare opportunity to witness one of Greece’s most recognisable symbols of national identity and tradition. Greek Film Festival Celebrates Greek Cinema Hellenic Week will also showcase Greek cinema through special screenings at Palace Cinemas in Canberra as part of the 2026 Greek Film Festival. The opening night on Thursday, October 29, features Best Friends Forever , a contemporary Greek comedy exploring friendship and the complications that arise when people try to help those around them. On Saturday, October 31, audiences can watch Kapodistrias , a historical epic by acclaimed Greek filmmaker Yannis Smaragdis about Ioannis Kapodistrias, one of the defining figures in modern Greek history. The festival program concludes on Sunday, November 1, with Saint Paisios , a film depicting the early life of the revered Orthodox Christian figure and his family’s journey from Cappadocia to Greece. Together, the screenings celebrate Greek storytelling, history, faith and contemporary culture as part of the inaugural Hellenic Week.
