title: Senegal party that controls parliament comes out against revised budget bill
body: Senegal’s Pastef party, which holds a large majority in the National Assembly, said it would not pass the government’s ​revised budget, reinforcing doubts over how quickly the country ‌can push ahead with its debt restructuring, A statement by the party headed by former Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko cited “disagreements over certain budgetary decisions, the chosen ​financing arrangements and the insufficient guarantees provided to parliament”, though ​it said the party was open to engaging with ⁠the government on getting a new budget in place The West ​African nation has been grappling with a debt burden that had ​reached 132% of gross domestic product by the end of 2024, International Monetary Fund figures show, after the government uncovered billions of dollars in misreported borrowing ​by the previous administration The government reached a staff-level agreement, with the IMF ​in early September for a $2.2 billion, 36-month Extended Credit Facility to support its ‌reform ⁠program. But without parliamentary approval of the revised budget, the government risks delaying the IMF program, which underpins its entire debt restructuring strategy, Prime Minister Ahmadou Al Aminou Lo plans to hold a press ​conference on Sunday ​to discuss the ⁠revised budget “which is intended to implement a revised framework aimed at improving the quality of life ​of Senegalese people” The amended 2026 budget bill paints ​a sharply ⁠deteriorating fiscal picture. It cuts real GDP growth to 2.7% from roughly 5% in the original budget and widens the deficit to ⁠7.6% ​of GDP from 5.4%, driven largely by ​a tripling of energy subsidies to 790.3 billion CFA francs ($1.36 billion) from 250 billion

title: Brazil's Lula reelected to a historic fourth term in runoff vote
body: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won an unprecedented fourth term on Sunday, the country's electoral court said, in a shock result that defied polls, precedent and global anti-incumbent sentiment to put the brakes on a wave of right-wing election victories across Latin America.Lula, an icon of the global left and the most dominant force in Brazilian politics this century, defeated Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro. The senator had finished first in the election's first round and hoped to revive his father's far-right movement.At times, Lula's reelection looked like a long shot, as voters soured on him and his Workers' Party after years of corruption scandals and rising prices, while sweeping societal changes left the former metalworker and union leader looking out of touch with an increasingly app-based economy and its growing ranks of informal workers.Lula's victory marks another comeback in a career full of them. The 80-year-old was jailed from 2018 to 2019 on corruption charges that were later overturned, paving the way for him to beat Jair Bolsonaro in the 2022 election."He is a statesman, a giant," leftist federal lawmaker Erika Hilton, who was with Lula in Sao Paulo during the vote count, told Reuters.Unlikely path to victoryPollsters said better-than-expected turnout had powered Lula to victory. Leonardo Barreto, the co-founder of consultancy Think Policy, said voters had chosen Lula's familiar embrace over Bolsonaro's novelty."People today are choosing between change, with some apprehension, and a known path, which guarantees certain rights," he said.During the campaign, Lula pointed to a track record of falling poverty and inequality, while unemployment, illiteracy and deforestation hit record lows during his third term.He warned Bolsonaro would cut welfare spending, backslide on social advances and hand over Brazil's sovereignty to US President Donald Trump, whose State Department led a campaign to get the Bolsonaros back to power.Lula's win deprives Trump of a major addition to what has been a growing bloc of friendly right-wing Latin American governments that have embraced Washington's agenda on security and migration.Celso Amorim, a former Lula foreign minister, told Reuters the leftist "would be very important for establishing a point of balance in Latin America. Lula is that balance."Comeback King Lula becomes the first candidate since Brazil's return to democracy in the 1980s to be elected after finishing second in the first round.Lula, who was president between 2003 and 2011, campaigned on a potent mix of pragmatism and populism that has shaped his career in national politics for half a century, rolling out a slew of reforms aimed at improving the lives of workers and poor Brazilians.These gained steam with late-campaign pledges that ranged from free nationwide weekend public ​transport, which has to be formally submitted to Congress, to a ‌15% increase in his trademark welfare program that is already being implemented.Lula also championed a constitutional amendment that became Brazil's biggest labor reform in decades, which passed with wide support in Congress.Challenging legislative realityStill, Lula's fourth term could be his most difficult yet, after Brazil elected its most conservative Congress since returning to democracy in the 1980s.Combined, Bolsonaro's Liberal Party (PL) and allied parties could control over 280 seats in the lower house and up to 50 seats in the Senate, enough for comfortable majorities in both chambers."He is likely to be a lame duck from the start," said Oliver Stuenkel, a professor of international relations at the Getulio Vargas Foundation in São Paulo.The incoming legislature will likely deepen recent trends of presidents ceding power to Congress, Stuenkel said, predicting Lula will face waning influence over Supreme Court nominations, unwieldy party coalitions, and even the threat of impeachment.Economic headwindsLula faces an economy that his government forecasts will grow a meager 2.3% next year, adding to fiscal concerns tied to high interest rates and public debt that has risen past 82% of GDP, the highest since the pandemic.The president's critics blame spending, though interest costs have driven most of the increase in debt.Goldman Sachs said it expects Lula to make modest progress at most to contain spending in a fourth term, as he stays committed to a state-led growth model.Surging household debt also concerns economists. Trying to address the issue, Lula rolled out a provisional ban on online betting and unveiled a new debt relief program during the campaign.The incoming right-wing Congress will try to pass structural reforms that favor businesses, experts say, prompting spending cuts that could fuel social upheaval.

title: Ebola: NCDC places 53 contacts under watch, approves N100,000 weekly support
body: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) said it is monitoring 53 primary contacts linked to Nigeria’s confirmed Ebola case, as it expands investigations to identify people who may have been exposed to the patient at multiple locations. Briefing newsmen on Sunday in Abuja, Director-General of the NCDC, Dr Jide Idris, said the agency had also approved a weekly payment of N100,000 per person to support individuals placed under isolation or quarantine as part of efforts to contain the outbreak in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). Idris said 44 of the 53 primary contacts were associated with the health facility where the patient was treated, while nine others had been identified outside the facility. The additional contacts include three members of the patient’s household and individuals who attended to her at an emergency room she visited before arriving at the facility where her Ebola infection was subsequently confirmed. The latest figure is up from the 44 contacts the Federal Government initially announced after confirming the Ebola case in the FCT on October 20. According to information previously provided by the World Health Organisation (WHO), the patient, a woman who recently travelled from Uganda, developed symptoms on October 7 and sought medical attention on October 11 before her infection was confirmed. Idris said investigations were ongoing to establish the full chain of possible exposure and ensure that everyone who might have come in contact with the patient was identified and placed under appropriate monitoring. He explained that the NCDC was extending its contact-tracing exercise beyond people who had direct contact with the patient to identify others who might have been exposed through the initial group of contacts. “As of now, we have 53 primary contacts. Of these, 44 are people from that health facility where the patient was treated,” he said. Explaining the process, Idris said health officials would interview each identified contact to determine whether they had interacted with other people who might also require monitoring. “For each person, we are going to ask questions. We have to establish who they have been in contact with. If we can identify those people, they will also be monitored,” he said. He disclosed that the patient’s medical history showed that she had visited an emergency room before presenting at the health facility where the infection was eventually confirmed. According to him, the agency had commenced efforts to trace individuals who attended to the patient during the earlier visit, with three healthcare providers from the emergency room included among the additional contacts identified. The investigation also covers healthcare personnel involved in collecting samples from the patient, underscoring concerns about the potential exposure of health workers during the management and investigation of suspected Ebola cases. The contacts identified so far include healthcare workers, members of the patient’s household, domestic staff and personnel involved in collecting samples from her. Health officials are categorising the contacts according to their level of exposure and conducting follow-up assessments to identify anyone who develops symptoms requiring further investigation. The NCDC said individuals under monitoring would be assessed promptly if they developed symptoms, with testing and other appropriate interventions provided where necessary. NCDC approves N100,000 weekly support Idris said the NCDC approved a weekly payment of N100,000 per person to ease the financial burden on individuals identified as contacts of the confirmed case. According to him, some of those under public health monitoring had raised concerns about the cost of feeding, accommodation and providing for their families while complying with the restrictions and monitoring arrangements. He said the financial assistance was considered necessary to ensure that those identified as contacts could cooperate with health officials without facing additional economic hardship. “We are paying for their accommodation; we are paying for their feeding. Some of them are asking for a stipend to maintain their families,” he said. The NCDC boss added that the agency had approved N100,000 weekly for each person requiring the support to cover essential needs during the monitoring period. He explained that the intervention was not part of the agency’s initial response plan but became necessary in view of the challenges confronting people placed under public health monitoring. “This was not planned for, but it is an emergency. We will continue to review it as we go along,” he said. Idris noted that the arrangement would be reviewed as the outbreak response progressed, with the agency assessing the support based on prevailing circumstances and emerging needs. He also called for a broader approach to emergency preparedness, insisting that the responsibility for supporting people affected by public health emergencies should not rest solely on the FCT authorities. According to him, other states must also be prepared to provide similar assistance if they experience comparable outbreaks or public health emergencies. Idris said the NCDC was working to strengthen infection prevention and control measures in healthcare facilities to reduce the risk of transmission among medical personnel, patients and other members of the public. He explained that the agency’s infection prevention and control teams routinely assess health facilities to determine whether appropriate safety procedures are in place and identify gaps requiring urgent attention. Virologist faults Nigeria’s preparedness Virologist and former president of the Nigerian Academy of Science, Prof. Oyewale Tomori, has faulted Nigeria’s preparedness for Ebola, saying funds earmarked for emergency response should have been used to train health workers and equip isolation centres before the disease entered the country. Tomori said the rise in the number of contacts being monitored following Nigeria’s first confirmed case highlighted the need for more extensive and rigorous contact tracing. In an interview with Trust TV’s Sunday Politics last night, Tomori said he initially considered the 44 contacts reported by health authorities insufficient, given the period between the patient’s onset of illness and confirmation of the case. “I was thinking we need to have more than that,” he said, adding that the increase in contacts under monitoring to 53 was welcome but that a more thorough search could identify additional people. Tomori said the priority should not be merely identifying contacts but ensuring that each person was closely monitored through regular temperature checks and promptly isolated if symptoms developed. He said effective contact tracing required personnel to visit households and communities, adding that the exercise would need adequate funding and logistical support. The virologist questioned whether the N10 billion approved by President Bola Tinubu in June 2026 for Ebola preparedness and other emerging public health threats had been released and deployed in good time. He said the funds should have been used to train health workers, equip facilities, establish isolation centres and ensure that relevant personnel were prepared to respond to an outbreak. He warned that approving funds alone would not guarantee preparedness unless the resources were released, properly deployed and translated into functioning systems. On screening at entry points, he said authorities should obtain accurate travel and contact details from passengers, while health workers should take proper histories when people report symptoms. He explained that Ebola’s incubation period could extend to 21 days, meaning health workers needed to ask patients about their movements over that period rather than immediately treating fever as malaria without investigating possible exposure. Tomori urged Nigerians arriving in the country to provide accurate phone numbers, addresses and seat numbers on travel forms, saying the information could help authorities trace people who might have been exposed.

title: NDC names Abdulkarim as campaign DG
body: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has appointed Mallam Ibrahim Hussain Abdulkarim as Director-General of its National Campaign Council and Ikenna Morgan Enekweizu as Council Secretary. The strategic lineup, announced via the party’s official channels, aims to provide overarching leadership, align national campaign structures, and mobilize citizens around the NDC’s vision for a just and prosperous Nigeria. At the top of the campaign leadership hierarchy, NDC National Leader Senator Henry Seriake Dickson will serve as Chairman of the Council, with Presidential candidate Peter Obi stepping in as Co-chairman. Rounding out the executive tier, NDC National Chairman Senator Cleopas Moses Zuwoghe takes the role of Vice Chairman, while Vice Presidential candidate Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso serves as Co-vice Chairman. Former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Babachir Lawal, is listed as a member of the National Campaign Caucus and chairman of the National Campaign Advisory Council. Other members of the National Campaign Caucus include Deputy National Chairmen Sidi Bomi Abdul and Babatunde F. Alli, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, Senator Victor Umeh, Director-General of the presidential campaign Ibrahim Hussain Abdulkarim, Buba Galadima, Professor Yakubu Ochefu, Professor Mahmud Gambo Jahun, Moshood Salvador and the party’s National Woman Leader, Dudu Manuga. Ossai Director will be the Council’s Director of Media and Communication and Ikeddi Isiguzo (Deputy Director) Constance Ikokwu will serve as the party’s campaign spokesman.

title: How APC set stage for 2027 presidential campaign
body: The All Progressives Congress (APC) on Saturday set the stage for its 2027 presidential campaign with a rally in Kaduna, where President Bola Tinubu urged voters to renew his mandate while blaming previous administrations for the country’s economic challenges. As early as 7 am, supporters began arriving at the Ranchers Bees Stadium, Kaduna, wearing colourful T-shirts with inscriptions promoting Tinubu’s second-term bid. Seven governors, including Abba Kabir Yusuf of Kano, Uba Sani of Kaduna, Dikko Umar Radda of Katsina, Umar Namadi of Jigawa, Ahmed Aliyu of Sokoto, Dauda Lawal of Zamfara and Nasir Idris of Kebbi, alongside other APC leaders, received the president at the Kaduna International Airport. Although the rally was scheduled for 10 am, Tinubu arrived at the airport shortly after 2 pm. He reached the stadium a few minutes before 3 pm and left shortly after 4 pm. Thousands of supporters lined the major roads leading to the venue, singing and dancing as the presidential convoy passed. Local drummers and entertainers also added colour to the reception. Soldiers, police officers, civil defence personnel, operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS) and other security agencies were deployed to strategic locations. Major roads leading to the stadium were also blocked during the visit. Tinubu blames opposition for hunger Addressing the crowd, Tinubu urged voters not to be misled by opposition parties ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election. He blamed previous administrations for the hunger and poverty facing Nigerians, saying his government was working to reverse years of economic mismanagement. “I hear my opponents talking about hunger and poverty. But who created these problems? They created them, and we are working to eradicate them,” he said. He urged Nigerians to renew his mandate, promising to consolidate what he described as ongoing economic recovery efforts. Tinubu said his government had laid the foundation for prosperity and growth, while creating opportunities for citizens. The president also defended the removal of fuel subsidy, insisting that the policy was necessary to address corruption and economic leakages. However, a moment of drama occurred when Tinubu shouted “Nigeria!”, apparently expecting the crowd to respond with “Sai Tinubu!” Instead, a section of the crowd chanted “Ba ma yi,” meaning “We don’t want.” President Tinubu was shielded by a bulletproof glass enclosure during the campaign rally, as security agencies mounted extensive measures around the venue and along major roads. The glass enclosure, positioned around the president’s seat, was one of the most noticeable features of the rally. Security was heightened across Kaduna metropolis ahead of Tinubu’s arrival. Major roads along his convoy route were placed under heavy surveillance, while several roads leading to the venue were temporarily closed to traffic. Armed personnel from various security agencies were deployed at strategic locations, including road intersections, access points and within the stadium. Tinubu gave you political refuge in 2007, Shettima tells Atiku Vice President Kashim Shettima took a swipe at former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, recalling that Tinubu gave him political support and a platform to contest the presidency after his fallout with the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in 2007. Shettima said Tinubu had consistently supported northern politicians and deserved the region’s backing for a second term. “It is pertinent to mention that when former Vice President Atiku Abubakar was harassed and chased out of the PDP in 2007, he ran to the Lion of Bourdillon, Bola Ahmed Tinubu, who gave him political succour, support and a platform to contest for the presidency,” Shettima said. He also recalled that Tinubu supported Ribadu’s presidential ambition in 2011 and played a key role in Buhari’s victories in the 2015 and 2019 elections. The vice president said the APC’s appeal to northern voters was based on its record in office rather than sentiment. He cited investments in education, including the establishment of the Federal University of Applied Sciences, Kachia, the upgrade of the Federal University of Education, Zaria, and funding for the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND). He also listed major infrastructure projects, including the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano (AKK) Gas Pipeline, Kano-Maradi railway, Lagos-Kano rail corridor, Abuja-Kaduna-Kano highway and Sokoto-Badagry Super Highway. Uba Sani: Tinubu has done more for North than any leader Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani said Tinubu had done more for Northern Nigeria than any previous leader, citing road reconstruction and support for agricultural transformation. He urged voters in the region to support the president’s re-election bid, highlighting infrastructure projects and the administration’s technical and vocational education programme. Sani said the Abuja-Kaduna-Kano expressway, which connects 12 states across the North-West, North-Central and North-East, was 95 per cent complete. He recalled that during a visit to Tinubu two years ago, he had stressed the importance of the road, which he described as one of the most strategic highways in Northern Nigeria. According to him, the president assured him that the Federal Government would provide the N740 billion required for the reconstruction. Sani identified insecurity and inadequate funding as the major reasons the project had previously stalled. He, however, said security along the road had improved, adding that more than 90 per cent of those who travelled from Abuja to Kaduna for the rally used the highway. The governor also challenged opposition politicians to present their records of performance rather than rely on appeals to regional identity. “When someone came to us and said we should vote for him simply because he is a northern candidate, we asked him: Can you show us your track record? “Until this moment, the so-called Northern candidate has not shown us his track record, Mr President. No track record,” he said. North will give Tinubu 100 per cent support – Yari The Director-General of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Abdulaziz Yari, has assured President Tinubu of overwhelming support from northern Nigeria. Yari said the campaign council was committed to mobilising support across the North through engagements with traditional rulers, Islamic scholars, imams and other influential stakeholders. “Northern Nigeria is 100% yours, insha Allah. This is the promise that we make, and you are going to see it in January 2027,” Yari said. According to him, the APC intends to use its campaign to communicate the government’s policies and achievements to Nigerians, particularly in the northern region. Yari said engagements with traditional and religious leaders were part of efforts to explain the administration’s programmes and encourage support for Tinubu’s re-election bid. He also defended the government’s relationship with farmers, dismissing allegations that the administration had neglected the agricultural sector. The APC chieftain claimed that about two million farmers had committed to supporting Tinubu in the 2027 election. Media stand collapses during rally A stand designated for journalists covering the APC rally in Kaduna collapsed in the middle of the event, causing dozens of cameramen and their equipment to fall to the ground. The incident occurred while media personnel from various organisations were filming and photographing proceedings at the rally. Some of the affected journalists were also livestreaming the event when the structure gave way. There were no reports of injuries, but the collapse temporarily disrupted media coverage as journalists scrambled to retrieve their cameras and reposition themselves. The development also created visibility challenges for many of the cameramen, who struggled to secure clear vantage points after the incident, with some unable to maintain uninterrupted coverage of speakers at the event due to obstruction from the crowd and other structures.

title: Pontian Greek Groups Challenge Atatürk Opera in Germany
body: Pontian Greek organisations in Germany are protesting a new opera about Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, warning that the production risks overlooking the persecution and mass killings of Pontian Greeks during the final years of the Ottoman Empire and the emergence of modern Turkey. The opera is scheduled to premiere at the Stuttgart State Opera on April 10, 2027. The protest was organised by Dodekapolis, an association representing Pontian Greek cultural organisations in Baden-Württemberg. Following an official letter of protest, Stuttgart State Opera artistic director Viktor Schoner invited representatives of Dodekapolis to a meeting to discuss their concerns. Stuttgart State Opera, where a new opera about Mustafa Kemal Atatürk is scheduled to premiere in April 2027. During the meeting, the association raised questions about the historical and ethical implications of presenting Atatürk on stage, highlighting his role in events associated with the Pontian Greek Genocide. Dodekapolis stressed that artistic freedom should go hand in hand with historical responsibility, particularly when publicly funded cultural institutions portray figures whose legacies remain deeply contested. The association called for greater transparency about the opera’s content and historical interpretation, urging the production team to reconsider any approach that could romanticise Atatürk or minimise the suffering of affected communities. Opera Promises a Complex Portrayal of Atatürk The Stuttgart State Opera describes the production as an exploration of Atatürk’s achievements and contradictions, rather than a straightforward celebration of his life. Composed by Bassem Akiki, with a libretto by Olga Bach, the opera will feature seven languages, including Greek, Armenian and Kurdish. According to the opera house’s description, the production will examine Atatürk through the perspectives of his allies, opponents and victims. The competing interpretations have placed the historical treatment of Atatürk at the centre of the dispute, with Dodekapolis seeking assurances that the experiences of communities affected by persecution will be addressed meaningfully. Appeal for Wider Community Dialogue Dodekapolis has also appealed to Armenian, Assyrian, Kurdish, Alevi and other communities affected by historical persecution to join a broader discussion about historical memory and human rights. The association’s concerns extend beyond artistic representation to the responsibility of cultural institutions to confront difficult historical legacies. The debate now centres on whether the production will meaningfully examine the suffering associated with Atatürk’s historical legacy or risk diminishing it. For Pontian Greek organisations, the opera presents an opportunity to ensure that the experiences of their ancestors are not overlooked in a cultural portrayal of one of modern Turkey’s most influential figures. title: Nigeria Ebola case linked to virus found in Kenya index case, health minister says
body: Genomic ​analysis of Nigeria’s only confirmed Ebola case ‌shows the virus is closely related to the strain detected in Kenya’s index case, Nigeria’s health minister ​Muhammad Ali Pate said on Friday, offering ​the first genetic link between the outbreaks. Nigerian authorities said there is no evidence that the Kenya index case travelled to Nigeria or had a direct connection to the Nigerian case. Pate said contacts linked to the case are being traced, ​quarantined and tested, with some results ​negative and others still pending Nigeria has recorded only one ‌confirmed ⁠Ebola case from a traveller who had visited Uganda Uganda, which borders the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and has previously battled Ebola outbreaks, ​said on ​Friday it ⁠remained Ebola-free but was tightening precautions Uganda’s health ministry said traveller locator ​forms had been reinstated for all ​arrivals, ⁠regardless of country of origin Uganda said travellers with a history of travel to the DRC, ⁠where ​the outbreak began, will not ​be permitted to transit the country

title: Trump repeats endorsement of Netanyahu, calls for Israel, US to 'finish the job'
body: US President Donald Trump endorsed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for the second time on Sunday evening in a Truth Social post days ahead of the upcoming election. "When you go to the Polls please remember that Bibi [Netanyahu] has been an outstanding Warrior Prime Minister!" Trump wrote. Trump said he and Netanyahu have had a strong relationship, "in winning together," referring to Operation Midnight Hammer and Operation Epic Fury. "Vote for Bibi Netanyahu for Prime Minister; we have to finish the job that we started!" Trump finished.Netanyahu pressures Trump for additional endorsementThis comes shortly after The Jerusalem Post reported that Netanyahu had intensified his efforts to secure additional support from Trump earlier on Sunday. Two American sources confirmed to the Post that Netanyahu and his supporters within Trump's inner circle were increasing pressure on the president to issue new statements of support. “We have never seen Netanyahu like this before. He is showing signs of political desperation,” they said.According to an earlier report published by Axios, Netanyahu and Trump have spoken twice over the past three days, and Netanyahu had even suggested possible wording for new endorsements. An Israeli source briefed on the efforts told Axios that the prime minister proposed having Trump speak with Israeli journalists to reiterate his support.Trump also suggested that the election of another candidate could have consequences for relations with the United States.“If Israel has the wrong leader, meaning anyone other than Bibi, America will have to do this job itself, and I'm not inclined to do that,” he wrote, referring to the confrontation with Iran.

title: Carney Visits Former Greek Orthodox Church Turned Mosque
body: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney visited a historic Byzantine Greek Orthodox church converted into a mosque during his trip to Turkey, as Ottawa and Ankara moved to strengthen defence, nuclear energy and trade cooperation amid strained relations between Canada and the United States. Carney visited the historic Church of the Holy Saviour in Chora in Istanbul on Saturday, October 24, accompanied by his wife, Diana Fox Carney. The building, now known as the Kariye Mosque, is renowned for its extraordinary Byzantine mosaics and frescoes and remains an important monument of Constantinople’s Christian heritage. Originally a Byzantine Greek Orthodox church, the monument was converted into a mosque following the Ottoman conquest of Constantinople in 1453. It was later used as a museum before returning to mosque use in 2020. The Canadian Prime Minister’s Office said the site was selected to highlight the importance of cultural heritage as a bridge between peoples and nations. The visit added a significant historical dimension to Carney’s trip, which focused primarily on expanding Canada’s strategic relationship with Turkey, including defence industry cooperation, energy security and trade. Canada and Turkey Establish Strategic Partnership Carney’s visit to Ankara on October 22 marked the first bilateral visit to Turkey by a Canadian prime minister. During talks with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, the two leaders launched a strategic partnership supported by a three-year action plan covering trade and investment, defence and security, energy, and people-to-people relations. The agreement reflects Ottawa’s efforts to diversify its international partnerships as trade tensions with Washington create pressure on Canada to reduce its reliance on the US market. Canada and Turkey are both NATO members, providing an established framework for cooperation on defence and wider security issues. The partnership is also intended to expand commercial opportunities for businesses in both countries, with particular attention to strategic industries and international investment. Defence Industry Cooperation Takes Centre Stage Defence cooperation is a central pillar of the new relationship. Canadian and Turkish officials signed an agreement on defence sector partnerships designed to connect companies in both countries and facilitate greater industrial collaboration. The initiative could create opportunities for joint projects, technology partnerships and expanded exports, although specific contracts and project details have yet to be announced. Turkey has developed a substantial domestic defence industry, while Canada is seeking to strengthen industrial capacity and diversify its international economic relationships. The two countries have also expressed an interest in expanding cooperation in aerospace and advanced technologies. For Ankara, closer ties with Canada could support its ambitions to expand defence exports and industrial partnerships. For Ottawa, the agreement provides another avenue to develop international commercial relationships within the NATO alliance. Nuclear Energy and Critical Minerals on the Agenda Energy cooperation is another major component of the partnership, with both governments identifying civil nuclear energy, liquefied natural gas, renewable energy and critical minerals as areas for closer engagement. A joint statement on energy cooperation is intended to encourage investment, strengthen supply chains and support collaboration between industry stakeholders. Canada has expertise in nuclear technology and uranium production, while Turkey is seeking to expand its energy infrastructure and diversify its energy sources. The two countries are also looking to develop cooperation in sustainable mining and critical minerals, resources that are increasingly important to advanced manufacturing, clean energy and defence industries. The announcements establish a framework for future cooperation rather than confirming specific nuclear construction contracts or investment commitments. Trade Target Reaches $10 Billion Ambition Canada and Turkey have set ambitious goals for expanding their commercial relationship. Turkish President Erdogan said the countries aim to increase bilateral trade from approximately $3 billion to $5 billion, with a longer-term target of $10 billion. The governments are also advancing negotiations towards a comprehensive free trade agreement, with the first round of talks scheduled to take place in Ankara from November 30 to December 4, 2026. An agreement could create new opportunities across energy, mining, aerospace, manufacturing and defence, depending on the final terms negotiated. The partnership also includes expanded air transport arrangements intended to improve connectivity between the two countries, support tourism and facilitate commercial activity. Canada’s two-way merchandise trade with Turkey reached $4.3 billion in 2025, according to the Canadian government, demonstrating an existing economic relationship that both sides want to expand. Canada Looks Beyond Its Traditional Trade Relationships The new partnership comes as Carney seeks to strengthen Canada’s economic resilience amid tensions with Washington over trade and tariffs. The United States remains Canada’s dominant trading partner, making diversification a significant challenge for Ottawa. Turkey offers access to a large domestic market and a strategic position connecting Europe, Asia and the Middle East. However, expanding trade with Ankara will require more than diplomatic agreements. The success of the partnership will depend on whether businesses establish new commercial relationships, investment commitments materialise and free trade negotiations produce a workable agreement. The two governments have now established a framework for cooperation spanning defence, energy, investment and transport. Historic Greek Orthodox Church Now Functions as a Mosque Carney’s visit to the Kariye Mosque brings renewed attention to the fate of one of Constantinople’s most important Byzantine Greek Orthodox churches. The Church of the Holy Saviour in Chora was built as a Christian place of worship and became renowned for its extraordinary mosaics and frescoes depicting Christ, the Virgin Mary and scenes from Christian tradition. Historic Greek Orthodox Church Now Functions as a Mosque Following the Ottoman conquest of Constantinople in 1453, the church was converted into a mosque. It was later turned into a museum before being reconverted into a mosque in 2020. Carney Visits Former Greek Orthodox Church Turned Mosque Although the building’s extraordinary Byzantine artwork remains a testament to its Christian past, its conversion has raised wider questions about the preservation and religious identity of historic Christian monuments in Turkey. For Greeks and Orthodox Christians, the church represents a tangible connection to the Byzantine heritage of Constantinople, a city that stood at the centre of Greek Orthodox Christianity for centuries. Carney’s visit took place as Canada and Turkey sought closer defence, energy and trade ties. However, the historic site also stands as a reminder that diplomatic engagement with modern Turkey exists alongside a difficult history involving the transformation of some of the most significant monuments of Byzantine Christianity. title: Institute moves to boost local content in Nigeria
body: The Nigerian Institute of Mechanical Engineers (NIMechE) has called for the enhancement of the relationship between engineering and national security as well as boost local production of facilities in thd country Engr. Dr. Babagana Modu Tela, the NIMechE National Chairman, stated this in his welcome address at the 39th International Conference, Exhibition and Annual General Meeting in Abuja recently He said the theme of this year’s conference “Mechanical Engineers as Catalysts of Innovation for Enhanced Security and Sustainable National Development” is timely and strategic because engineering is fundamentally about solving problems. While calling on mechanical engineers to build a profession where young Nigerians can confidently say “I can design, manufacture, and improve it”, he said the 2026 conference is a platform for knowledge exchange, professional networking, technology transfer and institutional collaboration. Engr. Dr. Babagana Modu Tela said mechanical engineers have the responsibility of contributing professionally and ethically to the development of technologies that strengthen national resilience while supporting peaceful and sustainable development. He said “we must also encourage collaboration among government, academia, industry and professional institutions so that engineering knowledge can be effectively converted into solutions that address real national needs”. NSE President, Engr. Ali Alimasuya Rabiu, in his message, said engineering has a vital role to play in contributing to the development, adaptation and mainteningof engineering machinery towards national security.

title: NPFL: Bendel Insurance end Rivers United’s unbeaten run as Southwest derby ends in stalemate
body:
Rivers United suffered their first defeat of the 2026/27 Nigeria Premier Football League (NPFL) season on Sunday, losing 2-1 to Bendel Insurance at the Samuel Ogbemudia Stadium in Benin City.
Despite the setback, the Port Harcourt club retained top spot with 17 points and a goal difference of +10 after 10 matchdays. Rangers International and Nasarawa United are also on 17 points, in second and third, with goal differences of +5 and +3, respectively. Rangers, however, have two games in hand due to continental commitments.
Plateau United sit fourth with 15 points, keeping the race for the top positions closely contested.
At the Samuel Ogbemudia Stadium, Freeman Wuchirwe opened the scoring for Bendel Insurance in the 48th minute before Chijioke Mbaoma equalised for Rivers United in the 73rd minute.
Mbaoma finished calmly after Shola Oladunjoye played a precise through ball behind the Bendel defence. However, Jonathan James scored in the 89th minute to secure victory for the hosts and end Rivers United’s nine-match unbeaten run.
Rivers United goalkeeper Clinton Andy had produced three point-blank saves in a goalless first half, but the visitors could not prevent the late winner.
In another Matchday 10 fixture, Ikorodu City and Shooting Stars drew 2-2.
Shooting Stars took an early lead through Taofeek Otaniyi in the third minute before Desmond Ojietefian doubled their advantage in the 36th minute.
Donald Obiajulu pulled one back for Ikorodu City in the 44th minute before completing his brace later in the match to earn the hosts a point.
Barau FC and Kwara United also shared the points in a 1-1 draw. Anthony Sunday scored for Barau before Goodluck Ogbolu equalised for Kwara United in the 63rd minute.
Nasarawa United strengthened their position among the leading teams with a 1-0 victory over Enyimba, courtesy of Jofrank Istifanus’ 23rd-minute goal.
Niger Tornadoes defeated Abia Warriors 1-0 in Aba, with Wasiu Jimoh scoring in the 56th minute.
Kun Khalifat FC also secured a 1-0 win over Inter Lagos, while Wolves and Kano Pillars played out a goalless draw.
Rivers United remain top with 17 points, but their defeat leaves them level on points with Rangers International and Nasarawa United. Rivers United hold the advantage on goal difference, while Rangers have two games in hand.
Plateau United occupy fourth place with 15 points, keeping pressure on the leading trio.
At the other end of the table, Abia Warriors sit 17th with 10 points. Ranchers Bees and Enyimba International occupy 18th and 19th positions, respectively, with eight points each. Enyimba have the poorer goal difference at -4, compared with Ranchers Bees’ -3.
Inter Lagos remain bottom in 20th place with two points following a three-point and three-goal deduction for an infraction.
Rivers United will seek to return to winning ways when they host Rangers International at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium in Port Harcourt on Sunday, 1 November.
The encounter offers the league leaders an immediate opportunity to respond to their first defeat against one of their closest rivals.
Tunde Eludini is a graduate of the Obafemi Awolowo University Ile-Ife, Nigeria where he studied International Relations. He is a Senior Correspondent coordinating the sports section for PREMIUM TIMES. Twitter : @tundeyeludini
