title: ‘An instruction to permit the commission of a crime’ – Prof Appiagyei-Atua challenges mining directive
body: A Professor of International Law and Human Rights at the University of Ghana School of Law has challenged a mining directive described by the GoldBod CEO as permitting criminal conduct. Prof Kwadwo Appiagyei-Atua, in an opinion article, rejected the suggestion that people without licences could mine in certain locations while awaiting registration. “So the instruction described is an instruction to permit the commission of a crime carrying, for a Ghanaian, a mandatory minimum of fifteen years,” he stated. The criticism follows comments by the GoldBod CEO about allowing miners to operate outside water bodies, forest reserves and other restricted locations. “Once it’s not a water body; it’s not a forest reserve or… place like a roadside, whether the person has a licence or not; the government says we should allow the person to mine and register and regularise them,” the CEO said. Prof Appiagyei-Atua argued that this approach reverses the legal requirements for mining. “The law permits: register first, then mine. The statement describes mining first, then registering.” Citing sections 9 and 82 of the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006, the professor said mining requires statutory authorisation. Ownership of the land does not remove that requirement. The article argues that the minister’s authority to grant licences does not include permission to operate without one. “A ministerial or administrative direction that unlicensed persons ‘should be allowed to mine’ is therefore ultra vires,” Prof Appiagyei-Atua said. The professor also challenged the emphasis on location. The article says operating outside a river, forest reserve or roadside does not remove environmental permitting requirements. “A site that is neither a water body nor a forest reserve nor a roadside is still unlawful to mine without an environmental permit,” he said. However, Prof Kwadwo Appiagyei-Atua distinguished formalisation from allowing unlicensed activity. The article supports lawful measures to bring artisanal and small-scale miners into the regulatory system. It identifies fast-track registration, designated mining areas and district-level licensing support as possible routes. The professor stressed that the objection concerns the order in which mining and licensing occur. “Regularisation cannot retroactively cure a completed offence,” Prof Kwadwo Appiagyei-Atua said. The article also warns that miners who rely on an official assurance could remain exposed to prosecution. “The Goldbod CEO’s assurance is no defence to the miner,” he emphasised. Beyond miners’ liability, the professor argues that officials who facilitate unlawful operations could face legal consequences, including possible liability for abetment. The article ends with a call for lawful resistance to illegal mining. “We must take all legal action to resist galamsey,” Prof Kwadwo Appiagyei-Atua said.

title: NFF Hails Alex Iwobi on another Milestone in Premier League
body: The Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) has celebrated Super Eagles’ midfield ace Alexander Iwobi on his new milestone of becoming the joint-second most-capped African football player in the English Premiership, alongside Egyptian icon Mohamed Salah. Iwobi, who celebrated his 100th cap for Nigeria during this summer’s friendly match with Portugal at the Estádio Dr. Magalhães Pessoa in Leiria, has now featured in 328 matches in the English Premier League. Acting General Secretary of the NFF, Dr Emmanuel Ikpeme MON, congratulated Iwobi on his latest accomplishment. “The NFF celebrates Alex Iwobi for this new achievement and we wish him even greater glory. We will be very happy to see him become the African with the most appearances in the Premier League in the near future,” prayed Dr Ikpeme. The 30-year-old, who has won silver and two bronze medals with Nigeria at the Africa Cup of Nations, achieved the latest milestone when he featured for his English Premiership club Fulham in their 1-0 win over Coventry City on Saturday. The game was his 328th appearance in the EPL, taking him joint-second with Salah, and 25 games more to match the all-time record holder, Ivorian Kolo Toure. Ivorian legend Toure played a total of 353 matches in the EPL – widely regarded as the biggest and most glamorous football league in the world. In the match with Coventry, the Nigerian superstar had 60 touches on the ball in his 73-minute appearance, during which he made 51 passes, and accomplished 86.3% passing accuracy.

title: Tinubu, Fashola, NESG, Governors, Others Headline Day One of National Grassroots Sports Summit
body: The stage is being set for a landmark gathering at the Presidential Villa as President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Raji Fashola, SAN, and leading figures from government, sports administration and international development feature in the proposed opening-day programme of the National Grassroots Sports Development Summit 2026. The two-day Summit, scheduled for November 18–19, 2026, at the Banquet Hall, State House, Presidential Villa, Abuja, is being organised by the Office of the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Grassroots Sports Development, Hon. Adeyinka Anthony Adeboye. With the theme “Creating a New Pathway for Sustainable Grassroots Sports Development,” the gathering seeks to produce practical solutions to Nigeria’s longstanding challenges in talent discovery, infrastructure, funding, coaching and athlete development. The opening day, Wednesday, November 18, promises high-level engagement, with President Tinubu listed as Special Guest of Honour, while Fashola is scheduled to deliver a keynote address. Also featuring in the Day One programme is Dr. Tayo Aduloju, Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian Economic Summit Group (NESG), whose organisation has been engaged as technical partner to help translate discussions into a workable development roadmap. Other personalities and institutions on the opening-day lineup include the Chairman and Director-General of the National Sports Commission, Mallam Shehu Dikko and Hon. Bukola Olopade; the Chairman of the Nigeria Governors’ Forum; the President of the Association of Local Governments of Nigeria (ALGON); and the Head of Office and UNESCO Representative to Nigeria. Also listed are Barrister Enitan Oshodi, President of the African Table Tennis Federation; the President of the Nigeria Olympic Committee, Engr Habu Gumel; and Dr. Musa Nakorji of the Central Bank of Nigeria’s Research Department. The involvement of these personalities reflects the Summit’s emphasis on connecting sports development with economic planning, education, grassroots governance, international cooperation and private-sector investment. Adeboye described the gathering as an opportunity to move Nigerian sports beyond isolated achievements towards a coordinated national development system. He stressed that the participation of state governments, local councils, development institutions and sports administrators would be critical to producing lasting outcomes. The Summit will continue on Thursday, November 19, with further stakeholder engagements aimed at developing actionable recommendations for sustainable grassroots sports development.

title: Simple NetBSD webserver
body:
There might be time you want to have a sensible space in that untangible mess that is modern World Wide Web. The choices run slim and at some point there are ~three operating systems that you can trust having on your server[^1].
I'll describe here the quick and proven route for running a NetBSD 11 web server - the 'stock' way with bozohttpd that requires only one additional package for HTTPS[^2]. It probably won't do if you expect heavy traffic, but for homebrew projects and small scale communities it should do just fine.
A VPS (or local machine or virtual machine) and a terminal emulator.
Maybe web-browser to check the results (though curl is quite sufficient for that imo).
I'm not affiliated but as far as recommendations go - I'm using netcup service, it looks okay. Not expensive and they already have NetBSD11 amd64 iso preloaded in their OS library to install OS on your machine.
There are others people recommend for netbsd:
If you can recommend or suggest even more - please email me, I'll add it to the list list.
NetBSD has a small web-server that is sufficient for tons of stuff right out of the box - bozohttpd(8) . It is somewhat limited by design, but the manpage is quite useful and describes a lot of interesting stuff you can do with just marker files and simple command line options.
Some guides out there explain a path to run it using inetd(8) , it is kinda native internet "super-server" for unix but I didn't like that it launches an instance of httpd (alias/hardlink to bozohttpd) on every connection. Bozohttpd is capable running as daemon itself, I like that option.
The only config httpd needs lies in command line options, which can be nicely wrapped in /etc/rc.conf with self-explanatory keys like this:
If you have something in /var/www/my_magical_domain/index.html , then after simple /etc/rc.d/httpd start voila - you already have it served via plain http. Simple as that.
I won't explain usage of self-signed procedure, instead resorting to one of the most popular freeware certificate issuer on the internet - letsencrypt.
There are several methods of obtaining the certificates from them, I'm using acme-client package (installed via pkgin ) - it is a portable version of an openbsd tool, I'm most used to it.
We need couple more directories to expose our challenge and to keep the certificates on. Try to not use "4" as a private key - it's been exposed recently, stick with prime numbers at least :)
And we need a config file for our domain - /usr/pkg/etc/acme-client.conf :
Running acme-client my_magical_domain should do the trick and put the neccessary certs to their corresponding paths. Do not forget to wait for at least few hours after putting your vps IP address into domain A record - it has to be propagated everywhere properly and resolve for letsencrypt as well.
Afterwards we have to pass the keys to the bozohttpd, and that enables it serving the port 443 automatically. So an addition to /etc/rc.conf should look like this:
Restart httpd and Bob's your uncle - we have a working web server showing whatever static files you put into the directory.
Now there is one more thing to that - Letsencrypt certificates expire after certain amount of time, so we have to renew them using same acme-client(1) program. The simplest way to do so would be a cronjob - daily or even weekly - that tries to update the certificate and then restarts the httpd, via crontab(5) :
Despite being spartan Bozotic httpd supports some interesting features like virtual hosts (you can serve each domain bound to your IP from different directory), CGI and http basic authorization .
Another interesting feature I'd like to try out sometime is native Lua scripting .
URL rewrites also looks promising - especially when coupled with CGI to seamlessly provide some feedback and interactivity (visitors' count haha).
bozohttpd(8) manpage contains quite a lot of useful info, don't forget to check it out.
[^1]: Obviously other than netbsd there is 9front and templeos, though latter lacks the network support (and therefore absolutely superior to everything else).
[^2]: The external tool is not needed if you want to run plain http or use self-signed certificate.

title: Nigeria Judo Federation Assures Stakeholders of Fair Electoral Process
body: The Caretaker Committee of the Nigeria Judo Federation (NJF) has reaffirmed its commitment to conducting a transparent, credible and inclusive electoral process, while maintaining its independence and neutrality in the discharge of its transitional responsibilities. In a statement issued by the Committee Chairman, Sheriff Hammed, the Committee clarified its position following recent public comments and reports concerning its activities and mandate. The Committee emphasised that although it operates under the authority granted by the National Sports Commission (NSC), it remains fully committed to acting independently, fairly and in the best interests of Nigerian judo. “The Caretaker Committee is not a mouthpiece for any individual, group or interest, nor is it a platform for advancing personal or political agendas,” the statement said. The Committee acknowledged that it has received information and concerns regarding the conduct of certain individuals associated with the former Board. However, it stressed that allegations, personal interests or preconceived positions will not be permitted to influence the electoral process. According to the statement, the principles of transparency, fairness, due process and equal opportunity will continue to guide all decisions and actions of the Committee throughout the transition period. To ensure a level playing field, the Committee confirmed that all qualified and interested aspirants are welcome to obtain nomination forms and contest in the forthcoming elections, provided they meet the eligibility requirements outlined in the NJF Statutes and other applicable governance regulations. The Committee further assured stakeholders that no candidate would be unfairly excluded on the basis of personal disagreements, affiliations or considerations outside the established rules. At the same time, it warned against any attempts to disrupt, manipulate or undermine the electoral process, noting that any individual found, through a fair and transparent procedure, to have violated applicable regulations or compromised the integrity of the process may face appropriate sanctions, including disqualification where legally justified. The Committee called on all stakeholders, including state associations, athletes, coaches, referees and members of the judo community, to support a peaceful, transparent and orderly transition.

title: Real Madrid Thump Barcelona in Dramatic El Clásico
body: Marvelous David Real Madrid secured a dramatic 2-1 victory over Barcelona in Sunday’s El Clásico at the Camp Nou with Kylian Mbappé scoring the decisive goal to hand the visitors a crucial win in the La Liga title race. Mbappé opened the scoring shortly before half-time, giving Real Madrid the advantage after a tense first half in which both sides struggled to create clear chances. The French forward benefited from a defensive clearance that deflected off him and ended up in the net. Barcelona responded strongly after the break and found an equaliser through Raphinha in the 61st minute. The Brazilian winger finished confidently after receiving a cleverly disguised pass from Pedri, bringing the home supporters back to life. The hosts pushed for a winner and came close when Gerard Martín attempted a header from a corner, but Real Madrid goalkeeper Andriy Lunin produced an excellent save to keep the visitors in the game. Real Madrid remained dangerous on the counterattack, using their pace to trouble Barcelona’s defence. Their persistence paid off late in the match when Mbappé struck again in the 87th minute and a beautiful assist from Camavinga to restore Madrid’s lead and seal all three points. The victory marked an important result for Real Madrid, strengthening their position in the title race and reducing the gap on their fierce rivals. For Barcelona, the defeat ended their perfect start to the La Liga season and highlighted defensive weaknesses they will need to address. The result also gave Madrid a major psychological boost in one of football’s most fiercely contested rivalries, with both teams expected to remain strong contenders for the Spanish league title.

title: Student-Led Movement Ends Serbian President’s 14 Year Rule
body: Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat on Sunday night after a historic election in which a movement born out of student protests challenged his 14-year rule, ushering in a new political era for Serbia. Celebrations erupted across Belgrade following Vucic’s announcement, as cars sounded their horns and students chanted “victory” and “it’s over”. Authorities called the snap election after nearly two years of student-led protests against corruption. The demonstrations began following the deaths of 16 people when the roof of a railway station in Novi Sad collapsed in 2024. “Dear Serbia, tonight the people’s voice was heard,” said Radomir Sajcic, a professor at the University of Belgrade, speaking on behalf of the students at the movement’s headquarters. “Tonight we celebrate victory; tomorrow we build the future,” he added. Voter turnout reached nearly 70%, marking the highest participation recorded since the breakup of the former Yugoslavia in 1992. Long queues formed outside polling stations, reflecting widespread demand for political change. “It is clear that we lost these elections. The Student List won. They will have 135–140 seats, while we will have 105. No one else will enter parliament,” Vucic said, referring to preliminary results. A representative sample from polling firm CESID-IPSPS projected that the Student List would secure 138 parliamentary seats, while Vucic’s Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) would win 104. Minority parties would share the remaining seats. “Unbelievable joy and happiness, and we have finally got rid of this mafia. I am so happy that I cannot speak,” said a woman named Tania as she celebrated the results on the streets of Belgrade. title: Footage Shows Ukrainian T-64 Tanks Destroyed on Frontlines
body: Footage circulating online on October 25 has shown the destruction of Ukrainian T-64 main battle tanks during combat operations. The video was reportedly filmed by Russian forces, although details concerning the precise location, circumstances of the engagement and unit responsible for the tank’s destruction have not been independently established. The T-64 has remained a central component of Ukraine’s tank fleet since the country inherited large numbers of the vehicles following the disintegration of the Soviet Union in 1991. Originally developed at the Kharkiv Design Bureau, the tank was prized for its lower maintenance needs and operational costs than the more advanced T-80, and for its higher mobility than the newer but much cheaper T-72. Although T-64s formed the backbone of the Ukrainian fleet up to 2022, considerable attrition has resulted in the T-72 now playing a more prominent role as these have been donated from abroad on a large scale. Ukrainain Army personnel have repeatedly stated that they have been forced to operate tanks further from the frontlines due to their vulnerability to Russian strikes. While this particularly applies to Western tanks such as the U.S. M1 Abrams, due to their much larger profiles and higher crew requirements, it also applies to a certain extent to tanks like the T-64 which are much easier to conceal. Although the fleet is largely obsolete, the limited number of tank-on-tank engagements in the Ukrainain theatres, and the emphasis both sides have placed on using tanks for infantry support, has allowed the T-64 to play a significant role in the conflict. The T-64’s high maintenance needs are thought to have contributed to the Ukrainian Army’s difficulties with availability. As revealed by Ukrainian armoured warfare specialist Mykola Salamakha, currently only a third, and in some cases just a fifth, of the Army’s tanks are considered combat-ready.

title: The Greek F-16 Fighter Pilot Leading The Air Display For October 28 Parade
body: Greek Air Force Squadron Leader Christos-Paris Charitos will pilot the Zeus demonstration team’s F-16 fighter during Greece’s October 28 national anniversary parade in Thessaloniki, following a final rehearsal flight scheduled for Monday, October 26. Charitos, who has logged more than 1,900 flight hours, including over 1,500 in F-16 aircraft, will perform the aerial demonstration that has become a highlight of the annual celebrations. According to the current schedule, he will also conduct a rehearsal flight over Thessaloniki’s waterfront at around noon on Monday, an event that attracts large crowds. A childhood dream of flying for Greece “Becoming a pilot in the Hellenic Air Force was my childhood dream, and I am very grateful that I achieved it,” Charitos told the Athens-Macedonian News Agency’s radio station, Praktoreio 104.9FM, in 2023, shortly before his first October 28 parade flight. He explained that the profession demands dedication, extensive training and long working hours, but also offers substantial rewards to those who love the job. Charitos entered the Hellenic Air Force Academy in 2006 and joined the 115th Combat Wing in 2012, where he flew F-16 Block 52+ aircraft. He currently serves with the 340 Squadron and has become a key member of the Zeus demonstration team, representing the Hellenic Air Force at air shows in Greece and abroad. He also flew over Thessaloniki during the October 28 celebrations in 2023, when he first took on the demonstration role for a national anniversary. Following this year’s parade, spectators will watch a powerful F-16 Viper streak across the waterfront before executing a series of dramatic manoeuvres. The fighter’s thunderous roar, rapid changes of direction and steep climbs routinely draw the attention of crowds and prompt spontaneous applause. During the display, the aircraft may climb vertically with its afterburner engaged, producing a bright glow at the engine nozzle as the pilot applies maximum thrust. For several minutes, the F-16 demonstrates its agility and performance, while the pilot maintains precise control throughout the manoeuvres. Precision under extreme pressure Flying a demonstration requires exceptional concentration, extensive preparation and virtually no margin for error. Charitos explained in 2023 that pilots have little time to think about anything outside the manoeuvre they are performing. The team prepares through intensive training and repeated flights, while pilots mentally rehearse the demonstration before executing it. Once airborne, they rely on that preparation to perform each manoeuvre with consistent accuracy. The live cockpit footage broadcast during the October 28 celebrations will once again give audiences on the waterfront and watching television a glimpse of the flight. However, the images offer little indication of the physical strain that pilots experience during high-performance manoeuvres. The aircraft’s rapid turns and climbs expose the pilot to powerful gravitational forces, known as G-forces, which demand constant concentration. The pilot’s specialised anti-G suit automatically applies pressure at the appropriate moments to help maintain blood flow to the brain and vital organs. Throughout the demonstration, the pilot must maintain complete situational awareness, processing the aircraft’s position and performance while executing manoeuvres developed through years of training. “Normal missions and what you do during a flight demonstration with the Zeus team are two completely different things,” Charitos said in autumn 2023. He added that the team was delighted to perform its mission in Greece and abroad. Flying for the country Charitos has said that flying the F-16 Block 52+ was a long-held ambition. When the opportunity arose to join the demonstration team, based at Souda Air Base in Crete, he embraced the chance. He has described his role in the Zeus cockpit as another mission for his country, reflecting the dedication and discipline behind one of the Hellenic Air Force’s most recognisable public displays. title: Okonjo-Iweala loses mother, as Tinubu mourns
body: ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has extended his heartfelt condolences to the Okonjo royal family of Ogwashi-Uku, Delta State, on the passing of Prof. Kamene Okonjo, who died at the age of 96. Prof. Okonjo was a distinguished scholar, a champion of women’s empowerment, and a revered matriarch. The President particularly commiserated with her daughter, Dr Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, Director-General of the World Trade Organisation, other family members, and the people of Ogwashi-Uku over the loss of their beloved mother, matriarch, and community leader. President Tinubu described Prof. Okonjo’s passing as the loss of an accomplished academic whose life was defined by intellectual distinction, service to humanity, and an enduring commitment to advancing women and society. He acknowledged her contributions to scholarship and her inspiring example as a woman who combined professional excellence with dedication to family, community, and the preservation of traditional institutions. The President prayed that Almighty God will grant the departed eternal rest and comfort the family and all who mourn her passing. Vanguard reports that Kamene Okonjo, a professor of sociology and advocate for women’s rights, died on Friday, according to reports citing a statement issued by the Umu Obi Obahai royal family of Ogwashi-Uku kingdom in Delta state. Okonjo-Iweala, in a post on X on Sunday, thanked friends and followers for their messages of condolence and support to her family. “Today, I have been overwhelmed with messages of condolences and tributes to my wonderful mother. “I just want to thank all my friends and followers and let you know how appreciative my entire family and I are of your support. “My mother lived a quality life till the end and we are very grateful we had her for so long. May her soul rest in perfect peace.” She wrote The post Okonjo-Iweala loses mother, as Tinubu mourns appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Einhorn's consulting firm paid Urich over NIS 1 million for work with foreign countries - report
body: Yonatan Urich, a senior aide and personal media adviser to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and a central suspect in the "Qatargate" investigations, received NIS 1.19 million in 2024 for work for foreign clients, KAN News reported Sunday evening.According to KAN, Urich received additional payments from Perception Media, a consulting firm owned by Israel (Srulik) Einhorn, while officially serving as an external adviser to the prime minister.His work for foreign countries included projects related to Qatar.Investigative materials show that Urich received NIS 1.19 million between January and September 2024. The payments included NIS 68,000 in January, NIS 178,000 in February, NIS 99,000 in March, NIS 79,000 in April, and NIS 206,000 in May. Three additional payments of NIS 178,000 each were made in August and September.KAN reported that Urich was not subject to a conflict-of-interest arrangement, nor was his work subject to a security review. While Judge Mizrahi generally accepted Urich's position regarding his status as an external adviser, Judge Michels raised concerns about the matter.Netanyahu held secret meeting with ex-Mossad official implicated in Qatargate affairMeanwhile, N12 News reported on Sunday evening that Netanyahu held a secret meeting several months after October 7 with a former senior Mossad official suspected of involvement in the Qatargate affair.The former official is believed to be the most senior Israeli involved in Qatar's influence operation in Israel. The meeting, held in the summer of 2024, does not appear in the prime minister's official schedules.According to the report, the former official asked Netanyahu during the meeting to rein in harsh statements made by some government ministers against Qatar. At the time, Netanyahu and other government ministers had taken a tough stance toward Qatar, while the former official was working to promote Qatari interests in Israel.After leaving the Mossad, the former official began pursuing business interests involving Qatar. He was involved in the country's World Cup project and continued to develop his business activities after October 7.As part of these activities, he is suspected of helping arrange meetings between Urich and Einhorn and Ali al-Thawadi, a senior Qatari official close to the emir.Those involved also met in London, Paris, and Berlin to discuss their joint project, "Lighthouse," which eventually became an effort to improve Qatar's image.Lahav 433 suspects Urich helped coordinate meetingsInvestigators from the National Unit for International Investigations at Lahav 433 suspect that Urich, who worked in the Prime Minister's Office and was also involved in the Qatari project, helped coordinate the meeting between Netanyahu and the former senior Mossad official.During questioning, Urich denied being asked to arrange the meeting or being approached by the former official to coordinate meetings with the prime minister.Last week, it emerged that Urich and Einhorn were involved in preparing political messaging for Romania's AUR party, whose senior members have faced accusations of antisemitism and Holocaust denial.According to a report by Romanian investigative website Snoop, Einhorn sent Urich a document outlining campaign topics for the party on August 31, and Urich approved its contents.Einhorn later sent a communications plan in Romanian that included proposed social media posts, images, a website article, and a video script.The campaign targeted Romanian President Nicușor Dan and coalition leaders, using the message "120 days without a government."According to the report, some of the messages discussed in the correspondence began appearing in official party publications and on social media accounts belonging to party politicians on September 2.The investigation found that the messages raised concerns about the potential loss of European funding and the uncertainty facing teachers and doctors, among other issues.Einhorn also recommended avoiding the use of images of party leader George Simion because of criticism over AUR's role in bringing down the government.Party spokesperson Ștefan Avrămescu was among those who subsequently published similar messages.

title: USS Pinckney undergoes upgrade with U.S. Navy’s first SPY-6(V)4 radar installation
body: The work marks the second phase of the Arleigh Burke-class ship’s upgrades under the Destroyer Modernization 2.0 program. The radar will be integrated with Aegis Combat System Baseline 10, while the new cooling plants will help support the combat systems’ electrical and thermal requirements. “The collective effort by all stakeholders has finally brought us to the point of execution,” said Capt. Tim Moore, program manager for DDG MOD 2.0. “Upon Depot Modernization Period completion, USS Pinckney will rejoin the Fleet equipped with the most comprehensive multi-spectral integrated sensor suite designed to maintain maritime superiority for decades to come.” Pinckney completed its earlier modernization period, designated DMP 1.5, in 2024. It became the first warship to receive the SLQ-32(V)7 Surface Electronic Warfare Improvement Program system and sponson modifications. The Navy adopted a phased installation approach, called Split Start, to build experience across its industry partners. Pinckney deployed to the Pacific and Middle East after completing the earlier work. The Navy said the deployment validated the ship’s advanced warfare capabilities in contested operational environments. The destroyer has now returned for the radar and cooling installations that form the next stage of its modernization.

title: Nigeria buys Aksungur, CH-4D Drones and Six More T-129 Helicopters
body: According to Unmanned Africa , the Nigerian Air Force (NAF) is planning to add more than the 12 Turkish Aksungur combat drones it has already named. Beyond the TUSAŞ aircraft, the service has announced the planned acquisition of two Chinese CH-4D unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and six additional T129 ATAK attack helicopters from Turkish Aerospace Industries (TAI), as part of a modernisation drive that has accelerated through 2026. The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has named a new aircraft type in its forward plans. In an infographic posted to its official X account on Sunday, 25 October 2026, the service listed 12 TUSAŞ Aksungur unmanned combat aerial vehicles among its “additional expected aircraft,” alongside other platforms planned for the force. If the plan goes ahead, Nigeria would become one of a small group of African air forces to operate one of Turkey’s largest armed drones. The graphic appeared on the same day the NAF’s Director of Public Relations and Information, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, issued a statement marking the first anniversary of the Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, on 30 October. That statement reported more than 6,100 flying hours and over 2,900 sorties between November 2025 and September 2026. It described a broader acquisition programme that includes 12 Bell AH-1Z attack helicopters and “other planned aircraft and unmanned aerial systems” for airlift, combat, training, and intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR). Two CH-4Ds to Sustain a Chinese Drone Line Nigeria’s relationship with the CASC Rainbow series is more than a decade old. The NAF has flown the CH-3A since about 2014. In October and November 2020, the Chief of the Air Staff at the time, Air Marshal Sadique Abubakar, disclosed that the NAF would receive eight Chinese unmanned aircraft: two Wing Loong II, four CH-4, and two CH-3. He said about 70 personnel had been nominated for training in China, and that the drones would be based at Gusau, Gombe, and the Operation Lafiya Dole headquarters in Maiduguri. Reports in February 2021 suggested the NAF was negotiating for six more CH-4 aircraft. Attrition has been part of that history. On 2 January 2026, the NAF lost a CH-4 near Kontagora in Niger State. The service said it secured and recovered the airframe quickly, and that technical teams began preliminary evaluations. Military Africa reported on the loss at the time. Two new CH-4Ds would not restore the fleet to a large size, but they would offset losses in a type the air force has trained crews, ground stations, and maintainers for. The CH-4 was introduced in 2011 and entered Chinese service in 2014. The CH-4B variant that Nigeria operates has a wingspan of about 18 metres and a length of about 8.5 metres. Published figures give it a maximum take-off weight of 1,330 kilograms, a payload capacity of 345 kilograms, and a standard endurance of up to 30 hours, with claims of up to 40 hours in some configurations. It carries electro-optical and infrared sensors with a laser rangefinder and designator, and it can carry up to six weapons. Aksungur, a domestically produced medium-altitude, long-endurance unmanned combat aerial vehicle (UCAV) developed by Turkish Aerospace Industries (TAI) The “D” suffix indicates a newer sub-variant. Janes has reported that CASC developed improved CH-3, CH-4, and CH-5 versions, including a CH-4D, with better range and speed, higher altitude, and larger weapons payloads. Detailed specifications for the CH-4D have not been published in the sources reviewed. Whether Nigeria’s two aircraft would be the improved variant or a description used in the announcement, the NAF has not said. Six More T129 ATAKs The T129 plan is easier to place in context. Nigeria ordered six T129 ATAK helicopters in July 2022. The first two arrived in November 2023 and were inducted at Makurdi on 6 February 2024, at a ceremony attended by Vice President Kashim Shettima. The second batch of two arrived on 3 September 2024 aboard a Turkish Air Force A400M. Military Africa covered that delivery . Open-source trackers now list all six as received. The helicopter has a 20 mm cannon and can carry 70 mm rocket pods, UMTAS anti-tank missiles, Cirit laser-guided rockets, and Stinger air-to-air missiles. After induction, the first two were assigned to the 115th Special Operations Group in Port Harcourt. The NAF has used the type in its counter-insurgency and counter-banditry operations, alongside its older Mi-35 gunships. Six additional aircraft would double the fleet. That matters because attack helicopters are limited by availability, not just by numbers. A fleet of six, once training, maintenance, and attrition are accounted for, often puts two or three aircraft in the air on a given day. A fleet of twelve gives commanders more flexibility to cover the North-East and North-West at the same time. Earlier reporting shows the plan has changed shape before. In February 2024, one report spoke of 12 T129s on order, while later reports gave six, so the “additional six” in the current plan may revive an earlier larger figure. One published account listed a unit price of 45 million dollars, while another says six were acquired for 45 million dollars in total. These cannot both be right, and neither is confirmed, so no price for the new helicopters is given here. A Fleet of Many Suppliers Taken together with the Aksungur, the new items reinforce a pattern. The NAF is buying from China, Turkey, the United States, Italy, Brazil, and Pakistan at once. The JF-17 Thunder came from Pakistan, the A-29 Super Tucano from Brazil, the M-346 aircraft from Italy, and the AH-1Z Viper helicopters from the United States. The Turkish T129 and Chinese CH-4 sit in that mix, and the Aksungur would join them. The benefit is that Nigeria is not dependent on one government’s export approvals. The cost is logistics. Each supplier brings separate spare parts, training courses, weapons, and software, and the NAF must keep all of them current. The October statement from the service’s spokesman, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, reflects this effort: five helicopters delivered in September 2026 ( three AW-109 Trekker Type B and two H125 ), six L-39ZA jets reactivated and upgraded in Slovakia and Nigeria, and a C-130 undergoing periodic depot maintenance in Portugal. The statement also lists 12 AH-1Z attack helicopters on the acquisition list. The numbers behind the push are large. The statement says the NAF flew more than 6,100 hours and over 2,900 sorties between November 2025 and September 2026, using close to 10 million litres of Jet A-1 fuel. Nigeria ranks third in Africa and 33rd globally in the 2026 Global Firepower Index, down from 31st the year before. What to Watch in the Coming Months The first question is whether any of these aircraft appear in a signed contract. The NAF has a record of announcing expected aircraft, and not all of them have arrived as planned, so the list is best read as intent. The second is the integration of Chinese and Turkish unmanned aircraft into one operating system. The CH-4D and the Aksungur have different data links, ground stations, and weapons, and an air force that runs both needs trained crews and separate support for each. The third is the safeguards that come with armed aircraft. The NAF’s statement says it is building civilian harm mitigation structures, an operational and safety audit committee, and a planned open-source intelligence centre. More armed drones and attack helicopters make those systems more important. The fourth is serviceability. New aircraft add value only if they fly. The CH-4 loss in January and the long reactivation programmes for older jets show how much of the NAF’s modernisation depends on maintenance as much as on purchasing.

title: Officials could face abetment liability for allowing unlicensed mining – Prof Appiagyei-Atua on GoldBod CEO’s comment
body: Officials who direct that unlicensed mining be allowed could face liability for abetting a criminal offence, Professor Appiagyei-Atua has warned. The Professor of International Law and Human Rights at the University of Ghana School of Law raised the concern in an opinion article responding to comments attributed to the Chief Executive Officer of GoldBod. The CEO had suggested that miners operating outside certain restricted locations should be allowed to work while their activities are regularised. “Once it’s not a water body; it’s not a forest reserve or… place like a roadside, whether the person has a licence or not; the government says we should allow the person to mine and register and regularise them,” the CEO said. Prof Appiagyei-Atua argued that such a direction would conflict with Ghana’s mining laws. He cited sections 9 and 82 of the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703), which require mineral rights and licences before mining can take place. “Mining without that licence is not merely irregular; it is a crime.” He said an official who directs that unlicensed mining be permitted could be liable as an abettor under section 20 of the Criminal Offences Act, 1960 (Act 29). He also raised possible liability under provisions concerning the unlawful facilitation of small-scale mining. His article also questioned whether such directions are compatible with constitutional obligations governing public discretion and environmental protection. According to the professor, the minister’s authority to issue licences does not include the power to permit mining without them. “The Minister’s statutory power under section 82 is a power to grant licences. It is not a power to authorise mining without one.” He rejected the suggestion that avoiding rivers, forest reserves and roadsides would make an otherwise unlicensed operation lawful. “The statement’s implicit test — anywhere that is not expressly prohibited is permitted — reverses the statutory scheme, which is a permission-based regime: nothing is permitted unless affirmatively licensed.” Prof Appiagyei-Atua stressed that formalising artisanal and small-scale mining was a legitimate policy objective. He identified designated mining areas, faster licensing processes and district-level support as lawful options. His objection, he said, concerned allowing mining before the required authorisation. “The illegality lies entirely in the sequence. The law permits registration first, then mining. The statement describes mining first, then registering.” He argued that subsequent registration could not erase an offence already committed. He also warned that miners could not rely on an official assurance as a defence. The professor urged citizens to challenge unlawful mining through legal means. “We must take all legal action to resist galamsey.”

title: Kazakhstan Fighter Units Gain Experience Operating Alongside Chinese J-10C Jets: J-35 Purchases Likely
body: Uzbekistan’s newly acquired Chinese J-10C fighters are confirmed to have operated closely alongside Kazakhstan Air Defence Forces Su-30SM fighters , with the two serving as the principle types of combat jets in the two respective services. Uzbekistan publicly unveiled its J-10Cs in August 2026, becoming the second confirmed foreign operator, and providing it with what is now by far the most advanced fighter type in Central Asia. Opportunities to operate alongside the J-10C, and potentially contrast its capabilities with those of Russian-origin fighter types, could influence a future Kazakh decision on the future of its fighter fleet , as the Air Defence Forces plan a transition away from reliance on the Soviet MiG-31 and Russian Su-27/30. While the Su-30SM serves as Kazakhstan’s principal modern multirole fighter, its most capable combat jet for air defence operations remains the MiG-31BM interceptor, which integrates a much larger more powerful radar and was designed to cruise at speeds of Mach 2.35. Both are ageing and very high maintenance designs, however, with the J-10C in many respects being more cost effective due to its combination of much lower operational costs and more sophisticated avionics and weaponry. Although the J-10C’s short range and small radar size may prevent it from being considered for procurement by Kazakhstan, larger Chinese fighter types, most notably the J-35, are considered frontrunners to re-equip its fleet, potentially first replacing its Soviet-built Su-27s and possibly its MiG-31s in service. The fact that Russia defunded two programs to develop successors to the MiG-31 after the USSR disintegrated has left Kazakhstan without options to procure a direct successor to the type, although a successor to the Su-27 and Su-30, the Su-57, saw its first exports made in 2025. In late August multiple Kazakh and Russian sources reported that the Kazakhstan Air Defence Forces were scheduled to receive its first fifth generation fighter aircraft within two years. The Su-57 and J-35 are considered the only likely options. It is highly possible that the service will procure a mixed fleet of both fighter types, with the Su-57 potentially replacing the MiG-31 and Su-27, while the J-35 later replaces the Su-30SM, which would allow Astana to balance its ties with its two primary neighbours and strategic partners. Evaluations of the J-10C could help inform decisions regarding the extent to which the J-35 should be prioritised.

title: Former Greek PM Rejects Turkish Permit Demand for Cyprus Cable
body: Former Greek prime minister Kostas Karamanlis has warned that Greece must reject any Turkish request for a permit or notification concerning the Greece-Cyprus electricity inter-connector, arguing that such a concession could undermine Greek sovereign rights in the Aegean. Speaking at the War Museum in Athens on Sunday, 25 October, during an event organised by the Union of Retired Army Officers ahead of Greece’s 28 October OXI anniversary, Karamanlis said Greece could not accept a Turkish permit requirement, regardless of whether Ankara described it as a notification, notice or another form of approval. “After that, we will no longer be able to do anything in the Aegean without Turkey’s permission. Not even the smallest infrastructure project between our islands,” he said. Dispute Over the Greece–Cyprus Interconnector Karamanlis’ remarks followed comments by Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, who said Ankara accepted the project but demanded notification of survey work . Known as the Great Sea Interconnector , the project aims to connect the electricity grids of Greece and Cyprus through a subsea cable. The dispute centres on whether Turkey can require notification or approval for survey activities in the area. Karamanlis also criticised the Libyan parliament’s ratification of the Turkish–Libyan maritime memorandum, describing it as a negative development for Greek national interests. He acknowledged that the move had limits but said it demonstrated what he described as Turkey’s effort to project influence and establish faits accomplis. Athens has already challenged the memorandum at the United Nations . Karamanlis Says Turkey Pursues a Broader Aegean Strategy Karamanlis rejected the argument that Greece overreacts to Turkey. He also argued that the two countries could not resolve their disputes through mutual concessions. He presented Turkey’s claims over the Aegean as parts of a broader strategy, citing Ankara’s position on Greece’s territorial waters, the continental shelf and exclusive economic zone, the demilitarisation of Greek islands, maritime “grey zones” and Turkish marine parks. Karamanlis said these issues formed part of what he described as Ankara’s “integrated planning” to overturn the status quo in the Aegean. He also claimed that Turkey sought to establish rights near the Greek islands and extend its influence towards the 25th meridian. Criticism of Allies and European Partners Karamanlis also criticised Greece’s allies and partners, accusing some of adopting what he called an “opportunistic neutral” position and maintaining equal distance between the parties to disputes. He pointed to European arms deals with Turkey, partners’ positions on the Cyprus issue and pressure on Athens over several matters. Karamanlis reaffirmed Greece’s place in the Western alliance and the European Union but argued that allies must demonstrate reciprocity through practical support and solidarity. He rejected suggestions that Athens should avoid pressing its concerns over the Aegean, maritime zones and Cyprus to prevent irritating its partners, describing such an approach as the epitome of subservience. “Nobody respects someone who does not defend their rights, their principles, their homeland,” he said. Karamanlis Calls for Unity and Strong Defence Turning to Europe’s wider challenges, Karamanlis warned of a deepening social and political crisis, pointing to growing inequality, a shrinking middle class and the erosion of the post-war social model. Drawing lessons from Greece’s resistance to the Axis powers in 1940, he highlighted three principles: “Leadership – Preparation – Morale”. He linked these principles to the need for national unity, credible deterrence and determination to defend Greece’s national integrity.
