title: Ukraine receives over 230,000 doses of inactivated polio vaccine
body:
According to Ukrinform, the Ministry of Health of Ukraine reported this on Facebook .
"Ahead of World Polio Day, 232,500 doses of inactivated polio vaccine (IPV) have arrived in Ukraine for the free vaccination of children in accordance with the National Immunization Schedule," the statement reads.
Ukraine receives these vaccines through cooperation between the Ministry of Health and the Global Alliance for Vaccines and Immunization (Gavi). A partnership agreement was signed in late 2024. Under the agreement, Gavi funds part of the vaccine supply in support of Ukraine's national immunization program, in line with the National Strategy for the Development of Immunization through 2030.
Under this partnership, UNICEF is responsible for procuring the vaccines and delivering them to Ukraine, while the Ministry of Health's Public Health Center coordinates their distribution to regional centers for disease control and prevention.
The vaccines are currently being stored at the national warehouse and will be distributed to healthcare facilities across all regions of Ukraine.
The Ministry of Health recalled that World Polio Day was observed worldwide on October 24.
"Thanks to mass vaccination campaigns, the number of polio cases worldwide has fallen by more than 99%, from approximately 350,000 cases in 1988 to 12 in 2023. However, this does not mean we can afford to let our guard down. As long as the virus continues to circulate in even one country, it poses a threat to children worldwide," the statement reads.
The Ministry of Health explained that polio vaccination protects against all three existing types of poliovirus. Immunization is administered using an inactivated polio vaccine. This vaccine contains no live virus and is safe, including for people with compromised immune systems.
To have a child vaccinated, parents should contact their family doctor or pediatrician, or visit the nearest healthcare facility. Vaccination under the National Immunization Schedule is free of charge.
The Ministry of Health also stressed that if a child has missed any routine vaccinations, parents should contact a doctor as soon as possible to arrange an individual catch-up schedule.

title: France’s Archange SIGINT Aircraft Arrives at Évreux Air Base Ahead of Operational Evaluation
body: The first Archange arrived at Évreux in early October, where France’s Military Air Expertise Center is participating in trials ahead of the aircraft’s planned entry into service. France’s Archange (Archangel) Signals Intelligence (SIGINT) and Electronic Warfare (EW) aircraft landed at its future operating base, Base Aérienne 105 (BA 105) in Évreux, for the first time, the Armée de l’Air et de l’Espace (French Air and Space Force – FASF) reported on Oct. 23, 2026 . Air Base 105 is home to the Airborne Electronic Squadron (Escadron électronique aéroporté) 5/64 “Dunkerque,” which is slated to operate the aircraft. The aircraft landed in Évreux, Normandy, on Oct. 7, 2026. The French Air and Space Force, however, only announced the milestone on Oct. 23, saying that the Military Air Expertise Center (CEAM) is participating in technical-operational experimentation to prepare the aircraft for future service. The FASF’s two Transall C-160G Gabriel SIGINT aircraft were retired prematurely in May 2022, leaving a gap in the country’s dedicated airborne signals-intelligence capability. An interim Saab 340 leased under the SOLAR contract provides some replacement capacity, but it does not fully replicate the Gabriel’s capabilities. The C-160G Gabriel’s successor, the Dassault Falcon 8X-based Archange, will restore the service’s Electronic Warfare (EW) capabilities with a total fleet of three aircraft to be delivered by 2030. The first airframe made its first flight on July 25, 2025 , from Dassault Aviation’s facility in Bordeaux-Mérignac. The aircraft, now bearing registration F-ZJFM, was also captured by aviation photographers in FASF colors and markings on June 2, 2026 at Bordeaux-Mérignac. The aircraft is also sporting the Dunkerque squadron’s insignia – a lion in a coat of arms right under the cockpit. The French Air and Space Force described Archange as “the Future pillar of electromagnetic origin intelligence for the AAE,” adding that it is now preparing to enter service. The system can “broadcast the enemy electronic order of battle in real time, illuminate planning, and better protect our forces.” Premier posé à Évreux pour ARCHANGE ! Futur pilier du renseignement d’origine électromagnétique de l’AAE, le Falcon 8X prépare son entrée en service. Diffuser en temps réel l’ordre de bataille électronique ennemi, éclairer la planification et mieux protéger nos forces. https://t.co/TCwwuHHjlA — Armée de l’Air et de l’Espace (@Armee_de_lair) October 23, 2026 Archange aircraft at Évreux According to Opex360 , when reporting on the Archange sporting FASF colors in June, the F-ZJFM registration suggests the aircraft is assigned to the Direction Générale de l’Armement Essais en Vol (Directorate General of Armaments Flight Testing – DGA EV) division. The Air and Space Force subsequently confirmed that CEAM is participating in technical-operational experimentation at Évreux to prepare Archange for future service, although this has not been publicly detailed. The program has already been delayed a few years, with deliveries originally slated to begin by 2025. The manufacturing of the first airframe was held back, according to Chief of Defence Staff General Fabien Mandon’s recent testimony to the Senate, due to Dassault Aviation facing “difficulty in fitting an electronic computing bay into an aircraft which has limited space.” Dassault is responsible for the airframe modification on the trijet Falcon 8X, integration, flight testing, and supplemental certification, while Thales has developed the EW payloads, mission systems and sensors, including the CUGE (Capacité Universelle de Guerre Électronique / Universal Electronic Warfare Capability) system. This is carried in a large ventral fairing under the aircraft’s chin. The first @Dassault_OnAir F8X Archange in French air force colors spotted at Bordeaux-Mérignac airport. The Falcon 8X Archange is France’s future airborne #SIGINT platform. Equipped with @thalesgroup CUGE electronic warfare system, it will collect and analyze radar and communications emissions, enhancing the French Air Force’s strategic intelligence capabilities. by Alexis Thocaven — Tom Antonov (@Tom_Antonov) June 2, 2026 CUGE is designed to detect and analyze communications and radar emissions, strengthening France’s signals-intelligence capability. Thales has previously said CUGE leverages technologies like multi-polarization antennas, Artificial Intelligence (AI) to automate data processing, and advanced sensors to simultaneously detect, analyze and classify electromagnetic emissions. Archange is now undergoing technical-operational experimentation intended to prepare it for future service. Such work is expected to evaluate the aircraft’s mission systems and establish how the new capability will be employed and supported, although the detailed test plan has not been publicly disclosed. France retains several complementary means of collecting electromagnetic intelligence, but these do not fully replace the capability previously provided by the Transall C-160G Gabriel. The Mirage 2000D RMV can carry the ASTAC (Tactical Signal Analyzer/Analyseur de signaux tactiques) pod, while the three (Capacité de Renseignement Electromagnétique Spatial/Space Electromagnetic Intelligence Capability) satellites provide space-based electromagnetic intelligence. Other capabilities include the Beechcraft 350 ALSR (Light Surveillance and Intelligence Aircraft) aircraft used for VADOR (Vector Airborne Designation Observation and Reconnaissance) missions and the Saab 340 leased under the SOLAR contract, which provides an interim platform equipped with radar, electromagnetic-intelligence sensors, and electro-optical equipment. The latter only partially compensates for the Gabriel’s retirement. L’Archange a réalisé son premier vol. Construit sur la base d’un Falcon 8X de @Dassault_OnAir, modifié pour y intégrer des systèmes de pointes développés par @thalesgroup, notre futur avion de renseignement sera doté de capacités au plus haut standard pour la détection de signaux de communication et d’émissions radar. D’ici la fin de la loi de programmation militaire 2024-2030, trois d’entre eux seront livrés à l’@Armee_de_lair et stationnés sur la Base aérienne 105 d’Evreux. — Sébastien Lecornu (@SebLecornu) July 25, 2025 The DGA had previously said that the Archange aircraft “will strengthen France’s signals intelligence capabilities. In particular, they offer unprecedented complementarity in the detection of communication signals and radar emissions.”

title: White supremacist sentenced to 17 years for arson, attempting to provide support for Hezbollah
body: A man was sentenced to over 17 years in prison for arson and attempting to provide material support for Hezbollah back in 2019, the US Department of Justice announced on Wednesday.Regan Darby Prater, 28, was sentenced and ordered to pay nearly $1.3 million in restitution after he pleaded guilty to the charges in April.The DOJ said that Prater used what they described as a "napalm-based incendiary device" to destroy the Highlander Center's buildings, a nonprofit research and education center in Tennessee, causing over a million dollars in damages.Before setting the facilities up in flames, court records showed that Prater spray-painted a Nazi symbol in the parking lot of the Highlander Center. The same symbol was engraved on a rifle used in the terror attack on two Mosques in Christchurch, New Zealand, back in 2019.Prater admitted to committing the arson on the Highlander Center motivated by white-supremacist ideology, and admitted to targeting the non-profit for its faith-based educational priorities and its association with civil rights.'Start the hunt'The DOJ also disclosed that Prater admitted to providing material support to Hezbollah. According to the DOJ, Prater obtained documents containing personal information on more than 35,000 individuals allegedly affiliated with Israel's government; however, the DOJ did not specify how Prater obtained them.Prater took the sensitive information and provided it to an individual he believed was part of Hezbollah and reportedly told the operative to "start the hunt," the DOJ said.The FBI Nashville field office investigated the case with assistance from the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation, according to the DOJ.

title: Soldiers earn peanuts, APC youth leader flaunts billion-naira SUVs — Utomi
body: Professor Pat Utomi has criticised the All Progressives Congress (APC) over the distribution of luxury sport utility vehicles (SUVs) to selected youth leaders, contrasting the expenditure with what he described as poor salaries paid to Nigerian soldiers. Utomi, a chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), said it was troubling that an APC youth leader could display expensive vehicles at a time Nigerians had been told that government funds were limited. In a post on X on Sunday, Utomi wrote: “Nigerian soldiers are being paid peanuts as salaries, yet an APC youth leader is flaunting SUVs worth billions of naira. This is the same government that told Nigerians there was no longer money in the treasury. At this point, they must think we are fools!” In another post, the professor questioned whether the money spent on the vehicles could have been put to better use, particularly in the health sector. “Each of the SUVs in this video costs more than ₦100 million. I wonder how many world-class ambulances the millions being spent on these vehicles could buy. What a pity!” he wrote. The comments followed a video posted by APC National Youth Leader, Dayo Israel, showing brand-new 2026 Toyota Prado SUVs he said were presented to selected youth leaders to support election mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections. “Today, I presented brand new 2026 Prado to my committed selected youth leaders to aid their election mobilisation activities,” Israel wrote. He also expressed gratitude to First Lady Oluremi Tinubu for what he described as her continued support for the party’s structure under his leadership. “The party is supreme and that supremacy will show in our action in this election period — we will deliver polling unit by polling unit,” he added. The video, which has since been deleted, drew criticism from Nigerians on social media, with some questioning the timing of the vehicle distribution amid the economic hardship associated with the Tinubu administration’s reforms. Utomi’s remarks add to the criticism surrounding the display, with the NDC chieftain raising questions about public spending priorities and the cost of the vehicles. The post Soldiers earn peanuts, APC youth leader flaunts billion-naira SUVs — Utomi appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: GoldBod CEO’s comment: Allowing unlicensed mining breaches the law – Prof Appiagyei-Atua
body: Professor Kwadwo Appiagyei-Atua has challenged the GoldBod CEO’s comments about allowing unlicensed miners to operate pending registration, arguing that such a directive breaches Ghana’s mining laws. The Professor of International Law and Human Rights at the University of Ghana School of Law says administrative assurances cannot override statutory licensing requirements. In an opinion article, he challenged the position attributed to the GoldBod CEO: “Once it’s not a water body; it’s not a forest reserve or… place like a roadside, whether the person has a licence or not; the government says we should allow the person to mine and register and regularise them”. Prof Appiagyei-Atua argues that a mining operation’s location does not remove the requirement to obtain a licence. He cites Section 9 of the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703), which requires a mineral right before mining, prospecting or exploration. He also points to Section 82’s separate licensing requirement for small-scale mining. “Mining without that licence is not merely irregular; it is a crime.” Citing penalties under the 2019 amendment, he says Ghanaian offenders face fines and prison terms of between 15 and 25 years. He argues that a ministerial or administrative direction permitting unlicensed mining would exceed the powers granted by law. “The Minister’s statutory power under section 82 is a power to grant licences. It is not a power to authorise mining without one.” Prof Appiagyei-Atua also challenges the suggestion that avoiding rivers, forest reserves and roadsides makes an operation permissible. He cites Section 18’s environmental and forestry clearance requirements. “The statement’s implicit test — anywhere that is not expressly prohibited is permitted — reverses the statutory scheme, which is a permission-based regime: nothing is permitted unless affirmatively licensed.” He distinguishes between supporting formalisation and allowing mining before the legal requirements are met. He says formalisation is lawful and identifies designated mining areas, faster registration and district-level licensing support as possible routes. “The illegality lies entirely in the sequence. The law permits registration first, then mining. The statement describes mining first, then registering.” He argues that subsequent registration cannot erase an offence already committed. “Regularisation cannot retroactively cure a completed offence.” The professor further warns that miners who rely on an official assurance remain exposed to prosecution. He argues that an official representation cannot create a right that Parliament withheld. He also raises possible liability for officials who facilitate unlawful mining and questions whether such directions comply with constitutional duties concerning discretionary power and environmental protection. Calling for lawful resistance to galamsey, he concludes: “We must take all legal action to resist galamsey.”

title: Mbappe’s Brace Helps Real Madrid Beat Barcelona In La Liga Clasico
body: Kylian Mbappe struck twice to earn Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid a 2-1 Clasico victory over La Liga leaders Barcelona on Sunday at Camp Nou, cutting the gap to three points. French superstar Mbappe opened the scoring before the interval and then slotted home late on to inflict Barca’s first domestic defeat of the campaign after Raphinha had equalised for the champions. Real Madrid remain third, behind Atletico Madrid and Hansi Flick’s Barca, who had won their first nine games before a chastening week. The Catalans suffered a second straight defeat after losing on Tuesday against Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League. Barca had won six of the seven previous Clasicos since the German arrived but were surprisingly subdued against Mourinho’s side. “In general we didn’t have a great game; in the first half we weren’t ourselves, there were a lot of things we could have done better,” Barcelona midfielder Pedri told DAZN. “We wanted to win the Clasico in front of our fans, but the season is very long… a league is not won here.” Los Blancos, without suspended winger Vinicius Junior, won their fifth straight game across all competitions and are finding their footing under veteran Portuguese coach Mourinho. After two trophyless seasons, Madrid turned back to Mourinho to try and stop Barca’s dominance, and this result will give them hope they are on the right track. The opening period of the game was cagey, with few opportunities. Barca defender Pau Cubarsi twice reacted well to shut down Mbappe, while Real Madrid’s Marc Cucurella took a rapid liking for Lamine Yamal’s shirt, constantly grabbing at the 19-year-old winger. Anthony Gordon, playing in his first Clasico since joining Barcelona from Newcastle, backheeled the ball to Raphinha, who fired narrowly wide as Barca threatened. The hosts were dealt a setback when young defender Xavi Espart pulled up hurt and needed to be replaced by Alejandro Balde before the half-hour mark. Andriy Lunin, playing in goal for Madrid after Thibaut Courtois pulled out of the squad with flu, saved at his near post from Gordon before the visitors took the lead. Mbappe scored his 10th league goal of the season and also his easiest, with Barca’s Gerard Martin clearing a cross straight at the Frenchman, who deflected it into the net. Barca responded by carving out a glorious chance for an equaliser but teenage sensation Yamal, for once, miskicked in front of goal, firing wide when poised to level. The game opened up, and Yan Diomande came close to doubling Madrid’s lead before half-time, drilling into the side netting. Sting In The Tail Martin redeemed himself early in the second half as he held off Jude Bellingham, who could neither beat the defender nor find a free Mbappe. Raphinha, who had a quiet first half, pulled Barcelona level just after the hour mark. Pedri fed the Brazilian, La Liga’s top goalscorer with 13, who fired through Bellingham’s legs and Lunin could not keep the shot out. The Ukrainian goalkeeper did make a superb save to deny Martin at a corner, as Barcelona flowed forward with the wind finally in their sails. Yamal bent an effort wide with Lunin at full stretch, and Barca substitute Frenkie de Jong had a shot desperately blocked by Dean Huijsen. There was a sting in the tail for the Catalans, though as substitute Gabriel Jesus lost possession and Madrid raced through on goal. Eduardo Camavinga beat Cubarsi and unselfishly cut the ball back for Mbappe to tuck home his second of the night into an empty net with Joan Garcia drawn out of position. The post Mbappe’s Brace Helps Real Madrid Beat Barcelona In La Liga Clasico appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Kiev troops bombard Donetsk People’s Republic five times over past day
body:
DONETSK, October 26. /TASS/. The Ukrainian military shelled residential areas in the Donetsk People’s Republic (DPR) five times over the past 24 hours, two civilians were wounded, the department for documenting Ukraine’s war crimes at the DPR head’s office and government said in a statement on Monday.
"Over the past 24-hour period, five shelling attacks by Ukraine’s armed formations were registered," the statement said adding that two civilians, including a teenager born in 2009, sustained wounds.
According to the statement, five munitions of various types were fired from Ukraine.

title: Two musings on the design of compiler warnings (2020)
body:
Two musings on the design of compiler warnings
Today I finally write down some musings on two peripheral aspects of compiler diagnostic design that I think are very important for certain kinds of warnings. My first musing relates to fixits , and my second to suppression mechanisms .
Most C++ compilers these days don’t just tell you that a problem occurred (like ed ’s famous ? prompt ), and what the problem is (“expected identifier,” for example). They’ll try to tell you how to fix the problem.
Compare GCC 4.1’s error messages with GCC 4.6’s. ( Godbolt. ) For this input:
GCC 4.1 complains merely that you have put multiple types in one declaration . GCC 4.6 more helpfully complains that it expected ';' after struct definition , and points to the exact position where it believes a semicolon should be inserted.
GCC 7 goes even further, and suggests a fixit — a machine-readable “spellcheck suggestion” that some IDEs are able to apply with a single click.
In medical terms, the compiler has gone from simply detecting the symptom (“this declaration seems to contain two types, which isn’t valid C++”) to producing a diagnosis of the disease (“I bet you forgot a semicolon somewhere”); and a compiler that supports fixits is actually prescribing a treatment plan . Each of these steps is a quantum leap beyond the previous one in terms of both user-friendliness and implementation complexity.
Suppression mechanisms relate to compiler warnings , not compiler errors. Consider the following snippet ( Godbolt ):
Every mainstream compiler warns on this suspicious-looking code (GCC and Clang with -Wall ; MSVC with -W4 ). Here’s GCC’s diagnostic:
Notice that GCC doesn’t even bother to explain really what its diagnosis is; it emits a passive-aggressive warning message that does nothing more than suggest how to shut itself up!
The diagnosis, of course, is that frequently people mean to write if (argc == 1) but their finger slips and they write if (argc = 1) instead, which unfortunately is also valid C++ code. Every mainstream compiler has evolved the same way to deal with this: if you really mean = , then you write an extra pair of parentheses around the expression, like so:
The extra pair of parentheses is what I’m calling a “suppression mechanism.” It’s just an arbitrary way of silencing a warning diagnostic — telling the compiler “no, I really meant to write this legal but unusual construct.”
Another well-known suppression mechanism is writing (void) in front of unused results to silence -Wunused-value and -Wunused-result warnings ( Godbolt ):
And a trivial suppression mechanism is implied by the name of the -Wparentheses warning:
Here the compiler just wants you to add a pair of parentheses to clarify the precedence for the reader.
It’s easy for the programmer to “fix” diagnostics like -Wunused-result and -Wlogical-op-parentheses , because they’re just asking the programmer to clarify intent that is already pretty clear: Yes , I mean to discard this result. Yes , I mean to evaluate (a && b) || c .
The more interesting diagnostics are the ones where the compiler believes it has identified a mismatch between the code’s actual behavior and the programmer’s intent . Our if (argc = 1) example above was like that. A more realistic example might be something like
Here it is almost certain that the programmer intended to write
However, the literal behavior of the code as written is equivalent to
When the compiler suggests a fixit for this warning, it has to choose: Should we suggest the fix that changes the behavior of the code to what you probably meant to type — the “spellcheck” option? Or should we show how to silence the warning while preserving the existing code’s behavior — the “Add To Dictionary” option, if you will? (Or, continuing our medical analogy, there’s the “treatment” option and the “ DNR ” option.)
Showing just the “treatment” option puts the compiler in the awkward position of “recommending” that you change the behavior of code that is, after all, perfectly legal C++ already; blindly applying the fixit to working code might break that code. But showing just the “suppression” option might encourage a programmer to blindly apply the fixit to broken code, thus leaving the bug in place but making it harder to detect in the future.
For certain kinds of warnings, Clang shows both fixits. Two examples of this in Clang 10 are ( Godbolt ):
Notice that in both cases, Clang decides to print the “suppression” option first and the “treatment” option second. But sometimes Clang prints the “treatment” option first and the “suppression” option second:
Of course, there are many more cases where Clang emits only the “suppression” option as a fixit, leaving the programmer to figure out the “treatment” on their own. (GCC 10.2 emits a fixit for only the last of these four examples; and it’s the “suppression” option.)
Even in the absence of any machine-readable fixits, the phrasing of the warning message itself can induce the human reader to think in terms of suppression or in terms of treatment. A warning message can be phrased as “Please confirm that you meant X”; or “You did X; did you mean Y?”; or even as “Your attempt to do Y failed.”
Compiler warnings of the kind we’re discussing here are basically of the form “You wrote X, but I think you meant Y.” This happens only when X and Y are in some sense close together . Sometimes the “closeness” is semantic, not syntactic (as when the programmer means to invoke copy elision but writes return std::move(x) instead). But for our purposes today, let’s just think about syntactic closeness. You meant to write Y, but a minor typographical slip caused you to write X. In the examples above, the slips are things like “omit one = ,” or “omit a pair of parens” or “put < 0 inside the parens instead of outside.”
Take X=”equality-compare !a to b ” and Y=”negate the sense of a == b .” There are some pieces of code that clearly intend to express X, such as (!a)==(b) . There are some that clearly intend to express Y, such as a != b . But you wrote (!a==b) , which falls into a gray area: it’s not clear which of X and Y you really intended to express.
The job of the compiler-diagnostic-developer is to create some separation between the space of inputs that the compiler considers “clearly X” and the space of inputs that the compiler considers “clearly Y.” Essentially, we create an error-correcting code by deliberately increasing the edit distance between pairs of inequivalent C++ programs — deliberately increasing the number of keystrokes the programmer would have to screw up in order to transform a working (and warning-free) C++ program into an inequivalent broken (yet warning-free) C++ program.
Furthermore, in cases where Y is more commonly intended than X, it should be relatively easier to write Y than X. In our example that’s true even at the core-language level: a != b is already easier to write than !a == b . But when we increase the distance between X-space and Y-space, we shrink X-space by more than we shrink Y-space. If you really intend to express !a == b , we’ll force you to retreat all the way to (!a) == b . This is kind of analogous to the signaling principle in economics or evolutionary biology: Basically, if you want the compiler to accept your intent, your code must adopt some cumbersome and frankly maladaptive ornamentation in order to prove its worthiness to the compiler.
According to the prevailing theory of sexual selection in the animal kingdom , when a peahen is deciding whether to accept a particular peacock, she uses his ornamental tail as a proxy for his success. A peacock with a big cumbersome tail must be healthy and successful, and thus a good mate for the peahen. A peacock with an unremarkable tail won’t merit mating with.
When the C++ compiler is deciding whether to accept a particular program without complaint, it uses certain ornamental syntactic flourishes as a proxy for the code’s intent. A questionable snippet that adopts those flourishes — say, if ((argc = 1)) with an extra set of parentheses, or (void)x; , or strncmp(a, b, size_t(len < 0)) — must be intentional, and thus a good match for the compiler. A questionable snippet that lacks any flourishes — say, if (argc = 1) or x; or strncmp(a, b, len < 0) — won’t merit suppressing the warning.
Here’s this musing’s payoff: When deciding whether to warn on a sketchy construct, it’s tempting to encode absolute rules such as “Don’t warn on (argc = 1) if it’s surrounded by a pair of parentheses.” But we should instead think in terms of relative rules — rules that compare the “degree of ornamentation” of what the programmer actually wrote versus the “degree of ornamentation” of the code they would have written without their (hypothetical) typo. Observe:
As of September 2020, neither Clang nor GCC catches this single-character typo. They see that the subexpression (argc = 2) is parenthesized, which suffices to suppress their warning.
I think what they should do is compare the program as written to the “typo-corrected” program
That’s obviously a plausible and unremarkable program, so the likelihood is high that the programmer did indeed typo = for == . If the programmer really wants to silence the warning in this case, I think the programmer should be forced to write
Now the hypothetically “typo-corrected” program would be
which is remarkable and implausible — it’s clearly got an ornamental excess of parentheses!
To put this yet another way: The compiler should separate the space of acceptable programs into “those that use = with a remarkably high number of parentheses” and “those that use == with an unremarkable number of parentheses.” Then, for purposes of warning diagnostics, the compiler should essentially treat = and == as synonymous; it can rely on the number of parentheses to indicate the programmer’s intent.
As of September 2020, Clang 10.1 and GCC 10.2 don’t do very well on these test cases.
This post was inspired by the mailing-list thread “[cfe-dev] parentheses flag warning” (May 2020).

title: IDF chief pushed back on Netanyahu order for ‘action’ against Iran, fearing political motives
body: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and IDF Chief of Staff Lt.-Gen. Eyal Zamir clashed over a military action that could renew the conflict with Iran days before Israel's elections, N12 News reported Sunday evening. Recently, Zamir received a directive from the political echelon to carry out an action, which security officials told N12 would "trigger a rapid escalation into a confrontation with Iran."Due to the sensitive nature of the action, N12 reported that Zamir requested an in-depth discussion and formal authorization before moving forward with the action. Sources familiar with the details told N12 that Zamir and additional IDF leadership are concerned that the political echelon may be trying to exploit the front with Iran ahead of elections for political gain. Netanyahu denied the report late on Sunday night, saying on Channel 14's The Patriots that “there is no confrontation” and that “someone is trying to obscure the fact that Zamir himself had said Iran was attempting to interfere in the elections.”US President Donald Trump and Zamir have, at different points during the election season, acted as constraints on Netanyahu's approach regarding aspects related to a potential renewed conflict with Iran.It remains unclear how far Netanyahu would have been willing to go if he had not anticipated that certain figures would place the brakes on certain actions.The prime minister would have welcomed a US return to war with Iran in August, earlier in October, and again more recently. In some of those scenarios, Israel would have been prepared to join the US.Netanyahu may also have played with the possibility of Israel taking a leading, 'first-attacker' role, or serving as a spoiler to prevent versions of an Iranian nuclear deal which he would view as a bad deal. In all of these discussions, Trump, while vacillating, has ultimately, to date, come out in trying to continue to stare down Tehran with a mix of military threats and economic pressure.Likewise, in all of these decisions, Zamir has had Israel on a war footing versus Iran if necessary, but has viewed the meaning of "necessary" before Election Day in a limited fashion.To avoid interfering with the election, and given that Iran poses no immediate existential threat since prior Israeli attacks have pushed back its nuclear and ballistic missile threats, Zamir has only been ready to attack Iran if two conditions were met: If Iran were preparing to strike Israel, or if Trump initiated a new round of fighting and Israel had full US backing for both offensive and defensive operations.Generally, Zamir's instinct has been that he is ready to strike Iran if it starts recovering its threat capabilities too fast, which it has not yet done, or if such a strike would be part of a well-thought-out and considered strategy to finally push Tehran into making key nuclear concessions to the US.More broadly, Zamir has viewed military action as potentially justified if Iran rapidly rebuilt its nuclear and ballistic missile capabilities or if a strike formed part of a carefully considered strategy to compel Tehran to make significant nuclear concessions to Washington. Previous Israeli attacks have set back Iran's capabilities, reducing the immediate urgency for another round of strikes, according to this assessment.The requests for formal authorization and an in-depth discussion, as reported by N12, could serve to clarify the government's intentions and ensure that any military action had a clear legal and strategic basis.The report further described 'new lows' in the Netanyahu-Zamir relationship.Netanyahu selected Zamir to lead the military because he was his personal military secretary, and for the latter's known aggressive approach to warfare. The prime minister partially alienated the IDF chief by refusing to draft haredi (ultra-Orthodox) men into the IDF and allowing Defense Minister Israel Katz to politicize certain key military appointments.Zamir has likewise partially alienated Netanyahu even before this point, by slowing the Gaza war in late 2025 and by pressuring him over the haredi conscription issue.Eisenkot warns Netanyahu against using IDF as political toolYashar party chairman Gadi Eisenkot on Sunday night said he supports Zamir's decision to be cautious, warning Netanyahu against putting his political interests above the state's."Netanyahu, my eyes are on you," stated Eisenkot. "The man, on whose watch the greatest disaster in the nation's history occurred, refuses to grasp that Israel's security is not a political plaything; that the lives of Israeli citizens and IDF soldiers are not to be treated with reckless disregard; and that the State of Israel is not his private property.""I have full confidence in IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir and the IDF commanders, who act with professional responsibility and an absolute commitment to the nation's security. We will not allow the IDF to be turned into a tool for Netanyahu's political survival campaign.""Do not dare to place your own political interests above the security of the State," Eisenkot warned the prime minister.He added that holding elections according to the set schedule is a "cornerstone of Israel's national resilience," stating that he "will not let you [Netanyahu] jeopardize Israel's future just to preserve your own rule.""In two days, the citizens of Israel will put an end to this era of reckless, lawless governance and restore responsibility, a sense of statehood, and the security of Israel," Eisenkot said. "I give you my word."Betrayal of state, securityThe Democrats party chair Yair Golan echoed Eisenkot's support for Zamir's caution in a Sunday night post on X/Twitter, saying that he wholeheartedly backs Zamir for "standing firm on his professional duty.""It is forbidden to allow any military action that lacks a clear security need, a strategic purpose, and a responsible action plan behind it," Golan wrote. "When Israeli citizens go to the polls next Tuesday, they must remember this: Netanyahu constitutes a security threat to Israel. He does not hesitate to sacrifice the lives of our children for his survival on the eve of elections, and this is what the IDF is trying to thwart.""Israel's security is in the hands of a corrupt political echelon, unfit and deranged people who do not hesitate to sacrifice Israel's security in order to cling to their seats."Yisrael Beytenu head Avigdor Liberman called Netanyahu's attempt to "drag Israel into military action in order to prevent the elections" an act of "betrayal of the state and its security.""The duty of the chief of staff is to prevent the political use of the IDF and to safeguard the lives of IDF soldiers, not endanger them because of the prime minister's fear of losing the elections."

title: Northern Lights Over Greece: When The Sky Resembled the North Pole
body: The Northern Lights have appeared over Greece on several rare occasions, with historical records dating back to 25 October 1870, when a Royal Navy captain reported an unusual glow in the sky to the National Observatory of Athens. Powerful geomagnetic storms can push the aurora borealis far south of its usual range, occasionally making it visible from Athens and other parts of the country. Although the phenomenon usually appears near Earth’s magnetic poles, intense solar activity can trigger geomagnetic disturbances that extend the auroral zone to much lower latitudes. Reports of unusual lights in the Greek sky also date back to antiquity. The philosopher Anaxagoras and Aristotle feature among the ancient Greek thinkers associated with early descriptions of celestial phenomena that may resemble the aurora. What Causes the Northern Lights? The Northern Lights occur when charged particles associated with solar activity interact with Earth’s magnetic field and collide with atoms and molecules in the upper atmosphere. These collisions release light in different colours, creating luminous bands that appear to move across the sky. The phenomenon usually occurs near the magnetic poles. However, powerful geomagnetic storms can expand the area in which the aurora appears, making it visible from countries much farther south, including Greece. The corresponding phenomenon in the Southern Hemisphere is known as the Southern Lights, or aurora australis. The colours depend on the gases involved and the altitude at which the collisions occur. Oxygen primarily produces green and red light, while nitrogen can contribute blue and purple hues. Although auroras can occur during daylight, observers usually see them at night, when the brightness of the sky does not overwhelm the display. Greece’s First Recorded Sighting in 1870 On 25 October 1870, A. Vatsaxis, a Royal Navy captain from Lefkada, sent a telegram to the National Observatory of Athens describing an unusual light he had observed in the sky. His message read: “Την 6ην και 55 ώραν εφάνη άνωθεν νεφών μέχρι αστερισμού Μεγάλης Άρκτου πύρινος λάμψις έχουσα κέντρον σώματι φωτεινόν μέχρι ορίζοντος”. The captain described a fiery glow stretching above the clouds towards the constellation Ursa Major, with a luminous centre extending towards the horizon. He did not identify the phenomenon as the Northern Lights. Instead, he recorded what he had seen without knowing its cause. The report ranks among the earliest modern records of auroral activity in Greece. The Spectacular Display of 1940 Another significant sighting occurred on 24 March 1940, when the Northern Lights appeared over Greece and astonished residents of Athens. The Astronomy Laboratory of the University of Athens recorded the event and described the display as particularly intense and bright. Contemporary accounts reported that some Athenians spoke of “divine veils” covering the capital. The sighting remains one of the most notable historical records of the aurora in Greece. When the Northern Lights Returned to Greece The Athens Sighting of 2003 On 20 November 2003, Antonis Agiomamitis photographed the Northern Lights over Athens, providing a photographic record of the rare phenomenon in the Greek sky. Meteorologist and former director of the National Meteorological Service Thodoris Kolydas has explained that visibility does not depend solely on a location’s latitude. Its position in relation to Earth’s geomagnetic field also plays a role. A powerful geomagnetic storm can therefore make the aurora visible much farther south than usual. Northern Lights Over Greece in November 2023 On the evening of 5 November 2023, the Northern Lights appeared again over parts of Greece following strong geomagnetic activity. Observers recorded reddish glows in Central Macedonia, including the regions around Serres, Pieria and Halkidiki. Residents and amateur photographers shared images and videos of the rare display. The aurora’s appearance at such low latitudes reflected the intensity of the geomagnetic storm. The October 2024 Display Another widespread appearance occurred overnight from 10 to 11 October 2024. Photographers captured the phenomenon across several parts of Greece, including: Macedonia: Paiko, Hortiatis, Plagiari, Nea Moudania and Kilkis. Central Greece and Attica: Livadeia, Evia, Oropos and Penteli. The islands: Corfu, Lesvos and Crete. The sky took on vivid red hues, while photographs from different locations revealed the geographical extent of the geomagnetic disturbance. The Northern Lights in January 2026 One of the most recent widely reported sightings in Greece occurred overnight from 19 to 20 January 2026. Strong solar and geomagnetic activity made the aurora visible in parts of northern Greece and the Ionian Islands. Spectacular images emerged from Hortiatis, near Thessaloniki, and Corfu, while observers reported sightings elsewhere. Red and purple hues dominated the photographs as the phenomenon appeared far south of its usual range. The Northern Lights in Ancient Greece Descriptions of celestial phenomena that may be associated with the aurora predate modern records by centuries. Anaxagoras, the fifth-century BC philosopher from Clazomenae, is among the ancient Greek thinkers linked to early observations of unusual lights in the sky. Aristotle also described luminous phenomena in his work Meteorology . He wrote: “Φαίνεται δέ ποτε συνιστάμενα νύκτωρ αἰθρίας οὔσης πολλὰ φάσματα ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ…” The passage has been associated with displays resembling the aurora, although historians cannot confidently identify every ancient description as the same phenomenon scientists understand today. Long before modern astrophysics emerged, ancient observers were already attempting to describe and explain unusual lights in the sky. Science has since established the physical processes that produce the aurora. Yet every appearance over Greece remains a rare spectacle, drawing attention to the night sky and offering a glimpse of a phenomenon more commonly associated with the Arctic. title: NDC Unveils Campaign Council, Names Dickson, Obi, Kwankwaso As Members
body: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has constituted its national campaign council for the 2027 general elections. The list, released on Sunday, has Senator Seriake Dickson as the chairman, while the presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and vice-presidential candidate, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, were listed as co-chairman and co-vice chairman of the national campaign caucus, respectively. Others are Senator Cleopas Zuwoghe as vice chairman, and former secretary to the government of the federation, Babachir Lawal (National Campaign Advisory Council), as a member. Also on the list are Ikenna Enekweizu, Sidi Abdul, Babatunde Alli, Senator Ovie Omo Agege, Senator Victor Umeh, Ibrahim Abdulkarim (DG, Presidential Campaign), Buba Galadima, Yakubu Ochefu, Mahmud Jahun, Moshood Salvador, Mrs. Dudu Manuga, Victor Ogene, and Muktar Usman. The list also has a 40-member national campaign advisory council, and 37 state campaign coordinators. The NDC National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, was named Director of Communication and Media. A former defence spokesperson, Major General John Enenche (retd.), was named Director of Security and Intelligence. The party, in a statement announcing the campaign council on its X handle, said, “The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) is pleased to announce the constitution of its National Campaign Council for the 2027 general elections. “The National Campaign Council will provide strategic leadership, coordinate campaign activities across the country, and drive the mobilisation of Nigerians behind the party’s vision of a new, just, and prosperous Nigeria. “The Council will work under the chairmanship of His Excellency, Senator Henry Seriake Dickson CON, NDC National Leader; Co-Chairman, His Excellency, Mr. Peter Obi CON, our presidential candidate; Vice Chairman, Senator Cleopas Moses Zuwoghe, NDC National Chairman and our vice-presidential candidate, His Excellency, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, Co Vice-Chairman, Ikenna Morgan Enekweizu, NDC National Secretary, Council Secretary, and the Director-General, Mallam Ibrahim Hussain Abdulkarim to deliver a people-centred and issue-based campaign. “We call on all party members, supporters, and well-meaning Nigerians to remain united and focused as we work together to rescue our country.” The post NDC Unveils Campaign Council, Names Dickson, Obi, Kwankwaso As Members appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Kratos pushes into European market through Airbus partnership in Germany
body: The maiden flight of the U740 Valkyrie, an American-German unmanned aircraft, recently took place in northern Germany. In 2026, history has repeated itself: back in 2013, the two countries were also working together on an ambitious high-altitude project. That transatlantic effort, the purchase of five Euro Hawk unmanned aerial platforms, never reached a successful conclusion. Thirteen years ago, Germany made its first attempt, ultimately unsuccessful, to field a high-altitude reconnaissance drone for the German Air Force based on the proven American RQ-4 Global Hawk. This already well-known platform was to be fitted with European electronics from EADS, the now-defunct European industrial giant that preceded Airbus. The program turned into a major financial and public-relations failure for the German Ministry of Defense, which was widely blamed for the setbacks. After roughly $500 million had been spent on flight-testing the prototype, Germany canceled the project. Officials cited limits on conducting such missions in Europe’s congested airspace and the lack of any realistic prospect of certification by EASA, the European Union Aviation Safety Agency. Photo: Airbus. Thirteen years later, we are witnessing another spectacular and highly ambitious attempt to combine the capabilities of industrial partners on both sides of the Atlantic. This time, two industry heavyweights have taken on the challenge: Europe’s Airbus and America’s Kratos. Their task is to develop a joint solution built on the latest advances in autonomy, one intended to enhance the capabilities of German and European fighter aircraft. The concept adds a new class of unmanned aircraft to combined combat formations, powered by a European “brain” called MARS (Multiplatform Autonomous Reconfigurable and Secure). It is Europe’s take on the U.S. Air Force’s Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) program, which aims to supplement a fleet of advanced combat aircraft that is too small with new unmanned platforms. The base airframe for the project is Kratos’s Valkyrie, which has been undergoing successive rounds of testing for several years. As with the Euro Hawk, the German side is responsible for the onboard systems. Airbus and Kratos are not the only contenders offering the Bundeswehr European CCA capabilities, however. On March 31, 2026, citing the Bundeswehr’s goal of having such a capability ready by 2029, Rheinmetall and Boeing Australia announced a competing proposal based on the MQ-28 Ghost Bat. Earlier, on July 17, 2025, General Atomics (GA) announced that its facility in Oberpfaffenhofen, near Munich, would support the development of a European CCA. The effort will draw on GA’s work on one of the two designs currently competing for contracts in the first increment of the U.S. program. The prototype being offered in Europe is the YFQ-42A, which is competing against Anduril’s YFQ-44A. Photo: Airbus. It is widely recognized that in an increasingly complex and contested threat environment, modern air forces facing shrinking manned fleets need more affordable combat mass, meaning more aircraft, both manned and unmanned. In the future, the Valkyrie is also expected to extend the reach, firepower, and survivability of European manned fighters such as the Eurofighter Typhoon. According to Airbus, the U740 will feature an internal weapons bay, which could prove a significant advantage. It will also have a maximum takeoff weight of about three tons, a range of more than 5,000 kilometers (3,100 miles), and an operational ceiling of approximately 13,700 meters (45,000 feet). Notably, runway operations are being offered as an alternative to rail-launched takeoffs, which are preferred for safety reasons. Kratos has also tested a special cart for launching the aircraft from a runway. Photo: Airbus. In March 2026, Airbus announced that it was preparing two Valkyries, purchased specifically from Kratos, for flight testing at its facility in Manching, near Munich. These tests deserve close attention. In the previous decade, Germany failed in its attempt to close a gap in its reconnaissance capabilities. That effort was also an attractive offer to strengthen NATO: it would have added a national asset for airborne ground surveillance to the Alliance Ground Surveillance (AGS) system, an offer Germany ultimately could not fulfill. It is worth remembering that Germany has already suffered a deep disappointment and a very costly financial and reputational failure, when its defense ministry misjudged the full range of risks inherent in international ventures of this kind. Joint international projects are, by their very nature, more difficult than national ones. About the author Col. (Ret.) Józef M. Brzezina, a former Polish Air Force officer, is a defense writer and analyst with more than 25 years of experience contributing to leading military publications and online outlets. His work focuses on unmanned aircraft systems (UAS), manned combat aviation, and the employment of weapons and military equipment in modern armed conflict.

title: Behind the scenes on how IDF got its biggest ‘hasbara’ win of the war - exclusive
body: It was the early evening of October 17, 2023, Israel time, and then IDF Chief Spokesman Daniel Hagari was on the way to make a daily statement about the state of the then 10-day-old war.A female officer whispered to him that there were reports of a mass death incident at an attack on a hospital.Hamas had fired a barrage of rockets at 6:15 p.m., Palestinian Islamic Jihad had fired its own barrage of around 10 rockets around 7:00 p., and shortly after that barrage there were reports of an explosion at the al-Ahli Hospital.No reporters asked Hagari any questions about the incident because the reports were still fresh, which was good because no one within Israel's military or government apparatuses had a clue at that point of whether Israel was responsible or not.Hamas claimed around 500 Palestinian civilians had been killed, and the news spread like wildfire across the planet from Al Jazeera to the BBC to The New York Times, and on to other secondary sites taking their information from those major outlets.The IDF Spokesperson's Office went into high gear trying to connect the dots between videos and imagery of the alleged incident coming out from open sources compared to any inside special intelligence Israel might have.There were several calls between senior IDF spokesperson's office officials and senior air force officials to ascertain what had really happened and to quickly decide how to probe the situation.Top air force officials did not initially know about the incident.Within a few hours, the initial reports and the beginnings of second-round reports started to present the incident as a more solid fact.IDF Spokesperson's Office insisted on gathering facts firstThere was already pressure from the political echelon to simply deny it as a ridiculous allegation, but the IDF Spokesperson's Office would insist on first gathering the facts.This was no easy call. Simply the initial reports themselves, without even being validated, were already causing real-world riots in Amman, Turkey, and Cairo.Also, then-US president Joe Biden had boarded his plane before the incident and was on his way to the Middle East for a summit with Arab leaders.However, because of the unconfirmed reports, his summit was canceled by the Arab leaders who were alternating between fury at Israel and fear for their own populations if the incident were true.But Biden was already on his plane, so he said he was still going to land in Israel to show solidarity with the Israeli people after Hamas's horrifying invasion.The IDF Spokesperson's Office hoped that they would be able to resolve the issue before Biden landed, but there was still significant uncertainty.But because of all of the unique momentous events happening at once, they understood the magnitude and gravity of the incident. It was an incident which could have stopped the entire war in its tracks. There would later be a few other major incidents of that magnitude that could have stopped the war, but this was the first one. At a second stage, the air force's first review of battle damage assessments (BDA) in Gaza was that there was an air force bomb for which there still was no BDA.It had been fired at a target that was a full kilometer away from the hospital in terms of the strike radius. But there were concerns that the proximity was close enough that a misfire could not be ruled out completely without probing further.What if JDAM bomb had gone off course?What if a JDAM bomb had gone off course? The IDF was carrying out a huge volume of airstrikes, and it was inevitable eventually that there would be errors, as with all wars.Throughout the crisis, then-Defense Minister Yoav Gallant and then-IDF Chief of Staff Herzi Halevi were seeking and receiving debates about the incident, because it was viewed as having the potential power to prematurely end the war before Israel's counter-invasion of Gaza began (the full invasion only started on October 27).In light of the second air force status update, it was decided to send a drone to the hospital perimeter to see if the hospital had been hit accidentally by an Israeli missile.This process, including receiving footage and assessing the footage, would take a few precious hours, with much of the world continuing to boil over against Israel.The IDF would later release a map showing the rocket launches of Hamas and the Islamic |Jihad against Israel.As The Jerusalem Post would later report when visiting Israeli radars and interviewing Israeli LOTEM digital data-sharing commanders, IDF operations had tools that recorded every rocket launch from Gaza.One could see from the vectors that there were launches fired from close proximity to the hospital and which passed over the hospital. The IDF spokesperson's office, the Intelligence Directorate, and the air force were working to connect that map to hitting the hospital.IDF intercepts Hamas conversation about incidentAfter a few more hours, the IDF intelligence division intercepted astounding messages from two Hamas operatives. In these discussions, they admitted that they had misfired a rocket from a cemetery and that it hit the hospital.Intercepted Hamas communications verified internally that this was what in fact happened, despite the fact that they continued to lie to the world externally.The IDF spokesperson's office was buoyed and requested taking the almost unprecedented step of publishing the secretly intercepted information.A deputy of IDF Intelligence Chief Aharon Haliva, at the rank of brigadier general, approved publishing the conversations. They said to paraphrase some of it to protect certain security considerations, but did not ask for too much in terms of editing.Around 11:00 p.m., Hagari issued a statement in English – as opposed to his standard Hebrew statements - that the IDF had obtained intelligence proving that Palestinian Islamic Jihad had fired its missiles at the hospital.Maybe this would turn the tide.The IDF spokesperson's office was dismayed by the world and media reaction: there was almost no change.The world was in such a frenzy of condemnation and anger, and the narrative was so extreme and important to maintain for critics of Israel that Hagari's words about having intelligence, without more, had zero impact.Halevi asked the IDF spokesperson's office for recommendations.Swiftly, the response came back that the discussions should be released.It was one thing to have the approval of Haliva's top IDF intelligence deputy, and another to also have Halevi, who was the IDF chief and had previously headed IDF intelligence.Haliva, Unit 8200 Chief Yossi Sariel, and others were also on board and invested massive efforts to prepare for the release of this highly classified intercepted conversation.This required an extensive fast-forward process, but which still ensured not to harm Israeli intelligence sources. It was due to take 4-6 additional agonizing hours.There was a debate among top IDF Spokesperson's Office officials about what else to do.It was decided that the IDF would publish video footage from the air force of the attack and portions of information from Israeli radars.Further, Hagari would carry out a major press conference live in English in the morning to give the disclosures more volume.There was a third exchange with the air force.Their drone, which had been sent hours earlier to probe the situation, had finally proven that Israel's missile had not hit the hospital.It was unequivocally not a hit by an Israeli or American weapon.Also, it clarified that what had been hit was not the hospital itself, but the parking lot, which had many evacuated refugees.An analysis learned that the rocket had traveled such a short trajectory that it was still full of gas, and it was this gas and the sharp nails inside that caused dozens of deaths, around 50 - not 500.Later, the IDF learned that Hamas always just rushed, without checking any facts, to claim around 500 were dead anytime it thought it had a chance at claiming a mass death incident.A reservist from the international spokesperson team wrote the text of Hagari's speech the next morning. There was no time to rehearse.IDF Col. and chief Arabic spokesperson Avichai Adraee personally translated the Gazan discussions to make sure they were worded correctly.It started to seem possible that when Biden would check, he would be able to view the information as highly verified, and that it really would be released before he landed in Israel.The next steps were coordinated not only with the air force and IDF intelligence, but also with Halevi, with Maj. Gen, Yaron Finkleman.An entire operational probe which could take weeks or months was completed in a matter of several hours.But much of this had been accomplished ad hoc.Later, the IDF would build an improved apparatus for handling such crises.Hagari's speech the morning afterFinally, it came time for Hagari's big morning speech.The Post was present at the time, and there was an unusual air of excitement given that often such press conferences were just a rehash of news which had been disseminated throughout the day.Hagari issued his list of dramatic statements, but that was only stage one.Despite all the highly specific data points and astounding Hamas conversation transcripts, the first question showed there was still a major problem.The angle of the first question was: the IDF lied to us about Shireen Abu Akleh; why should we believe you? In their understanding of the IDF's spokesperson's office, much of the foreign media viewed the IDF as having lost its credibility over two prior incidents: with a false denial of the IDF's mistaken killing of Al Jazeera Arab-American reporter Abu Akleh in the West Bank on May 11, 2022 (later the IDF admitted killing her) and with the false Gaza invasion and bombing of the "Gaza Metro" on May 14, 2021 (the IDF misled foreign media to say an invasion had started to try to trick Hamas into entering its tunnel network just before the IDF then bombed the network).Hagari responded that he had been in his role only during 2023 and that before that he was the commander of Israel's navy commandos. He said he never spoke about Abu Akleh, but was presenting three facts about the current incident.These facts were: 1) radar data on Gaza rockets; 2) telephone call intercepts; and 3) video provided by the air force. Hagari told reporters they could check with all of their local-home military officials: this was not a US or Israeli munition - 1000%.After a few hours, BBC and The New York Times changed their coverage of the incident.Biden saw the press conference while he was flying to Israel on Air Force One.When he later commented on the incident, he completely adopted the Israeli version of events.This incident rebuilt some IDF credibility, but it was still very hard to keep.The IDF knew that it would not do as well in every crisis. Put simply: sometimes the IDF does not understand what happened in the fog of war.Or the IDF figures out what happened, but it lacks the perfect video and phone calls.Sometimes even if the IDF gets all of the data, it does not get all the relevant data until much later, when the media might have already moved on.The longer a war goes, the harder it gets to impact the narrative and the curve of the coverage.Later, there was the World Central Kitchen incident and the bakeries incident, and these were not always resolved well, and the government apparatus as a whole was often not ready.There is also a difference between the mainstream media and social media. On social media, there were sites still falsely claiming that Israel had killed children at the al-Ahli hospital on a large scale even months later, because they can choose to ignore the facts.How IDF disclosed informationHow could Israel disclose classified sources and methods?The Post has learned that disclosing eavesdropping on cellular communications is less complicated than some other instances.In this case, the Post understands that the sources were intelligence operatives. In contrast, there are some sources which Israel cannot burn, as in the Eli Feldstein episode. But in this case, with different kinds of technology, the IDF could cope with the losses.IDF sources believe Israel needs a diplomatic public relations mechanism, not just the IDF spokesperson's office.Over three years, there were many crises, and there is a strategic price that Israel needs to take into account, according to the IDF.The war over the narrative is complex, but it is profoundly important to combat disinformation with facts, data, and knowledge.

title: Real Madrid beat Barcelona 2-1 in La Liga Clasico
body: Kylian Mbappe struck twice to earn Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid a 2-1 Clasico victory over La Liga leaders Barcelona on Sunday at Camp Nou, cutting the gap to three points. French superstar Mbappe opened the scoring before the interval and then slotted home late on to inflict Barca’s first domestic defeat of the campaign after Raphinha had equalised for the champions. Real Madrid remain third, behind Atletico Madrid and Hansi Flick’s Barca, who had won their first nine games before a chastening week. The Catalans suffered a second straight defeat after losing on Tuesday against Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League. Barca had won six of the seven previous Clasicos since the German arrived but were surprisingly subdued against Mourinho’s side. Los Blancos, without suspended winger Vinicius Junior, won their fifth straight game across all competitions and are finding their footing under veteran Portuguese coach Mourinho. The opening period of the game was cagey, with few opportunities. Barca defender Pau Cubarsi twice reacted well to shut down Mbappe, while Real Madrid’s Marc Cucurella took a rapid liking for Lamine Yamal’s shirt, constantly grabbing at the 19-year-old winger. Anthony Gordon, playing in his first Clasico since joining Barcelona from Newcastle, backheeled the ball to Raphinha, who fired narrowly wide as Barca threatened. The hosts were dealt a setback when young defender Xavi Espart pulled up hurt and needed to be replaced by Alejandro Balde before the half-hour mark. Andriy Lunin, playing in goal for Madrid after Thibaut Courtois pulled out of the squad with flu, saved at his near post from Gordon before the visitors took the lead. Mbappe scored his 10th league goal of the season and also his easiest, with Barca’s Gerard Martin clearing a cross straight at the Frenchman, who deflected it into the net. Barca responded by carving out a glorious chance for an equaliser but teenage sensation Yamal for once miscued in front of goal, firing wide when poised to level. The game opened up and Yan Diomande came close to doubling Madrid’s lead before half-time, drilling into the side-netting. – Sting in the tail – Martin redeemed himself early in the second half as he held off Jude Bellingham, who could neither beat the defender nor find a free Mbappe. Raphinha, who had a quiet first half, pulled Barcelona level just after the hour mark. Pedri fed the Brazilian, La Liga’s top goalscorer with 13, who fired through Bellingham’s legs and Lunin could not keep the shot out. The Ukrainian goalkeeper did make a superb save to deny Martin at a corner, as Barcelona flowed forward with the wind finally in their sails. Yamal bent an effort wide with Lunin at full stretch and Barca substitute Frenkie de Jong had a shot desperately blocked by Dean Huijsen. There was a sting in the tail for the Catalans though as substitute Gabriel Jesus lost possession and Madrid raced through on goal. Eduardo Camavinga beat Cubarsi and unselfishly cut the ball back for Mbappe to tuck home his second of the night into an empty net with Joan Garcia drawn out of position. title: Testing new Goldbod CEO’s ‘new law’ on small-scale mining against the law
body: “Once it’s not a water body; it’s not a forest reserve or… place like a roadside, whether the person has a licence or not; the government says we should allow the person to mine and register and regularise them” – CEO, GoldBod 1. Section 9 of the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703) provides that a person shall not conduct mining, prospecting or exploration on land in Ghana unless granted a mineral right under the Act — and this applies even where the person owns or holds rights in the land. Section 82 separately provides that a person shall not engage in asmall-scale mining operation without a licence granted by the Minister or an authorised officer, and it does so “notwithstanding any law to the contrary.” 2. Mining without that licence is not merely irregular; it is a crime. Under section 99 as originally enacted, small-scale mining without the Minister’s licence attracted a minimum fine of 1,000 penalty units and up to three years’ imprisonment. The Minerals and Mining (Amendment) Act, 2019 (Act 995) dramatically increased this. According to the Minerals Commission, a Ghanaian engaged in unlicensed mining or mining support services faces a fine of 10,000 to 15,000 penalty units and 15 to 25 years’ imprisonment; a non-Ghanaian faces 100,000 to 350,000 penalty units and 20 to 25 years, with deportation after sentence. Equipment and product are seized on arrest and must be forfeited to the State on conviction. 3. So the instruction described is an instruction to permit the commission of a crime carrying, for a Ghanaian, a mandatory minimum of fifteen years. 4. A ministerial or administrative direction that unlicensed persons “should be allowed to mine” is therefore ultra vires. The Minister’s statutory power under section 82 is a power to grant licences. It is not a power to authorise mining without one. A public officer who purports to exercise a power he does not have acts outside the law, and Article 296 — which requires that discretionary power be exercised fairly, candidly and not arbitrarily or capriciously — bites on top of that. 5. Section 18 of Act 703 (Minerals and Mining Act) requires environmental and forestry clearance from every mineral right holder — not only from those operating in forests or rivers. A site that is neither a water body nor a forest reserve nor a roadside is still unlawful to mine without an environmental permit. 6. The statement’s implicit test — anywhere that is not expressly prohibited is permitted — reverses the statutory scheme, which is a permission-based regime: nothing is permitted unless affirmatively licensed. 7. Formalisation of artisanal and small-scale mining is not contrary to Ghanaian law. It is lawful policy, and it is arguably obligatory. As a party to the Minamata Convention on Mercury, Ghana must, under Article 7 and Annex C, develop a national action plan for artisanal and small-scale gold mining, and formalisation is an express element of that plan. The Minister has express power under section 89 to designate areas, and under section 82 to grant licences. A properly structured fast-track registration drive, the Community Mining Scheme model, and district-level licensing support are all lawful vehicles. 8. The illegality lies entirely in the sequence. The law permits: register first, then mine. The statement describes mining first, then registering. Regularisation cannot retroactively cure a completed offence. Once unlicensed mining has occurred, the offence under section 99 is complete. Subsequent registration does not expunge it. Only a nolle prosequi by the Attorney-General under Article 88(3)–(4) or a presidential pardon under Article 72 can affect criminal liability, and neither is available as a general administrative policy. 9. The Goldbod CEO’s assurance is no defence to the miner. Mistake of law does not excuse, and no estoppel can arise against a statute — a citizen cannot acquire by official representation a right that Parliament has withheld. The miner who relies on this assurance is exposed to fifteen years’ imprisonment; the official who gave it faces no exposure at all. That asymmetry is itself an argument that the practice is indefensible. 10. An official who directs that unlicensed mining be permitted may be: • liable as an abettor under the Criminal Offences Act, 1960 (Act 29), s.20, to the section 99 offence; • liable under the Act 995 offences relating to facilitating participation in small-scale mining and providing equipment contrary to law; • in breach of the following provisions of the 1992 Constitution: Article 284 (conflict of interest) and Article 296; • in breach of the State’s Article 36(9) duty to protect and safeguard the national environment, with the citizen’s reciprocal duty under Article 41(k). The CEO cannot claim ignorance of the law. This is not a slip of the tongue. This is a deliberate strategy to test Ghanaians’ resolve to fight the galamsey menace, which poses an existential threat to the State. It confirms a bold attempt by the NDC to take us a step deeper into galamsey and to confirm that Ghana is a galam-state. This statement undermines all the so-called efforts that the government has been touting as a success story in its fight against galamsey. It also affirms, in no uncertain terms, the allegation that at least some of the gold Goldbod buys is linked to galamsey. Indeed, this is not the first time the current government has made pronouncements on galamsey, which suggests an unwillingness to help fight the galamsey menace. Yet, overall, society’s reaction to them has been largely weak. So they are emboldened to stretch it further. We should not lie down and let this happen. We voted the NDC into power. We did not give them the power to trample over us. The power is still with us. We must take all legal action to resist galamsey.

title: Ukraine is stalling EU-required reform of bureau that can raid any official, risking European money it badly needs
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Whoever controls Ukraine’s State Bureau of Investigation wields enormous influence over law enforcement, judges, and government officials. The EU wants Ukraine to reform it, and Ukraine’s government is likely to pass changes that satisfy monitoring requirements on paper while leaving the body effectively under the President’s Office’s control, the investigative outlet Texty reports . The stakes are money and power at once. The State Bureau of Investigation, known by its Ukrainian initials DBR, investigates officials, judges, prosecutors, and soldiers. So choosing an independent director is one of the rule-of-law conditions the EU has tied to Ukraine’s 2026 and 2027 budget aid. Yet the version the government may pass would change how the director is chosen only for the one after next, in 2032. Brussels wants the model used at the anti-corruption bureau NABU, where the chief cannot be confirmed without the votes of independent foreign experts. Who picks the watchdog Today a nine-member commission selects the director: three named by the president three by a parliament his party dominates three proposed by the government on international partners’ suggestion. That leaves the foreign experts without a decisive vote and the President’s Office effectively choosing the winner. Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy promised in January that a reform bill would reach parliament within a month. It is now October, and there is none. Director Oleksii Sukhachov’s term ends this year, so his successor will be picked under the old rules. Sukhachov has publicly argued that overhauling the bureau during the war would threaten the state. The deadline to adopt the reform was October. To carry it out, the end of 2026. Miss it, and Ukraine risks reputational damage and the European funding it needs amid a budget deficit, money the EU has frozen before when anti-corruption guarantees slipped. A factory of “procedural nightmaring” What makes the fight so bitter is that the bureau’s searches, seizures, and summonses are levers over individuals and whole institutions. For example, NABU’s Operation Midas tapes, from the $100 million kickback case at the state nuclear company Energoatom, mention the bureau’s entire leadership. In March 2025, its investigators searched the commission that vets and appoints Ukraine’s judges, itself reformed with international experts, in what the commission called pressure that could stall the courts. Cases against the bureau’s own officials, meanwhile, are handled by a unit inside the bureau. And its director sits under his own cloud: the outlet Slidstvo.Info reported that his brother bought 143 apartments cheaply from a developer. Nevertheless, a court banned publication, and eight newsrooms jointly ran the story.
