title: Zelensky says Serbia faces 'new chapter' after Vucic concedes defeat
body:
Editor's note: The story has been updated to include comments from President Volodymyr Zelensky.
Ukraine is ready to continue expanding cooperation with Belgrade, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Oct. 26, after former Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat in parliamentary elections to a student-led protest movement.
"Based on a stratified sample, it is clear that we have lost this election. The student blockade list won," Vucic said in a press briefing on Oct. 25.
According to Vucic, the Students' List party, backed by the protest coalition, is projected to take between 135 and 140 seats in Serbia 's Parliament. Vucic's Serbian Progressive Party appears to have come in second in the elections, and will have 105 seats in Parliament.
"This is clearly a new chapter in the history of the country and its people", Zelensky said in a social media post following the election.
"We wish Serbia success, real development, and warm relations with the European community. We in Ukraine thank Serbia for respecting our people, our state, and our independence."
For almost two years, student-led demonstrations in Serbia rallied against Vucic's right-wing incumbent Serbian Progressive Party. Protesting against alleged corruption in the government, the movement was triggered when a train station canopy in the city of Novi Sad collapsed in 2024, killing 16.
Vucic previously announced his resignation as Serbia's president on Sept. 27, allowing him to run as prime minister in the nation's October parliamentary elections.
Vucic, having served as either Serbia's prime minister or president since 2014, was known as a right-wing populist leader with authoritarian tendencies and warm ties with Russia.
The elections saw Serbia's highest voter turnout, 70%, since the dissolution of Yugoslavia in 1992, according to Reuters.
The election results are being hailed as a momentous political shift for Serbia, potentially turning the Balkan country away from ties with Russia and Vladimir Putin, who endorsed Vucic.
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov told reporters on Oct. 26 that Moscow "greatly appreciated" Vucic's contribution to Russia-Serbia ties.
He added that Moscow hopes Serbia's new government would continue developing relations with Russia, which he said "was in Serbia's interests."
The defeat of Serbia's right-wing government echoes recent elections in Hungary. In April, populist leader Viktor Orban, also endorsed by Putin, was defeated in a landslide election.
Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar drew an explicit parallel between this election and that in his country which saw him rise to power, celebrating the Serbian opposition's victory in an Oct. 25 post on X.
"In Serbia, (Aleksandar Vucic) has conceded defeat. The Students’ List has won an absolute majority in the elections. Celebrations have begun in the streets across Serbia. Sound familiar?" Magyar wrote.
The Guardian also reported that Magyar subsequently spoke with the Students' List leadership and offered Hungary's support, saying his own electoral victory in April had encouraged the Serbian movement during its struggle.
Since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Serbia has sought to strike a careful diplomatic balance between Moscow and the West. Russia has historically been one of Serbia's key diplomatic allies, and Serbia relied heavily on Russia for natural gas .
According to reports, Serbia has also indirectly supplied arms to Ukraine, although Vucic publicly denied it in May 2025.

title: Airbus to Open Helicopter Maintenance Hub in Morocco for West Africa
body: Airbus will open a helicopter maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) subsidiary in Morocco in the coming months, Mickaël Bertrand, Managing Director of Airbus Helicopters Morocco, told Morocco World News (MWN) at the Marrakech Air Show. The centre will serve Morocco first and is designed to cover all of West Africa, Bertrand said. Bertrand framed the step as a climb up the value chain. Airbus started “75 years ago with basic parts,” he told MWN, moved into composites, and now moves into helicopter maintenance. What Airbus already supports in Morocco Airbus supports “more than 60 aircraft today, mainly helicopters” in the kingdom. The Royal Moroccan Air Force, the Royal Navy and the Royal Gendarmerie operate them. Airbus Helicopters first announced the Moroccan subsidiary in July 2024. The plan has three parts: technical and customer support for the roughly 60 helicopters in service, more MRO capacity, and a training centre with flight simulators for Moroccan and international pilots. Two orders drive the timing. On 18 November 2025 at the Dubai Airshow, Morocco signed for ten H225M helicopters for the Royal Moroccan Air Force. They replace Puma helicopters that have flown for more than 40 years, according to Airbus. The H225M order centres on combat search and rescue (CSAR). Airbus says the aircraft carry a double rescue hoist, a searchlight and a Safran Euroflir 410 electro-optical system, a sensor turret that gives day and night imaging. Training fleet and support partner The Royal Moroccan Air Force also ordered the H135 light twin-engine helicopter for primary military training. Airbus announced the order at the Farnborough Airshow in July 2022 and named Moroccan firm Heliconia as its support partner. Arnaud Montalvo, Head of Africa and Middle East at Airbus Helicopters, called the type “a reliable, cost-efficient multirole helicopter” at the time. The order covered 12 H135M helicopters , according to later Airbus reporting. The first two arrived in Meknes on 7 September 2023 and replace the AgustaBell AB206A and AB206B helicopters at the air force flight school at 1 Air Base, Rabat/Salé. The package includes flight training devices and training for instructor and maintenance pilots. Bertrand told Hespress in July 2024 that all 12 had been delivered. A mixed fleet to support The workload is not uniform. The Royal Gendarmerie alone flies a long list of Airbus-family types, according to Airbus Helicopters reporting on its H125 delivery: AS355 Ecureuil, AS365 Dauphin II, AS550 Fennec, SA315 Lama, SA316 Alouette III, SA342 Gazelle, SE3130 Alouette II, EC135 and EC145 helicopters, plus two new H125s for search, rescue and firefighting. That inventory is undated, so current numbers may differ. Older types like the Alouette and Lama need spares and skills that are harder to source each year. New types like the H225M and H135M need connected diagnostics and trained technicians. One facility that handles both would carry real cost, and the trade-off is how fast Airbus can build the workforce. Industrial base behind the hub Airbus runs five legal entities in Morocco, Bertrand told MWN: Airbus Atlantic Maroc, Airbus Atlantic Maroc Composites, Airbus Atlantic Maroc Aero, Airbus Defence and Space Maroc and Airbus Helicopters Maroc. They employ about 1,300 people directly and support “more or less 10,000” indirect jobs, by his account. Airbus Atlantic Maroc Aero is the newest. It is the former Spirit AeroSystems site in Casablanca, which makes A321 and A220 components. Airbus closed the Spirit purchase on 8 December 2025. On 7 October, Gabriel Sémelas, Airbus President for Africa and the Middle East, signed the consortium agreement for the African Centre of Manufacturing Excellence (ACME). The consortium is tied to Mohammed VI Polytechnic University and includes Morocco’s Ministry of Industry and Trade, the National Defense Administration, OCP, Boeing, Lockheed Martin, Safran Nacelles, Airbus and CETIM Maroc. Bertrand said it opens research and engineering work for military and civil programmes. Asked about a final assembly line, Bertrand said that is “really complex in terms of aircraft” and that Airbus is not at that stage. Asharq Bloomberg reported on 10 October that Airbus plans a third Moroccan factory of about 6,900 square metres, which would raise its local footprint by 30%. What it means A local MRO centre shortens the support chain for Moroccan operators. Helicopters that now depend on overseas facilities for heavy checks could be serviced at home, which should raise availability for the incoming H225M fleet. The regional case is still prospective. Airbus has not said how many helicopters the site can handle or which West African air forces and civil operators will use it. A formal announcement is expected in the coming months, and the site, the investment and the first outside customer are the details to watch.

title: The odds against Tinubu, By Wole Olaoye
body:
…If major opposition figures (Obi, Atiku, Kwankwaso, Adebayo, or a broader coalition platform) successfully present a single consolidated ticket, they would have aggregated core voting blocs across the South-East, South-South, urban centres, and northern strongholds, creating a direct head-to-head race with a real possibility of an opposition victory or, at worst, triggering Nigeria’s first-ever presidential run-off.
Candidate Bola Ahmed Tinubu is formidable enough without the presidential halo. Now, with all presidential powers at his command, he has to be considered a frontrunner in the forthcoming elections. But there are headwinds signalling the fact that although he is redoubtable, he is not unbeatable.
The problem with many of his opponents over the years is that they took him for granted. Part of that mindset is demonstrated when the opposition relies on rehashed stories of Tinubu’s failings to sway the electorate, instead of presenting alternative programmes to some of his manifestly unpopular policies.
The way things stand at the moment, none of the other presidential candidates has enough gravitas to unseat Tinubu. The ruling APC is the only party that has unveiled its campaign structure and rolled out its vote-catching machine. All the opposition parties have barely 83 days to overtake the current order.
Where the game will begin to appear interesting is if, as I argue later in this piece, Atiku Abubakar of the ADC and Peter Obi of the NDC team up to present what Anti-Tinubu elements have described as a dream ticket.
In 2023, the opposition vote was split among the PDP, Labour Party (LP), and NNPP. A unified ticket between Obi and Atiku could pool their substantial voting bases — bringing together Obi’s strong momentum in the South-East, South-South, and urban youth demographics alongside Atiku’s established political machinery and influence across parts of the North.
Under the Nigerian Constitution, a winning candidate must secure a plurality of votes and at least 25 per cent of the votes in two-thirds of the states (24 out of 36) plus the Federal Capital Territory. A dispassionate assessment of the current state of affairs shows that neither Obi nor Atiku can singlehandedly attain this threshold.
The most significant hurdle in any merger would be deciding who takes the presidential slot. If Atiku heads the ticket, it might alienate Obi’s supporters in the South-East and many reform-minded voters who view Obi as a symbol of structural political change. If Obi heads the ticket, it could face friction from impatient traditional northern political elites who can’t wait for power to return to the North.
The accepted wisdom in political circles is that 80-year-old Atiku cannot conceivably accept being vice president to Obi, while Kwankwaso will rue being left out in the cold in the event of an Atiku/Obi ticket. It’s all about self-interest. Until the elections come and go, you cannot vouch for where some of the major players will eventually cast their lot.
The looming ghost of tribal/geopolitical manoeuvres cannot be discountenanced in the calculus. If the wishes of many northern opposition elements were horses, Peter Obi will subordinate his ambition to Atiku and agree to play second fiddle. As already stated, an alliance of the two leaders would fundamentally reshape the political landscape, presenting a formidable challenge to President Tinubu and the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).
The recent gathering of anti-Tinubu elements in the G-100 is a significant development. The coalition has tried to bypass direct ego clashes by setting up joint legal and media committees to manage expectations, but individual loyalists often pressure their preferred principals not to compromise.
While national opposition leaders negotiate a mega-coalition in Abuja, local state chapters operate under entirely different survival tensions. In many states, opposition parties (such as factions of the PDP, SDP, and ADC) are fierce rivals at the local level. If a national coalition mandates that a specific party yield its structure in a particular state to accommodate another coalition partner, local party executives often rebel, leading to localised anti-coalition friction or secret parallel alignments.
An example of how local politics and personal ambition affect loyalty can be seen in the case of the former deputy senate president, Ovie Omo-Agege, who defected to the National Democratic Congress (NDC) after he officially quit the All Progressives Congress (APC) in May. Internal friction and ticket rivalries within the APC played a central role in his defection to NDC, whose flag he will be flying in the race for the Delta Central Senatorial District in 2027.
The looming ghost of tribal/geopolitical manoeuvres cannot be discountenanced in the calculus. If the wishes of many northern opposition elements were horses, Peter Obi will subordinate his ambition to Atiku and agree to play second fiddle. As already stated, an alliance of the two leaders would fundamentally reshape the political landscape, presenting a formidable challenge to President Tinubu and the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).
But diehard Obi supporters will not be receptive to their hero reverting to the role of a spare tyre. Obi is the most credible face of the South-East in the current electoral race. The South-West has multiple notable aspirants, including President Bola Tinubu, Prince Adewole Adebayo and Governor Seyi Makinde, while the North-East features figures such as Atiku Abubakar and Mohammed Hayatuddeen. The South-South has Rotimi Amaechi. The North-Central and North-West regions are yet to produce strong frontline contenders.
Perhaps the three regions in the North are strategically avoiding multiple aspirants to prevent vote splitting?
There are other strategic machinations in the mix. If you have your ears to the ground, you will hear the whispering campaign in the North of a plan to encourage political attrition between the South-West and South-East, so that while the Yoruba and Igbo Turks of the South are at each other’s throats, the Northern elite can perfect their plan of installing one of their own in power.
It sounds so childishly pedestrian at first until you re-analyse the verbal effusions of one of the perennial appointees whose definition of the ‘North’ is “I, Me and Myself”.
…If the election were contested under the existing multi-candidate dynamic (APC, PDP, LP, NNPP), despite economic headwinds, President Tinubu and the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) can secure a national plurality, even with a reduced vote share, dependent on state spread requirements.
The Northern Elders’ Forum and other such bodies who could have led the way in campaigning for their elected governors to banish the almajiri system (which hides under the cloak of religion to legitimise destitution), and other social drawbacks in the region are suddenly awake in this season of political horse-trading. Their critics are asking where they were when Buhari was running for a second term after his uneventful first leg.
There will always be jostling for elbow room between various ethnic nationalities, but I think the Yoruba and Igbo wouldn’t be foolish enough to swallow the bait of seasoned provocateurs determined to drive a wedge between them. Elections will come and go. People will remain.
The same admonition goes to the fake reprisalists in the north, who are always ready to justify ethnic cleansing and forceful takeover of other people’s ancestral lands in the name of revenging some ancient indeterminate wrongs done by the routed victims. In this season of electioneering, we are seeing how some people are digging up their demons from infernal depths in the name of political strategy.
Difficult as it may seem, the opposition should either come together to put their best combination forward or be prepared to lick their wounds as disparate vanquished wannabes.
(a) If the election were contested under the existing multi-candidate dynamic (APC, PDP, LP, NNPP), despite economic headwinds, President Tinubu and the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) can secure a national plurality, even with a reduced vote share, dependent on state spread requirements.
(b) If major opposition figures (Obi, Atiku, Kwankwaso, Adebayo, or a broader coalition platform) successfully present a single consolidated ticket, they would have aggregated core voting blocs across the South-East, South-South, urban centres, and northern strongholds, creating a direct head-to-head race with a real possibility of an opposition victory or, at worst, triggering Nigeria’s first-ever presidential run-off.
Wole Olaoye is a Public Relations consultant and veteran journalist. He can be reached on [email protected] , Twitter: @wole_olaoye; Instagram: woleola2021

title: Major European countries do not want to renew energy alliances with Russia — Zelensky
body:
Volodymyr Zelensky made these remarks in an interview with TSN.Tyzhden , according to Ukrinform.
“So far, I haven’t seen any requests from major European countries… to lift sanctions and restore energy alliances with the Russian Federation. I don’t see this happening, because we would react. I would definitely react,” the President assured.
At the same time, he noted that some European countries depend on oil and gas supplies from Russia. “Unfortunately, this is a request from Europe to keep everyone in the EU together—to somehow accommodate these countries,” Zelensky noted.
He recalled that the EU has decided to terminate major energy contracts with Russia by the end of 2027.
“The replacement of ‘Russian’ products is being led by the Americans anyway; it’s everywhere on the market. We see this presence. Europe is with us; Europe is united,” the head of state emphasized.
As reported by Ukrinform, last year EU countries officially approved a regulation on the phased cessation of imports of Russian pipeline and liquefied natural gas by 2027.

title: Police Arrest Bakery Chain Owner in €100 Million Tax Fraud Probe
body: Greek police have arrested the owner of a major bakery chain and around 50 other people in an investigation into an alleged tax fraud scheme estimated to have cost the Greek state more than €100 million, including unpaid social security contributions. Officers from the Directorate for Combating Organised Crime are conducting a large-scale operation that remains ongoing. The arrests include accountants and executives from the businessman’s companies. According to reports, police operations are taking place simultaneously in Athens, Mykonos, Rhodes and Volos. Authorities reportedly arrested the businessman near Ioannina on Sunday as he attempted to leave Greece for Albania, despite being subject to a travel ban. The bakery chain owner had reportedly been living in Dubai and recently returned to Greece. Police had initially planned to arrest him on Monday morning, but information received by investigators indicated that he had left by car and was heading towards Albania, prompting officers to bring forward the operation. According to information released so far, investigators began examining the alleged scheme early this year. More than 520 companies are reportedly linked to the investigation. Authorities suspect that individuals used nominees, or so-called “front men”, to conceal the companies’ actual ownership or business activities. The investigation extends beyond the bakery chain to cover the businessman’s wider commercial operations. Police have not yet completed their operation, and further details are expected as the investigation progresses. title: Courage Babanawo Kwabla elected Ketu South constituency Deputy Youth Organiser
body: A nurse, Courage Babanawo, has been elected as the Ketu South Constituency Deputy Youth Organiser for the National Democratic Congress. He recorded a convincing victory as his contender, Allah Thomas Kwame, polled 80 votes, representing 28% of the total votes. Mr Babanawo’s message to build a stronger youth base for the party resonated well with the delegates, who gave him 205 votes, representing about 72% of the total votes in the constituency executives’ election. In an interview with Joy News, he assured of his readiness to serve, mobilise, and empower the youth at the grassroots level, stressing that the youth are the “backbone and driving force of the NDC”. He believes that committing to building a stronger and more vibrant youth base would increase the party’s performance in the 2028 general election. Mr Babanawo added that he would not relent in working with the other executives to strengthen party structures and ensure unity at every level of the party. “I pledge to serve with loyalty, discipline, humility, and dedication. I will work closely with party leadership, executives, comrades, and all stakeholders to advance the fortunes of the NDC and deepen youth participation in party activities”, he added. Mr Babanawo has served as Deputy Tertiary Education Institutions Network (TEIN) Organiser, Tamale Nursing and Midwifery Training College; TEIN President, Tamale Nursing and Midwifery Training College; Branch Communications Officer, Wuduoba LA Primary; Member, Communications Committee, Ketu South Constituency; Member, Special Operations Committee (Youth Wing), Ketu South NDC; and Communications Team Member, Volta Region.

title: Greece Agrees to Keep Patriot Missile Deployment in Saudi Arabia
body: Greece has agreed to Saudi Arabia’s request to keep a Greek Patriot missile battery in the Kingdom amid the current Middle East crisis, Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis announced during a meeting with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman Al Saud in Riyadh. Mitsotakis condemned attacks against Saudi Arabia and reaffirmed Greece’s practical solidarity with the Kingdom. Greece has supported Saudi air defence with the Patriot battery since 2021. The prime minister said the Greek deployment contributes to both Saudi Arabia’s security and wider regional stability. The battery protects critical energy infrastructure in Yanbu, on Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea coast. During their meeting, Mitsotakis and Mohammed bin Salman reaffirmed the strategic nature of relations between Greece and Saudi Arabia and discussed ways to expand cooperation, particularly in defence, energy and connectivity. They also examined regional developments, with particular attention to Iran and the wider Middle East. Mitsotakis stressed the importance of safeguarding freedom of navigation, noting that Greece, as a major maritime power, places the highest priority on protecting international shipping routes and ensuring the uninterrupted flow of global trade. He reiterated that all parties must respect international law and avoid imposing restrictions on freedom of navigation, warning that such measures could establish a dangerous precedent. Greece and Saudi Arabia Advance Digital Connectivity Project The two leaders also discussed cooperation in digital connectivity, particularly the East to Med Data Corridor (EMC), a project designed to connect Europe and Asia through Greece and Saudi Arabia. The initiative aims to strengthen digital links between the two regions, positioning both countries as key connection points for international data infrastructure. Mitsotakis and Mohammed bin Salman also reviewed preparations for the second meeting of the Greece-Saudi Arabia Supreme Council for Strategic Cooperation. The leaders assessed progress since the council’s first meeting in January 2025, which established a structured institutional framework for cooperation across several sectors. title: U.S. Army: DARPA tests autonomous vehicles at Fort Knox with human-controlled strikes
body: Four autonomous ground vehicles searched for targets and supported a simulated strike at Fort Knox, Kentucky, in a DARPA demonstration of robotic operations beyond friendly front lines. The vehicles handled movement and target detection independently, while a human operator retained authority to approve any engagement, according to the U.S. Army. The October 15 test at St. Vith Range followed a request from U.S. European Command to explore how robots could detect threats ahead of soldiers. It was the team’s first demonstration linking satellite imagery to tactical ground operations, following component and integration testing at contractor sites. The vehicles use technology developed under DARPA’s Robotic Autonomy in Complex Environments with Resiliency program, known as RACER. The program aims to enable autonomous off-road travel at speeds at least comparable to those of a human driver. “We’ve completed about a five-year program on software development for autonomous mobility to go highspeed off-road in complex environments,” said Dr. Jason Gregory, a technical advisor at DARPA. “So, now we can take a vehicle that has a sensor suite and drive-by-wire and equip it with autonomy software so it can be tasked by a Soldier as opposed to manually driven.” At Fort Knox, an operator received satellite imagery indicating a simulated threat and sent the robotic team to investigate. The lead vehicle drove along a road, spotted a potential target halfway up a hill and stopped to await a command. It carried a drone inside a closed box that, in an operational scenario, could be launched to inspect a target or carry munitions for an aerial strike, the Army said. Two other vehicles moved forward to provide cover and support before a simulated rocket hit a target about 300 yards away on an adjacent hill. The fourth vehicle then advanced while the lead vehicle continued over the hilltop. Gregory said the distinction between autonomous movement and human control of weapons was central to the demonstration. “All the targets that are detected by our autonomous assets provide a chip of what they have seen downrange to a human, who then has to approve any type of engagement,” Gregory said. “The operator has total control as to what they want to do about what the robots are seeing.” “All the mobility, all the movement, all the detections, all of that is autonomous,” he said. “But they don’t pull the trigger until a human says pull the trigger.” European Command’s request focused on deploying robotic assets beyond the forward line of troops to provide early warning and help soldiers decide how to respond. Fort Knox was recommended as a test location because its terrain represented conditions in the European theater, Gregory said. “We always had intentions for EUCOM applicability,” Gregory said. “When working with our stakeholders and touchpoints, they had recommended Fort Knox specifically as a representation of the European theater.” The Army said different payloads could also allow the vehicles to transport food, ammunition and other supplies or support casualty evacuation. A further test is expected in December, when DARPA plans to ask soldiers how they would employ the systems. “Soldiers are the best evaluators because they give you honest feedback,” Gregory said. “They know best how they would want to use it.” Go deeper: U.S. Army .

title: Serbia’s Vucic concedes defeat against student-led opposition movement
body:
The long-serving strongman leader of Serbia , Aleksandar Vucic , conceded defeat on Sunday in an election that pitted him and his right-wing party against a diverse student-led opposition movement that spent two years protesting his government.
It was a seismic political shift in the Balkan country where Vucic, who had been endorsed by Russian President Vladimir Putin and who denounced the student movement as a foreign-led attempt to unseat him, led with virtually absolute power for 14 years.
High turnout and gathering tensions marked the highly contested parliamentary election that was a showdown between Vucic and his right-wing Serbian Progressive Party and university students who, accusing the government of corruption and dismantling democracy, had built a popular following across the country.
Serbia’s 6.4 million voters were electing lawmakers to the 250-member Parliament. In conceding the election, Vucic said his party projects that his opponents, the youth-backed Students’ List, will take between 135 and 140 seats while his SNS party will have around 105.
“The Students’ List has won,” Vucic told supporters at his party’s election night event, though he blamed Serbia’s independent media as well as alleged interference by unnamed European countries and an ”American deep state” for the loss.
Vucic said that his SNS party won around 1.7 million votes compared to the Students’ List, which he said took around 2.2 million.
Supporters of the Students’ List immediately flooded onto the streets of Belgrade and other cities, honking horns, shouting and chanting: “Aleksandar is gone,” referring to Vucic.
The outcome, which Vucic announced only around an hour and a half after polls closed, came after tensions had built as voting progressed during the day.
Police in anti-riot gear cordoned off an area in central Belgrade around the election commission headquarters. Special police vehicles could be seen near a Belgrade park where Vucic’s loyalists have been camping for over a year, and large groups of black-clad men had congregated at various points throughout the city.
Vucic was seeking become Serbia’s prime minister after serving two near-full terms as president. He resigned the presidency last month to lead the campaign.
Support for the populist had eroded since 16 people were killed in 2024 when a concrete canopy collapsed at a train station in Novi Sad. That set off a wave of youth protests that blamed the collapse on high-level corruption, cronyism and rampant graft during renovation work at the station.
Despite the protests, Vucic retained considerable support among many of Serbia’s voters. Admirers viewed him as a capable leader who can steer the nation through global uncertainties — the image that was carefully crafted by the mainstream media.
While the increasingly authoritarian Vucic has routinely outplayed Serbia’s fractured opposition in the past, the leaderless youth movement proved to be a tough opponent that rattled his firm grip on power in Serbia like no one else in the 14 years since his party took office.
The newly formed Students’ List movement was shaped by university students but none actually appeared on the election list. Instead, its candidates are little-known experts, athletes, farmers and artists.
This approach was meant to counter Vucic’s one-man rule and restore a sense of community and solidarity. The students’ message during the campaign focused on a non-partisan effort to rebuild Serbia’s economy and restore its democracy.
The students have used youthful energy to attract voters who are disillusioned with local politicians. Vilified by pro-government media, they cycled and walked through the country to reach voters in rural areas — Vucic’s traditional strongholds.
The student victory echoed the recent electoral defeat of a Vucic ally in Hungary, where youth participation helped oust the autocratic Viktor Orbán after 16 years and bring in a new pro-European government. It was likely to resonate beyond Serbia as countries across Europe have faced angry youth and student protests.
Monitors predicted that total turnout in the election could reach around 70%, unseen in Serbia since 2000. During the day, long queues formed at polling stations in Serbia and in cities around the world. Some in the Serbian diaspora were made to vote in the middle of the night after authorities tied voting hours to local Serbian time.
Recent Serbian elections had been marred by irregularities and the EU was closely watching the conduct of Sunday’s vote in a candidate nation for the bloc’s membership.
Independent election monitors reported dozens of cases of irregularities on Sunday such as photographing of ballots that suggested pressure on voters and attempted vote buying.
Both international and local election monitors had expressed concern about the safety and fairness of an election campaign marked by detentions, near-total government control over the media and reports of surveillance and cyberattacks against activists.
Local elections earlier this year in 10 municipalities in Serbia saw violent attacks on journalists and activists. The previous parliamentary vote in 2023 was followed by opposition protests alleging fraud.

title: Iran fears only Netanyahu. On Tuesday, make sure it stays that way - opinion
body: Here is a question: Imagine social media had been around in the early 1930s. What would Winston Churchill's political rivals have said if he had posted images of German troops marching across Europe, warning of what was to come?Well, he didn't have social media, but he did sound the alarm.Churchill warned of the threat of Hitler in a speech to the British Parliament a mere two months after Hitler came to power. The response? His opponents labeled him a warmonger, his remarks dismissed as hysteria.On Sunday, Benjamin Netanyahu shared an AI image of an Iranian nuclear bomb exploding in Tel Aviv. His principal rival, Gadi Eisenkot, called him “hysterical” and accused him of using “lies and scare tactics”.Eisenkot might have said the same about Churchill in 1933. History proved that the danger then was not imaginary and that Churchill was right. Very, very right.Benjamin Netanyahu is today's Churchill at a time when Israel faces a threat which, in my opinion, is many times greater than Europe faced with Hitler in 1939. We know, tragically, the Holocaust happened before Nazi Germany was defeated. But Israel rose out of its ashes.This time, more than seven million Jews - and two million Arabs - face annihilation, and, hit by an Iranian nuclear bomb, Israel will not come back again.The very existence of our country is at stake, and only one man can save it. This is not hyperbole. Gadi Eisenkot dismisses Netanyahu's nuclear warning as political histrionics.Alternative choices to Netanyahu are one and the sameEisenkot's allies offer little reassurance either. Naftali Bennett has already shown his willingness to lead a government which included the left-wing Meretz and the Islamist Ra'am.Avigdor Lieberman for years supported a two-state solution involving handing over territory. And Yair Golan? Here is a would-be prime minister who suggested that Israel killed babies in Gaza "as a hobby"!Why do I mention these names? Because they are the alternative choice to Netanyahu when Israelis go to the polls on Tuesday. Vote for one and you vote for them all.They are the Change Bloc - an assortment that has only one thing in common: ousting Bibi. That objective is their only common ground. Not policy. Not ideology. Not the direction of Israel's future. Just toppling one man. Beyond that, chaos.We have witnessed what happens when chaos and division ensue. Hamas saw the demonstrations, the incitement, the refusals to serve in the IDF, the appearance of Israel as vulnerable. The result was October 7th.Who was behind the protests? The same forces trying to bring Bibi down today. The same forces who do not see the writing on the wall. The same forces who think Netanyahu is a greater threat to Israel than Iran. This is delusional, and it is fatal.Had Iran had the chance, Israel would not be here now. Believe Iranian leaders when they say they want to destroy us. It did not end with the elimination of Khamenei.On the contrary, Iran is more determined than ever to get its hands on a nuclear bomb. It is already rebuilding its nuclear facilities and will recover the enriched uranium - currently buried under rubble thanks to US and Israeli strikes - needed for a weapon.It is only a matter of time. Netanyahu knows this, and only Netanyahu can stop this. Netanyahu is the reason why Iran has not yet managed to build a nuclear bomb. Netanyahu saw the writing on the wall, 30 years ago. He was the Churchill of the day then, and he still is now.If Iran gets the bomb, no amount of street protests will make it disappear. Political differences will not make it disappear. Neither will arguments about the cost of living or judicial reform.Iran does not fear Eisenkot, Bennett, Lieberman or Golan. Iran only fears Netanyahu. If you care about Israel, if you care about your children, and if you care about your grandchildren, when you vote on Tuesday, make sure it stays that way.

title: Greece’s Most Advanced Frigate Kimon Draws Crowds in Thessaloniki
body: Hundreds of people gathered at the Port of Thessaloniki on Sunday, 25 October 2026, to visit the Greek Navy’s advanced FDI HN frigate Kimon , as its first commanding officer highlighted the warship’s technological capabilities and strategic importance for Greece’s defence. Families with young children and groups of visitors began arriving before the official visiting hours opened at 10 am, forming long queues to board the vessel. The enthusiastic reception delighted the crew, who welcomed visitors aboard. “It was tremendously moving to arrive in the city and see the colours of the East over Thessaloniki,” Commander Ioannis Kizanis, the frigate’s commanding officer, told the Athens-Macedonian News Agency (AMNA). He also described the experience of mooring near the historic armoured cruiser Averof , which had previously visited the port, and alongside the preserved destroyer Velos , calling the location and the public reception a source of immense pride. A Major Technological Leap for the Greek Navy Commander Kizanis described Kimon as a major technological advance for the Hellenic Navy, marking a transition from ships equipped with technology dating back to the 1980s to a platform incorporating modern systems. The frigate can perform a broad range of naval missions, including area air defence, long-range defensive operations, anti-submarine warfare and support for special operations. Unlike vessels designed primarily for a single warfare role, Kimon combines capabilities across multiple operational domains. The ship builds on the proven FREMM frigate design used by the French and Italian navies. Its improvements include the Herakles multifunction radar, which uses fixed antenna panels and active electronically scanned array (AESA) technology, rather than the rotating multifunction radar used on earlier FREMM configurations. Kizanis said the vessel’s design particularly suits the Greek Navy’s operational requirements in the Aegean archipelago. Advanced Missiles and Air Defence Capabilities The frigate’s weapons systems attracted particular attention during the public tours. Its vertical launch system (VLS) can deploy 32 Aster missiles, giving the ship substantial air-defence capabilities. Kizanis explained that the missiles combine long interception ranges with high manoeuvrability, making it difficult for hostile aircraft to approach or attack the frigate successfully. He added that the ship’s design addresses a wide range of aerial threats, a capability that has become increasingly important amid developments in the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East. The commanding officer also noted international interest in the design. France operates the underlying frigate family, Greece has selected the FDI HN configuration, and Sweden has also chosen the design. Pride, Responsibility and a Challenging Voyage to Greece Kizanis described commanding Kimon as both an honour and a significant responsibility. He and the ship’s first chief engineer spent 18 months in France preparing the vessel and its crew for service. The journey to Greece marked the culmination of an extended period of training, preparation and sea trials. The frigate sailed from Brest after taking on its ammunition and encountered difficult weather conditions in the Bay of Biscay, but its design enabled it to complete the passage without significant problems, according to the commander. He praised the crew’s professionalism and said the responsibility of the mission remained at the forefront of his mind. Kimon to Join Thessaloniki’s 28 October Celebrations The frigate is scheduled to anchor off Thessaloniki’s White Tower in the early hours of Wednesday, 28 October, ahead of Greece’s national anniversary celebrations. The vessel will depart after the commemorations. Kizanis said he hoped the frigate would return to Thessaloniki and visit Piraeus and other Greek islands in the future. He also sent his wishes to the city ahead of the feast of Saint Demetrius, Thessaloniki’s patron saint, and the anniversary of the city’s liberation, as well as Greece’s 28 October national holiday. “The Greeks can be certain that, if necessary, we will rise to the challenge, just as our ancestors did,” he said. title: Letter making claims about Meghan’s father written by his first wife, BBC understands
body: His ex-wife, Roslyn Loveless, wrote a letter to the Metropolitan Police making a number of claims about the Duchess of Sussex’s father, the BBC understands. Meghan confirmed on Friday she had previously been informed about “disturbing allegations” about her estranged father, Thomas Markle. On Saturday, the Met confirmed it received a letter about Markle in 2019 and shared it with the Duke and Duchess of Sussex at the time. It has been reported that images of child sexual abuse allegedly belonging to Markle, 82, had been found in his former home in the Philippines. Markle, who is based in the US, denies all such allegations. Loveless, who has since died, is the mother of Meghan’s half-siblings Samantha Markle and Thomas Markle Jr. Loveless divorced Markle in 1975 before he married the Duchess’ mother Doria Ragland in 1979. Meghan was born in 1981 and is the only daughter of Markle and Ragland. In a statement shared on Friday, Meghan confirmed the existence of the letter and wrote: “I am deeply distressed… my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed.” She said she hoped it could be understood why she had largely cut off contact with her father and did “not allow him to have contact with our children”. Meghan has been estranged from her father since 2018. The BBC understands she broke contact with him last year, telling him she and the authorities knew he had abused young girls. Sources close to the duchess said Meghan warned Markle in a letter – sent while he was in hospital in the Philippines after having his leg amputated – that he would never meet his grandchildren. Undated image shows Thomas Markle with his daughter Meghan Markle On Friday, Meghan’s half-brother claimed to the Sun he found a stash of images belonging to his father at his former Philippines home. He is reported to have told police he discovered child abuse videos and pictures among the items. He also apologised to Meghan for initially siding with her father during their long-running estrangement, and said he had “been protecting the wrong person for the past nine years”. It is understood that he contacted the US Federal Bureau of Investigations (FBI) about the images in July. The FBI has since confirmed it is aware of the allegations. Officials in the Philippines have confirmed they are investigating allegations relating to Markle. They told the BBC on Friday that the Philippines’ anti-human trafficking and child sexual exploitation task force was investigating the matter. Markle gave an interview to the Mail on Sunday in which he acknowledged paying for sex in the Philippines on past visits but denied sleeping with underage girls and ever possessing child abuse images. The Met Police has said it did not pass on the contents of the letter shared with the Sussexes to other law enforcement agencies. The force is now reviewing how it handled the matter. Markle moved to the Philippines last year after he had a series of strokes. He is reportedly now living in a Florida rehabilitation centre learning to walk again after having his leg amputated.

title: MTN Yellow Ladies Network screens 500 market women for breast cancer
body: The Yellow Ladies Network, a non-profit organisation made up of female staff of MTN, has organised a free breast cancer screening for 500 women in Accra as part of activities to mark this year’s Breast Cancer Awareness Month. The programme was used to educate women on maintaining healthy breasts. Speaking during the programme, MTN Ghana’s Chief Finance Officer and Chairperson of the MTN Yellow Ladies Network, Antoinette Kwofie, said the network is extending its activities beyond staff welfare to impact communities through health interventions. Madam Kwofie said the Yellow Ladies Network was established in 2025 to empower, inspire, and coach women within MTN, but it was not limited to staff; it also reaches out to customers and communities. She said last year the network organized a fundraising walk and donated the proceeds to the Breast Cancer Unit of the Korle Bu Teaching Hospital and to Breast Care International. She said this year’s theme focuses on better outcomes through action, hence the decision to take screening to the community, particularly market women who hardly get time to visit hospitals.” We thought we would come to the marketplace because as women, we always put ourselves last when it comes to healthcare,” she said. She said the outreach was designed to bring healthcare providers to the women, educate them, share survivors’ experiences, teach self-examination and offer free screening. She said early detection saves lives and the exercise sought to help women know their status and identify lumps that need further checks. No specific target was set, as the aim was to screen as many women as possible. She said envoys were sent to market queens and beauticians’ associations to mobilize participants, with doctors from various hospitals conducting the screening and referring cases that need further attention. She expressed satisfaction with the turnout, noting that screening started at 8:00 a.m. and women had already formed long queues to be screened, indicating that many had overcome fear. The President of Breast Care International and CEO of Peace and Love Hospitals, Dr Beatrice Wiafe Addae, who partnered MTN for the exercise, called for increased awareness to reduce fear, stigma and mortality. She said many people still attribute breast cancer to witchcraft, leading women to prayer camps and delaying treatment. She disclosed that over 5,000 Ghanaian women are diagnosed with breast cancer annually and over 2,300 die, but early reporting can reduce mortality. Dr Wiafe Addae said breast cancer is not painful at the early stage, hence the need for monthly self-examination and education. She said about 60 to 70 per cent of patients are diagnosed at stage three or four cancers, but detection at stages one and two allows for breast-conserving surgery. She said risk factors include being a woman, family history, late childbirth, excessive alcohol intake, smoking including shisha, skin-lightening products, hair relaxers, lack of exercise and fatty diets. She cautioned against cosmetic products without English labelling, noting some contain carcinogens, and called for financial support for patients, since screening and biopsy are not covered by health insurance. She proposed enrolling vulnerable breast and prostate cancer patients on the Livelihood Empowerment Against Poverty programme.

title: Basketball Federation President In Custody Over Alleged Match-Fixing
body: Evangelos Liolios and a close business associate will remain in custody after a Greek investigating magistrate and prosecutor ruled against their release following questioning over an alleged basketball match-fixing scandal involving 49 games across multiple divisions and competitions. The judicial officials ordered the pre-trial detention of the two men, whom the case file identifies as central figures in the alleged manipulation scheme. Their detention marks the third such order in the investigation, following the remand of a former referee who gave evidence first on Friday. Both defendants reportedly denied allegations that they participated in a series of bribes over a decade to manipulate basketball results in various competitions. Liolios, who has served as a leading institutional figure in Greek basketball, reportedly told the investigating magistrate that he was facing prosecution because “some people want to remove me from the Hellenic Basketball Federation” (EOK). He reiterated his longstanding claim that people with whom he has been involved in legal disputes for the past four years had orchestrated a conspiracy against him. According to Liolios, they were using false allegations to force him out of the federation’s presidency. Liolios also reportedly presented details of his financial affairs to the investigating magistrate. He submitted findings from four tax audits conducted over the past decade, claiming that the authorities had raised no concerns. He also referred to an audit that he said took place in 2025 and examined the 2019–2020 period. According to his account, the audit covered his personal assets, his Promitheas basketball club, his business interests, safe-deposit boxes and domestic and overseas bank accounts. He maintained that investigators had found nothing improper. Liolios’s business associate, who faces allegations in connection with the same case, also categorically denied the charges during a brief questioning session. The judicial process is scheduled to continue on Monday, when three of the six people arrested under warrants are due to give their statements. They include a serving referee and two former referees, who face allegations of accepting bribes. title: Egypt Readies Troops for Somalia, Amid Tension in Horn of Africa
body: Egypt is preparing to station troops near Mogadishu under the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM), but neither Cairo nor Mogadishu has announced when the main force will arrive. Egyptian advisers, trainers and technical officers are reportedly readying a site at Ceelcade, near the former Cisiley airfield in the Middle Shabelle region. The site sits just north of Mogadishu’s administrative boundary and, about 400 kilometres from the nearest point on the Ethiopian border. An Egyptian military delegation met Somali Defence Minister Ahmed Moallim Fiqi in Mogadishu on 20 Sep. Five days earlier, Egyptian officers had met senior Somali commanders to discuss training and capacity-building for the Somali National Army. The groundwork is not new. Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud and General Abdel-Magid Saqr, Egypt’s commander-in-chief and defence minister, attended a lineup of Egyptian troops assigned to AUSSOM on 11 Feb 2026, according to Egypt’s military spokesperson. Lieutenant General Ahmed Khalifa, the Egyptian chief of staff, also attended. Officials were briefed on the preparation and equipping of the units, and a display of vehicles was part of the programme. The force and the delay Egypt’s planned contribution is 1,091 troops in the AU force structure, according to UN planning documents cited by Somali media. That compares with 4,500 from Uganda, 2,500 from Ethiopia, 1,520 from Djibouti and 1,410 from Kenya. Egyptian troops are meant to replace Burundian forces, who have been allowed to stay until relief arrives. Some reports describe the Egyptian contingent as already in place with about 1,100 personnel. The 1,091 number is a planned allocation, and Somali officials still described the main deployment as pending in September. Reports of equipment, including Mine-Resistant Ambush Protected (MRAP) vehicles, armoured personnel carriers, helicopters and surveillance aircraft, come from press accounts and have not been itemised by either government. Somalia’s State Minister for Foreign Affairs Ali Mohamed Omar, known as Ali Balcad, addressed the delay on 1 Sep. “The problem is not Egypt’s political commitment or lack of readiness,” he told the Asharq Al-Awsat newspaper. He pointed to AU and United Nations procedures, troop rotation, logistics and unsettled funding for the mission. The funding problem is real. AUSSOM has operated under financial pressure since it began in January 2025, and the UN logistics office that feeds, fuels and moves its troops depends on donor money. A May 2026 report by The Reporter, an Ethiopian outlet, said the AU Peace and Security Council extended the mission to December 2026. The timetable has slipped more than once. In September 2025, a 16-member Egyptian delegation led by Major General Islam Radwan surveyed sites in Mogadishu. AU sources then said Egypt planned up to 1,100 troops at three bases in Middle Shabelle, with full deployment expected by the end of 2025. That did not happen. Why Cairo wants a foothold Egypt and Somalia signed a military cooperation protocol in August 2024. Cairo then flew and shipped arms to Mogadishu , and announced in December 2024 that it would join AUSSOM. The AU council later approved the request, making Egypt a first-time troop contributor to the mission. Reports also describe Egyptian help to rebuild the Somali Air Force. Later on, in September 2024 again, Somalia received one of the largest modern arms shipments from its ally, Egypt. An Egyptian warship delivered a substantial cache of weaponry, including anti-aircraft guns and artillery, to Somalia’s port, according to port and military officials. This marked the second major arms delivery from Egypt to Somalia that year, reflecting the growing military cooperation between the two nations. The strengthening of ties is largely driven by their shared mistrust of Ethiopia. AUSSOM began on 1 Jan 2025 under UN Security Council Resolution 2767, replacing the AU Transition Mission in Somalia (ATMIS). Its mandate covers support for offensive operations, protection of civilians and humanitarian access. Egypt’s entry changes its makeup, since earlier AU missions drew troops from Ethiopia, Kenya, Burundi, Djibouti and Uganda. Egypt has delivered more than words. Its arms shipments to Mogadishu have included anti-aircraft guns and artillery. Those deliveries began in 2024 and ended a gap of roughly four decades in Egyptian military aid to Somalia. Egyptian officials treat Somalia as part of their security perimeter. Lieutenant General Khaled Okasha, an Egyptian security expert, described Somalia as Egypt’s “strategic depth” in comments carried by Hiiraan Online. “Somalia’s disintegration would threaten Red Sea and Suez Canal navigation,” he said. Roughly speaking, instability on the Somali coast reaches the Bab al-Mandeb Strait and, beyond it, the southern entrance to the Suez Canal. Ethiopia reads the move differently. Addis Ababa and Cairo are at odds over the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD) on the Blue Nile and over Ethiopia’s push for Red Sea access. Ethiopia’s ambassador to Somalia, Suleiman Dedefo, said last year that Ethiopia is “neither threatened nor comfortable” with Egyptian troops in Somalia. The picture is further complicated by Israel’s recognition of Somaliland in December 2025. Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud called the decision a serious violation of Somali sovereignty. What it means on the ground Any Egyptian contingent will operate against al-Shabaab, the Al-Qaeda-linked group that still controls territory and can strike government forces and civilians. Somali analyst Hassan Muhammad said the group “constitutes one of the most outstanding security challenges facing the government now.” Egyptian troops in fixed bases would also become obvious targets, a risk that analysts cited, reporting raise alongside fears of a proxy contest with Ethiopia. The siting matters politically as well. A base north of Mogadishu keeps Egyptian forces far from the Ethiopian frontier, where earlier reports had placed them. That placement is consistent with Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s September 2025 statement that Egyptian troops would work in Middle Shabelle under the AU mission. The next markers are plain. Watch for an announced arrival date, confirmation that the Ceelcade site is operating, and a funding arrangement that lets the AU rotate out the Burundian contingent.

As is tradition, iFixit has torn open the latest iPhone and laid its parts bare on a table. It found some interesting details about how Apple might be hiding the crease on the Duo’s folding screen and gave it a 5/10 repairability score. That might not seem particularly high, but it’s the best score the site has given to a foldable yet.
The internal screen’s matte nano-texture cover doesn’t just make it more readable in bright sunlight; it also helps mask the crease by scattering reflections. When looking at the display under a microscope, iFixit also found oval-shaped subpixels arranged at various angles, which the site believes are designed to reduce artifacts and further mask the crease down the middle of the display.
The nano-texture outer layer is relatively easy to replace without swapping out the OLED underneath. If you do need to repair the display itself, however, good luck. As is the case with other foldables, it’s an expensive nightmare. Dust did make it into the USB-C port, speaker grills, and the hinge — making it a bit crunchy. But noticeably less of the glow dust found its way inside the phone than the Z Fold8 or Pixel 11 Pro Fold.
As for reports of damaged screens and cracking hinges , iFixit has some theories. The hinge on the iPhone Duo is incredibly complex, and they suspect part of it sometimes isn’t descending properly. There is also an accordion cable that passes over that exact spot, and it’s near the edge of the battery. It’s possible this is concentrating pressure and leading to the “ audible crack ” reported by some and the broken screens. Apple did not immediately return a request for comment.

title: Feast Day of Agios Dimitrios
body: October 26 is the Feast Day of Agios Dimitrios, who was born in Thessaloniki, in 270 AD. October 26 is the Feast Day of Agios Dimitrios, who was born in Thessaloniki, in 270 AD. He came from a wealthy family and because he was athletic in appearance and heroic in spirit, he became a high-ranking officer in the Roman Army at a very young age. (This is why he is depicted in Byzantine icons in military dress, either standing or riding a horse.) He considered himself a soldier of Christ first, and a military soldier second. He spent most of his time as a devout missionary, preaching the Gospel at secret meetings and converting pagans to the Christian faith. At one of these meetings, he was captured and placed in front of Emperor Maximian, who wanted to learn the truth about the conversions. Agios Dimitrios proclaimed his faith by saying: “…only in Christ do I believe.” With that proclamation, Maximian ordered that Saint Demetrios be sent to prison and subjected to the cruellest tortures. Even though Agios Dimitrios was imprisoned, he did not stop preaching the gospel to those who came to see him. In jail, he was visited by his follower, Nestoras. Nestoras was a man of small stature and had come to ask for his beloved teacher’s blessing to fight in the upcoming gladiator games. The emperor had decided to use the games as a duel between Christianity and paganism by challenging any Christian to a fight against the athletic giant, Leo. Image Credit: Dogma With the blessing of Agios Dimitrios, Nestoras fought and killed Leo. Enraged at the loss of his favourite gladiator, the emperor commanded that Nestoras be beheaded on the spot. Recognising that Agios Dimitrios was the inspiring power behind Nestoras, the emperor ordered that Agios Dimitrios be executed by spear on October 26, 306 AD. Christians buried the body of Agios Dimitrios at the place of his execution and because of the beautiful scent that emanated from his tomb, he was named ‘Mirovlitis’ or “The Myrrh Gusher”. The most ancient icons of Agios Dimitrios may be found in his temple in Thessaloniki where he is the patron saint. This is not just because he was born and died there, but because the people believe it was his intervention that saved the city during many attacks by Slavic nations, the Bulgarians, Arabs, Saracens, and others. Happy Name Day to everyone celebrating today! Wishing you all love, happiness and above all good health! title: Musk warns military use of Starlink could spark space war. Kyiv’s ex-disinformation chief says he’s building alibi after Starshield scandal
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); SpaceX founder Elon Musk says that if Ukraine fires through Starlink, Russia would be entitled to shoot the network down. That is why Starlink must remain a civilian operation and cannot be used for outright offensive strikes that would put its very existence at risk. The warning lands in the middle of a fight over Musk’s own hand on that network. Weeks ago, his company unexpectedly throttled the service Ukraine’s drones depend on amid US President Donald Trump diesel deal with Russia, which led to the disruption of a few operations on the front. The US Treasury authorized the sale, delivery, offloading, and import of Russian-origin diesel fuel, effectively suspending sanctions on that trade until 7 April 2027, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) said on its website on 9 October. The diesel deal combining intelligence halt and military Starlink, with pressure on Ukraine to make a quick peace deal, has angered both Democrats and Republicans ahead of the US elections on 3 November, where Democrats could win. Meanwhile, a Ukrainian official interprets Musk's talk of strikes as an attempt to build an alibi before a possible investigation into that decision. A civilian network, or a target Musk was responding to a post warning that if Starlink shifted from a civilian network into a military system, Russia could treat it as a target for retaliation, and that destroying satellites in orbit could scatter enough debris to make space unusable for years or centuries. “An adversary blowing up Starlink satellites would create a domino effect of destruction that would generate a vast field of debris, making space unusable," he writes. When the shield and the warnings failed together Overnight into 14 October, SpaceX quietly capped the speed of Starshield, the military version Ukraine’s drones run on, without telling Kyiv. Ukrainian units said the limit broke a series of missions, with connections dropping mid-flight and leaving drones hard to control. At the same time, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine relies on the network for air defense, not attack, to intercept the Russian drones Moscow sends to its cities, and that once the speed was cut, his forces could no longer stop some of them as effectively as before. Simultaneously, Ukraine's other American lifeline also went dark: for about three days, the US stopped passing the intelligence that warns of Russian ballistic launches. On 12 October, Russian ballistic missiles hit Kyiv before the air-raid alert reached people, with no advance data from partners. In a strike during that window, three people were killed in the capital, the sirens sounding only after the blasts. A Ukrainian official sees alibi-building Meanwhile, Andrii Kovalenko, the ex-head of Ukraine’s Center for Countering Disinformation, read Musk’s statement as self-protection rather than physics “Musk, having taken responsibility for the restrictions on Starlink and Starshield for Ukraine, is now trying to build himself an alibi before a possible investigation into that decision,” he wrote . He said that regardless of who was behind the idea of restricting Starlink and Starshield access for Ukraine, it represents a strategic setback for the US in the long run, as it risks portraying the country as an unreliable partner that may fail to honor its commitments. "Europe purchases around 60% of its imported weapons from the US. Trust in the US as a security guarantor directly supports sales for American defense companies. Moves like this only undermine that trust and encourage European countries to develop their own systems," he said. The US has sent a message that its guarantees may not be reliable and that even paid-for services can be subject to political decisions, Kovalenko stressed. title: US Rewords Turkish-Libyan Deal As “Unhelpful and Provocative”
body: The US State Department has corrected its statement regarding the Libyan Parliament’s ratification of the Turkish-Libyan maritime delimitation memorandum following coordinated diplomatic efforts by the US Embassy in Athens and the Greek Embassy in Washington. The revised statement says the announcement of the ratification has raised regional tensions and is “unhelpful and provocative”, adding that Washington’s position on the matter has not changed. The correction followed significant efforts by US Chargé d’Affaires in Athens Josh Huck and his team, working with regional partners and State Department colleagues. Greek Ambassador to Washington Antonis Alexandridis also played a key role, alongside diplomats Fotis Boulogiannis, Martinos Mandalidis, Lana Zochiou and Thanos Leousis. The State Department said it encourages all countries, including partners in the Eastern Mediterranean, to resolve maritime disputes through good-faith negotiations and avoid provocative behaviour. It also stressed that Greece and Türkiye, both NATO allies, should engage bilaterally to address areas of disagreement. “Peaceful resolution of such disputes opens the way for commercial investment and exploration that will benefit the entire region,” the department said.
