title: 20:24 Inability To Transmit 2023 Presidential Election Results Eroded Trust In INEC — Ex-REC Igini
body: A former resident electoral commissioner, Mike Igini, on Sunday said that the inability of INEC to transmit the results of the 2023 presidential election eroded trust in INEC and is responsible for the lack of public confidence in the commission. Igini, who stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Sunday Politics, said that despite serving as a REC, he still could not explain clearly what constituted the glitch that the electoral umpire claimed was experienced during the election. He said that while BVAS worked, the failure to transmit one of the results of the three elections held on one day made trust in INEC evaporate. “Now, in 2023, what worked and what broke public confidence? The BVAS worked. But what broke confidence, which has created a liability and a cloud of distrust that the current leadership is suffering, was the fact that there were three elections, same day; only one could not be transmitted, which was the presidential,” Igini said. “That was what evaporated public trust and confidence. Even people like us, who put out our integrity to explain to people, to give a clarion call to the Nigerian people, up till date I don’t have a clear explanation of what constituted that glitch.” The lawyer, however, said that the 2027 elections would be a verdict on whether Nigerians can learn a lesson from what happened in 2023. “Every election is a test, but in 2027, it will be more than a test. It will be a verdict on whether we, as a people, can learn from what has happened,” the former REC said. He urged Nigerian voters to stay awake, especially on the night of the election when collation happens, to protect their votes. “But the greatest power of the people, which is unassailable, is that in every polling unit, the people will be more than the polling officials that are going to be compromised,” he said. The post 20:24 Inability To Transmit 2023 Presidential Election Results Eroded Trust In INEC — Ex-REC Igini appeared first on Channels Television .

title: OpenAI and Anthropic cut their LLM prices by up to 80% within a few months. Why?
body:
Let’s look at a quick timeline of the major LLM model announcements from both OpenAI and Anthropic over the past few months. All pricing numbers provided are input MTok / output MTok / cache read MTok.
June 26, 2026 OpenAI announced GPT-5.6 Sol and Luna. Sol is the direct successor to GPT 5.5 at the same price of $5 / $30 / $0.50, while Luna is a small model specifically designed for cheaper use cases at $1 / $6 / $0.10. They also announced a Terra model that’s in between those two models, but few cared about it.
June 30, 2026 Anthropic announced Claude Sonnet 5, which Anthropic claimed to be closer to their Opus models, but feedback was mixed. Notably, it had launch pricing of $2 / $10 / $0.20 which was initially supposed to be temporary but would go up.
July 24, 2026 Anthropic announced Claude Opus 5, which was a long-awaited major-version update given the impact Opus 4.5 had on the rise of agentic coding, at a price of $5 / $25 / $0.50 (similar to GPT-5.6 Sol). Although some of the provided benchmark results surprisingly exceeded those of the much larger Fable 5, real-world feedback was more mixed.
July 30, 2026 OpenAI announces that they cut the price of GPT-5.6 Luna by 80% (???) to $0.20 / $1.20 / $0.02.
Model quality vs. Cost-per-task for GPT-5.6 Luna after the massive price reduction. Top-and-left is better, and if OpenAI didn’t do the 80% price cut, it would have lost to DeepSeek V4 Pro. via OpenAI
August 10, 2026 Anthropic announces the temporary Sonnet 5 price cut for the launch is now permanent.
August 21, 2026 OpenAI announces that they are cutting the price for GPT-5.6 Sol by ~20% ($4 / $20 / $0.40) for the next three months.
September 1, 2026 Anthropic announced Fable 5.1 at a price of $10 / $50 / $0.25, which, in addition to having strictly better benchmark performance in all areas than Fable 5 from June at $10 / $50 / $1, cut the cache read cost by 75%.
Cache read costs When using agents for coding, cache read costs are the vast majority (96% - 99%) of the total token expenditure as the cache is what contains the entire previous conversation each turn. Additionally, the cache tends to be hit around 90 - 100% of the time (varies by the infrastructure of the LLM inference provider). Taken together, a 75% reduction in the cache read cost correlates to a 70-75% reduction in the cost of using the model—obviously notable, even if cache costs are typically a footnote!
September 3, 2026 OpenAI announced GPT-6 Astra, which is similar in size to Fable 5.1 and has similar pricing at $10 / $50 / $1 but without the lower cache read cost. Astra’s model performance is indeed comparable to Fable.
September 22, 2026 OpenAI announced GPT-6 Sol at at a shocking price of $2 / $10 / $0.20 that halves the input and output price relative to the temporarily-discounted GPT-5.6 Sol! They simultaneously released GPT-6 Luna also at half the input and output price ($0.10 / $0.50 / $0.01) of the previous version.
On the same exact day, Anthropic announced Claude Opus 5.5, where it’s explicitly stated “Opus 5.5 requires less compute to serve than Opus 5, and its pricing reflects that”. Its price of $4 / $20 / $0.20 is much lower in total than Opus 5’s due to a 20% input/output cost cut and a larger cache read cut, resulting in a total cost reduction of 40-60% for a model that’s even better than Fable 5.1 (I have quite a lot of things to say about Opus 5.5, but that’s for another post).
September 29, 2026 It turned out that GPT-6 Sol was a dud performancewise, so a week later OpenAI announced GPT-6.1 Sol, which surprisingly has comparable performance to Astra (can confirm after personal use), but OpenAI casually cut the cache price in half ($2 / $10 / $0.10) matching Anthropic’s 5%-of-input cache read cost, making this model family cumulatively 75% cheaper.
Overall, starting from the release of the GPT-5.6 model families in June to now, the cost of using these popular LLMs has cratered, which is not something I would have expected a year ago. These price cuts also apply to model usage from subscription agentic harnesses such as Codex and Claude Code. More importantly, these models do not appear to have cut any corners in terms of output quality to achieve their price cuts.
Data from Vercel’s AI model gateway supporting the decreasing cost-per-token trend to 43.3% of the April 2026 cost. However, aggregate spend has been increasing because the models are getting better faster than they’re getting cheaper! via Vercel
From the timeline above, there is a clear tit-for-tat between Anthropic and OpenAI, and it is reasonable to assume that these particular price cuts from OpenAI and Anthropic are in reaction to each other. However, no one cuts prices by 80% unless there is some externality in play. So, what gives?
The Behavioral Economics of LLMs and Competitor Pricing Pressure If you have been testing agents with new LLMs as they are released, it can be very difficult to differentiate them outside of subjective vibes. Since last November that launched the hypergrowth of agentic LLMs, models have become more of a commodity where it’s trivial to try a new model on your codebase with just a toggle in a harness like OpenCode and Zed Agent, or a different API endpoint string through OpenRouter, and as a result there is little moat. Additionally, there are many competitors—not just large companies like Google and Meta—who can provide models which are sufficient substitutes and therefore allow pricing pressure.
For open weight models, let’s take another look at DeepSeek Flash V4.1, which also recently released an updated 1017 variant.
OpenRouter at this point is the place you go for open-weight models. Retrieved October 24th, 2026.
The original DeepSeek V4 Flash 0420 was released in April 2026 at a price of $0.14 / $0.28 / $0.0028 and went megaviral as a result, especially as OpenAI didn’t have a small-class model for simple tasks at the time. That $0.0028 turned out to be the key, as a cache read proportion of 2% is substantially lower than the 5%-10% of the OpenAI and Anthropic models above, which makes the effective cost even lower than what is advertised. I suspect the 80% GPT-5.6 Luna price cut in July was meant to specifically compete with these smaller open-weight models. Now, the new DeepSeek Flash V4.1 1017 model performs significantly better than DeepSeek Flash V4 benchmark-wise (45 on the Artificial Analysis index vs. 24) and the cost from DeepSeek remains similar at $0.15 / $0.60 / $0.003. Note the operative words “from DeepSeek”.
On OpenRouter, any inference provider can list a model that they host, and when a user hits the OpenRouter API, the request is routed to one of those models—it’s routed to any available model by default for load balancing but the developer can specify preferences such as “lowest price” in the API request. Back in May, I noted that there were 13 distinct providers hosting DeepSeek V4 Flash on OpenRouter. For the updated 1017 variant, there are now 29 distinct providers.
Providers for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 sorted by cache read cost. Retrieved October 24th, 2026.
However, looking at the effective input costs (which account for the interaction between cache read costs and cache hit rates), many distinct providers are close costwise.
Effective costs by endpoint, with Cloudflare and DeepInfra within 10% of DeepSeek’s cost. Despite the fact that these models are the cheapest, note that these models only have a minority of the total token share. Retrieved October 24th, 2026.
OpenAI and Anthropic will have to differentiate from these open weight models with higher-quality models—they are currently doing a good job with that particularly with Opus 5.5—but they need to keep doing that, which is why billions of dollars are being invested into R&D. Open-weight models are catching up fast: just a few days ago, Moonshot AI announced Kimi K3.1 Pro which has comparable performance to Opus 5.5 (Kimi at 55 vs. Opus 5.5 at 58) at half the input/output price and the same cache read cost ($2 / $10 / $0.20). It’s the same size and architecture as Kimi K3 which is currently being hosted by over 20 distinct inference providers: once the weights drop on November 4th, you can therefore expect most of them to support the new Kimi K3.1 Pro model at a roughly equivalent price. Notably, Moonshot AI itself is joining the price cut fun and priced Kimi K3.1 Pro at less than the original Kimi K3 ($3 / $15 / $0.30).
One recurring trend among vocal AI detractors is that the price of tokens has been kept artificially low to hook people into the LLM ecosystem, but then the prices will increase to “the true cost of a token” and the AI boosters will be screwed once the free ride ends. The theory is that OpenAI and Anthropic are loss-leading just like what Uber and Lyft did to the ridesharing industry in the 2010s, but unlike then, OpenAI and Anthropic are not a duopoly who have the sole power to set prices in the ecosystem and the barrier to entry for the inference industry is not as high. As long as these many inference providers can continue to serve models at a similar price and a similar quality to what OpenAI and Anthropic can provide, and switching cost is negligible, then the prices may continue to decrease more. It’s no surprise both companies are trying to build moats to defend against this trend, such as a focus on enterprise commitments and personal agentic assistants like OpenAI Dots and Claude Duet.
The idea that token prices will suddenly rise is more a fantasy that is not supported by both behavioral economics and the actual trends of LLM prices going down significantly over the last few months for better models, and not just from OpenAI and Anthropic. As long as scalers can price at a cost-per-token lower than the revenue-per-token, then those inference providers will reduce token costs to compete with each other to a point that OpenAI/Anthropic will have to lower their prices to compete too. The 29 distinct providers on OpenRouter have little incentive to serve an unprofitable model (they would just stop serving it and use the compute capacity for a profitable model instead) and “the true cost of a token” may end up being where price equals marginal cost.
On that note, both OpenAI and Anthropic are indeed close to IPOing, which raises further questions about the price cuts.
IPO Pumping The timing of these price cuts is notable because both OpenAI and Anthropic are rumored to be IPOing soon—OpenAI in 2027, and Anthropic within a couple months. So far, leaked financials from both OpenAI and Anthropic show unsurprisingly that they are losing billions due to R&D/scaling, albeit in both cases these reports do not account for the hyperexpansion of agentic LLM use over the past few months. Investors will scrutinize the massive negative profits and demand that they have a plan to turn things back around.
So, why did they cut their primary revenue source by up to 80%? That’s the opposite of what you would want to do to look good on an S-1 prospectus! The profit margins on inference themselves likely tell a different story, with some reports saying the profit-per-token margins are as healthy as 80% with caveats. How much of a profit margin do they have after these major cuts?
Speaking personally, the price cuts have indeed affected how I spend on LLM agents, but not in the way I expect OpenAI/Anthropic want their typical customer to behave. I used to have a $100/month subscription to Codex (the 5x Pro plan) when GPT-5.6 Sol was the top model, and I managed to just fully exhaust all the usage included in the subscription despite getting annoyed with random usage resets. Once GPT-6.1 Sol released and I noticed that the cost of using it was effectively cut by 75%, you know what I did?
I cut the max usage quota to 1/5th after getting 4x more efficient usage of the same model, so it ends up roughly neutral and the obvious choice.
In fairness, the profit margins for subscriptions such as Claude Code and Codex are uncertain given their immense value relative to the API usage, and if there are capital crunches I suspect subscription value will be cut before the base price of the models. For example, at the same time GPT-6.1 Sol was announced, OpenAI cut the usage allowance by 50% for the $200/month tier in Codex under the argument “to reflect our increasingly efficient models”—which is technically correct but it’s funny to put in writing.
I will be very curious to see the Anthropic IPO prospectus and the inference profit margins once it becomes public soon.
I also question whether it’s good for OpenAI/Anthropic if they intentionally obsolete their more expensive models. After Opus 5.5 released a month ago, there hasn’t been any discussion about either Fable 5.1 or GPT-6 Astra because Opus 5.5 is just that good.
Top-and-left. via Anthropic
I fully expect a Fable 5.2/GPT-6.1 Astra to release in a couple weeks and prove me wrong, and I will be very curious to see how it will be priced.
Another less-cynical factor that could explain the price cuts is that LLM infrastructure has improved over the past few months—when Anthropic said “Opus 5.5 requires less compute to serve than Opus 5, and its pricing reflects that,” I believe it. One outcome that would be genuinely ironic is that if these models are more compute efficient, it reduces the need for these massive data center buildouts, which could cause cascading economic failures. However, that likely won’t happen since inference is only one part of the compute mix and those data centers are still needed for other parts of the pipeline.
Overall, the price cut is weird, but as a user I’m certainly not complaining! Open-weight models and secondary inference providers will continue to serve as an economic check on the prices of LLMs and other business shenanigans the large labs may concoct. Even if Anthropic’s and OpenAI’s IPOs are catastrophic and cause both companies to fold, it will not suddenly cause LLMs and agents as an industry to die.

title: Israel must choose national unity over political division - opinion
body: The latest polls leave little room for doubt: Israel is heading toward a political deadlock more complex than ever before. Current projections suggest that neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor Gadi Eisenkot can secure a stable coalition with a majority of 61 MKs.The current political reality suggests that there is no realistic prospect of forming a government without relying on the Arab parties, a scenario that faces mutual boycotts and offers little prospect of governmental stability.In these circumstances, Israeli society faces two options: another descent into a cycle of recurring political crises, which tore the country apart and deepened internal divisions between 2019 and 2022, or the courageous and pragmatic choice of establishing a broad national unity government.The advantage of a unity governmentIsrael's history demonstrates that in times of national emergency, a unity government is not an undesirable compromise but the most appropriate response to the challenges of the moment. The clearest example is the national unity government formed in 1984 between the Alignment, led by Shimon Peres, and Likud, led by Yitzhak Shamir.At the time, Israel's economy was on the verge of total collapse, with inflation soaring into the hundreds of percent. It was precisely this broad political partnership that made it possible to implement the dramatic economic stabilization plan that rescued the economy and steered Israel toward safer waters. The strength of such unity lies in its ability to make difficult and painful decisions while securing broad public legitimacy.Beyond the urgent economic and security challenges, Iran, Hezbollah, and Hamas continue to pose serious security challenges and even existential threats to the Jewish state.A national unity government formed after the 2026 election would therefore faithfully represent the mainstream of Israeli society. It would comprise the major Zionist parties while keeping extremist elements on both the Right and the Left outside the government, forces whose divisive rhetoric has fueled social fractures in recent years.Moreover, such a moderate and balanced government, built on broad agreement across most of Israeli society, would be welcomed and highly regarded internationally. It would help restore Israel's international standing and diplomatic relations at a critical juncture in global affairs.Israel's recent experience further reinforces the conclusion that there is no viable alternative. We saw this during the global COVID-19 crisis, when an emergency government was formed, and again in the immediate aftermath of the national catastrophe of the October 7 massacre.The remarkable resilience of Israeli society and the mobilization of hundreds of thousands of citizens on the front lines and at home demonstrated beyond doubt that the country's strength lies in its unity.The difficulties of a unity governmentAdmittedly, this would be a complex undertaking, likely to generate difficulties and disagreements, as previous national unity governments throughout Israel's political history clearly demonstrate. History remembers the so-called dirty trick orchestrated by the Labor Party under Peres in 1990 to bring down the national unity government led by Shamir, amid claims that Likud was unwilling to advance the peace process.Nor must we look far into the past: The collapse of the Netanyahu-Gantz government at the end of 2020 remains a fresh and painful memory. Yet given Israel's current circumstances, with the country still grappling with a prolonged internal crisis alongside external threats to its very existence, there appears to be no alternative.In conclusion, the time has come to choose unity over division. Israel's leaders must rise to the occasion and put personal grievances and narrow political interests aside. This complex task will fall to Israel's president, Isaac Herzog, who has repeatedly demonstrated that he is the right person to lead efforts at national reconciliation.Herzog must use the full weight of his public standing to help establish a stable national unity government. We can only hope and pray that he will do so, and that Israeli democracy will choose partnership, healing, and unity for the sake of future generations. Whatever the election results may be, this is the time for national unity!The writer is a lecturer and research fellow at the University of South Wales in the United Kingdom. He is the author of Collapse: The Israeli Labor Party, 1992-2024.

title: Hard-hitting Ali G is back, leading new group of idiots in 'Ali G: Who Iz I?'
body: For once in his life, Ali G, Sacha Baron Cohen's iconic white guy who thinks he's black character, did something quietly.Ali G snuck into theaters in Israel and around the world for the new movie Ali G: Who Iz I?, which was set for a two-day release on Friday and Saturday.It will come to Amazon's Prime Video later, but the good news for fans in Israel is that certain theater chains, including Planet, Cinema City, Movieland, Rav-Chen, and Hot Cinemas, have extended the release until Wednesday.For those who can roll with Baron Cohen and his often sophomoric humor, it could be the perfect movie to see on Election Day on Tuesday, especially because most of the participants, from both the Left and Right of the political spectrum, were not “in on it”: they were duped into taking part in what they thought was a serious political documentary, a guerrilla tactic that Baron Cohen has been pulling off for decades.The movie starts with a quote from Voltaire, “Those who can make you believe absurdities can also make you commit atrocities,” and it's key to understanding the movie.Baron Cohen handles lawsuits over pranks in the movieEven though the movie says that only Baron Cohen and Morgana Robinson, who plays his pregnant girlfriend, Julie, were in on the joke, while watching it, I had a hard time believing that this was true. It's hard to imagine that anyone who is not mentally ill or drugged could have gone along with the pranks that Baron Cohen pulls in this movie.But they did, and he is currently dealing with a few lawsuits from participants who don't find it funny and regret that they gave their permission for him to use the segments he filmed with them.It's an insane piece of performance art that functions as a critique of our absurd political climate, and it will hit harder than a thousand op-eds, mainly because it is designed to be not only entertaining but a teaching moment aimed at those who would never read an op-ed.As the movie opens, it's tough times for Ali G, who has had trouble adjusting to life as a regular guy since his HBO series was canceled over 20 years ago. He is back at home in a quiet British suburb and reeling from the news that Julie is pregnant.As he sells various relics from his former life as a celebrity to support her and their soon-to-be-born child, an ancient fax machine spits out one more page that says that HBO has agreed to pay him an additional $3 million. So it's off to Los Angeles and back to the high life for Ali and Julie.You can guess the reception he gets in Hollywood (HBO says the offer is null and void), but at the same time, an ultra-left, straight, white Berkeley professor who hates himself, Dr. Nira Cain-N'Degeocello (an utterly unrecognizable Baron Cohen, using one of several characters he introduced in the series Who Is America?) decides that Ali G is a menace who must be stopped because he is a cultural appropriator.Baron Cohen's critique of the leftHe recruits a few young, woke, useful idiots to help in his pursuit of Ali.These recruits don absurd faux-Rastafarian costumes and a sequined bodysuit with strategically placed black hands in a plot to deceive and entrap Ali G by collecting his DNA to prove he is white – and if you've ever seen a Baron Cohen movie, you can guess what bodily substance they end up getting.These characters are the main source of Baron Cohen's critique of the Left, and it's the more restrained part of the movie. At the heart of his satire of the Right, Baron Cohen gets a similarly clueless band of useful idiots from the other side of the spectrum involved, in his guise as a poker-faced Mossad agent, Erran Morad.I won't give away the main joke, but the sequence gives him the chance to use a little Hebrew.Hearing these all-American good old boys reciting Israeli slang terms for certain body parts got the biggest laugh and even applause from the mostly 20-something and younger audience in the auditorium where I saw the movie.Unlike in the Borat movies, where Baron Cohen speaks Hebrew when Borat is supposedly conversing in Kazakh, there isn't nearly as much Hebrew in this movie.Those laughing away may not have known or cared that Baron Cohen duped a baker's dozen of right-wing media and political figures into taking part in the movie, including disgraced former congressman George Santos and Jacob Chansley, aka the Qanon Shaman.Ali G is tapped to host a show on a right-wing network called The Free Speech Show with Ali G. It shouldn't surprise anyone at this point that he gets the studio audience for this show to imitate Elon Musk and has them all doing a “Heil Hitler” salute.Celebrity features in the filmA couple of celebrities from the entertainment industry appear in the movie, including Rihanna and A$AP Rocky. While they may not technically have been “in on it,” they were smart enough to know that Baron Cohen was playing the Ali G character.How entertaining you will find the movie depends on how much of Baron Cohen's bathroom and sex humor you can stomach. In addition to the verbal jokes, the movie has some of the funniest costumes Baron Cohen has ever come up with, from a giant puffy jacket to the return of some of the FUBU (“For Us, By Us”) outfits he has sported in the past.All jokes aside, Baron Cohen has said in interviews that he returned to the comedy of Ali G for a serious reason: “Because I'm terrified of where our society is headed, and the way I can comment on that is through my comedy. I wanted to show the extremism on both sides of the political spectrum and the danger of virtuous violence,” he told The Hollywood Reporter last week.While he has not spoken out on issues concerning Israel, other than to call for the release of the hostages held by Hamas after October 7, when he was asked by The Hollywood Reporter about a boycott campaign proposed by left-wing activists against his movie and whether it was linked to antisemitism and anti-Israel sentiment:“Well, I haven't said anything about Israel … I think people are being portrayed as things that they are not on social media and it's problematic. We are in a world where people can't distinguish between facts and lies, and that's something that I've spent a lot of the last few years trying to fix …“So, I'm not surprised that prominent Jews are being targeted. I knew that this was going to happen. The level of organization is surprising, but this is a trend of Jews being portrayed in certain ways and trying to be silenced.”In an essay he penned for Time Magazine, he wrote, “We are once again entering an age of 'virtuous' violence, where any atrocity – by racists, Jew haters, or Islamophobes, the Right or the Left – can be somehow justified. It is not a place any of us should want to live.”Perhaps the biggest virtue of Ali G: Who Iz I? is that it shows that while we may not have much of a choice about living in such a world these days, the ideologues on both sides don't have enough smarts or sense of humor to get Baron Cohen's jokes. As such, Ali G's creator has his pick of endless targets, and he can give us something to laugh at.

title: Egypt set to buy 2,020 Javelin missiles in $832M deal
body: On October 2, 2026, the US State Department approved a possible $832 million Foreign Military Sale of Javelin anti-tank missiles to Egypt, marking Cairo’s first purchase of the system. The Defense Security Cooperation Agency notification covers up to 2,020 Javelin FGM-148F missiles, including 20 “fly-to-buy” rounds for testing, and up to 200 Javelin Lightweight Command Launch Units (LWCLUs), the shoulder-fired sighting and firing systems used to cue and launch the missile. The package also includes a LWCLU basic skills trainer, missile simulation rounds, battery coolant units, spare parts, technical documentation, and training support from the US government. Lockheed Martin of Orlando, Florida, and RTX Corporation of Arlington, Virginia, are identified as the principal contractors. Washington states that it is not aware of any offset arrangement at this stage; any such agreement would be negotiated separately between Cairo and the contractors. The sale requires approval from the US Congress before a formal contract can be concluded. Although this step is routine for Foreign Military Sales of this scale, it may take several months. Notably, the Javelin notification was issued one day after the State Department lifted human-rights-related restrictions on $320 million in Foreign Military Financing for Egypt that had previously been withheld, according to a report by Army Recognition. The timing suggests that the missile sale is part of a broader easing of restrictions on security assistance to Cairo. The State Department’s standard language concerning the case states that the sale would help “a friendly country that continues to be an important force for political stability and economic growth in the Middle East.” It adds that Egypt would have no difficulty incorporating the equipment into its armed forces and that the sale would not alter the region’s basic military balance. The Javelin is a man-portable, fire-and-forget anti-tank guided missile developed for the US Army and Marine Corps by the Javelin Joint Venture, a partnership between Lockheed Martin and Raytheon, now RTX. Production began in 1994, and by 2021 more than 50,000 missiles had been delivered to US and international customers, according to DefenceWeb. Once locked on, the missile guides itself to its target using automatic infrared guidance. This allows the gunner to move to cover immediately after firing, rather than maintaining a line of sight throughout the engagement. Its tandem high-explosive anti-tank warhead can strike armored vehicles from above, where their protection is thinnest. The system can also operate in a direct-attack mode against fortifications or slow-moving and hovering helicopters. A soft-launch mechanism allows the gunner to fire from inside buildings or confined positions, a feature relevant to urban and defensive operations. Flight time to a target two kilometers away is approximately 14 seconds. Lockheed Martin delivered the first production FGM-148F, an upgraded variant with an improved seeker and software, in May 2020. Egypt would receive this version under the proposed deal. The sale continues a pattern of Javelin exports across North Africa in recent years. Morocco received US approval in March 2024 for 612 FGM-148F missiles and 200 launch units, valued at approximately $260 million. Tunisia took delivery of a large batch of FGM-148F missiles in 2024 and, in 2025, secured a US Army contract extension worth $900.5 million, reinforcing its position among Javelin operators. At the time, the move was presented as part of efforts to modernize its ground forces amid regional instability. For Egypt, the Javelin purchase complements a broader series of recent US arms approvals. Washington approved a possible $691 million sale of TOW 2A anti-tank missiles to Cairo in May 2022, authorized the AN/TPS-78 long-range radar system in 2025, and approved a $740 million Stinger air-defense missile package in 2024. In 2024, the State Department also moved to release $1.3 billion in military aid to Egypt that had been withheld over human-rights conditions. Taken together, these deals indicate a steady rebuilding of US-Egyptian defense ties following a period of tension. Operationally, Javelin missiles would provide Egyptian infantry and mechanized units with a precision anti-armor capability independent of vehicle-mounted platforms. This capability could be useful for counterinsurgency operations in Sinai as well as conventional defense planning. The top-attack mode, in particular, addresses a capability gap against modern main battle tanks fielded by regional actors, whose frontal armor is substantially harder to penetrate than their turret roofs or engine decks.

In my mind, Spooky Season music comes in two distinct flavors. There are the fun, occasionally goofy songs like “The Monster Mash” and John Carpenter’s “Halloween Theme.” Then there is the genuinely terrifying: Throbbing Gristle , The Body , or Scott Walker’s The Drift .
This 2006 album from the singer-songwriter is truly upsetting. On it, Walker explores death, disease, and tragedy. But not just from some abstract perspective. There are visceral descriptions of the hanging of Benito Mussolini and his mistress Clara Petacci. He sings about 9/11, his stillborn twin brother, and the Srebrenica genocide. Lyrically, it’s about as dark as an album gets.
But it’s the experimental backdrop that drives it all home.
At times, the record sounds more like the score to an Ari Aster film than anything that could be called pop music under even the most generous definitions. Seasick guitars in the verses of “Jesse” give way to dissonant strings that drone oppressively over the chorus. You can feel the low-bitrate MP3 noise that opens “Clara” in your jaw, which also allegedly features the sound of his percussionist punching a pig carcass as part of the rhythm track.
Songs stop on a dime, linger in uncomfortable silence, then erupt in bursts of mechanical noise. Animal bleating, foley work, and atonal orchestra sections grind against Walker’s warble. Nothing is ever quite in tune, and it can be challenging to get through the record in a single sitting if you’re not in a very particular mood. But sticking with it can be quite rewarding.
Some songs and performances are so beautiful they send shivers down your spine or give you goosebumps. Scott Walker’s The Drift is the opposite of that. You will still have an involuntary physical reaction, but it’s more shudders than shivers. It will make your skin crawl.
Scott Walker’s The Drift is available on Bandcamp and most major streaming services, including YouTube Music , Apple Music , Qobuz , Deezer , and Spotify .

title: Zelensky details expectations for upcoming trilateral peace talks with Russia, US
body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky outlined his expectations for upcoming trilateral peace negotiations, and discussed air defenses and the planned ceasefire in the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky in an interview on Oct. 25.
In an exclusive interview with Alla Mazur, host of "TSN The Week," Zelensky detailed Ukraine's readiness to meet with Russian and American teams for peace negotiations scheduled for early November .
Above all, Zelensky stressed the need for robust security guarantees for Ukraine in any deal aimed at ending the war.
"Our security guarantees are our guarantees, and they cannot be dictated by the Russian side," Zelensky said. "Restrictions on our army and Ukraine's neutrality are not up for discussion."
The question of NATO' s involvement in Ukrainian security will "undoubtedly" come up in the negotiations, Zelensky said. The president suggested that if Ukraine is not allowed to join NATO, European countries and the U.S. should agree to extend the body's Article 5 defensive pact to Ukraine. Ukraine would also need to maintain a strong army after a peace deal is reached. "The best, in my opinion, is NATO plus a strong Ukrainian army, as part of the alliance," Zelensky said. "If I have enough finances, I want to keep the army of 800,000 people. We decide for ourselves what our army will be. If we are in NATO, the number can be 800,000 or less. But it will be a question of who is willing to finance or co-finance with us."
Before a meeting between Zelensky, Russian President Vladimir Putin , and U.S. President Donald Trump can take place, technical talks among the three countries' negotiating teams must be held first, said Zelensky.
"The issue of territory is a red line that can only be discussed at the level of leaders," Zelensky said. "Everyone should understand: first, we are not exchanging anything for anything. We are ready to discuss. If it's a territorial issue, then at the level of leaders. Other issues can be discussed at the level of technical groups." As part of the negotiations, Zelensky said he was prepared to discuss an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, establishing a new deal to protect grain shipments in the Black Sea , and prisoner exchanges .
"Energy, grain, and people – these are the specifics," Zelensky said. "A meeting at the level of leaders is an opportunity to achieve those specifics after our trilateral meeting. That's what we are asking for and offering."
Zelensky said that by offering these points for negotiation, a refusal by the Russian team to engage on the items will help expose whether the Kremlin is serious about peace with Ukraine or not.
"We are not demanding, but rather offering this to the American side," Zelensky said. "That would demonstrate seriousness. But if it's just a political maneuver and Putin is simply saying, 'Yes, I'm ready,' because he doesn't want to escalate tensions with America before the [midterm] elections , we will very quickly see in November whether it was a trick or not."
The president also warned that loosening sanctions on Russia before the negotiations would weaken Ukraine's leverage. This follows Trump waiving sanctions on Russian oil exports in October in an attempt to ease oil prices heightened by his war with Iran.
"I don't want us to be left without tools – without sanctions, without money, or without frozen assets – at the meeting with Putin," Zelensky said. "Because then, as Mr. Trump said, we will really have very few cards in our hand." Turning his attention to the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky , Zelensky said that the planned Oct. 27 ceasefire would need to last several days and include Russian assistance.
Oleshky has been under Russian occupation since the early days of the full-scale invasion. Residents face severe shortages of food, water, and electricity, while mined roads and constant drone attacks make safe evacuation virtually impossible. "Of course, Russia will do everything it can to clear the roads in a way that encourages people to go towards Russia and stay there; they won't simply let people go," Zelensky said. "Some people will be evacuated to Ukraine – to the part that we control – in one format or another. The most important thing is to unblock the people so they can live. Ideally, they should be able to reach their destination and evacuate here, to us, to Ukraine, where they will receive everything they need and be supported."
Zelensky also detailed his conversations with U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo, Norway, in October that set the stage for the planned round of trilateral negotiations. In meeting with Witkoff, Zelensky said they discussed limits placed on Ukraine's Starlink military systems, restrictions on intelligence the U.S. shares with Kyiv, and air defense shortages.
While the issues plaguing Ukrainian forces' use of Starlink systems and the matter of American intelligence sharing have been resolved for now , Zelensky stressed that Kyiv still lacked key air defense assistance.
"There is progress; it's just very slow," Zelensky said. "It's not enough to simply say, 'Yes, we will give [ Patriot missiles ] to you,' and then not deliver them for a month or two. That simply doesn't work."

title: Vucic says winning Student List will impose anti-Russian sanctions by spring
body:
BELGRADE, October 25. /TASS/. Serbia’s former President Aleksandar Vucic anticipates that the Student List, which has won the snap parliamentary elections in the country, will impose anti-Russian sanctions by spring.
"This confirmed the revolution carried out with the direct support from a number of European countries and the US deep state, the faction that opposes Donald Trump. What worries me most is that sanctions will be imposed against Russia by March or April. They will do everything they didn’t want me to tell you about," Vucic said at the headquarters of the Serbian Progressive Party.
The Student List said earlier that it rejects anti-Russian sanctions.

title: One Dead After Car Plunges Into Sea at Piraeus Port
body: A 45-year-old man has died and two elderly passengers were pulled unconscious from a car that plunged into the sea at Greece’s Port of Piraeus on Sunday. The vehicle entered the water near Gate E2, triggering a major search and rescue operation involving the Hellenic Coast Guard and specialist divers. The two other occupants, aged 82 and 79, were trapped inside the submerged vehicle before being rescued unconscious. Their conditions have not yet been confirmed. Coast Guard vessels, a specialist team from its Underwater Missions Unit, private boats and a vessel from the Port Pilotage Service took part in the rescue effort. Three ambulances from Greece’s National Emergency Aid Centre (EKAB) were also dispatched to the scene. The circumstances surrounding the incident remain unclear , with authorities yet to establish how the vehicle ended up in the water. title: Canada receives first F-35 jets from U.S. as full order still under review
body:
Canada has received its first pair of new F-35 fighter jets, with Ottawa still deliberating on how many of the American planes it will buy.
The Royal Canadian Air Force announced receiving the two Lockheed Martin jets Friday on social media with a photo from Phoenix showing one plane with a maple-leaf roundel.
The air force could not immediately say when it will start training pilots with the new planes, which U.S. Ambassador Pete Hoekstra recently hailed as “the best fighter in the world.”
Prime Minister Mark Carney has paused plans to proceed with a planned order for 88 of these stealth fighter jets, and it may instead have a mixed fleet that includes Gripen jets made by Saab.
Carney launched a review of the purchase amid U.S. President Donald Trump’s repeated trade and annexation threats, and the review was supposed to have concluded a year ago.
Last year, Trump mused about providing allies with jets that have limited capabilities in order to maintain American supremacy, and former foreign minister Lloyd Axworthy warns in a Saturday blog post that Washington controls software used by F-35 jets.

title: Are California voters about to impose ‘world’s first’ tax on billionaires?
body: Few places on the planet have as many ultra-wealthy residents as California, a US state known for glamour, coastal mega-mansions, and being home to the rich and famous. Now voters are about to decide whether the mega-rich among them – including media mogul Oprah Winfrey, Meta head Mark Zuckerberg, Skims cofounder and reality television star Kim Kardashian, and filmmaker George Lucas – should hand over billions of dollars to pay for improvements to healthcare. Proposition 40 aims to levy a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of all of California’s billionaires. There are a little more than 200 such individuals in the state – but that hasn’t stopped the measure from dividing leaders and causing some of its ultra-wealthy residents to flee. One billionaire businessman says he’s brought jobs to California, but the proposition made him feel “a little bit like I wasn’t wanted”. But the vote is also offering regular residents a voice on an issue that has roiled politics for decades. “I believe this is the first billionaire tax – meaning a wealth tax that is targeting a very extreme percentile of the wealth distribution,” says Francesco Trebbi, a public policy professor at the University of California, Berkeley. He noted the measure’s historic nature and how it could help even out California’s wealth gap. The state has the largest economy in the country and boasts the fourth-largest global economy, bigger than India and the UK. It is also home to one of the highest concentrations of billionaires in the world. But it also has the largest share of homeless people in the nation and one of the highest wealth gaps. Supporters of the measure argue it helps ensure the ultra-wealthy contribute their fair share and will help backfill gaps in the state’s budget. The move aims to raise $100bn (£75bn) to make up for federal funding cuts to the state’s health-care system. Suzanne Jimenez, chief of staff for Service Employees International Union-United Healthcare Workers West, which helped lead the initiative, says the measure is a “short-term solution” to massive federal funding cuts coming to California as a result of US President Donald Trump’s sweeping tax and spending bill . “If we do nothing, we’re going to see a collapse of our healthcare system, while we figure out a longer-term solution to fund our healthcare,” she tells the BBC. While the ballot measure has many supporters, including billionaires like Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, it has faced fierce opposition from a range of figures, from billionaires to the state’s liberal governor. Google co-founder Sergey Brin has donated more than $100m to a political organisation that funds ballot measures that could block the wealth tax, the Los Angeles Times reports . California Governor Gavin Newsom, whose tenure is coming to an end, is perhaps the most notable political leader opposing it. He has voiced concerns that the measure could drive the wealthy out of the state and cut off crucial income tax revenue. A September poll from the Berkeley Institute of Governmental Studies and the Los Angeles Times found the proposition has not clearly won over a majority of voters, with 45% of likely voters in favour of the tax, 42% opposed and 13% undecided. The statewide ballot measure would need a majority of residents to approve it. California is not the first place to toy with the idea of taxing the rich. Also on the West Coast, voters in the US state of Washington are considering whether to accept or reject a “millionaires tax” – a 9.9% tax on income over $1m a year. While wealth taxes were once a fairly common form of taxation in Europe, they have rapidly fallen out of favour and now exist in only three European countries, Spain, Norway and Switzerland, says Dr Kristian Niemietz, head of political economy at the Institute of Economic Affairs. Niemietz believes wealth taxes are “more trouble than they are worth” because they create administrative burdens, suppress investment, drive capital flight and, in the end, raise little revenue. In Norway, a local news organisation found that a wealth tax increase led more super-wealthy people to leave the country in 2022 than in the preceding 13 years combined. A study on Switzerland found that a 0.1 percentage point increase in a wealth tax reduced taxable wealth by 3.5%.

title: Israel Police uncover, remove X accounts accused attempting to influence election
body: Israel Police exposed a network of accounts on the social media platform X/Twitter suspected of trying to influence the outcome of the upcoming Knesset elections, the police announced on Sunday. The suspicious activity was uncovered through a joint monitoring operation by the police and the State Attorney's Office, and a number of the accounts were removed to prevent them from exerting undue influence on the Israeli public's voting decisions.Police Commissioner Danny Levy said on Sunday that the police have completed extensive preparations to ensure the security of the elections and public safety in the wake of election results. “We will not allow violence, threats, incitement or criminality to harm the will of the voter. I have declared in recent months that we will not allow bullying from any side to harm the democratic process, and so we will,” Levy vowed. “Preserving Israeli democracy is our mission. We will fulfill it impartially and without compromise."On Thursday, the Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency) announced a similar move in which numerous accounts were removed from social media sites for manipulation efforts. According to the Shin Bet, the activity of the now-removed accounts may have allowed for foreign influence on the election.OSINT investigation found Iran-linked accounts posing as IsraelisIn late September, an investigation conducted by open-source intelligence platform Golden Owl found that Iran-linked actors had been tied to social media accounts where individuals posed as Israeli citizens and made claims about Israeli politics.Researchers found that multiple of the accounts were found to have made posts claiming that the election results would be stolen, and others posted misinformation about the voting process itself.Danielle Greyman-Kennard and Yonah Jeremy Bob contributed to this report.

title: Zelensky on Oleshky evacuation: Russia will try to force residents to flee to its territory
body:
The Ukrainian president made these remarks in an interview with “ TSN Tyzhden ” host Alla Mazur, responding to a question about the agreement to establish a ceasefire in the Oleshky area starting October 27 and about which roads the Russians might clear of mines, since, for example, they could clear the roads leading deeper into the occupied territory, according to Ukrinform.
“Of course, Russia will do everything to clear the roads in such a way that these people head toward Russia and stay there. In other words, they’re not going to simply let people go. Some of the people will certainly be evacuated to Ukraine in one way or another—to the part of Ukraine that we control. Whatever happens on the ground—that’s how it will be on the ground,” he said.
Zelensky emphasized the importance of how many people trapped in Oleshky can be rescued.
“Let them live. Ideally, I believe, they should be able to achieve their goal and evacuate here, to us, to Ukraine, which will certainly provide them with everything they need and support them, and so on… The Russians themselves blocked them, mined the road, and shelled the area themselves. And the people—our society—must be prepared for the fact that they will present it (for example, in this vein—ed.): ‘Here we see a thousand people who really want to go to Russia, and these fascists were shelling them,’ the President said.
He also stated that it was the American side that proposed establishing a ceasefire starting on the 27th.
“And it can’t be just one day. It will be several days, because humanitarian missions need to get there. They’ll arrive there, and there must be a ceasefire in the region so that people can get there… The missions will arrive—the Americans, us, and the Russians—it’s clear that the Russians are already on the ground there,” Zelensky noted.
The President reminded that, in order to ensure the evacuation of people, the Russians must clear the roads of mines in this situation.
“We need to assess the situation and work on all of this. And there—I think—at least the ombudsman has received the relevant instructions from me; we’ve spoken with both the Security Service and the military. We need them to give us indications of how the evacuation might proceed… Of course, if the roads are cleared of mines, people will simply leave,” the head of state said.
As reported, U.S. First Lady Melania Trump stated that she had secured a local ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, which applies only to the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky in the Kherson region.
According to the White House press office, the parties agreed to temporarily suspend all military operations in Oleshky to ensure the delivery of humanitarian aid and prepare for the evacuation of civilians through an agreed-upon safe corridor.
The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reported that, starting on the night of October 27, Ukraine is implementing a ceasefire in the designated area to conduct a humanitarian operation in the temporarily occupied town of Oleshky.

title: Farmers urged to grow more with less as horticulture project promotes climate-smart methods
body: A young farmer from Asante Mampong says his confidence in agriculture has been renewed after seeing how simple technologies can improve vegetable production, highlighting the potential of practical training to change how farming is done in Ghana. Obiri Yeboah Daniel had considered venturing into farming but was uncertain about how to begin. A visit to a demonstration farm under the Agricultural Colleges for Horticulture Innovation (ACHI) Project in Ejura exposed him to techniques he had previously only heard about. “I have learned a great deal this morning,” he said, describing his first practical experience with drip irrigation, sprinklers and plastic mulch, which helps retain soil moisture and suppress weeds. “When I return home, I will share what I have learned with others, especially members of my cooperative, and encourage them to adopt these innovative farming practices,” he added. His experience reflects the approach of the ACHI Project, which is working with agricultural colleges, farmers and industry partners to bridge the gap between classroom instruction and the demands of commercial horticulture. Supported by the Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO), the four-year initiative, running from 2024 to 2028, is implemented by TU Delft and Holland Greentech in collaboration with five agricultural colleges in Ghana. The project aims to equip students, graduates and farmers with practical production skills, business knowledge and access to improved technologies to help build a more productive and profitable horticultural sector. Producing more from smaller plots For farmers operating with limited land and resources, the project promotes methods intended to make better use of available water, improve crop quality and reduce avoidable losses. At the demonstration farm in Ejura, participants were introduced to drip irrigation, plastic mulch, hybrid seeds and sticky traps used in integrated pest management. Rather than relying solely on classroom explanations, trainees are assigned plots where they can practise the techniques and observe how the different technologies work together. Programme manager at Holland Greentech, Deborah Anobil, said the objective was to ensure participants left with the confidence and skills to apply what they had learnt on their own farms. “With the right technologies and practices, farmers can produce more from less land and increase their income,” she said. According to Deborah, farmers who combine efficient irrigation with improved seeds and good agricultural practices can improve yields and produce better-quality vegetables with a longer shelf life. The approach challenges the assumption that increasing production must always involve cultivating more land. Instead, it places emphasis on using available resources more efficiently. For smallholder farmers, however, adopting these methods will depend on whether the technologies are affordable, accessible and suitable for their individual farming conditions. The project’s practical demonstrations offer an opportunity to assess their usefulness before applying them more widely. From agricultural education to enterprise The initiative also seeks to address a longstanding challenge for young people entering agriculture by turning technical knowledge into a sustainable source of income. At Ejura College of Agriculture and Mechanisation Centre, students gain experience in irrigation, crop production, harvesting, grading and marketing. A student and farm manager at the ACHI Garden, Elizabeth Aboagyewa Amoah, said the farm provides a practical learning environment for students who arrive with limited experience of modern production methods. “We teach them how to use drip irrigation lines, sprinklers, and other irrigation facilities,” she said. After harvesting, the farm’s produce is sorted and graded, while records are kept and vegetables distributed to markets in Kumasi and elsewhere. The process exposes students to activities beyond cultivation, including quality control, record-keeping and marketing — skills that are essential to running a commercial farm. The project’s training also includes business planning, financial management, production cost analysis and marketing. Students taking part in a four-month training programme are introduced to entrepreneurship and business pitching to help them develop commercially viable ventures. Anobil said some graduates had already established businesses in produce aggregation and other areas of the horticultural value chain. The wider ambition is to encourage young people to build enterprises not only in crop production but also in logistics, storage, aggregation and post-harvest management. These activities could create opportunities for graduates who may not have the land or capital to establish large farms of their own, while helping address weaknesses in the movement and handling of fresh produce. Taking the lessons beyond the demonstration farm The ACHI Project’s model extends beyond agricultural colleges through demonstration plots, lead farmers and farmer field days. The project reports that 85 demonstration plots have been established and 115 farmer field days organised, reaching more than 5,000 farmers. Over 900 participants have received training in improved horticultural practices and related skills. The field days allow farmers to observe technologies in use, exchange experiences and consider how improved practices might work under their own conditions. For the approach to deliver lasting benefits, the knowledge gained at demonstrations must translate into changes on farms. Continued access to suitable equipment, technical advice and markets will be important in determining whether farmers can sustain those changes. His response points to one way agricultural knowledge can spread: through farmers learning from one another and adapting practical methods to local needs. Principal of the Ejura College of Agriculture and Mechanisation Centre, Dr Bright Akoto, said agricultural education needed to go beyond theory. “Addressing these challenges requires innovation, practical training, and the adoption of modern agricultural practices,” he said. He identified low productivity, climate variability, post-harvest losses and limited access to improved technologies among the challenges facing farmers. The project’s emphasis on water-efficient irrigation, improved production techniques and integrated pest management is intended to help farmers respond to some of these pressures while improving the quality and commercial value of their crops. Its focus on entrepreneurship and the wider horticultural value chain also recognises that higher production alone may not guarantee better livelihoods if farmers struggle to store, transport or sell their produce. The longer-term goal is to strengthen agricultural colleges as centres of practical learning, prepare graduates for employment and enterprise, and encourage investment and commercial partnerships between Ghanaian and Dutch businesses.

title: U.S. Navy orders next-generation electronic attack units to modernize EA-18G Growler fleet
body: General Dynamics Mission Systems will produce Next Generation Electronic Attack Units for the U.S. Navy under a $184 million contract that also covers sustainment support. The award moves the units into full-rate production for the EA-18G Growler Block II modernization program, with work continuing through 2032. The contract was awarded in September, and the company said work would begin immediately at its Bloomington, Minnesota, facility. Production is covered by firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity terms, while sustainment work falls under cost-plus-fixed-fee terms. “General Dynamics Mission Systems is proud to support the U.S. Navy’s EA-18G Growler modernization with the Next Generation Electronic Attack Unit,” said Scott Dunderdale, vice president and general manager, Land and Air Systems at General Dynamics Mission Systems. “This award advances the production and sustainment of a resilient, open-architecture capability designed to help ensure the fleet can rapidly adapt to evolving electronic-warfare threats.” The units form part of a broader effort to upgrade the Growler’s cockpit, internal systems and airborne electronic attack suite. The Navy says the Block II program, which remains in development, is intended to keep the aircraft ahead of evolving threats throughout its planned service life. Planned changes include an Advanced Cockpit System and other internal improvements shared with the F/A-18E/F Super Hornet Block III. The Growler’s commonality with the Super Hornet and the flexibility of its design leave room for further upgrades, according to the Navy. Built to replace the EA-6B Prowler, the Growler combines the F/A-18F Super Hornet airframe with a specialized electronic warfare suite. It retains the Super Hornet’s multirole capabilities and can perform a range of missions to suppress enemy defenses. The first Growler test aircraft flew in August 2006, followed by delivery of the first production aircraft to Electronic Attack Squadron 129 at Naval Air Station Whidbey Island in June 2008. The aircraft reached initial operational capability and entered full-rate production in fall 2009, before its combat debut during Operation Odyssey Dawn in Libya in 2011. The U.S. Navy is the Growler’s sole operator within the Department of Defense, while the Royal Australian Air Force also operates the aircraft. Four Navy expeditionary electronic attack squadrons support Air Force and Navy operations from shore bases.

title: Students’ List wins snap parliamentary elections in Serbia — Vucic
body:
BELGRADE, October 25. /TASS/. The newly formed, youth-backed Students' List, which emerged from a mass student protest, has won the snap parliamentary elections in Serbia, former President Aleksandar Vucic said.
"Many will be surprised, and you'll realize just how much some people lied. Judging by the results of the stratified sample frames, it's clear that we lost this election," he said at his Progressive Party headquarters.

title: Tel Aviv rivals run riot as Maccabi, Hapoel cruise to emphatic Premier League wins
body: Hapoel Tel Aviv cruised to a 3-0 victory over Hapoel Jerusalem at Teddy Stadium, while Maccabi Tel Aviv overwhelmed Hapoel Haifa 6-2 as the two Tel Aviv sides enjoyed convincing victories in the latest round of Israeli Premier League action.With 7,000 Hapoel Tel Aviv supporters in attendance at Teddy Stadium, Daniel Dappa opened the scoring just before halftime, collecting a superb through ball from Douglas Owusu before dribbling past a defender inside the box and unleashing a powerful strike into the net.The visitors doubled their advantage in the 53rd minute when Omri Altman finished off a magnificent backheel from Yannick Leliendal. Less than 10 minutes later, substitute Roie Alkukin tapped home a terrific Leliendal cross to complete the scoring and secure all three points for the Reds.Hapoel Tel Aviv coach Elyaniv Barda acknowledged that his side had struggled early on before finding its rhythm after the break.“We weren't good enough in the first half and didn't control the tempo enough,” Barda said. “We struggled until we made adjustments at halftime, and bringing on Roie Alkukin also helped us. The second and third goals came from excellent attacking moves involving plenty of passing and movement. They were incredible attacking sequences.”Hapoel Jerusalem coach laments team's shortcomingsHapoel Jerusalem coach Lior Zada lamented his team's defensive shortcomings, particularly the goal conceded just before halftime.“We had some good spells in the first half and played well, controlling the tempo of the game. But then we conceded a very soft goal at the end of the half,” Zada said. “It was a tough game, but we need to work hard to get results. We're conceding too many goals, although we're also playing many of our games against top teams with a lot of quality.”Maccabi Tel Aviv delivered an even more emphatic performance, defeating Hapoel Haifa 6-2 as Ali Camara scored twice in the second half to help the yellow-and-blue pull away.Elad Madmon gave Maccabi the lead from inside the box off an assist from Noam Ben Harush, but Arial Mendy equalized for Hapoel Haifa in the 38th minute to send the teams into halftime level at 1-1.Camara restored Maccabi's advantage with a header from a corner kick, and Dor Peretz extended the lead to 3-1 in the 58th minute. Sagiv Yehezkel added another shortly afterward, before Alon Turgeman pulled one back for the visitors in the 72nd minute.However, Camara struck again to complete his brace, and Itamar Noy added a sixth goal from inside the box to cap a dominant performance.Maccabi Tel Aviv coach Kenny Miller was pleased with the attacking display but insisted his team still had work to do.“We scored a lot of goals and we had plenty of chances even before we started scoring,” Miller said. “There are a lot of things I'm happy with and a lot of things I'm not. We can't give the opposition hope at any stage of the game. I'm very pleased with the result. We scored goals, but there's still plenty of room for improvement.”Hapoel Haifa coach Haim Silvas said his team struggled to recover after conceding from a set piece in the second half.“We came into the game determined to show that we're a good team,” Silvas said. “In the second half, we conceded from a set piece and then there was a kind of collapse. The game opened up and Maccabi Tel Aviv raised the tempo. We were still stunned by the goal and they scored another. From that point on, the hole was too deep to climb out of.”Elsewhere, Bnei Sakhnin edged Kiryat Shmona 1-0, with Sana Gomes scoring the decisive goal in the 40th minute to secure all three points.Sakhnin coach satisfied with winSakhnin coach Yossi Abukasis was satisfied with the result, even if he felt his team could have won by a greater margin.“We'll remain humble. I don't think this was a great football performance from us, but we created a lot of chances,” Abukasis said. “We had four or five clear-cut opportunities that should have resulted in goals. We could have put the game away much earlier, but we're happy with the win. It's very important.”Kiryat Shmona coach Shai Barda was left frustrated by another disappointing result, with his team having collected just three points from its first eight games.“We've only collected three points from 24, and that's a fact. This is unequivocally not where we expected to be,” Barda said. “Right now, we're struggling with a lack of confidence, and the losses are making it difficult to turn things around.”Ironi Tiberias and Maccabi Netanya shared the points in a dramatic 1-1 draw, as Bar Cohen scored in the 92nd minute to rescue the hosts after Oz Bilu had put the visitors ahead in the first half.Netanya coach Roni Levy was furious that his side had surrendered its advantage in stoppage time.“It's frustrating not to score, but we shouldn't be conceding in stoppage time,” Levy said. “That's irresponsible and says a lot about the state of our team. Our mentality probably isn't good enough, because with the right mentality in a game like this, you win 4-0 comfortably. We didn't do that and we paid the price.”Tiberias coach Alon Ziv said his team had overcome a difficult start to earn a valuable point.“We were about to make a switch in the middle of the match as we started off really poorly,” Ziv said. “We gave up a goal at the end of the half which could have really broken us, but we were able to come back and play well and take a point.”Maccabi Petah Tikva also picked up a valuable victory, beating Hapoel Ramat Gan 2-1 thanks to a first-half brace from Jose Cortes.Luan Campos pulled a goal back for the hosts after the break, but Ziv Arie's side held on to claim all three points and end a five-game losing streak.Petah Tikva coach Arie welcomed the result after a difficult run of form.“We'll take every win we can get. We started well and the first half was very good,” Arie said. “We wanted to win so badly that we weren't calm enough on the ball. We didn't play the way we wanted to in the second half, but after five losses, some of them bizarre, we'll take the win and won't complain about anything.”Ramat Gan coach Masai Dego was disappointed with his team's first-half performance, despite a stronger showing after the interval.“Ultimately, we can't perform the way we did in the first half,” Dego said. “We responded well after the break and we shouldn't have fallen apart. We restored some of our pride and could even have equalized, but it's a tough defeat.”See more Israeli sports coverage at www.sportsrabbi.com/en

title: Full list: NDC unveils 2027 presidential campaign council
body: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has unveiled its National Campaign Council for the 2027 general elections, with the party’s National Leader, Senator Henry Seriake Dickson, named chairman and its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, appointed co-chairman. The council also includes the party’s National Chairman and vice-presidential candidate, Senator Cleopas Moses Zuwoghe, as vice-chairman, while its National Secretary, Barrister Ikenna Morgan Enekweizu, will serve as co-vice-chairman.
