title: Slovak governmental delegation arrives in Moscow
body:
MOSCOW, October 25. /TASS/. A Slovak governmental delegation led by Foreign Minister Juraj Blanar has arrived in Moscow, a TASS correspondent reported.
The delegation was welcomed by Russian Deputy Minister of Science and Higher Education Konstantin Mogilevsky.
The delegation will take part in a meeting of the intergovernmental cooperation commission on Monday. The commission’s Russian co-chair is Minister of Science and Higher Education Valery Falkov. The meeting’s agenda is focused on issues of cooperation in the areas of energy, agriculture, environment protection, and culture.

title: At least 40 civilians killed in terrorists’ attack in southeastern Nigeria — media
body:
HARARE, October 25. /TASS/. At least 40 civilians were killed in a terror attack in Nigeria’s southeastern Taraba State, the Premium Times newspaper reported, citing human rights activists.
A group of gunmen invaded the village of Binnari from the neighboring Plateau State. They burned the peasants' crops, destroyed their homes, looted shops, and indiscriminately killed civilians.
According to eyewitnesses, the final death toll may be higher, as many residents are still missing. Search and rescue operations are continuing.
Nigeria has been fighting terrorism for about 20 years, with the extremist group Boko Haram, founded in 2009 in the city of Maiduguri, the administrative center of Borno State, being considered the main terrorist threat in northeastern Nigeria. The group’s goal is to seize power in the country, and it consistently carries out terrorist attacks. In 2015, the Nigerian armed Forces dealt a major blow to Boko Haram and significantly reduced the territory under its control. The militants began establishing bases in neighboring countries, primarily in the Lake Chad region. In 2015, a group of militants broke away from Boko Haram to form the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP, part of the terrorist organization Islamic State, which is banned in Russia).

title: ‘Cyberselfish’ author takes aim at Silicon Valley libertarians as her book returns from the dead
body:
It’s hard for books about technology to age well. They always risk becoming outdated as companies rise and fall, and as one hot new product is replaced by the next.
But last year, “The Nerd Reich” author Gil Durán declared that it was time to revive the career of Paulina Borsook, who he said “saw it all very clearly and tried to warn us 25 years ago.” Later that fall, The New York Times reported that Borsook’s “Cyberselfish ” — first published in 2000 — was finding new fans who want to understand why the tech industry “lost its way.”
Now, long after going out of print, “Cyberselfish” is returning in a new edition from Tin House (and Zer0 Books in the U.K. ).
Borsook told me in a Zoom interview that the book is meant to be “almost a travelogue” of her attempts to understand what she calls the techno-libertarian influence on Silicon Valley culture.
“That’s a 12-year-old view of the world,” Borsook said, describing it as “a kind of basket of beliefs” that’s “violently anti-regulation,” despite the fact that “no sector of society had benefited more and suffered less from the government than these guys.” In her telling, “even after the dot-com crash, that attitude was just there, percolating around, contaminating the aquifers. It was uncorrected, and it just spread out more and more.”
Borsook has yet to publish a second book, and she said that after “Cyberselfish” was first released, “no one was interested in anything I might have to say about anything, tech or not tech, forever after.”
But last year, she began to notice that prices for used copies were beginning to creep up, and she was starting to see “very out-of-the-blue, I-did-not-know-these-people posts on social media about how important this book was,” as well as inquiries from “European academics,” eventually leading to more press coverage and the new Tin House edition, with a new introduction by Durán.
Keep reading for our full conversation, edited for length and clarity, in which Borsook discusses AI, how Silicon Valley has transformed in the past 25 years, and what advice she has for young people seeking a career in tech.
Do you want to talk a little bit about how your interest in techno-libertarianism started, and how you decided that there was a book in this?
Everything with me is always inadvertent. I started knocking around tech circles, however we define it, in the early-middle ‘80s, in the Bay Area. And then I would say, starting around maybe the early ‘90s, I would hear these — to me — very weird, offhand remarks that some people would make that I couldn’t make any sense out of.
It’s not my nature to argue with people. It’s my nature to listen, and so I didn’t have the term for it except libertarian. But it seemed very screwy because initially, I grew up in Pasadena, which was [the home of the] Caltech-JPL space program, and so the parents of the kids I knew were another STEM culture. When I first got into Silicon Valley, I thought, “Oh, this is just another STEM culture like I’m familiar with.” And those guys [at Caltech and JPL] had a very clear sense of what the government can do for you, were not into enlightened self-interest. It was a different personality type, and they certainly didn’t self-anoint with how glorious and grand and magisterial they were, even though they were doing great things.
I was just listening, I guess, and being confused. Even then, I knew no sector of society had benefited more and suffered less from the government than these guys. So why are they acting like this?
So, backstory: My agent picked me up right after my MFA in Columbia, and he said to me, “You know, it’s really hard to get fiction published. Do you have a nonfiction book in you?” And I said, “Well, there’s this weird subculture that I’ve been observing that I don’t understand, and any time I don’t understand something, I want to explore it.” That got me down the rabbit hole of looking at this stuff and writing about it, and I consider it really almost a travelogue, in the sense of “Black Lamb and Gray Falcon” or that kind of stuff, almost more than, “This is a polemic.” It’s more like: snapshot, snapshot, snapshot.
I just fell into it, and also I’m sufficiently narcissistic that I felt I was uniquely qualified to write about this, and no one else was paying any attention, and that was very important to me.
I haven’t done a backread of all the other books written about the tech industry before “Cyberselfish.” My sense is that you do recognize, say, reading Steven Levy’s work that there is this alternative philosophy, libertarian streak running through Silicon Valley. But no one really pulled it out and put it under the microscope in that way.
That’s really true. And then most of the writing — certainly in the ’90s, but maybe later — was very celebratory. It wasn’t, “Wait a minute, what’s going on here?”
I heard [New York Times reporter] John Markoff give a talk about six months ago, and he said something I really liked. He said, “Silicon Valley is a multicultural place.” By which he didn’t mean your country of origin. What he meant is there’s all these different kinds of cultures in there, and he was always more focused on these countercultural [elements,] that kind of thing.
I’m never saying that wasn’t there. I’m just saying there was this other thing that I was more interested in. So they’re running in parallel. I don’t even think they’re in conflict.
It sounds like you don’t see the techno-libertarian side of it emerging from the counterculture, but rather [as] distinct cultures within Silicon Valley.
One of the distinctions I made in — I call it TDB, that damn book — is that distinction I made between Ravers and Gilders, and the Gilders being the social conservatives. I named them after George Gilder, who was this repellent thought leader of the early ’90s, very conservative, very reactionary, very backward-looking. And then the Ravers, in homage to John Perry Barlow, drugs and sex and rock and roll, “we’re going to Burning Man,” much more culturally liberal.
And that distinction has held up, because you have that in contemporary Silicon Valley. You have these Christian nationalists and conservative Catholics in positions of leadership, and then you also have the Burners and people having interesting experimentations with sexuality and drugs and the [effective altruist] and AI worlds. And so, what’s the counterculture bit of it? Maybe the personal freedom aspect of it is countercultural.
Another weird thing we always have to point out is that the [San Francisco] peninsula votes blue, still. Ro Khanna is the congressman from there. So I’m really talking about culture rather than electoral politics. [And I’m talking about] the leadership class here, the tech overlords. It’s not so clear to me how much the rank and file are like this, though probably more than when I was more familiar with what was going on there.
Because I think a lot of people have been attracted to work in crypto or AI, and they’re not thinking about the greater political surround. But they’ll drink whatever they’re handed, and they don’t much care.
We can point to people who are in charge, who have these [right-wing] beliefs or are allied with the Trump administration. There’s another executive class that maybe doesn’t have exactly the same beliefs, but is able to make themselves very comfortable with it.
And then you have that same diversity that you were talking about. There’s different communities, different cultures underneath. I’ve certainly spoken to people who work for someone like Elon Musk, and they’re like, “Yeah, I don’t love this guy, but right now, I can’t afford to lose this job.”
Right, I think there’s a lot more of that going on than in times past, because there’s greater precarity in terms of employment, and so people [say,] “I’ve got a job, I’m going to hold on to it.” […] Or, “I don’t espouse the beliefs that they’re giving out, but my project is okay.” Those kinds of things always go on.
For you folks who aren’t familiar with the book and maybe have a general sense that there is a libertarian strain in Silicon Valley, can you say more why — if somebody thinks, “I believe in technology being liberatory, and maybe it can free us from the shackles of government bureaucracy and things like that,” why is techno-libertarianism a bad thing?
First of all, that’s a 12-year-old view of the world.
I didn’t really have a good word, but it was a kind of basket of beliefs, and now we’d say maybe a cloud, and it was violently anti-regulation. It was bad borrowing from biology. “Let’s just let things evolve and they will be fine.” They have no idea how much government has subsidized and made possible their life, their world, all the R&D.
Government can do bad things. I’m an old hippie. I know about the war in Vietnam. I know what the CIA did with Allende. So I don’t want to come across [as if] I think it’s all okay. I don’t. But this sector of society has less to complain about.
And one thing that just makes me grit my teeth right now is a lot of these guys are moving to Nevada to live on the Nevada side of Tahoe, because they want to escape California taxes. Sergey [Brin] saying , “California is turning into Soviet Russia.” Are you nuts? Because the thing is, they all love Tahoe. Why do they think the water of Tahoe is so pure and blue? That is decades of government intervention and interference, environmental scientists, regulation. I mean, there’s this inability to connect the dots and lack of history.
To what extent is what we’re seeing now with the tech industry, with their alignment with the Trump administration, with all these other dystopian things going on, how much of that is a shift? And to what extent is this all one story, continuous with what you were seeing before?
Unfortunately, I see more the continuity. Excuse me for [my own] bad borrowing from biology, but […] I really see the Netscape IPO is when things really began to change, and Silicon Valley was invaded by the finance bros, and a real change in attitude. You got the culture of flip and flee, all that kind of stuff. Even after the dot-com crash, that attitude was just there, percolating around, contaminating the aquifers. It was uncorrected, and it just spread out more and more.
When you have things like Airbnb or Uber, which are strictly financial plays, they’re not technology innovation by my definition, but there was too much investment money in the world that didn’t know where to go. It would invest in these things, and these people would parrot this language. So I thought, “Ah, this is left over from 15 years ago,” in terms of their self-justification.
And the way that something like Airbnb fought so hard against any kind of regulation and anything that would ask them to be any kind of a good community actor in the communities they basically destroyed, in a lot of ways, in terms of the housing market. It’s like, “Yeah, that’s that attitude I was talking about way back then.” It’s like Giardia in the water system.
You can say, with good reason, that there was a lot of wonderful stuff that came out, and all the children of General Magic and all the great things that they created. I would never say that’s not true, but I’m not talking about that. I’m talking about the business culture of these people, how they see themselves. Sociopathy is a business virtue in a way that was never there before.
How do you see the rise of AI through that lens?
It’s perfect. “We don’t need to be regulated. We’re the most brilliant, genius, wonderful people in the world.” I see AI right now as a big Ponzi scheme.
You probably saw that really horrible ad that Apple did a couple of years ago, for one of their new computers, and they had all the musical instruments and all writing and [it all went into] the hydraulic press. How did Apple become so tone deaf? This is not the Apple that all the quote “creative class” loved for so many years. It’s not the Apple of the 1984 ad . But they still see themselves in this liberatory way.
If you buy the stockholder theory of value, it justifies whatever the AI companies are doing because of the stock play, not because it’s intrinsically valuable.
In the last couple of years, [“Cyberselfish”] has had this renaissance, leading up to the current reissue. When was that something that you started to notice?
This was maybe an exercise in masochism, but a couple of times a year, I’d look at the used book platforms, and it was selling for three bucks, which means that the seller is making more money on the shipping and handling than on the book, which is really humiliating.
I would say starting maybe a year and a half ago, I began to notice the prices are creeping up — not hugely, initially, but they were creeping up. And also, I was beginning to be contacted by European academics who wanted to talk to me. And I thought, “How did you even hear about this?” And then there were some very out-of-the-blue, I-did-not-know-these-people posts on social media about how important this book was, it shouldn’t have been forgotten, this is wrong.
Long story short, I got led to Gil Durán, who wrote “The Nerd Reich,” and then we went for lunch, and we realized we are kindred spirits. Around that same time, Steven Levy, who was working on a piece for Wired about “How did I get it so wrong? ” — and of course, I’m sitting here thinking, “Yeah, Steven, how did you?” — Steven contacted Gil and talked to him for 45 minutes, and Gil said, “You should really talk to Paulina, she’s been tracking this stuff forever.”
So Steven never quoted Gil. He never contacted me. And when Steven’s piece came Gil put this incredible rant on Bluesky saying I got everything right. “We really need to support her. Let’s try to bring this book back into print.” And between that and the podcast I did with him, all of a sudden, you could not get a copy of TDB for love or money.
[In the new edition,] there’s the new introduction by Gil, but otherwise it’s the book as it appeared [in 2000.]
Absolutely, and then I wrote a little introduction, going into more, “This is how this came back from the dead.” The acquiring editor at Tin House, she said to me, “Don’t change a word,” which is exactly what I wanted to hear. Because I think it’s an artifact of a time and place.
And with a book like this, if you start thinking, “Well, should we update this? Should we add to that?” it turns into a different book. People were glomming on to the book as it was. They weren’t saying, “Oh, it would be great if we updated this.” So, no, it’s not updated.
Hopefully, it’s not naive of me to imagine that there are people who might read this interview, read your book, and they are mostly on-board with what you’re saying about the tech industry and techno-libertarianism. Maybe they work at some big tech company [or] they have a startup themselves, and they’re like, “I don’t agree with the Peter Thiels and Elon Musks of the world.” Do you think that those people can reform or change the tech industry from within?
I want it to be true, because one of the questions that I’m getting these days, and I wish I could answer it better, is running into young people, they’re in CS or engineering or something, and they want a career in that, and they don’t buy this toxic stuff. “What can we do?”
And I go, “I’m not sure, because first of all, AI is sucking up all the investment money right now. So if you want to do almost anything, if it’s not AI-related, you can’t do it. Or a military-industrial thing. Government is so broke right now. Can you get a job in government? I’m not sure. Even the state governments, or I’d say the nonprofit sector, but that’s not doing well, either.”
I have this frantic thing of, I adore these kids and I want to support them and I don’t know what to tell them to do. It used to be that you could start a small company, a small consultancy, just you and a friend or two, and it didn’t have to elephantise as a grotesque growth, you could just bootstrap, but the revenue supported the growth, and you could do that. I’m not too sure how much of that world still exists. I think during the app era, you could also do that. I’m not sure now, but I never want to underestimate the both desperation and ingenuity of people, and so it may be possible.
I think your larger question — which is, do I think these big companies can be reformed from within — I think all it takes is a change. They’re amoral enough that if it’s not in their interest to link arms with the MAGA thing, they’ll do something different. I’m very cynical about it.
But I think the people who might be thinking about what used to be called appropriate technology , I’d love to see those people get funded or find a company that does that. It could be possible — whether they can do it within the venue of the hyperscalers, I don’t know, but I would hope that they could spin off and maybe do something else.

title: BC premier-designate Doerkson says province ‘chose change’ in election
body:
B.C. Premier-designate Lorne Doerkson said he was “deeply humbled” by his party’s victory and vowed to earn the trust British Columbians have placed in him.
Doerkson’s BC Conservatives won a resounding victory on Saturday night, with Global News projecting a majority government less than an hour after polls closed.
“I’m very excited that yesterday British Columbians chose change and they chose that,” Doerkson said Sunday in his first official news conference after election day. “People in every corner of this province, from the Peace to the island, from the Kootenays to the Coast placed their trust in us … It was lent to us for purpose and it must be earned back every single day.”
The man who was previously a relatively unknown backbench MLA took the reins of the party as an interim leader heading into the election after Kerry-Lynne Findlay resigned amid numerous departures.
On Sunday, his party was projected to win 64 seats, a total no party has surpassed since the BC Liberals won 77 seats in 2001.
Outgoing premier David Eby triggered the election less than two years into his mandate, initially saying it was necessary in response to U.S. President Donald Trump’s tariffs, though he later shifted his focus to affordability issues, a key part of Doerkson’s campaign.
Doerkson stressed he was an ally of British Columbia when asked about Trump reposting about the Conservatives’ win on his Truth Social platform.
“I’m an ally to British Columbia and we should have taken the opportunity years ago to protect ourselves against these attacks,” Doerkson said. “My focus is going to be to supercharge our economy … It’s just about endless, where I believe we can support different industries that will protect us against these attacks.”
Work was already underway in forming government, with the premier-designate saying he’s spoken with Lt. Gov. Wendy Cocchia and named Kim Henderson as chair of the government’s transition team. Henderson previously served as deputy minister to then-premier Christy Clark.
“When this party is sworn in, it will be ready on day one and it will hit the ground running,” he said.
He said his government will launch an independent review of the province’s finances on day one to “know where things stand,” promising residents would have a “full picture” before a budget is tabled.
He also reiterated campaign promises, stating within the first 100 days an expert commission would look into keeping emergency rooms open and cutting wait times.
But the first priority, Doerkson said, was raising the basic personal exemption to $32,000, amounting to about $1,000 a year “back in the pocket” of working British Columbians.
“These are serious times, people are stretched, the economy has stalled and too many British Columbians have stopped believing government can get anything done,” he said.
Though the BC Conservatives won a resounding victory, they also achieved a majority with the lowest voter turnout in decades. Preliminary figures from Elections BC show 48 per cent of those eligible voted. Prior to this year, no provincial election in recent history has seen turnout fall below 50 per cent.
Doerkson’s party was projected to win 64 seats with 48.05 per cent of the votes, with the NDP receiving 27 seats and 37.38 per cent. The Green Party won two seats and received 10.97 per cent.
During the campaign, Eby questioned if Doerkson would remain as premier going forward. As interim leader of the party, he is not currently permitted to run in an eventual leadership race.
Asked whether he would stay, Doerkson said that’s an “administrative detail” that will see information provided “imminently.”
“But I will remain leader of the party and I am thrilled to be the premier-elect of British Columbia right now,” he added.
The next premier also faced questions on his stance on repealing the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (DRIPA).
He stressed he was committed to working with First Nations as premier, but remained firm on his plan.
“It has not worked in this province, and frankly, it has caused more problems to date than I think potentially anything else,” Doerkson said, questioning what it has done to solve problems in the province.
Congratulations for the premier-designate have come in from across the province and country, with Doerkson adding he’s heard from “a number of First Nations,” including in his riding of Cariboo Chilcotin.
Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew congratulated Doerkson on his win and thanked Eby for his friendship over the past few years.
Kinew did have caution though when questioned about Doerkson’s policies on DRIPA and Indigenous rights.
“I think the election results in BC should concern every elected politician and every consultant out there for this reason,” Kinew said. “It’s a reminder that what we’re doing is not a game. When you’re elected to serve the people of your province or of your country, it is a serious responsibility that isn’t to be played with.”
A date for when Doerkson’s government will be sworn in has yet to be announced and he did not say if there would be a fall session, though he didn’t rule it out.

title: Navantia launches seventh Avante corvette for Saudi Arabia
body: On October 25, 2026, Navantia launched the seventh corvette built for the Royal Saudi Naval Forces at its shipyards in the Bay of Cádiz. The ship, to be named Neom, is the second in the batch contracted in 2025, following the five units built between 2019 and 2024. Navantia press release The ceremony was presided over by the Chief of Staff of the Royal Saudi Naval Forces, Vice Admiral Mohammed Bin Abdulrahman Al-Ghuraybi, and Navantia’s Chairman, Ricardo Domínguez, with the attendance of Her Highness Princess Haifa bint Abdulaziz Al Muqrin, Ambassador of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to the Kingdom of Spain. Following the opening of the event, verses from the Quran were recited, after which the speeches commenced. Vice Admiral Mohammed Bin Abdulrahman Al-Ghuraybi highlighted that the ship will carry a name that is one of the flagship projects of Saudi Vision 2030 and reflects the ambition of an entire Kingdom. “NEOM combines “NEO,” meaning “new,” with the letter “M,” representing His Royal Highness Prince Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Crown Prince and Prime Minister, may Allah protect him”. “From the shores of Spain to the shores of Saudi Arabia, HMS NEOM will stand as a lasting symbol of what our two Kingdoms can build together”, he said, in a speech in which he also commended his appreciation of Navantia’s team and Chairman. “From today, a new chapter begins: the integration of her systems, testing, sea trials, training, and the road toward full operational readiness. And one day, HMS NEOM will leave these shores and set her course toward the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. She will carry Saudi ambition and Spanish craftsmanship, the trust built through years of working side by side”, he stated. Navantia’s Chairman, Ricardo Domínguez, highlighted the professionalism of the workforce and partner companies in delivering a programme with demanding requirements and deadlines. “Launching one ship every four months is in line with the industrial schedule established for the programme and reflects the commitment of Navantia’s workforce to the customer. Your dedication, experience and professional excellence allow us to say with confidence that Navantia is rigorously fulfilling the commitments it has undertaken. This ship, which will soon enter service with our customer, is yet another demonstration of this shipyard’s capabilities.” Navantia picture He also thanked the Royal Saudi Naval Forces for the trust they have placed in Navantia, describing it as “the greatest recognition of our efforts and excellence.” Alberto Cervantes, director of Naval Shipbuilding in the Bay of Cadiz, also expressed his “gratitude to all our families, because their sacrifice, understanding and affection are also part of every ship we deliver and every success we achieve”. The second batch of three corvettes is being built at the San Fernando and Puerto Real facilities, with delivery of the final ship scheduled for 2029. Navantia will deliver the first ship in Spain and will send the second and third ships to Saudi Arabia for the installation, integration and testing of the combat system, as was the case with the fourth and fifth ships under the previous contract. The Implementing Agreement between Royal Saudi Naval Forces and the Spanish Navy includes the provision of an integrated logistics support package and crew training, together with a period of operational evaluation of the ships by the Navy at Rota Naval Base, where Navantia will provide support services. This contract represents a substantial workload for the Bay of Cádiz, estimated at approximately four million working hours and requiring an average of 2,200 skilled jobs per day. In addition, as under the previous contract, more than 20 subcontractors and 50 suppliers from several countries will be involved. Avante 2200 design This second batch of three corvettes for Saudi Arabia will be identical to the first batch. Their design is based on NAVANTIA’s AVANTE 2200 model, a versatile ship specifically designed for maritime traffic surveillance and control, search and rescue operations, and assistance to other ships, among other missions. The ships will also offer significant capabilities for the protection of strategic assets, as well as intelligence, anti-submarine, anti-air, anti-surface and electronic warfare capabilities. The corvettes feature a state-of-the-art design that maximises Navantia’s contribution by incorporating proprietary products, including the HAZEM combat system through the SAMINavantia joint venture, the HERMESYS integrated communications system, the DORNA fire-control system, the Integrated Platform Management System, the MINERVA integrated bridge, propulsion engines manufactured under licence from MTU, diesel generator sets, and gearboxes manufactured under licence from Schelde. Lastly, Navantia’s Repairs business unit will also take part in the programme by carrying out work during the corvettes’ dry-docking periods in San Fernando. – End – Check out our interview with Juan de la Cueva, Commercial Director at Navantia, on the Avante 2200 corvettes delivered to the Royal Saudi Naval Forces, during WDS 2026: The post Navantia launches seventh Avante corvette for Saudi Arabia appeared first on Naval News .

title: ‘Filled with content creators’ — Bwala disparages NDC campaign council list
body: Daniel Bwala, an aide to President Bola Tinubu, has criticised the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) over its National Campaign Council for the 2027 general elections, describing the list as being “filled with content creators”. Bwala, in a post on X shortly after the party announced the council on Sunday, also accused the NDC of concealing the identities of its media surrogates in mainstream media. “@PeterObi and NDC have released their list of campaign council members; and as expected it is filled with content creators,” he wrote. “They stylishly refused to name their campaign media surrogates in the mainstream media masquerading as OAP.” @PeterObi and NDC have released their list of campaign council members; and as expected it is filled with content creators. They stylishly refused to name their campaign media surrogates in the mainstream media masquerading as OAP. — D. H Bwala (@BwalaDaniel) October 25, 2026 The NDC had earlier announced the constitution of its National Campaign Council, saying it would coordinate campaign activities nationwide and mobilise support for its candidates ahead of the 2027 elections. Under the arrangement, the party’s National Leader, Senator Henry Seriake Dickson, will serve as chairman, while its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, will be co-chairman. The party’s National Chairman, Senator Cleopas Moses Zuwoghe, was named vice-chairman, while its vice-presidential candidate, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, will serve as co-vice-chairman. The NDC’s National Secretary, Barrister Ikenna Morgan Enekweizu, was named council secretary, while Mallam Ibrahim Hussain Abdulkarim will serve as director-general. Announcing the council, the party said it would provide “strategic leadership” and drive nationwide mobilisation behind its vision of “a new, just, and prosperous Nigeria”. The NDC also said the council would deliver a “people-centred and issue-based campaign” and urged its members, supporters and other Nigerians to remain united ahead of the elections. Bwala’s comments came shortly after the announcement, as political parties prepare their structures and mobilisation strategies for the 2027 general elections. The post ‘Filled with content creators’ — Bwala disparages NDC campaign council list appeared first on Vanguard News .

Social media and the iPhone Duo subreddit are filled with reports of Apple’s foldable failing quickly and in spectacular fashion. Some users report having the phone for only a few hours before the hinge seems to catch on something, then audibly crack and break the screen . Tellingly, the cracks all seem to happen in the same place.
YouTuber CuriousHagi was able to reproduce the cracked screen during some durability testing of the iPhone Duo. Then he pulled it apart to try and find the culprit. What he found is that the Duo’s hinge is quite complex, consisting of a gear-like central hinge and two different types of linking hinges.
The piece that broke is one of the links in the middle of the phone that happens to be thinner than the links below or above it, and it snapped at a small notch where it would be weakest. He also found marks where the hinge met the support plate, indicating where it may have gotten caught.

title: Infamous Nazi-era alpine retreat mostly destroyed in deliberate fire
body: The Eagle's Nest, a Nazi-era chalet in southeastern Germany, was mostly destroyed in a major fire believed to be the result of arson on Friday night, Berchtesgaden police confirmed.The historical landmark - in German, Kehlsteinhaus - was engulfed in flames at 9:15 pm local time on October 23. Police and firefighters said access to the fire site, which is located in an exposed position, was difficult, as were the subsequent firefighting operations.️A major fire was set at Adolf Hitler's former teahouse in his alpine retreat, the Eagle's Nest, in Bavaria's Berchtesgaden, Germany Beside Bavarian's, tourists from the United States were the largest group of foreign visitors. Austrian's ranked second and Poles were the seventh most foreign visitors. The state of Bavaria will rebuild the location.— Hawkeye1812Z (@Hawkeye1745) October 24, 2026Around 200 emergency personnel from fire brigades in six municipalities, the district fire inspection service, the Bavarian Red Cross, mountain rescue services and the police worked throughout the night, and residual operations are still ongoing.According to findings so far, no one was injured in the fire, but for safety reasons, investigators have not yet been able to enter the burned building safely.Shortly after the fire broke out, firefighters noticed a suspicious individual in the vicinity of the scene.33-year-old man arrested on suspicion of arsonThe 33-year-old man was subsequently arrested and is suspected of having deliberately started the fire. At the request of the public prosecutor's office, he was brought before an investigating judge and, following a diagnosis of mental illness, was provisionally placed in a secure psychiatric hospital.The public prosecutor's office and criminal police are continuing to investigate the background to the incident and the suspect's motive.The area around the incident remains cordoned off, and a drone no-fly zone is currently in place.Joachim Hermann, Bavaria's Interior Minister, suggested the site will be rebuilt; “We'll hardly be able to leave a ruin standing there,” he said during a press conference in Munich.He also thanked the firefighters and police officers for their “courageous and determined response,” and praised the “swift arrest of the suspect in the brutal arson attack.”What is the Eagle's Nest?The Eagle's Nest is a historic mountain-top building in the Bavarian Alps near Berchtesgaden, southern Germany.It was commissioned under senior Nazi official Martin Bormann as a reception house for Nazi leaders and their guests between 1937–1938, and sits about 1,834 meters (6,017 ft) above sea level.Hitler visited the chalet, although not frequently. It nevertheless symbolizes the Nazi era. Hitler's residence, the Berghof, was situated not far away.The Eagle's Nest survived WWII and opened as a mountain restaurant in 1952 before becoming a major tourist attraction. It usually hosts a historical exhibition.The TV miniseries 'War and Remembrance' (1988) filmed its fictional scenes featuring Hitler inside the actual building.Normally, access to the building involves a special bus ride up a mountain through five tunnels, then a walk through a 124-meter tunnel and a gold brass elevator ride up to the building.However, the normal access route was destroyed in the fire.

title: Show HN: Ledge – an open-source app that puts the MacBook notch to work
body:
Or install with Homebrew Watch the 1-minute film
Free, signed and notarized. You need a MacBook with a notch and macOS 26 or later.
Ledge is a macOS app that puts a small status area around the MacBook notch. It shows what's playing, a running timer, your next meeting, the weather and your notes, and it takes over the volume and brightness pop-ups. It's free and open source under GPL-3.0. There's no account and no telemetry.
Works with Music, Spotify and anything playing in a browser tab. Move the pointer to the notch and the card opens under it. From there you can skip, scrub through the track, or switch the output to your AirPods.
The card shows the day's events next to a month view. In Settings you can pick which calendars show up for each account.
When a meeting is about to start, a small mirror shows up on the Join button. Click it and your camera opens inside the card, so you can check how you look before you join. Nothing is recorded, and the camera turns off when the card closes.
How the calendar and the camera mirror work .
Right now, the next few hours, and a heads-up before it rains.
Keep Awake holds the Mac and the screen on, like caffeinate without the terminal. One stop further and your agents and long builds keep running with the lid shut, until the time you set.
The lid-closed stop uses a small root helper, installed only while that stop is on. If Ledge quits, the Mac can sleep again. How Keep Awake works .
For a phone number, a terminal command, or anything else you'd forget in ten minutes. Notes are plain files on your Mac, and any of them goes to Apple Notes in one click.
You can turn each of these off separately. Anything you turn off stops running and won't ask for permissions.
Ledge doesn't capture your screen or audio, and it doesn't save anything from the camera. The equalizer next to the song isn't listening to your music. It's an animation generated from the track. Ledge is also hidden from screenshots, screen recordings and screen sharing, unless you turn that off.
There's no account and no tracking, in the app or on this site. The privacy page has the details.
Ledge only draws on the MacBook's built-in screen, on purpose. External monitors and Macs without a notch don't get anything. There's no Dock icon: the notch is the app. To get to Settings, open Ledge again from Finder or Spotlight.
Yes. There's no trial or subscription, and you don't need an account. The source is on GitHub under GPL-3.0. Donations are optional.
It works in the same spirit. macOS doesn't use the notch for anything, so Ledge puts things around it: what's playing, a timer, your next meeting and short notices. Move the pointer there and a card opens.
A MacBook with a notch in its built-in display, such as the 14-inch or 16-inch MacBook Pro from 2021 and the MacBook Air from 2022 onwards, running macOS 26 or later. It does not run on macOS 15 or earlier.

No. It doesn't capture your screen or audio, and nothing from the camera is saved. The equalizer next to the song is an animation. It doesn't listen to anything.
The app is signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple, so macOS opens it normally. It isn't sandboxed, and it uses three private Apple frameworks. The README lists them and what each one is for. Nothing is asked for at launch: each permission is requested by the feature that uses it.
Yes: brew install --cask egemertbalcik/tap/ledge . Ledge updates itself through Sparkle, so you don't need to run brew upgrade for it.
From ledgeapp.dev, from the Releases page of github.com/egemertbalcik/Ledge or with Homebrew. All three give you the same app, signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple. Other sites with similar names are not connected to Ledge.
The full source is on GitHub . If something breaks, you can open an issue there.

title: CBD COP17: Nigeria, six others each win $50,000 grant for biodiversity projects
body:
Nigeria and six other countries under the High Ambition Coalition (HAC) for Nature and People have won $50,000 seed grants each under the Rapid Deployment Mechanism (RDM) to execute projects aimed at accelerating progress towards their 30×30 conservation targets.
The grants were announced and awarded on the sidelines of the ongoing 17th session of the United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD COP17) in Armenia.
The beneficiary countries are Costa Rica, Mexico, Nigeria, Nepal, Zambia, Rwanda, and Kenya, each receiving a certificate confirming a $50,000 grant for its respective project.
Nigeria received the grant for its project proposal titled “Strengthening Nigeria’s 30×30 Progress through Ecological Connectivity, Terrestrial and Marine OECMs, and Protected Area Management Effectiveness”.
PREMIUM TIMES gathered that the project will be implemented by the Nigerian Conservation Foundation (NCF).
Costa Rica’s project, titled “From 30×30 Coverage to Effective Conservation: Developing an Acceptable Visitation Load Tool for Cocos Island National Park”, seeks to improve conservation management at the national park.
Mexico received the grant for its project, “Strengthening Mexico’s Marine 30×30 through Underwater Acoustic Baselines and Evidence-Based Protected Area Management”.
Nepal’s project, “Operationalising Nepal’s National OECM Guideline: Recognising New OECMs to Advance the 30×30 Target”, focuses on recognising other effective area-based conservation measures (OECMs) to advance its conservation target.
Zambia’s project is titled “Strengthening Zambia’s 30×30 Progress through the Busanga Swamps Wetland Inventory and Management Effectiveness Assessment”.
Rwanda’s project, “Advancing Rwanda’s 30×30 Commitments through Community-Based Terrestrial OECMs and Ecological Connectivity”, seeks to strengthen community-based conservation and ecological connectivity.
Kenya’s project, “Advancing Kenya’s Marine 30×30 through Community-Led OECMs, Indigenous and Local Knowledge, and Effective Marine Protected Area Management”, focuses on marine conservation.
Nigeria’s award was presented to Sikeade Egbuwalo, the country’s focal point to the Convention on Biological Diversity.
Representatives of the other beneficiary countries also took turns receiving their awards, except Kenya, whose representative was unavoidably absent.
In her remarks, Mrs Egbuwalo appreciated the HAC secretariat and the RDM for the recognition and support.
“This support will not only help us to achieve the 30×30 targets but also help us to address the issue of fragmented habitat, which has been a big issue in Nigeria,” she said.
The RDM is an initiative of the HAC for Nature and People designed to address funding gaps by providing small-scale financing to catalyse broader conservation impacts.
“By providing fast, flexible seed grants, the RDM bridges the gap between early-stage requirements and larger funding sources, helping countries accelerate actions to achieve their 30×30 goals,” the organisers said.
During the gala, some recipients of the 2025 RDM grants shared their experiences and highlighted the funding’s importance to biodiversity conservation efforts in their respective countries.
In his closing remarks, Labaran Ahmed, Nigeria’s Chief Scientific Officer at the Federal Department of Forestry and HAC for Nature and People Co-Chair, expressed the Nigerian government’s appreciation to the HAC secretariat for its deliberations.
“We look forward to seeing your projects move forward and contribute to your country’s effort to achieve the 30×30 targets,” he said.
In his reaction to the award, Director-General of the Nigerian Conservation Foundation (NCF), Joseph Onoja, said the award represents a significant milestone in Nigeria’s conservation journey and reinforces NCF’s leadership in advancing biodiversity conservation, ecological connectivity, and sustainable natural resource management.
“Working in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Environment, NCF will provide scientific and technical support to the Federal Government of Nigeria in advancing the country’s commitment to the global 30×30 target of conserving at least 30% of land and sea by 2030,” he said.
Mr Onoja explained that the project will identify, map, and profile priority terrestrial and marine Other Effective Area-based Conservation Measures (OECMs); assess protected area management effectiveness; and develop a national Management Effectiveness Framework.
These interventions, he said, will generate critical evidence and recommendations to strengthen Nigeria’s protected and conserved area network, improve conservation governance, and support the implementation of Target 3 of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework.
He said the award underscores the importance of strategic partnerships between government and conservation organisations in translating global biodiversity commitments into measurable national outcomes.
“NCF remains committed to working closely with the Federal Ministry of Environment, relevant government agencies, research institutions, conservation partners, and local communities to strengthen ecological connectivity, improve protected area management, and advance Nigeria’s 30×30 ambition,” he said.
Mr Onoja said the initiative represents an important investment in Nigeria’s ecological future, safeguarding biodiversity, strengthening ecosystem resilience, and ensuring that nature continues to support the wellbeing and livelihoods of present and future generations.

title: Iowa’s Senate rivals pitch independence from their parties
body: Republican Ashley Hinson wants Iowans to know she’ll pick a fight with President Donald Trump. Democrat Josh Turek wants them to know he’ll work with him. The rivals in Iowa’s closely contested Senate race each sought to establish their independence in separate interviews aired Sunday on ABC’s “This Week,” pitching themselves as willing to put their state ahead of their respective party loyalty. Asked about her campaign pledge to be Trump’s “strongest ally” in the Senate, Hinson added a condition: “If it’s for Iowa.” “I will be someone’s ally when they’re with me on the issues that are important to Iowa,” the Republican lawmaker said. “And if they’re wrong, I’m going to pick a fight with them, no matter who that is.” The conflicting comments come in a state Trump won by 13 points in the 2024 presidential election, but where Democrats now see an opportunity to win their first Senate election since 2008. The president campaigned in Iowa this past week as high fuel costs and frustration with his tariffs complicate Republicans’ efforts to maintain the seat. Republicans close to Hinson told POLITICO last month that she needed to put some distance between herself and Trump, warning that his tariff agenda and the Iran war were undermining her chances. On Sunday, Hinson rejected Trump’s positive assessment of the economy. “Well, sure doesn’t feel like it right now,” she said, later criticizing the administration’s dealings with Moscow. “I don’t think we should be making any deals with Russia,” she said, pointing to her vote for sanctions. Her campaign told POLITICO on Friday that she opposed sanctions relief for Russia while supporting Trump’s use of the Defense Production Act to bolster domestic energy production. But there were limits to her criticism. While calling for the Iran war to end quickly, Hinson declined to oppose a potential new offensive after the midterms, saying she trusted Trump and the military to determine what needed to be done. Turek, meanwhile, called himself a “proud moderate” and sidestepped a question about whether Democrats had moved too far left. “I don’t think a lot about the party as a whole. I think about myself, and I think about Iowa,” the Democratic state representative said. That pitch follows a primary victory aided by national Democratic support , including from Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer’s leadership PAC — which contributed the maximum to Turek’s campaign, though Schumer did not formally endorse. VoteVets spent more than $10 million advertising on Turek’s behalf. He’s also secured the formal endorsement of former President Barack Obama, who appeared in an ad alongside Turek as the two played basketball. Asked what Trump had done right, Turek said Trump had done “a better job on the border than Biden, for sure.” He also cited agreement on keeping private equity out of housing and eliminating taxes on tips, overtime and Social Security, while arguing that Trump’s economic policies had concentrated wealth and power. Also asked whether endorsements mattered, Turek offered a blunt assessment: “Probably not.”

title: Lagos govt on alert, says no Ebola case in state
body: The Lagos State Government has reiterated its readiness to prevent, detect and respond to potential Ebola threats, urging residents to remain calm and vigilant. The state Commissioner for Health, Prof. Akin Abayomi, in a statement on Sunday assured residents that there was no Ebola case in Lagos. Abayomi’s reassurance followed the confirmation of an imported case of Ebola Bundibugyo virus in Abuja. He disclosed that the state Ministry of Health, through its Directorate of Epidemiology, Biosecurity and Global Health, was strengthening disease surveillance, risk communication and community engagement. According to him, the state is also collaborating with agencies at points of entry, including the Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA), to enhance early detection and response to suspected cases. “As part of its preparedness efforts, the State has conducted a strategic engagement and assessment at MMIA with airport management, Port Health Services and other aviation and public health stakeholders. “The engagement focused on passenger screening, information sharing, infection prevention and control, and coordination of emergency response measures. “The ministry is also intensifying public enlightenment through educational materials on Ebola, its symptoms, transmission and prevention,” Abayomi said. Ebola Virus Disease is a severe illness that can be fatal. It spreads primarily through direct contact with the blood and other body fluids of an infected person who is showing symptoms, contaminated materials, or the bodies of people who have died from the disease. Infection may also occur through contact with infected animals. The commissioner advised residents to avoid contact with potentially infectious materials and rely on verified information rather than rumours or speculation. He explained that Ebola symptoms might develop between two and 21 days after exposure and included fever, severe weakness, headache, muscle pain, sore throat, vomiting, diarrhoea and abdominal pain. The commissioner added that unexplained bleeding or bruising might occur in some cases. He said, “As early symptoms can resemble malaria and other common illnesses. “Residents who become unwell, particularly after possible exposure or travel from an area with active transmission, should seek prompt medical assessment.” In line with Lagos State’s fever-management policy, Abayomi advised anyone with a fever to undergo a malaria rapid diagnostic test before taking antimalarial medicines. “Where the test is negative, a healthcare professional should assess other possible causes and determine appropriate treatment.” Abayomi also advised residents to wash their hands regularly, avoid contact with the body fluids of sick persons, refrain from handling potentially contaminated materials and avoid contact with sick or dead wild animals. He appealed to travellers arriving in Nigeria, particularly from areas reporting Ebola transmission, to cooperate with Port Health Services and other authorised officials. The commissioner urged them to provide accurate travel and health information when requested, and comply with applicable public health guidance. “Anyone who develops symptoms during travel or after arrival should promptly notify the appropriate health personnel and seek guidance before visiting a healthcare facility.” He emphasised that airlines and airport operators should sustain established public health protocols, while travellers should consult official advisories from the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention. The commissioner also urged travellers to consult the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority and the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) for current guidance. “Anyone who suspects exposure to Ebola, especially following contact with a suspected or confirmed case, should promptly contact public health authorities for guidance before visiting a healthcare facility. “Suspected cases or relevant exposure concerns in Lagos may be reported through the State’s emergency numbers, 112 or 767.” He added that exposures could also be reported to the Directorate of Epidemiology, Biosecurity and Global Health, Lagos State Ministry of Health, on 08023169485. “Early detection and prompt reporting save lives.” The commissioner stated that the Lagos government would continue to monitor developments, strengthen surveillance and response readiness, coordinate with relevant stakeholders and provide verified updates as necessary. title: Show HN: Comparing SF Bay Area trash rates
body:
Comparison of waste collection rates across Bay Area cities. How does yours compare?
I made this website because I knew Oakland's trash bills were expensive, but I wanted to quantify how expensive.
A major contributor to illegal dumping in Oakland is high rates and small trash containers, as noted by the 2025–2026 Alameda County Grand Jury Final Report . That report also calls out the very high expense of trash disposal at the Davis Street Transfer Station in San Leandro, which is the closest place to dispose of trash for much of East Oakland.
And not all illegal dumping in Oakland is done by residents. With lax enforcement and high trash rates across the region, the city is seen as a dumping ground by neighboring cities.
Oakland's contract with Waste Management runs from 2015 to 2030 . Now is the time to get involved to bring down East Bay trash bills and end illegal dumping systemically. Volunteer your free time to clean illegal dumping sites and that does make an immediate difference, but the ultimate long-term solution is to make simple changes to public policy.
Illegal dumping in Oakland is a multi-faceted issue. Here are some ideas to end it:
Remember: This is not just an Oakland problem. People from outside Oakland have been caught renting U-Hauls to dump within Oakland. We need to work together to address the cost of waste management in neighboring cities, certainly including San Pablo, Orinda and Piedmont. Their high rates hurt the region.
Pass this page on to a neighbor, your neighborhood group or your city council member!
Significant effort has been spent validating rate data. If you identify any data quality issues or mistakes on this website, please report them to the email above.

title: 2027: NDC releases campaign council list, names Dickson chairman, Obi co-chair
body: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has named its National Leader, Senator Henry Seriake Dickson, as chairman of its National Campaign Council for the 2027 general elections, with its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, as co-chairman. The party announced the constitution of the council in a statement posted on its X account on Sunday. The council is expected to coordinate the party’s campaign activities nationwide and mobilise support for its candidates ahead of the elections. According to the announcement, NDC National Chairman Senator Cleopas Moses Zuwoghe will serve as vice-chairman, while the party’s vice-presidential candidate, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, has been named co-vice-chairman. The party’s National Secretary, Barrister Ikenna Morgan Enekweizu, will serve as council secretary, while Mallam Ibrahim Hussain Abdulkarim has been appointed director-general. Announcing the appointments, the NDC said the council would provide strategic leadership for its campaign and coordinate mobilisation efforts across the country. “The National Campaign Council will provide strategic leadership, coordinate campaign activities across the country, and drive the mobilisation of Nigerians behind the party’s vision of a new, just, and prosperous Nigeria,” the statement said. The party said the council would work towards delivering a campaign focused on the needs of Nigerians and policy issues. It described its proposed campaign as “people-centred and issue-based”, while urging party members and supporters to remain united ahead of the 2027 elections. “We call on all party members, supporters, and well-meaning Nigerians to remain united and focused as we work together to rescue our country,” the NDC said. The announcement comes as political parties begin preparations for the 2027 general elections, with campaigns expected to focus on candidates, policy proposals and nationwide mobilisation. The post 2027: NDC releases campaign council list, names Dickson chairman, Obi co-chair appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Oil prices could rise to $150 a barrel if war on Iran resumes
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 25 (MNA) – The chairman of Energy Commission at the Iranian parliament has predicted that the rising oil prices could go up to over 150 pbd if the war on Iran resumes.
Hojjatoleslam Mousa Ahmadi warned in an interview with local Iranian media on Sunday that a resumption of war and further disruptions to global oil supplies could push crude prices above $150 per barrel. Citing oil prices exceeding $117 per barrel and declining U.S. strategic petroleum reserves, he said a prolonged energy crisis could increase economic pressure on the United States and oil-importing countries.
He noted that higher oil prices would have consequences beyond energy markets, raising transportation, production, and energy costs while intensifying inflationary pressures in oil-consuming countries.
He said the U.S. government would face greater pressure to contain energy prices and protect domestic consumers. The longer the crisis continues, he added, the more difficult it would become to manage its economic and political consequences.
Ahmadi also said Iran intends to maintain long-term pressure on oil markets, drawing on its strategic position in the energy sector and the defensive capabilities of its armed forces. He argued that preventing prices from falling could prolong the energy crisis and increase the economic and political costs for Washington.
Concluding his remarks, Ahmadi pointed to energy-related challenges facing several European countries, including France, Portugal, Albania, and Italy. He warned that continued disruptions to oil supplies could pose further challenges to economic stability in both the United States and Europe.

title: AI has a language gap. That could be a problem for some voters.
body: AI chatbots are feeding non-native English speakers inaccurate information about the election, community activists and researchers warn, creating a barrier for some voters ahead of the midterms. The challenge — which leading AI companies say they’re working to address — is distinct from intentional disinformation campaigns that have plagued the internet for decades. Instead, some researchers and community leaders warn that voters prompting chatbots in non-English languages are unintentionally being fed inaccurate and ambiguous information — like whether they can vote by mail in their state — or overly literal translations that confuse electoral terms and lack context in various languages’ unique dialects. But the end result, the activists said, could still be the same: Voters whose native language is not English are more vulnerable to incorrect information and excluded from the most reliable answers ahead of the midterms. “Latino communities cannot afford to be left behind as artificial intelligence transforms how people work, learn, communicate and access information,” said Héctor Sánchez Barba, the president and CEO of Mi Familia Vota. “The history of the immigrant community and the Latino community has been one where we have been historically and structurally excluded from the best technology and access to information.” This digital divide has arisen, the activists and researchers say, in large part because AI models are trained in English, and fail to capture the nuances of other languages. Experts and grassroots organizations say this discrepancy in accuracy unintentionally disenfranchises non-English speaking voters across the country, where more than 20% of Americans speak a language other than English at home. National voter organizations that work in Latino and Asian American communities are grappling with how to bridge the gap and keep up with the rapidly developing technology to ensure that their communities don’t get left behind. Mi Familia Vota, which oversees some of the largest Latino voter mobilization efforts in the country, has built its own AI assistant dubbed “Nubi,” which comes from la nube or cloud in Spanish, for Spanish speakers seeking information on voting, voter registration and citizenship. The model is trained on government and nonpartisan datasets — as well as community data collected over 30 years of canvassing, town halls and citizenship workshops, said Denise Cook, chief innovation officer of Mi Familia Vota. She said it includes dialects of Mexican, Central American, South American and Caribbean Spanish, which have different words for election-related terminology. Polling place, for example, can be referred to as casilla , recinto or colegio electoral depending on the dialect, she said. Christine Choi, director of strategic communications at APIAVote, a civic engagement group for Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders, added that if AI fails to capture cultural and political nuances, “you can alienate a whole community or turn them off if you use the wrong interpretation.” A study by the Institute of Strategic Dialogue released in September found that accuracy of AI chatbots declined 16% when prompted in Spanish about voter information. Spanish prompts were more likely to produce incomplete or ambiguous answers, omitting relevant details and relying on overly literal translations, said Valeria de la Fuente Suárez, the lead author of the ISD study. “When voters are asking about registration deadlines or ID requirements, missing details can have real consequences,” she said. “Spanish-speaking voters deserve the same standards of clear, reliable and properly sourced information as English-speaking voters.” The study tested six frontier models through their respective APIs, or application programming interfaces, which are available for other developers to use. OpenAI, Anthropic and Google said in separate statements that they were working to refine their models for non-English languages, but APIs are not appropriate representations of how consumers interact with the actual chatbot interfaces, because they often include other fail-safes like popups or banners linking to external sources of information on voting. "Gemini is designed to respond with accurate and timely information and performed well in this analysis,” David Thompson, a spokesperson for Google, said in a statement. “However, this report accessed Gemini through our developer API, not the Gemini App, which has different protections and is how most people use our AI." Still, the leading AI companies say they are working to better provide election-related information to a wider swath of voters. To improve election information ahead of the midterms, OpenAI and Anthropic both said they are integrating information from Democracy Works , a nonprofit that collects official election information from the government, in its answers. “OpenAI's goal is to support people’s ability to participate freely in elections and make their own decisions with reliable information, transparency, and effective safeguards,” Nate Evans, a spokesperson for OpenAI, said in a statement. Some groups like Asian Texans for Justice, a nonprofit that works to increase voter engagement in Asian American communities in the battleground state, have opted to steer clear of the technology ahead of the midterms. “I do know that AI is being used more and more by AAPI communities, and we have made an organizational decision not to use AI for our in-language outreach due to inaccuracies,” said Nabila Mansoor, executive director of the organization. Spanish, Chinese and Vietnamese are among the most widely spoken languages in the U.S. besides English, but there are more than 500 other languages and language groups spoken across the country, according to the U.S. Census Bureau . The vast majority are considered low-resource languages with limited digitized data to train AI models, including Arabic, which has 1.3 million speakers in the U.S., and Swahili, which has about 150,000 speakers. And leading tech companies say they will try to address language-related access to AI systems more broadly. The Gates Foundation announced in September a coalition of 60 companies including OpenAI, Anthropic and Google dedicated to improving AI tools for an estimated 3.4 billion people around the world who speak languages underrepresented in AI models over the next five years. The joint commitment said, “The barrier is no longer the technology, which will only continue to improve. It requires a decision — to treat the world's languages as a shared foundation worth building, together, for everyone.” Community organizers say that while they welcome industry efforts to improve, the changes need to happen as soon as possible so immigrant communities can be equipped with the most reliable information for not only the midterms but the presidential election in 2028. “The way people get information has fundamentally changed and civic engagement has to change with it,” said Mi Familia Vota’s Barba.

title: Zelensky announces security meeting in Brussels with U.S., Ukrainian, EU and NATO representatives
body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky announced this in an interview with TSN.Tyzhden , according to a Ukrinform correspondent.
The President emphasized that last Tuesday in Oslo, not only did he hold talks with U.S. President’s Special Representative Steve Witkoff—with Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gar Støre in attendance—but there were also negotiations involving a much broader group — involving security advisors to the leaders of the United Kingdom, France, and Italy, as well as Björn Seibert, Chief of Staff to European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen.
Now, having received information from Witkofff about his talks with Russian leader Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg, the Europeans are planning a security meeting.
“Now they no longer want just a briefing [a brief update in this context on Witkof’s talks in Russia], but to discuss security, guarantees, and the EU in depth; they want a meeting this week in Brussels—the Americans, Ukraine, and the EU at the presidential level, and NATO at the secretary-general level. I don’t know if anyone else will be part of this group in Brussels, since that’s where the headquarters of NATO and the European Union are located. We are already planning such a meeting for Tuesday or Wednesday,” the President said.
As reported by Ukrinform, on October 20 in Oslo, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky held talks with U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff , with the participation of Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gar Støre and Finnish President Alexander Stubb.
On October 21, Witkoff met with Putin in St. Petersburg.
Earlier, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced that the U.S. had invited Putin to the G20 summit.
President Volodymyr Zelensky expressed the view that the G20 summit could serve as a platform for a productive trilateral meeting between Ukraine, the U.S., and Russia.

title: Kebbi is not invisible: A Rejoinder to Abba Anwar’s media visibility theorem
body: There is a curious contradiction in Abba Anwar’s article, “Kebbi: The Performing State Nobody Sees.” It begins by acknowledging Governor Nasir Idris, Kauran Gwandu, as a performing governor, proceeds to accuse his media aides of failing to communicate his achievements, and concludes that Kebbi’s development story is buried beneath a national media blackout. Yet, in attempting to establish this supposed invisibility, the writer catalogues several of the administration’s achievements, raising an obvious question: how did he obtain this information if the state’s communication machinery is as ineffective as he suggests? The article presents itself as a media audit, but its sweeping conclusions are unsupported by the research methodology and verifiable evidence necessary to sustain them. It invokes statistics, unnamed studies and an alleged 12-month media audit to portray Kebbi as almost invisible in national discourse, without providing sufficient information for readers to independently verify its findings. Anwar claims that Kebbi ranks 31st among Nigeria’s states and the Federal Capital Territory in media visibility, with a national Share of Voice below 0.9 per cent. He further asserts that six out of every 1,000 stories about state governments concern Kebbi, while 42 per cent of mentions relate to insecurity and only five per cent concern agriculture. These are specific statistical claims that demand credible evidence. Which organisations conducted the research? What media platforms were monitored? What was the sample size and measurement period? How were the figures calculated, and what criteria determined whether a story was classified as prominent, secondary or insignificant? Without answers to these questions, the figures cannot reasonably be treated as established facts. A statistic does not become credible merely because it is expressed in percentages. If the writer conducted a genuine media audit, he should publish the methodology, sources, findings and limitations for public scrutiny. Otherwise, what he has presented is an opinion supported by figures whose reliability remains unverified. The central issue, however, extends beyond statistics. Anwar appears to have confused media prominence with governmental performance, national attention with public value, and publicity with development. A governor does not become effective simply because his face dominates television screens, just as a state does not become prosperous because its government produces viral videos or secures prominent newspaper headlines. The proper measures of governance include education, healthcare, infrastructure, agricultural productivity, employment, security, accountability and the responsible management of public resources. Media visibility can communicate these outcomes, but it cannot substitute for them. Nevertheless, the importance of effective communication is fully recognised by the administration of Governor Nasir Idris. This explains why the Governor’s media aides have consistently engaged journalists, editors, correspondents, broadcasters and digital publishers to ensure that government policies, projects and interventions receive appropriate public attention. Contrary to Anwar’s portrayal, the Kebbi State media team has not remained confined to issuing press releases and taking protocol photographs. The team has continuously engaged major media organisations to showcase the milestones and achievements of Governor Nasir Idris across all sectors of the state’s development. This sustained engagement is a deliberate responsibility that the team remains committed to pursuing, ensuring that Kebbi’s development initiatives, government policies and interventions receive wider coverage and reach audiences beyond the state. It is an ongoing assignment, not a one-off exercise, and the team will continue to strengthen its efforts to project Kebbi positively through credible and strategic media engagement. As part of these efforts, we have visited major media organisations and engaged their editorial and management teams to strengthen Kebbi’s visibility at the national level. These engagements have involved discussions on sustained coverage of the state’s development initiatives, improved access to credible information and stronger professional relationships with media organisations. The efforts have also contributed to arrangements for sustained media coverage, including retainer engagements with Channels Television, TVC, NTA and Third Eye Africa, approved by the Governor following recommendations from his media aides. These initiatives demonstrate a deliberate attempt to expand the reach of Kebbi’s development story through established media platforms. It is therefore misleading to portray the Governor’s media aides as professionals who have failed to understand contemporary communication practices. The team recognises that modern government communication requires a combination of conventional journalism, digital distribution, multimedia storytelling, documentaries, feature articles, interviews, strategic media engagement and reliable public information. The existence of further opportunities to improve visibility does not mean that nothing has been done. Every state can strengthen its communication strategy, regardless of how much attention it currently receives. Anwar’s argument that a handful of states control more than 60 per cent of national media attention also fails to establish that Kebbi’s position, assuming his figures are accurate, is principally attributable to the competence of its media team. Population, commercial activity, political competition, the concentration of media organisations, advertising markets, entertainment industries and the frequency of nationally consequential events all influence media coverage. Lagos benefits from its commercial and entertainment industries, while the Federal Capital Territory hosts federal institutions, diplomatic missions and national agency headquarters. Kano has substantial demographic and commercial significance, while Rivers has a prominent petroleum economy. These factors generate news independently of the performance of individual governors’ media teams. Anwar has identified a possible disparity in media attention but has not established its cause. That distinction is fundamental to any credible assessment. His argument about insecurity is similarly incomplete. Even if security-related stories constitute a substantial proportion of coverage concerning Kebbi, that does not automatically demonstrate professional incompetence on the part of government media aides. News organisations exercise editorial independence and report events according to their news value and public significance. A government cannot reasonably expect journalists to suppress security-related reporting simply because it would prefer a different public narrative. The relevant questions are whether the writer’s statistics are accurate, whether they distinguish between stories specifically about Kebbi and reports mentioning several states, and whether the actual prominence and context of the coverage were properly assessed. Without that information, his conclusions remain questionable. The same applies to his claim that Kebbi’s agricultural potential receives insufficient national attention. The state’s rice production, fishing economy, irrigation potential and agricultural communities deserve sustained coverage. However, establishing an agricultural publicity deficit requires evidence of the activities undertaken, the coverage they received, comparable figures from other states and the reasons particular stories may not have attracted national publication. The distinction between agricultural performance and agricultural publicity must not be ignored. A state may achieve substantial agricultural output without every development becoming national news. Conversely, extensive publicity does not automatically translate into superior productivity. Both issues deserve attention, but neither should be used as a substitute for examining the other. Perhaps the most troubling aspect of Anwar’s article is his attempt to attribute Kebbi’s supposed national invisibility almost entirely to the Governor’s media aides without presenting an independent evaluation of their work. Did he examine the team’s media engagements, publications, digital content, crisis communication, editorial placements and relationships with journalists? Did he interview editors, correspondents or communication professionals? Did he compare Kebbi’s media output with that of other states using consistent criteria? The article provides no convincing evidence that such a comprehensive assessment was undertaken. Instead, it moves from alleged differences in media attention to a sweeping verdict on professional competence. That is an accusation, not an adequately demonstrated conclusion. The suggestion that Kebbi’s lack of permanent bureaus belonging to certain national television stations proves communication failure is equally questionable. Media organisations determine their bureau locations according to editorial priorities, commercial considerations, operational requirements and logistical realities. Their decisions are not simply a referendum on the competence of a governor’s press office. More importantly, Anwar’s portrayal overlooks the efforts already made by the Kebbi State Government to strengthen the presence and coverage of major media organisations in the state. The media team has actively pursued these relationships because it recognises the importance of sustained national visibility. The progress made through these engagements, alongside the arrangements for continued coverage, deserves acknowledgment rather than dismissal. The team’s efforts have also received commendation from Governor Nasir Idris and positive recognition from senior professionals in the information sector, including the Minister of Information, as well as media leaders. Such recognition does not place the team beyond criticism, but it is relevant to any balanced assessment of its work. Anwar also asserts that inadequate publicity could prevent Kebbi from attracting investment, suggesting that a state that is not seen or heard will not be funded or considered. This is an oversimplification of how public finance and investment decisions operate. Visibility can help investors discover opportunities, but investment decisions depend on credible economic prospects, infrastructure, security, access to markets, regulatory conditions, institutional capacity and expected returns. No evidence is provided that Kebbi has lost a particular investment or funding opportunity because of the alleged media visibility deficit. A compelling agricultural investment proposition requires reliable data, viable projects, infrastructure and practical engagement with investors. Publicity can communicate these advantages, but it cannot replace them. Similarly, the Argungu International Fishing and Cultural Festival deserves sustained national and international promotion. However, comparing its visibility with that of other cultural festivals without examining media coverage, tourism infrastructure, visitor numbers, sponsorship, accessibility and promotional strategies does not establish that Kebbi’s media team has failed. If improvements are necessary, they should be identified through evidence and addressed with practical proposals.
