title: Space Force wants to embed more guardians into the joint force
body: Space Force intends to send more guardians to support combatant commands in frontline roles, the service’s new leader said. In a message to the force, Chief of Space Operations Gen. Douglas Schiess outlined several of his mission priorities for Space Force. Alongside growing the size of the force — Space Force is currently the smallest branch of the military but has goals to double its personnel size — Schiess called for better integrating guardians into the wider force “at scale.” According to the top officer, the service needs to refine how it embeds “combat-effective” guardians into the wider force, and have enough service members in those roles to achieve “space superiority.” “We have proven that spacepower produces battlefield success. This means providing effective and well-equipped space forces, in the right quantities, to combatant commands on the front lines, staying ahead of threats through rapid acquisitions, and bringing space expertise directly to the fight no matter where it is,” Schiess wrote. Space Force leadership has pointed to multiple major U.S. campaigns this year where the branch has played a key role, including Operation Absolute Resolve which saw U.S. forces attack Venezuela and capture President Nicolás Maduro. In the aftermath of that, Space Force set up dedicated command elements for U.S. Northern Command and U.S. Southern Command. In addition, guardians supported Operation Epic Fury, the first phase of the ongoing war with Iran. In April, then-Chief of Space Operations Gen. Chance Saltzman said that the war proved that Space Force was “ combat credible .” “Looking ahead, we must build a sustained pipeline of Guardian talent, tailored with the appropriate training, and equipped with the most advanced capabilities, to ensure the Joint Force is fully powered by space expertise,” Schiess said. This month, Space Force also established its component field command under U.S. Special Operations Command, with the goal of institutionalizing “how the Space Force organizes, trains, equips and presents forces for the special operations enterprise,” the service said. Schiess also cited a need to build up the force’s arsenal of on-orbit weapons. Space Force has been developing various types of weapons systems for “orbital warfare,” ranging from kinetic ones to jamming devices and other electromagnetic warfare tools. Last month, Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink revealed that Space Force already has “space control weapons” in orbit. It was the first disclosure of such weapons, although neither Meink or Space Force elaborated on what kind of weapons they are. The post Space Force wants to embed more guardians into the joint force appeared first on Task & Purpose .

title: Why I Am a Programmer
body:
There they sit, the preschooler class encircling their mentor, the substitute teacher.
"Now class, today we will talk about what you want to be when you grow up. Isn't that fun?"
The teacher looks around and spots the child, silent, apart from the others and deep in thought.
she encourages him. Jonny looks around, confused, his train of thought disrupted. He collects himself, and stares at the teacher with a steady eye.
he says, his words becoming stronger and more confidant as he speaks.
"I want to write something that will change peoples perception of reality. I want them to walk away from the computer dazed, unsure of their footing and eyesight. I want to write something that will reach out of the screen and grab them, making heartbeats and breathing slow to almost a halt. I want to write something that, when it is finished, they are reluctant to leave, knowing that nothing they experience that day will be quite as real, as insightful, as good. I want to write demos."
Silence. The class and the teacher stare at Jonny, stunned. It is the teachers turn to be confused. Jonny blushes, feeling that something more is required.
"Either that or I want to be a fireman."
-- Denthor of ASPHYXIA (aka Grant Smith), TUT7.TXT (1993)
I grew up in a pre-mainstream Internet world. A time when only a handful of kids at my primary school had a computer. We lived in a rough neighbourhood and so having a computer meant that you were a target for robbery. As we all knew somebody who had their computer stolen at least once, having a computer was kept on the low down. But we still found each other. Each time word got out that some kid got a new computer, they was suspiciously quizzed before being let into our digital posse.
A lot of my childhood was spend living indoors behind a buzzing 14" CRT, pirating games with other kids via 3.5" single-density floppies with their corners drilled out, and once in a while even playing them. But I was more of a collector than gamer. Like Ash from Pokemon - got to catch them all. And the people who created computer games were my idols. I was always in awe of what they could do with that big, heavy, beige box under the table.
One day word spread that there was a way to edit saved game files via XTreeGold's Hex View that gave you unlimited lives and allowed you to skip stages. With each new game that came out, the race was on to see who could be the first to flip the right bits to get the powerups. It was seriously heart pumping. Although only tinkering, it felt like we were our own gods.
We bought a modem a few years later and soon after got a copy of The Australian BBS Listing - a textfile containing most of the publically accessible BBSes online. I dialed every one of them (but that's for another blog post). It opened up a whole new world to explore. Instead of just a handful of kids pirating games via Sneakernet, I was connected to the digital underground - a world where anything digital was within reach (some even had Internet gateways). Even the newest blockbusters that I had only read about in PC Zone magazine were all there for me to leech. All of them, soon slowly trickling down the wire via ZMODEM.
But there was something different with these BBS downloaded games. Not something bad, but something exciting. Each time these games were run, it was like a short commercial was played before the title screen. Now I'm not talking about commercials selling steak knives. Instead, these were brazen posters screaming fuck you by the people who had managed to crack the game's copy protection code and were now distributing the game illegally for free. I later found out that these commercials were called cracktros. The precursor to demos and what started the whole demoscene. But simply calling them demos just doesn't give them justice. They were more of an out of body experience. Sensory overload. Like what you would feel at 2am, half tipsy, half asleep and being woken up stunned as you stare at a late 90s acid hard trance film clip, feeling it inject directly into your cerebral cortex. Once it finished playing, you were frozen. Still unsure whether you saw something real or just imagined it all. The only thing you were sure of, was that it was awesome.
Then one day while browsing the file section of some random BBS, I stumbed onto a file innocently called TUT1-9.ZIP. It's FILE_ID.DIZ caught my attention:
How to code demo like effects? You mean I too could be one of those sorcerers that had the computer under their complete control!? My heart raced as I added it to the download queue, fired up the aging Epsom LQ-300, then covered me ears as its loud ink needles hit the blue and white computer paper.
I didn't know anything about programming but I was completely estatic with the potential. I followed along with Denthor's tutorials as much as I could, typed everything out and hoped that Borland's Turbo Pascal 6.0 wouldn't laugh at me too much. It only gave me a basic understanding of how all the pieces to the puzzle fit together, but it was enough to whet my appetite and crave for more. I wasn't even into my teens yet but I definitely knew at the time that I didn't want to watch demos or play computer games anymore. I wanted to make them. I wanted to be elite. I wanted to be a programmer.

title: Gheist campaign plants secret-dumping workflows using stolen GitHub tokens
body:
Since September 15, 2026, Wiz Research has been tracking Gheist: a new campaign performing mass abuse of compromised GitHub tokens. The attack commits a workflow named sync-check to every repository to which each token has access. The workflow seeks to print the repository's secrets into its own workflow log. Then, the tool downloads the log through the GitHub API and deletes the run seconds later. The tool's API requests carry the user agent gheist , which gives the campaign its name.
We have recovered more than 13,500 planted branches from more than 850 compromised accounts, ranging from personal projects to enterprise organizations' private repositories.
A recent GitHub control has been blocking the exploitation in public repositories, but we've observed successful exploitation and follow-on activity in private repositories and GitHub enterprise environments.
roughly ⅔ of implicated accounts are no longer available on GitHub. This likely indicates response activity, as we have reported this activity to GitHub.
For each repository, the tool creates a branch named ci-sync- plus six random characters, then commits .github/workflows/sync-check.yml with the message ci: sync config . The commit is unsigned and authored as the token's owner. The push event triggers the workflow:
GitHub masks secret values in logs only when they appear verbatim. A base32-encoded secret doesn't match, so it prints in full.
While permissions: {} restricts the job's GITHUB_TOKEN , which the attacker doesn't need, it doesn't restrict the secrets context.
When a repository has deployment environments, the tool lists them in a job matrix with environment: ${{ matrix.environment }} , so environment-scoped secrets, often production credentials, are printed too.
Because the secrets leave through GitHub's own API, there is no attacker domain or outbound connection to block.
In enterprise organizations, we saw the tool cycle through tokens of several users and automation accounts within minutes, clone private repositories before planting the workflow, and hours later, cloud credentials from the same organization used to enumerate AWS Secrets Manager.
Two variants of this attack have been observed in parallel. They can be distinguished via the branch names.
Tool A uses a hexadecimal suffix and the plain payload.
Tool B uses a base36 suffix, added timeout-minutes: 6 and the environment matrix within hours of its first run on September 28, and modifies the selected payload per repository.
On October 19, Tool B added echo X | base32 -w 120 between the dumps, which prints LAFA==== as a separator, likely for the operator's log parser. Hours later it pushed a second job, sync-host , with runs-on: self-hosted , apparently only to repositories with a registered self-hosted runner. It writes three helper files ( .gdmp_pat , .gdmp_patg , .gdmp_sweep ) and logs each stage under a ===== gdmp-pivot: <stage> ===== header :
A recursive search of the home directory, workspace and system paths for 31 token formats (including keys for AI providers such as Anthropic, Hugging Face, Groq and NVIDIA), private keys, .env files, Terraform state and shell history.
The environment of every process, from /proc/*/environ .
Through the Docker socket, a container with the host's root filesystem mounted, to repeat the search on the host.
AWS instance-role credentials, plus GCP and Azure metadata.
GitHub Actions and GitLab runner credential files.
However, this job is buggy: it looks for the wrong runner key file, its URL-credential regex is broken, and it doesn't collect GCP or Azure tokens.
Since July 28, 2026, GitHub has held potentially malicious workflow runs in public repositories until a collaborator approves them. Every public Gheist run we checked, across all variants including the self-hosted job, sits at action_required. The control worked, and the malicious payloads never ran.
Unfortunately, that hold doesn't apply to private repositories or GitHub Enterprise Server. There, GitHub audit logs show runs on ci-sync-* branches completing and then being deleted by the gheist user agent. CloudTrail shows the organizations' own workflows running on those branches and assuming AWS roles, which proves Actions executed without approval.
For defenders, that last signal finds Gheist without any GitHub logs, as shown below.
This campaign is leveraging compromised GitHub access. The same accounts are used by other actors and campaigns, which demonstrates how compromised credentials can move throughout the threat actor ecosystem. We've observed overlaps with the following campaigns:
Lure repositories (malware distribution). On October 6, 391 accounts renamed about 1,461 repositories to cracked-software lures like fl-studio-crack and solana-sniper-lite. The rename wiped 610 ci-sync branches as a side effect. 166 of these accounts never appear in Gheist activity, so the pool is larger than Gheist's footprint.
Free compute. On October 18, 25 Gheist accounts each created a "Windows RDP Runner" repository within nine minutes, attempting to abuse GitHub Actions for free compute cycles.
PolinRider. Some victims appear to be infected with PolinRider , the DPRK-linked malware that hides JavaScript in build config files and force-pushes back-dated commits. On October 19 and 20, three victims re-pushed their Gheist commits with a loader appended to vite.config.js behind hundreds of whitespace characters, and in two cases an api.js that package.json runs before every dev and build.
Megalodon. 57 accounts from Gheist's first phase were also victims of Megalodon in May.
The credential sources we could trace fit this picture: infostealer logs, and tokens exposed in earlier supply-chain compromises such as the Trivy compromise in March.
Note: Gheist is distinct from GhostAction , which uses different workflow files and exfiltrates secrets to 193.32.204[.]199.
Look for branches named ci-sync- followed by six random characters, where the only change is a new file at .github/workflows/sync-check.yml with the commit message ci: sync config .
In GitHub audit logs, look for workflow runs on ci-sync-* branches that were deleted within a minute of completing, and for any activity from the user agent gheist .
If your workflows authenticate to the cloud with OIDC, check cloud audit logs for role assumptions or token exchanges whose subject includes a ci-sync- branch. That shows GitHub Actions ran on an attacker branch, even if you don't collect GitHub logs.
On self-hosted runners, look for the files .gdmp_pat , .gdmp_patg and .gdmp_sweep , and the string gdmp-pivot in job logs.
Rotate every repository, organization and environment secret available to an affected repository. Deleting the run or the branch doesn't undo the exposure.
Revoke the tokens that pushed the commits, and check their owners' devices for infostealers.
If a ci-sync branch ran on a self-hosted runner, treat the host and its instance role as compromised.
Don't approve held sync-check runs, and don't run code from ci-sync branches.
Harden. Require reviewers on environments with production secrets, scope OIDC trust policies to protected branches or environments, use GitHub Apps or short-lived fine-grained tokens instead of personal access tokens, and run self-hosted runners as ephemeral hosts without Docker socket or unrestricted metadata access.
Branch ci-sync- followed by six characters, matching ^ci-sync-[0-9a-z]{6}$
Commit message ci: sync config adding only .github/workflows/sync-check.yml
Markers toJSON(secrets) }}' | base32 -w 120 and ===== gdmp-pivot: ; files .gdmp_pat , .gdmp_patg , .gdmp_sweep
Workflow blob SHAs: f3da2b8b357dcda02fd455d314be2a95007516a6 (plain), d09535857a741bbb976bdc084a9a021713133291 (timeout), 1dc5af9cce950aad1eb1546ecce8565b117540c4 (separator), c665b778b2d822453293003e7ca0bbb2cb08e39d (self-hosted job). Environment-matrix variants differ per repository.
The Threat Center advisory includes an Event Explorer query covering planted commits, Gheist activity in GitHub audit logs and cloud role assumptions from attacker branches. Wiz Defend detects the activity with rules including "New Workflow Completed And Deleted In Short Time Span", "Workflow Pushed With Secret Dump" and "Commit Created With Known Malicious Commit Message".

title: Were Young People Removed From Nigeria’s Voter Register?
body: The recent voter registration figures released by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) have raised important questions about the declining number of young people on Nigeria’s voter register. Let’s look at what the data tells us. According to INEC, Nigeria had 93,469,008 registered voters in 2023, distributed across four age categories: • Youth: 18–34 years: 37,060,399 (39.6 per cent) • Middle age: 35–49 years: 33,413,591 (35.8 per cent) • Elderly: 50–69 years: 17,700,270 (18.9 per cent) • 70 years and above: 5,294,748 (5.7 per cent) The 2026 figures show that the voter register has increased to 103,428,715 registered voters, representing an increase of 9,959,707 voters, and representing 10.66 per cent compared with the 11.27 per cent increase recorded in 2023. The 2026 age distribution is as follows: • Youth: 18–34 years: 29,777,578 (28.79 per cent) • Middle age: 35–49 years: 43,265,946 (41.83 per cent) • Elderly: 50–69 years: 22,982,900 (22.22 per cent) • 70 years and above: 7,402,291 (7.16 per cent) What Do These Figures Tell Us? 1. While the overall voter register figure for 2026 increased by 10.66 per cent, the number of registered voters aged 18–34 declined by 7,282,821, representing a 19.65 per cent reduction in this age category. Their share of the register also declined from 39.6 per cent in 2023 to 28.79 per cent in 2026, a decrease of approximately 10.9 percentage points. 2. The number of registered voters aged 35–49 increased by 9,852,355, representing an increase of approximately 29.5 per cent. Does this mean young people were removed from the register? Not necessarily. Between 2023 and 2026, three years elapsed. Voters who were aged 32, 33, and 34 in 2023 would have transitioned into the 35–49 age category by 2026. This demographic shift could partially explain the decline in the youth category and the increase in the older age category. A voter checking a voter register during the Federal Capital Territory area council elections in Abuja. However, ageing alone does not fully account for these changes. It is also necessary to examine new additions to the register, particularly the rate of youth registration, and any administrative adjustments. This raises a critical question: Are young Nigerians registering to vote at a rate sufficient to replace those who are ageing out of the youth category? For historical perspective, Nigeria’s voter register increased from 68,833,476 in 2015 to 84,004,084 in 2019, representing a 22.04 per cent increase. Between 2019 and 2023, the register grew to 93,469,008, an increase of 9,464,924 voters (11.27 per cent). By 2026, it had risen further to 103,428,715, representing an additional 9,959,707 voters (10.66 per cent). Although the absolute increase between 2023 and 2026 was slightly higher than that recorded between 2019 and 2023, the percentage growth was marginally lower. These figures demonstrate a declining rate of growth in Nigeria’s voter register: 22.04 per cent in 2015–2019, 11.27 per cent in 2019–2023, and 10.66 per cent in 2023–2026. The most recent period, however, covers three years rather than four. The critical issue, therefore, is not simply whether the voter register is growing, but who is entering the register, how voters are transitioning between age categories, and what these demographic changes mean. My proposal to INEC is to publish a detailed age-cohort analysis explaining changes between the 2015, 2019, 2023 and 2026 registers, including new registrations, age transitions, removal of dead and unqualified persons from the register and other adjustments. If the decline shows inadequate registration among newly eligible young voters, it must prompt increased investment in youth mobilization for voter registration. If it reflects administrative adjustments, those changes must be clearly documented and explained. Samson Itodo is the Executive Director of Yiaga Africa. The post Were Young People Removed From Nigeria’s Voter Register? appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Iran prepared for any scenario, will not succumb to threat
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 25 (MNA) – Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei has reiterated Iran’s resolve to defend itself against any aggression, saying that while the country keeps the door open to diplomacy, it is fully prepared to confront any US threat.
In an interview with German broadcaster ARD on Sunday, Baghaei said Iran has learned that Washington and its leadership cannot be trusted, as their strategy “is not diplomacy, but attacking the Islamic Republic.”
Responding to President Donald Trump’s rhetoric that the US will not attack Iran before the midterm elections, he emphasized that regardless of what the US president says or does not say, Iranians remain prepared, given American attacks even while diplomatic processes were underway.
He recalled a statement by Omani Foreign Minister Badr bin Hamad Al Busaidi that Iran and the US had made significant progress, yet Washington still chose to attack Iran—a reference to the American war amid talks with Oman acting as an intermediary. “The US has not shown the least bit of goodwill and will for a diplomatic approach,” Baghaei noted.
In response to a question regarding Europe’s approach toward Iran, Baghaei said it was regrettable to see the Europeans appeasing the United States rather than adopting an independent stance. The international community expects the European Union to act maturely in global politics, he added.
Consequently, the Europeans, instead of playing a constructive role regarding the nuclear issue, chose to side with the United States—despite knowing the illegality of the war launched against Iran, the US breach of the nuclear deal, JCPOA, in 2018, or following Washington in misusing the UN Security Council to re-impose sanctions.
Responding to developments around the Strait of Hormuz, the Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson said the strategic waterway “was not secure,” because the United States and Israel had exploited it to launch attacks on Iran—utilizing not only the Strait itself but also the territory and military infrastructure of several Persian Gulf states located on the opposite shore.
He emphasized that Iran has served as the guardian of this waterway for centuries but was compelled to take serious measures to safeguard its national security and territorial integrity—actions he said are lawful under international law.
Baghaei also referred to continued US intervention in the regional waters, saying CENTCOM—with the cooperation of certain regional states—has been pressuring vessels to use routes other than those specified by Iran, resulting in explosions and other incidents.
Stating that the Americans were exploiting the “southern route” to transport military equipment, he said any littoral state has the right to take necessary measures to prevent the aggressors from utilizing these waterways for military purposes.
Regarding Iran-Germany relations, Baghaei noted that Berlin must decide whether it wants to change its approach or simply appease the United States.
Germans once enjoyed a strong reputation in Iran, he said, but that standing has been tarnished since they failed to provide a convincing explanation as to why they provided the former Iraqi dictator Saddam Hussein with chemical agents when he attacked Iran in the 1980s.
Baghaei also said that Germany’s support for the US-Israeli war over the past two years, 2025 and 2026, and other anti-Iran measures have impacted the good relations Tehran and Berlin enjoyed in the past.

title: Ukraine war latest: Starshield operations restored to normal speed, Zelensky confirms as Elon Musk claims Ukraine violated Starlink terms
body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed that Starlink and Starshield, the militarized version of Elon Musk's satellite internet system, Starlink, was working at full speed as of the morning of Oct. 24, after it had previously been limited to 161 kilometers per hour (about 100 miles per hour).
"The speeds are now where they need to be," Zelensky said. "I thank all Americans and all our partners who took this seriously and truly helped us. I thank members of Congress , senators, all the media, the State Department, and the President."
Ukraine's Defense Ministry told reporters on Oct. 24 that Starshield was working above speeds of 400 kilometers per hour (about 248 miles per hour) again.
"We record a speed of more than 400 kilometers per hour, the connection is stable," the ministry said.
The ministry continues to monitor and record the work of Starlink and Starshield, according to Defense Minister Yevhen Khmara.
"This is another example of direct dialogue and the persistent position of the President of Ukraine at the highest level yielding results. And this result is, above all, important for our front, for the military, the work of drones, logistics, and communications," the ministry added.
Musk later said that Ukraine's military violated the terms of service for Starlink, adding that the "loophole" has now been closed.
Ukraine's "military violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people. That loophole was closed last week," he said in a post to X.
"Were Starlink to be turned off, the Ukrainian front line would collapse immediately. This is not a threat, it is simply a statement of fact," Musk said.
He also claimed that SpaceX has done more than any other company to help Ukraine in its fight against Russia's war.
Ukrainian activist and former Defense Ministry adviser Serhii Sternenko denied that Ukraine violated Starlink's terms of service.
"As someone who was inside the process at the Ministry of Defense, I can say with certainty that this is not true. In February of this year, whitelists were introduced. Stationary terminals could be registered by both military personnel and civilians," he said in a post to X.
"But for any satellite terminal to work while on the move, it had to be added to a special list and connected to the military Starshield system. Otherwise, no satellite communication terminals in Ukraine would work," Sternenko added.
Using Starlink for drone missions has been "technically impossible" since all drone campaigns that require satellite communications would only work with the military Starshield service, he said.
Presidential adviser Serhii "Flash" Beskrestnov also denied Musk's claims, saying that all Starlink terminals operating in Ukraine have a speed restriction of 70-90 kilometers an hour and do not work on Russian territory.
"Thus, we physically cannot use commercial Starlink for deep strikes and medium-range strikes," he said in a post to Facebook. "It is very strange that Elon Musk is not aware of Starlink restrictions in Ukraine."
Russian attacks killed eight people and injured 51 others across Ukraine over the past day, local authorities said on Oct. 24-25.
A Russian drone struck a five-story residential building in the city of Vinnytsia overnight on Oct. 25, injuring six people, one of whom was hospitalized, Nataliia Zabolotna , head of the Vinnytsia Oblast Military Administration, said.
The strike caused structural damage between the second and third floors, completely destroying four apartments and damaging nearby parked cars, Zabolotna added.
Alongside attacks on Vinnytsia, Russia launched 153 Shahed-type drones at Ukraine overnight on Oct. 25, including 92 jet-powered drones, as well as low-cost Banderol cruise missiles, the Ukrainian Air Force said.
Ukrainian air defenses intercepted 119 drones, including 64 jet-powered ones. As of 8 a.m., efforts to intercept the remaining drones were ongoing, with at least nine still in Ukrainian airspace.
Some drones evaded Ukrainian air defenses and struck 15 locations, while falling debris was recorded at nine other locations, according to the Air Force.
In Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, Russian attacks on the Synelnykove District on Oct. 24 killed three people and injured 14 others, including an 11-year-old girl, Governor Oleksandr Hanzha said. Five of the injured were hospitalized in serious condition.
In the Nikopol District , Russian attacks over the past day killed two women and injured five people, including a 14-year-old boy, Hanzha added.
In Kharkiv Oblast, Russian attacks killed a 45-year-old man in the town of Lozova and injured two other men, aged 43 and 26, Governor Oleh Syniehubov said.
In Kharkiv, a 39-year-old man was injured. Russian attacks also wounded three men, aged 70, 54, and 47, in the town of Derhachi, and a 45-year-old woman in the village of Mala Danylivka, Syniehubov added.
In Donetsk Oblast, Russian attacks killed one person in the village of Yarova and injured six others elsewhere in the region, Governor Vadym Filashkin said.
In Sumy Oblast, a 31-year-old woman was killed in a Russian attack on a farm in the Buryn community, which also injured an 18-year-old man. In the Boromlia community, a Russian drone struck a car, injuring three women aged 68, 56, and 36, according to local authorities .
Russian attacks injured four people in Zaporizhzhia Oblast over the past day. Russian forces carried out 832 strikes on 52 settlements across the region using drones, artillery, aircraft, and multiple-launch rocket systems (MLRS), local authorities said.
In Kherson Oblast, Russian attacks targeted 43 settlements, including the regional center of Kherson, injuring two people, Governor Oleksandr Prokudin said.
In Chernihiv Oblast, two women suffered acoustic trauma in a Russian strike on the regional capital, Chernihiv, on Oct. 24, Governor Viacheslav Chaus said.
One person was injured in a Russian drone attack on Kyiv on Oct. 24, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said.
The Kremlin is ready to resume trilateral talks with Ukraine and the U.S. after Nov. 4, when Russia celebrates National Unity Day, Russian President Vladimir Putin's foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov told state-controlled outlet Vesti on Oct. 25.
The statement follows Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky 's Oct. 23 remarks that a new round of trilateral talks is expected in the first half of November, with Abu Dhabi a possible venue.
"The next deadline is now Nov. 4, our major holiday. After that, we will be ready to resume negotiations," Ushakov said.
The Kremlin has repeatedly rejected ceasefire proposals, demanding instead that Kyiv cede the only partially occupied Donbas, a strategically important region in eastern Ukraine. Such a concession would give Moscow territory that Russian forces have been unable to capture on the battlefield. Ukraine, in contrast, has agreed to multiple ceasefire proposals put forward by the U.S.
Ushakov said he did not expect the first trilateral meeting after the pause to yield significant results, calling it a "trial run." A peace agreement between Russia and Ukraine "still needs work," he added.
On Oct. 20, U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and European partners, including Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store.
The following day, Witkoff held a three-hour meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg, after which the Kremlin said it was ready to resume trilateral talks in November.
Witkoff said on Oct. 21 that discussions among Ukrainian, U.S., and Russian representatives would "continue at the technical level."
Putin has long avoided meeting with Zelensky. Instead, the Kremlin chief is reportedly seeking a meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump in China next month in an effort to secure a favorable peace deal without Ukraine's participation .
In recent weeks, Trump has also lashed out at Zelensky, unilaterally announced an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine that ultimately failed, threatened to cut off intelligence-sharing with Kyiv, and eased sanctions on Russian oil exports.
Trump has defended the sanctions relief, arguing that it could encourage Moscow to take part in peace negotiations with Kyiv.
Russian attacks hit four Epicentr hypermarkets in less than 24 hours, the company said on Oct. 25.
The latest wave of strikes highlights Russia's campaign of terror against civilians, with stores, shopping centers, and other civilian infrastructure among the targets. Epicentr, one of Ukraine's largest home improvement and retail chains, has been particularly hard hit.
In a post on Facebook , the company said Russian attacks damaged or destroyed facilities in the cities of Zaporizhzhia, Kharkiv, Vinnytsia, and Poltava on Oct. 24-25, and described the attacks as amounting to "total destruction of the network."
The company did not specify the extent of the damage or when the affected facilities might reopen.
The Poltava Oblast Military Administration said a 52-year-old woman was injured in an attack on a hypermarket on Oct. 25. Authorities in other regions did not report any civilian casualties from attacks on Epicentr stores during the same period.
Founded in 2003, Epicentr operated 72 hypermarkets across Ukraine before Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022.
Since the start of the all-out war, ten of the company's shopping centers have been completely destroyed and another 13 have been damaged, Epicentr told the Ukrainian outlet Ekonomichna Pravda in August 2026.
Epicentr's head of public relations, Yuliia Chudnovets , said on Oct. 22 that Russian forces had struck five company sites, including one in Kyiv , in the previous 48 hours.
A massive swarm of Ukrainian drones attacked the Russian border region of Belgorod overnight on Oct. 25, according to local officials and eyewitness footage posted to social media.
The bulk of the drones have concentrated on one area in the Belgorod city center, locals report . According to the monitoring channel Exilenova-Plus, the target was the MegaGRINN shopping complex, Belgorod's largest retail and entertainment center.
MegaGRINN covers an area of more than 163,000 square meters and houses over 200 stores, as well as a supermarket, cinema, and restaurants. The facility was closed and empty of visitors during the overnight attack.
Local residents also reported a fire in the courtyard of a residential complex in the area.
The Belgorod Oblast Operational Headquarters confirmed a "massive UAV attack" against the city and said emergency services had been dispatched to the impacted areas, though they did not name any specific targets.
The attack killed one civilian and injured 14 others, authorities said. At least 30 apartment buildings, 35 vehicles, four houses, three administrative buildings, and eight commercial properties were damaged.
The Kyiv Independent could not verify these reports at the time of publication.
Videos published on social media by eyewitnesses show explosions, fires, and air defense operations over the city of Belgorod. The Operational Headquarters has warned residents to stay indoors as attacks are ongoing in the region.
The city of Belgorod lies just 34 kilometers (21 miles) from Ukraine's northeastern border with Russia and approximately 70 kilometers (43 miles) from Kharkiv. Its proximity to the front lines makes it a frequent target of Ukrainian attacks , even as Kyiv's expanding long-range capabilities allow its drones to penetrate deep in the Russian interior .
Previous Ukrainian strikes on Belgorod have targeted energy infrastructure and logistics warehouses , including facilities belonging to the Russian retail giant Ozon .
The reported drone blitz on Belgorod comes shortly after Ukraine confirmed on Oct. 24 that its Starshield system had been restored to full speed , allowing troops to more effectively coordinate drone strikes on Russian targets.
Starshield, the military application of the Starlink satellite internet system, had been operating at drastically reduced speed in Ukraine since Oct. 14. The unexplained restriction disrupted key military missions and Ukraine's ability to shoot down Russian jet-powered drones .

title: Britain's Renewable Energy Boom Is Hitting a Grid Bottleneck
body: The United Kingdom has invested heavily in expanding its renewable energy capacity in recent years to reduce its dependence on fossil fuels and support a green transition. However, one major problem stands in the way of it achieving this goal  its unprepared transmission infrastructure. Despite several new wind and solar projects coming online, the U.K. still relies heavily on natural gas due to grid inefficiencies that are delaying the shift to green energy.  The U.K. is spending up to 50 million a day to balance its power grid, as it's forced to regularly take wind farms offline due to nationwide transmission network bottlenecks. On 14th October, the grid operator reportedly spent 47.9 million to switch off wind farms in areas experiencing an oversupply of electricity. At the same time, it had to power up gas plants in other areas with a low electricity supply.  The U.K. spent 505 million in September alone on balancing power on the grid, the highest monthly cost recorded to date. The figure is expected to reach up to 3.2 billion over the next year as Great Britain continues to work through its 150 billion transmission infrastructure upgrades. These balancing costs ultimately shift to consumers, as they are levied on household energy bills. Despite big plans for a modernised grid, upgrades are not keeping pace with the deployment of new renewable energy capacity, which is occurring at a record pace.  In total, wind farms and hydropower with a total of 9 GW of capacity, enough to power around 8 million households, were paid not to produce power on 14th October, according to the consultancy LCP Delta. Meanwhile, the grid operator funded the operation of several gas and biomass plants and purchased additional electricity imports from Europe via high-voltage subsea power cables.  In early October, the National Energy System Operator Neso was forced to request "last resort" emergency assistance from France, which responded by sending last-minute power supplies to the U.K. Shivam Malhotra, the head of power trading at LCP Delta, explained, "The system overall wasn't tight in terms of power supplies It's the age-old story of a lack of infrastructure to transport power to where it's needed, leading to lots of windfarms being turned off."  It has long been common for the grid operator to pay wind farms in Scotland to go offline due to the lack of high-voltage cabling connecting them to high-demand areas in the south. There are currently only two cables moving power between Scotland and England, creating a "B6 boundary bottleneck". Costs associated with managing the bottleneck have averaged roughly 800,000 per day so far in the 2026-2027 period, which is around double the 2025-2026 average.  In addition, while Scotland uses just 8 per cent of the U.K.'s electricity on average, it produces roughly 19 per cent of total generation, contributing 37 per cent of its wind output, so the surplus generation must travel south to fulfil demand in England and Wales.  Meanwhile, during the summer months, Neso experienced major transmission infrastructure challenges as a high-pressure heat dome reduced renewable energy output and sent electricity demand to power air conditioning and refrigerators soaring. This led Neso to bring in independent investigators to explore whistleblower claims that its staff were involved in a cover-up of a near-blackout during record-high temperatures in late June.  The U.K. energy regulator Ofgem reported that the demand for new grid connections increased from 41 GW to 125 GW between November 2024 and June 2025 in line with the accelerated deployment of new renewable energy capacity. This has left several green energy projects stranded in the connection queue, even while the U.K.'s power demand continues to grow.  National Grid has submitted an additional package of proposals to Ofgem under the RIIO-T3 load re-opener process, to obtain approval for additional investment across its electricity transmission network to meet the country's growing power demand, unlock connections, and enable economic growth across England and Wales, the company announcedon 15th October.  The recent package includes 19 projects across England and Wales, representing about 4.5 billion of proposed investment. It forms part of National Grid's plans to invest approximately 31 billion on the grid in England and Wales between 2026 and 2031. The investments are expected to help "increase network capacity, maintain system resilience, and ensure the electricity network is ready to accommodate increasing levels of clean power generation and demand, including from new industries and technologies", according to National Grid.  The U.K. has big upgrade and expansion plans for its transmission infrastructure. However, the accelerated pace of renewable energy deployment is currently outpacing grid upgrades, leaving many companies waiting for their projects to be connected. This has led the U.K. to continue relying heavily on gas for power even as new wind, solar, and hydrogen projects are completed.  By Felicity Bradstock for Oilprice.com

title: Zelensky warns against lifting sanctions on Russia “just to have chat”
body:
The head of state made these remarks in an interview with TSN.Tyzhden , according to a Ukrinform correspondent.
“I would like to tell the Americans that I would not want us to approach the meeting of the three leaders (referring to the talks between the leaders of Ukraine, the U.S., and Russia—ed.) (…) having lifted all sanctions against the Russian Federation. This is an important point. Sanctions were imposed because of aggression, not for the sake of having a chat,” Zelensky emphasized.
He noted that when it comes to ending the war, “there is a specific procedure for lifting sanctions.”
The president stressed that restrictions on Russia were imposed precisely because of its aggression—the crossing of Ukrainian borders, the illegal occupation, and the killings—and that lifting sanctions before the war has actually ended is very dangerous.
“I have a feeling—and I’ve lived with it long enough—that when we talk about Russia’s loyalty, we shouldn’t buy it at such a price. In my view, if we remain without sanctions and within the trilateral format, we could end up in a situation where nothing is clear—what happens next? And the sanctions have already been lifted. Who will have the strength—the kind we had at the start of the war—to reimpose all of them, to rally people in such a way that there would be 20 or more sanctions packages around the world? That is why I approach this with great caution,” the Ukrainian president noted.
At the same time, he once again assured that he is ready to participate in a trilateral meeting of the leaders of Ukraine, the U.S., and Russia. Zelensky did not rule out that it could take place in Florida during the G20 summit.
As reported by Ukrinform, President Volodymyr Zelensky assured that he would attend the G20 summit in Florida if there were an opportunity to hold talks there with U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian dictator Vladimir Putin to reach peace agreements, but he has not yet received an invitation to the summit.

title: Asher Grunis steps down from leading Submarine Affair commission due to health concerns
body: Retired Supreme Court justice Asher Grunis will not continue in his post heading the Submarine Affair commission, the Courts Administration announced on Sunday.Supreme Court President Isaac Amit appointed retired Supreme Court justice Zvi Zylbertal to lead the commission on Sunday. Zylbertal was already one of the five members on it, so former Central District Court President Judge Ruth Lorch was appointed as a commission member.Grunis, 81, informed Amit on Friday that he will not be able to continue due to medical circumstances that will affect him in the coming months, preventing him from participating in the hearings, which are scheduled throughout the months of November and December.The commission was established in 2022 to examine how political and professional officials handled decisions concerning submarine and naval vessel purchases between 2009 and 2016. Its mandate also covers plans to privatize naval shipyards and Israel's consent to Germany selling submarines to a third country.In January, the commission published its report on systemic failures. This report examined flaws in decision-making and defense purchases – including the political leadership's failure to set clear policy. It also proposed changes.Netanyahu, Zamir due to testify in hearingsNow, the commission is due to begin hearing testimony on personal responsibility in the case on November 1. Grunis requested a replacement because postponing the hearings would harm the commission's work, the announcement said.The hearings will be behind closed doors and are set to focus on evidence relating to the personal warnings issued by the commission.The panel includes economist Prof. Karnit Flug, who previously served as the governor of the Bank of Israel, Gideon Frank, a former director-general of the Israel Atomic Energy Commission, and Prof. Jacob Bortman, a professor of mechanical engineering at the Faculty of Engineering Sciences at Ben-Gurion University of the Negev (BGU).Among those due to testify are Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, IDF chief of staff Lt.-Gen. Eyal Zamir, former president Reuven Rivlin, former defense minister Moshe “Bogi” Ya'alon, former Mossad chief Yossi Cohen, Navy commander V.-Adm. Eyal Harel, and former Navy commanders Eli Sharvit and Ram Rothberg.The proceedings center on warnings issued in June 2024 to Netanyahu, Ya'alon, Cohen, Rothberg, and former National Security Council official Avner Simhoni.The warnings notified them that the commission's eventual findings could adversely affect them, allowing them to examine evidence and challenge the preliminary conclusions before personal responsibility is determined.Being summoned as a witness does not mean an official received such a warning.The hearings allow those facing possible adverse findings to question witnesses and present evidence in their defense; the commission has emphasized that its conclusions could change after that process.Amit wished to “express deep appreciation” to Grunis “for his dedicated and professional work and important contribution” to the commission since its establishment.A government decision established the commission on January 23, 2022. Appointments were made later that year, on February 20.The commission of inquiry is separate from the criminal proceedings known as Case 3000. It examines decision-making and public responsibility surrounding the deals, while the criminal proceedings concern alleged corruption.

title: Israel Election 2026: What does Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar stand for?
body: Yashar, founded in September 2025, is one of many vying for citizens' votes in the elections for the 26th Knesset, which will be held on October 27.Led by Gadi Eisenkot, Yashar occupies the political center and currently leads the polls, making the former IDF chief of staff the top contender to lead the next government and replace Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.Eisenkot entered politics in August 2022 through Benny Gantz's National Unity alliance, which brought together Gantz's Blue and White and Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar's New Hope, taking third place on the list.Although Eisenkot initially ruled out serving under Netanyahu, he and Gantz joined the emergency government after the October 7 massacre. Gantz became a member of the war cabinet, while Eisenkot served as an observer. Both left the government in June 2024, accusing Netanyahu's leadership of failing to make the strategic decisions needed to achieve the war's objectives.In July 2025, Eisenkot left National Unity and resigned from the Knesset, citing the need for a transparent and democratic process for selecting the party's candidates. He said he wanted to build a broader leadership alternative capable of defeating the government, arguing that National Unity had failed to implement the internal reforms he sought. Two months later, he founded Yashar alongside former politicians, senior security figures, and other public figures, presenting it as a broad alternative focused on Israel's security, national interests, and democratic character.Yashar did not exist in the 25th Knesset, but the party has quickly risen through the ranks to become the leading party in the polls, which predict the party to win some 21-23 seats.Confronting Iran, Hamas, and Hezbollah while opposing Palestinian statehoodYashar places national security at the center of its platform, reflecting Eisenkot's background as a former IDF chief. The party's foreign policy focuses on confronting Iran, dismantling Hamas's rule in Gaza, containing Hezbollah in Lebanon, and determining the future of Palestinian governance and security arrangements.Yashar presents Iran as a continuing strategic threat. Eisenkot himself has favored a lasting, verifiable resolution of Iran's nuclear threat.If diplomacy fails, his proposals include US-enforced restrictions around remaining enriched-uranium sites and wider covert action against Iran's missile capabilities.On Gaza, the party's stated approach combines replacing Hamas with retaining an Israeli security corridor. Eisenkot would also allow reconstruction to advance incrementally alongside partial disarmament. Earlier in October, Eisenkot pledged to destroy Hamas's military wing and dismantle its leadership within 18 months.In Lebanon, Eisenkot supports a security zone while seeking stronger American and French involvement in efforts to confront Hezbollah.Regarding Palestinian statehood, Eisenkot has opposed establishing a Palestinian state, though he told The Jerusalem Post he would consider the Palestinian Authority preferable to continued Hamas rule if those are the alternatives.On settlements, he told the Post he would return Civil Administration responsibilities to military coordination and restore military coordination of policing in the West Bank.Eisenkot's goals: Ease cost of living, draft haredim, and reform Israel's economyYashar's domestic platform focuses on reforming military-service obligations, easing the cost of living, and directing economic support toward working Israelis, young people, and those who serve the country.Yashar's clearest established position is its opposition to blanket haredi (ultra-Orthodox) exemptions from military service. Eisenkot has proposed sanctions for evasion and benefits for those who serve, while allowing a limited Torah-study exemption for 3% of each annual haredi cohort. That allowance qualifies his universal-service message and has drawn criticism from opposition rivals demanding no exemptions.Yashar also proposes expanding service obligations and giving servicemen greater priority in civilian benefits. Its September youth plan proposed raising compulsory-service soldiers' pay by 15%, with a 50% increase for combat soldiers in their third year.The party's proposals place particular emphasis on those who contribute through military service and work.Economist and Yashar candidate Shaul Meridor placed the “working middle class, young people, and service people” at the center of its economic policy.Meridor outlined tax changes to reward those bearing the economic and security burden, together with priority in housing assistance and daycare subsidies. The reporting does not specify a full schedule of tax rates.On living costs and competition, the party has advocated challenging exclusive import arrangements and reducing barriers in concentrated markets such as groceries and cosmetics.The party's September youth plan also outlined renter protections, paid internships, and practical financial guidance.What a vote for this party is likely to produceA vote for Yashar is most likely a vote to strengthen Eisenkot's claim to the premiership and help build a coalition with former prime minister Naftali Bennett's B'Yachad, Avigdor Liberman's Yisrael Beytenu, and Yair Golan's Democrats.The four parties have agreed to coordinate campaigning and prepare principles for a future government, but have not settled how the bloc's candidate for prime minister would be selected.Eisenkot favors the leader of the largest party becoming the candidate for prime minister and has rejected a rotation arrangement. While that position still requires agreement from prospective partners, all four opposition leaders stressed in separate interviews during the election campaign that they would coalesce around an agreed-upon candidate following the election.In a September interview with the Post, Eisenkot laid out his conditions for coalition eligibility, including accepting Israel's Jewish and democratic identity, service obligations, and supporting the dismantling of Hamas.His parameters exclude Arab parties Ra'am and the Joint List, and likely the haredi (ultra-Orthodox) parties Shas and United Torah Judaism as viable partners.If the bloc falls short of 61 seats, it would need additional partners or support. Haredi parties accepting service reform represent a conditional opening in Eisenkot's position, although his allies' red lines could complicate it.For voters, Yashar offers a path toward replacing Netanyahu, but the election result will determine how far that path goes. Eisenkot must turn support for his leadership into a majority whose members agree on who should govern and what they are prepared to concede. The decisive test will be whether he can assemble those 61 seats while preserving the promises that brought voters to him.

title: Go Church Belgium documentary: What viewers were not told about two former Lighthouse bishops
body: Two former bishops have criticised Dag Heward-Mills. But their earlier statements, legal histories and a disputed multimillion-dollar settlement figure deserve attention too. Lawrence Odonkor and Emmanuel Oko Mensah, both former Lighthouse bishops, and Dag Heward-Mills, the church’s founder. The Belgian documentary investigating Go Church has raised serious allegations concerning Bishop Dag Heward-Mills and Lighthouse Chapel International. Those claims deserve examination. So does the background of the people making them. Emmanuel Oko Mensah and Lawrence Odonkor once held senior positions in Lighthouse. Both now criticise its leadership. Here are three pieces of context viewers should consider before reaching conclusions. 1. Oko Mensah: Two strikingly different accounts In the documentary, Emmanuel Oko Mensah is asked whether he was brainwashed during his years in the church. He answers: “Absolutely. One hundred per cent.” He also says the pressure works because God, the church, and the pastor merge into one entity. Yet at his own consecration, he publicly thanked Dag Heward-Mills for being a patient father and for giving him opportunities. He said: “Bishop has been so good to me.” He also thanked Dag Heward-Mills for giving a chance to people he described as flawed and unqualified, including himself. What changed between those two accounts? Earlier praise does not automatically disprove later criticism — and a man who says he was brainwashed would expect to have felt grateful at the time. But the public should hear both statements, in context, and ask what explains the difference. The same man, years apart. Left: at his consecration. Right: in the Belgian documentary. 2. Larry Odonkor: The legal record matters Lawrence “Larry” Odonkor alleges that problems within Lighthouse came from the top. His own legal history is also relevant background. He is also the source of the harshest language in the programme. He says that if the devil walks the earth in the form of a human being, that is Mills; that he uses his brilliance to do evil; and that it is not about God at all, but about fame and money. In April 2023, a court in Antananarivo, Madagascar, convicted him of breach of trust in proceedings concerning church funds and property. The judgment was delivered in his absence; it imposed a two-year prison sentence and 75 million Malagasy Ariary in damages. A December 2025 Ghana News Agency report said appeals had been dismissed in May 2024 and November 2025. Odonkor disputed the judgment. In a separate Ghanaian case, an Accra Circuit Court acquitted him in September 2023, finding dishonest appropriation had not been established. The Attorney-General subsequently challenged that decision on appeal. These are separate cases with different outcomes. Neither the Madagascar conviction nor the Ghanaian acquittal settles the truth of Odonkor’s allegations about Dag Heward-Mills. Readers should be given the full legal context. 3. The $12 million settlement controversy In 2021, reports emerged about a $12 million figure discussed in a dispute involving six former Lighthouse pastors, including Oko Mensah and Odonkor. Lighthouse’s lawyers alleged the former pastors had demanded that amount. Their lawyer denied making a formal demand; a mediator said the figure arose during settlement discussions as a possible calculation, not a formal demand. That distinction matters. It would be inaccurate to state as an established fact that the men demanded $12 million or that money explains their later criticism. What is clear from the reporting is that a significant financial dispute formed part of the wider history. Separately, a 2021 SSNIT determination was reported as largely supporting Lighthouse’s position on pension contributions, with one month’s contribution outstanding for Oko Mensah. That finding, and the former pastors’ objections, should be considered together. A settlement letter of 16 December 2022 set the claim out person by person, under four headings, with a sub-total for each man and then a second figure four times larger. Name Years Underpayment Compensation Severance and resettlement Sub-total Luke 19:8 total Faith Makafui Fiakojo 6 25,200 3,400 125,000 178,800 715,200 Edem Amankwah 9 39,600 195,100 181,000 455,300 1,821,200 Seth Duncan 10 62,400 7,100 271,000 402,900 1,611,600 Edward Laryea 12 58,800 79,216 287,400 484,216 1,936,864 Emmanuel Oko-Mensah 17 — 25,630 519,750 545,380 2,181,520 Lawrence Odonkor 19 14,400 385,400 579,600 993,800 3,975,200 TOTAL 3,060,396 12,241,584 All figures in US dollars, payable in cedis. Pension contributions are not costed, only marked for update. Fees are stated as ten per cent of whatever is paid. The itemised claim — underpayment, compensation, severance and resettlement — comes to about $3.06 million. The $12.24 million appears only in the final column, after a fourfold multiplier drawn from Luke 19:8, in which Zacchaeus the tax collector offers to restore fourfold anything he has taken. Every line is exactly four times its own sub-total. The largest single claim is Lawrence Odonkor’s, at nearly $4 million — almost twice the next man’s, and roughly a third of the whole figure. What about Dag Heward-Mills and Go Church? Go Church Belgium has publicly disputed allegations about its practices and has said donations are voluntary. Its responses deserve to be examined alongside the documentary’s claims, rather than left out of the conversation. When relationships break down, memories and interpretations can change. But a falling-out does not erase genuine kindness, just as earlier gratitude does not rule out later grievances. That is why the recordings, court decisions, financial dispute and the church’s response should all be available to readers. Watch the videos. Read the records. Hear the response. Then decide for yourself.

title: Show HN: Security Headers Checker
body:
Check the Content-Security-Policy and security headers of any page.
They are HTTP response headers that tell the browser what a page may do: where scripts can load from, whether other sites can put it in a frame, and whether to always use HTTPS. They protect visitors from attacks like cross-site scripting and clickjacking.
Start with default-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none' and add the hosts your page loads from. Send it as Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only first, check the browser console for blocked requests, then switch to Content-Security-Policy .
It lets every inline script run, including one an attacker injects. Give the inline scripts you need a nonce or a hash instead. When a nonce or a hash is in script-src , browsers ignore 'unsafe-inline' .
Most of it does. Browsers ignore frame-ancestors , report-uri and sandbox in a meta tag, so send those in the header.
No. The page is fetched when you press Check, and nothing is stored.
The page at the link is fetched from our server, once at its address and once over http:// to see if it redirects to HTTPS. The checks read the response headers and any Content-Security-Policy in a <meta> tag. When both are set, the browser applies both, so the checks read them together.
The checks cover the headers most sites need. A page can pass all of them and still have other security problems.
Company of Craft also builds stateofpixel , which catches UI regressions before they merge.

title: Houthis say they attacked Riyadh Airport and military bases
body:
DOHA, October 25. ./TASS/. The Houthis from the Yemeni rebel movement Ansar Allah say they have struck Riyadh International Airport and military bases in Khamis Mushait and Jizan with ballistic missiles.
"The Yemeni armed forces (Houthi units - TASS) <…> conducted three military operations with the use of dozens of ballistic missiles," Houthi spokesman Yahya Saria wrote on Telegram.
According to the Houthi spokesman, the attacks targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, the Khamis Mushait airbase in southern Saudi Arabia, and the naval base in Jizan.
He once again warned international air carriers and passengers against flying to Riyadh’s airport.

title: 2027: NDC slams Tinubu, APC over ₦1bn worth of Prado SUVs for youth leaders
body: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has criticised the All Progressives Congress (APC) after its National Youth Leader, Dayo Israel, announced the distribution of brand-new 2026 Toyota Prado SUVs to selected youth leaders for election mobilisation. The NDC said the seven vehicles shown in a video posted by Israel were worth about ₦1.015bn, accusing the ruling party of spending taxpayers’ money on the lavish lifestyles of politicians while Nigerians grapple with economic hardship. The average cost of a brand-new 2026 Toyota Prado is ₦145,000,000. In this video, we counted seven such vehicles, and the number could be even higher. The total cost of these seven vehicles alone amounts to ₦1,015,000,000. While the rudderless, clueless, and ruinous… https://t.co/QYeB7UU21y — Nigeria Democratic Congress (@NigeriaNDCHQ) October 25, 2026 In a post on X reacting to Israel’s video, the opposition party said the estimated cost of the vehicles reflected what it described as wasteful spending by the President Bola Tinubu-led administration. “The average cost of a brand-new 2026 Toyota Prado is ₦145,000,000. In this video, we counted seven such vehicles, and the number could be even higher,” the NDC said. “The total cost of these seven vehicles alone amounts to ₦1,015,000,000.” The party criticised the government’s economic policies, saying Nigerians had been asked to endure hardship while political leaders continued to enjoy expensive benefits. “While the rudderless, clueless, and ruinous administration of President Bola Tinubu has been asking Nigerians to endure the pains of its wicked and cruel reforms, this is how taxpayers’ money is being spent,” it said. “The wasteful APC-led administration is funding the lavish lifestyles of politicians while ordinary Nigerians wallow in poverty.” The NDC called on Nigerians to vote the ruling party out in the 2027 general election, describing opposition to the administration as a civic responsibility. “We cannot continue like this. We owe Nigerians and the unborn generation the civic duty to vote the ruinous administration of President Bola Tinubu out of power,” the party said. It also used the controversy to promote its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, pledging that his administration would reduce the cost of governance. “Our presidential candidate is strongly committed to cutting the cost of governance,” the NDC said, urging voters to support Obi for what it described as “a new and working Nigeria for all, and not for a corrupt few”. Israel had earlier posted a video showing the vehicles, saying they were presented to selected youth leaders to support their election mobilisation activities. “Today, I presented brand new 2026 Prado to my committed selected youth leaders to aid their election mobilisation activities,” he wrote. He also thanked First Lady Oluremi Tinubu for her support for the party’s structure under his leadership. “I am grateful to my Mummy, H.E Mrs Oluremi Tinubu for her continuous support to the party structure under my leadership,” Israel said. He added that the APC would focus on grassroots mobilisation ahead of the election, saying the party would “deliver polling unit by polling unit”. The NDC’s valuation is based on its estimate of the vehicles’ average price and its count of seven SUVs in the video. title: Flights resume at Riyadh airport as Houthis attack Saudi Arabia
body: Flights resumed at Riyadh’s international airport on Sunday following a series of deadly attacks on the facility that saw it closed for two weeks, even as Yemen’s Houthis targeted the country with strikes. King Khalid International Airport’s website showed several domestic and international flights scheduled on Sunday, including arrivals to the kingdom from Dubai, Paris and Cairo. The renewed operations at the airport came as explosions rattled Riyadh early Sunday, after a text message was sent to residents warning of a hostile threat targeting the city. The airport closure was a major blow for Saudi Arabia, with the kingdom’s flagship investment conference postponed until 2027 as residents scrambled to find alternatives to enter and exit the country. The prestigious motor sport race, the Dakar Rally, also added its name to a long list of events to be cancelled, postponed or relocated amid the fallout from the war. Saudi officials did not provide additional information when asked by AFP about the scope of the renewed operations at the airport. But the tracking website Flightradar24 showed a small number of flights had departed, though the vast majority were cancelled. The Houthis have carried out waves of strikes on the airport, including an attack this month that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree earlier warned that Riyadh airport was still “unsafe” and a “military target”. “The Yemeni Armed Forces warn all international, regional and local airlines — as well as staff and travellers — against using King Khalid Airport in Riyadh, as it is unsafe and serves as a military target for our forces,” he said. “The Saudi regime shall bear the consequences of any operations at the airport.” – ‘Everything is shaking’ – Later on Sunday, Saree said Saudi Arabia had struck Yemen dozens of times over the previous 24 hours. “During the past 24 hours, Saudi warplanes launched 56 airstrikes and missiles targeting civilian objects in the governorates of Hajjah, Lahj, Amran, Saada, Al-Jawf, Taiz and Ibb using F-15 and “Typhoon” planes that took off from the bases of Khamis Mushait and Taif, and missiles from Najran,” he said on X. As operations at the airport restarted, Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis arrived in Riyadh and met with Saudi de facto ruler Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. During the meeting, Mitsotakis “responded favourably to the kingdom’s request to keep the Patriot system in Saudi Arabia, given the current challenging circumstances”, his office said. Greece has deployed a battery to operate the US-made Patriot air defence system in Yanbu, a major oil export hub on the Red Sea coast. The SPA news agency added that the two leaders “underscored the critical importance of safeguarding the security and integrity of international maritime corridors and ensuring the safe and continuous flow of energy supplies to global markets”. Earlier, the Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis said it intercepted at least 10 ballistic missiles. The fighting erupted after a years-long truce between the Houthis and Yemen’s Riyadh-backed government fell apart. “The bombardment has been very heavy since this morning — may God keep us safe. Everything is shaking because of the explosions,” one resident in Khamis Mushait told AFP on Sunday on condition of anonymity. The kingdom’s civil defence agency later said two people were injured in the south by falling debris, also reporting damage to several buildings and vehicles. Images released by the official Saudi Press Agency showed a building with part of its upper facade destroyed, exposing metal rods. Another image captured large windows shattered, with shards of glass strewn across the pavement and part of the road. – Attack warning – AFP journalists in Riyadh heard three explosions in the early hours of Sunday, with residents receiving alert messages for a “hostile aerial threat” and urging them to stay in a safe place. The warning came as the Saudi-led coalition said it had downed a ballistic missile launched by the group towards the capital, as well as two drones in the Riyadh area. “Air defences intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward Riyadh,” the coalition posted on X. Later Sunday morning, the coalition said its forces intercepted a cruise missile fired by the Houthis at the kingdom’s southern city of Khamis Mushait. Attacks appeared to target areas across the south, with warnings also issued for Abha city along with areas in Taif, Namas and Jazan. The attacks came after the Houthis said they targeted three Saudi airports, including in Riyadh, energy installations, a pipeline and an air base within 24 hours. Vanguard News The post Flights resume at Riyadh airport as Houthis attack Saudi Arabia appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: 2027 Elections: Lagos APC Gov Candidate, Hamzat To Unveil Manifesto On Friday
body: The All Progressives Congress (APC) 2027 governorship candidate and Deputy Governor of Lagos State, Kadri Hamzat, will officially unveil his manifesto on Friday, October 30, 2026. ​The Director-General of the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Kadri Obafemi Hamzat (PBAT-KOH) Campaign Council, Senator Musiliu Obanikoro, announced this at a press conference at the PBAT-KOH Campaign Office in Ikeja. ​Obanikoro stated that the high-profile event will take place at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts (formerly known as the National Arts Theatre) in Iganmu, Lagos. ​According to the campaign council, the launch will run from 3 p.m. to 5 p.m., with guest arrivals starting at 11 a.m. Due to venue seating capacity, the physical event is strictly by invitation, but will be broadcast live across major television and digital platforms, including Channels TV. Senator ​Obanikoro said the campaign is built on two core principles: continued shared progress and inclusivity. He stressed that building a stronger Lagos requires preserving the master plan initiated in 1999 under Bola Tinubu and successfully expanded by successive administrations of Babatunde Fashola, Akinwunmi Ambode, and the incumbent Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu. ​”Continuity is not about doing things the same way simply because they have been done before. “It is about protecting what works, correcting what needs improvement, and building on existing progress,” Obanikoro stated. ​He also underscored that inclusivity remains a priority to ensure that no Lagos resident is left behind regardless of religion, tribe, gender, or social status. ​The campaign DG drew attention to the rich private and public sector background of the governorship candidate, Kadri Hamzat (popularly known as KOH). He noted that Hamzat earned a PhD in Systems Process Engineering from Cranfield University, England, at age 28, and worked with global financial institutions such as Merrill Lynch, Morgan Stanley, and Citibank before serving Lagos State as a three-time commissioner and deputy governor. ​The campaign council revealed that extensive consultations have already been conducted with traditional rulers, religious leaders, market traders, youth groups, professionals, and artisans across the state. ​”Following Friday’s launch, digital copies of the manifesto will be made available for public download,” he added. The campaign DG encouraged residents to study the document and submit constructive feedback and suggestions through official party channels to ensure grassroots participation in the state’s future development.
