title: UAE officials reject Iran's criticism of UN candidate Nusseibeh
body: Senior UAE officials have responded strongly to Iran’s criticism of Emirati diplomat Lana Nusseibeh 's campaign to become secretary general of the UN. Ms Nusseibeh joined the race for the UN 's top job last Wednesday after no clear front-runner emerged among eight other candidates. Her campaign has gathered support from a wider range of countries. Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf, who is also the country's top negotiator in talks with the US, on Sunday questioned Ms Nusseibeh's agenda in a post on X. Ms Nusseibeh on Monday responded to Mr Ghalibaf's remarks, saying she would pursue dialogue with Iran if selected for the top UN position. “I commit to engaging with Iran, like all member states, to advance peace and stability,” she said in an interview with Bloomberg . Dr Anwar Gargash, diplomatic adviser to President Sheikh Mohamed, said discussion of Ms Nusseibeh's agenda was welcome but that Mr Ghalibaf's remarks “lack objectivity”. He said they also “overlook the fact that the United Nations was established to promote dialogue and resolve conflicts, not to entrench enmities and settle scores”. Dr Gargash described Ms Nusseibeh as a professional figure known for bridging differences and prioritising diplomacy, and said this would naturally “provoke objections from some hardline voices”. Dr Ali Al Nuaimi, chairman of the defence, interior and foreign affairs committee of the Federal National Council, accused Mr Ghalibaf of trying to lecture the UAE despite Iran's record of “exporting instability”. “Lana Nusseibeh represents diplomacy, competence and the courage to build bridges. Your rhetoric represents the very destructive mentality that has brought so much suffering to our region,” Dr Al Nuaimi said in response. “The Middle East deserves a future shaped by those who build peace, not those who thrive on conflict.” UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres's second and final term will finish at the end of the year. Members of the Security Council have held several informal votes on a successor but no consensus has yet emerged. Ms Nusseibeh has called for generational change and pledged to reform the UN with “clearer priorities” if she is elected. She would be the first woman to lead the UN and the second Arab after Egypt's Boutros Boutros-Ghali. Appointed the UAE's ambassador to the UN in 2013, she previously held several positions in Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

title: Zelensky: Public outcry helped restore Starlink speeds to required levels
body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said this in an interview with “TSN Tyzhden” host Alla Mazur, according to Ukrinform.
“I think it was precisely that (the media attention—ed.) that helped. It’s not as if that was the main strategy behind our work with partners. We’re open and straightforward, but it worked. For now, anyway. We’ll see how things go from here, because we’re seeing different developments every day, and there may be various challenges during the U.S. elections. Nevertheless, for now, this is a positive development, and we need it very much,” Zelensky said.
He added that the issues of resuming Starlink operations in Ukraine and exchanging intelligence with the U.S. were resolved following a meeting in Oslo on October 20 between delegations from Ukraine, the United States, and European allies.
“We’ve achieved the right result. We came away with what we needed. And today (the interview took place on Saturday, October 24—Ed.), the military personnel were congratulating one another that it’s back. This was one aspect of our discussions in Oslo—the emotional nature of our dialogue, which was accompanied by three challenges: a shortage of air defense systems, restrictions on Starlink, and restrictions on intelligence data from the United States of America. “And so today I can confirm—and I am grateful to the Americans and our team—that two issues—regarding intelligence and Starlink—have now been resolved,” Zelensky said.
He noted that as of 5:20 a.m. on Saturday, October 24, Starlink’s speed was 420 km/h following the restrictions. Additionally, he said, intelligence data regarding Russian ballistic strikes on Ukraine is being exchanged.
“We still have the issue of air defense. That’s one part of our discussions,” Zelensky said.
As previously reported, in mid-October, the operation of the Starlink system in Ukraine was limited to a speed of 161 km/h, which made it impossible to use it on interceptors against “Shahed” drones.

title: Summit Calls for Women’s Inclusion in Water Policy Decisions
body: Policy advocates and cultural leaders have called for greater representation of women in water governance and budgetary decisions in Nigeria. They urged institutions to move beyond token participation to give women meaningful decision-making power. The call was made at the UNFPA Office in Copenhagen during a multimedia exhibition titled ‘Stories of a Broken Water Cycle’, organised by the Lokoja Dialogues Climate Initiative. Featuring creative expressions, panel sessions and community perspectives from regions including Argungu, the exhibition highlighted how failing water infrastructure disproportionately affects women’s health, privacy, menstrual hygiene and economic mobility. The summit was attended by prominent figures, including the Head of the UN Women Nordic Liaison Office, Sarah Brun; UNFPA Nordic Representative, Ulla E. Muller; Nigeria’s Ambassador to Denmark, Sweden and Finland, Lola Akande; Polly Alakija and Adwoa Edun, both co-founders of Lokoja Dialogues Climate. Speaking during a panel session on gender and governance, advocate Patricia Emmanuel said women must be included in decisions on water management. “We cannot fix the broken water cycle with half the population excluded from the solution. We must move women from water carriers to water governance,” she said. Panellists criticised development models that treat women as passive participants in consultative workshops rather than as leaders capable of managing resources and influencing budget allocations. “When we talk about inclusion, women are often just invited to participate in a roundtable, conference, or workshop, and at the end, it stops there,” speaker Flora Asieri said, calling for institutional reforms beyond superficial representation. Sarah Brun of UN Women also stressed the connection between visibility, political influence and budgetary allocations. “What remains invisible remains unfunded. The real question for us here is whether our institutions are prepared to listen to them, but also to share our power,” Brun said. In her opening remarks, Polly Alakija, Trustee and CEO of Lokoja Dialogues, observed that equitable access to water in Nigeria had worsened over the past 37 years since she first arrived in the country. She emphasised that women’s daily experiences of water insecurity should directly inform government spending and utility management. By bringing community perspectives into discussions with policymakers, the Copenhagen exhibition seeks to promote women’s participation in shaping water policies and improving national water security. https://meet.google.com/call?authuser=0&hl=en&mc=KAIwAZoBFDoScGludG9fd3ZqbmpjZ3J5aWs3ogE3MgJQADoCEAFKBAgBEAFaAggAagIIAXICCAF6AggCiAEBkgECEAGaAQQYASAAogECEADiAQIIALIBBxgDIAAqATDCAQIgAdgBAQ&origin=https%3A%2F%2Fmail.google.com&iilm=1792886734336

title: Burning tires, halted traffic: Druze protesters block Route 6 days after Tel Aviv club attack
body: A Druze protest broke out in northern Israel on Sunday, during which Route 6 was blocked to southbound traffic near the Elyakim Interchange.Protesters blocked the highway and set tires on fire, Israel Police said, causing heavy traffic in the area. Officers from the Northern District and the Traffic Division were dispatched to the scene and reopened the road.The protest comes in response to an attack on three young Druze men at a club in Tel Aviv overnight between Thursday and Friday, after they were heard speaking Arabic among themselves.According to eyewitness accounts, the attackers shouted, "We don't want Arabs here," before assaulting them. One of the young men, who is due to enlist in the IDF soon, was stabbed during the incident while attempting to shield his two friends, both active-duty soldiers, with his body.The young man who was stabbed sustained injuries to his back, arm, and face and was evacuated to a hospital, where he was admitted in moderate condition.Police said officers at the scene of the protest were directing traffic and working to maintain public order. Police also emphasized that they would allow freedom of expression and protest within the bounds of the law but would not permit actions that endanger public safety or disrupt public order.Druze, Arab inseparable part of Israeli societyEarlier on Sunday, Democrats party chairman Yair Golan condemned the incident in a post to X/Twitter, after visiting one of the injured young men. "It's hard to stand in front of a person who was harmed solely because of the language he spoke," wrote Golan. "The Druze and Arabs are an inseparable part of Israeli society, and anyone who attacks them is attacking the values that our country must uphold.""This violence is fueled by incitement, racism, and a government that legitimizes them," he said, accusing National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich of spreading hate."When hatred comes from the government, from Ben-Gvir and Smotrich, racist ministers, it seeps straight into the streets.""I promised A. [the injured young man] that his safety would be one of the first and most important tasks for us Democrats in government. We will restore security to the streets, fight racism without blinking, and build a society here that ensures true equality."Yisrael Beytenu leader Avigdor Liberman also condemned the incident on X, calling on Israel Police to properly investigate the incident and apprehend attackers "to the fullest extent of the law with utmost severity."

title: Over 200 US rabbis demand US Senate candidate El-Sayed make Jewish safety commitments
body: More than 220 liberal and progressive rabbis from 34 states signed an open letter to Democratic US Senate nominee Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, endorsing the campaign demands of Nonnegotiable Michigan.This initiative was launched in September by rabbis, cantors, and lay leaders representing congregations serving an estimated 40,000 Jewish Michiganders.The signatories allege that a disconnect exists between El-Sayed's public assurances regarding Jewish safety and rhetoric that they argue undermines it.The letter was released on Friday ahead of a Saturday Get Out the Vote rally at Cass Technical High School in Detroit, where former president Barack Obama made his first public campaign appearance alongside El-Sayed.Addressing thousands of rally attendees, Obama praised El-Sayed's candidacy, compared the Senate nominee's political path to his own, and urged voters to back Democratic candidates as a crucial check on the Trump administration.However, Obama avoided mention of the ongoing primary disputes over Jewish inclusion and foreign policy.Throwing their support behind Nonnegotiable Michigan, the new signatories called on El-Sayed to align his campaign with Obama's legacy of Jewish inclusion within the Democratic Party and requested that Obama reaffirm that Zionist Jews remain full members of the political coalition.Disconnect between Obama, El-Sayed's inclusion of Jewish voters in Democratic Party The letter points to what the rabbis describe as a contrast between Obama's political record and El-Sayed's campaign statements.While Obama “welcomed Zionist Jews as full partners in his coalition, and never asked [them] to leave [their] love of Israel at the door,” the rabbis claimed that El-Sayed has repeatedly dismissed concerns raised by Jewish voters.Further, they said that El-Sayed has been using language that they allege echoes antisemitic stereotypes.“You have described your campaign as picking up the baton [Obama] carried,” the rabbis wrote. “We urge you to honor the part of his legacy that made Jewish Americans feel safe in our communities and at home in the Democratic Party.”The signatories stated that while El-Sayed has expressed a commitment to Jewish safety when speaking to Jewish audiences, his broader public rhetoric presents a different narrative.“Asked about our safety here at home, you offer warm words about Jews and Judaism, but immediately pivot to Israel and foreign wars,” the signatories wrote. “Where [US] President [Donald] Trump blames immigrants for our country's woes, your rhetoric casts Israel and American supporters of Israel, which includes most of mainstream Jewry, as the source of our neighbors' pain.”Specific concerns raised by the rabbis cited past instances where they allege El-Sayed called Israelis “bloodthirsty,” characterized American financial and diplomatic support for Israel as “legalized bribery” and “purchased loyalty,” and described a Jewish state as inherently illiberal.They also say he told a national audience that Israel uses American funds to push the US into foreign wars. “When El-Sayed's words reach a national audience, Jews across America feel the consequences – in our inboxes, on our campuses and, even, painfully, within our sanctuaries,” the letter stated.National impact of El-Sayed's platform Addressing the national scope of the Senate race, the signatories argued that El-Sayed's platform extends beyond local Michigan politics.“Until now, this has been a conversation between you and Michigan's Jewish community,” the letter noted. “But you are asking to serve in the United States Senate. There, the laws you write, the votes you cast, and the words you speak would shape the safety and belonging of Jews throughout America. A senator from Michigan legislates for all of us.”The letter even urged Obama directly to use his platform during Saturday's Detroit rally to address the coalition.“Please use your voice in Detroit to remind the coalition you built that Jews belong in it fully, safely, and proudly,” the rabbis wrote. “That includes the many of us deeply and inextricably connected to Israel.”The open letter follows a renewed appeal issued Wednesday by Nonnegotiable Michigan, which said it documented six weeks of unanswered requests for dialogue with El-Sayed before expanding its campaign to include elected officials, Democratic leaders, and college students.In the letter, the signatories endorsed five core commitments and urged El-Sayed to adopt them publicly.The five fundamental points are: Affirming that Jewish safety is nonnegotiable; supporting Jewish statehood and self-determination in Israel; asserting that Jews alone define Jewish identity; ensuring Zionist Jews are welcomed in the Democratic Party; and pursuing Palestinian aspirations for safety, dignity, and freedom alongside Israel rather than in place of it.“When you stand beside president Obama in Detroit, say these five things publicly, in your own words,” the rabbis wrote.“Then, demonstrate through your words and actions that you mean them. Jewish safety cannot be something you invoke when speaking to Jews, but undermine when speaking to everyone else.”Neither El-Sayed nor Obama responded to The Jerusalem Post's request for comment by the time of publication.

title: Summit Therapeutics reports survival benefit for cancer drug in trial
body: Summit Therapeutics ( SMMT ) on Sunday said its experimental cancer drug ivonescimab helped patients with advanced biliary tract cancer live significantly longer than those receiving an established immunotherapy treatment, according to results from a late-stage clinical trial conducted in China.

title: IDF seriously injures, fails to detain Palestinian accused of attempted ramming attack - report
body: The IDF seriously wounded a Palestinian man for allegedly attempting to run over soldiers near Hebron, but failed to detain him afterward, Army Radio reported on Sunday afternoon. According to Army Radio, the incident occured on Friday near Kafr Dura, shortly after the fatal Hebron attack that killed Staff Sergeant Ron Yonatan Roytman and Sergeant Yuval Shai Svilem. Three others were lightly wounded in the attack.Two terrorists were killed during the confrontation, and the IDF said no additional terrorists were involved.Army Radio reported that while it reached out to the IDF for clarification on the matter on Friday, the military only responded on Sunday, saying that soldiers operating in the area "spotted a vehicle driving suspiciously and accelerated toward them, and in response, opened fire."Despite claiming the man tried to run over soldiers, Army Radio reported that the IDF did not detain the man for questioning over the incident.The IDF told Army Radio that it was reviewing the matter, but allegedly did not answer additional questions about its failure to detain the Palestinian.IDF, Shin Bet forcibly evacuate Hebron Palestinians in response to Friday attackSince the Friday attack, Israeli security forces have forcibly evacuated some 2,000 Hebron-area Palestinians and destroyed an unspecified number of structures in the vicinity.In a Friday night statement, the IDF said that it had launched a counterterrorism operation in the Hebron area following Friday morning's deadly Hamas terrorist attack. Security forces are conducting systematic searches for terrorist infrastructure and weapons in the area and questioning dozens of suspects, according to the joint statement.The operation follows a series of counterterrorism measures carried out since Friday morning, including mapping the terrorists' homes, sealing off the Hebron and Halhul areas, establishing roadblocks, and conducting operations in nearby villages. Security forces are also removing illegal infrastructure that could pose a security threat near the site of the attack.Evacuated Palestinians connected to Hamas-linked Gaza clan, IDF saysHowever, the IDF provided little information about the offenses of the 2,000 evacuated Palestinians, other than to say that they were familially connected to the Hamas-linked Gaza clan.It also said it destroyed illegally built structures that could make security operations harder to carry out. However, the military was extremely vague about what those operations were and why entire buildings needed to be destroyed to carry them out.Pressed about how many of the 2,000 hamula (“clan”) members have records linking them to terror (or at a minimum, to rock throwing), multiple IDF sources did not appear to have any specific information on the topic.Rather, the operation seemed to be motivated by public statements made by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz about clearing or destroying the neighborhood of the two men involved in the terror incident on Friday – apparently a collective punishment measure.Yonah Jeremy Bob and Richard Offenbacher contributed to this report.

title: Australian defense land selloff runs into multiparty opposition
body: SYDNEY — Former Prime Minister John Howard urged the Australian government to reverse its plans to sell defense land in prime locations at a rally Sunday characterized by multipartisan bonhomie on-stage — and angry calls for Prime Minister Anthony Albanese to resign off stage. Howard told a crowd of a few thousand gathered in Sydney near the site of its Victoria Barracks that he would be the first to congratulate Albanese if he changed course on the land selloff. Also present at the rally were members of the nationalist One Nation party. Orange shirt-clad members of the far-right party and others wearing blue Make Albo Go Away (MAGA) hats called instead for Albanese to resign or be sacked. Decades of local opposition to higher density, often characterized by not-in-my-backyard politics, has left Sydney with one of the most expensive housing markets in the world. Most mainstream political parties have responded, now declaring themselves "YIMBY." The defense land selloff is one exception to this pendulum reversal, uniting groups across the political spectrum. Few things unite Australia like its Australia and New Zealand Army Corps legend, the belief that the values embodied by its armed forces, such as mateship, are central to its national character. So the decision by the Albanese government to sell Department of Defense assets around the country, including prime harbor-front properties in Sydney, to raise 3 billion Australian dollars (in gross terms), or 1.8 billion (net), may seem like a strange one. With calls to reduce the deficit and the need to find land for housing in Australia’s sprawling cities, the government thought it was on firm footing disposing of properties it says are surplus to requirements. Deputy Prime Minister Richard Marles has argued his Department of Defense is not best placed to preserve the heritage value of the sites, and that money for their upkeep would be better spent on future fighting capability. The selloff proposal has met fierce resistance across parties: from the conservative Liberal-National Coalition, the traditional opposition in Australia; right-wing nationalist One Nation; the left-wing Greens; and even members of Albanese’s own party, his Labor colleagues in the NSW state government. The Albanese government has been urged by its opponents to spend less to lower inflation and prevent the need for further interest rate hikes. But many savings measures have been blocked: from its attempts to make the private health insurance rebate and veterans’ allied health entitlements less generous, to charging residents of aged care more for services. Howard, a conservative Liberal, told the crowd he is “all in favor of governments spending less and taxing less” but that was not the issue at hand. “What is more important to the soul of a nation? [Than] its history, its heritage, and those that have gone before,” he said. “You don’t give that up for a few bob.” Howard’s speech veered from his memories of seeing Australian cricket legend Don Bradman bat at the nearby Sydney Cricket Ground, to Victoria Barracks’ history as the departure point for soldiers bound for the 1885 Sudan War, to his description of the 28-degree Celsius day — 4.3 degrees above the historical late-October average — as “seasonably warm.” Tony Abbott, another former Prime Minister and now the Liberal Party president tasked with combating the rise of One Nation, said it was “wonderful” to gather with Australians who respect its history and heritage. “And isn’t it wonderful to be at this protest, where the only flag on display is the Australian flag — and not the Palestinian one.” Labor’s NSW parliamentary secretary for transport, Marjorie O’Neill, one of the protest organizers, was jeered by the One Nation-heavy crowd: first, for beginning the rally with an acknowledgment of country for Australia’s First Nations people and for 150 Aboriginal men who had signed up to serve the defense forces at Victoria Barracks; and then again for omitting mention of One Nation as she credited the multilateral coalition of Labor, Liberal and Greens against the sale. Liberal senator Jess Collins, her co-organizer, added “I will acknowledge that we do have One Nation here too” — to loud cheers. Independent MP Allegra Spender urged the crowd to join a convoy to Canberra being organized for Nov. 23 to protest the sale. One Nation members approached ahead of the rally declined to comment, due to party rules forbidding speaking to the media. Justin Bowra, a member of the Greens and local resident, told POLITICO that “despite all the political colours, whether you’re orange, blue, red or green, we all agree on one thing: The wrong thing to do is sell off the land to the highest bidder for private development.” “The right thing to do is let the community decide, let locals decide, and make those decisions with the benefit of all Australians in mind rather than turning them into a bunch of condos.” The NSW Government, led by Labor’s Chris Minns, has also opposed the sale, but has no constitutional power to stop it, leaving the ball in Albanese and Marles’ court. Abbott told the rally that “people power” will prevail. Former Army chief Lt. Gen. Ken Gillespie told the rally that with politically motivated violence on the rise in Australia, including the Bondi antisemitic terror attack of Dec. 14, 2025, it was important to retain the barracks, which is used for counter-terrorism exercises by the Special Air Service. “When police need military support in a crisis, minutes matter,” he said. Marles angered many by previously dismissing those campaigning against the sale as “a few former generals who liked hanging out there.” The description appears particularly inapt now — a poor read on the practical difficulty of opposing so many political interests simultaneously, and an underestimation of the potent symbolism of the ANZAC legend.

title: 2027: Keyamo to lead APC presidential campaign air operations
body: By Dickson Omobola President Bola Tinubu has appointed Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, to head the Directorate of Air Mobilisation of the All Progressives Congress, APC, 2027 re-election campaign Keyamo would serve as Director of the Directorate of Air Mobilisation, with the Managing Director of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, FAAN, Mrs Olubunmi Kuku, appointed Deputy Director 1, while Engr Farouk Ahmed Umar would serve as Deputy Director II. Special Adviser on Media and Communications to the Minister, Tunde Moshood, in a statement, said the appointments underscored the strategic importance of air transportation, operational coordination and aviation logistics to the organisation of a nationwide presidential campaign in a country as geographically extensive as Nigeria. The statement reads: ‘The Directorate of Air Mobilisation is expected to play a crucial role in coordinating the campaign’s air-movement requirements, facilitating travel arrangements for designated campaign officials and personnel, and ensuring effective planning for air transportation in support of campaign activities across the six geopolitical zones of the country. “Given the scale of the 2027 presidential campaign, the directorate is expected to work closely with other relevant campaign structures to promote seamless coordination, operational efficiency and effective deployment of available logistical resources, subject to applicable aviation regulations and electoral laws. “Keyamo’s appointment brings to the campaign structure the experience of a serving aviation minister who has been at the forefront of policy initiatives aimed at strengthening Nigeria’s aviation sector, improving its international standing and positioning the country as a major aviation hub in Africa. “His familiarity with the operational demands of the aviation industry is expected to provide useful leadership in coordinating the directorate’s activities and establishing an effective framework for air-mobilisation planning. “The appointment of Mrs. Olubunmi Kuku and Umar as Deputy Directors also brings aviation-sector leadership and technical experience into the directorate, strengthening its capacity to address the planning and coordination demands associated with nationwide campaign movements.” The post 2027: Keyamo to lead APC presidential campaign air operations appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: NACOC Director-General urges journalists to investigate drug trafficking networks in Ghana
body: The Director-General of the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC), Major General Maxwell Obuba Mantey, has challenged journalists to investigate the networks and vulnerabilities that enable drug trafficking rather than focusing mainly on arrests and drug seizures. He said deeper media investigations into how trafficking networks operate and the gaps they exploit could improve public understanding of the narcotics trade and strengthen efforts to protect vulnerable communities. The Ashanti Regional Director of NACOC, Rees Hakeem Oduro, delivered the message on behalf of the Director-General at the Ashanti Media Excellence Awards in Kumasi. He urged journalists to look beyond dramatic headlines and examine the wider issues surrounding narcotics, including institutional responses and measures needed to safeguard communities. “When the public hears about a drug seizure or an arrest, there is an understandable interest in the immediate facts. But there is also a wider story,” he said. Major General Mantey encouraged journalists to use their platforms to highlight community concerns, particularly those affecting young people and other vulnerable groups. He also stressed the need for evidence-based reporting on narcotics cases, warning journalists against presenting allegations as established facts. The Director-General said NACOC remained committed to constructive engagement with the media to promote public education, accountability and efforts to protect society from the harms associated with illicit drugs. The remarks were delivered under the theme, “Celebrating Excellence, Championing Credibility: Journalism in the Age of AI.”

title: Iran, Russia gas agreement near finalization: Acting oil min.
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 25 (MNA) – Hamid Bovard, caretaker head of the Iranian oil ministry, said Sunday broad agreements on gas exchange between Iran and Russia had reached the final stages.
Bovard made the comments on a visit to Moscow on Sunday to accompany President Masoud Pezeshkian at the eighth summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum.
Cooperation between Iran and Russia in the gas sector entered a new phase in June 2024, when the National Iranian Gas Company and Russia’s Gazprom signed a memorandum of understanding to explore the transfer of Russian natural gas to Iran.
In April 2025, officials from the two countries said they were examining plans to transport Russian gas to Iran via Azerbaijan. At the time, the initial transfer volume was estimated at around 1.8 billion cubic meters per year, while the project’s potential capacity in subsequent phases was estimated at up to 55 billion cubic meters annually.
As the negotiations progressed, Saeed Tavakoli, managing director of the National Iranian Gas Company, said in June 2026 that gas pricing and payment arrangements remained among the issues under discussion for finalizing a Russian gas import contract.
Bovard also reported progress on the broad gas exchange agreements as negotiations between the two countries continued. However, the details of the new agreement and its relationship with the proposed gas import project via Azerbaijan were not specified in the reported remarks.
The presidents of Iran and Russia are scheduled to meet in the coming days on the sidelines of the eighth summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF).
Earlier, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Russian President Vladimir Putin had emphasized the development of economic and strategic cooperation in the energy sector during a meeting on the sidelines of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) summit.

title: JoyNews’ Nana Boakye Yiadom wins Community Impact Journalism Award; two others at Ashanti GJA Awards
body: JoyNews journalist Nana Boakye Dankwah Yiadom has won the Best in Community Impact Journalism award at the 2025 Ashanti Regional Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Awards, alongside two other recognitions for his work in environmental and health journalism. He won the top award with his investigative documentary, Deadly Doses – Unmasking Ghana’s Drug Epidemic, which examined the growing challenge of substance abuse and its devastating effects on individuals and communities. The documentary explored the realities of drug use, particularly among young people, highlighting the social and health consequences of addiction while drawing attention to the need for effective interventions. Nana Boakye also placed second in the Best in Environment, Science and Climate Journalism category with his feature, Greens to Pit, which focused on the destruction of the cocoa farms through illegal mining. He secured third place in the Health Journalism category with his feature, A Sick Hospital, which examined challenges confronting healthcare delivery at the Tafo government hospital in Kumasi. The three recognitions underscore his reporting on critical social, environmental and public health issues, with a focus on stories that highlight community concerns and promote public accountability. His award-winning works were produced for JoyNews and Luv FM.

title: Learn leadership from Macron amid killings, hardship – ADC to Tinubu
body: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) on Sunday challenged President Bola Tinubu to learn from French President Emmanuel Macron, accusing him of failing to show sufficient empathy for Nigerians grappling with insecurity, hunger and economic hardship. The council said the reported postponement of Macron’s scheduled state visit to Nigeria underscored the need for leaders to pay attention to pressing domestic challenges, arguing that Nigerians facing killings, mass abductions and rising living costs deserve more visible concern from their president. In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC cited reports that Macron had rescheduled his October 28–29, 2026 visit to Nigeria, including the planned France-Nigeria Business Forum in Lagos, to early 2027 amid domestic challenges in France. “A president will not travel when his home is contending with internal combustion,” a Nigerian official familiar with the development was quoted as saying. The ADC-PCC said the welfare of citizens should remain central to governance, citing attacks and killings in Plateau, Niger, Benue, Zamfara, Kaduna, Kogi, Kwara, Katsina, Sokoto and other parts of the country. It also raised concerns over a reported incident in Niger State involving the detention of more than 60 young Nigerians under allegedly inhumane conditions, with over 37 reportedly dying in custody. Describing the incident as a grave national concern, the council demanded urgent government intervention, accountability and justice for the affected families. It faulted Tinubu’s response, claiming that Vice President Kashim Shettima visited the state weeks after the incident, following a visit by former Vice President Atiku Abubakar to commiserate with affected communities and bereaved families. The council said Atiku’s visit demonstrated the importance of identifying with citizens in moments of grief, arguing that public office holders must show concern through direct engagement with affected people, not merely official statements. “President Macron has offered a reminder that the concerns of citizens must remain central to leadership. When a country faces a serious domestic crisis, its leadership must demonstrate urgency, compassion and a willingness to take responsibility,” the council said. The ADC-PCC urged the Tinubu administration to prioritise the protection of lives, tackle insecurity and ease the economic hardship confronting Nigerians. It also demanded answers over deaths in custody and alleged unlawful detention, insisting that affected families deserved justice and those responsible should be held accountable. The post Learn leadership from Macron amid killings, hardship – ADC to Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: MMDAs directed to maintain Nissan Patrol vehicles for Traditional Councils
body: The Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs has directed Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MMDAs) in possession of Nissan Patrol four-wheel-drive vehicles to maintain them in good working condition for use by Traditional Councils within their respective jurisdictions. In a directive dated October 22, the Chief Director, Amin Abdul-Rahaman, said the Minister had instructed the Assemblies to ensure the vehicles were maintained to facilitate traditional authorities’ official movements and engagements. “In recognition of the important role of Traditional Councils in local governance, customary administration, dispute resolution, community mobilisation and development, appropriate logistical arrangements must be made to facilitate their official movements,” the directive stated. The Assemblies have been instructed to establish administrative arrangements to facilitate the use of the vehicles for official travel and other authorised engagements, subject to agreed scheduling and accountability procedures. They are also expected to make budgetary and logistical provisions for routine servicing, insurance and other essential operating costs, in line with applicable financial and procurement regulations. The directive explicitly prohibits the Assemblies from selling or transferring the vehicles, stressing that “no Assembly shall auction, dispose of, transfer or otherwise alienate its existing Nissan Patrol four-wheel-drive vehicles.” It added that the vehicles “are to be preserved, repaired where necessary and maintained for the intended purpose of facilitating official travel by Traditional Councils”, unless otherwise authorised in writing by the appropriate competent authority in accordance with applicable laws and regulations. The Ministry has directed all MMDAs to give the matter priority and ensure that their administrative, transport and finance units take immediate steps to implement the directive. “Regional Ministers are requested to monitor compliance by Assemblies within their respective regions,” the letter stated, adding that the directive should be treated as urgent and for immediate compliance.

title: Kongsberg plans to bring Zone 5 missiles to Australian market and explore local production
body: Kongsberg Australia is pursuing opportunities to supply Zone 5 Technologies’ long-range strike and air-defence missiles to Australia and explore local production. A memorandum of understanding announced on 6 October also covers New Zealand and cooperation on supply chains. The agreement follows Kongsberg’s acquisition of a controlling stake in the US missile company in June. It brings Zone 5’s weapons into Kongsberg Australia’s efforts to expand its guided weapons business, with an emphasis on affordability and manufacturing at scale. Zone 5’s Rusty Dagger is a long-range strike cruise missile designed for launch from aircraft, ground platforms and ships, which Kongsberg describes as combat-proven. Its White Spike interceptor targets subsonic threats, particularly drones, and is being integrated into NASAMS air-defence command and control. “As we have seen in Europe and the US, the current environment requires the ability to produce capable and affordable effectors quickly and at scale,” said John Fry, managing director of Kongsberg Australia. “Building resilient supply chains and industrial capacity is critical to ensuring Australia and its allies can sustain capability when it matters.” “Key design principles for Zone 5 Technologies’ solutions are simplified supply chains and manufacturability at scale,” Fry said. The companies will use the memorandum to assess manufacturing and supply chain opportunities, rather than proceed under an announced production contract. Kongsberg Australia is already establishing a missile factory at Williamtown, New South Wales, to manufacture and maintain the Naval Strike Missile and Joint Strike Missile. The facility will be the first of its kind for those weapons outside Norway, and the company is a strategic partner to Australia’s Guided Weapons and Explosive Ordnance Enterprise. Kongsberg completed its purchase of a 90% stake in California-based Zone 5 on 10 June 2026 after receiving US regulatory approval. Founder and chief executive Thomas Akers and the management team retained ownership stakes and continue to lead the business as an independent subsidiary. “Zone 5 adds a distinct capability to the KONGSBERG portfolio, bringing a proven track record of rapid production, highly scalable and affordable missiles,” Kongsberg president and chief executive Eirik Lie said when the acquisition closed. “Together with the Zone 5 leadership, KONGSBERG will support and accelerate the company’s scale-up and international growth.” Zone 5 has received contract awards under the US Air Force’s AGM-188 Family of Affordable Mass Missiles programme and its export initiative, the Extended Range Attack Munition. Founded in 2011, it employs more than 350 engineers, technicians and support staff, with major manufacturing operations in California and Texas and another planned in Ohio.

title: Bright Simons proposes $13m civil service AI assistant as alternative to Ghana’s $270m GhanaChat plan
body: Vice-President and head of Research at the IMANI Centre for Policy and Education, Bright Simons has proposed a cheaper alternative to Ghana’s planned US$270 million GhanaChat project, arguing that a sovereign artificial intelligence (AI) assistant for the civil service could be a more practical starting point for the country’s AI ambitions. In a post on X, Mr Simons questioned the rationale for developing a national AI platform to compete with global services such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude when existing models could potentially support government operations at a lower cost. 1. Readers of this page know by now that JoyNews held a forum on Ghana’s AI strategy and prospects. And the Digital Minister and I got into a serious debate about his Ministry’s plan to build Ghana’s competitor to Gemini, Kimi, ChatGPT, Qwen, Claude, etc. 2. Ghana’s competitor to these global AI platforms is called GhanaChat. 3. It will be trained and hosted in a brand new AI datacenter. 4. 48 registries pooling data from across the public sector will make this AI smarter about Ghana than the foreign ones. 5. The AI datacenter and the "AI Fund" will cost about $270 million. Expect more to be spent on the registries and the apps. A lot of contracts. You can bet that a lot of ICT contractors are very happy. 6. The question is, if we have a couple of hundred million dollars to spend on making AI deliver great benefits for Ghana, should we spend it on GhanaChat, a top-tier AI data center, and the data-pooling system? And should we do it according to the strategy the Ministry has devised? 7. Or could we do much better by more critically assessing all our strategic options and comparing them to the Ministry’s? 8. My argument on the show was that I am not convinced about GhanaChat offering the best value for our money. 9. It would take many pages to explain my position fully. But in this post I will highlight just the most important points. 10. Attached are extracts from page 13, 50, and 68 of Ghana’s AI strategy. 11. If you have even the barest exposure to AI, you can see a massive error. Can you? 12. The target for how much computing capacity the country needs for next year (2027) is indicated as "1021 FLOPS" and the 2035 target as "1025 FLOPS". 13. He drew a comparison with a sugar factory he says was designed to fail, arguing that inadequate critical review has contributed to the failure of other government programmes. “Throughout the Ministry’s own review, cabinet approval, and a high-profile media launch, it is absolutely clear that not one critical reviewer was engaged,” he wrote.

title: Ukraine disputes Elon Musk’s claim that its military violated Starlink terms during drone operations
body:
A Ukrainian official disputed SpaceX CEO Elon Musk's claim that Ukraine's military violated Starlink's terms of service, prompting the company to restrict Ukraine's access to the high-speed satellite technology.
Serhii Beskrestnov, a defense technology advisor to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy , wrote an online post on Sunday contesting Musk's reason for temporarily throttling Ukraine's access to high-speed service from SpaceX's Starlink satellite communication systems.
Ukrainian officials previously said the restrictions disrupted the country's military drone services and left the country vulnerable to Russian attacks .
Musk on Saturday claimed in a post on X that the "Ukraine military violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people."
Beskrestnov pushed back on Musk's allegation, arguing that pre-existing restrictions on the systems would have made it "physically impossible" for Ukraine to use Starlink in the types of strikes the SpaceX CEO described.
"It is very strange that Elon Musk is unaware of the operational limitations of Starlink in Ukraine," Beskrestnov wrote in a post on Telegram , noting that Starlink's civilian system in Ukraine "does not function over the territory of Russia" and that Ukrainian drones operating with Starlink have had a speed restriction of 70 to 90 km/h (roughly 43 to 56 miles per hour) for months.
"Consequently, it is PHYSICALLY IMPOSSIBLE for us to use commercial Starlink for deep-strike or medium-range strike operations," Beskrestnov wrote.
Ukraine officials acknowledged on Saturday that high-speed service for SpaceX's Starlink and Starshield satellite communications systems had been restored. The country has blamed that restricted service for disrupting its drone air defense capabilities during frequent Russian air attacks.
Starshield is SpaceX's military-focused satellite network for government and national security use, built on technology developed for Starlink, the company's broader commercial satellite internet network.
Before Musk acknowledged that he had restricted the systems, confusion and speculation abounded over who ordered the high-speed service changes.
At one point, Musk wrote in a social media post that the U.S. government was behind the decision, though President Donald Trump claimed he had no knowledge of the decision . Ukrainian officials have also said Starlink or the U.S. had imposed the restrictions without warning, leaving the country blindsided.
Musk has not explained the reported lack of notification to Ukraine before his company implemented the restrictions.
Musk and SpaceX did not respond to CNBC's requests for comment.
The restrictions on Starlink and Starshield in war-torn Ukraine have driven Ukraine and its allies to seek or build alternative, "sovereign" satellite communication systems.
Poland's Deputy Minister of National Defense, Cezary Tomczyk, discussed his country's plans on a podcast called Influence Zone (Strefa Influenceów) earlier this month. Ukraine also announced partnerships with Norway and Finland's mobile giant Nokia , as well as satellite maker ICEYE, to develop alternatives.
Beyond Ukraine, several countries are also exploring sovereign systems. The European Union is building IRIS² , a constellation of hundreds of satellites, but it doesn't expect its first launches until 2029.
SpaceX's Starlink generated $5.25 billion in revenue in the third quarter of 2026, up from $3.1 billion a year earlier. Revenue from consumer Starlink subscribers totaled $3.12 billion, while the company generated $2.13 billion from government and enterprise customers during the quarter.
A wide array of customers, including non-government entities, the governments of Poland and France, and the Pentagon, have paid SpaceX to provide its Starlink and Starshield hardware and wireless internet services to Ukraine.

title: Kwara Monarch: Despite Petitions, AbdulRazaq Refused to Reverse My Selection
body: The Elerin of Erin-Ile, Oba Adesoye Adebowale Jimoh, has narrated how Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq refused to overturn the kingmakers’ decision that produced him as monarch despite petitions and opposition from some princes, elders and elected representatives. The monarch disclosed this during the commissioning of his newly constructed palace in Erin-Ile, Oyun Local Government Area of Kwara State. He explained that the governor’s stance helped conclude the contentious succession process. “When the process of my emergence as the Elerin of Erin-Ile began about two years ago, it generated considerable controversy because I was not the preferred candidate of many people. Ebola: NCDC approves N100k weekly for each person in isolation Uba Sani: Bond Between North, Tinubu Strong “The princes, elders and even some elected representatives in the community opposed my emergence,” he said. Oba Jimoh said the kingmakers unanimously endorsed him but faced opposition from stakeholders who wanted the selection process cancelled and restarted. “His Excellency, being a governor who respects traditional institutions, stood firmly by the decision of the kingmakers. He insisted that he would not reverse their decision unless the community reached a consensus,” he said. He added that the community eventually accepted the outcome. The Elerin thanked the governor for standing by the kingmakers’ decision. “I have therefore dedicated this palace to His Excellency because, without his commitment to the traditional institution and his insistence on respecting the decision of the kingmakers, this project might not have become a reality,” the monarch said. The succession dispute followed the death of the previous Elerin, Oba AbdulGaniyu Ajibola Olusokun II, on May 20, 2023. During the selection process, Prince Joel Omokanye, a contestant for the stool, reportedly challenged the composition of the kingmakers. He alleged that prominent families had been excluded and called for the exercise to be suspended pending an independent investigation. Around May 2024, three candidates were identified and reportedly forwarded to the governor. They were Jimoh Adeoye, Rauf Usman Aroyehun and Adewale Omorinoye. Oba Jimoh was subsequently presented with his staff of office on October 19, 2024. During the event, Oba Jimon pledged to pursue peace with neighbouring Offa. He said sustained dialogue was necessary to resolve disagreements between the two communities that he said had persisted for more than 60 years. He thanked the presidents of the Offa Descendents Union (ODU) and Erin-Ile Progress Union (EPU) for their peace initiatives. He recalled how interventions by community leaders helped contain an incident involving a commercial tricycle that would have led to a serious fracas within 24 hours. “I assured them that I came to the throne with an open mind and a determination to work with everyone. Peaceful coexistence and cooperation are essential if our communities are to make meaningful progress,” he said. The Olofa of Offa, Oba Mufutau Muhammed Oloyede Gbadamosi, urged the people of Erin-Ile to support their monarch. He expressed confidence that his commitment to peace could advance the community’s development. “The Elerin has assured me personally that he wants peace and is determined to develop his community,” he said. He prayed that the monarch would reign for more than the 65 years spent on the throne by his predecessor. The Deputy Governor of Kwara State, who represented AbdulRazaq at the ceremony, thanked Oba Jimoh for personally financing the palace. He described it as a contribution to cultural preservation and community development. He urged traditional rulers to remain neutral and promote peaceful participation ahead of the 2027 general elections. “Our royal fathers should remain unifying figures, ensuring that political differences do not become sources of division, hostility or conflict among their subjects,” he said. The Atayeshe of Erin-Ile, Hon. Tajudeen Olabisi Abioye, said the monarch personally conceived the palace project, developed its master plan and supervised its construction. He described the edifice as a source of pride for Erin-Ile, saying it could be showcased not only in Kwara State but across Nigeria. Abioye also commended the monarch’s efforts to resolve longstanding differences with Offa, citing repeated visits by the Olofa and his representatives as evidence of growing cooperation between the two communities. He said the misunderstandings were gradually becoming a thing of the past. He attributed the progress to the Elerin’s commitment to dialogue and peaceful coexistence. “What we need, particularly in our relationship with neighbouring communities, is peace and mutual understanding,” he said. He pledged the community’s continued support for the monarch’s peace initiatives. The Chairman of the Kwara State House of Assembly Committee on Petitions and Public Complaints, Hon. Yusuf Atoyebi Musa, similarly thanked the monarch for investing personal resources in the palace and prioritising community welfare.
