title: Caretaker oil minister heads to Moscow for GECF meeting
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 25 (MNA) – Caretaker oil minister left Tehran for Moscow on Sunday to accompany President Masoud Pezeshkian at the eighth summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum.
Hamid Bovard will also take part in the group's 28th ministerial meeting, scheduled for Monday, a day before the leaders' summit, oil ministry's news service reported.
Preparatory sessions began Sunday. An extraordinary meeting of the forum's Executive Board, chaired by Ali-Mohammad Mousavi, the Oil Ministry's deputy for international affairs and trade, and a meeting of a high-level ad hoc panel were held to review and finalize key documents, including the summit's final statement.
The forum is an intergovernmental body for dialogue and coordination among natural gas producers and exporters. Its summits and ministerial meetings focus on gas market developments, supply and demand outlooks, energy security and the role of natural gas in the global energy mix. Members also discuss gas market development, trends in liquefied natural gas and the investment needed to meet future demand.
Leaders' summits are held every two years. The first took place in Doha, Qatar, in 2011, followed by Moscow in 2013, Tehran in 2015, Santa Cruz, Bolivia, in 2017, Malabo, Equatorial Guinea, in 2019, Doha in 2022 and Algiers in 2024. The forum has held 27 ministerial meetings since its founding.
It has 12 full members: Algeria, Bolivia, Egypt, Equatorial Guinea, Iran, Libya, Nigeria, Qatar, Russia, Trinidad and Tobago, the United Arab Emirates and Venezuela. Angola, Azerbaijan, Iraq, Malaysia, Mauritania, Mozambique, Peru and Senegal are observers.
According to figures cited by the forum, members together hold about 70% of the world's proven natural gas reserves, 38% of commercial gas production and 42% of gas exports. Their share of global LNG exports is estimated at about 47%.

title: Wife stabs husband over phone in Bauchi
body: An 18-year-old woman, Fatima Dalha, has allegedly stabbed her 30-year-old husband in the stomach in Lirr Bajar, Dass Local Government Area of Bauchi State. She stabbed the husband during a disagreement over wrappers, a phone and some money she claimed belonged to her. Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO), SP Nafi’u Habib, who confirmed the incident to journalists in Bauchi, said it occurred on Sunday, 25th October, 2026 at about 06:00 o’clock. He said the argument between the couple turned violent after the wife took a knife and stabbed the husband in the stomach. Ebola: NCDC approves N100k weekly for each person in isolation Ebola: Nine fresh persons isolated as Number on watchlist hits 53 Habib explained that trouble started after the wife confronted the husband and demanded her money, wrappers and a phone she claimed were with him. “In a moment of rage and desperation, Fatima reached for a knife lying close by and stabbed her husband in the stomach. The husband fell, bleeding. The neighbourhood erupted. An angry mob gathered, ready to lynch the young woman. “Police operatives from Dass Division raced to the scene and saved her from instant jungle justice, while the wounded husband was rushed to a Hospital, where he is now receiving treatment. “Behind the uniform, behind the case file, are two young lives, a marriage of barely months, now shattered by anger that could have been resolved with words.” Habib said the suspect had been detained while the knife allegedly used in the attack was recovered, adding that the case will be transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID), Bauchi for discreet investigation. According to the PPRO, the Commissioner of Police, CP Sani-Omolori Aliyu, expressed concern over rising domestic violence cases among young couples and advised couples to seek peaceful means of resolving disagreement, through family, elders and lawful channels, instead of resorting to violence. He warned against jungle justice and reiterated the Command’s resolve to ensure justice is served professionally and humanely.

title: Shadab Khan's world record century secures thrilling tri-series win for Pakistan
body: Pakistan broke a number record as a stunning final stand helped secure a one-wicket win over England in the ODI tri-series in Lahore on Sunday. The hosts seemed down and out at 154-9, chasing a target of 242. However, all-rounder Shadab Khan smashed a career best 113 not out, with tail-ender Haris Rauf providing excellent company on seven from 19 deliveries. The last-wicket partnership of 89 not out was the highest 10th wicket stand in a successful chase in the history of ODIs. Shadab's score was also the highest individual score in ODI history by a batter batting at number eight or lower. England opener Ben Duckett held the innings together with a brilliant 105 but the rest of England's batting struggled just days after they scored 429 against Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi. SHADAB SUPERSTAR KHAN! WHAT A KNOCK! 🤩 A century to savour. @76Shadabkhan , take a bow 💯👏 #PAKvENG | #CricketKaJashan | #PinkDay pic.twitter.com/Vc9F63mE9V — Pakistan Cricket (@TheRealPCB) October 25, 2026 Captain Shaheen Afridi led the way with the ball with 4-46 while debutant quick Razaullah took 2-38. In reply, Pakistan batters too struggled against a disciplined England pace attack. Seamers Gus Atkinson (2-62), Jamie Overton (3-43) and spinner Liam Dawson (2-30) all but wrapped up the game as they reduced Pakistan to 154-9 in the 34th over. However, Shadab kept up the attack and found excellent support from Rauf. Shadab smashed 13 fours and five sixes in his 96-ball innings to take Pakistan close to the finish line. His effort seemed in vain when he was trapped lbw off a low full-toss from Atkinson. The players shook hands and were walking towards the pavilion when a belated review spotted an inside edge. 𝑷𝒂𝒌𝒊𝒔𝒕𝒂𝒏 𝒄𝒓𝒊𝒄𝒌𝒆𝒕 𝒂𝒕 𝒊𝒕𝒔 𝒗𝒆𝒓𝒚 𝒃𝒆𝒔𝒕 🇵🇰💚 A @HarisRauf14 boundary to seal a stunning one-wicket win! 🤩 #PAKvENG | #CricketKaJashan | #PinkDay pic.twitter.com/kngsaqs4in — Pakistan Cricket (@TheRealPCB) October 25, 2026 Shadab survived and took them to the finish line. Rauf hit debutant quick Henry Crocombe for boundary down the ground to seal victory. Pakistan captain Afridi was overjoyed after snatching victory from the jaws of defeat. “I can't say anything, Shadab and Haris, the way they finished the game, 89-run partnership. I've never seen like that in my life. Really happy as captain, starting from the morning, the team effort was top drawer,” the left-arm seamer said. England captain Harry Brook, whose team lost while defending 429 in the previous match, said the players did not do much wrong. “I don't think we went wrong with the ball, to be honest. I thought we did an exceptional job. Probably didn't quite get enough runs on the board, but the effort put up was phenomenal, couldn't have asked for more,” he said. England have now lost all three matches in the tri-series and are unlikely to qualify for the final.

title: Bright Simons flags computing capacity error in Ghana’s AI strategy and questions GhanaChat costs
body: Vice-President and head of Research at the IMANI Centre for Policy and Education, Bright Simons, has raised concerns about Ghana’s national artificial intelligence (AI) strategy, pointing to what he calls a critical mathematical error in its computing capacity targets and questioning the feasibility of its infrastructure and cost projections. Referring to an argument he made on Joy News’ Digital Economy Forum on AI and the Ghana Economy on Wednesday, Mr Simons said in a post on X that the strategy lists Ghana’s computing capacity target for 2027 as “1021 FLOPS” and the 2035 target as “1025 FLOPS”. He argued that, if interpreted literally, the figures would represent computing power far below what the government’s ambitions require. 1. Readers of this page know by now that JoyNews held a forum on Ghana’s AI strategy and prospects. And the Digital Minister and I got into a serious debate about his Ministry’s plan to build Ghana’s competitor to Gemini, Kimi, ChatGPT, Qwen, Claude, etc. 2. Ghana’s competitor to these global AI platforms is called GhanaChat. 3. It will be trained and hosted in a brand new AI datacenter. 4. 48 registries pooling data from across the public sector will make this AI smarter about Ghana than the foreign ones. 5. The AI datacenter and the "AI Fund" will cost about $270 million. Expect more to be spent on the registries and the apps. A lot of contracts. You can bet that a lot of ICT contractors are very happy. 6. The question is, if we have a couple of hundred million dollars to spend on making AI deliver great benefits for Ghana, should we spend it on GhanaChat, a top-tier AI data center, and the data-pooling system? And should we do it according to the strategy the Ministry has devised? 7. Or could we do much better by more critically assessing all our strategic options and comparing them to the Ministry’s? 8. My argument on the show was that I am not convinced about GhanaChat offering the best value for our money. 9. It would take many pages to explain my position fully. But in this post I will highlight just the most important points. 10. Attached are extracts from page 13, 50, and 68 of Ghana’s AI strategy. 11. If you have even the barest exposure to AI, you can see a massive error. Can you? 12. The target for how much computing capacity the country needs for next year (2027) is indicated as "1021 FLOPS" and the 2035 target as "1025 FLOPS". 13. If this was indeed correct, it would mean that the Ministry would like the entire computing capacity of the country in 2027 to be equivalent to a 1970s desktop computer. Or 2% of the capacity of the 1980 Intel math chip. 14. Howzat? 15. I’m sure you can agree that this would be totally ridiculous if that was the Ministry’s intent. So, what happened? 16. Somebody who didn’t fully understand how FLOPS work must have been involved in the drafting. What was meant to be 10 raised to the power 21 operations per second (10²¹ operations a second) was written out as "1021". Same for "1025". 17. Why wasn’t the error caught? Because in Ghana when doing "consultations", governments rarely engage independent and critical voices who will point out absurdities without fear of offending big men and women. 18. I am not being petty. There is a serious strategic confusion beyond mere typos. 19. Read properly as 10²¹ FLOPS, the Ministry is telling us that by next year it will have some 200,000 of Nvidia’s newest chips in use in Ghana, 500 MW of power devoted to AI, all costing about US$24 billion (close to the Ghanaian government’s entire programmed spending for 2026). 20. The US$250 million AI datacenter now being procured supplies about 1% of this 2027 target. 21. Howzat? 22. Clearly, no serious critique of the plan would have okayed such a vision. Throughout the ministry’s own review, cabinet approval, and a high-profile media launch, it is absolutely clear that not one critical reviewer was engaged. 23. My first major point here is that this is classic KATANOMICS: the lack of critical policy audiences. This is exactly how a sugar factory that was "designed from the start to fail" was allowed to be built. Many programs and initiatives in Ghana fail for precisely this absence of critical review. 24. In the strategy, you find statements like: "government aggressively building AI compute clusters" and by courting hyperscalers, "to leverage the scaling laws towards building general purpose AI and AGI". Then: "drastically increase Ghana’s energy capacity 0.5 to 1 OOM per year". "OOM" means "order of magnitude". 25. When I challenged the Minister on TV, he confidently rebutted by claiming that the Energy Minister/Ministry has assured him of feasibility. Ghana’s energy Ministry is committing to increase Ghana’s power output by 3x to 10x EVERY YEAR so that the Digital Minister can deliver his AI strategy? Did anyone in Cabinet not protest that this projection in 8 years would mean expanding Ghana’s electricity output by 10,000x? 26. I can bet you any amount that the Energy Minister will deny making any such commitments in Cabinet. Can we have clarity? Can JoyNews check? 27. Page 68 of the strategy defines an "Artificial General Intelligence Lab" as "an AI lab with access to more than 1010 compute". No unit is given at all. In fact, as written it is totally meaningless. What they likely mean is that Ghana will support the establishment of a lab with computing capacity of 10¹⁰ FLOPS (10 gigaFLOPS). 28. The problem is that such a lab would be totally useless. To give you perspective, an iPhone 7 has about 350 gigaFLOPS of capacity. 29. What would be required to meet the Ministry’s 2027 AI target? If for frontier model development, then the following spec would be reasonable: 400,000 16-bit Nvidia B300 GPU units, 1,114 MW of dedicated power (which is 26% of Ghana’s peak demand). And the budget could easily hit US$47.2bn. For less frontier use, we can halve these numbers. 30. Counted in the 64-bit arithmetic that scientific supercomputers are ranked by, Ghana’s 2027 target is 455 times the world’s fastest machine, China’s LineShine at 2.2 exaflops, and 53 times all 500 machines on the list combined. 31. Anyone with the barest exposure to Ghana’s fiscal context can tell the Minister for free that this won’t happen next year. 32. Ghana’s 2035 target of 10²⁵ is 160 times the entire global stock of AI compute today. Even if chips grow 1.4 times more energy-efficient every year, it would draw about 377 GW, 65 times Ghana’s current installed generating capacity. 33. I will be charitable and propose that the strategy’s drafters may have been thinking about training FLOP (note: without the "per second" at the end). For example, GPT-4’s training run used about 2.1×10²⁵ FLOP, the same order of magnitude as Ghana’s 2035 endpoint. 34. Unfortunately, that doesn’t save the strategy. Recast this way, the target collapses the other way. 10²¹ FLOP is about 12 days’ work for one H100 chip at 16-bit precision. 10²⁵ FLOP is one GPT-4-sized training run, which the US$250 million centre could finish in about four months. On that reading the centre meets the 2035 target before its first anniversary. Not meaningful. 35. Given how confusing the overall strategic plan is, would you bank on the first AI compute center and GhanaChat product already being procured at about $270 million? 36. Here are some bare numbers: the budget, per our modelling, maps to about 2,100 GPUs and 4.3 MW of IT load. That alone adds the equivalent of 90% of Ghana’s entire commercial data-centre load in 2024 (4.8 MW). Running it costs about US$76 million a year, which is about six times the revenue of the whole commercial industry. 37. A utilised GPU-hour costs about US$22 at base-case demand, against a market rate of US$6.71 today and roughly US$4.50 averaged over the hardware’s life. The base case thus implies a subsidy of about US$61 million a year. 38. If the concern is about Ministers and their Directors uploading sensitive documents into Gemini or Kimi, then why not a simpler sovereign AI assistant for the civil service first? 39. That would need roughly 144 GPUs: about 7×10¹⁷ operations a second at 8-bit, US$13 million up front and US$6.7 million a year. That is under a thousandth of the 2027 target, and a far more realistic initial-term strategy. Does Ghana really need to train its base model when orchestrators now allow one to host their own data and switch across multiple advanced open-weight models to serve an Assistant or Agentic system? 40. Howzat? — Bright Simons (@BBSimons) October 25, 2026 “If this was indeed correct, it would mean that the Ministry would like the entire computing capacity of the country in 2027 to be equivalent to a 1970s desktop computer. Or 2% of the capacity of the 1980 Intel math chip,” he wrote. Mr Simons suggested that the figures were likely intended to represent (10^{21}) and (10^{25}) floating-point operations per second (FLOPS), rather than the plain numbers 1021 and 1025. He attributed the apparent discrepancy to a possible misunderstanding of how computing capacity is expressed, arguing that the error raised questions about the technical scrutiny applied to the strategy before its approval and launch. “Somebody who didn’t fully understand how FLOPS work must have been involved in the drafting,” he stated. Mr Simons said interpreting the 2027 target as (10^{21}) FLOPS would imply a substantial investment in computing infrastructure, energy and advanced chips. He estimated that achieving the target could require about 200,000 of Nvidia’s newest chips and 500 megawatts of power, at a cost of approximately US$24 billion. He argued that the amount would be comparable to a substantial share of the government’s programmed spending for 2026. “The US$250 million AI data centre now being procured supplies about 1% of this 2027 target,” he noted. The estimates form part of Mr Simons’ critique of the strategy’s proposed scale and affordability. The figures and their underlying assumptions would require independent technical and financial assessment. Beyond the computing targets, Mr Simons argued that the apparent error pointed to shortcomings in the review of major government policies. “Clearly, no serious critique of the plan would have okayed such a vision. Throughout the Ministry’s own review, cabinet approval, and a high-profile media launch, it is absolutely clear that not one critical reviewer was engaged,” he wrote. He described the situation as “classic KATANOMICS”, linking it to his criticism of a sugar factory project he says was allowed to proceed without adequate scrutiny. “This is exactly how a sugar factory that was ‘designed from the start to fail’ was allowed to be built. Many programs and initiatives in Ghana fail for precisely this absence of critical review,” he added. Mr Simons also questioned the strategy’s stated ambition to increase energy capacity by “0.5 to 1 OOM per year”, interpreting the wording as a proposed increase by orders of magnitude. He argued that such a projection, if taken literally, would imply an extraordinary expansion in Ghana’s electricity output over the strategy’s implementation period. “Did anyone in Cabinet not protest that this projection in 8 years would mean expanding Ghana’s electricity output by 10,000x?” he asked. Mr Simons also expressed doubt that the Energy Ministry would have committed to such an expansion, saying he expected the Minister to deny making any such commitment. The interpretation of the energy target and the feasibility of the projected expansion would need to be clarified by the government. The national AI strategy includes plans to develop GhanaChat, a platform intended to compete with international AI systems such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Kimi, Qwen and Claude. Under the proposal, GhanaChat would be trained and hosted in a new AI data centre, with 48 public-sector registries expected to contribute data to help the platform respond more effectively to Ghana-specific needs. The proposed AI data centre and an accompanying AI Fund are estimated at about US$270 million, with further spending expected on registries and applications. The strategy is being pursued by the Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations under Minister Sam George, as part of the government’s ambition to position Ghana as a leader in artificial intelligence in Africa. Rather than immediately pursuing a large-scale national model, Mr Simons proposed beginning with a sovereign AI assistant for the civil service. He estimated that such a system could require about 144 graphics processing units (GPUs), delivering approximately (7 \times 10^{17}) operations per second at eight-bit precision. He put the initial cost at US$13 million, with annual operating costs of about US$6.7 million. “That is under a thousandth of the 2027 target, and a far more realistic initial-term strategy,” he wrote. Mr Simons also questioned whether Ghana needed to train its own foundational AI model from scratch, suggesting that systems built around existing open-weight models could allow the government to retain control over its data while using established AI capabilities. His comments raise questions about the scale of investment, technical assumptions and available alternatives that should be assessed as Ghana advances its national AI ambitions.

title: Kaduna rally turnout vindicates our mobilisation — City Boy Movement
body: — Shoga hails successful APC campaign flag-off, says youth enthusiasm reflects growing support for Tinubu — Says commissioning of Abuja–Kaduna highway section opens economic opportunities for North-West By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA– THE Director-General of the City Boy Movement (CBM), Hon. Francis Oluwatosin Shoga, has commended the large turnout of young Nigerians at Saturday’s flag-off of the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign in Kaduna. He described the turnout as a testament to the Movement’s sustained grassroots enlightenment and mobilisation efforts in support of President Bola Tinubu. Shoga said the strong turnout of young people at the political gathering reflected their growing interest in the President’s development agenda and their resolve to play an active role in shaping Nigeria’s political and economic future. In a statement titled “Beyond the Road: Unlocking Opportunities, Empowering Young Nigerians, and Building a Prosperous Future,” the CBM Director-General said the enthusiasm at the Kaduna rally was partly driven by sustained grassroots engagements, including the Movement’s mobilisation activities and street walk in Kano. According to him: “The City Boy Movement was proudly on the ground, engaging with young Nigerians and grassroots supporters who came out to demonstrate their commitment to the future of our country. “The enthusiasm witnessed in Kaduna, alongside our grassroots engagement and street walk in Kano, reinforces our conviction that young Nigerians want to be part of a national conversation about development, opportunity, and a more prosperous Nigeria,” he stated. Shoga explained that the Movement’s activities extended beyond mobilising electoral support for Tinubu, stressing that its central mission was to educate and empower young people to understand government policies and take advantage of emerging economic opportunities. He particularly hailed the commissioning of an 81-kilometre section of the Abuja–Kaduna highway during the campaign flag-off, describing the development as a demonstration of the Tinubu administration’s commitment to improving infrastructure and stimulating economic activities in the North-West. According to him, the strategic road corridor linking Abuja, Kaduna, Zaria and Kano offers opportunities for agricultural transformation, industrial expansion, regional trade, private investment and employment generation. He noted that improved connectivity could benefit farmers, traders, transport operators and young entrepreneurs by facilitating access to markets, reducing transportation difficulties and encouraging investments in logistics, manufacturing, food processing and related businesses. “The objective is not simply to build infrastructure. It is to create the conditions in which people can build businesses, earn sustainable incomes, create jobs, and improve their standard of living,” Shoga said. He, however, emphasised that infrastructure development must be complemented by sustained security operations, effective intelligence gathering, reliable electricity and investment-friendly policies to unlock the region’s full economic potential. “A good road connects destinations. A secure road connects people to opportunity. Together, infrastructure and security can help unlock the economic potential of an entire region,” he declared. Looking ahead to the 2027 general election, Shoga said the City Boy Movement would intensify its grassroots engagements across the federation, educating young Nigerians about the administration’s reforms while encouraging peaceful democratic participation. He commended the thousands of supporters who participated in the Kaduna rally and Kano mobilisation activities, describing their enthusiasm as an encouragement to the Movement’s nationwide efforts. “Every conversation, every community engagement, and every effort to educate and mobilise people can contribute to a stronger national movement and a more informed citizenry,” he said. Shoga urged young Nigerians to assess the administration’s achievements and challenges, acquire relevant skills, embrace entrepreneurship and make informed political decisions. “Our message is simple: Do not sit on the sidelines while decisions that will shape your future are being made. Get informed, get involved, and make your voice count,” he declared. He reaffirmed the Movement’s commitment to building a generation of informed, enterprising and responsible young Nigerians, stressing that the ultimate success of infrastructure development must be measured by the jobs, businesses and prosperity it creates for ordinary citizens. The post Kaduna rally turnout vindicates our mobilisation — City Boy Movement appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Russian forces attack three districts in Dnipropetrovsk region, injuring one person
body:
According to Ukrinform, Mykola Lukashuk, chairman of the Dnipropetrovsk Regional Council, reported this on Facebook .
In the Nikopol District, the enemy launched attacks using artillery, FPV drones, and UAVs against Nikopol, Marhanetsk, Chervonohryhorivka, Myrove, Tomakivka, the urban and rural communities of Pokrovsk, and the Mozolevka community.
Three private homes, two summer cottages, a business, a passenger bus, a combine harvester, and power lines were damaged there.
In Dnipro, UAV attacks caused fires and damaged infrastructure. In the Solonyanska community, a garage was destroyed and a private home was damaged. In the Mykolaivska community of the Dniprovskyi district, power lines were damaged by a “Banderol” strike.
Additionally, in the Mykolaivska community of the Synelnykivskyi district, a man was injured in an FPV drone attack.
As reported by Ukrinform, on October 24, the Russian military attacked the Dnipropetrovsk region more than 20 times ; four people were killed and another 14 were wounded.

title: Moscow to host 2030 International Weightlifting Championships following lifting of Olympic suspensions
body:
The International Weightlifting Federation (IWF) announced on Oct. 25 that the 2030 International Weightlifting Championships will be held in Moscow.
Recognized by the International Olympic Committee (IOC), the IWF will be the first Olympic organization to hold a competition in Russia since its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
"Concerning the IWF (Senior) World Championships in 2029, it will be staged in Ahmedabad (India), and Moscow (Russia) will host the 2030 edition," the IWF said on its website .
Between its nationwide doping scandal and international outcry over its war with Ukraine, Russia has remained largely sidelined from participating in the Olympics and related competitions since 2017.
On July 7, the IOC provisionally lifted the suspension of the Russian Olympic Committee (ROC), which had been in place since October 2023. The IOC said on July 7 that the decision followed a legal review that found the ROC "no longer includes as its members any regional sports organizations in territories falling under the jurisdiction of the National Olympic Committee (NOC) of Ukraine."
In response, a group of nine European countries urged the European Commission to halt funding programs for international sports organizations allowing Russian and Belarusian athletes to compete. Ukraine's NOC subsequently appealed the IOC's decision for arbitration.
On Oct 14, Dutch authorities refused to grant visas to three Russian gymnasts, preventing them from taking part in the world gymnastics championships held in Rotterdam later that month.
Previously, Moscow hosted ⁠the World Weightlifting Championships in 1983. Since the fall of the Soviet Union, Russia has won a total of 17 medals in Olympic weightlifting competitions. In order to compete internationally, all Russian athletes will have to meet anti-doping requirements set by the IOC.
Russia's all-out war has taken a heavy toll on Ukraine, with hundreds of Ukrainian athletes and coaches killed and hundreds of sports facilities destroyed by Russian missile and drone attacks.

title: New Canadian procedure could revolutionize AFib treatment
body:
A new Canadian approach to treating a common heart rhythm condition could change the game for patients who deal with atrial fibrillation or AFib.
AFib is considered the most common arrhythmia and occurs in the upper chambers of the heart.
Affecting one to two per cent of the general population, the irregular heartbeat can cause symptoms such as shortness of breath and fatigue, but can lead to severe consequences such as stroke or heart failure.
Fatigue caused Jon Davies of Edmonton to suspect something was wrong.
“I used to go mountain hiking and played a lot of squash and then that sort of quickly went away as I got into my early 50s,” he told Global News in an interview. “I just figured it was old age and having a desk job and not enough exercise maybe.”
His wife, Nora, said he was often tired and would sleep a lot.
He was eventually diagnosed with atrial fibrillation, but when speaking about treatment options, he was left in shock.
“They told me that my heart had enlarged so much that it wouldn’t make sense for them to treat it surgically, so that’s when they said you’re going to stay on blood thinners,” Davies said.
Until this year, he said he’s had to accept the “status quo,” adding he got a second opinion with the same result.
People with AFib often receive treatment either through medication or with what’s known as “catheter ablation.”
“Patients are usually sedated or put to sleep entirely and we put little tubes in the groins and we pass wires into the heart, cross over to the left side of the heart and what we try and do is kill the tissue around the pulmonary veins,” said Dr. Paul Angaran, cardiac arrhythmia director at St. Michael’s Hospital in Toronto.
The process involves creating tiny scars in the heart, according to the Mayo Clinic. During AFib, faulty signals can tell the heart to beat irregularly. The scars prevent those faulty signals from reaching their target.
“Typically we burn, so we use energy sources that overheat the tissue, and sometimes we can use energy sources that freeze the tissue,” said Dr. Gianluigi Bisleri, the director of minimally invasive and robotic cardiac surgery at St. Michael’s Hospital. “But either way, we create these scars that become permanent and stop the irregular heart rate.”
But Angaran said not everyone with AFib will see such a treatment be effective.
Angaran joined with Bisleri to develop a new approach for helping people with AFib.
The result is a two-part robotic technique using ablations from outside the heart and then going inside using a catheter technique.
“It allows us to not only use the robotic technologies which give us more dexterity, more ability to reach and see the heart, but also to treat broader areas of the heart with the ablation,” Bisleri said.
Using both minimally invasive robotic surgery and catheter technology is a Canadian first, Bisleri said.
Patients interested in the procedure must be referred to Bisleri and Angaran, but the former told Global News while a referral is simple there isn’t enough awareness of their approach.
Patients need to wait a few weeks or months between each procedure, with Angaran noting doctors want patients’ scars on the outside to have healed before they proceed with the internal procedure.
One of their first patients was Davies, who learned about the procedure by searching online.
Davies had the first part of the procedure, the robotic technique, in September and is expected to return to Toronto in the coming weeks for the catheter ablation.
“It’s nice to be able to potentially, you know, take that diagnosis and direct it in a much more human, in a way that, you know, appreciate much more than the alternative,” he said.
Angaran told Global News that in patients with long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation, the long-term success rate through this approach could hit as high as 70 to 80 per cent.

title: U.S. Central Command says Strait of Hormuz shipping routes remain clear of Iranian mines
body: The main shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz remain clear of Iranian sea mines, U.S. Central Command commander Adm. Brad Cooper said during an October 25 visit. CENTCOM said its forces had supported more than 3,000 commercial vessel transits over the past six months and helped Gulf partners export more than 1.5 billion barrels of crude oil since summer. Cooper surveyed the waterway from a U.S. Army CH-47 Chinook helicopter and met with American service members who supported mine-clearance operations. The command said U.S. forces had cleared international shipping lanes of mines laid by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. “We continue to stand shoulder to shoulder with our Gulf partners and the shipping industry,” Cooper said. “This visit underscores our strong commitment to continued freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.” Cooper thanked the personnel involved in the clearance mission for their continued commitment and dedication. He said keeping commercial traffic moving remained a priority for U.S. forces working with regional partners and the shipping industry. “Today, primary transit routes in the Strait of Hormuz remain free and clear of Iranian sea mines thanks to incredible efforts by our people,” Cooper said. “We remain intensely focused on keeping commercial traffic flowing as we work with our teammates in the U.S. interagency, Gulf Cooperation Council, and shipping industry.” CENTCOM said more than 95% of ships navigating the strait in recent months had passed through safely despite aggression by the Revolutionary Guard. It said those transits demonstrated that the United States and its regional partners controlled the international waterway.

title: Iliana Iotova winning first round of presidential election in Bulgaria — exit poll
body:
SOFIA, October 25. /TASS/. Bulgarian’s incumbent President Iliana Iotova is winning in the first round of the presidential election with 35.3% of votes, according to exit polls.
Her rival, the former prime minister of the technical government Andrey Gyurov, who was supported by the opposition, is garnering 32.2% votes. The two will face each other in the runoff election on November 1.
The record-low voter turnout came as a surprise. According to polls, about 22.3% of took part in the voting.

title: My father saw acting as prostitution — Uzoamaka Power
body: By Ayo Onikoyi Actress Uzoamaka Power, known for her role in The Call of My Life, has revealed that her father’s perception of acting initially made her afraid to pursue her dream of becoming an actress. Speaking during an interview on the Tea With Tay podcast, Power recalled how her father frequently criticised actresses whenever they appeared on television, questioning their dressing and commitment to education. “With my father, I was cowardly about pursuing my dreams because my father’s idea of acting, the way he saw acting, was prostitution,” she said. According to her, watching films with her father often meant listening to his disapproval of the women appearing on screen. “Anytime we watched a film, he was always criticising the women. He would be like, ‘Don’t they have parents? Look at what they are wearing, and they are in the university. When do they have time to study?’” Despite his reservations, Power said she had always been certain about her desire to become an actress and believed she would succeed in the profession. “I had a knowing in me that I was going to be an actor, and I knew I was going to succeed doing this thing I love doing,” she said. The actress, however, acknowledged that her father’s concerns came from a place of care, explaining that he wanted her to pursue a career he considered more financially secure. “I understood that he was looking out for me and he wanted the best for me. He also knew these kinds of jobs were not sustainable. You needed, like, an office job,” she recalled. Speaking further about her personality and how she handles perceptions of arrogance, Power maintained that she had never felt the need to diminish herself to make others comfortable. “I have never felt the need to downplay myself or to make myself feel small for the benefit of everyone else. I have always known who I am. I have always known my shortcomings, to be honest,” she said. She added that being aware of her strengths and limitations had helped her remain comfortable with herself, regardless of how others interpreted her confidence. “I am very honest with myself about where I am, what I am doing, what I am capable of, what I am unable to do, and whether I am willing to learn. “So, I have just been myself, really. And if anyone considers that not being humble, I am sorry, I can’t,” she said. The post My father saw acting as prostitution — Uzoamaka Power appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Uneven petrol prices, lingering hardship as Zaria residents question NNPC discount
body:
Residents of Zaria Local Government Area in Kaduna State have expressed dissatisfaction with the impact of the federal government’s petrol price reduction at Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) retail stations, saying the intervention has done little to ease the rising cost of living.
In interviews with PREMIUM TIMES Hausa, commercial drivers, motorcycle and tricycle operators, traders and other residents said the reduction had yet to translate into meaningful relief for households and businesses struggling with high transportation costs, expensive food items and declining purchasing power.
While some residents acknowledged the reduction in petrol prices, others complained that the price difference was too small to affect their daily expenses significantly.
Some also questioned whether the relief was being implemented uniformly across filling stations.
The complaints highlight the challenges of translating a temporary reduction in fuel costs into broader economic relief, particularly for low-income households and small businesses that depend heavily on petrol-powered transportation and generators.
For commercial drivers, who spend a significant portion of their daily earnings on petrol, even a modest price reduction can make a difference.
However, Danlami Garba-Dan Kabo, a commercial driver in Zaria, said he has yet to see any meaningful benefit despite buying petrol at an NNPC station in Dakatsalle.
Mr Garba-Dan Kabo said he preferred buying fuel from privately owned filling stations because he saw little difference between their prices and those offered at NNPC outlets.
“The price reduction is supposed to help the poor, but we are yet to benefit from this relief, especially those of us who are drivers,” he said.
He explained that the high cost of petrol had made it increasingly difficult for commercial drivers to earn enough to support their families.
According to him, some drivers could go two or three days without working because they could not afford to operate their vehicles.
“Some drivers have two or three wives and children to cater for, yet they spend two to three days without work because of the high cost of petrol in the country,” he said.
Commercial motorcycle and tricycle operators also said petrol prices remained a major burden on their businesses.
Idris, a commercial motorcycle rider in Zaria, called on the government to further reduce petrol prices, arguing that the existing reduction had not provided enough relief for operators who depend on daily earnings to sustain themselves and their families.
Sanin Mallan, a commercial tricycle operator popularly known as a Keke NAPEP rider, said he regularly bought petrol from NNPC stations because he considered the fuel good quality.
However, he said the price remained high and appealed to the government to introduce further reductions.
Transport operators’ accounts show how fuel prices affect not only petrol buyers but also commuters who depend on commercial vehicles to travel to work, schools, and markets.
Beyond the transport sector, traders in Zaria said the high cost of living had weakened consumer demand, making it increasingly difficult for businesses to sell their goods.
Alhaji Dahiru, a retailer at Sabon Kasuwa market, said high petrol prices contributed to rising commodity prices and reduced his customers’ purchasing power.
He illustrated the pressure by comparing parboiled rice prices over the past five years.
According to him, a tier of parboiled rice that sold for between ₦450 and ₦500 about five years ago later rose to ₦7,500 before dropping to ₦3,500.
He said the price had recently increased again to ₦4,500 per tier, while local rice sold for between ₦3,800 and ₦4,000 per tier.
Mr Dahiru said the high cost of essential commodities had left many customers unable to buy food in the quantities they could previously afford.
He added that on some days, he spent more than 24 hours in his shop without selling a single bag of parboiled rice.
His account reflects the wider pressure facing small retailers when customers cut back on purchases because their incomes cannot keep pace with the prices of essential goods.
Not all residents were dissatisfied with the petrol price reduction.
Hamisu Sani, chairman of a cooperative car wash in Zaria, welcomed the reduction, saying petrol prices at NNPC stations had fallen from ₦1,423 to ₦1,379 per litre.
He expressed hope that the government would sustain policies that improve the economic conditions of low-income earners.
However, Suleman Abba-GT, a mobile phone dealer at PZ in Zaria, said the reduction had not brought the relief many Nigerians needed.
He argued that a meaningful reduction should substantially lower the amount consumers spend on petrol.
“The reduction in petrol prices should be significant enough to make a real difference. For instance, if it costs ₦50,000 to fill your tank, the cost should be reduced to at least ₦40,000 or ₦30,000,” he said.
His position reflects the expectations of consumers who believe a modest reduction in fuel prices may not offset the cumulative increases in transportation, food, and other household expenses.
To examine the implementation of the price reduction, we visited several NNPC and privately owned filling stations in Zaria to check petrol availability and compare prices.
The visits revealed varying pump prices across the stations inspected, raising questions about how far the reduction had been implemented at the time of the visits.
At the former NNPC station at Danmagaji Market, now operated by Eterna, petrol sold for ₦1,410 per litre. Customers, including commercial drivers, tricycle operators, and motorcycle riders, bought fuel there. Some said they considered the petrol good quality.
At Shafa Filling Station near the Kwangila flyover, a staff member, who requested anonymity, said petrol sold for ₦1,430 per litre. He said customers frequently complained about the price and hoped it would be reduced.
At the NNPC station in Randan Kano, Zaria, petrol sold for ₦1,379 per litre. A staff member at the station said he was unaware of the government’s price-reduction arrangement and could not confirm whether the station was selling fuel under the new terms.
At the NNPC station in Silver, Samaru, petrol sold for ₦1,414 per litre.
A staff member there, who also spoke on condition of anonymity, said he knew about the price-reduction initiative but claimed it had not been fully implemented at the station.
“Some time ago, some people came to the station, took photographs and conducted inspections intending to implement the reduced petrol price. However, the reduction has yet to be implemented at this station,” he said.
However, Samuel Omata, manager of the NNPC station in PZ, Zaria, said his station had implemented the reduced price since 8 October.
Mr Omata explained that customers could access the discount by downloading an application developed by NNPC and transferring money from their bank accounts into its wallet to pay for petrol.
According to him, customers received a discount of ₦66 per litre, which increased with the quantity of petrol purchased.
The differences in prices recorded at the stations visited, along with the varying accounts of implementation, suggest consumers may not have experienced the same level of relief across the outlets inspected.
However, the visits capture prices at the time of reporting and, on their own, do not establish the extent of nationwide compliance with the policy.
The petrol price intervention followed a federal government announcement that NNPC Retail would forgo its retail profit margin and sell petrol at cost for 30 days to cushion Nigerians against rising international crude oil and refined petroleum product prices.
PREMIUM TIMES previously reported that Bayo Onanuga, spokesperson to President Bola Tinubu, announced the arrangement, which was backed by the president.
Under the arrangement, NNPC Retail was expected to sell petrol at its landing cost rather than add its usual retail profit margin. For example, if the landing cost were ₦1,300 per litre, the company would sell the product at that price under the stated arrangement.
The Presidency said the intervention was among measures announced by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, to mitigate the effects of rising international oil prices on Nigerians, particularly vulnerable households.
The policy was intended to provide temporary relief by reducing the amount consumers paid for petrol at participating NNPC outlets.
However, residents in Zaria point to the limits of a temporary fuel-price intervention when household incomes remain under pressure and food and other essential goods remain expensive.
The residents interviewed said they wanted further reductions in petrol prices and more consistent implementation across filling stations.
Their accounts also point to a broader concern: reducing the pump price of petrol does not automatically translate into lower food prices, cheaper transport fares, or improved household purchasing power.
For residents already struggling to meet basic needs, the intervention’s impact will ultimately depend on the size and duration of the savings, how consistently the policy is implemented, and whether lower fuel costs translate into reduced expenses elsewhere in the economy.
In Zaria, many interviewees said the reduction had yet to make a substantial difference in their daily lives.

title: Police Probe Fatal Shooting Of Two Officers In Kogi
body: The Kogi State Police Command said it has commenced an investigation into a fatal shooting at ASCO Camp, Ajaokuta, which led to the death of two serving police officers. It said that preliminary findings indicated that male corporal, Amos Yusuf, who was on night duty, shot his female colleague, Corporal Grace Onimisi, and thereafter shot himself. The incident, the command said, was reported at 11:04 p.m., and the Divisional Police Officer, Ajaokuta, led a team of police officers to the scene. It said that both officers were taken to separate medical facilities, where they were confirmed dead by medical personnel. “Their remains have been deposited at the mortuary of ASCO Hospital,” Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Saliu Afusat, said in a statement on Sunday. “An AK-47 rifle and four expended cartridges were recovered at the scene as exhibits.” The PPRO stated that the case had been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) for in-depth investigation. The circumstances and motive remain subjects of investigation, and the Command would not speculate on matters yet to be established. “The Commissioner of Police, CP Naziru Bello Kankarofi, extends his condolences to the families, colleagues and loved ones of the deceased officers over this tragic incident,” the statement added. “The Command will provide verified updates as appropriate.” Read the full statement below. KOGI POLICE COMMAND INVESTIGATES FATAL SHOOTING INVOLVING TWO OFFICERS AT ASCO CAMP, AJAOKUTA The Kogi State Police Command is investigating a fatal shooting at ASCO Camp, Ajaokuta, on 23rd October 2026, in which two serving police officers died. The incident was reported at 11:04 p.m., and the Divisional Police Officer, Ajaokuta, led a team of police officers to the scene. Preliminary findings indicate that Corporal Amos Yusuf, who was on night duty, shot Woman Corporal Grace Onimisi and thereafter shot himself. Both officers were taken to separate medical facilities, where they were confirmed dead by medical personnel. Their remains have been deposited at the mortuary of ASCO Hospital. An AK-47 rifle and four expended cartridges were recovered at the scene as exhibits. The case has been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) for in-depth investigation. The circumstances and motive remain subjects of investigation, and the Command will not speculate on matters yet to be established. The Commissioner of Police, CP Naziru Bello Kankarofi, psc, mni, extends his condolences to the families, colleagues, and loved ones of the deceased officers over this tragic incident. The Command will provide verified updates as appropriate. ASP Saliu Oyiza Afusat Police Public Relations Officer Kogi State Police Command 25th October, 2026 The post Police Probe Fatal Shooting Of Two Officers In Kogi appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Sri Lanka Rescues 40 Iranian Sailors
body:
Essential news coupled with the finest maritime content sourced from across the globe.
Sri Lanka Navy personnel assist Iranian sailors during a rescue operation after responding to a distress call from their vessel, the Iranian military ship, IRIS Dena, while at sea within Sri Lanka’s maritime search and rescue region, in Indian Ocean, Sri Lanka, March 4, 2026. Sri Lanka Navy/Handout via REUTERS
COLOMBO, Oct 25 (Reuters) – Sri Lanka coordinated the rescue of 40 Iranian sailors from multiple commercial ships in international waters off the coast of the country and supported their return to Iran, a spokesman for the island nation’s foreign ministry said on Sunday.
The ministry received a request from the Iranian embassy via diplomatic channels to r escue the sailors , Thushara Rodrigo, a spokesman for the ministry, said, adding they had been suffering unspecified medical emergencies.
The ministry didn’t give any further details of why they had to be rescued but local media including Indian national newspaper The Hindu reported they were on board vessels which were US-sanctioned oil tankers.
Washington has imposed a blockade on Iranian shipping as part of its war on Iran.
The sailors from 19 ships were brought ashore at Galle Harbour, about 126 km from commercial capital Colombo, and were given medical treatment before returning to Iran early on Sunday morning, the spokesman added.
Sri Lanka’s navy and coastguard typically provide support during humanitarian efforts, a government source with direct knowledge of the rescue told Reuters.
Earlier this year Sri Lanka rescued dozens of Iranian sailors on humanitarian grounds after the Iranian warship IRIS Dena was sunk by a torpedo from a U.S. submarine on March 4.
The bodies of more than 80 sailors who died in the attack were flown back to Iran in mid-March. Thirty-two survivors of the sunken ship, as well as 208 crew members from another vessel, were returned to Iran in April.
(Reporting by Uditha Jayasinghe; Editing by David Holmes)

title: Open Senate seat up for grabs in Iowa as candidates tout populism, bipartisanship
body:
GOP Rep. Ashley Hinson and Democratic state Rep. Josh Turek face off Nov. 3.
With days to go until the midterms, President Donald Trump is traveling the country on a red-state blitz to stave off a potential blue wave, including in Iowa, where an open U.S. Senate seat is up for grabs.
Democrats are pinning their hopes on state Rep. Josh Turek, a two-time Paralympic gold medalist, to flip the seat for the first time since 2008. He's running as a centrist on what he calls a "common-sense prairie populist" platform against Republican Rep. Ashley Hinson.
Iowa Republicans hold the governorship, majorities in the statehouse and represent the state's entire congressional delegation. But in a midterm environment broadly seen as unfavorable to Republicans, Democrats see a competitive opportunity to flip control of Congress amid growing economic discontent over rising gas and fertilizer costs in the agriculture-heavy state.
Trump, who is backing Hinson, handily won the state in the last three presidential elections, but Hinson is walking a political tightrope. Though she praised Trump at his Sioux City rally last week for "preserving our country for generations to come," she has criticized the president's recent deal with Russia he said would lower diesel fuel costs. And in September, she reversed her position on Iran, calling for an end to the war.
When asked by ABC News about the Pentagon's timeline for a new offensive after the midterms, Hinson deferred to the commander-in-chief.
"I trust the president and the U.S. military to get this done on the time frame that works right to make sure we can actually achieve the result of making sure Iran does not get a nuclear weapon," Hinson told ABC News' Jon Karl.
On Ukraine, Hinson disagreed with the president's waiving of sanctions against Russia President Vladimir Putin.
"I don't think we should be making any deals with Russia," Hinson said, later adding, "I want to bring all of these conflicts abroad to an end as quickly as possible. I don't think anybody likes forever wars, but certainly we cannot be empowering dictators to win wars."
The congresswoman also took issue with the U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff calling Putin a "humanitarian" last week when Russia released formerly detained American Stephen Hubbard.
"He's a murderer. I don't think we should be making deals with murderers and dictators, and that's why I stood up for Ukraine," Hinson said.
Former President Barack Obama, who twice carried the Hawkeye State, endorsed Turek in July and reminded voters, "I know a little something about winning Iowa."
"Probably not," Turek told ABC News. "One thing I do believe is that we're not a red state. We're a common-sense state that's masqueraded more red than what we actually are."
Turek has leaned into his personal story. The state lawmaker was born with spina bifida due to his father's exposure to Agent Orange during the Vietnam War. "I am an example of the generational consequences of these forever wars," he has said .
On Thursday, Turek visited a local manufacturer in Shell Rock, home to some 1,260 people in Butler County, Iowa, which Trump carried by 45 percentage points in the 2024 presidential election. He said too many Democrats have overlooked small communities like this one – areas where some Iowans say they're reeling from the economic fallout of Trump's seesaw tariff policies and the Iran war.
A recent CNN poll found that majorities of likely Iowa voters say Trump's policies have increased their cost of living, that gas prices have caused them hardship and that tariffs are bad for the state.
Hinson told ABC News she is unafraid "to tell [Trump] when I think he's wrong on something."
"I think that's how Iowans expect you to do your job. They don't like empty rhetoric," she added. "They like results here in Iowa, and that's exactly what I've done."
Turek has slammed Hinson for her votes in Congress to continue the war with Iran. But the Democrat has also touted his bipartisan bona fides in ads, promising voters he would work across the aisle, including with Trump, on issues like immigration.
"He's done a better job on the border than Biden," Turek said. "I agree with him that we need to drive private equity out of housing. I would also like to see us drive private equity out of housing, healthcare, and nursing homes. And I agree with him that we should have no tax on tips, overtime, and Social Security."
Turek, who hails from the deep-red city of Council Bluffs, also recently launched a coalition of Republicans backing him, including members of his own family. He told ABC News his father is a two-time Obama voter and three-time Trump voter. His sister, he added, is a registered Republican and he's unsure whether his mother "has ever voted for a Democrat besides me."
Democrats like Turek have also slammed the GOP for voting to pass Trump's signature tax legislation, the "One Big Beautiful Bill," arguing it has threatened rural hospitals and reduced healthcare access, even as the state faces rising cancer rates.
The bill slashed Medicaid funding by $1 trillion over the next 10 years , in part through new work and eligibility requirements. Republicans said their goal is reducing "waste, fraud and abuse" in these programs.
Hinson, pitching herself as a "minivan-driving mom," told ABC News that she knows Iowans are economically struggling and defended the "One Big Beautiful Bill" for delivering tax relief to families. The congresswoman pledged to take more action to lower healthcare premiums and gas prices.
At 43, Hinson could become the youngest elected Republican woman in the U.S. Senate. And like Turek, she's pitching herself as a bipartisan lawmaker, despite her initial campaign promise to be Trump's "strongest ally" if elected.
"I found common ground with President Biden. He and I didn't agree on much, but we were able to get some things done for Iowa, even when I was in the minority," Hinson said. "I'm going to operate that same way, no matter who's in the White House.
In Shell Rock, Turek said that Iowans are telling him they're tired of the "political theater" and "tribalism."
"'I'm struggling to keep food on the table, a roof above my head, pay my electric bill, and keep gas in my tank,'" Turek said voters are telling him. "Can you please go up there and solve problems through policy in a bipartisan way?'"

title: Ebola: NCDC urges hospitals to act before laboratory confirmation
body:
The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has urged public and private healthcare facilities nationwide to strengthen infection prevention measures and isolate suspected Ebola cases before laboratory results are available.
The NCDC Director-General, Jide Idris, issued the directive during a media briefing in Abuja on Sunday, stressing that healthcare workers must promptly identify and report suspected cases without waiting for laboratory confirmation.
The call comes five days after Nigeria confirmed its first Ebola case in more than a decade, involving a 42-year-old Ugandan-born woman living in Abuja who recently travelled to Uganda.
Officials confirmed her infection on 20 October, prompting the federal government to activate a coordinated public health response.
Speaking further on the response, Mr Idris called on leaders of all public and private healthcare facilities in Nigeria to review and strengthen infection prevention and control measures.
He said hospitals must consistently implement screening and triage procedures, ensure appropriate personal protective equipment is available, and train healthcare workers to use it correctly.
“Any suspected case must be promptly separated from other patients and reported to the relevant public health authorities,” he said.
“Healthcare workers should not wait for laboratory confirmation before taking appropriate precautions.”
Mr Idris also emphasised the importance of standard precautions, including regular hand hygiene, environmental cleaning, injection safety, safe handling of sharps and proper waste management.
Mr Idris said the NCDC was working with FCT health authorities to strengthen screening, triage, isolation readiness and healthcare worker protection.
The agency was also assessing priority facilities and deploying trained infection prevention and control professionals to provide practical guidance and mentorship.
The directive comes as health authorities continue investigating the circumstances surrounding the confirmed infection and work to prevent further transmission.
PREMIUM TIMES previously reported that the woman developed symptoms on 6 October, three days after returning to Nigeria, and initially sought treatment at a private hospital, believing she had malaria.
She later visited another private hospital, where she was admitted on 11 October after her condition failed to improve. Her infection was subsequently confirmed through laboratory testing.
Explaining how the case was detected, Mr Idris said healthcare workers attending to the patient recognised clinical features that raised concern. Their vigilance contributed to an alert being captured through the NCDC’s event-based surveillance system.
He said the development demonstrated the importance of surveillance systems and the role of healthcare workers in identifying unusual health events that require investigation.
According to him, the national response involves the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the NCDC, FCT health authorities, other relevant government agencies and technical partners.
He said the response is being coordinated through a structured Incident Management System and the Emergency Operations Centre, under the national leadership of the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare and the Presidential Task Force on Ebola virus disease.
Mr Idris commended healthcare workers whose clinical judgement and vigilance helped identify the case, saying their role was critical in triggering the public health response.
He said the government was drawing on experienced clinicians and case managers, including professionals who participated in Nigeria’s previous Ebola response, to support clinical management and infection prevention efforts.
The NCDC is also maintaining heightened surveillance and strengthening laboratory capacity to ensure that suspected cases can be promptly investigated and tested.
Mr Idris said the response would prioritise the safety, health and welfare of healthcare workers, adding that the government would continue to review its plans as new information became available.
He said the immediate priorities remained protecting healthcare workers, providing appropriate clinical care and preventing transmission into the wider community.

title: Saudi-signed statement blaming Israel for instability doesn't rule out Abraham Accords, expert says
body: The fact that Saudi Arabia was among the signatories of a joint statement declaring Israel as “the fundamental source of instability in the region and beyond” is not a sign that Riyadh has abandoned all future interest in joining the Abraham Accords, Gulf analyst Dr. Ahmed Alkhuzaie told The Jerusalem Post on Sunday.The statement signed on Sunday by Turkey, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Egypt shows a regional alignment among major powers whose “strategic priorities do not always align,” Alkhuzaie said.“By collectively declaring that, as per their statement, 'the Israeli occupation' constitutes the principal source of instability in the region, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Turkey, and Pakistan are signaling the emergence of a broader diplomatic consensus that views the Palestinian issue not as an isolated conflict, but as a central driver of wider regional turbulence.”The statement is “particularly noteworthy” as Riyadh has traditionally balanced its support for Palestinians with pragmatism and diplomacy, he continued, and so by publicly endorsing language that places responsibility for instability on Israeli policies and reaffirming support for a Palestinian state based on the 1967 borders, Riyadh “appears intent on anchoring its position within a broader Arab and Muslim framework rather than pursuing an independent diplomatic track.”Though Alkhuzaie acknowledged that the statement placed Israel as the problem in the region, he advised that it should not be interpreted as the concrete end of hopes for Saudi-Israel normalization.“It suggests that the political and diplomatic conditions surrounding normalization have become considerably more demanding. The statement reinforces the message that Riyadh is unlikely to separate relations with Israel from meaningful progress on the Palestinian file,” he said.“In effect, Saudi Arabia is signaling that normalization can no longer be advanced solely through strategic, economic, or security calculations while the Palestinian question remains unresolved.”He noted that Riyadh was positioning itself as “a leading architect of regional stability.”Pointing to the fact that the same joint statement also condemned the Houthis attacks against Saudi Arabia and maritime shipping, Alkhuzaie said that the calls for diplomacy signal that “Saudi policymakers increasingly view Palestine, regional security, maritime stability, and de-escalation with Iran as interconnected components of a single regional order.”“Viewed through that lens, the statement is less a rejection of future normalization than a reminder that any such process will likely remain contingent on credible movement toward a political settlement of the Palestinian issue,” he said.Special envoy doesn't view statement as sign of abandoning idea of normalizationWaqas Javed, the Global Abrahamic Movement's special envoy for Saudi Arabia, an NGO that promotes peace across the Middle East, told the Post that he also didn't view the statement as a sign that Riyadh was abandoning the idea of normalization altogether.“Saudi Arabia may have reasons to strengthen its defense relationships with Pakistan and Turkey. However, such partnerships need not be directed against Israel or interpreted as a rejection of the Abraham Accords. Regional security arrangements are most constructive when they reduce the risk of conflict rather than reinforce divisions between competing political blocs,” he said.“For Riyadh, the strategic opportunity lies in maintaining its independent diplomatic relationships while exploring whether engagement with Israel could contribute to a more secure and economically integrated region. Saudi Arabia can retain strong ties with Pakistan and Turkey without making its future relationship with Israel a zero-sum choice.”

title: Latvian ex-foreign minister offers Riga as EU negotiator on Ukrainian conflict
body:
VILNIUS, October 25. /TASS/. Latvia "understands Russian people" and could act as a European Union negotiator in talks on a Ukrainian settlement, Latvia’s former Foreign Minister (1990-1992) Janis Jurkans said.
"We know the Russian language and we understand Russian people," he said, as cited by the NRA newspaper. Latvia, in his words, could use this advantage and act as a EU negotiator.
He said that Riga should come out with an initiative at the European Union level to "lead the dialogue." Latvia could create conditions under which the European Union would want to "turn toward Russia, rather than turn away from it and be in constant conflict," he added.
Moscow has repeatedly declared its readiness to negotiate European security framework with European leaders, taking into account the interests of both sides. Russian President Vladimir Putin told Vesti journalist Pavel Zarubin in an interview on October 22 that discussions on ensuring the future security of Ukraine and Russia would naturally have to address the European security architecture as well. Moscow will monitor the situation in the coming days, he added.

title: Blanche defends DOJ lawsuit blocking Alaska Senate results if Republican loses
body:
President Trump walks past Attorney General Todd Blanche after speaking at a roundtable event in the East Room of the White House on Oct. 21. Alex Brandon/AP hide caption
U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche on Sunday defended his department's lawsuit seeking to stop Alaska from automatically certifying the results of its Senate election if the Republican incumbent there loses.
Earlier this week he had said the Justice Department could get involved in the vote certification process in a "doomsday" scenario.
Pressed on CNN about whether the suit was setting the stage for President Trump to challenge the outcome of next week's midterm elections, Blanche denied it.
The seat is seen as one vital for Republicans if they are to maintain control of the Senate for the second half of Trump's term in office.
The Justice Department claims that potential confusion over candidates with similar names is the reason for the suit, though some Democrats have argued that it is actually an attempt to interfere in the democratic process.
A candidate on the Nov. 3 ballot is a retired schoolteacher from Petersburg, named Daniel J. Sullivan, with a remarkably similar name to the current Republican senator, Dan Sullivan.
Republicans have accused Daniel J. Sullivan of running as a spoiler to try and divert votes away from the incumbent. But the other Sullivan has said the decision to run was his own and denied his candidacy was intended to confuse voters or siphon votes in Republican Sullivan's tight race against Democrat Mary Peltola, a former congresswoman.
This combination photo shows Sen. Dan Sullivan, R-Alaska, left, in Palmer, Alaska, Aug. 17, 2026, and a candidate in Alaska's Senate race, Dan Sullivan, right, in Petersburg, Alaska, July 3, 2026. Mark Thiessen; Becky Bohrer/AP hide caption
The Justice Department has argued in its suit that the name overlap risks confusing voters.
"We're not laying any groundwork for the president to do that," Blanche told anchor Dana Bash on CNN's State of the Union, after she asked whether the administration was positioning Trump to overturn a result he did not like.
"President Trump is not trying to take over a state election in any way, shape or form," Blanche added.
The exchange grew heated when Bash raised Blanche's "doomsday" remark to reporters in Virginia.
Bash asked Blanche whether the Alaska case risked repeating some of the events during the aftermath of the 2020 election and the Jan. 6 attacks on the Capitol. "Oh, you got to stop it with that. You are not being a real person. Come on, man," Blanche replied, calling the suggestion "crazy."
The Justice Department's lawsuit has demanded that Alaska not "certify any election results that may be impacted by voter confusion." Blanche insisted the more precise demand for relief from the Justice Department is "to not certify if the law is broken," and that it would ultimately be a question for Alaska and its courts to settle.
Blanche suggested it was "so embarrassing" for CNN that the discussion had turned to Jan. 6, and framed the case as a test of whether Alaska had violated federal law and the Constitution by permitting such a potentially confusing ballot process to continue.
"It is an obligation of the states to avoid confusion, among other things, confusion in the minds of voters in the election process," he said.
A state court and the Alaska Supreme Court kept Daniel J. Sullivan on the ballot, after Republican election officials in Alaska had sought to remove him on the grounds that his candidacy was to mislead voters intentionally. That Alaska court decision, Blanche said, "explicitly didn't consider federal law."
Democrat Mary Peltola smiles ahead of a debate with Republican U.S. Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska's Senate race, Thursday, Oct. 15, 2026, in Anchorage, Alaska. Becky Bohrer/AP hide caption
The suit was filed late Thursday in federal court in Alaska and, citing the National Voter Registration Act, asked for certification to be blocked after the election until the government has investigated whether votes for Daniel J. Sullivan were indeed intended for the senator.
The Department of Justice has not clarified how that determination could be made in light of the secret nature of the ballot, but Trump said Friday that he ordered the case. "I'm the one that said do it," he told reporters in Florida.
Sen. Lisa Murkowski, Alaska's other Republican senator and a backer of her colleague Sullivan's reelection, said on social media that the state had already distinguished the candidates and that the department should not have sued.
State officials have already moved to distinguish the two men, with the senator appearing as "Dan S. Sullivan," marked as a registered Republican and the incumbent. Meanwhile "Daniel J. Sullivan Jr." carries no party label beside his name.
Alaska's ranked choice system also allows voters to rank both candidates, and back in August during the state's primary, the senator won more than 68,000 votes to the other Sullivan's 4,107.
The lawsuit was signed by Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward, who had represented several people accused of participating in the Jan. 6 attack on the Capitol before he joined the department.
