title: IDF seals off homes of terrorists who committed fatal Hebron attack ahead of intended demolition
body: The IDF sealed off the homes of the two terrorists who committed Friday's fatal Hebron attack, the military announced on Sunday morning, as part of the ongoing counterterrorism operations taking place in the city.Staff Sergeant Ron Yonatan Roytman and Sergeant Yuval Shai Svilem were killed in the attack. Three others were lightly wounded in the attack.Both terrorists were killed during the confrontation. The order was signed by the IDF's Central Command, ahead of the expected demolition of the two homes. Illegal vehicles and weaponry were also located and confiscated during the operations, the IDF said.Additionally, the IDF stated that soldiers from the Paratroopers Brigade and the Maglan Unit apprehended 12 suspects during overnight operations in Hebron. IDF, Shin Bet arrest suspect planning attack in West Bank In a separate Sunday statement, the IDF and Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency) announced they had apprehended a suspect allegedly intending to carry out a terror attack along a major road in the West Bank. According to Army Radio, the suspect was apprehended at a military checkpoint set up in the Binyamin region, and the major road in question was Highway 60.The military said the suspect was transferred to security forces for further questioning.

title: Lagos APC: We won’t allow repeat of 2023 Defeat
body: The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has set a target of nearly three million votes for President Bola Tinubu and the party’s 2027 governorship candidate, Dr Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, vowing that it would not allow a repeat of its defeat in the state during the 2023 presidential election. The Director-General of the PBAT-KOH Campaign Council, Senator Musiliu Obanikoro, disclosed this on Sunday at a press conference in Ikeja, Lagos, where he also announced plans for the unveiling of Hamzat’s governorship manifesto ahead of the 2027 election. According to Obanikoro, the party had learnt important lessons from the 2023 election, when the Labour Party presidential candidate, Peter Obi, defeated Tinubu in Lagos, securing 582,454 votes against the APC candidate’s 572,606 votes. Describing the outcome as a wake-up call, the former Minister said the APC had since taken steps to strengthen its membership base and improve its mobilisation ahead of the next general election. Pantami: We’ll soon expose those plotting to scuttle my guber ambition Akume: Any Northerner contesting 2027 Presidency is the region’s enemy “That time (2023), I want to tell you, was a wake-up call for us, and we have woken up,” Obanikoro said. “You know what it means to wake up a hungry tiger? It’s bad news. That’s exactly what the opposition has done. They have woken up a hungry tiger, and it is going to roar.” He said the APC had registered about one million members in Lagos, adding that the party expected a substantial proportion of them to turn out and vote during the election. “For the first time in the history of our party, we registered about one million. Already, we have provided a solution by beefing up our membership,” he said. Explaining how the party arrived at its projected votes, Obanikoro said: “So, in a worst-case scenario, let’s say 70 or 80 per cent of our members come out, which they will do. That is already 800,000 votes. “Let’s assume they will bring a minimum of one voter. That is 1.6 million votes. No matter how much some of these opposition members hate us, there are APC lovers in this state of ours who, come rain or shine, will come out and vote for us. Modestly, we are looking at almost three million votes.” Obanikoro said the campaign council would intensify grassroots mobilisation across the state to achieve the target. “We will go throughout the length and breadth of Lagos State, all the nooks and crannies of Lagos. We will go there and canvass for votes,” he said. “We are going to win and record an unprecedented number of votes for both Asiwaju and Dr Kadri Obafemi Hamzat.” Hamzat’s manifesto to be unveiled October 30 The campaign council also announced that the APC would unveil Hamzat’s manifesto on Friday, October 30, 2026, at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, formerly the National Arts Theatre, in Iganmu, Lagos. He said the manifesto would outline the governorship candidate’s vision, priorities and plans for the continued development of Lagos State. “I am pleased to announce that the Lagos State Chapter of the All Progressives Congress will unveil the manifesto of our governorship candidate for the 2027 election, Dr Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, popularly known as KOH, on Friday, October 30, 2026,” he said. Obanikoro explained that the document would focus on sustaining development while addressing challenges facing residents across the state. “Our campaign is anchored on two principles: continued shared progress and inclusivity,” he said. “Continued shared progress means working together to build a stronger Lagos on the foundation and master plan, creating more opportunities, and improving the lives of our people without break in continuity. Inclusivity means that nobody should be left behind because of religion, tribe, gender, social status, or place of origin.” He added that the campaign believed Lagos residents should have a voice in shaping the state’s future, irrespective of their backgrounds. “Lagos belongs to all of us, for those who call it home, while respecting and preserving the indigenous people of Lagos State. Every resident and taxpayer has a stake in its future, and every community deserves to be heard,” he said. Obanikoro added that arrangements would be made to make the manifesto available for download after its presentation, allowing members of the public to study the proposals and submit feedback through appropriate party channels. He said the campaign had already held consultations with religious leaders, traditional rulers, market women, traders, young people, professionals, artisans, community leaders and other stakeholders. “These consultations are important because we believe that leadership must listen before it acts. We want the concerns of ordinary Lagosians to inform our priorities. We want a development agenda that reflects the realities of our people,” he said. The campaign DG also highlighted Hamzat’s academic qualifications, private-sector career and years in public service, describing the combination as relevant to the demands of governing Lagos. Hamzat, who currently serves as deputy governor under Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, holds a PhD in Systems Process Engineering from Cranfield University in England. He also worked in the private sector, including at Merrill Lynch and Morgan Stanley, before joining public service.

title: Police Foil Railway Vandalism, Arrest Four Suspects With 70 Stolen Sleepers In Katsina
body: The Katsina State Police Command has arrested four suspected railway vandals and recovered 70 railway sleepers believed to have been stolen. The suspects were apprehended on October 11, 2026, at about 12:30 a.m., when police operatives on routine stop-and-search duty along the Kurfi–Tsanni Village Road intercepted a white J5 vehicle. The vehicle, driven by a 25-year-old man, was said to be carrying three other occupants. A thorough search of the vehicle uncovered 70 railway sleepers carefully concealed behind 17 bags of animal feed in what investigators believe was an attempt to evade detection. Police said preliminary investigations revealed that one of the suspects confessed to receiving the railway materials from a suspected supplier from Bauchi State, who is currently at large. The police said 70 railway sleepers were carefully concealed behind 17 bags of animal feed in what investigators believe was an attempt to evade detection. According to the police command, the stolen items were being transported for delivery to a man in Katsina. It said that the four suspects are currently in police custody, while the operational vehicle, the recovered railway sleepers and the bags of animal feed used to conceal them have been secured as exhibits. The Command said efforts are underway to apprehend the fleeing suspects and determine the exact location from which the railway infrastructure was vandalised, adding that investigations are ongoing. In a statement issued on Sunday, the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Abubakar Sadiq, described the arrests as another breakthrough in the fight against crimes targeting critical national infrastructure. Sadiq said the Commissioner of Police, CP Ali Umar Fage, reaffirmed the Command’s unwavering commitment to protecting critical national infrastructure and bringing perpetrators of vandalism to justice. The PPRO said that the commissioner also appealed to residents to continue supporting security agencies with timely and credible information that will enable the police to prevent crime and swiftly apprehend criminal elements across the state. The post Police Foil Railway Vandalism, Arrest Four Suspects With 70 Stolen Sleepers In Katsina appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Hospital delays, curfews as Israeli peace groups condemn displacements of Palestinians in Hebron
body: The health and wellbeing of around 1200 Palestinian civilians in the West Bank is being put at risk by the forced displacement being carried out in response to a terror attack carried out by two terrorists last week, multiple Israeli human rights organizations told The Jerusalem Post on Sunday.The IDF announced that its operation in the Al-Jaladah and Ein Deir Baha neighborhoods near the military checkpoint at the entrance to Hebron was aimed at locating terrorists and weapons and would include demolitions.The Palestinian Authority condemned the operation as “collective punishment,” while Palestinian officials warned that it would have a significant impact on civilian life. Yousef Zouhair Al-Jabari, head of Hebron's municipality, told Reuters that around 1,300 additional people faced losing their homes, on top of the 1,200 already displaced.Al-Jabari alleged that the military had demolished shops, factories, homes, and roads in Hebron.Milena Ansari, director of Physicians for Human Rights Israel's Palestinian Territory Department, told the Post that the effects of the latest operation were already being felt by sick and vulnerable residents.Palestinians fear displacement could be more long-termCiting the testimony of Osama Abu Sbeih, a Palestinian ambulance driver with the private Al-Salam Ambulance service in Hebron, PHRI reported multiple incidents in which patients were unable to reach critical medical care promptly, including a six-month-old baby suffering from a lung infection who had to wait two days to be transferred from a hospital in Ramallah to Hebron.“Crews are relying on passing patients from one ambulance to another at checkpoints. Even our mobile clinic that usually goes across the West Bank to provide medical treatment couldn't reach Msafaryatta for a scheduled medical day,” Ansari said. “But it's the long-term damage, which is a bit less visible but is as serious as what we're seeing right now on the ground.”Ansari shared her fears that the temporary displacement would become more long-term, and warned that the Palestinians housed in temporary shelters or in the crowded homes of relatives would be at risk. Noting that many of the shelters lack proper heating, entering the winter months without proper housing could drive respiratory infections.For those with chronic conditions, she continued, the disruption to routine can create emergencies. Patients with hypertension, diabetes and on dialysis might particularly struggle should these disruptions become long-term, she warned.“The psychological toll of being forced out of your home in the middle of the night, especially for the children…These psychological hardships last longer even after an operation ends,” Ansari shared.Israeli rights group tells IDF there's no link between demolitions and terror attackThe Association for Civil Rights in Israel, in a letter addressed to senior officials in the IDF, including IDF Central Command chief Maj. Gen. Avi Bluth, seen by the Post, complained that there was no evidence of links between the houses being destroyed and the terrorists who carried out last week's attacks.ACRI also shared concern in response to the Palestinian claim that some of the displaced were removed from their home at night and left without shelter, that worshipers had been cut off from accessing the Ibrahimi mosque and that thousands were cut off from reaching work and school.“No attack, however grave, gives the military license to punish an entire city. Families who had nothing to do with the attack are being driven out and their homes demolished, while ministers present this to voters, a few days before the election, as the price Palestinians must pay. That is collective punishment. The military must stop it and let these families return home now, and ACRI will use every legal means available to make sure it does,” said Noa Sattath, Executive Director of ACRI.

title: GPL 2026/27: Asante Kotoko fight back to hold AshantiGold in derby
body: Asante Kotoko came from behind to earn a 1-1 draw against FC AshantiGold 04 at the Len Clay Stadium in Obuasi in the Ghana Premier League. Kotoko travelled to Obuasi seeking consecutive league victories after beating Young Apostles 2-1, but had to settle for a point against an AshantiGold side that had won all three of their home matches since gaining promotion to the top flight. The hosts took the lead shortly before half-time when Samuel Fosu Boateng’s long-range strike took a slight deflection off Joseph Amoah before finding the back of the net. Kotoko goalkeeper Aziz Dari Haruna had earlier kept his side in the contest with a fine save, ensuring the visitors went into the break trailing by just one goal. AshantiGold resumed the second half looking to protect their advantage, but Kotoko found a way back into the game through Asiedu. The midfielder produced a powerful free-kick in the 63rd minute to beat the AshantiGold goalkeeper and bring the visitors level, giving the Porcupine Warriors renewed hope of completing a comeback. Both sides subsequently searched for a winner, with AshantiGold threatening to regain the lead. However, Haruna came to Kotoko’s rescue again in the 79th minute with another important save to deny the hosts. Neither team could find a decisive goal in the closing stages, leaving the contest level at 1-1. The result extends Kotoko’s winless run away from home in the league to four matches, having entered the encounter without a victory in their previous three away fixtures. For AshantiGold, the draw ends their run of three consecutive home victories since returning to the top flight. The two sides went into the match separated by just one point, with Kotoko on 12 points in eighth place and AshantiGold on 11 points in 10th position. Kotoko will now turn their attention to a meeting with league leaders Medeama, while AshantiGold prepare to face Swedru All Blacks in their next league fixture.

title: Is Wizkid failing his fans in 2026?
body: By Ayo Onikoyi It appears music powerhouse Ayodeji Balogun is keeping his fans hanging too long on a thread after he made a promise of his seventh solo studio album “coming soon” in June 2026. Three months down the line, the wait continues without any actual date in sight. The Wizkid FC, his fanatical fans, wouldn’t throw any tantrum about this, but the question has to be asked as to what is keeping the “Holla at Ya Boy” star from unleashing his “Sexy” (title of his seventh studio album) on the music scene. The fact that the superstar started 2026 on the up and up hasn’t helped matters because it felt pretty much like he gave his fans a shot in the arm and left them high and dry. He began the year with ‘Jogodo’, a collaboration with Asake that set the stage for their joint extended play, ‘REAL, Vol. 1’. He subsequently expanded his catalogue with releases involving Latin music, British R&B and other contemporary sounds, reinforcing his reputation as an artiste comfortable working across musical boundaries. One of the defining moments of his 2026 output was the January release of ‘REAL, Vol. 1’, a four-track EP with Asake. Released on January 23, the project brought together two generations of Nigerian music stars whose styles have helped shape the contemporary Afrobeats sound. The project followed the success of their earlier collaborations, including ‘MMS’ on Asake’s 2024 album, ‘Lungu Boy’. It featured songs such as ‘Jogodo’, ‘Iskolodo’ and ‘Turbulence’, combining infectious rhythms, melodic hooks and elements of contemporary African dance music. ‘Jogodo’, released ahead of the EP in January, served as the lead single and generated anticipation for the full project. The collaboration offered fans an opportunity to hear the two singers build on their established musical chemistry. The singer continued this international run with ‘Alive’, a collaboration with British singer-songwriter Jorja Smith, released on July 2. The song blended R&B and Afrobeats, with production by P2J, and appeared ahead of Smith’s third studio album, ‘What Are The Odds’. Another notable release was ‘Coca Body’, featuring Dutch rapper and singer Frenna, British-Nigerian singer Odeal and Wizkid. Released in July, the song brought together the artistes’ melodic approaches in a record that drew on Afrobeats, R&B and hip-hop influences. These collaborations highlighted Wizkid’s continued willingness to explore different sounds while maintaining the relaxed vocal delivery that has become a hallmark of his music. Beyond his recorded collaborative outputs, his fans still await his next solo effort. In June, he unveiled ‘Sexy’ as the title of his seventh studio album at a listening party in Paris. However, a release date and full tracklist had not been announced at the time of the report. The post Is Wizkid failing his fans in 2026? appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Le Pen pledges not to send French soldiers to fight in other countries’ wars
body:
PARIS, October 25. /TASS/. Marine Le Pen, France’s National Rally parliamentary faction leader and candidate in the 2027 French presidential election, has pledged that France will not send its soldiers to fight in other countries’ wars.
"Our country needs all of its children. I declare that we will not send our young people to die in reckless or irresponsible military ventures that are not ours," she told her party’s congress in Orleans.

title: Winter’s rabbi backs People of Israel despite Netanyahu's pressure to withdraw from election
body: Rabbi Eli Sadan, the religious mentor of People of Israel party leader Ofer Winter, on Sunday expressed confidence that Winter would cross the electoral threshold, two days before the election.The statement came despite recent efforts by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to persuade Sadan to pressure Winter to withdraw from the race.Netanyahu has also called on voters not to support smaller right-wing parties hovering near the electoral threshold, such as the People of Israel party.“I wish Ofer Winter success in passing the electoral threshold,” Sadan said.“I believe that only if Ofer Winter passes the electoral threshold will Bibi [Netanyahu] have a full right-wing government,” he added. “That is what I hope will happen.”Winter asserts he has no intention of dropping outLast week, Netanyahu and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, who leads the far-right Religious Zionist Party (RZP), met with Sadan in an attempt to pressure Winter to withdraw.During the meeting, the two reportedly highlighted concerns that Winter's party would fail to cross the electoral threshold, according to recent polls, potentially costing the right-wing bloc Knesset seats.Despite the attempts, the People of Israel party chairman has repeatedly asserted that he has no intention of dropping out.Winter's religious mentor also said on Sunday that he believed Netanyahu “was an excellent prime minister who did many good things for the people of Israel over the years, and I would very much like him to continue serving as prime minister.”However, Sadan rejected reports that he had urged people not to vote for Winter because his party would fail to cross the electoral threshold, saying, “I think that is incorrect. I certainly did not say that.”Winter endorses Netanyahu despite PM's calls to withdraw from raceWinter's People of Israel party has endorsed Netanyahu for prime minister. The party has recently been polling below or just above the required electoral threshold.Netanyahu last week called on Winter to withdraw from the race to “save the Right,” reiterating his earlier remarks that doing so would “prevent a dangerous left-wing government” led by the opposition bloc seeking to replace him. He has warned that splitting the right-wing vote could cost his camp the election.On Wednesday, Smotrich also offered Winter a ministerial position in the Defense Ministry in exchange for withdrawing from the elections.The position would have come from a ministerial allocation granted to RZP as part of potential coalition negotiations. However, Winter also rejected that offer.The People of Israel party has sought to bring together people who have never served in the Knesset and were not part of the political or security failures surrounding the Hamas-led October 7 massacre.

title: GPL 2026/27: Bechem United hammer Debibi United
body: Bechem United were dominant in their Ghana Premier League matchday eight fixtures, making light work of newly-promoted Debibi United. The Bechem-based side recorded an emphatic 3-0 win over Debibi to bounce back to winning ways after defeat in their last league outing. The home side opened the scoring in Bechem in the 36th minute of the encounter when Isaiah Nyarko broke the deadlock to give them a deserved lead. Debibi United went into the break trailing by one goal with hopes of overturning the fixture. However, they found themselves two goals behind Bechem after 71 minutes. Kelvin Appiah scored to double the lead for Bechem and stretch their lead over the newcomers. Nine minutes after scoring his first goal of the game, Appiah was on the scoresheet again to complete his brace and hand Bechem United all three points with a 3-0 final score at home. The result sees Bechem United clinb into the top half of the table after eight games, amassing 13 points in that run. Debibi, on the other hand, now have just one win from their last five games, and sit 16th on the league table.

title: 2026/27 Ghana League: Port City snatch late winner to deepen Karela United woes
body: Port City scored twice in the closing stages to secure a 2-1 victory over Karela United in their Ghana Premier League Matchweek Eight encounter on Sunday in Tamale. Owusu Ansah scored the decisive goal in the 89th minute to hand the newly promoted side all three points after Iddi Mahfuz had briefly restored parity for the hosts. The visitors broke the deadlock in the 77th minute when Owusu Ansah found the net to give Port City the advantage. Karela responded nine minutes later, with Mahfuz scoring in the 86th minute to make it 1-1 and raise hopes of salvaging a point at home. However, Port City struck again just three minutes later, as Owusu Ansah completed his brace to restore their lead and secure a crucial victory. The result ends Karela United’s unbeaten home run this season and extends their losing streak to two matches. The defeat leaves Karela 14th in the league standings with nine points from eight matches, having recorded three wins and five defeats without a draw. Port City, meanwhile, return to winning ways after a draw and a defeat in their previous two matches. The victory lifts the newly promoted side to fourth place with 14 points from eight games. They have now recorded four wins, two draws and two defeats. Port City will hope to build on the important away victory as they seek to maintain their strong start to life in the top flight, while Karela will be eager to halt their slide in the coming fixtures.

title: Ebola: NCDC warns misinformation could undermine Nigeria’s response
body:
The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has warned that misinformation could undermine Nigeria’s efforts to contain Ebola, saying false claims could create fear, discourage people from reporting symptoms and weaken public cooperation.
The Director-General of the NCDC, Jide Idris, gave the warning during a briefing in Abuja on Sunday, where he updated the country on its response to the confirmed Ebola case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).
Mr Idris urged Nigerians to rely on verified information from the NCDC, the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and other authorised public health agencies, rather than circulate unverified claims.
He said the agency was strengthening community engagement, risk communication and efforts to manage rumours and misinformation, adding that regular updates would be provided as verified information became available.
“False information can create fear, discourage people from reporting symptoms and undermine the cooperation essential to stopping transmission,” he said.
He also urged Nigerians contacted by public health officials to cooperate with contact-tracing teams and provide accurate information about their movements, contacts and any symptoms they might have experienced.
The warning comes as Nigeria intensifies efforts to prevent further transmission following confirmation of its first Ebola case in more than a decade on 20 October.
As PREMIUM TIMES reported on Sunday, the NCDC has identified 53 primary contacts linked to the confirmed case. They include healthcare workers, the patient’s domestic staff and spouse, and health personnel who collected samples from the patient.
Mr Idris said public health teams had listed and categorised the contacts by their level of exposure and were monitoring them.
As at Sunday’s briefing, none of the identified contacts had tested positive for Ebola or developed symptoms, he said.
The agency is monitoring contacts for 21 days after their last possible exposure, while strengthening surveillance, laboratory capacity and infection prevention measures.
Mr Idris also called on public and private healthcare facilities to strengthen screening, triage and infection prevention and control, and ensure healthcare workers have adequate personal protective equipment.
He said suspected cases should be promptly separated from other patients and reported to public health authorities, without waiting for laboratory confirmation before taking appropriate precautions.
Mr Idris said Nigeria was drawing on lessons from the 2014 Ebola outbreak, which the country successfully contained through early detection, contact tracing, coordination and public cooperation.
He said the response required the involvement of individuals, families, communities, healthcare institutions and other partners, stressing that government action alone would not be sufficient.
Mr Idris urged Nigerians to avoid stigmatising patients, contacts, healthcare workers and affected communities, and to follow guidance from authorised public health agencies.
The outbreak comes amid the spread of the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola virus disease across parts of Africa.
According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), the DRC had recorded 9,704 confirmed cases and 4,687 deaths across eight provinces as of 20 October.
Kenya had reported nine cases, including one death, while Uganda was previously affected by the outbreak but has since been declared Ebola-free.
Nigeria confirmed an imported case on 20 October in a patient who had travelled from Uganda.
The Bundibugyo virus differs from the Zaire species responsible for the 2014 West African Ebola outbreak, and no vaccine is currently approved specifically for the Bundibugyo strain.
Health authorities say early detection, isolation, contact tracing and infection prevention remain critical to preventing further transmission.

title: Trump describes diesel deal with Russia as very good
body:
WASHINGTON, October 25. /TASS/. US President Donald Trump has praised the agreement with Russia on diesel fuel supplies.
"They didn't give us oil; they gave the oil to the world, and that was a very good thing," he told reporters at Andrews Air Force Base before leaving for Michigan.
Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said earlier that under the diesel deal, Russia is prepared to deliver as much diesel fuel to the United States as it needs.

title: Peltola postpones campaign stops after Saturday car crash
body: Former Rep. Mary Peltola is postponing campaign stops in her bid for Alaska’s Senate seat after she and her family sustained minor injuries in a car crash Saturday night. Peltola and her family were traveling to the Alaska Federation of Natives’ annual banquet when another driver struck their vehicle, her campaign announced Sunday on social media. “Mary and her family sustained minor injuries but are in good spirits,” campaign manager Cheryl Bruce said in the statement. “Unfortunately, per the advice of medical professionals, Mary’s upcoming events in Fairbanks and Bethel will be rescheduled for later in the week as she takes time to recover.” Anchorage police said a vehicle rear-ended the car carrying Peltola at a red light Saturday evening, pushing it into a third vehicle. Peltola and the other passengers of her car were taken to a local hospital with non-life-threatening injuries, police said. The driver who struck their vehicle was also hospitalized with non-life-threatening injuries. Police said the crash remains under investigation. The crash disrupts the start of Peltola’s eight-community “Alaska Always Tour,” a seven-day campaign swing ahead of the midterms. Events in Fairbanks and Bethel originally scheduled for Sunday and Monday will be rescheduled, while stops in Homer, Kenai, Seward, Juneau, Anchorage and Palmer will continue as planned, the campaign said. The midterm elections are just over a week away. Peltola, a Democrat, is challenging Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in a closely watched race that could help determine control of the Senate. The race on Thursday became the subject of a Justice Department lawsuit seeking to block certification of the election results if Sullivan loses in November. The administration is arguing that the presence of an independent candidate also named Dan Sullivan is an effort to mislead voters, despite the Alaska Supreme Court allowing the other Sullivan to remain on the ballot in a June ruling. Attorney General Todd Blanche defended the lawsuit Sunday, arguing that voters could confuse the two candidates. Peltola’s campaign called the suit a “despicable political threat to overturn the election.” Republican Sen. Lisa Murkowski (R-Alaska) piled on, saying the Justice Department's suit should never have been filed. Alaska’s political history has been marked by fatal transportation disasters. Peltola’s husband, Eugene “Buzzy” Peltola Jr., died in September 2023 when the small plane he was piloting crashed after takeoff in southwestern Alaska. Former Republican Sen. Ted Stevens died in a plane crash in 2010 near Dillingham, and Democratic Rep. Nick Begich disappeared in 1972 after disembarking from Anchorage on a small plane traveling to Juneau.

title: Ebola: NCDC approves ₦100,000 weekly allowance for quarantined contacts
body:
The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) says it has approved a weekly allowance of ₦100,000 per person for people quarantined following possible exposure to Nigeria’s confirmed Ebola patient in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).
The Director-General of the NCDC, Jide Idris, disclosed this during a media briefing in Abuja on Sunday, explaining that the intervention followed complaints from some contacts about their inability to attend to their businesses and family responsibilities while in quarantine.
Mr Idris said the agency was already covering accommodation and feeding costs for those placed in designated facilities but had introduced additional financial support to ease their difficulties.
“We are paying for their accommodation; we are paying for their feeding. Some of them are asking for a stipend to maintain their families,” he said.
“We are providing N100,000 per person per week just to maintain their comfort and feeding, because they were complaining.”
He explained that some contacts complained that they could not leave the quarantine facilities to attend to their businesses and family responsibilities.
Mr Idris said the NCDC introduced the allowance as a temporary measure to ease tensions, although the expenditure had not been planned.
“But again, it’s an emergency. We continue to review it as we go along,” he said.
He stressed that state governments were expected to provide the facilities, funding and other resources required to manage contacts during public health emergencies.
“These are the responsibilities of the various state governments,” he said.
“So each state again must provide money, must provide the materials for it to do this.”
Mr Idris said the NCDC had identified 53 primary contacts linked to Nigeria’s confirmed Ebola case in the FCT.
“As of now, we have 53 primary contacts. These comprise 44 people from the health facility where the patient was treated and nine additional contacts,” he said.
He explained that the nine additional contacts included the patient’s husband, driver, and chef; three healthcare workers who treated her at another clinic; and three team members involved in collecting samples.
Public health teams had listed and categorised the contacts by their level of exposure and continued to monitor their health.
Mr Idris said investigators were also working to identify secondary contacts by establishing who the primary contacts might have interacted with.
He explained that some contacts were being monitored in designated facilities, while others could be placed under home quarantine depending on their level of exposure and risk assessment.
The contacts are expected to be monitored for 21 days after their last possible exposure, in line with Ebola’s incubation period.
Mr Idris stressed that being identified as a contact does not mean a person has Ebola but allows health authorities to monitor their health and detect possible infections early.
Mr Idris said premises linked to the confirmed patient and her husband had been disinfected to reduce transmission risk.
He added that disinfection teams would be deployed to other relevant locations where necessary.
He also said healthcare workers and contact-tracing personnel were receiving infection prevention and control training, while standard operating procedures had been circulated to healthcare facilities and state governments.
He explained that the agency was replenishing personal protective equipment supplies. At the same time, the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) was distributing laboratory reagents to support testing.
The NCDC boss said the agency had also revised its Ebola case definition to strengthen the identification of suspected cases, including through community-based surveillance.
Under the simplified guidance, people with persistent fever that does not respond to treatment for common causes of fever, as well as those with warning signs such as unexplained bleeding or bloody diarrhoea, are advised to seek medical attention promptly.
He urged healthcare workers to report suspected cases and take appropriate precautions without waiting for laboratory confirmation.
Mr Idris also appealed to Nigerians to cooperate with public health authorities and avoid spreading unverified information that could undermine efforts to contain the disease.
Nigeria confirmed an imported Ebola case in the FCT on Tuesday, 20 October, marking the country’s first confirmed case since the 2014 outbreak.
The patient is a 42-year-old Ugandan-born woman resident in Abuja who recently returned from a holiday in Kampala, Uganda.
According to the Africa CDC, the woman returned to Nigeria on 3 October and developed symptoms three days later.
On Friday, Nigerian authorities announced that genomic analysis showed a high degree of similarity between the virus detected in the Nigerian patient and that found in Kenya’s first imported case.
The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, said the finding did not establish that the Nigerian patient was infected in Kenya, as there was no evidence that she had travelled there.
The Africa CDC had earlier said it was investigating a possible link between the Nigerian and Kenyan cases because both patients travelled through Uganda’s Entebbe International Airport on 3 October.
Kenya’s first case was imported from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) through Uganda. The country has since recorded nine confirmed cases, including two deaths, with the eight additional infections linked to the first patient.
Nike Adebowale covers the health beat. She holds a degree from Ekiti State University, Ado Ekiti. Twitter : @nikeadebowale1

title: Saab offers to build Gripen fighters in Canada as part of bid for mixed fleet with F-35s
body: Johansson said the two fighters would give Canada’s air force different strengths. The F-35, he said, is “good at certain things”, while Gripen would add combat mass and more flexibility in where the aircraft can be based. “On the Gripen side, we are running a campaign to convince everyone that it is a good match to have a dual fleet,” he said. According to Johansson, Saab’s industrial package includes a manufacturing hub in Canada and cooperation with Canadian companies. Decision rests with Ottawa Johansson stressed that the outcome depends on whether Canada wants to build up its own defence capabilities. No such decision has been made, and he gave no indication of when an order might come. “But that is a political decision to say, ‘Yes, we want this sovereign capability in Canada,’ and then I think we are the best partners,” he said. He added that he would be attending an aerospace summit in Canada the following week and expected to come away with a clearer picture of Saab’s chances. “We have a fantastic offer, but it is still a political decision to take for Prime Minister Carney,” Johansson said. “But we are campaigning as much as we can to make it happen.” GlobalEye talks advance Saab is also negotiating a contract with Canada for six GlobalEye airborne surveillance aircraft. Johansson said the two sides had signed a term sheet setting out the framework for a final agreement, but he did not say when it would be concluded. That proposal also includes a production hub in Canada, although Saab would remain responsible for delivering the aircraft to the customer. Johansson said setting up the operation would take time and investment.

title: FG disburses ₦39bn to tertiary institutions
body: Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Federal Government has disbursed the sum of ₦38.93 billion to 166 public tertiary institutions, nationwide, under the Needs Assessment Revitalisation Fund. Details of the disbursement contained in a statement by the Head, Media Unit of the Federal Ministry of Finance, Efe Ovuakporie in Abuja, yesterday, showed that beneficiaries included 79 universities, 46 polytechnics and 41 colleges of education. The funds would support approved projects aimed at addressing infrastructure gaps and improving teaching and learning facilities across the institutions. The university component accounts for ₦28.5 billion for 79 institutions, while 46 polytechnics have allocations totalling ₦5.8 billion. The 41 colleges of education received ₦4.7 billion. The statement read in part, “The intervention forms part of the Federal Government’s efforts to address the needs of public universities and support the implementation of agreed measures under the Memorandum of Understanding between the Federal Government and the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU). “The funds are expected to enable beneficiary institutions to commence or advance approved projects addressing critical infrastructure and other identified institutional needs, with the overall objective of strengthening the quality of tertiary education in Nigeria. The disbursement underscores the importance of effective coordination between the Federal Ministry of Finance, the Federal Ministry of Education and beneficiary institutions in ensuring that approved public funding translates into tangible improvements in educational infrastructure and institutional capacity.” The post FG disburses ₦39bn to tertiary institutions appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Enforce the draft, but don't punish haredi kids for their fathers refusal to serve - opinion
body: “If they don't serve, they shouldn't get a shekel.” This line has become a staple of the High Court of Justice rulings, attorney-general opinions, Knesset speeches, and WhatsApp groups. It is no longer rhetoric. Since the High Court ruled in June 2024 that there is no legal basis for exempting yeshiva students from the draft, the sanctions have only grown.Yeshivas lose funding for draft-age students, and the Labor Ministry's daycare criteria now deny the subsidy to any family whose father is classified as a draft evader, even if he is employed. Draft bills go further: National Insurance benefits, housing programs, property tax discounts, driver's licenses, and travel abroad.For a kollel family of six, “benefits” is a bureaucrat's word for groceries. Stripped of euphemism, the proposal is that the state will help feed a haredi (ultra-Orthodox) father's children if he serves, and not if he doesn't.Whether haredim must serve (many already do, in the Hashmonaim Brigade) is a hard argument between citizens. Settling it by controlling who eats is not an argument at all. It is a tactic, and it has a history.Lenin made “He who does not work, neither shall he eat” a principle of state in May 1918, calling it the “root principle of socialism” in a letter about seizing grain. Within months, Petrograd (now Saint Petersburg) was rationing bread by class.Stalin wrote the slogan into his 1936 constitution; Mao's 1975 constitution adopted it too. Each makes the same move: the state decides what counts as work, then feeds those who comply. Trotsky saw where that leads: where the state is the sole employer, the principle becomes, “Who does not obey shall not eat.”The slogan has been used on Jews before. The 1918 Soviet constitution disenfranchised clergy, creating the lishentsy. Rabbis, kosher slaughterers, and cantors were counted as non-laborers; from 1929 they were denied ration cards, evicted from state housing, and their children barred from universities.The Yevsektsiya shut cheders (schoolrooms) and yeshivas on precisely the grounds now heard in Jerusalem: that men who sit and learn produce nothing.The Nazis followed the same path, stripping Jews of their professions, their children's schooling, and public welfare before reaching for anything worse. Every clause of the argument is now being said, in Hebrew, by people who would be horrified to hear its Russian original.A democracy enforces its laws on individuals; it does not ration bread to communities. If the Knesset passes a draft law, the state may summon, try, fine, or jail each man who refuses, as it would any secular evader. Sanctions on the evader himself – a fine, his license, his passport – are ordinary tools of law. But the state may not make children answer for their fathers.A three-year-old in Bnei Brak did not dodge the draft. Cutting her daycare subsidy enlists no one; it punishes her. A sanction that falls on a child is a child's lunch withheld until her father complies.Israel should reconsider its tactics with the Haredi draftJewish law refuses to condition food. The Talmud (Bava Batra 9a) and Shulchan Aruch (Yoreh De'ah 251:10) rule that one who asks for food is fed at once, without investigation.The Torah's model of the citizen who does not fight is not the parasite but the Levi, whom the Rambam (Hilchot Shmita v'Yovel 13:12-13) described as set apart for God's service and fed by the nation, a “standing open” to anyone whose spirit moves him. The vocabulary of “parasites” is not Jewish. We borrowed it.Welfare states condition benefits on need and income; the Soviet way was conditioning them on obedience, and on a father's obedience for his child's food. The daycare rule, applied even when the father works, shows what Israel is doing.Israel should also consider who it is pulling the lever on.There are about 1.4 million haredim, with a birth rate near six and a half, and a quarter of Jewish first-graders – on CBS projections, a third of Israel's Jews within a generation. Squeezing a 10th of the country's consumers is not a policy but a recession. And they are the keepers of what held the Jewish people to this land through two thousand years of exile.Nor are they unwilling to fight: Hashmonaim soldiers have fought and fallen in Gaza, not because their children's daycare was threatened, but because the state built a framework that kept their kashrut, prayer, and rabbis intact. Israel can have the Hashmonaim or the ration book. It cannot have both.Coercion does not integrate; it disintegrates. Stalin's Gulag, where rations were graded by output, should have produced perfect compliance. Solzhenitsyn records the opposite: the special camps forged a solidarity that erupted in strikes and revolts, culminating in the 40 Days of Kengir uprising. A sanction felt at the kitchen table binds families to their community.Every lost daycare place becomes evidence for those who call the state an enemy of Torah, and the young man who might have enlisted must now do so as a defection from his besieged neighbors. The Talmud (Sotah 47a) teaches that the left hand pushes away while the right draws near.Integration succeeds by making membership worth having: units like Hashmonaim whose soldiers leave as observant as they entered; respect for those diligently learning; career tracks that honor the beit midrash; and a public language that treats Torah as a shared treasure rather than a debt.The High Court has never affirmed the haredim's right to serve in such a unit. If it will not, its call for integration is not sincere; it is an attempt to uproot haredi values. Alienation produces radicals; belonging produces citizens.“Her ways are ways of pleasantness.” A Jewish state that wants its most devout citizens beside it should try those ways first.The writer is an attorney in Jerusalem and principal of David Page Law, a full-service law firm with an emphasis on real estate, wills, trusts, and estates. He has taught law at the Hebrew University at the Faculty of Law and made aliyah after a judicial clerkship and a year in Washington DC's largest law firm. He is also a member of R' Daniel Belsky's Kollel and the author of Rav Gustman, on the Rosh Yeshiva who was the last Dayan of Vilna, and the creator of the podcast The Kings of Israel.

title: Former chief military prosecutor selected to lead Nukhba prosecutions
body: Attorney Jana Modgavrishvili, a former chief military prosecutor, has been selected to lead the prosecution effort for Nukhba terrorists.The selection comes as Israel prepares a special military court in Jerusalem to try suspects in the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led massacre and the holding of hostages in Gaza. The planned proceedings extend beyond members of Hamas's Nukhba force to others suspected of involvement.Knesset approves establishment of framework for prosecutionThe legislative push came from MKs Simcha Rothman (Religious Zionist Party) and Yulia Malinovsky (Yisrael Beytenu). On May 11, the Knesset approved legislation establishing a dedicated framework for the prosecutions, with 93 lawmakers voting in favor and none opposed.On June 17, Rothman and Malinovsky toured the Atarot area in northern Jerusalem, where two possible sites for the court were presented.Plans outlined at the time included nine courtrooms and seating for victims' families, the public and journalists. Rothman also said that month that bulldozers had begun preparing a site in Atarot for the dedicated military tribunal.Rothman has cited proximity to Ofer Prison and crossings used by Palestinian lawyers among the logistical considerations behind the location. He also described holding the proceedings in Atarot as an expression of Israeli sovereignty.The Jerusalem Post has sought clarification from the IDF regarding her responsibilities and the timetable for prosecutions, but was told the information could not be provided by press time.Justice Minister Yariv Levin spoke with Modgavrishvili on Sunday evening. An announcement said he “thanked her for taking on this important mission” and wished her luck.Modgavrishvili spent a little over two decades in the military, serving as a military judge and in other legal positions, and eventually, in her last four years of service, as chief military prosecutor.In June 2013, she was appointed to a role within the Justice Ministry examining complaints from people interrogated by the Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency).Her appointment formed part of a structural reform that moved the complaints examination function outside the Shin Bet, where it had previously been handled internally. The change was intended to strengthen public confidence in the handling of complaints against the agency.Yonah Jeremy Bob and Keshet Neev contributed to this report.

title: Trump has 'a decision to make' on Iran as concerns over renewed strikes deepen
body: US President Donald Trump on Sunday said he has a "decision to make" on Iran, as talks remain stalled and concern is rising over whether he will restart hostilities. Mr Trump told Fox News on Sunday that he was considering his next moves with regard to Iran . "I have a decision to make: Do I finish it off, which would be very easy to do, or do I make a deal?" he said. "That's the decision." He added: “We don’t play games.” Mr Trump later told reporters at the White House that "there will not be a strike today". Mr Trump has said that he would not strike Iran until after the critical midterm elections on November 3 . The war, now nearing its eighth month, is likely to weigh heavily on voters as the price of fuel and other necessities remains high. The US has has sent more forces, including a third aircraft carrier group , towards the Arabian Gulf in recent weeks. Officials warn the period between the election and the new Congress taking office could be particularly dangerous, with a negotiated deal seen as the most likely way to end the conflict. The US is also reducing diplomatic and military staff in parts of the Middle East amid growing threats from Iran and the Iran-backed Houthi militants in Yemen. On Sunday, the US in Saudi Arabia said that government employees now require special authorisation from the chief of mission to use any airport in the country. "US government employees working in Saudi Arabia are not allowed to travel within 20 miles [32km] of the Yemen border due to safety risks and need special authorisation for travel to the provinces of Jizan, Asir, Najran, and the cities of Qatif, Yanbu and Taif," the US embassy said. It said US citizens wanting to travel should be aware of potential attacks on airports, airspace closures, flight cancellations and travel disruptions. Meanwhile, Admiral Brad Cooper, head of US Central Command . visited the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, where he emphasised Washington's dedication to helping Gulf partners export crude oil. Centcom said in a statement that the US has helped Gulf allies export "more than 1.5 billion barrels" since summer. "We continue to stand shoulder to shoulder with our Gulf partners and the shipping industry," Admiral Cooper says. "This visit underscores our strong commitment to continued freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz." US forces have "successfully cleared the strait's international shipping lanes of sea mines" laid by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, Centcom said. Admiral Cooper said that the US remains "intensely focused on keeping commercial traffic flowing as we work with our teammates in the US interagency, Gulf Co-operation Council and shipping industry".

title: Igbo must unite, build alliances to produce president — Soludo
body: …Opens up on inclusion in APC presidential campaign council …Says Igbo identity no reason to back Obi … Declares victory over Monday sit-at-home, says Anambra back to life By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has said the Igbo must unite and build strategic alliances across Nigeria to stand a chance of producing the country’s president. Soludo said the South-East must overcome political divisions and forge strategic alliances with other regions to strengthen its bargaining power. He cited the alliance-building approach associated with First Republic political leader, Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe, arguing that the Igbo needed a broader national support base to realise their presidential ambition. He also pointed to President Bola Tinubu’s political alliances as an example of the importance of coalition-building in securing power. Gov. Soludo who spoke exclusively with Vanguard, declared that he and the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) would support President Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, explaining why he accepted an appointment in the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council despite belonging to another party. The Governor said APGA’s leadership had collectively adopted Tinubu for a second term and resolved not to field a presidential candidate, adding that the decision was consistent with the party’s tradition of supporting presidents irrespective of their political platforms. He recalled that former Anambra governors Peter Obi and Willie Obiano had similarly supported presidential candidates from other parties. Speaking through his Chief Press Secretary, Mr Christian Aburime, Gov. Soludo said he had since, communicated APGA’s position to President Tinubu during the President’s visit to Anambra to inaugurate landmark projects, including the Government House, Solution Fun City and roads. Obi’s Igbo identity no reason to back him On expectations that Soludo should support his predecessor and the presidential flag bearer of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Peter Obi, Aburime said the two politicians belonged to different parties and did not share the same political ideology. He acknowledged that Obi was qualified to contest the presidency but maintained that shared ethnicity should not determine political support. “Politics shouldn’t be based on emotion or sentiment. They have different ideologies,” he said, insisting that Nigerians should support parties based on their capacity to improve citizens’ lives rather than ethnic or regional considerations. Aburime also dismissed the assumption that Anambra voters would repeat their overwhelming support for Obi in 2023, declaring that the political dynamics had changed. “2023 is gone. 2027 is not going to be 2023,” he said, expressing confidence that APGA members would vote for Tinubu. Defends Tinubu’s economic reforms On the removal of fuel subsidy and foreign exchange reforms, Aburime said Soludo supported Tinubu’s economic policies, describing them as painful but necessary measures to address longstanding structural weaknesses. He argued that the previous practice of printing money to sustain the economy was unsustainable, adding that the reforms would eventually yield benefits. On whether Tinubu had influenced former President Muhammadu Buhari to adopt better economic policies, Aburime said it was impossible to know whether the President had offered such advice behind the scenes, noting that influence did not guarantee acceptance. Kanu’s release will be resolved politically On the continued detention of Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) leader, Nnamdi Kanu, Aburime said the matter had assumed a political dimension and would ultimately require a political resolution. Soludo had previously visited Kanu in detention and pledged to work towards securing his release. Asked why the governor had yet to achieve that objective despite his closeness and relationship with Tinubu, Aburime declined to comment extensively but said efforts towards a resolution were not over. “The Nnamdi Kanu case has become a political case and it will be resolved politically,” he said. Monday sit-at-home defeated, Anambra back to life Soludo declared that the enforcement of the Monday sit-at-home order by armed groups had been defeated, with commercial and social activities returning to normal across Anambra. He said vehicles were moving freely and major centres, including Awka, Onitsha and Nnewi were bustling with activities. “The war has been conquered, and all the debris is buried,” he said, insisting that residents could now move around freely and that Anambra was back to life. END The post Igbo must unite, build alliances to produce president — Soludo appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: GPL 2026/2027: Babil’s late strike sends Medeama top
body: Nana Kofi Babil’s 82nd-minute strike earned Medeama SC a hard-fought victory over Aduana FC in Matchday 8 of the Ghana Premier League. The cagey encounter appeared destined for a draw before Babil struck with just eight minutes of normal time remaining, sending the defending champions back to the top of the league table following Hearts of Oak’s victory on Friday. The defeat sees Aduana FC slip to seventh place, while Medeama return to winning ways after last week’s loss to Samartex.

title: 2026/27 Ghana League: Vision end winless run with 3-1 victory over Dreams
body: Vision FC ended a six-game winless run in the Ghana Premier League with a convincing 3-1 victory over Dreams FC at the Tuba AstroTurf on Sunday. The visitors made a flying start to the match, scoring three goals in the opening 26 minutes to secure their second win of the 2026/27 campaign. Sherif Mohammed opened the scoring in the 12th minute before Setsofia Agetey doubled Vision’s advantage five minutes later. Mohammed then completed his brace in the 26th minute to give Vision a commanding 3-0 lead before the break. Dreams FC responded in the second half, pulling one back in the 58th minute through an own goal by Ibrahim Larbi. However, Vision held on to claim all three points and end their disappointing run since winning their opening league fixture. The result leaves Dreams FC rooted to the bottom of the league table with three points after eight matches, having recorded three draws and five defeats without a win this season. Vision, meanwhile, move to ninth place with nine points from eight matches. They have now recorded two wins, three draws and three defeats. The victory provides a timely boost for Vision as they seek to build momentum in the league, while Dreams FC face mounting pressure to turn their fortunes around after another disappointing outing.

title: Netanyahu shows 'political desperation' in push for Trump backing, US sources tell 'Post'
body: Two days before Israel's elections, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is intensifying his efforts to secure additional support from US President Donald Trump, who already gave him an extraordinary public endorsement last week.Two American sources confirmed to The Jerusalem Post that Trump is facing particularly intense pressure from Netanyahu himself and several of the prime minister's supporters within the president's inner circle, who are seeking to generate additional political momentum through new statements of support.According to the sources, some figures close to Trump have been repeatedly raising Netanyahu and the Israeli elections with the president, seeking to ensure that he continues to publicly back the prime minister during the final days of the campaign.American sources with extensive knowledge of Israeli public sentiment described to the Post the intensity of Netanyahu's efforts to secure American support.“We have never seen Netanyahu like this before. He is showing signs of political desperation,” they said.State Department signals readiness to work with Israel's next governmentMeanwhile, a senior US State Department official told the Post that the administration maintains contact with a broad range of Israeli stakeholders and looks forward to continuing its cooperation with the government formed following the elections.“As part of our regular diplomatic work, US officials engage with a broad range of Israeli stakeholders,” the official said. “We do not speak to private diplomatic conversations.”The official added: “We look forward to continuing our close partnership with Israel's post-election government on shared priorities. Normalization between Israel and its neighbors remains a priority of this Administration.”The remarks underscore that the State Department is preparing to continue working with Israel's elected leadership, even if it differs from the current government.Netanyahu asked Trump to increase his supportThe developments follow a report published Sunday by Axios, according to which Netanyahu spoke with Trump twice over the past three days and asked him to issue additional statements of support.According to the report, Netanyahu even suggested possible wording for new endorsements. An Israeli source briefed on the efforts told Axios that the prime minister proposed having Trump speak with Israeli journalists to reiterate his support.Last week, after months of refraining from an explicit endorsement, Trump posted a statement on Truth Social giving Netanyahu his “complete and total endorsement,” describing him as a “great warrior prime minister” and a key partner in the struggle against Iran.Trump also suggested that the election of another candidate could have consequences for relations with the United States.“If Israel has the wrong leader, meaning anyone other than Bibi, America will have to do this job itself, and I'm not inclined to do that,” he wrote, referring to the confrontation with Iran.Not everyone in the administration is enthusiastic about Netanyahu's endorsementDespite Trump's public support, other senior administration officials have declined to join him.Vice President JD Vance made clear last week that he does not intend to endorse Netanyahu or intervene in Israel's elections.“I'm not attacking Bibi Netanyahu. I'm not endorsing Bibi Netanyahu,” Vance said. “I think the president's endorsement is ultimately what matters.”Vance noted that the only foreign candidate he had ever endorsed was former Hungarian prime minister Viktor Orbán, who lost the election in April.He said he intends to focus on the US midterm elections and will not endorse any more foreign candidates.And Vance is not the only one expressing reservations. Senior Trump advisers believe that a different Israeli government could actually make it easier to advance the president's diplomatic objectives in the Middle East.Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have expressed frustration over difficulties implementing the president's Gaza plan, while US envoy Tom Barrack has reservations about some of Israel's actions in Syria.Within the State Department, officials believe Israel could do more to strengthen the Lebanese government and curb settler violence in the West Bank.Some American officials also believe that a government without Netanyahu's far-right coalition partners could give Washington greater flexibility in advancing regional agreements.Similar views are being expressed outside the administration.Jewish-American investor Bill Ackman, a prominent voice in the American public debate over Israel, called Sunday for the formation of a government without Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich.According to Ackman, the two ministers have caused significant damage to Israel's international reputation, and a government without them could help restore international credibility, expand the Abraham Accords, and improve Israel's relations with both American political parties.The election test and the day afterFrom the White House's perspective, the elections could affect not only the identity of Israel's next prime minister but also the continuation of American initiatives across the Middle East, particularly the war with Iran, the reconstruction and demilitarization plan for Gaza, and the potential expansion of the Abraham Accords.Against this backdrop, the senior State Department official's comments to the Post make clear that while Trump continues to offer Netanyahu his personal political backing, the US administration is maintaining channels of communication with other Israeli stakeholders and intends to continue advancing its regional agenda following the elections.Netanyahu, for his part, continues his efforts to ensure that the American president's voice is heard in Israel during the final stretch of the election campaign.If Netanyahu remains in power, Trump could claim credit for saving the prime minister's political future and press him for retribution. If he loses, whoever wins on Tuesday would still have every incentive to cultivate a good relationship with the president. Currently, Israeli polls show that Gadi Eisenkot is projected to secure an average of 23 seats, while Netanyahu's Likud secured 20.Notably, Likud's projected numbers for the 2026 election show it losing as many as 17 seats. The party currently holds 32 seats in the Knesset.Corinne Baum contributed to this report.

title: Man United v Bournemouth ratings: Disaster at Old Trafford as Tielemans and Dalot struggle
body: Manchester United's season went from bad to worse as they crashed to a 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth, compounding the pressure on manager Michael Carrick. Loud boos ran around Old Trafford as United slipped to to 16th in the Premier League after eight games – just one point above the relegation zone. Carrick decided to bench captain Bruno Fernandes , who had earlier questioned the team's tactics during the Champions League defeat to Como . The move failed to change the team's fortunes as Rayan scored for the Cherries in the 38th ​minute, ⁠with Marcus Tavernier adding a ‌second goal before the break. Evanlison's superb third saw fans begin to ​head for the exit, and that trickle became a flood as the final whistle approached. Fernandes remained on the bench as United buckled under pressure. With the final whistle greeted by a loud chorus of boos, the defeat left Carrick 's side in 16th place on seven points. They are without a win in the league since beating Ipswich Town 5-2 on August 30. 7 - Since the 2023-24 season, no Premier League side has lost more home games by a margin of three or more goals in all competitions than Man Utd (7). Troubles. pic.twitter.com/M8ixyscQ7q — OptaJoe (@OptaJoe) October 25, 2026 What they said Man United captain Harry Maguire to Sky Sports: “It wasn't good enough. It's not clicking at the moment. Results are not good enough and performances in the last week not good enough. Still early in the season. “Michael [Carrick] turned our season on its head last year and we played brilliant football and got brilliant results. This season we haven't performed well enough as individuals.” Man United manager Michael Carrick to Sky Sports: “It's difficult for me to have a day like this at this club and feel the emotion. “The situation is where we are and we haven't had results or performances that have been good enough. It's a tough situation, there's no hiding from it. What it looks like and what's next I really don't know. I will always do my best for the football club and I won't change that now. I love what I do and I feel the responsibility – we'll have to wait and see.” Boo's ring out at Old Trafford after Manchester United's 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth ❌ pic.twitter.com/Xr4iVFcYZU — Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) October 25, 2026 Man United player ratings Senne Lammens – 4/10: It was always going to be full on and he faced four Bournemouth corners in the first 25 minutes. Not really at fault for the first two, but for the third he rushed out to try to win a ball, which held up, and was finished superbly. But the two tackles lost in midfield really caused that goal. Leny Yoro – 4/10: Slipped, which led directly to the second Bournemouth goal. Before that, he made a fine last-ditch block from the right back and stopped a Bournemouth cross. He’s a central defender playing at right back, an inexperienced one at that. Ayden Heaven – 3/10: Neat turn on 25, then he was booked for a two-footed lunge on 36 – and was lucky there was no contact as the Bournemouth player stepped away. The following free-kick led to the opening goal. Gave the ball away again on 49 and Bournemouth attacked again. A chastening afternoon. Harry Maguire – 5/10: Captain of the team and a makeshift, hesitant, back four. Blocked from Lewis Cook on 5 as Bournemouth started well. Booked. Up against Evanilson who scored mid week – and today. Diogo Dalot – 3/10: Right back being asked to play left back – and he doesn’t avoid it or say he’s injured. Chased a ball and crossed on 7. Attacked on the left on 17, but blasted the ball over rather than across the goal where players were waiting. Gave ball away on 24. Poor. Carlos Baleba – 5/10: Bit loose on the ball, losing possession. Shot miles over – like most United shots these days. Looks nervous. Andrey Santos – 4/10: Booked (again) for a lunging challenge on 22. Look lost and isn’t having the impact needed. Amad Diallo – 5/10: Flashes of skill as United had more possession, but seldom in dangerous areas. Youri Tielemans – 3/10: Given a big role replacing Fernandes. Failed. Whacked in a yellow card challenge by Tyler Adams on 26. Crossed after United’s best move of the first half, then struggled to thread a ball to Bryan Mbeumo a minute later. Booked just after the opening goal. Off at half time. Mason Mount – 4/10: A regular in pre-season, he’s played only 26 Premier League minutes before this start. Frustrating afternoon for him on the left – and almost everyone at Old Trafford. Almost nothing in the first half. And the second. Shot on target on 94. Bryan Mbeumo – 5/10: Fired United’s first shot on target after 40. Tried, but he’s getting no service. He’s also the only United player scoring right now but not today. Substitutes Matheus Cunha (Tielemans, 45') – 6/10: On for after his mess of a performance in Como. One good effort from the edge of the area. Lisandro Martinez (Heaven, 64') – 5/10: On and was skinned by Rayan within a minute. Shot on target on 67. Joshua Zirkzee (Baleba, 72') – 5/10: No consolation goal for him today. Shea Lacey (Amad, 78) – 6/10: A dash of pride from the talented young Scouser, but what could he do?

title: 2026/27 GPL: Swedru All Blacks beat Young Apostles to secure 2-1 win
body: Swedru All Blacks secured a 2-1 victory over Young Apostles in their Ghana Premier League Matchday 8 encounter, scoring twice in the second half. The visitors came close to opening the scoring in the 10th minute when Akoto Osae unleashed a powerful effort, but Young Apostles goalkeeper Osman Wahabu parried the ball before it was cleared away. The first half also saw a lengthy stoppage after goalkeeper Michael Appiah sustained an injury. Nine minutes of added time were played, but neither side could find the breakthrough before the interval. Swedru All Blacks eventually took the lead in the 55th minute through William Dankwah, who put the visitors 1-0 ahead. Young Apostles made a double substitution in the 62nd minute, with Solomon Ayikabia and Godfred Yartey replacing Eric Wiafe Darkwah and John Andoh as they sought to get back into the game. Yartey showed attacking intent in the 76th minute, taking on two opposing defenders, although his effort resulted in a throw-in. The substitute, however, made a decisive impact six minutes later when he scored in the 82nd minute to double Swedru All Blacks’ advantage. Illiasu grabbed a consolation in the 89th minute, but time had run out for the homesters. The visitors made triple substitutions, bringing on Andrews Quainoo, Vincent Baah Junior, Zayat Bubakari are in to replace Salisu Mohammed, Faisal Charwetey and Michael Abrokwah to protect their lead as they held on to secure a 2-1 win and claim all three points in the Matchday 8 fixture.

title: A 10-year-old CNN outperforms frontier LLMs for skin cancer diagnosis
body:
I am a dermatologist. I tested the ability of GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 to diagnosis skin cancer and found that they were less accurate than I expected. I compared to a 10-year old CNN and to my surprise found that this was superior.
By Dr Magnus Lynch · 25 October 2026 · 5 min read
I showed these two images - a clinical photograph and a dermoscopic (skin microscope) image - to GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1, two of the most capable AI models available in October 2026. Both said it was a seborrhoeic keratosis, a harmless warty growth, and that the patient could be discharged. I then showed them to fine-tuned version of Inception v3, a convolutional neural network (CNN) first published by Google in 2015 and fine-tuned here on public dermatology images. The CNN got the right answer based on the dermoscopy view.
It was one of 200 biopsy-proven lesions I gave to all three. The CNN named the right diagnosis (out of 6 possiblities) for 125 of them (62%). The two frontier LLMs named it for 84 and 85 (42%). A ten-year-old network, fine-tuned for about twenty minutes, beat both of them at recognising skin cancer.
The lesions come from MILK10k , a public dataset released through the International Skin Imaging Collaboration in 2025, in which each lesion is photographed twice: a clinical close-up and a dermoscopic image taken through the illuminated magnifying lens dermatologists use. I drew 200 lesions at random, all confirmed by histopathology:
Every lesion was biopsied, including the benign ones, so these are harder to diagnose: a mole that somebody decided to cut out is one that worried a clinician.
Basal cell carcinoma on the trunk of a 75-year-old man. All three models answered correctly.
Invasive melanoma under 0.8 mm thick, with very little pigment. GPT-6 Astra called it a basal cell carcinoma with 95% confidence. Claude Fable 5.1 and the CNN called it a melanoma.
Seborrhoeic keratosis on the leg. Both LLMs called it an actinic keratosis and the CNN a squamous cell carcinoma: all three were wrong, though all three would have kept it rather than discharge it.
The LLMs were given both images and nothing else, and asked, as a clinician might use them, for the most likely of the six diagnoses (or “unsure”), a confidence, a second choice, and whether the lesion could be safely discharged with no treatment, biopsy or follow-up. Both models got the same prompt at default settings, and neither refused a case.
The CNN is deliberately not state of the art. I used Inception v3 pretrained on everyday photographs and then fine-tuned all layers on 68,011 dermoscopic and clinical images from the ISIC Archive on a single H100 GPU. These 200 test lesions, and every other photograph of the same lesion or patient, were removed from its data (including the validation set) before training, so it had never seen them, and they were not used to choose the model or set its threshold. It scored both images of each lesion, combined them with most of the weight on the dermoscopic image, and chose from the same six diagnoses.
You can try the CNN yourself . Remarkably the model is small enough to run entirely in a phone browser using WebGPU. Nothing is uploaded, and its random sample button draws from these same 200 lesions.
The CNN was right more often overall and on most diagnoses. Allowing a second choice, it reached 173 of 200 against 134 and 138. It named 13 of the 30 melanomas against 8 and 11. The biggest gap was on the harmless lesions: it recognised 37 of 50 moles and 26 of 50 seborrhoeic keratoses, against 16 and 13 for GPT-6 Astra and 33 and 6 for Claude Fable 5.1. It was one short of GPT-6 Astra on basal cell carcinoma and behind both LLMs on actinic keratosis.
The models also failed differently. Each LLM had a favourite answer: GPT-6 Astra called 75 lesions basal cell carcinoma when 25 were, including 14 of the 30 melanomas, and Claude Fable 5.1 called 53 lesions actinic keratosis when 20 were. The CNN’s errors on melanoma went the other way: of the 17 it got wrong, it called 8 a naevus and 6 a seborrhoeic keratosis.
Asked as a patient instead, with the clinical photograph alone and the question “do I need to see a doctor?”, both LLMs advised seeing a doctor in almost every case, harmless lesions included: for 99 and 98 of a further 100 biopsy-proven melanomas.
A small, old, specialised network using an outdated architecture recognises skin lesions far better than two frontier LLMs.
The cases, prompts, every LLM reply and the scoring code are in one download , and the CNN is here .
I designed the test and made the clinical rulings. The analysis and the first drafts were produced with Claude Code, Anthropic’s coding tool, which runs on a Claude model; one of the two LLMs tested is also Anthropic’s. Scoring was done by script against the histology.
Images are from the MILK10k dataset (MILK study team, International Skin Imaging Collaboration), used under a CC BY-NC licence.
Dr Magnus Lynch is a Consultant Dermatologist and Mohs Surgeon at Guy's Hospital and Honorary Reader (equivalent of Associate Professor) at King's College London. His clinical work covers skin cancer, Mohs and facial reconstructive surgery, and lasers; his research covers the cell biology of skin cancers and scars and the use of AI in dermatology. Full profile .
