title: 2026 U17 WWC: Nothing is tough for Black Maidens – Seidatu Wahab
body: Player of the Match, Seidatu Wahab, says the Black Maidens came into the Canada game with only one thing on their minds — victory. The midfield enforcer, who led by example in Ghana’s 2-0 win over Canada to send the Maidens into the Round of 16, admitted she has been down in recent matches but saved her best for the qualification decider. “I’m really excited. Lately, in my matches, I have been down, but this is the final game. Not the final, but this is the qualification match, so I have to bring my all out,” Wahab said. “The match was really tough, but I have to show I’m a leader. So, I brought all what I have in me. We really came for a win. That’s the only thing we came for. No draw, no loss, but a win.” The combative midfielder, who bossed the middle of the park against Canada, said the Maidens thrive under pressure. “It was really a tough game, but nothing is really tough for the Maidens,” she added. Wahab reserved special praise for her support system. “I would like to thank my best friend. Yeah, she’s the person I really thank, and my parents too. My teammates, they really helped me.” Wahab was named Player of the Match after Ghana’s 2-0 victory over Canada, with goals from Linda Achiaa and Christiana Ashiaku sealing Ghana’s place in the Round of 16 where they will face Argentina on Wednesday, October 28, 2026.

title: Carrick unsure over Man Utd future after Bournemouth loss
body: Michael Carrick said he will do what is best for Manchester United after a 3-0 demolition by Bournemouth plunged his future as manager into doubt on Sunday. Winless in eight games in all competitions, the 20-time English champions slipped to within one point of the relegation zone after a damaging defeat at Old Trafford. “It’s a tough situation,” Carrick told Sky Sports. “What is next? I don’t know. “I’ll always do what’s best for this football club. I’ve said it all along, I don’t change that now. I love what I do. I love the responsibility, but we’ll have to wait and see.” Despite a dismal run of results, the United fans largely supported Carrick as he made his way off the field at full-time before they turned on the club’s players. “I have mixed emotions to have that connection with the supporters in the moment we’re in. I need time to digest that,” added Carrick. “I appreciate their support but the situation is where it’s at. We haven’t been good enough.” Carrick’s decision to drop captain Bruno Fernandes to the bench and not even introduce the Portuguese international as a substitute backfired. Fernandes, last season’s Premier League player of the year, had criticised Carrick’s tactics after a 4-1 thrashing by Como on Wednesday. “There’s always times in games when you are trying to change the course of the game and to make a difference,” said Carrick as he swerved questions on Fernandes’s absence. “Those were the decisions we made today.” The post Carrick unsure over Man Utd future after Bournemouth loss appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Zamfara steps up Ebola containment measures after Passenger with 38°C fever arrives airport
body: The Zamfara State Government has intensified Ebola surveillance at Gusau airport, major motor parks and other entry points after a passenger arriving from Saudi Arabia was found with a body temperature of 38 degrees Celsius during screening. The passenger, an indigene of the state, was identified by health officials and referred for further medical assessment as part of measures to detect and respond promptly to suspected cases. The state Commissioner for Health, Nafisa Maradun, disclosed this while leading a medical team to inaugurate passenger screening at the airport. She said the government had deployed medical personnel to strategic locations, including the airport and major motor parks, to screen travellers and strengthen the early detection of potentially infectious diseases. Ebola: NCDC approves N100k weekly for each person in isolation Ebola: Nine fresh persons isolated as Number on watchlist hits 53 The surveillance measures are part of the state’s efforts to prevent the possible spread of Ebola following Nigeria’s confirmation of a case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) on October 20. The government said the screening exercise was designed to identify travellers who might require further medical evaluation and ensure that suspected cases were promptly referred to the appropriate health authorities. Maradun said the state was taking precautionary measures to protect residents and prevent the virus from spreading into Zamfara. She urged residents to remain calm, cooperate with health officials and support the government’s disease surveillance efforts. The commissioner’s disclosure comes amid heightened public health vigilance following the confirmation of Ebola in Nigeria, with health authorities across the country strengthening surveillance and preparedness to minimise the risk of further transmission. As part of the response, the Zamfara State Ministry of Health has directed public and private healthcare facilities, disease surveillance officers and local government health authorities to reinforce their preparedness measures. The directive requires health facilities to maintain vigilance for suspected cases, strengthen screening procedures and promptly report individuals who exhibit symptoms or have a relevant history of exposure. The government is also working with relevant agencies, including the Nigeria Customs Service and the Nigeria Immigration Service, to improve surveillance and coordination at entry points. The collaboration is intended to strengthen the identification of travellers who may require medical assessment and ensure that relevant authorities can respond quickly to potential public health threats. Transport operators and other workers in the transportation sector are also expected to support the surveillance exercise by identifying and reporting passengers who appear unwell or may require further medical attention. The state government said the combined measures were aimed at strengthening early detection, improving coordination among relevant agencies and preventing the potential spread of Ebola within Zamfara. However, a passenger presenting with a fever does not, by itself, confirm an Ebola infection. Further medical assessment is required to establish the cause of the elevated temperature.

title: CBD COP17: Nigeria, France Push for Faster Action on 30×30 Biodiversity Target
body:
Nigeria and France have called for stronger political leadership, increased financing and concrete commitments to accelerate the implementation of the global target to protect 30 per cent of the world’s land and seas by 2030.
The two countries made the call during a Target 3 Action Day at the ongoing 17th Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD COP17) in Yerevan, Armenia.
As co-chairs of the High Ambition Coalition (HAC) for Nature and People, the countries stressed the need to sustain political commitment and translate global biodiversity pledges into measurable conservation outcomes.
HAC is the largest multilateral coalition united to protect nature. With 123 member countries, the coalition is leading the historic effort to conserve and protect at least 30 per cent of the world’s land and 30 per cent of the ocean by the year 2030 (“30×30”).
This ambitious plan is a key target of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. Established in 2023, the permanent HAC for N&P Secretariat has made significant progress in supporting its members to implement this global target, aiming to halt and reverse biodiversity loss and put nature on a path to recovery.
Charles Nicolai, who spoke on behalf of the coalition, said political leadership must continue beyond adopting the target at CBD COP15 in Montreal, Canada.
“Political leadership did not end in Montreal, when Target 3 was adopted at CBD COP15. It must endure until the target has been collectively achieved,” he said.
Mr Nicolai warned that weak political commitment could slow implementation, adding that only four years remained to achieve the 2030 target.
“Where leadership falters, implementation slows. With only four years remaining until 2030, we cannot afford to lose momentum,” he said, expressing confidence that the 30×30 target remained achievable.
The 30×30 target is a central component of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework adopted in 2022. It calls on countries to ensure that by 2030, at least 30 per cent of terrestrial, inland water, coastal and marine areas are effectively conserved and managed.
Mr Nicolai said France had used its presidency of the Group of Seven (G7) this year to advance the effective management of marine protected areas.
He said G7 environment ministers agreed to make the issue a collective priority and established a dedicated platform to exchange knowledge and best practices to improve the management of protected marine areas.
In West Africa, he said, Nigeria had played a leading role in advocating for the 30×30 target, using its diplomatic influence to promote a coordinated approach to expanding and strengthening protected areas on land and at sea.
He added that the coalition had organised six regional and global consultations, with support from its secretariat, to identify measures needed to strengthen implementation.
The consultations, held through platforms including ChangeNOW, the Our Ocean Conference, and meetings of the Convention’s scientific subsidiary body, helped develop a 30×30 Ministerial Declaration.
According to Mr Nicolai, the declaration was designed to renew political leadership and encourage coalition members to make more ambitious commitments.
The coalition also presented the declaration and a 30×30 Global Assessment at a Nature Leaders event at the United Nations headquarters, attended by heads of state and ministers from several countries.
In her remarks, Sikeade Egbuwalo, Nigeria’s focal point person to the Convention on Biological Diversity, said achieving the target would require coordinated action across governments, communities, businesses and civil society.
She described the 30×30 ambition as more than a slogan, saying it represented a commitment to nature, people and future generations.
Ms Egbuwalo outlined six guiding principles underpinning the ministerial declaration:g collective responsibility, transparency, effective management, community participation, local implementation and adequate financing.
She said governments must demonstrate progress through transparent reporting, including submissions to the World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas and national reports to the CBD.
She also warned against treating the target as a numerical exercise, stressing that protected areas must be effectively managed, ecologically connected, representative and well governed.
“Quality matters just as much as quantity! It is not enough to draw lines on a map and declare victory,” she said.
Ms Egbuwalo further emphasised the need to ensure that Indigenous Peoples and local communities had meaningful roles in conservation decisions, noting their longstanding contributions to protecting nature.
She called for stronger national implementation and regional cooperation, including progress toward ratifying and implementing the Agreement on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas Beyond National Jurisdiction, known as the BBNJ Agreement.
Mrs Egbuwalo identified financing as a major requirement for achieving the 2030 target, particularly in developing countries.
“Ambition is wonderful, but ambition without resources will not get us very far,” she said, calling for adequate, accessible and timely funding to translate commitments into conservation outcomes.
She urged governments, development partners, businesses, civil society organisations and other stakeholders to sustain the momentum generated at COP17 beyond the conference.
Mrs Egbuwalo also announced that the coalition would work towards organising its first 30×30 Global Summit in 2027, providing another platform to assess progress and share successful conservation initiatives.
She said the initiative would bring together governments, non-governmental organisations, funders, Indigenous Peoples and local communities, businesses,s and other partners.
“30×30 is not a competition over who protects the most. It is a collective mission to ensure that nature wins — and when nature wins, humanity wins!”

title: Ebola: NCDC approves N100k weekly for each person in isolation
body: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has approved a weekly payment of N100,000 per person to support individuals placed under isolation or quarantine as part of efforts to contain the Ebola outbreak in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) . Briefing newsmen on Sunday in Abuja, Director-General of the NCDC, Dr Jide Idris, explained that the intervention was introduced to ease the financial burden on people identified as contacts of the confirmed case. According to Idris, some of the individuals under public health monitoring had raised concerns about the cost of feeding, accommodation and providing for their families while complying with the restrictions and monitoring arrangements. He said the financial assistance was considered necessary to ensure that those identified as contacts could cooperate with health officials without facing additional economic hardship. Ebola: Nine fresh persons isolated as Number on watchlist hits 53 Zamfara steps up Ebola containment measures after Passenger with 38°C fever arrives airport “We are paying for their accommodation; we are paying for their feeding. Some of them are asking for a stipend to maintain their families,” he said. The NCDC boss added that the agency had approved N100,000 weekly for each person requiring the support to cover essential needs during the monitoring period. “We are providing N100,000 per person per week just to maintain their comfort and feeding, because they were complaining,” Idris said. He explained that the intervention was not part of the agency’s initial response plan but became necessary in view of the challenges confronting people placed under public health monitoring. “This was not planned for, but it is an emergency. We will continue to review it as we go along,” he said. Idris noted that the arrangement would be reviewed as the outbreak response progressed, suggesting that the agency would assess the support based on prevailing circumstances and emerging needs. He also called for a broader approach to emergency preparedness, insisting that the responsibility for supporting people affected by public health emergencies should not rest solely on the FCT authorities. According to him, other states must also be prepared to provide similar assistance if they experience comparable outbreaks or public health emergencies. “This is not the responsibility of the FCT alone. What we have to do for the FCT, we have to do for any other state, just in case,” he said. The NCDC director-general stressed that state governments needed to make adequate financial and logistical provisions to support contact tracing, isolation arrangements and other activities required to contain infectious disease outbreaks. He said preparedness at the subnational level was essential to ensuring a coordinated response and preventing delays in the deployment of resources when emergencies occurred. The financial support comes amid intensified efforts by health authorities to prevent further transmission following the confirmation of an imported Ebola case in Abuja on October 20. At the time of the briefing, Idris said Nigeria had recorded one confirmed case, while 53 primary contacts had been identified for monitoring. The contacts include healthcare workers, members of the patient’s household, domestic staff and personnel involved in collecting samples from the patient. Health officials are categorising the contacts according to their level of exposure and conducting follow-up assessments to identify anyone who develops symptoms requiring further investigation. The NCDC said individuals under monitoring would be assessed promptly if they developed symptoms, with testing and other appropriate interventions provided where necessary. As part of the response, the agency has also established isolation arrangements for contacts who require them, while public health teams continue to monitor their health during the 21-day incubation period following their last possible exposure. The monitoring exercise is aimed at identifying potential infections early, interrupting possible chains of transmission and protecting healthcare workers and the wider public.

title: 2026 U17 WWC: Seidatu Wahab wins Player of the Match against Canada
body: Midfielder Seidatu Wahab was named Player of the Match after an outstanding performance in Ghana’s crucial 2-0 victory over Canada at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Wahab was the engine room of the Black Maidens side, breaking up play, winning duels, and keeping Ghana ticking with her composure on the ball. While goals from substitutes Linda Achiaa and Christiana Ashiaku grabbed the headlines, it was Wahab’s tireless work in midfield that allowed Ghana to dominate proceedings and secure the win that sent them through to the Round of 16. Partnering Jessica Appiah in the middle of the park, Wahab screened the back four superbly, denying Canada any space to play, and was instrumental in launching Ghana’s attacks. Her standout moment came in the first half with a perfectly timed last-ditch tackle to deny Canada a clear goalscoring opportunity, before playing a key role in the build-up to Ghana’s opener. The award caps a strong tournament for Wahab, who has grown in stature with each game, from the defeat to Norway, to the thrilling 3-3 draw with Brazil, and now the vital win over Canada. The Black Maidens will now turn their attention to the Round of 16, where Wahab will again be crucial to Coach Nana Joe Adarkwa’s plans.

title: Appeals court hears arguments in Trump admin's voting suit against California
body:
The three-judge panel included two Trump appointees and a Biden appointee.
A rare Sunday federal appeals court hearing for the Justice Department's voting lawsuit against California closed without a ruling.
The department requested that the court issue one by Tuesday prior to the scheduled 1 p.m. PDT hearing before the district court.
The arguments followed a surprise appeal by the Trump administration, which claims a district judge did not act quickly enough to address the administration's allegations of roughly 20,000 potential noncitizen voters on the state's voter rolls.
A three-judge panel that includes two appointees of President Donald Trump and one appointee of former President Joe Biden heard arguments on DOJ's efforts to segregate ballots from the alleged noncitizens.
California officials have countered that the list is unverified and includes the names of lawful voters , despite recent charges announced by DOJ of roughly 28 individuals from the list accused of voting and immigration-related crimes.
Earlier the DOJ sent letters last week to every county in California asking local elections officials to help identify potential voters who may be in the U.S. illegally, according to a letter described to ABC News.
"Within 48 hours, we ask that you commit to working with DOJ and DHS to identify who on the accompanying list is a citizen and who is not," according to a letter sent by Justice Department officials to every county in California and described to ABC News. "The Department strongly urges you and your agency to work with the Department of Justice to ensure the integrity of California's federal elections before taking actions that risk significant federal scrutiny and legal exposure."
Earlier this month, the DOJ filed suit against California accusing the state of failing to review a list of alleged noncitizens that the Trump administration claimed were sent mail-in ballots for next month's midterm election.
In court papers filed earlier this week, Los Angeles officials said a preliminary analysis of 200 of the names on the 20,000-person list, included a "high percentage" of individuals who say they were born in the U.S. and many more who have no voting history at all.
Of those 200 individuals, officials said, nearly 40% "indicate that they were born in the United States, which is strong evidence of citizenship; and 71.2% of the records have no voting history," according to a filing.
The Justice Department's rushed efforts to have an appeals court quickly rule on its lawsuit faced considerable skepticism from the three-judge panel in Sunday's emergency hearing.
Circuit Judge Mark Bennett, a Trump appointee, repeatedly questioned whether the appeals court had jurisdiction to step in at this stage in the litigation, and expressed considerable constitutional concerns over the lawsuit itself.
"I don't see how we have jurisdiction," Bennett said to DOJ attorney Matthew Donnelly after pressing him over the timeline of the government's decision to seeking emergency appeal when a hearing before the district judge is already set for this Tuesday.
Donnelly claimed that the DOJ's decision to seek relief from the appeals court came after disclosures by the state of the numbers of mail-in ballots already being processed in advance of the election -- which number in the hundreds of thousands.
But Bennett's most significant concerns appeared to be the nature of the lawsuit and it appearing to directly contradict the Constitution's Elections Clause -- which mandates that states have jurisdictions over the manner their elections are run.
"How can it preempt something that is expressly authorized by a provision of the Constitution?" Bennett asked. "How can the legislature making laws with regard to the manner of holding elections be preempted by a criminal statute passed by the Congress, especially when both the Congress and the California Legislature have made it illegal for non-citizens to vote?"
Donnelly repeatedly pointed to DOJ's position that the way California is administering its elections -- and not acting on the hard drive of potential 20,000 likely non-citizens -- infringes on the federal government's ability to enforce the federal statute barring voting by illegal immigrants.
That explanation didn't appear to sit well with Bennett, however, who pointed out that the Constitution specifically tasks Congress with jurisdiction over how states administer their elections and not the Judiciary.
"How can we, a federal court, do what is reserved to Congress, which Congress, in my view, hasn't done?" Bennett asked.
"Your Honor, I would just simply -- unfortunately -- disagree with you that 18 USC 611 is not an election law that fits in the power of Congress," Donnelly replied.
The judges also appeared to express concern about last-minute intervention to force California to segregate certain mail-in ballots given the state has provided a declaration saying if such an order was implemented it could have a "catastrophic" impact on tabulating the upcoming election.
Circuit Judge Patrick Bumatay, a Trump appointee, repeatedly pressed California's attorney Samuel Siegel over why an injunction wouldn't be appropriate to ensure non-citizens votes are being actively cast in the ongoing election.
"Without an injunction, you will never know, correct?" Bumatay asked. "Because if -- if the ballots are cast and separated, then they're going to be tabulated, and there's no way of knowing."
"Your Honor, we would respectfully disagree with that because of the number of steps that people have to take to attest to their citizenship, to declare consistent with what is required by both federal and state law that they are citizens when they register to vote," Siegel responded.
Even as Bumatay's questioning suggested he had more sympathy to granting the government some kind of relief, both Bennett and Circuit Judge Gabriel Sanchez, a Biden appointee, appeared unified that the extraordinary relief being sought by DOJ was not appropriate at this juncture.
"That's why I have a problem with the relief that's being sought here because I just don't see -- Congress and the California legislature have said non-citizens can't vote, and this lawsuit is about 'we don't like the way you're sorting citizens from non-citizens, and I just don't see 611 as telling California how to do the sorting," Bennett said.
"That's absolutely right, Your Honor, and to reiterate my earlier point, if the federal government, if the Executive Branch wants that authority in the first instance, they need to go ask Congress for it, they haven't done that," Siegel said. "They ask this court to short circuit the democratic process and issue an order, not just on the eve of an election, but as an election is underway."
In closing remarks, Bennett said the panel "will try to decide this case as quickly as possible."

title: IMF delegation assesses TOR’s rehabilitation and financial recovery efforts
body: A delegation from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) has visited the Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) to familiarise itself with the refinery’s operations, assess ongoing rehabilitation works and gain insight into management’s efforts to restore the facility to sustained operational and financial stability. The visit formed part of the IMF team’s engagements with relevant government authorities and selected state-owned enterprises in Ghana to gain a better understanding of their operations, financial positions, challenges and contributions to the national economy. The delegation was led by the IMF’s Ghana Resident Representative, Dr. Adrian Alter, while the TOR team was led by its Managing Director, Mr. Edmond Kombat, Esq. During a meeting with the delegation, Mr. Kombat outlined the operational and financial challenges inherited by the current management, as well as measures introduced since May 2025 to restore confidence in the refinery’s operations and revive its major processing plants. Addressing the delegation, Mr. Kombat emphasised that management had relied on internally generated funds to sustain the refinery’s operations since assuming office. “Since this new management took over, we have not received a dime from government. Every single thing is done through our internally generated funds,” Mr. Kombat said. He explained that management had prioritised financial discipline, operational improvements and the rehabilitation of critical facilities as part of efforts to reposition the refinery for long-term sustainability. Mr. Kombat disclosed that TOR was engaging the government over its outstanding debt obligations, with discussions focusing on possible restructuring and the reconciliation of historical financial commitments between the refinery and the state. According to him, TOR inherited a debt burden of approximately US$517 million, of which about US$120 million is owed to the government. “Out of the US$517 million debt we inherited, we owe about US$120 million to the government. We are trying to restructure our debt with the government,” he explained. The refinery is also engaging other state institutions to resolve outstanding financial obligations between TOR and the respective entities. Management is exploring possible netting-off arrangements to reconcile the obligations and establish the actual financial position of the parties involved. On the refinery’s financial performance, Mr. Kombat disclosed that TOR recorded a profit in the previous year, expressing optimism that the company could sustain profitability in the current and subsequent years. He attributed this positive outlook, in part, to improved macroeconomic stability and ongoing efforts to strengthen the refinery’s operational and financial position. As part of its long-term strategy, management is considering a potential listing of TOR on the Ghana Stock Exchange to attract investment and provide additional capital for the refinery’s operations and expansion. Mr. Kombat explained that a stock market listing could create opportunities for Ghanaian institutions and other investors to acquire shares in the company, providing an additional avenue for raising funds to support its recovery and growth. The IMF delegation also sought clarification on the volume of crude oil processed by TOR, particularly supplies sourced from Ghana’s domestic oil fields. In response, Mr. Kombat indicated that the refinery had processed approximately five million barrels of crude oil, including about two million barrels sourced from Ghanaian fields, with the remainder coming from external sources. He explained that TOR’s first domestic crude supply came from the Jubilee field through a transaction with Vitol, which was fully paid for. He also acknowledged the contribution of the Ghana National Petroleum Corporation (GNPC), which supplied its share of Ghana’s crude allocation to the refinery. “Our first domestic crude came from the Jubilee field through Vitol, and it was fully paid for. GNPC also gave us its portion of Ghana’s allocation,” Mr. Kombat stated. He further noted that Ghana produces approximately 38 million barrels of crude oil annually, with about 11 million barrels representing the government’s share. The Managing Director expressed hope that GNPC would make its full crude allocation available to TOR for refining by the following year. He said this would improve feedstock availability and support more consistent refinery operations. The delegation also sought to understand the impact of TOR’s resumption of operations on the Ghanaian economy and consumers. In response, Mr. Kombat highlighted the refinery’s contribution to domestic petroleum product availability, price stability, and the country’s ability to withstand disruptions in international petroleum markets. He explained that domestic refining could help reduce Ghana’s exposure to external supply shocks, particularly during periods of geopolitical tension and uncertainty in global oil markets, including the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. He also acknowledged government interventions aimed at cushioning consumers against the effects of changes in petroleum prices, noting the importance of maintaining a reliable domestic supply of petroleum products. Highlighting the refinery’s commercial potential, Mr. Kombat drew attention to TOR’s tank farm, storage infrastructure and product distribution network. He indicated that TOR has approximately one million metric tonnes of storage capacity, which is three times the capacity of the Bulk Oil Storage and Transportation Company (BOST). The Managing Director further explained that TOR is connected to eight privately operated depots, enabling the refinery to pump petroleum products directly to those facilities. He said these arrangements provide additional revenue opportunities for the refinery, alongside other commercial activities, including laboratory services for petroleum product testing. The discussions also covered corporate governance and financial accountability, particularly efforts to clear a six-year backlog of unaudited accounts. Mr. Kombat explained that the Ghana Audit Service had undertaken the audit exercise to address the six-year backlog of outstanding accounts. He added that management intended to appoint an external audit firm at the refinery’s next Annual General Meeting (AGM) to undertake subsequent audits. KPMG had previously conducted audit assignments for the company. The Managing Director also briefed the delegation on improvements in financial reporting and internal controls, staff-related reforms, and measures to sustain crude supply for continued operations. He noted that these initiatives formed part of a broader management strategy to improve accountability, strengthen financial discipline and enhance operational efficiency. The IMF team was further briefed on ongoing efforts to increase the refinery’s processing capacity, rehabilitate other critical units and restore facilities required to support more reliable operations. These interventions are intended to strengthen TOR’s contribution to Ghana’s energy security, improve its financial sustainability and position it to play a more significant role in the country’s petroleum value chain. Following the discussions, the delegation toured parts of the refinery to observe rehabilitated facilities and ongoing engineering works. The tour provided the IMF team with an opportunity to gain first-hand insight into TOR’s operational environment, the progress made under the current management and the work that remains to be completed. Members of the delegation expressed appreciation for the engagement and the opportunity to gain a better understanding of the refinery’s operations and recovery efforts. The visit also provided a platform for TOR management to outline the measures being pursued to restore critical infrastructure, improve financial performance and strengthen the refinery’s contribution to Ghana’s energy security. The Tema Oil Refinery remains Ghana’s premier refinery, serving customers within the country and beyond its borders.

title: World Is on Track for Up to 2.8 Degrees of Warming Despite Clean Energy Boom
body:
Blackstone-Led Investors Buy into LNG Canada for $3.1 Billion
Haley Zaremba is an energy journalist and researcher with more than a decade of professional experience covering global energy systems, land and natural resources, and…
The United Nations says that it is now an inevitability that the world will fail to meet the legally binding goals set forth by the Paris climate accord as a result of “ decades of insufficient climate action ”. The Paris Agreement, ratified in 2015, targeted limiting global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial averages, with a fallback target of 2?, with the understanding that this looser allowance would lead to far more devastating consequences for global ecosystems, human health, the economy, and future generations. As it stands today, not only are we on track to blow past 2 degrees, but will likely reach 2.6? and 2.8? by the end of the century.
A new bombshell report from the United Nations Environmental Program (UNEP) is a call to action, finding that while the 1.5? target is no longer in reach, there is still plenty that global leaders can do to avoid the worst impacts of climate change. The annual report, optimistically titled The Point of Return, finds that there is “ample opportunity to accelerate action”, and concludes that “countries can still limit peak warming, shorten the duration of overshoot and keep the goals of the Paris Agreement within reach”.
This report is coming out against the backdrop of the fastest buildout of clean energy resources in human history. Catalyzed by back-to-back oil and gas affordability crises stemming from the wars in Ukraine and Iran, the global clean energy transition is going gangbusters as we speak. Renewable energy sources now have a larger share of the global energy mix than coal, and one in four new cars sold last year was an electric vehicle, avoiding the consumption of 1.2 million barrels of oil a day .
The problem is that while this is all great news for climate change mitigation, it may very well be too little, too late. “The scale and speed of the transition has been far too slow to arrest global warming as climate pollution continues to build up in the atmosphere,” Politico wrote this week in a report entitled “ Clean Energy Isn’t Fixing Climate Change ”. The report goes on to highlight that, based on figures from the UNEP report, “emissions from fossil fuel use increased last year and methane remained stagnant, despite commitments by countries and companies to quickly curb the potent pollutant.”
Plus all the clean energy we can add may not be enough without also improving energy efficiency and creating tighter regulations for consumption. While clean energy production capacity is expanding rapidly, so too is energy demand, driven by the artificial intelligence boom in the Global North and economic and human development in the Global South.
What is more, the proliferation of clean energy as an energy security strategy has become a double-edged sword. Renewables are growing faster than ever before, even in the poorest parts of the world, because countries see them as the cheapest and most secure pathway to energy independence in an era of extreme geopolitical turmoil and out-of-control fossilflation . In short, clean energy development is no longer about climate; it’s about security.
“Wind and solar cannot be embargoed, blockaded, or shut off by a foreign power,” David Frykman, General Partner at Stockholm-based venture capital group Norrsken, wrote in an op-ed for Fortune earlier this year. “Every terawatt-hour of domestic renewable generation is a terawatt-hour that no adversary can weaponize.”
While this is great for the growth of the global renewable energy sector, it means that clean energy goals have become completely divested from climate goals – and that could be a major issue for the Paris Agreement targets, which will require enormous global effort and investment for the future and the greater good, not the here and now and the bottom line.
“For years, clean energy has been sold as a moral imperative. Now it is simply an economic and geopolitical necessity,” Forbes reported earlier this year. “It’s not about emissions. It’s about resilience and price stability.” But in order to seize the point of return, it needs to be about both.

title: This Switch 2 sequel accessory was a few millimeters away from being good
body:
The Crkd Nitro Deck was a saving grace for the original Nintendo Switch. The slide-on $59.99 accessory brought Hall effect sticks to drift-plagued consoles — no need to open up your Joy-Con for a complicated repair. The Nitro Deck 2, made for both the original Switch and the larger Switch 2, continues the tradition of having better sticks than what Nintendo puts in even the newest Joy-Con (though these aren’t Hall effect or TMR). But it doesn’t feel as essential, and there’s one thing I really can’t stand about it.
It’s too difficult to use the Nitro Deck 2’s ABXY face buttons without the right stick getting in the way. The stick-to-button arrangement is a big step down from the original Nitro Deck (and especially bad compared with the symmetrical Steam Deck-like stick layout in the video output-ready Nitro Deck Plus). I’m surprised Crkd’s team thought this was an improvement. My patience with the run-based gameplay in Echo Weaver is already tested enough, and trying to quickly hammer inputs on the Deck 2 only adds to the frustration.
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/crkd3_c5cc23.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/crkd2.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
Your preference may differ, but I like having a little breathing room between the right stick and the face buttons. Some companies choose to space them out or, in the case of the Switch 2’s Joy-Con, make the stick small enough to allow my thumb to hover over it so I can press the buttons. The Deck 2 makes me adjust my thumb’s angle of approach outside of what’s comfortable. It’s just a few millimeters off.
The original’s superior slide-in design was traded for a vice-grip design to ensure compatibility with both the newer and older Switch consoles. The Deck 2 has a twisting mechanism on the back that you can loosen, tighten, or lock. It’s clever, though the tradeoff for broader compatibility is a design that feels inherently less secure. Crkd is asking Switch 2 owners to put a ton of faith in this mechanism staying tight around their $500 consoles. My Switch 2 didn’t feel wobbly during testing, but I’d rather not have to think about its safety at all when I’m gaming. I would have preferred a slide-in design for the Deck 2 made expressly for the Switch 2.
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/crkd5_abfa71.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/crkd6_af3db3.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
It’s disappointing that Crkd’s Joy-Con-replacing solution isn’t as good because I like some things about it more than the original. For instance, the accessory has adjustable tension on both sticks, so they can snap back to their original position faster or slower than the default speed. Also, the accessory’s bulkier design makes the console more comfortable in my medium-size hands to use in handheld mode. It also has a bunch of customizable buttons: four on its back and an extra near the triggers.
Not many similar accessories are out there yet, and the other one I tried (the abxylute N6) wasn’t all that good, either. I plan to test Mobapad’s latest take on Joy-Con soon, and it seems promising. Alternatively, you can add a bunch of comfort to your Switch 2 in handheld mode with either the Dbrand Killswitch 2 or the Mechanism Basecase. And with the money left over, you could buy a good wireless Switch 2 controller with long-lasting sticks and better rumble.
[Product: Crkd Nitro Deck 2 | https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0G6MNCNSG?tag=theverge02-20, https://crkd.gg/products/nitro-deck-2-smoke-black-edition]
Photography by Cameron Faulkner / The Verge

title: Netanyahu's final campaign strategy: Fear - opinion
body: Benjamin Netanyahu has entered the scorched-earth phase of his election campaign. It is a familiar ritual for Israelis, one that almost always comes in the final days before an election. And the message is always the same: I am the only person who can protect Israel. Without me, the country will fall apart. Without me, Israel will be destroyed. You need me.The talk last week about a possible new military operation against Iran was just the preview. The real campaign began on Friday.In an interview on Channel 10, Netanyahu warned that Israel could soon face unprecedented international banking sanctions and that he was already working on ways to circumvent them using blockchain technology and cryptocurrency.The comments sent shock waves through Israel's financial establishment. Even the Bank of Israel issued an unusually harsh statement, rejecting the idea that cryptocurrency could provide a way around sanctions. The central bank made an obvious point: The best way to deal with sanctions is to prevent them in the first place, not to look for ways to bypass them.But Netanyahu was just getting started.On Saturday night, he released a video warning that Iran had resumed its nuclear program, wanted to destroy Israel, and that the country's very survival was at stake in Tuesday's election. If Israelis wanted to stop Iran, he said, they needed to listen to US President Donald Trump and vote for Netanyahu.Netanyahu's message: If you want Israel to survive, vote BibiThen came Sunday afternoon. Netanyahu shared an AI-generated image of a mushroom cloud rising over Tel Aviv after a nuclear explosion, accompanied by a warning that if Iran obtains a nuclear weapon, nothing else will matter.The message could not be clearer. If you want Israel to survive, vote Netanyahu. If you are willing to risk the country's destruction, whether through financial collapse brought on by international sanctions or a nuclear explosion over Tel Aviv, then go ahead and vote for someone else.This is Netanyahu's election strategy in its most naked form: Fear.Let's be clear. Iran poses a genuine and serious threat to Israel. The danger of international sanctions is also real. These are challenges that any Israeli government will have to confront. But there is a difference between confronting threats and exploiting them, between preparing the public for difficult decisions and deliberately frightening people into believing that the survival of their country depends on one man.And that is precisely what Netanyahu is doing.This is electioneering at its worst. It is fear-mongering dressed up as national security. It is the familiar Netanyahu playbook of trying to scare Israelis into submission, convincing them to vote not out of confidence in his leadership or support for his policies, but out of fear of what might happen without him.The tragedy is that this strategy has worked before. Netanyahu knows it, which is why he keeps returning to it.But Israelis should know better by now. After October 7, after everything this country has endured, the idea that any one politician has a monopoly on protecting Israel should be dismissed.Israel existed before this prime minister, and it will exist after him. Its survival does not depend on one politician, one party, or one election.

title: AI delivers ‘zero financial payoff’ to most companies, Apollo economist says
body:
AI hasn’t benefited the bottom line of any big corporations outside the tech industry, according to a note recently published by the chief economist at Apollo Global Management (the private equity giant that used to own TechCrunch).
Apollo’s Torsten Slok focuses on what he calls the S&P 493 — the S&P 500, minus Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, and Tesla — finding that profit margins and revenue per worker appear to be flat, with no evidence that AI is improving productivity.
“Despite massive investments and widespread hype around artificial intelligence, the technology has delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside of tech,” Slok said.
Is this simply a matter of non-tech companies lagging behind the tech giants? Slok sounded skeptical, arguing that it will be tough for corporate America to “turn increasingly cheap intelligence into higher revenue growth and higher profit margins.”
“AI may be a great calculator, but in business, intelligence is mostly judgment,” he wrote, later adding, “AI does not understand accountability, trust, culture, unwritten rules, ethical trade-offs or fairness, all of which shape reputational risk and ultimately drive revenue growth and profit margins.”
Recent studies have also found that AI has yet to deliver significant productivity gains .

title: Power Out, Flight Cancelled As Storm Boelo Hits UK
body: Tens of thousands of homes were without power Sunday as Storm Boelo battered northern parts of the United Kingdom with strong winds and heavy rain, disrupting travel services. Boelo is Britain’s second named storm of the season and quickly follows the first — Storm Austen, which brought strong gusts to southern areas of the country on Friday. More than 82,000 properties had no electricity as of 8:00 am (0800 GMT), industry body the Energy Networks Association said in an update. It added that almost 350,000 customers had been reconnected since Austen hit. An amber wind warning was in place in Scotland, where collapsed trees, fallen cables and damaged surfaces prompted road and railway track closures. Winds gusts peaked at 84 mph (135 kmh) in Argyll and Bute in western Scotland, according to the Met Office weather agency. Scotland was also under a yellow rain warning, along with northern England, with up to 80 milimetres expected in some areas, bringing a chance of flooding. Also affected was Northern Ireland, where several flights out of Belfast were cancelled. There were also cancellations to some ferry services across the Irish Sea between Belfast and northwest England. The Met warned that Boelo brings a danger to life from flying debris and crashing waves and that people should stay indoors as much as possible. title: Igboho seeks wider security role for traditional rulers
body: …unveils 20,000 Iru Ekun volunteers in Oyo …links Abuja trip to strengthening regional security network By Adeola Badru Yoruba nation activist, Chief Sunday Adeyemo, popularly known as Sunday Igboho, has called for a stronger security role for traditional rulers across the South-West, declaring that the Iru Ekun Security Network, which he described as the brainchild of the region’s traditional institutions, has attracted 20,000 volunteers in Oyo State. Igboho made the declaration on Sunday at the launch of the network at the popular Mapo Hall in Ibadan, where he explained that his recent visit to Abuja was aimed at strengthening the organisation’s security responsibilities and expanding its effectiveness in protecting communities. The development was on the heels of the persistent security concerns across Nigeria, including abductions, killings and other criminal activities, which have placed renewed emphasis on cooperation between traditional institutions, local communities and conventional security agencies. According to a statement issued by Igboho’s media office, no fewer than 20,000 volunteers joined the organisation in Oyo State, with its operational reach extending across Yorubaland and parts of Kwara and Niger states. The statement said the Oyo launch followed similar inaugurations in Osun, Ekiti, Lagos, Ogun and Ondo states, alongside engagements with traditional rulers and community leaders. It added that the organisation had collaborated with the Nigerian Army, the Nigeria Police Force, the Department of State Services (DSS) and other security agencies to tackle abductions, killings and other forms of insecurity, particularly in the South-West. Commending the turnout at the Ibadan launch, Igboho said the participation of the volunteers demonstrated the willingness of residents to contribute to the safety of their communities, regardless of ethnic, religious or political differences. “The impressive development represents a milestone which indicates genuine interest of Oyo people in active participation to ensure safety and security of residents, irrespective of tribes, religion and political affiliations,” he said. Explaining the purpose of his Abuja trip, Igboho said the engagement was aimed at advancing the responsibilities of the security network, which he maintained was established through the initiative of traditional rulers in the South-West. “I was in Abuja this morning so that Iru Ekun’s security responsibilities can be further strengthened.“ “This is because Iru Ekun is the brain child of South West traditional rulers and it will continue to serve its purpose for the peace and effective security of our communities,” he said. He disclosed that the trip followed an invitation he received the previous night and linked the engagement to his collaboration with the Olubadan of Ibadanland. “I received the call last night to come to Abuja. My Abuja trip was as a result of the collaboration with our traditional ruler, the Olubadan of Ibadanland,” he stated. Igboho also expressed gratitude to God for what he described as protection against banditry, while acknowledging the contributions of traditional rulers to peace and security across the country. “Firstly I want to thank Almighty God who has all powers, owns us, preserves us. The God that says we won’t be overcomed by bandits. We thank God,” he said. He added: “After that, we thank all traditional rulers in Nigeria and may God grant them a long life.” The activist subsequently commended President Bola Tinubu, whom he credited with providing a platform for members of the initiative to interact and pursue their security objectives. “We are also paying homage to the person, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, who provided this platform so that we can interact as Iru Ekun members,” he said. Addressing the volunteers, Igboho expressed concern over what he described as the contemptuous attitude of some people towards them, predicting that their efforts would eventually attract recognition. “Some people are still taking a despicable look at you (Volunteers). Soon they will lobby you for positions,” he remarked. Meanwhile, Igboho urged Nigerians, including members of the Iru Ekun Security Network, to support Tinubu’s re-election bid and vote for the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the forthcoming January presidential election. title: Isak Scores As Liverpool Defeat Brighton
body: Alexander Isak extended his hot streak in Liverpool’s 2-0 win against Brighton on Sunday as Reds boss Andoni Iraola savoured his first Premier League victory at Anfield. Iraola’s side struck twice in quick succession in the first half, with Pascal Gross’s own goal followed by Isak’s latest strike. Isak has netted six times in seven league games this season and has three goals in his last four matches. After a turbulent debut season following his acrimonious move from Newcastle, the Sweden striker is finally beginning to repay his £125 million ($167 million) fee. It was a welcome first taste of top-flight success at Anfield for Iraola, who had failed to win his first three league games on Merseyside since arriving from Bournemouth in the close season. The Spaniard, who had won Champions League and League Cup games at Anfield, has led Liverpool to four successive victories in all competitions since the chastening 3-0 home defeat against Manchester City. Liverpool have climbed to fourth place, just one point behind third-placed Brighton after inflicting the high-flying Seagulls’ second league loss this term. The Reds are six points behind leaders City as they eye a potential title challenge. Liverpool were winless in their previous five home league matches dating back to last season, drawing four times and losing once. But they put Brighton to the sword in composed fashion, stopping the visitors’ recent goal blitz after they arrived at Anfield as the league’s top scorers. Brighton should have taken an early lead when Diego Gomez’s pass caught out Virgil van Dijk and Gross crossed to Yasin Ayari, who fired wastefully over with the goal at his mercy. Rampant Reds Liverpool took full advantage of that escape to open the scoring in the 17th minute. Ronald Araujo’s buccaneering run and cross into the Brighton area picked out Florian Wirtz for a powerful strike that took a hefty deflection off Gross as it whistled into the bottom corner. Cody Gakpo nearly doubled Liverpool’s lead moments later with a rising drive that Bart Verbruggen tipped over. Liverpool were rampant and it was no surprise when Isak bagged their second goal in the 21st minute. Iraola opted for Bradley Barcola and Gakpo on the flanks despite Rio Ngumoha’s virtuoso performance in the midweek win against Villarreal. And Barcola repaid that faith when he sprinted onto a long pass from Reds keeper Alisson Becker and guided a cross into Isak for a clinical close-range finish. Isak has scored in three consecutive league appearances for the first time since January 2025 for Newcastle. He was denied a fourth by Lewis Dunk’s last-ditch block after the Sweden striker took aim from Wirtz’s pass. Liverpool kept pushing and Araujo’s blast forced a superb save from Verbruggen just before half-time. The announcement that Liverpool’s troubled rivals Manchester United were losing to Bournemouth brought huge cheers from the Kop at the interval. It was that kind of day for Liverpool, who comfortably held their lead in the second half despite losing Wirtz to an injury. Iraola’s men are hitting their stride after an inconsistent start to the season. Now come a pair of intriguing tests as Chelsea visit Anfield in the League Cup fourth round on Wednesday before second-placed Arsenal arrive for a crucial clash on November 1. title: Hugging Face Releases Carbon-X, a 14B Open DNA Language Model that Brings DNA and Natural Language Together for the First Time
body:
Hugging Face has released Carbon-X , an open DNA language model with 14.8B parameters. Carbon-X is a decoder-only model from Hugging Face Bio. It reads raw DNA in a chat and answers in English. It predicts whether mutations are benign or pathogenic, flags regulatory regions, classifies organisms and predicts next bases. The weights ship under Apache 2.0, so labs can keep sensitive sequences on their own GPUs. Hugging Face built it with Zhongguancun Academy and TIGEM / University of Naples Federico II. TL;DR Size: 14.8B parameters (dense, no MoE), 40,960-token context. Runs on: 1 x 80 GB GPU in bfloat16 via vLLM or Transformers. Official GGUF: Q8_0 is 15.8 GB, Q4_K_M is 9.6 GB. Performance: 66.7% average on 5 DNA benchmarks, best of every open model tested (self-reported). Best: 74.9% on BioReason Coding, ahead of every model tested, open or closed. Worst: 29.8% on GenomeQA splice-site questions. What is Carbon-X and how does it work? Carbon-X starts from Qwen3-14B . DNA and text share 1 token stream in 1 decoder. There is no separate DNA encoder, unlike earlier work such as BioReason . The key structure piece is a hybrid tokenizer. It keeps Qwen3’s BPE vocabulary for text and adds 5,515 DNA tokens. These include 4,096 non-overlapping 6-mers, 1,364 tail tokens and 3 markers. One DNA token covers 6 base pairs. DNA runs of 6 or more A/C/G/T bases are tagged automatically. The backbone is a standard Qwen3 stack. It has 40 layers, hidden size 5120 and GQA with 8 KV heads. How was Carbon-X trained? Training ran in four stages, per the model card : Embedding warmup: about 10B tokens with the transformer frozen, so only the new DNA embeddings learn. Mid-training: 302B tokens at 8,192 sequence length. The mix is 55% raw DNA, 20% English, 15% biology text and 10% instruction data. SFT: 3 epochs over 20 dataset subsets, with responses checked by deterministic verifiers built with domain experts. RL: asynchronous GRPO with verifiable rewards over 2 rounds, using TRL and vLLM. As per the release post, learning rate was the hardest knob. High rates learned DNA but forgot English. A lower rate, a 14B model and a long run fixed the trade-off. RL applied directly to Qwen3-14B never beat the 50% chance baseline on FrontierVEP. How does Carbon-X perform on DNA benchmarks? All scores are self-reported by Hugging Face. Carbon-X ran with thinking disabled. Competitors ran at their best reasoning effort. Benchmark Carbon-X GPT-6.1 Sol (Max) Opus 5.5 (Max) Kimi K3 (Low) BioReason Coding 74.9 71.0 70.3 53.9 BioReason Non-SNV 85.1 91.7 94.8 65.3 GenomeQA 63.6 67.2 62.2 52.0 NextBase 39.4 32.9 1.1 30.6 FrontierVEP 70.4 74.9 76.2 50.1 Average 66.7 67.5 60.9 50.4 Carbon-X sits 27 points above Qwen3-14B and 0.8 points below GPT-6.1 Sol. It leads on coding-variant effects and next-base prediction. Frontier models still win on complex variants and single-base variants. Refusals shape these numbers. On NextBase, Opus 5.5 falls from 17.7% at low effort to 1.1% at max effort as refusals rise. Gemini 4 Argon drops from 58% to 38% on FrontierVEP as effort increases. Carbon-X also keeps general skills: 79.3% prompt-level strict accuracy on IFEval. Tokenize

title: Isak extends hot streak as Liverpool sink Brighton
body: Alexander Isak extended his hot streak in Liverpool’s 2-0 win against Brighton on Sunday as Reds boss Andoni Iraola savoured his first Premier League victory at Anfield. Iraola’s side struck twice in quick succession in the first half, with Pascal Gross’s own goal followed by Isak’s latest strike. Isak has netted six times in seven league games this season and has three goals in his last four matches. After a turbulent debut season following his acrimonious move from Newcastle, the Sweden striker is finally beginning to repay his £125 million ($167 million) fee. It was a welcome first taste of top-flight success at Anfield for Iraola, who had failed to win his first three league games on Merseyside since arriving from Bournemouth in the close season. The Spaniard, who had won Champions League and League Cup games at Anfield, has led Liverpool to four successive victories in all competitions since the chastening 3-0 home defeat against Manchester City. Liverpool have climbed to fourth place, just one point behind third-placed Brighton after inflicting the high-flying Seagulls’ second league loss this term. The Reds are six points behind leaders City as they eye a potential title challenge. Liverpool were winless in their previous five home league matches dating back to last season, drawing four times and losing once. But they put Brighton to the sword in composed fashion, stopping the visitors’ recent goal blitz after they arrived at Anfield as the league’s top scorers. Brighton should have taken an early lead when Diego Gomez’s pass caught out Virgil van Dijk and Gross crossed to Yasin Ayari, who fired wastefully over with the goal at his mercy. – Rampant Reds – Liverpool took full advantage of that escape to open the scoring in the 17th minute. Ronald Araujo’s buccaneering run and cross into the Brighton area picked out Florian Wirtz for a powerful strike that took a hefty deflection off Gross as it whistled into the bottom corner. Cody Gakpo nearly doubled Liverpool’s lead moments later with a rising drive that Bart Verbruggen tipped over. Liverpool were rampant and it was no surprise when Isak bagged their second goal in the 21st minute. Iraola opted for Bradley Barcola and Gakpo on the flanks despite Rio Ngumoha’s virtuoso performance in the midweek win against Villarreal. And Barcola repaid that faith when he sprinted onto a long pass from Reds keeper Alisson Becker and guided a cross into Isak for a clinical close-range finish. Isak has scored in three consecutive league appearances for the first time since January 2025 for Newcastle. He was denied a fourth by Lewis Dunk’s last-ditch block after the Sweden striker took aim from Wirtz’s pass. Liverpool kept pushing and Araujo’s blast forced a superb save from Verbruggen just before half-time. The announcement that Liverpool’s troubled rivals Manchester United were losing to Bournemouth brought huge cheers from the Kop at the interval. It was that kind of day for Liverpool, who comfortably held their lead in the second half despite losing Wirtz to an injury. Iraola’s men are hitting their stride after an inconsistent start to the season. Now come a pair of intriguing tests as Chelsea visit Anfield in the League Cup fourth round on Wednesday before second-placed Arsenal arrive for a crucial clash on November 1. The post Isak extends hot streak as Liverpool sink Brighton appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: No plans for striking Iran on October 25 — Trump
body:
WASHINGTON, October 25. /TASS/. The United States will not strike Iran on October 25, US President Donald Trump said.
"The answer is no. There will not be a strike today," he told reporters responding to a corresponding question.
Earlier, when asked by blogger Mario Nawfal if a strike on Iran was possible this weekend, US Ambassador to Turkey and special envoy for Syria Tom Barrack said: "Absolutely." Later, Trump refuted his envoy’s statement.

title: Israel must confront double standards in Hebron security, accountability - opinion
body: I reject all armed attacks, and I believe that security for Israelis and dignity for Palestinians must form the foundation of any shared future. That position also compels me to ask: Why does an entire Palestinian city become the target of sweeping military measures after a single attack, while we see no equally determined response to protect Palestinians from repeated settler attacks?Events in Hebron following the October 23 attack make this question urgent. Reports of closures, families forced to leave their homes, raids and demolitions describe measures whose impact extends beyond the perpetrators, affecting large sections of the population and their daily lives.In my assessment, the speed and scale of this response reveal a political template ready for implementation, activated after Friday's attack: expanding responsibility from the perpetrator to those around him, then to the neighborhood and the city, and turning civilian life into an instrument of pressure.This is a political interpretation of the pattern of response, rather than a claim to possess a document proving that the operation's details were prepared in advance. The question this pattern raises is whether the objective is to pursue those responsible for the attack or to subjugate an entire community by making it bear the consequences.A double standard in responding to attacks on Palestinian civiliansThat question becomes even more pressing when we compare this response with the treatment of settler violence.When Palestinian civilians are killed in attacks, their property is burned, or their communities are assaulted, where is the mobilization to ensure their protection? Where are the effective, sustained measures to prevent further attacks and bring those responsible to trial?I reject collective punishment, whether directed at Hebron's residents or at the residents of settlements from which attackers targeting Palestinians emerge. I demand one standard: Pursue the perpetrator, protect the victim, and do not hold civilians responsible for crimes they did not commit.The fact that some settlers have been arrested does not, by itself, answer this question. The measure of a law enforcement system is its ability to prevent attacks, investigate them, and hold perpetrators accountable. The problem lies in the persistent gap between the scale of the violence and the effectiveness of deterrence and accountability.In its reports, the Israeli organization Yesh Din has linked settler violence against Palestinians to the settlement expansion project and described the support this violence receives from state institutions. These findings deserve serious scrutiny and accountability.In my view, this disparity reflects a deliberate political approach that has become entrenched in practice: tolerance of settler violence that pressures Palestinians to leave, alongside the use of extensive force and measures affecting entire communities when violence comes from the Palestinian side.The political consequence of this tolerance is clear: Remaining on their land becomes more difficult for Palestinians, while the settlement presence expands. When this pattern repeats itself, it becomes difficult to treat it as a series of security failures disconnected from politics.The result is two systems of protection and accountability operating on the same land, with their effectiveness varying according to the identity of the perpetrator and the victim.Protecting lives in the West BankAnother aspect of this contradiction appears in the way the West Bank is presented within Israel's statistical framework. Israeli tables covering the population of Israeli localities there count settlers, who number roughly half a million, while the millions of Palestinians living on the same land fall outside that population category.This statistical distinction reflects the scope of those tables. It does not mean that Palestinians are not counted by other bodies, nor does it establish, on its own, the existence of a discriminatory security policy.But it raises a deeper question about the exercise of authority: Do the Israeli military and security institutions regard Palestinians as residents whose rights and needs require protection, or primarily as subjects of surveillance and control?Palestinians exist, and they have a clear legal status and rights. Under the law of occupation, Israel has obligations toward them, such as protecting them from violence, including settler violence, and maintaining public order and civilian life. Those obligations do not disappear because Palestinians lack Israeli citizenship.The issue, therefore, is the responsibility of an authority legally obliged to provide protection, and the need to hold it accountable when it fails to fulfill that duty or applies it selectively.Any system that exercises military control over land, roads, and people's movement, while providing effective protection to one population and leaving another exposed to attack, creates a crisis that goes beyond an isolated security failure. It makes identity a decisive factor in determining who enjoys safety and whose life is restricted in the name of someone else's security.As a Palestinian who advocates dialogue and a democratic, demilitarized Palestinian state alongside Israel, I see this reality as a danger to the future of both peoples. We ask young Palestinians to believe in peaceful political action. That choice needs tangible results and confidence that the rights, lives, and property of those who embrace it will be protected.When a peaceful Palestinian cannot protect his home from an attack or reach his workplace because of a measure imposed on him despite his having no connection to any attack, the credibility of the path we urge him to follow is weakened.In Masar Jadid – New Path – our guiding message is “From confrontation to dialogue.” We work for politics that improve people's lives, institutions that protect them, and accountability for perpetrators, whoever they may be.The people of Hebron deserve protection, freedom of movement, and a life of dignity. So do Palestinians exposed to settler attacks throughout the West Bank.The true test of any policy claiming to deliver security is its ability to protect civilians and hold those responsible for violence accountable under one standard. Security for Israelis will not be sustainable as long as Palestinians living under Israeli control are denied effective and equal protection.

title: Audi defends plans for a $4 billion Georgia plant amid VW restructuring, tariffs
body:
DETROIT — Audi's CEO defended the carmaker's plans for a new $4 billion plant in Georgia on Sunday, calling it a business decision aimed at growing sales and reducing exposure to U.S. tariffs.
The plant, set to be Audi's first in the U.S., was announced Saturday by President Donald Trump during a rally in Georgia, near where the Volkswagen -owned luxury brand plans to build the new SUV-producing facility.
"We have significantly greater ambitions for Audi in America," Audi CEO Gernot Dollner said during a media roundtable Sunday. "The United States is the second largest premium market in the world, and today we are not fully exploiting this potential. We are changing that."
The announcement comes amid an intense restructuring of its VW parent company, including plans to cut 50,000 jobs and close four German plants , including an Audi facility, between 2031 and ​2034.
Dollner, who joined Trump at the rally, said the decision for a plant in the U.S. was years in the making, with more than 70 locations evaluated over "many months" and "intense" negotiations with public officials.
"This is not a decision against Germany. Germany remains the backbone of Audi," Dollner said. "We develop our cars here. Our technologies are created here, and Georgia does not take any task away from us in Germany."
Dollner said localized production is the best decision for the brand, which has struggled in sales this decade amid rising operational costs and Trump's tariffs on vehicles from Germany and other countries into the U.S. Current tariffs on vehicles from Germany are 15%, down from 25%.
Last year, U.S. tariffs cost Audi 1.2 billion euros ($1.4 billion), as it imports all its vehicles for the U.S. market from Europe or Mexico.
Dollner said the Trump administration asked Audi to announce the new plant at the Georgia rally promoting Republicans ahead of Nov. 3 midterm elections .
"It was … a three-year project that, at the end, by coincidence, led to that moment yesterday," he said Sunday. "With respect of the office and country, we joined the invitation."
Dollner noted Audi is the last major German luxury brand to establish U.S. production after Mercedes-Benz and BMW.
The company said the Georgia plant is expected to begin production of Audi's Q7, Q8 and Q9 in the early 2030s. The plant would have the capacity to produce up to 200,000 vehicles annually, roughly half of which the automaker said will be exported outside the U.S.
"This is to make Audi obviously a significant player here in the U.S. market," said Audi of America President Vito Paladino during the roundtable. He also said additional details on U.S. investments and production are forthcoming.
Audi's U.S. deliveries were roughly flat through the third quarter of this year, following a 16% decline from 2024 to 2025.
