title: Manchester United suffer home loss, Liverpool claim maiden Anfield win
body: Michael Carrick is on the brink as Manchester United coach as his team lost 3-0 to Bournemouth in front of the Old Trafford faithful. The English Premier League (EPL) match was dominated by the decision of Carrick to bench both captain Bruno Fernandes and forward Matheus Cunha for questioning his tactics and authority respectively. On the pitch, the team was all over the place and was picked apart by the visitors who scored twice in the first half through Rayan and Marcus Tavernier, before Evanilson sealed the easy win in the second half. Bournemouth had several chances to take the lead and eventually did on 38 minutes when a free kick delivery was met with a precise low shot from Rayan that beat Senne Lammens, Man United goalkeeper, at his near post. Ebola: NCDC approves N100k weekly for each person in isolation Kaduna rally as the north’s referendum on Tinubu A slip by Leny Yoro allowed Bournemouth sight of goal, and Tavernier slotted home Adrien Truffert’s pass to hand the visitors a healthy two-nil lead at the break. It was a catalogue of errors from Man United’s players, especially the defenders but Bournemouth failed to make one count until the 71st minute when Lammens misjudged Lewis Cook’s long ball. The costly mistake allowed Evanilson in and the forward slotted high into the empty net to seal the deserved win. Defeat means Man United are winless in eight consecutive matches in all competitions, and the 20-time EPL winners are closer to relegation, sitting in 16th position with just seven points. At Anfield, Liverpool won for the first time in front of their fans in the league with a 2-0 victory over high-flying Brighton. Pascal Gross’ own goal and Alexander Isak’s effort sealed all three points for Andoni Iraola’s side. The Reds moved up to fourth position on the log with 15 points from eight matches. RESULTS Manchester United 0-3 Bournemouth Liverpool 2-0 Brighton Hull City 1-1 Brentford Crystal Palace 0-2 Newcastle United

title: Man United’s misery continues, suffer 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth
body: Manchester United slumped further into crisis with a 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth on Sunday that plunged Michael Carrick’s future as manager into doubt. Carrick’s bold decision to drop captain Bruno Fernandes backfired as defeat stretched United’s winless run to eight games and left them 16th in the Premier League, just one point above the relegation zone. For the third time in four seasons, the Cherries won 3-0 at Old Trafford as goals from Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson secured a fully deserved win for Marco Rose’s side. Fernandes was critical of Carrick’s tactics in a 4-1 thrashing by Champions League debutants Como on Wednesday. The United boss said the decision to leave out last season’s Premier League player of the year was a “purely football” driven, but it was hard to believe Fernandes was not being punished as he was left on the bench for the entire match. Carrick was taunted with chants of “you’re getting sacked in the morning” from the Bournemouth fans. But on this evidence, dismissing another manager is far from a quick fix for a club that has fallen dramatically from grace since Alex Ferguson’s retirement 13 years ago. A strong finish to last season during Carrick’s interim spell in charge secured third place in the Premier League, but was aided by a lack of European or domestic cup football. United have won just twice — against newly-promoted Ipswich and Azerbaijani side Sabah — in 12 games in all competitions this season. Bournemouth began the day behind the Red Devils in the table after a difficult start for Rose. But just three days after beating AC Milan 3-0, they outclassed another giant of the European game. Rayan opened the floodgates when he connected sweetly with Justin Kluivert’s free-kick on 38 minutes. Five minutes later, Leny Yoro stumbled under pressure from Adrien Truffert and the French full-back had a simple task to square for Tavernier to tap into an empty net. Many expected Fernandes to be stripped and ready for the start of the second half, but he remained on the bench and the United performance got no better. Inside the first minute of the restart Evanilson found the net, but was flagged offside. That let-off mattered little as Bournemouth could have run out even more convincing winners. Senne Lammens denied Rayan before the Brazilian winger fired wide after racing past Lisandro Martinez. Evanilson did finally add a third 20 minutes from time when he rounded Lammens before curling in an exquisite finish from a narrow angle. The United support unleashed their fury at the club’s unpopular owners, the Glazer family, rather than Carrick in the closing stages. Carrick applauded the Stretford End and touched his chest as he made his way down the tunnel. However, it is the manager who will likely be the fall guy after another miserable afternoon for the 20-time English champions. Vanguard News The post Man United’s misery continues, suffer 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Ebola: NCDC tracks 53 contacts, orders hospitals to isolate suspects
body: Patient improves as DG warns against delayed precautions Rivers suspected case tests negative By Chioma Obinna & Chidinma Chukwu The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has identified 53 contacts of Nigeria’s confirmed Ebola patient for follow-up and directed hospitals nationwide to promptly isolate suspected cases without waiting for laboratory confirmation, as authorities intensify efforts to contain the outbreak. The Director-General of NCDC, Dr Jide Idris, gave the directive following confirmation of Ebola Disease caused by the Bundibugyo virus in the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, on October 20, warning that prompt identification of suspected cases and strict infection prevention measures were critical to protecting healthcare workers and preventing further transmission. The patient, a 42-year-old woman who returned to Nigeria from Uganda through Addis Ababa on October 3, was reported to have improved remarkably while receiving care in isolation, according to the NCDC’s Ebola Disease Situation Report dated October 24. The 53 contacts identified by the response team include healthcare workers, domestic staff and the patient’s spouse. They have been categorised and are being followed up, with monitoring to continue for 21 days after their last possible exposure. The NCDC said contact tracing remained a priority in the response, as public health teams worked to identify and monitor people who may have been exposed to the confirmed case. Idris said the detection of the case demonstrated the importance of surveillance systems and the vigilance of healthcare workers. “The detection of this case demonstrates the importance of the surveillance systems we have continued to strengthen over the years,” he said. He stressed that hospitals must not wait for laboratory confirmation before taking precautions when Ebola is suspected. “Any suspected case must be promptly separated from other patients and reported to the relevant public health authorities. Healthcare workers should not wait for laboratory confirmation before taking appropriate precautions,” the NCDC boss said. He also emphasised the need to protect health workers, who are at risk of exposure when suspected cases are not promptly recognised and managed. “Protecting healthcare workers is essential to protecting the communities they serve,” Idris said. The confirmed case followed an alert from a private health facility on October 19. According to the situation report, the woman developed symptoms on October 7, four days after arriving in Nigeria. Her symptoms included fever, diarrhoea, generalised body aches and sore throat. She presented at a private health facility on October 10 and was admitted to another private facility on October 11. The NCDC was notified on October 19, and laboratory testing confirmed the infection the following day. No bleeding was reported in the case details contained in the situation report. Following confirmation, the NCDC activated its national incident management system at the highest level, with response activities coordinated through the Emergency Operations Centre in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, FCT authorities and partners. The response includes surveillance, contact tracing, laboratory investigations, infection prevention and control, risk communication and measures to strengthen preparedness across health facilities. The agency said hospitals should maintain effective screening and triage systems, promptly separate suspected cases from other patients, notify public health authorities and apply appropriate infection prevention and control precautions. These measures include hand hygiene, environmental cleaning, injection safety, safe handling of sharps, proper waste management and the appropriate use of personal protective equipment. The NCDC’s warning is directed at preventing delays that could expose other patients, healthcare workers and caregivers before a suspected infection is recognised and the necessary precautions are implemented. In a related development, a suspected Ebola case reported in Rivers State on October 23 tested negative, according to the NCDC’s situation report. The negative result meant the Rivers alert had not resulted in another confirmed case in the report. However, surveillance and investigation of suspected cases remain important components of the response. The NCDC also emphasised the importance of cooperation from people identified as contacts, cautioning against stigma and misinformation. “Being identified as a contact does not mean that you have Ebola,” Idris said. The agency urged the public to rely on official information and cooperate with public health teams carrying out contact tracing and follow-up. Idris warned that misinformation could undermine containment efforts by creating fear and discouraging people from reporting symptoms. “False information can create fear, discourage people from reporting symptoms and undermine the cooperation essential to stopping transmission,” he said. He recalled Nigeria’s experience in containing the 2014 Ebola outbreak, noting that lessons from that response were informing current preparedness and containment efforts. As part of investigations into the confirmed case, genomic sequencing was completed by the NCDC’s National Reference Laboratory and the African Centre of Excellence for Genomics of Infectious Diseases. The sequencing formed part of the laboratory work being undertaken alongside contact tracing and other response activities. The NCDC said prompt reporting of suspected cases, effective surveillance, timely isolation and strict infection prevention measures remained central to the effort to contain the confirmed case and detect any further infections. The agency’s directive to hospitals is that suspected cases must be separated from other patients and reported promptly, with protective measures implemented before laboratory results are available. Idris said protecting healthcare workers and maintaining public cooperation were essential to the response, as authorities continued to monitor contacts and strengthen measures aimed at preventing further transmission. END The post Ebola: NCDC tracks 53 contacts, orders hospitals to isolate suspects appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: NAF Spends Nearly N18 Billion on Jet A-1 Fuel in 10 Months to Support National Security Operations
body: Linus Aleke in Abuja The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has spent nearly N18 billion on Jet A-1 aviation fuel between November 2025 and September 2026 to sustain air operations in support of national security, the Service has revealed. Security and aviation experts said the expenditure underscores the critical role of aviation fuel in powering combat missions, intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance, as well as air mobility operations across the country. In a statement highlighting the NAF’s operational successes to commemorate the first year anniversary of the incumbent Chief of the Air Staff (CAS), Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, the Director of Public Relations and Information, Nigerian Air Force, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, disclosed: “Between November 2025 and September 2026, the NAF recorded over 6,100 flying hours and more than 2,900 sorties, consuming close to 10 million litres of Jet A-1 fuel in support of national security operations. “These missions encompassed precision air strikes, armed reconnaissance, surveillance, close air support and other tasks designed to degrade hostile elements, disrupt their freedom of action and enhance the effectiveness of surface forces. “Central to this effort has been intelligence-led mission planning, with operations guided by actionable intelligence, defined objectives and assessments of mission outcomes. The emphasis remains on ensuring that every sortie serves a clear operational purpose and contributes meaningfully to national security.” Air Commodore Ejodame said the NAF had recorded significant operational, personnel, training, infrastructure and force modernisation milestones under the leadership of Air Marshal Aneke as he approaches his first anniversary in office on 30 October 2026. He stressed that, guided by the CAS’s command philosophy of sustaining a highly motivated, professional and mission-ready force capable of delivering decisive airpower effects in synergy with surface forces, the Service had pursued a focused transformation agenda anchored on operational effectiveness, personnel welfare, technological advancement and institutional accountability. Recognising personnel as the Service’s most valuable asset, Air Marshal Aneke has placed welfare at the heart of his leadership philosophy, encapsulated in the principle of ‘Welfare for Enhanced Warfare.’ “This approach recognises that adequately supported, professionally developed and highly motivated personnel are essential to sustained operational effectiveness. Accordingly, the Service has pursued improvements in personnel allowances and medical support, alongside the provision of accommodation and the development of supporting infrastructure to enhance living and working conditions across its formations,” he said. Ejodame stressed that these initiatives, complemented by the reactivation of welfare airlift services for personnel in frontline operational theatres, reflected a deliberate commitment to strengthening morale, improving the well-being of personnel and their families, and enhancing readiness to discharge the NAF’s constitutional responsibilities of defending Nigeria’s territorial integrity and protecting its citizens. He further disclosed that, in recognition of professional service and career progression, 57 senior officers had been promoted to the ranks of Air Vice Marshal and Air Commodore, while 1,534 senior non-commissioned officers and 1,936 non-commissioned officers had advanced to higher ranks. In addition, more than 550 personnel had participated in international training and professional engagements, while over 6,000 had received local training, strengthening specialised competencies, technical proficiency and leadership capacity. Beyond personnel development, the NAF has also advanced efforts to modernise its fleet and improve aircraft availability. Ejodame said, “In September 2026, the Service received five additional helicopters comprising three AW-109 Trekker Type B helicopters and two H125 helicopters, expanding its operational flexibility and support capacity. Beyond these deliveries, the Service is pursuing a broader acquisition programme that includes 12 AH-1Z attack helicopters and other planned aircraft and unmanned aerial systems intended to strengthen airlift, combat, training, intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance capabilities. “Maintenance and fleet regeneration efforts have also progressed, including the reactivation and upgrade of six L-39ZA aircraft in Slovakia and Nigeria, as well as the ongoing Periodic Depot Maintenance of a C-130 aircraft in Portugal. These efforts complement investments in technical support, indigenous upgrades and emerging aviation technologies.” He added that safety, accountability and the responsible employment of airpower remained important pillars of the CAS’s transformation agenda. According to the NAF spokesperson, the establishment of an Operational and Safety Audit Committee is intended to support independent assessments of operational, engineering and armament units. Meanwhile, a strengthened Safety Management System promotes leadership engagement, proactive risk management and a data-driven safety culture. The Service is also advancing Civilian Harm Mitigation and Response through dedicated structures, standardised training, and enhanced assessment and investigation capabilities, he said. “Plans to establish an Open-Source Intelligence Centre further reflect the drive to improve situational awareness and operational planning through better exploitation of available information and emerging technologies. “Infrastructure development and indigenous capability remain central to sustaining these gains. The NAF has approved 284 infrastructure projects, of which 145 have been completed and 139 remain ongoing. Covering residential accommodation, academic and medical facilities, administrative and operational infrastructure, roads, power, water supply and recreational facilities, these projects are designed to improve personnel welfare and strengthen the Service’s operational and institutional capacity. “Complementing these investments are local production initiatives involving Aircraft Release Device 863 impulse release cartridges, a 250-kilogram bomb-loading trolley, and the development and ground testing of locally produced 57-millimetre rockets. Community-focused healthcare, educational and other special projects have also continued to strengthen civil-military relations and public confidence,” the statement further revealed. As Air Marshal Aneke approaches his first anniversary in office, the NAF remains focused on translating investments in personnel, platforms, training, technology and infrastructure into tangible operational results. Ejodame said that, through stronger joint operations, strategic partnerships, improved maintenance, professional development and the responsible employment of airpower, the Service continued to pursue greater readiness and effectiveness in addressing Nigeria’s security challenges. He said the objective was not simply to expand capability but to sustain a professional, accountable and responsive force prepared to address evolving threats. He concluded that the enduring commitment remained clear: stronger airpower, safer skies and a more secure Nigeria. However, the statement was silent on air mishaps, unintended killings of unarmed and Innocent civilians during air operations, and the number of personnel who paid the supreme price in defence of the nation within the period under review.

title: From Israel to Camp Nou: Israeli teenager Orian Goren named to Barcelona squad for El Clasico
body: Israeli soccer player Orian Goren, 17, was officially named in Barcelona's squad for Sunday's El Clasico against Real Madrid in the 10th round of Spain's La Liga, becoming the first Israeli player to be included in a squad for one of the most prestigious and widely watched matches in world soccer.Goren's inclusion comes primarily as a result of Dani Olmo's injury, which is expected to keep the Spanish midfielder sidelined for several weeks. Nevertheless, his selection is another indication of the confidence Barcelona coach Hansi Flick has placed in the promising Israeli youngster, having already given him several opportunities during preseason matches and included him in first-team training sessions.Flick is well acquainted with Goren, who participated in Barcelona's first-team preseason preparations, including the Joan Gamper Trophy match.Spanish sports newspaper Marca highlighted Goren's progress on Saturday, writing: "During those weeks, Goren had the opportunity to train alongside members of the first-team squad.Now, his inclusion in the squad represents another step in his development. The midfielder trained on Friday and Saturday under the guidance of the German coach."Goren's rise through Barcelona's ranksThe newspaper also praised the Israeli midfielder's performances for Barcelona's reserve team."He has become a key player for Barça Atlètic, the club's reserve team, standing out for his consistency in the middle of the pitch. He is a regular starter. A possible call-up for El Clasico would mark another chapter in his progress. At 17, Goren faces a major opportunity to be included in the squad for a match every player dreams of taking part in."Catalan sports newspaper Sport also published an article on Sunday examining how Goren managed to win over Flick, further highlighting the growing attention surrounding the Israeli prospect. The hope now is that this milestone marks only the beginning of a promising career.Following in the footsteps of Gai AssulinGoren's achievement also recalls that of another Israeli player, Gai Assulin, who was previously part of Barcelona's senior squad. Assulin made appearances for the Catalan club in the Copa del Rey but never played for Barcelona in a La Liga match.Another young player included in Barcelona's squad is Alex Campos, who has received his first league call-up, having previously been named in the squad for the match against Paris Saint-Germain.Barcelona will face Real Madrid without several injured players, including Dani Olmo, Eric Garcia, Jules Kounde, Andreas Christensen, and Roony Bardghji.

title: Lubinets calls for information about people in Oleshky who need help
body:
According to Ukrinform, the ombudsman announced this on Facebook .
"It is extremely important for us now to obtain as much information as possible about people in the town who need help. This is particularly true of older people, people with limited mobility, and those who cannot take care of themselves. If you have any information that could help organize the humanitarian mission, please contact the Ukrainian Ombudsman's Office and share this information," Lubinets said.
He urged people to submit any information via WhatsApp, Viber or Telegram at +38 067 717 51 70 and +38 073 719 81 34. Requests for assistance to residents are also being accepted by email at hotline@ombudsman.gov.ua and through the electronic office.
Lubinets noted that the humanitarian mission to assist residents of Oleshky would be carried out jointly with Russian Human Rights Commissioner Yana Lantratova. Its implementation would be made possible through the assistance and coordination efforts of U.S. First Lady Melania Trump.
As Ukrinform reported, U.S. First Lady Melania Trump said she had secured a local ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine covering only the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky in the Kherson region. According to the White House press service, the parties agreed to temporarily halt all hostilities in Oleshky to allow humanitarian aid to be delivered and prepare for the evacuation of civilians through an agreed safe corridor.
Ukraine's General Staff said that, starting on October 27, Ukraine was introducing a ceasefire in a designated area to carry out a humanitarian operation in the temporarily occupied town of Oleshky.

title: Russian-Slovak intergovernmental commission to meet in Moscow on October 26
body:
MOSCOW, October 25. /TASS/. The Russian-Slovak intergovernmental commission on economic, scientific and technical cooperation will resume its work in Moscow on October 26, deputy speaker of the Slovak parliament, Tibor Gaspar, said.
"As for the concrete date of the meeting, it will take place in Moscow on October 26, 2026," he said.
The resumption of the commission’s activities "may create conditions for discussing the prospects for economic, scientific, technical, and other practical cooperation," he told TASS. "The specific areas and scope of cooperation will depend on agreements between the sides, as well as on the current legal norms and Slovakia’s international obligations. Regular expert dialogue can help identify areas of mutual interest and maintain channels of communication even amid a complex international situation."
According to the Slovak senior lawmaker, his country and Russia have resumed preparations for the meeting of the commission which suspended its activities in 2022. He recalled that the country’s Foreign Minister Juraj Blanar had been appointed the commission’s Slovak co-chair back in May 2026. On August 20, he held a preliminary meeting with the Russian co-chair, Minister of Science and Higher Education Valery Falkov to discuss organizational issues.
An agreement to resume the activities of the intergovernmental commission was reached by Russian President Vladimir Putin and Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico in 2025.

title: 2027: Bishop rallies northern christians for Tinubu
body: Bishop John Praise Daniel, has urged Christians across northern Nigeria to unite across denominational, ethnic and political differences to support 2027 re-election bid of President Bola Tinubu. Daniel, who is the General Overseer of Dominion Chapel International made the call at the commissioning of the national secretariat of Arewa Christians for Tinubu (ACT)2027 in Abuja. He said unity was essential to achieving the organisation’s political objectives, urging Northern Christians to prioritise their interests and vision over religious denominational differences and tribal affiliations. He said a collective agreement and cooperation would strengthen the group’s capacity to achieve its objectives. “When we are united, there is no impossibility that will stand against us,” he said. The bishop expressed confidence in the movement’s ability to mobilise support for Tinubu ahead of the 2027 presidential election.” Daniel urged ACT-2027 members to take their mobilisation efforts to communities across the region, including villages, local government areas and wards, to sensitise Christians about the group’s political agenda. He advised against allowing tribal affiliations and political differences to undermine the movement, insisting that members should work together irrespective of their diverse backgrounds. “We cannot be divided on politics and tribes. When we see something that is good, we hold to it and stand together,” he said. The cleric also expressed confidence in the organisation’s vision, saying unity would be critical to translating its objectives into tangible political gains. Explaining his support for Tinubu’s re-election, Daniel recalled meeting the president in 2022, when controversy surrounded the All Progressives Congress (APC) Muslim-Muslim presidential ticket. He said he had supported giving Tinubu an opportunity to lead, partly because he believed the president had the capacity to address insecurity and improve the balance of political appointments. According to Daniel, the administration’s appointments of Christians to key government positions had reinforced his decision to support the president. He cited the appointments of Sen. George Akume as Secretary to the Government of the Federation and Gen. Christopher Musa, as Minister of Defense, as examples of Christian representation in the administration. The man of God urged Northern Christians to assess their collective interests and remain united in pursuing their political objectives, regardless of party differences. He said supporting Tinubu’s re-election was key to the group’s immediate political strategy, expressing hope that a second term would create opportunities for further political engagement and negotiations on issues affecting Northern Christians. He said the inauguration of the secretariat was part of efforts by ACT-2027 to strengthen its organisational structures and coordinate mobilisation ahead of 2027 general election. He said the group had announced a target of five million votes for Tinubu in the forthcoming presidential election. The Convener and National Coordinator of the group , Amb. Ayuba Ngbako, had said the organisation would mobilise supporters across the 19 northern states and the Federal Capital Territory through state, local government and ward structures. “ACT-2027 has also announced plans to unveil a book in December, titled “Meet President Tinubu and His 52 Managers of the Economy”, as part of its advocacy activities. The post 2027: Bishop rallies northern christians for Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Iran’s wrestler Farrokhi wins gold at 2026 World C'ships
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 25 (MNA) – Iran’s Gholamreza Farrokhi won a gold medal at the 2026 World Wrestling Championships – Men's Greco-Roman 82 kg on Sunday.
He defeated Yüksel Sarıçiçek from Turkey 5-1 in the final, Tehran Times reported.
Earlier in the day, Payam Ahmadi from Iran had won a silver medal in the 55kg.
The 2026 World Wrestling Championships are being held in Astana, Kazakhstan on Oct. 24 and 25.

title: Druze leader Walid Joumblatt believes Israel will 'never leave' southern Lebanon
body: Druze leader Walid Joumblatt believes Israel will remain in southern Lebanon for decades. “They will never leave,” he tells On The Record with Hadley Gamble from his home in Beirut. "The Americans are withdrawing. What is left is [Benjamin] Netanyahu controlling and expanding his own territory , his biblical empire." It is a stark reading of the region from a man who has lived through Lebanon's civil war , the Syrian occupation and the assassination of his father. But it captures a shift visible across the region. With the US pulling troops out and Russia consumed by its own war, Israel is the region's dominant military power . As evidence, he refers to the scale of destruction in Lebanon. In earlier incursions, he said, southern Lebanon survived as a place. This time Israel is "just trying to eradicate all the memories of the south of Lebanon, as if they are preparing for settlements, colonies”. Israel now holds "security zones" on three fronts: across southern Lebanon, in southern Syria beyond the 1974 disengagement line, and over nearly 70 per cent of Gaza, according to Defence Minister Israel Katz. On October 21, he said Israel would not withdraw from any of them. "The policy of Israel, past, actual and future, is to erase Palestinian nationhood from Gaza to the West Bank, and expand to Syria and Lebanon," Mr Joumblatt says. "It doesn't matter who wins." Israeli officials claim their troops have destroyed more than 60 villages and about 23,000 structures in southern Lebanon. Israeli displacement orders have covered about 2,000 square kilometres south of the Zahrani River and residents are barred from returning. Israel's far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called in March for the annexation of all territory up to the Litani River. Lebanon's Health Ministry says 4,389 people were killed between March 2, when Hezbollah joined the regional war in support of Iran, and October 12. The group has been badly weakened but not broken. US and Israeli estimates put its losses since February at about 2,500 fighters. A June framework agreement between Lebanon, Israel and the US ties a phased Israeli withdrawal to Hezbollah's disarmament. Israel calls the deal "performance-based" and says its troops will stay as long as Hezbollah remains a threat. Seven rounds of direct negotiations have followed. Military talks at US Central Command ended on October 22 without agreement and with no further meeting set. Mr Joumblatt says Lebanon has mistakenly chosen "the path of [US Secretary of State] Marco Rubio, which will lead us to nowhere". The belief of some Lebanese ministers that Washington will press Israel to leave is, in his words, "a total fallacy". Mr Joumblatt also dismisses the disarmament demand itself. Most of the area south of the Litani has already been cleared, he says, but drones have changed the arithmetic. "They will tell you there is a factory of drones in Baalbek. You want to go there? It's absurd." Disarmament, in his view, can never be fully achieved, which is precisely why it suits a force that intends to stay. Israel's threats are growing rather than diminishing. On October 14, Mr Katz warned that if Hezbollah joined any Iranian attack, areas around Nabatieh and the Litani would become part of a permanent "security zone", residents wold be forced to leave Beirut's southern suburbs and more than a million Shiites would be displaced. "He said it, not me," Mr Joumblatt says. Asked whether Lebanon was simply waiting, he replies: "Unfortunately." The same logic applies in Syria. Israel moved past the 1974 disengagement line after the fall of former president Bashar Al Assad in December 2024 and Mr Joumblatt says its forces are now about 40km from Damascus. Part of the prize, he says, is water. "Mount Hermon is water." Syrian President Ahmad Al Shara, whom Mr Joumblatt backs, has no army to resist. Assad destroyed the military by turning it on his own people and Israel "will not ever allow him to have a modern army", he says. But Mr Joumblatt's sharpest words were aimed at members of his own community. The Druze, an offshoot of Islam with about a million members across Syria, Lebanon and Israel, straddle the very borders Israel is now redrawing. In Syria's Sweida province, much of the territory is held by militias loyal to Hikmat Al Hijri, a Druze spiritual leader who has advocated breaking away from Damascus under Israeli protection. Since April, his camp has run an administrative council for what it calls Jabal Bashan, the biblical name for the Druze mountain. In August, he declared the Druze an "inseparable part" of Israel and on October 7 his supporters marched through Sweida waving Israeli flags. "He's not a religious leader, just a puppet in the hands of the Israelis," Mr Joumblatt says. Those who follow Mr Hijri "have chosen to be used by the Israelis as good soldiers", Mr Joumblatt adds. "They are going the wrong path of history." Israel's own Druze community, he says, decide nothing. "The Israeli government decides." To Mr Joumblatt, the pattern on both sides of the border points to a single project – a belt of Druze-populated territory, running from the occupied Golan Heights through southern Syria and along the edge of southern Lebanon. That would give Israel strategic depth under the banner of protecting a minority. Arab and Turkish analysts have for more than a year described such a route, sometimes called "David's Corridor", running from the Golan Heights towards eastern Syria. Israel has never acknowledged any such plan. The evidence is growing. This week, Damascus sent troops to Sweida as Israel was reported to be flying surveillance and radar equipment into the province. Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad Al Shibani has accused Israel of funding and arming Druze militias, and a senior Syrian official has warned of an imminent Israeli-backed offensive. In February, the Israeli military created a new post to liaise with Druze communities in Syria and Lebanon, filled by Maj Gen Ghassan Alian, a Druze officer. In March, The National reported that Israeli officers had privately urged Christian and Druze villages in southern Lebanon to push out Muslim residents, both Shiite and Sunni, who were sheltering among them. More than 200 people fled. This week, Israeli tanks advanced towards the outskirts of Hebbariyeh in the Hasbaya district, the Druze-majority corner of southern Lebanon that borders Syria. Israel says its role in Sweida is to protect Druze from a massacre, a claim it made amid the events of July 2025, when violence in the province left about 1,700 people dead. Mr Joumblatt does not dispute the killings, but he says Druze fighters also drove Bedouin families from their homes and that a mission of inquiry and a compromise should have followed. "Nothing happened," he says. He insists Mr Hijri does not speak for all Syria's Druze, many of whom live in Damascus suburbs alongside Christians and Muslims and are alienated by his separatism. Mr Joumblatt invoked Sultan Al Atrash, who led the 1925 Druze uprising against French rule, and his father, Kamal Joumblatt, an Arab nationalist assassinated in 1977. "I feel that I am abandoned by some Druze," he says. "Never mind. I will go on my own, even if I stay alone." For a minority, abandoning Arab solidarity is "suicide", Mr Joumblatt says. With traditional counterweights gone, focused elsewhere, Mr Joumblatt says Israeli power will be unchecked "It doesn't mean that while they [America] were present it was more calm," he says. "But it was significant." Asked whether America has left a vacuum and Israel is filling it, he answers yes to both. Russia, a patron of Assad's regime in Syria, is in the fifth year of its war in Ukraine. Europe has been sidelined by Washington. Saudi Arabia is absorbed by its conflict with Yemen's Houthis – the Iran-backed group has launched missiles and drones at airports in Riyadh, Abha and Dammam, killing 22 people. "The Arab world nowadays is powerless," Mr Joumblatt says. He would like Lebanon to become a neutral state similar to the Swiss model, but says that requires the consent of its neighbours. "Israel will not ever accept that." His prescription at home is the one he has offered for years: a national dialogue, built on the principle that only the state may bear arms, leading to a negotiated decommissioning of Hezbollah's weapons, with Iran's backing. Critics, including some western diplomats, say he is too soft on the group. "Tough enough to civil war?" he says in reply, recalling how the Lebanese military splintered when it was turned on its own people in the 1980s. His request of Washington is brief. "Give us some better diplomats here, and better policy there." Then he returns to his central point. With the US stepping back, Israel feels free "to do whatever they want, everywhere, anywhere, using force".

title: Isak scores again as Liverpool beat Brighton
body: Liverpool recorded their first home Premier League win of the season thanks to an impressive performance against in-form Brighton. Two goals in a four-minute first half spell – an own goal from Seagulls midfielder Pascal Gross followed by Alexander Isak’s sixth goal of the season – put the Reds in control. They should have conceded before the goals came, but Brighton’s Yasin Ayari fired wastefully over the top after a fine move from the visitors. Ayari’s miss proved costly as Liverpool took a 17th-minute lead when Florian Wirtz’s shot, which was going wide, was diverted into his own net by the unfortunate Gross. That was the first goal the Seagulls had conceded in the league since a 1-1 draw against Leeds on 5 September. Brighton’s defence was breached again shortly after, when Bradley Barcola did superbly down the right wing to create a chance and his cross was met by Isak’s cushioned volley to double the Reds’ advantage. The visitors were nearly gifted a way back into the match when home goalkeeper Alisson lost possession when playing out for the back, but Ayari’s shot rebounded off the foot of the right-hand post. Liverpool saw out Andoni Iraola’s first league win at Anfield as Reds boss – to follow two home Champions League victories and one in the Carabao Cup since he replaced the sacked Arne Slot in the summer. Brighton’s loss was only their second in 13 matches in all competitions in 2026-27 and they stayed third in the Premier League, with Liverpool moving up from fifth to fourth, one point behind the Seagulls.

title: NCDC approves N100,000 weekly stipend for Ebola contacts
body: … Emergency support to cover feeding, accommodation, family upkeep By Chioma Obinna & Chidinma Chukwu The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention, NCDC, yesterday announced the approval of an emergency payment of N100,000 per person weekly for individuals placed in isolation or quarantine as part of efforts to contain the Ebola outbreak in the Federal Capital Territory, FCT. The Director-General of the NCDC, Dr Jide Idris, disclosed this at a press briefing in Abuja on Sunday, explaining that the financial intervention was introduced after some contacts raised concerns about the cost of feeding, accommodation and maintaining their families while undergoing mandatory public health monitoring. Idris said the measure was intended to ease the financial burden on individuals identified as contacts of the confirmed Ebola patient and ensure their cooperation with public health authorities. “We are paying for their accommodation; we are paying for their feeding. Some of them are asking for a stipend to maintain their families,” he said. He added: “We are providing N100,000 per person per week just to maintain their comfort and feeding, because they were complaining.” The NCDC chief described the payment as an emergency intervention that was not part of the agency’s original response plan but had become necessary under the prevailing circumstances. “This was not planned for, but it is an emergency. We will continue to review it as we go along,” he said. Idris warned that the responsibility for financing emergency public health interventions should not rest solely on the FCT, stressing that state governments must make adequate financial and logistical provisions to respond to similar outbreaks. “This is not the responsibility of the FCT alone. What we have to do for the FCT, we have to do for any other state, just in case,” he said. According to him, state authorities must be prepared to provide the resources, personnel and materials required for contact tracing, isolation and other emergency response activities within their jurisdictions. The warning comes as health authorities intensify surveillance and containment measures following the confirmation of an imported Ebola case in Abuja on October 20. Nigeria had recorded one confirmed case as of the briefing, with 53 primary contacts identified for monitoring, according to Idris. The contacts include healthcare workers, household members, domestic staff and personnel involved in collecting samples from the patient. He said public health teams were categorising the contacts according to their levels of exposure and conducting follow-up checks, while anyone who developed symptoms would be promptly assessed and tested. The NCDC has also established isolation arrangements for contacts who require them, with health officials monitoring their condition throughout the 21-day incubation period following their last possible exposure. Idris disclosed that one contact who reported feeling unwell had tested negative, adding that surveillance and follow-up activities remained ongoing. The agency is also strengthening infection prevention and control measures in healthcare facilities, training health personnel and supporting the availability of protective equipment and laboratory supplies. The confirmed case involves a woman who travelled to Nigeria from Uganda and tested positive for the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus. According to the timeline provided by the health authorities, she developed symptoms on October 7, sought medical attention in Abuja on October 11 and was confirmed positive on October 20. The World Health Organisation has identified the infection as an imported case, with investigations continuing to establish the likely source of exposure. The regional outbreak has also affected the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Kenya, highlighting the need for stronger cross-border surveillance, rapid case identification and effective tracing of people who may have been exposed. Nigeria is drawing on lessons from its successful containment of the 2014 Ebola outbreak, when coordinated case identification, contact tracing, isolation and public health interventions helped prevent wider transmission. Idris said the NCDC was strengthening preparedness across states, emphasising that containing the current outbreak would require cooperation among government agencies, healthcare workers, affected contacts and the general public. He urged Nigerians to rely on verified information, avoid spreading rumours and cooperate with public health officials conducting contact tracing and monitoring. The post NCDC approves N100,000 weekly stipend for Ebola contacts appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Ebola: 53 Contacts, Including Healthcare Workers Under Surveillance, Says NCDC
body: The number of contacts linked to the index case of Ebola recorded in October 2026 has risen to 53, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has said. The agency said the contacts comprise health workers as well as the domestic staff and spouse of the patient diagnosed with the disease. ﻿ The NCDC, in its Ebola Disease Situation Report, said that a newly suspected case was reported by Rivers State on October 23, but laboratory results returned negative for Ebola disease. “Fifty-three contacts linked to the index case have so far been identified, categorized and followed up. Contacts listed include healthcare workers, domestic staff and spouse,” the report dated October 24, 2026, partly read. Giving a background on the index case, it said the patient is a 42-year-old woman who returned from Uganda through Addis Ababa on October 3, 2026, via an international flight to Abuja, Nigeria. The agency said she became symptomatic four days later and presented to a private health facility on October 10, and another on October 11. “She presented to another private facility on the 11th of October 2026, where she was admitted. The NCDC was notified on the 19th of October, followed by in-depth case investigation and sample collection,” it said. “A confirmation by the NCDC National Reference Laboratory was made on 20th October 2026. Symptoms at presentation included fever, diarrhoea, generalised body aches and sore throat. Bleeding was not reported.” Meanwhile, the Director-General of the agency, Dr. Jide Idris, has reassured Nigerians that the Federal Government, through the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention, the FCT health authorities and partners, is fully committed to responding to the confirmed case of Ebola disease in the Federal Capital Territory. “I recognize the concern that the confirmation of Ebola may have caused among Nigerians. Ebola is a serious disease, and we are handling this situation with the urgency it deserves,” he said at a press briefing on Sunday. “We have a clear response plan, experienced personnel, and established public health systems that we are deploying to prevent further transmission.” What Nigerians Should Expect Idris explained that the government’s response is being implemented through a structured Incident Management System, coordinated by the Emergency Operations Centre, under the national leadership of the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Mohammed Pate, and the Presidential Task Force on EVD. “Our public health teams are working to identify everyone who may have been exposed to the confirmed case, assess their level of exposure, and ensure appropriate follow-up for 21 days from their last possible exposure. “This includes healthcare workers, patients, caregivers, household members, travel-related contacts and others who may have had relevant exposure.” While describing contact tracing as a detailed process requiring careful investigation, accurate information, and continued follow-up, the DG urged Nigerian to “cooperate fully” if contacted by a public health official. “I want to appeal directly to Nigerians: if you are contacted by a public health official, please cooperate fully. Provide accurate information about your movements, contacts, and any symptoms you may have experienced. “Being identified as a contact does not mean that you have Ebola. It means that public health teams need to assess and monitor your health so that any possible infection can be identified early. Your cooperation will help us identify potential cases quickly and prevent further transmission,” Idris added. ‘Our Healthcare Workers’ He commended the healthcare workers whose vigilance and clinical judgement contributed to the identification of this case, noting that their high index of suspicion was critical in triggering the public health response. “I equally recognise their dedication care under challenging circumstances. You are central to our ability to bring this situation under control,” Idris said. “These include not only doctors, nurses and other professionals working in hospitals, but also the public health workforce responsible for surveillance, contact tracing, laboratory diagnosis, case management, infection prevention and control, community engagement and risk communication.” The Director General of the NCDC said the Federal Government would prioritise the safety, health and welfare of health workers throughout the response. “I want to use this opportunity to call on the leadership of every public and private healthcare facility in Nigeria to immediately review and strengthen their infection prevention and control measures. “Screening and triage must be instituted and consistently implemented. Healthcare workers must maintain a high index of suspicion, particularly when attending to patients with compatible symptoms and relevant exposure histories,” he said. “Standard precautions must be observed at all times. Hand hygiene, environmental cleaning, injection safety, safe management of sharps and proper waste management cannot be compromised. “Healthcare facilities must ensure the availability of appropriate personal protective equipment in the right quantities and ensure that staff know how to use it correctly.” Idris further stated that any suspected case must be promptly separated from other patients and reported to the relevant public health authorities. “Healthcare workers should not wait for laboratory confirmation before taking appropriate precautions,” he added. “Protecting healthcare workers is essential to protecting the communities they serve.” The post Ebola: 53 Contacts, Including Healthcare Workers Under Surveillance, Says NCDC appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Venezuela's opposition leader María Corina Machado returns after months in exile
body:
Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado, center, greets supporters in Barquisimeto, Venezuela, on Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. Jesus Hernandez/AP hide caption
Venezuelan opposition leader and Nobel Peace Prize laureate María Corina Machado has returned to Venezuela after ten months abroad, announcing her arrival in a social media post.
In a post on X , Machado declared: "I'm here, with you all."
Machado made her first public appearance among worshippers at the Church of Santa Rosa in Lara state, western Venezuela, where she was quickly surrounded by an ecstatic congregation. She then travelled on to Caracas, where hundreds of cheering supporters swarmed her car. "Here" she tweeted, when she arrived in the capital.
Her return poses a challenge to interim President Delcy Rodríguez, who took over after U.S. forces captured former leader Nicolás Maduro in January.
The Trump administration has repeatedly sidelined Machado, despite her prominence in the opposition. She has called for elections to be held soon, but Washington says Venezuela must first stabilize.
In January 2025, Machado went into hiding in Venezuela after being briefly detained following a protest. Later that year, she left the country in a clandestine escape, and reappeared in December in Norway, where she was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for her peaceful challenge to Maduro's authoritarian government.
Opposition figure Edmundo González, who ran against Maduro in the disputed 2024 presidential election, confirmed Machado's return in a post on X , describing it as "a very important day for Venezuelans."
He wrote: "Our sovereign voice returns with her to lead and guide this process." González Urrutia, who is currently in exile in Spain, also said he expected to join Machado soon so the country could "truly advance towards freedom," concluding: "You know it, this is until the end."
Speaking to reporters as he left the White House on Sunday afternoon, President Trump said he knew nothing about Machado's return, describing her as "a very nice woman" and adding that she had given him her Nobel Prize.
"And I hope she's safe," he said, adding that "we're doing really well in Venezuela."
Secretary of State Marco Rubio released a statement claiming that Machado's return was a "direct result" of U.S. supported reconciliation talks.
"The United States expects the freedoms of all sectors of Venezuelan politics to continue to be respected," he wrote. "Likewise, we expect all political actors to support these talks which represent the best chance Venezuela has had in thirty years to peacefully achieve not just a free and fair election but an enduring democracy."

title: New Framework Agreement for Multiyear F-35 Production and Sustainment
body:
ARLINGTON, Va., Oct. 22, 2026. The Department of War and Lockheed Martin unveiled a transformative framework agreement for multiyear F-35 Lightning II production and sustainment. This framework includes 850 US aircraft over 10 years with associated initial spares, 10 years of modification kits and sustainment, and international customer orders across Lots 21-30, at a continued production rate of 156 aircraft per year.



"This multiyear framework strengthens the way we can plan and invest in the F-35 enterprise," said Lockheed Martin Chairman, President and CEO Jim Taiclet. "With the greater certainty that comes from the US government's transformative approach to F-35 production and sustainment, we can make the upfront investments needed to expand capacity, improve efficiency, and build a more resilient supply chain. That's good for the taxpayer, good for our suppliers and, most importantly, good for the United States and its allies."

If granted multiyear authority and associated appropriations in the coming months, the F-35 Joint Program Office and Lockheed Martin will work to finalize contract terms, pricing, and schedules through a formal contract award, which will fulfill the government's imperative for a predictable, affordable, and resilient fighter jet enterprise. This effort is expected to save taxpayers billions of dollars over F-35's lifecycle through long-term pricing and industry volume discounts.

The framework agreement directly addresses Department of War and Congressional priorities to improve F-35 readiness by:

 	Providing predictable, multiyear procurement planning that eliminates the need for supplemental appropriations for, obsolescence management and production tooling.
 	Delivering high-volume procurement efficiencies and discounts that translate into tangible taxpayer savings.
 	Ensuring transparent, data driven decision-making through integrated analytics that link budget inputs to readiness outcomes.
 	Providing real-time visibility into parts inventory and readiness metrics through integrated analytics.

Highlights

 	Supply Chain Stability – Predictable demand from long-term contracts with suppliers will enable bulk procurement of raw materials and critical parts, slashing turnaround times and reducing logistics bottlenecks. This will result in better mission capable rates by eliminating the annual contracting cycle that has historically strained the industrial base.
 	Affordability – The integrated procurement model that pairs aircraft production with purchases of spare and modification parts will deliver high-volume procurement discounts, drive down unit prices and provide the US government the cost predictability it requires.
 	Economic Impact – The program will support 317,000 US jobs and generate approximately $79 billion in annual economic activity over the next decade, strengthening the nation's industrial base and providing long-term stability for suppliers who have struggled to plan under the previous resourcing model.
 	Readiness – This framework adds investments in industry capacity and logistics that build upon Lockheed Martin's existing investments that inject parts into the global spares pool and will further improve fleet readiness and rapid repair turnaround for operations.
 	International Benefits – The multiyear procurement model enables economies of scale that lower costs and enhance readiness for all F‑35 customers, reinforcing confidence in the global sustainment network and enhancing interoperability across allied fleets.

"Our new multiyear framework gives suppliers stability to plan for the future and invest with confidence, improving readiness across the F-35 fleet," said OJ Sanchez, President of Lockheed Martin Aeronautics. "This, in addition to the investments Lockheed Martin is making to the global spares pool, will directly translate into higher mission capable rates and a more resilient supply chain – critical capabilities the warfighter needs to meet today's mission and prepare for tomorrow's threats."

title: Bournemouth beat Man Utd to increase pressure on Carrick
body: The pressure on Manchester United manager Michael Carrick was upped a further notch by another insipid performance as they slumped to a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth. The Cherries were superb throughout and thoroughly deserving of their victory, which extended United’s winless run to eight games. The pre-match narrative centered on Bruno Fernandes, with the United captain dropped to the substitutes bench after he blamed Carrick’s tactics for their 4-1 defeat by Como on Wednesday – though the manager said it was a “football decision”. But despite trailing 2-0 at half-time, Fernandes, so often United’s talisman was not brought on. Fernandes watched on as his side laboured through the first half, creating little as Evanilson and Rayan spurned early opportunities for the visitors. The warning signs were there and the visitors eventually took the lead when a superb Justin Kluivert free-kick found an unmarked Rayan at the back post and he beat Senne Lammens with a well-taken volley. United’s woes were compounded two minutes before half-time when an untimely Leny Yoro slip allowed Adrien Truffert to square for Marcus Tavernier to convert into the empty net. Boos greeted the half-time whistle, though some home fans did their best to encourage their players as they trudged down the tunnel. The offside flag denied Evanilson a third Bournemouth goal early in the second half, while Rayan shot straight at Lammens, with both chances coming from Ayden Heaven mistakes. Rayan wasted another chance to end the contest after a Lisandro Martinez stumble opened up a route to goal, but Evanilson eventually knocked in the third after more comedy defending. Evanilson raced on to a long clearance and nipped the ball past Lammens, who had come charging out of his penalty area, before curling the ball into an empty net. Bournemouth only won their first league game of the season last weekend, but have now won four consecutive games in all competitions. Defeat leaves United 16th in the table with seven points after eight Premier League games, while the Cherries climb to 13th.

title: Rights activist: Ceasefire top priority for Sudan’s women
body: Sudanese women’s rights activist Naemat Koko says a comprehensive ceasefire is essential to protect lives, ensure unrestricted humanitarian access, and allow Sudan’s civilians to determine the country’s political future without the warring parties. Dr Neamat Koko, a member of the Central Committee of the Sudanese Communist Party and Director of the Gender Centre (File photo: Radio Dabanga) A comprehensive ceasefire in Sudan is the top priority for women across the country, according to political and human rights activist, development policy researcher, and member of the Central Committee of the Sudanese Communist Party, Naemat Koko, who says ending the war is a fundamental right of Sudanese people to life and security, not merely an appeal to the warring parties. Speaking to Radio Dabanga, Koko said a ceasefire was the highest priority for protecting the lives of Sudanese people inside the country. She added that it was also at the forefront of the demands of Sudanese women and activists involved in feminist and human rights movements. She stressed the need to open safe humanitarian corridors without conditions once a ceasefire had been agreed, with aid distributed under the supervision of international institutions and with the participation of Sudanese civil society organisations. This should replace reliance on institutions she described as illegitimate and unrecognised by either side in the conflict. Humanitarian assistance must reach every part of Sudan, not only areas directly affected by fighting, she said, given the widening displacement crisis and growing humanitarian needs. Criticism of political dialogue Koko criticised calls for political dialogue, citing previous dialogue initiatives during the rule of Jaafar Nimeiri and the former Islamist government, known as the Ingaz regime, which she said had failed to achieve the desired results. Genuine political dialogue was the right of the Sudanese people and their civil and political institutions that had not been involved in shedding Sudanese blood, she said. Koko described both sides in the war as “war criminals” and called for them to face trial. She said they should have no place in Sudan’s future political landscape. She urged an immediate ceasefire and the opening of humanitarian aid routes, arguing that both parties were obliged in practice to take these steps. The Sudanese people, she said, should determine the course of the country’s next phase. Koko stressed that Sudan’s political future must belong to its people, allowing them to determine their own choices through civilian and political institutions, independently of the parties to the war. Share article The post Rights activist: Ceasefire top priority for Sudan’s women appeared first on Dabanga Radio TV Online .

title: Article of Faith: The acceptable sacrifice (3), By Femi Aribisala
body:
The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit.
In the tabernacle Moses built, the inner court was reserved for consecrated priests (descendants of Aaron) to perform sacrifices. The Holy of Holies was off-limits. It was a no-go area. It was a sacred space within the Temple where the Ark of the Covenant was placed, protected by a heavy veil. Only the High Priest could enter there, once a year, on Yom Kippur. This restriction represented the high holiness required to approach God’s presence.
If any man violated these restrictions, he died on the spot. This is what happened to Nadab and Abihu when they offered strange fire in the temple. Priests entering the inner court and the holy of holies had a rope tied around their waist. If they died as a result of ritual impurity or because of sins of disobedience, they were then pulled out with the rope around their waist.
However, what is impossible with man is possible with faith in God.
Assuredly, I say to you, if you have faith as a mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move; and nothing will be impossible for you. Matt 17:20).
Therefore, Abel could offer an acceptable sacrifice to God before the Law of Moses. He did this by faith.
By faith Abel offered to God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, through which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts; and through it, he being dead still speaks. (Heb 11:4).
But by the grace of God, David, the man after God’s heart, also found a way to bypass God’s legal limitations. He was not an Aaronite, and neither was he a Levite. He was from the tribe of Judah. Nevertheless, his faith in God made a way for him to offer an acceptable sacrifice to God.
Enter into (God’s) gates with thanksgiving, and into His courts with praise. Be thankful to Him, and bless His name. (Psa 100:4).
God sent me to pray for a man sick with cancer. But after I prayed for him, God did not heal him. His parents sent for me. They said that after I prayed for him, he became better. But then he became so much worse. Could I come back to pray for him?
God told me to go back. But I struggled with God. I told Him, “If You wanted to heal him, You could have done so the first time I prayed for him.” “Why do I have to pray a second time?” “If you want to kill him, just kill him without involving me.”
So, God said, “Don’t pray for him again.” “Just show him a video.” God said, “Go to the shelf, and I will show you which video you are to show him.”
When I got to the shelf, He asked me to stretch out my hand and take a videotape. When I did, I took one entitled, “If Satan Can’t Steal Your Joy, He Can’t Keep Your Goods.”
I watched the video and understood why it was relevant. Jesus says:
Therefore, you now have sorrow; but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and your joy no one will take from you. (John 16:22).
I copied the video and took it to the man on his sickbed. But when I played the tape, it only played for 10 minutes. There was a power cut, so the recording stopped. Not to worry. I told him about the message in the video. “Rejoice.” Thereafter, for two hours, I sang praises to God with the sick man and his family.
Two weeks later, the man died. Then, I changed gears with God. I told Him it did not matter whether those He sent me to pray for lived or died. He can heal them, or He can kill them if He wants to. My business is to touch and pray; healing is His department.
When I reached that juncture, God told me to sing a song:
“I will enter His presence with thanksgiving in my heart, I will enter His courts with praise I will say this is the day that the Lord has made I will rejoice for He has made me glad.”
When I sang that song, God switched on the light. I now have perfect understanding of the matter. Indeed, I was sent to heal the sick man. But his healing was spiritual. God was taking him home to Himself. God’s message to Him was to enter His heavenly gates with thanksgiving and His courts with praise.
What God required of the man was a sacrifice of praise.
“Thus says the Lord: ‘Again there shall be heard in this place — of which you say, “It is desolate, without man and without beast” — in the cities of Judah, in the streets of Jerusalem that are desolate, without man and without inhabitant and without beast, the voice of joy and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the voice of those who will say: “Praise the Lord of hosts, for the Lord is good, for His mercy endures forever” — and of those who will bring the sacrifice of praise into the house of the Lord. For I will cause the captives of the land to return as at the first,’ says the Lord. (Jeremiah 33:10-11).
The sacrifice of praise is acceptable to God. It is offered joyfully even under the most inconvenient circumstances. God does not accept praise that is not offered joyfully.
Why are you cast down, O my soul? And why are you disquieted within me? (Psa 43:5).
No matter the vagaries of life, God requires us to offer to Him joyful praise:
Because Your lovingkindness is better than life, my lips shall praise You. Thus I will bless You while I live; I will lift up my hands in Your name. My soul shall be satisfied as with marrow and fatness, and my mouth shall praise You with joyful lips. (Psa 63:3-5).
My lips shall greatly rejoice when I sing to You, and my soul, which You have redeemed. (Psa 71:23).
Then I will go to the altar of God, to God my exceeding joy; and on the harp I will praise You, O God, my God. (Psa 43:4).
Women like to dance. But make sure you are dancing on the inside
David resolved to build a house for God. He insisted God was too important to dwell in a tabernacle. However, God told David he could not build Him a temple because he had killed too many people and his hands were full of blood.
But God said through Isaiah that He does not desire a Temple built by fleshly men.
Thus says the Lord: “Heaven is My throne, and earth is My footstool. Where is the house that you will build Me? And where is the place of My rest? For all those things My hand has made, and all those things exist,” says the Lord. “But on this one will I look: on him who is poor and of a contrite spirit, and who trembles at My word. (Isa 66:1-2).
God sent men to destroy every temple built by men.
Believe Me, the hour is coming when you will neither on this mountain, nor in Jerusalem, worship the Father. You worship what you do not know; we know what we worship, for salvation is of the Jews. But the hour is coming, and now is, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth; for the Father is seeking such to worship Him. God is Spirit, and those who worship Him must worship in spirit and truth. (John 4:21-24).
Coming to Him as to a living stone, rejected indeed by men, but chosen by God and precious, you also, as living stones, are being built up a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ. (1 Pet 2:4-5). NKJV
Do you not know that you are the temple of God and that the Spirit of God dwells in you? If anyone defiles the temple of God, God will destroy him. For the temple of God is holy, which temple you are. (1 Cor 3:16-17).
God also cannot accept sacrifices made by sinful men. What He desires from men is love and mercy. That is the first and great commandment.
You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’ (Matt 22:37).
But you cannot love God unless you are born again.
I desire mercy and not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings. (Hos 6:6).
Go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy and not sacrifice.’ For I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners, to repentance. (Matt 9:13).
