title: 'Putin's paranoia' — New air defenses appear around Russian president's Valdai residence, analysis shows
body:
Russia has built an additional ring of air defense towers within 50 kilometers (30 miles) of Russian President Vladimir Putin's residence in Valdai, Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty (RFE/RL) and OSINT analyst Jembob reported on Oct. 25.
Valdai is a small town in Russia's northwestern Novgorod Oblast. The town had a population of around 13,600 in 2025, according to Russia's Federal State Statistics Service (Rosstat).
1/19v It is autumn in Valdai, and time for the latest manifestation of Putin’s paranoia. A new air defense ring of ~16 SHORAD towers so far, was constructed in September. The total number of towers for the protection of Valdai is now 49 or 50. ⚠️the towers are not yet confirmed! pic.twitter.com/hRlnohwthP
The defensive perimeter extends to the Khotilovo military base, which serves as an alternate landing site, and a secret biological laboratory on Lisiy Island, according to RFE/RL .
Satellite images indicate that the new perimeter encompasses both the military airfield in Khotilovo and the laboratory complex on Lisiy Island.
By October, air defense systems believed to be Pantsir or Tor units had been positioned south of Putin's residence, within the 50-kilometer (30-mile) zone.
No positions have yet been identified along the northern section of the perimeter, though additional sites could be established in the coming months, the report said.
One of the towers forming the outer defensive line was already in place by March 2026, on the grounds of the Khotilovo military air base. Putin reportedly uses the base regularly. A dedicated railway branch connects it to his Valdai residence, providing a direct train route, according to RFE/RL.
Other air defense sites have been established along the shores of the Vyshny Volochyok Reservoir.
RFE/RL published an investigation into the secret laboratory on the island on Sept. 3, around the same time construction began on two new air defense towers in the area.
The Kremlin accused Ukraine of attacking Putin's residence in Valdai with more than 90 drones on Dec. 29, 2025. Russian officials claimed the drones were carrying 6-kilogram (13-pound) high-explosive warheads, but claimed that air defenses had allegedly intercepted them all, with no casualties or damage reported.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and the Foreign Ministry denied the allegations, calling them a "lie." Kyiv also accused Moscow of fabricating the claims to undermine Ukraine's standing with U.S. President Donald Trump's administration and derail ongoing peace efforts.
In early January 2026, the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) informed Trump that Ukraine had not targeted Putin's Valdai residence. U.S. intelligence assessed that Ukrainian forces had struck a military facility in the same region that night, but far from the Russian president's residence.

title: Trump Administration says it has Revoked over 300,000 Visas
body:
By R Anil Kumar 

Washington/ Bengaluru, October 20, 2026. US President Donald Trump’s administration has revoked over 300,000 US visas during his second term, the State Department said on Tuesday, October 20, as the federal government continues its sweeping immigration crackdown.



The number showed an acceleration in the pace of visa revocations in recent weeks.

In an update issued on August 10, the State Department had put the number of visa revocations since Trump’s current term began in January 2025 at over 175,000.

Trump says his immigration crackdown and deportation drive aim to improve domestic security. Rights advocates say ⁠the crackdown has violated due process and free speech rights and has created an unsafe environment, particularly for ethnic minorities, who have raised concerns about racial profiling.

In announcing the latest number on X, State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott said the Trump administration “has revoked more visas at a faster pace than any administration in history.”

Pigott said the administration had “zero tolerance for foreigners here on visas who break the law, commit fraud, or undermine our national security.”

Among visa revocations particularly condemned by rights advocates are those of pro-Palestinian foreign protesters demonstrating against US ally Israel’s attacks on Gaza and of foreigners over their social media comments about conservative commentator Charlie Kirk’s assassination.

In addition to attempts to deport foreign protesters, the Trump administration has enforced tightened social media screening of immigrants and visa applicants.

Rights advocates say the government has deployed national security reasons to target critics and used isolated cases of fraud to broadly target immigrant communities such as the Somali American community in Minnesota.

While Trump campaigned in 2024 on stopping illegal immigration, his administration has also made legal immigration more difficult — for example by imposing expensive ​fees for certain work visas.

(Source: US DEPARTMENT OF STATE)

title: Algeria Senate Approves Deployment Of Troops To Niger
body: Algeria’s upper house of parliament on Sunday approved a proposal to deploy troops to neighbouring Niger to “protect energy facilities”, a senator speaking on condition of anonymity told AFP. Any overseas deployment would mark a first since Algiers sent troops to support Egypt during the 1973 Arab-Israeli war. The legislator said 148 senators in the 174-seat body voted in favour of the move. The parliament’s lower house is set to vote on the proposal later in the day, likely to approve it as well. The rare measure from Algeria comes as Algiers and Niamey strengthen security ties after moving earlier this year to repair strained relations and following a thwarted mutiny in Niger in August. Niger faces persistent attacks by armed groups, including in areas near the border with Algeria. The neighbours, who share a 960-kilometre (600-mile) desert border, have agreed to deepen cooperation against jihadist violence, cross-border crime and trafficking. “This decision marks a historic break with Algeria’s doctrine of non-intervention in military conflicts beyond its borders,” said Abdellah Akir, an international relations researcher. “It’s driven by the need to protect Algeria’s strategic depth in the Sahel and to secure the future trans-Saharan gas pipeline,” Akir told AFP. The two countries have been working to build the Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline (TSGP), a vast project to export natural gas to Europe from Nigeria via Niger. ‘Strong Signal’ Akir said the measure also sought to “send a strong signal to competing actors, including Morocco and the United Arab Emirates” — two countries with which Algiers no longer has diplomatic ties. Geoff Porter, an analyst with the North Africa Risk Consulting group, said the move was “illustrative of a shift in Algerian policy”. Algeria “had tried to maintain its national interests and exert its regional influence through its customary means — dialogue, international law, multilateral forums,” Porter told AFP. “But in a multipolar and transactional world, those don’t work anymore. Instead, Algeria moved toward more tangible means — actual physical presence.” “Algeria is still committed to its foreign policy principles,” he added. “It’s just demonstrating them in a new way.” Earlier this month, President Abdelmadjid Tebboune signalled the possibility of military involvement in the Sahel country. “We will protect Niger no matter what,” he said in a televised address on October 3. “There are countries, which I will not name, that have conspired against (Niger). We stand by its side.” “Today, we have interests,” Tebboune then said. “We have reached agreements (with Niger) in the oil, mining and other sectors, and some are seeking to destroy all of this overnight.” Algeria’s highly unusual measure to deploy troops outside its territory requires the approval of two-thirds of its parliament, according to a constitutional amendment from 2020. Gifted Warplanes The vote followed a visit last Wednesday by Niger’s Defence Minister Salifou Modi to Algeria, where he met with Tebboune and army chief Said Chengriha. A military cooperation protocol was signed by the two sides, according to Algerian reports, but no details were given at the time. The move also comes months after Algiers gifted four military helicopters to Niamey. The warplanes were deployed at the request of Nigerien authorities, the Algerian defence ministry said. Additionally, Algeria inaugurated a 40-megawatt power plant in June intended to supply electricity to Niamey and surrounding areas. Algeria and Niger’s relations had been strained for months following Algeria’s downing last year of a drone from Mali. The incident triggered a diplomatic row, with Niger joining fellow junta-led allies Mali and Burkina Faso in recalling its ambassador from Algiers. Algeria and Mali have since resumed diplomatic ties. Niger has been run by General Tiani since a coup in July 2023 that toppled the elected president Mohamed Bazoum, who has been detained ever since. AFP The post Algeria Senate Approves Deployment Of Troops To Niger appeared first on Channels Television .

title: [UPDATED] Bournemouth Batter Man Utd, Leave Carrick On The Brink
body: Manchester United fell further into a crisis with a 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth on Sunday that plunged Michael Carrick’s future as manager into doubt. Carrick’s bold decision to drop captain Bruno Fernandes backfired as the defeat stretched United’s winless run to eight games and left them 16th in the Premier League, just one point above the relegation zone. Bournemouth’s English midfielder Marcus Tavernier (C) celebrates with teammates after scoring their second goal during the English Premier League football match between Manchester United and Bournemouth at Old Trafford in Manchester, north west England, on October 25, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP) For the third time in four seasons, the Cherries won 3-0 at Old Trafford as goals from Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson secured a fully deserved win for Marco Rose’s side. Fernandes was critical of Carrick’s tactics in a 4-1 thrashing by Champions League debutants Como on Wednesday. The United boss said the decision to leave out last season’s Premier League player of the year was “purely football” driven, but it was hard to believe Fernandes was not being punished as he was left on the bench for the entire match. Carrick was taunted with chants of “you’re getting sacked in the morning” from the Bournemouth fans. Manchester United’s English head coach Michael Carrick gestures to fans on the pitch after the English Premier League football match between Manchester United and Bournemouth at Old Trafford in Manchester, north west England, on October 25, 2026. Bournemouth won the game 3-0. Photo by DARREN STAPLES / AFP But on this evidence, dismissing another manager is far from a quick fix for a club that has fallen dramatically from grace since Alex Ferguson’s retirement 13 years ago. A strong finish to last season during Carrick’s interim spell in charge secured third place in the Premier League, but was aided by a lack of European or domestic cup football. United have won just twice — against newly-promoted Ipswich and Azerbaijani side Sabah — in 12 games in all competitions this season. Bournemouth began the day behind the Red Devils in the table after a difficult start for Rose. But just three days after beating AC Milan 3-0, they outclassed another giant of the European game. Bournemouth’s English defender James Hill (R) blocks a shot from Manchester United’s French defender Leny Yoro (L) during the English Premier League football match between Manchester United and Bournemouth at Old Trafford in Manchester, north west England, on October 25, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP) Rayan opened the floodgates when he connected sweetly with Justin Kluivert’s free-kick in the 38th minute. Five minutes later, Leny Yoro stumbled under pressure from Adrien Truffert and the French full-back had a simple task to square for Tavernier to tap into an empty net. Many expected Fernandes to be stripped and ready for the start of the second half, but he remained on the bench, and the United performance got no better. Inside the first minute of the restart, Evanilson found the net, but was flagged offside. Manchester United’s Belgian goalkeeper Senne Lammens (C) reacts after making an error for Bournemouth’s third goal during the English Premier League football match between Manchester United and Bournemouth at Old Trafford in Manchester, north west England, on October 25, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP) That let-off mattered little as Bournemouth could have run out even more convincing winners. Senne Lammens denied Rayan before the Brazilian winger fired wide after racing past Lisandro Martinez. Evanilson did finally add a third 20 minutes from time when he rounded Lammens before curling in an exquisite finish from a narrow angle. The United support unleashed their fury at the club’s unpopular owners, the Glazer family, rather than Carrick in the closing stages. Carrick applauded the Stretford End and touched his chest as he made his way down the tunnel. However, it is the manager who will likely be the fall guy after another miserable afternoon for the 20-time English champions. AFP The post [UPDATED] Bournemouth Batter Man Utd, Leave Carrick On The Brink appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Inter Beat Fiorentina, Regain Serie A Lead
body: Inter Milan struck twice in stoppage time to complete a remarkable 2-1 comeback win over Fiorentina at San Siro on Sunday and return to the summit of Serie A. Alex Jimenez’s rocket strike had the struggling visitors heading for a shock win, but Marcus Thuram levelled in the 91st minute before winning a penalty that Piotr Zielinski converted in the 98th minute. The result meant the Nerazzurri returned to first place, level with surprise fellow pace-setters Lazio on 22 points, while the Florence club’s winless run stretched to four games to keep them in 18th spot. Cristian Chivu’s side had the better of the first half but could not find a way past David de Gea, who made a fingertip stop on a Pio Esposito header before showing quick reactions to parry Thuram’s angled drive. De Gea was alert again to parry a fierce Thuram strike over the bar early in the second half, but it was the visitors who struck first against the run of play after 65 minutes. Former AC Milan player Alex Jimenez took debutant Inter goalkeeper Ivan Provedel by surprise with an audacious angled strike from distance that flew into the top corner. Inter piled forward in search of an equaliser, with Carlos Augusto’s glancing header coming off the top of the bar and De Gea denying substitute Petar Sucic, but they could not find a way through until the game was into added time. Thuram guided a shot into the bottom corner to level the scores before winning a penalty when he was dragged down by Victor Valdepenas in the box, which Zielinski converted to complete a pulsating victory. Later on Sunday, Atalanta host Frosinone and Genoa face Venezia before Juventus travel to Lecce and AC Milan go to Udinese. AFP The post Inter Beat Fiorentina, Regain Serie A Lead appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Ebola: Nine fresh persons isolated as Number on watchlist hits 53
body: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) says it is monitoring 53 primary contacts linked to the country’s confirmed Ebola case, as investigations expand to include people who may have been exposed to the patient at multiple locations. The Director-General of the NCDC, Dr Jide Idris, disclosed this on Sunday during a press briefing, explaining that 44 of the contacts were associated with the health facility where the patient was treated, while nine others had been identified outside the facility. The additional contacts include three members of the patient’s household and individuals who attended to her at an emergency room she visited before arriving at the facility where her Ebola infection was subsequently confirmed. Idris said the agency was extending its contact-tracing exercise beyond people who had direct contact with the patient to identify others who might have been exposed through the initial group of contacts. Zamfara steps up Ebola containment measures after Passenger with 38°C fever arrives airport Ebola: Nine fresh persons isolated as Number on watchlist hits 53 “As of now, we have 53 primary contacts. Of these, 44 are people from that health facility where the patient was treated,” he said. The latest figure represents an increase from the 44 contacts initially announced by the Federal Government following the confirmation of the Ebola case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) on October 20. According to information previously provided by the World Health Organisation (WHO), the patient, a woman who recently travelled from Uganda, developed symptoms on October 7 and sought medical attention on October 11 before her infection was confirmed. The NCDC said investigations were ongoing to establish the full chain of possible exposure and ensure that everyone who might have come into contact with the patient was identified and placed under appropriate monitoring. Explaining the process, Idris said health officials would interview each identified contact to determine whether they had interacted with other people who might also require monitoring. “For each person, we are going to ask questions. We have to establish who they have been in contact with. If we can identify those people, they will also be monitored,” he said. He disclosed that the patient’s medical history showed that she had visited an emergency room before presenting at the health facility where the infection was eventually confirmed. According to him, the agency had commenced efforts to trace individuals who attended to the patient during the earlier visit, with three healthcare providers from the emergency room included among the additional contacts identified. The investigation also covers healthcare personnel involved in collecting samples from the patient, underscoring concerns about the potential exposure of health workers during the management and investigation of suspected Ebola cases. Idris said the NCDC was working to strengthen infection prevention and control measures in healthcare facilities to reduce the risk of transmission among medical personnel, patients and other members of the public. He explained that the agency’s infection prevention and control teams routinely assess health facilities to determine whether appropriate safety procedures are in place and identify gaps requiring urgent attention. “When our infection prevention and control teams visit a facility, they assess the systems in place and identify areas that need to be corrected,” he said. The NCDC director-general also acknowledged the need to improve preparedness and technical capacity among health workers at the state and local government levels, noting that effective outbreak management requires trained personnel and functional infection prevention systems across the country. “Capabilities and competencies at the subnational level are not as high as they should be. We are responsible for building those capabilities. That is why training is one of our most important priorities,” Idris said. He stressed that strengthening the capacity of healthcare workers remained central to the country’s efforts to contain the outbreak and prevent further infections.

title: Kaduna rally as the north’s referendum on Tinubu
body: Through Kaduna, its old political capital, the North spoke yesterday. And the echo will haunt those who have spent months marketing the lie that the North has abandoned President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. The Kaduna Township Stadium was full beyond capacity, and the mammoth crowd overflowed into the well-adorned streets. It was a confetti of colours, flags raised high and proudly: a sea of red caps, white babban riga, green wrappers, placards of Sai Asiwaju. It was a cacophony of languages — Hausa, Fulfulde, Tiv, Idoma, Gbagyi, Yoruba, Nupe, Kanuri, and English. Entire APC governors from the North, supported by their southern counterparts, sat shoulder to shoulder with former governors, legislators, imams, pastors, women leaders, and artisans who trekked kilometres to see the man they still call Jagaba, the leader. The gathering was beyond a rented crowd; it was organic, massive, and emotional. A few photos from the event displayed that spectacularly: the excited trio waving so happily at their president who wound down the window to greet them; the many people who kept vigil at the venue so they could get a good spot to witness history; and the excited young men and women who spent the whole day under the sun waving flags and chanting praises. It was Arewa saying, without apology: we still stand with our friend. As I wrote in February 2023, at the heat of the last campaign when the same suspects tried to whip up ethnic sentiments against him, Asiwaju Tinubu and the North have always been friends. This friendship is not transactional. It is historic. Tinubu’s consequential political journey did not begin in Lagos. It began with the North. In 1991, at the beginning of the aborted Third Republic, when General Ibrahim Babangida midwifed two parties, a young Tinubu had a choice. His kinsman, the great Chief Lateef Jakande, was in the field. Yet he chose to pitch his tent with General Shehu Musa Yar’Adua’s Peoples Front (PF) — the most organised, most progressive political machine of that era. On the SDP platform under that PF, Tinubu became Senator for Lagos West in 1992. When MKO Abiola emerged as SDP candidate, Tinubu was instrumental in pushing Ambassador Babagana Kingibe, a son of Borno, as the running mate. He chose North, again. That choice in 1992 has defined his politics ever since. When President Obasanjo wanted to skin Atiku Abubakar alive in 2007, Bola Tinubu was his saviour. In 2011, he propped up Nuhu Ribadu, and Muhammadu Buhari in 2015 and 2019. In 2011, he supported Aminu Tambuwal for Speaker at a time Tambuwal’s own party, the PDP, was against him. No other Southern politician has invested that much political capital in the North. Indeed, the North doesn’t forget. This is why Arewa for Asiwaju, a political movement of the crème de la crème of the Northern political establishment, is a commendable and timely intervention. At a time when the opposition offers only recycled fuel subsidy — illegal under the PIA — and AI-generated falsehoods which Governor Uba Sani rightly warned about in Kaduna, A4A provides what Arewa needs most: honest conversation, the voice of truth, in Hausa, Fulfulde, Tiv, Nupe, Gbagyi, Kanuri, in every market, motor park, mosque and church. A4A is not just a campaign apparatus. It is a reminder that friendship is a two-way street and that the North is faithful to its values of fairness, justice, peaceful coexistence and national unity. As a political movement, its raison d’être is consensus-building and evidence-based campaigning. The purpose is to counter with evidence the lies that as president, Asiwaju Tinubu has abandoned his old friend, the North. How? With the Ministry of Livestock Development the North craved for 60 years? With the North Central Development Commission and North West Development Commission? With the new Federal Universities in Mubi, Kachia and Kabo? Would the person who abandoned the North rush the completion of the Kano-Maradi rail or the Akwanga-Lafia-Makurdi road? Would he have established cancer centres and upgraded dozens of hospitals and schools? Well, Arewa for Asiwaju is throwing those questions with hard facts. Kaduna provided a ground to further deflate the vacuous noise of the opposition. The North came together in one powerful voice. Eighteen out of 19 governors, an array of former governors from the class of 1999 to date, a horde of Young Turks, an armada of party faithful. It was a spectacle. For months, a small but loud echo chamber in Abuja and on social media had been working hard to sell a fiction — that the North regrets 2023, that the President and his campaigners can no longer enter Arewa, that 2027 is already decided. Kaduna buried that fiction with one picture. As the Campaign Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, said from the podium, everyone that mattered in the North was at the stadium yesterday. Most of them were there in person, a lot more in spirit. The few and scattered dissenters are too insignificant to cause any political upheaval. Vice President Kashim Shettima and Yari did not come to Kaduna to speak grammar. They came with history and with receipts. VP Shettima was as sharp and straight as always. He used a clincher to remind voters from the North of the options before them. “We won in 2023 not because we were the wisest or richest, but because you saw the options before you and knew the alternative was a calamity. We have come to ask you to renew a second term for the APC from top to bottom.” Senator Yari, who was evidently pleased by the turnout across all walks of life, assured: “By God’s grace, Northern Nigeria is 101 per cent behind you, Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu, and we are determined to deliver our promise on 16 January 2027.” Speaking further in Hausa, Senator Yari said the President should as well go to sleep and wait for victory. Yet, President Tinubu did not just go to Kaduna to excite the crowd or display supporters. He went with deliveries. In a first for campaign rallies, President Tinubu used the occasion to inaugurate the 81-kilometre section of the Kaduna-Abuja highway with a symbolic ribbon-cutting. It is just one of many dividends Kaduna got from the Tinubu administration, as Governor Uba Sani reeled out so many benefits Kaduna reaped from the Tinubu administration in his welcome address. They range from roads to rail to universities and health institutions. The North, as Governor Sani testified, has never had it this good. President Tinubu is repaying loyalty in concrete, steel, and care. From Peoples Front in 1991 to Arewa for Asiwaju in 2026, President Tinubu has always operated as a friend. Kaduna proved it yesterday. On 16 January 2027, the ballot will confirm it louder. Abdulaziz Abdulaziz is Senior Special Assistant to the President on Print Media and Director of Media and Communication, Arewa for Asiwaju.

title: US Marine indicted in alleged Okinawa robbery homicide
body:
Cpl. Devin Jacob Ballard was arrested in the Oct. 3 incident, authorities said.
A 20-year-old U.S. Marine stationed in Okinawa, Japan, has been indicted on charges stemming from the death last month of a woman found strangled in a hotel, authorities said on Sunday.
LCpl. Devin Jacob Ballard, who is stationed at the Futenma Air Base in Okinawa, was indicted on charges of robbery and murder, according to NHK, Japan's public broadcaster, citing the Naha District Public Prosecutors Office and other sources,
Ballard is accused of strangling a 39-year-old resident of Naha City by wrapping a telephone receiver cord around her neck at a hotel in Naha City on Oct. 3 and also allegedly stealing a backpack containing her wallet and other belongings, according to NHK.
The incident has ignited protests on Okinawa and on the mainland of Japan in Tokyo. It also prompted the Japanese government to lodge a protest with the United States.
"The occurrence of such an extremely brutal and heinous incident is a matter of profound regret, and as the Government of Japan, we have lodged a strong protest with the U.S. side," Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said in a social media statement last month, in part.
Police identified the victim as 39-year-old Anna Yagi, according to NHK.
Ballard is assigned to the III Marine Expeditionary Force, a spokesperson previously told ABC News, adding that the force would not release further personal or administrative details "to protect the integrity of the ongoing investigation and adhere to privacy regulations."
Security footage allegedly places Ballard at the hotel around the time of the homicide. The security footage showed a person who "appeared to be foreign entering the hotel with a woman and later leaving with her belongings," investigators said, according to NHK.
The man seen in the security videos resembled Ballard, including having a similar hairstyle and tattoos, police said, according to NHK .
Some of the victim's belongings were found abandoned near the hotel, NHK further reported, citing local police.
The prosecution has not disclosed whether the suspect has made incriminating statements in the case.
According to the police, Ballard denied the allegations during questioning at the time of his arrest, allegedly saying, "I don't know anything about it," NHK has reported. During subsequent questioning, Ballard made statements that partially hinted at his involvement in the incident, investigators said, according to NHK.

title: TechCrunch Mobility: Blue-green is the color of autonomy
body:
Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility , your hub for the future of transportation and now, more than ever, the role AI is playing in it. To get this in your inbox, sign up here for free — just click TechCrunch Mobility !
U.S. federal safety regulators continue to tackle the sticky problem of autonomous vehicles, this time with a proposal that could signal to the public, quite literally, when a vehicle is operating autonomously.
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has proposed new lighting requirements for autonomous vehicles that include an option (dare I say a strong suggestion?) to use cyan-colored lights to signal when a vehicle is operating autonomously without a human occupant monitoring the road.
The agency is not proposing a mandate for blue-green lights. Importantly, under the proposal, the lights would be used when an AV is operating in autonomous mode.
Still, federal regulators are clearly seeking some uniform way of identifying autonomous vehicles.
The proposal establishes equipment specifications, including where the lights are mounted, the color they emit, and how they’re activated. It would also remove requirements for manually operated controls for turn signals, high beams, and hazard lights.
Under the proposal, the NHTSA suggests the lights be cyan (blue-green), remain steadily illuminated rather than flash, and be visible from the front, rear, and both sides.
This latest proposal is one piece of a bigger effort to update regulations that help speed up the adoption of AVs while maintaining safety, according to NHTSA administrator Jonathan Morrison.
The agency is already working on a federal automated vehicle framework and is trying to update federal motor vehicle safety standards, which already govern automakers today. For instance, FMVSS rules were not designed for vehicles like the Tesla Cybercab and Zoox robotaxi, which lack traditional, federally required equipment like pedals, steering wheels, and design features like side mirrors and rearview mirrors.
While the feds wrestle over regulating the future of transportation, GM laid out how it plans to be part of it. The automaker held its annual GM Forward event, and a lot of what was announced builds on last year’s push into AI. But now we have more details and dates.
The U.S. automaker is overhauling the electrical and computational guts of its future vehicles in a bid to deliver faster software, more capable automated driving features, and a custom, conversational AI assistant that will change its 30-year-old OnStar service.
This technological overhaul is set to debut in 2028 with the Cadillac Escalade IQ. The company will also roll out an autonomous highway driving feature in 2028 that will allow drivers to have their hands and eyes off the road and without the need to be ready to take over.
GM has also adopted enterprise AI across the company to slash its traditional four- to five-year development timeline in half.
I have been around long enough to remember previous efforts at GM and other legacy automakers, all of which were interpreted as a bid to compete with Tesla. This time, GM seems to be preparing for a bigger fight.
AI startups are getting snapped up across industries, including transportation. The latest example is Rivian’s acquisition of Third Dimension , a U.K. startup founded by veterans of the gaming and autonomous vehicle industries that uses AI to turn images and videos into lifelike 3D worlds.
This is all about simulation, and specifically the idea of taking driving data and bringing it into a virtual world that matches the physical world. Rivian’s head of autonomy, James Philbin, told me the company knew it needed a technology that could close the “sim-to-real gap,” meaning the data gap between real and simulated environments.
Students of the AV industry will likely shout “Simulation is so 2017!” And yes, that’s true, simulation is a tool AV developers have relied on and continue to do so. The technology behind simulation continues to evolve, and startups like Third Dimension are ripe for the picking.
The terms of the deal weren’t released. There are a few clues for what size of deal this may have been. Third Dimension previously raised a $7 million seed round, and it has about 15 engineers, and Rivian didn’t disclose this in an SEC filing (meaning it didn’t hit the bar for material information).
Ride-hailing company inDrive , known for letting passengers and drivers negotiate fares, is working with Chinese autonomous driving firm Pony.ai and Nvidia to begin testing robotaxis in Kazakhstan in 2027. The companies have signed a memorandum of understanding to explore bringing Pony.ai’s robotaxis to inDrive’s platform.
Reliable Robotics , a startup trying to commercialize autonomous flying technology that can be installed on existing aircraft, raised $115 million . The Series D extension round included $90 million in equity funding led by Nimble Partners and $25 million in debt from Silicon Valley Bank. The Series D round now totals $275 million and has pushed the startup’s valuation beyond the $1 billion mark.
A group fighting robotaxis has some mysterious origins, the Washington Post reported . This reminds me of another anti-robotaxi group that I dug into earlier this summer called Coalition for Accountability and Road Safety, which was canvassing voters and posting on social media. My reporting discovered that the organization was registered to an employee of a New York lobbying firm that has previously been retained by several labor unions and the New York Black Car Operators’ Injury Compensation Fund.
GM is closing a plant south of Detroit that assembled battery packs for Cadillac’s flagship EV, the Celestiq, and both electric drive units and battery packs for the plug-in hybrid Chevrolet Corvette E-Ray. The closure is not related to GM’s electric vehicle strategy but because the lease on the site was nearing its end, according to a GM spokesperson.
Google is upgrading Gemini in vehicles with a personal intelligence feature that can draw on information from Gmail, Google Calendar, YouTube, Maps, Google Search history, and other connected Google services to understand your preferences, activities, and past experiences.
Rivian CEO RJ Scaringe shared his vision for how autonomy will allow his company to build radically different kinds of vehicles than the R1S electric pickup truck and R1S and R2 SUVs it makes today. All eyes are on R4.
Tesla and SpaceX reported third-quarter earnings this week, and comments by Elon Musk, who is CEO of both companies, has kicked merger talk into fifth gear. Musk said the boards of each company have formed special committees to review a merger.
Meanwhile, SpaceX’s AI business is booming , generating $7.5 billion in revenue, and now makes up 52% of the company’s income. And Tesla’s revenue, across its segments, was flat, while the company’s expenses grew. The upshot: Profits fell 43% year-over-year. Musk is very much focused on the company’s AI and robotics future, though. Tesla started production of its Optimus humanoid robot, reported rosy FSD subscription growth even as the “unsupervised version” was delayed to Q2 next year, and said it plans to start selling its Cybercab to customers by the end of the year. As senior reporter Sean O’Kane wrote: Tesla is prepping for a Cybercab onslaught .
Waymo keeps expanding within cities it already operates and into new ones. The company said it plans to launch a robotaxi service in Spain, starting with Madrid. It expects to open it up to riders in 2027. Closer to home, Waymo is now shuttling customers to and from the Harry Reid International Airport in Las Vegas.
TechCrunch Disrupt just wrapped and I am already preparing for another event. This time, it is the Founder Summit — a one-day event in Boston focused on, you guessed it, founders. This event, taking place November 4, is valuable for startup founders, aspiring founders, and investors. Attendees can expect advice-driven talks from VCs and serial founders, plus lots of chances to network.
And I will be there! Come say hi. To help make that happen, I will give TechCrunch Mobility readers a 30% discount on tickets. Click this link and use the code mobility30.

title: Gaganyaan first test flight by year-end: ISRO Chairman Narayanan
body:
Chennai, October 25. The first uncrewed test flight of India’s ambitious maiden Gaganyaan human spaceflight mission will be conducted in two months, according to the Chairman of Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) Chairman V. Narayanan. The mission will carry the half-humanoid robot Vyommitra into a low Earth orbit.



As regards the first human flight mission, Narayanan said it would be announced by the Prime Minister.

Gaganyaan project envisages demonstration of human spaceflight capability by launching three member=crew to an orbit of 400 km for a three-day mission and bring them back safely to earth, by landing in Indian sea waters.

The Chairman who was the chief guest at the graduation day event of the Sri Ramachandra Centre for Higher Education and Research (SRIHER) said that the first test flight of Gaganyaan-I (G1) would be uncrewed, using the HLVM3 rocket and the indigenously developed ‘crew module’. The test flight will take place from the spaceport of Sriharikota.

ISRO has been carrying out critical qualification tests ahead of the first test flight to validate all systems. ISRO had completed the second integrated air drop Test (IADT-02) validating the parachute deceleration systems using an Indian Air Force helicopter, besides the crew module-service module separation tests, apex cover separation, and crew module up-righting system.



The pre-requisites for Gaganyaan mission include development of many critical technologies including human rated launch vehicle for carrying crew safely to space; Life support system to provide an earth like environment to crew in space, crew emergency escape provision and evolving crew management aspects for training, recovery and rehabilitation of crew. It will carry orbital module (OM) – equipped with state-of-the-art avionics systems with adequate redundancy considering human safety – that will be orbiting the earth with the crew module (CM) and service module (SM).

Narayanan stated that ISRO’s target was to launch 50 rockets a year, almost one rocket per week, from 2029-30 for which launch pads are required. “At present we have two launch pads at Sriharikota, from where PSLV and GSLV launches are taking place. Now we have added two more, one is Kulasekarapattinam, which will primarily cater to launch of small satellite launch vehicles, and another one (3rd launch pad) in Sriharikota. Once these four launch pads are ready, we can send 50 rockets per year.”

The well proven and reliable heavy lift launcher of ISRO, the LVM3 rocket, is identified as the launch vehicle for Gaganyaan mission. It consists of solid stage, liquid stage and cryogenic stage. All systems in LVM3 launch vehicle are re-configured to meet human rating requirements and christened Human Rated LVM3. HLVM3 will be capable of launching the orbital module to an intended low earth orbit of 400 km.

title: Voter turnout in Bulgaria’s presidential poll barely reaches 16% by 4:00 p.m. local time
body:
SOFIA, October 25. /TASS/. Only 15.95% of eligible voters had cast their voters in the presidential election in Bulgaria by 4:00 p.m. local time (2:00 p.m. GMPT), the country’s Central Electoral Commission said.
According to its data, voter turnout at this time of day during the parliamentary elections in April was 34.63%.
Voting will finish at 8:00 p.m. local time (6:00 p.m. GMT).

title: Wells Fargo, Cisco, Intuit Among 6 More Companies Objecting to Tokenized Stocks
body:
The list of companies that don’t want their shares traded on OKX and ICE’s planned tokenized stock venue keeps growing.
Wells Fargo, Cisco Systems, and Marvell Technology are among six new issuers named in an updated public notice from OKXICE TSV dated Friday. Arm Holdings, Moderna and Intuit round out the new additions. That brings the total to 22 objecting companies, up from 16 on Oct. 19 and nine on Oct. 15.
Earlier objectors include Microsoft, Alphabet, Goldman Sachs , Verizon, Broadcom, and UnitedHealth Group . None of the notices explain the companies’ reasons, or what effect an objection has on whether a stock can trade on the platform.
Wells Fargo joins Goldman Sachs as the second major U.S. bank on the list. Arm, Cisco, and Marvell add more chip and networking heavyweights to a roster already crowded with tech names, including Microsoft, Broadcom and Qualcomm.
OKXICE TSV , a 50-50 joint venture between NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange and OKX’s U.S. holding company, plans to let approved users trade tokenized U.S. stocks 24/7 . Trades would run through Uniswap v4 liquidity pools on OKX’s XLayer blockchain, paired with stablecoins such as USDC.
The venue is set to operate under the SEC’s innovation exemption , which the agency unveiled in September after the Clarity Act stalled in the Senate. Since its Oct. 19 notice, the venue has said it can list shares tokenized by issuers themselves as well as by outside parties, a path none of the objectors appear to have taken yet.
The latest notice spells out the venue’s risks in detail. Beyond pausing when the underlying stock is halted, it doesn’t use circuit breakers. It has no policies addressing maximal extractable value, the profit traders can capture by reordering transactions on a blockchain.
It warns that broker-dealers trading there face unsettled questions about trade reporting and best execution, which could limit their participation and thin out liquidity. Administrators can also upgrade the smart contracts without advance notice to users, and the contract that controls who can trade has been audited only internally.
OKX and ICE first teamed up on tokenized securities earlier this year before unveiling the venue this month. Nasdaq , which won SEC approval for its own tokenized securities pilot, has said it will opt its shares out of the exemption. The IMF recently found real demand for tokenized stocks, especially during off hours when the stock market is closed, but warned that the market remains volatile and illiquid.

title: Ukrainian Attacks Kill 5 in Belgorod and Lipetsk, Hit Perm Industrial Plant
body:
Overnight Ukrainian drone attacks killed four people in southwestern Russia’s Belgorod region, one in the Lipetsk region and damaged an industrial site in the Perm region of the Ural Mountains, officials said Sunday.
In the city of Belgorod near the Russian border with Ukraine, an attack killed three people and injured 13, said Belgorod regional governor Alexander Shuvayev.
The overnight attack on Belgorod damaged 30 apartment buildings, 35 cars, four houses, three administrative buildings, eight commercial premises and three social facilities, Shuvayev said.
In a separate incident on Sunday morning, one person was killed and another injured when a Ukrainian drone struck a car in the village of Voznesenovka near the town of Shebekino, local authorities said.
A drone attack on Russia's Perm region damaged an industrial facility, injuring five of its workers, regional governor Dmitry Makhonin said on Sunday.
Emergency services were at the scene and the injured people received the necessary medical help, he said on the state-backed MAX messaging app without providing further detail on the nature of the damage.
Meanwhile, Russia’s Defense Ministry said that its drones had struck a cargo vessel bound for the Black Sea port of Chornomorsk during an overnight attack.
The ministry said the vessel was being used to supply the Ukrainian army.
Russian forces also hit a logistics center, a distribution center and a logistics terminal in the Ukrainian city of Kharkiv. The ministry said the facilities had been used for storage and distribution of dual-use cargo for the Ukrainian military.
Reuters could not independently verify the Defense Ministry's information.
Later on Sunday, southwestern Russia's Lipetsk region Governor Igor Artamonov said a Ukrainian missile strike on an industrial zone in the city of Yelets killed a security guard and injured a paramedic.
Artamonov said the security guard worked at one of the industrial facilities located on the site. The paramedic at the medical center was taken to hospital, where she was receiving the necessary treatment, the governor said.
The governor did not identify the facility that was hit in the strike.
Reuters could not independently verify the report. There was no immediate comment from Ukraine.
We are facing unprecedented challenges. Russia's Prosecutor General's Office has designated The Moscow Times as an "undesirable" organization, criminalizing our work and putting our staff at risk of prosecution. This follows our earlier unjust labeling as a "foreign agent."
These actions are direct attempts to silence independent journalism in Russia. The authorities claim our work "discredits the decisions of the Russian leadership." We see things differently: we strive to provide accurate, unbiased reporting on Russia.
We, the journalists of The Moscow Times, refuse to be silenced. But to continue our work, we need your help .
Your support, no matter how small, makes a world of difference. If you can, please support us monthly starting from just $ 2. It's quick to set up, and every contribution makes a significant impact.
By supporting The Moscow Times, you're defending open, independent journalism in the face of repression. Thank you for standing with us.

title: Israelis have changed. Will they change their leadership?
body:
A road sign stands in front of a large billboard featuring Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu (right) of the Likud party and his main center-right opponent, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, in Ramat Gan, Israel. Israel heads to the polls on Oct. 27. Jack Guez/AFP via Getty Images hide caption
TEL AVIV, Israel — Israelis are convinced that elections scheduled for Tuesday are the most pivotal in their nation's history.
Will they vote out Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu — and his coalition of far-right, ultranationalist and religious political parties — because he failed to prevent the Hamas attacks on Oct. 7, 2023, the deadliest day for Jews since the Holocaust?
Or will they reelect him to continue his campaign of retaliation, waging wars that aim to reshape the Middle East? His main challenger, former military chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot, leads a center-right opposition promising more diplomacy and less extremism.
It is Israel's first vote after these years of battle and bloodshed. Israelis are so concerned about their country's future that tens of thousands of expats are expected to fly back to cast ballots, since Israel does not allow absentee voting.
"We almost could have been destroyed on Oct. 7," said Israeli lawyer Shoula Romano-Horing, who flew in from Kansas City, Mo., to vote. "This is why I'm voting for Netanyahu, to make Israel so secure and so safe."
In the opposite corner are those Israelis distressed by the global backlash to the wars Netanyahu's government has waged.
"The actions of this government cause Israelis in general and Jews in general to be tagged as, you know, mass killers," said Yochai Ben-Haim, who works in renewable energy in California and is flying home to Israel for 36 hours just to vote. "This government is led by extremists that do not represent who we are, and we need to change it."
In conversations with dozens of Israelis over the last few weeks, a portrait has emerged of who Israelis are today.
A man stands in a destroyed building in the Jabalia camp for Palestinian refugees in the northern Gaza Strip on Oct. 20, 2026. Bashar Taleb/AFP via Getty Images hide caption
They are a people defiant, but also weary after three years of incessant war. They are enraged at their enemies, but also at their leaders.
Many are impervious to the pain of their Palestinian neighbors, but traumatized from the war they have wrought. They are resistant to Palestinian independence, but also revolted by the Israeli settlers pushing Palestinians off their land.
They are fed up with the world's rebuke over the Gaza war, but also fearful of their growing global isolation. They are a people in a tug-of-war with themselves.
"Israelis want to be feared and to be loved," said Israeli author Micah Goodman. "The problem is that you have two reputations you need to protect, but you can't."
Meir and Kati Zohar stand together at the memorial marker dedicated to their daughter, Bar Zohar, at the Nova festival memorial site in southern Israel, on Sept. 24, 2026. Their daughter was among the victims killed on Oct. 7, 2023. Erik Marmor for NPR hide caption
As elections near, Israelis are learning more about what led up to Oct. 7, 2023.
Throughout that year, as Israelis poured into the streets to protest Netanyahu's far-right government and its plan to weaken the judiciary, Netanyahu's security chiefs warned that regional enemies could take advantage of the turmoil to attack.
Behind the scenes, Israel received direct warnings that Hamas was planning something big. Israel and Hamas had been holding secret talks for more than a year, Palestinian mediator Sufian Abu Zaida said. When the talks stalled, Hamas' leader in Gaza had Abu Zaida relay a message threatening an "earthquake."
What kind of earthquake was unclear, said Abu Zaida, but he insists he relayed the warning to Israeli intelligence. The leader of the United Arab Emirates and Egypt's intelligence chief relayed similar warnings, according to reporting by NPR and other media outlets . "All what happened in 7 of October is needless," Abu Zaida said.
Burnt out vehicles in Ashkelon, southern Israel, are pictured following a rocket attack from the Gaza Strip on Oct. 7, 2023. Ahmad Gharabli/AFP via Getty Images hide caption
Nearly 1,200 people were killed when Hamas attacked army bases, residential communities and an outdoor music rave — and 251 people were taken hostage back to Gaza. Netanyahu denies he was warned and has never admitted any kind of responsibility for the security failure.
"Within days, his PR people were trying to shape the public narrative about events," said Amos Harel, a defense analyst for the Israeli newspaper Haaretz and author of 06:29 – Anatomy of a Failure , which details the Israeli failures to prevent the Oct. 7 attack. (The attack began that day at 6:29 a.m.) Netanyahu's strategy, he said, was "to shift the blame" to the security services and the military.
Amos Harel, military and defense analyst for the Israeli daily Haaretz, is pictured inside the newspaper's archival library in Tel Aviv. Harel has extensively reported on Israeli defense strategy, military operations, and Middle East security for decades. Erik Marmor for NPR hide caption
For much of the Gaza war, Israeli protesters flooded the streets demanding that Netanyahu strike a deal with Hamas to release Israeli hostages and end the fighting. It would take two years, Israel's longest ever war, before a hostage deal was reached. Netanyahu said he was seeking the total defeat of Hamas, though former officials who worked with Netanyahu allege he prolonged the war for political reasons — a charge that Netanyahu has denied.
"I'm absolutely convinced that this is what happened," Harel said. "He felt that if this would move on too fast, then there will be more of a significant public demand for a national commission of inquiry."
There is a great demand among Israelis for an investigation into the attack, like the 9/11 Commission in the United States. Netanyahu has blocked one in Israel.
So Israelis grappling with Oct. 7 go to the spot of the day's deadliest attack, where hundreds of people were killed when Hamas attacked the Nova music festival. The memorial there is a dusty field of plaques and thin poles bearing the pictures of smiling young people who were partying when they came under attack.
Meir and Kati Zohar hold hands as they pose for a portrait beneath a tree at the Nova music festival memorial site in southern Israel on Sept. 24, 2026. Their daughter, Bar Zohar, was killed during the Hamas-led assault on the festival on Oct. 7, 2023. Erik Marmor for NPR hide caption
Meir Zohar points to documentary photographs at the Nova festival memorial site. The center photograph shows his wounded daughter, Bar Zohar, receiving emergency treatment in the final minutes of her life on Oct. 7, 2023. Erik Marmor for NPR hide caption
A memorial marker displaying the photo and biography of Bar Zohar stands among hundreds of tributes at the Nova music festival site on Sept. 24, 2026. Hundreds were killed at the site during the Hamas-led attack on Oct. 7, 2023. Erik Marmor for NPR hide caption
Meir and Kati Zohar display matching memorial tattoos featuring the birth year and zodiac sign of their daughter, Bar Zohar. Erik Marmor for NPR hide caption
Israeli soldiers visit a memorial commemorating security personnel who died defending those who came under attack at the Nova festival site. Erik Marmor for NPR hide caption
Kati and Meir Zohar, whose 23-year-old daughter Bar was killed there, helped build the memorial with other families. The Zohars say they received no government funding for the effort and no phone call from Netanyahu expressing his condolences.
She believes Netanyahu bears the responsibility for what happened to her daughter on Oct. 7 and, like other Israelis, hopes Netanyahu faces a reckoning for it on election day.
"It's a hope that something will change," Zohar said. "I hope that someone will come and take his place and be the one who [is] trying to keep this country together."
The Oct. 7 attack left Israelis in a state of shock.
"I think the general line of thinking — not only among decision-makers, not only among ministers of the government, but also among commanders in the field — was that something biblical has happened to us and that something biblical needed to happen in return," Harel said.
What happened in return was an Israeli military onslaught that has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians and left most of Gaza destroyed. Today, Israel is fighting back against charges of genocide. Netanyahu faces an international arrest warrant for alleged war crimes. Israeli soldiers who fought in the war risk arrest in some countries.
"I'm proud of what I did and I know what I did," said Lior, 34, who was one of those soldiers. "I don't mind to be in front of a judge."
Lior, 34, an Israeli reservist soldier who commanded a sniper unit during wars in Gaza and Lebanon, poses for a portrait at a farm in Udim, Israel where he plans to launch a horse therapy program for veterans with post traumatic stress disorder. Maya Levin for NPR hide caption
Lior spoke on the condition that his last name be withheld to protect his family overseas from harassment because of the nature of his role: he commanded an Israeli sniper unit in Gaza and Lebanon, serving over 500 days in uniform.
" When you're inside Gaza, your life is under danger 24/7. There is shooting, there is booming… sometimes you hear about Hezbollah, Hamas, what they are doing. So your body, your mind is under survival tension 24/7," Lior said.
He is among the nearly 19,000 Israeli soldiers who have been newly diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder or related illnesses. It touches every part of his life: He imagines snipers on the streets. He sometimes breaks into tears riding the train. He struggles in his sex life. He and his fiancé broke up.
Lior said he often returns to one memory from Gaza: his order to shoot and kill a man he described as a Hamas terrorist, standing next to his child in a place where he shouldn't have been.
"Unfortunately, yeah, the kid saw his father dying in front of him," Lior said.
He does not regret any of his decisions to open fire.
"To be honest, in my opinion, I don't have any mercy of people in Gaza. I know what's going on there. I know of the poverty, I know about the lack of water, electricity. I don't have any mercy on them," Lior said. "When you see things with your own eyes and you remember what happened on the 7th of October, I'm not forgiving for that."
"You know, my Jewish identity (is) saying that I'm sure there is, but…I don't see it that way. That's what I told you about the kid," Lior said. "If he have the chance, he will kill me."
He is among the nearly 300,000 young Israeli military veterans ordered to leave their civilian lives and serve as reservist soldiers after Oct. 7.
Anat Saragusti, an Israeli journalist who reported from Gaza in the 1990s and early 2000s for Israeli Channel 12 TV, poses for a portrait in her home in Tel Aviv. Maya Levin for NPR hide caption
More than 67 percent of Israelis in a July 2025 poll said they were not very troubled about the suffering of people in Gaza. More than 60 percent of Israelis in an August 2025 poll said they believed there were no innocent people in Gaza. That view has been reinforced by mainstream Israeli media.
"There are no uninvolved civilians in Gaza," said Israeli reporter Almog Boker early last year on leading news network Channel 12.
This was not always the way Israeli media covered Palestinians in Gaza. Anat Saragusti, a veteran journalist, used to report from Gaza in the 1990s and early 2000s for Channel 12.
"I tried to cover Gaza as if I was living in a foreign country, to show the complexity of life, to show different stories," Saragusti said from her Tel Aviv apartment. "To show the Israeli audience that Gaza is not what they thought and think now, you know, a black hole of terrorists."
Twenty years ago, after Hamas took an Israeli soldier captive in Gaza, Israel practically sealed Gaza shut to Israeli journalists and to all Israelis. Then, Hamas took control of Gaza, Israel imposed a blockade, there were years of Hamas rocket fire into Israel and Israeli retaliation.
Tents sheltering people displaced by war stand between the rubble of destroyed buildings in the Jabalia camp for Palestinian refugees in the northern Gaza Strip on Oct. 20, 2026. Bashar Taleb/AFP via Getty Images hide caption
Since Oct. 7, most Israeli media chose not to show what Palestinian journalists were reporting day after day from Gaza: the tens of thousands of men, women and children killed; the forced displacement; the starvation; the misery of trying to survive.
"The majority of the Israeli journalists didn't do one story, you know, not even one story was done on Gaza… to see whether what these Palestinian journalists are claiming is true," said Saragusti. "They were afraid of the pushback by the audience if they dare say something about Gaza."
Amos Harel, defense analyst for the Israeli daily Haaretz, stands inside the newspaper's archival library in Tel Aviv. Erik Marmor for NPR hide caption
Harel, who writes a regular column for the Haaretz newspaper, says the nation's continuous war trauma also afflicted Israeli media.
" We were so busy with our pain and our suffering and worrying about the fate of the hostages — hundreds of hostages were held at that time by Hamas — that we didn't focus on what we did to the other side," he said.
Rubble and the remains of demolished Palestinian homes and agricultural structures lie scattered across a hillside in Masafer Yatta, in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, on Sept. 24, 2026. Erik Marmor for NPR hide caption
There is one place where even veterans of Israel's military and security establishment say what Palestinians are enduring has gone too far: the Israeli-occupied West Bank.
Since Oct. 7, Israeli settler violence toward Palestinians has skyrocketed . Settlers have seized more and more land there, with the support of the military and Netanyahu's pro-settler government, which has approved more than 100 new Jewish settlements in the West Bank, a record number.
Retired Israeli defense and government officials toured Palestinian communities affected by Israeli settler violence in the occupied West Bank, on Sept. 24, 2026. "This is evil," said Ari Shuali (second from left), a former senior Israeli intelligence official. Erik Marmor for NPR hide caption
A delegation of retired Israeli military and government officials meet with Eid Salem (right), a local community leader, in the Palestinian village of Umm al-Kheir in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, on Sept. 24, 2026. Erik Marmor for NPR hide caption
Rubble and concrete debris from the demolished home of Yaser Abu Sabha lie scattered beside a water tank trailer in Masafer Yatta, in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, on Sept. 24, 2026. Erik Marmor for NPR hide caption
"We are making a historic revolution," cabinet minister Bezalel Smotrich said this July as he announced the 104th new settlement approved by Netanyahu's current government. He said it "would prevent the establishment of a terror state in the heart of Israel."
A retired Israeli military general, Yaakov "Mendy" Or, leads groups of former Israeli military and security officials to Palestinian communities in the West Bank to show them the radical changes that have taken place over the last three years.
Maj. Gen. (Ret.) Yaakov "Mendy" Or poses for a portrait during a visit to Masafer Yatta in the occupied West Bank on Sept. 24, 2026. He leads independent groups of retired Israeli military, defense, and government officials visiting Palestinian areas affected by Israeli settler violence. Erik Marmor for NPR hide caption
A remote Palestinian pastoral hamlet with stone dwellings and shelters nestled into the arid hills of Masafer Yatta, in the occupied West Bank, on Sept. 24, 2026. Erik Marmor for NPR hide caption
On a recent tour, he brought them to Umm al-Kheir, a Palestinian village surrounded by an expanse of desert hills, where Israeli settlers have set up trailer homes right outside a Palestinian family's property.
Palestinian activist Eid Hatlin said barbed wire in the yard was placed by settlers. The settlers have blocked the family's outdoor bathroom and the Israeli army has blocked the path to their sheep, he said.
An Israeli settler drives an all-terrain vehicle along Route 317 in the South Hebron Hills, near Masafer Yatta in the occupied West Bank, on Sept. 24, 2026. Erik Marmor for NPR hide caption
Retired Israeli military and government officials tour the Masafer Yatta region of the Israeli-occupied West Bank, on Sept. 24, 2026. Erik Marmor for NPR hide caption
An Israeli flag erected by settlers is seen through the window of the home of Ikhlas al-Hathaleen in the Palestinian village of Umm al-Kheir, in the Masafer Yatta region of the Israeli-occupied West Bank, on Sept. 24, 2026. Israeli military closure orders have restricted the Palestinian family from accessing their courtyard toilet and sheep pen. Erik Marmor for NPR hide caption
"This is nasty. This is evil," said Ari Shuali, a former senior Israeli intelligence official who was part of the visiting group. "I don't believe that we as a people became such kind of unhuman behavior. I'm an Israeli. I'm a proud Israeli and I'm ashamed to be an Israeli [at] the same time."
It's one reason why some Israelis — like him — want to vote Netanyahu out.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stands amid security personnel as he meets with voters at a mall in Ramle, Israel on Oct. 19, 2026. Ilia Yefimovich/AFP via Getty Images hide caption
Netanyahu has downplayed Israeli settler violence in the West Bank and his allies are campaigning on a pledge to expel Palestinians — what they call encouraging emigration.
Netanyahu is campaigning on what he's done to fight back against external threats — with the wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran as examples of how he's making Israel safer since Oct. 7.
"On that darkest of days, our enemies expected us to collapse. Well, we didn't collapse. Instead, we rose and fought like lions!" Netanyahu said at the United Nations last month.
Over the last three years, Israel has killed the leaders of Hamas, Hezbollah and Iran. It has sent soldiers to capture new territory in the West Bank, Gaza, Lebanon and Syria. It has fought Houthis in Yemen and militias in Iraq. Netanyahu vows to destroy Iran's nuclear capabilities if he is reelected.
"We're entangled in endless wars and this was done on purpose," Harel said. "It's not a bug, it's a feature. The whole idea is for Israel to keep fighting, because endless wars serve Netanyahu to maintain… a constant state of emergency."
Netanyahu has called them wars of "no choice," alongside a "war for truth" waged in international media and social media.
Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party and candidate for prime minister, speaks during an election campaign conference. GIl Cohen-Magen/picture alliance via Getty Images hide caption
At a recent stump speech, Gadi Eisenkot took the stage. He is short with cropped white hair and he was wearing all black. He was speaking to a crowd in Kiryat Gat, a city near the Gaza border — historically a conservative Netanyahu stronghold.
Eisenkot is the former military chief of staff, appointed by Netanyahu a decade ago, who came back into the public spotlight in the days after Oct. 7 when he joined Netanyahu's war cabinet. Soon after, Eisenkot's son was killed as a soldier in the Gaza war. The very next day, his nephew, too, was killed there.
Eisenkot told the crowd that he began to disagree with Netanyahu's prosecution of the war three months in. "I saw a deep dysfunction in the decision-making process," Eisenkot said. "I saw that political and personal considerations were put above everything else."
He has pledged, if he wins, to launch an official national investigation into the security failure of Oct. 7 — something Netanyahu has refused to do.
"He's straight," said Yair Amar, a longtime Netanyahu voter, who said he has switched allegiances to Eisenkot.
"Many Israelis wish for a saner future," said Harel, the Haaretz columnist. "For somebody who perhaps is not as charismatic and doesn't look the part of an American senator, but is one of us and is seen as somebody who sacrificed a lot."
Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, visits the Western Wall in the Old City of Jerusalem on Oct. 22, 2026. Eisenkot is a retired chief of staff of the Israeli military. Erik Marmor/Getty Images Europe hide caption
The race is tight. Most polls show Eisenkot's camp ahead of Netanyahu's, but those same polls show neither has a clear path to victory. To win, parties must form a coalition to control a majority in Israel's parliament. The election could tip on a small amount of votes or it could end in stalemate, forcing a repeat election next year. If that were to happen, Netanyahu would stay in power with full authority to make fateful decisions, like going to war. He strongly suggests he wants to strike Iran again.
If Netanyahu loses, Eisenkot vows a different approach. He has spoken of cracking down on settler expansion and violence against Palestinians in the West Bank and of reaching diplomatic agreements in the wars Netanyahu has kept open, but cautioned he would not withdraw troops from Lebanon and Gaza anytime soon.
"Truth be told," Eisenkot told the crowd, "it will take a lot of time."
On the biggest question of all — how to solve Israel's conflict with the Palestinians — Eisenkot boasted that he "never said the solution was two states for two peoples." Meaning the creation of a Palestinian state alongside Israel — the vision that the U.S. and the majority of the world have advocated for decades. Eisenkot thinks Israel should preserve possibilities for a solution in the future. After Oct. 7, Israelis do not want to discuss a Palestinian state.
"It's not something that the Israeli public can swallow at this time," Harel said. "More and more people suspect that the Arabs, the Palestinians, are out to kill us and that the world is out to get us. And there's less support for any kind of concessions because people keep bringing up Oct. 7."
This is not a race of conservatives versus liberals, right versus left. Eisenkot is leading a group of politicians who are largely right-wing, focused on matters of security and campaigning to enlist religious ultra-Orthodox Jews to the military, which Netanyahu has resisted in order to placate his ultra-Orthodox political allies.
"I'm trusting him on the military level, but is it enough?" said Israeli high school theater teacher Anat Ben-Ari, who came to hear Eisenkot speak. She was almost nervous voicing an unpopular opinion out loud: she wants him to forge peace agreements.
"The only way to end war — all the history says that — is by agreements, is by people talking to people, even enemies. Mostly enemies," Ben-Ari said. "I think we should also pay the price for peace in order for less people to die here and not always live on our swords."
Lior, the soldier, is resigned to a future of war.
"There will always be an enemy, so I think we will always be in a war. We [will] always live on our sword," Lior said. "It will always be."
A worker uses a loupe to examine ballots at a printing factory, ahead of the Israeli legislative elections in Kiryat Gat, southern Israel, on Oct. 8, 2026. Jack Guez/AFP via Getty Images hide caption
Israeli voters now consider two different visions for their country. Should Israel fight to regain the world's acceptance or to increase their neighbors' deterrence?
Israelis yearn for both says author Micah Goodman, who has written about the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and previously served as an unofficial advisor to Israeli prime ministers.
"In the Middle East, you wanna have a certain kind of reputation. You want to be seen as unpredictable and a little crazy. Like, don't mess with us… and in the West, we want to be seen as a Norwegian, nice, sweet country playing by the rules, predictable."
Goodman said Israelis made their choice.
"After Oct. 7, the Middle East didn't fear us and you have to restore fear. But everything we did to restore fear eroded the love."
Additional reporting by NPR journalists Itay Stern, Abu Bakr Bashir and Michael Levitt.
NPR does not offer or accept money for coverage or interviews. Anyone who makes such an offer or request is not an NPR employee and does not represent NPR.

title: Man injured in Russian drone attack on minibus dies in Kherson hospital
